## 11. B2C Requirements

This section is the **canonical home of the consumer lifecycle**. Screen-level UI is owned by §14 (main website), §15 (customer portal) and §16 (Customer App); step-form workflows by §29; business rules by §30; money mechanics by §35. This section defines *what must be possible* and *what the system must do*, in lifecycle order.

The current live site has **no booking flow at all — only a quote form** (canon P10). Closing that gap is the single largest B2C build item.

### 11.1 Scope and model

B2C covers individuals, households, housing societies/RWAs and small businesses buying guarding directly, through the main website or the Customer App. The commercial model is **hybrid**: standard configurations are instantly bookable and payable online; non-standard configurations (armed, multi-site, enterprise, unusual duration) route to a quotation [CONFIRMED].

| Booking type | Path | Payment | Typical persona |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standard monthly guarding | Instant | Online, first period upfront | PER-01, PER-02 |
| Event / bouncer block | Instant (subject to D-004 rates) | Online, full block upfront | PER-05 |
| PSO / armed | Quotation | Online after quote acceptance | PER-01, PER-05 |
| Multi-site / non-standard | Quotation | Online after quote acceptance | PER-02, PER-03 |

### 11.2 The canonical B2C lifecycle

| # | Stage | System's job at this stage | Requirement IDs |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Discovery | Present services credibly, with only verifiable claims | SUR-B2C-001..004 |
| 2 | Service selection | Capture the service lane | SUR-B2C-005..007 |
| 3 | Location | Establish serviceability before anything else is promised | SUR-B2C-008..011 |
| 4 | Guard type | Capture category, which determines price and eligibility | SUR-B2C-012..014 |
| 5 | Count | Capture headcount with per-post implications | SUR-B2C-015..016 |
| 6 | Date | Capture start date and honour lead time | SUR-B2C-017..019 |
| 7 | Duration | Capture engagement length or event window | SUR-B2C-020..022 |
| 8 | Shift | Capture shift pattern and coverage hours | SUR-B2C-023..025 |
| 9 | Special requirements | Capture constraints that affect allocation | SUR-B2C-026..028 |
| 10 | Quote | Produce a priced, itemised, GST-correct offer | SUR-B2C-029..034 |
| 11 | Login / registration | Authenticate as late as possible, without losing the cart | SUR-B2C-035..038 |
| 12 | KYC | Collect identity where the service or value requires it | SUR-B2C-039..042 |
| 13 | Address / site details | Turn an address into a Site with a geofence | SUR-B2C-043..047 |
| 14 | Payment | Take money reliably and issue a compliant invoice | SUR-B2C-048..053 |
| 15 | Confirmation | Tell the client exactly what happens next and when | SUR-B2C-054..056 |
| 16 | Allocation | Assign own guards or a licence-eligible agency | SUR-B2C-057..061 |
| 17 | Guard details | Show the client who is coming | SUR-B2C-062..064 |
| 18 | ETA | Show when, and warn early if it slips | SUR-B2C-065..067 |
| 19 | Live status | Show current duty state, always truthfully | SUR-B2C-068..071 |
| 20 | Attendance | Accumulate proof the client can read and export | SUR-B2C-072..075 |
| 21 | Duty monitoring | Patrol, wake-checks and exceptions | SUR-B2C-076..079 |
| 22 | Incident / SOS | Capture, escalate, inform, resolve | SUR-B2C-080..083 |
| 23 | Replacement | Substitute without silence | SUR-B2C-084..087 |
| 24 | Completion | Close or roll the engagement cleanly | SUR-B2C-088..090 |
| 25 | Invoice | Bill from what actually happened | SUR-B2C-091..095 |
| 26 | Rating | Capture feedback that feeds allocation | SUR-B2C-096..098 |
| 27 | Repeat booking | Make the second booking trivial | SUR-B2C-099..102 |

### 11.3 Stage requirements

#### Stage 1–2 · Discovery and service selection

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2C-001 | Public pages must present the six service lanes (Home & Society, Business & Commercial, Bodyguards & Close Protection, Event Security & Bouncers, Night Patrols, Government & Tenders) each with a direct entry into the booking flow. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-002 | Every public statistic (guards on duty, sites, attendance %) must render from a live platform query; where no live number exists, the element must be omitted, not filled with a placeholder. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-003 | No client name, testimonial, award, press mention or tender may be displayed unless it exists and is evidenced; the canon's P2–P4 fabricated content must be removed before launch. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-004 | A visitor must be able to start a booking from any service page in one click, without first creating an account. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-005 | The booking flow must open with service-lane selection and carry the selection through to the quotation and the resulting Booking record. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-006 | Selecting a lane must pre-configure sensible defaults for that lane (e.g. Night Patrols defaults to a night shift pattern) while leaving every field editable. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-007 | Lane selection must be changeable at any point before payment without losing already-entered compatible data. | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### Stage 3 · Location and serviceability

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2C-008 | The flow must capture location as a pincode plus map pin, and must evaluate serviceability before showing any price or promise. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-009 | Serviceability must be evaluated against: Suraksha's own operational cities and licence scope, and the licence geography of available agency tenants (§3.4). A location is serviceable if either supply route qualifies. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-010 | For a non-serviceable location, the system must capture the requirement as demand-signal (pincode, service, count, contact) and tell the client honestly that the area is not yet covered — it must never accept a booking it cannot fulfil. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-011 | Serviceable cities for V1 launch must be an explicit configured list. [DECISION REQUIRED: D-005] | [CONFIRMED] |

#### Stage 4–9 · Configuration

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2C-012 | Guard type must be selected from the reference categories of §3.2, filtered to those available for the chosen lane and location. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-013 | Selecting an armed category must route the booking to the quotation path rather than instant checkout. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-014 | Category-specific constraints (female guard requirement, ex-serviceman preference, language, minimum height/age where the client requests it) must be capturable as structured allocation constraints, not free text. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-015 | Guard count must be captured with a stepper, with a per-lane minimum and a maximum above which the flow routes to quotation. Thresholds are configuration, not code. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-016 | Where the client's count and shift pattern imply more than one Post, the system must explain the implied post structure in plain language before pricing (e.g. "2 guards, 24×7 = 6 guard-slots across 3 shifts"). | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-017 | Start date must be capturable, with a configured minimum lead time per lane and category; a date inside the lead-time window must either be blocked with the earliest available date shown, or accepted as an urgent request with explicit urgency handling. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-018 | The system must display the committed deployment window ("guard on site by …") derived from configuration, and must record that commitment on the Booking for SLA measurement. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-019 | Lead-time and urgency rules must be per city and per category. [DECISION REQUIRED: D-104] | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-020 | Duration must be capturable as: monthly (recurring), fixed-term (n months), or event window (date + start time + hours). | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-021 | Event windows crossing midnight must be handled as a single continuous block, not as two days. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-022 | Minimum billable block per event/hourly lane must be configured and displayed before payment. [DECISION REQUIRED: D-004] | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-023 | Shift pattern must be selectable as Day, Night, or 24×7, with the underlying hours displayed explicitly (e.g. Night = 20:00–08:00). | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-024 | Custom shift timings must be capturable for non-standard needs, and must route to quotation if they fall outside configured standard patterns. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-025 | Weekly-off and relief coverage must be stated explicitly in the configuration summary, because it materially changes the number of guards billed. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-026 | Special requirements must be capturable as a structured set (uniform type, weapon requirement, dog, female personnel, language, vehicle, equipment provided by client) plus a free-text note. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-027 | Any special requirement flagged as allocation-affecting must be passed to the allocation engine as a hard or soft constraint, and must be visible to the assigned guard in the post instructions. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-028 | Free-text notes must never silently change price; if a note implies a price change, the booking must route to quotation with the note attached. | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### Stage 10 · Quote

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2C-029 | For standard configurations the system must compute and display a live price as the client configures, itemised as: rate per guard per unit × quantity × duration, subtotal, GST at the configured rate (currently 18%), total. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-030 | All displayed prices must state clearly whether they include or exclude GST; the live-site convention is exclusive-of-18%-GST and must be applied consistently. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-031 | Price computation must be server-authoritative; the client-side calculator is a display convenience and its output must be re-verified before payment. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-032 | Non-standard configurations must produce a Quotation record with `status=Pending`, a stated response commitment (currently "quote in 24 hours"), and an optional preferred site-visit slot. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-033 | An issued quotation must be visible in the client portal/app, must be acceptable online, and on acceptance must convert to a Booking without re-entry of any data. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-034 | Quotations must carry a validity period after which `status=Expired`; an expired quotation must be re-quotable in one action. | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### Stage 11–12 · Login, registration, KYC

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2C-035 | Authentication must be required only at checkout/quotation submission, never before configuration; the configured cart must survive login, signup and app/web switching. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-036 | Login must support phone OTP (primary), email + password, Google and Apple; phone verification is mandatory for every client account. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-037 | First-time profile completion must capture name, verified phone, and account type (Individual / Society-RWA / Business); account type must drive downstream document and invoicing behaviour. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-038 | Client sessions last 30 days; sensitive actions (payment method change, address deletion, user management) must require re-authentication. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-039 | KYC must be required where the service category or transaction value crosses configured thresholds — specifically for PSO/armed engagements and for society/business accounts requiring GST invoicing. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-040 | The exact KYC document set and thresholds per service category must be configured, not hard-coded, and must be reviewable by Compliance. [DECISION REQUIRED: D-105] | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-041 | KYC documents must be stored encrypted with access restricted to Verification, Compliance and audited break-glass access only (§38, §39). | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-042 | A booking must be able to proceed to payment with KYC `status=Pending` where configuration allows, but deployment must be blocked until KYC reaches `Verified` for categories requiring it; the client must be told this at booking time, not afterwards. | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### Stage 13 · Address and site details

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2C-043 | The address captured at booking must create or match a Site entity with: geocoded coordinates, geofence radius, address text, landmark, site contact name and phone, and access instructions. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-044 | Default geofence radius must be configurable per site type, with an operator-adjustable override, because a bungalow and an industrial estate cannot share one radius. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-045 | The client must be able to save multiple sites/addresses and reuse them for future bookings. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-046 | Post-level details (which gate, what the guard does, reporting person, equipment at post) must be capturable at booking or added later by Suraksha ops after the site survey, and must appear in the guard's post instructions. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-047 | Changing a site's location after deployment has started must be treated as a contract change with an explicit confirmation and possible price impact — never as an address edit. | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### Stage 14–15 · Payment and confirmation

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2C-048 | Payment must be taken via Razorpay supporting UPI, card and netbanking. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-049 | A GST-compliant invoice PDF must be generated automatically for every paid booking and be downloadable from the portal and app. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-050 | Every payment must produce a double-sided ledger entry in integer paise; no booking may be confirmed on an unreconciled payment signal alone (SUR-PLT-005, BR-003). | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-051 | The client wallet must be supported as a payment source and as a destination for refunds and credits, with a visible statement of every movement. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-052 | Payment for recurring monthly guarding must support both prepaid-per-period and invoice-with-pay-link modes; which mode applies to which client type is configuration. [DECISION REQUIRED: D-106] | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-053 | Payment capture must be idempotent: a retried or duplicated gateway callback must never create a second booking or a second charge. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-054 | The confirmation screen must state: booking reference, service, site, start date and time, guard count and category, committed deployment window, amount paid, what happens next, and the support channel. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-055 | Confirmation must be delivered on at least two channels (in-app/push and email; WhatsApp/SMS where policy and API permit) within 60 seconds of payment success. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-056 | The Booking must move to `status=Active` only when payment is confirmed and the record is complete; until then it is `Pending`. | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### Stage 16–18 · Allocation, guard details, ETA

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2C-057 | Every confirmed booking must enter the OPS fulfilment queue with a visible SLA countdown against the committed deployment window. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-058 | Allocation must offer two supply routes side by side: Suraksha's own guards (tenant `SURAKSHA-HQ`) and licence-eligible agency tenants for that district, each showing availability, category match and quality score. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-059 | Allocation to an agency tenant must be blocked where that agency holds no live licence covering the site's district (SUR-PLT-003, SUR-PLT-016). | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-060 | Assignment of a specific guard must validate: category match, special-requirement constraints, no overlapping active assignment (BR-001), valid documents, and rest-hours since last shift. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-061 | The client must never be exposed to which supply route was used unless Suraksha chooses to disclose it; the service relationship and accountability remain with Suraksha. [DECISION REQUIRED: D-107] | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-062 | On assignment, the client must receive the guard's name, photo, category/grade and a masked contact route; the guard's personal mobile number must not be exposed by default. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-063 | The client must see the assigned supervisor and an escalation contact for the site alongside the guard details. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-064 | Guard details visible to the client must update automatically on any replacement, with the reason category shown. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-065 | For first deployment and for event bookings, the system must show an ETA/arrival status against the committed reporting time. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-066 | If arrival is projected to breach the reporting time by more than a configured threshold, the client must be notified proactively with a revised ETA and a reason — before the client notices. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-067 | ETA display must degrade gracefully to "assigned, awaiting check-in" when live location is unavailable, and must never show a fabricated position. | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### Stage 19–21 · Live status, attendance, duty monitoring

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2C-068 | The client live view must show, per post: guard on duty, check-in time, current duty state, last patrol scan, last wake-check acknowledgement, and time since last verified signal. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-069 | Live location shown to a client must be limited to the contracted site and the contracted period; a guard's location outside duty hours or outside the site must never be exposed to a client (§39). | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-070 | Where the Guard App is not yet deployed for a given engagement, the live view must clearly state that the data source is ops-entered rather than device-verified. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-071 | Stale data must be labelled as stale with the age of the last signal; the UI must never present an old position as current. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-072 | Attendance must be presented to the client as a calendar and a per-day detail view, per site and per post, showing present/absent/late/replaced/leave states. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-073 | Each attendance record shown must be traceable to its evidence: check-in/out times (device and server), coordinates within/outside geofence, and photo where captured. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-074 | The client must be able to export an attendance statement for any period as PDF and Excel, readable by a third party (SUR-PLT-029). | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-075 | Any manual attendance entry or correction must be visibly marked as manual, with the operator identity and reason retained in the audit log and surfaced on hover/expand. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-076 | Night engagements must run wake-checks at a configured cadence with a configured acknowledgement window; results must be visible to the client as a per-night summary. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-077 | Patrol engagements must show checkpoint scan completion per round, with missed checkpoints flagged. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-078 | Duty exceptions (late check-in, missed check-out, geofence breach, missed wake-check, missed patrol round) must be surfaced to the client only after the configured internal grace/escalation window, so the client sees confirmed problems rather than noise. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-079 | Wake-check cadence, acknowledgement window and escalation thresholds must be configurable per contract, with platform defaults. [DECISION REQUIRED: D-108] | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### Stage 22–24 · Incident, SOS, replacement, completion

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2C-080 | The client must be able to view incidents affecting their sites with severity, time, description, photos where shared, current status and closure report. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-081 | A guard-raised SOS must reach the Command Center immediately and must notify the client's configured contacts per the escalation policy (mechanics owned by §24). | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-082 | The client must be able to raise an issue/incident themselves from the app or portal, attaching photos, and must receive an acknowledgement with a response-time commitment. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-083 | No screen may state or imply that Suraksha dispatches police, fire or ambulance services (NG-11); escalation copy must describe notification and coordination only. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-084 | Replacement must be triggerable by: guard absence, guard late beyond threshold, client request, medical/emergency, disciplinary action, or contract change — each recorded as a typed reason. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-085 | Every replacement must notify the client with the reason category, the replacement guard's details, and the revised arrival time. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-086 | A client-requested replacement must be distinguishable from an operational replacement, because the two have different money and SLA consequences. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-087 | Replacement must validate category equivalence; a lower-category substitute requires explicit client consent recorded on the record, and triggers a pricing adjustment. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-088 | Engagement completion must be explicit: fixed-term and event bookings close automatically at term end; monthly guarding rolls forward until cancelled. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-089 | On completion the system must produce a closure summary: period served, attendance totals, incidents, replacements, and final financial position. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-090 | Client data and proof records must remain accessible to the client for a configured retention period after completion (§39). | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### Stage 25–27 · Invoice, rating, repeat

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2C-091 | Monthly invoices must be generated from actual attendance against contracted units, showing: contracted units, delivered units, absences not replaced, replacements, overtime, adjustments, subtotal, GST, total. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-092 | Every invoice line must be traceable to the attendance records that produced it, in one click. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-093 | Absence not covered by a replacement must produce a pro-rata credit computed by a configured rule, applied automatically rather than on request. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-094 | A client must be able to raise an invoice dispute from the invoice itself, selecting the disputed lines; the disputed amount must be tracked separately from the undisputed balance. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-095 | Completed financial transactions must never be silently modified; corrections are credit notes or new entries (BR-003). | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-096 | The client must be able to rate an engagement (and optionally the guard) at completion and at each monthly cycle, on defined dimensions rather than a single star value. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-097 | Guard-level feedback must be visible only to the employing tenant and Suraksha ops, never publicly (NG-13). | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2C-098 | Ratings and SLA performance must feed the allocation quality score used in stage 16. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-099 | The client must be able to repeat any past booking in one action, pre-filled with the previous configuration and site, requiring only date confirmation and payment. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-100 | The client must be able to extend a running engagement (more guards, longer term, additional site) without cancelling and rebooking. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-101 | Saved payment methods and wallet balance must be usable for repeat bookings, subject to re-authentication rules. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2C-102 | Repeat and extension actions must reuse the original Site, geofence and post instructions rather than creating duplicates. | [RECOMMENDED] |

### 11.4 Alternate and exception flows

Each flow below is specified as: **trigger · actor · steps · system behaviour · money impact · notification · status outcome**. Step-form workflow detail is owned by §29; these are the contracts those workflows must satisfy.

#### F-01 Instant booking

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Client completes a standard configuration and taps Book & Pay |
| Actor | Individual Customer |
| Steps | Configure → live price → login/OTP → site details → pay → confirmation |
| System behaviour | Server re-verifies price and serviceability; creates Booking, Site (if new), Contract shell, invoice, ledger entries; pushes to fulfilment queue with SLA countdown |
| Money impact | Full first-period amount captured upfront, inclusive of GST line |
| Notification | Booking confirmed (push + email + WhatsApp/SMS where permitted); ops alert to City Operations |
| Status | Booking `Active`, Payment `Completed`, Fulfilment `Pending` |
| Requirements | SUR-B2C-103: instant booking must complete without any human step; SUR-B2C-104: server-side re-verification failure must stop the transaction before capture, not after |

#### F-02 Scheduled booking (future start date)

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Client selects a start date beyond the minimum lead time |
| Actor | Individual Customer |
| Steps | Same as F-01 with a future start date |
| System behaviour | Booking created `Active` with a future `service_start`; allocation task scheduled to open at a configured horizon before start; site survey scheduled where the lane requires it |
| Money impact | Configurable: capture now or capture at T-n days [DECISION REQUIRED: D-106] |
| Notification | Confirmation now; reminder at T-3 and T-1; guard-assigned notification when allocation completes |
| Status | Booking `Active`, Deployment `Pending` until start date |
| Requirements | SUR-B2C-105: allocation must not consume guard availability earlier than the configured horizon; SUR-B2C-106: a scheduled booking must be cancellable under the cancellation policy without penalty before the configured cut-off |

#### F-03 Recurring booking

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Client selects monthly/recurring duration |
| Actor | Individual Customer, RWA secretary |
| Steps | Configure → pay first period → engagement rolls forward each cycle |
| System behaviour | Creates a rolling Contract; each cycle generates shifts, attendance, and an invoice; renewal is automatic until cancelled |
| Money impact | Recurring charge per cycle; wallet/auto-pay where enabled; failed cycle payment follows F-16 |
| Notification | Cycle invoice issued; payment due reminder; payment received; renewal notice |
| Status | Contract `Active` continuously; each cycle's invoice has its own status |
| Requirements | SUR-B2C-107: recurring engagements must never silently lapse — non-payment triggers the dunning path, not an unannounced service stop; SUR-B2C-108: the client must see the next renewal date and next charge amount at all times |

#### F-04 Monthly guarding (standard residential/commercial)

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Client books a Home & Society or Business plan |
| Actor | Individual Customer, RWA secretary, small business owner |
| Steps | Configure guards + shift → price from plan card → pay → site survey (where configured) → deployment |
| System behaviour | Establishes Site, Posts and roster for the cycle; assigns guards with weekly-off relief coverage; runs attendance, wake-checks and patrol per configuration |
| Money impact | Per guard per month at the plan rate, excl. 18% GST; absences credited per SUR-B2C-093 |
| Notification | Monthly attendance summary; monthly invoice; expiry/renewal notice |
| Status | Contract `Active`; monthly cycles `In Progress` → `Completed` |
| Requirements | SUR-B2C-109: the relief/weekly-off model must be shown at configuration so the client understands guard-count vs coverage; SUR-B2C-110: monthly attendance summary must be issued before the invoice, not with it |

#### F-05 Event security booking

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Client books an event block (date, start time, hours, headcount, venue) |
| Actor | Event organiser (PER-05) |
| Steps | Configure event → block price → pay → team assignment → call-time arrival tracking → event completion |
| System behaviour | Creates a time-boxed deployment with a named team and a designated team lead; tracks arrival against call time; supports headcount change up to a configured cut-off |
| Money impact | Full block prepaid; minimum block enforced; overtime beyond the block billed in configured increments [DECISION REQUIRED: D-004] |
| Notification | Team assigned with roster; T-24h and T-2h reminders; arrival status; overtime authorisation request; completion summary |
| Status | Booking `Active` → `In Progress` at call time → `Completed` at block end |
| Requirements | SUR-B2C-111: the client must see per-person arrival status against call time; SUR-B2C-112: any extension beyond the booked block must require explicit client authorisation in-app before it is billable |

#### F-06 PSO / close protection booking

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Client selects Bodyguards & Close Protection or an armed category |
| Actor | Individual Customer, corporate client |
| Steps | Configure → quotation path → requirement/discretion discussion → KYC → quote acceptance → payment → assignment |
| System behaviour | Forces quotation; requires KYC verification before deployment; applies privacy restrictions on the protectee's movement data; assigns PSO-grade personnel only |
| Money impact | Quoted rate (anchor: armed officer from ₹38,000/month); deployment blocked until payment and KYC clear |
| Notification | Quote ready; quote accepted; KYC status; PSO assigned with profile summary |
| Status | Quotation `Pending` → `Active` → Booking `Active` |
| Requirements | SUR-B2C-113: protectee location data must be restricted to the client and a named ops role, excluded from general live-map views (§39); SUR-B2C-114: PSO assignment must validate grade, certification and any applicable armed-deployment records before confirmation |

#### F-07 Bouncer booking

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Client selects bouncers for a venue/event |
| Actor | Event organiser, venue manager |
| Steps | As F-05 with bouncer category and venue-specific requirements |
| System behaviour | Applies bouncer category constraints; assigns a team lead; captures venue access and dress-code instructions in post instructions |
| Money impact | Per-person per-block rate [DECISION REQUIRED: D-004] |
| Notification | Team roster with photos; arrival; incident alerts during the event |
| Status | As F-05 |
| Requirements | SUR-B2C-115: crowd-management incidents must be capturable in real time by the team lead with photo evidence and immediate client visibility |

#### F-08 Night guard booking

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Client selects a night-only shift pattern |
| Actor | Homeowner, RWA, small business |
| Steps | Standard configuration with Night shift |
| System behaviour | Enables wake-check schedule by default; sets night escalation policy; assigns night-eligible guards with rest-hour validation |
| Money impact | Standard monthly rate for the category; night differential where configured |
| Notification | Nightly wake-check summary next morning; immediate alert only on confirmed failure |
| Status | Standard |
| Requirements | SUR-B2C-116: night bookings must default to wake-checks enabled and must state the cadence at booking; SUR-B2C-117: a confirmed missed wake-check must escalate per §24 and appear in the client's morning summary with the resolution |

#### F-09 Society / RWA booking

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Account type Society-RWA books multi-gate guarding |
| Actor | RWA secretary (PER-02) |
| Steps | Configure per gate/post → combined price → committee approval (offline) → pay → deployment |
| System behaviour | Creates one Site with multiple Posts; supports multiple authorised committee users on one client account; supports handover of the account to a successor secretary |
| Money impact | Single invoice for the society; GST invoice in the society's registered name |
| Notification | Notices to all authorised committee users; monthly attendance sheet suitable for noticeboard display |
| Status | Standard |
| Requirements | SUR-B2C-118: a Society-RWA account must support multiple users with distinct client-side roles; SUR-B2C-119: account ownership transfer must be possible without losing history, with both parties notified and the change audit-logged |

#### F-10 Residential (individual home) booking

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Individual books 1–2 guards at a residence |
| Actor | Homeowner (PER-01) |
| Steps | Simplest instant path |
| System behaviour | Minimal configuration, tight geofence default, family-member contact list for notifications |
| Money impact | Plan-card rate (Home & Society ₹18,000 anchor) |
| Notification | Guard assigned with photo; daily check-in; wake-check summary for night engagements |
| Status | Standard |
| Requirements | SUR-B2C-120: a residential client must be able to add family members as notification recipients without granting them account control |

#### F-11 Cancellation

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Client cancels before or during an engagement |
| Actor | Client (any client role with authority) |
| Steps | Select booking → cancel → reason → policy consequence shown → confirm |
| System behaviour | Computes refund/charge per the cancellation policy tier (pre-deployment, post-deployment, mid-cycle); releases guard assignments; closes shifts; stops future billing |
| Money impact | Refund to original method or wallet per policy; cancellation charge where applicable; pro-rata for part-cycles |
| Notification | Cancellation confirmed with the exact refund amount and timeline; ops and assigned guards notified |
| Status | Booking `Cancelled`; Contract `Cancelled`; refund transaction its own status |
| Requirements | SUR-B2C-121: the exact financial consequence must be displayed before the client confirms, never after; SUR-B2C-122: the cancellation and refund policy tiers must be published on the site (the canon's P8 404 must be fixed) and implemented as configuration [DECISION REQUIRED: D-109] |

#### F-12 Rescheduling

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Client changes start date, event date/time, or shift pattern |
| Actor | Client |
| Steps | Select booking → reschedule → new parameters → price delta shown → confirm |
| System behaviour | Validates new date against lead time and availability; releases and re-creates shifts; preserves booking identity and history |
| Money impact | Price delta charged or credited; reschedule fee per policy where inside the cut-off |
| Notification | Reschedule confirmed with new details; affected guards reassigned and notified |
| Status | Booking remains `Active` with a new schedule; a reschedule event is recorded |
| Requirements | SUR-B2C-123: rescheduling must never be implemented as cancel-and-rebook, because it would destroy the engagement's history and SLA record |

#### F-13 Replacement

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Absence, lateness beyond threshold, client request, medical, disciplinary, or contract change |
| Actor | System-detected, Supervisor, Ops, or Client |
| Steps | Trigger → reason capture → reliever identification → assignment → client notification → arrival tracking |
| System behaviour | Creates a replacement Assignment linked to the original; validates category equivalence and rest hours; records gap duration |
| Money impact | Operational replacement: no client charge, but any uncovered gap accrues a credit per SUR-B2C-093. Client-requested replacement: no credit, possible charge per policy |
| Notification | Client informed with reason category, substitute details and revised ETA; supervisor and both guards notified |
| Status | Original Assignment `Cancelled` or `Completed-partial`; replacement Assignment `Active` |
| Requirements | SUR-B2C-124: the uncovered gap between the original guard's departure and the replacement's check-in must be measured and stored as a billable-credit input; SUR-B2C-125: replacement chains (a replacement being replaced) must remain traceable to the original assignment |

#### F-14 Guard no-show

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | No check-in by reporting time + configured grace |
| Actor | System |
| Steps | Grace expiry → supervisor alert → contact attempt → replacement triggered → client notified |
| System behaviour | Raises a P1 alert with escalation timer; opens the replacement flow automatically; marks the shift absent pending resolution |
| Money impact | Uncovered period credited to the client; guard-side absence recorded for payroll; repeat no-shows feed reliability scoring |
| Notification | Internal alert immediately; client notified once the internal grace/escalation window elapses (SUR-B2C-078) |
| Status | Shift `Failed`/absent; replacement Assignment `Active`; alert `In Progress` → `Completed` |
| Requirements | SUR-B2C-126: no-show detection must not depend on a human noticing; SUR-B2C-127: the client-facing message must state the fact, the action taken and the revised ETA, in that order |

#### F-15 Late guard

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Check-in after reporting time but within the no-show threshold |
| Actor | System |
| Steps | Late check-in recorded → lateness computed → supervisor notified → threshold evaluation |
| System behaviour | Flags the shift as late with the exact minutes; accumulates lateness for reliability scoring; escalates to no-show handling if the threshold is crossed |
| Money impact | Per contract: lateness beyond a configured tolerance may attract a pro-rata deduction on the client invoice and a payroll consequence per tenant policy |
| Notification | Supervisor immediately; client per contract configuration (some clients want every instance, most want a monthly summary) |
| Status | Attendance `Completed` with a `late` flag |
| Requirements | SUR-B2C-128: lateness tolerance and its billing consequence must be contract configuration, defaulted platform-wide, and visible to the client |

#### F-16 Payment failure

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Gateway declines, times out, or the callback is not received |
| Actor | Client / system |
| Steps | Failure detected → booking held → client shown a clear reason and retry → retry or alternate method → reconciliation sweep |
| System behaviour | Holds the configuration for a configured window without creating a confirmed booking; runs a reconciliation job against the gateway to catch late-success cases and auto-confirm; never double-charges (SUR-B2C-053) |
| Money impact | No capture on failure; on ambiguous state, funds are reconciled and either applied to the booking or refunded automatically within the configured window |
| Notification | Failure with reason and retry link; success notification if late reconciliation confirms; refund notification if reconciliation cannot be applied |
| Status | Booking `Pending`; Payment `Failed` or `Pending` until reconciled |
| Requirements | SUR-B2C-129: ambiguous payment states must be resolved by automated reconciliation, never left to the client to report; SUR-B2C-130: for a recurring cycle, payment failure must trigger the dunning ladder (reminder → grace → restricted → suspend) with each step configured and notified, and must not stop guards from being deployed inside the grace window |

#### F-17 Dispute

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Client disputes an invoice line, an attendance record or a service failure |
| Actor | Client |
| Steps | Raise dispute with lines selected and reason → evidence attached → ops review against attendance evidence → resolution (upheld / partially upheld / rejected) with explanation → credit note or closure |
| System behaviour | Splits disputed from undisputed amount; freezes collection on the disputed portion only; timestamps every step; keeps the original invoice immutable (BR-003) |
| Money impact | Credit note for upheld amounts; undisputed balance remains due |
| Notification | Dispute acknowledged with response commitment; resolution with reasoning and evidence reference |
| Status | Dispute `Pending` → `In Progress` → `Completed`/`Rejected`; invoice retains its own status |
| Requirements | SUR-B2C-131: resolution must cite the specific attendance/patrol evidence used; SUR-B2C-132: dispute rate and resolution time must be instrumented as quality metrics (§42) |

#### F-18 Emergency

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Guard SOS, client emergency raise, or a P0 incident detected at a site |
| Actor | Guard, client, Command Center Operator |
| Steps | Raise → P0 alert with escalation timer → operator acknowledges → contact ladder executed (guard, supervisor, client contacts) → coordination and logging → incident record → closure report |
| System behaviour | Bypasses normal notification batching; enforces acknowledgement within the timer; records every contact attempt and outcome; escalates automatically on timer expiry (mechanics owned by §24) |
| Money impact | None directly; may trigger contractual SLA consequences and a post-incident review |
| Notification | Immediate multi-channel to all configured emergency contacts; client informed of actions taken, not of outcomes Suraksha does not control |
| Status | Alert `In Progress` until acknowledged and resolved; Incident record `Completed` on closure report |
| Requirements | SUR-B2C-133: an emergency path must function even when the client has no app installed (SMS/voice fallback); SUR-B2C-134: emergency copy must never promise emergency-service dispatch (NG-11); SUR-B2C-135: every emergency must produce a closure report visible to the client within a configured window |

### 11.5 B2C status model

| Object | Statuses used | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Booking | Draft · Pending · Active · In Progress · Completed · Cancelled · Failed | `Draft` = configuration not submitted; `Failed` only where payment or fulfilment failed terminally |
| Quotation | Draft · Pending · Active · Rejected · Expired · Cancelled | `Active` = issued and open for acceptance |
| Assignment | Pending · Active · In Progress · Completed · Cancelled | Replacement creates a new Assignment |
| Attendance | Pending · Completed · Verified · Rejected | `Verified` after client/ops approval |
| Invoice | Draft · Pending · Completed · Cancelled | Disputed amount is an attribute, not a status |
| Payment | Pending · Completed · Failed · Cancelled | Refunds are separate transactions |
| Incident / SOS | Pending · In Progress · Completed · Archived | Severity P0–P3 is separate from status |
| Dispute | Pending · In Progress · Completed · Rejected | — |

Only the canonical status vocabulary is used; no B2C-specific status words are introduced.

## 12. B2B Requirements

This section is the **canonical home of the enterprise lifecycle** — the path from a lead to a renewed multi-site contract. It applies to Suraksha's own enterprise clients and, structurally, to the same lifecycle running inside an agency tenant's Agency Portal (§20). Screen detail is owned by §15 and §20; workflows by §29; contract and SLA money mechanics by §35.

The B2C lifecycle (§11) is not repeated here. B2B differs in five structural ways: **multi-site**, **multi-user with client-side roles**, **approval chains**, **attendance-approval before invoicing**, and **SLA as a contractual object**.

### 12.2 Stage requirements

#### Stages 1–2 · Lead and requirement capture

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2B-001 | Leads must be capturable from: website enquiry forms, inbound calls, Trinetra marketplace enquiries, tender discovery, referrals and manual entry, each with its source retained for attribution. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-002 | A lead must carry: organization, industry vertical, contact person and role, city/state, estimated guard count band, current vendor (if disclosed), and urgency. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-003 | Leads must be assignable to a Sales owner with an SLA on first response, measured and reported. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-004 | A lead must convert to an Opportunity without re-entry, carrying all captured data and its history. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-005 | Requirement capture must record, per prospective site: address, site type, operating hours, existing security arrangement, guard categories needed, headcount per shift, armed/unarmed, supervisory requirement, and special constraints. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-006 | A single opportunity must support many prospective sites, each with independent requirements, because enterprise deals are rarely uniform across locations. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2B-007 | Requirement capture must be possible offline in the field and synced later, since it happens at the client's premises. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-008 | Requirements must be versioned; a changed requirement during negotiation must not overwrite the basis of an issued quotation. | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### Stages 3–5 · Survey, risk assessment, guard calculation

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2B-009 | A site survey must be schedulable with a date, an assigned surveyor and the client's site contact, and must produce a structured survey record. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2B-010 | The survey record must capture: perimeter and entry/exit points, existing infrastructure (CCTV, barriers, lighting, guard room), footfall/vehicle movement, shift-change logistics, welfare facilities, network coverage at each proposed post, and photographs. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-011 | Network coverage per proposed post must be explicitly recorded, because it determines whether device-verified attendance will work there and whether offline capture is essential. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-012 | The survey must produce a proposed post layout that flows directly into stage 12 (post creation) without re-entry. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-013 | A risk assessment must be recordable against the site using a configured framework: threat categories, likelihood, impact, existing controls, residual risk and recommended countermeasures. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-014 | The risk assessment must be attachable to the quotation and the contract as a client-visible document, since it is a primary differentiator against price-only competitors. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-015 | Risk assessment content must be presented as professional recommendation, never as a statement of legal or statutory requirement (NG-06). | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2B-016 | The system must compute required manpower from post structure: posts × guards per post per shift × shifts per day × coverage days, plus a relief factor for weekly offs and leave. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2B-017 | The relief factor must be configurable and shown explicitly in the calculation, because it is the most common source of client confusion and margin error. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-018 | Guard calculation must produce both the deployed strength (guards on duty) and the employed strength (total guards needed including relief), and must price against the correct one. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-019 | The calculation must be re-runnable when requirements change, with a visible diff against the previous version. | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### Stages 6–7 · Quotation and negotiation

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2B-020 | A quotation must be generatable per opportunity covering many sites, itemised per site, per post and per guard category. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2B-021 | Quotation lines must show: category, count, rate basis (per guard per month / per manhour / per event block), rate, extended amount, and any site-specific loading. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-022 | The quotation must present a clear commercial summary: monthly value, annual value, GST, and inclusions/exclusions (uniform, equipment, statutory components, overtime treatment, festival coverage). | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-023 | Quotations must be exportable as a branded PDF and viewable/acceptable online in the client portal. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2B-024 | Quotation approval thresholds must be configurable: discounts or rates beyond a threshold require an internal approver before the quotation can be issued. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-025 | Every quotation revision must create a new version with a reason, preserving all prior versions and their approval history. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-026 | Negotiation notes, client counter-positions and internal margin analysis must be recorded against the opportunity and must not be visible to the client. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-027 | The system must show, per quotation version, the resulting gross margin after wage, statutory and supervision cost, so a deal is never signed blind. | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### Stage 8 · Compliance and document exchange

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2B-028 | The platform must support a bi-directional document exchange per opportunity: documents Suraksha/the agency must supply (licences, registrations, insurance, tax documents, past-performance references) and documents the client must supply (registration, tax identifiers, PO, site access authorisations). | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-029 | Each required document must have a type, an owner, a due date, a status and an expiry date where applicable, so the exchange is a tracked checklist rather than an email thread. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-030 | A reusable compliance pack must be generatable on demand for any prospect, assembled from current valid documents, so the same PDFs are not manually re-collected per deal. | [RECOMMENDED] |

| SUR-B2B-032 | Licence coverage must be validated against every proposed site's district before contract signature; a site outside licence scope must be blocked or explicitly flagged for resolution (SUR-PLT-003). | [CONFIRMED] |

#### Stages 9–10 · Contract and SLA

|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2B-033 | A Contract must be creatable from an accepted quotation without re-entry, carrying sites, posts, categories, counts, rates and terms. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2B-034 | A Contract must record: parties, effective and expiry dates, notice period, rate card with effective dates, escalation clause, payment terms, billing mode, PO reference, escalation matrix and signatories. | [RECOMMENDED] |

| SUR-B2B-040 | Every SLA metric must be computed from platform data; a metric that cannot be computed from platform data must not be offered as an SLA. | [RECOMMENDED] |

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2B-103 | The platform must support a single client organization spanning multiple states, with sites in districts served by different branches or different agency tenants, while presenting one consolidated client view. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-104 | On the supply side, a contract must be serviceable across multiple branches, with each site's operational ownership assigned to a specific branch and its supervisors. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-105 | Regional Manager scope must aggregate multiple branches for operational oversight without granting tenant-wide financial access. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-106 | The system must remain usable at a scale of at least 500 sites and 5,000 guards under a single client organization without list-based UI patterns; scale-driven UI (search-first, exception-first, hierarchical navigation) is mandatory above configured thresholds. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-107 | Bulk operations must be supported for: site creation, post creation, guard assignment, roster generation, attendance export and invoice generation, each with a preview-then-commit step and a full audit record. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-108 | Every bulk operation must be reversible or compensable, and must record who ran it, over what selection, with what result counts. | [RECOMMENDED] |

### 12.4 The client-side user mix

Enterprise accounts are not single-user. The design must assume four distinct people with conflicting needs on the same account.

| Client user | Cares about | Default landing view | What they must never see |
|---|---|---|---|
| Security Head (PER-04) | SLA, incidents, supervision quality | SLA scorecard + incident trend | Nothing restricted within their org, but guard personal PII beyond name/photo/grade |
| Facility Manager (PER-03) | Today's coverage at their sites | Live coverage board for assigned sites | Other sites; commercial terms |
| Procurement (PER-06) | Commercials, compliance documents, POs | Contract + document pack + invoice summary | Operational alert noise |
| Client Finance | Invoice accuracy and payment | Invoice list with approval state and ageing | Guard PII; operational detail beyond the attendance annexure |
| Site Manager | One site's daily reality | That site's post coverage and day log | Anything outside the site |
| Company Owner | The whole relationship and spend | Executive summary across all sites | — |

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2B-109 | Each client role must have a distinct default landing view aligned to its job; a single shared dashboard for all client roles is not acceptable. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2B-110 | Notification routing must be role- and scope-aware: a Site Manager receives their site's events, a Security Head receives P0/P1 across all sites, Client Finance receives only financial events. | [RECOMMENDED] |

### 12.5 Worked example — 12 sites, 180 guards, manufacturing client

**Client:** a mid-size auto-components manufacturer. 12 locations across two states: 3 manufacturing plants, 2 warehouses, 5 depots, 1 corporate office, 1 R&D centre. Contract value illustrative only.

**Post and manpower structure**

| Site type | Sites | Posts per site | Guards on duty per day (all shifts) | Shift pattern |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Manufacturing plant | 3 | 6 (main gate, material gate, weighbridge, finished-goods, patrol, control room) | 21 each | 3 shifts, 24×7 |
| Warehouse | 2 | 3 (gate, dock, patrol) | 9 each | 3 shifts, 24×7 |
| Depot | 5 | 2 (gate, night patrol) | 4 each | day + night |
| Corporate office | 1 | 3 (reception, basement, night) | 5 | day-weighted |
| R&D centre | 1 | 2 (gate, night) | 4 | day + night |
| **Total deployed** | **12** | **43 posts** | **~120 on duty** | — |

Applying a relief factor for weekly offs and leave (illustrative 1.5× on 24×7 posts, lower on day-only posts) gives an **employed strength of ~180 guards**, plus 6 supervisors (one per plant per major shift and one per cluster of depots), and 2 field officers covering the two states. This is the number that must be recruited, verified, inducted and paid — and the distinction between 120 deployed and 180 employed is exactly what SUR-B2B-018 exists to make explicit.

**How the platform handles it**

| Dimension | Handling |
|---|---|
| Structure | One client organization → 2 regions (state-wise) → 12 sites → 43 posts → shift patterns per post |
| Supply | Sites in State A served by Branch 1; State B sites served by Branch 2; both under one Regional Manager (SUR-B2B-105) |
| Licence | Two state licences required; each site's district validated against the licence covering it (SUR-B2B-032) |
| Roster | 43 posts × shifts = ~93 post-shifts per day → ~2,800 assignments per month, generated from post definitions with relief allocation |
| Attendance | ~2,800 device-verified check-in/out pairs per month; the R&D basement post has no coverage and runs offline capture (SUR-B2B-062) |
| Supervision | 6 supervisors with defined round schedules; round completion measured as an SLA metric |
| Client users | Security Head (org scope), 3 plant Facility Managers (site scope), 1 Procurement, 1 Client Finance, 5 depot Site Managers — 11 client users with 4 distinct roles |
| Approval chain | Site Manager approves site attendance → Facility Manager approves plant-level → Security Head approves organization-level → Client Finance approves the invoice (SUR-B2B-076) |
| Billing | Hybrid: one invoice per region with per-site breakdown and cost-centre codes; PO reference per region (SUR-B2B-082/083) |
| SLA | Post coverage ≥ 99%, replacement within 60 minutes, supervisor rounds ≥ 95%, P1 incident response ≤ 15 minutes, monthly report by the 5th |
| Reporting | Self-service SLA report per region and consolidated; incident trend by taxonomy across 12 sites |
| Renewal | Account health computed from the above; renewal quotation shows margin at the proposed revised rates |

**Failure modes this example must survive** — three depot guards absent on the same morning across two states; a plant material-gate post requiring a female guard on the general shift; a shutdown week where two plants need 40% fewer guards for 6 days; the client's Security Head demanding a quarterly SLA report at 22:00 on a Sunday. Each maps to: reliever pool (SUR-B2B-053), category constraints (SUR-B2C-014), temporary post variation (SUR-B2B-048), and self-service reporting (SUR-B2B-093).

## 13. B2G Requirements

Government, PSU and municipal work is a distinct commercial lane with its own discovery mechanism, eligibility rules, documentation burden and payment behaviour. This section specifies **readiness**, not integration.

### 13.1 The honesty statement on government integration

**No government-system API integration is claimed anywhere in this document.** We do not have, and do not assume, programmatic access to any government tender portal, e-procurement system, PSARA licence database, or payment/vendor-registration system. Any feature that appears to depend on such access is specified with a manual or assisted path as its primary implementation, and the integrated path is marked `[FUTURE]` or `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-101]`.

| Capability | What we build now | What we do not claim |
|---|---|---|
| Tender discovery | Manual entry, bulk upload, and assisted ingestion from documents the user supplies | Automatic scraping or API sync from any portal |
| Licence verification | Human verification of uploaded documents by the Verification role (SUR-PLT-017) | Authority-database validation |
| Bid submission | Preparation, checklist and tracking inside the platform; submission happens on the portal by the user | In-platform submission to any portal |
| Payment/receipt status | Manual status update and document upload | Automatic status from a government treasury or portal |

Terms of use of public procurement portals vary and may restrict automated access; any future ingestion must be reviewed and contracted before it is designed [DECISION REQUIRED: D-101]. This document states no conclusion about what is or is not permitted.

### 13.2 The B2G lifecycle

| # | Stage | Requirement IDs |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Tender discovery | SUR-B2G-001..007 |
| 2 | Eligibility tracking | SUR-B2G-008..013 |
| 3 | Documentation | SUR-B2G-014..019 |
| 4 | EMD and reference data | SUR-B2G-020..025 |
| 5 | Bid workflow | SUR-B2G-026..032 |
| 6 | Tender calendar and reminders | SUR-B2G-033..037 |
| 7 | Submission status | SUR-B2G-038..041 |
| 8 | Contract award | SUR-B2G-042..046 |
| 9 | Deployment | SUR-B2G-047..050 |
| 10 | SLA and compliance | SUR-B2G-051..055 |
| 11 | Billing and payment | SUR-B2G-056..061 |
| 12 | Renewal / extension | SUR-B2G-062..065 |

### 13.3 Stage requirements

#### Stage 1 · Tender discovery

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2G-001 | The platform must maintain a Tender entity with: issuing authority, tender reference, title, description, state/district, category, estimated value, EMD amount, publication date, pre-bid meeting date, submission deadline, opening date, and source URL/document. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2G-002 | Tenders must be creatable by manual entry with all fields, and by bulk upload (CSV/Excel) for teams that maintain their own lists. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-003 | Assisted ingestion must be supported: a user uploads a tender document or pastes text, and the system extracts candidate field values for human review and correction before saving. Extraction is a suggestion, never an autosave. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-004 | Every tender record must show its provenance: manually entered, bulk uploaded, or assisted-extracted, with the source file retained. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-005 | Tenders must be filterable and searchable by state, district, authority, category, value band, deadline window and eligibility match. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2G-006 | Tender discovery must be a Professional-plan capability for agency tenants, and available to Suraksha's own Sales role, consistent with the plan definitions. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2G-007 | Any automated ingestion from an external source is `[FUTURE]` and must not be implied in product copy or sales material until it exists and is permitted. | [CONFIRMED] |

#### Stage 2 · Eligibility tracking

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2G-008 | Each tender must support a structured eligibility criteria set: licence requirement and state, minimum years in operation, minimum annual turnover, minimum guard strength, past-performance/similar-work criteria, statutory registrations, certifications, and blacklisting declarations. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-009 | The platform must compute an eligibility assessment by comparing each criterion against the tenant's own profile data (licences, turnover as entered, guard strength, contract history, certifications) and show per-criterion Met / Not met / Cannot determine. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-010 | "Cannot determine" must be an explicit outcome — the system must never assert eligibility it cannot evidence. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2G-011 | The eligibility assessment must be a decision-support output, clearly labelled as such, and must never be presented as a legal determination of qualification (NG-06). | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2G-012 | Where a criterion fails, the platform must state what specifically is missing (e.g. "no live licence for Madhya Pradesh") and link to the record that would satisfy it. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-013 | Eligibility must be re-evaluated automatically when the tenant's underlying data changes (a licence renewed, a contract completed adding to past performance). | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### Stage 3 · Documentation

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2G-014 | Each tender must support a document checklist derived from a reusable template plus tender-specific additions, each item having a status, an owner and a due date. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-015 | Documents already held in the tenant's vault (licences, registrations, certifications, audited financial statements, past-performance certificates) must be attachable to a checklist item by reference, without re-uploading. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-016 | The system must flag any attached document that expires before the tender's submission deadline or before the expected contract start. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-017 | A complete bid document pack must be assemblable and exportable as a single ordered PDF with an index page. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-018 | Documents requiring notarisation, attestation or physical signature must be trackable as such, with a separate physical-status field. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-019 | Document checklist templates must be maintainable per authority type, so repeat bidders do not rebuild the list each time. | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### Stage 4 · EMD and reference fields

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2G-020 | The Tender entity must record EMD amount, EMD instrument type (bank guarantee, demand draft, online payment, exemption claimed), instrument reference, issuing bank, issue date, validity date and current status. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2G-021 | EMD status must follow: Pending → Active (submitted) → Completed (refunded/released) → Expired, with the refund date and amount recorded. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-022 | The platform must track total EMD money currently locked across all open bids, because it is working capital the agency cannot see today. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-023 | EMD instruments approaching expiry must generate alerts, since an expired instrument can invalidate a live bid. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-024 | Performance security / security deposit must be tracked with the same structure as EMD, from award through contract closure and release. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-025 | Reference/past-performance records must be maintainable as structured entities (client, scope, value, period, guard strength, contact for verification, certificate document) and attachable to bids. | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### Stage 5 · Bid workflow

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2G-026 | A Bid entity must exist per tender per bidding entity, with its own status lifecycle: Draft → Pending (internal approval) → Active (submitted) → Completed (awarded) / Rejected (lost or disqualified) / Cancelled (withdrawn or tender cancelled). | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2G-027 | Bid preparation must support technical and financial components separately, reflecting two-envelope processes. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-028 | Financial bid construction must reuse the guard-calculation and rate-card engine of §12 so that a bid price is built from real cost, not typed into a box. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-029 | The bid must show computed margin at the proposed price, including statutory components and supervision cost, before internal approval. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-030 | Internal bid approval must be a configurable chain with value thresholds; a bid below computed cost must require an explicit override with a recorded reason. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-031 | Pre-bid meeting attendance, queries raised and corrigenda received must be recordable against the tender, with corrigenda able to update deadline and criteria fields (with change history). | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-032 | Bid submission itself occurs outside the platform; the platform records the submission act with date, time, submitter, acknowledgement reference and the acknowledgement document. | [CONFIRMED] |

#### Stage 6 · Calendar and reminders

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2G-033 | A tender calendar must present all tracked tenders by key date: pre-bid meeting, query deadline, submission deadline, opening date and validity expiry. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2G-034 | Reminders must fire on a configurable ladder before each key date (default T-15 / T-7 / T-3 / T-1 / same-day) to the assigned bid owner and their manager. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-035 | Reminders must escalate: an unacknowledged T-3 reminder on a bid with incomplete documents must notify the manager. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-036 | The calendar must show readiness state per tender (eligibility met, documents complete, EMD arranged, approval obtained) so a deadline is never met with an incomplete bid. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-037 | Calendar entries must be exportable to standard calendar formats (ICS) for users who live in Outlook. | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### Stage 7 · Submission status

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2G-038 | Submission status must be maintained manually with a defined set of states: Not submitted · Submitted · Technically qualified · Technically disqualified · Financially opened · L1/L2/L3 position · Awarded · Not awarded · Cancelled. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-039 | Each status change must record the date, the source of the information, and any supporting document. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-040 | Loss reasons must be capturable against a configured taxonomy (price, technical disqualification, documentation, eligibility, cancelled, other) to make bid performance analysable. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-041 | Bid win rate, average margin at win, and loss-reason distribution must be reportable per period, per authority and per state. | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### Stages 8–10 · Award, deployment, SLA and compliance

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2G-042 | An awarded bid must convert into a Contract carrying the tender reference, award letter, awarded rates, scope and period, without re-entry. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-043 | Government contracts must support the additional fields common to public procurement: work order number, sanction reference, budget head/cost centre, contract period with extension clauses, performance security details and liquidated-damages terms. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-044 | Where the awarded scope differs from the bid, the variation must be recorded explicitly with its financial impact. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-045 | Rate revisions driven by statutory wage revisions must be supportable as dated rate-card versions with a claim/adjustment record, since this is a routine feature of public contracts. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-046 | Any statutory-wage reference data must be maintained as dated configuration with an attributed source; the platform must not state what any wage rule requires (SUR-PLT-009, NG-06). | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2G-047 | Deployment for a government contract must follow the §12 site/post/roster model, with the additional ability to record department-side site contacts and access authorisations per site. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-048 | Guard-level documentation demanded by public clients (police verification status, training certificate, photo ID card issued, uniform issue) must be reportable per site as a deployment compliance pack. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-049 | Substitution of personnel may require client-side approval under public contracts; the platform must support an approval-gated replacement mode configurable per contract. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-050 | Deployment strength must be reportable against sanctioned strength per site per day, because that is the standard public-sector verification artefact. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-051 | SLA definition, measurement and reporting follow §12 (SUR-B2B-038..096); B2G adds the ability to produce the report in a prescribed format supplied by the department as a template. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-052 | Statutory register maintenance and audit-ready exports must be supported as configurable document generation from platform data, with the register formats maintained as reference data. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-053 | Compliance evidence packs (attendance registers, wage records, statutory contribution proof references, licence copies) must be exportable for a defined period and site set in one action. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-054 | The platform must never assert that a produced register or pack satisfies any statutory requirement; it produces documents from data, and the tenant remains responsible for filing and adequacy (NG-05, NG-06). | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2G-055 | Inspection events (departmental inspection, audit visit) must be recordable against a contract with findings and closure actions. | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### Stages 11–12 · Billing, payment, renewal

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-B2G-056 | Government invoicing must support the department's required annexures: deployment statement, attendance abstract, and wage-payment declaration references, attached to the invoice. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-057 | Invoices must carry work order number, sanction reference and budget head where supplied, in addition to the standard fields of §12. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-058 | Deductions applied by the department (TDS, liquidated damages, penalty, retention) must be recordable against an invoice so the receivable reconciles, with each deduction typed and evidenced. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-059 | Payment cycles in public contracts are long and irregular; receivables ageing must support a per-contract expected-cycle configuration so ageing alerts are meaningful rather than constant. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-060 | The platform must track the bill submission act separately from invoice generation (submitted to which office, on which date, with which acknowledgement), because in practice this is where payment delay originates. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-061 | No integration with any government payment or treasury system is claimed; status is maintained manually [FUTURE for integration]. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-B2G-062 | Contract extension (common in public contracts) must be supported as a dated amendment with revised period and rates, retaining the original tender and award linkage. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-063 | Re-tender of an existing contract must link the new tender to the incumbent contract, carrying performance history into the bid preparation. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-064 | Performance security release must be tracked to completion, since unreleased security is trapped working capital. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-B2G-065 | Contract closure must produce a completion record suitable for use as a past-performance reference in future bids (linking to SUR-B2G-025). | [RECOMMENDED] |

### 13.4 B2G scope boundaries

| Boundary | Statement |
|---|---|
| Not a bidding agent | Suraksha does not bid on behalf of a tenant, sign, or submit. The platform prepares and tracks; the tenant acts. |
| Not a compliance authority | The platform produces documents from data. It makes no assertion of statutory adequacy (NG-05, NG-06). |
| Not integrated | No portal, database or treasury integration exists or is assumed (§13.1, NG-04). |
| Not a legal advisor | Tender interpretation, eligibility determination and contractual risk are the tenant's decisions; the platform's outputs are decision support only. |

| D-106 | For recurring monthly guarding, is payment prepaid per cycle or invoiced in arrears with a pay link — and does it vary by client type? | Determines cash-flow model, dunning design and the entire recurring-billing implementation. | Prepaid for Individual and Society-RWA; arrears with credit terms for Business, subject to approval. | §11, §12, §35 |
| D-107 | When a B2C booking is fulfilled by a partner agency rather than Suraksha's own guards, is that disclosed to the client? | Affects trust positioning, liability framing, notification copy and the marketplace's role in the B2C funnel. | Do not disclose the supplying agency by default; Suraksha remains the accountable counterparty. Revisit if clients ask. | §11, §14, §19, §22 |
| D-108 | What are the default wake-check cadence, acknowledgement window and escalation thresholds for night duty? | This is the headline differentiator; too frequent exhausts guards and burns battery, too sparse is not proof. | 90-minute cadence with a 5-minute acknowledgement window and escalation on the second consecutive miss; contract-overridable. | §11, §18, §24 |
| D-109 | What are the B2C cancellation and refund policy tiers? | Currently the footer links to a non-existent Refund page (canon P8); the policy must exist before booking goes live. | Free cancellation before deployment; pro-rata refund after deployment with a configured notice period; event blocks non-refundable inside 48h. | §11, §14, §35 |
| A-101 | We have no measured baseline for the frequency or cost of the twelve problems in §4 (absenteeism rate, dispute value, payroll error rate, attrition). | Every ROI claim, every goal target and the SaaS pricing argument rest on these numbers. | Instrument Suraksha's own operation first and publish internal baselines before quoting numbers externally. | §4, §5, §42, §52 |
| A-102 | All numeric targets in §5 (GOAL-01 to GOAL-15) are planning placeholders, not validated targets. | Teams will be measured against them; wrong targets misallocate effort. | Re-baseline every GOAL target after one quarter of live operation on the platform. | §5, §42, §51 |
| A-103 | We assume agencies will accept a monthly SaaS fee at the stated price points against their thin margins, and that the buying decision sits with the owner alone. | The entire B2B revenue model depends on it; ₹5,000/month is real money to a 20-guard agency. | Validate with 20 paying pilots across size bands before scaling acquisition spend. | §1, §19, §20, §52 |
| A-104 | We assume guards will install and keep an app on personal devices, and will not systematically defeat geofencing or photo verification. | Every proof claim (GOAL-01, NS-1) depends on it. | Design assuming some circumvention: server-side anomaly detection, mock-location detection, and periodic supervisor physical verification. | §18, §24, §38 |
| A-105 | We assume clients will actively use monthly attendance approval rather than ignoring it. | The invoicing model and the dispute-elimination goal both depend on client participation. | Configure deemed-approval after a window (SUR-B2B-079) so the process never stalls on client inaction. | §12, §35 |
| R-101 | Building ten surfaces in parallel exceeds a realistic early-stage delivery capacity and risks all of them shipping half-finished. | Classic ecosystem-first failure mode; the ecosystem is the strategy but not the sequence. | Sequence hard: main site + booking + OPS first, Guard App next (it unlocks every proof claim), Agency Portal after, companion apps last. | §8, §51 |
| R-102 | The marketplace has a cold-start problem on both sides — agencies will not list without buyer traffic, buyers will not search without listings. | Trinetra is the acquisition engine for the whole SaaS business. | Seed with Suraksha's own partner-agency network and use B2C demand routing as the initial value exchange for listing. | §19, §51, §52 |
| R-103 | Fabricated content on the current live site (canon P1–P5) is a live credibility and legal-exposure risk while it remains published. | A single enterprise prospect verifying a named client will end the deal and the reputation. | Remove all fabricated content before any enterprise or investor outreach; treat as a launch blocker (GOAL-14). | §14, §19, §40 |
| R-104 | Suraksha's guarding operation competes with the agencies it sells software to, which may deter marketplace participation. | The two-sided model's central tension. | Be explicit and structural: Suraksha routes demand to partner agencies and does not use tenant operational data for its own competitive advantage; encode this as an access boundary, not a promise. | §7, §19, §38, §39 |
| R-105 | Payout rails for guard salary and agency settlement are undecided, yet salary timeliness (GOAL-06, S-5) is a headline promise. | Cannot commit to on-time salary visibility without a disbursement mechanism decision. | Phase 1: compute payroll and export a bank-ready disbursement file; defer in-platform disbursement until the rail is chosen. | §20, §35 |
| R-106 | Wake-check, continuous location and photo evidence create a significant surveillance footprint over a low-wage workforce. | Privacy exposure, worker-relations risk, and a real ethical obligation. | Collect location only during duty hours and only within/around the assigned site; make retention short and explicit; never expose guard location to clients outside contracted scope (SUR-B2C-069, §39). | §18, §39, §41 |
