## 14. Main Website (surakshaguards.in)

### 14.1 Scope and role of this property

surakshaguards.in is the public face of Suraksha and the only place on the internet where a member of the public can buy guarding from Suraksha. It carries three jobs at once: (a) convince a stranger that a PSARA-licensed, GPS-monitored guarding operation is materially different from the local guard contractor, (b) let a standard-need buyer book and pay online without talking to sales, and (c) route a complex buyer into a qualified quote pipeline. After login, the same domain serves the Customer Portal (§15) — the portal is **not** on app.surakshaguards.in (that subdomain does not belong to clients; `ap.` is the Agency Portal — see canon P9).

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-WEB-001 | The public website and the logged-in Customer Portal must be served from the same origin `surakshaguards.in`; `/dashboard/*` is the authenticated area. No client-facing surface may link to `app.surakshaguards.in` or `ap.surakshaguards.in`. |
| SUR-WEB-002 | Every public page must be server-rendered or statically generated with hydration, so that title, meta description, canonical, Open Graph tags and body copy are present in the initial HTML response for crawlers. |
| SUR-WEB-003 | No page may display a statistic, client name, testimonial, award, press mention, tender, or team member that is not verifiable in the Ops panel content store. Marketing numbers are read from a single `site_stats` config record, not hard-coded per page. |
| SUR-WEB-004 | Every route listed in §14.5 must resolve with HTTP 200. Footer and header links must be covered by an automated link-integrity test in CI (fixes canon P8). |

**Primary conversion objectives, in priority order:** 1) completed instant booking with payment, 2) submitted quote request with pincode + guard count, 3) phone/WhatsApp contact, 4) newsletter/resource capture. Every page below declares which of these it serves.

Right rail: promo card "Not sure what you need? Take the 60-second guard finder → `/book`" | Opens on hover (desktop) and on click/Enter (keyboard). Closes on Esc. |

### 14.4 Cross-cutting page standards

Applied to every page spec in §14 without restating them per page.

**Responsive rule set.** Desktop ≥1200px: 12-column grid, 1200px max content width, section vertical rhythm 96px. Tablet 768–1199px: 8-column, 64px rhythm, multi-column card grids drop to 2-up. Mobile <768px: single column, 48px rhythm, cards stack full-width, horizontal card rails become swipe carousels with a scroll-position indicator, tables become stacked label/value pairs. Tap targets ≥44×44px. See §27 for tokens and component names (`Button/Primary`, `Card/Service`, `Stat/Tile`, `Accordion/FAQ`, `Form/Field`, `Banner/Alert`).

**Loading standard.** Skeletons, never spinners, for content blocks; hero copy is static HTML and must never depend on JS. Above-the-fold LCP budget 2.5s on a 4G connection and a mid-range Android device (see §46).

**Error standard.** Any dynamic block that fails to load (stats strip, reviews, blog rail) collapses silently and logs to observability; it never renders a broken box or a zero. Forms show inline field errors on blur and a summary at the top on submit failure.

**404 / 500.** `/404` — H1 "This page has moved post." Body: "The page you were looking for isn't here. Try booking a guard, checking our solutions, or calling the command center." Three links + search box. `/500` — H1 "Something broke on our side." with the support number and an incident reference.

**SEO standard.** Every page declares: one primary keyword, one title (≤60 chars), one meta description (≤155 chars), one canonical, Open Graph + Twitter card, and JSON-LD. Site-wide JSON-LD: `Organization` (with `SecurityService` service catalogue), `WebSite` with `SearchAction`. Page-level JSON-LD as noted per page. `robots.txt` allows all except `/dashboard/*`, `/book/checkout`, `/book/success`; XML sitemap auto-generated and pinged on publish.

**Analytics standard.** GA4 + server-side event mirror. Global events on every page: `page_view` (with `page_group`, `city_guess`, `device_class`), `scroll_depth` (25/50/75/100), `cta_click` (with `cta_id`, `position`), `phone_click`, `whatsapp_click`, `form_start`, `form_submit`, `form_error`. Conversion events: `book_start`, `book_configure_complete`, `serviceability_pass`, `serviceability_fail`, `checkout_start`, `payment_success`, `quote_submit`, `lead_submit`, `signup_complete`. Full catalogue in §14.21.

**Consent.** A cookie banner appears on first visit with Accept all / Reject non-essential / Manage. Analytics and marketing tags do not fire before consent. Choice stored 180 days; the Cookie Policy page links to a preference re-opener.

### 14.6 Home — `/`

**Purpose.** Convert a first-time visitor into either a booking or a quote within one screen-height of scrolling, and establish in the first 5 seconds that Suraksha is a licensed, technology-monitored operator rather than a manpower broker.
**Audience.** Facility managers, RWA secretaries, small-business owners, event organisers, individuals seeking a PSO.
**SEO.** Primary keyword: *security guard services in India*. Title: "Suraksha Guards — PSARA-Licensed Security Guards, Booked Online". Meta: "Book verified, PSARA-licensed armed and unarmed security guards with GPS attendance, night wake-checks and a 24/7 command center. Instant online booking." JSON-LD: `Organization` + `SecurityService` + `AggregateRating` (only once ≥20 verified reviews exist).
**Header state.** Transparent-over-hero on desktop, solidifying on scroll; solid on mobile.

**Hero.**
- H1: **Guards you can trust, watching every post.**
- Subheading: "PSARA-licensed armed and unarmed guards, with GPS attendance, night anti-sleep wake-checks and a 24/7 command center behind every deployment."
- Primary CTA: `Book a guard online ▸` → `/book`. Secondary CTA: `Get a free quote` → `/quote`.
- Under-CTA microcopy: "Standard plans confirm in minutes. Armed and multi-site needs get a quote within 24 hours."
- Inline serviceability teaser: a single pincode field with placeholder "Enter your pincode" and button `Check availability`. On success: green inline row "We deploy in Ahmedabad (380015). Typical start: 72 hours." + `Continue booking ▸` (carries pincode into B2). On failure: "We don't cover 799001 yet. Leave your number and we'll tell you when we do." + phone field → `waitlist_submit`.
- Trust badge row directly beneath: PSARA Licensed · KYC-Verified Guards · GST Registered · ISO 9001:2015 · 24/7 Command Center. Each badge is a link to the corresponding proof section on `/psara-compliance` or `/platform`.
- Media: a muted, auto-playing 8-second loop of a real deployment (no stock footage), with a static poster image fallback and `prefers-reduced-motion` respected.

**Section 2 — Live operations strip.** Four `Stat/Tile` components fed from the Ops read-model, refreshed every 60s: **Guards on duty right now** · **Attendance verified today (%)** · **Sites protected** · **Patrol scans logged this week**. Each tile shows the number, the label, and a timestamp "as of 14:32 IST". Clicking a tile opens `/platform#live-operations`. If the read-model is unavailable, the whole strip is removed from the DOM — it never shows zeros or fake numbers (fixes canon P5).

**Section 3 — What do you need guarding?** Six `Card/Service` tiles in a 3×2 grid: Home & Society · Business & Commercial · Bodyguards & Close Protection · Event Security & Bouncers · Night Patrols · Armed Protection. Each card: icon, name, one-line description ("Gate guards for apartments, villas and gated communities — day, night or 24×7."), a from-price line where a published anchor exists ("from ₹18,000 / guard / month"), and two actions `Book` → `/book?service=<slug>` and `Details` → the solution page. Armed Protection card shows "Quote only — licence-scoped" instead of a price.

**Section 4 — How Suraksha works.** Six numbered steps in a horizontal timeline (vertical on mobile): **1 Survey** "We visit or video-survey your site and map the posts." · **2 Plan** "You get a post-wise deployment plan and a written quote." · **3 Deploy** "Verified guards arrive with ID cards, uniform and site instructions." · **4 Monitor** "GPS attendance, patrol scans and night wake-checks stream to the command center." · **5 Bill** "Approve attendance once a month; the GST invoice generates itself." · **6 Support** "Replacements, escalations and incident reports through one channel." CTA under the timeline: `See the platform ▸`.

**Section 5 — Technology pillars.** Four blocks with a screenshot each: **24/7 Command Center** (operators watching alerts, escalation ladder), **GPS Attendance** (geofenced check-in with photo, no proxy attendance), **Night Anti-Sleep Wake-Checks** (randomised acknowledgements through the night, missed check escalates), **Transparent Billing** (attendance-linked invoices, nothing billed that wasn't worked). Each block ends with a text link into `/platform`.

**Section 6 — Pricing preview.** Three cards mirroring `/pricing`: Home & Society ₹18,000 · Business ₹22,000 (`Most popular` ribbon) · Enterprise Custom. Each shows 4 included items and a CTA (`Book online` / `Book online` / `Talk to our team`). Footnote: "Per guard, per month, excluding 18% GST. Final rate depends on shift pattern, skill level and site conditions." Link: `Compare all plans ▸` and `Open the price calculator ▸`.

**Section 7 — Trust & compliance architecture.** Four columns: Licensing (PSARA state licences, listed on `/psara-compliance`), People (police verification, KYC, reference checks, training hours), Operations (SOP per site, supervisor visits, field officer audits), Data (encrypted document vault, audit logs, GST-compliant invoicing). CTA `Read our compliance approach ▸`.

**Section 8 — Reviews.** A 3-card rail of verified client reviews (name, role, city, rating, quote, verified-client badge, date). **Rendered only when ≥3 approved reviews exist in the CMS**; otherwise the whole section is absent. No logos of companies that are not contractually permitted to be shown (fixes canon P2).

**Section 9 — Coverage.** India map with served cities highlighted, plus a city chip list. Copy: "We currently deploy in {N} cities across {M} states, under our state PSARA licences." Numbers from config, tied to D-005. CTA `See all branches ▸`.

**Section 10 — FAQ.** Six accordion items: How fast can guards be deployed? · Are your guards police-verified? · Can I book just one guard? · What happens if a guard doesn't turn up? · Do you provide armed guards? · How is billing calculated? JSON-LD `FAQPage`.

**Section 11 — Closing CTA band.** Full-width navy band. H2: **When India thinks safety, it should think SURAKSHA.** Sub: "Tell us what you need guarded. We'll take it from there." Buttons: `Book a guard ▸` · `Talk to our team`. Phone number displayed in large type.

**Analytics.** `home_hero_pincode_check`, `serviceability_pass|fail`, `home_service_card_click{service}`, `home_pricing_card_click{plan}`, `home_faq_open{question}`, `cta_book_now_click{position: hero|pricing|closing}`.

**Empty / loading / error.** Stats strip: skeleton for ≤1.5s then remove if unresolved. Reviews: absent if none. Coverage map: falls back to a text list of cities.

**Purpose.** The proof page. It converts the sceptical facility manager who has been let down by a guarding vendor before.

Screenshot of the ops live board with client data masked.

4. **Night anti-sleep wake-checks** — randomised prompts, acknowledgement window, escalation on miss, client-visible night report.

Lightbox with keyboard navigation and captions. Video items play inline. **Rule:** every asset must be an owned photograph; stock imagery is permitted only in marketing headers and must be tagged `stock` in the CMS so it never appears in the gallery. Empty tab state: "Photos from this category are coming soon."

#### 14.14.6 Media & Press — `/media`
Hero H1: **Press and media.** Sections: (1) Press kit — logo pack (SVG/PNG, light/dark), brand guidelines PDF, founder headshots, boilerplate paragraph, `Download press kit`; (2) Media coverage — **only genuine, linked coverage; the section renders "No coverage to report yet — journalists, we'd love to talk." when empty** (fixes canon P4); (3) Awards & recognition — same conditional rule; (4) Media contact: name, email, phone, response-time promise. No fabricated award badges anywhere on the site.

#### 14.14.7 Branches & coverage — `/branches`, `/branches/{city}`
Hub hero H1: **Where we deploy.** Sub: "Our coverage follows our PSARA licences. If your pincode is on the list, we can start."
Hub content: pincode serviceability checker (same component as the hero); state accordion listing cities; each city row shows branch address (where a physical branch exists), contact number, licence coverage note, and `View city ▸`.
City page (`/branches/ahmedabad`): H1 "Security guard services in Ahmedabad", localised sub, areas covered chip list, services available in that city, from-prices, branch address + map embed + phone, `LocalBusiness` JSON-LD, local FAQs, city-specific CTA `Book a guard in Ahmedabad ▸` which pre-fills city in B2. Serviceable-city list governed by D-005.
Non-serviceable city visited via search: page renders with a banner "We don't deploy in {city} yet" + waitlist form + link to Trinetra for local agencies [RECOMMENDED — turns dead traffic into B2B value].

#### 14.14.8 Blog — `/blog`, `/blog/{slug}`
Index: H1 **Security notes.** Category filter chips (Facility security · Society security · Compliance & PSARA · Event security · Industry news · Product updates), search, featured post, 12-per-page grid with pagination, sidebar newsletter capture. Post page: breadcrumb, title, author + role + date + reading time, hero image, body with anchored table of contents on desktop, inline CTA card after the second section ("Need guards for a site like this? Get a quote"), author bio, 3 related posts, share buttons, `Article` JSON-LD. Comments are not enabled in V1.

#### 14.14.9 Resources — `/resources`
Hero H1: **Things worth downloading.** Grid of gated and ungated assets: Security audit checklist for facility managers (PDF), RWA security tender template, Post-wise deployment planner (XLSX), PSARA compliance primer for buyers, Incident report template, Guard duty roster template. Gate: name + work email + company + phone (phone optional) → emailed link + a nurture sequence flag. Ungated items download directly. Each card shows format, size and page count. Events: `resource_view`, `resource_download{asset}`, `resource_gate_submit`.

#### 14.14.10 Reviews & testimonials — `/reviews`
Hero H1: **What clients actually say.** Sub: "Every review here is from a verified Suraksha client, with the site type and duration of engagement shown."
Content: summary bar (average rating, count, distribution histogram — hidden until ≥20 reviews), filter chips (service, city, rating), review cards (rating, headline, body, client first name + last initial, role, site type, city, engagement length, verified badge, date, optional Suraksha response), pagination, and a "Leave a review" CTA visible only to logged-in clients with an active or past booking → opens the portal review form (see §15.11). `Review` + `AggregateRating` JSON-LD only over genuine, moderated reviews.
Empty state (V1 launch): "We're a young operation and we publish only verified client reviews. Ours will appear here as engagements complete." — this is the honest state and is acceptable to ship (fixes canon P2).

#### 14.14.11 Affiliate & referral — `/affiliate`
**Purpose.** Turn RWA committee members, facility consultants, interior/PMC firms and existing clients into a lead channel.
Hero H1: **Refer a site. Earn every month it stays protected.** Sub: "Society secretaries, facility consultants and existing clients earn a referral payout for every deployment that goes live through them."
Sections: how it works (4 steps: sign up → get your referral link/code → the site books → you get paid); who it's for (3 personas); earnings illustration table (deployment size band × indicative payout — figures are D-121); payout terms summary (qualification = first invoice paid; payout cadence; TDS note); tracking dashboard preview; FAQ ×6; terms link.
Signup form: Name*, Mobile* (OTP), Email*, City*, Type (Individual / Society office-bearer / Consultant / Business)*, PAN (required only before first payout), How you'll refer (dropdown), Consent to programme terms*. On submit: creates a referral account, issues a code `SUR-REF-XXXXXX`, and gives access to a light referral view inside the Customer Portal (§15.12.4).
Attribution: referral code captured as a query param `?ref=`, stored in a 90-day first-party cookie, written to the booking record at B3/B4 and shown to Ops.

### 14.15 Contact — `/contact`

**Purpose.** Provide every contact channel with honest response expectations, and capture leads that don't want a form-first experience.
**SEO.** *contact security agency* / "Contact Suraksha Guards — 24/7 Command Center".
**Hero.** H1: **Talk to someone who can actually deploy.** Sub: "Command center answers 24×7. Sales answers 9 a.m.–8 p.m., every day."
**Layout.** Two columns on desktop: left = contact methods, right = form. Stacked on mobile with methods first.
**Contact methods block:** 24/7 Command Center (phone, tap-to-call) · Sales & new deployments (phone + hours) · WhatsApp (deep link with prefilled text "Hi Suraksha, I need guards for…") · hello@surakshaguards.in (general) · contact@surakshaguards.in (existing clients) · careers@ · press@ · Registered office address + map + directions link · Grievance officer (name, email, response window) → `/grievance`.
**Form fields and validation:**

| Field | Type | Required | Validation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name | text | Yes | 2–60 chars, letters/spaces/dot/apostrophe |
| Phone | tel | Yes | India 10-digit, first digit 6–9; optional country selector |
| Email | email | No | RFC-basic; required if "Email" chosen as preferred contact |
| City | select + free text | Yes | From serviceable list, with "Other" |
| Service needed | select | Yes | Six lanes + "Not sure yet" |
| Number of guards | number | No | 1–500; >50 flags the lead as enterprise |
| Preferred contact method | radio | Yes | Phone / WhatsApp / Email |
| Best time to call | select | No | Morning / Afternoon / Evening |
| Message | textarea | No | ≤1000 chars |
| Consent | checkbox | Yes | "I agree to be contacted about my enquiry." |

Anti-spam: honeypot field + time-to-submit threshold + rate limit 5/hour/IP + invisible captcha on the third attempt. On submit: `POST /leads`, creates a Lead with `source=contact_form`, routes by city to the branch queue, sends the visitor an acknowledgement email and WhatsApp (if consented), and shows the success state: "Thanks {Name}. Your enquiry reference is **ENQ-2026-01843**. Sales will call you on {phone} within 2 working hours. For anything urgent, call the command center on {number}." Failure state keeps the entered data, shows a retry button and offers the phone number as a fallback.
**Trust elements:** response-time promise, PSARA badge, "Your details are never sold or shared" line linking to `/privacy`.

### 14.16 Pricing, the calculator, and the booking flow

#### 14.16.1 Pricing — `/pricing`

**SEO.** *security guard price per month India* / "Security Guard Pricing — ₹18,000 to ₹38,000/month \| Suraksha". Meta: "Transparent guarding rates: Home & Society ₹18,000, Business ₹22,000, Enterprise custom. All rates per guard per month, excluding 18% GST."
**Hero.** H1: **Clear rates. No surprises on the invoice.** Sub: "What you see here is what the calculator computes and what the contract says. GST is the only thing added on top."
**Section 1 — Plan cards (3):**

| Card | Price | Sub-line | Includes (5 bullets) | CTA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Home & Society | ₹18,000 /guard/month | For apartments, villas and gated societies | Unarmed verified guard · 12-hour shift · GPS attendance · monthly supervisor visits · replacement within 24h | `Book online ▸` → B2 with plan preselected |
| Business | ₹22,000 /guard/month · `Most popular` | For offices, showrooms, IT parks and warehouses | Trained corporate guard · 12-hour shift · GPS attendance + patrol scans · fortnightly supervisor visits · visitor register · replacement within 12h | `Book online ▸` |
| Enterprise | Custom | Multi-site, armed, or 50+ guards | Dedicated account manager · SLA-backed replacement · custom reporting · site risk assessment · consolidated invoicing | `Talk to our team ▸` → `/quote?tier=enterprise` |

**Section 2 — Service rate table:** Unarmed guard from ₹18,500/month · Armed officer (PSO) from ₹38,000/month · Supervisor, patrol officer, lady guard rates from config · Bouncer & event blocks "Rates on request" until D-004 is resolved · B2B/Government tenders "Custom quoted". Columns: Role · Shift · From-rate · Booking path.
**Section 3 — Comparison table:** 16 rows across the three plans (guard type, shift patterns available, armed option, GPS attendance, patrol scanning, night wake-checks, supervisor cadence, replacement SLA, incident reporting, live portal access, number of sites, users on the account, invoicing, payment terms, dedicated manager, custom SLA).
**Section 4 — What changes the price:** shift pattern (day/night/24×7), armed vs unarmed, city and site risk band, skill level (guard/supervisor/PSO), number of guards (volume slabs), duration of contract, statutory wage floor applicable in the state. Each is one line explaining direction of impact.
**Section 5 — Calculator embed:** the calculator component inline, with `Open full calculator ▸`.
**Section 6 — Billing & payment:** monthly billing cycle, attendance-approval-to-invoice flow (cross-ref §15.5), payment methods (UPI/card/netbanking via Razorpay), wallet, GST invoice PDFs, payment terms, late-payment policy pointer to `/terms`.
**Section 7 — FAQs ×6** with `FAQPage` JSON-LD.
**Footnote (mandatory, on every price surface):** "Rates are indicative, per guard per month, excluding 18% GST. Final rate is confirmed after site assessment."

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-WEB-012 | All displayed prices must come from a single versioned pricing configuration (`pricing_version`), and every quote and booking must store the `pricing_version` it was computed under, so a historical booking can always be reconstructed. |
| SUR-WEB-013 | GST must be displayed as a separate line everywhere a total is shown, never merged into the headline rate. |

#### 14.16.2 Price calculator — `/pricing/calculator`

**Purpose.** Let a buyer self-serve a credible monthly number in under 30 seconds, and feed that configuration straight into booking.
**Hero.** H1: **Work out your monthly cost.** Sub: "Set the shift, the number of guards and the site type. The number updates as you move."

**Inputs (left column on desktop, top on mobile):**

| Input | Control | Options / range | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| Service lane | segmented control | Home & Society · Business · Industrial · Event · Patrol · Close protection | Business |
| Guard type | radio cards | Unarmed · Armed (licence-gated) · Supervisor · Lady guard · Bouncer | Unarmed |
| Number of guards | stepper | 1–50 (above 50 → enterprise path) | 2 |
| Shift pattern | radio | Day 12h · Night 12h · 24×7 (2 shifts) · 8h single · Custom | Day 12h |
| Days per week | segmented | 7 · 6 · 5 · Custom | 7 |
| Duration | radio | Monthly (min 1 month) · 3 months · 6 months · 12 months · Event (hours) | Monthly |
| City / pincode | input with autocomplete | Serviceable list | — |
| Site type | select | Apartment · Villa · Office · Showroom · Warehouse · Factory · Hospital · School · Event venue · Other | — |
| Add-ons | checkboxes | Supervisor visits (weekly) · Extra patrol rounds · Visitor management register · Female guard requirement · Body camera (armed only) | none |

**Output panel (sticky on desktop, sticky bottom sheet on mobile):**
- Big number: **₹44,000 / month** with "excl. GST" beneath.
- Breakdown rows: Base rate × guards · Shift-pattern factor · Night allowance · City factor · Add-ons · **Subtotal** · GST 18% · **Total payable per month**. Each row has an info tooltip explaining the factor.
- Slab hint: "Add 3 more guards to reach the 5+ volume slab and save ~4%."
- Duration hint: "A 12-month term reduces the monthly rate by ~{x}%."
- Actions: `Book this configuration ▸` (carries the full config into B2), `Get this as a written quote` (into B4), `Email me this estimate` (email field; sends a PDF estimate), `Copy link` (shareable URL with config encoded in query params).

**Calculation logic (V1, deterministic and configurable — no ML):**

```
base            = rate_card[service_lane][guard_type][shift_pattern]      // ₹ per guard per month
city_factor     = city_config[city].factor                                 // e.g. 0.95–1.20
risk_factor     = site_type_config[site_type].factor                       // e.g. 1.00–1.15
days_factor     = days_per_week / 7                                        // pro-rata for <7 days
volume_slab     = slab_table(guard_count)                                  // 1–2: 1.00, 3–4: 0.98, 5–9: 0.96, 10–24: 0.94, 25+: 0.92
duration_factor = duration_table(duration)                                 // 1m: 1.00, 3m: 0.99, 6m: 0.975, 12m: 0.96
addons          = Σ addon_price[i]                                         // flat ₹ per month
subtotal        = round_to_rupee( base × guard_count × city_factor × risk_factor
                                  × days_factor × volume_slab × duration_factor ) + addons
gst             = round_to_rupee( subtotal × gst_rate )                    // gst_rate = 0.18, configurable
total           = subtotal + gst
```

All factors live in the pricing config and are editable by Finance in Ops without a deploy. Money is computed in integer paise and rounded once, at the end, to the nearest rupee (canon §4). Event/hourly pricing uses a separate block table and is disabled until D-004 resolves; the event option then shows "Rates on request" and routes to the quote path.

**Guard rails.** The calculator never displays a number below the statutory wage floor configured for the state; if the computed figure would fall below it, the floor applies and a note appears: "Rate adjusted to meet the minimum wage applicable in {state}." The calculator shows an estimate only — the copy under the total always reads "Indicative estimate. Final rate confirmed after site assessment."
**States.** Loading: skeleton on the output panel. Error (config fetch fails): output panel replaced by "We couldn't load live rates. Get a written quote instead ▸". Non-serviceable pincode: total still computes but the CTA switches to `Join the waitlist` + `Get a quote`.
**Analytics.** `calc_open`, `calc_input_change{field,value}`, `calc_result_view{subtotal,guards,lane}`, `calc_to_booking`, `calc_to_quote`, `calc_email_estimate`, `calc_share_link`.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-WEB-014 | The calculator must be fully usable without an account and must never require a phone number before showing a price. |
| SUR-WEB-015 | The calculator's output must be reproduced exactly by the server at checkout; a client-side/server-side mismatch aborts checkout with "Prices have been updated — please review" rather than charging the client-side figure. |

#### 14.16.3 The hybrid booking rule

| Condition | Path | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Standard plan (Home & Society, Business), unarmed, ≤10 guards, single site, serviceable pincode, monthly or fixed-term | **Instant book** → B3 checkout, pay online, confirmed | Priced from the rate card with no assessment risk |
| Patrol service, unarmed, single site, ≤10 guards | Instant book | Same |
| Any armed requirement (armed guard, PSO with weapon) | **Force quote** → B4 | Licence scope, site assessment and authorisation are mandatory |
| Enterprise tier, >10 guards, or >50 in calculator | Force quote | Volume pricing and contract terms need a human |
| Multi-site (>1 site in one booking) | Force quote | Post mapping and consolidated billing need configuration |
| Event / bouncer / hourly blocks | Force quote until D-004 resolves; instant thereafter | Rates not yet published |
| Government / PSU buyer flag | Force quote | Tender/PO process |
| Non-serviceable pincode | Waitlist + quote | Cannot commit a start date |
| Client with an overdue invoice >30 days | Force quote (blocked from instant) | Credit control [RECOMMENDED] |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-WEB-016 | The hybrid rule must be evaluated **server-side** at the end of B2. The client may render an optimistic path, but the server's decision is authoritative and B3 must reject any request that fails the instant-book conditions. |

#### 14.16.4 B1 — Service select — `/book`

**Purpose.** One decision, no form fatigue.
**Header.** Booking-mode header: logo, step indicator `1 Service — 2 Configure — 3 Confirm`, `Need help? {phone}`, and a `Save & exit` link (saves a draft booking if logged in, otherwise stores config in localStorage for 7 days).
**Hero.** H1: **What do you need guarded?** Sub: "Pick the closest option. You can change every detail on the next screen."
**Content.** Six large selectable cards (Home & Society · Business & Commercial · Event Security · Bodyguard / PSO · Night Patrol · Enterprise / Multi-site), each with icon, one-line description, typical price line or "Quote", and a small "Instant booking" or "Quote in 24 hours" badge so expectations are set before the user invests time. Below: "Not sure? **Answer 4 questions** and we'll pick for you" → a 4-question wizard (What are you protecting? · How many entry points? · Day, night or both? · When do you need to start?) that lands on a recommended card with the answers pre-applied.
**Deep links.** `/book?service=business&guards=3&city=ahmedabad` pre-selects and jumps to B2.
**States.** No selection → `Continue` disabled with helper text "Select a service to continue." Returning user with a saved draft → banner "You have an unfinished booking for Business (2 guards). **Resume ▸** · Start over".
**Analytics.** `book_start`, `book_service_select{service}`, `book_wizard_start`, `book_wizard_complete{recommended}`.

#### 14.16.5 B2 — Configure — `/book/configure`

**Purpose.** Collect everything needed to price and to fulfil, while the live price updates.
**Layout.** Desktop: 2/3 form + 1/3 sticky price panel. Mobile: form full-width, price panel as a persistent bottom sheet showing the running total, expandable to the breakdown.
**Hero.** H1: **Configure your deployment.** Sub: "Change anything — the price updates as you go."

**Form blocks and fields:**

| Block | Field | Control | Validation / behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| Guards | Number of guards | Stepper 1–50 | >10 sets `force_quote=true` and shows an inline note "More than 10 guards needs a quick assessment — we'll take you to the quote step." |
| Guards | Guard type | Radio cards: Unarmed · Armed · Supervisor · Lady guard | Selecting Armed sets `force_quote=true` and shows "Armed deployment depends on our licence in your state and a site assessment." |
| Guards | Female guard required | Checkbox | Availability re-checked at fulfilment |
| Shift | Shift pattern | Radio: Day 12h (08:00–20:00) · Night 12h (20:00–08:00) · 24×7 (2 shifts) · 8-hour shift · Custom | Custom reveals start/end time pickers; 24×7 automatically doubles the guard count in pricing and states so ("2 guards × 2 shifts = 4 deployed") |
| Shift | Days per week | Segmented 7/6/5/Custom | Custom shows day checkboxes |
| Duration | Engagement type | Radio: Monthly (rolling) · Fixed term · Event (date + hours) | Event routes to quote until D-004 |
| Duration | Start date | Date picker | Minimum = today + 3 days for standard, +7 for armed; earlier dates show "Need it sooner? Call the command center — we'll try." |
| Duration | Term length | Select 1/3/6/12 months | Only for fixed term |
| Location | Pincode | Input, 6 digits | Serviceability check on blur (below) |
| Location | City / Area | Auto-filled from pincode, editable | — |
| Location | Site type | Select | Drives risk factor |
| Location | Number of sites | Stepper 1–20 | >1 sets `force_quote=true` |
| Site details | Site name | Text | e.g. "Sunrise Business Park" |
| Site details | Full address | Textarea | Required at B3, optional here |
| Site details | Posts to be guarded | Repeatable rows: post name + guards per shift | Optional at B2; helps the survey; total must not exceed guard count |
| Add-ons | Checkboxes | Supervisor visits · extra patrols · visitor register · body camera | Prices shown per item |
| Contact | Name, Mobile, Email | Text | Only shown to anonymous users; prefilled and read-only for logged-in users |

**Serviceability check by pincode.** On blur of the pincode field, `GET /serviceability?pincode=380015` returns `{serviceable: true, city, state, branch_id, earliest_start_date, armed_allowed: bool, note}`.

| Result | UI |
|---|---|
| Serviceable | Green row: "We deploy in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. Earliest start: 19 Aug 2026." Start-date picker minimum updates. |
| Serviceable but armed not permitted under the branch's licence | Amber row: "We deploy in {city}, but armed protection is outside our current licence scope here. Choose unarmed, or request a quote and we'll check partner options." |
| Not serviceable | Grey row: "We don't deploy in {city} yet." Primary action becomes `Notify me when you launch here` (phone + email) and `Request a quote anyway` (routes to B4 with a flag so Ops can consider a partner deployment). |
| Invalid pincode | Inline error "Enter a valid 6-digit pincode." |
| Lookup failure | "We couldn't check availability right now. You can still continue — we'll confirm serviceability before charging you." Booking proceeds down the quote path, not instant. |

**Live price panel.** Same calculation as §14.16.2. Panel contents: line items, subtotal, GST, total per month, a "what's included" mini-list, and a "what changes this price" link. It updates within 200ms of an input change (client-side computation from a config payload fetched once), and re-validates against the server before B3. For quote-path configurations the panel replaces the number with "Priced after assessment — typical range ₹X–₹Y per month for this size" where a range is publishable, otherwise "We'll price this within 24 hours."
**Continue behaviour.** Server evaluates the hybrid rule; button label reflects the outcome — `Continue to payment ▸` (instant) or `Continue to quote request ▸` (forced). The reason for a forced quote is always stated above the button.
**Validation summary.** On failed submit, the page scrolls to the first error, announces the count via `aria-live` ("3 fields need attention"), and highlights each.
**Analytics.** `book_configure_view`, `book_field_change{field}`, `serviceability_pass|fail{pincode,city}`, `book_force_quote{reason}`, `book_configure_complete{path, guards, lane, subtotal}`.

#### 14.16.6 B3 — Instant checkout — `/book/checkout`

**Purpose.** Take payment for a standard deployment with zero ambiguity about what is being bought.
**Access.** Requires an authenticated session. Anonymous users hit an inline auth step (phone OTP by default, with Google/Apple/email options) rendered **inside** the checkout page — never a redirect away from it. The configuration survives login.
**Layout.** Two columns: left = steps, right = sticky order summary. Mobile: summary collapsed at top, expandable.

**Step 3.1 — Confirm your identity.** Phone OTP (6 digits, 30s resend, 3 attempts then 10-minute lockout), or social/email. For a new user, this creates the account and continues; profile completion is deferred to after payment.
**Step 3.2 — Site & contact details.** Site name*, Full address*, Landmark, Pincode (locked from B2), Site contact name*, Site contact phone*, Alternate phone, Gate/entry instructions, Site photos (up to 5, optional — helps the survey), GST details block (GSTIN, legal entity name, billing address) shown when account type is Business/Society, with a "Same as site address" toggle. GSTIN validated by format (15 chars, checksum) and, where the verification integration is available, by lookup [ASSUMPTION: A-121 — GSTIN verification API availability; manual verification is the fallback].
**Step 3.3 — Review.** A read-only summary in plain language: "**2 unarmed guards**, day shift 08:00–20:00, 7 days a week, at **Sunrise Business Park, Ahmedabad 380015**, starting **19 August 2026**, on a rolling monthly engagement." Below: post breakdown, add-ons, replacement SLA, notice period, what happens after payment. Edit links return to B2 with state intact.
**Step 3.4 — Payment.** Options: **Pay first month now** (default) · **Pay first month + refundable deposit** (if the configuration requires a deposit) · **Wallet balance** (if any, shown as "Apply ₹5,000 from wallet"). Methods via Razorpay: UPI, card, netbanking. Amount block: Monthly charge · Add-ons · Subtotal · GST 18% · **Amount payable now**. Terms checkbox: "I have read and accept the Terms of Service and Refund Policy" with both links. Coupon/referral field: applies a code, shows the discount as its own line, invalid codes show "That code isn't valid or has expired."
**On payment success.** Server: creates `Booking` (status Pending → Confirmed), creates the `Site`, issues the GST invoice, credits the ledger, notifies Ops branch queue, sends confirmation email + WhatsApp + push, then redirects to B5.
**On payment failure.** Booking is held as Draft for 24 hours; page shows "Payment didn't go through. Your configuration is saved." with `Try again`, `Choose another method` and `Pay later — we'll send you a link`. Never double-charges: idempotency key on the order; a duplicate webhook is ignored.
**On payment pending (UPI collect timeout).** "Your payment is still processing. We'll confirm by SMS within 10 minutes." Booking sits in Pending; a reconciliation job resolves it; the client is notified either way.
**Security.** Card data never touches Suraksha servers (Razorpay-hosted fields). Re-authentication required if the session is older than 24 hours. Rate limit on OTP and order creation.
**Analytics.** `checkout_start`, `checkout_auth_complete{method}`, `checkout_details_complete`, `checkout_review_view`, `payment_attempt{method,amount}`, `payment_success{booking_id,amount}`, `payment_failure{reason}`, `checkout_abandon{step}`.

#### 14.16.7 B4 — Quote request — `/book/quote`

**Purpose.** Capture a qualified enterprise/armed/multi-site requirement with enough detail that Ops can quote without a second call.
**Hero.** H1: **Tell us the site. We'll send a written quote in 24 hours.** Sub: "Multi-site, armed or large deployments are priced after a short assessment — so the number you get is the number you pay."
**Content.** All B2 data carried forward and shown as an editable summary card, plus these additional fields:

| Field | Control | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Organisation name | text | Yes for business/society | — |
| Buyer type | radio | Yes | Individual · Society/RWA · Business · Government/PSU |
| Contact name / designation | text | Yes | — |
| Phone (OTP-verified) | tel | Yes | Verification inline, not a separate page |
| Email (work) | email | Yes | — |
| Number of sites | stepper + repeatable site rows | Yes | Each row: site name, city, pincode, guards, shift |
| Current security arrangement | select | No | None · In-house · Another agency · Mixed |
| What's driving this requirement | select | No | New site · Contract ending · Incident occurred · Expansion · Cost review |
| Budget range | select | No | Bands; optional and clearly marked so it doesn't scare buyers off |
| Decision timeline | select | Yes | Immediate · Within 2 weeks · This month · Exploring |
| Preferred site-visit slot | date + time-band picker | Yes | Next 7 days, morning/afternoon/evening bands, per-branch capacity aware |
| Compliance requirements | checkboxes | No | ESI/PF documentation · Police-verified only · Ex-servicemen preferred · Female guards required · Uniform specification · Background-check reports |
| Upload | file | No | RFP/tender/site layout, PDF/DOC/XLS/JPG ≤10MB ×5 |
| Message | textarea | No | ≤2000 chars |
| Consent | checkbox | Yes | Contact consent |

**Promise block (above the submit button):** "What happens next — 1) A branch manager calls you within 2 working hours. 2) A site visit at your chosen slot (or a video survey). 3) A written, post-wise quote in your portal within 24 hours of the visit. 4) Accept and pay online; deployment planning starts the same day."
**On submit.** Creates `Quotation` in status Draft with an Opportunity/Lead; assigns to the branch by pincode; SLA timer starts; the client gets an account (if new) so the quote can land in the portal; confirmation shows reference `QTN-2026-00318` and the promised timeline; email + WhatsApp confirmation sent.
**States.** Duplicate detection: same phone + same pincode within 24h → "You already have a quote request in progress (QTN-2026-00318). Add to it instead?" File upload progress per file with cancel; upload failure keeps the form intact.
**Analytics.** `quote_start`, `quote_field_change`, `quote_upload{count}`, `quote_submit{buyer_type, sites, guards, timeline}`, `quote_submit_error{reason}`.

#### 14.16.8 B5 — Success — `/book/success`

Two variants, one route, differentiated by `type=booking|quote`.

**Booking variant.** H1: **You're confirmed. Guards are being assigned.** Content: booking reference `BKG-2026-01207` with copy button; a 4-step "what happens next" tracker (Confirmed ✓ → Site survey call within 4 hours → Guards assigned 24h before start → Deployment on 19 Aug) with the current step highlighted; the deployment summary card; invoice download link; `Go to your dashboard ▸` (primary); `Add site photos` and `Download the Suraksha app` (with store badges and a QR); support block with the branch manager's name and number once assigned, otherwise the command center number. Confetti-free, calm design — this is a security purchase, not a shopping cart.
**Quote variant.** H1: **Request received. Your quote is being prepared.** Reference `QTN-2026-00318`, the promised timeline restated with actual clock times ("A branch manager will call you before 4:30 p.m. today"), an "add more detail" link back into the request, and `Go to your dashboard ▸` where the quote will appear.
**Both.** Google Analytics conversion fires once per reference (dedup by reference in session storage to survive refresh). The page is `noindex`.

### 14.17 Standalone quote — `/quote`

A short-form entry point for visitors arriving from industry pages, ads and the header. Fields: Name*, Phone* (OTP on submit, not before), Email, City/Pincode*, Service*, Number of guards, Start timeline, Message, Consent*. It creates the same `Quotation` object as B4 but with fewer fields, and the confirmation invites the client to "add the details that speed this up" → B4 with data carried across. This exists because the full B4 form is too heavy for cold traffic. Hero H1: **Get a written quote in 24 hours.** Sub: "Six fields. No sales pressure. A real number, in writing."

### 14.18 Authentication pages

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-WEB-017 | Login must accept **phone, email or username** plus password, and must additionally offer phone-OTP, Google and Apple — matching the identity service in canon §4 and the live Ops behaviour. |
| SUR-WEB-018 | `/login` and `/register` must preserve a `?next=` parameter and return the user to their intended destination, including a mid-flight booking configuration. |

#### 14.18.1 `/login`
Centred card on a subdued brand background. H1: **Welcome back.** Sub: "Sign in to see your guards, attendance and invoices."
Tabs: **OTP** (default) | **Password**.
- OTP tab: Phone field with +91 prefix → `Send OTP` → 6-box OTP input with auto-advance and paste support, 30s resend countdown, "Change number" link, 5 attempts then 15-minute lock.
- Password tab: "Phone, email or username" field + password field with show/hide, `Forgot password?`, `Remember me for 30 days`.
- Divider "or continue with" → Google, Apple buttons.
- Footer: "New to Suraksha? **Create an account**" and "Are you a guard? **guards.surakshaguards.in**" and "Are you a security agency? **trinetra.surakshaguards.in**".
Errors: invalid credentials → "That phone/email and password don't match." (never reveals which); locked → "Too many attempts. Try again in 14 minutes, or sign in with OTP."; unverified phone → routes to `/verify`.
Optional 2FA challenge screen when enabled on the account: 6-digit TOTP or SMS, "Trust this device for 30 days" checkbox.

#### 14.18.2 `/register`
H1: **Create your Suraksha account.** Sub: "One account for booking, tracking and billing."
Fields: Full name*, Mobile* (OTP-verified), Email*, Password* (with a strength meter and rules: ≥8 chars, one number, one letter; blocklist of common passwords), Account type* (Individual · Society / RWA · Business · Government), Company/Society name (conditional*), City*, How did you hear about us? (optional), Consent to Terms & Privacy*, Marketing opt-in (unchecked by default).
Social signup skips password and pre-fills name/email, then requires mobile verification before any booking action.
Post-submit → `/verify` → `/account-setup`.

#### 14.18.3 `/verify`
H1: **Verify your mobile number.** Sub: "We sent a 6-digit code to +91 98XXXXXX12." Six-box input, resend after 30s (then 60s, then 120s), "Change number", "Call me with the code instead" [FUTURE], and a support link. On success → next destination.

#### 14.18.4 `/account-setup`
Three short steps with a progress bar. Step 1 Profile: name, designation, preferred language (English/Hindi), profile photo (optional). Step 2 Organisation (skipped for Individual): legal name, GSTIN, billing address, industry. Step 3 Preferences: notification channels (push/SMS/WhatsApp/email toggles per event group), and "Who else should get alerts?" (add teammates by phone/email — creates pending invites, see §15.10). `Skip for now` is available on steps 2 and 3 and the tasks resurface in the portal.

#### 14.18.5 `/forgot-password` and `/reset-password`
Forgot: "Enter your registered email or phone." → email link (60-minute expiry, single use) or SMS OTP. Neutral confirmation regardless of existence: "If an account exists for that, we've sent reset instructions." Reset: new password + confirm, strength meter, invalidates all other sessions, sends a "your password was changed" email and SMS with a "wasn't me" link to support.

#### 14.18.6 `/client` — client account entry router
A single memorable URL to hand out on invoices, WhatsApp and printed material. Behaviour: if a valid session exists → 302 to `/dashboard`. If not → renders a branded entry page: H1 **Client login**, sub "Track your guards, attendance and invoices.", the login card, and three explainer tiles (Live guard status · Attendance & approvals · Invoices & payments). This page also carries a prominent line: "Looking for the agency software? That's **ap.surakshaguards.in**." — the disambiguation that fixes canon P9.

| Route | H1 | Required content | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/privacy` | Privacy Policy | Data controller identity, categories of data collected (client, guard, visitor), purposes, lawful basis, sharing (payment processor, communication providers, agency partners), retention periods per data class, security measures, data-subject rights and how to exercise them, children's data, changes log, grievance officer contact | Must be reviewed by counsel before launch; V1 ships a drafted, non-template document specific to Suraksha's actual data flows (fixes canon P7). Configurable jurisdiction references only — no legal conclusions in product copy. |

Content is data-driven, never hard-coded. |
| `/grievance` | Grievance Redressal | Grievance officer name, designation, email, phone, postal address, acknowledgement and resolution timelines, escalation matrix, complaint form | Linked from footer and Privacy. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-WEB-019 | Legal pages must render a "Last updated" date and keep a version history accessible at `/{page}/versions`, because clients contract against a specific version. |
| SUR-WEB-020 | The PSARA licence table must be generated from the compliance module's licence records with an "as at" timestamp; an expired licence must not be displayed as valid (cross-ref BR-002). |

| AC-WEB-01 | **Given** an anonymous visitor on `/`, **when** they enter a serviceable pincode in the hero and press Check availability, **then** the earliest start date for that branch is displayed within 1 second and `Continue booking` carries the pincode into B2. |
