## 15. Customer Portal

### 15.1 What this is, and where it lives

The Customer Portal is the authenticated client area served from the main domain at `surakshaguards.in/dashboard/*` (SUR-WEB-001). It is the client's operational window onto their own deployment: who is on duty, whether they turned up, what happened last night, what is owed, and who to shout at. It is **not** an admin panel — every destructive or operational action (reassigning a guard, editing attendance, cancelling a contract) is a *request* that Ops action, never a direct write into the operational schedule.

Two client shapes use the same portal:

- **Individual / small client** — one site, one user, cares about "is my guard there and what do I owe". Sees a simplified nav (no Team, no approval chain, no multi-site switcher).
- **B2B / enterprise client** — many sites, many users, an approval chain, a procurement process and a finance team that will not pay an invoice that isn't reconciled to attendance. Sees the full nav, the site switcher, roles, and the monthly attendance-approval → invoice cycle.

The portal's shape is driven by `account_type` and the number of active sites; there is one codebase, not two.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CPT-001 | The portal must render a reduced navigation for accounts with `account_type=Individual` and exactly one active site, and the full navigation otherwise. The switch must be automatic on the second site being added, with an in-app notice: "You now have two sites — site switching and team access are available." |
| SUR-CPT-002 | No portal action may directly mutate a Roster, Assignment or Attendance record. Client-initiated changes create a request object (Replacement, Change Request, Dispute) that Ops resolves. |
| SUR-CPT-003 | Every data point in the portal must declare its source: `Guard App (live)`, `Supervisor entered`, `Ops entered`, or `Client submitted`. The source is shown as a small label on attendance rows, live status and incident entries. |

### 15.2 Portal shell — navigation, scoping and global elements

**Left sidebar (desktop, 240px, collapsible to 64px icons):**

| Item | Route | Visible to |
|---|---|---|
| Dashboard | `/dashboard` | All |
| Live view | `/dashboard/live` | All |
| Attendance | `/dashboard/attendance` | All |
| Bookings & quotes | `/dashboard/bookings` | All except Client Viewer (read-only for Viewer) |
| Invoices & payments | `/dashboard/billing` | Company Owner, Client Finance, Procurement, Security Head; hidden for Site Manager and Client Viewer |
| Incidents & SOS | `/dashboard/incidents` | All |
| Documents & contracts | `/dashboard/documents` | All except Site Manager (site-scoped subset) |
| Sites | `/dashboard/sites` | All (scoped) |
| Team & roles | `/dashboard/team` | Company Owner, Security Head |
| Support | `/dashboard/support` | All |
| Settings | `/dashboard/settings` | All (own profile); org settings limited to Company Owner |

Nav badges: Incidents shows a red dot for any open P0/P1; Attendance shows a count badge when an approval is pending; Billing shows an amber badge for overdue invoices; Bookings shows a badge for quotes awaiting client action.

**Top bar:** global search (guards by name/ID, sites, invoices, incidents, bookings — results grouped by type, keyboard `/` to focus), **site scope selector** ("All sites ▾" / a specific site — persists per user and filters every screen), date-range selector on data screens, notification bell (drawer with grouped, filterable notifications and "mark all read"), help menu, and the account chip. Breadcrumbs render under the top bar on all detail screens.

**Empty account state.** A client who has an account but no confirmed booking yet sees a purpose-built dashboard: "Your account is ready. Nothing is deployed yet." with `Book a guard`, `See your open quote (QTN-…)`, and `Talk to your branch manager`.

**Global states.** Offline: a top strip "You're offline — showing data from 14:32." Session expiry: a modal 2 minutes before expiry with `Stay signed in`. Permission denied: a full-page state naming the role required and offering "Ask {Company Owner name} for access" which sends an in-app request.

### 15.3 Dashboard — `/dashboard`

**1 Purpose.** Answer four questions in one screen without scrolling on a laptop: is my security running right now, is anything wrong, what needs my decision, and what do I owe.
**2 Users.** All client roles. **3 Permissions.** Cards render per role; a Site Manager sees only their sites' cards; Client Finance sees financial cards prominently and operational cards read-only. See §31.
**4 Screens.** `/dashboard` (single screen, no sub-routes).

**5 UI detail — the cards, in order:**

| # | Card | Contents | Click behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Guards on duty now** | Big number "7 of 8 on duty", split by site as a mini bar, "as at 14:32", source labels | → `/dashboard/live` filtered to on-duty |
| 2 | **Not on duty** (renders only when >0) | List of up to 3 rows: site · post · shift · reason (Absent / Late / Replacement en route) · time since | Row → the attendance record; card → `/dashboard/attendance?status=exception` |
| 3 | **Needs your action** | Stacked action items with counts: "Approve August attendance for 2 sites", "Accept quote QTN-2026-00318 (₹1,42,000/month)", "Pay invoice INV-2026-00412 (₹1,32,750, due in 3 days)", "3 team invites pending" | Each row deep-links to the exact screen with the item open |
| 4 | **Last night's report** | Patrol rounds completed X/Y · wake-checks acknowledged X/Y · incidents raised N · first check-in and last check-out times | → `/dashboard/attendance?date=yesterday&view=night` |
| 5 | **Open incidents** | Count by severity chips (P0/P1/P2/P3), latest incident headline + site + time | → `/dashboard/incidents` |
| 6 | **This month's attendance** | Present days / scheduled days as a percentage with a 30-day sparkline, plus "Billable days so far: 172" | → `/dashboard/attendance` |
| 7 | **Billing summary** | Current outstanding ₹ · next invoice date · wallet balance · last payment | → `/dashboard/billing` |
| 8 | **Your deployment** | Per-site rows: site name · guards deployed / contracted · shift pattern · contract end date · supervisor name | Row → site detail |
| 9 | **Your Suraksha team** | Branch manager (name, photo, phone, WhatsApp), assigned supervisor, 24/7 command center number | Tap-to-call / WhatsApp deep link |
| 10 | **Quick actions** | `Request a replacement` · `Report an incident` · `Book more guards` · `Raise a ticket` · `Download last invoice` | Each opens the relevant modal or route |

**6 UX flow.** Land → scan cards 1–3 → act on "Needs your action" → drill into live or attendance. Everything above the fold on a 1366×768 laptop is cards 1–3.
**7/8 Fields & validation.** Read-only screen; only the date-range and site-scope selectors accept input, both validated against the account's permitted sites.
**9 Business logic.** "On duty" = an Assignment whose shift window contains now AND which has a check-in without a check-out. "Exception" = scheduled shift with no check-in 15 minutes past shift start (threshold configurable per contract). Percentages exclude days before contract start.
**10 Backend logic.** Served by a per-client read-model refreshed on attendance/incident/invoice events, with a 60-second cache; the dashboard makes exactly one aggregate API call, not one per card.
**11 Status lifecycle.** N/A (aggregate view).
**12 Notifications.** No notifications originate here; the bell surfaces them.
**13 Integrations.** Read-models from attendance, incidents, billing; WhatsApp/tel deep links.
**14 Security.** Site-scoped queries enforced server-side by the user's site grants; never client-side filtering.
**15 Audit.** Dashboard views are logged at a coarse level (user, timestamp) for security review, not per card.
**16 Edge cases.** Contract starts tomorrow → cards 1/2/4 replaced by a countdown card "Deployment starts in 18 hours". Contract ended → banner "This engagement ended on 31 Jul. Your records remain available." Guard App not live at this site → card 1 shows "Attendance is supervisor-verified at this site" with the source label and no live map link.
**17 QA.** Verify each role's card set; verify site-scope filtering; verify the 60s staleness label; verify the exception threshold against contract config.
**18 Acceptance criteria.** *Given* a client with 8 contracted guards and 7 checked in, *when* the dashboard loads, *then* card 1 reads "7 of 8 on duty" and card 2 lists the missing guard's post with the minutes elapsed. *Given* a pending August approval and an unpaid invoice, *when* the dashboard loads, *then* both appear in "Needs your action" ordered by deadline.
**19 Analytics & KPIs.** `portal_dashboard_view`, `dashboard_card_click{card}`, `dashboard_action_click{action}`. KPIs: time-to-first-action, % of sessions that reach an action item, dashboard load p95 <1.5s.
**20 Future.** Configurable card order per user; a TV/wall-display mode for facility control rooms [FUTURE]; per-card AI summary ("last night in one line") within the read-only AI action class (§25).

### 15.4 Live view — `/dashboard/live`

**1 Purpose.** Show the client where their guards physically are and whether the shift is being run properly — the single most-requested capability from clients who have been burned by ghost shifts.
**2 Users.** All roles. **3 Permissions.** Site-scoped. Client Viewer read-only (no replacement request). Guard personal data limited to the client-visible field set (§17.4).

**4 Screens.** `/dashboard/live` (map + list), guard drawer, post drawer.

**5 UI detail.**
- **Left panel (360px): guard list**, grouped by site → post. Each row: guard photo, name, Suraksha Guard ID, post name, shift window, status pill (On duty · Checked out · Late · Absent · Replacement en route · No data), check-in time, last patrol scan time, battery/connectivity dot, and a `…` menu (View profile · Request replacement · Report an issue).
- **Right: map** (full height) with site geofence polygons, post pins, guard markers with photo avatars, patrol route lines and checkpoint pins coloured by scan status (scanned on time / late / missed). Controls: recenter, zoom, layer toggles (Geofence · Patrol route · Checkpoints · Guard trail), and a time-scrubber for "replay the last 12 hours" [V2 — see phasing].
- **Top strip:** on-duty count, exception count, last data update timestamp, and a data-source legend.
- **Guard drawer** (on marker/row click): photo, name, Guard ID, category, languages, verification badges (Police verified · KYC verified · Trained), assigned post, today's timeline (check-in → patrol scans → wake-checks → check-out), this month's attendance for your site only, and actions `Request replacement`, `Report an issue`, `View public profile` (opens the guard's client-visible profile from §17).

**6 UX flow.** Land → see the count → spot a red status → open the drawer → either accept the explanation (replacement en route) or request a replacement.
**7 Fields.** Filters: site, post, status, shift. Search by guard name/ID.
**8 Validation.** Replacement request requires a reason (select) and optional note (≤500 chars).
**9 Business logic.** Location shown is the guard's last reported position while on duty, inside a shift window only. **Outside a shift, a guard's location is never shown to anyone** — a hard privacy rule (cross-ref §39). Position accuracy circle rendered where accuracy >50m. A guard outside the geofence for >5 minutes shows an amber "Off-site" pill and generates a command-center alert (§24).
**10 Backend.** Positions stream over the real-time channel (§34) with a fallback to a 60-second poll; the client channel receives only guards assigned to that client's sites.
**11 Status lifecycle.** Scheduled → Checked in (On duty) → On break (optional) → Checked out (Completed); exception states Late, Absent, Replacement pending, Replacement en route.
**12 Notifications.** Client-configurable: guard checked in, guard did not check in by T+15, guard left geofence, patrol round missed, shift completed. Channel per event group (§36).
**13 Integrations.** Map provider [DECISION REQUIRED: D-122 — Google Maps vs MapMyIndia/Mappls vs OSM: cost, Indian address quality and offline tiles differ materially]; real-time transport (§34).
**14 Security.** Guard location is client-visible only for guards assigned to that client's site, only during shift, and only at the precision needed (10m). No historical trail export for clients in V1.
**15 Audit.** Every guard-drawer open and every replacement request is written to the audit log with user, guard ID, site and timestamp.
**16 Edge cases.** No GPS fix → "Location unavailable — attendance was verified at the gate device"; device offline → last-known position greyed with "Last seen 14:02"; guard on an authorised break → "On break until 15:00"; guard reassigned mid-shift → both the outgoing and incoming guard shown with a handover marker.
**17 QA.** Cross-site leakage test (a Site Manager for Site A must never receive Site B's position events); shift-boundary test (position disappears at check-out); permission test for Viewer.
**18 Acceptance criteria.** *Given* a guard checked in and inside the geofence, *when* the client opens Live view, *then* the guard appears on the map with an "On duty" pill and a check-in time. *Given* the same guard 20 minutes after check-out, *when* the client opens Live view, *then* no position is rendered and the row reads "Checked out at 20:04".
**19 Analytics.** `live_view_open`, `live_guard_drawer_open`, `live_replacement_request{reason}`, `live_map_layer_toggle{layer}`. KPI: % of active clients using Live view weekly (a leading indicator of retention).
**20 Future.** 12-hour replay scrubber, body-camera stream for armed deployments, geofence-breach heat map, guard-to-client in-app messaging with moderation [all FUTURE].

**Phasing (honest).** Live positions, patrol scans and wake-check acknowledgements exist **only where the Suraksha Guard App (§18) is deployed on that site's guards**. Until then this screen renders in "Roster mode": the guard list, post assignments, shift windows and supervisor-entered check-in/check-out times are shown, the map shows site and post pins but no guard markers, and a persistent notice reads: "Live tracking activates at this site once your guards are on the Suraksha Guard App. Attendance is currently verified by your supervisor at the gate." The screen ships in V1 in this mode — it is not hidden — so the client sees the structure they will get.

### 15.5 Attendance — `/dashboard/attendance`

**1 Purpose.** Be the single source of truth for what was worked, and drive the monthly approval that unlocks invoicing. This is the most commercially important screen in the portal: for an enterprise client, attendance *is* the invoice.
**2 Users.** All; approval limited to roles with the `attendance.approve` grant (typically Security Head or Facility Manager; Procurement/Finance may be configured as a second approver).
**4 Screens.** Monthly grid · Daily detail · Guard detail · Exceptions · Approval & sign-off · Dispute.

**5 UI detail.**
- **Monthly grid (default):** rows = guards (grouped by site → post), columns = days 1–31, cells = status glyph (P present · A absent · R replaced · L leave · H holiday · ½ half shift · — not scheduled). Cell colours per §27 status tokens. Sticky first column and header. Footer row totals per day; right-hand totals per guard: present days, absent days, replaced days, overtime hours, billable days.
- **Header controls:** month picker, site scope, post filter, status filter, `Export CSV`, `Export PDF (signed register)`, and the **approval bar** (below).
- **Cell click → daily detail popover:** guard name + ID, post, scheduled window, check-in time + source + location accuracy + selfie thumbnail, check-out time + source, breaks, patrol scans (list with times and checkpoint names), wake-checks (count acknowledged / prompted), incidents raised, supervisor remarks, and `Raise a dispute on this record`.
- **Exceptions tab:** every anomaly for the month as a work list — no check-in, late by >15 min, early check-out, missing patrol round, missed wake-check, geofence breach, unapproved replacement — each with site, guard, date, minutes, current resolution status and Ops' explanation.
- **Approval bar (month-end):** "August 2026 · 4 sites · 248 billable days · 6 exceptions unresolved" with `Review exceptions` and `Approve attendance ▸`. Approval opens a modal listing per-site totals, requiring a checkbox "I confirm these attendance records for billing" and, where a second approver is configured, showing the approval chain state.

**6 UX flow (the monthly cycle, cross-ref WKF in §29):** Ops closes the month → portal shows "August attendance is ready for your approval" (in-app + email + WhatsApp) → client reviews exceptions → client either approves, or disputes specific records → disputes go to the branch manager with a stated response window → on resolution the client approves → invoice generates from approved billable days → invoice appears in Billing with a payment link. If the client does not act within the configured window (default 5 working days), an auto-approval rule may apply **only if the contract enables it**; otherwise the invoice is raised on Ops-recorded attendance with the dispute window preserved [DECISION REQUIRED: D-120 — auto-approval after N days: legally and commercially sensitive, must be a contract-level flag, not a global default].

**7 Fields.** Approval: month, site set, approver identity, approval note (optional), timestamp, IP. Dispute: record reference, dispute reason (select: guard absent but marked present · wrong shift hours · wrong guard · duplicate entry · other), evidence upload (≤5 files), description.
**8 Validation.** Cannot approve a month that is not closed; cannot approve with unresolved disputes unless the disputed records are excluded (the modal shows "Approving 242 of 248 days; 6 disputed days held back"); cannot approve a month twice.
**9 Business logic.** Billable day = a shift with a verified check-in and check-out, or an Ops-authorised exception (e.g. a replacement served the shift). Replacements are billable to the client only where the post was actually covered. Half-shifts bill at the configured fraction. Overtime requires prior client authorisation to be billable.
**10 Backend.** Attendance rows are immutable once the month is closed; corrections create adjustment rows referencing the original (canon: no silent modification, BR-003). Approval writes an `Approval` record and emits `attendance.approved` which the billing service consumes.
**11 Status lifecycle.** Attendance month: Open → In Progress (live) → Pending (closed, awaiting client) → Verified (approved) → Archived. Dispute: Pending → In Progress → Resolved (Accepted / Rejected with reason) → Archived.
**12 Notifications.** "Attendance ready for approval" (day 1 of the following month), reminder on day 3, escalation to Company Owner on day 5, "Dispute received", "Dispute resolved", "Attendance approved — invoice on its way".
**13 Integrations.** Billing (invoice generation), Ops (dispute handling), export to CSV/PDF, and a signed PDF register suitable for the client's own audit file.
**14 Security.** Approval requires a fresh authentication if the session is older than 12 hours, and is recorded with the approver's identity — this record is contractually load-bearing.
**15 Audit.** Every view of the approval modal, every approval, every dispute and every Ops correction is audit-logged and visible to the client in an "Activity" tab on the month.
**16 Edge cases.** Mid-month contract change (guard count increased on the 14th) → the grid shows the change as a divider row with the effective date. Guard replaced permanently → both guards' rows appear with their active date ranges. Site added mid-month → prorated totals. Public holiday configured per state → H glyph with the holiday name, billing per contract. Client approves and then finds an error → they raise a **post-approval dispute**, which creates a credit-note request rather than editing the approved month.
**17 QA.** Reconciliation test: sum of billable days in the grid must exactly equal the invoice's billed days for every site and month. Timezone test: all times rendered in IST regardless of device locale.
**18 Acceptance criteria.** *Given* a closed month with 248 billable days and no disputes, *when* the Security Head approves, *then* an Approval record is written, the month becomes Verified, and an invoice for exactly 248 days is generated within 5 minutes. *Given* 6 disputed records, *when* the client approves, *then* the invoice covers 242 days and the 6 remain Pending with a stated resolution deadline.
**19 Analytics.** `attendance_view{month}`, `attendance_cell_open`, `attendance_export{format}`, `attendance_dispute_raise{reason}`, `attendance_approve{days, sites, latency_days}`. KPIs: median days from month-close to approval; dispute rate per 1,000 shifts; % of invoices raised on approved attendance.
**20 Future.** Biometric/face-match attendance evidence inline; automatic exception explanations from the AI layer (recommendation class only); attendance API/webhook for enterprise clients pulling into their own ERP.

### 15.6 Bookings & quotes — `/dashboard/bookings`

**1 Purpose.** One place for everything commercial that is in flight or historic: active engagements, pending quotes to accept, past bookings, and change requests.
**4 Screens.** List · Booking detail · Quote detail & acceptance · Change request · Cancellation request.

**5 UI detail.**
- **List** with tabs `Active (3) · Quotes (1) · Upcoming · Completed · Cancelled`. Row: reference, service lane, site, guards × shift, start date, contract end, monthly value, status pill, next action. Filters by site, service, date range; sort by start date or value.
- **Booking detail:** header (reference, status, site, `Download contract`), summary card (service, guard count, guard type, shift pattern, days/week, start, term, notice period, monthly value ex-GST, add-ons), post map (posts → guards per shift), assigned personnel list (with Guard IDs and verification badges), supervisor and branch manager, documents tab (contract PDF, deployment plan, SOP, guard ID list), billing tab (invoices raised against this booking), and an activity timeline (created → paid → guards assigned → deployed → changes).
- **Actions on a booking:** `Add guards` (opens a change request pre-filled), `Reduce guards`, `Change shift pattern`, `Pause deployment`, `Request replacement`, `Extend contract`, `Cancel` (opens the cancellation flow with the notice period and charges shown before confirmation).
- **Quote detail:** the written quote rendered natively (not just a PDF): scope, post-wise breakdown, rate per guard, add-ons, monthly total, GST, term, validity date with a live countdown ("valid for 6 more days"), assumptions and exclusions, SLA terms, and the Suraksha signatory. Actions: `Accept & pay ▸`, `Accept & request invoice` (for clients on credit terms), `Ask a question` (threaded, notifies the branch manager), `Request changes` (structured: change guard count / shift / start date / commercial terms, with a note), `Decline` (with a reason select — feeds win/loss analytics), and `Download PDF`.

**6 UX flow.** Quote arrives → notification → open → read → accept & pay (Razorpay, same checkout component as B3) → booking created → deployment timeline appears.
**7/8 Fields & validation.** Change request: field to change, new value, effective date (≥ notice period where the contract requires it), reason, note. Cancellation: effective date (validated against notice period), reason, confirmation typed as the site name for destructive confirmation.
**9 Business logic.** Quote acceptance is a commercial act: it freezes the quoted `pricing_version`, generates the Contract, and creates the Booking. An expired quote cannot be accepted — the UI offers `Request a refreshed quote`. Cancellation computes charges from the contract's notice terms and shows them **before** the client confirms.
**10 Backend.** Accept → Contract + Booking + first Invoice (or wallet debit) in one transaction; failure rolls back and the quote stays Active.
**11 Status lifecycle.** Quote: Draft → Pending (sent) → In Progress (under negotiation) → Verified/Accepted → Rejected → Expired → Archived. Booking: Draft → Pending → Active → In Progress (deployed) → Completed → Cancelled → Archived.
**12 Notifications.** Quote ready · quote expiring in 3 days · quote expired · booking confirmed · guards assigned · deployment starts tomorrow · change request approved/rejected · contract expiring in 30/15/7 days.
**13 Integrations.** Razorpay, contract PDF generation, e-signature [FUTURE — D-123].
**14 Security.** Acceptance requires a role with `booking.accept`; the acceptor's identity, timestamp and IP are stored on the Contract.
**15 Audit.** Full trail on quote versions (v1, v2 after negotiation) with a diff view showing what changed between versions.
**16 Edge cases.** Quote superseded while the client is reading it → live banner "A revised quote (v2) has been issued. **View v2**". Two users accept simultaneously → optimistic lock, second sees "Already accepted by {name} at 14:32". Client accepts but payment fails → Contract stays Pending for 24h with a payment link.
**17 QA.** Notice-period math across month boundaries; quote-expiry timezone handling; concurrent acceptance.
**18 Acceptance criteria.** *Given* an Active quote within validity, *when* the client accepts and pays, *then* a Contract and Booking are created, the quote becomes Accepted, and the deployment timeline shows the first milestone. *Given* an expired quote, *when* the client opens it, *then* Accept is disabled and `Request a refreshed quote` is offered.
**19 Analytics.** `quote_view`, `quote_accept{value, days_to_accept}`, `quote_decline{reason}`, `quote_question_asked`, `booking_change_request{type}`, `booking_cancel_request{reason, notice_days}`. KPIs: quote→acceptance rate, median days to acceptance, change-request volume per contract.
**20 Future.** In-portal e-signature, multi-quote comparison for procurement, contract auto-renewal with client confirmation.

### 15.7 Invoices, payments & wallet — `/dashboard/billing`

**1 Purpose.** Let finance pay without emailing anyone, and let procurement reconcile every rupee against attendance.
**2 Users.** Company Owner, Client Finance, Procurement, Security Head (view), Individual Customer.
**4 Screens.** Overview · Invoices list · Invoice detail · Payments · Wallet · Payment methods · Billing settings.

**5 UI detail.**
- **Overview cards:** Outstanding balance (₹, with count of invoices) · Overdue (₹, red, with the oldest days) · Due in next 7 days · Wallet balance · Paid this financial year · Next invoice date and estimated amount.
- **Invoices list:** columns Invoice no · Period · Site(s) · Billable days · Amount ex-GST · GST · Total · Due date · Status (Draft/Pending/Paid/Overdue/Partially paid/Credit noted) · Actions (`Pay`, `Download PDF`, `View`). Filters: status, site, date range, financial year. Bulk select → `Pay selected` and `Download selected (ZIP)`.
- **Invoice detail:** the invoice rendered natively with a GST-compliant layout (supplier GSTIN, client GSTIN, place of supply, HSN/SAC, taxable value, CGST/SGST or IGST split, invoice number and date), a **line-item table tied to attendance** (per site, per post: contracted days, billable days, rate, amount) with a link "View the attendance that produced this invoice" opening the approved month in read-only, add-ons, adjustments/credits, and the payment box (Pay now · Pay from wallet · Part payment where allowed). A `Raise a billing query` action creates a ticket linked to the invoice.
- **Payments:** every transaction — date, method, reference, amount, invoice(s) settled, status, receipt download.
- **Wallet:** balance, `Add money` (₹ input with quick chips 10k/25k/50k/1L, Razorpay), auto-debit toggle ("Settle invoices from wallet automatically on the due date"), ledger of credits and debits with running balance, and refund request action.
- **Payment methods:** saved methods (tokenised, via Razorpay), UPI mandate / e-NACH for recurring [FUTURE — D-124], default method.
- **Billing settings:** billing entity name, GSTIN, billing address, PO number requirement toggle (when on, an invoice cannot be raised without a PO reference from the client), invoice email recipients (multiple), invoice delivery preference, TDS applicability declaration and rate.

**6 UX flow.** Notification "Invoice ready" → open → reconcile against attendance → pay → receipt emailed → status Paid.
**7/8 Fields & validation.** Add money: min ₹1,000, max ₹5,00,000 per transaction. PO number: alphanumeric, ≤30 chars. GSTIN format-validated. Part payment blocked unless the contract allows it.
**9 Business logic.** Invoices are generated **only** from Verified (approved) attendance, or on Ops override with a recorded reason. Money in integer paise; GST computed per configured place-of-supply rules; TDS deducted by the client is reconciled as a separate ledger entry, not a discount. Overdue status at due date + configured grace. Wallet debits are ledger entries, never a silent balance edit (canon §4).
**10 Backend.** Razorpay orders with idempotency keys; webhook-driven reconciliation; every movement double-sided in the ledger (§35).
**11 Status lifecycle.** Invoice: Draft → Pending → Partially paid → Paid → Overdue → Cancelled (credit note) → Archived.
**12 Notifications.** Invoice generated · due in 3 days · due today · overdue (day 1, 7, 15, with escalation to Company Owner) · payment received · wallet low balance · refund processed.
**13 Integrations.** Razorpay; GST invoice PDF generator; email delivery to multiple recipients; accounting export (Tally/Zoho Books CSV) [FUTURE].
**14 Security.** Financial screens require the finance grant; downloading invoices is logged; refund requests require re-authentication.
**15 Audit.** Every payment attempt, every settings change (especially GSTIN and billing address) and every download is audit-logged with actor and IP.
**16 Edge cases.** Payment succeeds but webhook is delayed → invoice shows "Payment processing — we've received your payment reference" and never asks for a second payment; duplicate payment → automatic wallet credit with an explanatory notification; credit note issued after a post-approval dispute → shown as a negative line against the next invoice and separately downloadable; client GSTIN changed mid-year → historical invoices retain the GSTIN in force at issue.
**17 QA.** Rounding tests (paise-level), GST split tests (intra vs inter-state), reconciliation test (attendance days = invoice days), idempotency test.
**18 Acceptance criteria.** *Given* an approved August attendance of 248 days, *when* the invoice is generated, *then* the line items sum to 248 days at contracted rates and the GST is shown as a separate line. *Given* a client with a ₹50,000 wallet balance and a ₹1,32,750 invoice, *when* they choose Pay from wallet, *then* ₹50,000 is debited, the invoice shows Partially paid with ₹82,750 outstanding, and two ledger entries exist.
**19 Analytics.** `invoice_view`, `invoice_pay_click`, `payment_success{amount, method}`, `wallet_topup{amount}`, `billing_query_raise`. KPIs: DSO (days sales outstanding), % paid by due date, % paid from wallet, billing-query rate per invoice.
**20 Future.** Auto-debit mandates, multi-entity billing for groups, purchase-order matching, consolidated group invoicing across subsidiaries.

### 15.8 Incidents & SOS log — `/dashboard/incidents`

**1 Purpose.** Give the client a complete, timestamped record of everything that went wrong and what was done about it — the artefact that survives an insurance claim or a board question.
**4 Screens.** List · Incident detail · Report an incident · SOS log.

**5 UI detail.**
- **List:** severity chip (P0/P1/P2/P3), title, site, post, date-time, reported by (Guard / Supervisor / Client / Command Center), status (Pending · In Progress · Completed · Verified), assigned Suraksha owner, and a "days open" counter. Filters: severity, site, status, type, date range. Tabs `All · Open · SOS · My reports`.
- **Incident detail:** header with severity and status; **timeline** (raised at 02:14 by Guard SG-2026-004871 → command center acknowledged 02:15 → supervisor dispatched 02:19 → on site 02:41 → resolved 03:20 → report filed 09:00), narrative, categorised type (theft/attempted theft · trespass · fire/safety · medical · altercation · property damage · access violation · vehicle · equipment failure · other), location on a mini-map, attachments (photos, videos, PDFs) with a viewer, people involved (guards by ID; third parties recorded without personal identifiers unless the client provides them), actions taken, police intimation (yes/no + reference where applicable, entered by Ops), preventive recommendation, and a client comment thread.
- **Report an incident (client-raised):** type*, severity suggestion, site*, post, date-time*, description*, attachments (≤10 files, 25MB each), "Do you want a callback?" toggle with a preferred window, and "Should this be treated as an emergency?" which, if yes, immediately shows the command center number and creates a P1.
- **SOS log:** a separate tab listing SOS events raised from the Guard App on the client's sites: time, guard, site, resolution time, outcome, and the command center's action record. Read-only for the client.

**6 UX flow.** Push notification for P0/P1 within 60 seconds of the command center acknowledging → client opens → sees live status → adds a comment → receives resolution notification and, for P0/P1, a written report within the configured window.
**9 Business logic.** Severity is set by the command center, not the client; a client can *request* a re-grade with a reason. SOS mechanics, escalation ladder and command-center actions are owned by §24 — this screen is the client's read view plus commentary.
**11 Status lifecycle.** Pending → In Progress → Completed → Verified (client acknowledged) → Archived.
**12 Notifications.** P0: push + SMS + call to the primary contact. P1: push + SMS. P2/P3: push + daily digest. Plus "incident report ready" and "incident closed".
**14 Security.** Incidents are site-scoped; a Site Manager sees only their site's incidents. Attachments are served through signed, expiring URLs.
**15 Audit.** Every view, comment and download logged; the incident record is append-only after closure (corrections are addenda).
**16 Edge cases.** SOS raised with no network → appears when the Guard App syncs, with both device and server times shown and a "delayed sync" label. False alarm → status Completed with outcome "False alarm — no action required", still permanently recorded. Incident spanning two sites → linked incidents with a shared parent reference.
**18 Acceptance criteria.** *Given* a P0 SOS on the client's site, *when* the command center acknowledges, *then* the client's primary contact receives push + SMS within 60 seconds and the portal shows the incident in In Progress with a live timeline.
**19 Analytics.** `incident_view`, `incident_report_submit{type, severity}`, `incident_comment`, `sos_log_view`. KPIs: incidents per 1,000 guard-shifts, median acknowledgement time, median resolution time, % with a report filed within SLA.
**20 Future.** Client-side incident analytics (hot spots by post and hour), insurance-ready export pack, CCTV clip attachment where integrated.

### 15.9 Documents & contracts — `/dashboard/documents`

**Purpose.** Every document the client is entitled to, in one place, without emailing the branch.
**Screens.** Library · Document viewer · Compliance pack request.
**UI.** Folder-style categories: **Contracts** (signed contract, annexures, amendments), **Quotes** (all versions), **Invoices & receipts** (mirrors billing), **Compliance** (Suraksha PSARA licence copy for the relevant state, GST certificate, ESI/PF registration, insurance certificate — each with a validity date and an "expires in N days" chip), **Deployment** (site SOP, post instructions, deployment plan, guard ID list with photos and Guard IDs, uniform and equipment list), **Reports** (monthly attendance register PDF, monthly security report, incident reports, night patrol summaries), **Client-uploaded** (site layout, access rules, emergency contacts, NDA). Each row: name, type, size, uploaded by, date, validity, actions (View · Download · Share link with expiry · Replace for client-uploaded). Bulk download as ZIP.
**Compliance pack request:** a one-click action producing a dated ZIP with the licence set, registrations, insurance and the guard verification summary for the client's own audit file — generated on demand, watermarked with the client name and generation date, valid for 30 days.
**Logic & statuses.** Documents are versioned; superseded versions remain accessible under "Version history". Expiring compliance documents raise a client-visible chip and an Ops task.
**Security & audit.** Signed expiring URLs; every download logged with actor; shared links carry an expiry (max 7 days) and are revocable. **Guard documents (Aadhaar, PAN, police verification papers) are never present in this library** — clients receive verification *status*, not source documents (cross-ref §17.4 and §39).
**Acceptance criteria.** *Given* a client requesting a compliance pack, *when* generation completes, *then* the ZIP contains only currently valid documents and is watermarked with the client name and timestamp.

### 15.10 Sites — `/dashboard/sites`

**Purpose.** The client's own model of their premises: where guards are posted, what the standing instructions are, who to call.
**Screens.** Site list · Site detail · Add site request · Post map · Site contacts.
**UI.** List: site name, address, city, guards deployed/contracted, shift pattern, contract status, supervisor, site manager (client-side owner), last incident. Detail tabs: **Overview** (address, map, geofence radius, contract summary, deployment schedule), **Posts** (each post: name, location description, guards per shift, shift windows, duty instructions, equipment at post, patrol route it belongs to), **Team** (client-side contacts for this site with roles and escalation order), **Attendance** (site-filtered view), **Incidents** (site-filtered), **Documents** (site-scoped), **Access instructions** (gate codes are explicitly **not** stored — the field is labelled "Entry process, without secrets"), **Emergency contacts** (fire, police, hospital, facility electrician, with click-to-call).
**Client-editable vs request-only.** Editable directly: site display name, client-side contacts, emergency contacts, entry process notes, site photos. Request-only (creates an Ops task): address/geofence changes, post additions or removals, guard-count changes, shift-pattern changes, patrol route changes.
**Add site.** Form: site name*, address*, pincode* (serviceability check), site type*, guards required, shift pattern, expected start date, site contact*, notes. Creates a Quotation for the additional site linked to the existing account, and notifies the branch manager. Existing clients skip the whole marketing funnel.
**Edge cases.** Site temporarily suspended (client shutdown/holiday) → status Suspended with a resume date, billing per contract; site closed permanently → Archived, with records retained and read-only.
**Acceptance criteria.** *Given* a Site Manager scoped to Site A, *when* they open Sites, *then* only Site A is listed and a direct URL to Site B returns the permission-denied state.

### 15.11 Team & roles — `/dashboard/team`

**1 Purpose.** Let an enterprise client run the account the way their organisation actually works: several people, different jobs, an approval chain, and a clean handover when someone leaves.
**2 Users.** Company Owner (full), Security Head (manage below own level). Not visible to Individual accounts.

**5 UI detail.**
- **Members list:** name, email, phone, role, site scope ("All sites" or a chip list), status (Active · Pending invite · Suspended), last active, MFA status. Row actions: Edit role & scope · Resend invite · Suspend · Remove · Transfer ownership (Company Owner only).
- **Invite member:** name, email or mobile*, role*, site scope*, "Can approve attendance" toggle, "Can approve spend up to ₹X" field, personal note. Sends an invite valid 7 days; the invitee sets their own credentials.
- **Roles tab:** the six client roles with a plain-language description of what each can do, rendered from the permission matrix (§31 is canonical — this screen renders it, it does not redefine it):

| Role | Plain-language description shown in the UI |
|---|---|
| Company Owner | Everything, including billing, team management and contract acceptance. |
| Security Head | All sites: live view, attendance approval, incidents, bookings and quotes. No team ownership transfer. |
| Facility Manager | Assigned sites: live view, attendance review and approval, incidents, replacement requests, support. |
| Site Manager | One or more specific sites: live view, attendance review (no approval), incident reporting, replacement requests. |
| Procurement | Quotes, contracts, pricing and vendor documents. Read-only on operations. |
| Client Finance | Invoices, payments, wallet and billing settings. Read-only on operations. |
| Client Viewer | Read-only across granted sites. No requests, no approvals, no financial data. |

- **Approval chain tab:** configure who must approve what. Two configurable chains in V1: **Attendance approval** (single approver, or two-step: Facility Manager → Security Head) and **Commercial approval** (quote acceptance: single, or Procurement → Company Owner above a configured value threshold). Each chain shows the current configuration as a visual stepper, with an escalation timer ("if not actioned in 3 days, escalate to …").
- **Activity tab:** who did what in this account for the last 90 days (approvals, payments, role changes, downloads), filterable and exportable — the artefact an internal auditor asks for.

**6 UX flow.** Owner invites → invitee accepts, verifies phone, sets password/MFA → lands on a role-appropriate dashboard → appears in the members list.
**8 Validation.** Cannot remove the last Company Owner; cannot grant a role above your own; cannot set a site scope outside your own; email/phone uniqueness within the account; role change on a pending approver reassigns their queue with a warning.
**9 Business logic.** Approval chains are stored per account and versioned; an approval always records the chain version in force. Suspended members lose access immediately (session revocation), not at next login.
**12 Notifications.** Invite sent/accepted/expiring, role changed (to the affected member and the owner), approval pending assigned to you, escalation triggered, member suspended.
**14 Security.** Role changes and ownership transfer require re-authentication and MFA where enabled; ownership transfer sends a confirmation to both parties and is reversible for 24 hours.
**15 Audit.** All membership and permission changes are permanently audit-logged and shown in the Activity tab.
**16 Edge cases.** Invitee's email already belongs to another Suraksha account → they are linked as a member of both, with an account switcher. Member leaves the company → Suspend preserves their historic approvals (approvals are never anonymised or deleted). Two accounts for one legal entity → merge is an Ops-assisted process, not self-serve.
**18 Acceptance criteria.** *Given* a two-step attendance chain, *when* the Facility Manager approves, *then* the month moves to "Awaiting Security Head" and only the Security Head can complete it; *when* the Security Head approves, *then* the month becomes Verified and invoicing is triggered.
**19 Analytics.** `team_invite_sent`, `team_invite_accepted`, `role_changed`, `approval_chain_configured{type, steps}`. KPI: accounts with ≥3 active users (a strong retention correlate for B2B).
**20 Future.** SSO/SAML for enterprise accounts, SCIM provisioning, custom roles, department-level cost centres.

### 15.12 Support, Settings, and the referral view

#### 15.12.1 Support — `/dashboard/support`
**Purpose.** One channel, with visible state, replacing WhatsApp chaos.
**UI.** Top action row: `Request a guard replacement` · `Report a problem` · `Ask a billing question` · `Request a site visit` · `Call the command center` · `WhatsApp us`. Below: ticket list (reference, subject, category, site, priority, status, last update, assigned to). Ticket detail: threaded conversation with attachments, status timeline, SLA clock ("first response promised by 16:30"), rating prompt on closure, and a `Reopen` action for 7 days.
**Replacement request form:** site*, post*, guard (select or "any guard on this post")*, reason* (attendance issue · conduct · skill fit · language · shift change · other), urgency (Immediate / Within 24h / Next roster), note, evidence upload. Immediate requests page the branch manager and open a P2 incident automatically.
**Statuses.** Pending → In Progress → Waiting on client → Completed → Archived. **Notifications** on every state change. **SLA display** is the promise from the contract, not an invented number.
**Also here:** a client review prompt after 30 days of deployment and at each contract renewal, feeding `/reviews` (§14.14.10) after moderation.

#### 15.12.2 Settings — `/dashboard/settings`
Tabs: **Profile** (name, photo, designation, language English/Hindi, timezone locked to IST) · **Security** (password change, MFA enable/disable with TOTP or SMS, active sessions list with device/location/last-active and `Sign out` per session, `Sign out everywhere`, login history for 90 days) · **Notifications** (a matrix of event groups × channels — Push, SMS, WhatsApp, Email, In-app — with sensible defaults: P0/P1 incidents on all channels and not disableable for the primary contact; attendance approval reminders on email + in-app; marketing off by default) · **Organisation** (legal name, GSTIN, billing address, industry, logo — Company Owner only) · **Preferences** (default landing screen, default site scope, date format) · **Privacy & data** (download my data, data retention summary, delete account request which is a supervised Ops process, not an instant delete).
**Rule:** P0 incident notifications to the account's designated emergency contact cannot be switched off — the UI shows the toggle locked with the reason.

#### 15.12.3 Notifications drawer
Grouped by day, filterable by type (Operational · Financial · Commercial · Account), each item with an icon, title, one-line body, timestamp and deep link. Actions: mark read, mark all read, mute a type for 7 days. Retains 90 days.

#### 15.12.4 Referral view — `/dashboard/referrals`
Visible only to accounts enrolled in the affiliate programme (§14.14.11). Shows: referral code and share link with copy/WhatsApp buttons, referrals table (referred site/company, status: Signed up → Quoted → Deployed → Qualified, date, payout status, amount), earnings summary (pending, approved, paid), payout details (PAN, bank — collected only at payout stage and stored encrypted), and programme terms. Payout mechanics depend on the payout rail decision in canon §4.

### 15.13 V1 data-source phasing (honest statement)

| Portal capability | V1 source when the Guard App is **not** live at that site | V1 source when the Guard App **is** live | Client-visible label |
|---|---|---|---|
| Guard on-duty status | Supervisor marks arrival in the Ops panel; Ops-entered attendance | GPS geofenced check-in with selfie | "Supervisor entered" / "Guard App (live)" |
| Guard position on map | Not shown; map displays site and post pins only, with the Roster-mode notice | Live position during shift | — |
| Patrol scans | Not available; the section reads "Patrol scanning activates with the Guard App" | Checkpoint scans with times | — |
| Night wake-checks | Supervisor's night-round remarks, entered by Ops | Randomised prompts with acknowledgement records | — |
| Attendance grid | Fully functional from Ops-entered data | Fully functional from device data | Per-row source label |
| Monthly approval → invoice | Fully functional in V1 regardless of source | Same | — |
| Incidents | Fully functional; raised by client, supervisor (via Ops) or command center | Additionally raised by guards in the field with photos | Per-incident "reported by" |
| SOS log | Empty state: "SOS is available on sites running the Suraksha Guard App." | Live | — |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CPT-004 | Every attendance, status and incident record must carry an immutable `source` attribute set at write time, and the portal must render it. A record's source may never be back-edited to appear more authoritative than it was. |
| SUR-CPT-005 | Screens whose data depends on the Guard App must ship in V1 with a designed degraded mode (as specified per screen), never as a hidden or a broken screen. |

## 16. Customer App

### 16.1 The parity decision

**Decision: functional parity, experiential divergence.** The Suraksha Customer App exposes the same capabilities as the Customer Portal (§15) — nothing a client can do on the web is impossible in the app — but the app is not a wrapper and is not laid out like the web. The portal is organised around *screens*; the app is organised around *moments*: a push arrives, the client taps it, and lands on exactly the thing that needs attention.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CAP-001 | The app must be a native or cross-platform native build (React Native or Flutter — see D-125), not a WebView shell. Live status, camera capture, push handling and offline reads require native behaviour. |
| SUR-CAP-002 | Every portal capability must be reachable in the app. Three capabilities are permitted to be *deferred to web* with an in-app explainer and a "Continue on web" handoff that carries the session: (a) bulk invoice download as ZIP, (b) approval-chain configuration, (c) organisation legal/GSTIN editing. All three are low-frequency desktop-shaped tasks. |
| SUR-CAP-003 | The app must never show a client a capability their role lacks; role resolution happens server-side and drives the tab set and the action sheet contents. |

**Rationale.** Field evidence from this buyer set: society secretaries and facility managers check status on a phone many times a day and touch a laptop once a month. Attendance approval and payment, however, are decisions with money attached and are frequently done at a desk. So the app optimises for *checking and reacting*, the web optimises for *reviewing and approving*, and both can do everything.

### 16.2 Navigation model

**Five bottom tabs**, fixed, with a centre action:

| Tab | Icon | Landing screen | Badge |
|---|---|---|---|
| Home | shield | Status feed (§16.4) | — |
| Live | map-pin | Live view | Amber dot on any exception |
| **Book** (centre, accented) | plus | Booking sheet | — |
| Activity | list | Attendance · Incidents · Bookings (segmented) | Count of items needing action |
| More | grid | Billing, Sites, Documents, Team, Support, Settings | Red dot for overdue invoice |

Rationale for the centre Book button: rebooking and adding guards is the revenue action, and burying it in a menu costs conversions. Deep-link scheme `suraksha://` plus universal/app links on `surakshaguards.in/*` so every notification, email and WhatsApp message opens the right in-app screen.

### 16.3 Screen inventory

| ID | Screen | Route | Differs meaningfully from web? |
|---|---|---|---|
| CAP-01 | Splash + auth gate | `/` | Yes — biometric unlock |
| CAP-02 | Onboarding carousel | `/onboarding` | Yes — app only |
| CAP-03 | Login / OTP | `/auth` | Yes — SMS autofill, one-tap |
| CAP-04 | Home status feed | `/home` | **Yes — specified below** |
| CAP-05 | Live view | `/live` | **Yes — specified below** |
| CAP-06 | Guard detail sheet | `/live/guard/:id` | Minor |
| CAP-07 | Book — service select | `/book` | Yes — includes one-tap rebook |
| CAP-08 | Book — configure | `/book/configure` | Yes — sheet-based steppers |
| CAP-09 | Checkout | `/book/checkout` | Yes — native UPI intent |
| CAP-10 | Quote request | `/book/quote` | Minor |
| CAP-11 | Attendance month | `/attendance` | **Yes — specified below** |
| CAP-12 | Attendance day / guard | `/attendance/:date` | Minor |
| CAP-13 | Attendance approval | `/attendance/approve` | **Yes — specified below** |
| CAP-14 | Incidents list | `/incidents` | Minor |
| CAP-15 | Incident detail | `/incidents/:id` | Minor |
| CAP-16 | Report incident | `/incidents/new` | **Yes — camera-first** |
| CAP-17 | SOS alert screen | `/sos/:id` | **Yes — full-screen interrupt** |
| CAP-18 | Bookings & quotes | `/bookings` | Minor |
| CAP-19 | Quote detail & accept | `/bookings/quote/:id` | Minor |

| CAP-27 | Replacement request | `/support/replacement` | Yes — 3-tap flow |

| CAP-29 | Settings | `/settings` | Yes — app lock, permissions |
| CAP-30 | Offline / no-network state | overlay | Yes — app only |

Screens marked "Minor" follow §15 exactly with mobile layout rules from §27; they are not re-described here.

### 16.4 CAP-04 Home status feed (app-specific)

Not a card grid. A single scrollable feed, newest-relevant-first, that reads like a status report:

1. **Status header** — a coloured band: green "All 8 guards on duty" / amber "7 of 8 on duty — 1 replacement en route" / red "SOS at Sunrise Business Park". Tapping opens Live.
2. **Action strip** — horizontally scrolling pills for items needing action: "Approve August attendance", "Pay ₹1,32,750 by 20 Aug", "Accept quote ₹1,42,000". Each pill is a one-tap route into the exact action.
3. **Today** — a chronological list of the day's meaningful events: check-ins, patrol rounds completed, wake-checks, incidents, replacements. Each row has time, site, and a source label.
4. **Last night** — a collapsed summary card for the overnight window (rounds X/Y, wake-checks X/Y, incidents N), expanded on tap.
5. **Your sites** — compact per-site rows with the on-duty fraction.
6. **Your Suraksha team** — branch manager and command center, with call/WhatsApp buttons.

Pull-to-refresh; the feed is cached and renders instantly from cache with a "Updated 14:32" line while it refetches.

### 16.5 CAP-05 Live view (app-specific)

Map-first, list-second: full-bleed map with a draggable bottom sheet at three detents (peek: on-duty count and exceptions; half: guard list; full: filters + list). Guard markers are photo avatars; tapping opens the guard sheet with a call-the-supervisor button. Location is battery-conscious: the app never requests the client's own location for this screen — only for "navigate to my site". Roster-mode (Guard App not live at that site) renders the same sheet with the schedule and supervisor-entered times and a one-line explainer, identical in substance to §15.4.

### 16.6 CAP-11 / CAP-13 Attendance and approval on mobile

The 31-column grid is unusable on a phone. Instead:
- **Attendance month** = a per-guard list with a 31-dot strip per row (colour-coded, tap a dot for the day), plus a summary header (present / absent / exceptions / billable days) and a prominent "6 exceptions need review" row.
- **Exception review** = a swipeable card stack, one exception per card: what happened, the evidence (selfie thumbnail, times, map snippet), and three actions — `Accept`, `Dispute`, `Ask Suraksha`. This turns a spreadsheet task into a two-minute phone task and is the single biggest app-specific UX win.
- **Approval** = a summary sheet (sites, days, disputed items held back), a confirmation checkbox, and biometric confirmation (Face ID / fingerprint) as the signing act, recorded with the same evidentiary weight as web approval.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CAP-004 | Attendance approval in the app must require a biometric or device-passcode confirmation, and the approval record must store the authentication method used. |

### 16.7 App-optimised capabilities

| Capability | Specification |
|---|---|
| **One-tap rebooking** | On the Book tab, above service selection: "Book the same again" cards derived from past bookings — "2 unarmed guards, day shift, Sunrise Business Park — ₹44,000/month". One tap loads the full prior configuration into B2 with only the start date left to set. For expired short engagements (events), the card says "Repeat this event booking". |
| **Push-first status** | Every operational state change the client cares about is a push with an actionable deep link and, where useful, notification actions (Android actions / iOS categories): "Guard didn't check in" → [View] [Call supervisor] [Request replacement]. |
| **SOS visibility** | A P0 SOS produces a full-screen interrupt (CAP-17) with sound and vibration even in silent mode where the platform permits (Android notification channel with `IMPORTANCE_HIGH` + critical-alert entitlement on iOS if granted; otherwise a time-sensitive notification). The screen shows site, post, guard, time, live command-center status and two buttons: `Call command center` and `View live`. It cannot be swiped away without acknowledging. |
| **Camera for site photos** | Native camera capture for incident reports, site photos at booking, replacement evidence and document upload. Images are compressed client-side to ≤1.5MB, EXIF-stripped of everything except capture time, and tagged with the site (not the client's GPS, unless the client explicitly enables "attach location"). Queue-and-retry on poor networks. |
| **Offline read of active deployment** | The app caches, encrypted at rest: current deployment summary, today's and yesterday's attendance, assigned guard list with photos and Guard IDs, site contacts, emergency numbers, the last 10 incidents, the last 3 invoices (metadata + PDF if opened once), and the branch manager's number. All are readable offline with an "Offline — as of 14:32" banner. No writes are attempted offline except incident drafts and support messages, which queue and sync with a visible pending state. |
| **Biometric app lock** | Optional (default on for accounts with financial permissions): Face ID / Touch ID / Android BiometricPrompt on cold start and after 5 minutes in background. Fallback to device passcode; never a separate app PIN. Re-auth always required before paying, approving attendance, or changing team roles. |
| **Native payment** | UPI intent handoff to installed UPI apps (the dominant Indian flow), plus cards/netbanking via the Razorpay SDK. Payment status is resolved server-side, so an app crash mid-payment never loses the payment. |
| **Share & print** | Native share sheet for invoices, reports and compliance packs; AirPrint/Android print for PDFs. |
| **Widgets** | Home-screen widget showing on-duty count and any exception, refreshed every 30 minutes [FUTURE — post-V1]. |

### 16.8 Onboarding

Four screens, skippable, shown once: 1) "Your guards, on your phone" — live status; 2) "Attendance you can approve in two minutes" — the exception cards; 3) "One tap to book more" — rebooking; 4) "We'll tell you the moment something's wrong" — the notification permission request, asked **here with context**, never on first launch cold. Then auth (phone OTP with SMS autofill on Android via SMS Retriever API; iOS one-time-code autofill), then, for a brand-new user with no booking, a "Book your first guard" prompt; for an existing client, straight to Home.

### 16.9 Notification-driven journeys

| Trigger | Notification copy | Deep link | Actions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Guard checked in | "Rakesh K. checked in at Main Gate, 07:58." (digest — one per site per shift, not per guard, unless the client opts into per-guard) | `/live` | — |
| Missed check-in T+15 | "No check-in at Main Gate, night shift. We're on it." | `/live` | View · Call supervisor |
| Replacement dispatched | "Replacement guard assigned to Main Gate, arriving by 21:10." | `/live` | View |
| P0/P1 incident or SOS | "SOS — Sunrise Business Park, Main Gate. Command center engaged." | `/sos/:id` | Call command center · View live |
| Night report ready | "Last night: 6 of 6 patrol rounds, 8 of 8 wake-checks, no incidents." | `/home` | — |
| Attendance ready | "August attendance is ready for your approval — 248 days, 6 exceptions." | `/attendance/approve` | Review |
| Invoice generated | "Invoice INV-2026-00412 for ₹1,32,750 is ready. Due 20 Aug." | `/billing/:id` | Pay now |
| Payment received | "Payment of ₹1,32,750 received. Receipt in your documents." | `/billing/:id` | — |
| Quote ready | "Your quote for 4 guards at Site B is ready — ₹1,42,000/month." | `/bookings/quote/:id` | View · Accept |
| Contract expiring | "Your contract for Sunrise Business Park ends in 30 days." | `/bookings/:id` | Renew · Talk to us |

All notification copy is templated server-side (§36) so it can be changed without an app release, and every notification respects the per-event-group channel preferences from Settings — except P0, which is not disableable for the designated emergency contact.

### 16.10 Mobile-specific states

| State | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| First launch, no account | Onboarding → auth → "Book your first guard" |
| Logged in, no active deployment | Home shows the booking prompt plus any open quote, not an empty status band |
| Offline | Amber banner "Offline — showing data from 14:32"; cached screens readable; write actions disabled with "This needs a connection" and queued where safe |
| Slow network (>3s) | Skeletons plus "Still loading — your connection looks slow"; the app never blocks the whole screen on a spinner |
| Background → foreground after >5 min | Biometric prompt (if enabled) and a silent refresh |
| Push permission denied | A dismissible Home card: "You'll miss SOS and attendance alerts. **Enable notifications**" → deep link to OS settings. Re-asked at most once every 30 days |
| Version out of date (below min-supported) | Blocking screen "Update Suraksha to continue" with a store link; supported for security-critical releases only |
| Account suspended by the org owner | Login succeeds, then a full-screen "Your access was removed by {owner}. Contact them or Suraksha support." |
| Multiple accounts (member of two orgs) | Account switcher in the More tab and in the top bar of Home |

### 16.11 Platform differences

| Area | Android | iOS |
|---|---|---|
| Min version | Android 8.0 (API 26) — covers the low-end device base this market actually uses | iOS 15 |
| Push | FCM; notification channels per event group (Emergency, Operations, Billing, Marketing) so users can tune granularly in OS settings; Emergency channel `IMPORTANCE_HIGH` | APNs; notification categories with actions; time-sensitive interruption level for SOS; critical alerts only if the entitlement is granted |
| OTP autofill | SMS Retriever API (no SMS-read permission needed) | One-time-code autofill from the keyboard |
| Biometrics | BiometricPrompt with device-credential fallback | LocalAuthentication (Face ID / Touch ID) with passcode fallback |
| Payments | UPI intent to installed apps; Razorpay SDK | Razorpay SDK; UPI intent where supported; no Apple Pay requirement (services are delivered offline, so IAP rules do not apply — but the store listing must be clear that this is a real-world service) |
| Maps | Google Maps SDK or Mappls (D-122) | Same provider; Apple Maps not used, to keep one rendering model |
| Back navigation | Hardware/gesture back must always work and must never exit mid-transaction without a confirm | Swipe-back gesture on all pushed screens |
| Share/print | Android Sharesheet, Print framework | UIActivityViewController, AirPrint |
| Files | Scoped storage; downloads to app-scoped dir with a share action | Files app integration |

### 16.12 Permissions requested, and why

| Permission | When asked | Why | If denied |
|---|---|---|---|
| Notifications | During onboarding screen 4, with context | Operational alerts, SOS, attendance and billing reminders | App fully usable; a Home card explains what is being missed; SOS falls back to SMS + call |
| Camera | At first photo capture | Incident photos, site photos, document upload | User can pick from gallery instead |
| Photo library (read/add) | At first gallery pick or save | Attach existing photos; save invoices | Manual upload via web |
| Location (while in use) | Only when the user taps "Navigate to my site" or uses "Use my current location" while adding a site | Address prefill and navigation | Manual address entry; no functional loss |
| Biometrics | At app-lock enablement | Secure the app and sign approvals | Device passcode fallback |
| Contacts | Only when inviting a team member and the user taps "Pick from contacts" | Convenience only | Manual entry |

The app **never** requests background location, SMS read, call log, microphone or storage-wide access. This restraint is a stated privacy position and appears in the app-store privacy labels and in `/privacy`.

### 16.13 Low-end device and poor-network behaviour

- **Budget:** APK/AAB download size <25MB, cold start <2.5s on a 2GB-RAM Android 8 device, memory ceiling 180MB, no jank at 60fps on the Home feed with 200 rows.
- **Images:** all guard photos and thumbnails served in WebP at device-appropriate resolutions with a CDN; full-size images fetched only on tap.
- **Data:** a "Data saver" toggle in Settings that disables map tiles (list-only Live view), disables auto-loading of incident photos, and increases the poll interval. Default on for connections the OS reports as metered/2G.
- **Network:** every request has a timeout and a bounded retry with exponential backoff; the real-time channel degrades to a 60-second poll; failed writes queue with visible pending state and never silently disappear.
- **Language:** English and Hindi at launch, with the language chosen at onboarding and stored server-side so it applies to notifications too. Additional Indian languages follow the AI/localisation roadmap (§25).
- **Accessibility:** dynamic type up to 200%, minimum 44pt targets, full screen-reader labels on status pills and map markers (which announce as text, not as images), and colour never used as the sole status carrier (each status pill carries a glyph).

### 16.14 App-store considerations

| Item | Position |
|---|---|
| Store listing | Title "Suraksha — Security Guards & Live Tracking"; subtitle "Book verified guards. Track every shift."; screenshots showing status feed, live view, attendance approval, invoice — with synthetic demo data only, never a real client's site |
| Category | Business (primary), Lifestyle (secondary on iOS) |
| Age rating | 4+/Everyone; no user-generated public content |
| Privacy labels | Data linked to the user: contact info, identifiers, usage. Data **not** collected: precise background location, contacts (unless the user picks one), health, financial account details (payments are processed by Razorpay). Must match `/privacy` exactly |
| Account deletion | Both stores require an in-app route to request account deletion — provided in Settings → Privacy & data, which opens a supervised deletion request with a stated timeline and an explanation of records that must be retained for statutory/contractual reasons |
| Login requirement | The app requires an account; the store review notes must include demo credentials and a demo tenant with representative data, refreshed each release |
| Payments | Real-world services, so external payment rails are permitted; the listing and the review notes must state this plainly to avoid IAP rejection |
| Location justification | iOS `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription`: "Used only to fill in your site address and to navigate to your site. We never track your location." |
| Release cadence | Monthly feature releases, out-of-band patch releases for security; a `min_supported_version` server flag drives the forced-update screen |
| Distribution | Google Play and Apple App Store; a direct APK is **not** distributed for the client app (unlike the Guard App, where sideloading may be operationally necessary — see §18) |

### 16.15 Acceptance criteria (sample)

| ID | Criterion |
|---|---|
| AC-CAP-01 | *Given* a client with app lock enabled, *when* the app returns from background after 6 minutes, *then* a biometric prompt is shown before any client data is rendered. |
| AC-CAP-02 | *Given* a P0 SOS on the client's site, *when* the push is delivered, *then* the app shows the full-screen SOS interrupt with the command-center call button, and the event cannot be dismissed without an explicit acknowledgement. |
| AC-CAP-03 | *Given* the device is offline, *when* the client opens Home, *then* the cached deployment, attendance and guard list render with an "as of" timestamp and all write actions are visibly disabled. |
| AC-CAP-04 | *Given* a past booking, *when* the client taps "Book the same again", *then* B2 loads with every prior parameter applied and only the start date empty. |
| AC-CAP-05 | *Given* a month with 6 exceptions, *when* the client reviews them in the swipe stack and disputes 2, *then* approval proceeds for the remaining days and the 2 disputes are created with the same payload shape as the web dispute. |
