## 17. Guard Platform (guards.surakshaguards.in)

### 17.1 What this property is for

guards.surakshaguards.in is the **professional identity layer for security personnel in India**. It is not the guard's daily field tool — that is the Suraksha Guard App (§18), which owns duty, GPS check-in, patrol scanning, wake-checks, SOS and incident reporting. The web platform exists to do four things the app should not:

1. Give every verified guard a **portable professional identity** — the Suraksha Guard ID — that outlives any single employer.
2. Run the **registration and verification lifecycle** (documents, KYC, police verification status, training records), which is document- and form-heavy and better on a larger screen or at a partner/branch desk.
3. Manage **agency association** — which agency a guard is currently attached to, and the linkage/de-linkage history that makes the workforce auditable.
4. Provide a **fallback surface** so a guard is never locked out of their own records for lack of a working phone or an app install.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-GRD-001 | The Guard Platform must be usable on a ₹6,000 Android phone browser at 360px width, in Hindi or English, on a 3G connection. It is a mobile-first web application even though it is a "web portal". |
| SUR-GRD-002 | The platform must not duplicate duty operations. Check-in, patrol scanning, wake-check acknowledgement, SOS and field incident reporting are Guard App functions (§18). The web portal shows their **records**, read-only, plus an emergency web check-in fallback that requires a supervisor's authorisation code (see §17.9). |
| SUR-GRD-003 | A guard's account belongs to the guard, not to an agency. De-linking from an agency must never delete or transfer the guard's identity, history, training records or verification status. |

### 17.2 The Suraksha Guard ID

**Concept.** Every verified individual gets a permanent identifier — `SG-2026-004871` (prefix · year of first registration · sequence) — printed on their Suraksha ID card, shown on their public profile URL `guards.surakshaguards.in/g/SG-2026-004871`, quoted on attendance records, incident reports and deployment lists, and used by clients and agencies to refer to a person **without exchanging personal data**.

**Why it matters commercially.** A client asking "who was on my gate last night?" gets `SG-2026-004871 — Rakesh K.` and can see verification status, training and reliability — but not the guard's Aadhaar, address or bank details. An agency hiring from the Trinetra network can check a candidate's verified history without collecting a folder of photocopies. The Guard ID is the trust primitive of the whole workforce side of the ecosystem.

**Properties.**

| Property | Rule |
|---|---|
| Uniqueness | One human = one Guard ID, enforced by deduplication on verified identity attributes at registration (§17.6). Duplicate detection is a verification-team workflow, not an automatic merge. |
| Permanence | Never reissued, never reused, never changed. If a guard leaves the industry and returns, the same ID resumes. |
| Portability | Survives agency changes, city changes and employment gaps. |
| Revocability | The ID is never deleted; its **status** can become Suspended or Archived with a recorded reason and an appeal path (§17.11). |
| Verifiability | A public verification endpoint `/verify/SG-2026-004871` returns only: ID validity, name, photo, category, verification status and agency association status — nothing else. Used by a client's front desk to check that the person at the gate is who the roster says. |
| QR | The physical ID card carries a QR that resolves to the public verification URL. Scanning does not require login. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-GRD-004 | The public verification endpoint must be rate-limited, must not accept enumeration (sequential scanning returns a generic response after a threshold), and must never expose any field outside the Public class of §17.4. |

### 17.3 The guard portfolio — complete field inventory

Every field the master brief requires, with its owner and how it is populated.

| # | Field | Source | Editable by guard |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Suraksha Guard ID | System | No |
| 2 | Full name | Guard at registration, confirmed against KYC | Change request only |
| 3 | Photograph | Guard (live capture preferred) | Yes, subject to re-approval |
| 4 | Date of birth / age | Guard, confirmed against KYC | Change request only |
| 5 | Gender | Guard | Yes |
| 6 | Category / role | Guard + verification (Guard · PSO · Bouncer · Supervisor (field) · Specialised Personnel) | Request |
| 7 | Years of experience | Guard, corroborated by work history | Yes |
| 8 | Skills | Guard from a controlled vocabulary (access control, frisking, CCTV monitoring, fire safety, first aid, crowd control, VIP protection, driving, dog handling, control-room operation) | Yes |
| 9 | Languages spoken | Guard, multi-select with proficiency (speak/read/write) | Yes |
| 10 | Training completed | Training module records (§14.14.3) | No — system-written |
| 11 | Training score | Assessment results per module, aggregated | No |
| 12 | Certifications | Guard uploads; verification team approves; issuer, number, issue and expiry dates | Upload, not approve |
| 13 | Agency association | Linkage workflow (§17.8) | Request to link/de-link |
| 14 | Work history | Deployment records + guard-declared prior employment (marked "self-declared" until corroborated) | Add self-declared entries |
| 15 | Verification status | Verification team (Unverified · In Progress · Verified · Expiring · Rejected · Suspended) | No |
| 16 | Police verification | Status + date + validity + issuing district. **Detail and documents are restricted.** | Upload only |
| 17 | KYC status | Aadhaar/PAN/Voter/DL verified — **status only, numbers masked** | Upload only |
| 18 | Document status | Per-document: type, status, expiry, rejection reason | Upload/replace |
| 19 | Licence info | For armed personnel: licence type, issuing authority, validity, scope — **number restricted** | Upload only |
| 20 | Ratings | Client and supervisor ratings, aggregated with a minimum-sample rule | No |
| 21 | Deployment history | Assignment records: site type, city, duration, role — **client identity shown only where the client permits** | No |
| 22 | Attendance history | Attendance records: present days, punctuality, unplanned absences | No |
| 23 | Reliability indicators | Derived: attendance %, punctuality %, patrol compliance %, wake-check response %, replacement-caused incidents, tenure | No |
| 24 | Availability | Guard-set: Available / Deployed / On leave / Not looking, with available-from date | Yes |
| 25 | Preferred work area | Guard-set: cities, pincode radius, willingness to relocate, preferred shift | Yes |
| 26 | Contact details | Guard: mobile (verified), alternate, email | Yes |
| 27 | Home address | Guard, for verification only | Yes |
| 28 | Bank details | Guard, for salary | Yes (with re-auth) |
| 29 | Emergency contact | Guard: name, relationship, phone | Yes |
| 30 | Physical attributes | Height, weight, blood group (blood group used for emergency response only) | Yes |
| 31 | Ex-servicemen status | Guard + document | Upload |
| 32 | Uniform & equipment issued | Agency/Suraksha operations | No |

### 17.4 Field-by-field visibility matrix (the critical control)

Classes: **Public** (anyone on the internet, including the QR verification page) · **Client-visible** (a client on whose site the guard is or was deployed) · **Agency-visible** (the agency the guard is currently linked to) · **Suraksha-only** (Suraksha staff with the relevant role) · **Guard-only** (the guard themselves) · **Legally-restricted** (accessible only to named verification/compliance roles, with per-access audit and a stated purpose).

| Field | Public | Client-visible | Agency-visible | Suraksha-only | Guard-only | Legally-restricted |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guard ID | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | — |
| Photograph | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | — |
| Full name | First name + last initial | Full name | Full | Full | Full | — |
| Category / role | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | — |
| Years of experience | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | — |
| Skills | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | — |
| Languages | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | — |
| Training completed | ✔ (titles only) | ✔ (titles + dates) | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | — |
| Training score | — | Band only (e.g. "Above standard") | ✔ exact | ✔ | ✔ | — |
| Certifications | ✔ (titles) | ✔ (titles, validity) | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | Certificate documents |
| Verification status | ✔ (badge) | ✔ (badge + date) | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | — |
| Police verification | Status badge only | Status + validity date | Status + validity | Status + validity | Status | ✔ **Detail, district, documents** |
| KYC status | Badge only | Badge only | Badge only | Badge + masked refs | Own masked refs | ✔ **Aadhaar/PAN numbers & images** |
| Document status | — | Summary ("all documents current") | Per-document status | ✔ | ✔ own | ✔ **Document files** |
| Licence info (armed) | Badge "Licensed" | Type + validity | Type + validity | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ **Licence number & document** |
| Agency association | ✔ (agency name + verified badge) | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | — |
| Work history | Site **type** + city + duration | Own engagement in full; others as type + city | ✔ within own tenure; prior as type + city | ✔ | ✔ | — |
| Deployment history | Count + years only | Own sites in full | ✔ own tenure | ✔ | ✔ | — |
| Attendance history | — | **Own site only** | ✔ own tenure | ✔ | ✔ | — |
| Reliability indicators | Band only (e.g. "Consistently reliable") | Band + own-site attendance % | ✔ exact | ✔ | ✔ | — |
| Ratings | Aggregate + count (≥5 ratings) | Aggregate + own ratings | ✔ aggregate + own-tenure detail | ✔ | ✔ | — |
| Availability | ✔ | — | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | — |
| Preferred work area | ✔ (city level) | — | ✔ (pincode level) | ✔ | ✔ | — |
| Mobile number | — | — | ✔ (while linked) | ✔ | ✔ | — |
| Alternate phone / email | — | — | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | — |
| Home address | — | — | — | Masked (city/district only) | ✔ | ✔ **Full address** |
| Bank details | — | — | — | Masked (last 4) — Payroll role only | ✔ | ✔ **Full details** |
| Emergency contact | — | — | Name + phone (for on-duty emergencies only) | ✔ | ✔ | — |
| Date of birth | — | Age band only | Age | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ **Full DOB** |
| Physical attributes | — | Height only where relevant to the role | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | Blood group (emergency access) |
| Uniform/equipment issued | — | — | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | — |
| Disciplinary records | — | — | ✔ own tenure only | ✔ | ✔ own | — |
| Grievances raised by the guard | — | — | **Never** (see §17.11) | HR/Compliance roles only | ✔ own | — |

**The data-minimisation rule (SUR-GRD-005, absolute):**

> No sensitive personal data of a guard — Aadhaar number or image, PAN, bank account or UPI details, home address, date of birth in full, police-verification case detail or documents, licence numbers, medical information, or any uploaded identity document — is ever exposed to a client, to the public, or to an agency other than through the explicitly permitted status badges and masked values in the matrix above. Clients receive **verification outcomes, never verification evidence**. Any feature request that would expose a Legally-restricted field to a client or the public is rejected at design review, not mitigated at runtime.

Supporting controls: Legally-restricted fields are stored encrypted with a separate key scope; every access is logged with actor, purpose code and timestamp and is visible to the guard in their own "Who looked at my data" view (§17.10); documents are served only through short-lived signed URLs; bulk export of guard personal data requires a dual-authorisation workflow in Ops; and screenshots of restricted screens are watermarked with the viewing user's ID.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-GRD-006 | The API must enforce the matrix server-side by returning different serialisations per audience. There must be no endpoint that returns the full guard record and relies on the client to hide fields. |
| SUR-GRD-007 | A guard must be able to see, from their own account, exactly what each audience class can see about them, rendered as a live preview ("View as: Public / Client / My agency"). |

### 17.5 Public guard profile — `/g/SG-2026-004871`

**Purpose.** A verifiable professional profile, shareable as a link, that helps a guard get hired and helps a client trust the person at their gate.
**Content, in order:** photograph and name (first name + last initial for Public); Guard ID with copy button; verification badge row (Verified by Suraksha · Police verification current · KYC complete · Trained); category and years of experience; a one-line professional summary (guard-written, moderated); skills chips; languages; training and certifications (titles, issuer, validity); experience summary ("6 years · 11 deployments · site types: corporate campus, warehouse, residential"); reliability band with a plain-language explanation ("Consistently reliable — based on 640 recorded shifts"); ratings aggregate (shown only at ≥5 ratings); availability status; preferred work area at city level; current agency association with the agency's verified badge; and a `Verify this ID` button. There is no contact information on the public profile — enquiries route through `Contact via Suraksha` which creates a lead, so the guard's number is never scraped.
**States.** Unverified guard: the profile is not public at all (404 to non-owners) until verification passes. Suspended: profile shows "This ID is currently suspended" with no other detail. Archived/left the industry: profile shows verification history but availability reads "Not currently available".
**SEO.** `noindex` by default. A guard may opt in to indexing from their privacy settings, with a clear explanation [RECOMMENDED — default private].

### 17.6 Registration and verification lifecycle

**Entry points.** Self-registration on the web or app; the `/careers` guard application (§14.14.4); bulk onboarding by an agency (agency uploads a roster, each guard receives an invitation to claim their own account); branch-desk assisted registration by Suraksha staff.

**Registration steps (web):**

| Step | Content | Validation |
|---|---|---|
| R1 Mobile | Mobile number + OTP, language selection (Hindi default) | Indian mobile; existing number → login instead |
| R2 Basic identity | Full name, DOB, gender, photo (live camera capture preferred; gallery allowed with a flag) | Age ≥18 and ≤ the configured upper limit for the role; photo must pass a basic quality/face-present check |
| R3 Contact & location | Current address, permanent address, city, pincode, emergency contact | Pincode validity |
| R4 Professional | Category applied for, years of experience, skills, languages, prior employers (self-declared: employer, role, city, from–to) | Non-overlapping employment dates warned, not blocked |
| R5 Documents | Aadhaar, PAN, bank proof, photo ID, education (optional), PSARA training certificate (optional), ex-servicemen discharge book (optional), armed licence (if applicable) | Type, size ≤5MB, legibility check; **numbers are captured into an encrypted store and immediately masked in every UI** |
| R6 Police verification | Existing certificate upload, or consent to Suraksha-initiated verification with the required declaration | Consent is explicit, timestamped and revocable with consequences explained |
| R7 Bank & payout | Account number + IFSC or UPI ID, name match declaration | IFSC format; penny-drop verification where the payout rail supports it |
| R8 Declarations & consent | Truthfulness declaration, background-check consent, data-processing consent with a plain-language summary of what is shared with clients and agencies, platform terms | All explicit, no pre-ticked boxes |
| R9 Submit | Summary review, then submit | Completeness gate; partial registrations are saved as Draft for 30 days with SMS reminders |

**Verification pipeline (owned by the Suraksha Verification role):**

| Stage | What happens | Status |
|---|---|---|
| V0 Submitted | Record created, deduplication check against existing identities | Pending |
| V1 Document check | Each document reviewed: legible, matching name/DOB, unexpired. Individual documents can be Verified or Rejected with a reason | In Progress |
| V2 Identity/KYC | Identity confirmed against the submitted documents; where a verification API is available it is used, otherwise manual review. **Do not assume a government verification API exists** [ASSUMPTION: A-122 — availability and permissible use of Aadhaar/PAN verification APIs; manual verification is the guaranteed fallback] | In Progress |
| V3 Police verification | Existing certificate validated, or a request initiated through the configured district process. This is a partly offline process with a tracked reference and expected turnaround | In Progress |
| V4 Reference / employment check | Prior-employer contact where declared; entries corroborated become "Verified employment", others remain "Self-declared" | In Progress |
| V5 Training gate | Induction training assigned; completion and assessment recorded | In Progress |
| V6 Decision | Verified (profile goes live, ID card issued), or Rejected with a reason and an appeal path, or Conditionally verified (deployable on unarmed posts pending police verification, if the configured policy permits) | Verified / Rejected |
| V7 Ongoing | Expiry monitoring on every dated artefact; at T-60/30/15/7 days the guard and their agency are notified; on expiry the status becomes Expiring then Expired, with configured deployment restrictions | Expiring / Expired |

**Re-verification.** Police verification and licences are re-verified on their own cycles; the platform tracks each artefact's validity independently rather than a single blanket "verified" flag. A guard's overall badge reflects the weakest current artefact.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-GRD-008 | Verification decisions must record the deciding staff member, the evidence reviewed and the reason. A rejection must always state a reason the guard can read and appeal. |
| SUR-GRD-009 | The platform must never present verification status as a legal conclusion. UI copy uses "Police verification on record, valid to 12 Mar 2028", never "legally cleared". Jurisdictional rules for what a valid verification is are configuration, not code. |

### 17.7 Guard registration & verification — condensed module spec

**Users/permissions.** Guard (own record), Verification role (review/decide), Agency Admin (view own linked guards' status only), Ops (all). **Screens.** Registration wizard R1–R9 · My verification status · Document locker · Appeal form. **Logic & statuses.** As above; per-document statuses roll up to an overall status. **Audit/security.** Every document view logged with purpose; documents encrypted at rest; guard sees their own access log. **Acceptance.** *Given* a guard whose police verification expires in 30 days, *when* the daily job runs, *then* the guard and their linked agency are notified, the profile badge changes to Expiring, and the deployment restriction configured for that state is applied on the day of expiry.

### 17.8 Agency association, linkage and de-linkage

**Model.** A guard has at most one **active** agency association at a time (`SURAKSHA-HQ` counts as an agency for guards employed directly by Suraksha), plus an immutable association history. Multi-agency simultaneous association is not supported in V1 — it creates roster conflicts and BR-001 violations.

| Flow | Steps | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| **Guard-initiated link** | Guard searches the agency directory → sends a request → agency accepts → association Active from the accepted date | Agency must be verified on Trinetra; a pending request expires in 14 days |
| **Agency-initiated link** | Agency enters the Guard ID or mobile → invitation sent to the guard → **guard must accept** | An agency can never link a guard without the guard's explicit acceptance — this is the anti-poaching and anti-conscription control |
| **De-linkage, guard-initiated** | Guard requests de-linkage with a reason and an effective date → notice period per the configured employment policy → agency notified → association Archived on the effective date | The guard's identity, documents, training and history remain with the guard. Pending dues and issued equipment are flagged for settlement but never block the de-linkage itself |
| **De-linkage, agency-initiated** | Agency ends the association with a reason and an effective date → guard notified with the reason → association Archived | An agency may record a disciplinary note; the note is visible to the guard and to Suraksha, and to a future agency **only as an aggregate integrity signal**, never as free text [DECISION REQUIRED: D-126 — whether prior-employer disciplinary notes are ever surfaced to prospective agencies; strong fairness and defamation exposure either way] |
| **Suspension by Suraksha** | Compliance or Verification suspends the Guard ID for a stated reason → all associations suspended → appeal path opens | Reason categories are a controlled vocabulary; every suspension is reviewable |

**Data consequences of de-linkage.** On the effective date, the agency loses access to the guard's contact details, exact reliability figures, document statuses and future availability. It retains, permanently and read-only, the deployment and attendance records generated **during its own tenure**, because those are the agency's own operational records. This split is enforced by tenure-bounded queries, not by a UI filter.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-GRD-010 | Agency access to a guard's data must be bounded by the association's start and end dates in the query layer. A de-linked agency querying the guard's profile must receive only the historical, tenure-bounded projection. |
| SUR-GRD-011 | A guard must be able to view their complete association history, including who ended each association and the recorded reason. |

### 17.9 Guard web screens

| Screen | Route | Contents | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Login / register | `/login`, `/register` | Mobile + OTP (primary), password fallback, language toggle Hindi/English | Same identity service as every other property (canon §4) |
| Home | `/home` | Today's duty card (site, post, shift, reporting time, supervisor name and number, duty instructions) · this week's roster strip · attendance summary this month · pending actions (expiring documents, unread notices, training due) · earnings snapshot · availability toggle | Duty **actions** (check-in etc.) are not here — a line reads "Check in from the Suraksha Guard App" with a download link |
| My profile | `/profile` | All portfolio fields grouped: Identity · Professional · Training & certifications · Verification · Availability & preferences · Contact & emergency · Bank (masked, re-auth to view/edit) | Includes the **"View as" preview** (SUR-GRD-007) |
| Documents | `/documents` | Per-document card: type, status pill, expiry, rejection reason, actions Upload/Replace/View | Documents open in a watermarked viewer; download disabled for restricted types |
| Verification status | `/verification` | The V0–V7 pipeline as a visual tracker with per-stage status, dates, what's pending from the guard, and the appeal action | Plain-language explanations in Hindi and English |
| Duty & roster | `/roster` | Calendar and list of assignments: date, site, post, shift window, reporting time, status; past assignments with attendance outcome | Read-only; changes are requests |
| Attendance | `/attendance` | Monthly view: present, absent, leave, overtime; per-day detail with check-in/out times, source, and the guard's own remarks; dispute action for a record the guard believes is wrong | Guard-raised attendance disputes route to the agency/Ops, mirroring the client dispute mechanic |
| Leave | `/leave` | Request form (type, from–to, reason, backup availability), balance, history, approval status | Approval is the agency's |
| Earnings | `/earnings` | Month-wise summary: days worked, overtime, gross, deductions (statutory contributions, advances), net; payslip PDF per month; payment status and date; advance request action where the agency permits; annual summary | Read-only; the paying party is the agency (or Suraksha for direct employment). Payout rails are unresolved at the canon level, so payment *status* is shown, not a payment instrument |
| Training | `/training` | Assigned modules with due dates; completed modules with dates, scores and certificates; the aggregate training score with an explanation of how it is computed; a catalogue of optional modules; a "how to improve your score" panel | Certificates downloadable and shareable as a link |
| Notices | `/notices` | Notices from the agency and from Suraksha, read/unread, acknowledgement where required | Acknowledgement is recorded with timestamp |
| Support & grievance | `/support` | Ticket list and a raise-ticket flow with categories; the separate **confidential grievance** channel (§17.11) | Two visually distinct paths |
| Job opportunities | `/opportunities` | Open positions matching the guard's category, availability and preferred work area, from Suraksha and from verified agencies; apply with one tap (the profile is the application) | [FUTURE for agency-posted roles; V1 shows Suraksha openings only] |
| My data & access log | `/privacy` | Who accessed my data (role, purpose, date), consents given with revocation, download my data, ID card download/reissue request | The transparency surface that makes §17.4 credible |
| Settings | `/settings` | Language, notification preferences, password, sessions, app lock note | — |
| Emergency web check-in | `/duty/checkin` | Only appears when the guard's assignment is active and the Guard App reports unavailable. Requires a supervisor-issued one-time code, captures a selfie and browser geolocation, and is recorded with source `Web fallback (supervisor authorised)` | Exists so a broken phone doesn't cost a guard a day's pay; deliberately friction-heavy to prevent it becoming the norm |

**Guard-side UX rules.** Hindi is the default language when the browser locale suggests it; text size is one step larger than the client surfaces; every screen has one primary action; icons always carry text labels; forms save progress after every step; error messages state what to do next, not what went wrong technically. No screen requires typing more than a phone number and an OTP to reach useful information.

### 17.10 Availability, preferences and the marketplace signal

**Availability model.** A single status the guard controls: **Available** (looking for a deployment, available from a date), **Deployed** (currently assigned — set automatically when an assignment is active), **On leave** (with dates), **Not looking** (visible to nobody as available). Guards on Deployed cannot be shown as available; the platform never advertises an actively deployed guard to another agency, which protects the current agency's roster and the guard's honesty at once.

**Preferences.** Preferred cities (multi), pincode radius from a home base, willingness to relocate (Y/N + notice), preferred shift (day/night/either), preferred site types, minimum expected salary band (Guard-only and Suraksha-only; **never shown to agencies** in V1 to avoid it being used to suppress offers) [DECISION REQUIRED: D-127].

**Matching signal.** The availability + preference + verification + reliability tuple is what makes the workforce side valuable to Trinetra (§19) and to Suraksha's own deployment planning. In V1 matching is a filtered search for Suraksha Ops and, where enabled, for verified agencies; automated recommendation sits in the AI Recommendation action class (§25) and never auto-assigns a guard.

### 17.11 Grievance and support

Two separate channels, deliberately:

1. **Support tickets** — operational issues (roster wrong, payslip mismatch, document rejected, app not working). Visible to the agency and to Suraksha Support. Standard ticket lifecycle with SLA display.
2. **Confidential grievance** — harassment, unsafe site conditions, non-payment of wages, illegal duty demands, discrimination, or a complaint about the agency itself. Routed **only** to Suraksha's HR/Compliance roles. **The agency cannot see that a grievance exists, who raised it, or its content** (enforced in the matrix, §17.4). The channel supports anonymous submission (identity known to Compliance only, or fully anonymous with the trade-off explained), evidence upload, a case reference, status tracking, and a stated response window. Retaliation-linked de-linkage — an association ended within N days of a grievance — is flagged automatically to Compliance for review.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-GRD-012 | The grievance channel must be reachable in two taps from every guard screen, in the guard's language, and must never route through, notify, or be visible to the agency named in the grievance. |
| SUR-GRD-013 | Grievance records must be stored under a separate access-control scope from operational guard data, with access limited to named Compliance/HR users and every access audit-logged. |

### 17.12 Guard Platform — condensed module specs

**Profile & portfolio.** *Purpose:* the guard's professional record. *Users:* guard (edit within allowed fields), Verification (approve changes to identity-bearing fields), Agency (read within tenure), Client (read the client-visible projection). *Screens:* Profile, Documents, View-as preview. *Logic:* identity-bearing fields (name, DOB, category) require a change request with evidence; cosmetic fields save immediately; every change is versioned. *Audit:* full field-level history. *Acceptance:* *Given* a guard changes their photo, *when* they save, *then* the public profile continues to show the previously approved photo until Verification approves the new one.

**Earnings.** *Purpose:* transparency of pay, which is the single largest driver of guard trust and retention. *Logic:* earnings are derived from approved attendance × the applicable rate, plus overtime and allowances, minus statutory deductions and advances — all as configuration, never hard-coded; the guard sees the arithmetic, not just the total. *Statuses:* Pending → Processed → Paid → Failed (with a reason and a re-initiation path). *Edge cases:* a payslip corrected after issue creates a revised payslip with both versions retained (BR-003). *Acceptance:* *Given* an approved month of 26 days, *when* the payslip is generated, *then* the days shown equal the approved attendance days and any variance is itemised.

**Training.** *Purpose:* raise capability and make it visible to buyers. *Logic:* modules have prerequisites, validity periods and refresher cadences; the training score is a weighted, published formula (module completion, assessment score, recency, refresher compliance) and the formula is shown to the guard so the number is not a black box. *Acceptance:* *Given* a guard completes a refresher, *when* the score recomputes, *then* the change and its cause are shown in the guard's training history.

**ID card.** Digital card in the app and downloadable PDF from the web: photo, name, Guard ID, category, agency, validity, QR to the verification URL, and the command-center number on the reverse. Reissue on loss is a request with a recorded reason. A suspended ID's QR resolves to a suspension notice.

### 17.13 Analytics and KPIs (guard side)

| Event | Fired when |
|---|---|
| `guard_register_start` / `_step_complete{step}` / `_submit` | Registration wizard |
| `guard_document_upload{type}` / `_rejected{type, reason}` | Document lifecycle |
| `guard_verification_stage_change{stage, status}` | Verification pipeline |
| `guard_agency_link_request` / `_accepted` / `_delink{initiator, reason}` | Association lifecycle |
| `guard_availability_change{status}` | Availability toggle |
| `guard_profile_public_view{referrer}` | Public profile viewed |
| `guard_verify_qr_scan` | ID QR scanned |
| `guard_grievance_submit{category, anonymous}` | Grievance raised (content never in analytics) |
| `guard_training_complete{module, score}` | Training completion |

**KPIs.** Registration completion rate by step (the drop-off point is almost always documents); median time from submission to Verified; % of active guards with all documents current; % of deployments filled by fully-verified guards; guard 90-day retention by agency; grievance resolution time; % of guards who log in to the web portal at least monthly (a proxy for whether the identity layer is real to them).

### 17.14 Guard Platform acceptance criteria (sample)

| ID | Criterion |
|---|---|
| AC-GRD-01 | *Given* a client user, *when* they open a guard's profile from Live view, *then* the response contains only Client-visible fields, and a direct API call for the guard's Aadhaar, address or bank details returns 403 with no field-existence disclosure. |
| AC-GRD-02 | *Given* a guard de-linked from Agency A on 31 July, *when* Agency A queries that guard on 1 August, *then* they receive only deployment and attendance records dated on or before 31 July, and no contact details. |
| AC-GRD-03 | *Given* an agency attempts to link a guard by ID, *when* the guard has not accepted, *then* no association exists and the agency sees only "Invitation pending". |
| AC-GRD-04 | *Given* a guard's police verification expires today, *when* the daily compliance job runs, *then* the profile badge becomes Expired, the configured deployment restriction is applied, and the guard, the agency and Ops are notified. |
| AC-GRD-05 | *Given* a guard submits a confidential grievance naming their agency, *when* any Agency Admin of that agency queries any endpoint, *then* no record, count, badge or notification indicating the grievance is returned. |
| AC-GRD-06 | *Given* a public visitor scans a valid ID QR, *when* the verification page loads, *then* it shows ID validity, name (first name + last initial), photo, category, verification badge and agency association only. |
