| R-122 | Instant booking creates a fulfilment obligation before any site assessment | A paid booking that cannot be staffed damages trust and forces refunds | Serviceability + capacity check at B2, and a stated 3-day minimum start date | Booking flow, ops capacity |
| R-123 | Publishing honest empty states (no reviews, no press, no awards) may read as a weaker brand than the current fabricated content | Short-term conversion cost versus long-term credibility and legal exposure | Ship honest states; prioritise collecting real reviews from the first 20 deployments | Website, brand, legal |


## 18. Guard App

**Product:** Suraksha Guard App (Android primary, iOS secondary) — the field tool used by every Guard, PSO, Bouncer, Supervisor (field) and Specialised Personnel working under Suraksha (`SURAKSHA-HQ`) or under any subscribed Agency tenant. Web companion: guards.surakshaguards.in (§17).

**Why this section is the most operationally critical mobile surface:** every number shown on the client portal (§15), the Command Center (§24), the Agency Portal dashboard (§20) and every payroll run originates as an event captured by this app. If the Guard App fails to capture a check-in, the client sees an absence, the agency raises a replacement, payroll under-pays a guard who actually worked, and the SLA report is wrong. The app is therefore designed for the worst realistic conditions, not the best.

### 18.0 Operating envelope (design constraints, not aspirations)

| Constraint | Target | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Minimum device | Android 8.0 (API 26), 2 GB RAM, 720×1280 screen, ~8 GB storage with <1 GB free | Entry-level handsets dominate the guard workforce |
| APK size | ≤ 25 MB download, ≤ 60 MB installed | Data cost and storage pressure |
| Cold start to Duty screen | ≤ 3.0 s on the minimum device, offline | Guard checks in at a gate, standing up, in a hurry |
| Data budget | ≤ 40 MB/month typical duty use excluding media uploads; media uploads compressed and deferrable to Wi-Fi | Prepaid daily-data packs |
| Battery budget | ≤ 6% of a 4000 mAh battery per 12-hour shift for location + app foreground service | Guards cannot charge mid-shift at many posts |
| Network assumption | Intermittent 2G/3G, frequent 0-bar pockets (basements, stairwells, industrial sheds) | Offline-first is mandatory (canon §4) |
| Literacy assumption | Functionally low text literacy; comfortable with WhatsApp voice notes, camera, and phone calls | Drives icon+voice+colour UI, minimal typing |
| Language | Hindi default offer, 19+ Indian languages, in-app switch without re-login | Canon §1.7 |

`[CONFIRMED]` iOS is a secondary target: a small share of supervisors and PSOs carry iPhones. Feature parity is required for duty-critical flows; platform differences are listed in §18.14.

---

### 18.1 Module: Onboarding & Registration

**1 Purpose.** Get a guard from "app installed" to "able to mark duty" with the fewest keystrokes possible, while binding the account to one device and collecting the identity/KYC artefacts the agency and PSARA compliance need.

**2 Users.** Guard · PSO · Bouncer · Supervisor (field) · Specialised Personnel. Invited by Agency HR / Recruiter / Agency Admin from §20 Guards module, or self-registered then claimed by an agency.

**3 Permissions.** Pre-activation the account can only see onboarding screens, help, and language switch. No duty data is served until the account is linked to a tenant and has at least one Active Assignment. See §31 for the full matrix.

**4 Screens.**

| Screen ID | Name | Entry |
|---|---|---|
| GAP-S-001 | Language picker (first launch) | App install |
| GAP-S-002 | Phone number entry | After language |
| GAP-S-003 | OTP entry (6-digit, auto-read) | After phone |
| GAP-S-004 | Identity capture (name, DOB, gender) | New user only |
| GAP-S-005 | Selfie enrolment (face template) | After identity |
| GAP-S-006 | Document upload (Aadhaar/ID, PAN, bank, PSARA training cert, police verification) | After selfie |
| GAP-S-007 | Agency link (invite code / agency search / "my agency will add me") | After documents |
| GAP-S-008 | Permissions primer (location, camera, notifications, battery-optimisation exemption) | After link |
| GAP-S-009 | Waiting-for-approval state | After submit |
| GAP-S-010 | Set 4-digit app PIN | On first approved login |

**5 UI detail.** GAP-S-001 shows a 2-column grid of language tiles, each rendered in its own script plus the English name (e.g. "हिन्दी / Hindi"), 88 dp tall, with Hindi pre-highlighted as the default choice and a "Listen" speaker icon that speaks the tile name. GAP-S-002 has a fixed +91 prefix, a 10-digit numeric-only field, a 64 dp-tall primary button "Get OTP / OTP भेजें", and no other input. GAP-S-003 auto-reads the SMS via the Android SMS Retriever API (no SMS-read permission requested); manual entry is 6 large boxes; a 30-second resend timer with "Call me instead" fallback after two failed SMS attempts. GAP-S-004 accepts name by voice dictation as well as keyboard. GAP-S-005 is a live camera oval with a spoken instruction track. GAP-S-006 shows a checklist of documents where each row is either "Camera" or "Gallery" — never a file browser — with an example thumbnail of a correctly framed document.

**6 UX flow.** Language → phone → OTP → (existing user: straight to Duty) → identity → selfie → documents (skippable, each item individually) → agency link → permissions → submitted. Document upload is explicitly non-blocking: a guard can reach the Duty screen with documents pending, because a guard who cannot mark duty is a guard who is not paid. Missing documents drive a persistent banner and the expiry/compliance flow (§18.11).

**7 Fields.**

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `preferred_language` | enum (19+) | Yes | Default `hi` |
| `phone` | E.164 | Yes | Login identifier; unique per person |
| `full_name` | string | Yes | Voice dictation allowed |
| `dob` | date | Yes | Wheel picker, not keyboard |
| `gender` | enum M/F/O | Yes | Icon buttons |
| `face_template_id` | ref | Yes | Template, not raw image; see §39 |
| `id_document_type` / `number` / `images[]` | enum/string/blob | Conditional | Number field optional if OCR extraction succeeds and guard confirms |
| `bank_account` / `ifsc` / `upi_id` | string | No at onboarding | Required before first payroll disbursement |
| `psara_training_cert` | doc | No | Required for compliance status Verified |
| `police_verification` | doc | No | Drives Verification entity (§32) |
| `agency_invite_code` | string(8) | No | Alternative to agency search |
| `emergency_contact_name` / `_phone` | string | Yes | Used in SOS notification chain (§24) |

**8 Validation.** Phone must be 10 digits starting 6–9. OTP 6 digits, 5 attempts then 15-minute lockout, then support-assisted recovery. DOB must yield age 18–65 (`[ASSUMPTION: A-160]` upper bound configurable per agency policy). Selfie must pass liveness (blink or head-turn challenge) and a minimum face-quality score before acceptance. Documents: max 8 MB per image pre-compression, auto-compressed to ≤ 400 KB long-edge 1600 px, blur detection rejects with a spoken "Photo is blurry, take again".

**9 Business logic.** A person is unique by verified phone. If the phone already exists under another tenant with status Active, registration becomes a **transfer request** routed to both agencies rather than a duplicate profile (see §20 Guards → transfer). Device binding is established at first successful login: `device_id` (Android ID + app-generated install UUID, keystore-backed) is bound to the guard account. A second device attempting login triggers `BR-1xx` device-change approval: OTP plus an approval task to the agency's Operations Manager. Only one active device per guard account at a time.

**10 Backend logic.** Identity service (canon §4) issues the OTP and the session; the Guard profile is created in the guard registry with `tenant_id` = null until agency link is accepted, at which point rows are re-parented within the same tenant-scoped guard record (never cross-tenant copied). Face template extraction runs server-side; the raw enrolment selfie is retained per the retention policy in §39.

**11 Status lifecycle.** `Draft` (registration incomplete) → `Pending` (submitted, awaiting agency acceptance) → `Active` → `Suspended` (agency-initiated) → `Archived` (separated). `Rejected` is reachable from Pending.

**12 Notifications.** OTP by SMS. "Your agency has added you" push + SMS on link acceptance. "Documents pending" push at D+1, D+3, D+7 after activation. Channels and templates per §36.

**13 Integrations.** SMS gateway (OTP + fallback), SMS Retriever API, face-matching provider, OCR for document field extraction. Where the OCR provider is uncertain, manual keying by the guard or by agency HR is the working design.

**14 Security/access.** No duty data cached before activation. PIN (4-digit) plus optional device biometric unlocks the app after 12 hours of inactivity or on any device restart. Session tokens are short-lived with silent refresh; refresh tokens are keystore-bound and revoked on device change.

**15 Audit.** Registration submitted, approved, rejected, device bound, device changed, face enrolment created/replaced, document uploaded/replaced — all append-only audit entries with actor, device, IP, `device_time` and `server_received_time`.

**16 Edge cases.** Guard has no smartphone → supervisor-proxy attendance (§18.5). Guard changes phone number → number-change flow requiring OTP on old number where possible, else agency-approved override. Two agencies invite the same guard → guard chooses; the other invite auto-expires in 7 days. Guard uninstalls and reinstalls on the same device → same `device_id`, no re-approval. Dual-SIM device where OTP arrives on the other SIM → manual entry path always visible.

**17 QA.** See §44; test cases `TC-GAP-001`–`TC-GAP-020` cover OTP retry, lockout, dual-SIM, low-light selfie, blurred document rejection, duplicate-phone transfer, device-change approval.

**18 Acceptance criteria.**
- Given a new user with a valid phone, When they complete language → phone → OTP, Then they reach identity capture in ≤ 4 taps and ≤ 1 typed field beyond the phone number.
- Given a guard whose documents are all pending, When their agency activates them, Then they can reach the Duty screen and mark attendance, and a persistent "Documents pending" banner is shown.
- Given a guard account already bound to Device A, When the same account logs in on Device B, Then duty data is withheld until an Operations Manager approves the device change, and both devices receive a notification.

**19 Analytics & KPIs.** Events: `gap_lang_selected`, `gap_otp_requested`, `gap_otp_verified`, `gap_selfie_enrolled`, `gap_doc_uploaded`, `gap_agency_linked`, `gap_activated`. KPIs: registration completion rate (target ≥ 85% of started), median time install→activated (target ≤ 6 min excluding agency approval), OTP delivery success (≥ 97% within 30 s), document completion within 7 days (≥ 70%).

**20 Future scalability.** DigiLocker-based document fetch `[FUTURE]`. Aadhaar-based eKYC only where an authorised entity/AUA relationship exists — not assumed `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-160]`. Offline enrolment at an agency office via a supervisor's device with later sync `[FUTURE]`.

---

### 18.2 Module: Language & Localisation

**1 Purpose.** Make the app usable by a guard who cannot comfortably read English or, in some cases, any script.

**2 Users.** All guard-side roles. **3 Permissions.** Self-service, always available, no restriction.

**4 Screens.** GAP-S-001 (first-run picker), GAP-S-060 (Settings → Language), plus a language chip in the profile header.

**5 UI detail.** 19+ languages `[CONFIRMED]` per canon §1.7: Hindi (default), English, Bengali, Marathi, Telugu, Tamil, Gujarati, Urdu, Kannada, Odia, Malayalam, Punjabi, Assamese, Maithili, Santali, Kashmiri, Nepali, Konkani, Sindhi, Dogri, Manipuri. Each language tile shows the endonym plus a speaker icon that plays the language name. Switching applies immediately without restart or re-login.

**6 UX flow.** Language is the first screen ever shown, before any account exists, because a guard who cannot read the phone-number screen cannot proceed.

**7–8 Fields/validation.** `preferred_language` persists to the server profile so a device change carries it forward; `voice_prompts_enabled` (default true); `text_size` (Normal / Large / Extra large).

**9 Business logic.** Three layers of localisation: (a) UI strings; (b) **spoken prompt pack** — pre-recorded or TTS audio for the ~60 critical prompts (check-in, check-out, wake check, SOS confirm, patrol scan, error states), bundled for Hindi + English and downloaded on demand for others; (c) **agency-authored content** (site instructions, notices, training) which is stored per-language with a fallback chain: guard language → agency default language → English.

**10 Backend logic.** Translation catalogue versioned and delivered over-the-air so a string fix does not need an app release. Missing key falls back to English and emits a `i18n_missing_key` telemetry event.

**11 Statuses.** N/A. **12 Notifications.** Push notification bodies are rendered in `preferred_language` at send time by the notification service (§36).

**13 Integrations.** TTS engine on-device where available; bundled audio where not. **14 Security.** None specific. **15 Audit.** Language change recorded on profile.

**16 Edge cases.** Device lacks the font/script for the chosen language → the app ships a subset webfont for the 21 scripts listed; if rendering still fails, the app offers Hindi/English and flags `i18n_font_missing`. TTS voice unavailable for the language → fall back to bundled recorded audio, then to Hindi audio, then silence with a vibration cue.

**18 Acceptance criteria.** Given a guard using Odia, When a notice is published only in Hindi, Then the notice is shown in Hindi with a visible "Available in Hindi" tag and a "Read aloud" button — never a blank screen.

**19 Analytics.** `gap_language_changed`, `i18n_missing_key`, `gap_voice_prompt_played`. KPI: share of active guards using a non-English language (expected ≥ 90%).

**20 Future.** On-device speech-to-text for incident voice notes in regional languages, subject to §41 AI governance. `[FUTURE]`

---

### 18.3 Module: Home / Duty Screen

**1 Purpose.** One screen that answers, in under two seconds and without reading: *am I on duty, what do I do next, and is anything wrong?*

**2 Users.** All guard-side roles. **3 Permissions.** Guard sees only their own assignments; Supervisor (field) additionally sees a "My team" tab (§18.16).

**4 Screens.** GAP-S-011 Duty Home · GAP-S-012 Shift detail · GAP-S-013 Site briefing.

**5 UI detail — named zones, top to bottom.**

| Zone | Content | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Status band | Full-width colour band: grey "Off duty", green "On duty", amber "Duty starts in 00:42", red "You are late" | Colour + icon + text; never colour alone |
| Primary action button | Single 96 dp-tall button: **CHECK IN** / **CHECK OUT** / **NEXT: 20:00 Gate 2** | Occupies ~25% of viewport; one tap opens the check-in sheet |
| Shift card | Site name, post name, shift window, supervisor name with call icon | Tap → GAP-S-012 |
| Duty timeline strip | Horizontal chips: Check-in ✓ · Patrol 1 ✓ · Patrol 2 ○ · Wake check ○ · Check-out ○ | Tap a chip → jump to that flow |
| Alert strip | Zero to three items: documents expiring, unread notice, pending replacement offer, training due | Each row one tap to resolve |
| Quick grid | 6 tiles: Patrol · Incident · Leave · Payslip · Documents · Help | 2×3 grid, 72 dp icons + label |
| SOS | Persistent red circular button, bottom-right, above all content on every screen in the app | Long-press 2 s → §18.9 |

**6 UX flow.** App open → PIN/biometric if required → Duty Home. No dashboard, no feed, no scrolling required to reach the primary action.

**7 Fields.** Derived, not entered: `current_assignment`, `shift_start`, `shift_end`, `site`, `post`, `supervisor`, `attendance_state`, `pending_actions[]`.

**9 Business logic.** The primary button's label is computed by a single state machine: no assignment today → "No duty today" + Leave/Replacement shortcuts; assignment exists and now < start − 60 min → countdown; within the check-in window (start − 60 min to start + 240 min, configurable per agency) → CHECK IN; checked in → CHECK OUT (enabled from shift_end − 30 min; earlier taps require an early-out reason); after check-out → summary + "Duty complete". Late threshold and grace period are agency configuration, not code.

**10 Backend logic.** A single `GET /guard/today` bundle returns assignment, site, post, geofence, checkpoints, briefing, notices, and pending actions in one round trip; it is cached and revalidated with an ETag. See §33.

**11 Status lifecycle (attendance-driven).** Not scheduled → Scheduled → Checked-in → On duty → Break (optional) → Checked-out → Verified (by supervisor/system) — with Absent, Late, Early-out as flags rather than states.

**12 Notifications.** Shift reminder at T−60 and T−15 min; "You have not checked in" at start + 15 min (guard) and start + 20 min (supervisor, per §24).

**16 Edge cases.** Two overlapping assignments (blocked by `BR-001`, but if an authorised exception exists the screen shows both and forces an explicit choice). Shift crossing midnight — the Duty screen belongs to the shift, not the calendar day. Guard opens the app at a site they are not assigned to → check-in blocked with "You are not on duty at this site" and a one-tap "Call supervisor".

**18 Acceptance criteria.** Given a guard with a shift starting in 20 minutes, When they open the app offline, Then the Duty Home renders from cache within 3 s showing the countdown and an enabled CHECK IN button.

**19 Analytics.** `gap_home_opened`, `gap_primary_action_tapped`, `gap_home_render_ms`. KPI: median home render < 1.2 s warm, < 3 s cold offline.

---

### 18.4 Module: Shift & Site Briefing

**1 Purpose.** Tell the guard exactly what this post requires, in a form they can consume standing at a gate.

**2 Users.** Guard, Supervisor (field). **3 Permissions.** Read-only; briefing content authored in §20 Sites/Posts.

**4 Screens.** GAP-S-012 Shift detail · GAP-S-013 Site briefing · GAP-S-014 Roster (7-day) · GAP-S-015 Post orders.

**5 UI detail.** Site briefing is a card stack, each card one instruction with an icon, a ≤ 12-word line, an optional photo, and a "Read aloud" control. Post orders support ordered do/don't lists, an equipment checklist, emergency contacts (each a one-tap call), and a site map image with the geofence and checkpoint pins. Roster is a 7-day vertical list — day, site, shift window, status chip — not a calendar grid.

**6 UX flow.** Check-in success automatically presents the briefing once per shift; it can be reopened any time from the shift card. First-time-at-this-site guards get a mandatory acknowledgement ("I have read the post orders") captured with timestamp.

**7 Fields.** `site_name`, `post_name`, `geofence`, `reporting_point`, `uniform_required`, `equipment_required[]`, `escalation_contacts[]`, `client_specific_instructions[]`, `checkpoint_list[]`, `briefing_version`.

**9 Business logic.** Briefing content is versioned; when the agency edits post orders, guards currently assigned receive a "Post orders updated" push and must re-acknowledge at next check-in. Acknowledgement is evidence for client disputes.

**16 Edge cases.** Briefing not yet authored → generic default plus a flag to the agency. Briefing longer than 12 cards → paginated, progress dots, resumable.

**18 Acceptance criteria.** Given post orders updated at 14:00, When a guard checks in at 20:00, Then re-acknowledgement is requested before the Duty timeline shows Check-in ✓ as complete.

---

### 18.5 Module: Attendance — GPS Check-in / Check-out

**1 Purpose.** Produce a trustworthy, disputable-in-court record that a specific person was at a specific post at a specific time.

**2 Users.** Guard (self), Supervisor (field) (proxy/verify), Field Officer (verify).

**3 Permissions.** Self check-in always; proxy check-in only for Supervisor (field) with `attendance.proxy` permission and only for guards on their own roster; see §31.

**4 Screens.** GAP-S-020 Check-in sheet · GAP-S-021 Face capture · GAP-S-022 Check-in result · GAP-S-023 Check-out sheet · GAP-S-024 Attendance history · GAP-S-025 Proxy attendance (supervisor).

**5 UI detail.** The check-in sheet is a bottom sheet with three stacked status rows — **Location** (green tick / amber "finding" / red "out of area" with distance in metres), **Time** (server-synced tick or "using device time" warning), **Face** (pending/captured) — then one full-width confirm button. Face capture is an oval overlay with automatic capture on quality threshold; no shutter button, no retake required unless quality fails. The result screen is a full-screen green tick with the site name, the recorded time, and a 3-second auto-dismiss.

**6 UX flow (the two-tap ideal).** See the worked example in §18.20.

**7 Fields captured per attendance event.**

| Field | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `assignment_id`, `shift_id`, `post_id`, `site_id` | Cached roster | |
| `event_type` | enum: check_in, check_out, break_start, break_end | |
| `device_time` | Device clock | Always stored (canon §4) |
| `server_received_time` | Server | Authoritative for pay and SLA |
| `monotonic_offset` | Device uptime clock delta | Detects clock tampering between capture and sync |
| `lat`, `lng`, `accuracy_m`, `provider` | Fused location | `provider` = gps/network/fused |
| `geofence_result` | enum: inside, outside, unknown | Plus `distance_m` |
| `is_mock_location` | Boolean | Android `isFromMockProvider` + app-list check |
| `device_id`, `device_model`, `os_version`, `app_version` | Device | |
| `battery_pct`, `is_charging` | Device | Explains gaps in tracking |
| `network_state` | enum: online, offline | Determines sync path |
| `face_match_score`, `liveness_result` | Face service | Score, not just pass/fail |
| `selfie_media_id` | Media store | Retained per §39 |
| `photo_hash` | SHA-256 | Tamper evidence |
| `capture_sequence_no` | Per-device counter | Detects deleted/re-ordered offline events |
| `client_event_uuid` | Device UUID | Idempotency key for sync |

**8 Validation.** Location accuracy must be ≤ 100 m to auto-accept (configurable per site; large industrial sites may need 200 m). Face match ≥ threshold `T_high` auto-accepts; between `T_low` and `T_high` accepts with a "manual review" flag; below `T_low` rejects with two retries then falls to supervisor verification rather than blocking duty. **Design rule: a failed verification never blocks the guard from marking duty — it downgrades the record's confidence and raises a review task.** Blocking a guard from working is a worse outcome than a low-confidence record.

**9 Business logic.**

| Rule | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Check-in window | shift_start − 60 min to shift_start + 240 min (agency-configurable) |
| Late | check-in after shift_start + grace (default 15 min) → `late_by_min` computed, flag raised |
| Absent | no check-in by shift_start + 60 min (configurable) → Absent flag, replacement workflow triggered (§18.12) |
| Outside geofence | Allowed with mandatory reason + photo; recorded as `geofence_result = outside`; supervisor approval required for it to count as paid duty |
| Early check-out | Requires reason from a fixed list + optional voice note |
| Missed check-out | Auto-close at shift_end + 120 min with `auto_closed = true`; hours credited to scheduled end; flagged for supervisor |
| Double check-in | Idempotent on `client_event_uuid`; a genuine second check-in on the same shift is rejected client-side and server-side |
| Proxy | Supervisor check-in records both `subject_guard_id` and `actor_user_id`, always flagged, always requires supervisor's own location + selfie |

**10 Backend logic.** Attendance ingest is a separate high-write path (canon §4). Events are idempotent by `client_event_uuid`, validated against the roster, geofence-evaluated server-side (never trusting the client's own geofence verdict), face-verified asynchronously if the media arrives later, then written to the Attendance entity (§32) and published to the real-time bus (§34) for the Command Center and client live view.

**11 Status lifecycle.** `Pending` (captured, queued) → `Active`/recorded → `Verified` (auto or supervisor) → `Rejected` (supervisor rejects, e.g. proven proxy fraud) → `Archived`. Corrections never overwrite: a correction creates a new linked record with `supersedes` and a reason.

**12 Notifications.** Guard: check-in confirmed, late warning, missed check-in. Supervisor: guard late, guard absent, out-of-geofence check-in awaiting approval, low face-match review. Client-facing notifications are governed by §36.

**13 Integrations.** Fused location provider; face-matching service; optional biometric device reconciliation for sites with hardware (§20 Biometric integration); SMS fallback path (§18.19).

**14 Security/access.** Selfies and location are personal data; access is role-scoped, watermarked on export, and retention-limited (§39). The app never exposes another guard's attendance to a Guard role.

**15 Audit.** Every attendance event, every correction, every approval/rejection, every proxy action, and every anti-spoof flag is audit-logged with actor and both timestamps.

**16 Edge cases.** GPS unavailable indoors → app accepts network-provider location with accuracy annotation and a mandatory selfie; if location is entirely unavailable, check-in is captured with `geofence_result = unknown` and routed to supervisor verification. Guard's face changed (beard, injury, bandage) → repeated low scores trigger a re-enrolment task rather than repeated blocks. Two guards sharing one phone at a post → blocked by device binding; the second guard uses the supervisor-proxy path and the pattern is flagged. Time zone always IST; devices set to other zones are normalised and flagged.

**17 QA.** `TC-GAP-021`–`TC-GAP-060`: airplane-mode check-in, mock-location app installed, clock set forward 3 hours, geofence edge at exactly the boundary, 100 queued events syncing at once, face capture in darkness, battery-saver killing the process mid-capture.

**18 Acceptance criteria.**
- Given a guard inside the geofence with a good GPS fix, When they tap CHECK IN and the face capture succeeds, Then attendance is recorded and confirmation shows within 4 s, and no other input is required.
- Given the device is offline, When the guard checks in, Then the event is queued locally with `device_time`, the confirmation states "Saved — will send when network returns", and the Duty timeline shows Check-in ✓ with a pending-sync icon.
- Given a mock-location app is active, When the guard checks in, Then the event is still captured but marked `is_mock_location = true`, the guard is told "Your location could not be trusted — your supervisor will confirm", and a P1 review task is raised.

**19 Analytics & KPIs.** `gap_checkin_started/succeeded/failed`, `gap_geofence_outside`, `gap_face_low_score`, `gap_mock_location_detected`, `gap_checkin_offline_queued`. KPIs: check-in success rate ≥ 98%; median taps to check in = 2; median check-in duration ≤ 12 s; share of attendance with `geofence_result = inside` ≥ 95%; offline-captured share (health signal, not a target).

**20 Future scalability.** Bluetooth beacon-assisted post confirmation for indoor posts `[FUTURE]`. Passive on-site presence detection (dwell-time verification) as a supporting signal `[FUTURE]`.

---

### 18.6 Module: Anti-Spoof & Device Integrity

**1 Purpose.** Make attendance and patrol fraud expensive and detectable without punishing honest guards on cheap phones.

**2 Users.** Invisible to guards except at the moment a signal is adverse; consumed by Supervisor, Operations Manager, Command Center (§24), and Compliance.

**4 Screens.** No dedicated guard screen. Adverse outcomes surface as plain-language messages ("Your location could not be checked — supervisor will confirm") and as review queues in §20.

**9 Business logic — the signal set.**

| Signal | Detection | Response |
|---|---|---|
| Mock location | Android `Location.isFromMockProvider()`; developer-options mock app selected; known mock-app package scan | Event accepted, flagged `is_mock_location`, confidence downgraded, P1 review task, repeat offences → agency policy action |
| Device time tampering | `device_time` vs `server_received_time` delta beyond ±120 s on sync; monotonic uptime clock cross-check for offline events | `time_confidence` = low; pay/SLA uses `server_received_time` or the corrected offline estimate (§18.19) |
| Device binding violation | Login/event from an unbound `device_id` | Duty data withheld pending approval; event flagged |
| Rooted / unlocked device | Play Integrity API verdict where available; root-indicator heuristics elsewhere | Recorded as `device_integrity = compromised`; not an automatic block (many legitimate low-end devices fail these checks) `[RECOMMENDED]` |
| Photo-of-a-photo (face spoof) | Liveness challenge (blink/turn), screen-glare and moiré heuristics from the provider | Retry, then supervisor verification |
| Reused media | `photo_hash` matching a prior event | Duplicate flag, P1 review |
| Impossible travel | Two events from the same guard at distance/time implying > 120 km/h | Both flagged, supervisor review |
| Sequence gap | `capture_sequence_no` gaps on sync (events deleted from the queue) | Gap flag; the missing range is reported to Compliance |
| App tampering | Signature/checksum verification, Play Integrity app-recognition verdict | Session refused; support-assisted reinstall |
| Emulator | Hardware/sensor fingerprint heuristics | Flagged; duty actions blocked pending review |

**10 Backend logic.** Signals combine into an `event_trust_score` (0–100) stored on each field event. Score bands: ≥ 80 auto-verified; 50–79 supervisor verification; < 50 mandatory review with the event excluded from automatic payroll credit until resolved. Weightings are configuration, not code, so they can be tuned without a release `[RECOMMENDED]`.

**14 Security/access.** Detection logic is server-side wherever possible; client-side checks are treated as hints, never as authority. Thresholds are never exposed in the client bundle.

**15 Audit.** Every flag, every score, every override with the overriding user's identity and reason.

**16 Edge cases.** Legitimate causes of adverse signals — a factory-reset phone with a wrong clock, a device with a broken GPS chip, a genuinely rooted budget phone — must all be resolvable by a supervisor in ≤ 2 taps, otherwise supervisors will start disabling the controls.

**18 Acceptance criteria.** Given a guard on a rooted device with correct location and a good face match, When they check in, Then attendance is recorded as valid with an integrity annotation, and the guard sees no warning.

**19 Analytics.** `gap_integrity_flag_raised` by type; KPI: flagged-event rate < 2% of all events, false-positive rate (flags overturned on review) < 20% `[ASSUMPTION: A-161]`.

**20 Future.** Cryptographic event signing with a keystore-held per-device key so offline events are non-repudiable `[RECOMMENDED, phase 2]`.

---

### 18.7 Module: Patrol & Checkpoint Scanning

**1 Purpose.** Prove that the guard physically walked the route, at the required times, and captured anything abnormal.

**2 Users.** Guard, Supervisor (field). **3 Permissions.** Guard scans only checkpoints belonging to their current site.

**4 Screens.** GAP-S-030 Patrol home (route list + next-due timer) · GAP-S-031 Scanner (QR/NFC) · GAP-S-032 Checkpoint detail (observation entry) · GAP-S-033 Round summary · GAP-S-034 Patrol history.

**5 UI detail.** Patrol home shows the current round as a vertical list of checkpoints with big state icons (○ pending, ✓ done, ⚠ missed) and a prominent "Next round starts in 00:23" timer. The scanner opens the camera directly with an NFC-ready banner; no mode selector — the app listens for NFC and scans QR simultaneously. Checkpoint detail offers three optional inputs, all one-tap: Photo, Voice note, "All OK" (default).

**6 UX flow.** Tap Patrol → tap Start round → point at the tag (auto-detect) → optional "All OK" or add observation → next checkpoint is auto-highlighted → after the last, round summary + submit. A full 8-checkpoint round with no observations is 10 taps.

**7 Fields.** `patrol_round_id`, `route_id`, `checkpoint_id`, `scan_method` (qr/nfc/manual), `scan_token`, `device_time`, `server_received_time`, `lat/lng/accuracy`, `distance_from_checkpoint_m`, `observation_type` (all_ok/issue/note), `note_text`, `voice_media_id`, `photo_media_id[]`, `trust_score`.

**8 Validation.** Scan must belong to the site's checkpoint set; scans more than `X` metres from the registered checkpoint location (default 50 m) are flagged. Manual code entry is allowed (for a damaged tag) but always flagged and requires a photo of the tag location.

**9 Business logic.** Rounds are scheduled per post (e.g. hourly 22:00–06:00). A round is `Completed` when all mandatory checkpoints are scanned within the round window; `Partial` when some are; `Missed` when none. Missed rounds escalate per §24. QR tokens are **rotating**: the printed tag encodes a checkpoint ID plus an HMAC that the server validates against a per-site secret and a time window, so photographing a tag and scanning the photo elsewhere fails the location check and (for dynamic tags) the token check. NFC tags carry a UID that is registered to the checkpoint; cloned-UID detection compares scan location patterns.

**10 Backend logic.** Patrol events use the same ingest and idempotency design as attendance. Round completion is computed server-side; the client's view is advisory.

**11 Status lifecycle.** Round: `Pending` → `In Progress` → `Completed` / `Partial` / `Missed`. Checkpoint scan: `Pending` (queued) → `Verified` / `Rejected`.

**12 Notifications.** Round-due reminder at T−5 min; round-overdue at T+10 min to guard, T+15 min to supervisor.

**16 Edge cases.** Tag destroyed/removed → "Tag not working" one-tap path capturing a photo and GPS, counted as a manual scan pending supervisor approval. Guard scans out of order → allowed; order compliance is reported, not enforced, unless the route is marked strict. Phone without NFC → QR only, detected at install and reflected in the UI.

**18 Acceptance criteria.** Given a night route with 8 checkpoints and NFC tags, When the guard completes the round offline, Then all 8 scans are queued with timestamps and the round is shown as Completed locally and reconciles to Completed on sync.

**19 Analytics.** `gap_patrol_round_started/completed/missed`, `gap_checkpoint_scanned` (by method), `gap_manual_scan_used`. KPIs: round completion ≥ 95% on contracted routes; manual-scan share < 5%.

**20 Future.** Route optimisation suggestions and dwell-time analytics `[FUTURE]`.

---

### 18.8 Module: Night Anti-Sleep Wake Check

**1 Purpose.** Confirm a night-shift guard is awake and present between patrol rounds — a `[CONFIRMED]` live-brand promise.

**2 Users.** Guard on a shift flagged `wake_check_enabled`. Monitored by Command Center (§24) and Supervisor.

**4 Screens.** GAP-S-035 Wake-check full-screen prompt · GAP-S-036 Wake-check history (guard's own compliance).

**5 UI detail.** The prompt takes the whole screen over the lock screen, at maximum brightness, with a loud alert tone that ignores silent mode (using the alarm audio stream), continuous vibration, and a single very large button: **"I AM AWAKE"**. A countdown ring shows the remaining acknowledgement time. The button position is randomised within a 3-position grid to prevent muscle-memory dismissal by a half-asleep guard `[RECOMMENDED]`.

**6 UX flow.** Prompt fires → guard taps I AM AWAKE → optional selfie (agency-configurable) → confirmation → screen dismisses.

**9 Business logic.**

| Rule | Default | Configurable |
|---|---|---|
| Firing window | Between 23:00 and 05:30, only on shifts flagged for wake checks | Per post |
| Firing pattern | Randomised interval, 45–90 min apart, minimum 30 min gap from a patrol scan (a scan proves wakefulness and suppresses the next prompt) | Per agency |
| Acknowledgement window | 120 seconds | 60–300 s |
| Escalation on miss | Miss 1: re-prompt after 60 s. Miss 2: auto-call the guard's phone (IVR "Press 1 to confirm") and notify the supervisor P2. Miss 3: notify Command Center P1 and, per §24, the escalation chain | Per agency |
| Selfie requirement | Off by default; on for high-value sites | Per post |
| Response capture | Acknowledgement records device_time, server_received_time, location, response latency in ms | — |

Escalation *mechanics beyond the app* — who is called, in what order, with what timers — are owned by §24 Command Center; this module owns the on-device prompt, capture, and local fallback only.

**10 Backend logic.** The schedule is generated server-side per shift and pushed to the device as part of the `/guard/today` bundle so it can fire **without network**: the device schedules local alarms (`AlarmManager` exact alarms with the appropriate permission, plus a foreground service watchdog). If the device is offline, the acknowledgement queues; if the acknowledgement is missed offline, the *miss* is recorded locally and syncs later, and the server independently detects the absence of an expected acknowledgement after a grace period and escalates.

**11 Status lifecycle.** Wake Check: `Pending` → `Acknowledged` / `Missed` / `Acknowledged Late` / `Suppressed` (patrol scan within window) / `Cancelled` (shift ended early).

**12 Notifications.** Local high-priority notification + full-screen intent; server-side push as a redundant path; IVR call on second miss; supervisor push on second miss.

**16 Edge cases.** Do-Not-Disturb / battery optimisation killing alarms → onboarding requests battery-optimisation exemption and the app health check (§18.18) warns daily if it is missing. Phone dead/charging elsewhere → server-side detection of "no acknowledgement and no heartbeat" escalates as a device-offline event, not as guard misconduct, until a supervisor confirms. Guard genuinely on a toilet/round break → the 120 s window plus the miss-1 re-prompt is designed to absorb this. Two guards at one post → prompts fire per assignment, each guard on their own device.

**18 Acceptance criteria.**
- Given a night shift with wake checks enabled and the device offline, When the scheduled prompt time arrives, Then the full-screen prompt fires with sound and vibration and the acknowledgement is stored locally with both timestamps.
- Given the guard does not acknowledge within 120 s and does not acknowledge the 60 s re-prompt, When the device is online, Then an IVR call is placed and the supervisor receives a P2 alert; when the device is offline, Then the server escalates on the missing-acknowledgement timer per §24.

**19 Analytics.** `gap_wake_prompt_fired/acknowledged/missed`, `gap_wake_ack_latency_ms`, `gap_wake_alarm_blocked` (detected non-fire). KPIs: acknowledgement rate ≥ 97%; median latency < 20 s; alarm-blocked device share < 3%.

**20 Future.** Optional low-power motion/activity signal to reduce prompt frequency for demonstrably active guards `[FUTURE]`, subject to privacy review (§39).

---

### 18.9 Module: SOS

**1 Purpose.** Let a guard raise a life-safety alarm in under two seconds, from any screen, in any network condition, including with the screen off.

**2 Users.** All guard-side roles. **3 Permissions.** Always available, even before the shift starts and even when off duty (an off-duty SOS is routed as a welfare alert).

**4 Screens.** GAP-S-040 SOS confirm (2 s long-press ring) · GAP-S-041 SOS active state · GAP-S-042 SOS cancel (PIN) · GAP-S-043 SOS history.

**5 UI detail.** The SOS button is a persistent red circle present on every screen. Activation requires a 2-second long-press with a filling ring and haptic ramp — deliberately not a single tap (accidental pockets) and deliberately not a multi-step confirmation (panic). Once fired, the screen becomes a full red "HELP IS COMING" state showing: alert sent/queued indicator, elapsed timer, the responder's name once acknowledged, a Cancel button that requires the guard's 4-digit PIN, and a live-audio indicator if audio capture is enabled.

**6 UX flow.** Long-press 2 s → immediate local fire (no network wait) → parallel transmission attempts → active state → acknowledgement → resolution by Command Center (§24).

**7 Fields.** `sos_id` (client UUID), `guard_id`, `assignment_id`, `site_id`, `trigger_method` (long_press/power_button/hardware/voice/watch), `device_time`, `server_received_time`, `lat/lng/accuracy`, `battery_pct`, `network_state`, `audio_media_id`, `photo_media_id`, `cancel_reason`, `resolution_code`.

**9 Business logic — transmission ladder (all attempted, in parallel where possible).**

| Order | Path | Condition | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Persistent socket / push-to-server API | Any data connectivity | Sub-second; primary |
| 2 | Retry burst over data | 0/2/5/10/20/30 s backoff for 5 min | Survives flaky 2G |
| 3 | **SMS fallback** | No data acknowledged within 8 s | Structured SMS to the agency's SOS shortcode/number: `SOS|<guard_id>|<site_id>|<lat>,<lng>|<hhmmss>|<battery>` — parsed server-side into a real SOS event |
| 4 | Supervisor SMS | No data and SMS gateway ack unknown | Direct SMS to the supervisor's phone in plain language, so a human is reached even if no server is |
| 5 | Auto-call | No acknowledgement within 30 s | Device places a call to the supervisor / control-room number from the cached escalation list |
| 6 | Local siren | Always, if enabled for the site | Device plays a loud alarm and flashes the torch — deterrence and locating |

The escalation *after* the server receives the SOS — operator assignment, timers, client and police notification, resolution codes — is owned by §24 Command Center. This module owns capture, on-device state, and the offline ladder.

**10 Backend logic.** SOS ingest is prioritised over all other traffic on a dedicated path. Deduplication is by `sos_id` so the socket, SMS and retry paths converge into one event. An SOS received by SMS is marked `channel = sms` and treated as fully valid.

**11 Status lifecycle.** `Pending` (fired, unacknowledged) → `Active` (acknowledged by an operator) → `In Progress` → `Completed` (resolved with code) / `Cancelled` (guard cancelled with PIN, or false-alarm closure). Guards can never delete an SOS.

**12 Notifications.** Guard receives acknowledgement, responder identity, and resolution. Supervisor, Operations Manager, Command Center per §24.

**13 Integrations.** SMS gateway (outbound from device — uses the guard's own SMS, no permission beyond `SEND_SMS` which is requested with a clear explanation and is optional); telephony for auto-call; optional Bluetooth panic button / smartwatch `[FUTURE]`.

**14 Security.** Cancel requires the guard's PIN to prevent an attacker cancelling on a snatched phone. Live audio capture, if enabled, is disclosed in-app and in the privacy notice (§39).

**16 Edge cases.** `SEND_SMS` denied → ladder skips step 3, goes to auto-call sooner, and the app health check warns the guard that SOS will be weaker. Airplane mode → local siren + auto-call fails; the queued SOS transmits the moment any radio returns, and the server timestamps both fire time and receipt time. Battery below 5% → SOS payload is trimmed to the minimum (no audio/photo) to maximise the chance of transmission. Repeated false alarms → recorded, never suppressed automatically; policy handling belongs to the agency.

**18 Acceptance criteria.**
- Given the device has no data connection, When the guard long-presses SOS for 2 seconds, Then within 10 seconds a structured SMS has been dispatched and the on-screen state shows "Sent by SMS", and the event reaches the Command Center as a valid SOS.
- Given an SOS is fired and later the device regains data, When the queued event syncs, Then it deduplicates against the SMS-originated event rather than creating a second alert.

**19 Analytics.** `gap_sos_fired` (by trigger + channel), `gap_sos_ack_latency_ms`, `gap_sos_sms_fallback_used`, `gap_sos_cancelled`. KPIs: fire-to-server median < 3 s online; fire-to-human-acknowledgement median < 60 s (§24 owns the target); SMS-fallback success ≥ 90% where a radio is present.

**20 Future.** Hardware panic button over BLE, wearable integration, silent/duress SOS with a decoy screen `[FUTURE]`.

---

### 18.10 Module: Incident Reporting

**1 Purpose.** Capture what happened, with evidence, at the moment it happens, from someone who may not be able to write it.

**2 Users.** Guard, Supervisor (field). **3 Permissions.** Guards create and view their own reports; supervisors view all reports for their sites.

**4 Screens.** GAP-S-045 Incident type picker · GAP-S-046 Capture (media + voice) · GAP-S-047 Details · GAP-S-048 Review & submit · GAP-S-049 My incidents.

**5 UI detail.** Type picker is a 3×3 icon grid with spoken labels: Theft · Trespass · Fight/Assault · Fire · Medical · Property damage · Vehicle · Suspicious activity · Other. Capture screen has three enormous buttons — **Photo**, **Video (max 30 s)**, **Voice note (max 2 min)** — plus a running strip of captured items. Details asks at most three things: severity (three coloured buttons: Low / Serious / Emergency), "Anyone hurt?" (Yes/No), "Police informed?" (Yes/No). Free text is optional and always paired with voice-to-text.

**6 UX flow.** Incident tile → pick type → record voice note (default suggested action) → add photo → severity → submit. Minimum path: 4 taps + one voice note, zero typing.

**7 Fields.** `incident_id`, `type`, `severity` (mapped to P0–P3), `site_id`, `post_id`, `occurred_at` (device + server), `location`, `description_text`, `voice_media_id[]`, `photo_media_id[]`, `video_media_id[]`, `injuries_flag`, `police_informed_flag`, `witnesses_text`, `submitted_by`, `trust_score`.

**8 Validation.** Type and severity mandatory; at least one of {voice note, photo, text} mandatory. Media size caps: photo 400 KB after compression, video 720p/30 s ≈ 4 MB, audio 2 min ≈ 500 KB opus.

**9 Business logic.** Severity Emergency also raises an SOS-class alert into the Command Center queue (but is not an SOS — see §24 for how the two queues differ). Drafts auto-save every 3 seconds and survive app kill. An incident created offline is a local draft that syncs as a real incident on reconnect, keeping the original `occurred_at`.

**10 Backend logic.** Media uploads are chunked, resumable, and Wi-Fi-preferred unless severity is Emergency, in which case they upload immediately over any network at reduced quality first (a 40 KB thumbnail is sent before the full image so the operator sees *something* fast) `[RECOMMENDED]`.

**11 Status lifecycle.** `Draft` → `Pending` (submitted) → `In Progress` (assigned) → `Completed` (closed with closure report) / `Rejected` (invalid/duplicate) → `Archived`.

**12 Notifications.** Guard gets acknowledgement and closure. Supervisor/Operations Manager get creation notifications by severity; client notification is governed by contract settings in §20 Incidents.

**16 Edge cases.** Storage full → the app reserves 200 MB and warns before capture; if unavailable, voice-only capture is offered. Guard reports an incident about their own supervisor → a "report to agency management / Suraksha" routing option exists to avoid the report dying with its subject `[RECOMMENDED]`. Duplicate reports of the same event by two guards → server clusters by site + time window + type and offers a merge to the operator.

**18 Acceptance criteria.** Given a guard with no network, When they record a 60-second voice note and submit an incident, Then the incident is stored locally, appears in "My incidents" as Pending sync, and uploads automatically when connectivity returns without any user action.

**19 Analytics.** `gap_incident_started/submitted`, media-type mix, `gap_incident_voice_used`, time-to-submit. KPIs: median time-to-submit < 90 s; share of incidents with at least one media attachment ≥ 80%.

**20 Future.** On-device auto-transcription and auto-classification of the voice note, presented as a suggestion the guard confirms `[FUTURE]`, under §41 guardrails.

---

### 18.11 Module: Documents & Expiry

**Condensed treatment.** **Purpose:** keep the guard's KYC, PSARA training certificate, police verification, licence (for armed personnel) and bank details current so deployment stays compliant. **Users/permissions:** guard (own documents, upload + view); agency HR/Compliance verify from §20. **Screens & key UI:** GAP-S-050 Document list — one row per document with a colour state chip (Verified green / Pending amber / Expiring orange with days remaining / Expired red / Rejected grey), a thumbnail, and a single "Update" button opening the camera; GAP-S-051 Document detail with rejection reason spoken aloud. **Logic & statuses:** `Pending` → `Verified` / `Rejected`; `Expiring` at T−60/30/15/7/1 days (configurable per document type); `Expired` triggers the agency's configured operational restriction (`BR-002` is the agency-licence analogue; guard-document restrictions are agency policy, e.g. block deployment to armed posts). **Audit/security:** documents encrypted at rest, access logged, downloads watermarked (§38/§39). **Acceptance:** Given a PSARA training certificate expiring in 30 days, When the guard opens the app, Then the Duty Home alert strip shows "Training certificate expires in 30 days — Update", one tap from the camera.

---

### 18.12 Module: Leave Request & Replacement Acceptance

**1 Purpose.** Let a guard request time off and let the agency fill the resulting hole quickly, using guards who are actually available.

**2 Users.** Guard (request), Supervisor (field) / Operations Manager (approve — in §20), Guard (accept replacement offers).

**4 Screens.** GAP-S-052 Leave list · GAP-S-053 New leave request · GAP-S-054 Leave detail · GAP-S-055 Replacement offer (push-opened) · GAP-S-056 My extra duties.

**5 UI detail.** New leave request: a date-range picker with big +/− day steppers and quick chips ("Today", "Tomorrow", "3 days"), a leave-type icon row (Sick · Casual · Emergency · Unpaid), an optional voice note reason, and a balance strip showing remaining entitlement. Replacement offer arrives as a high-priority push that opens a full-screen card: site name, distance from the guard's saved location, date/time, extra pay amount if configured, and two buttons — **ACCEPT** (green) and **CAN'T** (grey) — plus a countdown showing how long the offer is open.

**6 UX flow.** Leave: 3 taps + optional voice note. Replacement: 1 tap from the notification.

**7 Fields.** Leave: `leave_id`, `type`, `from_date`, `to_date`, `half_day_flag`, `reason_text`, `voice_media_id`, `attachment` (medical), `status`, `approver`, `decision_note`. Replacement offer: `offer_id`, `shift_id`, `site_id`, `distance_km`, `incentive_paise`, `expires_at`, `response`.

**8 Validation.** Leave cannot be requested for a past date except type = Emergency/Sick with a reason (retrospective, flagged). Overlapping leave requests are rejected. Accepting a replacement that conflicts with an existing assignment is blocked by `BR-001`.

**9 Business logic.** Offers are dispatched by the agency's replacement engine (§20 Replacement) in waves — nearest and best-matched first, then widening — with each wave open for a configured number of minutes. First ACCEPT wins; the offer is closed atomically server-side so two guards cannot both accept. Non-response is recorded as a reliability signal, not a penalty by default.

**11 Status lifecycle.** Leave: `Draft` → `Pending` → `Active`(approved) / `Rejected` → `Cancelled` (withdrawn) → `Completed`. Offer: `Pending` → `Accepted` / `Declined` / `Expired` / `Cancelled`.

**12 Notifications.** Leave approved/rejected push + SMS. Replacement offer push with sound; SMS fallback if push is undelivered for 60 s.

**16 Edge cases.** Guard accepts while offline → acceptance is queued and may lose the race; the app clearly states "Sent — waiting for confirmation" and never shows a confirmed state until the server confirms. Emergency leave mid-shift → a separate "I must leave duty" flow that notifies the supervisor immediately and creates both a leave record and an early-out attendance record.

**18 Acceptance criteria.** Given two guards receive the same replacement offer and both tap ACCEPT within the same second, When the server processes them, Then exactly one is confirmed, the other sees "This duty has been taken" within 3 seconds, and no double assignment exists.

**19 Analytics.** `gap_leave_submitted`, `gap_replacement_offer_shown/accepted/declined/expired`, offer-to-acceptance latency. KPIs: replacement fill rate ≥ 85% within 30 minutes; median offer response < 4 min.

---

### 18.13 Module: Earnings & Payslip

**1 Purpose.** Show a guard, in money terms they trust, what they have earned so far and what they were paid — the single biggest driver of app retention and of trust in the attendance system.

**2 Users.** Guard (own data only). **3 Permissions.** Strictly self; no supervisor visibility of another guard's payslip in this app.

**4 Screens.** GAP-S-057 Earnings home · GAP-S-058 Payslip list · GAP-S-059 Payslip detail · GAP-S-061 Advance request `[if enabled by agency]`.

**5 UI detail.** Earnings home leads with one very large number — "This month so far: ₹14,250" — under it three chips (Days worked 19 · Overtime 6 h · Deductions ₹300) and a simple bar row of the last 6 months. Payslip detail is a plain two-column list: Earnings (Basic, Overtime, Allowances, Incentives) and Deductions (Advance, Statutory as configured, Other), then Net pay in the largest type on the screen, then "Paid on 05 Sep · UTR xxxxxx" when disbursed, plus a "Download PDF" and a "Read aloud" button.

**7 Fields.** Read-only projections of the Payroll Run / Payslip entities (§32): `period`, `days_present`, `days_absent`, `paid_leave`, `ot_hours`, `gross_paise`, `deductions[]`, `net_paise`, `payment_status`, `paid_on`, `reference_no`.

**9 Business logic.** The in-month number is explicitly labelled **"Estimated"** until the payroll run is finalised, because attendance corrections change it; showing an authoritative number that later drops is the fastest way to destroy trust. Money is integer paise everywhere (canon §4). Disputes are raised as a support ticket pre-filled with the payslip reference, never as a free-form complaint.

**11 Statuses.** Payslip: `Draft` → `Pending` (finalised, unpaid) → `Completed` (paid) → `Archived`. **12 Notifications.** "Payslip ready", "Salary credited" push + SMS.

**14 Security.** Payslip PDF access requires re-authentication (PIN/biometric) if the app has been idle > 5 minutes `[RECOMMENDED]`.

**16 Edge cases.** Guard works for two agencies → the app scopes strictly by tenant and shows a tenant switcher; earnings never aggregate across tenants. Negative net pay (advances exceeding earnings) → shown as ₹0 net with a carried-forward advance line, never a negative number.

**18 Acceptance criteria.** Given a finalised payslip for August, When the guard opens Payslip detail, Then net pay, payment status and the payment reference are visible without scrolling, and "Read aloud" narrates gross, deductions and net in the guard's language.

**19 Analytics.** `gap_earnings_viewed`, `gap_payslip_downloaded`, `gap_payslip_dispute_raised`. KPI: payslip view rate ≥ 60% of active guards per cycle; dispute rate < 3%.

**20 Future.** Earned-wage access / salary advance rails `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-161]` — depends on the payout rail decision in canon §4.

---

### 18.14 Modules: Training · Notices · Profile · Support (condensed)

| Module | Purpose | Users/permissions | Screens & key UI | Logic & statuses | Audit/security | Acceptance criteria |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Training** | Deliver short, mandatory and optional modules (fire safety, first aid, site-specific SOP, PSARA refresher) in the guard's language | Guard; content authored in §20 Training | GAP-S-062 Training list with progress rings; GAP-S-063 Module player (video ≤ 3 min per lesson, audio-only mode, downloadable for offline); GAP-S-064 Quiz (3–5 picture-based multiple-choice questions); GAP-S-065 Certificate | Module: `Pending` → `In Progress` → `Completed`; pass mark configurable (default 70%); completion writes to the guard's training record and can gate deployment to specific post types | Completion timestamped and audit-logged; certificates are tenant-signed artefacts | Given a mandatory module due in 3 days, When the guard opens the app, Then the alert strip shows it with a one-tap start, and the module plays offline if previously downloaded |
| **Notices** | Agency and Suraksha announcements, site notices, policy changes | Guard read; supervisors can post site notices if permitted | GAP-S-066 Notice list (unread bold, pinned at top); GAP-S-067 Notice detail with Read-aloud and image support; acknowledgement button where required | `Pending` → `Completed` (acknowledged); mandatory notices block nothing but persist in the alert strip until acknowledged | Acknowledgement is audit evidence for policy communication | Given a mandatory notice, When the guard acknowledges it, Then the acknowledgement with timestamp is visible to the agency in §20 |
| **Profile** | Personal details, bank/UPI, emergency contacts, language, PIN, notification settings, app health, logout | Guard (self); some fields (name, DOB) locked after verification and require an agency-approved change request | GAP-S-068 Profile; GAP-S-069 Edit request; GAP-S-070 App health (permissions, battery exemption, alarm reliability, sync queue depth, storage, last server sync); GAP-S-071 Security (PIN change, biometric toggle, bound device) | Change requests to locked fields: `Pending` → `Active` / `Rejected` | Bank-detail changes require OTP re-verification and are audit-logged with a 24-hour cool-off before payroll uses them `[RECOMMENDED]` | Given a guard changes their UPI ID, When they submit, Then an OTP is verified, the change is recorded, and the agency's Payroll role is notified |
| **Support / Help** | Get help without literacy barriers | Guard | GAP-S-072 Help home: "Call my supervisor", "Call agency office", "Call Suraksha helpline", "Raise a ticket" (voice-note-first), FAQ as short illustrated cards, "Report a problem with the app" attaching diagnostics | Ticket: `Pending` → `In Progress` → `Completed`; SLA per §20 Support | Diagnostics attachment excludes personal media and includes app version, device model, queue depth, last sync | Given a guard taps "Call my supervisor", When the call is placed, Then the number used is the current rostered supervisor for the active shift, and the call attempt is logged |

**Platform differences (Android vs iOS)** for §18 as a whole:

| Capability | Android | iOS |
|---|---|---|
| Background location during shift | Foreground service with persistent notification | Background location with Always permission; stricter, more prone to suspension |
| Full-screen wake-check over lock screen | Full-screen intent | Critical alert entitlement required, otherwise a notification banner + sound; acknowledgement may require unlock `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-162]` |
| SMS fallback for SOS | Direct `SEND_SMS` from app | Not permitted — iOS falls back to opening the Messages composer (requires user send) and to auto-call sooner |
| Mock-location detection | `isFromMockProvider` + package scan | Limited; jailbreak heuristics only |
| Exact alarms | `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` | Local notifications, less precise |
| Device binding | Android ID + install UUID | `identifierForVendor` + keychain UUID |

Because of the SOS and wake-check gaps, **Android is the required platform for night-shift guards**; iOS is supported for supervisors, PSOs and day posts `[RECOMMENDED]`.

---

### 18.15 Deep subsection: OFFLINE-FIRST OPERATION

Offline-first is mandatory for the Guard App and only for the Guard App (canon §4). This subsection is the canonical specification of how it works; §20 and §24 consume its outputs.

#### 18.15.1 What is cached, when, and for how long

| Cache set | Contents | Refresh trigger | TTL / eviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| Duty bundle | Today + next 3 days of assignments, shifts, posts, sites, geofences, checkpoint lists, patrol schedules, wake-check schedules, post orders, supervisor + escalation phone numbers | On app open, on push `roster_changed`, every 4 h while online, always before shift start | Kept 7 days; assignments older than 7 days evicted |
| Identity & config | Guard profile, face-match thresholds (server-decided flags only, never raw thresholds), agency config (windows, grace periods), language pack | Login, config-version push | Until version change |
| Media pending | Selfies, incident photos/video/audio awaiting upload | — | Deleted 24 h after confirmed upload; hard cap 500 MB with oldest-non-critical eviction and a user warning |
| Reference content | Notices (30 days), training modules explicitly downloaded, help FAQ | On open / on demand | Notices 30 days; training until removed by guard |
| Event queue | All unsent field events | — | Never evicted; if the queue exceeds 2,000 events an alert is raised to the agency |
| Earnings/payslip | Last 3 payslips (metadata only, PDF on demand) | On open while online | 6 months |

**Encryption:** the local store is encrypted (SQLCipher or platform equivalent) with a key held in the hardware keystore, released on PIN/biometric unlock. Media files are stored in app-private storage, never in the public gallery, and never indexed by the media scanner.

#### 18.15.2 Offline capabilities matrix

| Capability | Works offline? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| View today's duty, site briefing, post orders | Yes | From duty bundle |
| Check-in / check-out with GPS + selfie | Yes | Queued; GPS works without data |
| Geofence evaluation | Yes, locally, as a hint | Server re-evaluates authoritatively on sync |
| Patrol QR scan | Yes | Static token validated on sync |
| Patrol NFC scan | Yes | UID captured locally |
| Wake-check prompt + acknowledgement | Yes | Local alarms from the cached schedule |
| SOS | Yes, degraded | SMS ladder + auto-call + siren (§18.9) |
| Incident capture | Yes | Draft with media, syncs later |
| Leave request | Yes | Queued |
| Replacement acceptance | **No (advisory only)** | Requires server arbitration; UI must not show "confirmed" offline |
| Payslip / earnings | Cached view only | No new data |
| Training video | Only if pre-downloaded | |
| Notices | Cached only | |
| Login / first activation | **No** | Requires OTP |

#### 18.15.3 Sync queue design

- **Structure.** A single durable, ordered outbox table with `client_event_uuid` (idempotency key), `event_type`, `payload_json`, `media_refs[]`, `created_device_time`, `monotonic_ts`, `capture_sequence_no` (monotonically increasing per device, never reset), `priority`, `attempt_count`, `next_attempt_at`, `state` (queued/sending/sent/failed_permanent).
- **Priority classes.** P0 SOS → P1 attendance and wake-check acknowledgements → P2 patrol scans → P3 incidents (metadata before media) → P4 leave/profile/telemetry. Media uploads always trail their parent metadata so an operator sees the event before the evidence.
- **Transport.** Batched POST of up to 50 events per request with per-event results, so one poison event cannot block the batch. Media uploads are separate, chunked and resumable.
- **Retry.** Exponential backoff 5 s → 15 s → 60 s → 5 min → 15 min → 60 min, capped, with immediate retry on connectivity-regained and on app foreground. `failed_permanent` only on a server 4xx that indicates a genuinely invalid event, and such events are surfaced to the guard ("1 record could not be saved — tap to tell your supervisor") rather than silently dropped.
- **Triggers.** Connectivity change, app foreground, periodic background work (WorkManager, ~15 min minimum interval), charging + Wi-Fi (media flush), and an explicit "Sync now" in App health.
- **Backpressure.** If the queue exceeds 500 events or 300 MB of media, the app switches media capture to lower quality and warns the guard; at 2,000 events it raises a server-side alert via any successful request.
- **Visibility.** A small cloud icon with a count badge sits in the Duty Home header; tapping it opens App health showing "23 records waiting · last sent 14:20".

#### 18.15.4 Conflict resolution rules

| Conflict | Rule |
|---|---|
| Duplicate submission of the same event | Idempotent by `client_event_uuid`; server returns the original |
| Roster changed after the device cached it (guard checks in for a shift that was reassigned) | Event is accepted and stored, then reconciled: if the guard is no longer assigned, the record becomes `Pending` review with reason `roster_conflict` and the supervisor decides. The guard is never told "your work does not count" automatically |
| Offline check-in for a shift that was cancelled | Same as above; cancellation reason is shown to the reviewer |
| Two devices for the same guard (device change mid-shift) | Only events from the currently bound device auto-accept; events from the previous device within a 12-hour window are accepted with a flag |
| Supervisor already marked the guard absent, then the guard's offline check-in arrives | Guard's evidence-bearing record supersedes the manual absence, creating a correction record with both entries visible; supervisor is notified |
| Leave request submitted offline for a period already worked | Rejected with reason; guard notified |
| Profile edits offline vs server-side edit by HR | Server wins for locked fields; guard-editable fields use last-write-wins by `server_received_time` with the loser preserved in audit |
| Patrol scan for a checkpoint deleted while offline | Accepted, marked `checkpoint_retired`, counted for the guard, excluded from route-compliance metrics |

**Guiding principle:** conflicts resolve in favour of *recording the guard's evidence and asking a human*, never in favour of silently discarding field data.

#### 18.15.5 Timestamp integrity for offline events

1. Every event stores `device_time` **and** the device's monotonic clock reading (`elapsedRealtime`, unaffected by user clock changes).
2. At the moment of sync the app also sends the current `device_time` and current monotonic reading. The server, knowing its own receipt time, computes the device's clock skew at sync time and back-projects each queued event: `estimated_true_time = server_receipt_time − (monotonic_now − monotonic_at_event)`.
3. `server_received_time` is stored as the actual receipt time; `estimated_true_time` is stored as the reconstructed occurrence time; both are exposed to reviewers.
4. If the device rebooted between capture and sync, the monotonic chain breaks; the app records reboot events, and affected items get `time_confidence = medium` and rely on `device_time` with skew annotation.
5. If `device_time` and `estimated_true_time` differ by more than the configured tolerance (default 5 min), `time_confidence = low`, a flag is raised, and payroll uses the reconstructed time.
6. Nothing in the app allows a guard to edit a timestamp. Corrections are supervisor actions in §20 with reason codes.

#### 18.15.6 Tamper resistance for the offline store

| Threat | Control |
|---|---|
| Guard edits the local database to fabricate a check-in | Encrypted store with keystore-held key; every event carries an HMAC computed with a per-install key provisioned at login; the server verifies the HMAC. `[RECOMMENDED]` upgrade: asymmetric per-device signing key so events are non-repudiable |
| Guard deletes inconvenient queued events | `capture_sequence_no` gaps are detected server-side and reported |
| Guard sets the clock back and captures a backdated check-in | Monotonic reconstruction (§18.15.5) + skew flag |
| Guard uses a mock-location app while offline | Detected at capture time and stored in the event (§18.6) |
| Guard replays a saved selfie file | `photo_hash` duplicate detection + liveness at capture |
| Guard reinstalls the app to clear flags | Server-side history is keyed to the guard and device, not the install; reinstall generates a new install UUID which is itself a signal |
| Rooted device extracting the HMAC key | Keystore-backed key with hardware attestation where available; degraded trust score where attestation fails |

#### 18.15.7 Battery and data budget

| Behaviour | Budget / policy |
|---|---|
| Location sampling while on duty | Adaptive: 60 s interval when stationary inside the geofence, 20 s when moving or during a patrol round, 5 s for 3 min after an SOS. Balanced-power accuracy by default, high accuracy only for check-in/checkpoint/SOS |
| Location when off duty | None. The app must never track a guard outside their shift window `[CONFIRMED as a privacy requirement — see §39]` |
| Foreground service | One, with a clear "On duty — location active" notification the guard can see and understand |
| Screen/wake usage | Wake-check prompt is the only forced wake |
| Media upload | Deferred to Wi-Fi or to charging, except Emergency-severity incidents and SOS |
| Data budget | Duty bundle ≈ 60 KB/day; events ≈ 3 KB each; a typical 26-shift month ≈ 12–18 MB excluding media; media is the variable and is user-visible in App health |
| Battery target | ≤ 6% per 12-hour shift on a 4000 mAh device; measured in QA on the reference low-end device and treated as a release gate |
| Degraded mode | Below 15% battery: location interval doubles, media capture drops to low quality, non-critical sync pauses; guard is told "Power saving on — duty features still work" |

### 18.16 Supervisor (field) additions in the Guard App

A Supervisor (field) uses the same app with an extra "My team" tab, not a different app.

| Capability | Detail |
|---|---|
| Team roster today | List of guards on the supervisor's sites with live state chips (On duty / Late / Absent / Not checked in) |
| Verify attendance | Approve out-of-geofence check-ins, low-face-match events, manual scans — each a 2-tap approve/reject with a reason list |
| Proxy attendance | Mark a guard present when the guard has no working phone; requires supervisor selfie + location; always flagged |
| Site visit check | Supervisor's own geo-stamped visit record at a site, with photo and notes |
| Escalate | Raise an incident on behalf of a guard; call any guard on the roster with one tap |
| Broadcast | Send a short notice to guards on their sites, if permitted |

Everything a supervisor approves is audit-logged with their identity; supervisors cannot edit timestamps or amounts.

### 18.17 UX subsection: field-UX rules and the two-tap check-in

#### 18.17.1 The rules (binding on every screen in §18)

| # | Rule | Concrete requirement |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Large touch targets | Primary actions ≥ 88 dp tall, full width; no target smaller than 48 dp anywhere |
| 2 | One-tap actions | Every duty-critical action reachable in ≤ 2 taps from Duty Home; never more than 3 |
| 3 | Voice everywhere | Every screen with instructions has a "Read aloud"; every text input has voice dictation; the 60 critical prompts have pre-recorded audio |
| 4 | Scan over type | QR/NFC for checkpoints; camera + OCR for documents; the guard never types an ID |
| 5 | Camera over forms | Evidence is a photo, not a description |
| 6 | GPS over addresses | Location is captured, never typed |
| 7 | Simple language | Max 12 words per instruction, no jargon, no double negatives; strings written at a basic reading level and reviewed by a native speaker per language |
| 8 | Minimal typing | Whole app requires typing only: phone number, OTP, name (voice alternative), PIN, optional notes |
| 9 | Colour + icon + text | Never colour alone; every state has an icon and a word |
| 10 | Feedback is physical | Every successful duty action produces a distinct sound + haptic pattern, so it is confirmable without reading |
| 11 | Errors say what to do | "No network — your check-in is saved and will send automatically" not "Error 503" |
| 12 | Nothing blocks duty | Verification failures, missing documents and expired items degrade or warn; they never prevent marking attendance |
| 13 | Works in sunlight and darkness | High-contrast palette (§27), auto-brightness boost on the check-in and wake-check screens, dark-friendly night mode after 19:00 |
| 14 | Works with gloves and wet hands | Large targets, no long-press except SOS, no swipe-only actions |
| 15 | Offline is a normal state, not an error | Offline UI is calm and informative, never red |

#### 18.17.2 Worked example — a guard checks in with two taps

**Situation.** Ramesh, a gate guard at Sunrise Apartments, night shift 20:00–08:00. He arrives at 19:52. His phone is a 2 GB Android 9 device on 2G, showing one bar.

| Step | What Ramesh does | What the app does | Elapsed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Opens the app (from the home screen icon or the shift-reminder notification, which deep-links to Duty Home) | Cold start from cache. Duty Home renders in 2.1 s: green-bordered status band "Duty starts in 00:08", a 96 dp button reading **CHECK IN**, and the shift card "Sunrise Apartments · Main Gate · 20:00–08:00" | 0 s |
| 1 | **Tap 1 — CHECK IN** | Bottom sheet opens instantly. Location row shows an amber spinner "Finding your location" (a fix was already being warmed since the app opened inside the geofence radius) and turns green "At Main Gate" within 2 s. Time row shows a green tick. Face row shows the camera preview already live with an oval guide. A spoken prompt says, in Hindi, "Look at the camera" | 2 s |
| 2 | Holds the phone up; auto-capture fires on the first good frame — **no shutter tap** | Face captured, row turns green. The confirm button, now labelled **CONFIRM CHECK-IN** and coloured green, becomes enabled | 6 s |
| 3 | **Tap 2 — CONFIRM CHECK-IN** | Event written to the local outbox with `client_event_uuid`, both timestamps, location, mock-location verdict, face media reference, battery, network state. A full-screen green tick appears with "Checked in · 19:54 · Sunrise Apartments", a success chime and a double haptic pulse. Because the network is weak, the sheet also reads "Saving… will send automatically" with a small cloud icon | 8 s |
| 4 | (nothing) | The screen auto-dismisses after 3 s to Duty Home, now showing the status band green "On duty since 19:54", the primary button switched to **CHECK OUT** (disabled until 07:30), and the timeline chip Check-in ✓. In the background the outbox flushes on the 2G link within 40 s and the cloud icon disappears | 11 s |

**Total: two taps, zero typing, no scrolling, one held-up phone.** The same flow with an entirely dead network is identical except the cloud icon persists and the confirmation line reads "Saved on your phone — will send when network returns". The same flow when Ramesh is 300 m away from the gate inserts exactly one extra screen: a reason chip row ("Traffic / Wrong gate / Site emergency / Other") plus a mandatory photo, making it four taps — the friction is proportional to the exception.

## 19. TRINETRA — Agency Marketplace

**Property:** trinetra.surakshaguards.in `[CONFIRMED]`. **Audience:** India's private security agencies (~35,000 PSARA-licensed, `A-001`), plus clients and partners searching for an agency, plus prospective Enterprise buyers.

### 19.1 The three roles Trinetra plays

| Role | What it is | Primary success metric | Who consumes it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Agency marketplace** | A public, searchable directory of PSARA-licensed agencies with verification status, service areas, capabilities and enquiry routing | Verified listings live; qualified enquiries delivered per listed agency | Clients/partners searching; agencies seeking visibility |
| **2. B2B SaaS marketing site** | The product site for the Agency Portal (§20): module tour, plan comparison, demo booking, self-serve signup for Starter/Professional | Demo requests; Starter/Professional self-serve activations; Enterprise pipeline created | Agency Owner, Agency Admin, Operations Manager evaluating software |
| **3. Desktop distribution point** | Download hub for the Agency Portal desktop app across Windows, macOS and Linux, with checksums, release notes and auto-update metadata | Downloads → installs → first desktop login | Existing subscribers and trial users |

These roles are deliberately fused: a listing is the top of the funnel, and the software is the monetisation. An agency arrives to be *found*, and is nurtured toward *subscribing*. The site's navigation therefore never forces a visitor to choose between "marketplace" and "product" — both are one tap from the header.

**Relationship to other properties.** Marketplace enquiries become Leads inside the agency's own CRM in §20 if it subscribes. Listing verification is performed by the Suraksha Verification role in §22 OPS. Login always routes to ap.surakshaguards.in. Trinetra itself holds no operational data.

### 19.2 Global UI

**Header (desktop):** `[TRINETRA by Suraksha]  Product ▾  Marketplace ▾  Pricing  Resources ▾  [Download ▾]  [Login]  [Book a Demo ▸]` `[CONFIRMED]`

| Element | Contents |
|---|---|
| Product ▾ | Features overview · Operations · Workforce · Clients & CRM · Finance · Compliance · AI · Desktop app · Mobile app |
| Marketplace ▾ | Browse agencies · Browse by state · List your agency · Claim your listing · How verification works |
| Resources ▾ | Blog · PSARA guides · Product updates · Help centre · Case studies (only when real) |
| Download ▾ | Windows · macOS · Linux · All downloads |
| Login | → ap.surakshaguards.in |
| Book a Demo | Primary accented button, present on every page, sticky on mobile |

**Footer:** four columns — Product (Features, Pricing, Desktop app, Mobile app, Integrations, API, Changelog) · Marketplace (Browse agencies, Browse by state, List your agency, Claim listing, Verification policy) · Company (About, Blog, Careers, Contact, Suraksha main site) · Legal (Privacy, Terms, Subscription refund & cancellation, Marketplace listing terms, Review policy, Security). Bottom bar: "TRINETRA is a Suraksha product · © 2026 Suraksha Guards".

**Global patterns.** One plan-comparison link appears in the footer and at the bottom of every product page. A sticky mobile bar carries "Book a Demo" on marketing pages and "Enquire" on agency-profile pages. Language: English primary, Hindi version of Home/Pricing/Marketplace `[RECOMMENDED]` — the buyer here is an agency owner, more likely bilingual than the guard workforce, but Hindi materially widens reach.

Analytics: `trn_pricing_view`, `trn_plan_select` (plan), `trn_compare_expand`, `trn_pricing_faq_open`, `trn_contact_sales_click`.
