#### 19.3.6 Claim listing — `/agencies/<slug>/claim`

Purpose: let the real owner take control of a listing that Suraksha or a third party created. Hero: "Is this your agency? Claim your listing." Flow: identify yourself → prove ownership → verification → control transferred. Ownership evidence required (any two of): licence document bearing the claimant's name/designation, GST certificate matching the agency name, official domain email (`@agencydomain.com`), a letter on agency letterhead with the signatory's ID, or a callback to the phone number already printed on the listing. Claims are always reviewed by a human (Verification role, §22). While a claim is pending, the listing is frozen against edits. A contested claim (two claimants) escalates to Compliance with both parties notified, and the listing displays no ownership change until resolved. See §19.6 for the anti-fraud treatment of this flow. Analytics: `trn_claim_start`, `trn_claim_evidence_upload`, `trn_claim_approved/rejected`.

### 19.4 Marketplace mechanics in depth

#### 19.4.1 Search and filter behaviour

Search is geography-first because PSARA licensing is geography-bound: a client in Surat needs an agency licensed to operate in Gujarat, and preferably present in Surat district. The query model is therefore `(state, district?, service?, free_text?)` with the state either explicitly selected, inferred from a pincode, or inferred from IP with an editable chip.

| Behaviour | Rule |
|---|---|
| Coverage matching | An agency appears for a district only if it holds a licence whose geography covers that district, or a state licence covering it, and the agency has declared that district as served. Claimed-but-unverified coverage is shown with a "claimed" label and ranked below verified coverage |
| Free-text | Matches agency name, description, specialisations and service synonyms (e.g. "bouncer" → event security), with typo tolerance |
| Facet counts | Every filter shows the number of results it would yield; zero-result facets are disabled, not hidden |
| Filter persistence | Filters persist in the URL so results are shareable and indexable |
| Result density | 20 per page, infinite scroll on mobile with a "load more" fallback |
| Contact protection | Phone/email revealed only after phone-OTP verification of the enquirer, rate-limited per number and per IP |

#### 19.4.2 Agency profile fields (master list)

| Group | Fields |
|---|---|
| Identity | Legal name, trade name, slug, logo, cover image, entity type, incorporation year, description, website, social links |
| Licence (repeatable) | Licence number, issuing state, district scope, issue date, expiry date, licence type (state/district), document, verification status, verified_on, verified_by |
| Coverage | States[], districts[], service radius, offices[] |
| Services | Unarmed guards, armed/PSO, bouncers/event, patrol services, supervisors, control-room services, gunmen (where legally applicable), specialisations[] |
| Capacity | Total guard strength, deployable-now band, armed personnel count, female guard count, supervisor count |
| Compliance signals | GST registered + GSTIN, PF registration, ESIC registration, ISO certificates, training centre affiliation |
| Commercial | Minimum contract size, typical response time to enquiry, accepting new clients (Y/N), languages spoken |
| Reputation | Rating, review count, enquiry response rate, response time median, dispute count (internal), verification badge tier |
| Media | Photos[], brochure PDF, intro video |
| Contact | Contact person, phone, email, office address |
| System | tenant_id (if subscriber), listing status, claimed_by, created_by, last_updated, listing_score |

#### 19.4.3 Verification and licence validation workflow

**Honesty statement (canon §0).** There is no reliable public, programmatic PSARA licence-verification API available pan-India. PSARA is administered state-by-state under the Ministry of Home Affairs, and state controlling authorities publish licence information inconsistently — some as searchable portals, some as PDF lists, some not at all. **Therefore the working design is document-based manual verification with assisted checks**, and any state-level automated lookup is an opportunistic enhancement per state, never an architectural assumption. `[ASSUMPTION: A-163]` — the availability of any given state's online verification is treated as a per-state configuration flag, not as a platform capability.

| Stage | Actor | Action | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Submission | Agency | Uploads licence document(s), enters number, state, district scope, issue/expiry dates | Listing status `Pending` |
| 2. Automated pre-checks | System | OCR extraction of licence number/dates and comparison to entered values; expiry-date sanity; duplicate licence-number check across all listings; duplicate name/phone/GSTIN/address fuzzy match; image-manipulation heuristics (EXIF absence, resave artefacts, copy-move detection) `[RECOMMENDED]`; GSTIN format + public GST-portal name match where available | A verification worksheet with flags |
| 3. Human review | Suraksha Verification role (§22) | Reads the document, compares with the worksheet, checks the state authority's published list where one exists, checks the agency's declared districts against the licence geography | Approve / More info / Reject with reason |
| 4. Contact confirmation | Verification | Callback to the listed office number; confirms the contact person's designation | Contact-verified flag |
| 5. Decision | Verification | Sets badge tier, verified_on, verifier, and next re-verification date | Listing status `Verified` / `Rejected` |
| 6. Ongoing | System | Expiry monitoring at T−90/60/30/7 days; on expiry, badge is removed and the listing shows "Licence expired — renewal in progress" or is suspended per policy (`BR-002` analogue) | Status `Expiring` → `Expired` |
| 7. Re-verification | Verification | Annual re-verification, or on any material profile change (name, licence, ownership) | Refreshed verified_on |

**Badge tiers.**

| Badge | Criteria | Display |
|---|---|---|
| (none) | Listing submitted, not yet reviewed | "Verification pending" grey chip; profile is `noindex`; ranked lowest |
| **Licence Verified** | ≥ 1 licence document reviewed and accepted, dates valid, contact callback completed | Blue check with tooltip and date |
| **Verified + Compliant** | Licence Verified plus GSTIN validated and PF/ESIC presence declared with documents seen | Blue check + "Compliant" tag |
| **Suraksha Trusted** | Verified + Compliant, plus ≥ 6 months on the platform, ≥ 10 delivered enquiries, enquiry response rate ≥ 80%, ≥ 4.0 rating over ≥ 5 genuine reviews, zero upheld fraud reports | Gold badge; eligible for premium placement |
| **Suspended** | Fraud upheld, licence expired beyond grace, or repeated unresponsiveness | Listing hidden from search; profile shows a neutral suspension notice |

Badges never claim legal compliance on behalf of the agency — the tooltip reads "Suraksha reviewed the licence document provided by this agency on <date>" (canon §0: no legal conclusions).

#### 19.4.4 Ratings and reviews

| Aspect | Rule |
|---|---|
| Who can review | Only a reviewer with a verified phone AND at least one of: an enquiry delivered through Trinetra to that agency ≥ 14 days ago, or a contract relationship recorded in the platform. Anonymous open reviews are not permitted |
| Structure | Overall 1–5 stars, plus four sub-ratings: Guard quality · Punctuality/attendance · Responsiveness · Billing transparency; free text ≤ 1000 chars; optional photos not permitted (privacy) |
| Identity | Reviewer's name shown as first name + last initial + city; company name only with consent |
| Publication | Auto-published after automated screening; held for human moderation if flagged |
| Agency response | One public response per review, ≤ 1000 chars, no contact details |
| Moderation triggers | Profanity, personal data (phone numbers, addresses, guard names), allegations of criminality (held for review, never auto-published), competitor language patterns, review from an IP/device cluster matching the agency's own sessions, burst detection |
| Disputes | Agency may dispute a review once; a disputed review is labelled "Under review" and hidden from the aggregate until resolved within a target of 7 working days |
| Removal | Only for policy violation, proven fabrication, or legal order — never for being negative; every removal is logged with a reason and is reportable |
| Aggregate display | Shown only at ≥ 3 published reviews; below that the profile shows "New to Trinetra" |
| Decay | Reviews older than 24 months carry half weight in the displayed aggregate and in ranking `[RECOMMENDED]` |

#### 19.4.5 Request-quotation and lead generation

1. Enquirer submits the quotation form on a profile, a compare view, or the directory's "Get 3 quotes" card.
2. Phone OTP verification occurs before the enquiry is dispatched — this single control removes the majority of spam and fake leads.
3. The system creates a **Lead** with: requirement type, guard count, armed/unarmed, site city/district, start date, duration, budget band (optional), contact details, source page, and the agencies selected.
4. Dispatch modes: **Direct** (enquirer chose one agency) or **Broadcast** (the "Get 3 quotes" card, capped at 3 agencies, chosen by ranking within the requested geography, each told they are one of three).
5. Delivery: in-product Lead in §20 CRM for subscribers; email + SMS + WhatsApp for non-subscribers, with a magic link to a lightweight lead inbox on Trinetra so non-subscribers can respond without a subscription (and see, on every response, what the full CRM would give them).
6. SLA and measurement: `first_response_at` is recorded when the agency opens and responds; response rate and median response time feed ranking (§19.5) and the Suraksha Trusted badge.
7. Outcome capture: after 14 days the enquirer is asked one question — "Did any agency contact you?" — a cheap, high-signal integrity check on both the agency and the marketplace.
8. Monetisation of leads (per-lead pricing, lead credits) is `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-164]`; the working default is that leads are free to verified agencies to build supply, with premium placement monetised instead.

#### 19.4.6 Compare, save, and premium placement

**Compare agencies.** Up to 4 agencies selected from the directory open a comparison table with rows: verification badge, licence states/districts, services, specialisations, guard capacity band, armed capability, years in operation, rating and review count, response time, GST/PF/ESIC presence, languages, accepting-new-clients. Sticky first column; export to PDF for procurement teams; a single "Request quotation from all" action that becomes a capped broadcast lead.

**Save / favourites.** Requires a light account (phone OTP). Saved agencies live in a "My shortlist" area with notes and a share link; procurement users can share a shortlist with colleagues. Notifications on badge changes for saved agencies (e.g. "an agency in your shortlist is now Suraksha Trusted", or "…licence expired").

**Premium and sponsored listings.**

| Placement | Rule |
|---|---|
| Sponsored slots | Maximum 2 per results page, always at the top, always with a visible "Sponsored" label in the same size as the agency name |
| Eligibility | Only **Licence Verified** or above; a suspended or unverified agency can never buy placement |
| Featured on state pages | 1 slot per state landing page, rotated among eligible sponsors |
| Profile enhancements | Premium tier unlocks a video, expanded photo gallery, brochure, and a "Featured" ribbon — presentation only, never a truth claim |
| Separation of concerns | Sponsorship affects placement in labelled slots only; it must not alter the organic ranking score (§19.5). This separation is a product rule, published in the review/listing policy |
| Pricing | Placement pricing model is `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-165]` |

### 19.5 The marketplace ranking algorithm

**Objective.** Rank agencies so that the enquirer is most likely to get a fast, competent, legally-permitted response, and so that agencies cannot buy or fake their way to the top.

**Signal set and weighting rationale.**

| # | Signal | Weight | Why this weight |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Geographic match quality** | 25% | The single most predictive signal of a usable result. Exact district licence + declared district presence scores full; state licence covering the district scores 0.8; adjacent-district office scores 0.4; no licence coverage scores 0 and is excluded entirely, not down-ranked. Legality is a filter before it is a ranking factor |
| 2 | **Verification tier** | 20% | Trust is the marketplace's product. Suraksha Trusted 1.0 · Verified + Compliant 0.85 · Licence Verified 0.7 · Pending 0.15 (only surfaced when there are too few verified results, and always labelled) |
| 3 | **Enquiry responsiveness** | 15% | Measures whether an enquiry will actually be answered — the enquirer's real need. Composite of response rate over the last 90 days (60%) and median first-response time (40%). Cold-start agencies receive the cohort median for 30 days rather than a zero |
| 4 | **Service and capacity fit** | 12% | An enquiry for 40 armed guards should not rank an agency with 12 unarmed guards first. Scored on service overlap, specialisation overlap and whether requested guard count fits within the declared capacity band |
| 5 | **Rating quality** | 10% | Bayesian-adjusted rating (shrunk toward the category mean until ≥ 5 reviews) with a 24-month decay, so a single 5-star review cannot outrank a long record |
| 6 | **Profile completeness** | 8% | A complete profile converts better and signals seriousness. Scored across a fixed 20-field checklist; deliberately capped so completeness alone cannot beat trust or fit |
| 7 | **Operational activity** | 5% | Recent login/profile update, active subscription-independent presence, accepting-new-clients flag. Prevents dormant listings from occupying prime positions |
| 8 | **Tenure and stability** | 3% | Years on the platform and years in operation, log-scaled. A small, honest weight — incumbency should not lock out new entrants |
| 9 | **Dispute and penalty modifier** | ×0.0–1.0 multiplier | Upheld fraud, licence expiry, review manipulation findings, or repeated non-response apply a multiplicative penalty (0.5 for a first upheld finding, 0.25 for a second, 0 = removal). Applied as a multiplier, not a subtraction, so penalties cannot be outweighed by buying completeness points |
| 10 | **Diversity/rotation jitter** | ±3% | A small deterministic jitter seeded per day per query so the same three agencies do not permanently own a district, and so ranking cannot be reverse-engineered by observation alone |

**Explicitly not signals:** whether the agency subscribes to the Agency Portal; how much it pays for sponsorship; how many enquiries it has *received* (which would compound incumbency); click-through rate alone (trivially gamed by bot traffic).

**Mechanics.** Score = Σ(weight × normalised signal) × penalty modifier, computed nightly and on material profile change, cached per (state, district, service) query shape. Weights are configuration held in OPS, versioned, and every weight change is audit-logged with the operator and reason, because ranking changes are commercially material. A "why am I ranked here" panel in §20 Marketplace Integration shows the agency its own component scores — transparency reduces both suspicion and gaming, because the visible levers are all legitimate ones (verify your licence, answer enquiries faster, complete your profile).

### 19.6 Anti-manipulation safeguards

| # | Abuse | Detection | Review process | Consequence & appeal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Fake agency** (no real business) | Onboarding pre-checks: licence-number format and duplicate check, address geocoding and reuse detection, phone reachability, GSTIN name match, website age, disposable-email detection, device/IP fingerprint clustering across signups. Post-launch: zero enquiry responses, no login activity, complaints | Verification role reviews the flagged worksheet; mandatory callback plus a request for a second document (GST certificate, utility bill, or bank letter naming the agency) | Listing not published, or suspended if already live. Appeal by submitting additional documents; reviewed by a second, different reviewer within 7 working days |
| 2 | **Fake or forged licence** | OCR field mismatch vs entered data; licence number reused on another listing; document image forensics (missing EXIF, resave artefacts, font inconsistency, copy-move); expiry dates inconsistent with the state's known validity durations; cross-check against the state authority's published list where one exists (per-state flag, `A-163`) | Two-person review for any forgery flag; where a state authority publishes a public list or accepts written verification requests, Suraksha sends a written confirmation request and records the outcome | Rejection with reason "document could not be verified" (never an accusation of forgery in public copy). Permanent block of the licence number pending resolution; the agency may appeal with an original document presented in a video verification call. Confirmed forgery is escalated internally and the listing is permanently suspended |
| 3 | **Review manipulation** (self-reviews, paid reviews, competitor attacks) | Eligibility gate (only enquiry- or contract-linked reviewers); device/IP/browser-fingerprint clustering between reviewer and agency sessions; burst detection (n reviews in a short window vs the agency's historical rate); text-similarity clustering across reviews; rating distribution anomaly (all-5 or all-1 with no middle); reviewer accounts with a single lifetime action; negative-review bursts arriving from a cluster that also reviewed a competitor positively | Automated hold → human moderation queue with the cluster evidence attached; both the reviewer and the agency may be contacted | Offending reviews removed and excluded from the aggregate; the agency receives a warning, then a ranking penalty multiplier, then suspension for repeat findings. Agencies may appeal a review-related penalty once; reviewers whose reviews are removed are told which policy clause applied |
| 4 | **Duplicate profiles** (one agency, many listings, to occupy more slots) | Fuzzy matching on legal name, trade name, licence number, GSTIN, phone, email domain, address, logo image hash, and description text similarity at submission time and nightly across the corpus | Verification reviews the candidate pair; the agency is asked to confirm which listing is canonical (branches are legitimate and are modelled as branches on one listing, not as separate listings) | Duplicates merged into the canonical listing preserving reviews and enquiry history; deliberate duplication after warning triggers a ranking penalty. Appeal available where the two entities are genuinely separate legal entities with separate licences — proven by documents |
| 5 | **Listing spam** (keyword stuffing, contact details in free text, irrelevant services, fake specialisations to widen matching) | Content checks at save time: contact-detail regex, keyword density, banned-claims list ("government approved", "police approved", any claim of state endorsement), service-claim vs licence-scope consistency, capacity claims wildly inconsistent with declared workforce | Auto-reject the edit with an inline explanation; repeated attempts route to human review | Edit blocked; repeated attempts freeze profile editing for 7 days and flag the listing. Appeal in-product; a human reviewer can whitelist a legitimate term |
| 6 | **Ownership-claim fraud** (a third party claims someone else's listing) | Claim requires two independent evidence types (§19.3.6); evidence documents run through the same forensic checks; the phone number already on the listing is always called; claimant identity is verified by OTP and an ID document; a claim from a device/IP previously associated with a competitor listing is auto-flagged | Human review always; the incumbent contact is notified of every claim and given 7 days to object; contested claims escalate to Compliance with both parties' evidence side by side | Listing control transfers only on a clear decision; while contested, the listing is frozen and shows no ownership statement. A rejected claimant may appeal once with additional evidence. Fraudulent claims result in an account ban and, for a listed agency, a penalty multiplier |
| 7 | **Enquiry/lead abuse** (agencies generating fake enquiries to inflate responsiveness, or scraping contacts) | Enquiry OTP verification; per-number and per-IP rate limits; detection of enquiries whose contact number matches an agency-associated number; contact-reveal rate limits and honeypot listings to detect scrapers | Automated throttling first, human review on repeat | Enquiries voided and excluded from responsiveness metrics; scraper IPs blocked; repeat abuse suspends the account |
| 8 | **Ranking gaming** (rapid profile churn, artificial activity) | Rate-limit profile updates counted toward the activity signal; require material change for the activity signal to refresh; cap completeness contribution; daily jitter | Anomaly report reviewed weekly by the marketplace owner | Signal contribution neutralised; persistent gaming applies the penalty modifier |

**Cross-cutting process rules.** Every enforcement action produces: an audit record (actor, evidence, policy clause, timestamp), a notification to the agency in plain language with the specific clause cited, an appeal route with a stated response target, and a second-reviewer requirement for any permanent suspension. Appeals are never decided by the original reviewer. Public copy never accuses; it states what could not be verified. Suspension and takedown criteria are published in `/legal/marketplace-terms` so enforcement is predictable.

## 20. Agency SaaS (Agency Portal — ap.surakshaguards.in)

**Property:** ap.surakshaguards.in `[CONFIRMED]`. **Delivery:** web app, desktop app (Windows/macOS/Linux, §20.30), mobile app (§21). One account, one subscription, one dataset across all three form factors.

**What it is:** the operating system of a private security agency. An agency subscribes, migrates its guards, clients and sites into it, and thereafter runs deployment, attendance, patrol, payroll, invoicing, compliance and growth from it. Every row in the portal carries `tenant_id` (canon §3); Suraksha's own guarding operation runs as tenant `SURAKSHA-HQ` on the same codebase, which is why the Agency Portal and the OPS panel (§22) share modules but not scope.

**Reading guide.** §20.1 maps every module to its treatment depth and plan. §20.2–20.3 define the shell and the multi-branch/multi-user model that every module inherits. §20.4 is the worked Dashboard specification. §20.5–20.24 are the major modules on the canon's 20-point template. §20.25 covers the minor modules on the condensed 6-point form. §20.26–20.29 cover plan gating, and §20.30 the desktop application. Design tokens and components live in §27; workflows in step form in §29; the permission matrix in §31; entities and fields in §32; endpoints in §33; SOS escalation mechanics in §24; AI guardrails in §25/§41.

**Standard list pattern** used by every list module: saved views (per user and shared), column chooser, multi-select with bulk actions, inline filter chips, server-side pagination, an export button governed by permission and watermarked (§38), and a "Create" primary action. **Standard detail pattern:** header with entity identity + status chip + primary actions; left column of facts; tabbed body; right rail with activity timeline and related records.

**Alerts** are severity-coloured P0–P3 (canon §3), human-readable, and always actionable — an expiring licence alert links directly to the renewal screen (§14 principle).

### 20.3 Multi-branch, multi-user and data scoping

#### 20.3.1 Branch hierarchy

| Level | Object | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Agency (tenant) | Shree Security Services Pvt Ltd | One subscription, one `tenant_id` |
| 1 | Region (optional) | West India | Enterprise only; a grouping layer for consolidated reporting `[RECOMMENDED]` |
| 2 | Branch | Ahmedabad Branch, Surat Branch | Holds its own guards, clients, sites, roster, payroll cost centre and P&L view |
| 3 | Sub-branch / unit (optional) | Ahmedabad — Industrial Cluster | Depth capped at 4 levels to keep scoping queries tractable |

Every branch carries: name, code, address, licence(s) applicable to its geography, branch manager, cost centre, GSTIN (a branch in another state generally needs its own GSTIN — modelled as a field on the branch, never as a hard-coded rule), contact details, operating states/districts, and status.

#### 20.3.2 Data scoping rules

| Rule | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Tenant isolation | Absolute. Every query is tenant-filtered at the data-access layer, not in application code. Cross-tenant access is impossible by construction (§38) |
| Branch scoping | A user is assigned to one or more branches, or to "All branches". Records carry `branch_id`. A user without "All branches" sees only their branches' records everywhere — lists, search, reports, dashboards, exports and the AI assistant |
| Shared objects | Some objects are agency-level by nature: agency licences (though each is geography-scoped), salary structures, roles, workflow rules, notification templates, marketplace listing. These are visible to all branches, editable only by agency-level roles |
| Guard mobility | A guard belongs to a home branch but can be deployed to another branch's site via a **loan assignment**, which grants the receiving branch read access to that guard's duty data for the loan period only, and attributes cost per the configured inter-branch rule |
| Client mobility | A client can have sites in several branches; the client record is agency-level, sites are branch-scoped, and invoices can be consolidated or per-branch (a contract-level setting) |
| Consolidated views | Users with "All branches" get a branch dimension on every dashboard card, report and chart, with a branch filter and a "compare branches" mode |
| Branch transfer | Moving a site or guard between branches is an audited action that preserves history in the originating branch and starts new attribution from the effective date; it never rewrites past attendance or invoices |
| Deletion | Branches are never deleted, only `Archived`; archiving requires zero active sites, guards and open invoices |

#### 20.3.3 Multi-user model

Agency roles are exactly the canon list: Agency Owner · Agency Admin · Branch Manager · Operations Manager · Field Officer · Supervisor · Agency HR · Recruiter · Payroll · Agency Finance · Agency Compliance · Agency Sales · Agency Viewer. The full matrix lives in §31; the portal-specific rules are:

| Rule | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Seats | Users are invited by email or phone; invitation expires in 7 days; seat limits per plan are `D-003` |
| Role assignment | One primary role plus optional additive permission sets; roles are fixed on Starter, customisable on Professional, and SSO-mappable on Enterprise |
| Branch assignment | Independent of role; a Branch Manager for two branches is normal |
| Delegation | Any approval authority can be delegated for a date range with an audit record (holiday cover) |
| Session policy | Agency roles support enforced MFA (canon §4); privileged sessions (Owner, Payroll, Finance) are shorter and re-auth on sensitive actions |
| Impersonation | Suraksha support impersonation of an agency user is possible only with recorded consent, is time-boxed, is visibly banner-flagged inside the session, and writes an audit record on both sides (§38) |
| Offboarding | Deactivating a user reassigns their open approvals and tasks through a mandatory reassignment step |

### 20.4 Module: Dashboard — the worked example

**1 Purpose.** The agency's morning screen: in one viewport, tell the user whether today's deployment is intact, whether anything is on fire, and what will hurt them this week if untouched. Role-aware and branch-scoped.

**2 Users.** Every agency role, with a different default card set per role. **3 Permissions.** Cards render only if the user has read permission on the underlying module; a Payroll user sees no incident cards, an Operations Manager sees no revenue cards unless granted.

**4 Screens.** AGN-S-001 Dashboard · AGN-S-002 Card drill-down (each card has a named destination) · AGN-S-003 Dashboard customisation.

**5 UI detail — every card, named, in three sections.**

**Section 1 — Right now (8 KPI tiles, single row on desktop, 2×4 on tablet, vertical on mobile):**

| # | Card | Value shown | Secondary line | Colour rule | Click destination |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Active guards** | Count of guards currently checked in | "of 312 rostered" + delta vs yesterday | Green ≥ 95% of rostered, amber 85–95%, red < 85% | → Command center, filtered `status = on duty`, branch-scoped |
| 2 | **Guards absent** | Count absent for shifts that have started | "4 unreplaced" | Red if any unreplaced | → Attendance, filter `flag = absent, date = today` |
| 3 | **Open posts** | Posts with fewer guards assigned than required, for today and tomorrow | "3 today · 5 tomorrow" | Red if any today | → Deployment, view "Unfilled posts" |
| 4 | **Active sites** | Sites with at least one active post today | "48 of 51 sites" | Neutral | → Sites, filter `has_active_post = true` |
| 5 | **Attendance %** | Present ÷ rostered for today so far | Sparkline of last 7 days | Against the agency's configured target | → Attendance analytics, today |
| 6 | **SOS alerts** | Count of SOS in the last 24 h, unresolved shown first | "1 active · 2 resolved" | Red if any active; the tile pulses while an SOS is unacknowledged | → Command center SOS queue (§24 owns handling) |
| 7 | **Unresolved incidents** | Incidents in Pending or In Progress | "2 P0 · 5 P2" | Red if any P0 older than its SLA | → Incidents, filter `status != Completed`, sorted by severity then age |
| 8 | **Today's replacements** | Replacement requests raised today | "6 filled · 2 open" | Amber if any open with a shift starting within 2 h | → Replacement queue |

**Section 2 — Operational picture (4 panels, 2×2 on desktop):**

| # | Panel | Contents | Interactions | Click destination |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 9 | **Deployment map** | Map of all sites in scope; pin colour = site state (green fully manned, amber partially, red unmanned/breach); clustered by district at low zoom; on-duty guard dots when zoomed in | Hover shows a site tooltip (name, posts, guards on duty, last check-in). Click a pin opens the site quick-view drawer | "Open full map" → Command center |
| 10 | **Attendance trend** | Line chart, attendance % by day for the last 30 days, with a target line and a branch-comparison toggle | Hover for the day's number; click a point | → Attendance for that date |
| 11 | **Incident trend** | Stacked bars by week for 8 weeks, split by severity P0–P3, with a top-3 incident-type list beside it | Click a bar segment | → Incidents filtered to that week + severity |
| 12 | **Site status** | Sortable table of sites: Site · Required · Deployed · Attendance % today · Last patrol round · Open incidents · state chip. Defaults to worst-first | Row click | → Site detail |

**Section 3 — This week will hurt you (4 alert cards):**

| # | Card | Contents | Click destination |
|---|---|---|---|
| 13 | **Payroll alerts** | Days to the next payroll cut-off; count of unapproved attendance exceptions blocking the run; count of guards with missing bank details; count of pending advances | → Payroll run pre-check screen, with the failing item pre-filtered |
| 14 | **Licence expiry** | Agency PSARA licences expiring in 90 days (per state), plus counts of guard documents expiring in 30 days and police verifications pending | → Compliance → Licences, or → Documents filtered by expiry window |
| 15 | **Pending invoices** | Total receivables in ₹, split into current / 30 / 60 / 90+ days, plus "invoices not yet raised for last month's attendance" | → Receivables ageing view, or → Invoices → "Ready to raise" |
| 16 | **Tender deadlines** | Tracked tenders with submission deadlines in the next 14 days, each with days remaining and document-checklist completeness | → Tender detail (Professional+; on Starter this card is replaced by an upgrade card) |

**Persistent elements.** A top alert bar shows any P0 condition (active SOS, unmanned site, agency licence expired) above everything else, coloured red, with a one-click action. A "Quick actions" row offers: Add guard · Create roster · Mark attendance · Raise invoice · Add client · New incident.

**6 UX flow.** Load → scan section 1 → act on anything red → glance at section 2 → schedule work from section 3. Target: the user's first meaningful action within 15 seconds of load.

**7 Fields.** All cards are computed projections; none are user-entered. Every card exposes `as_of` and `scope` (branch, date range).

**8 Validation.** N/A. **9 Business logic.** Card values are computed against the user's branch scope and the agency's configured targets (attendance target, SLA hours, ageing buckets, payroll cut-off). "Today" is defined by the agency's operational day boundary (default 06:00–06:00) so night shifts do not split across dashboard days — a detail that materially changes every number on this screen.

**10 Backend logic.** Dashboard is served by a read-optimised projection refreshed on event (attendance, incident, SOS) and on a 60-second timer for aggregates; the map and the SOS/absent tiles subscribe to the real-time channel (§34) so they update without reload. Heavy aggregates (trends, ageing) are materialised nightly and incrementally updated. Performance budget: first meaningful paint < 1.5 s, full render < 2.5 s on a 4G connection with 500 sites (§14 "fast dashboards" principle, enforced as a gate).

**11 Status lifecycle.** N/A. **12 Notifications.** The dashboard is the notification sink, not a source; the bell aggregates §36 deliveries.

**13 Integrations.** Map provider; real-time bus; report engine for drill-downs. **14 Security.** Every card is permission- and branch-filtered server-side; no client-side hiding of data.

**15 Audit.** Dashboard views are not audited individually; exports and drill-down exports are.

**16 Edge cases.** New agency with no data → an onboarding checklist replaces the cards ("Add your first site", "Add guards", "Create a roster") with progress. Single-site agency → the map collapses to a site card. Branch with no sites → empty states name the missing setup step. A user whose role sees only two cards gets a compacted layout, not a sparse grid.

**17 QA.** `TC-AGN-001`–`TC-AGN-015`: card values reconcile exactly with their drill-down list counts; branch scoping verified by cross-branch user comparison; operational-day boundary verified against a night shift crossing midnight; real-time SOS tile update within 3 s.

**18 Acceptance criteria.**
- Given a Branch Manager scoped to Ahmedabad, When they open the dashboard, Then every card counts only Ahmedabad records, and the drill-down list from each card returns exactly the same record count as the card displayed.
- Given an SOS is raised at 09:14, When the dashboard is open, Then the SOS tile turns red and begins pulsing within 3 seconds without a page reload.
- Given the agency's payroll cut-off is in 2 days and 14 attendance exceptions are unapproved, When the Payroll user opens the dashboard, Then the Payroll alerts card shows "14 exceptions blocking payroll" and clicking it opens the exception queue pre-filtered.

**19 Analytics & KPIs.** `agn_dashboard_view` (role, branch), `agn_card_click` (card_id), `agn_dashboard_render_ms`, `agn_quick_action_used`. KPIs: median render < 1.5 s; ≥ 60% of sessions include a card click (a dashboard nobody clicks is decoration).

**20 Future scalability.** User-customisable card layout with saved presets per role; agency-defined custom KPI cards from saved report definitions; a TV/wall-display mode for the agency's own control room `[FUTURE]`.

### 20.5 Module: Command Center (Live Operations)

| # | Point | Specification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Purpose | The agency's real-time operating picture: who is on duty where, right now, what is breaching, and the queue of live events requiring a human. The tenant-scoped mirror of Suraksha's own command center (§24) |
| 2 | Users | Operations Manager, Field Officer, Branch Manager, Agency Owner, Agency Admin |
| 3 | Permissions | Read for all operational roles; act (acknowledge, assign, resolve) requires `ops.act`; SOS resolution requires `ops.sos.resolve`. See §31 |
| 4 | Screens | AGN-S-010 Live map · AGN-S-011 Alert queue · AGN-S-012 Site live view · AGN-S-013 Guard live view · AGN-S-014 Shift handover · AGN-S-015 Wall mode |
| 5 | UI detail | Three-pane layout: left alert queue (severity-sorted, colour-banded, each row showing type, site, guard, age timer, assigned operator), centre map (site pins, guard dots, geofence circles, patrol route overlays, cluster counts), right context panel (selected site or guard with live facts and actions). Top strip: counters — On duty · Not checked in · Late · Absent · Geofence breaches · Missed wake checks · Open SOS · Open incidents. Wall mode is a full-screen, chrome-free variant for a control-room monitor with auto-rotating views |
| 6 | UX flow | Alert arrives → operator acknowledges (stops the age timer) → opens the context panel → acts (call guard, assign replacement, raise incident, dispatch field officer) → resolves with a reason code. Every alert must reach a terminal state; nothing silently disappears |
| 7 | Fields | Alert: `alert_id`, `type`, `severity`, `site_id`, `guard_id`, `raised_at`, `acknowledged_at/by`, `resolved_at/by`, `resolution_code`, `notes[]`. Live guard: last location, last event, battery, network state, device integrity flags |
| 8 | Validation | Resolution requires a code; P0 resolution requires a note |
| 9 | Business logic | Alert types: not-checked-in, late, absent, geofence exit during shift, geofence entry failure, missed patrol round, missed wake check, SOS, incident P0/P1, device offline > 30 min during shift, low battery < 10% during shift, mock-location detected, unmanned post. Each has a configurable threshold and an escalation ladder. Escalation *mechanics and timers* are owned by §24; this module consumes the same engine tenant-scoped |
| 10 | Backend logic | Subscribes to the real-time bus (§34); alerts are generated by the rules engine server-side, never by the client. Location retention for the live view is short (see §39); the map reads from a hot store, history from the event store |
| 11 | Status lifecycle | Alert: `Pending` → `Active` (acknowledged) → `In Progress` → `Completed` / `Cancelled` (false positive, with reason) |
| 12 | Notifications | Push/desktop-native/SMS by severity and role (§36); unacknowledged P0 escalates to the Branch Manager then the Agency Owner |
| 13 | Integrations | Map provider, telephony (click-to-call the guard/supervisor/client), SMS/WhatsApp, §24 escalation engine |
| 14 | Security | Live guard location is sensitive; visible only to operational roles within branch scope, never exported without permission, and never shown for off-duty guards |
| 15 | Audit | Every acknowledgement, action, call placed, and resolution with actor and timestamps |
| 16 | Edge cases | 500 sites on one map → clustering plus a "worst 20 sites" list mode. Guard's phone offline → alert says "device offline", not "guard absent". Duplicate alerts for the same condition → coalesced into one alert with an occurrence count. Operator shift change → handover screen forces explicit transfer of open alerts with a note |
| 17 | QA | `TC-AGN-020`–`TC-AGN-035`: alert generation at threshold boundaries, coalescing, escalation on non-acknowledgement, wall-mode 12-hour soak, 1,000 concurrent guard dots |
| 18 | Acceptance | Given a guard exits the geofence at 02:14 during a shift, When 3 minutes elapse without return, Then a P2 alert appears in the queue with the guard, site and last location, and the Operations Manager receives a push within 30 s. Given an alert is unacknowledged for 10 minutes, When the ladder fires, Then the Branch Manager is notified and the alert row shows the escalation stamp |
| 19 | Analytics | `agn_alert_raised/acknowledged/resolved` by type, acknowledgement latency, resolution latency, false-positive rate. KPIs: P0 acknowledgement < 60 s; alert false-positive rate < 15% |
| 20 | Future | Predictive absence alerts from historical no-show patterns (Recommendation class only, §41); video/CCTV panel integration `[FUTURE]` |

### 20.6 Module: Guards

| # | Point | Specification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Purpose | The workforce registry — the single source of truth for every guard the agency employs or engages, their capability, compliance state, deployment history and cost |
| 2 | Users | Agency HR (owner of the record), Operations Manager (deployment view), Recruiter (intake), Payroll (pay data), Agency Compliance (documents), Branch Manager, Agency Viewer |
| 3 | Permissions | Create/edit: Agency HR, Agency Admin. Blacklist/terminate: Agency Owner or Agency Admin only, with reason. Salary fields: Payroll only. Documents: Compliance + HR. Read: all operational roles within branch scope |
| 4 | Screens | AGN-S-020 Guard list · AGN-S-021 Guard detail (tabs: Profile · Documents · Deployment · Attendance · Payroll · Training · Assets · Incidents · Timeline) · AGN-S-022 Add/edit guard · AGN-S-023 Bulk import · AGN-S-024 Blacklist/termination · AGN-S-025 Transfer between branches/agencies · AGN-S-026 Guard availability board |
| 5 | UI detail | List columns (configurable): photo, name, guard code, branch, current site/post, status chip, compliance chip (green all-valid / amber expiring / red expired-or-missing), skills icons (armed, PSO, bouncer, driver, ex-serviceman, female), phone with click-to-call, last check-in. Filters: status, branch, site, skill, document state, availability, gender, age band, joining-date range, blacklisted. Bulk actions: assign to site, send notice, request documents, export (permissioned), mark inactive |
| 6 | UX flow | Add guard: minimal-first — name, phone, branch, skill, joining date — creates an Active record immediately and sends the app invite; everything else (documents, bank, salary) can be completed later, because forcing a 40-field form before a guard can be deployed is why agencies stay on paper |
| 7 | Fields | Identity (name, photo, DOB, gender, blood group, marital status), contact (phone, alternate phone, email, permanent + current address), employment (guard code, branch, designation, employment type, joining date, reporting supervisor, status), capability (skills[], armed licence ref, height/weight where the client contract requires it, languages, ex-serviceman flag), compliance (Aadhaar/ID ref, PAN, police verification ref, PSARA training cert, medical fitness), payroll (salary structure ref, bank/UPI, PF/UAN, ESIC/IP number, statutory applicability flags), operational (current assignment, availability, preferred sites, blacklisted-by-client flags), system (tenant_id, branch_id, created_by, source: manual/import/OCR/marketplace) |
| 8 | Validation | Phone unique per tenant; guard code unique and auto-generated with a configurable prefix; DOB age band per agency policy; IFSC format; UAN 12 digits; duplicate detection on (name + DOB) and (phone) and (ID number) with a merge suggestion |
| 9 | Business logic | Status drives deployability: only `Active` guards with no blocking compliance state can be rostered; blocking rules are agency-configurable (e.g. "no deployment without police verification" is a policy toggle, not hard-coded, per canon §0). Blacklisting requires a reason and optionally propagates as a warning if the guard is later added by another tenant — **never as a cross-tenant data leak**: the receiving agency sees only "this phone number has an adverse record on the platform" `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-166]`, which is a policy and privacy question, not a technical one. Guard transfer between agencies uses the request/accept flow of §18.1 |
| 10 | Backend logic | The Guard entity (§32) is tenant-scoped; the person identity (phone) is platform-level to support transfers and the Guard App. Deployment history is derived from Assignments, never stored redundantly |
| 11 | Status lifecycle | `Draft` (import staged) → `Pending` (added, not yet activated/documents pending) → `Active` → `Suspended` (temporary) → `Archived` (separated) ; plus flags: Blacklisted, On leave, Available, Deployed |
| 12 | Notifications | App invite SMS on creation; document-request push; deployment change; termination acknowledgement; supervisor notified on new joiner assignment |
| 13 | Integrations | Guard App (§18), payroll engine, document store, biometric enrolment (Enterprise), marketplace-sourced applicants |
| 14 | Security | Personal data with field-level permissions; salary and bank fields masked except to Payroll; document downloads watermarked and logged; bulk export requires elevated permission and produces an audit record naming every row exported |
| 15 | Audit | Creation, every field change with before/after for regulated fields, status changes, blacklisting, document actions, salary-structure assignment, exports |
| 16 | Edge cases | Same person employed by two agencies (legitimate for part-time) → one identity, two tenant records, no data sharing. Guard rejoins after separation → reactivate the archived record rather than creating a duplicate, preserving history. Guard dies or is hospitalised → a dedicated status and a workflow that stops payroll accrual, notifies HR and preserves dues for settlement. Guard has no bank account → cash/UPI disbursement flag with its own audit treatment |
| 17 | QA | `TC-AGN-040`–`TC-AGN-060`: duplicate detection, bulk import of 5,000 rows, permission masking of salary fields, blacklist propagation policy, rejoin flow |
| 18 | Acceptance | Given HR creates a guard with only name, phone, branch and skill, When they save, Then the guard is Active, an app invite SMS is sent, and the guard appears in the availability board as deployable-with-warnings. Given a guard's police verification is missing and the agency has enabled the blocking policy, When an Operations Manager tries to roster them, Then the assignment is blocked with the specific reason and a one-click path to request the document |
| 19 | Analytics | `agn_guard_created` (source), `agn_guard_activated`, time-to-first-deployment, document-completion rate, attrition rate by branch/site, `agn_guard_blacklisted`. KPIs: document completeness ≥ 90%; median add-to-deployable < 48 h |
| 20 | Future | Skill-matching engine for auto-suggesting guards for posts; workforce-supply forecasting; biometric-first onboarding at scale `[FUTURE]` |

| # | Point | Specification |

| 5 | UI detail | Requisition list shows post-driven demand (open posts by site with start dates) so hiring is tied to real deployment need. Pipeline is a kanban with columns Applied → Screened → Interview → Selected → Documents → Onboarded → Deployed, plus Rejected and On hold; cards show name, phone, source, skill, distance from the target site, and days-in-stage with an ageing colour |
| 6 | UX flow | Applicant enters (walk-in entered by a recruiter in 20 seconds: name, phone, skill; or public form; or referral) → screen call → interview slot → select → document collection (reusing the Documents module) → convert to Guard (one click, carrying all data) → assign to a post |
| 7 | Fields | Applicant: name, phone, source (walk-in/referral/agent/online/marketplace/job board), referrer, skills, ex-serviceman, height/weight, education, experience, expected wage, preferred locations, availability date, stage, rejection reason, interviewer, notes[], documents[] |
| 8 | Validation | Phone unique within open pipeline; duplicate applicant detection against existing guards (including archived) to catch rehires and previously blacklisted individuals |
| 9 | Business logic | Requisition demand auto-generated from unfilled posts and from contracts starting in the next 30 days. Rejection reasons are a fixed list for analytics. Referral bonus tracking feeds payroll as an allowance |
| 10 | Backend logic | Conversion creates a Guard record with `source = recruitment` and links the applicant record permanently for audit |
| 11 | Status lifecycle | Applicant: `Draft` → `Pending` (applied) → `In Progress` (screening/interview) → `Verified` (selected) → `Completed` (converted) / `Rejected` / `Archived` |
| 12 | Notifications | Interview reminders by SMS/WhatsApp to the applicant; recruiter reminders on stage ageing; HR notified on selection |
| 13 | Integrations | Public application page hosted on the agency's Trinetra profile or website module; WhatsApp for applicant comms |
| 14 | Security | Applicant data is personal data with a defined retention period for rejected applicants (§39) |
| 15 | Audit | Stage changes, offer approvals, conversions, rejections with reason |
| 16 | Edge cases | Applicant applies to two branches → single record, both requisitions linked. Applicant is a previously blacklisted ex-employee → hard warning at entry with the reason visible only to authorised roles. Bulk walk-in day (50 applicants) → a rapid-entry mode capturing name + phone + photo only |
| 17 | QA | `TC-AGN-070`–`TC-AGN-080` |
| 18 | Acceptance | Given a selected applicant with all mandatory documents uploaded, When the recruiter clicks Convert, Then a Guard record is created carrying every field and document with no re-entry, and the applicant card moves to Onboarded |
| 19 | Analytics | Time-to-fill per requisition, stage conversion rates, source effectiveness, cost per hire, 30/90-day retention by source. KPI: median applied→deployed ≤ 7 days |
| 20 | Future | Automated screening calls, applicant self-service document upload by WhatsApp link `[FUTURE]` |

| 16 | Edge cases | Group client with many legal entities → parent/child client structure with consolidated statements. Client also a marketplace enquirer → linked, not duplicated. Client demands data deletion at contract end → archival with retention per §39, since operational and financial records cannot be hard-deleted (canon §4) |

Quotation versions are immutable once sent; revisions create v2. Win converts atomically to Client → Site(s) → Post(s) → Contract |
| 10 | Backend logic | Marketplace enquiries arrive via the Trinetra lead API with `source = trinetra`; response time is written back to Trinetra to feed the responsiveness ranking signal (§19.5) |
| 11 | Status lifecycle | Lead: `Pending` → `In Progress` → `Completed` (won) / `Rejected` (lost) / `Archived`. Quotation: `Draft` → `Pending` (sent) → `Verified` (accepted) / `Rejected` / `Expired` |
| 12 | Notifications | New lead assignment (push + SMS, because speed of first response decides these deals), activity due, quotation viewed by the client, quotation expiring |
| 13 | Integrations | Trinetra marketplace, WhatsApp/email dispatch, e-signature for quotation acceptance `[FUTURE]` |
| 14 | Security | Rate-card margins visible only to Sales and Owner roles |
| 15 | Audit | Stage changes, reassignments, quotation versions, discounts beyond a threshold with approver |
| 16 | Edge cases | Lead for a geography the agency is not licensed for → warning shown with the licence gap named. Lead already a client → routed as an upsell opportunity on the existing client. Duplicate leads from two sources → merge with source attribution preserved for channel analytics |
| 17 | QA | `TC-AGN-110`–`TC-AGN-120` |
| 18 | Acceptance | Given a Trinetra enquiry arrives at 10:00 and the Sales user responds at 10:12, When the response is logged, Then `first_response_at` is written back to Trinetra and the pipeline shows a 12-minute first-response time |

### 20.10 Module: Sites and Posts

| # | Point | Specification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Purpose | Model the physical reality being guarded, precisely enough that rostering, geofencing, patrolling and billing all derive from it automatically |
| 2 | Users | Operations Manager (owner), Field Officer, Branch Manager, Agency Admin |
| 3 | Permissions | Create/edit sites and posts: Operations Manager, Agency Admin. Geofence edits are permission-gated and audited because they directly affect attendance validity |
| 4 | Screens | AGN-S-060 Site list · AGN-S-061 Site detail (tabs: Overview · Posts · Geofence · Checkpoints · Roster · Attendance · Incidents · Assets · Contacts · Instructions · Documents) · AGN-S-062 Add/edit site · AGN-S-063 Geofence editor (map) · AGN-S-064 Post editor · AGN-S-065 Checkpoint manager · AGN-S-066 Post orders editor |
| 5 | UI detail | Site list: name, client, branch, city/district, posts count, required strength, deployed now, attendance % (7-day), open incidents, last patrol, status. Geofence editor is a map with a draggable circle (centre + radius) or drawn polygon, showing the accuracy implications ("radius 80 m — guards within this area can check in") and a preview of recent check-in points overlaid so the manager can see whether the fence is wrong |
| 6 | UX flow | Add site → drop the pin (or search the address) → set the geofence → add posts (name, shift pattern, guards required, skills required, rate reference) → add checkpoints (print QR sheets / register NFC tags) → write post orders → done. A completeness meter shows what is missing before the site can be rostered |
| 7 | Fields | Site: name, code, client, branch, address, geo point, geofence (type, radius/polygon), site type (residential/commercial/industrial/event/ATM/warehouse), operating hours, contacts[], escalation matrix, equipment at site, access instructions, parking/entry notes, photos, documents, status. Post: name, site, shift pattern ref, guards required per shift, skill requirements, gender requirement (where lawful and contractually specified), armed requirement, rate reference, post orders, wake-check enabled, patrol route ref, reporting supervisor, effective from/to |
| 8 | Validation | Geofence radius between 30 m and 1000 m (larger requires a reason and approval, because a 5 km fence defeats the control); posts require at least one guard; a post cannot require a skill no active guard holds without a warning; effective dates cannot overlap contradictorily for the same post |
| 9 | Business logic | **Posts are the unit of demand** (canon §3): Sites contain Posts; Posts generate Shifts; Shifts get Assignments; Assignments produce Attendance. Changing a post's required strength immediately changes open-post counts, roster gaps and billing basis. Post orders are versioned and drive guard re-acknowledgement (§18.4) |
| 10 | Backend logic | Geofence evaluation is server-side for every attendance event (§18.5); site geo data is cached to the Guard App duty bundle |
| 11 | Status lifecycle | Site: `Draft` → `Active` → `Suspended` (service paused) → `Archived`. Post: `Draft` → `Active` → `Suspended` → `Archived` |
| 12 | Notifications | Site added to a guard's roster; post orders updated; site suspended; unmanned post alert |
| 13 | Integrations | Map/geocoding provider, QR print service, NFC tag registration, client portal site view |
| 14 | Security | Site access instructions and client contact details are sensitive; visible to deployed guards only for their own site and only during their assignment window |
| 15 | Audit | Geofence changes (before/after with map coordinates), post strength changes, post-order versions, site suspension |
| 16 | Edge cases | Multi-building campus → one site with multiple posts and a polygon fence, or several sites under one client, decided by billing structure. Mobile/patrol-only "site" with no fixed post → a route-based site type with route geofences. Temporary event site with a 3-day life → site with effective dates and auto-archival. Sites with no GPS reception (basements) → per-site relaxed verification profile with mandatory selfie, configured explicitly and visible in audit |
| 17 | QA | `TC-AGN-130`–`TC-AGN-145`: geofence boundary behaviour, post-strength change propagation to rosters, checkpoint reassignment |
| 18 | Acceptance | Given a post requiring 2 guards on the night shift, When only 1 guard is assigned for tomorrow, Then the post appears in Open posts on the dashboard and in the Deployment gap list with the shortfall named |
| 19 | Analytics | Sites by type, average posts per site, geofence-breach rate per site, sites with chronic shortfall. KPI: sites with a complete setup (fence + posts + checkpoints + orders) ≥ 95% |
| 20 | Future | Indoor positioning for large campuses; automatic geofence suggestion from historical check-in clustering `[FUTURE]` |

### 20.12 Module: Shifts, Rosters and Deployment

| # | Point | Specification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Purpose | Put the right guard at the right post at the right time, publish it so everyone knows, and keep it accurate as reality intervenes |
| 2 | Users | Operations Manager (owner), Field Officer, Supervisor (view + request), Branch Manager |
| 3 | Permissions | Create/publish roster: Operations Manager. Ad-hoc changes within 24 h: Field Officer with `roster.adjust`. Overtime beyond a threshold requires Branch Manager approval |
| 4 | Screens | AGN-S-080 Roster grid (site × date) · AGN-S-081 Roster grid (guard × date) · AGN-S-082 Shift template manager · AGN-S-083 Deployment board (today) · AGN-S-084 Gap list · AGN-S-085 Bulk roster generation · AGN-S-086 Roster publish & notify · AGN-S-087 Shift swap requests |
| 5 | UI detail | The roster grid is the workhorse screen: rows are posts (grouped by site) or guards, columns are dates, cells show the assigned guard's short name with a shift-colour block. Drag a guard onto a cell to assign; drag between cells to move; right-click for copy-week, clear, mark leave. A left rail lists available guards filtered by skill, distance and availability, showing each guard's hours this week to prevent over-scheduling. Conflicts render immediately: red hatching for double-booking (`BR-001`), amber for insufficient rest gap, grey for on-leave |
| 6 | UX flow | Choose a period → generate from the previous period or from templates → resolve conflicts and gaps → publish → guards receive notifications and their app rosters update. Typical monthly roster for 300 guards should take under 30 minutes, not two days |
| 7 | Fields | Shift template: name, start, end, duration, break, night flag, wake-check flag, overtime rules. Assignment: guard, post, shift, date, status, assigned_by, source (roster/replacement/overtime/loan), rate override, notes |
| 8 | Validation | `BR-001` — no overlapping active assignments without an authorised exception. Minimum rest gap between shifts (default 8 h, configurable). Maximum consecutive working days (configurable, warning not block, since agency policy varies). Skill and armed requirements must match the post. Guard must be Active and compliance-clear per the agency's blocking policy |
| 9 | Business logic | Generation engine: for each post and date in range, create the required shifts, then fill them by rule — continuity first (same guard as last period, which guards prefer and clients expect), then availability, then skill match, then distance, then fairness (hours balance). The engine proposes; the manager approves. Publishing freezes the roster and creates the Assignment records that the Guard App consumes; changes after publishing generate change notifications and are tracked as amendments |
| 10 | Backend logic | Roster generation runs as a background job with progress reporting for large agencies; assignment writes are transactional per post-date to avoid partial rosters |
| 11 | Status lifecycle | Roster: `Draft` → `Pending` (generated, unpublished) → `Active` (published) → `Completed` (period ended) → `Archived`. Assignment: `Pending` → `Active` → `Completed` / `Cancelled` / `Replaced` |
| 12 | Notifications | Roster published (push + SMS digest per guard); shift changed; shift starting reminder; unfilled post alert to the manager at T−24 h and T−4 h |
| 13 | Integrations | Guard App duty bundle, attendance, payroll (hours basis), replacement engine, client portal (client sees deployed strength, not guard personal data beyond what the contract allows) |
| 14 | Security | Roster changes are permission-gated; rate overrides are visible only to authorised roles |
| 15 | Audit | Publish events, every post-publish change with before/after, overtime approvals, exception authorisations for `BR-001` |
| 16 | Edge cases | Festival/strike mass absence → a bulk reassignment mode and a "crisis roster" that prioritises client-critical posts by contract SLA tier. Guard loaned from another branch → shown with a branch tag and costed per the inter-branch rule. 24×7 post with 3 shifts and a weekly-off pattern → template-driven rotation. Roster published then the contract is cancelled → guided demobilisation with guard reassignment suggestions |
| 17 | QA | `TC-AGN-170`–`TC-AGN-190`: double-booking prevention, rest-gap enforcement, 10,000-assignment generation performance, publish notification fan-out |
| 18 | Acceptance | Given a published roster and a guard assigned to two posts at overlapping times, When the manager attempts to save, Then the save is blocked with both conflicting assignments named, and proceeding requires an explicit authorised exception that is audit-logged |
| 19 | Analytics | Roster generation time, fill rate at publish, post-publish change rate, overtime hours, guard hour distribution/fairness. KPIs: fill rate at publish ≥ 98%; post-publish change rate < 10% |
| 20 | Future | Optimisation solver for cost/fairness/travel; guard preference bidding for open shifts `[FUTURE]` |

### 20.13 Module: Attendance (including GPS Attendance)

| # | Point | Specification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Purpose | Turn field events into an auditable attendance record that both payroll and client billing can be defended on. This module is where the agency's money is made or lost |
| 2 | Users | Operations Manager, Field Officer, Supervisor, Payroll, Agency Finance (read), Branch Manager, client (read-only via portal per contract) |
| 3 | Permissions | View: operational roles in scope. Approve exceptions: Supervisor/Field Officer. Manual entry and corrections: Operations Manager with `attendance.correct`; every correction requires a reason code. Lock a period: Payroll only |
| 4 | Screens | AGN-S-090 Attendance daily board (site × post × shift) · AGN-S-091 Attendance calendar (guard × month) · AGN-S-092 Exception queue · AGN-S-093 Attendance detail (single event with evidence) · AGN-S-094 Manual/bulk entry · AGN-S-095 Timesheet & period lock · AGN-S-096 Attendance reports · AGN-S-097 Biometric reconciliation (Enterprise) |
| 5 | UI detail | Daily board: rows = posts, columns = shifts, each cell showing the assigned guard, a state chip (Present / Late / Absent / Replaced / Not checked in / On leave), check-in and check-out times, and an evidence icon set (📍 location, 📷 selfie, ⚠ flag). Clicking a cell opens the attendance detail with a map showing the check-in pin relative to the geofence, the selfie with its match score, both timestamps, the device and integrity flags, and the full event trail. The exception queue is the operational heart: a single list of everything needing a human — out-of-geofence check-ins, low face-match, mock-location flags, missed check-outs, manual entries, time-confidence-low offline events — each with Approve / Reject / Correct in two clicks |
| 6 | UX flow | Morning: open the daily board, scan red cells, act. Through the day: work the exception queue to zero. Period end: run the timesheet, resolve remaining exceptions, lock, hand to payroll |
| 7 | Fields | Consumes the full Guard App event field set (§18.5) plus: `approval_status`, `approved_by`, `reason_code`, `corrected_from`, `payable_hours`, `ot_hours`, `late_by_min`, `early_out_min`, `billable_flag`, `period_lock_id` |
| 8 | Validation | Check-out cannot precede check-in; payable hours cannot exceed shift duration plus approved overtime; a correction must carry a reason code; a locked period rejects all writes except an authorised reopen |
| 9 | Business logic | **Two derived quantities, deliberately separate:** `payable_hours` (what the guard is paid, per attendance and agency policy) and `billable_units` (what the client is charged, per contract basis). They differ legitimately — a replacement guard is billable to the client and payable to a different guard; an unfilled post is neither. Conflating them is the classic error and is prevented at the data model level (§32). Late/absent thresholds, grace, overtime rules and rounding are agency configuration. Auto-approval: events with `event_trust_score ≥ 80`, inside geofence, face-matched, within the shift window are auto-approved; everything else queues |
| 10 | Backend logic | Attendance ingest is the high-write path (§34); the portal reads a projection. Recomputation of derived quantities happens on any correction and is idempotent. Period lock writes an immutable snapshot used by payroll and invoicing so later corrections cannot silently alter a paid period — corrections after lock produce an adjustment in the next period (`BR-003` spirit) |
| 11 | Status lifecycle | Attendance record: `Pending` → `Verified` (approved) / `Rejected` → `Archived`. Period: `Draft` → `In Progress` → `Completed` (locked) → reopened only by Owner with reason |
| 12 | Notifications | Guard late/absent (to supervisor), exception queue depth threshold, period-lock reminder before payroll cut-off, client notification of shortfall where the contract requires it |
| 13 | Integrations | Guard App (§18), biometric devices (Enterprise, §20.25), payroll, invoicing, client portal |
| 14 | Security | Selfies and location are personal data; the detail view is permission-gated, exports are watermarked and logged, and client-visible attendance excludes selfies and precise coordinates unless the contract specifies otherwise `[RECOMMENDED]` |
| 15 | Audit | Every approval, rejection, correction (before/after), manual entry, period lock/unlock, and bulk action |
| 16 | Edge cases | Guard works a double shift → two assignments, two attendance records, overtime rules applied once. Site with no network at all → supervisor proxy plus a scheduled paper-register reconciliation import. Guard checks in at the wrong site (adjacent client) → the record is captured against the actual location and routed as an exception with a one-click "reassign to correct post". Retrospective client dispute 45 days later → the evidence bundle (map, selfie, timestamps, device data) is exportable as a single PDF per shift |
| 17 | QA | `TC-AGN-200`–`TC-AGN-230`: geofence boundary, offline batch reconciliation, correction after lock, payable vs billable divergence, 100k-event month performance |
| 18 | Acceptance | Given a guard checked in 400 m outside the geofence with a reason and a photo, When the supervisor approves it, Then the record becomes Verified with `geofence_result = outside` preserved, the approver recorded, and the hours become payable. Given a locked period and a discovered error, When an authorised user corrects it, Then the original record is preserved, a linked correction is created, and an adjustment line flows to the next payroll and, if billable, the next invoice |
| 19 | Analytics | Attendance % by site/branch/client, late rate, absence rate, exception rate, exception resolution time, auto-approval rate, evidence completeness. KPIs: auto-approval ≥ 85%; exception queue cleared daily; attendance % vs contract SLA per client |
| 20 | Future | Anomaly detection on attendance patterns (buddy-punching signatures, systematic geofence edge-hugging) as a Recommendation-class insight `[FUTURE]` |

### 20.14 Module: Patrol and QR/NFC Checkpoints

| # | Point | Specification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Purpose | Prove route compliance to the client and detect the guard who signs the register from the guard room |
| 2 | Users | Operations Manager, Field Officer, Supervisor, client (read-only per contract) |
| 3 | Permissions | Configure routes/checkpoints: Operations Manager. View: operational roles. Approve manual scans: Supervisor |
| 4 | Screens | AGN-S-100 Patrol overview (rounds due/done/missed today) · AGN-S-101 Route builder · AGN-S-102 Checkpoint manager · AGN-S-103 Round detail with map trail · AGN-S-104 Patrol compliance report · AGN-S-105 Tag printing & registration |
| 5 | UI detail | Route builder: ordered checkpoint list with expected duration between points, round schedule (times or interval), mandatory/optional flags, strict-order toggle. Round detail replays the round on a map: checkpoint pins with scan times, the guard's location trail, gaps highlighted, and any observation media inline. Checkpoint manager supports bulk QR generation (a printable A4 sheet with tamper-evident labels, each showing the checkpoint name in the site's language) and NFC tag registration by scanning the tag with a phone |
| 6 | UX flow | Create route → place checkpoints (name, location, mandatory) → generate and print tags → register NFC UIDs → schedule rounds per post → monitor compliance |
| 7 | Fields | Route: name, site, checkpoints[] with order, schedule (interval or fixed times), window tolerance, strict order flag, applicable posts/shifts. Checkpoint: name, location, tag type, tag id/UID, HMAC secret ref, expected dwell, instructions, photo |
| 8 | Validation | Checkpoint location must be within the site geofence (or explicitly marked external, e.g. perimeter); tag IDs unique per tenant; a round schedule cannot exceed the shift window |
| 9 | Business logic | Round completion, partial and missed states per §18.7. Compliance % per post/site/period is the client-facing metric and feeds SLA. Manual scans (damaged tag) require supervisor approval to count. Tag rotation policy: QR HMAC secrets rotate per site on a schedule, invalidating photographed tags `[RECOMMENDED]` |
| 10 | Backend logic | Same ingest/idempotency path as attendance; round evaluation server-side on schedule and on late-arriving offline scans, which can retrospectively convert a Missed round to Completed — a reconciliation the UI must show honestly with a "reconciled from offline" tag |
| 11 | Status lifecycle | Round: `Pending` → `In Progress` → `Completed` / `Partial` / `Missed`. Checkpoint scan: `Pending` → `Verified` / `Rejected` |
| 12 | Notifications | Round overdue to supervisor; consecutive missed rounds escalate per §24; daily patrol digest to the client where contracted |
| 13 | Integrations | Guard App scanning, client portal patrol view, reports |
| 14 | Security | Checkpoint locations reveal site layout; treated as client-confidential and not exported without permission |
| 15 | Audit | Route and checkpoint changes, tag re-registration, manual scan approvals |
| 16 | Edge cases | Tag stolen/destroyed → deactivate and reissue with history preserved. Route changed mid-month → versioned; compliance computed against the version in force. Guard scans a checkpoint from another site (tags swapped) → mismatch detected by location and flagged |
| 17 | QA | `TC-AGN-240`–`TC-AGN-255` |
| 18 | Acceptance | Given a 4-round night schedule and 3 rounds completed offline, When the device syncs at 07:00, Then the three rounds are reconciled to Completed, the fourth remains Missed, and the compliance report shows 75% with the reconciliation noted |
| 19 | Analytics | Round completion %, average round duration, checkpoint miss frequency (identifies badly placed tags), manual scan share. KPI: patrol compliance ≥ 95% on contracted routes |
| 20 | Future | BLE beacons for tag-free checkpoints; route-time anomaly detection `[FUTURE]` |

### 20.15 Module: Incidents and SOS

| # | Point | Specification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Purpose | Handle what goes wrong: capture it, classify it, resolve it, tell the client, and learn from the pattern |
| 2 | Users | Operations Manager (owner), Field Officer, Supervisor, Agency Owner (P0 visibility), client (read per contract) |
| 3 | Permissions | Create: any operational role and guards via the app. Classify/assign/resolve: Operations Manager, Field Officer. Close a P0: Branch Manager or above. Client-visibility toggle: Agency Admin |
| 4 | Screens | AGN-S-110 Incident register · AGN-S-111 Incident detail (tabs: Summary · Evidence · Timeline · Actions · Client communication · Closure) · AGN-S-112 SOS queue · AGN-S-113 SOS detail with live context · AGN-S-114 Incident analytics · AGN-S-115 Closure report generator |
| 5 | UI detail | Register list: incident number, date/time, site, client, type, severity chip, status, assignee, age timer against SLA, client-notified flag. Detail shows the guard's original evidence (photos, video, voice note with a transcript where available) prominently, because the raw field evidence is the asset. Timeline records every action with actor and time. The SOS queue is separated from incidents, is severity-P0 by definition, and displays live guard location, battery, last event and the escalation state |
| 6 | UX flow | Incident arrives → auto-assigned by site/branch rules → acknowledged → investigated (actions logged, field officer dispatched if needed) → client notified per contract → resolved with a closure report → reviewed weekly in analytics |
| 7 | Fields | Incident: number, type, severity P0–P3, site, post, guard, occurred_at (device + server), reported_at, description, evidence[], injuries flag, police informed flag, FIR reference, client notified at/by, assignee, actions[], root cause, preventive action, closure report, closed_by/at, client-visible flag |
| 8 | Validation | Severity mandatory; P0/P1 require an assignee within the configured SLA; closure requires root cause and a closure note; police-informed = yes prompts for a reference |
| 9 | Business logic | SLA per severity (configurable defaults: P0 acknowledge 5 min / resolve 4 h; P1 15 min / 24 h; P2 2 h / 72 h; P3 24 h / 7 days). Client notification rules per contract: automatic for P0/P1, digest for P2/P3, or manual only. Escalation ladders are owned by §24 and consumed here tenant-scoped. An SOS event creates a linked incident automatically on resolution so the operational record is complete |
| 10 | Backend logic | Incident numbering per tenant per year; evidence stored in the tenant's media store with access control; transcription of voice notes where the AI layer is enabled (§25) |
| 11 | Status lifecycle | `Draft` → `Pending` → `In Progress` → `Completed` (closed) / `Rejected` (invalid/duplicate) → `Archived` |
| 12 | Notifications | By severity to the operational chain; client notification per contract; daily incident digest; weekly trend summary to the Owner |
| 13 | Integrations | Guard App, Command Center, client portal, WhatsApp/email for client notification, §24 escalation engine |
| 14 | Security | Incident evidence may include images of people and property; access is scoped to the site's branch and to the client's own incidents; exports are watermarked and logged |
| 15 | Audit | Every status change, assignment, client communication sent, evidence added or removed (removal only by Owner with reason and never a hard delete), closure |
| 16 | Edge cases | Incident implicating the guard who reported it → routing rule that escalates to the Branch Manager rather than the site supervisor. Incident at a site belonging to another branch (loaned guard) → visible to both branches. Client disputes the incident report → the immutable evidence bundle with device metadata is exportable. Mass event (fire, riot) generating 30 incidents → merge into a master incident with children |
| 17 | QA | `TC-AGN-260`–`TC-AGN-280` |
| 18 | Acceptance | Given a P0 incident created at 22:10 and unacknowledged at 22:15, When the SLA timer fires, Then the escalation ladder notifies the Branch Manager, the register row turns red with the breach stamp, and the breach is recorded for SLA reporting |
| 19 | Analytics | Incidents per 1,000 guard-shifts, by type, site, client and time-of-day; SLA compliance; repeat-site analysis; mean time to resolve. KPIs: P0 acknowledgement SLA ≥ 98%; incident rate trend flat or declining per site |
| 20 | Future | Auto-classification of incident type from the guard's voice note (Recommendation class, human-confirmed, §41) |

### 20.16 Module: Documents, KYC and Police Verification

| # | Point | Specification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Purpose | Hold every document the agency needs to prove that its workforce and its business are what it claims, and make expiry impossible to miss |
| 2 | Users | Agency Compliance (owner), Agency HR, Agency Admin, Payroll (bank documents), Agency Owner |
| 3 | Permissions | Upload: HR, Compliance, and the guard via the app. Verify/reject: Compliance only. View: role-scoped; bank documents restricted to Payroll. Download: permissioned, watermarked, logged |
| 4 | Screens | AGN-S-120 Document dashboard (by entity type and state) · AGN-S-121 Entity document vault (guard/employee/client/site/agency) · AGN-S-122 Verification queue · AGN-S-123 Expiry calendar · AGN-S-124 Bulk request · AGN-S-125 KYC status board · AGN-S-126 Police verification tracker |
| 5 | UI detail | Document dashboard is a matrix: document type × state (Missing / Pending / Verified / Expiring / Expired / Rejected) with counts, each cell clicking through to the filtered list. The verification queue shows the document image side by side with the extracted/entered field values, with Approve / Reject (reason) / Request better copy as three buttons. The expiry calendar is a month view with document expiries plotted and a bulk "request renewal" action |
| 6 | UX flow | Request → guard uploads via app → OCR pre-fills → Compliance verifies → state becomes Verified with an expiry date → alerts fire before expiry → renewal cycle repeats |
| 7 | Fields | Document: entity type + id, document type, number, issued date, expiry date, issuing authority, file(s), OCR confidence, verification status, verified_by/at, rejection reason, version history, retention class |
| 8 | Validation | Document-type-specific: PAN format, Aadhaar handled per the data-minimisation rule (store a masked reference and the verification outcome, not the full number, unless there is a lawful basis and an explicit configuration) `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-167]`; expiry date required for types that expire; file types and size limits enforced |
| 9 | Business logic | Document requirements are configurable per role and per client contract (some clients contractually require police verification for every deployed guard). Requirement sets drive the compliance state of a guard and, where the agency enables it, deployment blocking. Police verification tracking models the real process: application submitted → acknowledgement received → under process → report received (clear / adverse) → recorded, with a manual-entry design because there is no dependable pan-India programmatic interface for this `[ASSUMPTION: A-164]` |
| 10 | Backend logic | Documents stored encrypted at rest with per-tenant keys (§38); OCR extraction runs asynchronously; expiry jobs run daily generating alerts at configurable offsets |
| 11 | Status lifecycle | `Pending` → `Verified` / `Rejected`; `Expiring` (within the alert window) → `Expired`; `Archived` on entity separation per retention |
