| 12 | Notifications | Document requested, rejected (with the specific reason spoken in the Guard App), expiring at T−60/30/15/7/1, expired, verification completed |
| 13 | Integrations | Guard App upload, OCR provider, DigiLocker `[FUTURE]`, Trinetra listing verification (agency-level documents) |
| 14 | Security | The document vault is the most sensitive store in the product: encryption at rest, access logging on every view, watermarked downloads carrying the viewer's identity, no public URLs, time-limited signed access, and a documented retention schedule (§39) |
| 15 | Audit | Upload, view, download, verification decision, rejection reason, replacement, deletion request |
| 16 | Edge cases | Guard uploads a photo of a photocopy → quality rejection with guidance. Document expires while the guard is deployed → alert plus a policy-driven action (warn / block new assignments / block all deployment). Client requires a document the agency does not collect → contract-driven requirement set adds it for that client's deployed guards only. Agency licence expiry → `BR-002` operational restrictions |
| 17 | QA | `TC-AGN-290`–`TC-AGN-305` |
| 18 | Acceptance | Given a client contract requiring police verification, When a guard without a completed verification is rostered to that client's site, Then the assignment is blocked with the requirement named and a one-click path to the verification tracker |
| 19 | Analytics | Document completeness by branch, verification turnaround, expiry-caused deployment blocks, rejection reasons. KPI: verification turnaround < 24 h; zero deployments with expired mandatory documents |
| 20 | Future | DigiLocker-issued document fetch and verifiable-credential support `[FUTURE]` |

### 20.17 Module: Compliance and Licence Management

| # | Point | Specification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Purpose | Keep the agency operable: licences valid for the geographies it works in, statutory registers maintained, and an audit-ready evidence pack available on demand |
| 2 | Users | Agency Compliance (owner), Agency Owner, Agency Admin, Branch Manager |
| 3 | Permissions | Edit licences and compliance configuration: Compliance and Owner only. View: management roles. Export audit pack: permissioned and logged |
| 4 | Screens | AGN-S-130 Compliance dashboard · AGN-S-131 Licence registry · AGN-S-132 Licence detail · AGN-S-133 Statutory registers · AGN-S-134 Compliance calendar · AGN-S-135 Audit pack export · AGN-S-136 Client compliance requirements |
| 5 | UI detail | Compliance dashboard cards: **Agency licences** (valid / expiring / expired per state, with a map of covered geography vs where guards are actually deployed — the single most useful compliance visual, because deployment outside licensed geography is the classic failure), **Workforce compliance** (guards with complete documents %, police verifications pending, training certificates expiring), **Statutory registers** (which registers are configured and current), **Client requirements** (contracts with unmet compliance conditions), **Upcoming obligations** (calendar of renewals and filings). Licence registry rows: licence number, type (state/district), state, districts covered, issue date, expiry, status chip, document, verified-on-Trinetra flag |
| 6 | UX flow | Configure the applicable jurisdiction rule set → register licences → map licences to branches and geographies → the system continuously compares deployment geography to licence coverage and raises gaps |
| 7 | Fields | Licence: number, type, issuing state, issuing authority, districts covered, issue date, expiry date, conditions, document, renewal application status, linked branches. Register: register type, period, generated file, generated_by/at. Obligation: name, jurisdiction, frequency, due date, owner, status, evidence |
| 8 | Validation | A branch must be linked to at least one licence covering its operating geography; a site cannot be activated in a district with no covering licence without an explicit override recorded with a reason |
| 9 | Business logic | **Canon §0 rule applied strictly:** the platform never states what the law requires. Jurisdiction rules — which registers, what renewal cadence, what conditions — are **configurable data** maintained per state, and the product surfaces "your configured rule set says X is due on Y". Statutory register generation (employee register, wage register, attendance register, and similar) produces formatted exports from existing data; the *format templates are configuration*, versioned per jurisdiction, so a change in a state's format is a data update. `BR-002`: an expired agency licence triggers the configured operational restrictions (default: warn on every deployment in that geography, block new site activation, escalate to Owner daily) |
| 10 | Backend logic | Daily compliance evaluation job producing a compliance score per branch and a gap list; audit-pack export assembles licences, registers, document summaries, training records and attendance evidence into a single structured archive |
| 11 | Status lifecycle | Licence: `Active` → `Expiring` → `Expired`; renewal: `Draft` → `Pending` (applied) → `Active` (renewed). Obligation: `Pending` → `Completed` / `Failed` |
| 12 | Notifications | Licence expiry at T−90/60/30/15/7/1 to Compliance and Owner; deployment-outside-coverage alert (immediate, P1); obligation due reminders; register generation ready |
| 13 | Integrations | Trinetra verification (the same licence documents), Documents module, Reports |
| 14 | Security | Licence documents are in the encrypted vault; the audit pack export is a high-sensitivity action requiring re-auth |
| 15 | Audit | Licence additions and edits, override authorisations for uncovered geography, register generation, audit-pack exports |
| 16 | Edge cases | Agency operating in a new state before the licence is granted → the override path exists but is loud, dated, and reported to the Owner weekly. Licence covering a state but not a specific district under a district-scoped regime → district-level coverage modelling, not just state. Renewal filed but not yet granted at expiry → an "under renewal" state with its own restriction profile, configurable |
| 17 | QA | `TC-AGN-310`–`TC-AGN-325` |
| 18 | Acceptance | Given a guard deployed in a district not covered by any active licence, When the daily compliance job runs, Then a P1 gap is raised naming the site, district and missing licence, and the Owner and Compliance are notified |
| 19 | Analytics | Compliance score by branch, licence coverage vs deployment coverage, document completeness, obligations met on time. KPI: zero deployments in uncovered geography |
| 20 | Future | Per-state rule packs maintained centrally by Suraksha and pushed as configuration updates `[RECOMMENDED, phase 2]` |

### 20.18 Module: Payroll, Salary and Statutory Records

| # | Point | Specification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Purpose | Pay several hundred guards correctly, on time, from attendance data, with a defensible trail — the module agencies will judge the entire product on |
| 2 | Users | Payroll (owner), Agency Finance, Agency Owner (approval), Agency HR (inputs), guard (payslip via app) |
| 3 | Permissions | Run payroll: Payroll role. Approve and release: Owner or a delegated approver, always a different person from the preparer where the agency enables maker-checker `[RECOMMENDED]`. Salary structure edits: Payroll + Owner approval. View own payslip: guard only |
| 4 | Screens | AGN-S-140 Payroll dashboard · AGN-S-141 Salary structures · AGN-S-142 Guard salary assignment · AGN-S-143 Payroll run wizard (pre-check → compute → review → approve → release) · AGN-S-144 Run detail (guard-wise grid) · AGN-S-145 Payslip preview · AGN-S-146 Advances & loans · AGN-S-147 Statutory records (EPF/ESIC-related) · AGN-S-148 Disbursement file / payout · AGN-S-149 Payroll reports |
| 5 | UI detail | The run wizard is the centrepiece. **Pre-check** lists every blocker as a clickable item: unapproved attendance exceptions (n), guards without a salary structure (n), guards without bank details (n), unlocked periods (n), pending advances (n), documents blocking payment per policy (n). **Compute** runs as a background job with progress. **Review** is a dense grid: guard, days present, OT hours, gross, each earning component, each deduction, net, with variance-vs-last-month highlighting (any guard whose net moved more than ±20% is flagged, which catches most data errors before money moves). **Approve** requires a summary confirmation showing total gross, total deductions, total net and headcount. **Release** generates payslips and the disbursement output |
| 6 | UX flow | Lock attendance → open run → clear pre-check → compute → review variances → approve → release → disburse → mark paid with references |
| 7 | Fields | Salary structure: name, applicable to (designation/site/client/branch), components[] (name, type earning/deduction, calculation basis fixed/per-day/per-hour/percentage/slab, taxable flag, statutory flag), rounding rule, overtime rate rule, effective dates. Payroll run: period, branch scope, status, computed at, approved by/at, released at, totals. Payslip line: guard, component, amount in paise, basis, quantity |
| 8 | Validation | Money is integer paise, never floats (canon §4). Net cannot be negative (excess advance carries forward). A run cannot include an unlocked attendance period. A structure cannot be deleted while referenced; it is versioned instead |
| 9 | Business logic | Compute = attendance-derived quantities × salary structure + adjustments − deductions. Overtime, holiday and night-allowance rules are configuration. Statutory components (provident-fund-type, insurance-type, professional-tax-type) are modelled as **configurable component templates with configurable rates, wage ceilings and applicability rules per jurisdiction and per employee**, never as hard-coded arithmetic — this is the canon §0 rule applied to money. The product maintains **records and registers** in the shapes agencies need for their filings and produces export files; it does not itself file anything with any authority, and it does not assert what any authority requires `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-168: which statutory export formats ship in V1]` |
| 10 | Backend logic | Runs are immutable once released; corrections are adjustments in a later run linked to the original (`BR-003`). Every payroll movement creates double-sided ledger entries (canon §4). Disbursement: the payout rail is `[DECISION REQUIRED]` per canon §4; the working design produces a bank-ready disbursement file (agency's bank format, configurable) plus a UPI/NEFT reference capture screen for marking payment, with payment-gateway payout integration as a later option |
| 11 | Status lifecycle | Run: `Draft` → `In Progress` (computing) → `Pending` (awaiting approval) → `Verified` (approved) → `Completed` (released/paid) → `Archived`. `Failed` on compute error with a full error list |
| 12 | Notifications | Pre-check blockers to Payroll, approval request to the approver, "payslip ready" and "salary credited" to guards (push + SMS), disbursement file ready to Finance |
| 13 | Integrations | Attendance (hours), Leave, Advances, Assets (recovery deductions), accounting export, banking file formats, Guard App payslip view |
| 14 | Security | Payroll is the highest-privilege area: enforced MFA, re-auth before approval and release, no bulk export of salary data without Owner permission, salary fields masked elsewhere in the product |
| 15 | Audit | Structure changes with before/after, assignment changes, every run state transition with actor, approvals, adjustments with reason, disbursement references, any manual override of a computed amount (with mandatory reason and highlighted in the run detail) |
| 16 | Edge cases | Guard joins mid-month → proration by joining date. Guard separates mid-cycle → full-and-final settlement flow (dues, advance recovery, asset recovery, notice period), a distinct run type. Guard worked at two branches → costs split by branch per attendance. Attendance corrected after release → adjustment in the next run, never a rewrite. Bank rejects a payment → failed-payment handling with re-issue and reference tracking. Cash-paid guards → recorded with an acknowledgement capture (guard confirms receipt in the app) `[RECOMMENDED]` |
| 17 | QA | `TC-AGN-330`–`TC-AGN-360`: paise-level reconciliation across 1,000 guards, proration boundaries, negative-net handling, maker-checker enforcement, adjustment linkage, run immutability |
| 18 | Acceptance | Given a payroll run for 420 guards with 6 unapproved attendance exceptions, When the Payroll user opens the run, Then the pre-check blocks computation and lists the 6 exceptions with links; Given the run is approved and released, When an attendance correction is made for that period, Then the next run contains a linked adjustment line and the released run is unchanged |
| 19 | Analytics | Payroll cost by branch/site/client, cost per guard-shift, overtime share, adjustment rate, on-time release rate, variance flags raised vs errors found. KPIs: on-time payroll ≥ 99%; post-release correction rate < 2% |
| 20 | Future | Direct payout integration once the rail decision lands; earned-wage access (§18.13, `D-161`); cost-to-serve analytics per contract |

### 20.19 Module: Invoices, GST and Receivables

| # | Point | Specification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Purpose | Convert deployment into cash: raise correct invoices automatically, track what is owed, and chase it systematically |
| 2 | Users | Agency Finance (owner), Agency Admin, Agency Owner, Agency Sales (visibility of client dues) |
| 3 | Permissions | Create/issue invoices: Finance. Credit notes and write-offs: Owner approval. View: management roles. Client sees their own invoices in the client portal |
| 4 | Screens | AGN-S-150 Invoice list · AGN-S-151 Invoice builder · AGN-S-152 Invoice detail/preview · AGN-S-153 Ready-to-raise queue · AGN-S-154 Receivables ageing · AGN-S-155 Payment recording & allocation · AGN-S-156 Credit notes · AGN-S-157 Reminder campaigns · AGN-S-158 Client statement · AGN-S-159 Tax summary |
| 5 | UI detail | The **Ready-to-raise queue** is the money-making screen: after each period lock, it lists every contract with its computed billable quantities, the derived amount, and any exceptions (unfilled posts, disputed attendance, rate changes mid-period) — one click generates a draft invoice per contract, in bulk. Invoice builder shows line items derived from contract × attendance with an editable quantity/rate and a visible audit note whenever a value is overridden. Ageing view: buckets Current / 1–30 / 31–60 / 61–90 / 90+ with totals, client drill-down and a one-click reminder |
| 6 | UX flow | Lock period → open ready-to-raise → review exceptions → bulk generate drafts → review → issue → deliver (email/WhatsApp/portal) → track → record payment → allocate → reconcile |
| 7 | Fields | Invoice: number (per-tenant series, configurable prefix and financial-year reset), client, branch, contract, period, line items[] (description, site/post, quantity, unit, rate, amount, tax rate), taxable value, tax lines, total, place of supply, due date, PO reference, status, delivery log, payments[], credit notes[] |
| 8 | Validation | Invoice number series must be gapless and non-reusable; issuing requires a locked attendance period; a credit note cannot exceed the invoice value; tax fields must be complete before issue |
| 9 | Business logic | Billing bases supported: per guard per month (with proration for part-month deployment), per guard-shift, per hour, fixed monthly, and per-event/per-deployment for event security. Reimbursables and penalties appear as separate lines. **GST treatment is configuration:** rates, place-of-supply determination, intra/inter-state behaviour, reverse-charge applicability and any e-invoicing/e-way requirements are jurisdiction rules held as versioned configuration, and the product applies the configured rule — it does not assert tax law (canon §0). E-invoicing integration availability is `[ASSUMPTION: A-165]` and, where a client is in scope, the working design is generating the required payload for the agency's chosen provider rather than assuming a direct government API |
| 10 | Backend logic | Invoices are immutable after issue (`BR-003`); corrections are credit notes plus a fresh invoice. Every invoice and payment creates double-sided ledger entries. Payment allocation supports part-payments across multiple invoices and TDS-type deductions recorded as a separate allocation line so the receivable closes correctly |
| 11 | Status lifecycle | `Draft` → `Pending` (issued, unpaid) → `In Progress` (part-paid) → `Completed` (settled) / `Cancelled` (cancelled with a credit note) → `Archived`; plus `Expiring`-analogue ageing flags |
| 12 | Notifications | Invoice issued (client), due in 7/3/1 days, overdue at +1/+7/+15/+30, payment received (client + finance), credit note issued |
| 13 | Integrations | Contracts, Attendance, payment gateway for client online payment, accounting export (Tally-style CSV/XML and generic CSV `[RECOMMENDED]`), client portal, WhatsApp/email delivery |
| 14 | Security | Financial data restricted to Finance and Owner; exports logged; client portal access strictly scoped |
| 15 | Audit | Every invoice state change, every line override with reason, credit notes, write-offs with approver, payment allocations, reminder dispatches |
| 16 | Edge cases | Client disputes a shortfall → dispute flag on the invoice with the disputed amount held out of the ageing "collectible" figure while remaining in receivables. Rate changed mid-period → split lines by effective date. Client pays a lump sum across 6 invoices → allocation screen with auto-suggest. Invoice raised then attendance corrected → credit note + revised invoice, both linked. Advance/retainer billing → advance invoice with subsequent adjustment lines |
| 17 | QA | `TC-AGN-370`–`TC-AGN-395`: numbering gaplessness under concurrency, proration boundaries, tax configuration variants, part-payment allocation, credit-note limits |
| 18 | Acceptance | Given a locked period for a contract billing per guard per month with one post unfilled for 4 days, When the invoice is generated, Then the line item shows the prorated quantity, the shortfall is itemised, and the SLA report reflects the same shortfall — one number, two documents, no divergence |
| 19 | Analytics | DSO, ageing distribution, collection rate, disputed value, revenue by client/branch/service, invoice cycle time (period lock → issue). KPIs: invoice issued within 3 working days of period lock ≥ 95%; DSO trend improving |
| 20 | Future | Automated dunning workflows with escalation to service suspension; client self-service payment plans `[FUTURE]` |

### 20.20 Module: Reports and Analytics

| # | Point | Specification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Purpose | Answer the recurring questions without a person building a spreadsheet, and give the owner a view of the business that paper never could |
| 2 | Users | All roles within their scope; Agency Owner and Branch Manager are the primary analytics consumers |
| 3 | Permissions | Every report inherits the module permissions of its data; a user can never see through a report what they cannot see in the module. Export permission is separate from view permission |
| 4 | Screens | AGN-S-160 Report library · AGN-S-161 Report viewer with parameters · AGN-S-162 Scheduled reports · AGN-S-163 Analytics workspace · AGN-S-164 Custom report builder (Enterprise) · AGN-S-165 Export centre |
| 5 | UI detail | Report library grouped by domain with a search and a "recently run" strip. Viewer: parameter bar (date range, branch, client, site, guard, status) → results table with totals row → chart toggle → export (PDF/Excel/CSV) → schedule. Analytics workspace: a set of pre-built dashboards — Operations, Workforce, Client, Finance, Compliance — each a curated set of charts with drill-through to the underlying list |
| 6 | UX flow | Pick a report → set parameters → run → read → export or schedule. Scheduling is where the value compounds: the owner receives the same three reports every Monday at 08:00 without asking |
| 7 | Standard report set | **Operations:** daily deployment, attendance summary (site/client/branch), absence and late analysis, patrol compliance, wake-check compliance, incident register, SOS log, geofence-breach log, unmanned-post log, shift-coverage gap. **Workforce:** guard master, joiners/leavers, attrition, document compliance, training status, leave balance and utilisation, overtime, guard performance card. **Client:** client-wise deployment, SLA performance, incident summary per client, service delivery report (the document agencies attach to invoices), client profitability. **Finance:** invoice register, receivables ageing, collection, payroll register, payroll cost analysis, expense summary, branch P&L, cost per guard-shift, margin per contract. **Compliance:** licence status, document expiry, police verification status, statutory register set, audit-pack index |
| 8 | Validation | Date ranges capped per report to protect performance (with an async path for larger ranges); exports beyond a row threshold run as background jobs and are delivered as files |
| 9 | Business logic | Every report is defined declaratively (dataset, dimensions, measures, filters, permissions) so new reports do not require bespoke code. Numbers must reconcile: the same measure computed in two reports must use one shared definition — a measures dictionary that names, for example, exactly what "attendance %" means (present shifts ÷ rostered shifts within the operational day boundary) |
| 10 | Backend logic | Reads from read-replicas/materialised aggregates; heavy reports queue; results cached with a visible `as_of` |
| 11 | Status lifecycle | Scheduled report: `Active` → `Suspended` → `Archived`. Export job: `Pending` → `In Progress` → `Completed` / `Failed` |
| 12 | Notifications | Scheduled report delivered (email with attachment or a secure link), export ready, report failed |
| 13 | Integrations | Email delivery, accounting export, client portal (client-facing service reports), API for BI tools (Enterprise) |
| 14 | Security | Exports carry a watermark with the requesting user and timestamp; scheduled reports to external email addresses require Owner approval `[RECOMMENDED]`; every export is audit-logged with the row count and parameters |
| 15 | Audit | Report runs with parameters for sensitive reports (payroll, guard personal data), all exports, schedule creation and recipient changes |
| 16 | Edge cases | A branch manager schedules a report and then loses branch access → the schedule is suspended and the owner notified, rather than silently continuing to leak data. Report spanning a period where the org structure changed → reports are computed against the structure in force on each date, with a note |
| 17 | QA | `TC-AGN-400`–`TC-AGN-415`: reconciliation between report pairs, permission leakage tests, large-export behaviour |
| 18 | Acceptance | Given the attendance summary report and the dashboard attendance card for the same branch and date, When both are run, Then they show identical values, because both consume the same measure definition |
| 19 | Analytics | Report usage by type, schedule count, export volume, report latency. KPI: p95 report latency < 8 s for standard ranges |
| 20 | Future | Natural-language querying through the AI layer (Read-only class, §25/§41); custom dashboard builder for all plans |

### 20.21 Module: Government Tenders (Discovery and Tracking) — Professional+

| # | Point | Specification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Purpose | Surface relevant government security tenders, and manage the bid process to submission and outcome — for many agencies the largest single revenue lane |
| 2 | Users | Agency Sales (owner), Agency Owner, Agency Compliance (document readiness), Agency Finance (EMD/pricing) |
| 3 | Permissions | View and track: Sales, Owner. Bid pricing: Finance/Owner. Document pack assembly: Compliance |
| 4 | Screens | AGN-S-170 Tender feed · AGN-S-171 Tender detail · AGN-S-172 Tracked tenders board · AGN-S-173 Bid workspace (checklist, documents, pricing) · AGN-S-174 Bid calendar · AGN-S-175 Outcome log · AGN-S-176 Eligibility profile |
| 5 | UI detail | Feed rows: tender title, authority, state/district, estimated value, guard count if stated, publication date, submission deadline with a countdown, EMD amount, eligibility-match indicator (a three-state chip computed against the agency's eligibility profile: turnover, years of experience, licence geography, similar-work credentials, workforce size). Filters: state, district, authority type, value band, deadline window, service type, eligibility match. Bid workspace: a document checklist with each requirement mapped to a document already in the vault (green) or missing (red), a pricing sheet, EMD tracking, and a submission log |
| 6 | UX flow | Feed → filter by eligibility → track → workspace → assemble documents → price → submit (outside the platform, on the relevant portal) → record submission → record outcome |
| 7 | Fields | Tender: source, reference number, title, authority, geography, published date, deadline, pre-bid meeting date, estimated value, EMD, tender fee, document URL, eligibility criteria (parsed where possible, else free text), status, tracked_by, notes[], attachments[]. Bid: tender ref, decision (bid/no-bid + reason), checklist[], pricing sheet, EMD payment reference, submitted_at, outcome (won/lost/cancelled/technically disqualified), award value, lessons |
| 8 | Validation | Deadline must be in the future to move to bidding; checklist completeness is shown but never blocks, because a human decides |
| 9 | Business logic | **Honesty statement (canon §0):** government tender portals in India — the central procurement portal, GeM, and dozens of state portals — do **not** offer a dependable, uniform public API for programmatic tender discovery. Therefore the working design is: (a) a Suraksha-operated ingestion pipeline that aggregates tenders from permitted sources into a curated tender dataset shared across tenants, with clear source attribution and a "verify on the source portal" link on every record; (b) manual entry by the agency for tenders it finds itself; (c) per-source connectors added opportunistically where a lawful, permitted programmatic route exists. No tender is ever presented as authoritative — the source link is always the authority `[ASSUMPTION: A-166]`. Automated bid submission is explicitly out of scope `[FUTURE]` |
| 10 | Backend logic | Tender records are platform-level (shared corpus), tracking and bid records are tenant-scoped. Eligibility matching runs on the agency's profile and is advisory only |
| 11 | Status lifecycle | Tender: `Active` → `Expiring` (deadline near) → `Expired`. Bid: `Draft` → `Pending` (submitted) → `Completed` (won/lost recorded) / `Cancelled` |
| 12 | Notifications | New matching tender (daily digest, configurable), deadline at T−7/3/1 days, pre-bid meeting reminder, checklist item overdue, outcome recorded |
| 13 | Integrations | Documents vault (checklist mapping), Compliance (licence and turnover evidence), Finance (EMD), Reports |
| 14 | Security | Bid pricing is highly confidential — restricted to Finance/Owner, excluded from general exports, and access-logged |
| 15 | Audit | Tracking decisions, bid/no-bid decisions with reason, pricing changes, submission records, outcome entries |
| 16 | Edge cases | Tender in a state where the agency lacks a licence → eligibility chip shows the specific gap and links to the licence registry. Deadline extended by the authority → manual update with a change log. Consortium bids → a partner field and a flag, without modelling the partner's data |
| 17 | QA | `TC-AGN-420`–`TC-AGN-430` |
| 18 | Acceptance | Given a tender requiring a Gujarat licence and 5 years of experience, When the agency holds a Gujarat licence and was incorporated 3 years ago, Then the eligibility chip is amber with "experience: 3 of 5 years" named explicitly, and the source-portal link is present |
| 19 | Analytics | Tenders matched, tracked, bid, won; win rate; average bid value; reasons for no-bid and for loss. KPI: bid-to-win rate tracked per authority type |
| 20 | Future | Document auto-assembly into the authority's required pack format; historical award-price benchmarking `[FUTURE]` |

### 20.22 Module: OCR Migration (Enterprise)

| # | Point | Specification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Purpose | Get an agency's decades of paper registers and Excel files into the platform without three months of manual typing — the single biggest barrier to Enterprise adoption |
| 2 | Users | Agency Admin plus a Suraksha onboarding specialist (§22); reviewed by Agency HR/Finance |
| 3 | Permissions | Migration jobs require Agency Owner authorisation; commit to production data requires a named approver |
| 4 | Screens | AGN-S-180 Migration workspace · AGN-S-181 Upload batch · AGN-S-182 Template mapping · AGN-S-183 Extraction review grid · AGN-S-184 Validation report · AGN-S-185 Commit & rollback · AGN-S-186 Migration history |
| 5 | UI detail | The review grid is the whole product here: the scanned page on the left, the extracted rows on the right, low-confidence cells highlighted amber and empty-but-required cells red, keyboard-first correction, and a running "n of m rows verified" counter. Batches are chunked so a human can work in 20-minute sessions |
| 6 | UX flow | Scan/upload → choose entity type (guards, clients, sites, attendance history, salary history) → map columns/fields → extract → review and correct → validate → dry-run → commit → verify → (if needed) roll back |
| 7 | Fields | Batch: name, entity type, source type (scan/Excel/CSV), file count, page count, status, extracted rows, corrected rows, error rows, committed rows, committed_by/at, rollback_token |
| 8 | Validation | Every target entity's own validation rules apply before commit; duplicates are detected against existing data and against other rows in the batch; a batch cannot commit with unresolved required-field errors |
| 9 | Business logic | Migration writes with `source = ocr_migration` and a batch reference on every row, which is what makes rollback possible and makes provenance visible forever. Historical attendance and payroll are imported as **frozen historical records** that never participate in live computation — they are read-only history, so an imported attendance row can never leak into a live payroll run |
| 10 | Backend logic | OCR runs asynchronously with per-page confidence; handwriting accuracy on Indian-language registers is materially lower than print and must be assumed to require human review of most rows `[ASSUMPTION: A-167]` — the design goal is a 10× typing reduction, not zero typing, and the product must not promise otherwise |
| 11 | Status lifecycle | Batch: `Draft` → `In Progress` (extracting) → `Pending` (awaiting review) → `Verified` (reviewed) → `Completed` (committed) / `Failed` / `Cancelled` |
| 12 | Notifications | Extraction complete, review overdue, commit complete with a summary, rollback executed |
| 13 | Integrations | OCR provider, storage, all target modules |
| 14 | Security | Uploaded registers contain personal data of the whole workforce; the same vault controls apply, and source files are retained only for a defined window after commit (§39) |
| 15 | Audit | Every batch action, every corrected cell (before/after), commit and rollback with actor |
| 16 | Edge cases | Mixed-language handwritten registers → per-language OCR models where available, human review otherwise. Duplicate guards across registers → merge suggestions during review. Partial commit failure → transactional per chunk with a resume point. Rollback after downstream use → blocked once any live record references the imported data; a correction workflow replaces it |
| 17 | QA | `TC-AGN-440`–`TC-AGN-450` |
| 18 | Acceptance | Given a 500-page attendance register batch, When extraction completes, Then every low-confidence cell is flagged, the operator can correct rows without leaving the keyboard, and commit is blocked until all required fields validate |
| 19 | Analytics | Pages processed, extraction accuracy by field, human-correction rate, time per 100 rows, batches committed. KPI: ≥ 10× faster than manual entry, measured |
| 20 | Future | Learning loop that improves extraction from operator corrections `[FUTURE]`, subject to §41 |

### 20.23 Module: Workflow Automation (Professional+)

| # | Point | Specification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Purpose | Let an agency encode its own operating procedure — "if a guard is absent twice in a week, notify the branch manager and create a counselling task" — without asking for a code change |
| 2 | Users | Agency Admin (author), Agency Owner (approval for rules with financial or personnel effect) |
| 3 | Permissions | Create/edit rules: Agency Admin. Rules touching payroll, invoicing, blacklisting or permissions require Owner approval before activation |
| 4 | Screens | AGN-S-190 Rule list · AGN-S-191 Rule builder (trigger → conditions → actions) · AGN-S-192 Rule test/simulate · AGN-S-193 Run history · AGN-S-194 Template gallery |
| 5 | UI detail | Rule builder is a three-column form in plain language: **When** (event picker), **If** (condition rows with field/operator/value, AND/OR grouping), **Then** (action list). A live preview sentence renders the rule in English: "When a guard is marked absent, if the guard has 2 or more absences in the last 7 days and the site is a Priority-1 client, then notify the Branch Manager and create a task for HR." Simulation runs the rule against the last 30 days of real data and shows what it *would* have done — the control that prevents an agency from automating a disaster |
| 6 | UX flow | Start from a template or blank → build → simulate → activate → monitor run history |
| 7 | Triggers | Attendance marked/absent/late, geofence breach, patrol round missed, wake check missed, incident created/severity changed, SOS raised, document expiring/expired, licence expiring, contract expiring, invoice overdue, payment received, lead created/stage changed, guard created/status changed, leave requested, replacement unfilled, roster published, scheduled time (cron-like) |
| 8 | Actions | Send notification (role/user/guard/client, channel-specific), create task, assign to a user, add a tag, change a status (whitelisted statuses only), create an incident, trigger a replacement request, send a templated message, call a webhook, escalate to a role, add a note. **Explicitly forbidden actions:** anything that moves money, changes payroll amounts, alters permissions, deletes records, blacklists or terminates a guard, or changes compliance status — these mirror the AI restrictions in canon §1.7 and are enforced at the action-registry level, not by convention |
| 9 | Business logic | Rules run server-side on the event stream with a per-rule rate limit and a global tenant limit; loop detection prevents rule A triggering rule B triggering rule A; every rule execution is recorded with the input event, the condition evaluation and the actions taken |
| 10 | Backend logic | Rules are versioned; editing an active rule creates a new version and the run history shows which version ran |
| 11 | Status lifecycle | Rule: `Draft` → `Pending` (awaiting approval) → `Active` → `Suspended` → `Archived` |
| 12 | Notifications | Rule activated, rule failing repeatedly, rate limit hit |
| 13 | Integrations | Webhooks out, notification service, task service |
| 14 | Security | Webhook targets must be verified (a challenge-response on first use) and cannot be internal addresses; secrets stored encrypted |
| 15 | Audit | Rule creation, edits, approvals, activation/suspension, and every execution |
| 16 | Edge cases | Rule that would notify 400 people → a blast-radius warning at activation with a required confirmation. Rule firing on a data backfill → rules ignore events flagged as historical/migrated. Two rules acting on the same event with contradictory actions → deterministic ordering by rule priority, surfaced in the builder |
| 17 | QA | `TC-AGN-460`–`TC-AGN-470` |
| 18 | Acceptance | Given a rule that notifies the Branch Manager on a second absence in 7 days, When simulated against the last 30 days, Then the simulation lists every guard-date it would have fired on, and activation requires explicit confirmation of that blast radius |
| 19 | Analytics | Active rules per tenant, executions, actions taken, rules suspended for failure. KPI: agencies with ≥ 3 active rules retain measurably better (tracked, not assumed) |
| 20 | Future | Multi-step approval workflows and conditional branching; a marketplace of shared rule templates `[FUTURE]` |

### 20.24 Module: Settings, Roles, Permissions, Integrations, API and Audit Trail

| # | Point | Specification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Purpose | Configure the tenant, control who can do what, connect outward, and prove after the fact what happened |
| 2 | Users | Agency Owner (owner of this area), Agency Admin, Agency Compliance (audit read) |
| 3 | Permissions | Settings sub-areas are individually permissioned; Roles/Permissions and Security settings are Owner-only by default; audit trail is read-only for everyone including the Owner |
| 4 | Screens | AGN-S-200 Agency profile · AGN-S-201 Branches · AGN-S-202 Users · AGN-S-203 Roles & permissions · AGN-S-204 Plan & billing · AGN-S-205 Security (MFA, sessions, IP allowlist, password policy, SSO) · AGN-S-206 Notification templates & preferences · AGN-S-207 Operational configuration (shift windows, grace periods, geofence defaults, escalation ladders, operational day boundary, numbering series) · AGN-S-208 AI permissions · AGN-S-209 Integrations catalogue · AGN-S-210 API keys & webhooks · AGN-S-211 Audit trail · AGN-S-212 Data export & retention |
| 5 | UI detail | Roles screen: a matrix of role × module with four states per cell (None / View / Edit / Approve) plus expandable per-action detail for sensitive actions; a "compare roles" mode; a "what changed" diff before saving, because permission changes are the highest-risk edits in the product. Audit trail: a filterable stream (actor, entity, action, date, IP, device, before/after) with entity-anchored views ("show me everything that happened to this guard record") and export |
| 6 | UX flow | Owner configures once at onboarding (guided setup checklist), then edits rarely; the guided setup is what determines whether the agency ever becomes productive |
| 7 | Fields | Agency profile: legal name, brand name, logo, addresses, GSTIN, PAN, contact, licences (linked to §20.17), financial year, currency (INR), time zone (IST), operational day boundary. Integration: type, credentials (encrypted), status, last sync, error log. API key: name, scopes, environment, created_by, last used, expiry, IP restrictions. Webhook: URL, events[], secret, retry policy, delivery log |
| 8 | Validation | At least one Agency Owner must always exist; the last Owner cannot be removed or downgraded. Permission changes cannot grant a role more than the granting user holds. API scopes are least-privilege by default |
| 9 | Business logic | **Integrations catalogue:** biometric attendance devices (Enterprise, §20.25), accounting export (Tally-style and generic CSV), payment gateway for client payments, SMS/WhatsApp/email providers (agency's own credentials or Suraksha-provided), Google/Microsoft calendar for schedules `[FUTURE]`, and generic webhooks. **API:** a scoped REST API (§33) with read-only keys on Starter, full read/write on Professional, and higher rate limits plus dedicated support on Enterprise; every API call is attributed to the key and audited. **Audit trail** is append-only (canon §4), retained 90 days on Starter, 12 months on Professional, and configurably longer on Enterprise, with export |
| 10 | Backend logic | Settings changes are versioned and take effect at a stated time; some (operational day boundary, numbering series) require a change window because they alter derived data, and the UI must say so |
| 11 | Status lifecycle | User: `Pending` (invited) → `Active` → `Suspended` → `Archived`. API key: `Active` → `Suspended` → `Expired`/`Archived` |
| 12 | Notifications | User invited/joined/removed, role changed, MFA disabled (always notify the Owner), API key created, webhook failing, plan changed, payment for subscription failed |
| 13 | Integrations | Identity service (canon §4), billing/subscription service, Trinetra listing link |
| 14 | Security | This module is the security control plane: MFA enforcement per role, session lifetime, forced logout, device/session list, IP allowlist (Enterprise), SSO/SAML (Enterprise), password policy, re-auth requirements, and impersonation controls. See §38 for the control catalogue |
| 15 | Audit | Every settings change, every permission change with before/after, every user lifecycle event, key creation/revocation, and every audit-trail export |
| 16 | Edge cases | Owner loses access (device lost) → a recovery procedure requiring identity verification through Suraksha support with a mandatory delay and notification to all admins. Plan downgrade with data in a now-gated module → data is retained and read-only, never deleted (§20.29). Agency requests full data export on cancellation → structured export including media, within a defined SLA |
| 17 | QA | `TC-AGN-480`–`TC-AGN-500`: privilege-escalation attempts, last-owner protection, audit completeness on every sensitive action, API scope enforcement |
| 18 | Acceptance | Given an Agency Admin attempts to grant themselves Payroll approval rights they do not hold, When they save, Then the change is rejected with the specific rule cited and the attempt is audit-logged |
| 19 | Analytics | Users per tenant, MFA adoption, permission-change frequency, API usage, webhook failure rate. KPI: MFA adoption for privileged roles ≥ 90% |
| 20 | Future | SCIM provisioning, per-field permission granularity, customer-managed encryption keys `[FUTURE]` |

### 20.25 Minor modules — condensed 6-point specifications

Every module below is covered on: Purpose · Users/Permissions · Screens & key UI · Logic & statuses · Audit/security · Acceptance criteria. None is skipped.

**Employees (non-guard staff).** *Purpose:* manage office and supervisory staff — HR, accounts, field officers, control-room operators — who are not deployable guards but are on the payroll. *Users/permissions:* Agency HR owns; Payroll sees compensation; Owner approves designations. *Screens & UI:* AGN-S-220 Employee list (name, employee code, department, designation, branch, reporting manager, status), AGN-S-221 Employee detail sharing the guard record's tab structure minus deployment, AGN-S-222 Org chart view. *Logic & statuses:* same lifecycle as Guards (`Pending` → `Active` → `Suspended` → `Archived`); employees have attendance too, captured either by the app, by a biometric device, or as a monthly exception-based entry — configurable per employee. *Audit/security:* compensation fields restricted to Payroll/Owner; all changes audited. *Acceptance:* Given an employee marked as exception-based attendance, When the month closes, Then they are treated as fully present except for recorded leave, and payroll computes without any daily attendance record.

**Supervisors.** *Purpose:* model the supervisory layer that actually runs sites — who supervises which sites and guards, and how their own field activity is tracked. *Users/permissions:* Operations Manager assigns; Branch Manager oversees. *Screens & UI:* AGN-S-225 Supervisor list with span-of-control (sites, posts, guards), AGN-S-226 Supervisor detail (assigned sites, visit log, approvals made, response times), AGN-S-227 Supervisor allocation editor. *Logic & statuses:* a supervisor is an employee or a senior guard with the Supervisor (field) role; every site has exactly one primary supervisor and optional secondaries; supervisor site-visit records are geo-stamped (§18.16). *Audit/security:* supervisor approvals of attendance exceptions are individually audited, since this is the primary internal fraud vector. *Acceptance:* Given a site with no primary supervisor assigned, When a roster is published for it, Then a warning is raised and escalation notifications for that site route to the Branch Manager.

**Applicants.** *Purpose:* the raw intake pool feeding Recruitment (§20.7), including walk-ins, referrals and marketplace-sourced candidates. *Users/permissions:* Recruiter creates and progresses; HR converts. *Screens & UI:* AGN-S-230 Applicant list with rapid-entry mode (name, phone, photo, skill in one row), AGN-S-231 Applicant detail, AGN-S-232 Duplicate/rehire check panel. *Logic & statuses:* `Pending` → `In Progress` → `Verified` → `Completed`/`Rejected`; retention period for rejected applicants is configurable and defaults to 12 months (§39). *Audit/security:* personal data with a defined purge job. *Acceptance:* Given an applicant whose phone matches a previously blacklisted guard, When the recruiter opens the record, Then an authorised-role-only warning is displayed with the blacklist reason and date.

**Wake checks (agency view).** *Purpose:* configure, monitor and report the night anti-sleep checks specified in §18.8. *Users/permissions:* Operations Manager configures per post; Command Center monitors. *Screens & UI:* AGN-S-235 Wake-check configuration (per post: enabled, window, interval range, acknowledgement window, selfie requirement, escalation ladder), AGN-S-236 Tonight's monitor (live grid of guards on wake-check duty with next-prompt countdown and last acknowledgement), AGN-S-237 Compliance report by guard/site/period. *Logic & statuses:* prompt statuses per §18.8; agency-level compliance % feeds SLA and client reporting. *Audit/security:* configuration changes audited; acknowledgement selfies are personal data with short retention. *Acceptance:* Given a post with wake checks enabled between 23:00 and 05:30 at 45–90 minute intervals, When the night's report is produced, Then it lists every prompt, its acknowledgement latency, and every miss with the escalation actions taken.

**Leave.** *Purpose:* manage entitlement, requests, approvals and the roster consequences of absence. *Users/permissions:* guard requests via app; Supervisor/Operations Manager approve; HR configures policies. *Screens & UI:* AGN-S-240 Leave requests queue (with the roster impact shown inline: "approving this leaves Main Gate night shift unfilled on 12–14 Sep"), AGN-S-241 Leave calendar by site, AGN-S-242 Balances, AGN-S-243 Leave policy configuration (types, accrual, carry-forward, encashment — all configuration, never hard-coded). *Logic & statuses:* `Pending` → `Active` (approved) / `Rejected` / `Cancelled` → `Completed`; approval optionally triggers an automatic replacement request. *Audit/security:* approvals audited; medical documents in the vault. *Acceptance:* Given a leave request that would leave a post unfilled, When the approver opens it, Then the unfilled shifts are named and a one-click "approve and raise replacement" action is offered.

**Replacement.** *Purpose:* fill a hole in the roster fast, with the best available guard. *Users/permissions:* Operations Manager and Field Officer raise and confirm; guards accept via app (§18.12). *Screens & UI:* AGN-S-245 Replacement queue (open requests with a countdown to shift start), AGN-S-246 Candidate picker showing ranked available guards (distance, skill match, hours this week, reliability score, cost implication), AGN-S-247 Dispatch waves monitor. *Logic & statuses:* `Pending` → `In Progress` (offers out) → `Completed` (filled) / `Failed` (unfilled at shift start, which becomes an unmanned-post alert); first-accept-wins arbitration is atomic. *Audit/security:* every offer, acceptance and manual override audited; billing implications recorded (replacement is billable, the absent guard is not payable). *Acceptance:* Given a guard marked absent 30 minutes before a shift, When the replacement request is raised, Then offers dispatch in waves to ranked candidates and the queue shows the countdown, offers sent, and responses in real time.

**Visitor management (Professional+).** *Purpose:* log who entered a guarded site, when, to see whom — the second most requested client feature after live tracking. *Users/permissions:* guard records entries in the app; Site Manager (client) manages pre-authorisations; Operations Manager configures. *Screens & UI:* AGN-S-250 Visitor log per site (name, phone, purpose, host, vehicle, in/out times, photo, ID captured), AGN-S-251 Pre-authorised list, AGN-S-252 Visitor pass/badge print, AGN-S-253 Visitor analytics (peak hours, repeat visitors, average dwell). *Logic & statuses:* visit `Pending` (expected) → `Active` (checked in) → `Completed` (checked out); overstay alerts; host notification on arrival by SMS/WhatsApp. *Audit/security:* visitor data is third-party personal data with a short, configurable retention and no cross-site visibility; ID images optional and separately permissioned. *Acceptance:* Given a pre-authorised visitor arriving at the gate, When the guard searches their phone number, Then the pre-authorisation is found, check-in takes one tap, and the host receives an arrival notification within 30 seconds.

**Assets (Professional+).** *Purpose:* know what the agency owns, where it is, and who has it. *Users/permissions:* Agency Admin owns the register; supervisors issue and receive; Finance sees value. *Screens & UI:* AGN-S-255 Asset register (category, item, serial/tag, value, purchase date, condition, assigned to guard/site, status), AGN-S-256 Issue/return, AGN-S-257 Maintenance log, AGN-S-258 Loss/damage report, AGN-S-259 Site asset inventory. *Logic & statuses:* asset `Active` → `In Progress` (issued) → `Active` (returned) → `Suspended` (under maintenance) → `Archived` (disposed/written off); loss triggers a recovery-deduction proposal to payroll requiring approval. *Audit/security:* weapon and radio categories carry extra fields and stricter permissions; every issue/return is audited with both parties. *Acceptance:* Given a guard separating from the agency with an unreturned radio, When the full-and-final settlement runs, Then the outstanding asset is listed as a blocker with its recorded value and a proposed recovery line requiring approval.

**Uniform / equipment.** *Purpose:* track the consumables the guard wears and carries, their issue cycle, and their cost. *Users/permissions:* Agency Admin and store keeper role (a permission set, not a new role); guards acknowledge receipt in the app. *Screens & UI:* AGN-S-260 Uniform issue register (item, size, quantity, issue date, next-due date, cost, deduction applicability), AGN-S-261 Stock levels by branch, AGN-S-262 Issue-due list (guards due for replacement per the configured cycle), AGN-S-263 Client-specific uniform requirements. *Logic & statuses:* issue records are `Completed` on guard acknowledgement; stock decrements on issue; low-stock alerts by branch. *Audit/security:* deduction-bearing issues require the guard's in-app acknowledgement as evidence. *Acceptance:* Given a client contract specifying a particular uniform, When a guard is first rostered to that client's site, Then an issue task is created if the guard does not already hold that uniform set.

**Training.** *Purpose:* deliver, record and prove workforce training — a PSARA-relevant and client-demanded capability. *Users/permissions:* Agency HR authors and assigns; guards consume in the app (§18.14); Compliance reports on it. *Screens & UI:* AGN-S-265 Training catalogue (modules with language versions, duration, mandatory flag, validity period), AGN-S-266 Assignment (by role, site, client or individual), AGN-S-267 Completion tracker, AGN-S-268 Certificate register, AGN-S-269 Classroom session log (for in-person training with an attendance sheet and photo evidence). *Logic & statuses:* assignment `Pending` → `In Progress` → `Completed` / `Expired` (validity lapsed); completion can gate deployment to specified post types. *Audit/security:* completion records are compliance evidence and are immutable; certificates are tenant-signed. *Acceptance:* Given a client contract requiring fire-safety training for all deployed guards, When a guard without valid fire-safety training is rostered to that site, Then the assignment warns (or blocks, per policy) and offers one-click assignment of the module.

**Biometric integration (Enterprise).** *Purpose:* reconcile attendance from fingerprint/face terminals installed at large sites with app-based attendance. *Users/permissions:* Agency Admin configures; Operations Manager reconciles. *Screens & UI:* AGN-S-270 Device registry (device id, model, site, last heartbeat, firmware, status), AGN-S-271 Enrolment sync, AGN-S-272 Punch log, AGN-S-273 Reconciliation view (device punches vs app events side by side with a match/mismatch column). *Logic & statuses:* device `Active` / `Suspended` (offline > threshold) / `Archived`; punches import as attendance events with `source = biometric` and are subject to the same approval logic. **Honesty note:** biometric terminal vendors expose heterogeneous interfaces (vendor SDKs, local network APIs, file exports, push protocols); there is no single standard. The working design is a connector-per-vendor model, with the desktop application acting as the local bridge where the device is only reachable on the site LAN (§20.30), and a file-import fallback that always exists `[ASSUMPTION: A-168]`. *Audit/security:* biometric templates are never stored in the platform — only the device's user mapping and punch events (§39). *Acceptance:* Given a site with a registered terminal, When a guard punches at 20:02 and also checks in on the app at 20:03, Then reconciliation shows one attendance record with both sources attached and no double count.

**Expenses (Professional+).** *Purpose:* record what the agency spends so that branch P&L and contract margin are real numbers. *Users/permissions:* any user can submit with receipt; Finance approves; Owner sees all. *Screens & UI:* AGN-S-275 Expense list, AGN-S-276 Submit expense (category, amount, date, branch, site/client attribution, receipt photo), AGN-S-277 Approval queue, AGN-S-278 Category and budget configuration. *Logic & statuses:* `Draft` → `Pending` → `Verified` (approved) / `Rejected` → `Completed` (reimbursed); approved expenses post ledger entries and attribute to branch/contract. *Audit/security:* receipts stored in the vault; approval limits per role. *Acceptance:* Given an expense attributed to a client contract, When the contract margin report runs, Then the expense appears in that contract's cost and reduces its margin.

**Finance (overview).** *Purpose:* the money view of the agency in one place — a role-scoped summary rather than a separate ledger product. *Users/permissions:* Agency Finance and Agency Owner. *Screens & UI:* AGN-S-280 Finance dashboard (cash position, receivables, payables, payroll liability for the current period, month revenue vs cost, branch comparison), AGN-S-281 Branch P&L, AGN-S-282 Contract margin analysis, AGN-S-283 Ledger explorer (double-sided entries, filterable by account, date, entity). *Logic & statuses:* derived; no independent lifecycle. *Audit/security:* the ledger is append-only; adjusting entries require reason and approval. *Acceptance:* Given the ledger explorer filtered to a single invoice, When the entries are listed, Then every movement — invoice raised, payment received, tax component, write-off — appears as a balanced pair.

**Wallet.** *Purpose:* hold prepaid balances — a client's advance/retainer with the agency, and the agency's own prepaid balance for platform-charged services (SMS, verification, premium listing). *Users/permissions:* Agency Finance operates; Owner sees. *Screens & UI:* AGN-S-285 Agency wallet (balance, top-up, usage by service, auto-top-up threshold), AGN-S-286 Client advance balances (per client, with allocation history). *Logic & statuses:* every wallet movement is a double-sided ledger entry in integer paise; balances can never go negative without an explicitly configured credit line. *Audit/security:* all movements audited; top-ups reference the payment gateway transaction. *Acceptance:* Given a client advance of ₹50,000 and an invoice of ₹32,000, When the invoice is allocated against the advance, Then the wallet balance reduces to ₹18,000 and both the invoice and the wallet show the linked allocation.

**Agency settlement.** *Purpose:* settle money between Suraksha and the agency — subscription charges, marketplace fees, and (where Suraksha sub-contracts work to the agency or vice versa) service settlements. *Users/permissions:* Agency Finance views and disputes; Suraksha Finance operates the other side in §22. *Screens & UI:* AGN-S-290 Settlement statements (period, charges, credits, net, status), AGN-S-291 Statement detail with line-level drill-down, AGN-S-292 Dispute raise. *Logic & statuses:* statement `Draft` → `Pending` (issued) → `Verified` (accepted or auto-accepted after the dispute window) → `Completed` (settled); disputes freeze the disputed line only, not the whole statement. *Audit/security:* statements are immutable once issued; disputes and resolutions are audited on both sides. *Acceptance:* Given a settlement statement issued on the 1st with a 7-day dispute window, When no dispute is raised by the 8th, Then the statement auto-accepts and the payable becomes due.

**Notifications.** *Purpose:* one place where the agency controls everything the system sends to its staff, its guards and its clients. *Users/permissions:* Agency Admin manages templates and defaults; every user manages their own preferences. *Screens & UI:* AGN-S-295 Notification centre (in-app stream, severity-grouped, mark-read, snooze), AGN-S-296 Preferences (per event type × channel matrix per user), AGN-S-297 Template manager (per event, per language, per channel, with variable insertion and a preview), AGN-S-298 Delivery log (what was sent to whom, on which channel, delivered/failed). *Logic & statuses:* delivery `Pending` → `Completed` / `Failed` with retry; channel fallback (push → SMS) per event criticality. Architecture and channel policy live in §36. *Audit/security:* template edits audited; client-facing templates require Admin permission because they carry the agency's brand voice. *Acceptance:* Given a guard whose push token is stale, When a replacement offer is dispatched, Then push failure triggers the SMS fallback within 60 seconds and the delivery log shows both attempts.

**Marketing (Professional+).** *Purpose:* let an agency run basic outbound activity without another tool. *Users/permissions:* Agency Sales; Owner approves bulk sends. *Screens & UI:* AGN-S-300 Campaign list, AGN-S-301 Campaign builder (audience from CRM segments, channel email/WhatsApp/SMS, template, schedule), AGN-S-302 Results (sent, delivered, opened, replied, leads created), AGN-S-303 Collateral library (company profile PDF, service brochures, credentials pack generated from real platform data — guard strength, sites served, licences held). *Logic & statuses:* campaign `Draft` → `Pending` (scheduled) → `In Progress` → `Completed` / `Cancelled`. Consent and opt-out handling is mandatory: every recipient list is filtered against an opt-out register, and every message carries an opt-out path. *Audit/security:* bulk sends above a threshold require Owner approval and are audited with the recipient count. *Acceptance:* Given a campaign to 500 contacts of whom 12 have opted out, When the campaign runs, Then 488 messages are sent, the 12 are excluded with the reason logged, and the results screen reports both numbers.

**Website / profile management (Professional+).** *Purpose:* give the agency a credible web presence generated from data it already maintains. *Users/permissions:* Agency Sales/Admin edit; Owner publishes. *Screens & UI:* AGN-S-305 Site editor (template choice, sections: hero, services, coverage, credentials, team, contact, enquiry form), AGN-S-306 Domain settings (agency subdomain by default, custom domain on Enterprise), AGN-S-307 SEO settings, AGN-S-308 Enquiry inbox (feeding CRM leads), AGN-S-309 Publish/preview. *Logic & statuses:* page `Draft` → `Active` (published) → `Archived`; content pulled live from the platform (licences held, states covered, guard strength band) so the website cannot drift from reality — and claims that cannot be substantiated from platform data are simply not offerable as content blocks. *Audit/security:* published claims are audit-logged with the publisher; unverified licence claims cannot be rendered. *Acceptance:* Given an agency whose Gujarat licence expires, When the licence moves to Expired, Then the website's coverage section stops listing Gujarat as covered and the Owner is notified.

**Marketplace integration.** *Purpose:* manage the agency's Trinetra presence from inside the portal (§19). *Users/permissions:* Agency Admin. *Screens & UI:* AGN-S-310 Listing editor (mirrors the Trinetra profile fields with live preview), AGN-S-311 Verification status and required actions, AGN-S-312 Enquiry inbox with response-time tracking, AGN-S-313 Reviews (read, respond, dispute), AGN-S-314 Ranking transparency panel (§19.5) showing the agency's component scores and the specific actions that would improve each. *Logic & statuses:* listing `Draft` → `Pending` (submitted) → `Verified` / `Rejected` → `Suspended`. *Audit/security:* listing edits audited; licence documents are shared with the verification workflow, not duplicated. *Acceptance:* Given the agency's enquiry response rate is 62%, When the ranking panel is opened, Then it shows responsiveness as the lowest-scoring component with the concrete target ("respond to enquiries within 30 minutes to reach 80%").

**Tasks.** *Purpose:* the to-do layer that makes everything else finish — every module can create tasks, and this is where a user sees all of theirs. *Users/permissions:* everyone; tasks respect the underlying record's permissions. *Screens & UI:* AGN-S-315 My tasks (due today, overdue, upcoming), AGN-S-316 Team tasks (managers), AGN-S-317 Task detail (linked entity, checklist, comments, attachments), AGN-S-318 Task templates (e.g. "new site mobilisation" spawning 12 tasks). *Logic & statuses:* `Pending` → `In Progress` → `Completed` / `Cancelled`; overdue escalation to the assigner. *Audit/security:* task completion on compliance-linked tasks is audit evidence. *Acceptance:* Given a new site is activated, When the mobilisation template is applied, Then 12 tasks are created with owners and due dates derived from the site start date.

**Support.** *Purpose:* get the agency help from Suraksha without leaving the product. *Users/permissions:* any user raises; Agency Admin sees all tenant tickets. *Screens & UI:* AGN-S-320 Ticket list, AGN-S-321 New ticket (category, priority, description, attachments, auto-attached diagnostics: plan, module, browser/app version, tenant id), AGN-S-322 Ticket thread, AGN-S-323 Knowledge base search inline before submission, AGN-S-324 Onboarding checklist (Enterprise dedicated onboarding tracker). *Logic & statuses:* `Pending` → `In Progress` → `Completed`; SLA by plan (Enterprise has a contracted SLA per canon §1.4; Starter/Professional response targets are `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-169]`). *Audit/security:* support access to tenant data requires the impersonation controls of §20.3.3. *Acceptance:* Given an Enterprise tenant raising a P1 ticket, When the ticket is created, Then it is routed to the dedicated support queue and the contracted response clock starts and is visible to the agency.

### 20.26 Cross-module conventions

| Convention | Rule |
|---|---|
| Numbering series | Guard codes, employee codes, invoice numbers, incident numbers, contract numbers each have a configurable prefix and a per-tenant, per-financial-year sequence; sequences are gapless for financial documents |
| Effective dating | Rates, salary structures, post strengths, geofences and post orders are all effective-dated; the value in force on any date is always resolvable, which is what makes retrospective correction safe |
| Bulk operations | Every list supports bulk actions with a confirmation naming the record count; bulk actions above 500 records queue as background jobs with a completion notification |
| Import/export | Every master module supports CSV import with a template download, a dry-run validation pass, and an error report; every export is permissioned, watermarked and audit-logged |
| Search | Global search covers all entities; each module has its own scoped search with the same syntax |
| Attachments | Any record can carry attachments, subject to the vault's controls |
| Comments | Any record supports threaded comments with @mentions that generate notifications |
| Soft delete | Nothing operational or financial is hard-deleted (canon §4); `Archived` plus retention |
| Timezone | IST throughout; the operational day boundary is tenant configuration |
| Money | Integer paise; every movement double-sided (canon §4) |
| Idempotency | All write APIs accept an idempotency key (§33) |

### 20.27 Onboarding a new agency tenant (first-run experience)

| Step | What the agency does | System support | Blocking? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Agency profile and branding | Pre-filled from the Trinetra listing if one exists | Yes |
| 2 | Licences | Reuses documents already verified for the marketplace | Yes — nothing operational works without licence geography |
| 3 | Branches | Single branch created by default; multi-branch on Professional+ | No |
| 4 | Users | Invite by phone/email with role presets | No |
| 5 | Clients and sites | CSV import or manual; OCR migration on Enterprise | Yes for deployment |
| 6 | Posts and geofences | Guided per site with a completeness meter | Yes |
| 7 | Guards | CSV import, manual, or OCR; app invites sent in bulk | Yes |
| 8 | Salary structures | Templates provided; agency edits | Yes for payroll |
| 9 | Contracts and rates | From existing agreements | Yes for invoicing |
| 10 | First roster | Guided generation for the current week | — |
| 11 | Go live | Checklist verifying that guards have installed the app and checked in | — |

A persistent setup checklist with a completion percentage sits on the dashboard until complete. Time-to-first-value is the metric that matters: **first guard check-in within 7 days of signup** is the activation definition `[RECOMMENDED]`.

### 20.28 Plan-based feature gating — behaviour rules

| Rule | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Visible but locked | Modules not in the plan appear in the navigation greyed with a lock icon and a tooltip naming the plan that includes them, plus a "See what's included" link. They are never hidden, because agencies must be able to see what they could have |
| Preview | Locked modules open a static preview screen (a screenshot plus a three-bullet description and an upgrade CTA), never a functional partial |
| Data preservation on downgrade | Downgrading never deletes data. Data in a now-locked module becomes read-only and exportable for 90 days, then remains stored but inaccessible until an upgrade restores access `[RECOMMENDED]` |
| Limits | Any usage limits (guards, users, sites) are `D-003`; when set, the UI shows usage vs limit in Settings and warns at 80% and 95% rather than failing silently at 100% |
| "Basic" vs "Full" | Where the canon says Basic (live tracking, payroll, AI, analytics), the difference is specified concretely in §20.29, not left to interpretation |
| Enforcement | Entitlement checks happen server-side on every request; the client's rendering is a convenience, never the control |
| Trial | Trial model is `D-002`; the working assumption is that a trial grants Professional-level access with a visible countdown |

### 20.29 What "Basic" means — exact plan differences

| Capability | Starter (Basic) | Professional (Full) | Enterprise |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Live tracking** | Current on-duty status list + last check-in location per guard, refreshed on a 5-minute poll; site pins on a map; no live guard movement trail, no geofence-breach alerting beyond check-in/out | Real-time map with guard positions during shift, movement trail for the current shift, geofence-breach alerts, patrol route overlay, alert queue with escalation | Full + wall mode, multi-branch consolidated live view, longer location history retention (per §39 limits) |
| **Payroll** | Attendance-driven gross/net with a single salary structure per guard, fixed components, manual overtime entry, payslip PDF, disbursement CSV | Multiple structures, component library, slab and percentage components, automated overtime rules, advances/loans, full-and-final settlement, statutory record generation, maker-checker | Full + custom components, multi-entity payroll, custom export formats |
| **AI assistant** | Read-only queries over the user's own permitted data, Hindi + English, text only, capped daily interactions | Read-only + Recommendation classes, voice + text, 19+ languages, module navigation, drafting (quotations, notices) | Full + Approval-required action proposals within configured limits, custom workflows, higher quotas (all subject to §25/§41) |
| **Analytics** | 12 fixed reports, 30-day charts on the dashboard, CSV export | Full report library, scheduled delivery, analytics workspace dashboards, 24-month history, drill-through | Full + custom report builder, API/BI access, custom retention |
| **Marketplace integration** | Listing management, enquiry inbox, reviews | Same + ranking transparency panel, premium placement eligibility | Same |
| **Multi-branch** | Single branch only | Unlimited branches with consolidated views | Branches + optional region layer |

### 20.30 The desktop application

**Rationale.** A meaningful share of agency offices prefer installed software, run on Windows machines with intermittent internet, and need local hardware connectivity for biometric terminals `[CONFIRMED from the master brief]`. The desktop app is the same Agency Portal, packaged, not a reduced product.

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Platforms & artefacts | Windows `.exe` (NSIS) + `.msi` (managed deployment), x64 and ARM64 · macOS `.dmg` universal (Apple silicon + Intel), signed and notarised · Linux `.deb`, `.rpm`, `.AppImage` |
| Distribution | Trinetra downloads page (§19.3.10); no account needed to download, AP account needed to use |
| Feature parity | 100% of web modules. The desktop adds capabilities; it never removes them |
| Auto-update | Signed update manifest checked on launch and every 6 hours; delta updates where supported; download in background, install on quit with a "Restart to update" prompt; release notes shown after update; Enterprise tenants can pin a version and receive updates through an approved channel; a security-fix version floor can force an update with 7 days' notice |
| Native notifications | OS-native notifications for P0/P1 alerts (SOS, unmanned post, licence expired), with sound, click-to-open-the-record, and a Do-Not-Disturb-respecting mode that still surfaces P0 (configurable) |
| Multi-window | Detachable windows: live map, alert queue, attendance board, and any report can each open as an independent window; window layouts persist per user per machine; multi-monitor positions restored on launch |
| Local session security | Session tokens in the OS credential store (Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / libsecret); app lock after a configurable idle period requiring password/OS biometric; the same MFA and session policies as web; a "clear local data on logout" option; no plaintext cache of sensitive data on disk |
| Offline behaviour | **Not offline-first** (canon §4 restricts that to the Guard App). The desktop app caches the last-loaded views for read-only reference and shows a clear "You are offline — showing data from 14:32" banner; all writes are blocked while offline with a queue-free, honest failure rather than a fake success |
| Biometric device connectivity | The desktop app hosts the local bridge for biometric terminals reachable only on the site/office LAN: device discovery, enrolment sync, punch polling, and upload to the platform. Bridge status appears in the bottom status bar. Vendor connectors are plug-ins; a file-import fallback always exists (§20.25 biometric) |
| Printing | Native print for invoices, payslips, rosters, gate passes, QR checkpoint sheets and ID cards, with print-optimised layouts and printer selection persisted |
| Local file access | Bulk import/export via native file dialogs; scheduled export to a local folder (Enterprise) |
| Deep links | `suraksha://` protocol handler so notifications and emails can open a specific record in the desktop app |
| System integration | Launch on startup (optional), tray icon with alert count, global shortcut to open the alert queue |
| Performance | Cold launch < 4 s; memory footprint budgeted for 8 GB office machines; a "low-resource mode" that disables the live map animation |
| Crash & diagnostics | Local crash reporting with user consent, a diagnostics bundle attachable to support tickets, and a visible app-version and update-channel display |
| Uninstall | Clean uninstall removing cached data; an explicit "keep my local settings" option |

**Platform differences that matter:**

| Behaviour | Windows | macOS | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Installer signing | Authenticode; SmartScreen reputation build-up expected initially | Developer ID signed + notarised; Gatekeeper compliant | Repository signing key published; AppImage unsigned by nature, checksum published |
| Credential storage | Credential Manager | Keychain | libsecret / gnome-keyring, with a documented fallback |
| Notifications | Windows notification centre | Notification Center; Focus modes respected | libnotify; behaviour varies by desktop environment — documented as best-effort |
| Biometric bridge | Widest vendor SDK support | Limited vendor SDK support; USB-serial devices supported | Limited; file-import fallback expected to dominate |
| Auto-update | Silent background, install on quit | Same | AppImage self-update; `.deb`/`.rpm` via repository |
| Multi-monitor | Full support | Full support | Full support, subject to the window manager |

### 20.31 Agency SaaS requirement register

| ID | Requirement | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-AGN-001 | Agency Portal delivered as web, desktop and mobile against one account, one subscription, one dataset | P0 |
| SUR-AGN-002 | Tenant isolation enforced at the data-access layer for every query, with `SURAKSHA-HQ` as a peer tenant | P0 |
| SUR-AGN-003 | Application shell per §20.2: grouped left nav, branch selector, global search, breadcrumbs, right drawer, severity-coloured alerts | P0 |
| SUR-AGN-004 | Branch hierarchy to 4 levels with branch-scoped records, consolidated views and audited branch transfers | P1 |
| SUR-AGN-005 | Guard loan assignments across branches with scoped access and configured cost attribution | P1 |
| SUR-AGN-006 | Thirteen agency roles with branch scoping, delegation, enforced MFA for privileged roles and mandatory reassignment on offboarding | P0 |
| SUR-AGN-007 | Dashboard with the exact 16 named cards of §20.4 and a defined drill-down destination for every card | P0 |
| SUR-AGN-008 | Dashboard card values reconcile exactly with their drill-down list counts | P0 |
| SUR-AGN-009 | Operational day boundary as tenant configuration applied consistently to every date-bounded number | P0 |
