## 21. Agency App

**Product:** Suraksha Agency App (Android + iOS) `[CONFIRMED]` — the Agency Portal companion in admin format, for Agency Owners, Branch Managers, Operations Managers, Field Officers and Supervisors who spend their day away from a desk.

### 21.1 The parity decision

**Decision: the Agency App is monitoring- and approval-optimised, not a full ERP on a phone.** `[CONFIRMED by the master brief: "Full parity lives on web/desktop; the app is optimized for monitoring and approvals."]`

**Rationale:**

| Reason | Detail |
|---|---|
| The jobs differ by context | A person configuring salary structures, building a monthly roster for 300 guards, or reconciling receivables is sitting at a desk with two screens. A person opening the app is standing at a client's gate, in a car, or woken at 02:00 by an SOS. Those are different products wearing the same brand |
| Screen economics | The roster grid, the payroll review grid, the invoice builder and the report viewer are inherently dense two-dimensional surfaces. Squeezing them into 390 px produces something worse than the web app viewed in a mobile browser, which remains available as an escape hatch |
| Error cost | Payroll approval, permission changes and rate edits are high-consequence actions. Restricting them to a desk surface is a deliberate safety control, not a limitation — with the exception of payroll *approval*, which is explicitly supported on mobile with re-authentication because owners travel and payroll cannot wait |
| Build economics | Full parity would roughly double mobile scope and delay the modules that actually matter in the field |

**What this means concretely:**

| Capability class | Mobile treatment |
|---|---|
| Monitor | Full — dashboard, live map, alerts, attendance status, incidents, SOS, guard and client lookup |
| Approve / decide | Full — leave, attendance exceptions, replacements, roster changes, incident closure, expense approval, payroll approval (with re-auth), quotation approval |
| Act quickly | Full — call a guard, raise an incident, assign a replacement, mark a site visit, send a notice, create a task |
| Create simple records | Yes — guard (minimal-first), applicant (rapid entry), lead, client, expense, task, incident |
| Configure | No — settings, roles, permissions, salary structures, workflow rules, geofence editing, contract creation, report builder are **view-only** on mobile with a "Open on desktop" action that emails/deep-links the exact screen |
| Bulk work | No — roster building, payroll computation, invoice generation, migration |
| Escape hatch | Any view-only screen offers "Open full version", which launches the responsive web app in an in-app browser with the session carried over |

### 21.2 Navigation model

**Bottom tab bar (5 tabs, fixed):**

| Tab | Contents |
|---|---|
| **Home** | Role-aware dashboard (§21.3) |
| **Live** | Map + alert queue |
| **Approvals** | Unified approval inbox — the app's highest-value screen |
| **Search** | Global search across guards, employees, clients, sites, posts, invoices, incidents |
| **More** | Modules grid, notifications, AI assistant, profile, settings, support |

**Supporting patterns.** A branch selector lives in the Home header and persists across tabs. A floating action button offers context-appropriate quick actions (Home: Add guard / Raise incident / New task; Live: Raise incident / Call supervisor; Approvals: bulk approve). Push notifications deep-link to the exact record. Deep links use the same `suraksha://` scheme as the desktop app.

### 21.3 Screens that matter on mobile

#### 21.3.1 Dashboard (Home)

A vertically stacked, thumb-reachable subset of §20.4 — not all 16 cards, because a phone dashboard that requires scrolling past ten cards gets ignored:

| Position | Card | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Alert banner** | Any P0 condition (active SOS, unmanned post, expired licence) as a full-width red bar with a single action |
| 2 | **Right-now strip** | Horizontal scroll of 4 tiles: Active guards (with % of rostered) · Guards absent · Open posts · Attendance % |
| 3 | **Needs you** | Count of pending approvals, split by type, one tap into the Approvals tab pre-filtered |
| 4 | **Live snapshot** | A static map thumbnail with site-state counts; tap → Live tab |
| 5 | **Today's exceptions** | List of the 5 most urgent: unfilled shift starting in 2 h, unresolved P1 incident, guard not checked in at a priority site |
| 6 | **This week** | Compact version of the §20.4 section-3 alerts: payroll cut-off, licence expiries, overdue invoices, tender deadlines — each one line with a count |

Role variance: an Agency Owner sees a revenue/receivables line and the payroll cut-off; an Operations Manager sees deployment and incidents first; a Field Officer sees only their assigned sites; a Supervisor sees their team (and in practice uses the Guard App's supervisor tab, §18.16, rather than this app).

#### 21.3.2 Live map

Full-screen map with site pins coloured by state, a bottom sheet listing sites sorted worst-first, and a filter chip row (All / Unmanned / Partial / Alerts). Tapping a pin opens a site sheet: posts, guards on duty with photos and check-in times, last patrol round, open incidents, and one-tap call buttons for the site supervisor and the client contact. Tapping a guard opens the guard sheet: current status, last location and time, battery, phone, today's timeline. Performance is the constraint: pins cluster aggressively, the trail renders only for a selected guard, and the map falls back to a list view on a poor connection.

#### 21.3.3 Approvals inbox

The single screen that justifies the app. One unified list, grouped by type, each row showing enough context to decide without opening it, with swipe-to-approve and swipe-to-reject (reject always requires a reason).

| Approval type | Row context shown | Bulk? |
|---|---|---|
| Attendance exception | Guard, site, shift, exception type, distance outside geofence or face score, evidence thumbnail | Yes, within one exception type |
| Leave request | Guard, dates, type, reason (voice playable), roster impact ("leaves Main Gate night unfilled 12–14 Sep") | No |
| Replacement confirmation | Post, shift, proposed guard, distance, cost implication | Yes |
| Roster change | Post, date, from-guard → to-guard, requester, conflict flags | Yes |
| Overtime approval | Guard, hours, reason, cost | Yes |
| Expense | Submitter, category, amount, receipt thumbnail | Yes |
| Quotation / discount | Client, value, discount %, margin impact | No |
| Payroll run | Period, headcount, total net, variance flag count — approval requires biometric/PIN re-auth and shows the summary before confirming | No |
| Incident closure | Incident, severity, root cause, closure note | No |
| Document verification | Guard, document type, image, extracted values | Yes |

Every approval writes the same audit record as the web equivalent, tagged with `channel = mobile`.

#### 21.3.4 Attendance approvals and daily status

A day-scoped view: site selector → post list → shift cells with state chips, matching the web daily board in information but presented as a list. Tapping a cell opens the attendance detail with the map, the selfie, both timestamps and the integrity flags, and Approve / Reject / Correct actions. A "Not checked in" filter is the default because that is what a manager is looking for.

#### 21.3.5 Roster changes

View the roster by site-day or guard-week; make **individual** changes only — reassign one shift, mark a guard unavailable, trigger a replacement. Bulk generation and monthly grid editing are desktop-only, with a clear "Open on desktop" affordance. Every change made on mobile shows the conflict check result before saving.

#### 21.3.6 Incident and SOS handling

SOS arrives as a critical-priority push that opens a full-screen card even from the lock screen: guard name and photo, site, time, live location on a map, battery, phone number, and three actions — **Call guard**, **Acknowledge**, **Escalate**. Acknowledgement stops the escalation timer (mechanics owned by §24). The incident flow supports creating an incident with photo/voice, assigning it, adding timeline actions, notifying the client with a templated message, and closing with a root cause. The evidence viewer is optimised for one-handed review: swipeable media, playable voice notes with a transcript where available.

#### 21.3.7 Guard lookup and client lookup

Guard lookup: search by name, code or phone → guard card with photo, status, current deployment, compliance chips, today's attendance, phone/WhatsApp buttons, documents (view-only), recent incidents, and quick actions (mark unavailable, request document, send notice). Client lookup: search → client card with active sites, guards deployed now, attendance % this month, outstanding ₹ with ageing, open incidents, contract expiry, contacts with one-tap call, and a "Send service report" action that generates and shares the current month's service delivery report as a PDF — the single most useful thing a manager can do standing in a client's lobby.

#### 21.3.8 Notifications

Grouped by severity and type, with per-type channel preferences, snooze, and a "critical only" mode for off-hours that still allows SOS and unmanned-post alerts through. Notification taps always land on the record, never on a generic list.

#### 21.3.9 AI assistant

Voice and text, in the user's language, bounded by their role and branch scope (§25, §41). On mobile the assistant is disproportionately valuable because typing is expensive: "who is absent at Sunrise today", "how many guards do we have at Client X", "what is pending for my approval", "call the supervisor at Gate 2". Read-only and Recommendation classes on Professional; Approval-required proposals surface as an approval card the human confirms, never as an executed action. The assistant never performs the prohibited action classes of canon §1.7.

### 21.4 Field-officer and supervisor use cases while moving

| Use case | How the app serves it |
|---|---|
| Site visit round (a Field Officer visiting 6 sites a day) | Visit list for the day; at each site, a geo-stamped visit check-in, a short checklist (guards present, uniform, register, equipment, client feedback), photo capture, and instant submission — 90 seconds per site |
| Surprise night check | Live map filtered to night-shift sites, wake-check compliance visible per guard, one-tap call, and the ability to record a night-visit report |
| Handling a client call while driving | Voice query to the AI: "attendance at Metro Tower this week" → spoken answer; or the client lookup card read aloud |
| Guard no-show at 06:00 | Push alert → open post → replacement candidate list ranked by distance → dispatch offers → confirm — under 60 seconds, from bed |
| New client site mobilisation | Create site with GPS-captured location and a geofence drawn on the map at the actual gate (far more accurate than doing it from an office), photograph the post positions, place checkpoint tags and register NFC UIDs on the spot |
| Escalation from a supervisor | Incoming call/notification → incident created with the supervisor's evidence attached → assigned → client notified from a template |
| Approving payroll from a train | Payroll approval card with totals and variance flags, re-auth by biometric, approve — the run releases without the owner returning to the office |

### 21.5 Offline behaviour

The Agency App is **not** offline-first (canon §4 reserves that for the Guard App), but it is not offline-hostile either:

| Behaviour | Specification |
|---|---|
| Cached for read | Last-loaded dashboard, today's attendance summary, the approval list, guard and client cards viewed in the last 7 days, and the site list. All shown with a visible "as of HH:MM" stamp |
| Writes offline | Blocked, with one exception class: **approvals and simple actions are queued** with an explicit "Queued — will send when online" state and a visible queue count, because an approval made in a basement lift should not be lost. Queued approvals are re-validated server-side on send and can fail with a clear reason (e.g. "already approved by someone else") |
| Never queued | Payroll approval, permission changes, anything financial beyond expense approval, and any action whose safe execution depends on current state |
| Map offline | Falls back to the list view with the last known site states |
| Sync | On foreground, on connectivity regained, and on pull-to-refresh; a small indicator shows pending queued actions |
| Honesty rule | The app never shows a success state for an action the server has not confirmed |

### 21.6 Platform differences

| Capability | Android | iOS |
|---|---|---|
| SOS/critical alerts over the lock screen | Full-screen intent with alarm-stream sound | Time-Sensitive notifications; critical alerts require the entitlement — otherwise a prominent banner with sound `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-162 shared with §18]` |
| Biometric re-auth for payroll approval | BiometricPrompt (fingerprint/face) | Face ID / Touch ID |
| Background location for field-officer visit tracking | Foreground service during an active visit only | Always-permission avoided; visit tracking is explicit start/stop only |
| Widgets | Home-screen widget: active guards, absent, open approvals | Home-screen and Lock-screen widgets, same data |
| Share/export | Native share sheet for reports and service PDFs | Same |
| Deep links | App Links | Universal Links |
| Tablet | Two-pane layout (list + detail) on 7"+ | iPad two-pane with the map as a persistent left pane |
| Minimum OS | Android 8.0 | iOS 15 |

Tablet deserves a specific note: many agency owners use a 10" Android tablet as their primary device. The app therefore ships a genuine two-pane tablet layout and, on tablets, unlocks the weekly roster grid in read-write form — the one parity exception, justified by screen area rather than platform.

| D-160 | Is an Aadhaar-based eKYC route available to Suraksha or to agencies, and under what authorised-entity relationship? | Determines whether guard onboarding can be minutes or days, and how identity numbers may be stored | Assume no eKYC; capture masked reference + verification outcome only, document-based | Guard onboarding speed; §18.1, §20.16 data model |
| D-161 | Will the platform offer earned-wage access / salary advance to guards, and on what rail? | Major retention lever for guards, but depends on the unresolved payout-rail decision and on credit exposure | Defer to phase 2; ship advance *recording* only | §18.13, §20.18 |
| D-162 | Will the iOS apps pursue the critical-alert entitlement for wake checks and SOS? | Without it, iOS cannot reliably wake a guard or an owner at night, which forces Android-only night operations | Pursue the entitlement; ship Android-first for night-shift roles meanwhile | §18.8, §18.9, §21.6 |
| D-163 | What contact response-time commitment does Trinetra publish? | A published promise that operations cannot meet damages trust more than no promise | Publish "within 1 working day" only once staffed | §19.3.11 |
| D-164 | Are marketplace leads free to verified agencies, or monetised per lead / by credits? | Determines the marketplace business model and the ranking incentive structure | Free to verified agencies in V1; monetise placement instead | §19.4.5, §52 Monetization |
| D-165 | What is the pricing model for sponsored and premium listings? | Direct revenue line and a governance risk if placement can distort perceived trust | Flat monthly per state slot, verified agencies only, clearly labelled | §19.4.6 |
| D-166 | May an adverse record (blacklisting) on one tenant be surfaced as a signal to another tenant? | Real safety value versus a serious privacy and fairness exposure; cannot be decided by engineering | Do not surface across tenants in V1; revisit with legal and a due-process design | §20.6, §39 Privacy |
| D-167 | How are government identity numbers stored — full, masked, or verification-outcome only? | Determines the blast radius of any breach and the platform's obligations | Store masked reference + verification outcome only, unless a specific lawful basis is configured | §18.1, §20.16, §38, §39 |
| D-168 | Which statutory payroll export formats ship in V1, and for which jurisdictions? | Agencies will judge payroll on whether it produces the files they actually submit | Ship generic register exports + the two most requested formats after customer discovery | §20.18 |
| D-169 | What support response targets apply to Starter and Professional plans? | Sets expectation and staffing; Enterprise SLA is already promised in the plan definition | Starter next-working-day, Professional same-working-day, both business hours | §20.25 Support, §52 |
| A-160 | Guard age range 18–65 is assumed as a configurable agency policy default | Affects onboarding validation and deployment eligibility | Make it configuration with the stated default | §18.1 |
| A-161 | Anti-spoof false-positive rate below 20% is assumed achievable on low-end devices | If wrong, supervisors will disable the controls and the integrity model collapses | Measure in pilot; tune weights as configuration | §18.6 |
| A-162 | Trinetra's early proof blocks assume at least a handful of genuine reference agencies exist at launch | Without them the home page has no credibility layer and the blocks must stay hidden | Hide the blocks until real; never fabricate (live-site problems P1/P2/P4) | §19.3.1 |
| A-163 | No dependable pan-India programmatic PSARA licence-verification API is assumed to exist | The entire verification design and its cost model depend on this | Document-based manual verification as the working design; per-state automation as optional configuration | §19.4.3, §20.17 |
| A-164 | No dependable programmatic interface for police-verification status is assumed | Determines whether verification tracking is manual data entry or integration | Manual-entry tracker with document evidence | §20.16 |
| A-165 | E-invoicing/e-way applicability is assumed to be handled through the agency's chosen provider, not a direct government integration | Affects invoicing scope and Enterprise expectations | Generate the required payload; integrate with the agency's provider | §20.19 |
| A-166 | No uniform public API is assumed for government tender portals | Determines whether tender discovery is a curated pipeline or an integration | Curated corpus + manual entry + per-source connectors where lawful | §20.21 |
| A-167 | OCR on handwritten Indian-language registers is assumed to require human review of most rows | Sets the honest promise for Enterprise migration (10× faster, not automatic) | Design the review grid as the primary surface, not an exception path | §20.22 |
| A-168 | Biometric terminal integration is assumed to require per-vendor connectors with no common standard | Determines Enterprise integration effort and the desktop app's role as a local bridge | Connector-per-vendor plus a universal file-import fallback | §20.25, §20.30 |
| R-160 | Guards disable battery optimisation exemptions or force-stop the app, silently killing wake checks and location | The anti-sleep and tracking promises fail invisibly, and the failure looks like guard misconduct | Daily app-health check, server-side detection of missing heartbeats, and agency-visible device-health reporting | §18.8, §18.15, §20.5 |
| R-161 | Attendance fraud migrates from paper to device-level collusion (shared phones, mock location on rooted devices) | Undermines the core value proposition and client trust | Layered trust scoring, supervisor verification, impossible-travel and duplicate-media detection, periodic audit sampling | §18.6, §20.13 |
| R-162 | Marketplace fills with unverified or fake listings faster than verification capacity, damaging trust at launch | The marketplace's only asset is trust; a bad launch is very hard to recover | Gate indexing and ranking on verification; cap new listings per week to verification throughput | §19.4.3, §19.6 |
| R-163 | Payroll errors in the first cycles cause agency churn and guard unrest | Payroll is the module with the least tolerance for error and the highest emotional stakes | Mandatory parallel run against the agency's existing method for two cycles before cutover; variance flagging; maker-checker | §20.18, §20.27 |
| R-164 | Plan gating drives agencies to work outside the product (spreadsheets for gated modules), reducing data quality everywhere | Partial adoption produces unreliable dashboards, which destroys confidence in the whole product | Keep the data-capture spine (guards, sites, attendance) fully available on Starter; gate analysis and automation, never capture | §20.28, §20.29 |
| R-165 | Desktop and mobile clients drift from the web app as features ship, producing inconsistent behaviour across form factors | Users lose trust when the same action gives different results on different devices | Shared entitlement and business logic server-side; a per-release cross-client parity checklist | §20.30, §21.1 |







## 22. SURAKSHA OPS (ops.surakshaguards.in)

### 22.1 What SURAKSHA OPS is

SURAKSHA OPS is not an admin panel. It is the **operating system of the company**. Everything Suraksha does commercially, operationally, financially and legally either originates in OPS, is approved in OPS, or is audited in OPS. If OPS is down, Suraksha cannot deploy a guard, raise an invoice, verify an agency, publish a price, or answer an SOS. That is the design intent and the availability class it must be built to (see §46 non-functional requirements).

Three things distinguish OPS from a CRUD back-office:

1. **It runs two businesses at once** (§22.2). One is a labour-and-liability business (Suraksha's own guarding operation, tenant `SURAKSHA-HQ`); the other is a software-and-marketplace business (Trinetra + Agency Portal subscriptions across ~35,000 candidate agencies, A-001). These have different unit economics, different risk profiles and different daily rhythms, and OPS must present both without blending them.
2. **It is time-critical, not batch.** Large parts of OPS are a live console with sub-5-second data (§24 Command Center), not a page you refresh. The module list below is ordered so that the operational modules sit above the administrative ones in the navigation, because that is the order of consequence.
3. **It holds the authority model.** Every privileged act in the ecosystem — entitlement override, refund, settlement release, verification approval, licence status change, impersonation, break-glass — is exercised from OPS and is irreversibly recorded there.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-OPS-001 | OPS shall be a single application at `ops.surakshaguards.in` serving all fifteen Suraksha internal roles, with module visibility resolved per role and per geographic scope (§22.26), never per hard-coded page. |
| SUR-OPS-002 | OPS shall present Suraksha's own guarding operation and the SaaS/marketplace business as two distinct top-level "business contexts" with a persistent context switcher in the top bar; a user with rights to only one context never sees the switcher. |
| SUR-OPS-003 | OPS shall never render a module a role cannot access, including as a disabled item — absence, not greying, is the rule (avoids leaking organisational structure to junior staff). |
| SUR-OPS-004 | Every state-changing action in OPS shall emit an Audit Log entry containing actor, role, scope, target entity, before/after diff, request IP, device, session ID, and — where the action was AI-proposed — the AI Interaction ID (see §25.10). |
| SUR-OPS-005 | OPS shall enforce MFA for every internal role without exception; there is no "MFA optional" internal account (canon §4 permits enforcement for staff, this section elects it). |

#### 22.1.1 Global shell

| Element | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Left navigation | Nine collapsible groups: Command · Operations · Demand · Workforce · Trust & Compliance · Money · Growth · Platform & Content · Administration. Pinned favourites at top (user-configurable, max 8). |
| Top bar | Business-context switcher (Suraksha Operations / SaaS & Marketplace) · Scope selector (National → State → City → Branch, filtered to the user's permitted scope) · Global search · Alert bell (live count of P0/P1 in the user's scope) · AI launcher (§25) · User menu. |
| Global search | Single box, entity-typed results: Guard, Client, Agency, Site, Post, Booking, Quotation, Contract, Invoice, Ticket, Incident, Document, Employee. Query by name, phone, ID, licence number, GSTIN, invoice number, vehicle number. Results are scope-filtered before ranking, never after. |
| Density | Desktop-first, 32px table rows, 12-column grid, keyboard-first (`/` search, `g` then module letter to navigate, `j/k` row movement, `Enter` open, `Esc` close). Component vocabulary from §27. |
| Breadcrumbs | Mandatory below the top bar on every screen deeper than a module root. |
| Empty/error states | Every list has a defined empty state naming the first action; every failed fetch shows the last-known-good timestamp rather than a blank panel. |

### 22.2 The dual-business nature

| Dimension | Suraksha Operations (B2C/B2B guarding) | SaaS & Marketplace (Trinetra + Agency Portal) |
|---|---|---|
| Tenant | `SURAKSHA-HQ` (a tenant like any other, with privileges) | Many tenants, one per subscribed agency |
| Revenue object | Contract → Deployment → Invoice (₹18,500+/guard/month unarmed, ₹38,000+ armed; plan cards ₹18k/₹22k/custom) | Subscription → Plan → Invoice (Starter ₹5,000 · Professional ₹10,000 · Enterprise negotiated) |
| Cost object | Guard payroll, supervisor cost, equipment, travel | Infrastructure, support, onboarding effort |
| Daily rhythm | Shift-start sweep, night wake-checks, morning attendance close (§24.12) | Trials expiring, dunning runs, verification queue, moderation queue |
| Primary risk | Life-safety, unstaffed posts, PSARA exposure | Churn, unverified listings, tenant data isolation |
| Owning roles | National/State/City Operations, Command Center Operator | Sales, Support, Verification, Marketing |
| Shared roles | Super Admin, Founder/Management, Finance, Compliance, Auditor see both | |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-OPS-006 | Every OPS list, report and KPI shall carry an explicit business-context attribution; a mixed figure (e.g. total revenue) shall always be decomposable into guarding revenue and SaaS revenue in one click. |
| SUR-OPS-007 | Suraksha's own guarding operation shall use the same tenant-scoped data path as agency tenants (`tenant_id = SURAKSHA-HQ`), with no special-case query branch, so that a defect in tenant isolation is detected by Suraksha's own usage. |
| SUR-OPS-008 | A user scoped to the SaaS context shall be unable to read `SURAKSHA-HQ` operational rows (guards, attendance, incidents) and vice-versa, unless their role grants both contexts. |
| SUR-OPS-009 | `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-140]` Whether Suraksha's own guarding operation may also subcontract deployments to marketplace agencies (creating a Suraksha-as-client relationship over another tenant). The platform shall model the relationship as a first-class "Subcontract" object regardless of the commercial decision. |

### 22.3 Suraksha's own branch and city hierarchy

Suraksha's internal geography is a four-level tree, and it is the scoping axis for nearly every permission in §22.26.

```
National (HQ)
└── State  (PSARA state licence boundary — one licence object per state)
    └── City / District  (district licence where applicable)
        └── Branch  (physical office; owns a team, guards, clients, P&L)
            └── Site → Post → Shift
```

| Level | Owns | Head role | KPI rolls up to |
|---|---|---|---|
| National | Policy, pricing floors, national contracts, all licences | National Operations | Founder/Management |
| State | State PSARA licence, state clients, state compliance filings | State Operations | National |
| City/District | District licence (where used), city client base, local recruitment | City Operations | State |
| Branch | Guards, supervisors, sites, local finance, branch P&L | Branch Manager (an Employee record holding the City Operations role scoped to one branch) | City |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-OPS-010 | Every operational entity (Guard, Site, Post, Booking, Contract, Incident, Invoice) shall carry `branch_id`, and branch shall resolve to exactly one city, state and national node. |
| SUR-OPS-011 | Scope shall be enforced server-side on every query. A City Operations user requesting a guard outside their city shall receive 404, not 403 (existence must not leak). |
| SUR-OPS-012 | A user may hold multiple scope grants (e.g. two cities). The scope selector shall allow "All my scopes" as an explicit aggregate view, and every export shall stamp the scope it was produced under. |
| SUR-OPS-013 | Branch P&L shall be computed from ledger entries tagged with `branch_id` (revenue: invoices raised for that branch's contracts; cost: payroll runs, settlements, expenses), never from a manual allocation spreadsheet. |
| SUR-OPS-014 | Branch creation shall require: legal address, PSARA licence linkage (state and, where applicable, district), assigned branch head, GST place-of-supply, opening date, and a serviceable-pincode set. A branch cannot be Activated with an expired or missing licence linkage (BR-002). |
| SUR-OPS-015 | Branch closure shall be a workflow, not a delete: reassign guards, transfer contracts, settle receivables, final payroll, then `status=Archived` with a retained ledger. |

### 22.4 Executive Dashboard — full specification

**Purpose.** The first screen a Founder/Management, National Operations or Super Admin user sees. It answers, in under five seconds of reading: *is anyone in danger, is any post unmanned, is money moving, is the SaaS business growing, and is anything about to expire that could stop us trading.*

**Users.** Founder/Management, Super Admin, National Operations (national band), State Operations and City Operations (same cards, scoped), Finance (money band only), Auditor (read-only, all bands).

**Layout.** Six named bands, top to bottom, in descending order of consequence. Each band is a row of cards; each card is a fixed 3-column tile with: title, primary number, delta vs comparison period, sparkline (7 or 30 points), and a status dot (green/amber/red per its own threshold). Every card is clickable and every click lands on a **pre-filtered list**, never on a generic module root.

#### 22.4.1 Band A — Operations Now (refresh 15s)

| # | Card name | Primary number | Formula / source | Threshold (amber / red) | Drill-down target |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Guards On Duty Now | count | Assignments with an open Attendance check-in and no check-out, `server_received_time` within shift window | — | Live Operations, filtered `status=On Duty` |
| A2 | Required vs Deployed | `deployed / required` | Sum of Post required strength for shifts active now vs A1 | <98% / <95% | Unstaffed Posts list |
| A3 | Unstaffed Posts | count | Active shifts where deployed < required and no Replacement in progress | ≥1 / ≥5 | Post list, `gap=true`, sorted by client tier |
| A4 | Late Arrivals Today | count | Attendance check-ins later than shift start + grace (default 15 min) | ≥3% / ≥7% of shifts | Attendance, `flag=Late`, today |
| A5 | Open P0/P1 Alerts | count, split | Command Center alert queue, `severity in (P0,P1)`, `status != Resolved` | any P1 / any P0 | Command Center incident queue (§24) |
| A6 | Wake-Check Compliance | % | Acknowledged wake checks ÷ scheduled wake checks, current night window | <95% / <90% | Wake Check log, `status=Missed` |
| A7 | Offline Devices | count | Guard App devices with no heartbeat for > 20 min during an active shift | ≥2 / ≥5 | Device list, `state=Offline` |
| A8 | SOS in last 24h | count | SOS events, rolling 24h | ≥1 / ≥3 | SOS register |

#### 22.4.7 Executive Dashboard — remaining depth points

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| 3 Permissions | Band visibility per role in §22.26. Finance sees D + F; Compliance sees E + F; Marketing sees C1–C3 and campaign cards only; Auditor sees all read-only with an "audit view" watermark. |
| 5 UI detail | Card = 240×132px tile; number in display-L; delta chip green/red with arrow; sparkline 7-point default, 30-point on hover; status dot with tooltip naming the threshold ("Red because 90+ ageing ₹18.2L > ₹15L"). Bands collapsible and reorderable per user, persisted. |
| 6 UX flow | Land → scan bands → click a red dot → arrive at a pre-filtered list with the filter chips visible and removable → act or assign. "Explain this card" opens the AI panel with the card's definition and its query (§25.2.4). |
| 7 Fields | Each card is defined by: `card_id`, `title`, `metric_query_id`, `comparison_window`, `amber_threshold`, `red_threshold`, `drilldown_route`, `required_permission`, `refresh_seconds`, `business_context`. |
| 8 Validation | Thresholds must be numeric and amber must be less severe than red; a card whose query exceeds its latency budget renders a stale badge with the last successful timestamp instead of a spinner. |
| 9 Business logic | All cards are computed from the analytics read model (§42), never by scanning transactional tables at request time. Money cards read the ledger, never the invoice table alone. |
| 10 Backend logic | Metric definitions live in a versioned registry; changing a formula creates a new version and the card footer shows `formula v3, effective 2026-07-01` so historical screenshots remain explicable. |
| 11 Status lifecycle | Not applicable to the dashboard itself; each card inherits the lifecycle of the entity it counts. |
| 12 Notifications | Cards do not notify. Crossing a red threshold raises an alert through the Command Center alerting path (§24.6) so there is exactly one alerting mechanism. |
| 13 Integrations | Razorpay (collections), GST invoicing service, analytics store, alerting bus. |
| 14 Security | Every metric query is scope-injected server-side; a screenshot-safe mode blanks absolute money values for demo/screen-share use. |
| 15 Audit | Dashboard views are logged at the module level (who opened, which scope, when) for the Auditor role; individual card renders are not logged. |
| 16 Edge cases | New branch with no data (cards show "No data since <activation date>", not zero); metric query timeout; a card whose underlying entity is retired (card auto-hides after 30 days of null with a maintenance flag). |
| 17 QA | Golden-dataset test: a fixed fixture month must produce exactly the documented numbers for all 38 cards; threshold colour tests at boundary ±1. |
| 18 Acceptance | **Given** 12 active shifts requiring 30 guards and 28 checked in, **When** an Ops user opens the dashboard, **Then** A2 shows `28/30` with a red dot and A3 shows `2`, and clicking A3 lists exactly those two Posts with client name, shift end time and the replacement action. |
| 19 Analytics events | `ops_dashboard_view`, `ops_card_click{card_id}`, `ops_card_explain{card_id}`, `ops_scope_change`, `ops_context_switch`. KPI: median time from dashboard load to first drill-down (target <20s), % of P0 alerts first seen on dashboard vs Command Center. |
| 20 Future scalability | Card registry is data-driven, so new cards ship without a release; per-role default layouts; `[FUTURE]` a TV/wallboard rendering of Bands A and E for office display. |

### 22.5 Command Center entry

OPS contains the entry point to the Command Center, but the Command Center is specified in **§24** and owns all escalation, SOS and alert mechanics. OPS provides: the launcher, the operator assignment roster, the seat/shift configuration, and the post-incident review workspace.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-OPS-016 | The OPS left navigation shall carry "Command Center" as the first item for Command Center Operator, National/State/City Operations, Founder/Management and Super Admin, opening the console described in §24.4. |
| SUR-OPS-017 | OPS shall hold the Command Center staffing roster (seat, operator, shift, scope) and shall block a shift start if no operator is assigned to a seat covering a scope with active deployments (§24.3). |
| SUR-OPS-018 | Post-incident reviews raised in §24.9 shall be worked in OPS under Incidents, with the review outcome writing back to the incident record. |

### 22.6 Live Operations (major module — 20-point)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| 1 Purpose | The always-on operational picture for a scope: who is on duty, where, and what is wrong right now. Distinct from §24 in that Live Operations is the *management* view (any ops manager, any time) while the Command Center is the *manned watch* view with alert ownership. |
| 2 Users | National/State/City Operations (primary), Command Center Operator, Founder/Management, Support (read), Auditor (read). |
| 3 Permissions | Read for all above within scope; actions (force check-out, mark present, initiate replacement, dispatch supervisor) restricted to City Operations and above, and to Command Center Operator for alert-linked actions only. |
| 4 Screens | Live map · Guard list · Site list · Shift board (timeline) · Exception panel · Guard detail drawer · Site detail drawer. |
| 5 UI detail | Map with clustered pins coloured by state (green on duty, amber late, red absent/alerting, grey offline). Left rail: filters (state/city/branch/client/shift/guard category/agency). Right rail: exception panel listing the seven exception types with counts. Shift board: horizontal 24h timeline, one row per Post, blocks per Assignment, gaps rendered as hatched red. |
| 6 UX flow | Filter to scope → scan exception panel → click exception → guard/site drawer opens with last known GPS, last patrol scan, last wake check, phone number, supervisor contact → act (call, message, request replacement, escalate to Command Center). |
| 7 Fields | Per guard pin: guard ID, name, photo, category (armed/unarmed/PSO/bouncer/supervisor), site, post, shift window, check-in time, last ping time, battery %, accuracy radius, geofence state. |
| 8 Validation | A GPS ping with accuracy worse than 100m is rendered as a circle, not a pin, and never triggers a geofence violation on its own (§24.5). |
| 9 Business logic | Guard state machine: Scheduled → Checked In → On Duty → On Break → Checked Out; exception states Late, Absent, Geofence-Out, Offline, Wake-Missed layered on top. Absent is asserted only after grace + no-contact window (default 30 min after shift start). |
| 10 Backend logic | Location ingest is a separate high-write path (§34): device batches pings every 60s on duty (configurable per plan/site), server stores last-known plus a downsampled track; map subscribes to a scope-filtered stream, not to raw pings. |
| 11 Status lifecycle | Uses the canonical vocabulary; exceptions resolve when the underlying condition clears or an operator marks them handled with a reason code. |
| 12 Notifications | Live Operations does not notify directly; conditions raise alerts through §24. |
| 13 Integrations | Map tiles, reverse geocoding, telephony click-to-call, WhatsApp deep link. |
| 14 Security | Location of a guard is personal data (§39). Access is scope-limited, purpose-logged, and historical track replay beyond 24h requires a stated reason recorded in the audit log. |
| 15 Audit | Every replay request, every force-check-out, every manual attendance override with actor and reason. |
| 16 Edge cases | Guard's phone dead (device offline but guard present — supervisor can vouch, creating a Vouched Attendance record flagged for review); site with no mobile coverage (site flagged `low_connectivity`, offline-tolerance window extended per site); two guards sharing a device (blocked by device binding, §38). |
| 17 QA | Simulated fleet of 500 guards; verify map render <2s, exception counts match fixture, no cross-scope pin leakage. |
| 18 Acceptance | **Given** a guard whose last ping was 25 minutes ago during an active shift, **When** an Ops user opens Live Operations, **Then** the pin is grey, the guard appears in the Offline exception with "last seen 25 min ago", and the drawer offers Call, Message Supervisor and Raise Alert. |
| 19 Analytics | `liveops_view`, `liveops_exception_open{type}`, `liveops_action{type}`; KPI: mean time from exception appearance to first operator action. |
| 20 Future | Route/patrol heat maps; predictive absence flags fed by §25.13; multi-monitor detached map window in the desktop context. |

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| 1 Purpose | The single record of every buyer of Suraksha guarding services and everything about them: sites, contracts, money, service history, sentiment, risk. |
| 2 Users | Sales (own accounts), City/State/National Operations, Support, Finance, Founder/Management, Auditor. |
| 3 Permissions | Create: Sales, City Ops+. Edit commercial terms: Sales with approval per §22.16.3. Edit operational data: Ops. View financials: Finance, Founder/Management, Auditor, and Sales for own accounts. Delete: never — Archive only. |
| 4 Screens | Client list · Client 360 (Overview, Sites, Contracts, Bookings, Deployments, Invoices & Wallet, Tickets & Complaints, Documents, Contacts, Activity, SLA) · Create/Edit · Merge duplicates · Client health view. |
| 5 UI detail | Client list columns: Name, Type badge (Individual / Corporate / Government), City, Active guards, Contract value/month, Receivables, Health dot, Owner. Client 360 header: name, type, tier (Tier 1/2/3 by contract value bands), health dot, SLA state, quick actions (New booking, New quotation, Raise ticket, Add site, Open ledger). |
| 6 UX flow | Search → open 360 → the Overview answers "what do we do for them, are they paying, are they happy" without scrolling: three summary cards (Deployment, Money, Sentiment) plus a 90-day activity timeline. |
| 7 Fields | Common: client_id, type, legal name, display name, primary contact, phone, email, billing address, city/state, GSTIN (mandatory for Corporate/Government, optional Individual), PAN, tier, owner (Sales), branch, status. Corporate: CIN, industry vertical, procurement contact, PO requirement flag, payment terms (Net 15/30/45), escalation matrix contacts. Government: department, office, tender reference, work order number, budget head, EMD/PBG references, bill submission portal, GeM/PFMS identifiers where applicable. |
| 8 Validation | GSTIN checksum format validation; duplicate detection on phone + GSTIN + legal name fuzzy match at creation with a merge prompt; payment terms restricted to configured values; government clients require a linked work order before a contract can be Activated. |
| 9 Business logic | Client type drives: invoicing template, payment terms default, escalation matrix requirement, allowed booking path (Government cannot self-serve checkout — quote/tender path only), and SLA template. Tier drives priority in replacement and alert routing (§24.6). |
| 10 Backend logic | Client is the parent of Sites; Sites parent Posts. Deleting is blocked while any Active contract or non-zero ledger balance exists. Health score = weighted (payment punctuality 30%, SLA compliance 30%, complaint rate 20%, review score 20%), recomputed nightly. |
| 11 Status lifecycle | Draft → Pending (KYB/docs) → Active → Suspended (non-payment, per BR/dunning) → Archived. |
| 12 Notifications | Client-facing: onboarding welcome, contract activation, invoice, guard assigned, incident report. Internal: health drop below 60, receivable crossing 60 days, contract expiring 60/30/7 days. |
| 13 Integrations | GST validation service `[ASSUMPTION: A-140]` (availability of a reliable GSTIN validation API; fallback = format check + manual verification), Razorpay customer object, WhatsApp Business, e-mail (Zoho). |
| 14 Security | Client contact PII is masked in list views for Marketing and Recruitment roles; full reveal requires purpose selection and is logged. |
| 15 Audit | Commercial term changes (rate, payment terms, tier), contact changes, status changes, document access, merge operations (with full pre-merge snapshot retained). |
| 16 Edge cases | Individual upgrading to Corporate (type change permitted once, with new GSTIN; historical invoices remain under the old type); the same legal entity buying in three cities (one client, three branches, branch-tagged contracts); government client paying through a portal Suraksha cannot reconcile automatically (manual receipt entry with reference and attachment mandatory). |
| 17 QA | Duplicate merge does not orphan invoices; scope isolation across branches; government client blocked from self-serve checkout. |
| 18 Acceptance | **Given** a Corporate client with a 65-day-old unpaid invoice, **When** the Client 360 opens, **Then** the Money card shows the ageing bucket in red, the health dot is amber, and the dunning stage is named with the next scheduled action and date. |
| 19 Analytics | `client_create`, `client_merge`, `client_view`, `client_health_change`; KPIs: clients by tier, revenue concentration (top-10 share), churned clients per quarter. |
| 20 Future | Client-side portal SSO federation for large corporates; automated KYB via registry lookups; account-based scoring for upsell. |

### 22.8 Agencies — major module

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| 1 Purpose | The registry of every agency in the ecosystem: marketplace-listed, trial, subscribed, suspended or rejected. This module is where Suraksha's SaaS business lives operationally. |
| 2 Users | Sales, Support, Verification, Compliance, Finance, Founder/Management, Super Admin, Auditor. |
| 3 Permissions | Verification may change verification state only. Sales may change plan and commercial terms subject to approval. Finance may act on billing state. Only Super Admin may suspend a tenant's data access. |
| 4 Screens | Agency list · Agency 360 (Profile, Licences, Verification, Subscription, Usage, Billing, Marketplace listing, Support, Settlements, Users, Audit) · Verification workspace · Subscription administration · Dunning queue · Usage & entitlement view. |
| 5 UI detail | List columns: Agency name, State(s), Licence status chip, Verification chip, Plan chip, MRR, Guards under management, Last active, Health. Agency 360 header: verified badge, plan, renewal date, account owner, quick actions (Impersonate — §22.23, Change plan, Add entitlement override, Open ticket, Suspend). |
| 6 UX flow | Verification: queue → open submission → side-by-side document viewer and extracted fields (OCR, §25.13) → approve/reject with reason → listing state updates → agency notified. Subscription: 360 → Subscription tab → change plan (immediate/next cycle) → proration preview → confirm → ledger entries created. |
| 7 Fields | Agency: agency_id (tenant_id), legal name, brand name, registered address, states of operation, districts, GSTIN, PAN, CIN, owner name/phone/email, guard strength band, years operating, services offered, bank details (for settlements), listing status, verification status, plan, subscription status, billing contact, account owner. |
| 8 Validation | At least one licence per declared state of operation before verification can pass; bank account verified by penny-drop before any settlement release `[ASSUMPTION: A-141]`; GSTIN required for Professional and Enterprise plans. |
| 9 Business logic | Verification outcome gates marketplace visibility and the "Verified by Suraksha" badge. Licence expiry triggers BR-002 restrictions. Plan determines entitlements; entitlement overrides are additive and time-boxed. |
| 10 Backend logic | Agency = tenant. Tenant provisioning creates the tenant schema/rows, the default role set, the owner user, and the subscription record atomically; failure rolls back the whole provisioning. |
| 11 Status lifecycle | Listing: Draft → Pending → Verified → Rejected → Suspended → Archived. Subscription: Draft → Pending → Active → Expiring → Suspended → Cancelled → Archived. |
| 12 Notifications | Verification result, licence expiring at 90/60/30/7 days, invoice raised, payment failed (dunning ladder), plan changed, suspension warning, suspension applied, restoration. |
| 13 Integrations | Razorpay subscriptions/mandates, PSARA licence verification — **no reliable public API is assumed** `[ASSUMPTION: A-142]`; the platform ships a manual/assisted verification workflow (document upload + officer check + optional state-portal reference number) and treats any future API as an accelerator, not a dependency. |
| 14 Security | Suraksha staff never see tenant operational data by default; access is via impersonation (§22.23) or aggregate usage counters only. |
| 15 Audit | Every verification decision with evidence references; every plan and entitlement change with before/after; every suspension with authoriser and reason; every impersonation session. |
| 16 Edge cases | Agency operating in a state whose licence lapses mid-cycle; agency disputing a rejection (appeal path with a second reviewer); agency requesting deletion (data export then tenant archive, per §39 retention); duplicate agency registration by two employees of the same firm (merge with tenant consolidation — high-risk, Super Admin only). |
| 17 QA | Tenant isolation tests on every agency-scoped endpoint; plan-change proration arithmetic to the paise; suspension actually blocks login and API keys. |
| 18 Acceptance | **Given** an agency whose Gujarat licence expired yesterday, **When** Compliance opens the Agency 360, **Then** the licence chip is red, BR-002 restrictions are listed explicitly (which functions are blocked), and the marketplace listing shows "Verification lapsed" to the public rather than remaining "Verified". |
| 19 Analytics | `agency_verify_decision`, `agency_plan_change`, `agency_suspend`, `entitlement_override_create`; KPIs: verification TAT, activation rate, MRR by state, override prevalence. |
| 20 Future | Automated licence renewal reminders with document pre-fill; agency scoring from operational telemetry to power marketplace ranking. |

#### 22.8.1 Agency subscription administration

| Function | Specification |
|---|---|
| Plan change (upgrade) | Effective immediately by default; proration = unused days of old plan credited, new plan charged pro-rata for the remainder; entitlements unlock at commit; ledger: debit receivable, credit deferred revenue. Requires Sales role; no approval needed for upgrade. |
| Plan change (downgrade) | Effective at next cycle only. A pre-flight check lists entitlements that will be lost and the data that becomes read-only (e.g. tenders, CRM on leaving Professional). Requires Sales + Finance acknowledgement. Data is never deleted on downgrade — it becomes inaccessible until re-upgrade. |
| Entitlement override | A named, time-boxed grant of a feature outside the plan (e.g. "Tenders module, 30 days, pilot"). Fields: entitlement key, reason, start, end, approver, revenue impact (₹0 or negotiated). Max default duration 90 days; longer requires Founder/Management. Auto-expires with a 7-day warning to the account owner and the agency. |
| Trial administration | Trial start/extend/convert/expire. Extension max twice, 15 days each `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-141]` pending the trial model (D-002). Every extension records a reason and approver. |
| Dunning ladder | Stage 0 payment due → Stage 1 (D+1) in-app + email reminder → Stage 2 (D+3) email + SMS + WhatsApp, account owner notified → Stage 3 (D+7) feature soft-limit: exports and new user invites disabled, banner shown → Stage 4 (D+14) suspension: login blocked for all tenant users except the Agency Owner, who sees a payment screen only; API keys disabled → Stage 5 (D+45) subscription Cancelled, tenant Archived, data retained per §39 and exportable on request for the retention window. |
| Suspension (manual) | Reasons: non-payment, fraud suspicion, licence lapse, abuse, legal request. Requires Super Admin plus a second approver (Compliance or Founder/Management) for any reason other than non-payment. Suspension is reversible; every suspension writes a notice to the agency with the reason category (not free text) and the restoration condition. |
| Restoration | On payment or condition clearance, restoration is automatic within 5 minutes; entitlements return to the plan state at suspension, not to any prior override. |
| Refund / credit note on subscription | Finance-only; requires reason code and links to the ledger; a credit note never edits the original invoice (BR-003). |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-OPS-019 | Every entitlement in the platform shall be a named key evaluated at request time from `plan_entitlements ∪ active_overrides`; no code shall test the plan name directly. |
| SUR-OPS-020 | Dunning stage transitions shall be executed by a scheduled job with idempotency keys, shall be visible on the Agency 360, and shall be pausable per agency by Finance with a reason (e.g. cheque in transit) for a maximum of 15 days. |
| SUR-OPS-021 | Suspension shall never destroy tenant data, and a suspended tenant's Agency Owner shall always retain the ability to export their own data at least once per suspension episode. |

#### 22.8.2 Enterprise deal desk

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Manage the "Contact Sales" pipeline for Enterprise SaaS deals and large guarding contracts, where price is negotiated and never publicly displayed. |
| Board stages | Qualified → Discovery → Solution & Scoping → Pricing Approval → Contracting → Onboarding → Won / Lost. |
| Deal record | Opportunity ID, agency or client, deal type (SaaS Enterprise / Guarding contract / Tender), scope (guards, sites, states, users), requested entitlements, proposed price, floor price, discount %, term, payment terms, SLA level, onboarding effort estimate, competitor, close date, probability, owner. |
| Approval matrix | Discount ≤10% and term ≥12 months → Sales lead. Discount 10–25% → Founder/Management. Discount >25%, non-standard SLA, custom liability terms, or price below the configured floor → Founder/Management **and** Finance, both recorded. |
| Pricing floor | Configured per plan and per guarding service lane; a quotation below floor cannot be sent — it can only be submitted for approval. |
| Artefacts | Proposal generated from a template with the negotiated entitlement list; SLA annexure; onboarding plan; data-migration scope (OCR migration for Enterprise, §25.13). |
| On Won | Creates the subscription with the negotiated entitlement set as explicit overrides, creates the onboarding project with a named owner and milestone dates, and schedules the first QBR. |
| On Lost | Mandatory loss reason from a fixed list (price, feature gap, competitor, timing, no budget, no decision) plus free text; feeds the win/loss analytics used by product. |
| Audit | Every approval, every price change, every version of the sent proposal is retained immutably. |

### 22.9 Workforce modules

#### 22.9.1 Guards (major module — 20-point)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| 1 Purpose | The registry of every guard in Suraksha's own operation (and, for marketplace/subcontract cases, the read-only reference to agency guards): identity, verification, skills, deployment history, performance, pay. |
| 2 Users | HR, Recruitment, City/State/National Operations, Verification, Compliance, Finance (pay only), Command Center Operator (read + contact), Auditor. |
| 3 Permissions | Create: Recruitment/HR. Verify documents: Verification only. Deploy: Operations. Blacklist: City Ops proposal + Compliance approval. Salary structure: HR + Finance. View full KYC documents: Verification, Compliance, HR (logged reveal). |
| 4 Screens | Guard list · Guard 360 (Profile, Documents & KYC, Verification, Skills & Training, Deployment history, Attendance, Performance, Leave, Pay, Devices, Incidents, Notes) · Onboarding wizard · Bulk import · Blacklist register. |
| 5 UI detail | List columns: Photo, Name, Guard ID, Category, Branch, Current site, Status chip, Document compliance dot, Rating, Reliability score. Guard 360 header: photo, name, category badge (Unarmed / Armed / PSO / Bouncer / Supervisor / Specialised), verification badge, current assignment, quick actions (Assign, Replace, Call, Mark leave, Raise incident). |
| 6 UX flow | Onboarding wizard: Identity → Documents → Verification submission → Skills & training → Bank & salary → Kit issue → Activation. The guard cannot reach `Active` until mandatory documents are `Verified` and police verification is at least `In Progress` with an override reason if deployed early (override requires Compliance). |
| 7 Fields | guard_id, name, DOB, gender, blood group, photo, phone (login identity), alternate phone, permanent & current address, Aadhaar/ID reference (tokenised, §39), PAN, bank account + IFSC, category, height/weight (client requirement matching), languages spoken, ex-servicemen flag, licence-linked weapon details (armed only), PSARA training certificate, police verification, medical fitness, uniform size, kit issued, emergency contact, joining date, branch, supervisor, salary structure, reliability score, rating. |
| 8 Validation | Phone unique across the guard population; bank account penny-drop before first payout; armed category requires a valid weapon-related document set as configured for the jurisdiction (configurable rule set, never hard-coded); age within configured employable band; duplicate detection on phone + ID token + face match at onboarding. |
| 9 Business logic | Reliability score (0–100) = 40% attendance punctuality, 25% wake-check/patrol compliance, 20% incident-free days, 15% client rating, trailing 90 days, recomputed nightly; feeds the allocation engine (§25.15). Blacklisting blocks allocation platform-wide and requires a recorded reason category and evidence. |
| 10 Backend logic | Guard is an identity plus an employment record; a guard leaving and rejoining reuses the identity and creates a second employment period. Documents are stored encrypted with per-document access policy. |
| 11 Status lifecycle | Draft → Pending (verification) → Active → Suspended → Archived (exit). Deployment sub-state: Available · Deployed · On Leave · Off Roll. |
| 12 Notifications | Document expiring 60/30/7 days; verification result; assignment; roster change; payslip; disciplinary notice. |
| 13 Integrations | Face-match/liveness for attendance (§37), bank verification, document OCR (§25.13), background-verification vendor `[ASSUMPTION: A-143]`. |
| 14 Security | KYC document view requires purpose selection and is logged with the document ID; downloads are watermarked with the viewer's name and timestamp; bulk export of guard PII requires Super Admin plus a second approver. |
| 15 Audit | Verification decisions, blacklist decisions, salary changes, document views/downloads, deployment overrides, identity edits. |
| 16 Edge cases | Guard with no smartphone (attendance by supervisor vouching + biometric device where present); guard working across two branches in a month (payroll split by attendance branch tagging); guard whose ID document is genuine but name differs across documents (name-variance workflow with a canonical name decision); rehire of a previously blacklisted guard (blocked; requires Compliance unblock with reason). |
| 17 QA | Cannot activate without mandatory documents; cannot allocate a blacklisted or licence-lapsed guard (§25.15 veto); PII masking by role. |
| 18 Acceptance | **Given** a guard whose PSARA training certificate expires in 20 days, **When** the guard list is filtered by document compliance, **Then** the guard appears with an amber dot, the Guard 360 Documents tab shows the exact expiry date and a "Request renewal" action, and the allocation engine applies the soft penalty defined in §25.15. |
| 19 Analytics | `guard_onboard_complete`, `guard_activate`, `guard_blacklist`, `guard_exit`; KPIs: time-to-activate, document compliance %, attrition, reliability distribution. |
| 20 Future | Skill certification marketplace; guard-level profitability; portable verification credential reusable across agencies `[FUTURE]`. |

#### 22.9.2 Supervisors (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Manage field supervisors and Field Officers who own a cluster of sites, conduct visits, verify attendance, and are the first escalation rung above a guard (§24.7). |
| Users/Permissions | HR (records), Operations (cluster assignment), Command Center Operator (contact/dispatch). Supervisors are Guard-side identities with elevated app capability, not OPS users. |
| Screens & key UI | Supervisor list (name, cluster, sites count, guards count, visit compliance %, phone) · Supervisor 360 (Cluster, Visit log, Escalations handled, Attendance verifications, Performance) · Cluster editor (drag sites between supervisors, with a map). |
| Logic & statuses | Visit compliance = completed site visits ÷ scheduled visits (default: each site visited ≥2×/week, night sites ≥1 night visit/week). Escalation response time tracked per §24.7. Statuses: Active · Suspended · Archived. |
| Audit/security | Cluster reassignment logged; supervisor access to guard PII limited to their cluster. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a supervisor with 12 sites and 3 scheduled visits missed this week, **When** City Ops opens the supervisor list, **Then** visit compliance shows a red dot with the three missed sites named. |

#### 22.9.3 Employees (internal staff) (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Suraksha's own internal staff records: the people who hold OPS accounts, plus non-OPS office staff. Distinct from Guards (field workforce). |
| Users/Permissions | HR (full), Super Admin (account linkage), Founder/Management (read), Auditor (read). Salary data visible to HR and Finance only. |
| Screens & key UI | Employee list (name, designation, role held, branch, scope, joining date, status) · Employee 360 (Profile, Role & scope grants, Devices, Sessions, Leave, Payroll, Documents, Access history) · Joiner/mover/leaver wizard. |
| Logic & statuses | Creating an employee does **not** create an OPS login; access is granted separately (§22.22.3) so that HR and access administration are separated. Leaver workflow revokes all sessions, API keys, device registrations and role grants within 15 minutes of the recorded exit time, and reassigns owned records (accounts, tickets, approvals) to a named successor before completion. |
| Audit/security | Every role grant, scope grant, device registration and revocation is logged; quarterly access review export for Auditor. |
| Acceptance | **Given** an employee marked as exited, **When** the leaver workflow completes, **Then** all sessions are terminated, role grants show `Revoked`, and any pending approvals owned by them appear in the successor's queue. |

### 22.10 Deployment structure modules

#### 22.10.1 Sites (major module, compressed 20-point)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| 1 Purpose | Every guarded location: geography, geofence, posts, instructions, checkpoints, contacts, risk profile. |
| 2 Users | Operations (all levels), Sales (create during onboarding), Command Center Operator (read + edit risk notes), Support (read). |
| 3 Permissions | Create/edit: City Ops+ and Sales for new client sites; geofence radius change: City Ops+ (logged); site closure: State Ops+. |
| 4 Screens | Site list · Site 360 (Overview, Posts, Roster, Geofence & checkpoints, Instructions, Contacts, Equipment, Incidents, Attendance, Documents) · Geofence editor (map polygon/radius) · Checkpoint editor (QR/NFC tags with map positions). |
| 5 UI detail | Site 360 header: client name, address, city, branch, required strength (day/night), current deployed, risk band chip (Low/Medium/High/Critical), last incident date. Geofence editor: satellite map, draw polygon or radius (default 100m, min 50m, max 500m), accuracy warning overlay. |
| 6 UX flow | Create site → set address & map pin → draw geofence → define posts and required strength per shift → write post instructions → add checkpoints → add site contacts → activate. |
| 7 Fields | site_id, client_id, name, address, lat/long, geofence type & geometry, city, state, branch, site type (residential/corporate/industrial/event/retail/hospital/bank/IT park), risk band, operating hours, access instructions, parking, rest facility available, drinking water, washroom, night lighting, mobile coverage quality, escalation contacts, equipment list, patrol route IDs, wake-check schedule, photo set. |
| 8 Validation | Geofence must contain the site pin; radius below 50m rejected (GPS accuracy reality); a site cannot be activated without at least one Post and one site contact; a site marked `low_connectivity` must declare an offline tolerance window. |
| 9 Business logic | Risk band drives wake-check frequency, patrol frequency, supervisor visit frequency and alert severity uplift (a P2 at a Critical site is treated as P1, §24.5). |
| 10 Backend logic | Geofence evaluation is server-side on ingest with a hysteresis buffer (exit asserted only after 2 consecutive out-of-fence pings ≥60s apart) to avoid GPS jitter alarms. |
| 11 Status lifecycle | Draft → Active → Suspended (service paused) → Archived. |
| 12 Notifications | Site activation to client; instruction change to assigned guards and supervisor; risk band change to Command Center. |
| 13 Integrations | Maps, reverse geocoding, QR/NFC tag provisioning. |
| 14 Security | Site access instructions (gate codes, key locations) are sensitive: visible to assigned guards and supervisors only, never in exports, redacted in AI responses (§25.6). |
| 15 Audit | Geofence changes with before/after geometry, instruction changes, risk band changes, checkpoint additions/removals. |
| 16 Edge cases | Multi-building campus (one site, multiple posts with sub-geofences); mobile site (event with a moving perimeter — geofence widened and flagged `dynamic`); site whose address is unmapped (manual pin with a supervisor-confirmed photo). |
| 17 QA | Jitter test: a device oscillating at the fence boundary must not produce more than one violation per 10 minutes. |
| 18 Acceptance | **Given** a site with a 100m geofence and a guard pinging 140m away twice, 90 seconds apart, **When** the second ping is received, **Then** exactly one geofence violation alert is raised at the severity mapped for that site's risk band. |
| 19 Analytics | `site_create`, `geofence_edit`, `site_risk_change`; KPIs: incidents per site-month, attendance % per site, sites per supervisor. |
| 20 Future | Indoor positioning for large campuses; site risk scoring from local crime/incident data `[FUTURE]`. |

#### 22.10.2 Posts (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | A guarded position at a Site requiring N guards per shift (canon §3). Posts are the unit of staffing obligation and the unit of contractual billing. |
| Users/Permissions | Operations create/edit; Finance reads (billing basis); Command Center reads (gap detection). |
| Screens & key UI | Post list per site · Post editor (name, location within site, shift pattern, required strength per shift, guard category required, skills required, armed flag, gender requirement where lawful and client-specified, equipment, instructions). |
| Logic & statuses | Post generates Shifts on a rolling 42-day horizon from its pattern; changing required strength regenerates future shifts only, never past ones. Statuses: Draft · Active · Suspended · Archived. Unstaffed Post = active shift with deployed < required (drives card A3 and §24.5). |
| Audit/security | Required-strength changes are audited because they change both billing and the unstaffed-post alarm baseline. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a Post requiring 2 guards on the night shift and only 1 assigned at shift start, **When** the shift begins, **Then** an unstaffed-post alert is raised at P1 and the replacement workflow is offered pre-filled. |

#### 22.10.3 Shifts (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | The time-boxed staffing requirement generated by a Post, against which Assignments and Attendance are recorded. |
| Users/Permissions | Operations (roster), Command Center (read), Payroll (read for wage computation). |
| Screens & key UI | Shift board (timeline per post), shift detail (window, required, assigned, attendance state, exceptions), bulk roster editor, shift template library (Day 08:00–20:00, Night 20:00–08:00, General 09:00–18:00, 8-hour three-shift, 12-hour two-shift, event blocks). |
| Logic & statuses | Grace period default 15 min (configurable per contract); overtime beyond scheduled end requires supervisor confirmation; a guard cannot hold overlapping active assignments (BR-001) without an authorised exception; working-hour constraints (max consecutive hours, weekly hours, mandatory rest) are configured rules that hard-block allocation (§25.15). |
| Audit/security | Roster changes within 12 hours of shift start are flagged as late changes and reported weekly. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a guard assigned to a night shift ending 08:00, **When** an allocator attempts to assign them to a day shift starting 08:00 the same morning, **Then** the assignment is blocked by the rest-period rule with the rule name and the earliest permissible start time shown. |

#### 22.10.4 Deployments (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | The operational realisation of a Contract: which guards, at which sites/posts, from when, under what terms. Deployment is the object clients see as "my guards". |
| Users/Permissions | Operations own it; Sales read; Finance read (billing linkage); client sees a filtered view in the customer portal. |
| Screens & key UI | Deployment list (client, site, posts, strength, start date, status, fill %, supervisor) · Deployment detail (roster, assigned guards with photos, replacement history, kit issued, client instructions, SLA state) · Mobilisation checklist (guards allocated, documents verified, kit issued, site briefing done, client introduction done, first-day supervisor present). |
| Logic & statuses | Draft → Pending (mobilising) → Active → Completed / Cancelled. Fill % = assigned ÷ required across the deployment's posts. A deployment cannot move to Active until the mobilisation checklist is complete or an authorised exception is recorded. |
| Audit/security | Every guard swap on an active deployment is audited with reason; client-visible swaps trigger a client notification if the contract requires named-guard continuity. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a new deployment with 6 of 8 guards allocated on the mobilisation date, **When** Ops attempts activation, **Then** activation is blocked with the two unfilled posts named and an "Activate with exception" action available to State Ops+ that records the reason and notifies the client. |

### 22.11 Demand modules

#### 22.11.1 Bookings (major, compressed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| 1 Purpose | Every request for guarding service that arrives from the website, app, phone, WhatsApp, marketplace enquiry or field sales, funnelled into one queue with one lifecycle. |
| 2 Users | Support (intake), Sales (qualification), City Ops (fulfilment), Finance (payment state). |
| 3 Permissions | Intake: Support, Sales. Assign to branch: City Ops+. Cancel with refund: Finance approval. |
| 4 Screens | Booking queue (kanban by stage) · Booking detail · Manual booking entry · Assignment workspace · Cancellation & refund. |
| 5 UI detail | Queue columns: New → Qualified → Quoted → Confirmed → Mobilising → Active → Closed. Card shows client, city, guards needed, armed flag, start date, value, SLA timer (time in stage). Detail: requirement panel, price panel, allocation panel (AI suggestions from §25.15 with scores), timeline. |
| 6 UX flow | New booking lands → auto-assigned to a branch by pincode serviceability → owner reviews requirement → standard requirement goes straight to Confirmed on payment; non-standard routes to Quotation → on acceptance, Deployment is created and allocation begins. |
| 7 Fields | booking_id, source channel, client (existing or new), service lane, guard count, armed/unarmed, shift pattern, duration/dates, site address & pincode, special requirements (languages, gender where lawful, ex-serviceman, height), budget indication, urgency, assigned branch, owner, price, payment status, linked quotation/contract/deployment. |
| 8 Validation | Pincode serviceability check against the branch serviceability set (D-005 for launch cities); armed requests force the quotation path; event bookings require date + hours; start date cannot be in the past. |
| 9 Business logic | Auto-routing: pincode → branch; if unserviceable, booking is tagged `Out of area` and routed to State Ops for a partner/subcontract decision (D-140). Urgency <24h triggers a P2 alert to City Ops. |
| 10 Backend logic | Booking is the funnel object; it never carries money directly — money lives on Quotation/Contract/Invoice. Idempotent creation from web/app to prevent duplicate submissions. |
| 11 Status lifecycle | Draft · Pending (New/Qualified) · In Progress (Quoted/Confirmed/Mobilising) · Completed · Cancelled · Archived. |
| 12 Notifications | Client: received, quote ready, confirmed, guard assigned, deployment start. Internal: new booking to branch owner, SLA breach on stage timer. |
| 13 Integrations | Razorpay (checkout), WhatsApp, telephony (call recording reference), marketplace enquiry ingest. |
| 14 Security | Booking contains client address before contract — visible to the owning branch only. |
| 15 Audit | Stage changes with actor and timestamp, price changes, cancellations with reason. |
| 16 Edge cases | Duplicate booking from the same client within 24h (merge prompt); client books for a city with no branch; payment succeeds but allocation fails (booking held in Confirmed with an internal P1 and a stated client commitment date). |
| 17 QA | Payment-success/allocation-failure path; out-of-area routing; SLA timer accuracy. |
| 18 Acceptance | **Given** a website booking for 2 unarmed guards in a serviceable pincode with successful payment, **When** it arrives, **Then** it appears in the branch queue at Confirmed within 30 seconds, the client receives confirmation on WhatsApp and email, and the allocation workspace shows ranked guard suggestions. |
| 19 Analytics | `booking_create{source}`, `booking_stage_change`, `booking_cancel{reason}`; KPIs: conversion by source, time in each stage, out-of-area rate. |
| 20 Future | Instant-allocation for standing clients; predictive demand by city/season feeding recruitment. |

#### 22.11.2 Quotations (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Priced proposals for non-standard requirements, with a 24-hour turnaround promise made publicly on the website. |
| Users/Permissions | Sales create; pricing below floor requires approval per §22.8.2 matrix; Finance reviews GST treatment. |
| Screens & key UI | Quotation list (client, value, age, status, owner, expiry) · Quotation builder (line items: service lane, guard category, count, shift, rate, months; auto-computed subtotal, GST 18%, total; terms; validity; annexures) · Preview & send (PDF, email, WhatsApp) · Version history. |
| Logic & statuses | Draft → Pending (Sent) → Accepted → Rejected → Expired. Validity default 15 days. Acceptance can be online (client portal) or offline (signed copy uploaded with acceptor name). Accepted quotation generates a Contract draft with the same line items — no retyping. |
| Audit/security | Every sent version stored immutably as PDF with a hash; rate changes after sending create a new version, never an edit. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a quotation accepted in the client portal, **When** acceptance is recorded, **Then** a Contract in Draft is created with identical line items, the booking moves to Confirmed, and the Sales owner is notified within 1 minute. |

#### 22.11.3 Contracts (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | The binding commercial agreement: rates, strength, shifts, term, SLA, escalation matrix, billing rules. The contract is the source of truth for invoicing and for SLA evaluation. |
| Users/Permissions | Sales draft; Finance approves billing terms; State Ops+ approves operational commitments; Founder/Management for non-standard liability or SLA terms. |
| Screens & key UI | Contract list (client, sites, value/month, start, end, renewal state, SLA tier) · Contract detail (Commercials, Sites & posts, SLA & escalation, Billing rules, Documents, Amendments, Renewals) · Amendment wizard · Renewal workspace. |
| Logic & statuses | Draft → Pending (approval) → Active → Expiring (60 days) → Completed / Cancelled. Billing rules: monthly in advance/arrears, proration policy, overtime rate, holiday multiplier, replacement policy, penalty clauses. Amendments create versions with effective dates; billing uses the version effective for the billing period. |
| Audit/security | Every approval, amendment and rate change is audited; the executed PDF is stored with a hash and is never replaced, only superseded. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a contract amendment increasing strength from 4 to 6 guards effective the 15th, **When** the month's invoice is generated, **Then** the invoice shows two lines (4 guards × 14 days, 6 guards × 16 days) with the amendment referenced. |
