### 22.12 Field-operations modules

#### 22.12.1 Attendance (major, compressed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| 1 Purpose | The authoritative record of who worked, where, when — the input to client billing and guard payroll simultaneously, which is why its integrity rules are strict. |
| 2 Users | Operations, Supervisors (via app), Payroll, Finance, Compliance, Auditor, client (filtered view). |
| 3 Permissions | Manual entry/override: City Ops and Supervisor, both requiring a reason code; approval of overrides above a monthly threshold: State Ops. Payroll may read but never edit attendance. |
| 4 Screens | Attendance dashboard (today) · Site attendance calendar · Guard attendance detail · Exception queue (late, absent, missing check-out, geofence, duplicate) · Manual entry · Override approvals · Monthly attendance close. |
| 5 UI detail | Calendar grid: rows = guards, columns = days, cells colour-coded (present/late/absent/leave/holiday/replacement) with the check-in time on hover. Exception queue shows evidence: GPS accuracy, photo, distance from site, device, and both `device_time` and `server_received_time`. |
| 6 UX flow | Exception appears → Ops opens → sees evidence → resolves as Present/Absent/Half-day/Replacement with a reason → record locked for the day once the monthly close runs. |
| 7 Fields | attendance_id, assignment_id, guard, site, post, shift, check-in device_time, check-in server_received_time, check-in lat/long/accuracy, check-in photo/face-match score, check-out equivalents, hours worked, overtime hours, late minutes, flags, source (app/biometric/manual/vouched), reason code, approver. |
| 8 Validation | Check-in must be inside the geofence unless flagged with a reason; face-match score below the configured threshold routes to manual review rather than auto-rejecting; a check-out earlier than check-in is impossible; duplicate check-ins within 5 minutes are deduplicated. |
| 9 Business logic | Present requires check-in and check-out (or an authorised auto-close at shift end +2h with a flag). Billing counts contracted strength delivered; payroll counts hours worked; the two are reconciled in the monthly close and any variance is reported, never silently absorbed. |
| 10 Backend logic | Attendance rows are append-only with a correction record model: a correction creates a new row referencing the original, both retained (never an in-place update). |
| 11 Status lifecycle | Pending → Verified → (Corrected) → Locked (after close) → Archived. |
| 12 Notifications | Guard: check-in confirmation, missed check-in reminder at start+10 min. Supervisor: absence at start+20 min. Client: daily attendance summary if contracted. |
| 13 Integrations | Guard App (offline-first, §18), biometric devices at Enterprise sites, face-match service. |
| 14 Security | Attendance photos are biometric-adjacent personal data: retention per §39, access logged, never in bulk export without Super Admin approval. |
| 15 Audit | Every manual entry, override, correction and close, with actor, reason and evidence reference. |
| 16 Edge cases | Offline check-in synced 9 hours later (accepted, flagged `late_sync`, with device_time preserved and server time recorded; if the sync gap exceeds the configured window it routes to review); guard checks in at the wrong site (blocked, prompt to select correct assignment); shift spanning midnight (attributed to the shift start date); site with no network at all (biometric or supervisor vouching only, site pre-flagged). |
| 17 QA | Late-sync integrity, midnight-spanning shifts, duplicate suppression, close-lock enforcement, payroll/billing reconciliation on a fixture month. |
| 18 Acceptance | **Given** a guard who checks in 22 minutes after shift start with a 15-minute grace, **When** the record is created, **Then** it is flagged Late with 7 late minutes, appears in the exception queue, contributes to card A4, and applies the contract's late deduction rule only after Ops resolution. |
| 19 Analytics | `attendance_checkin{source}`, `attendance_exception{type}`, `attendance_override`; KPIs: attendance %, late %, override rate per branch (an override rate above 5% is itself an alert). |
| 20 Future | Passive presence verification (BLE beacons), rota-optimisation feedback loop. |

#### 22.12.2 Patrol (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Verify that night and roving guards actually walk the route: checkpoint scans (QR/NFC) at defined points and times. |
| Users/Permissions | Operations, Command Center (exceptions), Supervisors, client (report view). |
| Screens & key UI | Patrol schedule per site · Route editor (ordered checkpoints, expected duration, tolerance) · Patrol log (round, start, end, scans, missed points, photos) · Exception queue (missed round, missed checkpoint, out-of-sequence, too-fast round). |
| Logic & statuses | A round is Completed only if ≥ configured % of checkpoints scanned within the window (default 100% for Critical sites, 80% elsewhere). "Too-fast" rounds (below the minimum plausible duration) are flagged as suspicious, not accepted. Missed rounds raise P2 (P1 at Critical sites). |
| Audit/security | Checkpoint tag IDs are site-secret; a scan from a device not assigned to that site is rejected and raises a tamper alert. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a 6-checkpoint route with a 30-minute window and only 4 scans, **When** the window closes, **Then** the round is marked Incomplete, the two missed checkpoints are named, and a P2 alert routes to the Command Center. |

#### 22.12.3 GPS monitoring (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Continuous location assurance for on-duty guards, feeding the map, geofence logic, patrol verification and client transparency. |
| Users/Permissions | Operations, Command Center; historical replay beyond 24h requires a recorded reason (§39). |
| Screens & key UI | Live map (§22.6) · Track replay (timeline scrubber, speed, stops, gaps) · Accuracy diagnostics (per device: fix accuracy distribution, ping success rate, battery drain). |
| Logic & statuses | Ping cadence 60s on duty, 300s on break, 0 off duty (tracking stops at check-out — this is a privacy commitment, §39). Gaps >10 min flagged; accuracy >100m excluded from geofence decisions. |
| Audit/security | Off-duty tracking is technically prevented, not merely disabled by policy; any code path capable of it is a security defect. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a guard who checks out, **When** the device continues to run, **Then** no location is transmitted or stored, and the guard's app shows tracking as Off. |

#### 22.12.4 Wake checks (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | The anti-sleep control promised publicly: during night shifts, the guard must acknowledge randomised prompts to prove alertness. |
| Users/Permissions | Command Center owns the live cycle (§24.12); Operations configure schedules; clients see compliance in reports. |
| Screens & key UI | Wake-check schedule editor per site (window, count per night, randomisation, response timeout) · Live wake-check board (due, acknowledged, missed) · Missed-check queue with escalation state. |
| Logic & statuses | Default: 4 checks per night between 23:00 and 05:00, randomised with ≥45-minute spacing, 120-second response timeout, loud alarm + vibration, acknowledgement requires an in-app action plus (configurable) a selfie. Missed check → auto-retry once after 60s → still missed → P1 alert and supervisor call (§24.7). Critical sites: 6 checks and a 90-second timeout. |
| Audit/security | Acknowledgement records device, time (both clocks), location and optional photo; a pattern of acknowledged-but-immobile devices is flagged for review. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a scheduled wake check at 01:37 with a 120s timeout and no acknowledgement, **When** the retry also lapses, **Then** a P1 alert is created at 01:40, the supervisor is called automatically, and card A6 decrements. |

### 22.13 Exception & incident modules

#### 22.13.1 SOS (condensed here — full mechanics in §24.8)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | The panic path from a guard (or client contact) to a human being who acts. OPS holds the register and the after-action record; §24 owns the live handling. |
| Users/Permissions | Command Center Operator acts; Operations and Founder/Management see all; Support sees client-visible summary; Auditor reads everything. |
| Screens & key UI | SOS register (time, guard, site, client, trigger type, ack time, response time, outcome, false-alarm flag) · SOS detail (full timeline, audio/photo evidence, call log, escalation rungs fired, resolution note, incident report link). |
| Logic & statuses | Raised → Acknowledged → In Progress → Resolved → Reviewed. Acknowledgement target 30 seconds (§24.5). Every SOS produces a mandatory incident report before it can be Reviewed. |
| Audit/security | Immutable timeline; evidence files write-once; deletion impossible, redaction possible with Compliance approval and a retained redaction record. |
| Acceptance | **Given** an SOS raised at 02:14:03 and acknowledged at 02:14:26, **When** the register is viewed, **Then** ack time shows 23s against a 30s target, and the full escalation ladder state is visible per rung with timestamps. |

#### 22.13.2 Incidents (major, compressed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| 1 Purpose | The register of everything that went wrong at a site: theft, trespass, assault, fire, medical, property damage, guard misconduct, client complaint about conduct, equipment failure, natural events. |
| 2 Users | Command Center Operator, Operations, Compliance, Support, client (filtered), Auditor. |
| 3 Permissions | Create: guard (via app), supervisor, operator, ops, support. Classify severity: operator and above. Close: City Ops+ with a closure report. Reclassify severity downward: State Ops+ only (prevents quiet downgrading). |
| 4 Screens | Incident queue (severity, age, site, client, owner, status) · Incident detail (narrative, evidence, timeline, people involved, actions taken, client communications, closure) · Incident report generator · Trend analysis. |
| 5 UI detail | Queue is severity-ordered with an age bar that turns red past the response target; detail page has a left narrative column and a right evidence rail (photos, audio, video, documents, GPS snapshot at time of event). |
| 6 UX flow | Report → auto-classify suggestion from §25.13 → operator confirms severity and category → assign owner → actions logged → client informed per §24.7 rules → resolution → closure report → review for P0/P1. |
| 7 Fields | incident_id, datetime (device + server), site, post, guards involved, category, sub-category, severity, description, evidence refs, injuries flag, police involved flag + FIR reference, client informed flag + time + channel, financial loss estimate, actions taken, owner, status, closure summary, review outcome, preventive action. |
| 8 Validation | P0/P1 incidents cannot be closed without: closure summary ≥100 characters, at least one evidence item or a stated reason for none, client-communication record, and a preventive action. |
| 9 Business logic | Severity mapping is defined in §24.5 and is uniform across the platform. Repeat incidents at a site within 30 days uplift the site's risk band automatically with a notification to Ops. |
| 10 Backend logic | Incident is append-only in its timeline; edits to the narrative create revisions with author and time. |
| 11 Status lifecycle | Pending → In Progress → Completed (resolved) → Verified (reviewed) → Archived. |
| 12 Notifications | Per §24.7 fan-out. Client notification rules are contractual, not discretionary. |
| 13 Integrations | Storage for evidence, WhatsApp/email for client reports, PDF generation for the formal incident report. |
| 14 Security | Evidence may contain third-party PII and CCTV frames; access is role- and case-limited, downloads watermarked. |
| 15 Audit | Severity changes (with a mandatory reason on downgrade), closure, client-notification record, evidence access. |
| 16 Edge cases | Incident reported by a guard who is later found responsible (conflict flag, ownership reassigned); incident spanning two sites; a client raising an incident the guard disputes (dual-narrative record, both retained); police-involved incidents (legal hold — record cannot be archived while the hold is on). |
| 17 QA | Closure gating on P1; severity downgrade permission; evidence immutability. |
| 18 Acceptance | **Given** a P1 theft incident with no client-notification record, **When** an Ops user attempts closure, **Then** closure is blocked, listing exactly which mandatory closure elements are missing. |
| 19 Analytics | `incident_create{category,severity}`, `incident_close`, `incident_reopen`; KPIs: incidents per 1,000 guard-shifts, mean time to resolve by severity, repeat-site rate. |
| 20 Future | Automated narrative drafting from timeline (§25.13), pattern detection across sites and cities. |

#### 22.13.3 Escalations (condensed — engine owned by §24.7)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | The OPS-side view of escalations in flight and their history: which ladder fired, which rung is live, who has not responded, what the SLA state is. |
| Users/Permissions | Command Center Operator (act), Operations (act and override), Founder/Management (visibility), Auditor (read). |
| Screens & key UI | Escalation board (columns = ladder rungs, cards = live escalations with a countdown), escalation history per entity, ladder configuration screen (§24.7 defines the ladders; OPS is where they are configured and versioned). |
| Logic & statuses | Ladder configuration is versioned; changing a ladder never alters escalations already in flight. Manual escalation to the next rung is always available; manual de-escalation requires a reason. |
| Audit/security | Ladder edits require Super Admin plus Operations approval and are logged with a diff; every rung fire and acknowledgement is recorded. |
| Acceptance | **Given** an unacknowledged P1 at rung 2 with a 5-minute timer, **When** the timer expires, **Then** rung 3 fires automatically, the board card moves column, and both events appear in the audit trail with server timestamps. |

#### 22.13.4 Replacement management (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Fill a gap fast when a guard is absent, leaves mid-shift, is withdrawn by the client, or fails a check — the single most common operational task. |
| Users/Permissions | Command Center Operator and City Ops initiate; Supervisor executes on ground; client may request a replacement from the portal. |
| Screens & key UI | Replacement queue (site, post, reason, gap start, time open, candidates, status) · Replacement workspace (ranked candidates from §25.15 with distance, availability, skill match, reliability; one-click notify top 3; live acceptance state) · Replacement history per guard and per site. |
| Logic & statuses | Requested → In Progress (candidate notified) → Completed (replacement checked in) → Failed (no fill within target). Targets: Critical/Tier-1 site 60 minutes, standard 120 minutes, non-urgent next shift. Client-requested replacements for cause create a linked incident if the reason is conduct. |
| Audit/security | Reason codes are fixed (absent, sick, emergency, terminated, client request, disciplinary, no-show, document lapse); free text is supplementary. Repeated client-requested replacements of the same guard trigger an HR review. |
| Acceptance | **Given** an absence at a Tier-1 site at 20:15, **When** the operator opens the replacement workspace, **Then** ranked candidates appear within 3 seconds with distance and ETA, the top three can be notified in one action, and the 60-minute target countdown is displayed. |

#### 22.13.5 Leave (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Guard and internal-staff leave: request, approval, balance, and the roster consequence (leave without a replacement is a future gap, and the system must say so). |
| Users/Permissions | Guards request via app; Supervisor recommends; City Ops/HR approve; Payroll consumes balances. |
| Screens & key UI | Leave queue (guard, type, dates, site impact, status) · Leave calendar per site (shows coverage risk) · Balance ledger per guard · Policy configuration (types, accrual, carry-forward, encashment — all configurable data, never hard-coded). |
| Logic & statuses | Pending → Verified (approved) / Rejected → Completed. Approval is blocked (soft warning, overridable with reason) if it creates an unfilled post with no replacement plan. Emergency leave can be recorded retrospectively with an approver. |
| Audit/security | Approvals, rejections and retrospective entries audited; balance adjustments require HR with a reason. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a leave request covering three night shifts at a Post with no spare capacity, **When** the approver opens it, **Then** a coverage-risk warning names the three affected shifts and offers to open the replacement workspace for each. |

### 22.14 Money modules

Financial architecture (ledger design, GST engine, payout rails) is specified in §35; this section covers only the OPS surfaces and their operational rules. All amounts are integer paise; every movement is a double-sided ledger entry; completed transactions are never silently modified (BR-003).

#### 22.14.1 Payroll (major, compressed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| 1 Purpose | Convert verified attendance into guard wages, deductions and payslips, per branch and per pay cycle. |
| 2 Users | Payroll/Finance (run), HR (structures), State Ops (variance review), Auditor. |
| 3 Permissions | Only Finance may release a payroll run; the preparer cannot be the approver (segregation of duties enforced by the system, not by convention). |
| 4 Screens | Payroll calendar · Run workspace (Preview → Variance → Approve → Release) · Guard payslip · Deduction/advance register · Statutory components configuration · Bank file / payout export. |
| 5 UI detail | Variance screen is the heart: every guard whose net pay differs from last cycle by more than a configured % or ₹ is listed with the reason (attendance, overtime, deduction, structure change). Nothing releases until every variance line is acknowledged. |
| 6 UX flow | Attendance close (§22.12.1) → run preview → variance review → approvals → release → payouts → payslips published to Guard App → ledger entries posted. |
| 7 Fields | run_id, branch, cycle, guard count, gross, deductions, statutory components, net, status, preparer, approver, release time, payout batch reference. |
| 8 Validation | A run cannot start before attendance for the period is Locked; a guard with an unverified bank account is excluded and reported, never paid to an unverified account. |
| 9 Business logic | Wage = base per contract/structure + overtime + allowances − advances − deductions ± adjustments. Statutory components (PF/ESI-type items) are **configured jurisdiction rules**, never hard-coded logic. |
| 10 Backend logic | Runs are immutable once released; corrections are made through a supplementary run referencing the original. |
| 11 Status lifecycle | Draft → Pending (approval) → Completed (released) → Failed (payout failures listed) → Archived. |
| 12 Notifications | Guard: payslip available, payment credited, payment failed. Internal: run ready, variance threshold exceeded, payout failures. |
| 13 Integrations | Payout rail `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-142]` (bank bulk file vs payout API), accounting export. |
| 14 Security | Salary data is need-to-know; bulk payslip export requires Finance plus a second approver; bank details are masked except the last four digits. |
| 15 Audit | Preparer, approver, release, every manual adjustment with reason, every excluded guard. |
| 16 Edge cases | Guard worked in two branches (split by attendance branch tag); mid-cycle salary revision (proration by effective date); payout failure due to a closed bank account (auto-retry once, then HR task); guard exited mid-cycle (final settlement path). |
| 17 QA | Fixture-month arithmetic to the paise; segregation-of-duties enforcement; immutability of released runs. |
| 18 Acceptance | **Given** a payroll run where one guard's net pay is 40% below last cycle, **When** Finance attempts approval, **Then** approval is blocked until the variance line is acknowledged with a reason. |
| 19 Analytics | `payroll_run_release`, `payroll_variance_ack`, `payout_failure`; KPIs: cost per guard-shift, payout failure rate, on-time payroll %. |
| 20 Future | Weekly/daily pay options, earned-wage access `[FUTURE]`. |

#### 22.14.2 Client billing & GST/invoicing (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Generate, deliver and track client invoices from contracts and delivered attendance, with compliant GST documents. |
| Users/Permissions | Finance owns; Sales views; Ops supplies delivery data; clients receive. |
| Screens & key UI | Billing run (per branch, per cycle: preview → exceptions → approve → issue) · Invoice list & detail · Credit/debit note issue · Payment recording & reconciliation · Reminder scheduler · GST register and period summary · E-invoice/e-way references where applicable `[ASSUMPTION: A-144]`. |
| Logic & statuses | Invoice = Σ (contracted strength delivered × rate) ± overtime, holiday multipliers, penalties, credits. Statuses: Draft → Pending (issued/unpaid) → Completed (paid) → Cancelled (by credit note) → Archived. Partial payments are ledger entries; the invoice balance is derived, never overwritten. Reminders at D+1, D+7, D+15, D+30 with escalating tone and Sales owner CC. |
| Audit/security | Issued invoices are immutable; corrections are credit/debit notes; the invoice PDF hash is stored; GST fields are validated before issue. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a month where a client's site was short-staffed for 3 days under a penalty clause, **When** the billing run previews the invoice, **Then** the shortfall line and the contractual penalty appear as separate lines with references to the attendance dates. |

#### 22.14.3 Agency settlements (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Money owed to or from agencies: subscription receivables, marketplace lead fees, subcontract payouts (if D-140 permits), refunds and adjustments. |
| Users/Permissions | Finance only for release; Support raises disputes; Auditor reads. |
| Screens & key UI | Settlement statement per agency per period (opening, earnings, deductions, adjustments, TDS-type withholdings as configured, closing, payable) · Settlement run · Dispute workspace · Payout batch. |
| Logic & statuses | Draft → Pending (approval) → Completed (paid) → Failed → Archived. A settlement cannot be released while an open dispute exists on any line, unless Finance splits the disputed lines into a held sub-statement with a reason. |
| Audit/security | Bank account changes on an agency freeze settlements for 48 hours with an out-of-band confirmation to the registered owner contact — a deliberate anti-fraud control. |
| Acceptance | **Given** an agency that changed its bank account 12 hours ago, **When** a settlement release is attempted, **Then** it is blocked with the cooling-off expiry time shown and the verification status of the new account. |

#### 22.14.4 Guard payments (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Non-payroll money to guards: advances, reimbursements, incentives, ad-hoc/event payments, final settlements. |
| Users/Permissions | City Ops raise; HR verify; Finance approve and release. Three-party separation is mandatory above a configured amount (default ₹10,000). |
| Screens & key UI | Payment request queue · Request detail (guard, type, amount, reason, evidence, approvals) · Batch release · Advance ledger per guard (with recovery schedule). |
| Logic & statuses | Draft → Pending → Verified → Completed → Failed. Advances auto-generate recovery lines in future payroll runs; total outstanding advance is capped per guard (default one month's net). |
| Audit/security | Every request, approval and release audited; duplicate-request detection on guard + amount + 24h window. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a guard with an outstanding advance equal to their monthly net, **When** a further advance is requested, **Then** the request is blocked with the cap rule named and an override path to Finance. |

#### 22.14.5 Wallet, refunds, credits & debits (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Client wallet balances (a liability), refunds against payments, and manual credit/debit adjustments — the three places where money can move without a service event, and therefore the three places most tightly controlled. |
| Users/Permissions | Finance only; Support may raise refund requests but never approve; Founder/Management approval above a configured threshold (default ₹50,000). |
| Screens & key UI | Wallet ledger per client (credits, debits, running balance, expiry policy) · Top-up records · Refund queue (request, reason, original payment, method, status, approvals) · Manual adjustment form (mandatory reason code + reference + attachment). |
| Logic & statuses | Refund: Pending → Verified (approved) → In Progress (gateway) → Completed / Failed. Refunds go back to the original payment instrument by default; any other destination requires a second approver and a written justification. Wallet credits from refunds are permitted only with client consent recorded. |
| Audit/security | Manual credits/debits are the highest-risk action in OPS: dual approval, reason code, attachment, and a daily report of all manual adjustments to Finance leadership and Auditor. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a ₹75,000 refund request, **When** Finance approves, **Then** the action remains Pending until a Founder/Management approval is also recorded, and both approvals appear on the refund record. |

### 22.15 Growth modules

#### 22.15.1 Tenders (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Track government and large-enterprise tenders Suraksha itself bids for (distinct from the agency-facing tender discovery feature in the Agency Portal). |
| Users/Permissions | Sales own; Compliance checks eligibility documents; Finance approves pricing and EMD; Founder/Management approves submission. |
| Screens & key UI | Tender board (source, authority, scope, value, EMD, pre-bid date, submission deadline, status, owner) · Tender detail (documents, eligibility checklist, cost sheet, competitor notes, bid pack) · Deadline calendar with countdowns. |
| Logic & statuses | Identified → Qualified → Preparing → Submitted → Won / Lost / Cancelled. Eligibility checklist items map to compliance objects (turnover, licences per state, experience certificates, manpower strength, ISO/GST/PF registrations) and are auto-ticked where the platform already holds the evidence. Submission is blocked if any mandatory checklist item is unmet without an override. |
| Integrations | Tender portal integration is **not assumed**: `[ASSUMPTION: A-145]` no reliable public API is presumed for government tender portals; V1 uses manual entry plus optional document upload with AI extraction (§25.13), and an aggregator feed only if a commercial one is procured. |
| Audit/security | Bid pricing is restricted to the deal team; every version of the cost sheet is retained; access list per tender is explicit. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a tender requiring a Maharashtra PSARA licence that Suraksha does not hold, **When** the eligibility checklist runs, **Then** the item is red, submission is blocked, and the licence module deep-links from the checklist row. |

#### 22.15.2 Leads & CRM (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | One pipeline for both businesses: guarding leads (website quote forms, calls, referrals, events) and SaaS leads (Trinetra demo requests, marketplace signups, outbound). |
| Users/Permissions | Sales own their leads; Marketing create campaign leads; Founder/Management see all; City Ops see guarding leads in their city. |
| Screens & key UI | Lead inbox (source, name, city, need, score, age, owner, next action) · Pipeline board by stage · Lead/Opportunity detail (activity timeline, calls, emails, WhatsApp, notes, linked quotation) · Assignment rules editor · Activity calendar. |
| Logic & statuses | New → Contacted → Qualified → Opportunity → Won / Lost / Disqualified. Auto-assignment by city and business context with round-robin within the branch; an untouched lead reassigns after 4 working hours (SLA), and after 24 hours raises a P2 to the branch owner. Lead scoring: source weight + guard count/plan tier + urgency + response engagement. |
| Audit/security | Ownership changes and bulk edits audited; export of lead contact lists restricted and watermarked. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a demo request from Trinetra at 14:00, **When** no activity is logged by 18:00 the same working day, **Then** the lead reassigns to the next Sales user in the rotation and the original owner and their lead are notified. |

### 22.16 Service modules

#### 22.16.1 Support tickets (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | One ticketing surface for clients, agencies and guards, with distinct queues, SLAs and routing per audience. |
| Users/Permissions | Support own; Ops receive operational tickets; Finance receive billing tickets; Compliance receive verification tickets. |
| Screens & key UI | Ticket queue (priority, audience, subject, requester, age, SLA bar, owner) · Ticket detail (thread, internal notes, linked entities, attachments, resolution) · Macros/canned responses · SLA policy configuration · Merge/split. |
| Logic & statuses | Pending → In Progress → Completed (resolved) → Verified (confirmed by requester or auto after 72h) → Archived. Default SLAs: P1 first response 15 min / resolution 4h; P2 30 min / 8h; P3 4h / 2 working days. Operational tickets that describe a live safety issue are converted to Command Center alerts, not handled in the ticket queue. |
| Audit/security | Internal notes are never exposed to requesters; any ticket containing PII attachments inherits document access rules. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a client ticket saying "our guard has not arrived and it is 22:40", **When** Support triages it, **Then** a one-click "Escalate to Command Center" action creates a linked alert at the mapped severity and the ticket shows the alert's live state. |

#### 22.16.2 Complaints (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Formal grievances (client about service, guard about employer, agency about platform), which carry regulatory and reputational weight and therefore have stricter handling than tickets. |
| Users/Permissions | Support intake; Compliance own guard grievances; City Ops own service complaints; Founder/Management notified on any complaint aged >7 days. |
| Screens & key UI | Complaint register (complainant type, category, severity, age, owner, status) · Complaint detail (statement, investigation notes, evidence, outcome, remedy, communication log) · Category configuration. |
| Logic & statuses | Pending → In Progress (investigation) → Completed (outcome communicated) → Verified (closed with complainant acknowledgement or lapse) → Archived. Guard grievances relating to safety, harassment or wage non-payment are auto-escalated to Compliance at intake and cannot be closed by the branch that is the subject of the complaint. |
| Audit/security | Complainant identity may be restricted (whistle-blower mode) with access limited to Compliance; all access logged. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a guard complaint about unpaid wages at Branch A, **When** it is created, **Then** ownership routes to Compliance, Branch A staff cannot close it, and Founder/Management is notified if it remains open at day 7. |

#### 22.16.3 Reviews (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Client ratings of guards, sites and service; agency ratings on the marketplace; guard ratings of sites (two-way trust). |
| Users/Permissions | Support and Marketing moderate; Ops read; Founder/Management see trends. |
| Screens & key UI | Review stream (source, subject, stars, text, flags, status) · Moderation queue (rules: profanity, PII, defamation, off-topic, suspected incentivised) · Review analytics by branch/site/guard · Response composer for public replies. |
| Logic & statuses | Pending → Verified (published) → Rejected (with reason to author) → Archived. Only a client with a completed service period may review; one review per contract period per site; edits allowed for 7 days and versioned. |
| Audit/security | Moderation decisions logged with the rule applied; no silent deletion. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a review containing a guard's phone number, **When** moderation runs, **Then** it is held with reason "PII" and the moderator can publish a redacted version, with both versions retained. |

#### 22.16.4 Disputes (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Contested money: invoice disputes, settlement disputes, payment chargebacks, deduction disputes from guards. |
| Users/Permissions | Finance own; Support intake; Founder/Management approve write-offs above threshold. |
| Screens & key UI | Dispute register (party, amount, type, age, status, owner, exposure) · Dispute detail (claim, evidence from both sides, ledger references, proposed resolution, approvals) · Write-off approvals. |
| Logic & statuses | Pending → In Progress → Completed (resolved: upheld / partially upheld / rejected / written off) → Archived. Disputed amounts are ring-fenced in the ledger (a contra entry), never simply ignored, so receivables reporting stays truthful. |
| Audit/security | Every write-off requires reason, approver and ledger reference; a monthly write-off report goes to Finance leadership and Auditor. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a ₹1.2L invoice disputed for short staffing, **When** the dispute is opened, **Then** the amount is ring-fenced, ageing stops on the disputed portion, and the attendance evidence for the claimed dates is attached automatically. |

### 22.17 Trust & compliance modules

#### 22.17.1 Documents (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | The vault: every document belonging to guards, employees, clients, agencies, sites and the company, with type, validity, ownership and access control. |
| Users/Permissions | Verification and Compliance full; HR for people documents; Finance for financial documents; everyone else sees only documents attached to entities in their scope, and only the types their role permits. |
| Screens & key UI | Document explorer (entity, type, status, issue/expiry date, uploader, verifier) · Viewer (watermarked, no direct download for restricted types) · Expiry dashboard (90/60/30/7/expired buckets) · Bulk request tool (ask N guards for a missing document). |
| Logic & statuses | Draft (uploaded) → Pending (verification) → Verified → Rejected → Expiring → Expired → Archived. Expiry drives alerts and, for licences and mandatory guard documents, operational restrictions (BR-002 and the allocation veto in §25.15). |
| Audit/security | Every view and download logged with viewer, time, purpose; watermarking with viewer identity; encryption at rest; no document is ever hard-deleted. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a guard's police verification expiring in 25 days, **When** the expiry dashboard is opened, **Then** the guard appears in the 30-day bucket with a one-click "request renewal" that sends the guard an app task and SMS. |

#### 22.17.2 KYC & Verification (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Establish that a person or organisation is who they claim: guard KYC, client KYB, agency verification, employee verification. |
| Users/Permissions | Verification role owns the queue; Compliance audits it; no other role may set a Verified status. |
| Screens & key UI | Verification queue (type, subject, age, SLA, assignee) · Verification workspace (document viewer beside extracted fields with confidence scores from §25.13; check-list per verification type; approve/reject with reason codes) · Rejection reason library · Re-verification scheduler. |
| Logic & statuses | Pending → In Progress → Verified / Rejected → Expiring → Expired. SLA: guard KYC 24h, agency verification 48h, client KYB 48h. Four-eyes rule: agency verification and any high-risk guard verification require a second reviewer. |
| Audit/security | Every decision stores the evidence set, the checklist state, the reviewer(s) and the reason; decisions cannot be edited, only superseded by a re-verification. |
| Acceptance | **Given** an agency verification approved by reviewer A, **When** the four-eyes rule applies, **Then** the listing does not go live until reviewer B independently approves, and both identities are recorded on the listing's trust record. |

#### 22.17.3 Licences (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | PSARA state and district licences — Suraksha's own and every agency's — as first-class objects with geography, validity and operational consequence. |
| Users/Permissions | Compliance own; Verification validate documents; Operations read (it determines where they may deploy); Founder/Management see the national picture. |
| Screens & key UI | Licence registry (holder, type state/district, jurisdiction, number, issue date, expiry, status, document) · Geography map (states/districts coloured by licence status) · Renewal tracker (application date, reference, status, follow-ups) · Consequence panel (what is blocked if this licence lapses). |
| Logic & statuses | Active → Expiring (90/60/30/7) → Expired → Suspended → Archived. On Expired: BR-002 restrictions apply — new deployments in that jurisdiction blocked, existing deployments flagged for management decision, marketplace verified badge withdrawn, and a compliance task created. |
| Audit/security | Licence status changes are among the most consequential records in the platform: dual control (Compliance + Super Admin) for any manual status change, with the document evidence mandatory. |
| Acceptance | **Given** Suraksha's Rajasthan state licence expiring in 7 days with no renewal recorded, **When** the compliance dashboard loads, **Then** it appears at the top with the count of active deployments and guards in Rajasthan that would be affected, and a named owner with a due date. |

#### 22.17.4 Compliance (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | The company-wide compliance picture: licences, statutory registers, filing calendar, training currency, verification coverage, audit findings, and readiness for inspection. |
| Users/Permissions | Compliance own; Auditor read-all; Founder/Management see the score; Ops see their scope's items. |
| Screens & key UI | Compliance dashboard (score, open findings, upcoming filings, expiring licences, verification coverage) · Filing calendar (configurable obligations with owners, due dates, evidence upload) · Register generator (statutory registers as configured data) · Findings tracker (source, severity, owner, due, status) · Inspection pack export. |
| Logic & statuses | Findings: Pending → In Progress → Completed → Verified. Compliance score is a configured weighted composite (licence currency 30%, guard document compliance 25%, verification coverage 20%, filings on time 15%, open findings 10%) shown with its formula visible. |
| Audit/security | Nothing in compliance may be edited retrospectively without a superseding record; the inspection pack export is itself an audited event. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a filing obligation due in 5 days with no evidence uploaded, **When** the dashboard loads, **Then** it shows in red with the owner named, and the owner has received notifications at 15, 7 and 5 days. |

### 22.18 People-supply modules

#### 22.18.1 Training (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Track mandatory and optional guard training: induction, PSARA-linked training, fire safety, first aid, site-specific briefing, armed handling, refreshers — with currency and evidence. |
| Users/Permissions | HR/Training own; Compliance audit; Ops see currency because it gates allocation; guards see their own record. |
| Screens & key UI | Training catalogue (course, duration, validity period, mandatory-for categories) · Batch scheduler (trainer, venue, dates, enrolled, attendance) · Guard training record · Currency dashboard (% current by branch and category) · Certificate vault. |
| Logic & statuses | Scheduled → In Progress → Completed → Expiring → Expired. Expired mandatory training applies the soft penalty or hard veto defined in §25.15 depending on whether the training is statutory for that guard category at that site. |
| Audit/security | Certificates are documents under §22.17.1; trainer attestation recorded. |
| Acceptance | **Given** an armed guard whose weapon-handling refresher has expired, **When** the allocation engine evaluates them for an armed post, **Then** the compliance veto blocks allocation with the reason "mandatory training expired" and the training module deep-links. |

#### 22.18.2 Recruitment (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Fill the guard pipeline: sourcing, screening, interview, selection, document collection, onboarding handover — plus internal-staff hiring. |
| Users/Permissions | Recruitment own; HR approve offers; City Ops define demand; Verification handle the document stage. |
| Screens & key UI | Requisition board (branch, category, count, urgency, filled/open, age) · Candidate pipeline (Applied → Screened → Interviewed → Selected → Documents → Onboarded → Rejected/Dropped) · Candidate detail (source, profile, screening notes, AI screening summary per §25.13, documents) · Source performance report · Referral tracking. |
| Logic & statuses | Requisition: Draft → Active → Completed → Cancelled. A selected candidate becomes a Guard record in Draft — no re-entry of data. Time-to-fill measured per requisition; ageing requisitions escalate to City Ops at 14 days. |
| Audit/security | Rejection reasons from a fixed list; candidate PII retention per §39 with a defined purge for unsuccessful candidates. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a requisition for 10 unarmed guards in Ahmedabad open for 15 days with 4 filled, **When** the board loads, **Then** it shows red ageing, the shortfall of 6, the current pipeline count at each stage, and the source that produced the 4 hires. |

### 22.19 Marketplace moderation (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Keep the Trinetra directory trustworthy: moderate listings, listing edits, profile media, service claims, reviews and enquiry abuse. |
| Users/Permissions | Support/Marketing moderate routine content; Verification decide licence-linked claims; Compliance handle escalated cases; Super Admin can delist. |
| Screens & key UI | Moderation queue (item type, agency, submitted, age, flags, assignee) · Side-by-side diff for listing edits (what changed since the last approved version) · Rule library (prohibited claims, e.g. unverifiable government-client claims, guarantee language, competitor disparagement, incorrect licence claims) · Delisting workspace (reason, evidence, notice, appeal state) · Featured-placement manager (slot, agency, period, price or promotional basis, approver). |
| Logic & statuses | Pending → Verified (published) → Rejected → Suspended → Archived. Any edit to licence numbers, states of operation, or the verified badge area forces re-verification rather than simple moderation. Featured placements must be visibly labelled as promoted. |
| Audit/security | Every moderation decision, delisting and featured placement is audited with the rule and approver; appeals are handled by a different reviewer than the original decision. |
| Acceptance | **Given** an agency editing its states of operation from one state to three, **When** the edit is submitted, **Then** it does not enter routine moderation but creates two new licence verification tasks, and the public listing continues to show only the verified state until they pass. |

### 22.20 Communication & content modules

#### 22.20.1 Notifications (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | The internal control surface for everything the platform sends: templates, channels, routing rules, quiet hours, delivery health. Notification architecture is §36; this is the OPS administration of it. |
| Users/Permissions | Marketing own client-facing templates; Ops own operational templates; Compliance approve any template containing legal or safety language; Super Admin control channel credentials. |
| Screens & key UI | Template library (key, channel, language variants, version, owner, status) · Template editor with variable palette and live preview per channel · Routing rules (event → audience → channel priority → fallback) · Quiet-hours policy (operational alerts exempt) · Delivery dashboard (sent, delivered, read, failed by channel with failure reasons) · Test-send tool. |
| Logic & statuses | Templates: Draft → Pending (approval) → Active → Archived. Every template must exist in English and Hindi before activation; other languages are optional and fall back to English (§25.5). |
| Audit/security | Template changes are versioned and approved; no template may be edited directly in production without an approval record. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a template edit adding a new variable, **When** it is submitted, **Then** it cannot activate until the Hindi variant is updated too, and a test send to the editor's own number has been recorded. |

#### 22.20.2 Campaigns (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Outbound marketing and lifecycle communication to clients, prospects, agencies and guards, with consent and frequency control. |
| Users/Permissions | Marketing create; Compliance approve any campaign touching guards or containing claims; Founder/Management approve brand campaigns. |
| Screens & key UI | Campaign list (name, audience, channel, schedule, status, sent, engagement) · Audience builder (saved segments with a live count and a consent-eligible count that is always lower and explained) · Content composer per channel · Schedule & throttle · Results dashboard (delivery, open/read, click, conversion attributed to leads/bookings). |
| Logic & statuses | Draft → Pending (approval) → Active (scheduled/sending) → Completed → Cancelled. Hard rules: no marketing to guards outside working hours; no marketing on the operational alert channels; consent and unsubscribe honoured within 24 hours; global frequency cap (default 4 marketing messages per contact per month). |
| Audit/security | Every audience export is logged and watermarked; the consent basis for each recipient is retained with the send record. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a segment of 5,000 clients of whom 3,800 have marketing consent, **When** the campaign is scheduled, **Then** the UI shows both numbers, sends to 3,800 only, and the audit record stores the consent snapshot used. |

#### 22.20.3 Content management (major, compressed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| 1 Purpose | Manage everything published on the public surfaces — website content, services, industries, pricing, FAQs, blogs, testimonials, media, locations, notifications, campaigns and policies — from OPS, with a workflow that prevents another round of the fabricated content problems P1–P8 recorded in the canon. |
| 2 Users | Marketing (author), Compliance (legal/claims review), Founder/Management (brand approval), Super Admin (publish rights), Sales (pricing input), Auditor (read). |
| 3 Permissions | Author ≠ approver ≠ publisher for policy, pricing and testimonial content. Blog and media may be author + single approver. Nobody may publish their own approval. |
| 4 Screens | Content library (type, title, locale, status, owner, last published, next review) · Editor (block-based, with SEO panel: title, description, slug, canonical, OG image, structured data) · Media library (asset, rights basis, alt text, usage list) · Approval queue · Publish/schedule · Version history & rollback · Preview (desktop/tablet/mobile, and a public preview link that expires) · Redirect manager · Site-wide link checker. |
| 5 Content types | Pages (home, platform, solutions hub, six solution pages, about, team, careers, investors, contact) · Services (lane definition, inclusions, price anchor, FAQs) · Industries (verticals list with copy) · Pricing (plan cards, comparison table, GST note) · FAQs (grouped, per page) · Blogs (author, category, tags, publish date) · Testimonials (client, quote, consent record, verification evidence) · Media (image/video with rights) · Locations (city/branch pages with serviceable pincodes) · Notification templates (§22.20.1) · Campaign content (§22.20.2) · Policies (privacy, terms, refund, PSARA compliance). |
| 6 UX flow | Create/edit → validate (SEO, links, images, claims checklist) → submit for review → reviewer comments/approves → publisher schedules → published → scheduled review date set → expires or renews. |
| 7 Fields | content_id, type, locale, title, slug, body blocks, SEO fields, author, reviewer, approver, publisher, status, effective_from, review_due, version, change summary, evidence refs (for testimonials/claims/stats). |
| 8 Validation | **Evidence gate:** any content asserting a client name, a testimonial, an award, a press mention, a certification, or a numeric claim (guard count, city count, uptime) cannot be submitted without a linked evidence record — a signed consent for testimonials/logos, a certificate for certifications, or a query reference for platform statistics. Numeric claims about live operations must bind to a metric ID so they update or expire rather than drift. |
| 9 Business logic | Pricing content is generated from the pricing configuration, not typed: changing the displayed B2C plan prices or SaaS plan prices requires a pricing-change approval (Finance + Founder/Management) and publishes to the website and the booking calculator in one atomic action. Enterprise price is never rendered publicly. |
| 10 Backend logic | Content is versioned and immutable per version; publishing swaps the live pointer; rollback is a pointer move, available for the last 20 versions; CDN cache invalidation is part of the publish transaction, and a publish is not "Completed" until purge confirms. |
| 11 Status lifecycle | Draft → Pending (review) → Verified (approved) → Active (published) → Expiring (review due) → Archived. Scheduled publishes hold at Verified until the effective time. |
| 12 Notifications | Reviewer assigned; approval granted/rejected with comments; publish succeeded/failed; review due at 30/7 days; broken link detected. |
| 13 Integrations | CDN purge, sitemap regeneration, search-console ping, analytics annotation on publish (so traffic changes are explicable), image optimisation pipeline. |
| 14 Security | Publish rights are a distinct permission, not implied by edit rights; preview links expire in 72 hours and are unguessable; policy pages require Compliance approval and record the reviewing person. |
| 15 Audit | Full diff per version, approval chain with timestamps, publish and rollback events, evidence links, and who purged cache. |
| 16 Edge cases | Emergency correction of a live factual error (a fast path: Super Admin may publish with Compliance notified within 1 hour and a retrospective approval recorded — the only bypass, and it is logged loudly); a testimonial whose consent is withdrawn (immediate unpublish with the withdrawal record retained); a location page for a city no longer serviced (auto-flagged when the branch archives). |
| 17 QA | Publish/rollback integrity, evidence-gate enforcement, price-config binding, cache purge confirmation, link checker false-positive rate. |
| 18 Acceptance | **Given** a marketing user adding a testimonial quoting a named company, **When** they submit without a consent evidence record, **Then** submission is blocked with the message naming the missing evidence type, and the content cannot reach the approval queue. |
| 19 Analytics | `content_publish{type}`, `content_rollback`, `content_review_overdue`; KPIs: % of pages past review date, mean approval time, broken-link count, publish failure rate. |
| 20 Future | Multi-locale website content (Hindi site), A/B testing of hero copy, structured city-service landing-page generation from templates. |

##### Publish workflow and approval chain

| Content type | Author | Reviewer (mandatory) | Approver | Publisher | Review cadence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Marketing pages | Marketing | Marketing lead | Founder/Management | Marketing (with publish right) | 180 days |
| Services & industries | Marketing | Sales + Operations | Founder/Management | Marketing | 180 days |
| Pricing (B2C and SaaS) | Sales | Finance | Founder/Management | Super Admin | On change only |
| FAQs | Support | Marketing | Marketing lead | Marketing | 180 days |
| Blogs | Marketing | Marketing lead | — | Marketing | 365 days |
| Testimonials & client logos | Marketing | Compliance (consent evidence) | Founder/Management | Marketing | 365 days or consent term |
| Media assets | Marketing | Marketing lead (rights check) | — | Marketing | On use |
| Locations / city pages | Marketing | City Operations (serviceability) | — | Marketing | 90 days |
| Policies (privacy, terms, refund, PSARA) | Compliance | External legal review recorded | Founder/Management | Super Admin | 365 days or on change |
| Notification templates | Ops / Marketing | Compliance where legal or safety language | Marketing lead | Marketing | 365 days |
| Campaign content | Marketing | Compliance where claims present | Marketing lead | Marketing | Per campaign |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-OPS-022 | The CMS shall block publication of any content asserting a client relationship, testimonial, award, press mention, certification, or operational statistic without a linked evidence record, and shall expire such content when its evidence expires. |
| SUR-OPS-023 | Publicly displayed operational statistics shall bind to a metric ID and render the value as of a stated date, or not render at all — no hand-typed counts. |
| SUR-OPS-024 | The footer link set shall be validated on every publish; a publish that would leave a footer link 404 shall fail (directly addressing P8). |
| SUR-OPS-025 | Enterprise SaaS pricing shall never be rendered on any public surface by any content path. |

#### 22.21.1 Reports (condensed)

| Point | Specification |

| Purpose | Scheduled and ad-hoc reporting for internal use, client delivery and regulatory/inspection needs. |

Standard catalogue includes: Daily Operations Summary, Attendance Register, Absence & Replacement, Patrol Compliance, Wake-Check Compliance, Incident Register, SLA Performance per client, Deployment Fill Rate, Guard Reliability Ranking, Document Expiry, Licence Register, Payroll Summary, Billing & Collections, Receivables Ageing, Settlement Statement, Subscription MRR & Churn, Verification TAT, Support SLA, Complaint Register, Branch P&L. |
| Logic & statuses | Reports run against the analytics read model; every report carries the scope, the filter set, the generation timestamp and the generating user in its header and file metadata. |
| Audit/security | Every export logged with row count; exports containing PII are watermarked and, above a configured row count (default 1,000), require a second approver. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a City Ops user scheduling the Attendance Register weekly, **When** it delivers, **Then** the file contains only that user's city, the header states the scope, and the delivery is logged. |

#### 22.21.2 Analytics (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Trend and comparison analysis across branches, clients, guards, agencies and time — the layer above reports. Analytics architecture is §42; this is the OPS surface. |
| Users/Permissions | Founder/Management, National/State/City Ops within scope, Finance, Marketing (growth metrics), Auditor. |
| Screens & key UI | Analytics workspace with saved views: Operations performance (attendance, fill rate, incidents, SLA by branch), Growth (bookings, conversion, CAC by source), SaaS (MRR waterfall, cohort retention, feature adoption by plan), Workforce (attrition, reliability distribution, cost per guard-shift), Client (revenue concentration, health distribution, churn drivers). Comparison mode: any metric across branches or periods side by side. |
| Logic & statuses | All metrics come from the versioned metric registry used by the dashboard (§22.4), so a number never differs between two screens. |
| Audit/security | Cross-branch comparison is available only to State Ops and above; branch-level users see their own branch and an anonymised benchmark. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a State Ops user comparing four cities on attendance %, **When** the view renders, **Then** each city's figure matches the corresponding Executive Dashboard card exactly for the same period. |

#### 22.21.3 AI in OPS (cross-reference)

The AI capabilities available inside OPS — natural-language dashboard queries, report generation, anomaly detection, incident summarisation, document extraction, allocation recommendations — are specified in **§25** (Admin AI, Command Center AI, Analytics AI, Compliance AI surfaces). OPS provides only the surfaces: the AI launcher in the top bar, the per-module context panel, the approval cards in each module's action area, and the AI Interaction log viewer under Administration. Governance and policy live in §41.

### 22.22 Platform administration modules

#### 22.22.1 Integrations (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Configure and monitor every external connection: payments, messaging, maps, storage, face-match, biometric devices, accounting export, background verification, tender feeds. |
| Users/Permissions | Super Admin configures credentials; Ops and Finance see health for the integrations they depend on; nobody but Super Admin sees secrets, and secrets are never displayed after entry. |
| Screens & key UI | Integration catalogue (provider, purpose, environment, status, last success, error rate) · Configuration (credentials via a secret store reference, endpoints, retry policy, rate limits) · Health dashboard (success rate, latency p95, last 24h error timeline) · Webhook log with replay · Sandbox toggle. |
| Logic & statuses | Active · Degraded · Failed · Suspended. Each integration declares its fallback: payments (retry then manual reference entry), WhatsApp (fall back to SMS), maps (fall back to last-known coordinates with a stale badge), face-match (fall back to manual review), tender feed (manual entry). |
| Audit/security | Credential changes audited (who, when, which integration — never the value); webhook replays audited. |
| Acceptance | **Given** the WhatsApp provider returning errors for 10 minutes, **When** a client notification is triggered, **Then** it is delivered by SMS, the fallback is recorded on the notification record, and the integration shows Degraded. |

#### 22.22.2 API management (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Administer the platform's own API surface used by first-party apps, agency Enterprise integrations and partners. API design is §33; this is its administration. |
| Users/Permissions | Super Admin issues and revokes keys; Support views usage to help agencies; Finance sees usage for any metered pricing. |
| Screens & key UI | API client list (tenant, name, scopes, environment, created, last used, rate limit) · Key issue/rotate/revoke · Scope editor (least privilege, per-resource read/write) · Usage dashboard (calls, errors, p95 latency, top endpoints per client) · Rate-limit policy per plan (Enterprise API is a plan entitlement) · Deprecation notices. |
| Logic & statuses | Active · Suspended · Revoked. Keys are displayed exactly once at creation. Rotation supports an overlap window (default 7 days) so integrations do not break. |
| Audit/security | Key issue/rotate/revoke audited with scopes; any key with write scope on financial resources requires a second approver. |
| Acceptance | **Given** an Enterprise agency exceeding its rate limit, **When** requests are throttled, **Then** the agency sees a 429 with a documented retry-after, the account owner is notified once per day, and Support sees the usage spike on the dashboard. |

#### 22.22.3 Roles & permissions (condensed — matrix in §31)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Define which internal role may do what, and grant those roles to employees with a geographic scope. The full permission matrix is §31; the OPS module visibility table for internal roles is §22.26 below. |
| Users/Permissions | Super Admin only for role definition; HR proposes grants, Super Admin approves; Auditor reviews. |
| Screens & key UI | Role list (name, description, users, permission count, last changed) · Permission editor (module × action grid) · Grant workspace (employee, role, scope, start, end, justification) · Access review (quarterly campaign: each manager confirms or revokes their team's grants) · Segregation-of-duties rule editor (conflicting role pairs, e.g. Payroll preparer + approver, Verification + Compliance sign-off). |
| Logic & statuses | Grants: Pending → Active → Expiring → Revoked. Time-boxed grants are supported and preferred for temporary cover. Conflicting grants are blocked at assignment time with the rule named. |
| Audit/security | Every role definition change and every grant/revocation is audited; access review results are retained for the audit period. |
| Acceptance | **Given** an employee already holding Finance (payroll approve), **When** HR proposes the Payroll (preparer) role, **Then** the grant is blocked citing the segregation-of-duties rule, with an exception path requiring Founder/Management. |

#### 22.22.4 Audit logs (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | The append-only record of who did what, from where, to which record, with what result — the evidentiary backbone of the whole platform. |
| Users/Permissions | Auditor and Super Admin read all; Compliance reads compliance-relevant events; every role can see the audit trail of records within their scope; nobody can delete or edit an entry, including Super Admin. |
| Screens & key UI | Audit explorer (filters: actor, role, action, entity type, entity ID, date range, IP, session, result) · Entry detail (before/after diff, request metadata, related AI Interaction ID, related approval) · Saved investigations · Export (signed, hash-chained). |
| Logic & statuses | Entries are immutable and hash-chained so tampering is detectable; retention per §39 with legal-hold support. High-sensitivity events (impersonation, break-glass, permission change, manual ledger adjustment, licence status change, bulk export) are additionally streamed to a separate write-once store. |
| Audit/security | Reading the audit log is itself audited. Access to another employee's actions requires the Auditor or Super Admin role. |
| Acceptance | **Given** an investigation into a refund, **When** the auditor filters by entity ID, **Then** the timeline shows the request, every approval, the ledger entries, the notification sent, and any AI involvement, each with server timestamps and actor identities. |

#### 22.22.5 System settings (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | The configuration that changes behaviour without code: thresholds, grace periods, SLAs, escalation ladders, reason-code libraries, serviceability, pricing configuration, holiday calendars, statutory rule sets, feature flags. |
| Users/Permissions | Super Admin edits; owning functional role proposes; every change requires a second approver; Auditor reviews. |
| Screens & key UI | Settings explorer grouped by domain (Operations, Attendance, Alerts & Escalation, Finance, Compliance, Notifications, AI, Security) · Setting detail (key, current value, allowed range, default, owner, last changed, change history) · Change request workspace (proposed value, reason, effective time, approvals) · Environment comparison (staging vs production values). |
| Logic & statuses | Every setting has a type, allowed range and default; out-of-range values are rejected at entry. Changes to safety-relevant settings (wake-check timeout, SOS ack target, escalation timers, geofence minimums) take effect only at the next shift boundary to avoid mid-shift behaviour changes. |
| Audit/security | Full change history per setting with before/after and approvals; a weekly digest of all setting changes goes to Founder/Management and Auditor. |
| Acceptance | **Given** an attempt to set the SOS acknowledgement target to 300 seconds, **When** the value is entered, **Then** it is rejected as outside the allowed range (10–60s) with the range and owner shown. |

#### 22.22.6 Security settings (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | The controls governing access to OPS itself: MFA, session policy, device registration, IP allowlisting, password policy, key management, break-glass configuration. Control definitions are §38; this is their administration. |
| Users/Permissions | Super Admin only; changes require a second Super Admin or Founder/Management approval; Auditor reads. |
| Screens & key UI | Security posture dashboard (MFA coverage %, sessions active, devices registered, failed-login trend, privileged actions in last 24h) · Session policy (idle timeout default 20 min for OPS, absolute 8h; re-auth for sensitive actions) · Device registration list (employee, device, registered, last seen, revoke) · IP allowlist per role class (optional; mandatory for Super Admin and Finance release actions) `[RECOMMENDED]` · Failed-login and lockout policy (5 attempts, 15-minute lockout, notification to the user) · Break-glass configuration (§22.24). |
| Logic & statuses | Any reduction in a security control (longer session, MFA exemption, allowlist removal) requires dual approval, records a justification, and expires automatically after a maximum of 30 days. |
| Audit/security | All changes streamed to the write-once store; a control reduction generates an immediate notification to Founder/Management and Auditor. |
| Acceptance | **Given** a request to disable MFA for one account, **When** it is submitted, **Then** it requires two Super Admin approvals, is limited to a maximum of 24 hours, and notifies Founder/Management and Auditor at submission and at expiry. |

### 22.23 Impersonation and "view as" support tooling

Support and engineering need to see what a user sees. This is the single most abusable capability in the platform, so it is specified tightly.

| Aspect | Rule |
|---|---|
| Who may impersonate | Support (agency and client users, read-only), Super Admin (any user, read-only by default), Engineering on-call via break-glass only (§22.24). No other role. |
| Default mode | **View-as (read-only)**: the session can render every screen the target user can, but every write endpoint is refused with `IMPERSONATION_READ_ONLY`. |
| Write mode | Requires (a) a linked support ticket, (b) an explicit business reason from a fixed list, (c) recorded consent from the target user (in-app accept, or an email/WhatsApp confirmation captured against the ticket) for agency and client users, and (d) Super Admin approval. Write impersonation is capped at 30 minutes and cannot be extended more than once. |
| Consent exemptions | Consent is not required for Suraksha's own internal users (employees) when investigating a security incident, and for tenants where a signed Enterprise support agreement records standing consent — the standing-consent document must be linked to the session. |
| Never impersonable | Guard identities for the purpose of marking attendance, acknowledging a wake check, or raising/closing an SOS; any user for the purpose of approving a financial action; any Auditor account. These are hard blocks, not policy. |
| Session banner | A persistent, non-dismissible red banner across the top of every screen: "You are viewing as <name> (<role>, <tenant>) — read-only — 24:31 remaining — End session". The banner is rendered server-side so it cannot be hidden by client tampering. |
| Target-side visibility | The impersonated user sees an in-app notice at the start of the session and receives a notification afterwards listing who, when, how long, read or write, and the ticket reference. Agencies get a monthly digest of all impersonation sessions on their tenant. |
| Data limits | Impersonation never exposes another tenant's data (the impersonated identity's tenant scope applies), never reveals stored secrets, and blocks bulk export and report scheduling entirely. |
| Duration & idle | Read-only sessions expire at 60 minutes; idle timeout 10 minutes; both hard limits. |
| Audit | Session start/end, actor, target, mode, ticket, reason, consent evidence, approvals, and every screen viewed and action attempted (including refused writes) are written to the write-once store and are visible to the tenant on request. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-OPS-026 | Impersonation shall be implemented as an explicit session attribute (`acting_as`), never by issuing the target user's token; all downstream logs shall record both the real actor and the acting identity. |
| SUR-OPS-027 | Write-mode impersonation shall be impossible without a recorded consent artefact or a linked standing-consent agreement, enforced server-side. |
| SUR-OPS-028 | Attendance marking, wake-check acknowledgement, SOS actions, financial approvals and audit-role access shall be permanently non-impersonable. |
| SUR-OPS-029 | Every tenant shall be able to view the complete log of impersonation sessions on its own data from within the Agency Portal. |

### 22.24 Break-glass emergency access

Break-glass covers the case where normal access control would prevent Suraksha from responding to an emergency: a production incident locking out administrators, a life-safety event where the only person available lacks the role, or a security incident requiring immediate containment.

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger conditions | (1) P0 platform outage where no available Super Admin can authenticate; (2) life-safety emergency (§24 P0) where the on-duty operator lacks the scope needed to act; (3) confirmed security incident requiring immediate account or tenant containment; (4) lawful demand requiring immediate preservation. |
| Accounts | Two named break-glass accounts per environment, credentials split (password with Security custodian, MFA seed with a second custodian), stored in a sealed secret store. They are never used for routine work and have no email notifications suppressed. |
| Activation | Requires both custodians, or one custodian plus a Founder/Management authorisation recorded by phone with the reason stated. Activation opens a mandatory incident record before the session begins. |
| Scope of powers | Full administrative scope, except: cannot alter audit logs, cannot disable audit streaming, cannot delete data, cannot release payments or payroll, cannot change the break-glass configuration itself. |
| Time box | 60 minutes, single extension of 60 minutes with a re-recorded reason. Auto-revoke at expiry with all sessions terminated. |
| Alerting | Activation immediately alerts Founder/Management, Super Admins, Compliance and Auditor by push, SMS and email simultaneously — it is deliberately impossible to use quietly. |
| Post-use | Within 24 hours: mandatory review with a written record of what was done and why, credential rotation for both custodians, and an entry in the compliance findings tracker. Failure to complete the review within 72 hours raises a P1 compliance finding. |
| Testing | Break-glass is exercised quarterly in a controlled drill, with the drill itself logged and reviewed; an untested break-glass path is treated as a control failure. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-OPS-030 | Break-glass activation shall create an immutable incident record before granting elevated access, and shall notify at least four distinct recipients across three channels within 60 seconds. |
| SUR-OPS-031 | Break-glass sessions shall be incapable of modifying, disabling or redirecting audit logging, and shall be incapable of releasing money. |
| SUR-OPS-032 | Break-glass credentials shall be rotated after every use and after every drill, with rotation recorded. |

## 23. Admin App

### 23.1 What it is and the parity decision

The Suraksha Admin App is **SURAKSHA OPS in app format for authorised Suraksha personnel** — the fourth mobile application in the ecosystem. It is not a second product with its own rules: same identity, same roles, same scopes, same audit trail, same data.

**Parity decision `[RECOMMENDED]`: deliberate non-parity.** The Admin App implements roughly 30% of OPS by module count and close to 90% of OPS by *urgent event volume*. The reasoning is operational and security-driven, not effort-driven:

| Argument | Consequence |
|---|---|
| The work that genuinely happens away from a desk is *responding*: an alert at 03:10, an approval blocking a deployment, a client calling a manager at a wedding. | Ship alert response, approvals and lookup at full quality. |
| The work that must not happen on a phone is *irreversible and financial*: releasing a payroll run, approving a ₹2L refund, changing permissions, exporting 4,000 guard records. Phones are lost, shoulder-surfed and unlocked by others. | Forbid or step-up-gate these (§23.4). |
| Configuration work (escalation ladders, system settings, CMS publishing, role definitions) is dense, needs comparison and review, and is done rarely. | Exclude from mobile entirely. |
| A half-implemented module is worse than an absent one, because the operator believes they have acted when they have not. | Every included screen is complete for its job; nothing is a stub. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-ADP-001 | The Admin App shall implement the module set in §23.5 completely; modules not listed shall be absent from navigation and shall not be reachable by deep link, returning an in-app "available on ops.surakshaguards.in" screen with a copy-link action. |
| SUR-ADP-002 | The Admin App shall use the same permission service, scope resolution and audit pipeline as OPS; no mobile-specific permission logic shall exist. |
| SUR-ADP-003 | Every action performed in the Admin App shall be audit-logged with `channel=mobile`, device ID and app version, so that mobile-originated actions are distinguishable in investigations. |
| SUR-ADP-004 | The Admin App shall support Android and iOS with feature equality between them; no capability shall exist on one platform only. |

### 23.2 Security posture

The Admin App carries the same authority as OPS on a device that leaves the building, so its controls are stricter than any other app in the ecosystem.

| Control | Specification |
|---|---|
| Device registration | An OPS account must register a device before first use: device fingerprint, model, OS version, push token. Registration requires approval by Super Admin (or by the employee's manager where delegated). Max 2 registered devices per employee. Registration is revocable from OPS and from the employee's own session list. |
| Authentication | Phone/email + password + MFA on first login per device. MFA is mandatory for all internal roles (SUR-OPS-005). |
| App lock | Biometric (fingerprint/face) or 6-digit app PIN required on every foreground resume after 60 seconds in background. Biometric failure falls back to PIN, PIN failure five times wipes the local session. |
| Session | Idle timeout 10 minutes (stricter than OPS's 20). Absolute session 12 hours, after which full re-authentication with MFA. Command Center Operators on an active watch may hold a 12-hour session with app-lock resumes, which is why app lock and session timeout are separate controls. |
| Local storage | No operational data cached beyond the current session except: the alert list for the last 4 hours, and the on-call contact directory. All local storage encrypted with a key held in the platform keystore and destroyed on logout, app-lock wipe or device revocation. |
| Screenshots | Screenshot and screen recording blocked on screens showing guard PII, client financial data, documents and audit logs (Android FLAG_SECURE, iOS equivalent). Attempted screenshots on these screens are logged. |
| Export | **No bulk export from mobile.** No CSV, no XLSX, no PDF report generation, no multi-record share. Single-record share is limited to a deep link (not the data) plus a name and phone number where the role already permits it. |
| Network | Certificate pinning; refuses to operate on a device where a proxy-injected certificate is detected. Root/jailbreak detection: app runs in read-only mode on a compromised device and reports the condition. |
| Remote control | Super Admin can remotely revoke a device, terminate its sessions and force a local wipe of app data; effect within 60 seconds when the device is online, at next launch otherwise. |
| Offline | The Admin App is **not** offline-first (canon reserves that for the Guard App). With no connectivity it shows the last-known alert list with a prominent stale banner and disables every action. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-ADP-005 | The Admin App shall refuse to function on an unregistered device, and shall not permit registration and first login to be completed in the same session without MFA. |
| SUR-ADP-006 | The Admin App shall not implement any data export capability, and its API client shall not be granted export scopes. |
| SUR-ADP-007 | Screens displaying KYC documents, salary figures, audit logs and client financial detail shall block screen capture and shall watermark on-screen content with the viewer's name, employee ID and timestamp. |
| SUR-ADP-008 | Loss of the device shall be recoverable by a single action in OPS (revoke device) that terminates sessions, invalidates the push token, and wipes local data on next contact. |

### 23.3 The screens that matter on mobile

| Screen | Job it does | Key UI | Actions available |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alert feed | The home screen. Everything that needs a human, ordered by severity then age. | Grouped list: P0 pinned with a red band and a persistent sound; P1 next; P2/P3 collapsed under counts. Each row: severity chip, alert type, site, client, guard, age timer, ack state, assigned operator. Pull-to-refresh plus live socket updates. | Acknowledge · Call guard · Call supervisor · Assign to me · Add note · Escalate · Mark false alarm (with reason) |

No wallboard, no multi-panel. | Same alert actions · Initiate replacement · Dispatch supervisor |
| Booking assignment | Fill a booking or a gap from anywhere. | Booking card (client, site, guards needed, start time, urgency) then ranked candidates from §25.15 with name, photo, distance, ETA, reliability score and the top two reasons for the score. | Notify top 3 · Assign (if role permits) · Request supervisor to arrange · Escalate to City Ops |
| Approvals queue | Unblock work that is waiting on a human. | Single list of pending approvals routed to this user, each showing: what, who requested, amount or impact, age, and the two or three facts needed to decide. Swipe right approve, swipe left reject (reject always requires a reason). | Approve · Reject with reason · Defer with a note · Open full record (view-only) |
