Live countdown to the next rung. | Acknowledge · Take ownership · Call any rung participant in one tap · Add action note · Resolve (with mandatory outcome) · Escalate now |
| Client / agency lookup | Answer a question while on a call. | Search by name/phone/site/ID. Client card: sites, active guards now, today's attendance, open incidents, receivables status (masked amounts unless Finance), account owner, escalation contacts. Agency card: plan, verification state, licence status, open tickets, account owner. | Call · WhatsApp · Raise ticket · Open incident · Add note |
| Guard lookup | Verify a guard on the spot. | Photo, name, ID, category, verification badge, current assignment, document compliance, phone, supervisor. | Call · Message · View assignment · Raise incident |
| On-call actions | The narrow set of things that must be doable at 3 AM. | A single action sheet reachable from anywhere: Initiate replacement · Log incident · Notify client contact · Dispatch supervisor · Raise alert manually · Start conference call with escalation contacts. | As listed |
| Notifications & shift | Manage the operator's own duty state. | Current watch scope, shift end time, handover status, notification channel test, do-not-disturb override state. | Start/end watch · Begin handover (§24.12) · Test alert sound |
| My audit | Transparency for the actor themselves. | The last 50 actions this user performed on mobile, with timestamps. | View only |

### 23.4 Forbidden and step-up-gated operations

| Operation | Mobile treatment |
|---|---|
| Payroll run approval or release | **Forbidden.** Not present in the app. |
| Agency settlement release, payout batch release | **Forbidden.** |
| Manual ledger credit/debit, wallet adjustment | **Forbidden.** |
| Refund approval | **Forbidden** above ₹5,000; below that, step-up gated. |
| Role, permission or scope changes | **Forbidden.** |
| Security settings, system settings, escalation ladder configuration | **Forbidden.** |
| Bulk data export, report scheduling, audience export | **Forbidden.** |
| KYC/verification approval decisions | **Forbidden** (they need document scrutiny that a phone screen cannot give). |
| Impersonation (any mode) | **Forbidden.** |
| Break-glass activation | **Forbidden.** |
| Contract activation or amendment | **Forbidden.** |
| Guard blacklisting, termination | **Forbidden.** |
| CMS publish | **Forbidden.** |
| Assigning a guard to a deployment | Allowed, step-up gated for Tier-1 clients and armed posts. |
| Approving an exception deployment (unstaffed activation) | Allowed with step-up. |
| Approving leave that creates a coverage gap | Allowed with step-up. |
| Marking an SOS as false alarm | Allowed with step-up and a mandatory reason from a fixed list. |
| Reducing an incident's severity | Allowed with step-up, State Ops+ only, reason mandatory. |
| Viewing a KYC document | Allowed with step-up, watermarked, screenshot-blocked, view-only, logged with purpose. |
| Viewing full client financial detail | Allowed with step-up for Finance and Founder/Management only. |

**Step-up authentication** = a fresh biometric or PIN challenge plus a second factor (TOTP or push approval) completed within the last 5 minutes, recorded on the audit entry as `step_up=true` with the method used.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-ADP-009 | Forbidden operations shall be enforced server-side by rejecting the request when `channel=mobile`, not merely by hiding UI. |
| SUR-ADP-010 | Step-up authentication shall be required per action, not per session, and its validity window shall not exceed 5 minutes. |
| SUR-ADP-011 | Any attempt to invoke a forbidden operation from mobile shall be logged as a security event and shall be visible in the security posture dashboard (§22.22.6). |

Screen count: **28 screens** (listed in §28 screen inventory; not re-described here).

### 23.6 The on-call operator workflow at 3 AM

This is the workflow the app exists for, written as the actual sequence with the app's specific behaviour at each step.

| Time | Event | App behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| 03:07:12 | Wake check at Site "Sunrise Industrial Park, Gate 2" scheduled; guard does not respond within 120s; auto-retry fires. | Nothing yet — retry is in progress, no alert. |
| 03:08:14 | Retry lapses. Alert `WAKE_MISSED` raised at P1. | Push arrives on the on-call device with a critical-alert sound that bypasses silent mode (Android notification channel with `IMPORTANCE_HIGH` + full-screen intent; iOS Critical Alert entitlement `[ASSUMPTION: A-146]` — entitlement approval is not guaranteed, fallback is a repeating high-priority push plus an SMS after 60s). Phone shows a full-screen alert card: site, guard name and photo, client, last known location, time since. Two large buttons: **Acknowledge** and **Call guard**. |
| 03:08:31 | Operator taps Acknowledge. | Biometric app-lock challenge (device was asleep) → acknowledged at 03:08:31; ack time 17s recorded against the 60s P1 target; alert now owned by this operator and visible as owned on the console and to any other on-call device. |
| 03:08:40 | Operator taps Call guard. | Native dialler with the guard's number; call outcome captured on return to the app ("Answered / No answer / Busy / Switched off") — mandatory single tap, appended to the alert timeline. |
| 03:09:20 | No answer. | App surfaces the next rung automatically: **Call supervisor (Ramesh K., 2.4 km away)** with a one-tap call, plus **Dispatch supervisor to site** which sends a task with the site address, gate instructions and the SOP link. |
| 03:10:05 | Supervisor answers, agrees to reach the site; operator taps Dispatch. | Supervisor receives a task in the Guard/Supervisor app with navigation; the alert timeline records dispatch with ETA; the auto-escalation timer to rung 3 (Field Officer / City Ops) is extended by the configured dispatch grace (15 minutes) — an extension, never a cancellation, and it is recorded as an operator decision. |
| 03:14:00 | Operator adds a note. | "Guard not reachable, supervisor en route, ETA 03:22. Client not notified — within contractual grace." Notes are mandatory before the operator can move to another alert while this one is unresolved. |
| 03:23:40 | Supervisor arrives, finds the guard asleep in the guard room, wakes them, photographs the post. | Supervisor's app submits arrival with GPS and photo; the alert card updates live on the operator's phone. |
| 03:26:00 | Operator resolves. | Resolution requires: outcome from a fixed list (Guard asleep — counselled / Guard absent / Device failure / Network failure / Medical / False alarm / Other), a note, and — because the outcome is a conduct finding — an auto-created Incident at P2 assigned to the guard's supervisor for the disciplinary record. Client notification decision is presented explicitly with the contract's rule pre-selected (§24.7). |
| 03:27:10 | Alert closed. | Alert leaves the feed; the operator's scorecard (§24.14) records ack 17s, first action 26s, resolution 18m 56s; the shift log gains an entry that appears in the 06:00 handover. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-ADP-012 | P0 and P1 alerts shall be delivered to the on-call device by a channel that bypasses silent/DND, with an SMS fallback within 60 seconds if the push is not confirmed as delivered, and a voice call fallback within 180 seconds for P0. |
| SUR-ADP-013 | Acknowledgement from the Admin App shall be indistinguishable in effect from acknowledgement at the console, and shall immediately suppress duplicate notification to other on-call devices while showing them who owns it. |
| SUR-ADP-014 | The app shall require a call-outcome capture after any in-app-initiated call attached to an alert, and shall not allow an unresolved owned alert to be left without a note. |
| SUR-ADP-015 | If the on-call device loses connectivity while owning a P0/P1 alert, ownership shall lapse after 90 seconds and the alert shall re-fan-out to the next available operator, with the lapse recorded. |

### 23.7 Remaining depth points (condensed)

| Point | Specification |
|---|---|
| Users & permissions | All fifteen internal roles may install; module visibility follows §22.26 intersected with §23.5. In practice the heavy users are Command Center Operator, City/State Operations, Support and Founder/Management. |
| Validation | Every action form on mobile has the same server-side validation as OPS; client-side validation exists only to reduce round trips. |
| Notifications | Push categories: Critical (P0/P1 alerts, SOS), Operational (approvals, assignments, escalations at your rung), Informational (daily digest, mentions). Users may mute Informational only. Category mute state is visible to the on-call roster so a muted operator is not scheduled. |
| Integrations | Native dialler, WhatsApp deep link, maps navigation hand-off, push services, biometric APIs. |
| Edge cases | Two operators acknowledge within the same second (first server-received wins, second sees "already owned by X"); app killed by the OS while owning an alert (SUR-ADP-015 lapse applies); device clock skew (server time is authoritative everywhere, device time shown only as a secondary value); operator on a flight (watch state marked unavailable, roster reassigns). |
| QA | Alert delivery latency under poor network (target: push received within 5s at p95 on 4G, within 15s on 2G/EDGE); app-lock resume; forbidden-operation server rejection; device revocation effect within 60s. |
| Acceptance | **Given** an operator whose device is revoked in OPS while the app is open, **When** the next request is made or within 60 seconds, **Then** the app terminates the session, wipes local data, and shows a re-registration screen. |
| Analytics & KPIs | `adp_alert_ack{severity, seconds}`, `adp_action{type}`, `adp_stepup{result}`, `adp_forbidden_attempt`. KPIs: median mobile acknowledgement time by severity, % of P1 alerts first acknowledged on mobile, approval turnaround on mobile vs web. |
| Future scalability | Wearable acknowledgement for P0 `[FUTURE]`; push-to-talk to supervisors `[FUTURE]`; offline read cache for the alert feed if field experience demands it (would require a re-examination of the local-storage stance). |

## 24. Command Center

### 24.1 Why this section exists and what it owns

The 24/7 command center is the brand promise on the public website. It is also the single place where the platform's most consequential logic lives. **This section is the canonical home for alert severity, escalation, SOS handling and operator process.** Every other section cross-references it. Nothing here is repeated elsewhere.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMD-001 | The Command Center shall be operational 24×7×365 with no unmanned minute during which any deployment is active anywhere in Suraksha's operation. |
| SUR-CMD-002 | Every alert in the ecosystem — from any source, on any product, for any tenant Suraksha operates — shall be created, severity-graded, routed and resolved through the single alerting pipeline defined in §24.6, with no side channels. |
| SUR-CMD-003 | Every escalation shall run on a configured ladder (§24.7); no escalation shall depend on an individual remembering to call someone. |
| SUR-CMD-004 | Every P0 and P1 alert shall terminate in either a resolution with an outcome code or an incident record; silent expiry shall be impossible. |

### 24.2 The physical and virtual command center

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Concept | A hybrid: a **physical watch room** at the head office (and, as the operation grows, one per region) with wallboard displays and dedicated operator consoles, plus a **virtual capability** — the same console works from any authorised device, and the Admin App (§23) provides a reduced watch surface. The physical room exists because escalation is a social act (operators overhear each other, a supervisor walks in, a founder can stand behind a screen during a crisis); the virtual capability exists because 03:00 coverage in a young company is partly remote. |
| Physical layout | Wallboard wall (3 displays: national map, alert board, KPI strip) · 2–4 operator desks, each with dual monitors (console left, drill-down right), headset, dedicated telephony line and a hard-wired network path · a supervisor/shift-lead desk with visibility of all consoles · a whiteboard for the shift log that is also captured digitally · UPS-backed power and a secondary internet path (primary broadband + 4G/5G failover) · CCTV of the room itself, retained per §39. |
| Virtual capability | Console works in a browser on any registered device; a remote operator must be on a registered device with MFA, must be on the on-call roster, and must pass a start-of-watch readiness check (audio test, network test, alert-sound test) recorded in the shift log. |
| Redundancy | If the primary room is unavailable (power, network, access), the shift lead declares a **remote watch** in OPS; the roster's remote operators take the seats within 10 minutes; the declaration and the gap are logged and reviewed. |
| Client visibility | `[FUTURE]` A viewing gallery / video tour asset for enterprise sales; nothing in the client-facing product depends on it. |

### 24.3 Staffing model

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Seat model | A **seat** is a scope of watch responsibility, not a person: e.g. "West Seat — Gujarat + Maharashtra". Seats are defined in OPS with their scope, their required staffing per shift band, and their alert routing. |
| Shift bands | Three 8-hour watches: Morning 06:00–14:00, Evening 14:00–22:00, Night 22:00–06:00. The night watch is the heaviest (wake checks, patrols, lone-guard risk) and is staffed at no less than the evening level despite lower volume. |
| Minimum staffing | Never fewer than **one operator plus one reachable shift lead** for the whole operation at any minute. Scaling rule `[RECOMMENDED]`: one operator per **250 active guards on duty** or per **60 active sites**, whichever is the higher requirement, with a floor of one and a ceiling of six per room before a second room is opened. Night watch adds one operator per 400 wake-check-bearing guards. |
| Roles on watch | **Command Center Operator** (handles alerts, owns the console) · **Shift Lead** (a City/State Operations user on watch duty: owns escalations at rung 4, approves exceptions, runs handover, signs the shift log) · **On-call Manager** (State/National Operations, reachable by phone, rung 5) · **On-call Executive** (Founder/Management, rung 6, P0 only). |
| Competence | An operator may not take a seat until certified on: the alert taxonomy, the escalation ladders, SOS handling, the false-alarm policy, client communication rules, and the site SOPs for the seat's scope. Certification is a Training record (§22.18.1) with a 12-month validity, and the console blocks seat assignment without it. |
| Continuity | Handover is a formal process (§24.12). An operator may not end a watch with an unacknowledged P0/P1 in their scope; if the incoming operator has not accepted handover, the outgoing operator stays and the overrun is logged. |
| Wellbeing | Maximum 8-hour watch, minimum 11 hours between watches, maximum 5 consecutive night watches `[RECOMMENDED]`, mandatory 20-minute break at the midpoint with seat coverage arranged before the break is granted by the console. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMD-005 | OPS shall block the start of a watch band if any seat covering a scope with active deployments has no certified operator assigned, and shall raise a P1 to the on-call manager. |
| SUR-CMD-006 | The console shall refuse to grant a break if it would leave the seat's scope uncovered, and shall record every break with cover arrangements. |

### 24.4 Operator screen layout

Three surfaces, deliberately separated so the operator is never one misclick from losing the picture.

#### 24.4.1 Wallboard (shared, glanceable, no interaction)

| Zone | Content | Refresh |
|---|---|---|
| Left 40% | National/scope map with clustered live guard positions, colour-coded; alert pins pulse; the map auto-zooms to any new P0 for 30 seconds then returns. | 15s (positions), instant (alerts) |
| Centre 35% | Alert board: the live queue, severity-sorted, largest text in the room. Each row: severity, type, site, client, age, owner. P0 rows occupy a full-width band with an audible tone. | Instant |
| Right 25% top | Watch KPIs: guards on duty · required vs deployed · unstaffed posts · attendance % today · wake-check compliance tonight · open P0/P1 · mean ack time this watch. | 30s |
| Right 25% bottom | Expiry & risk strip: licences expiring ≤7 days · documents expiring ≤7 days · sites at Critical risk band with an open issue. | 5 min |
| Footer ticker | Shift log highlights, handover notes, planned events (VIP movement, festival, strike, weather warning) entered by the shift lead. | On change |

#### 24.4.2 Operator console (the working surface)

Four panes, fixed positions, keyboard-driven.

| Pane | Content | Interactions |
|---|---|---|
| Queue (left, 30%) | The operator's alert queue: assigned to me · unassigned in my scope · watching. Severity chips, age timers turning amber then red at the ack target, source icon. | `j/k` move, `Enter` open, `a` acknowledge, `e` escalate, `f` false alarm, `r` resolve |
| Alert workspace (centre, 45%) | The open alert: header (type, severity, site, client, guard, times), the **fact panel** (last GPS, last check-in, last patrol scan, last wake check, battery, device state, site risk band, client tier, contract SLA, site SOP link), the **ladder panel** (rungs with state and countdown), the **timeline** (every event and note, server-timestamped), and the **action bar** (Call guard · Call supervisor · Dispatch · Replacement · Notify client · Create incident · Resolve). | All actions; every action appends to the timeline automatically |
| Context (right, 25%) | Tabs: Site (details, SOPs, contacts, gate instructions, photos) · Client (tier, contacts, escalation matrix, contractual notification rule) · Guard (profile, reliability, history, recent incidents) · Related (other open alerts at this site/client/guard in the last 24h — the de-duplication view) | Read + one-tap call/WhatsApp on any contact |
| Status bar (bottom) | Operator identity, seat, watch time remaining, alerts handled this watch, mean ack this watch, connectivity indicator, telephony state, sound test button. | Sound test, break request, handover start |

#### 24.4.3 Drill-down (second monitor / expanded)

Opened from any alert: full map with track replay, attendance record, patrol round detail, wake-check history, incident history for the site, contract terms, and the client's SLA position for the month. Drill-down never replaces the console pane — it opens beside it, because an operator must not lose the queue to investigate.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMD-007 | The console shall be fully operable by keyboard, and the six most frequent actions shall each be reachable in one keystroke from the queue. |
| SUR-CMD-008 | The console shall never navigate away from the queue; drill-downs open in a panel or a second window. |
| SUR-CMD-009 | The console shall show a connectivity and data-freshness indicator at all times; if the live stream is more than 30 seconds stale, every panel shall be badged stale and the alert sound shall change to a distinct "data degraded" tone. |

### 24.5 Monitored objects, thresholds and severity

#### 24.5.1 The monitored-object catalogue

| # | Monitored object | Source | Detection rule | Default severity | Site-risk uplift |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Live deployment map | Location ingest | Continuous; not an alert source itself | — | — |
| 2 | Active guards | Attendance + location | Guard on duty with a heartbeat in the last 10 min | — | — |
| 3 | Active sites | Deployment | Sites with an active shift now | — | — |
| 4 | Attendance | Check-in events | Present vs rostered per shift | — | — |
| 5 | Missing guards | Attendance | No check-in at shift start + grace (15 min) and no contact | P1 | Critical → P0 if lone guard at night |
| 6 | Late arrivals | Attendance | Check-in after start + grace, within 60 min | P2 | Critical → P1 |
| 7 | SOS | Guard App panic, client portal panic | Any SOS event | **P0 always** | — |
| 8 | Panic alerts (client-side) | Client app/portal | Client raises panic at a site | **P0 always** | — |
| 9 | Missed wake checks | Wake-check engine | No acknowledgement within timeout + one retry | P1 | Critical → P0 |
| 10 | Patrol exceptions | Patrol engine | Missed round, missed checkpoint, out-of-sequence, implausibly fast round | P2 | Critical → P1 |
| 11 | Incident queue | Incident creation | Any incident of severity ≥ P2 not owned within its target | Inherits incident severity | — |
| 12 | Document expiry | Document engine | Mandatory guard document expiring ≤7 days or expired | P3 (≤7d) / P2 (expired, guard on duty) | — |
| 13 | Licence expiry | Licence engine | Suraksha or agency licence expiring ≤30 days or expired | P2 (≤30d) / P1 (expired with active deployment) | — |
| 14 | Guard replacement | Replacement engine | Replacement open beyond its target (60/120 min) | P1 | — |
| 15 | Unstaffed posts | Roster vs attendance | Active shift with deployed < required and no replacement in progress | P1 | Critical → P0; armed post → P0 |
| 16 | Geofence violations | Location + geofence | 2 consecutive out-of-fence pings ≥60s apart, accuracy ≤100m | P2 | Critical → P1 |
| 17 | Offline devices | Heartbeat | No heartbeat >20 min during an active shift | P2 | Lone night guard → P1 |
| 18 | Shift gaps | Roster | Future shift within 4 hours with unfilled required strength | P2 (4h) / P1 (1h) | — |
| 19 | Client escalations | Client portal, ticket, call | Client raises an escalation against a contractual SLA | P1 | Tier-1 client → P0 if life-safety |
| 20 | High-priority alerts (composite) | Correlation engine | Any two P2s at the same site within 30 min, or any P1 unresolved beyond 2× its target | Uplift by one level | — |
| 21 | Device tamper | Guard App integrity | Mock-location, rooted device, or checkpoint scan from an unassigned device | P1 | — |
| 22 | Battery critical | Guard App | On-duty device below 10% with >2h of shift remaining | P3 | Lone night guard → P2 |

#### 24.5.2 Severity model

| Severity | Definition | Concrete examples | Acknowledge target | First substantive action | Resolution target | Who is woken |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P0 Critical** | Life, safety or liberty is at immediate risk, or a client-facing catastrophic failure is in progress. | SOS pressed by a guard · client panic at a site · armed post unmanned · guard unreachable after an SOS · fire/assault/robbery in progress reported from a site · a Critical-risk site with no guard present at night · platform-wide alerting failure | **30 seconds** | 60 seconds | 60 minutes to a stable outcome (not necessarily closure) | Operator, shift lead, on-call manager, on-call executive, client security contact per §24.7 |
| **P1 High** | A protective control has failed and harm or contractual breach is plausible if not corrected now. | Missed wake check after retry · guard missing at shift start · unstaffed post (non-armed) · replacement overdue · geofence breach at a Critical site · expired licence with active deployment · Tier-1 client escalation · device tamper detected | **60 seconds** | 5 minutes | 4 hours | Operator, shift lead; on-call manager if unacknowledged at rung 3 |
| **P2 Medium** | A deviation that must be corrected this shift but does not by itself endanger anyone. | Late arrival · single missed patrol checkpoint · geofence breach at a standard site · offline device · shift gap in 4 hours · expired guard document while off duty · repeated small deviations at one site | **5 minutes** | 30 minutes | End of shift | Operator only |
| **P3 Informational** | Something to know and to schedule; no immediate operational consequence. | Document expiring in 7 days · battery low with ample shift remaining · patrol round completed late but complete · non-urgent client query routed to the console | **30 minutes** | Same day | 72 hours | Nobody is woken; appears in the digest |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMD-010 | Severity shall be computed by the alerting pipeline from the rule table above plus site-risk and client-tier uplift; an operator may raise severity freely, but may lower it only with State Operations authority and a recorded reason. |
| SUR-CMD-011 | Acknowledgement targets shall be measured from `alert_created_at` (server time) to `acknowledged_at`, and shall be reported per operator, per watch and per severity (§24.14). |
| SUR-CMD-012 | An alert whose acknowledgement target lapses shall auto-escalate per §24.7 without operator action. |

### 24.6 The alerting pipeline

```
Event source ──► Ingest ──► Rule evaluation ──► De-duplication & correlation ──► Alert created
   (Guard App,      (validates,   (severity table,        (§24.10)                    │
    client app,      time-stamps,  site/client uplift)                                 ▼
    engines,         both clocks)                                            Routing & fan-out (§24.7)
    integrations)                                                                      │
                                                                                       ▼
                                                       Console queue + push/SMS/call + wallboard
                                                                                       │
                                                                    Acknowledge → Act → Resolve/Incident
```

| Stage | Specification |
|---|---|
| Ingest | Accepts events from the Guard App (SOS, wake check, patrol, attendance, tamper), the client app/portal (panic, escalation), internal engines (roster, documents, licences, replacement, correlation), and integrations (biometric devices). Every event carries `device_time` and `server_received_time`. Ingest is idempotent on `(source, source_event_id)`. |
| Rule evaluation | Deterministic and versioned. The rule set version is stamped on every alert so historical alerts remain explicable after a rule change. No AI in this path — AI may summarise and suggest, never grade severity (§25.7). |
| Alert record | `alert_id`, type, severity, computed_severity_reason, tenant, branch, site, post, guard, client, source event ref, created_at, ack_at, ack_by, owner, ladder_id + version, rung state, actions, notes, resolution outcome, incident ref, false-alarm flag, dedup group. |
| Delivery | Console (WebSocket), wallboard, push to on-call devices, SMS fallback, voice call for P0, WhatsApp for client contacts where the contract permits. Delivery per rung is recorded with provider receipts. |
| Persistence | Alerts are never deleted. Resolved alerts remain queryable for SLA reporting and post-incident review; retention per §39 with a minimum that covers the longest contractual dispute window. |

### 24.7 The canonical escalation engine

**This is the platform's single escalation definition. Sections 11, 12, 15, 16, 17, 18, 20, 21, 22 and 23 reference it and do not restate it.**

#### 24.7.1 The rungs

| Rung | Who | Reached how | Default hold time before next rung |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | **Guard** (the subject) | App notification + call | 60s (P0) / 120s (P1) |
| 1 | **Supervisor / Field Officer** (the guard's cluster owner) | Push + call | 3 min (P0) / 5 min (P1) |
| 2 | **Agency Ops** — for a deployment run by a marketplace/subcontract agency; skipped for `SURAKSHA-HQ` deployments | Push + call to the agency's on-duty contact | 3 min (P0) / 10 min (P1) |
| 3 | **Suraksha Ops** — City Operations on call for the branch | Push + call + SMS | 5 min (P0) / 15 min (P1) |
| 4 | **Shift Lead / State Operations** | Push + call + SMS | 5 min (P0) / 30 min (P1) |
| 5 | **National Operations / On-call Manager** | Call + SMS | 10 min (P0) / 60 min (P1) |
| 6 | **Founder/Management** | Call | P0 only; no further rung |
| C | **Client security contact** | Per §24.7.4 — a parallel branch, not a rung in the same ladder | — |
| E | **Emergency services** | Operator-initiated, never automatic (§24.7.5) | — |

Rungs are additive: reaching rung 3 does not release rungs 1 and 2 — everyone already notified stays notified and stays able to act, and the ladder panel shows who has acknowledged.

#### 24.7.2 Ladders per alert type

| Alert type | Ladder | Timers | Client branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| SOS (guard) | 0 → 1 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 6, with rung 1 and rung 3 fired **simultaneously at t=0** (no waiting), rung 4 at t+3min if unresolved, rung 5 at t+10min, rung 6 at t+20min | Ack target 30s | Client contact notified at t+5 min unless the SOS is resolved and confirmed non-incident before then |
| Panic (client-raised) | 3 → 1 → 4 (immediate), 5 at t+5min | Ack 30s | Client is the source; keep informed continuously |
| Missed wake check | 0 (retry) → 1 → 3 at t+5min → 4 at t+20min | Ack 60s | Only if unresolved at t+30min, and only where the contract requires |
| Missing guard at shift start | 0 → 1 (t=0) → 3 at t+15min → 4 at t+45min | Ack 60s | Notify at t+30min if no replacement is en route (contractual) |
| Unstaffed post | 1 → 3 (t=0) → 4 at t+30min → 5 at t+2h | Ack 60s | Notify at t+60min, or immediately for Tier-1 and armed posts |
| Replacement overdue | 3 (t=0) → 4 at target+30min → 5 at target+2h | Ack 60s | Notify at target+30min |
| Geofence violation | 0 → 1 (t=0) → 3 at t+15min | Ack 5 min | Not notified unless the site is Critical or the guard is unreachable |
| Patrol exception | 1 (t=0) → 3 at t+30min | Ack 5 min | Included in the daily report, not notified live |
| Offline device | 0 → 1 (t=0) → 3 at t+30min | Ack 5 min | Not notified |
| Device tamper | 1 → 3 (t=0) → 4 at t+30min; guard is **not** notified (integrity) | Ack 60s | Not notified until investigated |
| Licence expired with active deployment | 3 → Compliance → 4 (t=0) → 6 at t+4h | Ack 60s | Notified per contract, with the mitigation plan |
| Client escalation | 3 (t=0) → 4 at t+15min → 5 at t+1h → 6 at t+4h for Tier-1 | Ack 60s | The client is the source; response commitments are tracked |
| Incident P0 | Same as SOS from the point of classification | Ack 30s | Immediate |

#### 24.7.3 Auto-escalation and acknowledgement

| Rule | Specification |
|---|---|
| Acknowledgement | A rung is acknowledged when a human at that rung presses Acknowledge in the console or Admin App, or answers the automated call and presses the confirmation key. Answering a call without confirming does not count. |
| Auto-escalation | If no acknowledgement at the current rung within its hold time, the next rung fires automatically. There is no manual step and no way to disable it for an individual alert; the only way to stop the ladder is to acknowledge or resolve. |
| Acknowledgement ≠ resolution | Acknowledging stops the ladder climbing for the hold period; if the alert is not moved to In Progress with a recorded action within the same hold time again, the ladder resumes climbing. This prevents "acknowledge and forget". |
| Ownership | Exactly one owner at a time; ownership transfer is explicit and logged. If the owner's device goes silent for 90 seconds on a P0/P1, ownership lapses and the alert re-fans out (SUR-ADP-015). |
| Manual escalation | Any participant may escalate to the next rung immediately, always. Escalating never requires permission. |
| De-escalation | Only the shift lead or above, with a reason; the ladder state is retained in the timeline. |
| Snooze | Does not exist for P0/P1. P2 may be snoozed once, for up to 30 minutes, with a reason. P3 may be scheduled. |
| Fan-out channels | Rung notifications go out on all configured channels for that rung simultaneously (push + SMS + voice as per the table), not sequentially, because sequential attempts waste the minutes that matter. |
| Quiet hours | Do not apply to P0/P1/P2 operational alerts, ever. They apply only to P3 and to non-operational notifications. |

#### 24.7.4 When the client is and is not notified

This is a contractual question, not an operator's judgement call, and the console must show the answer rather than ask for it.

| Situation | Client notified? | Timing | Channel | Content |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SOS at their site | **Yes** | Within 5 minutes unless resolved as a confirmed false alarm first | Call to the security contact + WhatsApp/SMS record | Nature, site, current status, what Suraksha is doing, next update time |
| Any P0 incident at their site | **Yes** | Immediately on classification | Call + written | As above, plus whether police/fire/medical are involved |
| Injury to any person at their site | **Yes** | Immediately | Call + written | Facts only; no attribution of fault |
| Police involvement or FIR | **Yes** | Immediately | Call + written | Facts, reference numbers |
| Unstaffed post at a Tier-1 site or armed post | **Yes** | Immediately | Call + written | Gap, cause, replacement ETA |
| Unstaffed post, standard site | **Yes** | At t+60 min if unresolved | Written | Gap, cause, ETA |
| Missing guard where a replacement is en route within the contractual window | **No** (recorded in the daily report) | — | — | — |
| Missed wake check resolved within 30 minutes with the guard safe | **No** unless the contract requires | Daily report | — | — |
| Patrol exception, geofence blip, offline device, late arrival | **No** live notification | Daily/weekly report | — | Aggregate |
| Guard misconduct affecting the client (theft, intoxication, absence with concealment) | **Yes** | Within 4 hours of substantiation | Call + written | Facts, action taken, replacement |
| Anything the contract's escalation matrix specifies | **Yes** per that matrix | Per contract | Per contract | Per contract |
| Suraksha-internal failures with no client impact | **No** | — | — | — |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMD-013 | The console shall display, on every alert, the client-notification rule that applies (from the contract's escalation matrix, falling back to the table above) with a pre-selected default, a countdown to the notification deadline, and a one-action send that records channel, recipient, time and content. |
| SUR-CMD-014 | Suppressing a due client notification shall require shift-lead authority and a recorded reason, and shall be reported to the account owner the same day. |
| SUR-CMD-015 | Every client notification sent from the Command Center shall be attached to the alert, the incident (if any) and the client record, and shall be visible to the client in their portal. |

#### 24.7.5 Emergency services

Contacting police, fire or ambulance is **always operator- or field-initiated and never automatic**, because a false automated call has legal and reputational consequences the platform cannot assess. The console provides: the correct local emergency numbers for the site's district, the site address in a call-ready format with landmarks, the site's nearest police station from the site record, and a one-tap "record emergency services contacted" action capturing which service, time, reference number given, and who called. `[ASSUMPTION: A-147]` No integration with emergency services dispatch is assumed to exist or be available.

#### 24.7.6 Resolution, closure and the mandatory incident report

| Step | Rule |
|---|---|
| Resolution | Every alert closes with an outcome code from a per-type fixed list (e.g. for a missed wake check: Guard asleep — counselled · Guard absent · Device failure · Network failure · Medical event · Duty legitimately away from post · False alarm · Other with mandatory text). |
| Incident creation | **Mandatory** for: every SOS (regardless of outcome), every P0, every P1 that resolves with a cause attributable to a person or a control failure, every event where police/medical/fire were contacted, every injury, every client-notified event, and every false alarm classified as deliberate. |
| Incident report content | Narrative, timeline (auto-populated from the alert timeline, editable only by appending), people involved, evidence, actions taken, client communications, outcome, root cause, preventive action, owner, reviewer. |
| Closure gate | A P0/P1 incident cannot be Completed without: outcome, root cause, preventive action, client-communication record (or a recorded reason none was due), and at least one evidence item or a stated reason for none (§22.13.2). |
| Review | Every P0 gets a review within 48 hours chaired by the shift lead with the operator present, producing findings that go to the compliance findings tracker. Every P1 with a control failure gets a review within 7 days. Reviews are blameless in tone and specific in output: what control failed, what change prevents recurrence, who owns it, by when. |
| Reopen | An alert or incident may be reopened within 30 days by State Operations or Compliance with a reason; reopening preserves the original closure record. |

#### 24.7.7 Audit trail

Every alert carries an immutable, append-only timeline with server timestamps. Recorded events: creation (with source event and rule version), severity computation and any change (with actor and reason), every rung fire (with channel, recipient, provider receipt), every acknowledgement (actor, channel, latency), every action (call attempted, call outcome, dispatch, replacement initiated, client notified, note added), ownership changes, escalation and de-escalation, resolution, incident linkage, review outcome, and any reopening. The timeline is exportable as a signed PDF for client dispute resolution and legal use, and the export itself is audited.

### 24.8 The SOS flow, end to end

#### 24.8.1 Online path

| t | Actor | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| t=0 | Guard | Presses SOS in the Guard App (long-press 2 seconds to avoid pocket triggers, or triple power-button press where the OS permits, or a hardware panic device where issued). |
| t+0.2s | Guard App | Immediately, before any network call: captures GPS (last known plus a fresh fix request), starts a 30-second audio recording, takes a silent photo if the policy for that site permits, vibrates once to confirm receipt, and shows a discreet screen (not a klaxon — the guard may be near a threat) with a 5-second **Cancel** window. |
| t+0.3s | Guard App | Sends the SOS event on the fastest available path: primary API call; if it fails, a lightweight retry endpoint; if that fails within 3 seconds, an SMS to the platform's SOS gateway number containing guard ID, site ID, coordinates and timestamp `[RECOMMENDED]`. |
| t+1s | Platform | Alert created at **P0 always**. No de-duplication suppression is ever applied to an SOS (§24.10). Rungs 1 and 3 fire simultaneously; the console klaxons; the wallboard takes over with the SOS card; on-call devices receive a critical push, and P0 voice calls begin. |
| t+2s | Guard App | Begins continuous location streaming at 10-second intervals until the SOS is resolved, regardless of shift state, and keeps recording audio in 30-second segments, uploading each as it completes. |
| t+5s | Client app | If the site's client has enabled it and the contract permits, the client's security contact receives a "security alert at your site — we are responding" notice. `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-143]` Whether immediate client notification on SOS is default-on or default-off per contract tier. |
| ≤30s | Operator | Acknowledges. The console opens the SOS workspace automatically for the operator who acknowledges: live location on map, streaming audio playback, guard profile and photo, site SOP, gate access instructions, site contacts, nearest other Suraksha guards with distance, nearest police station, and the one-tap call bar. |
| ≤60s | Operator | First substantive action: calls the guard. If the guard answers and confirms safety with the agreed challenge (a spoken duress code is configured per operation `[RECOMMENDED]` — a normal-sounding phrase that means "I am under duress"), the operator proceeds accordingly. If no answer, the operator calls the supervisor and dispatches. |
| t+3min | Platform | If unresolved, rung 4 (shift lead) fires automatically. |
| t+5min | Operator | Client security contact notified per §24.7.4 unless already resolved as a confirmed false alarm. |
| t+10min | Platform | Rung 5 (on-call manager). |
| t+20min | Platform | Rung 6 (Founder/Management). |
| Ongoing | Operator | Every action, call outcome and note is timestamped into the timeline. The console shows an "update client" prompt every 15 minutes while the SOS is open and a client has been notified. |
| Resolution | Operator + Shift lead | Outcome code recorded; **a mandatory incident report is created for every SOS without exception**, including confirmed false alarms; audio and photo evidence attached; guard welfare check recorded (was the guard spoken to, are they safe, do they need support). |
| +48h | Shift lead | P0 review completed; findings recorded. |

#### 24.8.2 Offline path

The Guard App is the only offline-first client in the ecosystem (canon §4), and SOS is the case that justifies it.

| Condition | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| No data, SMS available | The app sends the SOS by SMS to the platform's SOS gateway: a compact payload (guard ID, site ID, lat/long, device time, sequence number). The gateway creates the identical P0 alert with `source=sms` and a flag that location may be stale. The guard's device shows "sent by SMS — signal weak" so the guard knows it went. |
| No data, no SMS, but a voice call is possible | The app displays the Command Center's direct number in large type on the SOS screen with a one-tap dial, plus the supervisor's number as the second option. An SOS raised by inbound call is created manually by the operator with `source=voice` and the same P0 treatment, and the operator records who called and from what number. |
| Complete signal loss | The event is queued locally with its captured GPS, audio and photo, and is transmitted the instant any connectivity returns, marked `delayed_sync` with both `device_time` and `server_received_time` retained. The platform treats a delayed SOS as **live** on arrival (the guard may still be in trouble) unless the guard has since checked in normally, in which case it is created as a P1 for investigation rather than a P0 response. |
| Device destroyed or taken | Absence of the expected heartbeat is itself monitored: for a lone guard at a Critical site, loss of heartbeat within 5 minutes of any abnormal signal (sudden movement, geofence exit, missed wake check) raises a correlated P0 "possible incident — contact lost". |
| Post-recovery | When a delayed SOS arrives, the console shows the full offline gap explicitly (last known ping, gap duration, arrival time) so the operator does not mistake stale data for current data. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMD-016 | SOS shall never be suppressed, batched, rate-limited, de-duplicated or downgraded automatically, under any load condition. |
| SUR-CMD-017 | The SOS transport shall have at least three independent paths (API, retry endpoint, SMS gateway) and the app shall confirm to the guard which path succeeded. |
| SUR-CMD-018 | Every SOS shall produce an incident record, including confirmed false alarms, and no role shall be able to delete an SOS record. |
| SUR-CMD-019 | SOS audio and images shall be write-once, encrypted, access-logged, and retained for the period defined in §39; redaction shall require Compliance approval and shall retain a redaction record. |
| SUR-CMD-020 | The SOS cancel window shall be no longer than 5 seconds, shall be recorded when used, and repeated cancellations by the same guard shall be reviewed (they may indicate a faulty device, a pocket-press pattern, or coercion). |

### 24.9 Post-incident review workspace

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Automatic for every P0 within 48 hours, every P1 with a control failure within 7 days, every SOS, every client-notified event, and on demand from Compliance. |
| Participants | Shift lead (chair), the operator(s) involved, the field supervisor, the account owner where a client was affected, Compliance for regulatory matters. |
| Structure | Timeline replay (from the alert audit trail, no reconstruction from memory) → what the controls did → what a human decided and why → what worked → what failed → findings. |
| Output | Findings with type (control gap, process gap, training gap, tooling gap, external factor), owner, due date, and a link to the change (setting change, SOP update, training assignment, product ticket). Findings land in the compliance findings tracker (§22.17.4). |
| Tone rule | Reviews name controls and processes, not individuals, in their written findings; individual performance is handled separately through the operator scorecard (§24.14) and HR processes. This is stated because the quality of the timeline data depends on operators not fearing it. |
| Metrics | Review completion within target %, findings closed on time %, recurrence rate of the same finding type within 90 days. |

### 24.10 De-duplication, correlation and storm control

Without this, one bad night produces 400 alerts and the operator sees none of them.

| Mechanism | Rule |
|---|---|
| De-duplication key | `(alert_type, site_id, post_id, guard_id)` within a per-type window: geofence 10 min, offline device 30 min, patrol exception 1 round, late arrival 1 shift, document/licence expiry 24 h, wake check per scheduled check (never merged across checks). Duplicates increment a counter on the existing alert and append to its timeline rather than creating a new alert. |
| Never de-duplicated | SOS, client panic, and any P0. Two SOS events from the same guard are two alerts, always. |
| Correlation | The engine groups related alerts into an **incident cluster** when they share a site within 30 minutes, or share a guard within 15 minutes, or share a cause signature (e.g. 12 offline devices in one city within 5 minutes → a connectivity event, not 12 guard problems). The console shows the cluster as one card with its members expandable. |
| Uplift | Two P2s at one site within 30 minutes uplift to P1 (object #20 in §24.5.1). A cluster of ≥5 same-type alerts across sites uplifts to P1 as a **systemic** alert routed to Ops and Engineering, not to field supervisors. |
| Storm control | If alert creation exceeds 3× the trailing 7-day p95 rate for a 5-minute window, the pipeline enters **storm mode**: P2/P3 alerts are aggregated into cluster cards rather than individual rows, non-critical push notifications are batched at 5-minute intervals, and a banner announces storm mode with the trigger. P0 and P1 are never affected. Storm mode is logged, auto-exits when the rate normalises for 10 minutes, and is reviewed. |
| Maintenance suppression | Planned suppression windows can be declared for a site or a cause (e.g. a site under renovation with the geofence temporarily meaningless), by City Operations, with a reason, an end time (max 24 h), and an explicit list of alert types suppressed. P0 can never be suppressed. Suppressed alerts are still recorded, badged `suppressed`, and shown in the daily report. |
| Flap detection | An alert type that opens and closes ≥5 times for the same key within an hour is flagged as flapping, collapsed into one alert with a flap count, and routed for engineering/device investigation rather than repeated field response. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMD-021 | De-duplication, correlation, storm mode and suppression shall never apply to P0 alerts, and this shall be enforced by an explicit test in the CI suite. |
| SUR-CMD-022 | Storm mode entry and exit, and every suppression window, shall be logged with actor, reason, scope and duration, and shall appear in the daily operations report. |

### 24.11 False-alarm handling

| Aspect | Rule |
|---|---|
| Classification | An alert may be resolved as a false alarm only with a category: Accidental press · Device fault · Test (authorised) · Test (unauthorised) · Network/GPS artefact · Misunderstanding · Malicious. |
| Never assumed | An SOS is never treated as a false alarm until a human has spoken to the guard, or a supervisor has physically verified the post. "The guard did not answer, so it is probably a false alarm" is an explicitly forbidden resolution and the console will not offer it as a path — with no contact, the only resolutions available are ones that involve dispatch. |
| Consequences | Accidental press: no consequence, but ≥3 in 30 days by one guard triggers a device/app review and a refresher. Device fault: device replacement task. Unauthorised test: recorded, counselling. Malicious: incident, HR process, possible removal from the roster. |
| Cost tracking | Every false alarm records the response effort (people mobilised, minutes) so that the false-alarm rate can be reported alongside its cost, and so that suppressing genuine alerts to keep the rate low is visibly the wrong trade. |
| Reporting | False-alarm rate per 1,000 alerts, per type, per site, per guard cohort, in the weekly operations report. A false-alarm rate below 2% is treated as suspicious (it suggests under-reporting), not as excellent. |

### 24.12 Shift handover and the daily operations rhythm

#### 24.12.1 Handover

| Step | Rule |
|---|---|
| Pre-handover (T−15 min) | The console generates a **handover pack**: open alerts by severity with their state, alerts resolved this watch with outcomes, sites with active issues, planned events in the next 8 hours, gaps in the next 8 hours, devices/sites with known faults, any suppression windows active, any storm-mode episodes, and free-text notes. |
| Joint window (T−10 to T) | Both operators are on the console simultaneously. The incoming operator opens each open alert and presses **Accept** on it individually — there is no bulk accept, because bulk acceptance is how open alerts get lost. |
| Blocking rule | Handover cannot complete with an unacknowledged P0 or P1; the outgoing operator remains on watch and the overrun is logged and reported. |
| Sign-off | Both operators sign the handover in the console (their identity, server time). The signed pack is retained and is the first thing the shift lead reads. |
| Escalation of unresolved | Any alert older than one full watch is automatically escalated to the shift lead at handover with an ageing flag. |

#### 24.12.2 The daily rhythm

| Time (local) | Ritual | What happens | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| 05:45 | **Night close preparation** | Wake-check compliance computed for the night; missed checks with outcomes listed; overnight incidents summarised. | Night operator |
| 06:00 | **Morning handover** | Per §24.12.1. | Both operators |
| 06:15–08:00 | **Shift-start sweep (day)** | For every site with a day shift starting: confirm the rostered guard has checked in within grace; chase every non-check-in at T+10 min; open replacements for every confirmed absence by T+20 min; report the fill position to City Ops by 08:15. | Day operator |
| 09:00 | **Morning attendance close** | Yesterday's attendance exceptions reviewed and resolved; overrides recorded with reasons; the day's attendance baseline published to the dashboard and to client daily reports where contracted. | City Ops + operator |
| 10:00 | **Daily operations review (15 min)** | Shift lead walks the previous 24 hours: P0/P1 list, SLA position, unresolved gaps, expiring documents/licences in 7 days, top three risks for tonight. | Shift lead |
| 14:00 | **Evening handover** | Per §24.12.1. | Both operators |
| 17:30 | **Night readiness check** | Every night shift's roster confirmed filled; lone-guard sites identified and listed; wake-check schedules confirmed generated; supervisor night coverage confirmed; device battery and connectivity risks flagged. | Evening operator |
| 19:45–21:00 | **Shift-start sweep (night)** | As the morning sweep, with a stricter chase interval (T+5 min) because night gaps are harder to fill. | Evening/night operator |
| 22:00 | **Night handover** | Per §24.12.1, plus explicit read-back of lone-guard sites and Critical-risk sites. | Both operators |
| 23:00–05:00 | **Wake-check cycle** | The engine issues randomised checks; the operator works the missed-check queue continuously; each missed check follows its ladder; the operator logs every outcome. Between checks, the operator runs the patrol-exception queue and the offline-device queue. | Night operator |
| 02:00 | **Mid-night sweep** | A manual pass over the map: every Critical site confirmed occupied, every lone guard confirmed responsive within the last 90 minutes, every offline device chased. | Night operator |
| Weekly (Mon 11:00) | **Operations review** | SLA performance per client, incident trends, false-alarm rate and cost, operator scorecards, findings closure, staffing adequacy. | State/National Ops |

### 24.13 SLA reporting to clients

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Contracted metrics | Defined per contract from a fixed catalogue: deployment fill rate, attendance rate, punctuality rate, patrol round completion, wake-check compliance, incident acknowledgement time, incident resolution time, replacement fulfilment time, report delivery timeliness, supervisor visit frequency. |
| Measurement | Computed from the same records the operation runs on — attendance rows, alert timestamps, patrol logs — never from a separate reporting entry. A metric that cannot be computed from operational data is not offered as an SLA. |
| Exclusions | Contractually defined and applied transparently: client-caused access denial, force majeure with evidence, client-requested changes within notice periods. Every exclusion applied appears as a named line in the report with its evidence, never as a silent adjustment. |
| Cadence | Daily operational summary (email/portal, where contracted), weekly exception summary, monthly SLA statement issued with the invoice, quarterly business review pack for Tier-1 clients. |
| Content of the monthly statement | Per metric: target, achieved, variance, breach count, breaches listed with date/site/cause/remedy, exclusions applied, penalty or credit computed per the contract's clause, and the incident register for the period. |
| Dispute path | The client may dispute a metric in the portal within 15 days; the dispute freezes the associated penalty computation, routes to the account owner and Ops, and is resolved with evidence from the alert timelines (§22.16.4). |
| Internal view | Every client's live SLA position is visible in OPS and on the console context pane, so an operator handling an alert knows whether this client is already at breach risk this month — which affects urgency, not truthfulness. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMD-023 | SLA metrics shall be computed from operational records only; no manual entry shall be permitted into an SLA computation. |
| SUR-CMD-024 | Every SLA breach shall be traceable to the specific alerts, attendance rows or patrol logs that caused it, and that evidence shall be attachable to the client statement. |
| SUR-CMD-025 | Penalty and credit computation shall produce ledger entries, not spreadsheet notes, and shall follow the same approval path as any other credit (§22.14.5). |

### 24.14 Operator QA and scorecard

| Metric | Definition | Target | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|
| Acknowledgement latency | Median seconds from alert creation to acknowledgement, by severity | P0 ≤30s, P1 ≤60s, P2 ≤5 min | 25% |
| First-action latency | Median seconds from acknowledgement to the first substantive action | P0 ≤60s, P1 ≤5 min | 20% |
| Ladder integrity | % of alerts where the operator acted before auto-escalation was needed | ≥85% | 15% |
| Documentation quality | % of resolved alerts with complete outcome code, note and call outcomes; sampled review of note quality by the shift lead (5 per operator per week) | ≥95% complete, ≥4/5 quality | 15% |
| Client-notification compliance | % of due client notifications sent within their deadline | 100% | 10% |
| False-alarm classification accuracy | % of false-alarm classifications upheld on review | ≥95% | 5% |
| Handover quality | Handover packs accepted without missing items; no alert lost across a handover | 100% | 5% |
| Wellbeing/adherence | Watch adherence, break compliance, certification currency | 100% | 5% |

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Sampling | Every P0 is reviewed. 10% of P1s and 5% of P2s are sampled weekly by the shift lead, with a rubric covering: was the severity right, was the first action right, was the client rule followed, was the documentation sufficient to reconstruct events. |
| Calibration | Shift leads score a common set of five recorded alerts monthly to keep scoring consistent between leads. |
| Feedback | Scorecards are visible to the operator continuously — not delivered as a monthly surprise — with the underlying alerts linked so any score is inspectable. |
| Consequence | Below-target scores drive coaching and re-certification, not immediate sanction; deliberate suppression of alerts, falsified notes or unauthorised de-escalation are separate integrity matters handled by HR and Compliance. |
| Team metrics | Watch-level: alerts per operator-hour, mean ack by severity, % auto-escalated, false-alarm rate and cost, storm episodes, handover overruns, SLA breaches originating in the watch. |

### 24.15 Worked incident timeline

A real-shape example, used as the reference for testing the whole chain. Site: *Meridian Logistics Warehouse, Gate 3, Bhiwandi*. Client tier: Tier-1. Site risk band: High. Night shift 20:00–08:00, required strength 2 (one at Gate 3, one roving). Contract escalation matrix: security contact Mr. A. Deshmukh, notify on any P0 immediately and on any unstaffed post within 30 minutes.

| Server time | Event | System behaviour | Human action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01:12:00 | Wake check #3 scheduled for Guard G-4471 (roving) | Prompt issued, 120s timeout | — |
| 01:14:00 | No acknowledgement | Auto-retry issued | — |

Because the guard has not checked in normally since, it is treated as live. Rung 5 (on-call manager) fires immediately given the elapsed time. |
