## 25. AI Platform

This section is the canonical home for **what the AI does and how it is built**. §41 owns AI governance and policy — acceptable use, model risk management, bias and fairness review, vendor assessment, incident response for AI failures, and the regulatory posture. Where this section names a guardrail, it is naming a *mechanism*; the *policy* that requires it lives in §41.

### 25.1 One intelligence layer, ten surfaces

Suraksha does not build ten assistants. It builds **one AI intelligence layer** and exposes ten role-scoped surfaces onto it. The layer is shared; what differs per surface is the identity context, the retrieval scope, the tool set, and the action-class ceiling.

```
        Customer AI   Agency AI   Guard AI   Admin AI   Command Center AI
        Analytics AI  Compliance AI  Recruitment AI  Support AI  Tender AI
              │  │  │  │  │  │  │  │  │  │
              ▼  ▼  ▼  ▼  ▼  ▼  ▼  ▼  ▼  ▼
        ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │  Surface adapter: identity, locale, channel   │
        ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
        │  Policy gate: role, tenant, scope, entitlement │  ← denies before retrieval, not after
        ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
        │  Intent & planning                            │
        ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
        │  Permission-aware retrieval (§25.6)           │
        ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
        │  Tool layer: read tools · action tools        │  ← every tool declares its action class
        ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
        │  Model router (§25.12)                        │
        ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
        │  Response assembly + citation + redaction     │
        ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
        │  AI Interaction log (§25.10) → Audit          │
        └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-AI-001 | All ten AI surfaces shall be served by one intelligence layer with one policy gate, one retrieval implementation and one interaction log; no surface shall implement its own data access. |
| SUR-AI-002 | The policy gate shall evaluate identity, tenant, role, geographic scope, plan entitlement and action class **before** any retrieval is executed, so that a denied request never causes data to be read. |
| SUR-AI-003 | Every AI response shall carry an `interaction_id`, the surface, the model used, the tools called, the retrieval sources cited, latency and token cost, retained per §39. |
| SUR-AI-004 | No AI surface shall be capable of executing an action for which the requesting human lacks permission, and no AI surface shall be capable of executing any action in the Approval-required class without a recorded human approval. |
| SUR-AI-005 | AI shall never compute or alter alert severity, escalation state, attendance truth, ledger entries, verification status or permission grants. It may summarise, explain and propose changes to all of them. |

### 25.2 The ten surfaces

#### 25.2.1 Customer AI

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Users | Website/app visitors (anonymous), Individual Customer, Company Owner, Security Head, Facility Manager, Site Manager, Procurement, Client Finance, Client Viewer. |
| Where | surakshaguards.in (widget), Customer App, client portal. |
| Capabilities | Explain services and coverage; guide service selection; compute an indicative price from the published pricing configuration; check pincode serviceability; start and pre-fill a booking; explain a quotation; answer status questions for logged-in clients (who is on duty, today's attendance, this month's invoice, my incident reports); raise a support ticket; request a guard replacement (proposal); explain an SLA statement line. |
| Example (EN) | *"Are my guards on duty at the Andheri site right now?"* → "Yes — 2 of 2 guards are on duty at Andheri Warehouse. Ramesh S. checked in at 19:58 and Dinesh K. at 20:03 against a 20:00 shift start. Last patrol round completed 22:40, all 6 checkpoints. [View live]" |
| Example (HI) | *"मेरे साइट पर आज कितने गार्ड आए हैं?"* → "आपके अंधेरी साइट पर आज 2 में से 2 गार्ड ड्यूटी पर हैं। रमेश एस. ने 19:58 और दिनेश के. ने 20:03 पर चेक-इन किया। शिफ्ट 20:00 बजे शुरू हुई थी। [लाइव देखें]" |
| Example (HI, pre-login) | *"सोसाइटी के लिए 3 गार्ड चाहिए, कितना खर्चा आएगा?"* → "हाउसिंग सोसाइटी के लिए ₹18,000 प्रति गार्ड प्रति माह (+18% GST) का प्लान है। 3 गार्ड के लिए लगभग ₹54,000 + GST मासिक। सटीक दर शिफ्ट पैटर्न पर निर्भर करती है। क्या मैं आपके पिन कोड के लिए उपलब्धता जाँच लूँ?" |
| Data it may access | Public content and pricing configuration; for a logged-in client: only that client's own bookings, contracts, sites, deployments, attendance summaries, invoices, wallet, incidents and tickets. Never guard PII beyond first name, last initial, photo and on-duty status. Never another client's data. Never internal notes, costs, margins or guard salary. |
| Action class ceiling | **Approval-required** — it may propose a booking, a replacement request or a ticket; the client confirms. It may never make a payment, cancel a contract, change bank details or alter a booking's commercial terms. |
| Failure behaviour | If retrieval is unavailable: "I can't reach your live data right now — here is your account page and your manager's number." If confidence is low or the question is outside scope: no guessing, hand off to a human with the conversation attached. Anonymous users are never told account-specific facts under any prompt. |

#### 25.2.2 Agency AI

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Users | Agency Owner, Agency Admin, Branch Manager, Operations Manager, Field Officer, Supervisor, Agency HR, Recruiter, Payroll, Agency Finance, Agency Compliance, Agency Sales, Agency Viewer. |
| Where | Agency Portal web, desktop and mobile app. |
| Capabilities | Answer questions over the agency's own data; navigate to modules; draft quotations, notices, warning letters and client emails; explain payroll and invoice figures; summarise attendance and incidents; suggest replacements and roster fixes; flag expiring documents and licences; prepare a compliance snapshot; summarise a tender and assess eligibility (Professional+); explain a plan entitlement. |
| Example (EN) | *"Who is absent today at Site 12 and what will it cost me?"* → "2 absences at Site 12 today: Suresh P. (night, no check-in, replacement pending 38 min) and Anil J. (approved leave, covered). Unreplaced shortfall exposure under your contract's shortfall clause is ₹1,850 for today. [Open replacement] [View contract clause]" |
| Example (HI) | *"पिछले महीने कितनी सैलरी बनी और किसकी सबसे ज़्यादा कटौती हुई?"* → "अक्टूबर की कुल पेरोल ₹14,82,400 (128 गार्ड) रही। सबसे ज़्यादा कटौती: विनोद के. — ₹4,200 (एडवांस वसूली ₹3,000 + अनुपस्थिति ₹1,200)। [पेरोल रन खोलें]" |
| Data it may access | Strictly `tenant_id = <this agency>` and, within that, the branch and module scope of the requesting user. A Branch Manager asking about another branch is told the data exists but is outside their scope — never shown it, and never told a number. |
| Action class ceiling | **Approval-required** for anything writing to operations, HR or money (assign guard, send invoice reminder, mark attendance, approve leave, blacklist a guard, edit a contract). **Automated** only for: drafting into an editor, saving a draft, applying a filter, exporting a report the user could export anyway, marking a notification read. |
| Failure behaviour | Degrades to navigation help ("here is the Payroll module") and a search fallback. Never fabricates a number: if the metric is unavailable it says which system is down and offers the last successful value with its timestamp. |

#### 25.2.3 Guard AI

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Users | Guard, PSO, Bouncer, Supervisor (field), Specialised Personnel. |
| Where | Guard App (voice-first), Guards Portal. |
| Capabilities | "What is my duty today and where?"; site instructions read aloud; how to check in when GPS is weak; patrol route guidance; explain a payslip line; leave balance and how to apply; document status and what is missing; report an incident by voice with the app structuring it; emergency guidance (what to do, who to call) — but never replacing SOS; training reminders. |
| Example (EN) | *"Why is my salary less this month?"* → "Your October net is ₹14,320 against ₹15,600 in September. The difference: 2 absences (−₹1,040) and an advance recovery instalment (−₹1,000), plus overtime added (+₹760). [Open payslip] Want me to raise a query with HR?" |
| Example (HI) | *"आज मेरी ड्यूटी कहाँ है और कब शुरू होगी?"* → "आज आपकी ड्यूटी सनराइज़ इंडस्ट्रियल पार्क, गेट 2 पर है। रात की शिफ्ट 20:00 से 08:00 तक। साइट 3.2 किमी दूर है। चेक-इन 19:45 से खुल जाएगा। रास्ता देखना है?" |
| Example (HI, incident) | *"साइट पर एक गाड़ी का शीशा टूटा मिला है"* → "मैं घटना रिपोर्ट बना रहा हूँ: श्रेणी — संपत्ति क्षति, साइट — सनराइज़ गेट 2, समय — अभी। कृपया दो फोटो लीजिए और बताइए कि किसी को चोट तो नहीं आई? रिपोर्ट भेजने से पहले मैं आपको दिखाऊँगा।" |
| Data it may access | Only the guard's own records (roster, attendance, payslips, documents, leave, training, incidents they reported) plus the instructions and contacts for sites they are currently assigned to. Never other guards' pay or personal data. Never client commercial data. Never site gate codes for sites they are not on duty at. |
| Action class ceiling | **Approval-required** for leave requests, incident submissions and HR queries (the guard confirms before submission). **Never** for attendance check-in, wake-check acknowledgement or SOS — these must be direct human acts and are explicitly outside AI's reach (SUR-AI-005 and SUR-CMD-018). |
| Failure behaviour | Offline: answers from the locally cached duty card and site instructions, clearly marked "offline — as of <time>", and queues anything that needs the server. Low literacy is assumed: responses are short, spoken by default, and always offer a "call my supervisor" action. |

#### 25.2.4 Admin AI

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Users | All fifteen Suraksha internal roles, scoped per §22.26. |
| Where | OPS (top-bar launcher and per-module context panel), Admin App. |
| Capabilities | Natural-language dashboard queries; cross-module lookups; report generation; anomaly explanation; drafting client and agency communications; summarising a client's month; explaining why a number moved; preparing a deal-desk brief; proposing operational actions (replacement, reassignment, dunning pause). |
| Example (EN) | *"Why did Ahmedabad's attendance drop this week?"* → "Ahmedabad attendance fell from 96.4% to 91.2% (week-on-week). 71% of the drop comes from two sites: Meridian Logistics (11 absences, all night shift, 9 by the same 3 guards) and Silver Oak RWA (6 absences following a supervisor change on Tuesday). Two of the three repeat-absent guards have open advance recoveries. [Open site] [Open guards] [Draft supervisor briefing]" |
| Example (HI) | *"इस महीने कौन से क्लाइंट के इनवॉइस बाकी हैं?"* → "आपके स्कोप (अहमदाबाद) में 7 इनवॉइस बकाया हैं, कुल ₹9,42,300। सबसे पुराना: मेरिडियन लॉजिस्टिक्स ₹3,10,000 (68 दिन, डनिंग स्टेज 3)। [एजिंग रिपोर्ट खोलें]" |
| Data it may access | Everything the user's role and scope permit in OPS, and nothing more. Salary, KYC documents and audit logs are retrievable only by roles that hold them, and document *content* is never pasted into a response — the AI cites the document and links to the viewer. |
| Action class ceiling | **Approval-required** for all operational writes. **Forbidden** (no tool exists) for: payments, payroll changes, permission changes, account deletion, guard termination, compliance status changes, financial settlement, sensitive data export — the canon's absolute list, implemented as the absence of a tool, not as a refusal prompt. |
| Failure behaviour | Falls back to structured search across modules; states plainly when a metric is stale; refuses to answer cross-scope questions with a scope explanation rather than a denial that reveals the data's existence in detail. |

#### 25.2.5 Command Center AI

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Users | Command Center Operator, Shift Lead, on-call Operations. |
| Where | Operator console (a side panel that never occupies the queue or workspace panes), Admin App alert view. |
| Capabilities | Summarise an unfolding alert in two sentences; assemble the fact panel narrative; surface the site SOP section relevant to this alert type; list the nearest available guards for a replacement; draft the client notification text from the contractual template; draft the incident report from the alert timeline; recall "has this happened here before"; end-of-watch summary and handover pack drafting. |
| Example (EN) | *"Brief me on A-88213."* → "Missed wake check at Meridian Logistics Gate 3, guard G-4471 (roving), raised 01:15, P1, uplifted to P0 at 01:17 after contact loss. Supervisor dispatched 01:17, ETA 01:31. Client is Tier-1; the contract requires immediate notification on P0 — not yet sent. This site had 2 wake-miss events in the last 30 days, both device-related." |
| Example (HI) | *"इस साइट पर पिछले महीने क्या-क्या हुआ था?"* → "मेरिडियन लॉजिस्टिक्स पर पिछले 30 दिनों में: 2 वेक-चेक मिस (दोनों डिवाइस बैटरी), 1 जियोफेंस उल्लंघन, 0 SOS। साइट रिस्क बैंड: High। पिछली सुपरवाइज़र विज़िट: 3 दिन पहले।" |
| Data it may access | The alert, its cluster, the site, the guard, the client contract's notification rules, the site SOP, and historical alerts/incidents for the same site/guard. It may not read unrelated tenants, financial ledgers or HR records. |
| Action class ceiling | **Recommendation** for everything operational, **Approval-required** for drafting a client notification (the operator sends it), and **Read-only** for all safety-critical reasoning. It has **no** tool that can acknowledge, escalate, de-escalate, resolve, suppress or classify an alert. Severity is deterministic (§24.6) and AI does not touch it. |
| Failure behaviour | The console is fully usable without it. If the AI panel fails, it collapses with a one-line notice; no alert handling depends on it. Latency budget is strict (§25.11) because an operator will not wait. |

#### 25.2.6 Analytics AI

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Users | Founder/Management, National/State/City Operations, Finance, Marketing, Agency Owner/Admin (their own tenant), Auditor (read-only). |
| Where | OPS Analytics workspace; Agency Portal analytics; a natural-language bar above every dashboard. |
| Capabilities | Natural-language querying of the metric registry; comparison and trend explanation; cohort questions; forecast reads; scheduled narrative summaries ("your Monday morning briefing"); chart generation from a question; export of the result set the user is already entitled to. |
| Example (EN) | *"Compare guard attrition across our four cities for the last two quarters and tell me what's different about the worst one."* → Returns a table plus: "Surat is worst at 62% annualised vs a 41% mean. Two differences stand out: 68% of Surat exits occur within 90 days of joining (vs 34% elsewhere), and Surat's mean distance from guard home to site is 14.2 km vs 8.1 km. [Open cohort] [Open sites]" |
| Example (HI) | *"पिछली तिमाही में सबसे ज़्यादा इंसिडेंट किस साइट पर हुए?"* → "पिछली तिमाही में सबसे ज़्यादा घटनाएँ: मेरिडियन लॉजिस्टिक्स (14), फिर ओरियन आईटी पार्क (9)। मेरिडियन की 14 में से 9 रात की शिफ्ट में हुईं। [विवरण देखें]" |
| Data it may access | The analytics read model only, always scope-injected. It never queries transactional tables directly, so it cannot leak row-level PII that the read model does not carry. |
| Action class ceiling | **Read-only**, plus **Automated** for saving a view, scheduling a report the user may already schedule, and generating a chart. |
| Failure behaviour | If it cannot map a question to registered metrics, it says which part it could not map and offers the closest registered metrics rather than inventing a computation. It never writes its own SQL against production; it composes registered metrics with registered dimensions. |

#### 25.2.7 Compliance AI

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Users | Compliance, Verification, Auditor, Agency Compliance, Founder/Management. |
| Where | OPS Compliance and Verification modules; Agency Portal compliance dashboard. |
| Capabilities | Licence and document expiry detection and prioritisation; verification-pack assembly (what is present, what is missing, what looks inconsistent); extraction of fields from uploaded documents with confidence scores; consistency checks (name across documents, licence jurisdiction vs deployment geography, training vs guard category); filing-calendar reminders; drafting a compliance finding; assembling an inspection pack index. |
| Example (EN) | *"What will stop us deploying in Rajasthan next month?"* → "Three things: (1) the Rajasthan state licence expires in 21 days with no renewal application recorded; (2) 14 of 61 Rajasthan guards have police verification expiring within 30 days; (3) 3 armed guards have weapon-handling refreshers expiring before the 15th. [Open licence] [Open guard list] [Open training]" |
| Example (HI) | *"किन गार्डों के दस्तावेज़ इस महीने खत्म हो रहे हैं?"* → "इस महीने 23 गार्डों के दस्तावेज़ समाप्त हो रहे हैं: 14 पुलिस वेरिफिकेशन, 6 ट्रेनिंग सर्टिफिकेट, 3 मेडिकल। 5 गार्ड अभी ड्यूटी पर हैं जिनके दस्तावेज़ 7 दिन में खत्म होंगे। [सूची खोलें]" |
| Data it may access | Documents metadata always; document *content* only for extraction within the verification workspace, never reproduced verbatim into a chat response. Licences, training, verification records, filing calendar. |
| Action class ceiling | **Recommendation** and **Approval-required**. It may pre-fill a verification decision with extracted fields and a checklist state; a human verifier decides. It may **never** set a verification status, a licence status or a compliance score. |
| Failure behaviour | Extraction below the confidence threshold is presented as "could not read — please enter" rather than a guess. Any inconsistency it flags is presented as a question to a human, never as a conclusion. |

#### 25.2.8 Recruitment AI

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Users | Recruitment, HR, City Operations, Agency HR, Recruiter. |
| Where | OPS Recruitment; Agency Portal recruitment pipeline (Professional+). |
| Capabilities | Structure an unstructured application (walk-in form photo, WhatsApp message, phone screening notes) into candidate fields; check stated experience against requisition requirements; summarise a screening call; draft interview questions for a guard category; identify missing documents; suggest candidates for an open requisition from the existing pool (including previously rejected candidates whose reason no longer applies); draft offer and joining communications. |
| Example (EN) | *"Screen this batch of 40 walk-in forms against the Ahmedabad armed requisition."* → "12 of 40 meet the hard requirements (age band, licence-linked eligibility, minimum height per the requisition, prior armed experience). 9 are near-misses (missing training certificate only). 19 do not meet a hard requirement — the reason is listed per candidate. No candidate has been rejected automatically; all 40 remain in the pipeline for your decision." |
| Example (HI) | *"इस कैंडिडेट का अनुभव क्या है?"* → "रामनिवास यादव — 6 साल का अनुभव: 4 साल एक एजेंसी में अनआर्म्ड गार्ड, 2 साल सुपरवाइज़र। PSARA ट्रेनिंग सर्टिफिकेट 2024 का, वैध। पुलिस वेरिफिकेशन नहीं है — यह ज़रूरी है।" |
| Data it may access | Candidate records, requisitions, the guard pool for internal suggestions. Never salary data of existing employees; never a candidate's data across tenants. |
| Action class ceiling | **Recommendation** only, with a hard rule: **AI never rejects a candidate.** It may rank, flag and explain; a human makes every selection and rejection decision, and the reason recorded is the human's. This is a fairness control (policy in §41). |
| Failure behaviour | If it cannot parse a document, it presents the raw image beside empty fields for manual entry. It never infers protected characteristics, and any prompt asking it to filter on one is refused and logged. |

#### 25.2.9 Support AI

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Users | Support (assist mode), plus client/agency/guard users (self-serve mode). |
| Where | OPS ticket workspace (agent assist); the help widget on every product; WhatsApp support channel `[RECOMMENDED]`. |
| Capabilities | Deflect common questions with grounded answers from the knowledge base; classify and route incoming tickets; draft a reply for the agent with citations; summarise a long thread; detect a safety-relevant message and convert it to a Command Center alert; detect frustration and offer human handoff; suggest the knowledge-base gap when deflection fails repeatedly. |
| Example (EN, self-serve) | *"My invoice shows 28 guard-days but we had 30 guards."* → "Your invoice bills guard-days, not headcount: 30 guards for 28 days would be 840 guard-days. Your November invoice shows 812 guard-days — 28 fewer than contracted, because of 28 unreplaced shortfall days, which are credited on line 4. [Open invoice] [Talk to a human]" |
| Example (HI, agent assist) | *"इस टिकट का जवाब ड्राफ्ट करो"* → Drafts a reply in Hindi citing the two knowledge-base articles and the client's specific contract clause, marked "draft — review before sending", with the citations shown to the agent. |
| Data it may access | Knowledge base; the requester's own account data in self-serve mode; the ticket's linked entities in assist mode. Never internal notes in self-serve mode. |
| Action class ceiling | **Approval-required** to send any customer-facing message in assist mode (the agent sends). **Automated** for classification, routing, tagging and thread summarisation. In self-serve mode it may create a ticket and may not do anything else that writes. |
| Failure behaviour | Two failed deflection attempts on the same question hand off to a human automatically with the transcript. Any message containing safety keywords or an SOS-like description bypasses deflection entirely and creates a Command Center alert (§24.6) — deflection is never applied to a possible emergency. |

#### 25.2.10 Tender AI

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Users | Sales, Compliance, Founder/Management (Suraksha's own tenders); Agency Owner/Admin/Sales on Professional+ (agency tender discovery). |
| Where | OPS Tenders; Agency Portal Tenders module. |
| Capabilities | Summarise a tender document into a structured brief (authority, scope, locations, manpower, duration, EMD, PBG, submission mode, deadline, key eligibility clauses); map eligibility clauses to the organisation's held evidence and report gaps; extract the BOQ/manpower table; draft a bid checklist; flag unusual clauses (penalty regimes, liability, payment terms) for human review; summarise why a past similar bid was lost. |
| Example (EN) | *"Are we eligible for this tender?"* → "Assessed against 11 stated eligibility clauses: 8 met from held evidence, 2 gaps, 1 unclear. Gaps: (a) Maharashtra PSARA licence required — not held; (b) minimum 3 similar contracts of ≥₹1 Cr — we hold 2. Unclear: clause 7.3 references 'certified training partner' without defining certification — human review needed. This is an assessment against stated clauses, not legal advice." |
| Example (HI) | *"इस टेंडर की आखिरी तारीख और EMD कितनी है?"* → "जमा करने की अंतिम तिथि: 12 सितंबर 2026, 15:00। EMD: ₹2,50,000 (डिमांड ड्राफ्ट या BG)। प्री-बिड मीटिंग: 28 अगस्त। [पूरा सारांश देखें]" |
| Data it may access | The uploaded tender documents, the organisation's compliance evidence (licences, certificates, turnover records, past contracts), and past bid outcomes. Tender portal feeds are **not assumed to exist** (A-145). |
| Action class ceiling | **Recommendation** only. It never submits, never prices, and never asserts eligibility as a conclusion — it reports clause-by-clause assessment with the evidence it matched, and every eligibility judgement is a human's. |
| Failure behaviour | Poor-quality scans are reported page by page ("pages 4–7 unreadable"); it never summarises a document it could not fully read without saying so. |

### 25.3 Modality: text and voice

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Text | Available on every surface. Input is free text plus suggested prompts per module context. Output is short-form with structured blocks (tables, lists, cards) and always with source links. |
| Voice | Available on every surface; **default input mode in the Guard App**, opt-in elsewhere. Push-to-talk on mobile (hold to speak) to avoid hot-mic privacy problems; wake-word is not used anywhere `[RECOMMENDED]` — a wake-word on a guard's phone at a client site is a privacy liability. |
| Voice output | Text-to-speech on the Guard App and Customer App; off by default on OPS and the console (an operator room does not need more noise). Speed and voice selectable; language follows the user's locale. |
| Mixed | A voice question may produce a visual answer (a map, a table) with a spoken summary — this is the expected pattern for the Guard App. |
| Accessibility | Every voice interaction has a text equivalent and a transcript; every text interaction can be read aloud. Transcripts are stored with the interaction (§25.10) and are visible to the user. |
| Consent | Voice capture is push-to-talk and visually indicated; recordings are retained only as required for quality and dispute purposes per §39, with the retention stated in-app. Guards are told plainly that AI voice input is not a duty log and is not monitored by their supervisor. |

### 25.4 Language strategy

The canon commits to Hindi and English plus **at least 19 more Indian languages**. That commitment is kept honestly by tiering, because claiming uniform quality across 21 languages would be false.

| Tier | Languages | What "supported" means | Quality bar |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Tier 1 — Full support** | English, Hindi | Full ASR + intent + generation + TTS; all surfaces; all prompts, canned responses and notification templates authored natively; human-reviewed evaluation set; regressions block release. | Intent accuracy ≥95% on the eval set; ASR WER ≤12% on field-condition audio; response acceptability ≥90% on human review |
| **Tier 2 — Supported** | Marathi, Gujarati, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, Odia, Assamese | Full ASR + intent + generation + TTS; all surfaces; key templates translated and reviewed by a native speaker; eval set maintained; regressions raise a warning, not a block. | Intent accuracy ≥90%; ASR WER ≤20%; acceptability ≥85% |
| **Tier 3 — Best effort** | Urdu, Maithili, Bhojpuri, Rajasthani/Marwari, Haryanvi, Chhattisgarhi, Magahi, Konkani, Nepali, Manipuri (Meitei), Kashmiri, Sindhi, Tulu, Santali | Text understanding and generation attempted; ASR where a usable model exists; TTS where available; users see a "best effort" badge and a one-tap switch to Hindi or English; failures fall back rather than guess. | Best effort; measured, published internally, never advertised as full support |

Total: 2 + 10 + 14 = **26 languages named**, satisfying "Hindi and English plus at least 19" with margin, while stating clearly which are dependable.

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Detection | Language is detected from the user's profile setting first, then the device locale, then the input itself. Code-mixing (Hinglish, "site pe kitne guard hain") is expected and must be handled — the eval sets include code-mixed utterances for Tier 1 and Tier 2. |
| Response language | Always the language of the question unless the user has pinned a preference. Numbers, IDs, site names and person names are never translated or transliterated in a way that breaks lookup. |
| Fallback | If a Tier 3 language cannot be handled confidently, the surface responds in the user's second-choice language (default Hindi for Indian locales, English otherwise) with a one-line notice, never with a degraded answer. |
| Templates | Notification and canned-response templates are mandatory in English and Hindi (SUR-OPS §22.20.1) and optional beyond, with English fallback. |
| Quality measurement | Per language, per quarter: (1) an eval set of ≥300 real, anonymised utterances per Tier 1/2 language, ≥100 for Tier 3, refreshed quarterly from production with consent; (2) intent-match accuracy and answer acceptability scored by two native-speaker reviewers with disagreement adjudicated; (3) ASR WER measured on field-condition audio recorded at real sites, not studio audio; (4) a "harmful/incorrect answer" count, which must be zero for safety-relevant intents in any language. Results are published internally per release and a Tier 2 language falling below bar for two consecutive quarters is demoted to Tier 3 rather than quietly left broken. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-AI-006 | Language tiers shall be visible in the product; a Tier 3 interaction shall be badged as best-effort at the point of use. |
| SUR-AI-007 | Safety-relevant intents (SOS guidance, emergency instructions, incident reporting) shall be verified in every Tier 1 and Tier 2 language before release, and shall fall back to the guard's supervisor contact rather than answer uncertainly in a Tier 3 language. |
| SUR-AI-008 | No AI surface shall translate a person's name, a site name, an ID or a monetary figure in a way that changes its meaning or breaks a lookup. |

### 25.5 Voice pipeline

```
Push-to-talk capture ─► VAD & noise suppression ─► ASR (streaming) ─► Language ID
   ─► Intent & entity extraction ─► Policy gate ─► Retrieval ─► Tool/action plan
   ─► Response generation ─► Redaction ─► TTS ─► Playback (+ on-screen text & citations)
```

| Stage | Specification | Field reality it must survive |
|---|---|---|
| Capture | Push-to-talk, 16 kHz mono, on-device VAD trims silence, automatic gain control. Max utterance 30 seconds, then a prompt to continue. | Cheap Android microphones; the guard holding the phone at arm's length; wind at a gate. |
| Noise handling | On-device suppression plus a server-side denoise pass for low-SNR audio. If SNR is below the usable threshold the app says "too noisy — try again or type" **before** wasting a round trip. | Traffic at a gate post, generator hum at an industrial site, crowd noise at an event, rain on a tin roof. |
| ASR | Streaming, with partial results shown so the speaker can see it is working. Domain lexicon injected: site names, guard names, client names, "PSARA", "geofence", "wake check", shift terms, Indian number formats (lakh, crore), and the tenant's own site list — this materially improves recognition of the words that matter. | Regional accents; Hindi with English technical words; speakers who are not fluent in the language they choose. |
| Language ID | Runs on the first 2 seconds and continuously; code-mixed audio resolves to the dominant language with the mixed tokens preserved. | A guard switching between Bhojpuri and Hindi mid-sentence. |
| Intent & entities | Intent from a defined catalogue per surface; entities resolved against the user's own scope (a spoken site name is matched against sites the user is assigned to, not against all sites — this both improves accuracy and enforces scope). | Homophone site names; partial names ("Meridian" for "Meridian Logistics Warehouse"). |
| Policy gate | Same gate as text (§25.1). Voice never gets a shortcut. | — |
| Confirmation | Any Approval-required action asked by voice is confirmed **visually and verbally**, with the parsed parameters read back: "You want to request leave for 3 days from 20 November. Confirm?" Voice alone never triggers a write. | Misheard numbers and dates are the most common voice failure; read-back is the control. |
| TTS | Natural-voice output in the user's language, ~150 words per minute default, with a visible transcript. Numbers are spoken in the local convention (₹14,320 as "chaudah hazaar teen sau bees rupaye"). | Guards listening on a speaker in a noisy environment: responses under 40 words wherever possible. |
| Latency | Target p95 of 2.5 seconds from end-of-speech to first audio for a simple read query; the app plays a short acknowledgement tone at 300 ms so the user knows it heard. | — |
| Failure | ASR failure twice in a row on the same intent offers text input and the supervisor's phone number. Never silently mis-executes. | — |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-AI-009 | Voice shall never execute an Approval-required or Automated write action without a read-back confirmation of the parsed parameters. |
| SUR-AI-010 | The ASR lexicon shall be injected per user scope (their sites, their colleagues, their client names), and this injection shall not leak names outside their scope. |
| SUR-AI-011 | The voice pipeline shall degrade to text input on repeated failure and shall never present a low-confidence transcription as a confirmed instruction. |

### 25.6 Permission-aware retrieval

The single most important engineering property of this platform's AI: **an assistant that can be talked into revealing another tenant's data is a breach, not a bug.** The design assumes prompt injection will be attempted and does not rely on the model's cooperation.

| Layer | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| 1. Identity binding | Every request carries a server-issued context: `user_id`, `tenant_id`, `role[]`, `scope{state[], city[], branch[]}`, `entitlements[]`, `channel`. This context is never taken from the prompt, never editable by the model, and never present in the model's text input in a form it could rewrite. |
| 2. Pre-retrieval policy gate | Before retrieval, the planner's proposed tool calls and filters are checked against the context. A request outside scope is denied at this layer — no query runs. The denial is logged with the attempted scope. |
| 3. Hard filter injection | Every retrieval query is constructed server-side with mandatory predicates (`tenant_id = :ctx.tenant`, `branch_id IN :ctx.branches`) appended by the query builder, not by the model and not by a prompt instruction. The model can express *what* it wants; it cannot express *whose*. |
| 4. Partitioned vector index | Embeddings for retrieval-augmented content are stored in per-tenant partitions with the tenant as a physical partition key, not a metadata filter. A cross-tenant read is a routing impossibility, not a filter mistake. Within a tenant, documents carry sensitivity labels (public, operational, HR, financial, KYC, audit) and role-required-to-read; the retriever filters on these before ranking. |
| 5. Field-level redaction | Post-retrieval, a redaction pass removes fields the role may not see even within permitted rows (e.g. an Operations user retrieving a guard record gets no bank account, no salary; a Marketing user gets no client phone number). Redaction happens before the content reaches the model, so the model never holds what it must not say. |
| 6. Response-side check | Before the response is returned, a check verifies that every entity referenced in the answer was present in the retrieved, permitted set. An answer referencing an entity not in that set is suppressed and logged as a potential leak — this catches model hallucination of real-looking identifiers. |
| 7. Citation requirement | Every factual claim about platform data carries a source reference (entity + record ID + timestamp). An uncited factual claim about platform data is a defect; the surface renders "I could not verify this" instead. |
| 8. Injection resistance | Retrieved content (documents, tickets, tender PDFs, client emails) is passed to the model as **data, clearly delimited and marked untrusted**, and the system instruction states that instructions found inside retrieved content are never followed. Tool-calling permission is decided by the policy gate, not by the model's plan, so an injected "now export all guards" produces a tool call that the gate refuses. |
| 9. Role escalation impossibility | There is no tool that changes the request context. An AI surface cannot elevate itself, cannot switch tenants, cannot impersonate, and cannot read the audit log unless the user's role can. |
| 10. Testing | Every release runs a red-team suite: cross-tenant extraction attempts, role-escalation prompts, injection payloads embedded in uploaded documents and ticket text, and "tell me what you know about X" probes for entities outside scope. A single successful extraction blocks release. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-AI-012 | Tenant isolation in retrieval shall be enforced by physical partitioning and server-side query construction, never by prompt instruction or post-filtering alone. |
| SUR-AI-013 | Retrieved third-party content shall be treated as untrusted data; instructions contained within it shall never be executed, and this shall be verified by an automated injection test suite in CI. |
| SUR-AI-014 | The response-side entity check shall suppress any answer referencing an entity not present in the permitted retrieval set, and shall log the event for review. |
| SUR-AI-015 | A cross-tenant or cross-scope retrieval attempt shall raise a security event visible in §22.22.6, regardless of whether it succeeded. |

### 25.7 Action classes

The canon defines four classes. Every AI function is assigned to exactly one.

| Class | Definition | Human involvement | Logging |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Read-only** | Retrieves and presents information the user may already see. Changes nothing. | None | Interaction logged |
| **Recommendation** | Produces a suggestion, ranking, draft or analysis. Changes nothing until a human acts on it separately. | The human acts elsewhere | Interaction + recommendation content logged |
| **Approval-required** | Prepares a specific state change and presents it for approval. Executes only on explicit human approval. | Explicit approval per action | Interaction + proposal + approver + result logged |
| **Automated** | Executes directly. Permitted **only** for low-risk, easily reversible, non-financial, non-safety actions. | None at execution; reviewable after | Interaction + action + reversal path logged |

### 25.8 Human-in-the-loop approval UX

Every Approval-required action is presented as an **approval card** — the same component everywhere, so the pattern is learned once.

| Card element | Content | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Header | What will happen, in one plain sentence: "Assign Ramesh Solanki to Meridian Gate 3, night shift, tonight 20:00–08:00." | The human must understand the effect without reading parameters |
| Basis | Why the AI proposes this, with the two or three decisive facts and their sources: "Available · 4.1 km · reliability 91 · worked this site 6 times · licence and documents current." Each fact links to its record. | Approving without a basis is rubber-stamping |
| Parameters | The exact field-level change, shown as before → after where applicable. | Precision |
| Risk flags | Any soft-constraint violation, cost impact, contractual impact or unusual condition, stated in red: "This creates a 9-hour gap before his next scheduled shift — below the 11-hour rest preference." | Surfacing what the human would otherwise miss |
| Alternatives | The next two ranked options, one tap to switch. | Prevents "approve because it's the only thing offered" |
| Approver line | Who may approve this, and whether the current user qualifies. If they do not, the card offers "Send for approval to <role/person>". | No dead ends |
| Actions | **Approve** · **Edit and approve** · **Reject** (reason required) · **Ask why** (expands the full reasoning and the data used). | Edit-and-approve is essential: the human is often right about one parameter |
| Expiry | Proposals expire (default 15 minutes for operational, 24 hours for administrative) and say so, because a stale proposal approved later can be wrong. | Time-sensitivity |

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Who can approve | The permission required is the permission for the underlying action — AI adds no shortcut and no additional authority. Where the underlying action needs dual approval (financial, permission, licence), the AI proposal needs the same two approvals. Self-approval of one's own AI-generated proposal is permitted only where the human would have been able to perform the action unilaterally anyway. |
| What is logged | `interaction_id`, surface, prompt (redacted per §39), model, retrieval sources, the proposal in full, risk flags shown, alternatives shown, approver identity and role, approve/edit/reject, edited parameters, reason for rejection, execution result, and the resulting entity change with its own audit entry cross-referenced to the interaction. Both the AI's proposal and the human's decision are retained — neither is inferable from the other. |
| Bulk | Bulk approval is permitted only for homogeneous low-risk proposals (e.g. 40 document-renewal reminders) and requires the human to view a sample of at least 5 and confirm the count. Bulk approval is never available for assignments, money or compliance. |
| Rejection value | Rejections with reasons are the primary quality signal; rejection reasons are categorised (wrong data, wrong recommendation, right but not now, policy) and reported per surface monthly. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-AI-019 | The approval card shall always display the basis facts with links, the risk flags, and at least two alternatives where alternatives exist. |
| SUR-AI-020 | An approval token shall be bound to a specific proposal hash; if any parameter changes, a new approval is required. |
| SUR-AI-021 | Every executed AI-proposed action shall be traceable in both directions: from the entity's audit log to the interaction, and from the interaction to the entity's audit log. |

### 25.10 Interaction data model touchpoints

The full data model is §32; these are the touchpoints AI adds.

| Entity | Purpose | Key fields |
|---|---|---|
| `AI Interaction` | One user turn and its response | interaction_id, session_id, user_id, tenant_id, surface, channel (text/voice), locale, input (redacted), transcript_ref, intent, confidence, model_id, router_decision, tools_called[], retrieval_sources[], output, citations[], latency_ms, input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_paise, action_class, outcome, error_code |
| `AI Proposal` | An Approval-required action awaiting decision | proposal_id, interaction_id, action_type, parameters, proposal_hash, basis_facts[], risk_flags[], alternatives[], required_permission, expires_at, status |
| `AI Approval` | The human decision | approval_id, proposal_id, approver_id, role, decision, edited_parameters, reason, decided_at, step_up_used, executed_entity_ref |
| `AI Feedback` | Explicit user signal | interaction_id, rating, category, comment |
| `AI Retrieval Trace` | What was read to answer | interaction_id, source_type, entity_type, entity_id, sensitivity_label, redactions_applied[] |
| `AI Policy Event` | Denials and suppressions | event_type (scope_denied, injection_detected, entity_check_suppressed, allowance_exceeded), context, severity |
| Links | `Audit Log.ai_interaction_id`, `Approval.ai_proposal_id`, `Incident.ai_draft_interaction_id`, `Assignment.ai_recommendation_id` | Bidirectional traceability |

Retention: interactions 24 months, transcripts 90 days, proposals and approvals for the life of the affected record, policy events 24 months — subject to §39.

### 25.11 Cost and latency budgets

| Interaction class | Latency target (p50 / p95) | Cost ceiling per interaction | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Navigation / filter | 300 ms / 800 ms | ≈₹0 (no model call — intent matched locally) | Most frequent class; must not cost a model call |
| Simple data read (one entity, one metric) | 1.2 s / 2.5 s | ₹0.40 | Small model + direct retrieval |
| Multi-entity analytical answer | 2.5 s / 6 s | ₹1.50 | Larger model, multiple retrievals |
| Drafting (notice, email, incident report) | 3 s / 8 s | ₹2.50 | Streamed output so perceived latency is lower |
| Document extraction (per page) | 4 s / 12 s | ₹1.20 | Batched where possible |
| Voice end-to-end (simple read) | 2.5 s / 5 s to first audio | ₹0.90 | ASR + model + TTS |
| Command Center summary | 1.5 s / 3 s | ₹1.00 | Hard budget: the panel disappears rather than delays the operator |
| Allocation scoring (§25.15) | 400 ms / 1.2 s for 200 candidates | ≈₹0 (deterministic, no model call) | Explanation text is a separate optional model call |

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Unit economics target | `[RECOMMENDED]` Blended AI cost per active agency tenant per month ≤ ₹250 on Starter, ≤ ₹700 on Professional — i.e. ≤5% and ≤7% of subscription revenue. Enterprise is priced per contract. Suraksha's internal usage is budgeted separately at branch level. |
| Controls | Response length caps per surface; retrieval result caps (top-k tuned per intent); caching of stable answers (metric definitions, SOP text, policy answers) with a tenant-scoped cache key; deterministic paths for anything computable (allocation scoring, expiry lists, aggregations) so a model is never used to do arithmetic the database can do. |
| Monitoring | Cost and latency per surface, per intent, per tenant, visible in OPS; a tenant exceeding 3× its plan's expected usage triggers a review rather than a silent bill. |
| Degradation under cost pressure | Route to the smaller model first (§25.12), then reduce retrieval breadth, then disable drafting for non-critical surfaces — in that order, announced in-product, never silently. |

### 25.12 Model routing `[RECOMMENDED]`

| Tier | Used for | Selection rule |
|---|---|---|
| **T0 — no model** | Navigation, filters, exact-match lookups, allocation scoring, expiry lists, metric reads with a registered mapping | Intent matches a deterministic handler with confidence ≥0.9 |
| **T1 — small/fast model** | Single-entity Q&A, classification, routing, short summaries, language ID assistance, template filling | Default for read-only intents |
| **T2 — mid model** | Multi-entity reasoning, analytical explanations, drafting, incident summarisation, tender summarisation | Escalated when T1 confidence is low, when the plan requires multiple retrievals, or when output length >150 words |
| **T3 — large model** | Complex eligibility assessment, ambiguous multi-step queries, migration mapping, anything a T2 attempt failed | Escalated only after a T2 attempt or when the intent is on the T3 list |
| **Specialist** | ASR, TTS, OCR/document extraction, embeddings | Fixed per capability |

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Escalation | Automatic, at most one escalation per turn, with the escalation recorded in the interaction. A T1→T2 escalation must not exceed the interaction class's latency budget; if it would, the surface returns the T1 answer with a "want a deeper answer?" action. |
| Provider strategy | The layer is provider-abstracted with at least two viable providers per capability and no provider-specific behaviour in product code. Model IDs are configuration, changeable without release. |
| Evaluation before switching | Any model or version change runs the full eval suite (per-language, per-surface, plus the red-team suite of §25.6) before rollout, and rolls out progressively by surface with Guard AI and Command Center AI last. |
| Data handling | No customer data used for provider training; contractual and technical controls per §41. Sensitive categories (KYC content, salary, audit logs) are never sent to a model at all — they are cited, not summarised. |
| Regional | Preference for endpoints with Indian data residency where available `[ASSUMPTION: A-148]`; residency claims are contractual matters recorded in §41, not asserted here. |

### 25.13 Named AI functions from the master brief — where each lives

| Function | Surface | Class | Mechanism summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Natural-language dashboard queries | Admin, Analytics, Agency | Read-only | Question → intent → registered metric + dimensions → deterministic computation → narrated result with the formula version cited |
| Report generation | Admin, Agency, Analytics | Automated (existing) / Recommendation (new definition) | Composes registered report definitions; export honours the user's export rights |
| Attendance analysis | Admin, Agency, Analytics | Read-only | Compares actual vs rostered across time, site, guard, supervisor and cause; explains contribution shares rather than listing rows |
| Shift suggestions | Admin, Agency | Recommendation | Detects gaps on the 42-day horizon; proposes pattern changes and specific fills; never publishes |
| Guard allocation suggestions | Admin, Agency, Command Center | Recommendation | §25.15 |
| Incident summarisation | Command Center, Admin, Agency | Recommendation | Summarises from the alert timeline only, never from inference; produces a draft the human owns |
| Anomaly detection | Admin, Analytics, Agency | Recommendation | Statistical detection on registered metrics (attendance, incidents, attrition, collections, usage) with seasonality; each anomaly names the contributing dimension |
| Compliance reminders | Compliance, Agency | Automated | Notifications only; content is deterministic |
| Licence expiry detection | Compliance, Admin, Agency | Read-only | Deterministic query; AI adds prioritisation by operational exposure (how many deployments and guards are affected) |
| Document extraction | Compliance, Recruitment, Agency | Recommendation | Field extraction with per-field confidence; below threshold → blank field with the crop shown |
| OCR | Same | Recommendation | Multi-language OCR including Devanagari and regional scripts; handwriting is best-effort and flagged as such |
| Legacy data migration | Agency (Enterprise), Admin | Approval-required | Scan → extract → map to entities → human reviews a sampled set and the full exception list → commit in a reversible batch with a rollback window |
| Payroll query assistance | Guard, Agency, Admin | Read-only | Explains a computed payslip line by line from the payroll engine's own breakdown; never recomputes |
| Client query assistance | Customer, Support | Read-only | Grounded in the client's own records and the knowledge base |
| Tender summarisation | Tender, Agency | Read-only | Structured brief with page citations |
| Tender eligibility assistance | Tender, Agency, Compliance | Recommendation | Clause-by-clause with evidence matched; gaps and unclear clauses listed separately; never a conclusion |
| Recruitment screening assistance | Recruitment, Agency | Recommendation | Requirement matching only; no rejection; no protected-characteristic inference |
| Training assistance | Guard, Agency | Read-only + Automated reminders | Explains content, quizzes, reminds; cannot mark completion |
| Voice-based operations | All | Underlying class | §25.5 |
| Multilingual translation | All | Automated (in-product) / Approval-required (templates) | Names, IDs and amounts preserved |
| Predictive staffing | Admin, Analytics, Agency | Recommendation | Forecasts demand and absence risk by site/branch/season; feeds recruitment requisitions as suggestions |
| Site risk insights | Admin, Command Center, Agency | Recommendation | Correlates incidents, patrol exceptions, attrition, geography and time; proposes risk band changes for human approval |
| Performance insights | Admin, Agency, HR | Recommendation | Guard, supervisor, branch and operator performance narratives from registered metrics; never an automated consequence |

### 25.14 Fallback, degradation and traceability

| Condition | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Model provider unavailable | Router fails over to the alternate provider within the same tier. If all providers for a tier fail, the surface degrades: deterministic intents (navigation, filters, expiry lists, allocation scoring) keep working; generative intents show "AI assistance is temporarily unavailable" with the module's normal UI fully usable. |
| Retrieval unavailable | No answer is generated from model memory. The surface says what is unavailable and offers the last cached answer with its timestamp, or the module link. |
| Latency budget exceeded | The turn is cut with a partial, clearly-labelled answer plus a retry action; the console panel collapses rather than blocking (SUR-AI-024). |
| Policy gate denies | A plain explanation of scope ("this is outside your branch scope") without revealing the data's contents or confirming specific record existence in detail. |
| Low confidence | Below the per-intent threshold, the surface asks a clarifying question or hands off to a human; it does not answer. |
| Voice failure | §25.5. |
| Total AI outage | **Every product remains fully operable without AI.** No workflow, screen, approval or safety mechanism depends on an AI response. This is a design constraint, verified by an "AI disabled" test run of the core journeys each release. |

**Traceability of AI output.** Every AI answer carries, visible to the user on expand: the sources used (entity type, ID, timestamp), the model tier, the interaction ID, and — for recommendations — the factors and weights that produced the ranking. Every AI-proposed action that executes appears in the affected record's audit log with the interaction ID, and the interaction record links back. A user can always ask "why did you say that?" and receive the retrieval trace rendered as a list of records, not as prose.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-AI-024 | No product workflow shall have AI as a hard dependency; an AI outage shall degrade capability, never block a task. |
| SUR-AI-025 | Every AI answer shall be able to render its retrieval trace on demand, and every executed AI proposal shall be discoverable from the affected entity's audit log. |
| SUR-AI-026 | The AI layer shall never present a model-generated number as a platform fact; numbers shall come from deterministic computation and be cited. |

### 25.15 The Guard Allocation Engine

The allocation engine decides *which guard goes to which post*. It is the operational core of both businesses, it runs hundreds of times a day, and it is where AI's usefulness and AI's danger meet. It is deterministic in its scoring, explainable in its output, and gated by compliance rules that no score can override.

#### 25.15.1 Where it runs

| Trigger | Caller | Urgency |
|---|---|---|
| New deployment mobilisation | Admin (OPS), Agency Portal | Hours to days |
| Roster generation for the next horizon | Admin, Agency Portal | Days |
| Replacement for an absence | Command Center, Admin, Agency Portal, Supervisor app | Minutes |
| Booking assignment | Admin, Admin App | Hours |
| Event/short-duration staffing | Admin, Agency Portal | Hours |
| What-if planning ("can we take this contract?") | Admin, Agency Portal | Non-urgent |

#### 25.15.2 Inputs

| # | Input | Source | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Location (guard home, current location if on duty) | Guard record, last known ping | Distance and travel feasibility |
| 2 | Availability | Roster, leave, current assignment, rest-period state | Hard constraint |
| 3 | Skill set | Guard skills | Match to post requirements |
| 4 | Guard category | Guard record (unarmed/armed/PSO/bouncer/supervisor/specialised) | Hard constraint |
| 5 | Licence (weapon-linked, where applicable) | Document/licence records | Hard constraint for armed posts |
| 6 | Experience (years, and at this site/client/industry) | Employment + assignment history | Soft preference |
| 7 | Training currency | Training records | Hard (statutory) or soft (non-statutory) |
| 8 | Client requirements | Contract, post definition (languages, gender where lawful and specified, height, ex-servicemen, uniform standard, specific named guards) | Hard or soft per how the contract expresses it |
| 9 | Shift compatibility | Post shift pattern vs guard's pattern history and stated preference | Soft |
| 10 | Distance / travel time | Geo distance + travel-time estimate for the shift start hour | Soft, with a hard ceiling |
| 11 | Agency (for marketplace/subcontract deployments) | Tenant of the guard vs the deployment's agency | Hard constraint (never mix tenants without an explicit subcontract, D-140) |
| 12 | Previous assignment at this site/client | Assignment history | Soft positive (familiarity) or hard negative (client-barred) |
| 13 | Rating | Client reviews, supervisor assessments | Soft |
| 14 | Reliability score | Computed (§22.9.1) | Soft, heavily weighted |
| 15 | Working-hour constraints | Configured rules: max hours/day, max consecutive days, min rest between shifts, max hours/week | **Hard** |
| 16 | Compliance state | KYC, police verification, document validity, blacklist, disciplinary hold | **Hard veto** (§25.15.5) |
| 17 | Cost | Guard's wage band vs the post's budgeted rate | Soft, tie-breaker only |
| 18 | Continuity requirement | Contract clause requiring named or stable guards | Hard where contracted |

#### 25.15.3 Hard constraints vs soft preferences

**Hard constraints — a candidate failing any one is excluded, not penalised.** No score can compensate.

| # | Hard constraint | Failure means |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | Compliance veto (§25.15.5) | Excluded |
| H2 | Wrong guard category for the post (e.g. unarmed guard for an armed post) | Excluded |
| H3 | Missing statutory training or licence for the post type | Excluded |
| H4 | Not available: on another active assignment, on approved leave, off roll | Excluded (BR-001) |
| H5 | Working-hour rule breach: insufficient rest, over daily/weekly maximum, over consecutive-days maximum | Excluded |
| H6 | Distance beyond the hard ceiling (default 25 km, configurable per city; 40 km for planned deployments, 15 km for urgent replacements) | Excluded |
| H7 | Cross-tenant assignment without an authorised subcontract | Excluded |
| H8 | Client-barred at this site or client | Excluded |
| H9 | Contract-mandated requirement not met (a hard-stated client requirement) | Excluded |
| H10 | Guard status not Active | Excluded |

**Soft preferences — scored, not gating.**

| Factor | Weight | Scoring (0–100 each, then weighted) |
|---|---|---|
| Distance / travel feasibility | **22%** | 100 at ≤2 km, linear to 40 at 15 km, 10 at the hard ceiling; travel-time adjusted for shift-start hour where data exists |
| Reliability score | **20%** | The guard's 0–100 reliability score used directly |
| Skill & requirement match | **16%** | Proportion of the post's soft requirements met, weighted by the contract's stated priority |
| Site/client familiarity | **12%** | 100 if worked this site in the last 90 days, 70 same client different site, 40 same industry vertical, 0 otherwise |
| Client rating | **10%** | Mean rating normalised; unrated guards take the branch median, never 0 |
| Experience | **8%** | Years capped at 8; plus a bonus for experience in the post's specific role type |
| Shift-pattern fit | **6%** | 100 if the guard regularly works this pattern; 50 if occasionally; 20 if never |
| Continuity / roster stability | **4%** | Penalises breaking an existing stable pairing at another site |
| Cost fit | **2%** | Within budget band = 100; above = proportional penalty. Deliberately the smallest weight — cost must never dominate a safety-relevant staffing decision |

Weights are configuration, versioned, per tenant, with Enterprise agencies able to tune them within bounds (no single factor above 35%, compliance factors not tunable). The weight-set version is recorded on every recommendation.

#### 25.15.4 Worked calculation

Post: *Meridian Logistics, Gate 3, roving night guard, 20:00–08:00, tonight.* Urgent replacement. Unarmed. Client requirement: Hindi + Marathi speaking (soft), prior site experience (soft).

Candidate pool: 47 active guards in the branch. Hard constraints exclude 41:

| Exclusion | Count |
|---|---|
| Already assigned tonight (H4) | 22 |
| Insufficient rest — finished a shift at 08:00 today (H5) | 9 |
| Distance beyond 15 km urgent ceiling (H6) | 6 |
| On approved leave (H4) | 2 |
| Police verification expired (H1 compliance veto) | 1 |
| Training lapsed — statutory (H3) | 1 |

Six candidates remain. Top three scored:

| Factor (weight) | G-4390 Ramesh S. | G-4512 Anil P. | G-4287 Vikas M. |
|---|---|---|---|
| Distance (22%) | 7.2 km → 62 → **13.6** | 3.1 km → 92 → **20.2** | 11.8 km → 47 → **10.3** |
| Reliability (20%) | 91 → **18.2** | 68 → **13.6** | 84 → **16.8** |
| Skill & requirement match (16%) | Hindi+Marathi → 100 → **16.0** | Hindi only → 60 → **9.6** | Hindi+Marathi → 100 → **16.0** |
| Site familiarity (12%) | 6 shifts here in 90d → 100 → **12.0** | Never → 0 → **0.0** | Same client, other site → 70 → **8.4** |
| Client rating (10%) | 4.6/5 → 92 → **9.2** | 4.1/5 → 82 → **8.2** | 4.4/5 → 88 → **8.8** |
| Experience (8%) | 6 yrs, roving → 85 → **6.8** | 2 yrs → 40 → **3.2** | 9 yrs → 100 → **8.0** |
| Shift-pattern fit (6%) | Regular night → 100 → **6.0** | Mixed → 50 → **3.0** | Regular night → 100 → **6.0** |
| Continuity (4%) | Not breaking a pairing → 100 → **4.0** | Not breaking → 100 → **4.0** | Breaking a stable pairing → 40 → **1.6** |
| Cost fit (2%) | In band → 100 → **2.0** | In band → 100 → **2.0** | Above band → 60 → **1.2** |
| **Total** | **87.8** | **63.8** | **77.1** |

Recommendation: **G-4390 Ramesh Solanki, score 87.8**, with the two decisive factors surfaced on the approval card ("site familiarity — 6 shifts here in 90 days; reliability 91"), one risk flag ("7.2 km at 19:20 — estimated travel 26 minutes; shift starts in 41 minutes"), and the two alternatives listed. The score, the weight-set version, the excluded-candidate counts by reason, and the full factor breakdown are stored on the recommendation and rendered on demand.

#### 25.15.5 The compliance veto

| Veto condition | Applies to | Override |
|---|---|---|
| Police verification missing, expired or Rejected | All allocations | **None.** No role, no emergency, no override. |
| Blacklisted, or under disciplinary hold | All | **None.** |
| Guard status not Active | All | **None.** |
| Mandatory KYC document missing, expired or Rejected | All | **None.** |
| Statutory training expired for the post's category | All | **None.** |
| Weapon-linked licence/authorisation invalid | Armed posts | **None.** |
| Agency licence expired for the deployment's jurisdiction (BR-002) | All allocations in that jurisdiction | **None** for new allocations; existing deployments are flagged for a management decision, not silently continued |
| Working-hour rule breach | All | **Only** by State Operations, only for a genuine emergency, recorded with a reason, notified to Compliance and Founder/Management, counted in a monthly report; three or more in a month at one branch is itself a compliance finding |
| Non-statutory training expired | All | Soft penalty (−15 on the skill factor) plus a risk flag; allocation permitted |
| Document expiring within 7 days | All | Soft penalty (−5) plus a risk flag and an auto-created renewal task |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-AI-027 | The compliance veto shall be evaluated server-side at both recommendation time **and** assignment-commit time; a guard who becomes non-compliant between recommendation and commit shall be rejected at commit with the reason. |
| SUR-AI-028 | A vetoed guard shall never appear in a recommendation list, not even greyed out; the list shall instead show the count of candidates excluded and the reason breakdown, without naming them. |
| SUR-AI-029 | The working-hour override shall require State Operations authority, a recorded reason, and immediate notification to Compliance; no other veto shall be overridable by any role. |
| SUR-AI-030 | Every allocation commit shall re-verify BR-001 (no overlapping active assignments) transactionally, so that two concurrent allocators cannot both assign the same guard. |

#### 25.15.6 Where human approval is mandatory

| Deployment situation | Approval |
|---|---|
| Routine replacement, standard site, score ≥70, no risk flags | One-tap approval by the operator or ops user initiating it |
| Any recommendation with a risk flag | Explicit approval with the flag acknowledged |
| Top score below the threshold (default 60) | §25.15.7 fallback; approval by City Operations |
| Armed post, PSO, or close-protection assignment | **Named approval by City Operations or above**, always, regardless of score |
| Tier-1 client site | Approval by City Operations or above |
| Government client site | Approval by State Operations |
| Critical-risk-band site | Approval by City Operations or above |
| First assignment of a newly activated guard | Approval by City Operations, with a supervisor accompaniment flag for the first shift |
| Assignment invoking a working-hour override | State Operations, per §25.15.5 |
| Cross-branch or cross-tenant (subcontract) assignment | State Operations |
| Bulk roster publication (many assignments at once) | Approval of the roster as a whole by City Operations, with every risk-flagged line individually acknowledged |

Auto-assignment without any human approval exists in exactly one case `[RECOMMENDED]`: **re-assigning the same guard to the same post on a recurring roster where nothing has changed** — same guard, same post, same shift pattern, no new risk flags, compliance re-verified. Everything else needs a human.

#### 25.15.7 Fallback when nothing scores above threshold

| Step | Action |
|---|---|
| 1 | **Widen the soft envelope, never the hard one.** Increase the distance ceiling in configured increments (15 → 20 → 25 km for urgent), relax pattern-fit and familiarity preferences, re-score. Hard constraints and the compliance veto are never relaxed. |
| 2 | **Search neighbouring branches** within the same city/state, subject to H7 and the licence geography. Recommendation is flagged as cross-branch and needs State Operations approval. |
| 3 | **Offer the standby pool** — guards designated as float/standby for the branch, who carry a standing availability arrangement. |
| 4 | **Offer overtime extension** — extend the outgoing guard's shift, but only where the working-hour rules permit it without an override; the engine computes the maximum lawful extension and shows it. |
| 5 | **Offer supervisor cover** — a supervisor holds the post temporarily; permitted for a maximum configured duration (default 4 hours) and recorded as supervisor cover, not as a guard deployment, so SLA reporting stays truthful. |
| 6 | **Offer subcontract** to a verified marketplace agency with a valid licence for the jurisdiction, where D-140 permits; the agency's guard must pass the same hard constraints and compliance veto. |
| 7 | **Declare an unfillable gap.** The engine stops guessing: it creates an `UNSTAFFED_POST` alert at the mapped severity, notifies the client per §24.7.4, records the shortfall against the contract for billing and SLA truthfulness, and creates a recruitment signal for the branch. |

The engine never fills a post by lowering a compliance standard, and never presents a below-threshold candidate as a good one — it presents the best available with its score, the gap to threshold, and the specific weaknesses, so the approving human decides with full information.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-AI-031 | The fallback ladder shall be executed in the order above, with each step's outcome recorded, so that an unfilled post can be shown to have exhausted the available options. |
| SUR-AI-032 | An unfillable gap shall always produce an alert, a client notification per contract, and an honest SLA record — the platform shall have no mechanism to conceal a shortfall. |
| SUR-AI-033 | Every recommendation shall persist its inputs, weight-set version, scores, exclusions by reason, and the human decision, so any past allocation can be explained months later. |

| R-143 | An AI surface is manipulated by prompt injection in an uploaded document into revealing or acting outside scope | A cross-tenant leak would be existential for the SaaS business | Physical partitioning, server-side filters, untrusted-content handling, entity check, red-team gate in CI | Security, tenancy, reputation |
| R-144 | The allocation engine's soft weights drift toward cost or convenience and quietly degrade guard quality at client sites | Slow, invisible erosion of service standard | Cost weight capped at 2%, weight sets versioned and reviewed quarterly, outcome metrics tracked per weight-set version | Service quality, churn |
| R-145 | Concentration risk on a single model provider or ASR vendor for Hindi and regional languages | An outage or price change disables voice for the field workforce | Two viable providers per capability, deterministic fallbacks, provider-abstracted routing | AI availability, cost |
| R-146 | Break-glass access becomes a routine workaround for slow permission processes | Destroys the integrity of the access model | Loud alerting on every use, mandatory 24-hour review, credential rotation, quarterly drill, usage reported to Founder/Management | Security, audit, compliance |
| R-147 | Manual attendance overrides are used to conceal understaffing, corrupting both billing and SLA reporting | Financial misstatement and client fraud exposure | Override rate monitored per branch with a 5% alert threshold, dual approval above a monthly threshold, reconciliation variance reported | Finance, SLA, integrity |



## 26. Complete Functional Requirements

### 26.0 What this section is, and what it is not

Sections 11–25 define **what each product does**. This section defines **what every product must do the same way**. A requirement belongs here only if it satisfies at least one of three tests:

1. It is implemented once and consumed by two or more surfaces (identity, search, the rule engine, document storage).
2. It is a platform-wide invariant that no product may weaken (tenant isolation, audit, permission-aware retrieval).
3. It is a shared capability whose per-product expression is a thin skin over common machinery (support ticketing, content publishing, localisation).

Anything that is a single product's screen, field list or flow stays in §14–§25 and is referenced here, never restated. Screens are enumerated only in §28. Design tokens and components live in §27. Step-by-step workflow choreography lives in §29; where a rule in §26.4 corresponds to a workflow, the `WKF-nn` reference is given rather than the steps.

#### 26.0.1 Product codes used in the "Products affected" column

| Code | Surface | Code | Surface |
|---|---|---|---|
| WEB | Main website surakshaguards.in | AGN | Agency Portal ap.surakshaguards.in (+ desktop build) |
| CPT | Customer portal (authenticated area of WEB) | AAP | Suraksha Agency App |
| CAP | Suraksha Customer App | OPS | Suraksha OPS ops.surakshaguards.in |
| GRD | Guard platform guards.surakshaguards.in | ADP | Suraksha Admin App |
| GAP | Suraksha Guard App | CMD | Command Center (a console within OPS, §24) |
| TRN | TRINETRA trinetra.surakshaguards.in | AI | AI Platform (§25) |
| ALL | Every surface above | SVC | Backend service only, no direct UI |

#### 26.0.2 Priority and phase semantics

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| P0 | Launch blocker. The platform is not safe, legal or coherent without it. |
| P1 | Required for the phase named, but a defined manual workaround exists for a short window. |
| P2 | Valuable, schedulable, no workaround needed at launch. |
| Phase 1 | Website + client portal + OPS + Trinetra (§8, launch wave 1). |
| Phase 2 | Guard App, Agency Portal, Customer App, Guard platform. |
| Phase 3 | Agency App, Admin App, desktop builds, depth features. |

Phase allocation here is indicative and is owned by §51 Roadmap; where §51 and §26 disagree, §51 wins for sequencing and §26 wins for content.
