### 26.1 Identity & authentication

Canon §4 settles the stance: **one central identity service across all products, phone-first**. This subsection turns that stance into requirements. The identity service is the only component in the ecosystem that owns credentials; no product stores a password, an OTP, or a session secret of its own.

#### 26.1.1 The centralized identity decision

| Aspect | Decision |
|---|---|
| Model | Single Identity Service (`SUR-IDS`) issuing tokens for all ten surfaces. One human = one Identity, regardless of how many roles, agencies, branches or products they touch. |
| Identity key | Internal immutable `identity_id` (UUID). Never the phone number, never the email — both are mutable contact facts, not keys. |
| Login handles | Mobile number (primary), email, username. Canon §1: the live ops portal already accepts username OR email OR mobile + password; that behaviour is preserved and extended to all surfaces. |
| Role attachment | Roles are **not** properties of the Identity. An Identity holds zero or more **Memberships**: `(identity_id, tenant_id, branch_id?, role, status, valid_from, valid_to)`. A guard employed by two agencies over time has two Memberships, one Identity, one attendance history. |
| Cross-product SSO | A single session token is scoped to one product family at a time (see SUR-FRQ-014); "single sign-on" here means one credential and one MFA enrolment, not one omnipotent token. |
| Why centralized | Three reasons that are not negotiable: a guard's verification status must be identical everywhere it is read; a suspended account must be dead on all ten surfaces within seconds; and fraud signals (§26.8) are only detectable when login telemetry is pooled. |

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Products affected | Phase | Acceptance summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SUR-FRQ-001 | A single Identity Service shall own all credentials, OTP issuance, session issuance and MFA enrolment for the ecosystem. No product shall store or verify a password. | P0 | ALL | 1 | Static analysis and a design review confirm zero password-verification code paths outside `SUR-IDS`; a credential change is effective on all surfaces within 10 s. |
| SUR-FRQ-002 | Every human shall have exactly one Identity, keyed by immutable `identity_id`; phone number and email are mutable attributes with independent verification state. | P0 | ALL | 1 | Changing a verified mobile number preserves `identity_id`, all Memberships, and all historical audit references. |
| SUR-FRQ-003 | Mobile OTP shall be the primary authentication factor: 6-digit numeric, valid 5 minutes, single use, rate-limited to 3 sends per number per 15 minutes and 10 per 24 hours, with a 30 s resend cooldown and escalating backoff (30 s / 60 s / 180 s). | P0 | ALL | 1 | Rate limits verified by test; a reused or expired OTP fails with a non-enumerating message (§26.1.7). |
| SUR-FRQ-004 | OTP delivery shall attempt SMS first and fall back to WhatsApp and voice-call OTP on delivery failure or user request; the fallback offer shall appear after the first failed delivery, not before. | P1 | ALL | 1 | Simulated SMS gateway failure produces a WhatsApp attempt within 20 s and a visible "Get a call instead" action. |
| SUR-FRQ-005 | Phone verification shall be mandatory for every Identity before any transactional action (booking, roster publish, invoice, payment, document upload). Browsing and quote requests may precede it. | P0 | ALL | 1 | An unverified Identity attempting a transactional endpoint receives 403 with `PHONE_UNVERIFIED` and is routed to verification. |
| SUR-FRQ-006 | Email + password and username + password shall be supported as alternates, with password policy: minimum 10 characters, not in the breached-password list, no composition rules beyond length, no forced periodic rotation. | P0 | ALL | 1 | Passwords are stored with Argon2id; a known-breached password is rejected at set time with a clear reason. |
| SUR-FRQ-007 | Google and Apple federated sign-in shall be supported on client-facing surfaces (WEB, CPT, CAP) and shall still require phone verification before transactional actions. | P1 | WEB, CPT, CAP | 2 | A Google sign-in for a new user lands on the phone-verification step, not the dashboard. |
| SUR-FRQ-008 | MFA shall be optional for client roles, **enforced** for all Suraksha internal roles, and **configurable-but-default-on** for Agency Owner, Agency Admin, Payroll and Agency Finance. | P0 | OPS, ADP, AGN, AAP | 1 | An internal role without MFA enrolment can complete enrolment only; every other action is blocked. |
| SUR-FRQ-009 | Supported second factors: TOTP authenticator app (primary), SMS OTP (fallback, not permitted as sole factor for Super Admin, Finance or Compliance), and 10 single-use recovery codes issued once at enrolment. | P0 | OPS, ADP, AGN | 1 | Super Admin cannot complete enrolment with SMS alone; recovery codes are shown once and stored hashed. |
| SUR-FRQ-010 | Step-up authentication shall be required for a defined set of sensitive actions regardless of session age: payout release, payroll approval, permission grant, impersonation start, break-glass, bulk export >1,000 rows, account deletion, licence status change. | P0 | OPS, AGN, ADP | 1 | Each listed action prompts for MFA re-entry; a satisfied step-up is valid 15 minutes and is recorded on the audit entry. |
| SUR-FRQ-011 | Every authentication shall be bound to a registered **Device** record: device fingerprint, platform, OS version, app version, push token, first-seen, last-seen, trust state (Trusted / Pending / Blocked). | P0 | ALL | 1 | Two logins from the same device produce one Device row; a wiped app produces a new Pending device. |
| SUR-FRQ-012 | Guard App shall be limited to **one active device per Identity** by default; logging in on a second device shall terminate the first session and raise a P2 alert to the employing tenant. | P0 | GAP | 2 | Second-device login terminates the first within 5 s; the tenant sees a "Device changed" alert naming both devices. |
| SUR-FRQ-013 | A user shall be able to view all active sessions and devices (device name, platform, location city derived from IP, last active) and terminate any of them individually or all-but-current. | P0 | ALL | 1 | Terminating a session invalidates its refresh token within 5 s and forces re-auth on next API call. |
| SUR-FRQ-014 | Session lifetimes shall be: client roles 30 days sliding refresh; guard 30 days sliding (field reality — see §18); agency staff 12 hours idle / 7 days absolute; Suraksha internal 8 hours idle / 24 hours absolute; Command Center Operator 12 hours absolute tied to shift. | P0 | ALL | 1 | Token TTLs match the table; idle expiry produces a re-auth prompt that preserves unsaved form state where technically possible. |
| SUR-FRQ-015 | Access tokens shall be short-lived (15 minutes) with refresh-token rotation and reuse detection; detected reuse shall revoke the entire token family and raise a P1 security alert. | P0 | ALL | 1 | Replaying a rotated refresh token revokes the family and creates a security event with device and IP. |
| SUR-FRQ-016 | Login history shall be retained per Identity for 24 months: timestamp, result (success / failed / blocked / MFA-failed), method, IP, coarse geo, device, product, and — on failure — the failure class. Users see their own history; tenant admins see their members' history within their tenant. | P0 | ALL | 1 | History is visible in account settings, exportable by the user, and immutable. |
| SUR-FRQ-017 | Suspicious-login detection shall score each attempt on: new device, impossible travel (>800 km/h implied), new country, IP reputation, unusual hour for that Identity, failed-attempt velocity, and credential-stuffing pattern across the platform. | P1 | ALL | 1 | A scripted impossible-travel scenario triggers a challenge and a notification within 60 s. |
| SUR-FRQ-018 | Suspicious-login response ladder: score ≥40 → email/SMS "new sign-in" notice; ≥60 → force MFA challenge; ≥80 → block the attempt, notify the user on the last-trusted channel, and create a Fraud case (§26.8.9). | P1 | ALL | 1 | Each threshold produces the stated response in test; the ladder is configurable per role class without a deploy. |
| SUR-FRQ-019 | Account lockout shall be adaptive, not absolute: 5 failed attempts → CAPTCHA; 10 → 15-minute lock on the handle+IP pair; sustained attack → lock the handle and notify the owner. A permanent lock shall never be reachable by an unauthenticated attacker. | P0 | ALL | 1 | An attacker cannot deny service to a known mobile number for more than 15 minutes. |
| SUR-FRQ-020 | Password reset shall be OTP-based to a verified channel, shall invalidate all sessions except the resetting one, shall never confirm or deny the existence of an account, and shall be blocked while an account is Suspended. | P0 | ALL | 1 | Reset for a non-existent handle returns the same message and timing (±100 ms) as a real one. |
| SUR-FRQ-021 | Account recovery for a lost phone number shall require a human-reviewed flow: identity proof document + a second verified channel + (for guards) employer attestation; recovery shall never be fully automated. | P0 | ALL | 1 | A recovery request creates a Support case with an SLA (§26.7) and cannot be self-approved by the requester. |
| SUR-FRQ-022 | Role switching shall be explicit and visible: where an Identity holds multiple roles in the same tenant, the active role is shown in the top bar and switching re-resolves the entire permission set server-side, never client-side. | P0 | OPS, AGN, CPT, AAP | 2 | Switching role changes the rendered navigation and re-issues an access token with the new role claim. |
| SUR-FRQ-023 | Organization (tenant) switching shall be available where an Identity has Memberships in more than one tenant; the switch shall be a full context change — new token, new scope, cleared client-side caches — and shall be recorded in the audit log of **both** tenants. | P0 | AGN, AAP, GRD, GAP | 2 | After switching, no data from the previous tenant is present in any cache, list or search result. |
| SUR-FRQ-024 | Branch switching shall operate within a tenant only, shall be constrained to the branches the Membership permits, and shall support an "All permitted branches" aggregate view for roles that hold it. | P0 | AGN, AAP, OPS | 2 | A Branch Manager sees only their branches in the switcher; the aggregate view sums only permitted branches. |
| SUR-FRQ-025 | Remote logout shall be available to: the user (own sessions), a tenant admin (their members), and Suraksha Super Admin (any session, with reason and audit). Forced logout shall propagate to offline Guard App devices on next connectivity and shall wipe locally cached operational data. | P0 | ALL | 2 | Guard App reconnecting after a forced logout clears its local store before showing the login screen. |
| SUR-FRQ-026 | Account suspension shall be a first-class state with reasons (Fraud investigation, Non-payment, Compliance, Employment ended, User request, Security) and shall immediately: terminate sessions, block login with a reason-appropriate message, and preserve all data. | P0 | ALL | 1 | A suspended guard cannot mark attendance; the roster shows the post as at-risk and the tenant is alerted. |
| SUR-FRQ-027 | Suspension shall be reversible by an authorised role with a recorded reason; deletion shall follow the soft-delete rule (canon §4) — `status=Archived` plus the retention policy in §39, never a hard delete of operational or financial rows. | P0 | ALL | 1 | Reinstatement restores Memberships in their prior state and is auditable end to end. |
| SUR-FRQ-028 | Identity Service shall expose a single `/session/introspect` contract that every product uses to resolve `identity_id`, active Membership, role, tenant, branch scope, entitlements and MFA state in one call. | P0 | SVC | 1 | No product derives permissions from a JWT claim it decoded itself without introspection or signed-claims verification. |
| SUR-FRQ-029 | Impersonation ("view as") by Suraksha staff shall be read-only by default, time-boxed to 60 minutes, require step-up auth and a reason, be visible in the impersonated tenant's audit log, and display a persistent banner on every screen (§27.3.11). | P0 | OPS, ADP | 1 | The banner is unremovable; any write attempt in read-only impersonation returns 403 and is logged. |
| SUR-FRQ-030 | Identity Service shall publish authentication events (`login.succeeded`, `login.failed`, `mfa.challenged`, `session.revoked`, `device.registered`, `suspension.applied`) to the event bus for consumption by fraud (§26.8), analytics (§42) and notifications (§36). | P1 | SVC | 1 | Each event appears on the bus within 2 s with a stable schema and a correlation ID. |

#### 26.1.2 Handle collision and the guard-agency reality

Two India-specific facts break naive identity models and must be designed for:

| Situation | Rule |
|---|---|
| A guard leaves Agency A and joins Agency B | The Identity persists. Membership A is closed (`valid_to` set, status Archived). Membership B is created. Agency A retains historical records of the employment period only; Agency B sees nothing of Agency A's operational data (§26.2). The guard's own verification documents and training records follow the Identity, and each new employer must re-consent to view them (§39). |
| One phone shared by a family / a small agency's single number | Permitted, but a phone number can be the **primary** handle for exactly one Identity. Additional Identities may use it as a contact number only and must authenticate by another handle. This is a real support driver; the collision error must name a resolution path, not just refuse. |
| A guard with no email, low literacy, a feature phone in hand plus a smartphone at home | Email is never mandatory. OTP delivery must work over SMS and voice. The Guard App must support login by mobile + OTP with no password ever set. |
| Agency Owner who is also a Client (buys guarding from Suraksha) | Two Memberships, one Identity, tenant switcher exposed. The Agency Portal and the client portal are different products; the switch is a product switch, not a tab. |

---

### 26.2 Multi-tenant architecture requirements

#### 26.2.1 The absolute rule

> **SUR-FRQ-031 (The Isolation Rule).** No agency shall ever be able to read, infer, count, search, export, or have summarised to it any other agency's private operational data — by any interface, at any privilege level available to that agency, in any product, including through autocomplete suggestions, aggregate counts, error messages, timing differences, exported files, notification content, and AI-generated answers. Only data the platform explicitly classifies as **Marketplace-Public** (§26.2.4) crosses a tenant boundary, and only in the direction the classification permits.

This is the single requirement whose violation would end the SaaS business (R-104, R-190). It is enforced in seven independent layers, and the design intent is that **any one layer failing must not produce a leak**.

| Layer | Enforcement mechanism | Failure mode it stops |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Data model | Every tenant-owned table carries a non-nullable `tenant_id`. No tenant-owned row exists without one. Composite primary/foreign keys include `tenant_id` so a cross-tenant join is structurally invalid. | Orphan rows, accidental cross-tenant FK |
| 2. Query | Row-Level Security policies in the database bound to a session variable set from the verified token — not from a request parameter. Application code cannot disable RLS; the app's database role lacks `BYPASSRLS`. | A developer forgetting a `WHERE tenant_id = ?` |
| 3. ORM/repository | A repository base class that refuses to build a query without a tenant scope; a lint rule that fails CI on raw SQL against tenant tables outside the sanctioned data-access layer. | Raw SQL creeping into a service |
| 4. API | Tenant is resolved **only** from the session token. A `tenant_id` supplied in a path, query, body or header is either ignored or rejected as a tampering attempt; it is never trusted. Object-level authorization is checked on every read of a specific ID (no IDOR). | Parameter tampering, IDOR |
| 5. Storage | Object keys are prefixed `t/{tenant_id}/…`; all access is through short-lived pre-signed URLs (≤15 min) issued after an authorization check; buckets deny public reads; a per-tenant encryption key is used for Enterprise tenants. | Guessable URLs, shared links, bucket misconfiguration |
| 6. Search | Tenant is a filter applied **before** ranking and before result-count computation, at the index level (per-tenant index routing), not a post-filter on results (§26.3). | Leaked counts, leaked suggestions |
| 7. Analytics / AI retrieval | Every retrieval query carries the tenant scope; per-tenant vector namespaces are physically partitioned; a post-generation entity check verifies that no entity ID in an answer is outside the caller's scope (§25, §41). | Embedding-space bleed, prompt injection |

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Products affected | Phase | Acceptance summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SUR-FRQ-032 | Tenancy shall be modelled as `Organization → Agency (tenant) → Branch → Team`, where `tenant_id = agency_id` and Suraksha's own guarding operation is tenant `SURAKSHA-HQ` with no special-case code path. | P0 | ALL | 1 | A code search finds no `if tenant == 'SURAKSHA-HQ'` branch in the data-access layer. |
| SUR-FRQ-033 | Branch shall be a second scoping axis, never a substitute for tenant isolation; a branch-scoped user is additionally restricted, but a tenant-scoped check always runs first. | P0 | AGN, AAP, OPS | 2 | Removing branch scoping from a user never grants cross-tenant visibility. |
| SUR-FRQ-034 | The branch hierarchy shall support at least 4 levels (National → State → City → Branch) with unlimited sub-branches below, and shall permit a user to be scoped to a set of nodes rather than a single subtree. | P1 | AGN, OPS | 2 | A user scoped to {Jaipur, Kota} sees exactly those branches' data in every list, report and search. |
| SUR-FRQ-035 | Database Row-Level Security shall be enabled on every tenant-owned table with the tenant value taken from a session variable set by the authenticated context; the application database role shall not hold `BYPASSRLS`. | P0 | SVC | 1 | A deliberately unscoped query in a test returns zero rows rather than another tenant's rows. |
| SUR-FRQ-036 | A `tenant_id` supplied by a client in any request component shall never be used for authorization; the resolved tenant comes from the session token only. Supplying a mismatching value shall be logged as a security event. | P0 | SVC | 1 | Penetration test: altering a `tenant_id` in a request body changes nothing and raises an event. |
| SUR-FRQ-037 | Every read of a single object by ID shall perform an object-level authorization check; a caller requesting an out-of-scope ID shall receive **404 Not Found**, never 403, so that existence is not disclosed. | P0 | SVC | 1 | Requesting another tenant's known invoice ID returns 404 with no timing distinguishability beyond 50 ms. |
| SUR-FRQ-038 | File and media storage shall be tenant-prefixed, private by default, and served only through short-lived pre-signed URLs issued after authorization; direct object URLs shall never be embedded in emails, notifications, or exported documents. | P0 | ALL | 1 | A pre-signed URL expires within 15 minutes; a copied URL fails after expiry; no bucket permits anonymous listing. |
| SUR-FRQ-039 | Enterprise tenants shall be offered per-tenant encryption keys for documents and exports, with key rotation and a documented key-destruction path on contract termination. | P2 | AGN | 3 | Key rotation re-encrypts new writes and leaves old objects readable; destruction renders objects unrecoverable. |
| SUR-FRQ-040 | Tenant-specific settings shall be a first-class, versioned configuration object covering: branding (logo, colours within brand-safe bounds), locale defaults, working-week and holiday calendar, shift templates, overtime and attendance rules, approval chains, notification preferences, numbering series (invoice/quotation), rounding rules, and data-retention overrides within policy limits. | P1 | AGN, AAP | 2 | Changing a setting takes effect within 60 s across web and app, is versioned, and is attributed to an actor. |
| SUR-FRQ-041 | Feature flags shall support four scopes evaluated in order: global → plan → tenant → user; a tenant-level flag shall never grant a capability the tenant's plan does not include. | P0 | ALL | 1 | Enabling a Professional-only flag on a Starter tenant has no effect and logs a rejected-grant event. |
| SUR-FRQ-042 | Subscription entitlements shall be enforced server-side at the API boundary, not by hiding UI. Every entitlement check shall be expressed as a named capability (e.g. `tenders.discover`, `payroll.run`, `migration.ocr`) mapped to plans per canon §1.4. | P0 | AGN, AAP, TRN | 2 | Calling a Professional endpoint with a Starter token returns 402/403 with an upgrade-path payload, not data. |
| SUR-FRQ-043 | Entitlement limits (guards, users, sites, storage, AI interactions) shall be metered continuously with soft-cap warnings at 80% and 100%, and a defined over-limit behaviour per limit type — never silent data loss. `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-003]` for the numeric limits. | P0 | AGN | 2 | Reaching 100% of the guard limit blocks new guard creation with a clear message and does not disable existing guards. |
| SUR-FRQ-044 | Every state-changing action shall write an Audit Log entry containing: actor identity, active role, tenant, branch scope, action, target entity type + ID, before/after diff, timestamp (server), request IP, device ID, session ID, and correlation ID; AI-originated actions additionally carry the AI Interaction ID. | P0 | ALL | 1 | A random sample of 50 state changes across products shows a complete audit entry for each. |
| SUR-FRQ-045 | Audit logs shall be append-only, tenant-scoped for tenant visibility, retained per §39, and never editable by any role including Super Admin; corrections are new entries. | P0 | SVC | 1 | An attempt to update or delete an audit row fails at the database level. |
| SUR-FRQ-046 | A tenant admin shall be able to read their own tenant's audit log, filter it, and export it; Suraksha roles shall see cross-tenant audit only where §31 grants it, and every such cross-tenant read shall itself be audited. | P1 | AGN, OPS | 2 | Reading another tenant's audit log creates an audit entry visible to that tenant (see SUR-FRQ-047). |
| SUR-FRQ-047 | Suraksha access to a tenant's operational data shall be surfaced to that tenant: a "Suraksha access log" in the Agency Portal listing every impersonation and every support-purposed read of tenant data, with actor role, reason and duration. | P1 | AGN, OPS | 2 | Every impersonation session appears in the tenant-visible log within 5 minutes with a reason string. |
| SUR-FRQ-048 | Tenant deletion / churn shall follow a defined lifecycle — Active → Past due → Suspended (read-only) → Archived → Export window (30 days) → Purge per retention policy — with a self-service full export before purge. | P1 | AGN, OPS | 2 | A churned tenant can download a complete export for 30 days; after purge, only financial records required by §40 remain. |
| SUR-FRQ-049 | Cross-tenant isolation shall be verified by an automated test suite that runs on every build: for each tenant-owned entity type, a probe attempts read, list, search, count, export, notification retrieval and AI query as tenant B against tenant A's data and must fail on all seven. | P0 | SVC | 1 | The isolation suite is a required CI gate; a single failure blocks deploy. |
| SUR-FRQ-050 | Noisy-neighbour protection shall be applied per tenant: API rate limits, background-job concurrency caps, export queue fairness, and per-tenant query timeouts, so that one tenant's bulk operation cannot degrade another's real-time surface. | P1 | SVC | 2 | A tenant running a 100k-row export does not raise p95 latency for other tenants above the §46 threshold. |

#### 26.2.2 What is Marketplace-Public and what is never shared

| Data class | Visible to other tenants? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Agency profile: name, logo, districts served, licence state/district + validity status (not the document), services offered, verified badge, marketplace rating, response-time band, years active | Yes — public on TRN | This is the marketplace product (§19). Published deliberately, controlled by the agency. |
| Guard roster, attendance, GPS tracks, payroll, salary, documents, disciplinary records | Never | Not even in aggregate, not even anonymised, not even to Suraksha's guarding arm for competitive use (R-104). |
| Client list, contracts, rates, invoices, quotations, tenders bid on | Never | Rate leakage is the most commercially damaging leak. |
| Incidents, SOS events, patrol logs, wake checks | Never | Except where an incident is jointly owned (Suraksha-routed booking), in which case both parties see only that incident. |
| Aggregate market benchmarks (e.g. "median guard attrition in Jaipur") | Yes, only as k-anonymised statistics with k ≥ 10 tenants and ≥ 50 subjects, no tenant identifiable, opt-out available | §42 owns the methodology; a benchmark that could be reverse-engineered to a single tenant must not be published. |
| Reviews left by clients on an agency | Yes, as published on TRN | Moderated (§26.8.7); the reviewer's identity is shown per §19 rules. |

#### 26.2.3 Enforcement at the AI-retrieval layer

Because §25 permits natural-language questions over operational data, the AI layer is the newest and most fragile isolation surface. Four requirements are specific to it and are restated here as functional obligations, with governance owned by §41:

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Products affected | Phase | Acceptance summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SUR-FRQ-051 | Vector and keyword indexes used by AI retrieval shall be physically partitioned per tenant (separate namespace/collection), not logically filtered within a shared index. | P0 | AI | 2 | Deleting a tenant's namespace removes all of its retrievable content and nothing else. |
| SUR-FRQ-052 | Retrieval shall apply the caller's full permission scope (tenant + branch + role + record-level ACL), so a Branch Manager's question cannot surface another branch's data even inside their own tenant. | P0 | AI | 2 | A branch-scoped user asking "show me the highest paid guard" receives an answer computed only over their branch. |
| SUR-FRQ-053 | Content extracted from uploaded documents shall be treated as untrusted input and shall never be interpreted as instructions; a document containing prompt-injection text shall not alter tool selection or scope. | P0 | AI | 2 | Red-team corpus of injection payloads produces zero scope escalations in CI. |
| SUR-FRQ-054 | Every AI answer shall pass a post-generation entity check that verifies each referenced entity ID is within the caller's scope; a failed check suppresses the answer and raises a P1 security alert rather than redacting silently. | P0 | AI | 2 | Injected out-of-scope IDs cause suppression and an alert, not a partial answer. |

### 26.3 Global search

#### 26.3.1 Purpose and scope

One search box, present on every authenticated surface, that finds any record the user is allowed to see across **Guard, Agency, Client, Site, Post, Booking, Quotation, Contract, Invoice, Payment, Incident, Tender, Bid, Ticket, Document, Employee, Roster/Shift**. Its behaviour differs by product only in which entity types are enabled and how results are ranked, never in its permission semantics.

#### 26.3.2 The hard rule

> **SUR-FRQ-055 (Search Non-Disclosure Rule).** A user shall never learn of the existence of a record they cannot access — not through a result, a suggestion, an autocomplete entry, a facet count, a "no results in this tenant but 4 elsewhere" hint, a spelling correction derived from out-of-scope terms, a differing error message, or a measurable timing difference. Permission filtering is applied at query construction, before ranking, before counting, before suggestion generation.

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Products affected | Phase | Acceptance summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SUR-FRQ-056 | The search index shall be sharded by tenant with the tenant filter applied as a routing key; a query shall never be executed against another tenant's shard. | P0 | SVC | 1 | Query traces show a single-shard fan-out for tenant-scoped searches. |
| SUR-FRQ-057 | Record-level ACLs (branch scope, role scope, record ownership, client-visibility flags) shall be stored **on the indexed document** as filterable terms, so filtering happens in the engine rather than in application post-processing. | P0 | SVC | 1 | Removing application-side filtering in a test still yields correctly scoped results. |
| SUR-FRQ-058 | Autocomplete/type-ahead shall be generated from the caller's permitted document set only; the suggestion dictionary shall be scope-filtered, not global. | P0 | ALL | 1 | Typing the first three letters of an out-of-scope client name yields no suggestion. |
| SUR-FRQ-059 | Result counts, facet counts and "showing 1–20 of N" shall be computed post-filter; N shall never include inaccessible records. | P0 | ALL | 1 | Facet counts sum exactly to the visible result set. |
| SUR-FRQ-060 | A search for an identifier the user cannot access shall return the ordinary empty state — identical copy and identical latency profile to a search that genuinely matches nothing. | P0 | ALL | 1 | Timing analysis over 1,000 paired queries shows <50 ms mean difference. |
| SUR-FRQ-061 | Indexing shall be near-real-time: a created or updated record shall be searchable within 5 s (P95) and a permission change shall take effect within 30 s (P95); deletions/archival shall be removed within 5 s. | P1 | SVC | 1 | Measured in staging with synthetic load equal to 2× projected peak. |
| SUR-FRQ-062 | A permission revocation shall be applied to search results defensively: if the ACL cache is stale, the result is suppressed rather than shown, and a re-check is forced. | P0 | SVC | 1 | Revoking access and immediately searching returns no result. |
| SUR-FRQ-063 | Search shall support Indian-language name matching: transliteration between Devanagari and Latin, common name variants (Mohd/Mohammad/Muhammad; Kumar/Kr.), phonetic matching, and tolerance of 1–2 character typos on names ≥5 characters. | P1 | ALL | 2 | "Mohd Aslam", "Mohammed Aslam" and "मोहम्मद असलम" all find the same guard. |
| SUR-FRQ-064 | Search shall support exact-identifier matching that short-circuits ranking: mobile number (with/without +91), guard ID, employee code, invoice number, booking reference, GSTIN, PAN, licence number, vehicle number, Aadhaar last-4 (never full). An exact identifier match is always result #1. | P0 | ALL | 1 | Pasting an invoice number opens a single-result state with a direct "Open" action. |
| SUR-FRQ-065 | Ranking shall combine: exact-identifier match (highest), field weight (name > code > address > notes), recency, entity-type priority per product context, user's own recent interactions, and record status (Active ranked above Archived; Archived shown only when the user opts in via filter). | P1 | ALL | 2 | On OPS, searching a common surname ranks Active guards in the user's scope above Archived ones. |
| SUR-FRQ-066 | Filters shall include: entity type, status (canon vocabulary), date range, branch, city/state, assigned-to, and tenant (Suraksha roles only, within their §31 scope). Filters shall be URL-addressable so a filtered search is shareable — and the recipient's own permissions re-apply on open. | P1 | ALL | 2 | Sharing a filtered URL with a lower-privileged colleague shows fewer results, never an error revealing what was hidden. |
| SUR-FRQ-067 | Keyboard behaviour shall be standard across surfaces: `/` or `Ctrl/Cmd+K` opens search; typing filters; `↑/↓` moves; `Enter` opens; `Cmd/Ctrl+Enter` opens in a new tab; `Tab` cycles entity-type groups; `Esc` closes and restores focus to the prior element. | P1 | WEB, CPT, TRN, AGN, OPS | 2 | Full flow completable without a mouse; focus returns correctly on close. |
| SUR-FRQ-068 | Search results shall be grouped by entity type with at most 5 per group in the overlay and a "See all N in Guards" link to a full results page; the overlay shall render first results within 200 ms (P75) of the third keystroke. | P1 | ALL | 2 | Measured on a mid-range Android device on 4G. |
| SUR-FRQ-069 | Each result row shall show: entity icon, primary label, a disambiguating secondary line (e.g. guard: employee code · site · status), a status pill (§27.3.6), and a right-aligned context hint (branch or city). No result row shall show a field the user cannot see on the record itself. | P1 | ALL | 2 | A client user searching a site never sees the guard's phone number in the result line. |
| SUR-FRQ-070 | Search queries shall be logged (query text hashed for privacy where it may contain personal data, plus entity types clicked and result position) for relevance tuning; logs are tenant-scoped and never used to train cross-tenant models. | P1 | SVC | 2 | Query logs carry `tenant_id` and are excluded from any cross-tenant training pipeline. |
| SUR-FRQ-071 | Global search on GAP shall be reduced deliberately: guards search only their own site, post, roster, colleagues on shift and their own documents — a full-entity search box is not offered on the field app. | P1 | GAP | 2 | The Guard App search returns only the five permitted classes. |
| SUR-FRQ-072 | Zero-result states shall offer a productive next step appropriate to role and query shape (e.g. "No guard matches 98XXXXXX21. Add a guard" for a recruiter; "Check the spelling or try the employee code" for a viewer) and shall never suggest that the record might exist elsewhere. | P1 | ALL | 2 | Copy review confirms no zero-result string implies out-of-scope existence. |

#### 26.3.3 Indexing model

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Engine stance | A dedicated search engine (inverted index + filters), fed asynchronously from the transactional store via the event bus. Not database `LIKE` queries. `[RECOMMENDED]` |
| Document per entity | One denormalised search document per entity instance, containing display fields, searchable text, identifiers, ACL terms (`tenant_id`, `branch_ids[]`, `role_scopes[]`, `visibility_flags[]`), status, and timestamps. |
| Update path | Entity change event → indexer → upsert. A failed index write retries with backoff and raises a P2 alert after 3 failures; the record remains findable via a fallback direct-database lookup on exact identifier. |
| Reindex | Full reindex must be runnable per tenant and per entity type without downtime, using an alias swap. |
| Sensitive fields | Aadhaar, full bank account, and full document numbers are never indexed as searchable text; only last-4 tokens where §39 permits. |
| Attachment text | OCR-extracted document text is indexed into a separate field with its own ACL term so that document-content search can be disabled per tenant. |

---

### 26.4 Workflow automation & rule engine

#### 26.4.1 Model

The rule engine is one service used by every product. A **Rule** is:

```
WHEN  <trigger>
IF    <conditions>          (all must hold; groups support AND/OR, max depth 3)
THEN  <action sequence>     (ordered; each step may WAIT, ESCALATE, or ACT)
UNTIL <stop conditions>     (any one halts the remaining sequence)
```

| Concept | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger types | **Event** (something happened: `attendance.missing`, `sos.raised`, `invoice.issued`); **Schedule** (cron-like, tenant timezone); **Threshold** (a metric crosses a value, evaluated every 5 min); **Temporal** (a date field is N days away/past — the licence/document/contract family); **Manual** (a human fires it from a record). |
| Conditions | Field comparisons on the triggering entity and one hop of related entities; time-of-day and day-of-week windows; scope filters (branch, site, client tier, plan); "has happened / has not happened in the last N minutes" predicates; entitlement checks. |
| Actions | Notify (channel-aware, §36) · Create Task · Create Ticket (§26.7) · Change status · Assign · Escalate to role/person · Call webhook · Write audit note · Start another Rule · Ask for approval (§29) · Update a field (whitelisted fields only) · Add to a queue. |
| Wait | `WAIT <duration>` or `WAIT UNTIL <condition or clock time>`; the engine must survive restarts (durable timers), and a wait resumes correctly after downtime with a recorded "delayed by" figure. |
| Escalation | An ordered ladder of recipients with per-step timeouts; each step names a role (resolved at fire time to the on-duty holder) or a named person, and a channel set. |
| Stop conditions | The event that the rule exists to prevent has occurred (e.g. attendance marked, payment received), a human acknowledged, the entity moved to a terminal status, quiet hours suppression (except P0/P1), or the rule was manually stopped. |
| Idempotency | Every rule instance has a dedup key (`rule_id + entity_id + trigger_window`). Re-delivery of the same trigger does not create a second instance. |
| Safety | A rule may never perform an action the triggering tenant's plan does not entitle, may never cross a tenant boundary, and may never execute an action class that §25 reserves for humans (payments, payroll, permissions, terminations, compliance status). |

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Products affected | Phase | Acceptance summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SUR-FRQ-073 | A single rule engine service shall serve all products; per-product rules differ by content, never by mechanism. | P0 | SVC | 1 | One deployment; rules for OPS and AGN are rows in the same store with different tenant scopes. |
| SUR-FRQ-074 | Rules shall be tenant-scoped, with a set of **system rules** owned by Suraksha that tenants can enable/disable and parameterise but not delete, and **tenant rules** authored by the tenant. | P0 | AGN, OPS | 2 | Disabling a safety-critical system rule requires an authorised role and records a reason. |
| SUR-FRQ-075 | Rule execution shall be durable and exactly-once per dedup key; timers shall survive process restart; a delayed execution shall record actual vs intended fire time. | P0 | SVC | 2 | Killing the worker mid-wait resumes the wait on restart without duplicate notifications. |
| SUR-FRQ-076 | Every rule execution shall write a trace: rule version, trigger payload, condition evaluation results (per condition, true/false), actions attempted, delivery outcomes, stop reason. Traces are retained 12 months and visible to the tenant. | P0 | AGN, OPS | 2 | A user can answer "why did I get this alert?" and "why didn't I?" from the trace UI. |
| SUR-FRQ-077 | Rules shall be versioned; editing a live rule creates a new version, and in-flight instances complete on the version they started with. | P1 | AGN, OPS | 2 | An in-flight escalation is not re-pathed by a mid-flight edit. |
| SUR-FRQ-078 | The authoring UI shall offer three modes: **Template** (pick a packaged rule, fill parameters), **Builder** (visual trigger/condition/action editor), and **Advanced** (condition expression editor) — with Builder as the default and Advanced gated to Agency Admin and above. | P1 | AGN, OPS | 2 | A Branch Manager can create a template rule in under 2 minutes without training. |
| SUR-FRQ-079 | The authoring UI shall include a **dry run** that evaluates the rule against the last 30 days of real data and reports how many times it would have fired, against which entities, and how many notifications it would have sent. | P1 | AGN, OPS | 2 | Dry run completes in <30 s for a tenant with 1,000 guards and shows a per-day fire count. |
| SUR-FRQ-080 | The engine shall enforce anti-storm controls: per-rule max fires per hour, per-recipient max notifications per hour with digesting above it, and automatic rule quarantine (paused + P1 alert to the author) if a rule exceeds 10× its dry-run projection. | P0 | SVC | 2 | A misconfigured rule pauses itself rather than sending 5,000 SMS. |
| SUR-FRQ-081 | Rules shall respect quiet hours configured per tenant and per recipient, except for severity P0 and P1, which always deliver. | P0 | SVC | 2 | A P2 rule firing at 02:00 queues to 07:00; a P0 delivers immediately. |
| SUR-FRQ-082 | Escalation ladders shall resolve roles to people at fire time using the current roster/on-call table, and shall skip a step whose recipient is unavailable while recording the skip. | P0 | SVC | 2 | With the Field Officer off-duty, escalation moves to Operations Manager and the trace shows "skipped: off duty". |
| SUR-FRQ-083 | Rule actions that modify data shall be restricted to a whitelist of safe fields and statuses; no rule shall be able to approve a payment, change a permission, alter a compliance status, terminate an employment, or delete a record. | P0 | SVC | 2 | Attempting to build such a rule is impossible in the UI and rejected by the API. |
| SUR-FRQ-084 | Each rule shall carry an owner (a person, not a role) who receives failure notifications, and shall be reviewed at least annually with a "last reviewed" date shown in the list. | P2 | AGN, OPS | 3 | Rules unreviewed for 12 months are flagged in the rule list. |

#### 26.4.2 The twelve specified rules

These are packaged **system rules**. Parameters in `{braces}` are tenant-configurable within the stated bounds. Severities use the canon alert vocabulary. Workflow choreography beyond the rule itself is owned by §29.

**R1 — Guard absent after shift start**

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Temporal: `shift.start_time + {15} minutes` reached (bounds 5–30) with no Attendance record of type check-in for the Assignment. |
| Conditions | Assignment status = Active; shift not cancelled; guard not on approved leave; post not marked closed; site is not in a declared holiday state; no replacement already assigned. |
| Action sequence | T+0: push + SMS to guard — "Aap {site} par duty par nahi dikhe. Abhi check-in karein." · T+3 min: push + call-to-supervisor task; alert Supervisor (P2). · T+8 min: notify Field Officer + Operations Manager (P1); create "Unstaffed post risk" item in the ops queue. · T+15 min: escalate to Branch Manager; open Replacement request automatically (§20); mark post `At risk` on the live board. · T+30 min: notify the client contact **only if** the contract's client-notification flag is on; raise P1 in Command Center for Suraksha-operated sites. |
| Recipients | Guard → Supervisor → Field Officer + Operations Manager → Branch Manager → (conditional) Client, Command Center. |
| Stop conditions | Check-in recorded · replacement checked in · shift cancelled · supervisor marks "guard present, device issue" (which itself logs a manual-attendance exception, §26.8.5) · leave approved retroactively. |
| Severity | P2 → P1 at T+8 → P1 sustained at T+30 for client-notified sites. |

**R2 — Agency PSARA licence expiry**

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Temporal on `licence.valid_to`: T-90, T-60, T-30, T-15, T-7, T-3, T-1, T-0, T+1, T+7 days. |
| Conditions | Licence status ∈ {Active, Expiring}; agency status = Active; renewal document not already uploaded and Verified. |
| Action sequence | T-90 to T-15: email + in-app to Agency Owner and Agency Compliance, with a "Start renewal" deep link. · T-30: licence status → `Expiring`; badge changes on the Trinetra profile (§19). · T-7: add SMS; notify Suraksha Verification. · T-0: status → `Expired`; apply BR-002 configured operational restrictions; suppress the agency from marketplace search; block new bid submissions for the affected geography. · T+1: notify all clients with active contracts served under that licence geography, using the configured wording. · T+7: escalate to Suraksha Compliance for account review. |
| Recipients | Agency Owner, Agency Compliance, Suraksha Verification, Suraksha Compliance, affected Clients (T+1 only). |
| Stop conditions | Renewed licence uploaded **and** Verified (not merely uploaded) · agency archived. |
| Severity | P3 → P2 at T-30 → P1 at T-7 → P0 at T-0. |
| Note | The platform never states a legal consequence; it applies the configured jurisdiction rule (canon §0). |

**R3 — Payment overdue (client invoice)**

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Temporal on `invoice.due_date` + `{0}` days, then a dunning schedule at D+1, D+3, D+7, D+15, D+30, D+45. |
| Conditions | Invoice status ∈ {Pending, Partially paid}; amount outstanding > `{₹1,000}`; client not in an approved dispute (§26.7.6); no active payment plan. |
| Action sequence | D+1: email + WhatsApp to the billing contact with the invoice PDF and a pay link. · D+3: add SMS; notify the account owner (Sales). · D+7: notify Client Finance role and the Suraksha/agency Finance role; apply late-fee flag if the contract defines one. · D+15: P1 to Finance; contract flagged `Payment risk` on the account. · D+30: escalate to Operations for a service-continuity decision — a decision request, never an automatic service stop. · D+45: escalate to management; recommend legal/collection path as a task. |
| Recipients | Billing contact → Sales owner → Finance → Operations → Management. |
| Stop conditions | Payment received (full or agreed part) · dispute raised and accepted · payment plan approved · invoice cancelled/credit-noted. |
| Severity | P3 → P2 (D+7) → P1 (D+15). |
| Hard rule | Service suspension for non-payment is **never** an automated action. It is an approval-required decision (canon §1.7 class 3). |

**R4 — Guard document expiry**

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Temporal on any Document with an expiry: T-60, T-30, T-15, T-7, T-1, T-0, T+3 for document types {Police verification, Medical fitness, Training certificate, Driving licence, Arms licence, ID proof with expiry, PSARA guard training}. |
| Conditions | Guard status = Active; document status ∈ {Verified, Expiring}; no newer version already Verified. |
| Action sequence | T-60/T-30: push + in-app to the guard in their chosen language, with a one-tap "Upload now" that opens the camera (§18). · T-15: notify Supervisor and Agency HR. · T-7: notify Agency Compliance; guard flagged `Document expiring` on rosters. · T-0: document status → `Expired`; guard compliance state degrades; **if** the document type is deployment-blocking per tenant configuration, the guard is excluded from future roster publishing (existing shifts are flagged for review, not cancelled automatically). · T+3: escalate to Branch Manager with a list of affected posts. |
| Recipients | Guard → Supervisor + Agency HR → Agency Compliance → Branch Manager. |
| Stop conditions | New document uploaded **and** Verified · guard archived · document type de-configured as required. |
| Severity | P3 → P2 (T-7) → P1 (T-0 for deployment-blocking types). |

**R5 — Tender deadline approaching**

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Temporal on `tender.submission_deadline`: T-14, T-7, T-3, T-2, T-1 days, T-6 h, T-2 h. |
| Conditions | Tender status ∈ {Tracking, Bid in progress}; agency has the `tenders.discover` entitlement (Professional+); bid not yet submitted; tender not marked "Not bidding". |
| Action sequence | T-14: in-app + email to Agency Sales with a readiness checklist (documents, EMD, turnover proof, licence geography match). · T-7: flag missing checklist items explicitly. · T-3: SMS added; notify Agency Owner. · T-1: P1 in-app + call task for the Sales owner. · T-6 h: P1 to Agency Owner with "Submit or mark not bidding". · T-2 h: final alert; auto-create a decision task that must be closed with a reason. |
| Recipients | Agency Sales owner → Agency Owner. |
| Stop conditions | Bid submitted · marked "Not bidding" with reason · tender cancelled/withdrawn at source · deadline passed (rule closes with a missed-deadline record for analytics). |
| Severity | P3 → P2 (T-3) → P1 (T-1). |
| Note | Tender source data availability is constrained by A-145; the rule fires on whatever record exists, manual or ingested. |

**R6 — Missed patrol checkpoint**

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Temporal: patrol round's scheduled checkpoint window closes (`scheduled_time + {10} min`, bounds 5–20) with no Checkpoint scan recorded. |
| Conditions | Patrol schedule Active; guard checked in; site not in an alarm state that legitimately halts patrols; checkpoint not marked out-of-service. |
| Action sequence | T+0: push to guard — "Checkpoint {name} scan pending." · T+5 min: notify Supervisor (P2) with the guard's last known location and the missed checkpoint on the site map. · T+15 min: escalate to Field Officer; mark the patrol round `Incomplete`. · If **two consecutive** checkpoints are missed: raise P1, treat as a welfare concern, trigger a supervisor call attempt and, for Suraksha-operated sites, notify Command Center. · Daily: include in the site's patrol-compliance figure. |
| Recipients | Guard → Supervisor → Field Officer → (2 consecutive) Command Center. |
| Stop conditions | Scan recorded (late scans are accepted and marked late) · round cancelled · guard raised a legitimate incident that explains the deviation · checkpoint marked faulty. |
| Severity | P3 → P2 (T+5) → P1 (two consecutive). |

**R7 — Missed night wake check**

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Event: wake-check prompt issued (per §18 night schedule) and no response within `{120}` seconds (bounds 60–300). |
| Conditions | Shift is a night shift with wake-checks enabled; guard checked in; device last seen within `{30}` minutes. |
| Action sequence | T+0: repeat prompt with escalating alert tone and vibration, bypassing silent mode where the platform permits (A-146). · T+2 min: second prompt + push to Supervisor (P2). · T+4 min: automated voice call to the guard's number. · T+6 min: P1 to Field Officer and, for Suraksha-operated sites, Command Center; operator initiates a call per §24. · T+10 min: treat as a potential welfare incident — open an Incident record, notify Branch Manager, dispatch the nearest supervisor if one is configured. |
| Recipients | Guard → Supervisor → Field Officer → Command Center → Branch Manager. |
| Stop conditions | Wake check acknowledged · guard answers a call and is confirmed alert · supervisor confirms on site · incident opened and owned. |
| Severity | P2 → P1 (T+6). |
| Design note | This rule must never assume malice; a missed wake check is treated first as a possible medical or safety event (§24), and the copy the guard sees is supportive, never punitive. |

**R8 — SOS raised**

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Event: `sos.raised` from GAP (button, hardware key sequence, or voice trigger). |
| Conditions | None. An SOS is never conditioned away. Duplicate SOS from the same guard within 60 s is de-duplicated into one case with a repeat counter. |
| Action sequence | T+0 (target <5 s): P0 case opens in Command Center with live location, guard profile, site profile, contract escalation contacts, and audio/photo stream if captured; simultaneous push to Supervisor and Field Officer; loud alert on all Command Center consoles. · T+30 s: if no operator has acknowledged, alert every available operator plus the shift lead. · T+60 s: alert Operations Manager. · T+2 min: alert Branch Manager and, per contract flag or tier, the client contact (D-143). · Operator actions (calls to guard, supervisor, client, emergency services) are human-initiated and logged (§24). |
| Recipients | Command Center (all consoles) · Supervisor · Field Officer · Operations Manager · Branch Manager · Client (per contract). |
| Stop conditions | Only an authorised human closure with a recorded outcome. An SOS case never auto-closes, never times out, and is never closed by the guard alone. |
| Severity | P0, non-degradable. |
| Cross-ref | Full mechanics in §24; this rule row exists only to place SOS in the same engine and prove the ladder is uniform. |

**R9 — Agency subscription invoice overdue**

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Temporal on subscription invoice `due_date`: D+0, D+3, D+7, D+10, D+14, D+21. |
| Conditions | Subscription status = Active; auto-pay failed or absent; balance > 0. |
| Action sequence | D+0: in-app banner + email to Agency Owner with a pay link; retry auto-pay. · D+3: second auto-pay retry; SMS added. · D+7: subscription flagged `Past due`; non-critical features (marketing tools, tender discovery, advanced analytics) begin degradation warnings. · D+10: third retry; notify Suraksha Sales owner. · D+14: subscription → `Suspended` = **read-only tenant** — all data visible and exportable, no writes. Safety-critical read paths (live tracking view, SOS receipt) remain available so that a billing dispute never endangers a guard. · D+21: escalate to Suraksha Finance for a commercial decision. |
| Recipients | Agency Owner, Agency Finance, Suraksha Sales, Suraksha Finance. |
| Stop conditions | Payment succeeds · a payment plan is approved · the account is closed by agreement. |
| Severity | P3 → P2 (D+7) → P1 (D+14). |
| Hard rule | Suspension never deletes data and never disables SOS reception or the ability to export. |

**R10 — Contract renewal approaching**

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Temporal on `contract.end_date`: T-90, T-60, T-45, T-30, T-15, T-7, T-0, T+7. |
| Conditions | Contract status = Active; auto-renew flag off, or on but with a rate revision due; client not in termination notice. |
| Action sequence | T-90: task to the account owner with a renewal pack (service performance summary, attendance %, incident count, SLA credits, current vs proposed rate). · T-60: schedule a client review meeting task. · T-45: prompt for a rate proposal; if a statutory wage revision is configured as effective in the period, surface it as an input to the proposal (never as an automatic price change). · T-30: notify Operations to plan continuity; notify Finance for billing setup. · T-15: P2 if no renewal document exists. · T-7: P1 to Branch Manager and account owner. · T-0: contract → `Expiring` then `Expired` per the configured grace; deployment continuity requires an explicit extension record. · T+7: escalate to management with a churn record. |
| Recipients | Account owner → Operations → Finance → Branch Manager → Management. |
| Stop conditions | Renewal signed · extension recorded · client confirms non-renewal (creates an offboarding workflow) · contract terminated. |
| Severity | P3 → P2 (T-15) → P1 (T-7). |

**R11 — Training / certification expiry**

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Temporal on `training_record.valid_to`: T-45, T-30, T-14, T-7, T-0, T+7 for training types configured as mandatory (induction refresher, fire safety, first aid, armed-weapons refresher, site-specific induction). |
| Conditions | Guard Active; training type mandatory for the guard's role or for the site they are assigned to; no newer completion recorded. |
| Action sequence | T-45: notify guard + Agency HR; if e-learning modules exist, deep-link the module. · T-30: HR schedules a session; create a batch-scheduling suggestion grouping all guards expiring in the same 30-day window at the same branch. · T-14: notify Supervisor; flag on roster. · T-7: notify Agency Compliance. · T-0: training status → `Expired`; if the assigned site requires that training, the guard is excluded from new assignments to that site and existing assignments are flagged for supervisor review. · T+7: escalate to Branch Manager with the count of affected posts. |
| Recipients | Guard → Agency HR → Supervisor → Agency Compliance → Branch Manager. |
| Stop conditions | Training completed and recorded · requirement waived by an authorised role with a reason · guard archived. |
| Severity | P3 → P2 (T-7) → P1 (T-0 where site-blocking). |

**R12 — Unstaffed post**

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trigger | Threshold, evaluated every 5 minutes: for an Active Post in a live shift window, `checked_in_guards < required_guards`. |
| Conditions | Post Active; shift window open; site not closed; the gap is not explained by an approved variation (client-agreed reduced strength). |
| Action sequence | T+0: post shown `Understaffed` on the live board with the exact shortfall ("2 of 3"). · T+5 min: notify Supervisor and Field Officer (P1) with a ranked list of nearby available guards. · T+15 min: notify Operations Manager; auto-create a Replacement request; for Suraksha-operated sites, raise the post in Command Center. · T+30 min: notify Branch Manager; compute and display the billing implication (deduction exposure) for the shift. · T+60 min: notify the client if the contract's notification flag is on; flag the shift for SLA credit review in billing (§35). |
| Recipients | Supervisor + Field Officer → Operations Manager → Branch Manager → Client (conditional) → Finance (billing flag). |
| Stop conditions | Required strength met · client-approved variation recorded · shift ends (rule closes and writes an unstaffed-minutes figure to the SLA record). |
| Severity | P1 from T+5; P0 if the post is classified life-safety-critical (armed post, hospital, critical infrastructure) and the shortfall persists 30 minutes. |

#### 26.4.3 Additional packaged rules (specified more briefly)

| Rule | Trigger | Key actions | Stop |
|---|---|---|---|
| R13 Geofence breach on duty | Guard location outside site geofence + `{200}` m for >`{5}` min during a shift | Guard prompt → Supervisor P2 at 5 min → Field Officer P1 at 15 min → incident record at 30 min | Guard returns inside · authorised off-site task recorded |
| R14 Attendance anomaly cluster | ≥3 guards at one site check in within 60 s from the same device fingerprint or within 10 m of each other | Freeze auto-approval of that site's attendance for the day; P1 to Agency Compliance; open a fraud case (§26.8.5) | Compliance closes the case with a finding |
| R15 Payroll run not approved | Payroll cut-off date reached, run status ≠ Approved, T-3/T-1/T-0 to the salary date | Notify Payroll → Agency Finance → Agency Owner; P1 at T-1 | Run approved · run cancelled with reason |
| R16 Verification queue SLA breach | Document/agency verification pending > `{48}` h | Notify Verification lead; re-prioritise the item; P1 at 72 h | Item decided |
| R17 Guard salary not credited | Salary date + `{2}` days with payout status ≠ Success | Notify Payroll + Agency Finance (P1); inform the guard with a status message; open a Ticket automatically | Payout success recorded · dispute resolved |
| R18 Client SLA breach threshold | Monthly attendance % below the contract threshold, evaluated daily on rolling month-to-date | Notify Operations at 3 points below, Branch Manager at 5 points, Finance for credit calculation at month end | Metric recovers · credit issued |
| R19 Device offline on duty | Guard App last heartbeat older than `{20}` min during a shift | Guard push (may not deliver) → Supervisor P2 → Field Officer P1 at 45 min → treat as attendance risk | Heartbeat resumes · supervisor confirms guard present |
| R20 Bid outcome not recorded | Tender result date + 7 days with bid status still `Submitted` | Task to Agency Sales to record outcome; P2 after 14 days | Outcome recorded |

### 26.5 Document management

One document service for every product. A Document is always attached to an owning entity (Guard, Agency, Client, Site, Contract, Invoice, Incident, Ticket, Tender, Training, Payroll run) and inherits that entity's tenant.

#### 26.5.1 Status lifecycle

```
Draft ──▶ Pending ──▶ Verified ──▶ Expiring ──▶ Expired
             │             │                        │
             ├──▶ Rejected │                        └──▶ (new version) Pending
             │             └──▶ Suspended (integrity concern)
             └──▶ Cancelled            │
                                       └──▶ Archived
```

| Status | Meaning | Who sets it |
|---|---|---|
| Draft | Uploaded but not submitted (e.g. multi-page set incomplete) | Uploader |
| Pending | Submitted, awaiting verification | System on submit |
| Verified | A human verifier confirmed authenticity and data match | Verification role |
| Rejected | Failed verification; a reason code and free-text reason are mandatory | Verification role |
| Expiring | Within the configured pre-expiry window (default 30 days) | System (R4) |
| Expired | Past `valid_to` | System |
| Suspended | Verified previously, now under integrity investigation (§26.8.8) | Compliance / Fraud |
| Cancelled | Withdrawn by the uploader before verification | Uploader |
| Archived | Superseded by a newer version, or entity archived | System |

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Products affected | Phase | Acceptance summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SUR-FRQ-085 | A single document service shall handle upload, storage, versioning, preview, verification, expiry and secure retrieval for all products. | P0 | ALL | 1 | One API; per-product differences are configuration, not code. |
| SUR-FRQ-086 | Supported types shall be PDF, JPG, PNG, HEIC, WEBP, DOCX, XLSX, CSV; max 25 MB per file for documents and 100 MB for migration data files; max 20 files per upload batch. Type is validated by content sniffing, never by extension. | P0 | ALL | 1 | A renamed executable is rejected; a valid HEIC from an iPhone is accepted and converted for preview. |
| SUR-FRQ-087 | Every upload shall pass a malware scan before becoming retrievable; a file that fails is quarantined, the uploader is told plainly, and a security event is raised. | P0 | SVC | 1 | EICAR test file is quarantined and never served. |
| SUR-FRQ-088 | Images captured on GAP shall be compressed client-side to ≤ 1600 px on the long edge and ≤ 500 KB before upload, with the original discarded on device after successful upload, and shall carry capture metadata (device time, server time, GPS, accuracy). | P0 | GAP | 2 | A 4 MB camera photo uploads as ≤500 KB over 3G within 20 s and retains its metadata. |
| SUR-FRQ-089 | Documents shall be versioned: a re-upload creates version n+1, prior versions remain retrievable to authorised roles, and the verification state does not carry over — a new version returns to Pending. | P0 | ALL | 1 | Uploading a renewed licence does not inherit the previous Verified state. |
| SUR-FRQ-090 | In-browser and in-app preview shall be available for PDF and images without download, using a rendered preview rather than the original file where the viewer's permission is view-only. | P1 | ALL | 2 | A view-only role cannot obtain the original bytes via developer tools. |
| SUR-FRQ-091 | Every document type shall have a schema: required metadata fields, whether an expiry date is required, whether verification is required, whether it is deployment-blocking on expiry, retention period, and the role set permitted to view it. | P0 | ALL | 1 | Adding a new document type is configuration, requiring no deploy. |
| SUR-FRQ-092 | OCR shall run automatically on upload for configured types (ID documents, licences, certificates, invoices) and shall populate a **suggestion** layer, never the record fields directly (see §26.6). | P1 | SVC | 2 | Extracted values appear as suggestions with confidence and a one-tap accept. |
| SUR-FRQ-093 | The verification queue shall be a shared work surface with: filters (type, tenant, age, priority, verifier), SLA countdown, side-by-side document and extracted-field view, one-click Verify, and Reject with a mandatory reason code + free text. | P0 | OPS | 1 | A verifier can process a standard guard ID in under 45 s. |
| SUR-FRQ-094 | Rejection reasons shall come from a controlled list (Illegible, Wrong document type, Expired, Name mismatch, Number mismatch, Suspected tampering, Incomplete pages, Duplicate, Other) plus mandatory free text, and shall be shown verbatim to the uploader with a "What to do next" instruction. | P0 | ALL | 1 | The uploader sees the reason and a corrective action, in their chosen language. |
| SUR-FRQ-095 | "Suspected tampering" shall never be shown verbatim to the uploader; it routes to Compliance and the uploader sees a neutral "We need to re-check this document" message. | P0 | OPS | 1 | Copy test confirms the tampering path does not tip off a bad actor. |
| SUR-FRQ-096 | Access control shall be per document type × role × relationship: e.g. an Agency HR sees their own guards' ID documents; a Client never sees a guard's ID document, bank details or address, only the deployment-relevant verification status. | P0 | ALL | 1 | A client attempting a guard document URL receives 404. |
| SUR-FRQ-097 | Every view, download, print-intent and share of a sensitive document shall be audited with actor, purpose (where a purpose is required), and timestamp; the owning subject can see who viewed their identity documents. | P0 | ALL | 2 | A guard can see "Agency HR viewed your Aadhaar on 12 Aug 2026". |
| SUR-FRQ-098 | Downloads shall be through short-lived pre-signed URLs; sensitive documents shall be watermarked on download with viewer name, timestamp and a case reference. | P1 | ALL | 2 | A downloaded PDF carries a visible and a metadata watermark. |
| SUR-FRQ-099 | Bulk upload shall be supported (drag a folder, or a ZIP) with per-file status, retry of failed items only, and a summary report; a partially failed batch never rolls back successful files but reports them clearly. | P1 | AGN, OPS | 2 | Uploading 200 files with 3 failures yields 197 stored and a retry action for 3. |
| SUR-FRQ-100 | Documents shall support search over metadata always, and over OCR-extracted text where the tenant has enabled content search (§26.3.3). | P2 | AGN, OPS | 3 | Content search can be disabled per tenant and the toggle is audited. |
| SUR-FRQ-101 | Identity-document numbers (Aadhaar, PAN, licence) shall be stored encrypted, displayed masked by default (last 4), and revealed only on an explicit action that is audited and rate-limited. | P0 | ALL | 1 | A user revealing 20 Aadhaar numbers in an hour triggers a P2 review. |
| SUR-FRQ-102 | Deletion shall be soft by default; a hard-delete path exists only for a documented privacy request (§39) and requires dual authorisation, leaving a tombstone in the audit log. | P0 | SVC | 2 | Hard delete requires two distinct approvers and is itself audited. |

### 26.6 OCR & legacy migration

#### 26.6.1 Why this exists

Most of India's ~35,000 PSARA agencies (A-001) run on paper registers, Excel sheets and WhatsApp. The single largest barrier to adopting Agency Portal is not price — it is the fear of re-typing three years of records. OCR-based legacy migration is therefore an **Enterprise plan** capability (canon §1.4) and a sales weapon, not a convenience feature. It is also the highest-risk feature in the platform, because a mis-mapped salary column corrupts payroll for a thousand people.

#### 26.6.2 The pipeline

| # | Stage | What happens | Failure handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Upload | Files or ZIP; supported: XLSX/XLS/CSV (structured), PDF (digital or scanned), JPG/PNG (photographed registers), DOCX. Batch metadata captured: source system, period covered, uploader, intended entity type. | Unsupported type rejected with an explicit list of what is accepted. |
| 2 | Security scan | Malware scan; macro-bearing Office files are stripped or rejected; ZIP bombs and path-traversal entries rejected; formula injection (`=`, `+`, `@` leading cells) neutralised. | Quarantine + security event + notify uploader. |
| 3 | Classification | Detect whether the file is structured (spreadsheet), semi-structured (digital PDF table), or unstructured (photo of a register). Route to the right parser. | Ambiguous → ask the human "what is this?" with a preview. |
| 4 | OCR / parse | Structured: direct parse. Digital PDF: text-layer table extraction. Scanned/photo: OCR with layout analysis, Devanagari + Latin, handwriting flagged as low-confidence by default. | Per-page confidence recorded; unreadable pages listed for re-scan with guidance ("photograph flat, in daylight"). |
| 5 | Column detection | Infer column semantics from headers, sample values and known patterns (10-digit mobile, IFSC shape, 12-digit Aadhaar, date formats DD/MM/YYYY vs DD-MM-YY, ₹ amounts, PSARA licence format). | Every inference carries a confidence; nothing below the threshold is auto-mapped. |
| 6 | Mapping | Human confirms/corrects a source→target field mapping in a dedicated UI (§26.6.4). Mappings are saved as reusable **templates** per source system. | Unmapped required target fields block progress with a named list. |
| 7 | Validation | Per-field format, range and referential validation (site exists, branch exists, role valid, joining date ≤ today, salary > 0, IFSC checksum, mobile 10-digit starting 6–9). Cross-row validation (duplicate employee codes, overlapping employment periods). | Errors and warnings separated; errors block that row, warnings do not. |
| 8 | Duplicate detection | Against existing tenant data and within the batch: exact match on mobile/Aadhaar-hash/employee code; fuzzy match on name + DOB + father's name + address locality, scored. | Three outcomes offered per duplicate: Skip, Merge (field-level chooser), Import as new (requires reason). |
| 9 | Preview | A full simulated import: counts by entity, sample of 25 rows rendered exactly as they will appear post-import, list of errors, warnings, duplicates and low-confidence fields, and a "what will change" diff for updates to existing records. | Preview is mandatory; there is no path from mapping to import that bypasses it. |
| 10 | Human approval | An authorised role (Agency Owner or Agency Admin; for Suraksha-assisted migrations additionally a Suraksha migration operator) explicitly approves. Approval is recorded with the exact preview hash. | No approval → nothing is written. |
| 11 | Import | Transactional per batch chunk (1,000 rows), idempotent, resumable, with a live progress view and a per-chunk commit so a mid-way failure leaves a consistent, reported state. | Failed chunk retried; unrecoverable chunk reported with row ranges. |
| 12 | Error report | Downloadable XLSX with original row number, original values, the error/warning, and the suggested fix — designed to be corrected and re-uploaded directly. | Re-upload of a corrected error file resumes into the same batch. |
| 13 | Audit + rollback | Every imported row is tagged with `import_batch_id`. A batch can be rolled back within `{7}` days if no dependent transaction (attendance, payroll, invoice) references the rows. | Rollback blocked with an explicit list of dependencies if any exist. |

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Products affected | Phase | Acceptance summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SUR-FRQ-103 | The migration pipeline shall implement all 13 stages above; no stage may be skipped by any user, including Suraksha staff running an assisted migration. | P0 | AGN, OPS | 3 | An attempt to call the import endpoint without an approved preview hash is rejected. |
| SUR-FRQ-104 | **(Confidence rule)** A value extracted by OCR with confidence below the field's threshold shall never be written to a critical field. Critical fields are: any money amount, bank account number, IFSC, Aadhaar/PAN, mobile number, date of birth, joining date, salary, licence number, licence validity date, and any field used in payroll or compliance. | P0 | AGN, OPS | 3 | Injecting a 0.72-confidence salary into the pipeline produces a mandatory human-review item, never an imported value. |
| SUR-FRQ-105 | Confidence thresholds shall be: ≥0.95 auto-accept for non-critical fields; ≥0.98 required to pre-fill (still human-confirmed) a critical field; 0.80–0.98 flagged for review; <0.80 treated as empty and always requires manual entry. Handwritten content caps at "review" regardless of reported confidence. | P0 | SVC | 3 | Threshold table is configurable per field but the critical-field floor of 0.98 cannot be lowered below 0.95 by any role. |
| SUR-FRQ-106 | Every imported field shall record provenance: source file, sheet, row, column, extracted raw value, confidence, whether a human edited it, and who approved the batch. | P0 | SVC | 3 | For any imported guard, a "where did this come from?" view shows the original cell. |
| SUR-FRQ-107 | The mapping UI shall present source columns and target fields side by side with: auto-suggested mappings and their confidence, 3 sample values per source column, unmapped-required-field warnings, a transform picker (date format, name splitting, currency parsing, unit conversion, trim/case), and template save/load. | P1 | AGN, OPS | 3 | A 40-column payroll sheet can be mapped in under 10 minutes and the template reused for the next month. |
| SUR-FRQ-108 | Duplicate resolution shall support field-level merge with a clear "keep existing / take incoming" choice per conflicting field and a preview of the merged record before commit. | P1 | AGN, OPS | 3 | Merging two guard records preserves the longest-standing employee code by default and records the choice. |
| SUR-FRQ-109 | Rollback shall restore the pre-import state for the batch's rows, mark the batch Cancelled, and be itself fully audited; rollback is blocked when dependent transactions exist and shall name them. | P0 | AGN, OPS | 3 | Rolling back a 5,000-row batch completes in under 10 minutes and leaves no orphan rows. |
| SUR-FRQ-110 | Migration shall be resumable and non-blocking: a tenant may use the product normally while a migration runs; imported records appear progressively with an "Imported" badge until the batch is approved-complete. | P1 | AGN | 3 | Concurrent normal usage during a 50,000-row import shows no user-visible degradation. |
| SUR-FRQ-111 | Personal data in migration source files shall be encrypted at rest, access-restricted to the migration operator and the tenant, and purged from the staging area `{30}` days after batch completion or rollback. | P0 | SVC | 3 | Staging purge is automatic and audited; the original file can be retained by the tenant separately if they choose. |
| SUR-FRQ-112 | The Enterprise onboarding service model shall be defined as: a named Suraksha migration operator, a scoped data-handling agreement, a pre-migration data audit report, a pilot batch of ≤200 rows approved by the tenant, then the full migration, then a 14-day reconciliation window with a signed-off variance report. | P1 | OPS | 3 | Every Enterprise migration produces a variance report signed by the tenant. |
| SUR-FRQ-113 | Assisted migration by Suraksha staff shall require an explicit, time-boxed tenant grant (a migration mandate) visible in the tenant's Suraksha-access log (SUR-FRQ-047), and shall expire automatically. | P0 | OPS, AGN | 3 | Without an active mandate, staff cannot open the tenant's migration workspace. |
| SUR-FRQ-114 | Self-service migration shall be available on all plans for a restricted set: guards, clients, sites, and attendance history via a **published CSV template only** (no OCR). OCR-based and large-scale migration remain Enterprise. | P1 | AGN | 3 | A Starter tenant can import 500 guards from the template; the OCR path shows an upgrade prompt. |
| SUR-FRQ-115 | The pipeline shall handle Indian data realities explicitly: mixed date formats within one column, ₹ symbols and comma grouping (`1,20,000` lakh-style), name fields containing father's/husband's name, mobile numbers with `+91`/`0`/spaces, "NIL"/"-"/"NA" as null, merged header rows, and multi-sheet workbooks where each sheet is a branch. | P1 | SVC | 3 | A test corpus of 25 real-world-shaped sheets parses without manual pre-cleaning. |
| SUR-FRQ-116 | A migration dashboard shall show, per batch: rows read, parsed, valid, warned, errored, duplicated, imported, and pending review, with drill-through to rows in every bucket. | P1 | AGN, OPS | 3 | Every number on the dashboard is clickable to the underlying rows. |
