### 26.7 Support system

#### 26.7.1 Channels and their relationship

| Channel | Who | Availability | Feeds into |
|---|---|---|---|
| Help center (self-serve articles) | Everyone, unauthenticated for public articles | Always | Deflection; article rating; "still need help" creates a Ticket with the article context attached |
| Ticket | Authenticated users, all products | Always | The system of record. Every other channel resolves into a Ticket. |
| Chat | Client, Agency, Guard (in-app) | Business hours + AI assistant outside them | Creates or continues a Ticket; transcript attached |
| Call request ("call me back") | Client, Agency | Business hours, with a slot picker | Creates a Ticket with a scheduled callback task |
| Emergency escalation | Guard, Supervisor, Client | 24×7 | Bypasses ticketing into Command Center (§24); a Ticket is created afterwards for the record |
| Complaint | Client (about service), Guard (about employer/pay), Agency (about Suraksha) | Always | A Ticket with `type=Complaint` and a distinct handling path and SLA |
| Refund / Dispute | Client, Agency | Always | A Ticket with a financial workflow (§35) and mandatory finance approval |

> **SUR-FRQ-117.** Emergency escalation shall never queue behind support. Any support surface that receives a life-safety report shall route it to Command Center within 10 seconds and show the user an unambiguous confirmation ("Help is being contacted now"), independent of ticket creation.

#### 26.7.2 Ticket taxonomy

| Level 1 type | Level 2 examples | Default owner queue |
|---|---|---|
| Account & access | Login, OTP not received, MFA reset, device change, account recovery, role/permission | Support |
| Booking & service (client) | Change request, guard replacement request, service quality, site change, cancellation | Operations |
| Deployment (agency) | Roster, attendance dispute, replacement, post configuration | Operations |
| Payments & billing | Invoice query, payment failed, refund, GST detail correction, dunning dispute | Finance |
| Payroll & salary (guard) | Salary not received, wrong amount, deduction query, payslip missing, bank detail change | Payroll → Agency Finance |
| Verification & documents | Document rejected, verification delayed, licence verification, re-verification | Verification |
| Subscription & plan (agency) | Upgrade/downgrade, limits, invoice, trial, cancellation | Sales / Finance |
| Marketplace (agency) | Listing, reviews, bids, lead quality, profile | Support / Trust |
| Technical | App crash, sync failure, GPS accuracy, notification not received, performance | Engineering triage |
| Complaint | Service complaint, staff conduct, harassment, safety concern, discrimination | Compliance (harassment/safety routes to a restricted queue) |
| Data & privacy | Data access request, correction, deletion, consent withdrawal | Privacy (§39) |
| Feedback | Feature request, general feedback | Product (no SLA) |

#### 26.7.3 Priority and SLA matrix

Priorities use the canon severities. Business hours are the tenant's configured hours; P0/P1 clocks run 24×7.

| Priority | Definition | First response | Update cadence | Resolution target |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P0 Critical | Life-safety, active security event, total platform outage for a tenant, payroll blocked on salary day, SOS follow-up | 15 min | Every 30 min | 4 h or a credible workaround |
| P1 High | Cannot deploy/roster, payment blocked, guard salary missing, attendance data loss, verification blocking a deployment, harassment/safety complaint | 1 h (business), 2 h (out of hours) | Every 4 h | 24 h |
| P2 Medium | Feature not working with a workaround, invoice dispute, document rejection query, app bug affecting one user | 4 business hours | Daily | 3 business days |
| P3 Informational | How-to, feature request, cosmetic issue, general query | 1 business day | On change | 10 business days |

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Products affected | Phase | Acceptance summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SUR-FRQ-118 | A single ticketing service shall serve client, agency, guard and internal support, with queues, ownership, SLA timers, and a shared audit trail. | P0 | ALL | 1 | One ticket ID space; a ticket can move queues without losing history. |
| SUR-FRQ-119 | Ticket priority shall be assigned by rule from type + context (e.g. "salary not received" on/after salary date = P1) and shall be adjustable only upward by the requester, and in both directions by support with a recorded reason. | P1 | ALL | 2 | A guard cannot self-assign P0; support downgrading P1→P2 records a reason. |
| SUR-FRQ-120 | Tickets shall support linkage to Booking, Contract, Site, Post, Shift, Guard, Agency, Client, Invoice, Payment, Payroll run, Incident, Document and Tender, with the link both navigable and permission-checked at render time. | P0 | ALL | 2 | A support agent without payment access sees the linked invoice as a reference number only, with no amounts. |
| SUR-FRQ-121 | **(Support authorization rule)** A support agent's access to tenant data shall be purpose-bound: opening a linked record from a ticket grants a time-boxed, read-only, audited view scoped to that record and its immediate context — never a general browse of the tenant. | P0 | OPS | 2 | Navigating from a linked site to the tenant's full guard list is not possible from a support context. |
| SUR-FRQ-122 | Every support view of tenant data shall appear in the tenant's Suraksha-access log with the ticket reference as the stated purpose. | P0 | OPS, AGN | 2 | Tenant sees "Support viewed Site X in relation to ticket SUP-10432". |
| SUR-FRQ-123 | SLA timers shall pause only for "waiting on customer" and shall record pause reasons; a ticket cannot be parked indefinitely — a paused ticket auto-reminds the customer at 24 h/72 h and auto-closes at 10 days with a re-open link. | P1 | ALL | 2 | Pause/resume history is visible on the ticket. |
| SUR-FRQ-124 | Guard support shall be designed for low literacy and low bandwidth: category chips with icons, voice note submission, photo attachment, status in plain language and the guard's chosen language, and a callback option. A guard shall never be asked to write a paragraph to get help. | P0 | GAP, GRD | 2 | A guard can raise "salary not received" in ≤3 taps plus an optional voice note. |
| SUR-FRQ-125 | Guard complaints about their employing agency shall be routable to Suraksha independently of the agency, with the agency unable to see, edit, close or retaliate against such tickets, and with a documented anti-retaliation handling path. | P0 | GAP, OPS | 2 | An agency admin cannot see a Suraksha-routed guard complaint in any list, count or export. |
| SUR-FRQ-126 | Agency support shall include a plan-differentiated path: Starter/Professional use the shared queue; Enterprise has a named account contact, a dedicated queue and contractual response targets (canon §1.4). | P1 | AGN, OPS | 2 | An Enterprise ticket routes to the dedicated queue and shows the account contact. |
| SUR-FRQ-127 | Refund and dispute tickets shall follow a defined financial workflow: evidence capture → operations verification of the service facts → finance calculation → approval per the §35 authority matrix → execution → customer notification, with no step skippable and no auto-refund above `{₹5,000}` `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-190]`. | P0 | CPT, AGN, OPS | 2 | A refund above the threshold cannot be executed without a second approver. |
| SUR-FRQ-128 | Complaints classified as harassment, safety, discrimination or wage-theft shall route to a restricted queue visible only to Compliance and named handlers, shall never be visible to the subject's manager by default, and shall have their own retention and access rules (§39, §40). | P0 | OPS | 2 | Standard support agents cannot see the existence of such tickets. |
| SUR-FRQ-129 | The help center shall be multilingual (§26.10), searchable, article-versioned, and shall record deflection metrics (articles viewed before ticket creation, tickets avoided). | P1 | ALL | 2 | Every article shows a "was this helpful" control feeding a content backlog. |
| SUR-FRQ-130 | AI-assisted support shall be permitted only in the Read-only and Recommendation action classes (canon §1.7): it may answer from the help center, summarise a ticket, and draft a reply for a human to send; it shall never close a ticket, issue a refund, or change a status. | P0 | AI, OPS | 2 | An AI-drafted reply requires an explicit human send action, logged with the AI Interaction ID. |
| SUR-FRQ-131 | Every closed ticket shall trigger a CSAT prompt (1–5 plus optional comment) delivered on the channel the ticket was raised on; scores are reported per queue, per agent and per type. | P2 | ALL | 3 | CSAT response rate and score appear in the support dashboard (§42). |

### 26.8 Fraud & abuse prevention

#### 26.8.1 Stance

Fraud controls follow three principles: (1) **detect with signals, decide with humans** for anything that affects a person's livelihood; (2) **never explain the detector** to the suspected party; (3) **always provide an appeal** with a different human than the one who decided. Automated blocking is permitted only for reversible, low-harm actions.

#### 26.8.2 Fake guard profile

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Detection signals | Same face embedding across multiple guard identities; same Aadhaar hash / PAN across identities; same bank account across many guards; photo that matches a stock-image or a previously rejected upload hash; document metadata inconsistencies (EXIF absent on a "camera" capture, editing-software signature); mobile number reused across agencies within a short window; a guard "deployed" at two sites simultaneously; profile created and deployed within minutes with no verification; address geocodes to a non-residential/implausible location. |
| Automated response | Block deployment to a live post until verification; withhold marketplace visibility; flag payroll inclusion for review; never auto-terminate. |
| Human review queue | Verification queue, "Identity integrity" lane; SLA 24 h; reviewer sees all matched identities side by side with the matching signal named. |
| Appeal | Guard (or the agency on their behalf) submits fresh documents plus a live selfie challenge; reviewed by a second verifier; decision within 3 business days; outcome and reason communicated in the guard's language. |

#### 26.8.3 Fake agency

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Detection signals | PSARA licence number failing format/checksum or duplicated across agencies; licence document image reused from another agency; GSTIN/PAN mismatch with the registered name; address shared with an already-rejected agency; disposable email/VoIP phone; company incorporated days before signing up while claiming years of experience; no guards ever onboarded but bidding aggressively; bank account name mismatched with the entity. |
| Automated response | Hold marketplace listing in `Pending`; block bidding and lead receipt; block payout registration; allow the agency to continue configuring its own tenant (no data hostage). |
| Human review queue | Verification queue, "Agency onboarding" lane; SLA 48 h (R16 escalates). Verification is manual/assisted because no reliable public PSARA API is assumed (A-142). |
| Appeal | Submit originals plus a video verification call; escalation to Compliance; decision within 5 business days; a rejected agency is told the category of failure, not the signal. |

#### 26.8.4 Fake / forged licence

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Detection signals | OCR-extracted licence number, issuing authority, validity dates inconsistent with the document layout; font/kerning anomalies and re-compression artefacts; duplicate licence number across tenants; validity date in an impossible format; issuing district not matching the claimed geography; a scan of a scan (generation loss); PDF producer metadata indicating an editor. |
| Automated response | Document status → Pending with an internal integrity flag; the agency's `Verified` badge is withheld (never silently removed without review); geography-scoped capabilities blocked. |
| Human review queue | Compliance "Document integrity" lane, dual review required for a tampering finding; SLA 48 h. |
| Appeal | Physical/original verification, issuing-authority correspondence where possible, or a re-issued licence copy; a confirmed forgery routes to account suspension and, per §40, an internal legal review record. |

#### 26.8.5 Fake GPS / mock location & attendance fraud

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Detection signals | OS mock-location flag; developer options + known spoofing package installed; rooted/jailbroken device; teleport (implied speed >200 km/h between fixes); location accuracy suspiciously perfect (±1 m consistently) or constant coordinates to 6 decimals; check-in outside geofence with a "corrected" fix seconds later; multiple guards checking in from one device fingerprint (R14); check-in photo lacking live-capture signals; device time ≠ server time beyond ±120 s (canon §4 dual timestamps); attendance marked in bulk by a supervisor for many guards at the same second; a pattern of "device issue" manual overrides concentrated on one supervisor or site. |
| Automated response | Attendance record accepted but marked `Unverified` with the reason — never silently rejected, because a false rejection costs a guard their wage. Payroll treats `Unverified` attendance as requiring approval. Site's auto-approval suspended for the day. P1 to Agency Compliance. |
| Human review queue | "Attendance integrity" lane in the Agency Portal (tenant-owned) with a Suraksha oversight view for Suraksha-operated sites; SLA 24 h because it gates pay. |
| Appeal | Guard or supervisor supplies context (photo, supervisor attestation, site log); a second reviewer decides; wage is not withheld beyond the payroll cut-off — if unresolved by cut-off, pay is released and the amount is flagged for recovery, never withheld on suspicion alone `[RECOMMENDED]`. |

#### 26.8.6 Payment fraud

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Detection signals | Card testing (many small failed authorisations); mismatched billing identity; unusual booking value for a new account; rapid book-then-refund cycles; payout account changed shortly before a payroll run; payout account shared across unrelated guards; invoice details edited after issue; velocity anomalies on wallet top-up/withdrawal; chargeback history. |
| Automated response | Additional authentication on the payment; hold on the specific payout with notification; wallet withdrawal cooling period of 24 h after a bank-detail change; never a blanket account freeze without human decision. |
| Human review queue | Finance "Payment risk" lane; SLA 4 h during business hours because it blocks money movement. |
| Appeal | Documentary verification (bank proof, penny-drop, ID) reviewed by Finance with a second approver for reinstatement; every hold and release is a ledger-visible event (canon §4 money rules). |

#### 26.8.7 Review manipulation

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Detection signals | Reviews from accounts with no transaction against the reviewed agency; burst of 5-star reviews within a short window; reviewer accounts created same-day/same-IP/same-device; text similarity across reviews; reciprocal review rings between agencies; a competitor pattern of 1-star reviews with no engagement history; review immediately after a dispute loss. |
| Automated response | Hold the review in moderation (not published, not counted in the rating); rating recomputed only from published reviews; the reviewer sees "Under review", not the reason. |
| Human review queue | Trust & Safety moderation queue; SLA 48 h. |
| Appeal | Both the reviewer and the reviewed agency may contest; a removed review states the policy clause breached; agencies may post one public response per review regardless of outcome (§19). |
| Hard rule | Only a verified transacting client may leave a rating that affects the score; non-transactional feedback is visibly separated. |

#### 26.8.8 Document tampering

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Detection signals | Error-level analysis and re-compression artefacts; inconsistent font metrics within a field; PDF incremental-update history showing edits; metadata producer mismatch; identical document hash under different names/entities; a field value contradicting an authoritative source already on file (e.g. DOB differing across two verified documents). |
| Automated response | Document → `Suspended` (integrity concern) with the neutral user-facing message of SUR-FRQ-095; dependent capabilities pause; the previously Verified state is preserved in history, not erased. |
| Human review queue | Compliance "Document integrity" lane, dual review; SLA 48 h. |
| Appeal | Submission of an original or an authority-issued copy; independent verification; a confirmed tampering finding escalates to account action with a documented decision record. |

#### 26.8.9 Account takeover, marketplace spam, duplicate profiles

| Threat | Detection signals | Automated response | Human queue | Appeal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Account takeover | Signals of SUR-FRQ-017 plus: password + phone changed within 24 h; new device + immediate payout-detail change; session from a new ASN performing bulk export; MFA disabled followed by sensitive action | Force step-up, freeze payout-detail changes for 24 h, notify all verified channels, revoke sessions on high score | Security "ATO" lane, SLA 1 h | Identity re-verification with a human; restored access is logged and the true owner sees the full timeline |
| Marketplace spam | Lead volume without conversion; templated outreach; profile keyword stuffing; duplicate listings; contact details in fields not meant for them; off-platform payment solicitation | Throttle lead access, hide listing from search (still visible by direct link during review), block messaging | Trust & Safety, SLA 24 h | Written appeal; reinstatement with a warning record; three findings escalate to suspension |
| Duplicate profiles | Same Aadhaar hash / mobile / bank across guard profiles; same GSTIN across agencies; fuzzy name+DOB+father's-name match above threshold | Block the newer profile from deployment until resolved; never auto-merge | Verification "Duplicates" lane, SLA 48 h | Human merge with field-level choice (as §26.6 merge UI); the guard is informed of the merge outcome |

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Products affected | Phase | Acceptance summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SUR-FRQ-132 | A fraud signal service shall consume platform events, compute per-entity risk scores, and expose them to review queues; scores shall never be shown to the suspected party or to unauthorised roles. | P0 | SVC | 2 | Risk score is absent from every client- and agency-facing payload. |
| SUR-FRQ-133 | Any automated response that affects a person's income, employment or reputation shall be **reversible and human-decided**; the system may hold, flag or require review, but may not terminate, dismiss, blacklist or publicly mark a person or agency without a human decision. | P0 | ALL | 2 | No code path sets a terminal punitive state without a recorded human approver. |
| SUR-FRQ-134 | Every fraud case shall have: a case record, the triggering signals, the evidence snapshot, the reviewer, the decision, the reason, the notification sent, and the appeal outcome — retained per §40. | P0 | OPS | 2 | A case can be reconstructed end to end 18 months later. |
| SUR-FRQ-135 | Appeals shall be decided by a person other than the original decider, within the SLA stated per threat type, with the outcome communicated in the subject's chosen language and in plain terms. | P0 | OPS | 2 | Reviewer identity checks prevent self-review of an appeal. |
| SUR-FRQ-136 | Detection thresholds, model versions and rule changes shall be versioned and auditable, and a change that increases automated blocking shall require a documented review before activation. | P1 | SVC | 3 | Threshold changes appear in a change log with author and rationale. |
| SUR-FRQ-137 | False-positive rate shall be measured per detector and reported monthly; a detector exceeding a `{15}`% false-positive rate over 100 cases shall be automatically demoted to "flag only" pending review. | P1 | SVC | 3 | The demotion is automatic and notified to Trust & Safety. |
| SUR-FRQ-138 | Fraud-related restrictions shall be surfaced to the affected party as an action-oriented status ("Your account needs re-verification before you can be deployed") with a route to resolution, never as a silent failure or a generic error. | P0 | ALL | 2 | No fraud hold produces an unexplained failure state in any product. |

### 26.9 Admin content management

Content published to public surfaces (WEB, TRN, help center, app store copy, notification templates) is managed in OPS by Marketing, Sales and Compliance roles. This subsection defines the shared CMS mechanics; the page inventories live in §14 and §19.

| Content type | Owner role | Approver | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Website pages (home, about, services, industries, contact) | Marketing | Founder/Management for home/about; Marketing lead otherwise | Canon P1–P5: fabricated content must not be publishable — see SUR-FRQ-146 |
| Services & industries catalogue | Marketing + Sales | Marketing lead | Drives WEB and TRN navigation and the booking flow's service picker |
| Pricing & plan content | Sales | Founder/Management | Enterprise price is never displayed publicly (canon §1.4); the CMS shall make displaying it impossible |
| FAQs | Support + Marketing | Marketing lead | Feeds the help center and on-page FAQ blocks; shares one source |
| Blog / insights | Marketing | Marketing lead | Author, category, tags, SEO fields, scheduled publish |
| Testimonials & case studies | Sales | Compliance + Founder/Management | Requires a stored consent artefact per SUR-FRQ-146 |
| Media library | Marketing | — | Images, video, PDFs, logos; alt text mandatory; licence/consent field mandatory |
| Locations / serviceable cities | Operations | National Operations | Drives D-005 city list, the booking availability check and local landing pages |
| Notification & message templates | Marketing + Support | Compliance for legal/financial wording | Versioned, per-language, per-channel; variable placeholders validated |
| Campaigns | Marketing | Marketing lead | Audience segment, channel, schedule, consent filter, frequency cap |
| Policies (privacy, terms, refund, PSARA compliance page, grievance) | Compliance | Founder/Management | Versioned with effective dates and a public archive; canon P7/P8 fix |

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Products affected | Phase | Acceptance summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SUR-FRQ-139 | All public content shall move through Draft → In Review → Approved → Scheduled → Published → Archived, with role-gated transitions and no direct-to-Published path for any content type. | P0 | OPS, WEB, TRN | 1 | An author cannot publish their own content for approver-required types. |
| SUR-FRQ-140 | Every content item shall be versioned with author, timestamp, diff, and one-click restore of a prior version; the live version is always identifiable. | P0 | OPS | 1 | Restoring a prior version creates a new version rather than overwriting history. |
| SUR-FRQ-141 | Scheduled publishing and scheduled unpublishing shall be supported at minute granularity in IST, with a visible schedule calendar and a warning if a scheduled item conflicts with another change to the same URL. | P1 | OPS | 2 | A scheduled publish fires within 60 s of its time and is audited. |
| SUR-FRQ-142 | A preview shall render the exact published output for desktop and mobile, from a shareable link that does not require the viewer to hold CMS access but does expire in 7 days. | P1 | OPS | 2 | Preview link matches production rendering including localisation. |
| SUR-FRQ-143 | Content shall be localisable per §26.10 with per-language publication states; an English update shall mark dependent translations `Outdated` rather than silently serving stale content. | P1 | OPS, WEB | 2 | A Hindi page whose English source changed shows as Outdated in the CMS and still serves the last good Hindi version with a freshness date. |
| SUR-FRQ-144 | SEO fields (title, meta description, canonical, OG image, structured data type) shall be first-class on every public page with validation on length and uniqueness. | P1 | OPS, WEB, TRN | 2 | Duplicate titles across pages are flagged before publish. |
| SUR-FRQ-145 | Every publish, unpublish, schedule and rollback shall be audited with actor, role, item, version and reason (reason mandatory for policy and pricing content). | P0 | OPS | 1 | Policy changes carry a mandatory reason string. |
| SUR-FRQ-146 | **(Truth control)** Content asserting a named client, testimonial, award, press mention, certification or statistic shall require a linked evidence artefact (consent letter, certificate, press URL, or a data source reference) before it can leave Draft. Statistics shall be bound to a named data source and shall be re-verified on a configurable cadence. | P0 | OPS, WEB, TRN | 1 | Attempting to publish "40,000+ guards" without a bound source is blocked; canon P1–P5 items cannot recur. |
| SUR-FRQ-147 | Numeric claims used in more than one place (guard count, city count, agency count) shall be **single-sourced variables** rendered from one record, so two pages can never disagree (canon P5). | P0 | OPS, WEB, TRN | 1 | Changing the guard-count variable updates every surface that renders it. |
| SUR-FRQ-148 | Campaigns shall respect consent state, channel policy (WhatsApp template rules, SMS DLT registration), frequency caps per recipient per channel per week, and a global unsubscribe honoured across all campaigns. | P0 | OPS | 2 | An unsubscribed contact is excluded at send time, not merely at list build time. |
| SUR-FRQ-149 | Policy documents shall be published with an effective date, a change summary and a permanent archive of superseded versions accessible from a public URL. | P0 | OPS, WEB | 1 | Every prior privacy policy version remains publicly retrievable. |
| SUR-FRQ-150 | The CMS shall block publishing of any page containing a placeholder pattern (`+91 90000 00000`, `lorem`, `TBD`, `example.com`, an unreplaced `{{variable}}`) via a pre-publish lint (canon P6). | P1 | OPS | 1 | Pre-publish lint fails with the exact offending line. |
| SUR-FRQ-151 | Broken-link checking shall run on publish and nightly across public surfaces, reporting internal 404s (canon P8) to the content owner with the referring page. | P1 | OPS, WEB, TRN | 2 | A footer link to a non-existent page fails the publish check. |

### 26.10 Localization & language

#### 26.10.1 Stance

India-first means Hindi and English are peers at launch, and the field workforce is the population most in need of their own language. Canon §1.7 sets the ceiling: Hindi and English plus **at least 19 Indian languages** where technically feasible. That ceiling applies to the AI layer and to guard-facing surfaces; it does not mean every enterprise finance screen is translated into 21 languages, which would be waste. This subsection states exactly which surfaces are fully localised and which are English-only.

#### 26.10.2 Language tiers

| Tier | Languages | Coverage commitment |
|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 | English (en-IN), Hindi (hi-IN) | 100% of every surface, including all notifications, errors, help content and legal summaries. Launch requirement. |
| Tier 2 | Bengali, Marathi, Telugu, Tamil, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, Odia, Assamese | 100% of guard-facing surfaces (GAP, GRD), all guard notifications, all safety-critical copy, help center core articles. Phase 2. |
| Tier 3 | Urdu, Maithili, Santali, Kashmiri, Nepali, Konkani, Sindhi, Dogri, Manipuri (+ others as demand appears) | Safety-critical strings, notification templates, AI voice/text interaction where the model supports it. Phase 3, demand-driven. |
| English-only (deliberate) | — | Advanced finance and accounting screens, payroll configuration internals, API/developer documentation, admin/CMS authoring UI, OPS internal analytics, migration mapping UI, contract and tender legal text (source language preserved with a translated summary). |

> Tier 2 + Tier 3 together with Tier 1 exceed the "19+ languages" foundation rule. `[ASSUMPTION: A-190]` — that professional translation and ASR/TTS quality is procurable at acceptable cost for all Tier 3 languages; where it is not, the language ships text-only or with an English fallback and this is stated in the UI.

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Products affected | Phase | Acceptance summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SUR-FRQ-152 | Language shall be a per-Identity preference, not a per-device or per-tenant setting, and shall follow the user across web, app and notifications. | P0 | ALL | 1 | Changing language on the web changes the next SMS the user receives. |
| SUR-FRQ-153 | On first run, language shall be offered as an explicit choice with names written in their own script (हिन्दी, বাংলা, தமிழ்), defaulting to the device locale where it maps to a supported language, and shall be changeable at any time from a consistent location. | P0 | ALL | 1 | A guard can change language in ≤3 taps from the app home. |
| SUR-FRQ-154 | A tenant may set a default language for new users and may restrict the offered set, but shall never be able to prevent a user from choosing Hindi or English. | P1 | AGN, OPS | 2 | Tier-1 languages are always present in the picker. |
| SUR-FRQ-155 | Fallback shall be explicit and per-string: requested language → Hindi → English. A missing translation shall render the fallback text and log a missing-string event; it shall never render a raw key, an empty string, or a mixed half-translated sentence. | P0 | ALL | 1 | Removing a Bengali string renders Hindi and logs the key; no `screen.title.missing` appears in the UI. |
| SUR-FRQ-156 | Safety-critical strings (SOS, wake check, evacuation, emergency call, attendance failure, salary status) shall be marked as a protected set that cannot ship untranslated for any Tier 1 or Tier 2 language; the build shall fail if a protected string is missing. | P0 | GAP, GRD, CAP | 2 | CI gate blocks release on a missing protected string. |
| SUR-FRQ-157 | Translation management shall be a first-class workflow: string extraction, translator assignment, review by a second speaker, context notes and screenshots for translators, glossary of protected terms (Suraksha, PSARA, SOS, Guard, Post, Shift — never translated), and a per-language completeness dashboard. | P1 | OPS | 2 | Every string carries context; the dashboard shows % complete per language per surface. |
| SUR-FRQ-158 | Machine translation may be used for a first draft only; no machine-translated string shall reach production for safety-critical, legal, financial or notification content without human review. | P0 | OPS | 2 | Each string carries a `reviewed_by_human` flag that is enforced on the protected set. |
| SUR-FRQ-159 | Layout shall tolerate text expansion: Hindi and Tamil commonly run 20–35% longer than English, and German-style truncation bugs shall be caught by a pseudo-localisation build that inflates strings by 40%. | P1 | ALL | 2 | Pseudo-loc build shows no clipped labels or broken layouts on the reference screen set. |
| SUR-FRQ-160 | Devanagari and other Indic scripts shall render with correct conjuncts, matras and line-breaking; the type stack shall include a script-complete font per §27.2.1, and font files shall be subset and lazily loaded per language to protect app size and data. | P0 | ALL | 1 | Rendering test corpus of conjunct-heavy Hindi and Tamil strings shows no tofu, no broken matras. |
| SUR-FRQ-161 | Numbers shall be formatted per the Indian numbering system where the user's locale is Indian: `₹12,34,567.00` (lakh/crore grouping), with the ₹ symbol and no space; amounts in words (used on invoices) shall follow lakh/crore conventions in English and Hindi. | P0 | ALL | 1 | An invoice for 1234567 paise-based amount renders `₹12,345.67` and words match. |
| SUR-FRQ-162 | Dates shall render `DD MMM YYYY` (e.g. 15 Aug 2026) by default across all surfaces to eliminate DD/MM vs MM/DD ambiguity; time renders in 12-hour with AM/PM for field surfaces and 24-hour for operations consoles and logs; all times are IST unless a tenant configures otherwise, and the timezone is always shown on exports. | P0 | ALL | 1 | No surface displays a purely numeric ambiguous date. |
| SUR-FRQ-163 | Currency shall be INR only in V1; the money model (integer paise) already supports multi-currency but no non-INR currency shall be displayed or accepted. `[FUTURE]` multi-currency. | P0 | ALL | 1 | No currency selector exists; all amounts carry the ₹ symbol. |
| SUR-FRQ-164 | RTL layout is **not required**: none of the Tier 1–3 languages is right-to-left as rendered on this platform (Urdu is supported in Nastaliq/Perso-Arabic script only if a full RTL pass is funded; until then Urdu ships as Roman-Urdu text `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-191]`). The design system shall nonetheless use logical CSS properties so a future RTL pass is not a rewrite. | P1 | ALL | 2 | Stylesheets use `margin-inline-start` style properties; no hard-coded `left`/`right` in layout primitives. |
| SUR-FRQ-165 | Voice input and output shall follow the same tier model: Tier 1 at launch of the AI surfaces, Tier 2 as ASR/TTS quality permits, with a visible indicator of which languages support voice and a graceful text-only fallback (§25). | P1 | GAP, AI | 2 | Selecting a voice-unsupported language hides the mic with an explanatory tooltip, not a broken button. |
| SUR-FRQ-166 | Names, addresses and free text shall accept and store the full Unicode range with correct collation for search (§26.3), and shall never be transliterated destructively on save. | P0 | ALL | 1 | A name entered in Devanagari is stored, displayed and searched as entered. |
| SUR-FRQ-167 | Notification templates shall exist per language per channel, with SMS templates additionally respecting the operator's registered template constraints; if a language variant is missing at send time, the Tier-1 fallback is used and the gap is logged. | P0 | SVC | 2 | Every transactional template exists in en-IN and hi-IN before launch. |
| SUR-FRQ-168 | Plain-language rules (§27.10) shall apply to every localised string: short sentences, active voice, no idiom, no English loanwords where a common Hindi word exists — but retain the loanword where it is the word people actually use (e.g. "duty", "site", "shift" are used as-is in Hindi field speech). | P1 | GAP, GRD | 2 | Field-tested with 10 guards: comprehension of the 20 most critical strings ≥90%. |

## 27. UI/UX Specification

### 27.0 Scope

This section is the canonical home for the design system and UX standards across all ten surfaces (canon §6). Product sections §14–§25 describe **what is on each screen**; §28 lists screens; this section defines **the vocabulary those descriptions are written in** — tokens, components, states, interaction rules, accessibility floor and copy standards. Where a product section names a component ("status pill", "KPI tile", "queue row"), the definition is here.

Normative rules use IDs `SUR-UIX-nnn`.

---

### 27.1 Design principles

| # | Principle | What it means in practice | What it forbids |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Operational clarity over decoration** | Every pixel earns its place by helping someone decide or act. The product's beauty is in legibility, alignment and consistency, not in ornament. | Hero gradients on operational screens, decorative illustrations in dense tables, animated flourishes on data updates, icon-only buttons for destructive actions. |
| 2 | **Density-first on desktop operations, thumb-first in the field** | OPS, Command Center and Agency Portal are professional tools used for eight hours: 32 px rows, tight leading, many columns, keyboard-first. GAP and field surfaces are used one-handed, outdoors, in gloves: 56 px targets, one primary action per screen. | Shipping the same layout to both. Padding an ops table to "breathe" until only 6 rows fit. Shrinking a guard's check-in button to fit a desktop grid. |
| 3 | **The three-second scan** | On any command surface (Command Center, live board, dashboards, queues), a trained operator must be able to answer "is anything wrong, and where?" within three seconds of the screen appearing. Severity colour, count and location must be resolvable pre-attentively, before reading. | Burying a P0 count inside a paragraph; using the same visual weight for a P0 and a P3; making the operator scroll to see whether anything is red. |
| 4 | **Error prevention over error messages** | Design the interaction so the wrong thing is hard: disable impossible options with an explanation, validate at field level as the user leaves the field, default to safe values, require typed confirmation only where consequences are irreversible, and show the consequence before the act ("This will notify 47 guards"). | Free-text where a picker will do; letting a user complete a 6-step wizard before revealing the plan does not permit it; a modal that says "Are you sure?" without saying what will happen. |
| 5 | **Consistency across ten surfaces** | A status pill, a date, a rupee amount, a confirmation dialog and a table row action look and behave identically in OPS, Agency Portal, Trinetra and the apps. A user who learns one surface has learned the grammar of all of them. | Per-product component forks, per-team colour choices, one product using DD/MM and another MMM DD. |
| 6 | **Truthful state** | The UI never implies certainty it does not have. Stale data is labelled with its age; offline data is labelled offline; a pending write is visibly pending; a partially loaded screen says which part failed. | Showing a cached attendance figure as though it were live; a spinner that never resolves; silently dropping a failed save. |
| 7 | **Respect the person on the other side** | Guards are low-wage workers using their own phone on their own data. Clients are anxious about safety. Copy is plain, never punitive, never shaming; data and battery use are treated as costs we impose. | "You failed to check in." Auto-playing video. Background location outside duty hours. 6 MB of fonts on a 2 GB Android. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-001 | All ten surfaces shall consume one published design-system package (tokens + components); a product-local component fork requires a documented exception approved by the design system owner. |
| SUR-UIX-002 | Command surfaces shall satisfy the three-second scan rule, verified by a timed usability test with five trained operators on a seeded-anomaly dataset; median time-to-locate ≤3 s, worst case ≤6 s. |
| SUR-UIX-003 | No screen shall present a destructive or irreversible action without stating its consequence in the confirmation copy in specific, countable terms. |
| SUR-UIX-004 | Any displayed operational figure older than its freshness budget (§27.4.7) shall be visibly labelled with its age; a figure whose age cannot be determined shall not be displayed as live. |

---

### 27.2 The design system

#### 27.2.1 Typography

| Role | Family | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Primary UI (Latin + Devanagari + Indic) | **Noto Sans** family — Noto Sans (Latin), Noto Sans Devanagari, Noto Sans Bengali/Tamil/Telugu/Kannada/Malayalam/Gujarati/Gurmukhi/Oriya | The only widely available open family with complete, well-hinted coverage of every Tier 1–3 script (SUR-FRQ-160) and consistent metrics across scripts, so a Hindi label and an English label sit on the same baseline grid. |
| Numerals / tabular data | **Noto Sans** with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` | Money, counts and IDs must align in columns; proportional digits in a table are a defect. |
| Monospace (IDs, logs, code, API docs) | **JetBrains Mono**, fallback `ui-monospace` | Audit logs, correlation IDs, licence numbers. |
| Display / marketing (WEB, TRN only) | **Inter Tight** for headlines, Noto Sans for body | Marketing surfaces may use one display face; product surfaces may not. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-005 | Font files shall be subset per script and loaded only for the user's active language(s); total font payload shall not exceed 180 KB on first load for any single-language session. |
| SUR-UIX-006 | The type stack shall specify a script-appropriate fallback chain ending in a system font; no surface shall render tofu (□) for any Tier 1–3 script. |
| SUR-UIX-007 | Tabular numerals shall be used for every numeric column, every money value, and every countdown. |

| Token | Size / line-height | Weight | Letter-spacing | Use |

| `display-2` | 32 / 40 px | 700 | −0.01em | Marketing section head; app onboarding title |
| `heading-1` | 24 / 32 px | 600 | −0.01em | Page title |
| `heading-2` | 20 / 28 px | 600 | 0 | Section title, modal title |
| `heading-3` | 16 / 24 px | 600 | 0 | Card title, table group header |
| `body-lg` | 16 / 24 px | 400 | 0 | Field-app body text, primary reading text |
| `body` | 14 / 20 px | 400 | 0 | Default desktop body, table cell |
| `body-strong` | 14 / 20 px | 600 | 0 | Emphasised cell, KPI label |
| `caption` | 12 / 16 px | 400 | 0.01em | Helper text, timestamps, metadata |
| `overline` | 11 / 16 px | 600 | 0.06em, uppercase | Column group labels, status-pill text on desktop |
| `numeric-xl` | 32 / 36 px | 600, tabular | −0.01em | KPI tile value |
| `numeric-lg` | 24 / 28 px | 600, tabular | 0 | Secondary stat |
| `mono-sm` | 12 / 16 px | 400 | 0 | IDs, hashes, log lines |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-008 | Field surfaces (GAP, GRD, guard-facing parts of AAP) shall not use any token below `body` (14 px) for content, and shall use `body-lg` (16 px) as their default body size. |
| SUR-UIX-009 | Indic scripts shall render at the same token size with a line-height increase of +2 px for `body` and `body-lg` to accommodate matras and conjuncts without clipping. |

#### 27.2.2 Spacing, grid and breakpoints

**8pt spacing scale.** Every margin, padding, gap and offset comes from this scale. 4 px exists only for icon-to-text gaps and dense table cell padding.

| Token | px | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| `space-0` | 0 | — |
| `space-1` | 4 | Icon↔label gap, dense cell vertical padding |
| `space-2` | 8 | Inside chips and small buttons, form field internal padding |
| `space-3` | 12 | Between related controls, list item padding |
| `space-4` | 16 | Card padding (mobile), between form fields |
| `space-5` | 24 | Card padding (desktop), between form groups |
| `space-6` | 32 | Between page sections |
| `space-7` | 48 | Page top padding, between major blocks |
| `space-8` | 64 | Marketing section rhythm |
| `space-9` | 96 | Marketing hero spacing |

**Grid and breakpoints.**

| Breakpoint | Range | Columns | Gutter | Margin | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `xs` mobile-sm | 320–359 px | 4 | 16 px | 16 px | Floor. Every field screen must work at 320 px. |
| `sm` mobile | 360–767 px | 4 | 16 px | 16 px | Primary field-app target (360×800 is the reference device). |
| `md` tablet | 768–1023 px | 8 | 24 px | 24 px | Supervisor tablets, client portal on iPad. |
| `lg` laptop | 1024–1439 px | 12 | 24 px | 32 px | Minimum supported for OPS and Agency Portal. |
| `xl` desktop | 1440–1919 px | 12 | 24 px | 48 px | Reference desktop for operations surfaces (1440×900). |
| `2xl` wide | ≥1920 px | 12 | 32 px | 64 px, max content 1680 px | Command Center wall displays use a separate full-bleed layout, not this container. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-011 | Operations surfaces (OPS, CMD, AGN web/desktop) shall declare a minimum supported viewport of 1024×720 and shall show an explicit "This screen needs a larger window" state below it, rather than degrading into an unusable layout. |
| SUR-UIX-012 | Field surfaces shall be fully functional at 320 px width and at 200% OS font scaling without horizontal scrolling or clipped controls. |
| SUR-UIX-013 | All spacing shall come from the 8pt scale; arbitrary pixel values in layout code shall fail lint. |
| SUR-UIX-014 | Command Center wall/large-display layouts shall be a distinct layout mode with its own type scale multiplier (×1.5) and no interactive-only affordances (hover tooltips). |
