| `brand-navy-600` | `#24508C` | Primary button hover | 6.1:1 on white — AA normal text |
| `brand-steel-500` | `#4A6A8F` | Secondary accents, chart series 2, icon default on light | 4.6:1 on white — AA normal text |
| `brand-steel-300` | `#93A9C2` | Borders on navy surfaces, disabled on dark | Decorative / large text only |
| `brand-steel-100` | `#DCE4EE` | Selected row tint, subtle fill | Background only |
| `base-050` | `#F6F7F9` | **Canonical light base** (canon §4) — app background | — |
| `base-000` | `#FFFFFF` | Surface / card background | — |
| `base-100` | `#EDEFF3` | Table header, secondary surface, zebra row | — |
| `base-200` | `#DFE3E9` | Divider, input border (rest) | 1.5:1 vs white — non-text only |
| `base-300` | `#C3C9D2` | Input border (hover), disabled border | — |
| `base-500` | `#6B7480` | Secondary text, placeholder, icon muted | 5.1:1 on `base-050` — AA normal text |
| `base-700` | `#3A424E` | Body text secondary | 9.9:1 on `base-050` |
| `base-900` | `#161B22` | Primary text | 15.9:1 on `base-050` — AAA |

**Semantic colours.** Each has a 700 (text/icon on light), 500 (fill), 100 (tint background) and a paired on-colour.

| Semantic | 700 (text) | 500 (fill) | 100 (tint bg) | Contrast of 700 on 100 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Success | `#146B3A` | `#1E9E55` | `#E4F5EB` | 6.8:1 — AA |
| Warning | `#8A5A00` | `#C98A00` | `#FBF1DC` | 6.2:1 — AA |
| Danger | `#A11B1B` | `#D93A3A` | `#FBE7E7` | 7.1:1 — AA |
| Info | `#1B4A8A` | `#2A6BC4` | `#E6EEF9` | 7.4:1 — AA |
| Neutral | `#3A424E` | `#6B7480` | `#EDEFF3` | 9.1:1 — AAA |

**Status colour convention.** This maps the canon's exact status vocabulary (canon §3) to one visual treatment used everywhere. This table is normative; no product may invent a status colour.

| Status | Text/icon hex | Tint bg hex | Pill style | Contrast (text on tint) | Meaning cue |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | `#3A424E` | `#EDEFF3` | Dashed 1px border `#C3C9D2`, neutral text | 9.1:1 | Not yet real |
| Pending | `#8A5A00` | `#FBF1DC` | Solid tint, no border | 6.2:1 | Waiting on someone |
| Active | `#146B3A` | `#E4F5EB` | Solid tint + 6 px leading dot `#1E9E55` | 6.8:1 | Live and healthy |
| In Progress | `#1B4A8A` | `#E6EEF9` | Solid tint + animated 2-dot indicator (respects reduced motion) | 7.4:1 | Work is happening now |
| Completed | `#245C4A` | `#E3F1EC` | Solid tint + check glyph | 7.0:1 | Finished, no action |
| Verified | `#0F5C6B` | `#E0F2F5` | Solid tint + shield-check glyph | 7.2:1 | A human confirmed it |
| Rejected | `#A11B1B` | `#FBE7E7` | Solid tint + cross glyph | 7.1:1 | Failed a decision; reason always adjacent |
| Expiring | `#9A4A00` | `#FCEDDF` | Solid tint + clock glyph + days-remaining number | 6.4:1 | Time-bound, act now |
| Expired | `#7A1F1F` | `#F3DEDE` | Solid tint + strikethrough of the date, not the label | 8.3:1 | Past the deadline |
| Suspended | `#5B3E8A` | `#EFE9F8` | Solid tint + pause glyph | 7.6:1 | Deliberately halted, reversible |
| Cancelled | `#4C535D` | `#E7E9ED` | Solid tint, label in strikethrough | 8.4:1 | Ended by choice |
| Failed | `#A11B1B` | `#FBE7E7` | Solid tint + alert glyph + retry affordance where applicable | 7.1:1 | System could not complete it |
| Archived | `#5A626D` | `#EDEFF3` | Outline pill, 1 px `#C3C9D2`, 70% opacity label | 5.6:1 | Out of active use, still readable |

Rejected and Failed share a hue deliberately — both mean "did not succeed" — but are always distinguished by glyph and by the mandatory adjacent reason (Rejected) or retry affordance (Failed). Suspended is the only status with its own hue family, because it is the only reversible punitive state and must never be confused with Expired.

**Alert severity colours** (canon §3 severities):

| Severity | Hex (fill) | Text on fill | Tint bg | Where used | Contrast |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P0 Critical | `#C1121F` | `#FFFFFF` | `#FBE3E5` | SOS, life-safety, total outage. Full-width banner, sound, persistent until acknowledged. | 6.5:1 white on fill |
| P1 High | `#D9640A` | `#FFFFFF` | `#FCEEE1` | Unstaffed post, missed wake check, payment blocked. Banner + badge + push. | 4.6:1 white on fill (large text only; body text uses `#8A3E00` on tint at 6.9:1) |
| P2 Medium | `#C98A00` | `#161B22` | `#FBF1DC` | Late check-in, document expiring, SLA drift. Badge + list highlight. | 10.1:1 dark on fill |
| P3 Informational | `#2A6BC4` | `#FFFFFF` | `#E6EEF9` | Roster published, invoice generated. Toast or feed only, never a banner. | 5.2:1 white on fill |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-015 | Colour shall never be the sole carrier of meaning. Every status pill carries a text label; every severity carries a glyph and a label; every chart series carries a direct label or pattern. |
| SUR-UIX-016 | The status colour convention table is normative across all products; introducing a new status requires a canon change, not a local colour. |
| SUR-UIX-017 | Body text shall meet WCAG 2.1 AA 4.5:1 against its background; large text (≥18.66 px bold or ≥24 px) and non-text UI components shall meet 3:1. Every token pair shipped in the system carries a measured ratio in the token documentation. |
| SUR-UIX-018 | P0 and P1 treatments shall be reserved exclusively for their severities; no marketing, promotional or informational element may use `#C1121F` or `#D9640A` as a primary fill. |
| SUR-UIX-019 | Charts shall use a colour-blind-safe categorical ramp (`#1B3A66`, `#2A9D8F`, `#E9A23B`, `#8E5EA2`, `#4A6A8F`, `#C1121F` reserved for negative/critical series only) and shall be legible in greyscale. |

**Dark mode stance.** `[RECOMMENDED]`

| Surface | Stance | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Command Center (CMD) console | **Dark mode is the default and is required at launch.** | Operators work 12-hour shifts in a dimmed room facing wall displays; a `#F6F7F9` field of view for 12 hours is a genuine fatigue and glare problem. |
| Guard App (GAP) | **Dark mode required from Phase 2**, with an automatic night-shift switch tied to the shift schedule, not just OS setting. | Night guards use the app in darkness; a white screen destroys night vision and marks the guard's position. This is a safety matter, not a preference. |
| OPS, Agency Portal, Admin App, Agency App | **Phase 3**, OS-preference driven, opt-out available. | Desirable, not urgent. |
| WEB, TRN, CPT, CAP | **Light only in V1.** `[FUTURE]` | Marketing and client surfaces gain little; the cost is in imagery and content. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-020 | Dark mode shall be implemented as a token re-mapping, never as a per-component override; every semantic token has a dark value in the same package. |
| SUR-UIX-021 | Dark-mode surfaces shall use elevation-by-lightness (`#0E1218` base → `#161B22` surface → `#1E242D` raised), never shadows, and shall keep status hues at the same semantic meaning with lightness adjusted to hold ≥4.5:1. |
| SUR-UIX-022 | Guard App shall switch to dark automatically at the start of a night shift and offer a one-tap override that persists for that shift only. |

#### 27.2.4 Elevation, radius, borders, motion

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `elev-0` | none, 1 px border `#DFE3E9` | Cards on operations surfaces (borders read better in dense layouts than shadows) |
| `elev-1` | `0 1px 2px rgba(11,27,51,.08)` | Raised card, sticky table header |
| `elev-2` | `0 4px 12px rgba(11,27,51,.10)` | Dropdown, popover, autocomplete |
| `elev-3` | `0 12px 32px rgba(11,27,51,.16)` | Modal, drawer |
| `elev-4` | `0 24px 48px rgba(11,27,51,.22)` | Command Center P0 takeover |
| `radius-sm` | 4 px | Inputs, buttons, pills on desktop |
| `radius-md` | 8 px | Cards, modals, dropdowns |
| `radius-lg` | 12 px | Mobile cards, sheets, field-app buttons |
| `radius-full` | 999 px | Avatars, status dots, chips on mobile |
| `border-hairline` | 1 px `#DFE3E9` | Table rules, dividers |
| `focus-ring` | 2 px `#24508C` + 2 px offset, plus 1 px `#FFFFFF` inner ring on dark | Visible focus, never removed |

| Motion token | Duration / easing | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `motion-instant` | 0 ms | State toggles in dense tables |
| `motion-fast` | 120 ms `cubic-bezier(.2,0,.38,.9)` | Hover, button press, checkbox |
| `motion-base` | 200 ms same easing | Dropdown, tooltip, toast in |
| `motion-slow` | 320 ms `cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1)` | Drawer, modal, sheet |
| `motion-none` | All of the above collapse to 0 ms when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` | Accessibility |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-023 | No animation shall exceed 320 ms; no looping animation shall run for more than 3 cycles except a live-data pulse, which shall be suppressible and is suppressed by `prefers-reduced-motion`. |
| SUR-UIX-024 | Focus shall always be visible; `outline: none` without a replacement ring shall fail lint. |
| SUR-UIX-025 | Data updates in live views shall not animate row position; a changed row flashes its background tint for 600 ms and settles, so an operator's click target does not move under their cursor. |

#### 27.2.5 Iconography

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Set | One open icon set at 24×24 with a 20×20 and 16×16 optical variant; 2 px stroke at 24, 1.75 px at 20, 1.5 px at 16. `[RECOMMENDED]` a single library (e.g. Lucide-class) extended with ~30 domain icons. |
| Domain icons required | Guard, Post, Site, Shift, Roster, Patrol, Checkpoint, Wake check, SOS, Incident, Attendance, Licence, Tender, Bid, Payroll, Invoice, Wallet, Verification shield, Agency, Branch, Command Center, Geofence, Armed/Unarmed distinction. |
| Rules | Icons are never the sole label for a destructive or infrequent action. Icon-only buttons are permitted only for: close, more-menu, search, back, and table row expand — all with `aria-label` and tooltip. |
| Status glyphs | The status pill glyph set is fixed by the table in §27.2.3 and shall not vary by product. |
| Field app | Icons on GAP are 28×28 minimum with a text label beneath; no icon-only navigation. |

---

### 27.3 Component library

Every component below specifies **anatomy → variants → states → usage rules → accessibility**. Products reference these names; they do not redefine them.

#### 27.3.1 Buttons

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Anatomy | `[optional leading icon] label [optional trailing icon/count]`, horizontal padding `space-3` (sm) / `space-4` (md) / `space-5` (lg), radius `radius-sm` on desktop, `radius-lg` on field surfaces. |
| Variants | **Primary** (navy-700 fill, white label) — one per screen region, the expected action. **Secondary** (white fill, 1 px `#C3C9D2` border, `#161B22` label). **Tertiary/ghost** (no fill, navy-700 label) — for low-emphasis inline actions. **Destructive** (danger-500 fill `#D93A3A`, white label) — only for delete/terminate/cancel-with-consequence. **Destructive-secondary** (white fill, `#A11B1B` border and label) — for destructive actions in a list of options. **Link** (underlined text) — navigation only, never a state change. |
| Sizes | `sm` 28 px height (dense tables, inline row actions) · `md` 36 px (default desktop) · `lg` 44 px (forms, primary page actions) · `xl` 56 px (field surfaces, one-tap actions). |
| States | Rest · Hover (−1 lightness step) · Active/pressed (−2 steps, no scale transform) · Focus (focus ring) · Disabled (40% opacity, `cursor: not-allowed`, **always paired with a tooltip or helper text stating why**) · Loading (spinner replaces leading icon, label persists, button width locked to prevent layout shift) · Success-transient (checkmark for 1.2 s after an inline save). |
| Usage rules | Exactly one Primary per view region. Never place Primary and Destructive adjacent without a separator. Label must be a verb phrase naming the outcome (§27.10). A button that opens a dialog ends in "…" only in desktop menus. Disabled is preferred to hidden when the user could plausibly expect the action; hidden is preferred when the action is outside their role (see SUR-UIX-045). |
| Accessibility | Native `<button>`; minimum 44×44 px hit area on touch even when visually 36 px (padding expands the target); loading state announces via `aria-busy`; disabled buttons remain focusable when they carry an explanation (use `aria-disabled` rather than `disabled`). |

#### 27.3.2 Inputs, selects, pickers

| Component | Anatomy / variants | Key states | Usage rules | Accessibility |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Text input | Label (always visible, above), optional helper, field (40 px desktop / 48 px field), optional prefix/suffix (₹, %, +91), character counter where limited | Rest, hover, focus, filled, error (danger border + message below + icon), warning, disabled, read-only (no border, `base-100` fill), loading (async validation) | Placeholder is never a label. Helper text is persistent, not a tooltip. Error text replaces helper text and names the fix. Inline validation fires on blur, not on keystroke, except for length counters and format masks | `<label for>` always; error linked by `aria-describedby`; `aria-invalid`; never rely on red alone |
| Numeric / money input | Right-aligned, tabular numerals, `₹` prefix, lakh-grouped display, paise-precise storage | Same + out-of-range | No spinners for money. Paste of `1,20,000` or `₹1.2L` is parsed. Negative amounts shown in `#A11B1B` with a minus, never parentheses | `inputmode="decimal"`, announce the currency |
| Phone input | Fixed `+91` prefix, 10-digit field, auto-strips spaces/dashes/leading 0 | Invalid (not starting 6–9), duplicate-detected | Never a country dropdown in V1 (INR/India only); paste tolerant | `inputmode="tel"`, `autocomplete="tel"` |
| OTP input | 6 single-character boxes, auto-advance, paste fills all, auto-submit on complete, resend timer below | Entering, verifying, incorrect (shake suppressed under reduced motion; border + message instead), expired, locked | Never obscure the digits. Resend is a button with a live countdown, not a disabled link | One `<input>` with `autocomplete="one-time-code"` and visual boxes, or six inputs with a grouped label |
| Select | Native on mobile; custom listbox on desktop with type-ahead; ≤7 options renders as radio group instead | Open, filtered, empty-result, loading, error | Options exceeding 12 gain a search field. Never nest more than one level. Multi-select shows chips with individual remove and an "n selected" summary above 3 | `role="listbox"`, arrow-key navigation, `aria-activedescendant`, announces count |
| Combobox / entity picker | Async search over the entity types of §26.3, showing avatar/icon + primary + secondary line | Idle, searching, results, no-results (with a create action if permitted), error, selected | Always permission-filtered (SUR-FRQ-055). Recent selections shown before typing | Announce result count on each debounce settle |
| Date picker | Text field (`DD MMM YYYY`) + calendar popover; week starts Monday; Indian public + tenant holidays marked; quick ranges (Today, Yesterday, This week, This month, Last month, Custom) | Rest, open, invalid, out-of-allowed-range (disabled dates carry a tooltip reason) | Typing a date must always work without opening the calendar. Ranges use a single two-month calendar with a clear start/end affordance | Full keyboard grid navigation; each day announces its full date and any disabled reason |
| Time picker | 15-minute step list by default with free entry allowed; 12-hour on field surfaces, 24-hour on ops | Same | Shift times snap to the tenant's shift template values with an override | Announce as "09:00 PM" not "21" on field surfaces |
| Date-time range (shift/booking) | Start date+time, end date+time, computed duration shown live, overnight indicator | Invalid (end ≤ start), overlapping (BR-001), too long | Duration is always displayed and is the thing users check; overnight shifts show "+1 day" explicitly | Duration announced on change |
| File upload | Drop zone + browse button; per-file row with thumbnail, name, size, progress, status, remove; camera-first on mobile | Idle, dragging, uploading (per file %), scanning, success, failed (with retry), rejected-type, too-large, quarantined | Accepted types and size limit stated **before** selection. Failures are per file, never batch-fatal (SUR-FRQ-099). Camera capture is the default action on GAP | Drop zone is also a button; progress announced politely; error names the file |
| Toggle / switch | 20×36 px, label to the left on desktop, right on mobile | On, off, disabled, pending (applies async, shows a small spinner, reverts on failure with a toast) | Only for immediate, reversible settings. Anything requiring Save uses a checkbox | `role="switch"`, `aria-checked` |
| Checkbox / radio | 20×20 px (24×24 on field), 44 px touch target | Rest, hover, checked, indeterminate (checkbox only), focus, disabled, error | Indeterminate only for parent-of-partial-selection. Radio groups always have a default or an explicit "None" | Grouped in `<fieldset>` with `<legend>` |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-026 | Labels shall always be visible; placeholder-as-label shall fail design review. |
| SUR-UIX-027 | Validation shall be field-level on blur and form-level on submit; a failed submit shall move focus to the first error and list all errors in a summary at the top of the form. |
| SUR-UIX-028 | Every disabled control shall be able to explain itself: a tooltip, helper text, or adjacent message stating the condition that would enable it. |
| SUR-UIX-029 | Any input that accepts an identifier (mobile, GSTIN, PAN, IFSC, licence, vehicle) shall apply a format mask and a checksum/shape validation client-side, and shall never block paste. |

#### 27.3.3 Tables

The single most important desktop component. Used for guards, rosters, invoices, tickets, tenders, audit logs.

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Anatomy | Toolbar (search, filters, saved views, density toggle, column chooser, bulk-action bar when selected, export) → header row (sticky) → body rows → footer (pagination + selected count + totals row where applicable). |
| Density | **Compact** 32 px rows / `space-1` vertical cell padding — default on OPS and Agency Portal. **Comfortable** 44 px — default on client surfaces. **Relaxed** 56 px — tablet/touch. Density is a user preference persisted per table per user. |
| Columns | Column chooser with reorder and pin (left/right); a minimum column set that cannot be hidden (identifier + status); horizontal scroll with the first 1–2 columns pinned; column widths resizable and persisted. |
| Sorting | Single-column by default, shift-click for a second sort key; sort indicator in the header with the sort order number when multi; server-side sorting always (never client-side on a paged set, which would sort only the visible page — a classic defect). |
| Row actions | Up to 2 inline icon actions on hover/focus + an overflow "⋯" menu; on touch, actions live in the overflow only. Row click opens the detail (or the drawer); action buttons stop propagation. A destructive row action is always in the overflow, never inline. |
| Bulk selection | Header checkbox selects the visible page, with an explicit "Select all N matching this filter" link that appears after page-select; the bulk bar states the exact count and scope ("47 guards selected — all matching current filter"). |
| Pagination vs infinite scroll | **Pagination for every operations table** (25/50/100 per page, page jump, total count) because operators need position, totals, and reproducible URLs. **Infinite scroll only** for reverse-chronological feeds (activity, chat, notifications, audit stream) where position is meaningless. Never infinite scroll on anything a user must export, count, or bulk-select. |
| Totals | Money and count columns can show a footer total; the footer states its scope explicitly ("Total on this page" vs "Total for all 1,284 rows"). |
| Empty / loading / error | Per §27.4; skeleton rows equal in height to the chosen density, header rendered immediately so the table does not resize on load. |
| Accessibility | Real `<table>` semantics with `<th scope>`; sortable headers are buttons announcing the current sort; row selection announces the running count; sticky header does not trap focus; horizontal scroll region is keyboard-scrollable and labelled. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-030 | Sorting, filtering and pagination shall be server-side and reflected in the URL, so any table state is shareable and reproducible. |
| SUR-UIX-031 | A "select all matching filter" selection shall re-state its exact scope and count in every subsequent confirmation dialog. |
| SUR-UIX-032 | No operations table shall use infinite scroll; no chronological feed shall use pagination. |
| SUR-UIX-033 | Every table shall support keyboard row navigation (`j`/`k` or arrows), `Enter` to open, `x` to toggle selection, and `Esc` to clear selection. |

#### 27.3.4 Cards and KPI/stat tiles

| Component | Specification |
|---|---|
| Card | `base-000` surface, `radius-md`, `elev-0` (border) on ops surfaces / `elev-1` on client surfaces, padding `space-5` desktop / `space-4` mobile. Anatomy: header (title `heading-3`, optional status pill, optional overflow menu) → body → footer actions. A card with a single action puts it in the footer right; a clickable card is a `<button>`/link wrapping the whole surface with a visible focus ring. |
| KPI / stat tile | Anatomy: `overline` label · `numeric-xl` value · delta chip (▲/▼ + % + comparison period) · optional sparkline (48×20) · optional status dot. Fixed height 112 px desktop / 96 px mobile so a row of tiles never ragged-aligns. |
| KPI rules | Every tile is clickable and drills through to the filtered list that produced the number — a KPI that cannot be drilled into is not permitted (SUR-UIX-034). Every tile states its period ("Today", "MTD", "Last 30 days") and its freshness ("as of 09:42"). Deltas state the comparison basis. A tile whose data failed to load shows a partial-data state (§27.4.7), never a zero. |
| Anti-pattern | Never render `0` where the true meaning is "unknown" or "not loaded". Never show a percentage without its denominator available on hover or drill-through. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-034 | Every KPI tile shall be drillable to the record set behind it, in one click, with the same filters applied. |
| SUR-UIX-035 | Every KPI tile shall display its period and its data freshness timestamp. |

#### 27.3.5 Navigation

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Top bar (desktop) | Height 56 px, `brand-navy-900` on operations surfaces, white on client surfaces. Contents left→right: product mark · business/tenant context switcher · scope selector (where applicable) · global search (centred, max 640 px) · alert bell with live P0/P1 count · AI launcher · help · user menu (with role switcher and active-role label). |
| Sidebar (desktop) | 240 px expanded / 56 px collapsed (icon-only with tooltips), collapse state persisted. Grouped items with a group label; max 2 levels; active item marked with a 3 px left bar in `#24508C` plus a background tint. Pinned favourites (max 8) at the top. **Items the role cannot access are absent, not greyed** (see SUR-UIX-045 and SUR-OPS-003). |
| Bottom navigation (mobile apps) | Max 5 items, 56 px height + safe-area inset, icon + label always (never icon-only), active state by fill + label weight. GAP's items are fixed: Duty · Patrol · Report · Requests · Me. |
| Breadcrumbs | Mandatory on any screen deeper than a module root. Truncate the middle, never the last two. Each crumb is a link; the last is plain text. On mobile, only a back affordance with the parent's name. |
| Tabs | Underline style, 40 px height, horizontal scroll with edge fade on mobile; max 7 tabs before converting to a select. Tab state is URL-addressable. Tabs never change the record being viewed, only the aspect of it. |
| Context switcher | A distinct control, never a dropdown buried in the user menu. Shows current tenant/branch and a search when >7 options. Switching is a full context change with a brief confirmation if unsaved work exists (SUR-FRQ-023). |

#### 27.3.6 Badges, chips and status pills

| Component | Specification |
|---|---|
| Status pill | Height 20 px (desktop) / 24 px (mobile), `radius-full`, padding `space-2`, `overline` on desktop / `caption` on mobile, colour strictly per §27.2.3. Optional leading glyph, optional trailing count. Never truncated — if space is short, the pill wins and the adjacent text truncates. |
| Count badge | Circular for ≤2 digits, pill for 3+, capped display at `99+`. On the alert bell, split by severity: a P0 badge is `#C1121F`, P1 `#D9640A`, otherwise neutral. |
| Chip / filter tag | Removable filter representation with the filter name and value ("Branch: Jaipur ✕"); a chip row above the table shows all active filters plus "Clear all". |
| Guard chip / avatar | Avatar (photo or initials on a deterministic colour derived from the ID), name, and one qualifier (employee code, or post). Shows a verification shield when Verified, an amber clock when a deployment-blocking document is Expiring. Clicking opens a hover-card with the guard summary; permission-filtered fields only. |
| Plan badge | Starter / Professional / Enterprise, shown in agency-facing contexts; Enterprise never displays a price (canon §1.4). |

#### 27.3.7 Alerts, banners and toasts

| Component | Use | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Page banner | Persistent, page-level condition the user must know about: degraded service, tenant suspended (read-only), licence expired, subscription past due, impersonation active. | Full width, semantic tint background, icon + heading + one line + up to 2 actions. Dismissible only if the condition is informational; conditions that constrain the user are non-dismissible. |
| Inline alert | Section-level context, e.g. "3 guards on this roster have expiring documents". | Inside the section it concerns, with a direct action ("Review 3"). |
| Toast | Transient confirmation of a user-initiated action. | Bottom-centre on mobile, bottom-left on desktop; 4 s for success, 8 s for warnings, **never auto-dismiss for errors**; max 3 stacked; contains an Undo where the action is undoable (§27.5.8). |
| P0 takeover | SOS and life-safety only, in CMD and ADP. | Full-screen or docked panel with `elev-4`, sound, persistent until an operator acknowledges with an explicit action. Cannot be dismissed by `Esc` or by clicking outside. |
| Snackbar with progress | Long-running background jobs (export, import, bulk action). | Shows job name, progress, and a link to the job centre; survives navigation within the app. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-036 | Error toasts shall never auto-dismiss and shall always offer either a retry or a route to more detail. |
| SUR-UIX-037 | P0 alerts shall be acknowledged by an explicit action that is recorded with actor and timestamp; no P0 alert shall be dismissible by background click, `Esc`, or timeout. |
| SUR-UIX-038 | At most one banner shall be shown at a time; when multiple conditions apply, the highest severity is shown with a "+n more" affordance opening a list. |

#### 27.3.8 Modals, drawers and sheets

| Component | Use | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| Modal (desktop) | Confirmations, short forms (≤6 fields), single decisions. Widths: `sm` 400 px, `md` 560 px, `lg` 720 px. | Focus trapped, `Esc` closes **unless** unsaved changes exist (then a nested confirm), background click closes only non-destructive modals, focus returns to the trigger. Never nest modals more than one deep. |
| Drawer (desktop) | Record detail alongside a list, filter panels, activity timelines. Widths 400 / 560 / 720 px, right-side. | The list stays interactive behind it; the drawer's URL is addressable; opening a second record replaces content without closing/reopening. |
| Bottom sheet (mobile) | Action lists, pickers, short forms. | Drag-to-dismiss, three snap points where content is long, safe-area padding, primary action pinned to the bottom above the inset. |
| Full-screen (mobile) | Anything longer than 3 fields, wizards, camera flows. | Explicit Cancel and Save in a fixed header/footer; back gesture is treated as Cancel with a confirm if dirty. |

#### 27.3.9 Maps

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Uses | Live guard positions (CMD, AGN, CPT within contracted scope), site geofences, patrol routes and checkpoints, SOS location with accuracy radius, coverage/heat views. |
| Markers | Guard: circular avatar chip with a status ring (green Active on duty, amber Late/idle, red SOS, grey offline with last-seen age). Site: square pin. Checkpoint: small diamond, filled when scanned. Cluster markers show counts and split by worst status colour. |
| Layers | Base map (muted greyscale style so status colours dominate) · geofences (2 px stroke, 8% fill) · routes (3 px, direction arrows) · heat (optional) · labels. Layer toggles are persistent per user. |
| Accuracy honesty | Every position shows an accuracy radius when >25 m and a "last updated Xs/m ago" label; a position older than 5 minutes renders desaturated with an explicit age. |
| Interaction | Click marker → hover-card → "Open record"; box-select for bulk actions on operations maps; follow-mode for a single guard during an incident; north-up only (no rotation) on operations surfaces. |
| Performance | Clustering above 200 markers; viewport-bounded queries; updates via the real-time channel (§34), never polling; a degraded mode that switches to a list when the map fails to load. |
| Accessibility | Every map has an equivalent list view carrying the same records and statuses, reachable by keyboard; the map itself is not the only path to the information. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-039 | Every map view shall have a keyboard-and-screen-reader-accessible list equivalent showing the same data set. |
| SUR-UIX-040 | Guard positions shall display their age and accuracy; a stale position shall never be rendered as though it were current. |

#### 27.3.10 Charts, timeline, and the remaining primitives

| Component | Specification |
|---|---|
| Charts | Types permitted: line (trend over time), bar/stacked bar (comparison, composition), horizontal bar (ranked lists), donut (max 5 slices, always with values), sparkline (in tiles), gauge only for utilisation against a defined capacity. Every chart: direct series labels preferred over legends; axis units stated; zero baseline for bars; no dual y-axes; no 3D; no pie beyond 5 slices. Hover shows a tooltip; the underlying data is downloadable as CSV; an accessible table equivalent is available. Colour ramp per SUR-UIX-019. |
| Timeline | Vertical, newest-first by default with a toggle. Each entry: time (absolute + relative), actor avatar/name, action sentence, optional diff expander, optional attachment thumbnails, and a system/human/AI origin marker. Grouped by day with sticky day headers. Filterable by actor, type and date. Used for audit log, incident history, ticket history, and record activity. |
| Avatar | 24 / 32 / 40 / 64 px; photo, else initials on a deterministic hue; verification shield overlay bottom-right where applicable. Never used as the only identifier — always paired with a name in lists. |
| Empty state | Illustration (line, single-colour, never a stock cartoon) or an icon, a heading naming what is absent, one line explaining why it might be absent, and the single most useful action. Variants: no-data-yet, no-results-for-filter, no-access-relevant, all-clear (a *good* empty, e.g. "No open alerts"). |
| Skeleton loading | Grey `#EDEFF3` blocks matching final layout geometry, subtle shimmer (suppressed under reduced motion), shown only after 200 ms of latency to avoid a flash, and never for more than 10 s before converting to the error or slow state. |
| Stepper / wizard chrome | Horizontal on desktop (max 6 steps), compact "Step 2 of 5" on mobile, with completed steps navigable backwards and forward navigation gated by validation. Progress is saved per step (§27.5.7). |
| Tooltip / hover-card | Tooltip: ≤80 characters, 300 ms delay, keyboard-focus triggered too. Hover-card: rich summary of an entity, 500 ms delay, never contains the only path to an action. |
| Job centre | A global panel listing running/recent background jobs (exports, imports, bulk actions) with status, progress, result download and error report. Reachable from the top bar whenever a job is active. |

#### 27.3.11 Impersonation banner (special component)

Because SUR-FRQ-029 makes impersonation a platform capability, its UI is normative: a fixed 40 px bar at the very top of the viewport in `#5B3E8A` with white text, reading `Viewing as Rajesh Kumar (Agency Admin, Sharma Security) — read-only — 42 min remaining`, with an "Exit" button. It cannot be dismissed, it offsets all fixed layout, and it appears on every screen including modals and print output.

---
### 27.4 Universal state specifications

Every screen archetype (§27.11) must define nine states. A screen shipped without all nine specified is incomplete. The table below defines each state's purpose, layout, copy rules, and a worked example.

#### 27.4.1 Empty state

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| When | The query succeeded and returned zero records. |
| Layout | Centred within the content region: icon or line illustration (96 px), `heading-2` title, `body` explanation (max 2 lines), one primary action, one optional secondary/learn-more link. |
| Copy rules | Title names what is absent in the user's terms, not the system's. Explanation says why it might be empty. Action is the single most likely next step, permission-checked — if the user cannot create, the action becomes guidance, not a disabled button. Never apologise. Never say "No data". |
| Sub-variants | **First-use empty** (nothing exists yet) · **Filtered empty** (records exist but not for this filter — must offer "Clear filters" and state the active filter count) · **All-clear empty** (a good outcome; use success tint and a calm tone) · **Not-yet-empty** (data will arrive later, e.g. "Attendance for today appears after the first check-in at 06:00"). |
| Worked example — Agency Portal → Guards, first use | Icon: guard. Title: **"No guards added yet"**. Body: "Add your first guard, or import your existing team from a spreadsheet." Primary: `Add guard`. Secondary: `Import from spreadsheet`. |
| Worked example — filtered | Title: **"No guards match these filters"**. Body: "You have 284 guards. None are Active in Jaipur with an expiring licence." Primary: `Clear filters (3)`. |
| Worked example — all-clear | Title: **"No open alerts"**. Body: "All 42 posts across 11 sites are staffed. Last checked 09:41." Success tint, no action. |

#### 27.4.2 Loading state

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| When | A request is in flight. |
| Layout | 0–200 ms: nothing (avoid flash). 200 ms–10 s: skeleton matching the final geometry — table header rendered, skeleton rows at the chosen density; KPI tiles as grey blocks of the right height; charts as a grey rectangle with axis stubs. >10 s: convert to the **slow state** — keep the skeleton, add a line: "Still loading — this is taking longer than usual" plus a Cancel action where cancellation is meaningful. |
| Copy rules | Never "Please wait". Never a percentage you cannot compute honestly. If progress is known (imports, exports, bulk actions), show real progress with counts, not a decorative bar. |
| Partial loading | Regions load independently; a slow region shows its own skeleton while the rest of the page is usable. The page never blocks on its slowest widget. |
| Worked example — OPS live board | Header, filter bar and KPI labels render immediately; the 12 KPI values show skeletons; the map shows a grey canvas with a "Locating 284 guards…" caption; the alert list renders first because it is the safety-critical region and is fetched with priority. |

#### 27.4.3 Error state

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| When | The request failed, or the operation could not complete. |
| Layout | Scoped to the smallest region that failed. Page-level error: icon, title, plain cause, Retry (primary), and a support route carrying a correlation ID. Region-level: inline alert inside the region with Retry. Field-level: message under the field. |
| Copy rules | Say what happened, why (in user terms), and what to do next. Never show a stack trace, an HTTP code alone, or "Something went wrong" without a next step. Always expose a short correlation ID the user can quote to support (`Ref: 7K3-B2Q9`). Distinguish "we failed" from "you can't" (see permission-denied, §27.4.9). |
| Retry semantics | Idempotent reads retry automatically twice with backoff before showing an error. Writes never auto-retry; the user retries explicitly, and the client uses an idempotency key so a double submit cannot double-charge or double-create. |
| Worked example — payment failure | Title: **"Payment didn't go through"**. Body: "Your bank declined the transaction. No money has been taken. You can try another method or retry." Actions: `Try another method` (primary), `Retry`. Footer: "Ref: 7K3-B2Q9 · If this keeps happening, contact support." |
| Worked example — table fetch failure | Inline alert above the table: "Couldn't load guards. Check your connection and try again. `Retry`" — the toolbar and filters stay usable so the user can change the query. |

#### 27.4.4 Success state

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| When | An action completed. |
| Layout | **Small, reversible actions** → toast (4 s) with Undo where applicable. **Significant actions** (roster published, invoice issued, booking confirmed, payroll approved) → an in-page confirmation panel stating what happened, its identifiers, the consequences already triggered, and the 1–3 most likely next actions. **Transactional milestones** (booking paid, contract signed) → a dedicated confirmation screen with a reference number, a receipt/download, and a "what happens next" timeline. |
| Copy rules | State the outcome in past tense with the countable detail: "Roster published for 3 sites, 47 shifts. 47 guards notified." Never a bare "Success". Never celebrate a routine action with animation on an operations surface. |
| Worked example — roster publish | Panel: **"Roster published"**. Detail: "Week of 17–23 Aug · 3 sites · 47 shifts · 41 guards. 41 push notifications sent, 2 guards have no app installed (SMS sent instead)." Next: `View roster`, `Notify supervisors`, `Publish next week`. |

#### 27.4.5 Warning state

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| When | The user may proceed, but there is a consequence, a risk, or a degraded condition they must know about. |
| Layout | Warning tint inline alert positioned adjacent to the decision it affects — not at the top of the page, away from the action. Where the warning gates a submit, it appears above the submit button. |
| Copy rules | State the risk and the quantity. Offer the safer alternative when one exists. Do not block; blocking is an error, not a warning. |
| Worked example — assigning a guard with an expiring document | Inline: "**Licence expires in 6 days.** This guard can be assigned now, but will be blocked from this site from 21 Aug unless the renewed document is verified. `Upload renewal`" |
| Worked example — bulk action scope | "You are about to notify **1,284 guards**. This will send 1,284 push notifications and up to 1,284 SMS. `Review recipients`" |

#### 27.4.6 Confirmation state

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| When | Before an action that is destructive, expensive, irreversible, or affects other people. |
| Layout | Modal (desktop) or bottom sheet (mobile). Title states the action as a question or a statement of consequence; body states exactly what will happen with counts; the confirm button repeats the verb ("Cancel 12 shifts"), never "OK"/"Yes". Destructive confirm uses the destructive button variant. |
| Tiers | **Tier 1 — click confirm** for reversible actions affecting one record. **Tier 2 — click confirm + explicit consequence statement** for actions affecting many records or other people. **Tier 3 — typed confirmation** (type the record name, or the word `DELETE`) for irreversible destruction, tenant-level changes, or anything affecting money already settled. **Tier 4 — typed confirmation + step-up auth + reason** for the SUR-FRQ-010 sensitive action list. |
| Copy rules | Never ask "Are you sure?" alone. Always name what will be affected and whether it can be undone. If it can be undone, say how long the undo window is. |
| Worked example — Tier 3 | Title: **"Archive Sharma Security's tenant?"** Body: "This will end access for 34 users and make 1,842 records read-only. Data is retained and can be restored by Suraksha support within 30 days. Type **Sharma Security** to confirm." Confirm: `Archive tenant` (destructive). |

#### 27.4.7 Partial-data state

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| When | Some of the screen's data loaded and some did not, or some data is stale beyond its freshness budget. |
| Rule | Never present partial data as complete, and never discard the good data because one part failed. |
| Layout | The failed region carries its own inline error and Retry. Any aggregate computed over incomplete data is suppressed or marked: a KPI whose inputs are incomplete shows a "—" with an asterisk and a tooltip naming the missing source, never a wrong number. A stale region shows "as of HH:MM" in `caption` with a warning tint when past budget. |
| Freshness budgets | Live guard position 30 s · attendance counts 60 s · alert counts 15 s · dashboards 5 min · financial summaries 15 min · analytics 24 h. Beyond budget → label; beyond 3× budget → warning tint + explicit "may be out of date". |
| Worked example — Command Center | Alert panel and map are live; the "Attendance today" tile shows "—*" with a tooltip: "Attendance service is not responding. Last known value 1,182 at 09:12. `Retry`". The operator is never shown a plausible but wrong number. |

#### 27.4.8 Offline state

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Scope | Full offline capability is mandatory for GAP only (canon §4). Other clients show a degraded connectivity state. |
| GAP layout | A persistent 32 px bar: `Offline — 3 items waiting to sync`. All capture actions remain available; each captured item shows a per-item sync status (Queued / Syncing / Synced / Failed with reason). The bar becomes `Syncing 3 of 3…` then disappears on completion. A guard must always be able to check in, mark a patrol, and raise an SOS offline — SOS additionally attempts SMS fallback immediately. |
| Other clients | A non-blocking banner: "You're offline. Showing data from 09:41. Changes can't be saved right now." Forms retain entered values; submit is disabled with an explanation; the app retries automatically and confirms when back. |
| Copy rules | Plain, non-alarming, and specific about what still works. Never "Network error". Never lose typed input. |
| Worked example — GAP check-in offline | The check-in completes locally with a green tick and a caption: "Saved on your phone. Will send when you have network." The record shows `Queued`. Server time is applied on receipt and both timestamps are retained (canon §4). |

#### 27.4.9 Permission-denied state

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| The rule | Distinguish three cases and treat them differently: **(a) You cannot see this record because it is not yours** → behave as if it does not exist (404 pattern, SUR-FRQ-037). **(b) You can see the record but cannot perform this action** → the action is visible and disabled with a plain reason, or absent if its presence would leak organisational information. **(c) You have no access to this module** → the module is absent from navigation entirely (SUR-OPS-003), and a direct URL returns a generic "not available" page with a route back. |
| Copy rules | Never say "Access denied" alone; state what the user *can* do. Never name the role or person who does have access unless that is safe and useful ("Ask your Agency Admin to grant Payroll access" is fine; "Only Rajesh can approve this" may not be). Never reveal the existence of out-of-scope records. |
| Worked example — (b) | The `Approve payroll` button is visible and disabled with helper text: "Payroll approval needs the Payroll or Agency Finance role. `Request access`" |
| Worked example — (c) | "This section isn't available for your role. `Go to dashboard`" — with no hint of what the section contains. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-041 | Every screen archetype implementation shall specify all nine states in its design spec; a design review shall reject a screen missing any of them. |
| SUR-UIX-042 | No aggregate shall be displayed when its inputs are incomplete; the partial-data treatment shall be used instead. |
| SUR-UIX-043 | No error message shall consist solely of an HTTP status, an exception name, or "Something went wrong"; every error shall carry a cause in user terms, a next action, and a correlation reference. |
| SUR-UIX-044 | Offline capture on GAP shall never lose data and shall always show a per-item sync status; a failed sync shall be retryable and shall state its reason in plain language. |
| SUR-UIX-045 | Out-of-scope records shall be indistinguishable from non-existent records in every surface, including error copy and response timing. |

---

### 27.5 Interaction standards

#### 27.5.1 Global search behaviour

Defined functionally in §26.3. UX-normative points: `/` or `Cmd/Ctrl+K` opens an overlay anchored to the top bar; the input is pre-focused; results appear from the third character with a 200 ms debounce; grouped by entity type with at most 5 per group; the currently highlighted result shows a right-hand preview panel on `lg`+ viewports; `Enter` opens, `Cmd/Ctrl+Enter` opens in a new tab; recent searches and recently viewed records show before typing; `Esc` closes and returns focus to the previous element. On mobile, search is a full-screen surface with the keyboard raised and results replacing the recents list.

#### 27.5.2 Filters and saved views

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Placement | A filter bar directly above the table/list. Up to 4 high-frequency filters as inline controls; the rest behind a "Filters" button showing an active count. |
| Application | Filters apply immediately on selection (no "Apply" button) for single-select and toggles; multi-select panels apply on close or on an explicit Apply within the panel. |
| Visibility | Active filters always render as removable chips above the results with a "Clear all"; the result count updates with the filter and states the total ("284 of 1,842"). |
| Persistence | The last-used filter set per table per user is restored on return within the session; across sessions, the default view is restored unless a saved view is set as default. |
| Saved views | A named filter+sort+column+density combination. Personal by default; shareable to a role or the whole tenant by users with permission. A shared view respects the viewer's permissions — it never grants access, only pre-filters (SUR-FRQ-066). Views are listed in a dropdown next to the page title with the active one shown. |
| URL | Every filter state is URL-encoded and shareable. |

#### 27.5.3 Bulk actions

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Selection | Checkbox column; header checkbox selects the visible page; a distinct link offers "Select all N matching this filter". The selection scope is always stated in words in the bulk bar. |
| Bulk bar | Appears docked at the bottom of the content region when ≥1 row is selected: "47 selected" + up to 4 actions + overflow + "Clear selection". It never covers the last table row (the table gains bottom padding). |
| Limits | Interactive bulk operations are capped (default 500 rows); above the cap the action becomes a background job with a progress entry in the job centre and an emailed/notified completion. |
| Confirmation | Every bulk action requires a Tier 2 confirmation minimum, restating the exact count and scope. Bulk destructive actions require Tier 3. Bulk actions that notify people must state the notification count and channels. |
| Partial failure | Results are reported per row: "44 updated, 3 skipped (no permission), 0 failed", with a downloadable detail report and a "Retry failed" action. A bulk action never silently drops rows. |
| Undo | Where the action is reversible, an Undo is offered in the completion toast for 10 s and in the job centre for 15 minutes. |

#### 27.5.4 Destructive-action confirmation pattern

Canonical pattern, used identically everywhere:

1. The trigger is a destructive-variant button, always in an overflow menu when inside a table row.
2. A modal opens with: a title naming the action and the object; a body stating **what will be affected (with counts), what will be lost, and whether it is reversible and for how long**; a list preview when >1 object is affected (first 5 + "and 42 more").
3. Confirmation tier per §27.4.6.
4. On confirm, the button enters a loading state; the modal does not close until the server responds, so the user never sees a false success.
5. On success, a toast with Undo (if reversible) and the record removed/updated in place — no full-page reload.
6. On failure, the modal stays open with an inline error and the object untouched.

#### 27.5.5 Optimistic vs pessimistic updates

| Category | Mode | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Toggles of user preferences, read/unread, pin/unpin, filter changes | Optimistic | Zero consequence; instant feel matters. Revert with a toast on failure. |
| Adding a comment/note, uploading a file | Optimistic with a visible pending marker | The user's work must appear immediately; the pending marker keeps it honest. |
| Attendance capture on GAP | Optimistic locally, authoritative on server | Offline-first mandate; local success is shown but labelled as queued until confirmed. |
| Assignments, roster publish, status changes, approvals | **Pessimistic** | Other people act on these; a reverted assignment is worse than a 400 ms wait. |
| Anything financial — payment, refund, payroll, invoice, ledger | **Pessimistic, with idempotency keys** | Canon §4: money is never optimistic. A double-submit must be impossible. |
| Permission and role changes | **Pessimistic** | Security state must never be shown as applied before it is. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-046 | No financial, permission, or safety-critical action shall use an optimistic update; each shall use an idempotency key and shall show a definite server-confirmed outcome. |
| SUR-UIX-047 | Every optimistic update shall carry a visible pending indicator and shall revert with an explicit, non-dismissing error message on failure. |

#### 27.5.6 Autosave vs explicit save

| Context | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Long forms and wizards (guard onboarding, site setup, tender bid, contract) | **Autosave to Draft** every 20 s and on step change and on blur of a changed field, with a `Saved 12:04` indicator near the title. Explicit "Submit"/"Publish" remains the state-changing action. |
| Settings pages | **Explicit Save** with a sticky footer bar that appears when the form is dirty, showing "3 unsaved changes · Discard · Save". |
| Inline table edits | Save on blur/Enter with an inline pending marker; `Esc` reverts. |
| Rich content (blog post, article, notification template) | Autosave draft + version snapshot on each explicit save. |
| Anything financial | Explicit save only, never autosave. |
| Navigating away dirty | A confirm dialog listing what is unsaved; browser `beforeunload` for web; back-gesture interception on mobile. |

#### 27.5.7 Keyboard shortcuts (operations surfaces)

Applies to OPS, CMD, Agency Portal web and desktop. Shortcuts are discoverable via `?` which opens a searchable cheat sheet, and are disabled while a text input has focus (except `Esc` and `Cmd/Ctrl`-modified keys).

| Key | Action | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| `/` or `Ctrl/Cmd+K` | Open global search | Global |
| `g` then `d` / `g` `r` / `g` `g` / `g` `i` / `g` `t` | Go to Dashboard / Rosters / Guards / Invoices / Tickets | Global (sequence within 1.5 s) |
| `j` / `k` or `↓` / `↑` | Move row focus | Lists and tables |
| `Enter` | Open focused row | Lists and tables |
| `x` | Toggle selection of focused row | Tables |
| `Shift+click` | Range-select | Tables |
| `a` | Approve focused item | Approval queues (with confirmation) |
| `r` | Reject focused item (opens reason) | Approval queues |
| `e` | Edit focused record | Detail |
| `n` | New record in the current module | Module |
| `f` | Focus the filter bar | Lists |
| `[` / `]` | Previous / next record while in a detail drawer | Detail |
| `u` | Undo last undoable action | Global (within the undo window) |
| `?` | Shortcut cheat sheet | Global |
| `Esc` | Close overlay, clear selection, cancel edit (in that order) | Global |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-048 | Every operations surface shall implement the shortcut table above with identical bindings; product-specific additions are permitted but must not override these. |
| SUR-UIX-049 | Any workflow performed more than 20 times a day by an operator (approve, reject, assign, acknowledge) shall be completable without a mouse. |

#### 27.5.8 Undo policy

| Action class | Undo | Window |
|---|---|---|
| List-level edits (archive, status change, assignment, tag) | Toast Undo + job-centre undo | 10 s toast, 15 min job centre |
| Bulk operations | Undo the whole batch | 15 min, or until a dependent transaction references the rows |
| Notification/communication already sent | **No undo.** Instead, a "Send correction" action | — |
| Financial postings | **No undo.** Reversal by credit note / reversing ledger entry only (canon §4, BR-003) | — |
| Roster publish | Undo republishes the prior version and sends a correction notification stating the change | 10 min |
| Deletions (soft) | Restore from Archived | Per retention policy (§39) |
| Permission grants | No undo; revoke is a new, separately audited action | — |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-050 | Where undo is unavailable, the confirmation copy shall say so explicitly ("This can't be undone") before the action, not after. |
| SUR-UIX-051 | An undo shall be recorded as its own audit entry referencing the original action; undo is never a silent deletion of history. |

---

### 27.6 Responsive behaviour

#### 27.6.1 The governing rule

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-052 | **Desktop operations screens shall not be reproduced verbatim on mobile.** A dense multi-column operations table, a roster grid, a payroll run screen or the Command Center console shall be re-conceived for mobile as a task-focused subset — or shall be explicitly out of scope on mobile with a clear message and a "open on desktop" route — never shrunk, never horizontally scrolled as a whole. |
| SUR-UIX-053 | Each product shall declare, per screen, one of three mobile stances: **Full** (complete capability), **Focused** (a deliberately reduced task set), or **Not available** (with an explanatory state). §28 records the stance per screen. |

#### 27.6.2 Stance by surface type

| Surface type | Desktop | Tablet (`md`) | Mobile (`sm`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Marketing (WEB, TRN public) | 12-col, full layout | 8-col, stacked hero | Single column, sticky CTA, images lazy and compressed |
| Client portal (CPT) | 12-col, sidebar + content, tables | Sidebar collapses to icons; tables to 5-column subsets | Cards instead of tables; bottom nav; the 6 client tasks only (view sites, view live status, raise request, view invoices, pay, contact) |
| Agency Portal (AGN) | Density-first tables, multi-pane | Two-pane max; roster grid gains horizontal scroll within the grid region only | **Focused**: approvals, alerts, attendance summary, guard lookup, incident view. Roster editing, payroll, migration and bulk operations are **Not available** with a "Continue on desktop" state |
| OPS / CMD | Full console, multi-pane, wall mode | Read-mostly; queues and detail | **Not available** as a whole; the Admin App (ADP) is the mobile expression, with its own task-focused design (§23) |
| Guard App (GAP) | n/a | n/a | Sole target; designed at 360×800 and verified at 320 px |
| Guard platform (GRD) | Simple responsive pages | Same | Full — it is a records-and-fallback surface, deliberately simple |

#### 27.6.3 Adaptation patterns

| Desktop pattern | Tablet | Mobile |
|---|---|---|
| Table | Fewer columns (drop secondary metadata), density Relaxed | Card list: primary label, status pill, 2 key facts, one action; sort/filter via a bottom sheet |
| Multi-column form | 2 columns → 1 | Single column, one logical group per screen with a stepper for long forms |
| Sidebar + content + right rail | Sidebar collapses; right rail becomes a tab | Bottom nav; right rail content becomes a sheet |
| Master–detail | Two-pane persists | Full-screen list → full-screen detail with back |
| Dashboard grid of 12 tiles | 2-across | 1-across, reordered so safety and action tiles come first; charts become sparklines with a "View chart" action |
| Map + list | Split 60/40 | Toggle between map and list, defaulting to list |
| Modal | Modal | Bottom sheet or full-screen |
| Hover affordances | Long-press or always-visible | Always-visible; no functionality behind hover |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-054 | No functionality shall exist only behind hover; every hover affordance shall have a tap/focus equivalent. |
| SUR-UIX-055 | Mobile "Focused" screens shall state what is not available and how to reach it, rather than silently omitting capability. |

---

### 27.7 Field UX standards (guard and supervisor surfaces)

These rules govern GAP, GRD, and the field-facing parts of AAP. They exist because the user is standing at a gate at 02:40, possibly in gloves, possibly in rain, on a ₹7,000 Android phone with 11% battery and a 2G fallback.

#### 27.7.1 Touch, layout and one-tap actions

| Rule | Specification |
|---|---|
| Minimum touch target | 48×48 px for any control; **56×56 px** for the primary duty actions (Check in, Check out, Wake check acknowledge, Scan checkpoint, Report incident) and **72 px height** for the SOS control. |
| Spacing between targets | ≥8 px, and ≥16 px between a confirming and a cancelling action. |
| Thumb zone | The primary action of every screen sits in the bottom third, full-width or near it. Destructive or irreversible actions are never placed in the bottom-right thumb sweep by default. |
| One primary action per screen | The field app never presents two equally weighted actions. Secondary actions are text buttons above the primary or in an overflow. |
| One-tap duty actions | Check in, check out, wake-check acknowledge and checkpoint scan are single-tap from the app's home screen, with no intermediate confirmation. The confirmation is the *result* (a large green state change), not a dialog. |
| SOS | Always reachable: a persistent control on every screen, plus a hardware trigger (volume-key sequence) and a lock-screen path. It requires a deliberate gesture (press-and-hold 1.5 s with haptic ramp) to prevent pocket-fire, and it never asks "Are you sure?". |
| No horizontal scrolling | Ever, at any width from 320 px. |
| Bottom-of-screen safety | A 16 px safe-area margin above the gesture bar; controls never sit under the system bar. |

#### 27.7.2 Input modality

| Modality | Rules |
|---|---|
| Scan-first | QR/NFC scanning is the default for checkpoint, visitor, asset and shift verification; manual code entry is the fallback, always available, never hidden. Camera opens directly into scan mode with a torch toggle prominent. |
| Camera | One tap from the action that needs it; auto-capture guidance (frame outline, blur warning, "hold steady"); compression per SUR-FRQ-088; retake always offered; the photo is shown at the size it will be judged at, not a thumbnail. |
| Voice | Voice notes accepted anywhere free text is accepted, with a large mic button, a visible timer and a waveform; speech-to-text offered in the guard's language where supported (SUR-FRQ-165) with the transcript editable and the audio retained. A guard is never forced to type a paragraph. |
| Typing | Minimised. Prefer chips, pickers, and yes/no. Numeric keypad for numeric fields. Never require punctuation or capitalisation. |
| GPS | Requested only for duty-relevant actions and only during duty hours (§39); the app states in plain language why location is needed at the moment it asks; a weak-signal state offers "capture anyway" with the accuracy recorded rather than blocking the guard from working. |

#### 27.7.3 Environment: glove, sunlight, low light, noise

| Condition | Design response |
|---|---|
| Gloves / wet hands | Large targets (above), no long-press-only affordances for essential actions, no small drag handles, no precise gestures. Every gesture has a button equivalent. |
| Direct sunlight | High-contrast mode with pure `#000000` on `#FFFFFF` for critical screens; minimum 7:1 contrast for duty actions; no thin (300/400) weights for primary labels; large glyphs; no reliance on subtle tints. |
| Night / low light | Dark theme auto-enabled for night shifts (SUR-UIX-022); no full-white screens; red-tinted torch mode consideration; screen brightness never forced to maximum except during an active SOS. |
| Noise | Do not rely on sound alone for wake-check or SOS feedback: pair with strong haptics and a large visual state change. |
| Rain / cracked screens | Tolerate imprecise taps: a 48 px control has a 56 px hit slop; no destructive action adjacent to a frequent action. |

#### 27.7.4 Battery and data awareness

| Rule | Specification |
|---|---|
| Location sampling | Adaptive: 30 s when moving on patrol, 2–5 min when stationary on post, event-driven near geofence boundaries, and off outside duty hours. Never a fixed 5 s poll. |
| Sync | Batch uploads; defer non-urgent uploads (photos, completed patrol logs) to Wi-Fi where the guard opts in; SOS and check-in always sync immediately over any network. |
| Payload | Images compressed to ≤500 KB; API responses paginated small (20 items); no video autoplay; icons and fonts subset per language. |
| Measurement | Target: <4% battery per 8-hour shift attributable to the app in normal patrol conditions `[ASSUMPTION: A-191]`, and <15 MB data per shift excluding photos. Both are tested per release on a reference low-end device. |
| Transparency | A "Data & battery" screen shows this shift's app data use and lets the guard switch photo uploads to Wi-Fi-only. |
| Degradation | On <15% battery, the app enters a low-power mode: reduced location frequency (with a visible notice to the guard and to ops), no background image processing, dark theme forced. Safety functions are never degraded. |

#### 27.7.5 Plain-language copy guide (with Hindi guidance)

| Principle | English | Hindi guidance |
|---|---|---|
| Use the words the workforce uses | "Duty", "Site", "Shift", "Post" — keep the English loanwords; they are the actual field vocabulary | "आज की duty", "साइट पर पहुँचें" — do not translate `duty`/`site`/`shift` into formal Hindi (`कर्तव्य`, `स्थल`) which field staff do not use |
| Short sentences | ≤12 words per sentence, one idea per line | Same; avoid compound Sanskritised constructions |
| Active, direct, respectful | "Check in now" not "Check-in has not been completed" | Use the polite imperative (आप-form): "अभी check-in करें", never the तू-form |
| Never blame | "We didn't get your check-in" not "You failed to check in" | "आपका check-in नहीं मिला" not "आपने check-in नहीं किया" |
| Say what to do | Every message ends with the action | Same; keep the verb at the end naturally |
| Numbers over adjectives | "3 checkpoints left" not "a few remaining" | "3 checkpoint बाकी" |
| No jargon | Never "sync failed", "API", "geofence", "payload" | "अभी नेटवर्क नहीं है। बाद में अपने-आप भेज दिया जाएगा।" |
| Money is always explicit | "₹18,500 credited on 07 Aug" | "₹18,500 · 07 Aug को भेजा गया" |
| Safety copy is calm | "Are you okay? Tap to confirm." | "क्या आप ठीक हैं? Confirm करने के लिए दबाएँ।" |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-056 | Field surfaces shall meet the touch-target minimums above; a control below 48 px in any dimension shall fail design review. |
| SUR-UIX-057 | Every essential field action shall be completable in ≤3 taps from the app home. |
| SUR-UIX-058 | Field copy shall be tested for comprehension with at least 10 guards per major language before release; the 20 safety-critical strings shall reach ≥90% comprehension. |
| SUR-UIX-059 | The Guard App shall never block a duty action (check-in, patrol scan, incident, SOS) because of poor GPS, poor network, or a failed non-critical dependency; it shall capture with recorded quality metadata instead. |

---

### 27.8 Desktop operations UX standards

These govern OPS, CMD and Agency Portal — surfaces where a professional spends a full shift.

| Area | Standard |
|---|---|
| Tables | Compact density default (32 px). Sticky header and sticky first column. Server-side sort/filter/pagination in the URL. Column chooser with pinning. Totals footer with explicit scope. Row actions in an overflow. Keyboard row navigation (SUR-UIX-033). Never infinite scroll. |
| Filters | Persistent filter bar with active-filter chips and counts; saved views with a default; filters never silently reset on navigation within the module. |
| Bulk actions | Per §27.5.3, with an explicit scope statement, a cap of 500 interactive rows, background jobs above it, and per-row result reporting. |
| Keyboard efficiency | The §27.5.7 shortcut set; every queue supports approve/reject from the keyboard; `[`/`]` to move between records without returning to the list; focus is never lost after an action — it moves to the next logical row. |
| Search | Global search from any screen (`/`), plus an in-page search scoped to the current table. Exact identifier paste always resolves to a single record. |
| Dashboards | A fixed top row of ≤6 KPI tiles answering "is anything wrong?" before any chart. Everything drillable (SUR-UIX-034). Period selector applies to the whole dashboard with the period stated on each tile. Freshness stated. No dashboard exceeds one scroll for its decision-critical content. |
| Alerts | A single alert centre with severity grouping, an unread count split by severity, bulk acknowledge with reason where required, and a rule that acknowledging is distinct from resolving. Alert rows link directly to the record and to the rule trace (SUR-FRQ-076). |
| Maps | Per §27.3.9, with a mandatory list equivalent, box-select for bulk actions, and stale-position honesty. |
| Drill-down | A consistent path: KPI tile → filtered list → record detail → related record. Each level preserves the filters of the level above, and a breadcrumb allows returning without re-applying filters. Drill-down opens in a drawer when the user is likely to return to the list, and as a page when they are not. |
| Multi-tasking | Records open in drawers so the list context survives; `Cmd/Ctrl+click` opens a new tab; the job centre keeps long operations visible across navigation. |
| Screen budget | An operator's primary console (Command Center, live board) shall fit its decision-critical content in 1440×900 without scrolling. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-060 | Operations dashboards shall present their decision-critical content above the fold at 1440×900. |
| SUR-UIX-061 | Acknowledging an alert and resolving the underlying condition shall be distinct actions with distinct records; acknowledgement shall never clear an unresolved condition from the board. |
| SUR-UIX-062 | After any list action, keyboard focus shall move to the next logical element, never to the document body. |
