### 27.9 Accessibility

#### 27.9.1 Targets

| Surface class | Target | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Public web (WEB, TRN marketing) | **WCAG 2.1 AA, full** | Public-facing, legally and reputationally exposed; also the surface most likely to be audited by an enterprise buyer. |
| Client portal, Agency Portal, OPS, Customer App, Agency App, Admin App | **WCAG 2.1 AA** for all core flows; AAA contrast where cheap | Professional tools used daily; keyboard and screen-reader support are productivity features, not only accessibility ones. |
| Guard App | **Pragmatic accessibility floor** (below) | Full AA is the goal but the primary constraints are different: literacy, sunlight, gloves, low-end devices. |
| Command Center wall displays | Contrast and size targets only | Non-interactive; no keyboard/SR requirement. |

#### 27.9.2 Requirements

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-063 | Text contrast shall meet 4.5:1 (normal) / 3:1 (large); UI component and graphical-object contrast shall meet 3:1. Every shipped token pair carries a documented ratio. |
| SUR-UIX-064 | All functionality shall be operable by keyboard alone, with a visible focus indicator, a logical tab order, and a skip-to-content link on every page. |
| SUR-UIX-065 | Focus shall be managed on every route change (moved to the page heading), on modal open (first focusable element or the heading), and on modal close (returned to the trigger). Focus shall never be trapped outside a modal. |
| SUR-UIX-066 | Every interactive element shall have an accessible name; icon-only controls shall carry `aria-label`; every form control shall have a programmatically associated label; every image shall have alt text or be marked decorative. |
| SUR-UIX-067 | Live regions shall be used for asynchronous changes: `aria-live="polite"` for result counts, saves and toasts; `aria-live="assertive"` reserved for P0/P1 alerts and errors that block the user. |
| SUR-UIX-068 | Tables shall use semantic markup with header associations; sortable headers shall announce their sort state; data visualisations shall have a text or table equivalent. |
| SUR-UIX-069 | `prefers-reduced-motion` shall disable all non-essential animation, including status-pill pulses, skeleton shimmer and map fly-to transitions; essential motion shall be replaced by an instant state change. |
| SUR-UIX-070 | Layouts shall support 200% browser zoom and 200% OS font scaling without loss of content or functionality; text shall reflow rather than clip, and no content shall require two-dimensional scrolling at 320 px equivalent width. |
| SUR-UIX-071 | Colour shall never be the only means of conveying information (restates SUR-UIX-015 as an accessibility control). |
| SUR-UIX-072 | Session timeouts shall warn at least 2 minutes before expiry with an option to extend; users shall not lose entered data to a timeout. |
| SUR-UIX-073 | Error identification shall be programmatic (`aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`) as well as visual, and an error summary at the top of a form shall link to each errored field. |
| SUR-UIX-074 | Accessibility shall be verified per release by automated scanning (axe-class) on every route plus a manual keyboard and screen-reader pass on the top 20 flows; findings are tracked as defects, not as backlog wishes. |

#### 27.9.3 The pragmatic accessibility floor for field apps

The Guard App serves users who may have low literacy, limited schooling, ageing eyesight, and no experience of screen readers. The realistic floor, mandatory from Phase 2:

| Floor requirement | Detail |
|---|---|
| Text size | Body ≥16 px; honours OS font scaling to 200%; no fixed-height containers that clip scaled text. |
| Contrast | ≥7:1 for all duty-critical controls and labels (beyond AA), because of sunlight. |
| Touch | ≥48 px targets, ≥56 px for duty actions (§27.7.1). |
| Icon + label | Every action carries a text label; icons never stand alone. |
| Language | Full localisation per §26.10 Tier 1–2, with plain-language copy (§27.7.5). |
| Voice | Voice input available wherever text is required; audio playback of critical instructions in the guard's language `[RECOMMENDED]`. |
| Screen reader | TalkBack support for the core duty flows (home, check in/out, wake check, SOS, patrol scan, report) — not required for every settings screen at Phase 2. |
| No time-pressure traps | Except the wake-check window (a safety mechanism), no interaction expires; OTP and session timers warn and allow extension. |
| Error tolerance | Every destructive field action is either undoable or confirmed; no field flow loses captured data on an app kill. |

---

### 27.10 UX writing standards

#### 27.10.1 Tone

Suraksha's voice is **calm, precise, and respectful**. It is a safety company: it must sound like a competent professional on a radio, not like a consumer app. Three registers:

| Register | Where | Character |
|---|---|---|
| Operational | OPS, CMD, Agency Portal, alerts | Terse, factual, quantified. No pleasantries. "3 posts unstaffed at Site 12. Nearest available guard 1.4 km." |
| Field | Guard App, guard notifications | Plain, warm, short, never punitive. "Aapki duty 6 baje shuru hoti hai." |
| Client | WEB, portal, customer app, client notifications | Reassuring and specific. Never hype. "2 guards on duty at Sunrise Apartments. Last patrol 22:15." |

Marketing copy follows the brand line — tagline "TRUSTED. VERIFIED. ALWAYS." and closing line "When India thinks safety, it should think SURAKSHA" (canon §1) — but product copy never uses marketing language.

#### 27.10.2 Error message formula

> **[What happened] + [Why, in user terms] + [What to do next] + [Reference, if support may be needed]**

| Situation | Bad | Good |
|---|---|---|
| Upload rejected | "Invalid file." | "We can't read this file. It's a .exe — we accept PDF, JPG, PNG and HEIC up to 25 MB. Choose another file." |
| Payment declined | "Transaction failed (E502)." | "Your bank declined the payment. No money has been taken. Try another method or retry. Ref: 7K3-B2Q9" |
| Attendance out of geofence | "Location error." | "You're 340 m from Sunrise Apartments. Move closer to the gate and check in again, or tap 'I'm at a different location' to tell your supervisor." |
| Roster conflict | "Conflict detected." | "Ravi Kumar is already assigned to Gate 2, 18:00–06:00 on 18 Aug. Assign someone else, or ask your Branch Manager to approve an exception." |
| Permission | "Access denied." | "Payroll approval needs the Payroll or Agency Finance role. Request access" |
| Offline | "Network error." | "You're offline. Your check-in is saved on your phone and will be sent automatically." |

#### 27.10.3 Button label rules

| Rule | Example |
|---|---|
| Verb + object, in the user's words | `Publish roster`, `Add guard`, `Download payslip` — not `Submit`, `OK`, `Go` |
| The label matches the confirmation's verb | Trigger `Cancel booking` → confirm button `Cancel booking`, not `Confirm` |
| Never use "Cancel" for two meanings on one screen | If the screen cancels a booking, the dismiss action is `Close`, not `Cancel` |
| ≤3 words, ≤20 characters | `Approve payroll`, not `Approve this payroll run` |
| Sentence case | `Add guard`, not `Add Guard` or `ADD GUARD` |
| Loading label states the act | `Publishing…` |
| Destructive labels name the loss | `Delete draft`, `Archive tenant`, `Cancel 12 shifts` |

#### 27.10.4 Confirmation copy

Formula: **[Question or statement naming the action and object] / [Exact consequence with counts] / [Reversibility] / [Confirm verb = trigger verb]**.

> **"Cancel 12 shifts at Sunrise Apartments?"**
> This removes 12 assignments between 18–24 Aug and notifies 9 guards. The client contact will not be notified automatically.
> You can re-publish these shifts, but guards will receive a second notification.
> `Cancel 12 shifts` · `Keep shifts`

#### 27.10.5 Notification copy

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Front-load the fact | Push titles: subject + event, ≤40 chars. "Sunrise Apartments: 1 post unstaffed". |
| Body carries the specifics and the action | ≤120 chars, one action verb. |
| Severity is stated, not implied | P0/P1 notifications begin with the severity word or an unmistakable phrase ("Emergency", "Urgent"). |
| Never send a notification with no action or no information value | Every notification answers "so what should I do?" |
| Localise fully | Per §26.10; SMS respects registered template constraints. |
| Quiet hours honoured except P0/P1 | Per SUR-FRQ-081. |
| Money and time always explicit | "₹18,500 credited on 07 Aug" not "Your salary has been processed". |

#### 27.10.6 Do / don't table

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| "3 guards haven't checked in." | "Some guards are missing." |
| "We couldn't reach your phone. We'll try again in 2 minutes." | "Notification delivery failure." |
| "Saved 12:04" | "Your changes have been successfully saved to the system." |
| "This can't be undone." | "Please be careful." |
| "Add guard" | "Submit" |
| "You're offline. Your work is saved on this phone." | "Error: no network connectivity." |
| "Licence expires in 6 days." | "Compliance alert: document validity approaching threshold." |
| "Ask your Agency Admin to grant Payroll access." | "You do not have permission to view this resource." |
| "₹12,34,567" | "₹1234567" or "₹1,234,567" |
| "15 Aug 2026, 9:30 PM" | "15/08/26 21:30" on a field screen |
| "We didn't get your check-in." | "You failed to check in." |
| "No open alerts. All 42 posts staffed." | "No data available." |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-075 | All user-facing strings shall follow the error formula, button-label rules and confirmation formula above; copy is reviewed as part of design review, not written by engineers at implementation time. |
| SUR-UIX-076 | No production string shall contain a system term (API, payload, null, exception, token, endpoint, sync, geofence) on a client- or guard-facing surface. |
| SUR-UIX-077 | Every string shall exist in the string catalogue with context and screenshot before implementation, so translation (§26.10) is never a retro-fit. |

---

### 27.11 Screen archetype catalogue

Ten archetypes cover every screen in §28. Each defines a standard layout, standard actions, required states (all nine from §27.4 unless noted), and permission/audit implications. A new screen must declare its archetype; a screen that fits none requires design-system review.

#### 27.11.1 List

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Layout | Page header (title, record count, saved-view selector, primary action) → filter bar with active-filter chips → table (desktop) or card list (mobile) → pagination footer. Optional KPI strip above the filter bar (max 4 tiles) when the list has meaningful aggregates. |
| Standard actions | Create · Search · Filter · Sort · Choose columns · Save view · Export · Bulk actions · Row open · Row overflow actions. |
| States | All nine. Empty has three sub-variants (§27.4.1). |
| Permissions | The list is permission-filtered at query time; counts reflect only permitted rows (SUR-FRQ-059). Actions the role lacks are absent, not disabled, when their presence would reveal capability structure. |
| Audit | Exports are audited with the filter set, row count and columns. Bulk actions audit per affected row. Reading a list is audited only for sensitive entity types (guard personal data, payroll, audit log itself). |
| Examples | Guards, Invoices, Tickets, Tenders, Agencies, Sites, Documents. |

#### 27.11.2 Detail

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Layout | Header (entity name, status pill, key identifiers, primary + overflow actions, breadcrumb) → summary strip (4–6 key facts) → tabs or sections (Overview · Related records · Documents · Activity/Timeline) → right rail on `xl` with quick facts and related-entity chips. Opens as a drawer from a list, as a page from search or a deep link. |
| Standard actions | Edit · Status transition (only those legal from the current state) · Add related record · Upload document · Add note · Share/print/export · Archive. |
| States | All nine; partial-data is common here (e.g. related invoices fail while the guard loads). |
| Permissions | Field-level: a field the role cannot see is absent, not masked with dots, unless masking itself carries meaning (identity numbers, §26.5). Status transitions are gated by both role and state machine. |
| Audit | Every edit writes a before/after diff. Viewing sensitive documents and revealing masked identifiers are audited (SUR-FRQ-097, SUR-FRQ-101). |
| Examples | Guard, Site, Contract, Invoice, Incident, Agency. |

#### 27.11.3 Form / wizard

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Layout | Single column, max 640 px measure, grouped into labelled sections. Wizard: stepper at top (desktop) or "Step 2 of 5" (mobile), one logical group per step, a persistent summary rail on `lg`+ showing what has been entered, and a final review step listing everything with edit links. |
| Standard actions | Save draft (autosave, §27.5.6) · Back · Next · Submit · Cancel (with dirty-check). |
| States | All nine; plus a **validation-summary** treatment on submit failure (SUR-UIX-027) and a **resume** state ("You have an unfinished draft from 12 Aug — Continue / Start over"). |
| Permissions | Fields the role cannot set are absent; steps the role cannot complete are shown as "handled by your Agency Admin" rather than silently skipped, so the user understands the process. |
| Audit | Draft creation, each submission attempt, and the final submission are audited; the submitted payload is retained as a version. |
| Examples | Guard onboarding, Site setup, Booking creation, Tender bid, Payroll run configuration. |

#### 27.11.4 Dashboard

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Layout | Period + scope selector at top right → KPI tile row (≤6) → alert/attention region → charts (max 4) → ranked lists ("Top 5 sites by incidents"). Decision-critical content above the fold at 1440×900 (SUR-UIX-060). |
| Standard actions | Change period · Change scope (branch/city/tenant within permission) · Drill through any tile or chart point · Export the underlying data · Subscribe to a scheduled email version. |
| States | All nine; partial-data is the most important — a dashboard must never show a wrong total (SUR-UIX-042). |
| Permissions | Every figure is computed within the viewer's scope; two users with different scopes seeing "total revenue" see different, correct numbers, each labelled with its scope. |
| Audit | Exports and scheduled subscriptions are audited; viewing is audited for finance and HR dashboards. |
| Examples | OPS national dashboard, Agency Portal home, Client portal overview, Compliance dashboard. |

#### 27.11.5 Map-operations

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Layout | Left rail (filters + entity list, 320 px) · map (fills remaining) · right drawer for the selected entity. Top strip with live counts by status and a freshness indicator. Mobile: list-first with a map toggle. |
| Standard actions | Filter by status/branch/site · Select entity → detail drawer · Follow a guard · Box-select for bulk action · Toggle layers · Recentre · Switch to list. |
| States | All nine; **stale-position** and **offline-device** are first-class visual states (SUR-UIX-040); a map-load failure degrades to the list rather than to an empty page. |
| Permissions | Client users see only guards deployed to their own sites, only during contracted hours, per §39. Agency users see only their tenant. Suraksha roles see per §31 scope. |
| Audit | Viewing live guard locations is audited with the viewer, scope and time window, because it is surveillance of a person (R-106). |
| Examples | Command Center live board, Agency live tracking, Client site live view. |

#### 27.11.6 Queue / inbox

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Layout | Two-pane: queue list (left, 380 px, with priority/SLA sort) and item detail (right). Header shows counts by severity and the oldest item's age. Keyboard-first. |
| Standard actions | Claim/assign to me · Open · Act (approve/reject/reply/resolve) · Snooze with reason · Escalate · Reassign · Next item (auto-advance after acting). |
| States | All nine; plus **claimed-by-someone-else** (locked with the holder's name and time), **SLA-breached** (P1 tint on the row), and **auto-advance** behaviour on empty. |
| Permissions | Queue membership is role-based; an item may be visible but not actionable (a viewer role) and this is shown explicitly. Restricted queues (harassment, safety, §26.7) are invisible to non-members. |
| Audit | Claim, act, snooze, escalate and reassign are all audited with reason where required; SLA clocks are recorded. |
| Examples | Verification queue, Support queues, Alert centre, Attendance-integrity lane, Moderation queue. |

#### 27.11.7 Approval

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Layout | Request summary at top (who, what, when, why, amount/impact) → the diff or the item under review, side by side with the current state where applicable → policy context (limits, prior approvals, related requests) → decision bar pinned at the bottom with Approve / Reject / Request changes and a mandatory comment on anything but a clean approve. |
| Standard actions | Approve · Reject (reason mandatory) · Request changes · Delegate (where permitted) · View history of similar approvals. |
| States | All nine; plus **already-decided** (someone else acted first — show who and when, never a stale form), **out-of-limit** (this approver cannot approve this amount; shows who can), and **step-up-required**. |
| Permissions | Approval authority is checked at render and again at submit; self-approval is blocked (an approver cannot approve their own request) and appeals cannot be decided by the original decider (SUR-FRQ-135). |
| Audit | Every decision records approver, role, timestamp, comment, the exact payload approved (hashed), and the authority rule that permitted it. Approvals are never editable. |
| Examples | Payroll approval, Refund approval, Leave approval, Entitlement override, Verification decision, Migration batch approval. |

#### 27.11.8 Wizard with payment

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Layout | As the wizard archetype, plus a persistent price summary rail (line items, taxes shown as "18% GST", total) that updates as choices change, and a final review step that restates the total and what happens after payment. |
| Standard actions | Back · Next · Apply coupon · Choose payment method · Pay · Download invoice · Cancel. |
| States | All nine, plus the payment-specific set: **payment pending** (do not navigate away — with an explicit warning), **payment processing** (blocking, with a timeout and a "check status" path), **payment failed** (money not taken, retry, alternative method), **payment succeeded but provisioning pending** (money taken, service being set up — the most important state to design and the most commonly forgotten), **partially paid**, and **duplicate-submission guarded** (idempotency key). |
| Permissions | The payer must hold the billing role; a viewer can complete the configuration and hand off to a payer, with the draft transferred rather than lost. |
| Audit | Every step, the exact quote version, the payment attempt, the gateway reference, and the resulting ledger entries are audited (canon §4: double-sided entries, integer paise). No completed transaction is ever silently modified (BR-003). |
| Examples | B2C booking + payment, subscription upgrade, wallet top-up, invoice payment. |

#### 27.11.9 Report

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Layout | Parameter panel (period, scope, grouping, filters) → run action → results as a table with a chart summary → export bar. Long-running reports become background jobs with a job-centre entry. |
| Standard actions | Run · Change parameters · Save as a report definition · Schedule (email/recipient list) · Export (CSV, XLSX, PDF) · Drill to underlying rows. |
| States | All nine; plus **not-yet-run** (an explicit "Choose parameters and run" state rather than an auto-run of an expensive query), **too-large** (with guidance to narrow, or an offer to run in the background), and **generating**. |
| Permissions | Report scope is the intersection of the requested scope and the user's permitted scope, and the applied scope is printed on the report itself, so an exported PDF is self-describing. Scheduled reports re-check the recipient's permissions at each send and stop with a notification if permission was lost. |
| Audit | Every run and every export is audited with parameters, row count and destination. Exports of personal data carry an additional purpose field where §39 requires. |
| Examples | Attendance register, Payroll register, SLA report, Compliance report, Revenue report, Audit-log export. |

#### 27.11.10 Settings

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Layout | Left nav of setting groups → single-column form per group with section headers and helper text → sticky dirty-state footer ("3 unsaved changes · Discard · Save"). Dangerous settings live in a visually separated "Advanced" or "Danger zone" block at the bottom with destructive styling. |
| Standard actions | Edit · Save · Discard · Reset to default (with confirmation) · View change history. |
| States | All nine; plus **inherited** (a value set at a higher scope — tenant vs branch — shown with its source and an "Override" action), **entitlement-gated** (a setting the plan does not include, shown with an upgrade route rather than hidden, because hiding it hides the product's value), and **pending-effect** (a change that applies at the next cycle, e.g. next payroll run). |
| Permissions | Settings are role-gated per group; a user seeing a group in read-only mode sees values but no controls, with a line naming the role that can change them where safe. |
| Audit | Every setting change is audited with before/after, actor and reason (reason mandatory for security, financial, compliance and notification settings). A change-history view per setting group is available to tenant admins. |
| Examples | Tenant settings, Notification preferences, Roles & permissions, Billing, Integrations, Security, Language. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-UIX-078 | Every screen in §28 shall declare its archetype and its mobile stance (SUR-UIX-053); a screen with no archetype requires design-system review before build. |
| SUR-UIX-079 | Archetype-standard actions shall behave identically across products; a product may add actions but shall not remove or rename a standard one. |
| SUR-UIX-080 | Every archetype's permission and audit implications above are normative and shall be implemented by the shared component/layout, not re-implemented per screen. |

| D-190 | Auto-refund ceiling: below what amount may a refund be executed without a second approver? | Balances support responsiveness against financial-control risk; blocks the refund workflow build (SUR-FRQ-127) | ₹5,000 per transaction and ₹25,000 per client per month, with all refunds still audited and reported | Support, Finance, §35 |
| D-191 | Urdu script support: ship Roman-Urdu text, or fund a full Nastaliq + RTL pass? | Determines whether an RTL layout pass enters scope at all (SUR-FRQ-164) and affects a significant user population | Ship Roman-Urdu in Phase 3; revisit full Nastaliq/RTL after measuring demand | Localisation, design system, QA |
| D-192 | Data-retention period for login history and device records beyond the proposed 24 months | Security investigation capability vs privacy minimisation and storage cost | 24 months for login history, 12 months after last use for device records | §38, §39, storage |
| D-193 | Whether tenants may disable safety-critical system rules (R1, R6, R7, R8, R12) or only parameterise them | A tenant disabling wake-check escalation transfers real safety risk to Suraksha's brand | Parameterise within bounds only; disabling requires a signed acknowledgement recorded against the tenant | Rule engine, liability, contracts |
| D-194 | Whether the platform offers a formal SLA on identity-service availability to Enterprise tenants, and at what number | Identity is the single point of failure for all ten surfaces; an SLA commitment drives architecture cost | 99.95% monthly for the identity service, contractual only on Enterprise | §46, Enterprise contracts |
| D-195 | Confidence-threshold ownership: may an Enterprise tenant lower OCR thresholds for speed on their own migration? | Trades migration speed against data-integrity risk in payroll-critical fields | No — the 0.95 critical-field floor (SUR-FRQ-105) is non-negotiable for all tenants | Migration, payroll integrity |
| D-196 | Cross-tenant benchmark publication: opt-in or opt-out for agencies? | Determines the usefulness of market benchmarks (§26.2.2) and the trust posture of the marketplace | Opt-out with k≥10 anonymity, disclosed at onboarding | Analytics, trust, §42 |
| D-197 | Whether Suraksha staff impersonation may ever be write-enabled, and under what authority | Support effectiveness vs the integrity of tenant audit trails | Write-enabled impersonation only with an in-session tenant approval, dual authorisation, and a 30-minute cap | §38, support, tenant trust |
| A-190 | Professional translation and ASR/TTS quality is procurable at acceptable cost for all Tier 3 languages | Determines whether the "19+ languages" foundation rule is met with real quality or with a fallback | Ship text-only for languages where voice quality is inadequate, and state it in the UI | Localisation, AI, cost |
| A-191 | Guard App battery draw of <4% per 8-hour shift is achievable on a reference low-end Android with adaptive location sampling | Battery cost is the most common reason field workers disable a tracking app | Assume achievable with adaptive sampling; measure per release and publish the figure in-app | Guard App adoption, §46 |
| A-192 | A single open font family (Noto Sans) provides acceptable quality across all Tier 1–3 scripts at the required subset sizes | Typography consistency and app payload across 21 languages | Assume yes; commission per-script rendering tests before Phase 2 | Design system, app size |
| A-193 | Operators can reliably resolve severity by colour + glyph within three seconds on a wall display at 3 m | The three-second scan rule underpins the Command Center design | Validate with five operators on seeded anomalies before CMD launch | §24, design system |
| A-194 | Guards will accept and correctly use press-and-hold SOS rather than a single tap | Single tap risks pocket-fire and alert fatigue; hold risks delayed activation in a real emergency | Ship press-and-hold 1.5 s with haptic ramp plus a hardware key sequence; test with 20 guards before Phase 2 | Safety, §24, GAP |
| R-191 | A single identity service is a single point of failure across all ten surfaces; an outage stops guarding operations, not just logins | The availability class of the whole ecosystem is set by its weakest shared dependency | Multi-AZ, read-replica token validation, cached introspection with a short grace window, and a documented degraded-auth mode for safety-critical field actions | §46, §49, architecture |
| R-192 | Tenant isolation is enforced in seven layers, but a single defect in the shared search or AI-retrieval layer could leak across all tenants at once | This is the existential risk for the SaaS business (restates R-190 at the functional level) | Mandatory CI isolation suite (SUR-FRQ-049), physical partitioning for AI (SUR-FRQ-051), and quarterly third-party testing of the search and retrieval paths | Security, trust, commercial viability |
| R-193 | Rule-engine misconfiguration by a tenant floods guards and supervisors with notifications, causing them to mute the app and miss a genuine P0 | Alert fatigue is the most likely path to a missed safety event | Anti-storm controls and auto-quarantine (SUR-FRQ-080), per-recipient caps, and a monthly notification-volume review per tenant | Safety, §36, retention |
| R-194 | OCR migration writes a subtly wrong salary or bank account into payroll and money moves before anyone notices | The single highest-consequence data-quality failure in the platform | Critical-field confidence floor (SUR-FRQ-104/105), mandatory preview and human approval, a pilot batch, and a 14-day reconciliation window with a signed variance report | Payroll, finance, tenant trust |
| R-195 | Fraud detectors disproportionately flag guards with low-end devices (poor GPS accuracy, older Android) and effectively penalise poverty | An unfair detector that withholds attendance or pay would be both an ethical failure and a reputational one | Never withhold pay on suspicion (§26.8.5), measure false-positive rates by device class, and demote detectors exceeding the threshold (SUR-FRQ-137) | Ethics, trust, §41 |
| R-196 | Design-system drift: ten surfaces built by different teams fork components and the "one system" rule quietly dies | Consistency is a stated principle but is the first thing sacrificed under delivery pressure | One published package, a lint rule against raw hex and raw pixel values, a component-adoption dashboard, and a quarterly drift audit | UX consistency, build cost |
| R-197 | Localised safety-critical strings are mistranslated and a guard misunderstands a wake-check or SOS instruction | A translation defect in this class is a safety defect, not a cosmetic one | Protected string set with a CI gate (SUR-FRQ-156), dual human review, and field comprehension testing (SUR-UIX-058) | Safety, localisation |




## 28. Screen Inventory

This section is the **index**, not the specification. Every screen listed here is fully specified in its owning product section (§14 Main Website, §15 Customer Portal, §16 Customer App, §17 Guard Platform, §18 Guard App, §19 Trinetra, §20 Agency SaaS, §21 Agency App, §22 OPS, §23 Admin App, §24 Command Center, §25 AI Platform). Nothing here re-describes UI content; the Purpose column is a one-line reason the screen exists. Visual archetypes and components are owned by §27.

### 28.1 How to read this inventory

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ID | `SUR-SCR-nnn` — stable, permanent screen identifier. Never reused, never renumbered. A retired screen keeps its ID with status `Archived`. |
| Product | The surface the screen belongs to (one of the eleven surfaces in §8). |
| Platform | `Web` = responsive browser · `Web (desktop-density)` = ≥1280px operations UI · `Mobile` = Android + iOS · `Mobile (Android-first)` = Android is the required platform, iOS degraded (§18.13) · `Desktop` = installable Agency Portal build (§1.3) · `Wallboard` = large-format read-only display. |
| Module | The functional module in the owning product section. |
| Screen | Screen name as used in the owning section. |
| Role | Primary role(s) from the canon role list (§3). `Public` = unauthenticated. Additional roles may read the screen subject to §31. |
| Purpose | One line: why the screen exists. |
| Pri | Build priority: **P0** cannot ship the product without it · **P1** required for a credible launch · **P2** valuable, schedulable · **P3** nice-to-have. |
| Phase | Delivery phase: **Ph1** MVP · **Ph2** commercial completeness · **Ph3** scale & depth · **Ph4** deferred/`[FUTURE]`. Phases align to §51 Roadmap. |
| Dependencies | Screens (`SUR-SCR-nnn`), services, or architecture sections that must exist first. |

**Counting rule.** A screen is one addressable destination with its own URL/route or its own full-screen mobile state. Modals, drawers, bottom sheets and wizard steps are counted as screens **only** when they carry their own validation and their own audit consequence (e.g. a booking wizard step, an SOS confirmation). Tabs inside a 360-view are **not** counted separately; the 360 is one screen. Templated screens (city landing pages, vertical landing pages) count once with a `(templated ×N)` note.

**Numbering blocks.**

### 28.14 Shared screen patterns

Every screen above is an instance of an archetype defined in §27. Building the archetype once and instantiating it is the difference between a 503-screen build and a 60-component build. The archetype names below are the §27 pattern names; if §27 renames one, this table follows §27.

| Archetype (§27) | What it is | Instances (examples) | Approx. instance count |
|---|---|---|---|
| Marketing page | Hero + proof blocks + CTA, CMS-driven | 001–014, 026–046, 214–223, 239–241 | 58 |
| Legal/content page | Long-form text, TOC, version and effective date | 052–058, 245, 246 | 9 |
| Auth screen | Single-purpose credential capture with OTP fallback | 047–051, 108–109, 142, 148, 167–168, 244, 370, 400, 480 | 15 |
| Multi-step wizard | Numbered steps, per-step validation, resumable draft | 015–020, 112–115, 142–146, 224–229, 259, 280, 314, 416, 430 | 34 |
| Operational list + filter rail | Dense table, saved views, bulk actions, export | 063, 068, 072, 086, 094, 257, 275, 278, 305, 322, 414, 428, 432, 450, 464, 473 | 71 |
| Entity 360 | Header summary + tabbed detail + timeline + actions | 064, 069, 073, 258, 276, 279, 415, 429, 433, 465 | 22 |
| Live map console | Map + entity layer + status legend + follow mode | 075, 120, 254, 375, 407, 487 | 6 |
| Alert console | Priority queue + detail pane + escalation ladder + timer | 255–256, 376, 405, 408, 484–485 | 9 |
| Queue/worklist | FIFO or SLA-ordered work items with claim & dispose | 250, 291, 296, 305, 311, 403, 417, 434, 443, 446, 466, 473, 477 | 26 |
| Calendar/roster grid | Time × resource grid with drag assignment | 286, 289, 293, 440 | 5 |
| Allocation workspace | Requirement panel + ranked candidates + notify/assign | 288, 292, 378, 441, 443, 490 | 6 |

**Reuse consequence.** 23 archetypes cover 503 screens. §27 must specify each archetype's responsive behaviour, empty state, loading state, error state, permission-denied state and offline state once; individual screen sections then specify only their content and their divergences.

### 28.15 Phase 1 MVP critical path

These 40 screens are the minimum coherent product: a client can book and pay, a guard can be verified and deployed, a shift can be attended and monitored, an agency can subscribe and run its own guards, and Suraksha can watch and intervene. Everything else in Ph1 is important but this set is the path along which nothing may slip.

| # | ID | Screen | Why it is on the critical path |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | SUR-SCR-001 | Home | Entry to the entire funnel |
| 2 | SUR-SCR-012 | Pricing overview | Without price transparency the booking flow has no anchor |
| 3 | SUR-SCR-015 | Booking 1 — service & location | Start of the only revenue flow in Ph1 |

**Critical-path sequencing.** Identity (10, 11) → guard supply (16–18, 39) → site and roster (30–32) → field capture (19–29) → monitoring (35–37) → demand and cash (1–9, 38) → client visibility (12–15) → compliance gate (34, 40). A team can parallelise the client funnel and the guard funnel, but the field-capture chain (19 → 23 → 24) has no substitute and must be first to reach production quality.

## 29. Workflows

This is the canonical home for end-to-end process. Where a module section (§14–§25) describes what a screen does, this section describes what happens across screens, products and roles from trigger to terminal state. Everything else references `WKF-nn` rather than restating a flow.

### 29.1 How to read a workflow

| Element | Convention |
|---|---|
| Header line | `**WKF-nn — Name**` followed by owning product(s), trigger, actors and preconditions. |
| Step table | Eight columns: Step · Actor · Screen · Action · Validation · Backend · Notification · Resulting status. This is the one table type in this document permitted to exceed the seven-column A4 rule (§0 of the canon); it renders landscape. |
| Screen column | Always a `SUR-SCR-nnn` ID from §28, or `—` for a system-only step. |
| Status column | Only the canon status vocabulary (§3): Draft · Pending · Active · In Progress · Completed · Verified · Rejected · Expiring · Expired · Suspended · Cancelled · Failed · Archived. The entity the status belongs to is named in the cell. |
| Flow diagram | ASCII happy path plus the branches that materially change the outcome. |
| Alternate & failure paths | Every deviation with the system's exact behaviour — not "an error is shown". |
| Business rules | `BR-nnn` references. New rules raised here are `BR-1nn` and are tabulated in §29.41 for §30 to absorb. |
| Audit events | Event names emitted to the append-only audit log (§38). Naming is `snake_case`, `<entity>_<verb>`. |
| SLA/timing | Target and hard limit, with the escalation that fires on breach. |
| Acceptance | At least one Given/When/Then; operationally critical workflows carry several. |

**Depth is deliberately uneven.** WKF-11, 13, 15, 16, 17, 18, 20, 21, 22, 23, 33 and 35 carry the operational and financial risk of the platform and are specified in depth. Administrative workflows are specified to the level a developer can build without asking a question, and no further.

**Two mechanics are owned elsewhere and are not restated here:** SOS escalation ladders, rungs, hold times and operator console behaviour are owned by §24 Command Center; guard allocation scoring, weights, hard constraints and the compliance veto are owned by §25.15. WKF-16 and WKF-11 give the workflow-level view and reference those sections for mechanics.

---

### 29.2 WKF-01 — Customer registration

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Main website (§14), Customer app (§16) |
| **Trigger** | Visitor chooses Sign up, or completes booking step 4 as a new phone number |
| **Actors** | Individual Customer, Company Owner; Support (assisted creation) |
| **Preconditions** | Serviceable phone number; consent text version published (§39) |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visitor | SUR-SCR-049 | Enters name, mobile, email, password or chooses Google/Apple | Mobile is 10-digit Indian format; email RFC-valid; password meets §38 policy | Identity draft created, not yet queryable | — | Customer: `Draft` |
| 2 | Visitor | SUR-SCR-048 | Enters the 6-digit OTP | OTP valid, unexpired (5 min), ≤5 attempts | Phone marked verified; identity committed | SMS OTP; WhatsApp where opted in | Customer: `Pending` |
| 3 | Visitor | SUR-SCR-049 | Accepts terms and privacy notice | Consent version recorded with timestamp and IP | Consent record written (§39) | — | Customer: `Pending` |
| 4 | System | — | Creates the customer profile and default preferences | Duplicate check on verified mobile (BR-401) | Identity linked to any guest bookings on the same mobile | Welcome email (Zoho) + push if app | Customer: `Active` |
| 5 | Customer | SUR-SCR-101 | Completes profile: address, language, notification prefs | Address pin resolves to a serviceable city or is flagged | Preferences stored | — | Customer: `Active` |
| 6 | Company Owner | SUR-SCR-102 | Optionally creates the organisation and GSTIN | GSTIN checksum valid; legal name required | Organisation created; user becomes Company Owner | Email confirmation | Organisation: `Active` |

```
Sign up ──> OTP ──> Consent ──> Identity Active ──> Profile
   │          │                        │
   │          ├─ OTP fail x5 ──> Lockout 30 min ──> Retry / Support
   │          └─ Existing verified mobile ──> Login instead (merge guest bookings)
   └─ Social sign-in ──> Email verified ──> still requires phone OTP (mandatory, §4)
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Mobile already registered and verified | Registration converts to login: "This number is registered — sign in". No second identity is created (BR-401). |
| Mobile registered but never verified | Existing `Draft` identity is reused; a fresh OTP is sent; the older draft is not duplicated. |
| OTP not received | Resend enabled after 30 s, max 3 resends per 30 min; after the third, a voice-OTP call is offered; after that, Support-assisted verification (SUR-SCR-474) with a recorded reason. |
| 5 wrong OTPs | Identity locked 30 minutes; `auth_lockout` audit event; Support can unlock with reason. |
| Social sign-in email matches an existing account | Accounts are linked, not duplicated; the user must confirm by OTP on the registered mobile before linking. |
| Consent declined | Registration cannot complete; the draft identity is retained 24 h then purged. |
| GSTIN checksum fails | Organisation saves as `Draft` with the GSTIN field flagged; invoicing is blocked until corrected (BR-426). |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-401, BR-402 (at first booking), §39 consent rules.

**Audit events** — `customer_registration_started`, `otp_sent`, `otp_verified`, `consent_recorded`, `customer_activated`, `auth_lockout`, `identity_linked`, `organisation_created`.

**SLA/timing** — OTP delivery target ≤10 s, hard limit 60 s before the resend affordance appears and an alternate channel is offered.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a visitor whose mobile is already an `Active` customer, **When** they submit the signup form, **Then** no second identity is created and they are routed to SUR-SCR-047 with the mobile pre-filled.
- **Given** a guest who paid for a booking without an account, **When** they later register with the same verified mobile, **Then** the guest booking appears in SUR-SCR-063 without any manual linking.

### 29.3 WKF-02 — Guard registration

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Guard web (§17), Guard app (§18), Agency portal web (§20), Agency app (§21) |
| **Trigger** | Guard self-registers, or Agency HR / Recruiter creates the record, or an applicant is converted after recruitment (WKF-28) |
| **Actors** | Guard, Agency HR, Recruiter, HR (for `SURAKSHA-HQ`) |
| **Preconditions** | Tenant exists and is `Active`; the mandatory document set for the guard category is configured |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Guard | SUR-SCR-142 | Enters mobile, receives OTP | Mobile not already an `Active` guard in another tenant without release | Guard identity draft | SMS OTP | Guard: `Draft` |
| 2 | Guard | SUR-SCR-143 | Personal details: name, DOB, gender, address, languages, emergency contact | Age within the configured employable band; address pin required | Profile stored | — | Guard: `Draft` |
| 3 | Guard | SUR-SCR-144 | Experience, categories (Guard/PSO/Bouncer/Supervisor), armed licence flag | Armed flag requires an armed-licence document at step 4 | Category set stored | — | Guard: `Draft` |
| 4 | Guard | SUR-SCR-145 | Uploads ID, address proof, photo, PSARA training certificate, bank proof | Each file ≤10 MB, image or PDF; mandatory set per category complete | OCR extraction runs (§25.13); fields pre-filled for confirmation | — | Documents: `Pending` |
| 5 | Guard | SUR-SCR-146 | Confirms extracted fields, gives verification consent, submits | Name variance across documents raises the name-variance flag | Application submitted to the verification queue | SMS + push: application received | Guard: `Pending` |
| 6 | Agency HR | SUR-SCR-259 | (Agency-created path) Creates the record directly and invites the guard | Mobile uniqueness within tenant; mandatory fields | Guard record created with `source=agency` | SMS invite with app link | Guard: `Pending` |
| 7 | System | — | Routes to WKF-05 verification | Tenant verification config resolved | Verification case created | Verification queue notification | Verification: `Pending` |

```
Self-register ──┐
Agency-created ─┼──> Documents Pending ──> WKF-05 Verification ──> Guard Active
Applicant (WKF-28) ┘                            │
                                                ├─ Rejected ──> Guard Rejected (re-apply after cure)
                                                └─ Incomplete ──> Pending, blockers listed on SUR-SCR-147
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Guard already `Active` in another tenant | Registration is allowed to proceed to `Pending` but the verification case carries a `dual_employment` flag; activation requires an explicit acknowledgement by Agency Compliance and, for `SURAKSHA-HQ`, by Compliance. Concurrent active assignments across tenants are blocked by BR-001. |
| Guard has no smartphone | Agency HR completes registration on SUR-SCR-259 or SUR-SCR-387; attendance falls back to supervisor vouching (BR-413) and the guard record is flagged `no_device`. |
| OCR extraction low confidence | Fields are shown empty with the source image beside them; the guard/HR types them; the document still enters `Pending` for human verification (BR-439). |
| Armed category without armed licence document | Category selection is retained but the armed capability is withheld; the guard can be activated as unarmed only. |
| Duplicate detected on ID number | Application is held as `Pending` with a `possible_duplicate` flag routed to Verification; never auto-rejected. |
| Guard abandons mid-registration | Draft persists 30 days with resumable link by OTP; then `Archived`. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-001, BR-404, BR-439, BR-446.

**Audit events** — `guard_registration_started`, `guard_document_uploaded`, `ocr_extraction_completed`, `guard_application_submitted`, `duplicate_flag_raised`, `dual_employment_flag_raised`.

**SLA/timing** — Registration to verification queue: immediate. Applicant-visible status must never be stale by more than 5 minutes.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a guard who uploads a PSARA training certificate whose OCR confidence is below threshold, **When** the guard reaches SUR-SCR-146, **Then** the extracted fields are blank, the source image is displayed alongside, and submission is permitted only after manual entry.
- **Given** an agency-created guard record with no device, **When** allocation runs, **Then** the guard is eligible but the assignment carries a `vouched_attendance_required` marker visible on SUR-SCR-288.

| **Owning product(s)** | Trinetra (§19), OPS (§22) |

| **Actors** | Agency Owner, Sales, Verification |
| **Preconditions** | Plan catalogue published (§1.4); at least one PSARA licence to upload |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Agency Owner | SUR-SCR-224 | Creates the owner account with mobile OTP | Mobile not already an agency owner | Identity created | SMS OTP | Owner: `Active` |
| 2 | Agency Owner | SUR-SCR-225 | Agency profile: legal name, entity type, GSTIN, PAN, HQ address, guard count band | GSTIN checksum; PAN format; legal name mandatory | Tenant record created with `tenant_id` | — | Agency: `Draft` |
| 3 | Agency Owner | SUR-SCR-226 | Uploads PSARA licence(s) with state/district scope and validity dates | At least one licence; expiry must be future; scope must name states/districts | Licence records created; geography index built | — | Licence: `Pending` |
| 4 | Agency Owner | SUR-SCR-227 | Selects Starter / Professional / Enterprise | Enterprise routes to SUR-SCR-222, never shows a price | Subscription draft with entitlement set | — | Subscription: `Draft` |
| 5 | Agency Owner | SUR-SCR-228 | Pays the first period (or starts trial per D-002) | Payment captured or trial eligibility confirmed | Subscription created; WKF-31 runs | Payment receipt email | Subscription: `Active` |
| 6 | System | — | Provisions the tenant: schema scoping, default roles, default branch | Tenant isolation asserted (§3 tenancy) | Tenant provisioned; owner granted Agency Owner role | Welcome email with onboarding checklist | Agency: `Pending` |
| 7 | Verification | SUR-SCR-466 | Runs WKF-04 agency verification | — | — | — | Agency: `Pending` → `Active` |
| 8 | Agency Owner | SUR-SCR-249 | Works the onboarding checklist: branches, users, first client, first site | Checklist items map to `Active` preconditions | Progress tracked | In-app nudges | Agency: `Active` |

```
Signup ──> Profile ──> Licences ──> Plan ──> Payment ──> Tenant provisioned (Pending)
                                                              │
                                                              ├──> WKF-04 Verified ──> Agency Active ──> Marketplace eligible
                                                              └──> WKF-04 Rejected ──> Agency Rejected (refund per BR-449)
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Payment fails | Subscription stays `Draft`; the tenant is provisioned in a restricted state allowing profile and licence upload only; a retry link is valid 7 days, after which the tenant is `Archived`. |
| No PSARA licence available | Registration completes to `Pending` but the tenant cannot activate guards, create deployments or list on the marketplace (BR-405). A "licence required" banner persists on SUR-SCR-248. |
| Licence uploaded is already expired | Licence enters `Expired` immediately; verification cannot approve; the tenant remains `Pending`. |
| Duplicate GSTIN across tenants | Registration is blocked with a "this entity is already registered" message and a Support route; never silently merged. |
| Enterprise plan chosen | Subscription remains `Draft` and a sales-qualified lead is created in OPS (SUR-SCR-420); provisioning happens after a signed order. |
| Trial chosen | Subscription is `Active` with `trial=true` and the trial expiry date (D-002); entitlements are the selected plan's. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-002, BR-405, BR-406, BR-449.

**Audit events** — `agency_registration_started`, `tenant_provisioned`, `licence_uploaded`, `subscription_created`, `agency_activation_blocked`.

**SLA/timing** — Provisioning after successful payment ≤2 minutes. Onboarding checklist first-item completion target: 24 h.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** an agency that has paid but uploaded no licence, **When** the Agency Owner opens SUR-SCR-257 and attempts to activate a guard, **Then** activation is blocked with the message naming the missing licence and a link to SUR-SCR-347.
- **Given** an Enterprise selection, **When** the agency reaches SUR-SCR-227, **Then** no price is displayed anywhere in the flow and the outcome is a lead, not a subscription.

### 29.5 WKF-04 — Agency verification

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | OPS (§22), Trinetra (§19) |
| **Trigger** | Agency reaches `Pending` after WKF-03, or a licence is added/renewed |
| **Actors** | Verification, Compliance, Agency Owner |
| **Preconditions** | Agency profile complete; ≥1 licence document uploaded |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | — | Creates a verification case with a checklist per document type | All mandatory items present or flagged missing | Case created, SLA clock starts | Email to Agency Owner | Case: `Pending` |
| 2 | Verification | SUR-SCR-466 | Claims the case from the queue | Claimer must hold Verification role | Case locked to the claimer for 4 h | — | Case: `In Progress` |
| 3 | Verification | SUR-SCR-435 | Reviews each document against the source image with OCR-extracted fields | Licence number, issuing authority, state/district, validity dates must match the entered values | Field-level accept/correct recorded | — | Document: `Verified` / `Rejected` |
| 4 | Verification | SUR-SCR-465 | Cross-checks entity identity: GSTIN, PAN, registered address | External verification is assisted, not automated — no confirmed public PSARA verification API exists `[ASSUMPTION: A-210]` | Manual check outcome recorded with evidence note | — | Case: `In Progress` |
| 5 | Verification | SUR-SCR-466 | Records the decision: approve, reject, or request more information | Rejection requires a reason category and free text | Decision written; licence geography index activated | Email + in-app to Agency Owner | Agency: `Active` / `Rejected` / `Pending` |
| 6 | System | — | On approve, enables deployment capability and marketplace eligibility | Licence coverage must be non-empty | Entitlements unlocked; listing queued for moderation (SUR-SCR-468) | Push + email | Licence: `Verified` |

```
Case Pending ──> Claimed (In Progress) ──> Document review ──> Decision
                                                │                  ├─ Approve ──> Agency Active ──> Marketplace moderation
                                                │                  ├─ More info ──> Pending (clock paused) ──> resubmit
                                                │                  └─ Reject ──> Agency Rejected ──> appeal route
                                                └─ Suspected forgery ──> Compliance escalation (P1)
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Document illegible | Case moves to `Pending` with a specific re-upload request naming the document; SLA clock pauses until resubmission. |
| Licence scope narrower than the agency's declared operating geography | Approval proceeds but the operating geography is trimmed to the licence coverage; a banner names the excluded districts (BR-406). |
| Suspected forged document | Case is escalated to Compliance at P1; the agency stays `Pending`; a `forgery_suspected` audit event is written; no automated accusation is ever shown to the agency. |
| Verifier is also the Sales owner of the tenant | Claim is blocked — separation of duties (§31). |
| Case unclaimed beyond SLA | Escalates to the Verification lead at 24 h and to Compliance at 48 h. |
| Agency rejected | One appeal permitted with new evidence; a second rejection archives the tenant and refunds per BR-449. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-002, BR-405, BR-406, BR-436, BR-449.

**Audit events** — `verification_case_created`, `verification_case_claimed`, `document_verified`, `document_rejected`, `forgery_suspected`, `agency_verified`, `agency_rejected`, `licence_geography_activated`.

**SLA/timing** — Target decision 24 business hours from a complete submission; hard limit 72 h with escalation at 24 h and 48 h.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** an agency whose only licence covers Rajasthan, **When** verification approves, **Then** attempts to create a site in Gujarat on SUR-SCR-280 are blocked with a message naming the licence gap.
- **Given** a verification case awaiting re-upload, **When** the agency re-uploads, **Then** the SLA clock resumes rather than restarting, and the elapsed paused time is visible on SUR-SCR-466.

### 29.6 WKF-05 — Guard verification

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | OPS (§22), Agency portal web (§20), Guard web (§17) |
| **Trigger** | Guard reaches `Pending` after WKF-02 |
| **Actors** | Verification (Suraksha), Agency Compliance (tenant), Guard |
| **Preconditions** | Mandatory document set for the guard's category uploaded |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | — | Creates the verification case with a per-document checklist | Mandatory set resolved from category + jurisdiction config | Case created | Push to guard: "under review" | Case: `Pending` |
| 2 | Verification / Agency Compliance | SUR-SCR-434 / SUR-SCR-261 | Claims the case | Role check; tenant scoping | Case locked 4 h | — | Case: `In Progress` |
| 3 | Verifier | SUR-SCR-435 | Reviews ID, address proof, photo, training certificate, bank proof | Photo must be a face photo passing liveness heuristics; ID number format valid; name variance resolved to a canonical name | Field decisions recorded | — | Document: `Verified` / `Rejected` |
| 4 | Verifier | SUR-SCR-262 | Initiates or records police verification | Status one of: not started, submitted, received-clear, received-adverse | Tracker updated with reference number and date | SMS to guard on submission | Police verification: `Pending` → `Verified` |
| 5 | Verifier | SUR-SCR-434 | Records the decision | Rejection requires reason category; adverse police report requires Compliance review | Guard verification state written | Push + SMS to guard | Guard: `Active` / `Rejected` / `Pending` |
| 6 | System | — | On approve, enables allocation eligibility | Mandatory set all `Verified`; no blacklist entry | Guard becomes visible to §25.15 as a candidate | Push: "you can now be assigned duty" | Guard: `Active` |

```
Case Pending ──> In Progress ──> Documents Verified ──┬──> Police verification pending ──> Provisional Active*
                                                      └──> Police verification clear ──> Guard Active
   │
   ├─ Any mandatory doc Rejected ──> Guard Pending with named blocker on SUR-SCR-147
   └─ Adverse police report ──> Compliance review ──> Guard Rejected + blacklist consideration
```

`*` Provisional activation (deployment permitted while police verification is outstanding) is a configured tenant policy, not a default. Where enabled, the guard record carries a `pv_pending` flag surfaced to clients on SUR-SCR-073 `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-223]`.

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Name differs across documents | Name-variance workflow: verifier selects the canonical name, records the variants, and the guard's displayed name is the canonical one; all variants remain searchable. |
| Training certificate expired | Document enters `Expired`; guard may be activated only if training is non-statutory for the category, and §25.15 applies the soft penalty. |
| Bank proof name mismatch | Guard is activated but payroll disbursement is blocked until corrected (BR-427 does not apply; the block is a payout precondition). |
| Police verification adverse | Case escalates to Compliance; the guard cannot be activated; a blacklist decision is a separate recorded action (SUR-SCR-436). |
| Guard already blacklisted platform-wide | Verification is blocked outright with the blacklist reference; Compliance unblock is required before re-verification. |
| Verification stale >30 days without guard response | Case `Archived`; guard reverts to `Draft` with a resumable link. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-404, BR-435, BR-439, §25.15.5 compliance veto.

**Audit events** — `guard_verification_claimed`, `document_verified`, `document_rejected`, `police_verification_updated`, `name_variance_resolved`, `guard_activated`, `guard_rejected`, `blacklist_hit`.

**SLA/timing** — Document decision target 24 h, hard limit 48 h. Police verification is external; the tracker records the submission date and the expected turnaround `[ASSUMPTION: A-216]`.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a guard with all documents `Verified` and police verification outstanding in a tenant where provisional activation is disabled, **When** allocation runs, **Then** the guard is excluded by the compliance veto and the exclusion reason is displayed on SUR-SCR-288.
- **Given** a guard whose Aadhaar name is "Ram Kumar" and bank proof is "Ramkumar", **When** the verifier resolves the variance, **Then** the payslip and the client-visible profile both show the canonical name and the variant remains searchable.

### 29.7 WKF-06 — B2C booking

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Main website (§14), Customer app (§16), Customer portal (§15), OPS (§22) |
| **Trigger** | Visitor completes the booking wizard and pays |
| **Actors** | Individual Customer, City Operations, Finance |
| **Preconditions** | City is serviceable (D-005); price list published; payment gateway live |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Customer | SUR-SCR-015 | Selects service lane, city and address | Address geocodes; city in the serviceable list (BR-402) | Booking draft created | — | Booking: `Draft` |
| 2 | Customer | SUR-SCR-016 | Sets guards required, armed/unarmed, shift pattern | Armed selection requires a lane that permits it and a licensed geography | Requirement stored | — | Booking: `Draft` |
| 3 | Customer | SUR-SCR-017 | Sets start date, duration, shift timings | Start date ≥ configured minimum lead time (default 48 h); shorter routes to an urgent-booking path | Schedule stored | — | Booking: `Draft` |
| 4 | Customer | SUR-SCR-018 | Verifies mobile by OTP; WKF-01 runs if new | OTP valid | Booking bound to the customer identity | SMS OTP | Booking: `Draft` |
| 5 | Customer | SUR-SCR-019 | Reviews the priced quote and accepts terms | Price computed from the published list + GST 18%; terms version recorded | Quote frozen with a 24 h validity | — | Booking: `Pending` |
| 6 | Customer | SUR-SCR-020 | Pays the advance (D-210) | Razorpay order created; amount matches the frozen quote in paise | Payment captured; double-sided ledger entry (§35) | Payment receipt SMS/email | Payment: `Completed` |
| 7 | System | — | Confirms the booking and creates the fulfilment case | Payment `Completed`; serviceability re-checked at confirmation | Booking pushed to SUR-SCR-417; site stub created | Confirmation SMS + email + push | Booking: `Active` |
| 8 | City Operations | SUR-SCR-418 | Reviews the requirement, converts the stub into a real Site (WKF-10) | Site must reach `Active` before allocation | Site and posts created | — | Site: `Active` |
| 9 | City Operations | SUR-SCR-441 | Allocates guards (WKF-11) | Hard constraints satisfied (§25.15.3) | Assignments created | Guard push; client "your guard is assigned" | Assignment: `Active` |
| 10 | Customer | SUR-SCR-064 | Sees assigned guard cards and start date | Guard identity is redacted per §31 | — | Push on each fulfilment milestone | Booking: `Active` |
| 11 | System | — | On first successful check-in, marks the deployment live | Attendance event received (WKF-13) | Deployment start date stamped for billing | Push: "service started" | Booking: `In Progress` |
| 12 | System | — | At the end of the booked period, closes the booking | No open incidents blocking closure | Final invoice trigger (WKF-21) | Email summary + review request (WKF-24) | Booking: `Completed` |

```
Wizard ──> Quote ──> Payment ──> Booking Active ──> Site setup ──> Allocation ──> First check-in ──> In Progress ──> Completed
   │           │         │                                │
   │           │         ├─ Payment Failed ──> Booking Pending, retry link 24h ──> expire ──> Cancelled
   │           │         └─ Payment pending (bank) ──> Booking Pending, poll 30 min ──> confirm or Cancelled
   │           └─ Quote expired (24h) ──> re-price on reopen
   └─ City not serviceable ──> Waitlist capture ──> lead to Sales (SUR-SCR-420)
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| City not serviceable | The wizard stops at step 1 with a waitlist form; a lead is created with the requirement so Sales can respond; no payment is taken. |
| Urgent booking (<48 h) | Flagged `urgent`; routed to SUR-SCR-417 with an urgency badge and a shorter internal SLA; the customer is warned that fulfilment is subject to availability before payment. |
| Payment fails | Booking stays `Pending` with a 24 h retry link; three consecutive failures route to Support with the gateway error code; the booking is never confirmed on an uncaptured payment. |
| Payment captured but confirmation write fails | The payment is reconciled by the idempotency key on the Razorpay webhook; the booking is confirmed on webhook receipt even if the browser session ended (§37). |
| Allocation cannot fill by start date | City Operations must either propose a revised start date (customer confirms in SUR-SCR-064) or cancel with a full refund; the platform never lets the start date pass silently. |
| Customer cancels before deployment | Refund is computed on the refund policy version in force at booking time (BR-449) and shown before confirmation. |
| Customer cancels after deployment starts | Pro-rata computed to the last completed shift; notice period per terms; credit note if already invoiced (BR-429). |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-402, BR-403, BR-411, BR-426, BR-449, BR-001.

**Audit events** — `booking_created`, `booking_quote_frozen`, `payment_captured`, `booking_confirmed`, `booking_site_created`, `booking_allocated`, `booking_started`, `booking_completed`, `booking_cancelled`, `refund_computed`.

**SLA/timing** — Confirmation to first operations touch ≤2 h (business hours) / ≤4 h otherwise. Allocation complete ≥24 h before start for standard bookings; ≥2 h for urgent. Breach escalates to City Operations lead, then State Operations.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a confirmed booking with a start date 48 h away and no assignment 24 h before start, **When** the SLA monitor runs, **Then** a P1 alert is raised to City Operations and the booking appears at the top of SUR-SCR-417 with the time-to-start counter in red.
- **Given** a payment captured at the gateway but a failed confirmation write, **When** the Razorpay webhook arrives, **Then** the booking is confirmed exactly once and the ledger shows a single credit entry.

| 2 | System | — | Routes by geography, vertical and value band | Rules resolve to exactly one owner; unresolved routes to the Sales queue | Owner assigned; SLA clock starts | Push to owner | Lead: `Pending` |
| 3 | Sales | SUR-SCR-421 | First contact, qualification questions | Qualification requires: budget indication, decision timeline, site count, armed requirement | Qualification record stored | — | Lead: `In Progress` |
| 4 | Sales | SUR-SCR-421 | Marks qualified or disqualified | Disqualification requires a reason category | On qualify, an Opportunity is created | — | Lead: `Verified` (qualified) / `Rejected` |


| Deviation | System behaviour |

| No response after 3 contact attempts | Lead moves to a nurture state with a scheduled re-touch; it is not deleted. |

| Duplicate lead | Merged on company name + contact mobile within a 30-day window; activity histories are concatenated, never lost. |
| Government tender enquiry | Routed to the B2G path and linked to WKF-26/27 rather than the standard pipeline. |
| Lead SLA breached | First-response breach at 4 business hours escalates to the Sales lead; 24 h escalates to Founder/Management (BR-407). |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-407, BR-408 (at quotation).

**Audit events** — `lead_created`, `lead_routed`, `lead_qualified`, `lead_disqualified`, `lead_merged`, `opportunity_created`, `opportunity_stage_changed`.

**SLA/timing** — First response 4 business hours target, 8 h hard. Qualification within 3 business days. Quotation within 5 business days of qualification.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** an enterprise enquiry submitted at 23:00, **When** the routing rules run, **Then** an owner is assigned immediately and the 4-hour SLA clock starts at the next business-hours boundary, visible on SUR-SCR-420.

### 29.9 WKF-08 — B2B quotation

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | OPS (§22), Agency portal web (§20), Customer portal (§15) |
| **Trigger** | Qualified opportunity requires a price |
| **Actors** | Sales, Agency Sales, Finance, Procurement, Company Owner |
| **Preconditions** | Rate card and cost model configured; floor-price rule configured |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sales | SUR-SCR-423 | Builds line items: post type, headcount, shift hours, armed premium, site count | Headcount ≥1 per line; hours consistent with the shift pattern | Draft quotation with computed cost base | — | Quotation: `Draft` |
| 2 | System | — | Computes cost floor: wage + statutory + overhead + margin | Floor derived from the configured cost model, not typed | Floor stored with the quotation version | — | Quotation: `Draft` |
| 3 | Sales | SUR-SCR-423 | Sets the price; applies discounts | Price below floor blocks issue and requires approval (BR-408) | Discount and reason recorded | — | Quotation: `Draft` |
| 4 | Finance / Founder-Management | SUR-SCR-424 | Approves a below-floor or non-standard quotation | Approver must differ from the author | Approval recorded with identity and timestamp | Push to approver | Quotation: `Pending` |
| 5 | Sales | SUR-SCR-423 | Issues the quotation | Validity date mandatory (default 15 days); GST shown separately | Immutable version snapshot + PDF generated | Email with PDF; in-app to the client | Quotation: `Active` |
| 6 | Procurement | SUR-SCR-084 | Accepts, rejects or requests revision | Acceptance requires an authorised client role | Acceptance recorded with identity | Push + email to Sales | Quotation: `Completed` / `Rejected` |
| 7 | Sales | SUR-SCR-423 | On revision request, creates version n+1 | Prior version stays immutable and visible | Version chain maintained | Email with the new PDF | Quotation: `Active` (new version) |
| 8 | System | — | On acceptance, seeds contract creation (WKF-09) | — | Contract draft pre-filled from the quotation | — | Contract: `Draft` |

```
Build ──> Cost floor ──> Price ──┬──> at/above floor ──> Issue ──> Client decision
                                 └──> below floor ──> Approval (BR-408) ──> Issue
Client decision ──┬──> Accept ──> Contract Draft (WKF-09)
                  ├──> Revise ──> Version n+1
                  └──> Reject ──> Quotation Rejected (reason captured, opportunity may stay open)
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Quotation expires unaccepted | Status becomes `Expired`; reopening requires re-pricing against the current rate card, never the stale price. |
| Client accepts an expired quotation | Acceptance is blocked with "this quotation has expired"; Sales must reissue. A recorded exception by Founder/Management can honour it, with the reason logged. |
| Rate card changes mid-negotiation | Issued quotations are immutable; new versions use the new card and display a "revised pricing" note. |
| Multi-site quotation with mixed geographies | Any geography outside licensed coverage is blocked at issue (BR-406) with the specific district named. |
| Client requests a price the cost model shows as loss-making | Issue is blocked; only Founder/Management can approve, and the approval carries the computed loss per month. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-406, BR-408, BR-003 (immutability of issued documents).

**Audit events** — `quotation_created`, `cost_floor_computed`, `discount_applied`, `quotation_approval_requested`, `quotation_approved`, `quotation_issued`, `quotation_accepted`, `quotation_rejected`, `quotation_versioned`, `quotation_expired`.

**SLA/timing** — Approval decision target 4 business hours. Client decision reminder at day 3, day 7 and day 13 of a 15-day validity.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a quotation priced 8% below the computed floor, **When** Sales clicks Issue, **Then** issue is blocked, an approval request is created on SUR-SCR-424, and the approval card shows the floor, the price and the monthly gap in rupees.

### 29.10 WKF-09 — Contract creation

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | OPS (§22), Agency portal web (§20), Customer portal (§15) |
| **Trigger** | Quotation accepted (WKF-08) or a direct contract instruction |
| **Actors** | Sales, Agency Sales, Finance, Procurement, City Operations |
| **Preconditions** | Client entity exists with billing profile; quotation accepted or an override recorded |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sales | SUR-SCR-339 / SUR-SCR-425 | Creates the contract from the accepted quotation | Client billing profile complete incl. GSTIN (BR-426) | Contract draft with line items copied | — | Contract: `Draft` |
| 2 | Sales | SUR-SCR-340 | Sets term, billing basis, billing cycle, payment terms | Billing basis one of: fixed monthly, per-guard-per-month, per-shift, per-hour | Billing configuration stored | — | Contract: `Draft` |
| 3 | Sales | SUR-SCR-340 | Sets SLA terms: fill rate, replacement time, response time, penalties | Penalty caps required if penalties are enabled | SLA object stored and later evaluated by §42 | — | Contract: `Draft` |
| 4 | Sales | SUR-SCR-340 | Attaches sites and posts (creates them via WKF-10 if new) | At least one site and one post (BR-409) | Site/post links created | — | Contract: `Draft` |
| 5 | Finance | SUR-SCR-425 | Reviews commercial terms | Payment terms within policy or approved | Finance approval recorded | Push | Contract: `Pending` |
| 6 | Procurement | SUR-SCR-082 | Signs / accepts | E-sign or uploaded signed copy; identity of the signatory recorded | Signed document stored immutably | Email confirmation both sides | Contract: `Active` |
| 7 | City Operations | SUR-SCR-444 | Runs mobilisation: sites active, guards allocated, equipment issued | Mobilisation checklist complete before the start date | Deployment records created | Internal push | Deployment: `Pending` → `Active` |
| 8 | System | — | On contract start date, activates billing | Billing cycle anchored to the start date | First invoice scheduled (WKF-21) | Client email: service commenced | Contract: `Active` |

```
Quotation accepted ──> Contract Draft ──> Commercial terms ──> SLA ──> Sites/Posts ──> Finance review
                                                                                          │
                                        Client signature <── Contract Pending <────────────┘
                                                │
                                                └──> Contract Active ──> Mobilisation ──> Billing starts
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Client will not sign but wants service to start | Service cannot start on an unsigned contract by default; a Founder/Management override creates a `Pending` contract with a mandatory expiry (default 15 days), after which deployment auto-suspends. |
| Sites not ready by the start date | Start date is pushed with a recorded reason; billing anchor moves with it; the client is notified in writing. |
| Contract references a geography without licence coverage | Activation blocked (BR-406); the specific district and licence gap are named. |
| Signed copy differs from the system version | Contract stays `Pending`; a discrepancy note is required; Finance must reconcile before activation. |
| Amendment mid-term | A contract amendment creates a new version with an effective date; the prior version stays immutable and billing uses the version in force on each billing day. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-003, BR-406, BR-409, BR-426.

**Audit events** — `contract_created`, `contract_terms_set`, `contract_finance_approved`, `contract_signed`, `contract_activated`, `contract_amended`, `mobilisation_completed`.

**SLA/timing** — Contract draft within 2 business days of acceptance. Mobilisation completed ≥24 h before the start date; breach raises a P1 to City Operations.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** an `Active` contract with a start date of the 15th and a monthly billing cycle, **When** the first invoice runs, **Then** it bills the 15th to month-end pro-rata and the ledger records the pro-rata basis.

### 29.11 WKF-10 — Site setup

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Agency portal web (§20), OPS (§22) |
| **Trigger** | Contract attaches a new location, or a B2C booking is confirmed, or a client requests an additional site |
| **Actors** | Operations Manager, City Operations, Facility Manager |
| **Preconditions** | Client exists; licence covers the site's district (BR-406) |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-280 | Enters name, address, type, operating hours | Address geocodes; district resolved for licence check | Site draft created | — | Site: `Draft` |
| 2 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-281 | Draws the geofence (radius or polygon) | Radius 50–500 m; the site pin must fall inside the geometry | Geofence stored; server-side evaluation configured | — | Site: `Draft` |
| 3 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-282 | Defines posts and required strength per shift | ≥1 post; strength ≥1 per shift; armed posts require armed-capable guards | Posts created; shift demand computed | — | Post: `Draft` |
| 4 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-284 | Writes post orders and access instructions | Sensitive access details flagged as restricted (§31) | Instructions versioned | — | Site: `Draft` |
| 5 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-283 | Places checkpoints and provisions QR/NFC tags | Each checkpoint needs a map position and a unique tag ID | Tags provisioned; patrol routes seeded | — | Checkpoint: `Active` |
| 6 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-285 | Sets the risk band | Risk band drives patrol/wake-check/visit frequency | Frequency defaults applied | — | Site: `Draft` |
| 7 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-280 | Adds site contacts and activates | ≥1 site contact with a verified mobile (BR-410) | Site activated; roster becomes creatable | Email to the client contact; push to the supervisor | Site: `Active` |
| 8 | System | — | Publishes the site bundle to assigned devices | — | Guard App duty bundle refreshed (§18.14) | Push `roster_changed` | Site: `Active` |

```
Draft ──> Geofence ──> Posts ──> Instructions ──> Checkpoints ──> Risk band ──> Contacts ──> Site Active
   │                                                                                             │
   ├─ District outside licence ──> blocked (BR-406)                                              └──> Roster/WKF-12
   └─ Radius <50 m ──> rejected with GPS-accuracy explanation
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Address cannot be geocoded | Manual map pin permitted, flagged `manual_pin`, and a supervisor-confirmed site photo is required before activation. |
| Multi-building campus | One Site with several Posts, each with an optional sub-geofence; the parent geofence is the union. |
| Event site with a moving perimeter | Geofence flagged `dynamic` with a widened radius and a declared validity window; attendance tolerance is relaxed with the reason recorded. |
| Poor mobile coverage | Site is flagged `low_connectivity` and must declare an offline tolerance window; alerting thresholds for "device offline" are relaxed accordingly (§24). |
| Client refuses checkpoint installation | Site activates with patrol configured as photo+GPS rounds only, recorded as a contract deviation visible on SUR-SCR-340. |
| Site closed temporarily | `Suspended`; assignments end; billing pauses per contract; roster generation stops. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-406, BR-410, BR-415, BR-450.

**Audit events** — `site_created`, `geofence_set`, `geofence_changed`, `post_created`, `checkpoint_provisioned`, `risk_band_set`, `site_activated`, `site_suspended`.

**SLA/timing** — Site setup completed ≥48 h before the first shift for standard contracts; ≥4 h for urgent B2C bookings.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a site with a 40 m requested geofence, **When** the Operations Manager saves, **Then** save is rejected with the minimum-radius explanation and the field is highlighted, and no partial geofence is stored.
- **Given** a site activated with `low_connectivity`, **When** a guard's device is offline for 45 minutes inside the declared window, **Then** no "device offline" alert is raised.
