### 29.12 WKF-11 — Guard allocation

The scoring engine — factors, weights, hard constraints, the compliance veto and the fallback ladder — is owned by **§25.15** and is not restated. This workflow specifies what happens around the engine: who asks, what is validated, what is written, who is told, and what happens when the engine returns nothing usable.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Agency portal web (§20), OPS (§22), Agency app (§21), Admin app (§23) |
| **Trigger** | A published shift has an unfilled requirement; a booking is confirmed; a replacement gap opens (WKF-18); a roster is generated for a new period |
| **Actors** | Operations Manager, City Operations, Field Officer, Command Center Operator (urgent gaps), Guard (acceptance) |
| **Preconditions** | Site `Active`; Post defined with required strength; shift exists; candidate pool has at least one `Active` guard in the geography |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | — | Detects an unfilled requirement on a published shift | Requirement = required strength − confirmed assignments | Allocation request created with site, post, shift window, skill and armed flags | — | Allocation request: `Pending` |
| 2 | System | — | Builds the candidate pool | Pool = guards in the tenant (or in the Suraksha pool for HQ) within the configured radius, `Active`, not `Archived` | Pool assembled; cached 60 s | — | Allocation request: `In Progress` |
| 3 | System | — | Applies hard constraints (§25.15.3) | Compliance veto, overlapping assignment (BR-001), working-hour limits, mandatory rest, licence coverage, armed capability, blacklist | Excluded candidates retained with the exclusion reason for display | — | — |
| 4 | System | — | Scores and ranks survivors (§25.15.4) | Deterministic; no model call; ≤400 ms p50 for 200 candidates | Ranked list with per-candidate top-two reasons | — | — |
| 5 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-288 / SUR-SCR-441 | Reviews the ranked list: name, photo, distance, ETA, reliability, prior experience at this site | List shows both included and excluded candidates; excluded rows are non-selectable with the reason visible | — | — | — |
| 6 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-288 | Notifies the top N (default 3) or assigns directly where the role permits | Direct assignment requires the score ≥ threshold (default 60) or a named approver (§25.15.6) | Offers created with a response window | Push + SMS to each notified guard | Assignment: `Pending` |
| 7 | Guard | SUR-SCR-170 | Accepts or declines the offer | Acceptance re-runs hard constraints at accept time — the world may have changed since ranking | First valid acceptance wins; the others are closed as `Cancelled` with a courteous message | Push confirmation to the guard; push to the Operations Manager | Assignment: `Active` |
| 8 | System | — | Writes the assignment, updates the roster, refreshes the guard's duty bundle | No overlapping active assignment (BR-001, BR-419) | Assignment persisted; §34 pushes `roster_changed` | Push to guard and supervisor; client notified where contracted | Assignment: `Active` |
| 9 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-290 | Confirms the coverage gap has closed | Gap board recomputes on write | Gap closed | — | Shift: `Active` |
| 10 | System | — | Pre-shift reminder | Fires at the configured lead time (default T−2 h and T−30 min) | — | Push + SMS to guard | Assignment: `Active` |

**Flow**

```
Unfilled requirement
        │
        v
 Candidate pool ──> Hard constraints (§25.15.3) ──> Ranked list (§25.15.4)
        │                    │                              │
        │                    └─ everyone vetoed ────────────┐│
        │                                                   ││
        v                                                   vv
 Notify top 3 ──> Guard accepts ──> Re-check constraints ──> Assignment Active ──> Duty bundle push
        │              │                    │
        │              │                    └─ constraint now violated ──> offer voided, next candidate notified
        │              └─ all decline / no response in window ──> widen radius ──> re-rank ──> notify next 3
        │
        └─ nothing scores above threshold ──> §25.15.7 fallback ladder
                                                 │
                                                 ├─ widen radius / relax soft preferences
                                                 ├─ overtime offer to an already-assigned guard (working-hour check)
                                                 ├─ supervisor fills the post personally
                                                 ├─ escalate to City Operations for a cross-branch move
                                                 └─ subcontract to a marketplace agency (D-140) — if permitted
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Candidate pool is empty | Allocation request stays `Pending`; a P2 alert is raised immediately and escalates to P1 at T−12 h before the shift; the gap board shows "no candidates in radius" with the radius tried. |
| Every candidate is vetoed on compliance | The list renders empty of selectable rows but shows the vetoed candidates with their veto reason (expired document, blacklist, licence gap). This is deliberate: the operator must see that the shortage is a compliance shortage, not a supply shortage. |
| Top score below threshold | Direct assignment is blocked; the fallback ladder (§25.15.7) is offered; assigning anyway requires City Operations approval with a recorded reason. |
| All notified guards decline | Radius widens by the configured step (default +5 km, max 3 steps), the list re-ranks, and the next 3 are notified. Each round is logged so the difficulty of the fill is visible afterwards. |
| Guard accepts but a conflicting assignment was created in the interim | The acceptance is voided with an explicit message to the guard ("this duty was just filled"), the guard's reliability score is not penalised, and the next candidate is notified automatically. |
| Guard accepts then becomes unavailable before the shift | Treated as a replacement (WKF-18) with the original assignment `Cancelled` and the reason recorded against the guard. |
| Armed post with no armed-capable guard | Hard veto; the requirement cannot be filled by an unarmed guard under any override; escalates to State Operations. |
| Allocation for a `no_device` guard | Permitted; the assignment carries `vouched_attendance_required` and the supervisor is notified that they must vouch (BR-413). |
| Working-hour override needed | Requires State Operations approval per §25.15.5; the override reason and the resulting hours are written to the audit log and surfaced on the guard's payroll record. |
| Engine unavailable | Allocation degrades to a deterministic list sorted by distance and reliability only, banner-flagged "ranking degraded"; hard constraints are still enforced — they are never bypassed. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-001, BR-411, BR-412, BR-413, BR-419, BR-420, BR-436; §25.15.3 hard constraints; §25.15.5 compliance veto; §25.15.6 approval matrix.

**Audit events** — `allocation_requested`, `allocation_candidates_ranked`, `allocation_candidate_vetoed`, `allocation_offer_sent`, `allocation_offer_accepted`, `allocation_offer_declined`, `allocation_offer_voided`, `assignment_created`, `assignment_override_approved`, `allocation_radius_widened`, `allocation_fallback_invoked`.

**SLA/timing**

| Situation | Target | Hard limit | On breach |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ranked list returned | 400 ms p50 | 1.2 s p95 for 200 candidates | Degraded ranking banner |
| Guard offer response window | 10 min (urgent), 60 min (planned) | Window expires, next candidates notified | Logged as a decline-by-timeout, no reliability penalty |
| Planned roster filled | T−72 h | T−24 h | P1 to City Operations; booking/contract SLA risk flagged |
| Urgent gap filled (open post now) | 30 min | 60 min | P1 to Command Center; unstaffed-post record continues to accrue (BR-420) |

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** an unfilled night post at a Critical site 6 hours before shift start, **When** allocation runs, **Then** the top three candidates are notified within 60 seconds and the gap appears on SUR-SCR-290 and SUR-SCR-442 with a red time-to-start counter.
- **Given** a guard whose PSARA training certificate expired yesterday, **When** the allocation list is built, **Then** the guard appears as a non-selectable row with the reason "training certificate expired 1 day ago" and cannot be assigned by any role without a §25.15.5 exception.
- **Given** two operators assigning the same guard to overlapping shifts simultaneously, **When** the second write commits, **Then** it is rejected by BR-001 with a conflict message naming the existing assignment, and no overlapping assignment exists in the database.
- **Given** the allocation engine is unavailable, **When** an operator opens SUR-SCR-288, **Then** a distance-and-reliability list is still shown, the degraded banner is visible, and compliance-vetoed guards remain unselectable.

### 29.13 WKF-12 — Shift creation

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Agency portal web (§20), OPS (§22) |
| **Trigger** | Roster period generation, contract activation, or a manual ad-hoc shift |
| **Actors** | Operations Manager, Branch Manager, City Operations |
| **Preconditions** | Site `Active` with ≥1 Post; shift patterns configured; working-hour rules configured |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-287 | Defines the shift pattern per post: start, end, days, required strength | End must be after start (overnight shifts declared explicitly); strength ≥1 | Pattern stored against the post | — | Shift pattern: `Draft` |
| 2 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-286 | Generates the roster for the period | Generation window ≤ 92 days; existing assignments preserved | Shift instances created for each date | — | Shift: `Draft` |
| 3 | System | — | Applies patrol, wake-check and supervisor-visit frequencies from the site risk band | Night shifts inside 23:00–05:30 get wake checks where the post is flagged | Schedules attached to each shift | — | Shift: `Draft` |
| 4 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-288 | Allocates guards (WKF-11) or leaves posts open | Open posts must be explicitly flagged, not implicitly empty (BR-412) | Assignments created | — | Assignment: `Pending`/`Active` |
| 5 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-289 | Publishes the roster | Publishing validates working hours, rest gaps and licence coverage across the whole period | Roster published; version stamped | Push to every affected guard and supervisor | Shift: `Active` |
| 6 | System | — | Distributes the duty bundle to devices | — | Guard App caches the next 3 days (§18.14) | Push `roster_changed` | Shift: `Active` |
| 7 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-286 | Edits a published shift | Edits within 12 h of start require a reason; guards are re-notified | Change recorded with before/after | Push to affected guards | Shift: `Active` |

```
Pattern ──> Generate period ──> Attach patrol/wake schedules ──> Allocate (WKF-11) ──> Publish ──> Devices
                                                                        │                  │
                                                                        │                  └─ edit <12h ──> reason required + re-notify
                                                                        └─ open posts flagged ──> coverage gap board
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Generation would breach a guard's weekly hours | The conflicting shift instances are created but left unassigned and flagged; the roster cannot be published with an assignment that breaches hours without a §25.15.5 override. |
| Overnight shift crossing midnight | Declared explicitly with a `crosses_midnight` flag; attendance, payroll and wake-check windows all use the shift window, not the calendar day. |
| Public holiday / special day | Holiday calendar per state applies configured premium rates; the roster shows a holiday badge; payroll picks up the premium automatically. |
| Roster published then the contract is amended | New shift instances follow the amendment's effective date; existing published shifts inside the period are edited with reasons, not deleted. |
| Duplicate generation for the same period | Idempotent: existing shift instances are matched and left alone; only missing instances are created. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-001, BR-410, BR-412, BR-450.

**Audit events** — `shift_pattern_created`, `roster_generated`, `roster_published`, `shift_edited`, `shift_cancelled`, `open_post_flagged`.

**SLA/timing** — Roster published ≥7 days before the period starts (target), ≥72 h (hard). Breach raises a P2 to the Branch Manager.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a published roster and an edit made 6 hours before a shift start, **When** the edit saves, **Then** a reason is mandatory, the affected guard receives a push within 60 seconds, and the change appears in SUR-SCR-350 with before/after values.

### 29.14 WKF-13 — Attendance

The single most-executed workflow on the platform and the source of truth for payroll (WKF-20), invoicing (WKF-21) and SLA reporting. Both `device_time` and `server_received_time` are stored for every event (§4, BR-446).

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Guard app (§18), Agency portal web (§20), OPS (§22), Customer portal (§15) |
| **Trigger** | Guard arrives at a post for an assigned shift; or shift start passes without a check-in; or a supervisor vouches |
| **Actors** | Guard, Supervisor (field), Field Officer, Operations Manager, City Operations, Branch Manager, Payroll |
| **Preconditions** | Assignment `Active`; site geofence defined; face template enrolled or a vouching path configured |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Guard | SUR-SCR-170 | Opens the app; the primary action is "Check in" | Assignment exists and is within the check-in window (earliest T−30 min, BR-447) | — | Pre-shift reminder already sent | Attendance: — |
| 2 | Guard | SUR-SCR-174 | Captures GPS fix, face image and (where configured) a post photo | GPS accuracy ≤ configured metres or an accuracy warning is shown; face capture required | Location, face template comparison, device fingerprint captured | — | Attendance: `Draft` |
| 3 | System | — | Evaluates geofence, face match, time window and device binding | Inside geofence? Face score ≥ threshold? Time within window? Bound device? | Each check yields a pass/flag — never a silent rejection (BR-414) | — | Attendance: `Pending` |
| 4a | System | — | All checks pass | — | Attendance committed; late minutes computed against the grace period (default 15 min) | Push confirmation to guard; client daily summary where contracted | Attendance: `Verified` |
| 4b | Guard | SUR-SCR-175 | Any check flags → guard selects a reason and adds a note/photo | Reason mandatory from a controlled list (traffic, gate relocated, GPS drift, device issue) | Exception record created and queued | Push to supervisor | Attendance: `Pending` |
| 5 | Operations Manager / Branch Manager | SUR-SCR-296 / SUR-SCR-380 | Reviews the exception and approves or rejects | Approver must not be the guard (BR-413); decision requires a reason on reject | Attendance state resolved; payroll basis set | Push to guard with the outcome | Attendance: `Verified` / `Rejected` |
| 6 | System | — | Shift start passes with no check-in | Grace period exhausted | Absence candidate raised; chase notification sent | Push + SMS to guard at T+10; push to supervisor at T+20 (§24.7.2) | Attendance: `Pending` |
| 7 | Supervisor (field) | SUR-SCR-209 | Vouches attendance for a `no_device` guard, with photo + GPS proof | Supervisor must be within the site geofence at vouching time | Vouched attendance recorded with `source=vouched` | Push to Operations Manager | Attendance: `Pending` → `Verified` on approval |
| 8 | System | — | No check-in and no vouch by the escalation limit | — | `UNSTAFFED_POST` record opened (BR-420); replacement workflow triggered (WKF-18) | §24 ladder for "missing guard at shift start" | Attendance: `Failed` (no-show) |
| 9 | Guard | SUR-SCR-176 | Checks out at shift end | Check-out cannot precede check-in; overtime beyond the scheduled end requires confirmation | Hours worked computed; overtime split out | Push confirmation | Attendance: `Completed` |
| 10 | System | — | Auto-closes an open attendance at shift end + configured tolerance | Tolerance default 2 h | Attendance closed with `auto_closed` flag and the scheduled end time used for pay | Push to guard and supervisor | Attendance: `Completed` (flagged) |
| 11 | Payroll | SUR-SCR-298 | Locks the period after exception clearance | Zero unresolved exceptions, or each unresolved one explicitly dispositioned | Period locked; register frozen (BR-422) | Email to Payroll and Agency Finance | Period: `Completed` (locked) |

**Flow**

```
                        ┌─────────────── Guard opens app at post ───────────────┐
                        v                                                        │
                 Check-in capture (GPS + face)                                   │
                        │                                                        │
        ┌───────────────┼────────────────┐                                       │
        v               v                v                                       │
   inside fence    outside fence    face below threshold                          │
   face ok         (BR-414)         (BR-448)                                      │
        │               │                │                                        │
        │               └──> reason ─────┴──> Exception queue (SUR-SCR-296) ──> approve/reject
        v                                                          │
   Attendance Verified <───────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │
        v
   ...shift runs (patrol WKF-14, wake checks WKF-15)...
        │
        v
   Check-out ──> Attendance Completed ──> period register ──> Lock ──> Payroll (WKF-20) + Invoice (WKF-21)

   No check-in path:
   T+0 grace ──> T+10 guard chase ──> T+20 supervisor ──> T+45 City Ops ──> UNSTAFFED_POST + WKF-18
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Device offline at check-in | Capture succeeds locally; the event is queued at priority P1 with `device_time` recorded; on reconnect the server stamps `server_received_time` and evaluates the geofence against the stored coordinates. A delay >4 h between the two times raises an integrity flag for review. |
| GPS accuracy poor (>100 m) | Check-in proceeds with an `accuracy_warning`; the geofence decision uses a hysteresis buffer; the attendance is flagged for review rather than rejected. |
| Face match below threshold | Routed to manual review (BR-448); the guard is never told "you are not you" — the message is "additional verification needed" and the supervisor is notified. Repeat sub-threshold matches for the same guard raise a re-enrolment task. |
| Mock-location or rooted device detected | Attendance is recorded with a `tamper_suspected` flag, a P1 alert is raised to Command Center (§24), and the guard is not informed (integrity). Payroll treats the record as unresolved until dispositioned. |
| Same device used by two guards within one shift window | Both attendances are flagged `device_shared`; a P2 alert is raised; approval requires Branch Manager with a reason (R-210). |
| Guard checks in at the wrong site | Geofence fails for the assigned site but matches another site of the tenant; the system offers "you appear to be at <other site>" and creates an exception naming both sites; it never silently reassigns. |
| Early check-in (>30 min before start) | Blocked with the earliest permitted time shown (BR-447); the guard may wait or record an early-report reason for supervisor approval. |
| Check-out forgotten | Auto-close at scheduled end + 2 h with the `auto_closed` flag; overtime is not paid on an auto-closed shift without supervisor confirmation. |
| Guard leaves the geofence mid-shift | Geofence-exit alert per §24 after two consecutive out-of-fence pings ≥60 s apart; attendance is not cancelled; the exit is recorded on the attendance timeline. |
| Manual attendance entry | Permitted to Branch Manager and above with a reason code and evidence; the approver can never be the guard (BR-413); every manual entry is reported in a weekly manual-attendance digest to the Agency Owner. |
| Attendance disputed by the client | Client raises the dispute on SUR-SCR-077; the attendance record is not edited — a dispute case is opened, and if upheld the correction flows to a credit note (BR-429), never a retroactive attendance edit after the period is locked. |
| Period already locked when a correction is needed | The locked register is immutable; the correction is booked as an adjustment in the following period with a reference to the original (BR-422, BR-003). |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-001, BR-413, BR-414, BR-420, BR-422, BR-446, BR-447, BR-448, BR-003.

**Audit events** — `attendance_checkin_captured`, `attendance_checkin_flagged`, `attendance_exception_created`, `attendance_exception_approved`, `attendance_exception_rejected`, `attendance_vouched`, `attendance_manual_entry`, `attendance_checkout_captured`, `attendance_auto_closed`, `attendance_tamper_flagged`, `attendance_period_locked`, `attendance_dispute_raised`.

**SLA/timing**

| Event | Timing |
|---|---|
| Check-in grace period | 15 min default, configurable per contract |
| Guard chase on no check-in | T+10 min (push + SMS) |
| Supervisor notified | T+20 min |
| City Operations notified | T+45 min (§24.7.2 "missing guard at shift start") |
| Exception queue clearance | Same day; unresolved exceptions block the period lock |
| Client daily attendance summary | 09:00 local, where contracted |
| Offline event sync on reconnect | ≤60 s for P1 attendance events |

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a guard checking in 120 m outside a 100 m geofence, **When** they submit, **Then** the check-in is recorded as `Pending` with a mandatory reason, an exception appears on SUR-SCR-296 within 10 seconds, and the guard sees "recorded — pending supervisor confirmation", not a rejection.
- **Given** a guard whose device has been offline for 3 hours, **When** the device reconnects, **Then** the queued check-in is accepted with the original `device_time`, `server_received_time` is stamped at receipt, and both are visible on the attendance record.
- **Given** an attendance period with two unresolved exceptions, **When** Payroll attempts to lock the period on SUR-SCR-298, **Then** the lock is blocked and the two exceptions are listed with direct links.
- **Given** a mock-location app detected at check-in, **When** the event is processed, **Then** the attendance is stored with `tamper_suspected`, a P1 alert reaches Command Center, and nothing in the Guard App indicates that detection occurred.

### 29.15 WKF-14 — Patrol

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Guard app (§18), Agency portal web (§20), OPS (§22), Customer portal (§15) |
| **Trigger** | A patrol round window opens during an active shift |
| **Actors** | Guard, Supervisor (field), Operations Manager, Security Head (visibility) |
| **Preconditions** | Attendance `Verified` for the shift; checkpoints provisioned or photo-round fallback configured |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | — | Opens the round window per the site's patrol schedule | Window derived from risk band and post configuration | Round instance created | Push: "patrol round due" at window open | Round: `Pending` |
| 2 | Guard | SUR-SCR-180 | Sees the round and its checkpoint list | Offline-capable from the cached duty bundle | — | — | Round: `Pending` |
| 3 | Guard | SUR-SCR-181 | Scans each checkpoint (QR or NFC) | Tag ID must belong to this site; GPS at scan must be within the checkpoint tolerance (default 30 m) | Scan recorded with device_time, server_received_time, GPS | — | Round: `In Progress` |
| 4 | Guard | SUR-SCR-182 | Uses the manual fallback if a tag is damaged | Photo + GPS mandatory; reason from a controlled list | Fallback scan recorded and flagged | Push to supervisor | Checkpoint: `Pending` |
| 5 | Guard | SUR-SCR-183 | Closes the round with observations | All mandatory checkpoints scanned within the window (BR-415) | Round closed | — | Round: `Completed` |
| 6 | System | — | Window closes with mandatory checkpoints missing | — | Round marked missed; patrol exception created | Supervisor P2 alert (§24.7.2 "patrol exception") | Round: `Failed` |
| 7 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-302 | Investigates the exception | Disposition required: acceptable reason / non-compliance / device issue | Disposition recorded; guard reliability affected per §22.9.1 | — | Exception: `Completed` |
| 8 | System | — | Publishes patrol evidence to the client where contracted | — | Client-facing report generated | Daily/weekly report per contract | Report: `Completed` |

```
Window opens ──> Scans ──> All mandatory scanned in window ──> Round Completed
      │             │
      │             ├─ tag damaged ──> photo+GPS fallback ──> flagged scan
      │             └─ out-of-tolerance GPS ──> scan recorded + flagged
      └─ window closes incomplete ──> Round Failed ──> exception ──> supervisor disposition
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Tag scanned from a photograph of a QR code | Scan is accepted but flagged when the GPS is outside checkpoint tolerance or the scan interval is implausibly short; a `patrol_anomaly` is raised. NFC checkpoints are recommended for Critical sites for exactly this reason. |
| All checkpoints scanned within 90 seconds | `patrol_anomaly` (implausible route time) raised for supervisor review; the round still records as completed with the anomaly attached. |
| Device offline during the round | Scans queue at priority P2 and upload on reconnect; the round is evaluated against `device_time` for window compliance, with the delay recorded. |
| Guard on SOS or handling an incident during the round window | Round is auto-deferred with reason `incident_in_progress`; no exception is raised; the deferral is visible on the compliance board. |
| Checkpoint permanently removed by the client | Operations Manager retires the checkpoint on SUR-SCR-283; historical rounds keep their references; future rounds exclude it. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-415, BR-446, BR-450.

**Audit events** — `patrol_round_opened`, `checkpoint_scanned`, `checkpoint_fallback_used`, `patrol_round_completed`, `patrol_round_missed`, `patrol_anomaly_raised`, `patrol_exception_dispositioned`.

**SLA/timing** — Round window default 30 minutes at the scheduled hour; missed-round alert immediately on window close; supervisor disposition within 24 h.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a round with 6 mandatory checkpoints where 5 are scanned in the window, **When** the window closes, **Then** the round is `Failed`, the unscanned checkpoint is named in the exception, and a P2 alert reaches the supervisor.

### 29.16 WKF-15 — Wake check

The night anti-sleep control. Prompt behaviour and platform constraints are owned by §18.8; the escalation ladder is owned by §24.7.2. This workflow specifies the end-to-end path.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Guard app (§18), OPS (§22), Agency portal web (§20) |
| **Trigger** | A scheduled wake-check time arrives during a night shift on a post flagged for wake checks |
| **Actors** | Guard, Supervisor (field), Command Center Operator, Operations Manager |
| **Preconditions** | Night shift `Active` between 23:00 and 05:30; post flagged for wake checks; the schedule is cached on the device |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | — | Generates the night's wake-check schedule with randomised times inside the firing window | Randomisation must not be predictable across nights (BR-450); minimum spacing enforced | Schedule attached to the shift and pushed into the duty bundle | — | Wake Check: `Pending` |
| 2 | Guard app | SUR-SCR-185 | Fires the full-screen prompt locally at the scheduled time, with sound and vibration on the alarm stream | Fires even offline, from the cached schedule | Local alarm | Full-screen prompt | Wake Check: `Pending` |
| 3 | Guard | SUR-SCR-185 | Taps the acknowledgement control within the window (default 120 s) | Control position is randomised to defeat muscle memory | Acknowledgement stored with device_time; server_received_time on sync | — | Wake Check: `Completed` (Acknowledged) |
| 4 | System | — | Patrol scan or check-out occurs inside the window | Proof of wakefulness by another channel | Wake check suppressed with reason | — | Wake Check: `Cancelled` (Suppressed) |
| 5 | Guard app | SUR-SCR-185 | No acknowledgement in the window → re-prompt once after 60 s | Re-prompt is louder and cannot be dismissed by volume keys | Miss candidate recorded | — | Wake Check: `Pending` |
| 6 | System | — | Still unacknowledged → miss confirmed | Two consecutive unacknowledged prompts | Wake check marked missed; §24 ladder starts | IVR call to the guard; P2 push to the supervisor | Wake Check: `Failed` (Missed) |
| 7 | System | — | Unresolved at T+5 min | — | Escalation continues (§24.7.2) | Command Center P1 at T+5; State Ops at T+20 | Alert: `In Progress` |
| 8 | Supervisor (field) / Command Center Operator | SUR-SCR-210 / SUR-SCR-408 | Contacts the guard, records the outcome | Outcome from a controlled list: awake-device issue · asleep · absent · emergency | Alert resolved with the outcome | Push to Operations Manager | Alert: `Completed` |
| 9 | System | — | Late acknowledgement arrives after the miss | — | Recorded as `Acknowledged Late`; escalation is stood down but the miss remains in the record | Push to the escalating parties | Wake Check: `Completed` (Late) |
| 10 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-304 | Reviews the night's compliance | — | Compliance percentage feeds the guard reliability score (§22.9.1) | — | — |

```
Schedule (randomised) ──> Full-screen prompt ──┬─ ack ≤120s ──────────> Acknowledged
                                              ├─ patrol scan in window ─> Suppressed
                                              └─ no ack ──> re-prompt 60s ──┬─ ack ──> Acknowledged Late
                                                                            └─ no ack ──> MISSED
                                                                                   │
                                          IVR to guard + supervisor P2 <───────────┤
                                          Command Center P1 at T+5 <───────────────┤
                                          State Ops at T+20 <──────────────────────┘
                                                   │
                                          Outcome recorded ──> Alert Completed
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Device offline | The prompt still fires from the cached schedule; the acknowledgement is stored locally and uploaded at P1 priority on reconnect. A miss cannot be asserted by the server for an offline device until the device syncs or the offline-device alert threshold is crossed — the platform distinguishes "guard asleep" from "phone lost signal", and the operator sees which. |
| Device battery dead | No prompt fires; the offline-device alert (§24.7.2) carries the load; the wake check is recorded as `Cancelled` with reason `device_unavailable`, and the shift attracts a device-compliance flag. |
| iOS device on a night post | Full-screen prompt requires the critical-alert entitlement; without it the prompt degrades to a banner plus sound, which is not sufficient for the control. Night posts require Android (§18.13); an iOS guard on a night post is blocked at allocation with the reason shown. |
| Guard acknowledges but is demonstrably elsewhere | The acknowledgement is stored with the GPS at acknowledgement time; a location outside the geofence raises a `wake_check_location_mismatch` P2 alert independent of the acknowledgement. |
| Shift ends early | Remaining wake checks are `Cancelled` with reason `shift_ended`. |
| Guard is handling an SOS or incident | Wake checks are suppressed for the duration and for 30 minutes afterwards, with the reason recorded. |
| Repeated misses by one guard | Three confirmed misses in 30 days trigger an HR disciplinary task and a reliability penalty; the pattern is surfaced on the guard's 360. |
| Client contract does not require wake checks | The post is not flagged; no schedule is generated; the compliance board shows "not contracted" rather than 0%. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-416, BR-446, BR-450; §24.7.2 ladder.

**Audit events** — `wake_check_scheduled`, `wake_check_fired`, `wake_check_acknowledged`, `wake_check_suppressed`, `wake_check_missed`, `wake_check_escalated`, `wake_check_acknowledged_late`, `wake_check_location_mismatch`, `wake_check_outcome_recorded`.

**SLA/timing** — Acknowledgement window 120 s (D-213 confirms the final value). Re-prompt at +60 s. IVR + supervisor at miss confirmation. Command Center at T+5 min. State Operations at T+20 min. Operator outcome recorded within 15 minutes of contact.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a night shift with wake checks enabled and a device with no network, **When** the scheduled time arrives, **Then** the full-screen prompt fires with sound and vibration, and the acknowledgement is stored locally with both timestamps and uploaded within 60 seconds of reconnection.
- **Given** two consecutive unacknowledged prompts, **When** the miss is confirmed, **Then** an IVR call is placed to the guard and a P2 push reaches the supervisor within 30 seconds, and the alert appears on SUR-SCR-449.
- **Given** a wake check acknowledged from a location 800 m outside the site geofence, **When** the acknowledgement is processed, **Then** the wake check records as acknowledged and a separate P2 location-mismatch alert is raised.

### 29.17 WKF-16 — SOS

**Mechanics are owned by §24 Command Center**: alert creation, severity, the rung ladder, hold times, operator console behaviour, klaxon, wallboard takeover, client-branch notification and emergency-services policy. This workflow gives only the end-to-end view and the states each party sees.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Guard app (§18), OPS (§22, §24), Admin app (§23), Customer app (§16) |
| **Trigger** | Guard activates SOS (in-app control or configured hardware gesture); or a client raises panic (SUR-SCR-125), which enters the same pipeline as a client-sourced alert |
| **Actors** | Guard, Command Center Operator, Supervisor (field), City Operations, State Operations, National Operations, Founder/Management, Security Head |
| **Preconditions** | None. SOS must work on an unassigned guard, an off-shift guard, an offline device and a locked screen. This is the only workflow with no preconditions. |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Guard | SUR-SCR-187 | Activates SOS | None — never validated, never blocked | Local capture starts immediately: GPS, 30 s audio, silent photo where site policy permits | Single confirming vibration | SOS: `Draft` (local) |
| 2 | Guard app | SUR-SCR-188 | Shows the discreet active state with a 5 s cancel window | Cancel only inside 5 s and only by the guard | Event transmitted on the fastest available path: API → retry endpoint → SMS gateway fallback | — | SOS: `Pending` |
| 3 | Platform | — | Creates the alert at P0 | Never de-duplicated, never suppressed, never auto-closed (BR-417) | Alert created; rungs 1 and 3 fire simultaneously (§24.7.2) | Console klaxon; wallboard takeover; critical push and P0 voice calls | SOS: `Active` |
| 4 | Guard app | SUR-SCR-188 | Streams location every 10 s and uploads 30 s audio segments | Continues regardless of shift state | Stream ingested on the real-time path (§34) | — | SOS: `Active` |
| 5 | Command Center Operator | SUR-SCR-409 | Acknowledges and works the alert | Acknowledgement target 30 s | Ownership recorded; ladder timers visible | Ladder notifications continue per §24.7.2 | SOS: `In Progress` |
| 6 | Command Center Operator | SUR-SCR-409 | Contacts the guard, supervisor and site; decides the response | Every contact attempt is logged with outcome | Timeline appended | Client security contact at T+5 min unless resolved as a confirmed false alarm | SOS: `In Progress` |
| 7 | Command Center Operator | SUR-SCR-409 | Records the resolution and classification | Classification mandatory: genuine emergency · accidental · test · unable to contact · false alarm | Resolution written; streaming stops | Push to guard, supervisor, City Operations; client update | SOS: `Completed` |
| 8 | System | — | Creates a linked Incident where the classification is a genuine emergency | — | Incident seeded from the SOS with all media attached (WKF-17) | — | Incident: `Pending` |
| 9 | Guard | SUR-SCR-189 | Completes the debrief | Free text plus a structured outcome | Debrief attached to the SOS record | — | SOS: `Completed` |
| 10 | National Operations | SUR-SCR-413 | Runs a post-incident review for every P0 | Review within 72 h | Review record with actions | — | Review: `Completed` |

```
Guard presses SOS
      │ (0.2s) local capture: GPS + audio + photo
      v
 5s cancel window ──cancelled──> SOS Cancelled (still logged, never deleted)
      │
      v (0.3s) transmit: API ─fail─> retry endpoint ─fail(3s)─> SMS gateway
      v
 P0 alert created ──> rung 1 (supervisor) + rung 3 (Suraksha Ops) fire together at t=0
      │                                            │
      ├─ operator acknowledges (target 30s) ───────┤
      ├─ t+3min unresolved ──> rung 4 shift lead   │
      ├─ t+5min ──> client security contact        │  (§24 owns all of this)
      ├─ t+10min ──> rung 5 on-call manager        │
      └─ t+20min ──> rung 6 Founder/Management ────┘
      │
      v
 Resolution + classification ──┬─ genuine ──> Incident created (WKF-17) ──> post-incident review
                               ├─ accidental / test ──> closed, no incident, no penalty
                               └─ unable to contact ──> stays open, physical dispatch, never auto-closed
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| No data connectivity | The SMS fallback carries guard ID, site ID, coordinates and timestamp; the alert is created from the SMS with a `degraded_payload` flag; media uploads when connectivity returns. |
| No connectivity at all | The event queues at the highest priority and fires the moment any channel returns; the guard's last known position and the shift's site are used by the operator in the meantime. |
| Guard cannot be contacted | The alert never auto-closes (BR-417). The operator escalates to physical dispatch: supervisor to site, then City Operations, then, at the operator's decision and never automatically, emergency services (§24.7.5). |
| Accidental activation | Cancel inside 5 s marks it `Cancelled`; after 5 s the guard cannot cancel — only an operator can classify it as accidental after contact. The record is never deleted and no penalty is applied to the guard for accidental activation; penalising it would suppress real SOS use. |
| Repeated SOS from the same guard | Every one is treated at P0. A pattern report is generated for Operations, but no throttling, rate-limiting or de-duplication is ever applied (BR-417). |
| Client-raised panic | Enters the same pipeline with the ladder for "panic (client-raised)" per §24.7.2; the client is the source and is kept informed continuously. |
| Multiple simultaneous SOS events | Each holds its own console lane; the wallboard splits; §24 owns the operator load rules and the surge procedure. |
| Media upload fails | Metadata is always transmitted before media (§18.14 priority classes); the operator sees the event with a "media pending" indicator and the media attaches later without changing the alert timeline. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-417, BR-418, BR-446; §24.7 ladder; §24.10 no-suppression rule.

**Audit events** — `sos_triggered`, `sos_cancelled_by_guard`, `sos_alert_created`, `sos_transmission_path_used`, `sos_acknowledged`, `sos_contact_attempted`, `sos_client_notified`, `sos_escalated`, `sos_resolved`, `sos_classified`, `sos_incident_linked`, `sos_debrief_recorded`.

**SLA/timing** — Transmission attempt within 300 ms of the press. Alert creation within 1 s of receipt. Operator acknowledgement target 30 s, hard 60 s before the next rung. Ladder timings per §24.7.2. Post-incident review within 72 h for every P0.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a guard with no mobile data and no wifi, **When** SOS is pressed, **Then** an SMS is dispatched to the SOS gateway within 3 seconds and a P0 alert exists in the console with the guard ID, site ID and coordinates.
- **Given** an SOS where the guard cannot be reached for 20 minutes, **When** the ladder completes, **Then** the alert is still `In Progress`, Founder/Management has been called, and no automated process has closed it.
- **Given** an SOS classified as a genuine emergency, **When** the operator records the resolution, **Then** an Incident is created with every captured media file already attached and its investigator field pre-populated.

### 29.18 WKF-17 — Incident

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Guard app (§18), Agency portal web (§20), OPS (§22), Customer portal (§15), Customer app (§16) |
| **Trigger** | Guard reports an incident; an SOS is classified as genuine (WKF-16); a client reports an incident; a supervisor records one during a visit |
| **Actors** | Guard, Supervisor (field), Operations Manager, City Operations, Compliance, Security Head, Command Center Operator |
| **Preconditions** | Site exists; incident category taxonomy configured |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Guard | SUR-SCR-191 | Selects category and severity | Category from the configured taxonomy (theft, trespass, fire, medical, altercation, property damage, safety hazard, vehicle, other); severity P0–P3 | Incident draft created with site, post, shift, guard | — | Incident: `Draft` |
| 2 | Guard | SUR-SCR-192 | Captures description plus photo / video / audio | At least one of description or media required; media compressed on device | Media queued at P3 with metadata first (§18.14) | — | Incident: `Draft` |
| 3 | Guard | SUR-SCR-193 | Submits | Time and location auto-attached (device_time + server_received_time) | Incident submitted; severity-based routing runs | Push to supervisor immediately; P0/P1 also to Command Center | Incident: `Pending` |
| 4 | System | — | Routes by severity and site risk band | A P2 at a Critical site is uplifted to P1 (§24.5) | Alert created for P0/P1; queue entry for P2/P3 | §24 ladder for P0/P1 | Alert: `Active` |
| 5 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-306 | Claims and investigates: statements, evidence review, site contact | Investigator must be named for P0/P1 (BR-418) | Investigation log appended | Push to the claimant | Incident: `In Progress` |
| 6 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-306 | Records actions taken and corrective measures | Corrective action mandatory for P0/P1 | Actions stored with owners and due dates | Push to action owners | Incident: `In Progress` |
| 7 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-306 | Generates the client incident report | Client report mandatory for P0/P1 (BR-418); redacts guard PII per §31 | Report versioned and shared | Email + in-app to the client's security contact | Report: `Completed` |
| 8 | Security Head | SUR-SCR-079 / SUR-SCR-124 | Reviews and optionally responds | Client comments are appended, never overwrite | Client response recorded | Push to Operations Manager | Incident: `In Progress` |
| 9 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-306 | Closes the incident | Closure requires: cause category, actions completed or scheduled, client informed for P0/P1 | Incident closed | Push to guard, supervisor, client | Incident: `Completed` |
| 10 | Compliance | SUR-SCR-451 | Reviews closures for P0 incidents and reportable categories | Reportable categories are configuration, never hard-coded | Compliance sign-off recorded | — | Incident: `Completed` (signed off) |

```
Report (guard/client/SOS/supervisor)
        │
        v
  Category + severity + evidence ──> Submitted (Pending)
        │
        ├─ P0/P1 ──> §24 alert + ladder ──> Command Center involvement
        └─ P2/P3 ──> Operations queue
        │
        v
  Investigation (In Progress) ──> Actions ──> Client report (P0/P1) ──> Closure ──> Compliance sign-off (P0)
        │
        ├─ evidence missing ──> supervisor tasked to collect within 24h
        └─ client disputes the account ──> dispute thread on the incident, never an edit of the original report
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Guard is offline when reporting | Metadata syncs first at P3, media follows; the incident appears in the queue with "media pending" and the timeline shows both timestamps. |
| Media upload fails permanently | Incident remains valid; a `media_missing` flag is set and the supervisor is tasked with obtaining a written statement instead. |
| Incident involves the guard as a subject (misconduct) | Routed to Agency HR / HR rather than the standard operations queue; the reporting guard's identity is protected from the subject guard; visibility is restricted per §31. |
| Incident implicates the client's staff | Report is shared with the client at Security Head level only; the platform records the sharing decision and its approver. |
| Duplicate reports of the same event | Operations Manager merges them on SUR-SCR-306; both original submissions are retained and linked; the merged record names the primary. |
| Incident raises a legal or regulatory reporting question | The platform surfaces the configured jurisdiction rule and requires Compliance sign-off; it never states a legal conclusion. |
| Incident closed then new evidence appears | The incident reopens as `In Progress` with a reopening reason; the prior closure record is preserved. |
| P0 incident not closed within SLA | Escalates to State Operations at 24 h and Founder/Management at 72 h. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-417 (SOS-linked), BR-418, BR-433, BR-446.

**Audit events** — `incident_reported`, `incident_submitted`, `incident_routed`, `incident_claimed`, `incident_evidence_added`, `incident_action_recorded`, `incident_client_report_shared`, `incident_merged`, `incident_closed`, `incident_reopened`, `incident_compliance_signoff`.

**SLA/timing**

| Severity | Acknowledgement | Investigation start | Client report | Closure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | 5 min | 30 min | 2 h | 72 h |
| P1 | 15 min | 2 h | 12 h | 7 days |
| P2 | 2 h | 24 h | With the periodic report | 14 days |
| P3 | 24 h | 72 h | Periodic report only | 30 days |

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a P2 incident at a site with risk band Critical, **When** the incident is routed, **Then** it is uplifted to P1, an alert is created in the Command Center console, and the uplift reason is recorded on the incident.
- **Given** a P0 incident with no named investigator, **When** the Operations Manager attempts to close it, **Then** closure is blocked and the missing investigator and corrective action are named.

### 29.19 WKF-18 — Guard replacement

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Agency portal web (§20), OPS (§22), Agency app (§21), Admin app (§23), Customer portal (§15) |
| **Trigger** | No-show at shift start (WKF-13 step 8); guard leaves mid-shift; approved leave uncovered (WKF-19); client requests removal (SUR-SCR-074); guard suspended or blacklisted; medical emergency during a shift |
| **Actors** | Operations Manager, Field Officer, City Operations, Command Center Operator, Supervisor (field), Guard, Security Head |
| **Preconditions** | An `Active` post with an unmet requirement now or in the near future |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System / Operator | SUR-SCR-291 | Opens a replacement case with reason and gap start time | Reason from a controlled list: no-show · sick · left mid-shift · leave · client request · disciplinary · injury · other | Case created; gap clock starts; `UNSTAFFED_POST` opened if the gap is live (BR-420) | §24 ladder for "missing guard at shift start" or "unstaffed post" | Replacement: `Pending` |
| 2 | System | — | Marks the original assignment | Original assignment `Cancelled` with reason, or `Completed` if partially worked | Attendance for the partial shift preserved | Push to the outgoing guard | Assignment: `Cancelled` |
| 3 | System | — | Ranks replacement candidates (§25.15) with distance and ETA weighted higher than for planned allocation | Hard constraints unchanged — urgency never relaxes compliance | Ranked list produced | — | Replacement: `In Progress` |
| 4 | Operations Manager / Field Officer | SUR-SCR-292 / SUR-SCR-378 / SUR-SCR-490 | Notifies the top 3 with the gap details and travel time | One-click notify; acceptance is first-come | Offers created with a 10-minute response window | Push + SMS + voice call for urgent gaps | Offer: `Pending` |
| 5 | Guard | SUR-SCR-170 | Accepts | Hard constraints re-checked at acceptance (BR-419) | Assignment created; ETA recorded | Push to Operations Manager and supervisor | Assignment: `Active` |
| 6 | System | — | Tracks the replacement's travel against the ETA | Late arrival beyond ETA+15 min raises `replacement overdue` (§24.7.2) | Live tracking on the map | Push to Operations Manager; client where contracted | Replacement: `In Progress` |
| 7 | Guard | SUR-SCR-174 | Checks in at the site | Standard attendance validation (WKF-13) | Attendance created; gap closed | Push to Operations Manager and client | Replacement: `Completed` |
| 8 | System | — | Closes the `UNSTAFFED_POST` record with the true gap duration | Duration is never rounded down or hidden | Gap duration written to SLA reporting (§42) | Client SLA impact noted where contracted | Unstaffed post: `Completed` |
| 9 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-291 | Records the root cause and any action against the outgoing guard | Cause mandatory before the case closes | Reliability score adjusted; HR task created for repeat no-shows | — | Replacement: `Completed` |

```
Gap detected ──> UNSTAFFED_POST opened ──> Candidates ranked (§25.15, distance-weighted)
      │                                             │
      │                                    Notify top 3 (10 min window)
      │                                             │
      │              ┌──── none accept ─────────────┤
      │              v                              v
      │      widen radius / overtime offer     Guard accepts ──> travelling ──> check-in ──> gap closed
      │              │                                                │
      │              ├─ supervisor covers personally                  └─ ETA breach ──> "replacement overdue" alert
      │              ├─ cross-branch move (City Ops)
      │              └─ subcontract (D-140, if permitted)
      │
      └─ client notified per contract tier (§24.7.4)
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| No replacement found within the SLA | Escalates per §24.7.2 "unstaffed post": rung 3 at t=0, rung 4 at t+30 min, rung 5 at t+2 h. The client is notified at t+60 min, or immediately for Tier-1 and armed posts. The gap keeps accruing; it is never quietly closed. |
| Armed post gap | Only armed-capable guards are eligible; if none are available the post cannot be filled and City Operations must inform the client of the specific capability gap. No unarmed substitution, ever. |
| Client requests a specific guard be replaced | Reason is recorded; the outgoing guard is reassigned rather than penalised unless the reason is substantiated misconduct, which routes to HR. The guard is never told "the client dislikes you" — the message is a neutral reassignment. |
| Replacement accepts then does not arrive | ETA breach raises `replacement overdue`; the case reopens and the next candidate is notified; the non-arriving guard's reliability is penalised and an HR task is raised. |
| Outgoing guard left mid-shift due to a medical emergency | The case is opened with reason `injury`/`medical`; no reliability penalty; the guard's welfare follow-up task is created for HR; the `UNSTAFFED_POST` record is still created for SLA truthfulness. |
| The only available candidate would breach working hours | Requires a §25.15.5 override by State Operations with the reason and the resulting hours recorded; without approval the gap stands. |
| Replacement needed at a `low_connectivity` site | Voice call is used as the primary notification channel rather than push. |
| Repeat replacements at one site | Three or more replacement cases at a single site in 30 days raise a site-health flag for City Operations review, since the cause is often site conditions rather than guards. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-001, BR-411, BR-419, BR-420, BR-446; §24.7.2 ladders; §25.15 ranking.

**Audit events** — `replacement_case_opened`, `unstaffed_post_opened`, `assignment_cancelled`, `replacement_candidates_ranked`, `replacement_offer_sent`, `replacement_offer_accepted`, `replacement_eta_recorded`, `replacement_overdue`, `replacement_arrived`, `unstaffed_post_closed`, `replacement_root_cause_recorded`.

**SLA/timing**

| Situation | Target fill | Hard limit | Client notification |
|---|---|---|---|
| Day post, standard site | 60 min | 120 min | t+60 min |
| Night post, standard site | 45 min | 90 min | t+60 min |
| Any post, Tier-1 or armed site | 30 min | 60 min | Immediate |
| Planned gap (known ≥24 h ahead) | Filled before the shift | T−4 h | Only if unfilled at T−4 h |

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a no-show at a Tier-1 site at 22:00, **When** the replacement case opens, **Then** the client security contact is notified immediately, the top three candidates are notified within 60 seconds, and an `UNSTAFFED_POST` record exists with a running duration.
- **Given** a replacement who accepted with an ETA of 45 minutes and has not checked in after 60 minutes, **When** the ETA monitor runs, **Then** a `replacement overdue` alert is raised, the case reopens, and the next candidate is notified without operator action.
- **Given** an armed post with no armed-capable guard available, **When** an operator attempts to assign an unarmed guard, **Then** assignment is blocked with no override path in the UI and the escalation to State Operations is offered instead.

### 29.20 WKF-19 — Leave

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Guard app (§18), Guard web (§17), Agency portal web (§20), Agency app (§21), OPS (§22) |
| **Trigger** | Guard applies for leave; or HR records leave on the guard's behalf |
| **Actors** | Guard, Branch Manager, Agency HR, Operations Manager, HR |
| **Preconditions** | Leave policy configured with types and balances |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Guard | SUR-SCR-199 | Applies with type, dates, reason | Dates not in the past unless the type permits (sick, emergency); balance sufficient or the request is flagged as unpaid | Request created | Push to the approver | Leave: `Pending` |
| 2 | System | — | Computes the coverage impact for each affected shift | Identifies the shifts that would become unstaffed | Impact attached to the request | — | Leave: `Pending` |
| 3 | Branch Manager | SUR-SCR-311 / SUR-SCR-389 | Reviews with the coverage impact visible | Approving a request that leaves a post uncovered requires either a pre-assigned replacement or an explicit acknowledgement (BR-421) | Decision recorded | Push to guard | Leave: `Active` (approved) / `Rejected` |
| 4 | System | — | On approval, releases the affected assignments and opens allocation requests | — | Assignments cancelled with reason `leave`; WKF-11 runs for the freed shifts | Push to Operations Manager | Assignment: `Cancelled` |
| 5 | System | — | On leave start, sets the guard's deployment sub-state | — | Guard becomes ineligible for allocation for the leave window | — | Guard: `Active` (sub-state On Leave) |
| 6 | System | — | On leave end, restores availability | — | Guard re-enters the allocation pool | Push to guard: "you are back on roster from <date>" | Guard: `Active` (sub-state Available) |
| 7 | Payroll | SUR-SCR-295 | Leave days flow into the attendance register with the correct pay treatment | Paid/unpaid per policy | Register updated | — | — |

```
Apply ──> Coverage impact computed ──> Approve/Reject
              │                            │
              │                            ├─ approved ──> assignments released ──> WKF-11 refill ──> On Leave
              │                            └─ rejected ──> reason mandatory ──> guard notified
              └─ emergency/sick after the fact ──> retrospective request ──> approval ──> attendance reconciled
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Sick leave applied after the shift was missed | Retrospective request permitted for configured types; if approved, the prior absence is reclassified from no-show to sick leave and the reliability penalty is reversed. |
| Insufficient balance | Request proceeds as unpaid leave with a clear label; it is never silently converted to paid. |
| Leave clashes with a Tier-1 or armed post with no cover | Approval is blocked until a replacement is pre-assigned (BR-421); the approver sees the specific posts. |
| Leave cancelled by the guard | Assignments are not automatically restored; the guard re-enters the pool and the freed shifts stay with whoever was allocated. |
| Approver is on leave | Delegation chain applies; if no delegate is configured, the request escalates to the Agency Owner after 24 h. |
| Long leave (>30 days) | Requires Agency HR approval in addition to the Branch Manager, and the guard's sub-state is set to On Leave for the whole period with a return-to-work task. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-419, BR-421.

**Audit events** — `leave_requested`, `leave_coverage_impact_computed`, `leave_approved`, `leave_rejected`, `leave_cancelled`, `assignment_released_for_leave`, `leave_retrospective_reclassified`.

**SLA/timing** — Approval decision within 48 h for planned leave; within 4 h for emergency/sick. Unactioned requests escalate to the Agency Owner at 72 h.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** an approved leave that leaves two night shifts uncovered, **When** the approval commits, **Then** two allocation requests appear on SUR-SCR-290 within 60 seconds and the leave record links to both.

### 29.21 WKF-20 — Payroll

Payroll converts a locked attendance register into money. It is irreversible in practice, so every gate is explicit and every approval is two-person above a threshold.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Agency portal web (§20), OPS (§22), Guard app (§18), Guard web (§17) |
| **Trigger** | Payroll cycle cut-off reached (D-215), or an off-cycle run is authorised |
| **Actors** | Payroll, Agency Finance, Agency Owner, Finance, HR, Founder/Management, Guard |
| **Preconditions** | Attendance period `Completed` (locked, BR-422); salary structures defined; bank details verified for each payable guard |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Payroll | SUR-SCR-298 | Locks the attendance period | Zero unresolved exceptions or each explicitly dispositioned (WKF-13 step 11) | Register frozen and hashed | Email to Payroll, Agency Finance | Period: `Completed` |
| 2 | Payroll | SUR-SCR-314 | Creates the payroll run for the period and branch scope | A run cannot be created against an unlocked period (BR-422) | Run created; register snapshot attached | — | Payroll Run: `Draft` |
| 3 | System | — | Computes gross: base, shift premiums, overtime (approved only), holiday premium, allowances | Overtime included only where approved on SUR-SCR-299; all amounts in integer paise | Line items generated per guard | — | Payroll Run: `In Progress` |
| 4 | System | — | Computes deductions: statutory heads per configured jurisdiction rules, advances, asset recovery, penalties | Statutory heads are configuration, never hard-coded logic | Deduction lines generated | — | Payroll Run: `In Progress` |
| 5 | System | — | Runs anomaly detection | Flags: variance >±25% vs the guard's trailing 3-month average · zero-day guards on roster · negative net pay · duplicate bank account across guards · bank details unverified · guard `Archived` mid-period | Exception list produced | Push to Payroll | Payroll Run: `In Progress` |
| 6 | Payroll | SUR-SCR-315 | Works every exception to a disposition | Each exception must be resolved or explicitly waived with a reason; no bulk-waive control exists | Dispositions recorded | — | Payroll Run: `In Progress` |
| 7 | Payroll | SUR-SCR-314 | Submits the run for approval | The submitter cannot approve (BR-423) | Run frozen; totals locked | Push to approvers | Payroll Run: `Pending` |
| 8 | Agency Finance / Agency Owner (or Finance / Founder-Management for HQ) | SUR-SCR-316 / SUR-SCR-459 | Reviews totals, headcount, variance vs last period; approves | Two-person approval above the configured threshold (BR-424); approval is not available on a mobile surface (BR-425) | Approvals recorded with identity, timestamp and IP | Push to Payroll | Payroll Run: `Verified` |
| 9 | Agency Finance | SUR-SCR-317 | Generates the disbursement batch | Payout rail per D-211; batch total must equal the approved net total to the paisa | Batch created; double-sided ledger entries written (§35) | — | Disbursement: `Pending` |
| 10 | System | — | Executes the payout and ingests the result file | Per-guard success/failure reconciled | Successful lines settled; failed lines isolated | Push + SMS to each paid guard | Disbursement: `Completed` / partial |
| 11 | System | — | Publishes payslips | Payslip generated per guard from the approved run only | PDFs generated and stored | Push to guard | Payslip: `Completed` |
| 12 | Payroll | SUR-SCR-317 | Handles failed payouts | Failure reason recorded; corrected bank details trigger a re-attempt in a supplementary batch | Re-attempt batch created | Push to guard: "payment could not be completed" | Disbursement line: `Failed` → `Completed` |
| 13 | Payroll | SUR-SCR-321 | Produces the configured statutory registers and returns | Outputs are jurisdiction configuration | Files generated and archived | — | Register: `Completed` |

**Flow**

```
Attendance period ──lock──> Payroll Run Draft
        │                        │
        │                  compute gross ──> compute deductions ──> anomaly detection
        │                                                              │
        │                                        ┌── exceptions ───────┘
        │                                        v
        │                              disposition every exception
        │                                        │
        │                                  Submit (Pending)
        │                                        │
        │                    ┌──── approver 1 ───┴──── approver 2 (BR-424) ────┐
        │                    │                                                  │
        │                    └────────────> Payroll Run Verified <──────────────┘
        │                                        │
        │                              Disbursement batch (D-211)
        │                                        │
        │                        ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
        │                        v                               v
        │                  all succeed                    partial failure
        │                        │                               │
        │                  Payslips published        failed lines isolated ──> corrected ──> supplementary batch
        │
        └─ correction after approval ──> NEVER edits the run ──> supplementary run in the next cycle (BR-003)
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Attendance exception discovered after the lock | The locked register is immutable. A correction is booked as an adjustment line in the next run, referencing the original period, and the guard's payslip shows the adjustment with its reason (BR-003, BR-422). |
| Guard's bank details unverified | The guard is included in the run and the payslip, but the disbursement line is held; the guard receives "your salary is ready but your bank details need confirmation" with a link to SUR-SCR-151. |
| Negative net pay | The run cannot be approved with a negative net line; the deduction is capped per policy and the balance carried forward as a recoverable, with the carry-forward shown on the payslip. |
| Duplicate bank account across two guards | Hard exception; approval is blocked until dispositioned; a genuine shared family account requires HR sign-off recorded against both guards. |
| Payout rail returns partial success | Successful lines settle and their payslips publish; failed lines are isolated, the guards are notified honestly, and a supplementary batch is created. The run's status reflects partial completion rather than claiming success. |
| Payout file rejected wholesale | No ledger entries are marked settled; the run stays `Verified` with disbursement `Failed`; Finance is alerted at P1; nothing is silently retried. |
| Guard exits mid-period | Final settlement runs in the same cycle including notice pay, leave encashment and asset recovery per policy; the exit checklist (WKF-36) must be complete or the line is held (D-221). |
| Guard worked across two branches | Payroll splits the cost by the branch tagged on each attendance record; the payslip shows a single net figure; internal cost allocation is per branch. |
| Off-cycle run required | Permitted only with Agency Owner approval and a recorded reason; it follows the same approval and anomaly gates. |
| Run created for the wrong period | The run can be discarded only while `Draft`; after submission it can only be `Cancelled` with a reason and a full audit entry. |
| Approver attempts approval on the Agency App | Blocked (BR-425); SUR-SCR-394 is read-only and shows "approval must be completed on the web or desktop portal". |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-003, BR-422, BR-423, BR-424, BR-425, BR-427 (adjacent, for invoices), BR-446.

**Audit events** — `attendance_period_locked`, `payroll_run_created`, `payroll_computed`, `payroll_anomaly_flagged`, `payroll_exception_dispositioned`, `payroll_submitted`, `payroll_approved`, `payroll_approval_rejected`, `disbursement_batch_created`, `disbursement_line_settled`, `disbursement_line_failed`, `payslip_published`, `payroll_adjustment_booked`, `offcycle_run_authorised`.

**SLA/timing**

| Milestone | Timing |
|---|---|
| Attendance lock | Cycle cut-off + 1 business day |
| Run computed and exceptions listed | Within 2 h of lock |
| Exceptions dispositioned | Within 2 business days of lock |
| Approval | Within 1 business day of submission |
| Disbursement executed | Per the committed pay date; a slip requires a proactive notification to every affected guard before the pay date passes |
| Payslip availability | Same day as disbursement |

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** an attendance period with one unresolved exception, **When** Payroll attempts to create a run, **Then** creation is blocked and the exception is named with a link to SUR-SCR-296.
- **Given** a payroll run submitted by user A, **When** user A opens SUR-SCR-316, **Then** the approve control is absent and the screen states that the submitter cannot approve.
- **Given** a disbursement batch where 3 of 240 lines fail, **When** the result file is ingested, **Then** 237 payslips publish, the 3 guards receive an accurate failure notification, and the run shows partial completion with the 3 lines listed.
- **Given** an approved payroll run, **When** anyone attempts to edit a line item, **Then** the edit is rejected and the only available path is a supplementary adjustment in the next run.

### 29.22 WKF-21 — Client invoice

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Agency portal web (§20), OPS (§22), Customer portal (§15), Customer app (§16) |
| **Trigger** | Billing cycle date reached for an `Active` contract; or a booking completes; or an ad-hoc charge is raised |
| **Actors** | Agency Finance, Finance, Client Finance, Procurement |
| **Preconditions** | Contract `Active` with a billing basis; attendance period locked for usage-based bases (BR-426); client billing profile complete with GSTIN where applicable |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | — | Triggers billing on the cycle date | Contract `Active` on the billing date; version in force resolved | Invoice draft created against the contract version | — | Invoice: `Draft` |
| 2 | System | — | Assembles billable quantities | Fixed monthly: contract value. Per-guard-per-month: deployed guard-days ÷ month days. Per-shift / per-hour: from the locked attendance register only (BR-426) | Line items generated in integer paise | — | Invoice: `Draft` |
| 3 | System | — | Applies contractual adjustments | SLA penalties from §42 (fill rate, unstaffed post minutes, response breaches); agreed deductions; pro-rata for mid-cycle start or stop | Adjustment lines added with their source reference | — | Invoice: `Draft` |
| 4 | System | — | Computes tax | GST 18% on service value unless the client's configured tax treatment says otherwise; place-of-supply from the site state | Tax lines computed; HSN/SAC applied from configuration | — | Invoice: `Draft` |
| 5 | Agency Finance / Finance | SUR-SCR-323 / SUR-SCR-455 | Reviews the draft against the attendance register and contract | Variance vs last cycle >±15% is flagged for explicit confirmation | Review recorded | — | Invoice: `Draft` |
| 6 | Agency Finance / Finance | SUR-SCR-324 | Issues the invoice | Sequential invoice number from a gapless series per legal entity; once issued the invoice is immutable (BR-427) | PDF generated and stored; ledger entries written (§35) | Email with PDF; in-app to Client Finance; push to the customer app | Invoice: `Active` |
| 7 | Client Finance | SUR-SCR-087 / SUR-SCR-128 | Views the invoice with line items, attendance backing and GST breakup | Attendance backing is drill-through, not a claim | — | — | Invoice: `Active` |
| 8 | System | — | Runs the dunning ladder as the due date approaches and passes | Reminder schedule per contract payment terms | Reminders dispatched | Email + in-app at T−7, T−1, T+1, T+7, T+15 (default) | Invoice: `Active` |
| 9 | Client Finance | SUR-SCR-088 | Pays (WKF-22) | — | Payment allocated to the invoice | Receipt | Invoice: `Completed` |
| 10 | Agency Finance | SUR-SCR-325 | Issues a credit note where a dispute is upheld | Reason category and approver required (BR-429); credit note references the original invoice | Credit note issued; ledger reversal entries written | Email to the client | Credit note: `Active` |
| 11 | System | — | Ages unpaid invoices | Overdue buckets 0–30, 31–60, 61–90, 90+ | Ageing computed nightly | Receivables board updates | Invoice: `Active` (overdue) |

```
Cycle date ──> Draft assembled (contract + locked attendance) ──> Adjustments ──> Tax ──> Review
                                                                                        │
                                                          ┌───── variance >15% ─────────┤
                                                          │  explicit confirmation      │
                                                          v                             v
                                                     Issue (immutable, gapless number) ──> Client
                                                          │
                          ┌───────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┐
                          v                               v                              v
                    Paid (WKF-22)                   Overdue ladder               Disputed ──> investigation
                          │                               │                              │
                    Invoice Completed          collections / suspension       upheld ──> Credit note (BR-429)
                                                                             rejected ──> dispute closed, invoice stands
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Attendance period not locked at the billing date | Usage-based invoices are held with a "pending attendance lock" state and Finance is alerted; the invoice is never estimated and later corrected. Fixed-fee invoices are unaffected. |
| Client GSTIN missing or invalid | Issue is blocked; a task is raised for the client on SUR-SCR-093 and for the account owner; the invoice stays `Draft`. |
| Contract amended mid-cycle | The invoice splits into two line groups, each priced by the version in force on its days, and names the amendment. |
| Client disputes a line | A dispute case opens against the invoice; the invoice is not edited (BR-427); if upheld, a credit note follows; the dispute is visible on both sides throughout. |
| Duplicate invoice generated | Guarded by an idempotency key of contract + period + version; a second attempt returns the existing invoice rather than creating one. |
| Invoice issued in error | Cancelled only by a credit note for the full value with a reason; the original stays in the series so the numbering has no gaps (BR-003, BR-427). |
| Site added or removed mid-cycle | Pro-rata lines are added with the effective dates shown; the client can see exactly which days were charged. |
| SLA penalty exceeds the invoice value | Penalty is capped at the contractual cap; any residue carries to the next cycle with the carry-forward shown. |
| Client on hold for non-payment | Invoicing continues; service suspension is a separate, deliberate decision (WKF-38 / contract terms), never an automatic consequence of an unpaid invoice. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-003, BR-422, BR-426, BR-427, BR-429, BR-449.

**Audit events** — `invoice_draft_created`, `invoice_quantities_assembled`, `invoice_adjustment_applied`, `invoice_tax_computed`, `invoice_issued`, `invoice_pdf_generated`, `invoice_reminder_sent`, `invoice_dispute_raised`, `credit_note_issued`, `invoice_settled`, `invoice_aged`.

**SLA/timing** — Invoice issued within 3 business days of the cycle close (or of the attendance lock, whichever is later). Dispute acknowledged within 1 business day and resolved within 7. Reminder ladder as in step 8.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a per-shift contract whose attendance period is not yet locked, **When** the billing cycle date arrives, **Then** the invoice remains `Draft` with a "pending attendance lock" reason and Finance receives a task, and no estimated invoice is issued.
- **Given** an issued invoice, **When** anyone attempts to change a line item, **Then** the change is rejected and the UI offers a credit note as the only correction path.
- **Given** a client dispute upheld for ₹12,400, **When** the credit note is issued, **Then** the ledger shows a matching reversal, the receivables ageing reduces by exactly ₹12,400, and both parties see the credit note linked to the original invoice.
