### 29.23 WKF-22 — Payment

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Customer portal (§15), Customer app (§16), Main website (§14), OPS (§22), Agency portal web (§20) |
| **Trigger** | Client initiates payment of an invoice or a booking advance; or a gateway webhook arrives; or Finance records an offline payment |
| **Actors** | Individual Customer, Client Finance, Finance, Agency Finance |
| **Preconditions** | An `Active` invoice or a frozen booking quote; Razorpay configured for the receiving entity |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Client Finance | SUR-SCR-088 / SUR-SCR-128 | Selects an invoice and starts checkout | Amount must equal the invoice balance, or a part-payment must be explicitly chosen | Payment intent created with an idempotency key | — | Payment: `Draft` |
| 2 | Client Finance | Gateway | Completes UPI / card / netbanking | Gateway-side validation | Gateway order created and tracked | — | Payment: `Pending` |
| 3 | Gateway | — | Returns success to the browser and fires a webhook | The webhook is the source of truth, never the browser redirect | Webhook signature verified; idempotency key deduplicates | — | Payment: `Pending` |
| 4 | System | — | Captures the payment and allocates it | Allocation is oldest-invoice-first unless the client directed otherwise (BR-428) | Double-sided ledger entries written in integer paise (§35) | Receipt email + SMS; push | Payment: `Completed` |
| 5 | System | — | Updates the invoice | Full allocation closes the invoice; partial allocation leaves the balance | Invoice balance recomputed | Push to Client Finance and account owner | Invoice: `Completed` / `Active` (part-paid) |
| 6 | Finance | SUR-SCR-456 | Reconciles the gateway settlement file against captured payments | Every settled line must match a captured payment; unmatched lines are exceptions | Settlement reconciliation recorded | — | Settlement: `Completed` |
| 7 | Finance | SUR-SCR-456 | Records an offline payment (NEFT/RTGS/cheque) | UTR or cheque reference mandatory; bank statement evidence attached | Payment created with `source=offline`; ledger entries written | Receipt to the client | Payment: `Completed` |
| 8 | Finance | SUR-SCR-457 | Processes a refund | Refund reason and approver required; refund never exceeds the captured amount | Refund initiated at the gateway; reversal ledger entries written | Email + push to the client | Refund: `Pending` → `Completed` |
| 9 | System | — | Handles a chargeback or dispute raised at the gateway | Amount held; case opened | Ledger entry for the hold; Finance alerted at P1 | Finance push | Payment: `Pending` (disputed) |

```
Checkout ──> Gateway ──┬── success redirect (informational only)
                       └── WEBHOOK (source of truth)
                                 │
                        signature verified + idempotency
                                 │
                        Payment Completed ──> allocation (BR-428) ──> Invoice updated ──> Receipt
                                 │
      ┌──────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┐
      v                          v                           v
 Failed ──> retry link      Pending >30 min ──> poll     Chargeback ──> hold + P1 to Finance
      │                          │
      └─ 3 failures ──> Support  └─ still pending 24h ──> Failed, client told honestly

Offline payment ──> UTR + evidence ──> Finance records ──> same ledger treatment
Settlement file ──> reconcile ──> unmatched lines ──> exception queue
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Browser closes before redirect | The webhook still confirms the payment; the client's next login shows the receipt. Nothing depends on the redirect. |
| Duplicate webhook | Idempotency key deduplicates; exactly one ledger entry exists per gateway payment ID. |
| Payment succeeds at the gateway but the ledger write fails | The webhook is retried by the gateway and by an internal retry queue; a payment captured with no ledger entry is a P0 finance alert and appears on a daily unreconciled report. It is never left silent. |
| Client pays more than the invoice balance | The excess is recorded as an unapplied credit on the client's ledger and is offered against the next invoice; it is never absorbed. |
| Client pays less than the balance | Recorded as a part-payment; the invoice stays `Active` with the reduced balance; the dunning ladder continues on the balance. |
| Payment against a cancelled booking | Auto-refunded per the refund policy version in force (BR-449) with the client notified before the refund initiates. |
| Refund fails at the gateway | Refund line marked `Failed`; Finance is alerted; a manual bank transfer path is available with the UTR recorded against the same refund record. |
| Chargeback | Amount is held, the invoice reverts to an open balance, and a dispute case opens; the ledger records the hold rather than reversing the original entry. |
| Offline payment with no UTR | Recording is blocked; Finance must attach evidence — untraceable receipts are the root of reconciliation failure. |
| Settlement file line without a matching payment | Exception queue entry; never auto-created as a payment. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-003, BR-427, BR-428, BR-429, BR-449.

**Audit events** — `payment_intent_created`, `payment_webhook_received`, `payment_captured`, `payment_allocated`, `payment_failed`, `payment_refund_initiated`, `payment_refund_completed`, `payment_chargeback_opened`, `offline_payment_recorded`, `settlement_reconciled`, `settlement_exception_raised`.

**SLA/timing** — Webhook processing ≤5 s. Receipt dispatch ≤60 s of capture. Gateway settlement reconciliation daily by 11:00. Refund initiation within 2 business days of approval; gateway credit timeline is disclosed to the client, never promised as instant.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a payment captured at the gateway and a duplicate webhook delivery, **When** both webhooks are processed, **Then** exactly one payment record and one pair of ledger entries exist.
- **Given** a client who pays ₹50,000 against a ₹47,200 invoice, **When** allocation runs, **Then** the invoice closes and ₹2,800 appears as an unapplied credit on SUR-SCR-090.
- **Given** a captured payment with no corresponding ledger entry, **When** the nightly reconciliation runs, **Then** a P0 finance alert is raised and the payment appears on the unreconciled report with its gateway reference.

### 29.24 WKF-23 — Agency settlement

Settlement pays a marketplace or subcontract agency for work performed on Suraksha-routed demand. Commercial scope depends on D-140; the workflow is specified so it can be switched on without redesign.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | OPS (§22), Agency portal web (§20), Trinetra (§19) |
| **Trigger** | Settlement cycle date reached (D-216) for an agency with completed, client-invoiced deployment periods |
| **Actors** | Finance, Agency Owner, Agency Finance, Compliance, Founder/Management |
| **Preconditions** | Agency `Active` and not `Suspended`; deployment periods `Completed`; client invoices for those periods issued; commercial terms recorded |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | — | Assembles settlement lines for the cycle | Only `Completed` deployment periods that have been client-invoiced qualify (BR-430) | Statement draft built per agency | — | Settlement: `Draft` |
| 2 | System | — | Computes gross entitlement per line | Basis: contracted rate × verified attendance from the locked register; never the roster | Line items in integer paise with attendance references | — | Settlement: `Draft` |
| 3 | System | — | Applies deductions | Platform commission per agreement; SLA penalties from §42; unstaffed-post deductions; advances; recoveries; TDS per the configured jurisdiction rule | Deduction lines with source references | — | Settlement: `Draft` |
| 4 | System | — | Applies holds | Compliance holds where the agency's licence is `Expired` or the tenant is `Suspended` (BR-431); dispute holds on contested lines | Held lines excluded from the payable total but shown | Push to Agency Owner | Line: `Pending` (held) |
| 5 | Finance | SUR-SCR-460 | Reviews the statement | Variance vs the prior cycle >±20% flagged; every deduction must have a source reference | Review recorded | — | Settlement: `In Progress` |
| 6 | Agency Owner | SUR-SCR-331 | Reviews and accepts, or disputes specific lines | Dispute must name lines and a reason; silence past the review window is acceptance | Acceptance or dispute recorded | Email + in-app | Settlement: `Pending` |
| 7 | Finance | SUR-SCR-461 | Works each disputed line | Evidence from attendance, incidents and SLA data; outcome uphold or adjust | Adjustment lines added, never edits of the original | Push to Agency Owner | Dispute: `Completed` |
| 8 | Finance + Founder/Management | SUR-SCR-460 | Approves the statement | Two-person approval above the configured threshold (BR-424 pattern) | Statement locked | — | Settlement: `Verified` |
| 9 | Finance | SUR-SCR-460 | Executes the payout | Payout rail per D-211; batch total equals the approved payable total | Payout batch; ledger entries both sides | Push + email to Agency Owner | Payout: `Pending` → `Completed` |
| 10 | System | — | Publishes the settlement statement and payment advice | — | PDF stored; agency ledger updated | Email + in-app | Settlement: `Completed` |
| 11 | Finance | SUR-SCR-461 | Handles a failed payout line | Reason recorded; corrected bank details trigger a supplementary batch | Supplementary batch | Push to Agency Owner | Line: `Failed` → `Completed` |

```
Cycle ──> Lines from completed + client-invoiced periods ──> Gross ──> Deductions ──> Holds
                                                                              │
                                          Finance review <─────────────────────┘
                                                │
                                     Agency review (window) ──┬── accept ──┐
                                                              └── dispute ──> resolution ──> adjustment lines
                                                                                            │
                                     Two-person approval <─────────────────────────────────┘
                                                │
                                     Payout ──┬── all succeed ──> Settlement Completed
                                              └── partial ──> failed lines ──> supplementary batch
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Client has not paid the corresponding invoice | Settlement policy decides: pay-on-invoice or pay-on-collection. The platform supports both per agreement; the statement shows which basis applies to each line so the agency is never surprised `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-216]`. |
| Agency licence expired during the period | Lines for the expired window are held pending Compliance review (BR-431); work already performed is not forfeited by default, but release requires a recorded Compliance decision. |
| Agency suspended (WKF-37) | Settlement continues to be computed but payout is held; the agency can see the statement and the hold reason. Suspension must not be used as a silent payment freeze. |
| Attendance disputed after settlement | Correction is booked in the next cycle as an adjustment referencing the original line; settled statements are immutable (BR-003). |
| Agency disputes the platform commission | Commission is contractual, not per-cycle; the dispute routes to the account owner and Founder/Management rather than the line-level dispute flow. |
| Negative net settlement | Payout is zero and the balance carries forward as a recoverable, shown explicitly on the statement; no reverse debit is ever attempted. |
| Bank details unverified | Payout line held with a clear reason and a link for the agency to correct. |
| Payout partially fails | Successful lines settle and the statement records partial completion; failed lines are isolated and reattempted. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-003, BR-424 (approval pattern), BR-430, BR-431, BR-446.

**Audit events** — `settlement_cycle_started`, `settlement_line_computed`, `settlement_deduction_applied`, `settlement_hold_applied`, `settlement_published_for_review`, `settlement_disputed`, `settlement_dispute_resolved`, `settlement_approved`, `settlement_payout_executed`, `settlement_payout_failed`, `settlement_completed`.

**SLA/timing** — Statement published within 3 business days of the cycle close. Agency review window 5 business days. Dispute resolution within 7 business days. Payout within 3 business days of approval.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a settlement line for a period during which the agency's licence was `Expired`, **When** the statement is assembled, **Then** the line appears with a compliance hold, is excluded from the payable total, and names the licence and the expiry date.
- **Given** an agency that raises no dispute within the 5-day review window, **When** the window closes, **Then** the statement is treated as accepted, the acceptance basis is recorded as "no dispute in window", and approval proceeds.

### 29.25 WKF-24 — Review

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Customer portal (§15), Customer app (§16), OPS (§22), Agency portal web (§20) |
| **Trigger** | Booking completes; monthly service period closes; or a client is prompted after an incident closure |
| **Actors** | Individual Customer, Site Manager, Security Head, Support, Marketing, Operations Manager |
| **Preconditions** | An `Active` or `Completed` contract/booking at the site being reviewed (BR-432) |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | — | Sends the review request | Only to a role authorised to review (BR-432); one request per period per site | Review invitation created | Push + email + in-app | Review: `Draft` |
| 2 | Client | SUR-SCR-097 / SUR-SCR-132 | Rates service and optionally the individual guard, adds comments | Overall rating mandatory; guard rating optional; free text ≤1,000 characters | Review stored with the reviewer identity | — | Review: `Pending` |
| 3 | System | — | Screens the content | Automated screening for PII, abuse and named allegations | Flagged reviews held for moderation | Push to Support if flagged | Review: `Pending` |
| 4 | Support / Marketing | SUR-SCR-475 | Moderates flagged reviews | Rejection requires a reason category; the reviewer is told the outcome | Decision recorded | Email to the reviewer | Review: `Verified` / `Rejected` |
| 5 | System | — | Publishes the review to internal analytics and, where consented, to public surfaces | Public display requires explicit consent and never shows the client's full identity without it | Ratings aggregated into guard reliability (15% weight, §22.9.1) and site health | — | Review: `Verified` |
| 6 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-306 / SUR-SCR-276 | Responds to a low rating | Ratings ≤2/5 create a follow-up task with an owner | Task created and tracked | Push to the client on response | Task: `In Progress` |
| 7 | System | — | A rating ≤2 with a service complaint spawns a complaint case | — | Complaint created (WKF-25) linked to the review | — | Ticket: `Pending` |

```
Period closes ──> Invitation ──> Client rates ──> Screening ──┬─ clean ──> Verified ──> analytics + reliability
                                                              └─ flagged ──> moderation ──┬─ approve ──> Verified
                                                                                          └─ reject ──> Rejected (reviewer told)
                                     rating ≤2 ──> follow-up task + complaint case (WKF-25)
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Review submitted by someone with no relationship to the site | Blocked by BR-432; the submission is not stored. |
| Review names a guard in an allegation of misconduct | Held from publication, routed to HR as a potential disciplinary matter, and the guard's rating is not adjusted until the matter is dispositioned. |
| Client edits a review | One edit permitted within 7 days; the original version is retained in the audit log. |
| Review contains PII of a third party | Automatically held; moderation redacts and publishes, or rejects with a reason. |
| Guard disputes a rating | Guard can raise a grievance (SUR-SCR-160); the rating stands unless the moderation outcome removes it, and the guard is told the outcome. |
| No response to the invitation | One reminder at day 3; no further nagging; the absence of a review is not treated as a negative signal. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-432, BR-433 (where a complaint spawns).

**Audit events** — `review_invited`, `review_submitted`, `review_flagged`, `review_moderated`, `review_published`, `review_edited`, `review_linked_to_complaint`.

**SLA/timing** — Invitation within 24 h of period close. Moderation within 2 business days. Response to a ≤2 rating within 2 business days. Publication decision reported to the reviewer either way.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a review of 1/5 with a comment describing a missed patrol, **When** it is submitted, **Then** a complaint case is created and linked, a follow-up task is assigned to the Operations Manager, and the client receives an acknowledgement within 24 hours.

### 29.26 WKF-25 — Complaint

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Customer portal (§15), Customer app (§16), OPS (§22), Agency portal web (§20), Guard web (§17) |
| **Trigger** | Client raises a complaint; a low review spawns one (WKF-24); a guard raises a grievance; Support logs a phone complaint |
| **Actors** | Any client role, Guard, Support, Operations Manager, City Operations, Compliance, Founder/Management |
| **Preconditions** | Complaint category taxonomy and severity matrix configured |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Complainant | SUR-SCR-095 / SUR-SCR-130 / SUR-SCR-160 | Files with category, severity, site, description, evidence | Category mandatory; site required for service complaints | Ticket created with SLA clock | Acknowledgement push + email | Ticket: `Pending` |
| 2 | System | — | Routes by category, severity and geography | Unrouted after 15 min goes to the Support queue | Owner assigned | Push to owner | Ticket: `Pending` |
| 3 | Support | SUR-SCR-474 | Acknowledges within the severity SLA (BR-433) | Acknowledgement is a real human response, not an auto-reply | Acknowledgement recorded | Push to the complainant | Ticket: `In Progress` |
| 4 | Support / Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-474 / SUR-SCR-392 | Investigates: attendance, patrol, incident, guard records | Evidence references attached to the ticket | Investigation log | — | Ticket: `In Progress` |
| 5 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-474 | Records the resolution and any remedial action | Resolution category mandatory; remedial actions get owners and due dates | Actions created | Push + email to the complainant | Ticket: `Completed` |
| 6 | Complainant | SUR-SCR-096 / SUR-SCR-131 | Confirms satisfaction, or reopens | Reopening is permitted once within 7 days without a new ticket | Reopen recorded with reason | Push to owner | Ticket: `In Progress` / `Completed` |
| 7 | System | — | Escalates on SLA breach | Breach at each severity per BR-433 | Escalation raised | Push to the owner's manager, then City Operations, then Founder/Management | Ticket: `In Progress` |
| 8 | Compliance | SUR-SCR-473 | Reviews complaints in reportable categories | Reportable categories are configuration | Compliance note recorded | — | Ticket: `Completed` |

```
File ──> Route ──> Acknowledge (SLA) ──> Investigate ──> Resolve ──> Confirm
   │                     │                                            │
   │                     └─ SLA breach ──> escalation ladder          ├─ satisfied ──> Completed
   │                                                                  └─ reopened (once, 7 days) ──> In Progress
   └─ safety-critical category ──> immediate P1 alert to Command Center in parallel
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Complaint alleges a safety incident in progress | A P1 alert is raised to Command Center in parallel with the ticket; the ticket does not gate the operational response. |
| Complaint about a guard's conduct | Routed to HR in parallel; the guard is heard before any disciplinary outcome; the complainant is not given the guard's personal details. |
| Complaint about billing | Routed to Finance and linked to the invoice; if upheld, a credit note follows (BR-429). |
| Anonymous guard grievance | Supported; the guard's identity is visible only to HR; retaliation-risk categories restrict visibility further (§31). |
| Repeated complaints at one site | Three or more in 30 days raise a site-health review task for City Operations. |
| Complainant unreachable | Two documented contact attempts, then the ticket is closed as "unable to contact" with the attempts recorded and a reopen link valid 30 days. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-429, BR-432, BR-433.

**Audit events** — `ticket_created`, `ticket_routed`, `ticket_acknowledged`, `ticket_investigated`, `ticket_resolved`, `ticket_reopened`, `ticket_escalated`, `ticket_closed_unreachable`, `grievance_restricted_visibility_applied`.

**SLA/timing**

| Severity | Acknowledge | Resolve | Escalation on breach |
|---|---|---|---|
| P0 (safety) | 15 min | 4 h | Command Center immediately, then State Operations |
| P1 | 1 h | 24 h | Support lead at breach, City Operations at 2× |
| P2 | 4 h | 3 business days | Support lead at breach |
| P3 | 1 business day | 7 business days | Support lead at 2× |

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a P1 complaint unacknowledged after 1 hour, **When** the SLA monitor runs, **Then** the Support lead is notified, the ticket is flagged breached on SUR-SCR-473, and the breach is visible in the client's SLA view.

### 29.27 WKF-26 — Tender discovery

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Agency portal web (§20, Professional plan and above), OPS (§22) |
| **Trigger** | Scheduled discovery run; or manual entry of a tender by Agency Sales |
| **Actors** | Agency Sales, Agency Owner, Sales |
| **Preconditions** | Agency profile declares services, geography and eligibility attributes (turnover band, experience years, certifications) |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | — | Runs discovery against configured sources | **No confirmed public API exists for Indian government tender portals**; the platform must support (a) a licensed data feed, (b) an operator-assisted ingestion queue, and (c) manual entry `[ASSUMPTION: A-211]`, `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-219]` | Tender records created with source attribution | — | Tender: `Draft` |
| 2 | System | — | Normalises and de-duplicates | Match on issuing authority + reference number + closing date | Duplicates merged, sources listed | — | Tender: `Draft` |
| 3 | System | — | Matches tenders to agencies | Match on service category, geography vs licence coverage, eligibility attributes | Match score and reasons stored | Push where the match score exceeds the threshold | Tender: `Active` |
| 4 | Agency Sales | SUR-SCR-342 | Reviews the feed with match reasons and closing dates | Feed shows why each tender matched | — | Digest email daily | Tender: `Active` |
| 5 | Agency Owner | SUR-SCR-343 | Opens a tender and runs the eligibility check | Checklist: licence coverage, turnover, experience, EMD capacity, certifications | Eligibility result stored with gaps named | — | Tender: `Active` |
| 6 | Agency Owner | SUR-SCR-343 | Marks intent: pursue, watch, or decline | Decline requires a reason for future match tuning | Intent recorded | — | Tender: `In Progress` / `Archived` |
| 7 | System | — | Reminds as the closing date approaches | T−7, T−3, T−1 days | Reminders dispatched | Push + email | Tender: `Expiring` |
| 8 | System | — | Closes past-date tenders | — | Status set | — | Tender: `Expired` |

```
Sources (feed / assisted ingest / manual) ──> Normalise ──> De-duplicate ──> Match to agencies
                                                                                  │
                                                     Feed + digest <──────────────┤
                                                                                  v
                                                       Eligibility check ──> pursue ──> WKF-27
                                                                          ├─ watch ──> reminders
                                                                          └─ decline (reason) ──> match tuning
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Source unavailable | The feed shows its last successful refresh time and a staleness warning; the platform never presents stale tender data as current. |
| Tender geography outside licence coverage | Shown with an explicit ineligibility badge naming the missing licence, not hidden — the agency may choose to apply for the licence. |
| Duplicate from two sources | Merged; both source links retained. |
| Corrigendum issued | Recorded as a new version on the same tender; a change alert is sent to every agency that marked pursue or watch. |
| Agency on Starter plan | Module is visible but locked with an upgrade prompt (§20.29); no tender data is delivered. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-406, BR-434.

**Audit events** — `tender_ingested`, `tender_deduplicated`, `tender_matched`, `tender_eligibility_checked`, `tender_intent_recorded`, `tender_corrigendum_recorded`, `tender_expired`.

**SLA/timing** — Discovery refresh at least daily; staleness warning after 36 h without a successful refresh.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a tender in a state where the agency holds no licence, **When** it appears in the feed, **Then** it is shown with an ineligibility badge naming the state and the missing licence, and the bid workspace cannot be opened without an override.

### 29.28 WKF-27 — Tender workflow

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Agency portal web (§20), OPS (§22) |
| **Trigger** | Tender marked "pursue" in WKF-26 |
| **Actors** | Agency Sales, Agency Owner, Agency Finance, Agency Compliance, Sales (for Suraksha's own bids) |
| **Preconditions** | Eligibility check completed; document library populated |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Agency Sales | SUR-SCR-344 | Opens the bid workspace | Eligibility pass, or a recorded override with a reason (BR-434) | Bid created with a document checklist from the tender requirements | — | Bid: `Draft` |
| 2 | Agency Compliance | SUR-SCR-344 | Attaches compliance documents | Each required document must be `Verified` and unexpired at the submission date | Attachments linked from the document library | Push on missing items | Bid: `Draft` |
| 3 | Agency Finance | SUR-SCR-344 | Prices the bid against the cost model | Below-floor pricing requires Agency Owner approval (BR-408 pattern) | Price sheet stored | — | Bid: `Draft` |
| 4 | Agency Finance | SUR-SCR-344 | Records EMD / bid security arrangements | Instrument type, amount, validity, reference | EMD record created with a return-tracking task | — | EMD: `Active` |
| 5 | Agency Owner | SUR-SCR-344 | Approves the bid | Approval requires the checklist complete and the price approved | Approval recorded | — | Bid: `Pending` |
| 6 | Agency Sales | SUR-SCR-344 | Submits on the tender portal and records the submission | Submission is performed on the external portal; the platform records the acknowledgement reference and receipt | Submission evidence stored | Push to Agency Owner | Bid: `Active` |
| 7 | Agency Sales | SUR-SCR-345 | Records the outcome | Outcome: won, lost, disqualified, cancelled, with the reason where published | Outcome stored; win/loss analytics updated | Push | Bid: `Completed` / `Rejected` |
| 8 | System | — | On a win, seeds contract creation (WKF-09) | — | Contract draft pre-filled from the bid | — | Contract: `Draft` |
| 9 | Agency Finance | SUR-SCR-345 | Tracks EMD return | Overdue EMD returns raise a task | EMD reconciled | Push on return or overdue | EMD: `Completed` |

```
Pursue ──> Bid workspace ──> Documents ──> Pricing ──> EMD ──> Owner approval ──> External submission (recorded)
                                                                                          │
                                                        ┌─────────────────────────────────┤
                                                        v                                 v
                                                     Won ──> WKF-09 contract          Lost / Disqualified
                                                        │                                 │
                                                        └──> EMD return tracking <────────┘
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| A required document expires before the submission date | The checklist blocks approval and names the document and its expiry; renewal is routed through WKF-29. |
| Submission deadline missed | Bid is `Cancelled` with reason `deadline_missed`; a review task is raised so the cause is visible. |
| Corrigendum changes requirements after approval | Bid reverts to `Draft` with the changed requirements highlighted; re-approval is required. |
| Disqualified on a technical ground | Reason is recorded in a structured field so the pattern is analysable across bids. |
| EMD not returned within the stated period | Task escalates to the Agency Owner and appears on the receivables board as a recoverable. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-408 (pricing approval pattern), BR-434, BR-435.

**Audit events** — `bid_created`, `bid_document_attached`, `bid_priced`, `emd_recorded`, `bid_approved`, `bid_submitted`, `bid_outcome_recorded`, `emd_returned`, `bid_cancelled`.

**SLA/timing** — Bid approval ≥48 h before the closing date. EMD return chase begins at the stated return date + 7 days.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a bid whose PSARA licence copy expires two days before the tender closing date, **When** the Agency Owner attempts approval, **Then** approval is blocked and the licence and its expiry date are named with a link to SUR-SCR-348.

### 29.29 WKF-28 — Recruitment

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Agency portal web (§20), Guard web (§17), Main website (§14), OPS (§22), Agency app (§21) |
| **Trigger** | A requisition is opened because of contract demand, attrition or a coverage forecast |
| **Actors** | Recruiter, Agency HR, Recruitment (Suraksha), Branch Manager, applicant |
| **Preconditions** | Requisition approval rules configured |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Branch Manager | SUR-SCR-268 | Raises a requisition: role, count, location, pay band, start date | Pay band within policy or requires approval | Requisition created | Push to approver | Requisition: `Pending` |
| 2 | Agency HR | SUR-SCR-268 | Approves | Headcount justified against demand | Approval recorded | Push to Recruiter | Requisition: `Active` |
| 3 | Recruiter | SUR-SCR-268 | Publishes to the guard platform and job boards | Publication requires a complete job description | Posting created on SUR-SCR-139/140 | — | Posting: `Active` |
| 4 | Applicant | SUR-SCR-140 / SUR-SCR-042 | Applies with basic details and documents | Mobile OTP verified; mandatory fields complete | Applicant created | SMS acknowledgement | Applicant: `Pending` |
| 5 | Recruiter | SUR-SCR-269 | Screens and advances through stages | Stage exit criteria: screening → assessment → interview → offer | Stage history retained | Push/SMS to applicant on each stage | Applicant: `In Progress` |
| 6 | Recruiter | SUR-SCR-271 | Schedules assessment/interview | Slot conflicts prevented | Calendar entries created | SMS with time and venue | Applicant: `In Progress` |
| 7 | Recruiter | SUR-SCR-272 | Makes an offer | Offer within the approved pay band | Offer record created with validity | SMS + call task | Applicant: `Pending` (offer) |
| 8 | Applicant | — | Accepts | Acceptance recorded with date of joining | — | — | Applicant: `Verified` |
| 9 | Agency HR | SUR-SCR-272 | Converts to a guard record | Runs WKF-02 and WKF-05 | Guard created with `source=recruitment` | SMS with app link | Guard: `Pending` |
| 10 | System | — | Closes the requisition when the count is filled | — | Requisition closed; time-to-fill computed | — | Requisition: `Completed` |

```
Requisition ──> Approve ──> Publish ──> Applications ──> Screen ──> Assess ──> Interview ──> Offer
                                                             │                                 │
                                                             └─ reject (reason) ──> talent pool ├─ accept ──> WKF-02/05 ──> Guard Active
                                                                                                └─ decline ──> reason recorded, next candidate
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Applicant rejected | Reason category recorded; the applicant enters a talent pool for future requisitions unless the reason is disqualifying. |
| Applicant is an existing guard of another tenant | Flagged `dual_employment`; proceeds only with the acknowledgement described in WKF-02. |
| Offer declined | Reason recorded; the requisition reopens automatically and the next candidate advances. |
| No-show on joining date | Recorded; the requisition reopens; the applicant is flagged for future reference with the reason. |
| Requisition unfilled past the target date | Escalates to the Branch Manager and appears on the coverage risk board. |
| Ghost applications / duplicates | De-duplicated on verified mobile; the newest application is linked to the existing applicant record. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-404, BR-001 (dual employment at assignment).

**Audit events** — `requisition_created`, `requisition_approved`, `posting_published`, `applicant_created`, `applicant_stage_changed`, `applicant_rejected`, `offer_made`, `offer_accepted`, `offer_declined`, `applicant_converted_to_guard`, `requisition_closed`.

**SLA/timing** — Screening within 2 business days of application. Offer to joining ≤14 days target. Requisition to first joiner ≤21 days target.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** an accepted offer, **When** Agency HR converts the applicant, **Then** a guard record is created in `Pending`, the documents already collected are carried over, and no document is re-requested from the guard.

### 29.30 WKF-29 — Document expiry

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | All surfaces that hold documents: Agency portal web (§20), OPS (§22), Guard app (§18), Guard web (§17), Agency app (§21) |
| **Trigger** | Nightly expiry scan; or a document is uploaded with an expiry date |
| **Actors** | Guard, Agency Compliance, Compliance, Agency HR, Operations Manager |
| **Preconditions** | Documents carry an expiry date where the type requires one |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | — | Nightly scan of all documents with expiry dates | Runs per tenant, batched | Expiry horizon computed | — | Document: `Verified` |
| 2 | System | — | 60 days before expiry | — | Status set; renewal task created for the owner | Push + email to the holder and the compliance owner | Document: `Expiring` |
| 3 | System | — | 30 days and 7 days before expiry | Reminder cadence escalates | Reminder dispatched | Push + SMS at 7 days | Document: `Expiring` |
| 4 | Guard / Agency Compliance | SUR-SCR-204 / SUR-SCR-349 | Uploads the renewed document | New document supersedes the old; the old is retained | Verification case created (WKF-05 path) | — | Document: `Pending` |
| 5 | Verifier | SUR-SCR-435 | Verifies the renewal | Expiry date of the new document must be later than the old | New document verified; expiry horizon recalculated | Push to holder | Document: `Verified` |
| 6 | System | — | On the expiry date with no renewal | — | Configured operational restriction applied (BR-435) | Push + email + in-app banner | Document: `Expired` |
| 7 | System | — | Applies the restriction | Mandatory guard document expired → allocation veto (§25.15.5). Non-mandatory → soft penalty. Licence expired → BR-436 geography block | Restriction recorded with its source document | Push to Operations Manager and Agency Compliance | Guard: `Active` (allocation-restricted) |
| 8 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-349 | Reviews affected deployments | Guards currently deployed on an expired mandatory document must be replaced (WKF-18) | Replacement cases opened where required | Push | Replacement: `Pending` |

```
Nightly scan ──> 60d Expiring ──> 30d ──> 7d ──> expiry date
                    │                              │
                    └─ renewal uploaded ──> verify ─┴─> Verified (horizon reset)
                                                   │
                                                   └─ no renewal ──> Expired ──> restriction (BR-435)
                                                                          │
                                                   ┌──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┐
                                                   v                      v                      v
                                        mandatory guard doc         non-mandatory          agency licence
                                        → allocation veto           → soft penalty         → BR-436 geography block
                                                   │
                                        currently deployed? ──> replacement (WKF-18)
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Renewal uploaded but not yet verified at the expiry date | A configurable grace window (default 7 days) treats the document as `Expiring` rather than `Expired` provided a `Pending` renewal exists; the grace is visible and audited. |
| Document has no expiry date but the type requires one | Flagged at upload; verification cannot complete until an expiry date is supplied or the document is marked perpetual by type. |
| Guard on duty when a mandatory document expires mid-shift | The current shift completes — pulling a guard off a live post creates a worse risk — but no further assignment is possible and a replacement case opens for the next shift. This behaviour is explicit, logged and visible to Compliance. |
| Bulk expiry (many guards, same training batch) | The board groups by document type and expiry date so a single renewal drive can be run; notifications are batched to avoid alert fatigue. |
| Renewed document has an earlier expiry than the original | Accepted with a warning; the horizon uses the new date. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-002, BR-404, BR-435, BR-436; §25.15.5.

**Audit events** — `document_expiry_scan_run`, `document_expiring`, `document_expiry_reminder_sent`, `document_renewed`, `document_expired`, `document_restriction_applied`, `document_grace_applied`.

**SLA/timing** — Scan nightly. Notifications at 60/30/7 days and on the expiry date. Restriction applied at 00:05 local on the expiry date (or at grace expiry).

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a guard whose mandatory training certificate expires today with no renewal uploaded, **When** the nightly job runs, **Then** the document is `Expired`, the guard is excluded from allocation with a named reason, and any assignment beyond the current shift generates a replacement case.

### 29.31 WKF-30 — Licence renewal

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Agency portal web (§20), OPS (§22) |
| **Trigger** | A PSARA licence reaches the `Expiring` horizon (default 120 days for licences, longer than ordinary documents because renewal is slow) |
| **Actors** | Agency Compliance, Agency Owner, Compliance, Verification |
| **Preconditions** | Licence record exists with issuing authority, scope and validity |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | — | Flags the licence at 120/90/60/30/7 days | — | Renewal case created at 120 days | Push + email to Agency Owner and Agency Compliance | Licence: `Expiring` |
| 2 | Agency Compliance | SUR-SCR-348 | Opens the renewal workspace with the authority's checklist | Checklist is configuration per state/district, never hard-coded | Case populated | — | Renewal: `In Progress` |
| 3 | Agency Compliance | SUR-SCR-348 | Assembles supporting documents and records the application | Application reference and date mandatory once submitted externally | Evidence stored | — | Renewal: `Pending` |
| 4 | Agency Compliance | SUR-SCR-348 | Records the authority's outcome and uploads the renewed licence | New validity dates; scope compared against the old scope | New licence version created; geography index updated | Push to Agency Owner | Licence: `Pending` |
| 5 | Verification | SUR-SCR-466 | Verifies the renewed licence (WKF-04 document path) | Same verification rigour as first issue | Licence verified | Push | Licence: `Verified` |
| 6 | System | — | Recomputes operating geography | Districts removed from scope trigger a deployment review | Coverage updated | Push to Operations Manager where coverage shrank | Licence: `Active` |
| 7 | System | — | Expiry reached with no renewal | — | BR-436 restrictions applied: no new allocations in that geography | Push + email + persistent banner | Licence: `Expired` |
| 8 | Compliance | SUR-SCR-467 | Decides on operational restrictions for the tenant | Restriction set is configured, proportionate and recorded | Restrictions applied | Push to Agency Owner | Agency: `Active` (restricted) or `Suspended` |

```
120d ──> Renewal case ──> Assemble ──> Apply (external) ──> Outcome recorded ──> Verify ──> Coverage updated
   │                                        │
   │                                        └─ authority delay ──> grace decision by Compliance (recorded)
   └─ expiry with no renewal ──> BR-436 restrictions ──> existing deployments reviewed ──> possible suspension (WKF-37)
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Authority processing exceeds the licence validity | The platform records the application reference and date. Whether operations may continue on a pending renewal is a **configured jurisdiction rule**, not a platform assumption; Compliance records the decision and its basis, and the client-facing position is stated explicitly. The platform never asserts a legal conclusion. |
| Renewed scope is narrower | Districts lost trigger a deployment review; sites in lost districts are flagged and a transition plan is required before the old licence expires. |
| Licence rejected by the authority | Compliance decides on restriction or suspension (WKF-37); clients in the affected geography must be informed per contract. |
| Agency operates in four states | Each licence renews independently; the compliance dashboard shows the earliest expiry as the binding constraint. |
| District-only licence | Coverage is district-scoped; site creation is validated at district granularity (BR-406). |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-002, BR-406, BR-435, BR-436.

**Audit events** — `licence_expiring_flagged`, `renewal_case_opened`, `renewal_application_recorded`, `licence_renewed`, `licence_verified`, `licence_coverage_changed`, `licence_expired`, `licence_restriction_applied`.

**SLA/timing** — Renewal case opened 120 days before expiry. Application recorded by 60 days before expiry (target). Escalation to the Agency Owner at 30 days and to Compliance at 7 days if no application is recorded.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a licence expiring in 25 days with no recorded application, **When** the daily check runs, **Then** the Agency Owner receives an escalation, a persistent banner appears on SUR-SCR-248, and the compliance dashboard shows the affected districts and deployed guard count.

### 29.32 WKF-31 — Subscription purchase

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Trinetra (§19), Agency portal web (§20), OPS (§22) |
| **Trigger** | Agency selects a plan during registration (WKF-03), upgrades, downgrades, or renews |
| **Actors** | Agency Owner, Agency Finance, Finance, Sales |
| **Preconditions** | Plan catalogue published; billing period and GST treatment settled (D-001) |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Agency Owner | SUR-SCR-220 / SUR-SCR-357 | Selects Starter ₹5,000, Professional ₹10,000, or Enterprise | Enterprise never shows a price and routes to sales | Subscription draft with the entitlement set | — | Subscription: `Draft` |
| 2 | System | — | Computes the amount for the billing period | Period and GST per D-001; proration on mid-period changes | Order created in integer paise | — | Subscription: `Draft` |
| 3 | Agency Owner | SUR-SCR-228 | Pays via Razorpay | Payment webhook is the source of truth (WKF-22) | Payment captured; ledger entries written | Receipt email | Payment: `Completed` |
| 4 | System | — | Activates the subscription and applies entitlements | Entitlement set matches the plan exactly; usage limits per D-003 | Feature flags and limits applied to the tenant | Push + email; in-app entitlement banner | Subscription: `Active` |
| 5 | Agency Owner | SUR-SCR-357 | Upgrades mid-period | Upgrade takes effect immediately; the difference is prorated | New entitlements applied at once | Push | Subscription: `Active` |
| 6 | Agency Owner | SUR-SCR-357 | Downgrades | Downgrade takes effect at the period end, never mid-period; over-limit entities become read-only rather than deleted (BR-437) | Scheduled change recorded with the affected entity counts shown | Push + email with the exact consequences | Subscription: `Active` (change scheduled) |
| 7 | System | — | Renews at the period end | Auto-renew if a mandate exists; otherwise a renewal invoice | Renewal payment attempted | Reminder at T−7, T−3, T−1 | Subscription: `Active` |
| 8 | Finance | SUR-SCR-463 | Tracks subscription revenue and MRR | — | Revenue recognised per §35 | — | — |

```
Select plan ──> Amount + GST ──> Pay ──> Entitlements applied ──> Active
                                   │
                                   ├─ payment fails ──> Draft retained, retry 7 days ──> lapse
                                   ├─ upgrade ──> immediate + prorated
                                   └─ downgrade ──> scheduled to period end ──> over-limit entities read-only (BR-437)
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Payment fails at renewal | Subscription moves to the grace path in WKF-32; service is not cut on the first failure. |
| Downgrade would orphan data | Nothing is deleted (BR-437). The agency is shown exactly which entities exceed the new plan's limits and which become read-only; export is offered before the change takes effect. |
| Enterprise agreed offline | Finance creates the subscription with a recorded order reference; the price is never rendered in any agency-facing screen. |
| Trial converts | Entitlements are unchanged; only the billing state changes; no data migration occurs. |
| GST treatment changes | Applies from the next period; issued invoices are immutable (BR-427). |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-427, BR-437, BR-438; D-001, D-002, D-003.

**Audit events** — `subscription_created`, `subscription_activated`, `subscription_upgraded`, `subscription_downgrade_scheduled`, `subscription_renewed`, `entitlements_applied`, `usage_limit_breached`.

**SLA/timing** — Entitlements applied within 60 s of payment capture. Renewal reminders at T−7/T−3/T−1 days.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a Professional agency with 4 branches downgrading to Starter, which supports 1, **When** the downgrade is scheduled, **Then** the agency is shown the 3 branches that will become read-only, an export is offered, and nothing is deleted at the period boundary.

### 29.33 WKF-32 — Subscription expiry

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Trinetra (§19), Agency portal web (§20), Agency app (§21), OPS (§22) |
| **Trigger** | Renewal date reached without a successful payment, or explicit cancellation |
| **Actors** | Agency Owner, Agency Finance, Finance, Support |
| **Preconditions** | Subscription `Active` with a renewal date |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | — | Reminds before renewal | T−7, T−3, T−1 days | Reminders dispatched | Email + push + in-app banner | Subscription: `Active` |
| 2 | System | — | Attempts renewal payment | Mandate present or invoice raised | Payment attempted | — | Subscription: `Active` |
| 3 | System | — | Payment fails → enters grace | Grace length per D-220 (recommended 7 days) | Grace state applied; full functionality retained | Email + push daily during grace | Subscription: `Expiring` |
| 4 | System | — | Grace ends without payment | — | Restricted mode applied (BR-438): read-only for management modules; **operationally critical paths stay live** — attendance capture, SOS, incident reporting and wake checks continue | Email + push + persistent banner | Subscription: `Expired` |
| 5 | Agency Owner | SUR-SCR-357 | Pays the outstanding amount | — | Entitlements restored immediately | Push + email | Subscription: `Active` |
| 6 | System | — | 30 days in restricted mode | — | Data export offered; account flagged for archival review | Email | Subscription: `Expired` |
| 7 | Finance / Support | SUR-SCR-465 | Decides on archival after the retention window | Archival requires a recorded decision; data is retained per §39 | Tenant `Archived`; data retained under policy | Email with export links | Agency: `Archived` |

```
T−7/−3/−1 reminders ──> renewal attempt ──┬── success ──> Active
                                          └── failure ──> Grace (full function, D-220)
                                                              │
                                                    grace ends ──> Restricted mode (BR-438)
                                                              │   (SOS, attendance, incidents, wake checks STILL WORK)
                                                              │
                                            payment ──────────┴──> Active restored
                                                              │
                                                     30 days ──> export offered ──> archival decision
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Guards are on duty when restriction begins | Field operations are never cut. The Guard App continues to function for attendance, patrol, wake checks, incidents and SOS. Only agency management functions become read-only. Cutting safety capability for a billing failure is not an acceptable behaviour. |
| Agency disputes the charge | Restriction is paused while the dispute is open, for a maximum configured window, and the pause is recorded. |
| Agency cancels deliberately | A wind-down date is agreed; deployments must be transitioned; the same restricted-mode rules apply after the date. |
| Payment succeeds after archival | Restoration is possible within the retention window; after it, data is restored only from backup per §49 and with a recorded approval. |
| Clients of the agency affected | Where Suraksha-routed clients are served by the agency, Suraksha is alerted so continuity can be arranged (BR-444). |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-437, BR-438, BR-444.

**Audit events** — `subscription_renewal_attempted`, `subscription_grace_started`, `subscription_restricted`, `subscription_restored`, `subscription_export_offered`, `tenant_archived`.

**SLA/timing** — Grace per D-220. Restricted mode 30 days before archival review. Restoration within 60 s of payment.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** an agency in restricted mode with 40 guards on active shifts, **When** a guard presses SOS, **Then** the alert is created at P0 and handled normally, and no billing state affects the alert path.

### 29.34 WKF-33 — OCR migration

Enterprise-only legacy data migration (§1.4). The risk is not extraction — it is quietly importing wrong data into a live operational system. Every gate below exists to prevent that.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Agency portal web (§20), Agency portal desktop (§20/§1.3), OPS (§22) |
| **Trigger** | Enterprise agency starts a migration, or Suraksha onboarding runs one on the agency's behalf |
| **Actors** | Agency Admin, Agency Owner, Agency Compliance, Agency Finance, Support (assisted migration), Super Admin |
| **Preconditions** | Enterprise entitlement `Active`; source material available (scans, PDFs, spreadsheets, photographs of registers); a signed data-processing basis (§39) |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Agency Admin | SUR-SCR-355 | Creates a migration project and selects the entity types to migrate | Entity types: guards, clients, sites, contracts, attendance history, payroll history, documents | Project created with a scope manifest | — | Migration: `Draft` |
| 2 | Agency Admin | SUR-SCR-363 / SUR-SCR-364 | Uploads source material in batches, or scans directly on the desktop build | Batch size limits; file types; every file hashed for de-duplication | Files stored in a quarantined migration area, isolated from live data | — | Batch: `Pending` |
| 3 | System | — | Runs OCR and structure detection | Per-field confidence scores retained; nothing is auto-accepted below the configured threshold | Extracted records staged with confidence and provenance (file + page + region) | Push on batch completion | Batch: `In Progress` |
| 4 | System | — | Maps extracted fields to platform entities | Mapping template per source layout, reusable across batches | Field mapping applied; unmapped fields retained as notes rather than discarded | — | Batch: `In Progress` |
| 5 | System | — | Validates every staged record | Mandatory fields present; date sanity; duplicate detection against live data and within the batch; referential integrity (a site must reference an existing or in-batch client) | Validation results attached per record | — | Record: `Pending` |
| 6 | Agency Admin | SUR-SCR-355 | Reviews the exception list, correcting against the source image shown beside the field | Low-confidence and failed-validation records must be reviewed individually; there is no bulk-accept for identity or financial data (BR-439) | Corrections recorded with the corrector's identity | — | Record: `Pending` → `Verified` |
| 7 | System | — | Produces the reconciliation report | Counts by entity type: extracted, auto-validated, corrected, rejected, duplicate; financial totals compared against the agency's declared control totals | Reconciliation report generated | — | Migration: `In Progress` |
| 8 | Agency Owner (+ Agency Finance for financial data) | SUR-SCR-355 | Signs off the reconciliation | Sign-off requires the control totals to match, or every variance to be explained (BR-440) | Sign-off recorded with identity and timestamp | Push | Migration: `Pending` |
| 9 | Agency Admin | SUR-SCR-355 | Commits the batch to live data | Commit is transactional per batch; a dry-run must have been executed first | Records written to live tables with `source=migration` and a link to the source page | Push on completion | Records: `Draft` / `Pending` per type |
| 10 | System | — | Sets the post-commit state per entity type | Guards and clients enter as `Pending` (they must pass verification, never auto-`Active`, BR-439); historical attendance and payroll enter as `Archived` reference data, non-editable and excluded from live payroll; documents enter as `Pending` verification | States applied | — | Guard: `Pending` |
| 11 | Agency Admin | SUR-SCR-355 | Runs the post-commit audit sample | A configurable sample (default 5%, minimum 20 records) is compared field by field against the source | Sample result recorded | — | Migration: `In Progress` |
| 12 | Agency Owner | SUR-SCR-355 | Closes the migration | Sample accuracy must meet the configured threshold (default 98% field-level) or the batch is rolled back | Migration closed; source files retained per the retention policy | Email summary | Migration: `Completed` |
| 13 | Agency Admin | SUR-SCR-355 | Rolls back a committed batch | Rollback is available for a configured window (default 7 days) and only where no dependent live records exist | Batch reversed; audit entries retained | Push | Batch: `Cancelled` |

**Flow**

```
Project ──> Upload batches (quarantined) ──> OCR + confidence ──> Field mapping ──> Validation
                                                                                        │
                    ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                    v
            Exception review (source image beside field, no bulk-accept for identity/financial)
                    │
                    v
            Reconciliation report ──> control totals match? ──no──> explain every variance
                    │yes                                                    │
                    v                                                        v
            Sign-off (Owner + Finance for financial data) <──────────────────┘
                    │
                    v
            Dry run ──> Commit (transactional per batch)
                    │
                    ├── guards/clients ──> Pending (must pass verification)
                    ├── historical attendance/payroll ──> Archived reference data (never feeds live payroll)
                    └── documents ──> Pending verification
                    │
                    v
            Post-commit 5% audit sample ──┬── ≥98% ──> Migration Completed
                                          └── <98% ──> rollback batch ──> re-map ──> re-run
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Source is a photograph of a handwritten register | Extraction confidence will be low; those records route entirely to manual review with the image displayed. The platform must not pretend to have read what it could not. |
| Duplicate guard already exists in live data | The staged record is flagged as a duplicate with a side-by-side comparison; the operator chooses merge, skip or create-new, and the choice is recorded per record. |
| Financial control totals do not match | Sign-off is blocked (BR-440). Every variance must be individually explained and recorded before commit. |
| Historical payroll data imported | Enters as `Archived` reference data only. It never feeds a live payroll run, never generates payslips and never creates ledger entries. This is absolute. |
| Historical attendance imported | Enters as `Archived` reference data. It cannot be used as the basis for an invoice (BR-426 requires a locked period generated by the platform). |
| Commit fails partway | The batch is transactional: either all records in the batch commit or none do. A partial commit is a defect, not a state. |
| Migration data contains PII beyond the agreed scope | The out-of-scope fields are retained as unmapped notes only if the data-processing basis covers them; otherwise the operator is prompted to discard them, and the discard is logged. |
| Agency downgrades from Enterprise mid-migration | The project is suspended, not deleted; staged data is retained for the configured window; commit requires the entitlement to be restored. |
| Rollback requested after dependent records exist | Rollback is refused with the dependent records named; the correction path is normal editing with audit, not a silent reversal. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-003, BR-422, BR-426, BR-439, BR-440.

**Audit events** — `migration_project_created`, `migration_batch_uploaded`, `ocr_extraction_completed`, `migration_mapping_applied`, `migration_validation_run`, `migration_record_corrected`, `migration_duplicate_resolved`, `migration_reconciliation_generated`, `migration_signed_off`, `migration_dry_run`, `migration_committed`, `migration_sample_audited`, `migration_rolled_back`.

**SLA/timing** — OCR processing target 500 pages/hour per project `[ASSUMPTION: A-212]`. Reconciliation report generated within 1 h of validation completion. Rollback window 7 days from commit.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** a batch of 400 guard records where 60 have field-level confidence below threshold, **When** the Agency Admin opens the exception list, **Then** all 60 require individual review with the source image displayed, and no bulk-accept control exists on that screen.
- **Given** committed historical payroll data, **When** a live payroll run is created for the current period, **Then** the migrated records are not included in any computation and do not appear in the run's line items.
- **Given** a post-commit audit sample scoring 94% field accuracy against a 98% threshold, **When** the Agency Owner attempts to close the migration, **Then** closure is blocked and rollback is offered with the failing fields listed by type.

### 29.35 WKF-34 — AI request

Action classes, guardrails and the prohibited-action list are owned by **§25** and **§41**. This workflow covers the request path only.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | All surfaces with an assistant: SUR-SCR-134, 206, 353, 396, 501 |
| **Trigger** | A user submits a voice or text request to an assistant surface |
| **Actors** | Any authenticated role, scoped by §31 |
| **Preconditions** | User authenticated; AI enabled for the tenant and role; language supported (§25) |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | User | Assistant surface | Submits voice or text | Language detected: profile → device locale → input | ASR where voice; transcript retained per §39 | — | Interaction: `Draft` |
| 2 | System | — | Resolves intent and action class | Read-only · Recommendation · Approval-required · Automated (low-risk only) | Intent classified; tier routing (T0 deterministic where possible) | — | Interaction: `In Progress` |
| 3 | System | — | Applies role and tenant scoping before retrieval | The user's permission set bounds the retrievable data; cross-tenant retrieval is impossible | Scoped retrieval executed | — | Interaction: `In Progress` |
| 4 | System | — | Executes by class | Read-only: answers with citations. Recommendation: proposes with reasons, no write. Approval-required: creates an approval (WKF-35). Automated: executes only if the action is on the low-risk allowlist | Result produced; every write path logged | Push where an approval is created | Interaction: `Completed` / Approval: `Pending` |
| 5 | User | Assistant surface | Acts on the response: accepts a recommendation, opens the cited record, or submits an approval | — | User action linked to the interaction | — | Interaction: `Completed` |
| 6 | System | — | Logs the interaction for governance | Prompt, intent, class, data scope, output, user action, model tier | Interaction log written (§41) | — | Interaction: `Completed` |

```
Utterance ──> language ──> intent + action class ──> role/tenant scoping ──> retrieval
                                                                                │
     ┌──────────────────────┬────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┤
     v                      v                    v                              v
 Read-only              Recommendation      Approval-required              Automated (low-risk)
 answer + citations     proposal + reasons  ──> WKF-35 approval queue      execute + log
     │                      │                    │                              │
     └──────────────────────┴────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┘
                                       │
                            Interaction logged (§41)
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Request falls in the prohibited list (§1.7) | Refused with a plain explanation and a link to the correct human path. No partial execution, no "I can draft it for you" workaround on payments, payroll, permissions, deletions, terminations, compliance status or data export. |
| Intent confidence low | The assistant asks one clarifying question rather than guessing; two failed clarifications route to the module UI. |
| Language is Tier 3 and the intent is safety-relevant | The assistant does not answer; it surfaces the supervisor and control-room contacts instead (§25). |
| Model provider unavailable | Deterministic intents (navigation, filters, expiry lists, allocation scoring) keep working; generative intents show an unavailability message with the module UI fully usable. |
| Response would include restricted data (site access codes, guard PII beyond role) | Redacted per §25.6, with the redaction visible rather than silent. |
| User asks about another tenant | Impossible by construction; the assistant states that the data is outside the user's scope. |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-441, BR-442; §1.7 foundation rule; §41 governance.

**Audit events** — `ai_interaction_started`, `ai_intent_classified`, `ai_scope_applied`, `ai_response_generated`, `ai_action_refused`, `ai_redaction_applied`, `ai_approval_created`, `ai_interaction_logged`.

**SLA/timing** — Deterministic intents ≤1.2 s p95. Generative responses ≤4 s p95 with a streaming indicator beyond 1 s.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** an Operations Manager asking "increase Ravi's salary by 2,000", **When** the intent is classified, **Then** the request is refused as a prohibited action class, the reason is stated plainly, and a link to the payroll module is offered.

### 29.36 WKF-35 — AI approval

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | Agency portal web (SUR-SCR-354), OPS (SUR-SCR-477), Admin app (SUR-SCR-482), Agency app (SUR-SCR-373) |
| **Trigger** | An AI interaction produces an Approval-required action (WKF-34 step 4) |
| **Actors** | The role authorised to approve that action class per §31; the requesting user; Auditor |
| **Preconditions** | The proposed action is within the approver's permission set; the action is not on the prohibited list |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System | — | Creates the approval with a full change preview | Preview must show before → after for every field the action would change; an action with no computable preview cannot be proposed | Approval record created with the originating interaction ID | Push to the approver | Approval: `Pending` |
| 2 | System | — | Routes to the approver | Approver resolved from §31; never the AI, never the requester where separation applies | Routing recorded | — | Approval: `Pending` |
| 3 | Approver | SUR-SCR-354 / SUR-SCR-477 | Reviews: what was asked, what the AI proposes, why, the data it used, the exact diff | The approver can open every cited record before deciding | View events recorded | — | Approval: `In Progress` |
| 4 | Approver | SUR-SCR-354 | Approves, modifies then approves, or rejects | Rejection requires a reason category; modification is recorded as the approver's own action, not the AI's | Decision recorded with identity, timestamp, IP and device | Push to the requester | Approval: `Verified` / `Rejected` |
| 5 | System | — | Executes only after approval | Preconditions re-validated at execution time — the world may have changed since the proposal | Action executed under the **approver's** identity, with the AI recorded as the proposer | Push to affected parties | Action: `Completed` |
| 6 | System | — | Handles a stale approval | Preconditions no longer valid → execution refused | Approval marked `Failed` with the specific precondition named | Push to approver and requester | Approval: `Failed` |
| 7 | System | — | Expires unactioned approvals | Default 24 h for operational actions, 72 h for administrative | Approval expires; nothing executes | Push at T−4 h and on expiry | Approval: `Expired` |
| 8 | Auditor | SUR-SCR-476 | Reviews AI-originated approvals periodically | Sampling for rubber-stamping: approvals decided in under a threshold time with no record views are flagged | Review record | — | — |

```
AI proposes (Approval-required) ──> Approval created WITH full before→after diff
                                          │
                              routed to authorised approver (§31)
                                          │
        ┌─────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┐
        v                                 v                                 v
   Approve                          Modify + approve                    Reject (reason)
        │                                 │                                 │
        └────────────> re-validate preconditions <───────────┘              └──> nothing executes
                          │
              ┌───────────┴───────────┐
              v                       v
        still valid              stale ──> Failed, precondition named
              │
        execute under APPROVER's identity (AI recorded as proposer)
              │
        audit: ai_approval_executed
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Approver is also the requester | Permitted only where §31 allows self-approval for that action class; otherwise routed upward. The rule is explicit per action class, never implicit. |
| Approver lacks permission for part of the action | The action cannot be partially approved. It is rejected with the missing permission named, and re-proposed within the approver's scope. |
| Action would touch a prohibited class | It could never have been proposed (WKF-34); if such an approval is detected, it is voided and a P1 governance alert is raised (§41). |
| Bulk approvals | Bulk approval is not offered for actions affecting money, permissions, compliance status or employment. Where bulk is permitted, each item still records its own decision. |
| Approval executed and the outcome is wrong | The correction path is the normal workflow for that entity with its own audit; the AI approval record is never edited. |
| Rubber-stamping pattern detected | Approvals decided in under 5 seconds with zero cited-record views are flagged to the Auditor; the pattern is reported, not blocked (R-216). |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-441, BR-442; §31 approval matrix; §41 governance controls.

**Audit events** — `ai_approval_created`, `ai_approval_routed`, `ai_approval_viewed`, `ai_approval_record_opened`, `ai_approval_approved`, `ai_approval_modified`, `ai_approval_rejected`, `ai_approval_executed`, `ai_approval_stale_refused`, `ai_approval_expired`, `ai_approval_rubber_stamp_flagged`.

**SLA/timing** — Operational approvals expire in 24 h; administrative in 72 h. Reminder at T−4 h. Execution within 5 s of approval.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** an AI-proposed roster change approved 3 hours later, during which one of the guards took leave, **When** execution is attempted, **Then** execution is refused, the approval is `Failed`, the specific precondition (guard on leave) is named, and no partial roster change is written.
- **Given** an approved AI action, **When** the audit log is inspected, **Then** the executing identity is the approver, the AI is recorded as the proposer, and the originating prompt is retrievable.

### 29.37 WKF-36 — User offboarding

| | |
|---|---|
| **Owning product(s)** | OPS (§22), Agency portal web (§20), Guard web (§17), Agency app (§21) |
| **Trigger** | Resignation, termination, contract end, or role removal — for a guard, an agency user, or a Suraksha employee |
| **Actors** | HR, Agency HR, Agency Owner, Super Admin, Branch Manager, Finance |
| **Preconditions** | Exit date recorded; successor identified for owned records |

| Step | Actor | Screen | Action | Validation | Backend | Notification | Resulting status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | HR / Agency HR | SUR-SCR-267 / SUR-SCR-438 | Records the exit: type, last working day, reason | Reason category mandatory; termination requires an approver above the initiator | Exit record created | Push to the manager and Finance | Exit: `Pending` |
| 2 | System | — | Computes the impact | Active assignments, owned tickets, pending approvals, issued assets, outstanding advances | Impact list produced | Push to Operations Manager | Exit: `In Progress` |
| 3 | Operations Manager | SUR-SCR-291 | Releases future assignments and opens replacements (WKF-18) | No assignment may remain beyond the last working day | Assignments cancelled; replacements opened | Push | Assignment: `Cancelled` |
| 4 | Branch Manager | SUR-SCR-310 | Records asset return: uniform, radio, ID card, device, weapon where applicable | Every issued asset must be returned or its value recorded as a recovery | Asset register updated | Push to Finance | Asset: `Completed` |
| 5 | System | — | Reassigns owned records | Successor must be named before completion | Tickets, approvals and accounts reassigned | Push to the successor | — |
| 6 | Super Admin / Agency Admin | SUR-SCR-479 / SUR-SCR-357 | Revokes access | All sessions, API keys, device registrations and role grants revoked within the configured window (BR-443, default 15 min from the recorded exit time) | Access revoked; device unbound | — | User: `Suspended` |
| 7 | Payroll / Finance | SUR-SCR-314 | Runs final settlement in the current cycle | Notice pay, leave encashment, advances and asset recoveries applied | Final payslip generated | Push + SMS to the exiting person | Payslip: `Completed` |
| 8 | HR | SUR-SCR-267 | Completes the exit | All checklist items complete | Record set to exited | Email with documents (relieving letter where applicable) | Guard/Employee: `Archived` |

```
Exit recorded ──> Impact computed ──> Assignments released (WKF-18)
                                   ├─> Assets returned / recovered
                                   ├─> Owned records reassigned
                                   ├─> Access revoked (≤15 min, BR-443)
                                   └─> Final settlement ──> Archived
                                            │
                                            └─ assets not returned ──> recovery deduction (D-221)
```

**Alternate & failure paths**

| Deviation | System behaviour |
|---|---|
| Immediate termination for cause | Access is revoked first, before the impact computation, and assignments are released immediately with urgent replacements; the remaining steps follow. |
| Guard absconds | Exit is recorded as `absconded`; assets are booked as recoveries; final settlement is held pending the configured policy and the guard is flagged for future verification (never automatically blacklisted — blacklisting is a separate recorded decision). |
| Assets not returned | Value recovered from final settlement per policy; if that is insufficient, the balance is recorded as a receivable against the individual `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-221]`. |
| Pending approvals owned by the exiting user | Reassigned to the successor; the exit cannot complete while any approval is unassigned. |
| Re-hire later | The identity is reused and a second employment period is created; the prior period is retained in full (§22.9.1). |
| Suraksha employee with privileged access | Additional step: quarterly access review record is updated and any shared credentials they held are rotated (§38). |

**Business rules invoked** — BR-443, BR-419 (replacement), BR-003 (financial records).

**Audit events** — `exit_recorded`, `exit_impact_computed`, `assignments_released_for_exit`, `assets_returned`, `asset_recovery_booked`, `records_reassigned`, `access_revoked`, `final_settlement_run`, `exit_completed`.

**SLA/timing** — Access revocation ≤15 minutes from the recorded exit time. Assignment release before the last working day. Final settlement in the next payroll cycle.

**Acceptance criteria**
- **Given** an employee marked as exited at 14:00, **When** 14:15 passes, **Then** every session is terminated, all role grants show revoked, all API keys are invalid, and any pending approvals appear in the successor's queue.
