### 30.6 Domain (e) — Financial

Canon §4: money is integer paise, never floats; every financial movement is a double-sided ledger entry; operational and financial records are never hard-deleted. This domain expands BR-003 into an enforceable family. Financial *architecture* is §35; these are the rules it must implement.

#### 30.6.1 The immutability family (BR-003 expanded)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Violation behaviour | Override authority | Audit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-141 | **Double-entry invariant.** Every financial movement is recorded as a balanced set of Ledger Entries whose debits equal credits, in integer paise, in a single atomic transaction. A transaction that would leave the set unbalanced is rejected. | Single-sided writes are the root cause of ledgers that cannot be reconciled. | API, DB (constraint + trigger) | Block | **None** | For |
| BR-142 | Ledger Entries are **append-only**. There is no `UPDATE` and no `DELETE` path to a posted ledger entry in the application, in the ORM, or in the database role used by the application. | BR-003 made structural rather than behavioural. | API, DB (revoked privileges) | Block | None | For |
| BR-143 | All monetary amounts are stored and transported as integer paise with an explicit currency code. Floating-point types are prohibited in any code path that touches money, enforced by an automated conformance check in CI. | Float arithmetic silently loses paise, and the loss compounds across a payroll run. | API, DB, Job | Block (build fails) | None | Std |
| BR-144 | A financial document (Invoice, Payment, Payslip, Settlement, Credit Note, Debit Note) that has reached a terminal state (`Completed`, `Verified`, issued, paid) is immutable in every field that affects value, tax, counterparty or period. Non-value metadata (internal notes, tags, attachments) may be added, never removed. | Preserves the distinction between "correcting the record" and "annotating the record". | API, DB | Block | None | For |
| BR-145 | A financial document may be `Cancelled` only before it has been issued to the counterparty or consumed downstream. After that, the only route is reversal. | Cancellation after issuance destroys the counterparty's copy's meaning. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-146 | **Correction by reversal + re-post.** Correcting an issued financial document is performed as: (1) a reversing entry set that exactly negates the original, referencing it; (2) a new correct document referencing both. All three remain visible and linked forever. Partial in-place amendment does not exist. | This is the only correction mechanism the platform offers, and stating it once here prevents twenty local variants. | API, DB | Block on any other correction path | None | For |
| BR-147 | Every reversal carries a reason code from a closed list (data entry error · duplicate · wrong counterparty · price correction · tax correction · service not delivered · dispute settlement · write-off) plus free text, and an approver distinct from the creator. | Reversals are the most abuse-prone operation in any financial system. | API | Block; `Approve` (four-eyes) | Agency Finance approves tenant reversals; Finance (Suraksha) approves platform reversals; never self-approval | For |
| BR-148 | Reversal above the configured value threshold requires a second approver at Agency Owner (tenant) or Finance + Founder/Management (Suraksha) level. Thresholds are `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-301]`. | Approval limits must scale with value or they are meaningless. | API | Approve | As stated; no self-approval at any tier | For |
| BR-149 | **Rounding and paise handling.** Rounding occurs exactly once per document, at the configured rounding point (line · tax-group · document), using the configured rounding mode, and the residual is posted to a dedicated rounding account so the ledger balances to the paise. Rounding never silently disappears. | An unposted residual is a permanent, invisible imbalance. | API, DB | Block on unbalanced posting | None (configuration of point/mode only) | For |
| BR-150 | Tax computation, tax rates and tax treatment are **configuration data** keyed by date, place of supply, HSN/SAC and counterparty registration state. The platform applies the configured treatment for the document date and never re-applies a later configuration to an earlier document. | Canon §0: no hard-coded legal conclusions; and tax config changes must not rewrite issued documents. | API, DB | Block on retroactive application | Finance may correct only via BR-146 | For |
| BR-151 | Any change to tax configuration requires four-eyes approval and a stated effective date; back-dated effective dates require Founder/Management authorisation and generate a report of affected documents for review. | Back-dating tax configuration is a high-impact, high-risk act. | API | Approve | Finance + Founder/Management | For |

#### 30.6.2 Invoicing, numbering and credit/debit notes

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Violation behaviour | Override authority | Audit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-152 | **Invoice numbering integrity.** Invoice numbers are drawn from a gapless, monotonically increasing sequence per (tenant × GSTIN/place of business × configured series × financial year). Numbers are allocated at issuance, never at draft creation, and never reused. | Gaps and reuse are the two failure modes that make a tax-facing sequence indefensible. | API, DB (sequence + unique index) | Block | **None** | For |
| BR-153 | A number, once allocated, is never released — including on cancellation. A cancelled issued invoice retains its number and is neutralised by a credit note (BR-156), leaving the sequence intact. | Releasing numbers creates gaps or duplicates. | API, DB | Block | None | For |
| BR-154 | Invoice series configuration (prefix, series reset behaviour at financial-year boundary, place-of-business mapping) is set per tenant by Agency Finance and locked once the first invoice in a series is issued; changes create a new series rather than mutating the old. | A mutated series retroactively changes the meaning of issued numbers. | API | Block | Agency Owner may create new series only | For |
| BR-155 | An invoice cannot be issued unless: the underlying period is locked (BR-073) or explicitly issued as a provisional/advance invoice marked as such; the contract is `Active` (or the invoice is a final invoice on a `Completed`/`Cancelled` contract); the counterparty's billing details required by the configured tax treatment are present. | Prevents invoices built on moving numbers. | API | Block | Agency Finance may issue a provisional invoice with the marker | Enh |
| BR-156 | **Credit note rules.** A credit note references exactly one issued invoice, cannot exceed that invoice's outstanding value net of prior credit notes, draws from its own gapless sequence, carries a reason code, and posts a full double-sided reversal of the credited portion. | Unlinked or over-value credit notes are the standard revenue-leakage path. | API, DB | Block | Agency Finance; above the configured threshold, Agency Owner | For |
| BR-157 | **Debit note rules.** A debit note references an invoice or a contract, is used for post-issuance additional charges, requires the same approval tier as an invoice of equal value, and requires the counterparty-facing reason to be stated. | Debit notes surprise customers; the process must force an explanation. | API | Approve | Agency Finance | For |
| BR-158 | An invoice's billable quantities must be traceable to source records (attendance lines, contract fixed charges, adjustments, penalties). Every invoice line stores its derivation reference set; an invoice line with no derivation is not permitted except for explicitly typed manual lines, which require approval and a reason. | "Where did this number come from" must be answerable in one click, or disputes take weeks. | API, DB | Block; `Approve` for manual lines | Agency Finance | Enh |
| BR-159 | **Shortfall and SLA consequences.** Where a contract configures shortfall deductions or SLA credits, the corresponding adjustment is computed automatically from the coverage record and presented as a proposed line requiring Agency Finance confirmation. Never posted silently; never omitted silently — an unconfirmed proposal blocks invoice issuance until accepted or explicitly waived with reason. | Both silent posting and silent omission are commercial failures; forcing a decision is the only safe design. | API, Job | Approve | Agency Finance; waiver requires Agency Owner | For |
| BR-160 | Invoices are delivered to the counterparty through a recorded channel with a delivery status; an invoice with no recorded delivery attempt does not start its payment-terms clock. | Ageing that starts before delivery produces false receivables and unfair dunning. | API, Job | Flag | Agency Finance | Std |
| BR-161 | Dunning (payment reminders) follows the contract's configured schedule; reminders stop automatically on payment, on dispute (BR-171) and on an agreed payment plan. | Chasing a disputed invoice damages the relationship the platform exists to protect. | Job | Auto-correct (stop) | Agency Finance | Std |

#### 30.6.3 Payments, wallet, payouts and settlement

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Violation behaviour | Override authority | Audit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-162 | Every inbound payment is reconciled to a payment-gateway reference, an amount and a payer, and is posted to the ledger only on confirmed settlement status from the provider — never on client-side success callbacks. | Client-side success is spoofable and is not evidence of money movement. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-163 | Payment webhooks are idempotent by provider reference; duplicate delivery must never double-credit. Signature verification failure results in rejection and a P1 security alert. | Duplicate credit and forged webhooks are the two classic gateway integration failures. | API, DB (unique index) | Block + Escalate | None | For |
| BR-164 | Partial payments are permitted and are allocated to invoices by the configured allocation rule (oldest-first by default) or by explicit allocation; allocation is a recorded, reversible-by-reversal act, never an implicit side effect. | Implicit allocation makes statements irreproducible. | API | Block on implicit allocation | Agency Finance may re-allocate via reversal | Enh |
| BR-165 | **Wallet negative balance prohibition.** A Wallet balance may never be negative. Any operation that would take a wallet below zero is rejected atomically; there is no overdraft, no "settle later" state, and no compensating job that permits a transient negative. | A negative wallet is an unsecured credit line the platform never agreed to extend. | API, DB (check constraint) | Block | **None** | For |
| BR-166 | Wallet debits and credits are ledger-backed like every other movement; a wallet balance is a projection of its ledger, and any divergence detected by the nightly reconciliation raises P0 and freezes wallet operations for that account. | A balance stored independently of its ledger will drift, and drifted balances are unrecoverable without freezing. | API, DB, Job | Block + Escalate (P0) | Finance, after reconciliation | For |
| BR-167 | **Refund authority thresholds.** Refunds require approval by value band: below the tier-1 threshold, Support may raise and Finance approves; tier-2, Finance approves with a second Finance approver; above tier-3, Finance + Founder/Management. Support can never approve. Thresholds are `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-302]`. | Refund is the most common internal-fraud vector in consumer platforms. | API | Approve | As stated; no self-approval | For |
| BR-168 | A refund can never exceed the net amount actually received against the referenced payment, less prior refunds. Refunds to an instrument other than the original require a documented reason, an identity re-verification of the requester, and the higher approval tier. | Redirected refunds are the standard account-takeover cash-out. | API, DB | Block | Finance + Founder/Management | For |
| BR-169 | **Payout holds.** A payout (guard salary, agency settlement, referral payout) is held automatically when any of the configured hold conditions is true: incomplete KYC/bank verification, an open dispute touching the underlying amount, a compliance veto (BR-126), an unreturned asset or weapon (BR-034), a failed prior payout to the same instrument, or a fraud-review flag. Every hold has a reason, an owner and an age. | A payout system without holds pays fraud out at machine speed. | API, Job | Block + Flag | Finance may release a hold with reason, except a compliance veto (Compliance only) and a fraud-review hold (Finance + Founder/Management) | For |
| BR-170 | Payouts follow **maker–checker**: the user who creates or uploads a payout batch cannot approve or release it. Bank/UPI detail changes impose a cooling period (default 24 hours, Policy) before the instrument can receive a payout, with notification to the account holder on both the old and new contacts. | The two controls that stop the majority of payout fraud. | API | Block | None — no role may self-approve a payout | For |
| BR-171 | **Dispute freeze.** Raising a dispute on an invoice line, an attendance line or a settlement line freezes the disputed amount: it is excluded from dunning, excluded from payout release, and marked on statements. The undisputed remainder continues to flow normally. | Freezing the whole invoice punishes both parties; freezing nothing makes disputes meaningless. | API, Job | Block (on the frozen amount only) | Finance may lift with documented resolution | For |
| BR-172 | A dispute has a mandatory owner, a reason code, an evidence set and a resolution (`upheld` · `partially upheld` · `rejected` · `withdrawn`), and its resolution posts through the normal correction mechanism (BR-146), never as a direct balance edit. | Dispute resolution is a financial event and must look like one in the ledger. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-173 | **Settlement cut-offs.** Settlement runs on the configured cycle with a stated cut-off timestamp. Records created after cut-off belong to the next cycle; a record can never be moved between cycles after a cycle is closed. Cycle closure is irreversible. | Movable cut-offs make every period reconciliation provisional. | API, Job, DB | Block | None | For |
| BR-174 | A closed settlement cycle's figures are immutable; corrections appear in the next cycle as adjustments referencing the original. | Same discipline as BR-073, applied to settlement. | API, DB | Block | None | For |
| BR-175 | Settlement statements must reconcile line-by-line to the ledger and to the operational source records; a statement that does not reconcile cannot be published, and the failure raises P1 to Finance. | Publishing an unreconciled statement is worse than publishing nothing. | API, Job | Block + Escalate | None | For |
| BR-176 | Platform commission, subscription fees and any deduction taken by Suraksha from an agency settlement must be itemised on the statement with the rule that produced them, and must match the contracted rate in force on the transaction date. | Opaque deductions are the fastest way to lose a marketplace's supply side. | API | Block on unitemised deduction | None | For |
| BR-177 | Money movement between tenants is impossible: every ledger account belongs to exactly one tenant (or to `SURAKSHA-HQ`), and a journal may not span tenants except through explicitly modelled inter-tenant settlement accounts with both sides recorded. | Cross-tenant leakage in a ledger is unrecoverable and destroys trust irreversibly. | API, DB | Block | None | For |

#### 30.6.4 Payroll

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Violation behaviour | Override authority | Audit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-178 | A Payroll Run consumes a locked attendance period (BR-073) and a versioned salary structure; both versions are recorded on the run so that any payslip can be recomputed exactly. | Recomputability is the only defence in a payroll dispute. | API, DB | Block on unlocked period | None | For |
| BR-179 | A Payroll Run has states `Draft → Pending (preview) → Verified (approved) → Completed (released)`. Release is a separate, four-eyes act from approval, and is never performed by the same user who prepared the run. | Preparation, approval and release are three distinct authorities. | API | Block; `Approve` | Payroll prepares; Agency Finance approves; Agency Owner or a second Agency Finance user releases. `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-303]` on the exact release authority per plan tier | For |
| BR-180 | A released Payroll Run is immutable. Corrections are made as adjustments in the next run, referencing the original payslip line, with the guard's payslip showing both. | BR-003 applied to payroll. | API, DB | Block | None | For |
| BR-181 | Deductions (advances, asset loss, penalties) require an existing approved source record and may not be created ad hoc inside a payroll run; the total deduction in one run may not exceed the configured share of net pay without explicit approval. | Ad hoc deductions inside a run are invisible to everyone except the person making them. | API | Block; `Approve` above the share | Agency Owner | For |
| BR-182 | A guard's payslip must be available to the guard through the Guard App and Guard Platform on release, and must not be modifiable after publication. | Transparency is the product promise to the supply side. | API | Block on post-publication edit | None | Std |
| BR-183 | Payroll data (individual pay, deductions, bank details) is never visible to clients, never visible to other guards, and never included in client-facing exports or AI answers. | Employment data is not a client entitlement. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-184 | Statutory-record generation (EPF/ESIC-related records and similar) is driven entirely by configuration keyed to jurisdiction and effective date, with the platform producing records per the configured scheme. The platform makes no determination of applicability; applicability is configured by Agency Compliance. | Canon §0 in its most sensitive application. | API, Job | Block on unconfigured scheme | Agency Compliance configures | For |
| BR-185 | Payroll may never be executed, altered, approved or released by AI (§25.7 #28, #29). | Canon §1.7 absolute. | API | Block (no tool exists) | None | For |
| BR-186 | Final settlement on a guard's exit is blocked until: attendance is finalised for all worked periods, assets and weapons are returned or written off (BR-034), advances are recovered or written off with approval, and any open disciplinary or dispute item has a disposition. | Exit is the last moment at which anything can be recovered or clarified. | API | Block | Agency Owner may release with a written-off balance and reason | For |
| BR-187 | Salary-structure changes take effect from a stated effective date and never retroactively alter a completed payroll run; a retroactive change is implemented as an arrears adjustment in the next run. | Same discipline as BR-150. | API | Block on retroactive edit | Agency Owner may approve arrears | For |
| BR-188 | A guard must exist as `Active` with verified identity and a verified payout instrument before any payout is released to them; a payout to an unverified instrument is impossible. | Prevents ghost employees and misdirected payments. | API, DB | Block | None | For |
| BR-189 | Ghost-employee detection runs on the configured cycle, flagging: guards with attendance but no device events, duplicate bank instruments across guards, duplicate identity signals, and guards created and paid within the same period without verification. Findings go to Agency Compliance and, for `SURAKSHA-HQ`, Compliance. | Payroll fraud in this industry is overwhelmingly ghost employees. | Job | Flag + Escalate | None | For |

### 30.7 Domain (f) — Booking & contract

Booking lifecycle (B2C) is §11; enterprise lifecycle is §12; these are the rules both implement.

#### 30.7.1 Booking creation and lead time

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Violation behaviour | Override authority | Audit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-196 | A booking requires: a serviceable location (per configured serviceability, D-005), a service type, a start date/time, a duration, and a verified mobile number on the account. | Bookings that cannot be served are worse than no booking: they create a promise the platform breaks. | UI, API | Block | Sales may create an out-of-area booking as an `Opportunity` with an explicit non-guaranteed marker | Std |
| BR-197 | **Minimum booking duration** is configured per service type (defaults: monthly guarding 1 month; event security 1 shift with a configured minimum hours block; PSO per the configured minimum engagement). Requests below the minimum are quoted at the minimum, with the uplift shown transparently. | Hiding the minimum until invoicing is the complaint pattern this rule prevents. | UI, API | Block; quote at minimum | Agency Sales / Sales, with approval, per BR-217 pricing floor rules | Std |
| BR-198 | **Lead time.** Each service type has a configured standard lead time (defaults: monthly guarding 48 hours; event security 72 hours; PSO 24 hours; emergency/urgent deployment path with an urgency surcharge where configured). Bookings inside lead time are accepted only where live availability confirms fulfilment, and are marked `urgent`. | Accepting an unfulfillable urgent booking is the single most damaging thing the platform can do to trust. | UI, API | Block unless availability-confirmed | City Operations may accept inside lead time with a named fulfilment owner | Enh |
| BR-199 | A booking is not `Active` until the configured confirmation condition is met: payment or authorised advance for B2C, contract acceptance for B2B, work order for B2G. Until then it is `Pending`. | One vocabulary, one gate; prevents "confirmed" meaning different things per channel. | API | Block | Sales may mark `Active` on a recorded credit approval for enterprise accounts | Enh |
| BR-200 | A booking cannot be confirmed for a site whose configured onboarding minimum (address, contact, access instructions, site survey where required) is incomplete. | A guard sent to an unspecified location is a guaranteed failure. | UI, API | Block | City Operations, with a named owner for completing the data before deployment | Std |
| BR-201 | Quotations expire at the configured validity (default 15 days) and cannot be accepted after expiry; re-quotation is required and re-applies current pricing. | Stale quote acceptance is a margin leak and a pricing-integrity problem. | API, Job | Block | Agency Sales may extend once, with reason, within the configured cap | Std |

#### 30.7.2 Cancellation, rescheduling, no-show and replacement

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Violation behaviour | Override authority | Audit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-202 | **Cancellation windows and charges** are configured per service type as a band table (e.g. free before T−X; partial charge between T−X and T−Y; full charge after T−Y), shown to the customer before confirmation and stored with the booking as the version in force at booking time. | The terms that apply must be the terms shown, frozen at the moment of agreement. | UI, API | Block on applying a different version | Agency Owner / Founder/Management may waive a charge with reason | Enh |
| BR-203 | A cancellation charge is posted through the normal financial path (invoice or wallet debit with a ledger entry), never as an opaque deduction from a refund. | Opaque netting is unexplainable at dispute time. | API | Block | Finance | For |
| BR-204 | **Rescheduling limits:** a booking may be rescheduled the configured number of times (default 2) at no charge if outside the configured reschedule window; beyond that, or inside the window, the cancellation band applies. Each reschedule is recorded with its old and new times. | Unlimited free rescheduling is functionally free cancellation. | UI, API | Block beyond limit | City Operations / Agency Sales, with reason | Std |
| BR-205 | Rescheduling a booking with a deployed roster triggers roster regeneration and re-checks every rostering rule (BR-004 to BR-038); it never silently carries assignments to new times. | Time-shifted assignments break rest, overlap and eligibility rules invisibly. | API | Block on carry-over without re-check | None | Std |
| BR-206 | **Replacement guarantee.** Where the contract or plan includes a replacement guarantee, the guarantee is expressed as a timer (default: replacement guard on site within the configured hours, per contract) that starts at the confirmed absence event (BR-059) or at the client's accepted replacement request, whichever is earlier. | A guarantee with no defined start time is unenforceable and undisplayable. | API, Job | Escalate on timer breach | None — the timer cannot be reset; a new timer for a second failure runs separately | For |
| BR-207 | Replacement timer breach automatically creates the configured SLA consequence proposal (BR-159) and notifies the client per contract settings. | Guarantees that require the customer to notice the breach are marketing, not guarantees. | Job | Escalate + Approve (for the credit) | Agency Finance confirms the credit; the breach record itself is not editable | For |
| BR-208 | A replacement guard must satisfy every suitability and compliance rule that applied to the original assignment (BR-029 to BR-035, BR-106). Urgency is never a ground for bypassing the compliance gate. | The moment when standards are most likely to slip is exactly when they matter most. | API | Block | **None** | For |
| BR-209 | **No-show handling (guard side):** a guard no-show is `Absent` (BR-059), triggers replacement, and is recorded against the guard's reliability metrics. Consequence beyond the record is an HR process, never an automatic financial or account penalty applied by the system. | Automatic penalties on field data produce injustice at scale. | API, Job | Flag | Agency HR / HR | Enh |
| BR-210 | **No-show handling (client side):** where a client's site is inaccessible or the engagement is cancelled on arrival, the guard's attendance is recorded as `Present — site inaccessible` with evidence; the shift is payable per policy and billable per contract. | The guard travelled and presented; the commercial question is separate from the pay question. | API | Reason + evidence | Operations Manager | Enh |

#### 30.7.3 Contracts, pricing and SLA

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Violation behaviour | Override authority | Audit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-211 | A Contract has explicit start and end dates, a rate card, a billing basis, notice terms, escalation terms, an SLA set, and a named client signatory. A contract missing any of these cannot move to `Active`. | Incomplete contracts are the origin of most billing disputes. | UI, API | Block | Agency Owner may activate with a documented exception and an expiry for completing the missing terms | Enh |
| BR-212 | A contract cannot be `Active` for a site outside the agency's licensed geography (BR-120). | Consistency with the licence gate at the commercial layer, not only at deployment. | API | Block | Compliance | For |
| BR-213 | **Price change effective dates.** A rate change on an active contract takes effect from a stated future effective date, requires the configured acceptance (client acceptance for B2B, notice period for B2C recurring), and never applies to periods already invoiced. Mid-period changes prorate per the configured proration rule. | Retroactive price changes are the fastest route to a lost account. | API, DB | Block on retroactive application | Founder/Management may approve a backdated change only with recorded client consent | For |
| BR-214 | A contract's rate card version is stamped on every invoice and every billable computation, so any invoice can be explained from the terms in force on its date. | Explainability is the requirement; version stamping is the mechanism. | API, DB | Block on unstamped computation | None | Std |
| BR-215 | **Contract renewal:** contracts carry an auto-renew flag, a renewal notice lead time (default T−60 days) and a renewal price basis. Auto-renewal fires only if the flag is set, the client has not served notice, and no compliance veto exists. Renewal always notifies both parties. | Silent auto-renewal without notice is a trust and dispute problem. | Job, API | Block silent renewal | Agency Owner | Enh |
| BR-216 | **Contract expiry:** on expiry without renewal, the contract becomes `Expired`; new deployments stop; existing deployments continue only under an explicit configured grace with a named owner, defaulting to no grace. Invoicing for the completed period proceeds normally. | Deploying under an expired contract is unbillable work and an unmanaged exposure. | Job, API | Block (forward) | Branch Manager may grant the configured grace once, up to 15 days | Enh |
| BR-217 | **Pricing floors.** A quotation or contract rate below the configured floor for the service type and geography cannot be issued without approval at the configured tier; the floor and the approval tier are configuration. AI may draft a quotation but cannot bypass the floor (§25.7 #33). | Below-cost pricing is the classic route to insolvency in guarding. | API | Block; `Approve` | Agency Owner (tenant) / Founder/Management (Suraksha) | For |
| BR-218 | **SLA credit rules.** SLA definitions are contract data (metric, measurement window, target, credit formula, cap). Credits are computed automatically from platform data, presented as proposals (BR-159), capped per the contract, and never exceed the configured maximum share of the period's invoice value. | Uncapped automated credits can exceed the contract's value; the cap must be in the model. | API, Job | Approve; `Block` above cap | Agency Finance may propose an ex-gratia credit above cap with Agency Owner approval | For |
| BR-219 | SLA measurement uses the platform's own operational records (attendance, replacement timers, incident response times, patrol/wake-check completion), and the measurement method for each metric is stated on the contract. A metric with no stated method cannot be credited. | Unstated methods produce two versions of the truth. | API | Block | None | Std |
| BR-220 | Contract termination requires: notice per terms, a stated last service date, a demobilisation plan for deployed guards, final invoicing, and settlement of open disputes. Termination never immediately deletes operational history or the client's access to their historic records (BR-311). | Termination is a process, not a delete. | API | Block on incomplete termination | Agency Owner | For |
| BR-221 | On termination, guards deployed to that client's sites are returned to the bench and re-rostered; the platform never leaves assignments pointing at a terminated contract. | Orphan assignments produce phantom coverage and phantom billing. | Job | Auto-correct + notify | Operations Manager | Std |
| BR-222 | A client cannot hold more active deployed strength than the contract's configured maximum without an amendment; requests beyond it create an amendment proposal, not a silent expansion. | Silent scope expansion is unbillable work. | API | Block; `Approve` | Agency Sales raises the amendment; Agency Finance confirms rates | Enh |
| BR-223 | Site addition to an existing contract inherits the contract's rates unless site-specific rates are configured, and requires the site to pass BR-025 completeness and BR-120 licence coverage. | Prevents the "just add a site" path from bypassing every gate. | API | Block | Branch Manager | Std |
| BR-224 | Advance/security deposit handling: deposits are held as a distinct ledger liability, never recognised as revenue, and are refundable per contract terms on termination less agreed deductions posted as documented lines. | Recognising deposits as revenue is a material misstatement and an unpleasant surprise on exit. | API, DB | Block on revenue recognition of a deposit | None | For |
| BR-225 | An `Individual Customer` booking with no contract uses the platform's published standard terms version, stamped on the booking, and those terms govern cancellation, replacement and refund for that booking. | B2C needs a contract equivalent; the stamped terms version is it. | API | Block on unstamped booking | None | Std |
| BR-226 | A booking or contract cannot be created for a client account that is `Suspended` for non-payment or compliance reasons; existing services continue per the configured suspension policy. | Extending more service to a suspended account increases exposure. | API | Block | Agency Finance may permit with a recorded credit decision | Enh |
| BR-227 | Any commercial commitment displayed to a customer (response time, replacement time, guard count, coverage hours) must be sourced from contract or plan data, never hard-coded into a template or a marketing surface. | Canon §1.8 P5: contradictory published claims are an existing, known defect of the live site; the platform must make that class of error impossible. | UI, API | Block at design review (conformance test) | None | Std |
| BR-228 | Government/B2G engagements follow the same contract model with additional configured fields (work order reference, tender reference, department, sanction authority) and cannot be activated without them where the client type is `government`. | Public-sector billing is rejected without these references. | API | Block | Sales, with a documented exception and expiry | Enh |

### 30.8 Domain (g) — Subscription & entitlement

Plans are canon §1.4 (Starter ₹5,000 · Professional ₹10,000 · Enterprise "Contact Sales", price never displayed). Plan usage limits are `D-003`; billing period and GST treatment are `D-001`; trial model is `D-002`. These rules govern behaviour, not the unresolved commercial values.

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Violation behaviour | Override authority | Audit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-236 | Entitlement is derived from the Subscription's Plan plus any explicitly granted add-on Entitlements; no feature is ever unlocked by role, by request path, or by client-side flag alone. | A single derivation point is the only way plan gating stays correct. | API | Block | None | Std |
| BR-237 | Entitlement is evaluated server-side on every request to a gated capability, not only at menu render. A hidden menu item is not a control. | Hidden-but-callable endpoints are the standard plan-gating bug. | API | Block | None | Std |
| BR-238 | **Plan limit enforcement.** Countable limits (guards, users, sites, branches, API calls, storage — values per D-003) are enforced at creation time with a clear message naming the limit and the upgrade path. Existing records are never deleted or disabled to force compliance. | Punishing existing data for a limit change destroys trust irrecoverably. | API, Job | Block on create | Super Admin may grant a temporary limit uplift with expiry (a recorded Entitlement, not a code change) | Enh |
| BR-239 | Soft limits (approaching threshold) notify the Agency Owner at the configured points (default 80%, 95%, 100%) before any block occurs. | Being blocked without warning at 09:00 on a roster day is a churn event. | Job | Flag | None | Std |
| BR-240 | **Grace period on failed payment.** On a failed subscription payment the subscription enters a configured grace (default 7 days) during which full access continues, retries run on the configured schedule, and the Agency Owner and Agency Finance are notified on every failure. `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-304]` sets grace length and retry schedule. | Immediate lockout on a card failure takes guards off rosters for a banking problem. | Job, API | Flag + notify | Finance may extend grace with reason | Enh |
| BR-241 | After grace, the subscription becomes `Suspended`: write access to gated modules is removed, read access and export remain available, and **all safety-critical functions continue** — SOS, incident reporting, wake checks, and attendance capture are never disabled for non-payment. | Withdrawing safety functions over a billing dispute is not an acceptable commercial lever, at any price. | API, Job | Block (writes only) | **None** — safety functions cannot be disabled by any role | For |
| BR-242 | A `Suspended` subscription retains all data intact for the configured retention (default 90 days) before archival; nothing is deleted during suspension. | Data destruction as a collection tactic is prohibited. | Job | Block on deletion | None | For |
| BR-243 | **Downgrade behaviour:** on downgrade, features above the new plan become inaccessible immediately, but **all data created under the higher plan is retained** and becomes visible again on re-upgrade. Records above the new plan's countable limits are retained in read-only form; new creation is blocked until usage is within limits. | Canon-level product promise: access is removed, data is retained. | API, Job | Block (creation only) | None | For |
| BR-244 | Downgrade takes effect at the end of the paid period unless the customer explicitly elects immediate downgrade; no proration credit is issued for mid-period downgrade unless the configured policy allows it. | Prevents both surprise loss of function and unbudgeted credits. | API | Block on immediate downgrade without election | Finance | Enh |
| BR-245 | Upgrade takes effect immediately on successful payment, with proration per the configured rule; entitlement changes must be visible in the portal within 60 seconds. | The customer has paid; the wait is unjustifiable. | API | Escalate on delay | None | Std |
| BR-246 | **Expiry behaviour.** A subscription that reaches its end date without renewal follows the same sequence as post-grace suspension (BR-241 to BR-243) rather than an abrupt termination path. | One code path, one behaviour, fewer edge cases. | Job | — | None | Std |
| BR-247 | **Data export right on cancellation.** On cancellation or expiry, the tenant retains the ability to export their operational and financial data in machine-readable form for the configured window (default 90 days), without payment, without negotiation and without a support ticket. Export is self-serve. | This is a deliberate product commitment: no data hostage-taking. It is also the strongest possible signal to a prospect evaluating lock-in. | API, UI | Block on any attempt to gate export behind payment | **None** | For |
| BR-248 | Export of a tenant's data on cancellation excludes other tenants' data absolutely and applies the same PII masking rules that applied to the exporting user's role in-product (BR-323). | Cancellation is not a privilege escalation event. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-249 | **Reactivation** within the retention window restores the tenant to its prior state with data intact, at current pricing, with a new subscription period; reactivation after archival requires a restore process which is a supported, priced operation, not a guarantee. | Distinguishes what the platform can promise from what it cannot. | API | — | Super Admin authorises post-archival restore | Enh |
| BR-250 | Trial subscriptions (model per D-002) carry the same enforcement as paid plans, with a trial marker on the tenant, and convert or suspend at trial end following BR-241. Trials never receive elevated entitlements beyond the trialled plan. | A trial that behaves differently from the product teaches the wrong thing. | API, Job | Block | Sales may extend a trial once, with expiry | Enh |
| BR-251 | A tenant may not hold two active subscriptions; plan change is a modification of one Subscription, versioned, never a second record. | Two active subscriptions make entitlement ambiguous. | API, DB | Block | None | Std |
| BR-252 | Enterprise plan pricing is never displayed publicly (canon §1.4); any surface that would render an Enterprise price fails validation. | Explicit canon rule made enforceable. | UI, API | Block at design review + automated content check | None | Std |

### 30.9 Domain (h) — Marketplace

TRINETRA is the agency marketplace (canon §1.1). Moderation mechanics are §22.19; these are the rules.

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Violation behaviour | Override authority | Audit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-256 | **Listing eligibility.** An agency may hold a public marketplace listing only if: the tenant is `Active`; at least one licence is `Active` with a jurisdiction scope; the organisation KYC document set is `Verified`; a named contactable owner exists with a verified mobile; and no compliance veto is in force. | The marketplace's only asset is that being on it means something. | API, Job | Block listing publication | Compliance may permit a provisional listing with a visible "verification in progress" state and an expiry | For |
| BR-257 | A listing's displayed service geography may not exceed the union of the agency's `Active` licence jurisdictions plus any explicitly configured partner-coverage declarations, which are labelled as partner coverage in the UI. | Overstated coverage is the most common marketplace misrepresentation. | API, Job | Block | Compliance | For |
| BR-258 | Listing claims that are computable from platform data (guard count, sites served, years active, response times, attendance performance) are rendered **only** from platform data. Self-declared numbers, where permitted at all, are visually distinguished and labelled as self-declared. | Directly addresses canon §1.8 P5 — contradictory, unverifiable statistics — as a structural rule rather than an editorial one. | UI, API | Block on unsourced claim rendering | None | For |
| BR-259 | **Verification badge criteria.** The verified badge is granted only when all of: licence(s) `Active` and jurisdiction-covered; organisation KYC `Verified`; the configured minimum share of deployed guards holding a complete verified document set (default 95%); no open P0/P1 compliance finding; and platform tenure and activity above the configured minimum. The badge is recomputed on the configured cycle and on every material change. | A badge that is granted once and never re-checked becomes a lie over time. | Job | Auto-correct (badge removal) + notify | **None** — the badge is computed, never granted manually | For |
| BR-260 | Badge removal notifies the Agency Owner with the specific failing criterion and a remediation path, and is reversible automatically the moment the criterion is met again. | Punitive-feeling controls must always show the way back. | Job | Flag + notify | None | For |
| BR-261 | **Review eligibility.** A Review may be created only by an account with a **verifiable completed interaction** with the reviewed party: for a client reviewing an agency, a contract or booking that reached `Completed` (or a deployment of at least the configured minimum duration); for an agency reviewing a client, the same. No interaction, no review. | Unverifiable reviews are the mechanism by which every marketplace's trust layer dies. | API, DB | Block | **None** | For |
| BR-262 | One review per interaction per reviewer. A reviewer may update their review within the configured edit window (default 30 days); after that the review is frozen, with the edit history retained and the "edited" state visible. | Prevents both review farming and permanent revisionism. | API, DB | Block | None | Enh |
| BR-263 | Reviews are published after moderation against the configured content policy. Moderation may reject a review only for policy reasons from a closed list (personal data, abuse, unrelated content, unverifiable factual claim about a third party, extortion attempt), never for negativity. | The rule that decides whether the marketplace is credible. | API | Block on unreasoned rejection | Support moderates; Compliance arbitrates appeals; no role may reject for sentiment | For |
| BR-264 | A reviewed party may post one public response per review and may raise a dispute; neither removes the review. | Right of reply without right of erasure. | API | Block on removal via response | None | Std |
| BR-265 | **Review removal** is permitted only where moderation upholds a policy breach, where the reviewer requests removal of their own review, or where a legal-process request is processed through the configured lawful-request workflow (§40). Removal is always recorded, and the aggregate rating is recomputed. | Silent removal is indistinguishable from manipulation. | API | Block | Compliance | For |
| BR-266 | Ratings are displayed as an aggregate only above the configured minimum count (default 5) to avoid single-review distortion, with the count always shown alongside. | A 5.0 from one review misleads. | UI, API | Block on sub-threshold aggregate display | None | Std |
| BR-267 | **Ranking manipulation penalties.** Detected manipulation — reciprocal review rings, reviews from accounts sharing device/IP/payment fingerprints with the listed agency, incentivised-review solicitation, artificial interaction creation to manufacture review eligibility, or bulk listing keyword stuffing — results in: affected reviews voided, ranking suppression for the configured period, badge suspension, and, on repetition, listing suspension. | Ranking is the marketplace's currency; manipulating it must be more costly than it is profitable. | Job, API | Flag + Escalate + Auto-correct | Compliance decides; Support cannot | For |
| BR-268 | Ranking inputs are disclosed in general terms to listed agencies (what improves rank), while the exact weights are not published. Paid placement, where it exists, is always visibly labelled as promoted and never blended into organic ranking. | Undisclosed paid placement is the fastest way to lose both sides of a marketplace. | UI, API | Block on unlabelled promotion | None | For |
| BR-269 | **Suspension.** A listing may be suspended for: compliance veto, licence lapse (BR-123), verified fraud, unresolved P0 client-safety complaint, manipulation (BR-267), or non-payment beyond the configured threshold. Suspension always states the reason and the remediation. | An unexplained suspension is unappealable in practice. | API | Block (listing hidden) | Compliance; Finance for the non-payment ground | For |
| BR-270 | **Appeal.** Every suspension, badge removal and review-moderation decision is appealable once through a defined path with a configured response time (default 5 working days), decided by a role that did not make the original decision. | Appeal decided by the original decider is not appeal. | API, Job | Escalate on breach of response time | Compliance decides appeals; Founder/Management decides appeals against Compliance | For |
| BR-271 | Suspension of a listing never suspends the agency's operational tenant: rosters, attendance, payroll and client service continue. Marketplace visibility and platform-sourced demand are separable from the SaaS product. | Cutting off an agency's ability to run existing sites endangers guards and clients who did nothing wrong. | API | Block on coupling | None | For |
| BR-272 | Leads or opportunities routed to a suspended or unbadged agency are withheld and re-routed; the platform never allocates new demand to an agency it is simultaneously flagging as non-compliant. | Internal consistency is what makes the compliance signal credible. | Job, API | Block | Compliance | For |
| BR-273 | Agencies may not contact clients sourced through the marketplace outside the platform for the configured period in order to avoid platform fees, where the marketplace agreement configures such a term; detection is signal-based and always human-reviewed before any consequence. | Disintermediation rules are commercially necessary but must never be enforced automatically on weak signals. | Job | Flag (human review only) | Founder/Management | For |
| BR-274 | A client's identity, contact details and site addresses are disclosed to a listed agency only after the configured engagement milestone (accepted quotation or awarded booking), never at browse time. | Contact-harvesting is the marketplace's first abuse vector. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-275 | An agency's listing content (logo, description, imagery, certifications) must be its own or licensed; certification claims must map to a `Verified` document in the platform, or they are not rendered. | Prevents the ISO/certification claim inflation that the industry is prone to. | API | Block on unmapped claim | Compliance | For |

### 30.10 Domain (i) — Identity & access

Canon §4: one central identity service, phone-first, phone verification mandatory, MFA optional for clients and enforceable for staff/agency roles, 30-day client sessions and shorter privileged sessions. Permission architecture is §31; security controls are §38.

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Violation behaviour | Override authority | Audit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-281 | **One identity per verified mobile number.** A verified mobile maps to exactly one identity in the central identity service, across all five web properties and four apps. Multiple *memberships* (guard at agency A, client contact at company B, Suraksha staff) hang off one identity with an account switcher. | Duplicate identities per product destroy the Guard ID's portability, the review-eligibility model and every audit trail. | API, DB (unique index) | Block | None | For |
| BR-282 | A mobile number released by a telecom operator and re-issued to a different person must not silently grant access to the prior holder's account: re-verification after the configured inactivity period, plus a second factor or a support-verified path, is required before an existing identity is reattached. | India-specific and real: recycled numbers are a genuine account-takeover route. | API, Job | Block + `Approve` | Support may complete verification; never grants access without a second signal | For |
| BR-283 | Email is an optional alternate credential; it is never a substitute for mobile verification for any operational role. Login accepts username, email or mobile plus password (canon §1), but the *account* is anchored to the verified mobile. | Reflects the live product while keeping one anchor. | API | Block | None | Std |
| BR-284 | **Role assignment authority.** A user may only be granted a role that is less than or equal to their own authority level, and only within their own scope (tenant, branch, site). No user may grant themselves a role or a permission. | The single most important anti-escalation rule. | API | Block | **None** | For |
| BR-285 | **Privilege escalation prohibition.** There is no request path — API, admin tool, import, workflow automation, integration, or AI — by which a user's effective permissions can increase without an explicit, audited grant by an authorised granter. Bulk imports, workflow rules and API keys inherit the creator's authority ceiling and can never exceed it. | The escalation paths that matter are always the indirect ones. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-286 | Privileged grants (Super Admin, Agency Owner, Finance, Payroll, Compliance, Verification, break-glass custodian) require **four-eyes**: a second authorised approver distinct from the requester and the subject. | Four-eyes on the roles that can move money or change access. | API | Approve | None | For |
| BR-287 | **Segregation of duties** is enforced as mutually exclusive role pairs, not merely as guidance. The exclusion set is in §31.1.6 and is enforced at grant time: a grant that would create a prohibited combination is blocked, naming the conflict. | SoD stated as policy is SoD not implemented. | API | Block | Only Founder/Management may authorise a documented, time-boxed exception with compensating controls | For |
| BR-288 | **Delegation** of an approval authority is time-boxed with a mandatory end date (maximum 90 days), is visible to both parties and to the audit log, does not transfer role membership, and cannot delegate an authority the delegator does not hold. | Holiday cover is a real need; permanent invisible delegation is a control failure. | API, Job | Block; auto-expire | Agency Owner / Super Admin sets the tenant maximum, capped at 90 days | For |
| BR-289 | **Temporary elevation** requires a stated reason, a maximum duration (default 4 hours, ceiling 24), an approver, and automatic revocation with session termination at expiry. Elevation is never renewable silently; a renewal is a new request with a new approval. | Time-boxing is what makes elevation safe. | API, Job | Auto-correct (revoke) | Super Admin approves for Suraksha; Agency Owner for tenants | For |
| BR-290 | Delegated and elevated authority is stamped on every action taken under it, so any record shows both the acting user and the authority under which they acted. | "Who approved this and by what right" must be answerable from the record. | API, DB | Block on unstamped action | None | For |
| BR-291 | **Session rules.** Client sessions expire after 30 days of inactivity; agency and Suraksha staff sessions per role class, shorter for privileged roles; Guard App sessions are long-lived by design (offline-first) but bound to the device (BR-053) and revocable centrally. | Canon §4, made explicit per audience. | API | Auto-correct (expire) | Super Admin may shorten, never lengthen beyond the platform ceiling | Std |
| BR-292 | Sensitive actions require **step-up authentication** (re-entry of password or MFA) regardless of session age. The list is §31.11. | Session age is not evidence of presence. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-293 | MFA is enforceable per role class and is **mandatory** (not optional) for: Super Admin, Finance, Payroll, Compliance, Verification, Agency Owner, Agency Finance, and any user holding a payout-release or permission-grant authority. | The accounts whose compromise is unrecoverable. | API | Block login without MFA enrolment | None | For |
| BR-294 | Concurrent sessions are permitted but enumerable and individually revocable by the user; privileged roles have a configured concurrent-session cap, and a new session beyond the cap terminates the oldest with notification. | Visibility plus a cap on the accounts that matter. | API | Auto-correct | Super Admin configures the cap | Std |
| BR-295 | A device used for privileged access is registered; access from an unrecognised device for a privileged role triggers step-up plus notification to the user and, for Suraksha privileged roles, to Security. | Cheap, high-value control. | API, Job | Block until step-up + notify | None | For |
| BR-296 | **Offboarding revocation timing.** Deactivation of a user revokes all sessions, tokens, API keys and device bindings **within 60 seconds**, platform-wide, across web and mobile. It is never deferred to next login or to token expiry. | Deferred revocation is the standard insider-risk gap. | API, Job | Escalate on breach of the 60-second target | None | For |
| BR-297 | Offboarding requires mandatory reassignment of the user's open approvals, tasks and owned records before deactivation completes; the reassignment is part of the offboarding transaction, not a follow-up task. | Orphaned approvals stall operations invisibly. | API | Block | Agency Owner / Super Admin may reassign to themselves as a last resort, recorded | Enh |
| BR-298 | A deactivated user's historic actions, approvals and records are **never** anonymised, deleted or reattributed. The user record persists as `Archived` for attribution. | An audit trail pointing at a deleted user is not an audit trail. | API, DB | Block | None | For |
| BR-299 | The last remaining Agency Owner (tenant) or Super Admin (platform) cannot be deactivated; ownership transfer must complete first. | Prevents self-inflicted permanent lockout. | API | Block | None | Std |
| BR-300 | **Break-glass** access is permitted only under the conditions, custodial split, time box and post-use review specified in §22.24. Break-glass can never modify or disable audit logging, delete data, or release money. | Restating the boundary here because it is a business rule, not only an ops procedure. | API | Block | **None** | For |
| BR-301 | Break-glass activation is deliberately loud: simultaneous alerts to Founder/Management, Super Admins, Compliance and Auditor within 60 seconds across at least three channels. There is no quiet mode. | The control is social as much as technical. | Job | Escalate | None | For |
| BR-302 | Impersonation ("view as") of a tenant user by Suraksha staff requires recorded consent or a documented incident ground, is time-boxed, is banner-visible inside the session, writes audit records on both sides, and is **read-only by default**; write-capable impersonation requires Super Admin approval per session. | Support needs it; unlogged write impersonation is indefensible. | API, UI | Block without consent/ground | Super Admin for write mode | For |
| BR-303 | Impersonation can never be used to view `Legally-restricted` fields (§17.4), to release money, to change permissions, or to accept a contract on the tenant's behalf. | Impersonation must not be a permission-laundering route. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-304 | API keys and integration credentials are scoped to a tenant, a role-equivalent permission set and an IP/scope allowlist where configured; they expire on a configured schedule and are revoked on the creator's offboarding unless explicitly reassigned to a service owner. | Orphan API keys outlive employees and are the classic forgotten door. | API, Job | Block; auto-revoke | Agency Owner reassigns ownership | For |
| BR-305 | Failed-authentication handling uses progressive delays and lockout per the configured policy, and never reveals whether the identifier exists. | Account enumeration is free reconnaissance. | API | Auto-correct | None | Std |
| BR-306 | Every permission change — grant, revoke, role change, scope change, delegation, elevation — is notified to the affected user and recorded with the granter, the approver, the reason and the effective window. | People must know what they can do and who decided it. | API, Job | Block on silent change | None | For |

### 30.11 Domain (j) — Data & privacy

Privacy architecture is §39; security controls are §38; the guard field-visibility matrix is §17.4 and is canonical for guard data. These rules govern platform behaviour.

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Violation behaviour | Override authority | Audit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-311 | **Retention is configured per data class**, with a defined minimum and maximum for each class, and no record is deleted before its class minimum or retained beyond its class maximum without a documented legal-hold or dispute-hold. | Retention that is neither enforced nor bounded is not a policy. | Job, DB | Block on out-of-policy deletion; `Flag` on over-retention | Compliance sets classes; Founder/Management approves exceptions | For |
| BR-312 | **Deletion vs archival.** Operational and financial records are never hard-deleted (canon §4): they move to `Archived` with retention applied, and become invisible to normal queries while remaining available to Auditor and to lawful-request processing. Hard deletion occurs only at end of retention, as a scheduled, audited, irreversible job. | One vocabulary for "gone from view" versus "gone". | API, DB, Job | Block on hard delete outside the retention job | None | For |
| BR-313 | Audit logs are append-only and are never deletable, editable or redirectable by any role, including Super Admin and break-glass. Their retention is the longest configured and never shorter than the records they describe. | If the audit log is mutable, nothing else in this register is enforceable. | API, DB, Job | Block | **None** | For |
| BR-314 | A deletion request from a data subject is processed through the configured privacy workflow, which distinguishes: data that can be deleted, data that must be retained under a configured obligation or an active contract/dispute, and data that is de-identified instead. The requester receives an explanation of each category. | Promising deletion the platform cannot perform is worse than explaining the limits. | API, Job | Block on undocumented refusal | Compliance decides; Founder/Management for contested cases | For |
| BR-315 | Deletion or de-identification never breaks financial integrity: ledger entries, invoices, payslips and settlements retain the counterparty references required to reconcile, with personal identifiers reduced to the minimum necessary. | Financial reconstruction must survive privacy operations. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-316 | **PII classification is mandatory at the field level.** Every field in every entity carries a data-classification tag (Public · Internal · Confidential · Restricted). Untagged fields default to Restricted and are excluded from exports and AI retrieval until classified. | Fail-closed classification is the only classification that survives a growing schema. | API, DB | Block (default-deny) | None | For |
| BR-317 | **PII masking rules.** Masking is applied server-side per role and audience, not by the client. Defaults: mobile numbers masked except to roles with an operational need (last 4 visible); bank details never visible in full except to Payroll/Finance roles with step-up, and never to clients; identity-document numbers never visible in full to anyone except the `Legally-restricted` roles with a stated purpose code; addresses reduced to city/district except for the guard themselves and Legally-restricted roles; DOB reduced to age or age band except where full DOB is required. | Field-level, role-aware masking is the practical mechanism behind SUR-GRD-005. | API | Block on unmasked serialisation | Compliance may define an audited unmask purpose; unmasking is always logged and visible to the subject | For |
| BR-318 | Unmasking any Restricted field is a discrete action requiring a purpose code, is rate-limited per user, is logged with actor, purpose and timestamp, and is visible to the data subject in their "Who looked at my data" view (§17.10). | Making surveillance visible to the surveilled is the strongest available control. | API, Job | Block above rate limit | Compliance | For |
| BR-319 | Search results, list views, reports, dashboards, notifications and AI answers all apply the same masking as the record view. There is no surface on which masked data leaks through aggregation or preview. | Leakage happens at the edges, not the centre. | API | Block at design review (conformance test) | None | For |
| BR-320 | **Export authority.** Export of personal data is a distinct permission (the Export action plus the PII-access flag, §31.2), is limited by row-level scope, is rate-limited and volume-capped per role, and above the configured volume requires approval. | Bulk export is exfiltration's final step. | API | Block; `Approve` above threshold | Agency Owner (tenant) / Compliance (Suraksha); dual authorisation for bulk guard personal data (SUR-GRD-005) | For |
| BR-321 | Every export records: actor, scope, filters, row count, columns, purpose, destination and a content hash. Exports are watermarked where the format permits, and export records are retained for the configured period. | Post-incident, the question is always "what exactly left". | API, Job | Block on unrecorded export | None | For |
| BR-322 | **Cross-tenant prohibition (absolute).** No query, export, report, notification, search index, cache, AI retrieval or support tool may return data from a tenant other than the caller's, except for Suraksha platform roles acting within their defined scope, and never for `Legally-restricted` fields. Isolation is enforced at the data-access layer, not in application code (§20.3.2). | Canon §3 tenancy rule; the single most damaging possible defect in this platform. | API, DB, Job | Block | **None** | For |
| BR-323 | Aggregated, anonymised cross-tenant statistics may be published only where the aggregation meets the configured k-anonymity threshold and no single tenant contributes more than the configured share; per-tenant identifiable metrics are never disclosed to another tenant. | Benchmarking is valuable and must not become disclosure. | API, Job | Block below threshold | Founder/Management approves the publication set | For |
| BR-324 | Client access to guard data is limited to the Client-visible column of §17.4 and to guards deployed at that client's own sites, during and after their deployment per the configured historical window. | The client's need is bounded by their own site. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-325 | Agency access to a guard's data is limited to the Agency-visible column of §17.4 and to the period of association; on de-linkage, access to new data ends and historic access is limited to the association period. | Portability of the Guard ID depends on this boundary. | API, Job | Auto-correct on de-linkage | None | For |
| BR-326 | Guard grievances are never visible to the agency the grievance concerns (§17.11). | An unprotected grievance channel is not a grievance channel. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-327 | Location data of a guard is collected only during rostered duty windows plus the configured buffer, is never collected off-duty, and is retained per the configured location-retention class (shorter than operational records by default). | Continuous tracking of workers off duty is not something this platform does. | API, Job | Block on off-duty collection | None | For |
| BR-328 | Photographs, selfies and biometric-derived scores captured for attendance are used only for attendance verification, are retained per their own class, and are never repurposed for marketing, model training outside the configured consent, or client display. | Purpose limitation stated where the data is created. | API | Block on repurposing | Compliance, with recorded consent basis | For |
| BR-329 | Data residency and processing location are configuration; where a configured residency constraint exists, processing and storage must satisfy it, and an integration that cannot must be disabled rather than silently exempted. | Configuration-driven, not a legal assertion. | API, Job | Block (disable integration) | Compliance | For |
| BR-330 | Any new field, integration or report that introduces a new personal-data flow requires a recorded privacy review before release, and the review record is linked to the change. | Privacy review as a release gate, not a document. | Job (CI gate) | Block release | Compliance | For |

### 30.12 Domain (k) — AI

Canon §1.7 is the foundation; §25.7 assigns every AI function to a class; §41 governs AI governance. These rules restate the enforceable boundary.

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Violation behaviour | Override authority | Audit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-336 | Every AI tool declares exactly one action class — Read-only · Recommendation · Approval-required · Automated — in code, and the execution path refuses to run an Approval-required tool without an approval token bound to that specific proposal (SUR-AI-016). | The class must be a property of the tool, not of the prompt. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-337 | **The prohibition list (canon §1.7, absolute).** AI may never autonomously execute: payments · payroll changes · permission changes · account deletion · guard termination · compliance status changes · financial settlement · sensitive data export. | Canon-level, non-negotiable. | API | Block | **None** | For |
| BR-338 | Prohibition is **structural, not behavioural**: for every prohibited function there is no tool implementation at all (SUR-AI-017). Refusal must not depend on model behaviour, prompt content or guardrail text. | A prompt-based refusal is one jailbreak away from failure. | API | Block (nothing exists to call) | None | For |
| BR-339 | The additional not-permitted functions enumerated in §25.7.1 — incident severity classification, licence status change, document verification decision, candidate rejection, bid submission, training completion marking, guard blacklisting/termination — carry the same structural prohibition. | Keeps §25 and §30 in exact agreement. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-340 | AI retrieval is **permission-aware by construction**: the AI executes queries as the requesting user, through the same authorisation and masking layer as the UI (§25.6). There is no service account with broader read access backing the assistant. | An assistant with a superuser backing account is a data-exfiltration API with a friendly interface. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-341 | AI answers apply the same row-level scoping and field masking as the equivalent screen (BR-319, BR-322). An answer that would require unmasked data returns the masked form and says so. | Consistency across surfaces is the whole point. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-342 | AI must never disclose data across tenants, including in aggregate form, unless the aggregate satisfies BR-323. | Restating BR-322 for the surface most likely to violate it. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-343 | **Approval authority for AI proposals** is the same authority that would be required for the equivalent human action — never lower, and never a generic "AI approver" role. An AI-prepared payroll adjustment needs exactly the approvals BR-179 and BR-181 require. | AI must not become a lower-friction path to a higher-privilege outcome. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-344 | An AI-prepared proposal must be approved by a human who is not the AI's requester where the equivalent human action requires four-eyes; AI participation never satisfies one of the two pairs of eyes. | AI is not a second person. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-345 | Approval tokens are bound to the exact proposal content; any change to the proposal invalidates the token and requires re-approval. | Prevents approve-then-mutate. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-346 | **Automated class** is permitted only for actions that are low-risk, easily reversible, non-financial and non-safety-affecting, and every Automated action must declare a reversal path available in one action from the interaction record (SUR-AI-018). | The reversal path is what makes the class defensible. | API | Block on registration of a tool without a reversal path | None | For |
| BR-347 | Voice never elevates an action class (§25.7.1 #43). A voice-issued instruction follows the same class, the same approvals and the same step-up authentication as the typed or clicked equivalent. | Voice is an input modality, not an authority. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-348 | **Traceability.** Every AI interaction records: actor, role, tenant, scope, surface, input, retrieved sources with record IDs, model and version, action class, proposal content, approver, outcome and reversal state. Every AI-derived assertion in a user-facing answer must be traceable to the records that produced it. | An untraceable AI answer cannot be defended, corrected or audited. | API, DB | Block on untraced action | None | For |
| BR-349 | AI-generated content that reaches a third party (client notification, incident report, quotation, support reply) is always attributed internally as AI-drafted and human-approved, with the approver recorded, and is never presented externally as an unreviewed system statement. | The human who sent it owns it; the record must show that they did. | API | Block on unattributed send | None | For |
| BR-350 | AI never produces a compliance, legal or eligibility **conclusion**. It may summarise, extract, cite and assess clause-by-clause with evidence (e.g. tender eligibility, §25.7.1 #36), always leaving the determination to a human. | Canon §0 applied to the AI layer. | API, UI | Block on conclusion-shaped output patterns at design review | None | For |
| BR-351 | AI may never create, modify or resolve an operational alert or an incident severity; alerting is owned by §24's deterministic engine. The one deliberate exception is safety-keyword detection **creating** an alert (§25.7.1 #52), because creating an alert is fail-safe. | Fail-safe direction is the deciding criterion. | API | Block | None | For |
| BR-352 | AI features are entitlement-gated per plan (§25.9) and permission-gated per role; a user can never reach data or an action through AI that they cannot reach through the UI. | The assistant is a surface, not a shortcut. | API | Block | None | Std |
| BR-353 | On AI unavailability or low confidence, the platform degrades to the deterministic path and says so explicitly; it never silently substitutes a guess for a computed answer, and never blocks an operational action because AI is unavailable. | Operations must not depend on the assistant. | API | Auto-correct (fallback) + notify | None | Std |

### 30.13 Rule governance

#### 30.13.1 Where rules live

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Registry | Every `BR-nnn` exists as a row in a **rule registry** with: ID, domain, statement, class (Invariant/Policy/Jurisdiction data), enforcement points, default values and bounds, override authority, audit depth, and the code symbols implementing it. |
| Implementation | Policy and Jurisdiction-data rules are evaluated by a shared rule-evaluation service reading tenant/jurisdiction configuration. Invariant rules are code and database constraints. |
| Conformance | A CI check asserts that every registry row has at least one API enforcement point and at least one automated test referencing its ID; a rule with no test fails the build. |
| Drift | A nightly job compares deployed configuration against the registry's declared bounds and raises a P2 finding on any out-of-bounds value. |
| Versioning | Configuration values are versioned with effective dates; every enforcement decision records the configuration version it used, so past decisions remain explainable (BR-130). |

#### 30.13.2 Override reporting

| Report | Contents | Audience | Cadence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Override register | Every override of every rule in the period, with rule ID, actor, approver, reason, and the record affected | Agency Owner (tenant), Compliance + Auditor (Suraksha) | Weekly |
| Top-overridden rules | Rules whose override rate exceeds their configured expected rate | Founder/Management, Compliance | Monthly |
| Never-fired rules | Rules with zero evaluations in 90 days — usually a sign the rule is unreachable or its feature is unused | Product, Compliance | Quarterly |
| Blocked-operation report | Operations blocked by rule, by role — the input to usability work, because a rule blocking legitimate work 200 times a week is a design defect | Product, Operations | Monthly |

#### 30.13.3 Alias table (populated at §29 merge)

| §29 provisional ID | Absorbed as | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| *(to be populated mechanically per §30.0.7 at merge time)* | | |
