## 31. Permissions

This section is the canonical home for the permission architecture and the permission matrices (canon §6). Every product section renders these matrices; none redefines them. Role names are exactly the canon §3 names and nothing else. Security controls that implement these rules live in §38; the guard field-visibility matrix (§17.4) remains canonical for guard personal data and is referenced, not restated.

### 31.1 The access-control model

#### 31.1.1 RBAC base + ABAC attributes

| Layer | What it decides | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **RBAC (base)** | *What kind of thing* a user may do — the verb–object pairs. Role → permission set. | "Operations Manager may Approve attendance." |
| **ABAC (attributes)** | *Which instances* of that thing — the row set the verb may touch. | "…for assignments whose `branch_id` is in the user's branch set and whose site is not marked `sensitive`." |
| **Entitlement (plan)** | Whether the capability exists at all for this tenant (§30.8). | "Workflow automation is Professional+." |

The three layers are evaluated in a fixed order, and **all three must permit** the operation:

```
ALLOW  ⟺  Entitlement(tenant, capability) = true
       ∧  RBAC(role_set, action, object_type) = permit
       ∧  ABAC(user_attributes, object_attributes, action) = permit
       ∧  NOT SoD_conflict(user, action, object)
       ∧  NOT Compliance_veto(object)        (BR-126)
```

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRM-001 | The authorisation decision shall be computed by a single central authorisation service. No module shall implement its own access logic, and no access decision shall be made in a UI component. |
| SUR-PRM-002 | Authorisation shall be **deny-by-default**: an action with no explicit permit is denied, an object type with no declared policy is inaccessible, and a newly added field is Restricted until classified (BR-316). |
| SUR-PRM-003 | Every authorisation decision shall be explainable: the service shall be able to return, for any (user, action, object), the deciding rule, the failing layer and the role or attribute responsible — surfaced in support tooling as "why can't this user do this?". |
| SUR-PRM-004 | Entitlement, RBAC and ABAC evaluation shall be enforced server-side on every request. Hidden UI controls are not access control (BR-237). |

#### 31.1.2 The ABAC attribute set

| Attribute | Source | Values | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tenant_id` | Identity membership | Agency ID, or `SURAKSHA-HQ` | Absolute isolation (BR-322) |
| `branch_scope` | User record | Set of branch IDs, or `ALL` | Branch-level row scoping (§20.3.2) |
| `site_scope` | User record / client membership | Set of site IDs, or `ALL_IN_SCOPE` | Client-side and supervisor-side scoping |
| `assignment_scope` | Live roster | The guards/shifts currently assigned to this user's supervision | Supervisor and Field Officer scoping |
| `geo_scope` | Suraksha org structure (§22.3) | National · State · City/branch | Internal Ops scoping |
| `data_classification` | Field metadata (BR-316) | Public · Internal · Confidential · Restricted | Field-level masking |
| `object_sensitivity` | Site/client/contract flags | `standard` · `sensitive` · `government` | Extra gates (BR-035) |
| `record_owner` | Record | User ID | `O` (own records only) scoping |
| `duty_state` | Live attendance | On duty · Off duty | Guard App capability gating |
| `authority_source` | Session | Direct role · Delegation · Temporary elevation · Break-glass | Stamping and extra audit (BR-290) |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRM-005 | Row-level scoping shall be applied at the data-access layer as a mandatory predicate, not as a filter added by each query author. A query that omits the tenant predicate shall be impossible to construct. |
| SUR-PRM-006 | `assignment_scope` shall be evaluated against the roster in force at the time of the request, and shall expire automatically when the assignment ends — a supervisor loses visibility of a guard when the guard leaves their supervision, without any administrative action. |

#### 31.1.3 Permission inheritance and its limits

| Rule | Statement |
|---|---|
| Hierarchical inheritance | Scope inherits **downward** only: a user scoped to a tenant sees its branches; a user scoped to a branch sees its sites; a user scoped to a site sees its posts. Nothing inherits upward or sideways. |
| Role inheritance | Roles do **not** inherit from each other by seniority. Agency Owner is not "Branch Manager plus more" by construction; each role's permission set is declared explicitly. This is deliberate: implicit seniority inheritance is how Finance quietly acquires operational write access. |
| Additive permission sets | A user may hold one primary role plus named additive permission sets (§20.3.3). Additive sets can only add; there is no subtractive set, because a subtractive model makes the effective permission unknowable. |
| Ceiling rule | The effective permission of any grant, API key, workflow automation, import or AI action is capped at the granter's own authority at grant time (BR-285). |
| No transitive elevation | Holding permission to manage users does not confer the permissions those users hold. A Branch Manager who can invite a Payroll user does not thereby gain payroll access. |
| Scope union | A user with multiple branch assignments has the union of those branches, never the union of *roles* across them — the role is one, the scope is many. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRM-007 | Effective permissions shall be computable and displayable for any user as a flat list, showing for each entry the source (role, additive set, delegation, elevation) and its expiry. |
| SUR-PRM-008 | No role shall be able to grant itself or another role additional module access other than through the declared grant workflow (mirrors SUR-OPS-035). |

#### 31.1.4 Delegation and temporary elevation

| Mechanism | Purpose | Constraints |
|---|---|---|
| **Delegation** | Cover an absent approver | Time-boxed with a mandatory end date (max 90 days); delegates a specific *approval authority*, never role membership; cannot delegate what the delegator does not hold; visible to both parties; auto-expires; actions stamped with `authority_source = Delegation` (BR-288, BR-290). |
| **Temporary elevation** | Handle an exceptional situation needing a higher authority | Requires reason, approver, max duration (default 4 h, ceiling 24 h); auto-revokes with session termination; not silently renewable; every action stamped (BR-289). |
| **Break-glass** | Emergency where normal access control blocks emergency response | Per §22.24 and BR-300/BR-301; dual custodian; 60-minute box; loud alerting; cannot touch audit, money or deletion. |
| **Impersonation** | Support and diagnosis | Read-only by default; consent or documented ground; banner-visible; dual-sided audit; never reaches Restricted fields, money release, permission change or contract acceptance (BR-302, BR-303). |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRM-009 | Delegated and elevated authority shall appear in the delegator's, the delegate's and the administrator's views with a live countdown, and shall be revocable in one action. |
| SUR-PRM-010 | An action performed under delegation, elevation, break-glass or impersonation shall render in every audit and record view as "X acting under Y", never as X alone. |

#### 31.1.5 Deny-by-default in practice

| Situation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| New module shipped without a declared policy | Inaccessible to every role including Super Admin until a policy is declared and reviewed. |
| New field added without a classification | Treated as Restricted: excluded from exports, list views, search indexing and AI retrieval (BR-316). |
| New role created in a tenant | Starts with zero permissions; every permission is added explicitly. |
| Missing jurisdiction configuration | Treated as *not permitted*, never as *permitted* (BR-032). |
| Authorisation service unavailable | Requests fail closed. The platform does not degrade to permissive mode under any circumstance. |
| Ambiguous scope (user in no branch) | No rows visible, rather than all rows visible. |

#### 31.1.6 Segregation of duties (mutually exclusive authorities)

Enforced at grant time (BR-287): a grant that would create any pair below is blocked and names the conflict.

| # | Authority A | Authority B | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| SoD-1 | Create/upload a payout batch | Approve or release a payout | The core maker–checker control (BR-170) |
| SoD-2 | Prepare a payroll run | Release a payroll run | BR-179 |
| SoD-3 | Create a manual attendance entry | Approve that attendance entry | The number's creator must not bless it (BR-068) |
| SoD-4 | Raise a refund | Approve a refund | BR-167 |
| SoD-5 | Create/edit an invoice | Approve a credit note against it | Prevents self-cancelling billing |
| SoD-6 | Verify a document | Upload that document | BR-109 |
| SoD-7 | Grant a permission | Approve that grant | BR-286 four-eyes |
| SoD-8 | Manage a supplier/vendor record | Approve payment to that vendor | Standard procurement control |
| SoD-9 | Operate a compliance veto | Approve deployment overridden by that veto | BR-126 |
| SoD-10 | Administer audit configuration | Hold any money-moving authority | Protects the evidence layer |
| SoD-11 | Supervise a guard | Approve one's own attendance/patrol/incident record | BR-028 |
| SoD-12 | Moderate a review | Be the subject of, or commercially responsible for, that listing | BR-263 |
| SoD-13 | Close a compliance finding | Have performed the action that created it | BR-132 |
| SoD-14 | Approve a rate below the pricing floor | Own the commission/target on that deal | BR-217 |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRM-011 | The SoD exclusion set shall be configuration in the permission service and shall be evaluated at grant time, at delegation time, at elevation time and at approval time — because a conflict can be created after the grant by a role change. |
| SUR-PRM-012 | Where a small tenant cannot staff both sides of an SoD pair, the platform shall permit a documented, time-boxed exception approved by the Agency Owner with a compensating control (e.g. mandatory Suraksha-side review of all payouts above a threshold), recorded and reviewed quarterly. It shall never silently disable the check. |
| SUR-PRM-013 | An approval attempt by a user who is in SoD conflict with the record shall be blocked at approval time even if the grant predates the conflict, and shall raise a P2 finding. |

### 31.2 The permission taxonomy

Seven action verbs and four special flags. These exact terms are used in every matrix, every API scope, every role definition and every audit record across the platform.

#### 31.2.1 Action verbs

| Verb | Precise definition | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **View** | Read a record or a list, including its detail screen, in the form permitted by field-level masking. Includes reading derived views (dashboards, reports) built from those records. | View never implies Export. A user may be able to see 5,000 rows on screen and be unable to export one. |
| **Create** | Bring a new record into existence in its initial status (typically `Draft` or `Pending`). | Create never implies Approve. Creating an invoice draft is not issuing it. |
| **Edit** | Modify an existing record's mutable fields, within its current status's mutability rules. | Edit is status-aware: a `Verified` or `Completed` record's value fields are immutable regardless of the Edit permission (BR-144). |
| **Approve** | Move a record across an authority boundary — issue, verify, release, publish, accept, authorise. This is the verb that carries commercial, financial or compliance consequence. | Approve is always a distinct permission from Edit, always audited at Enh or For depth, and is subject to SoD. |
| **Reject** | Terminate a pending item with a mandatory reason code, returning it to its originator. | Reject is granted with Approve in most roles but is separable, because some roles may return work without being able to authorise it. |
| **Export** | Extract data out of the platform in a portable form: file download, report export, API bulk read, print-to-file, or scheduled delivery. | A distinct, separately grantable, rate-limited, volume-capped and always-logged permission (BR-320, BR-321). |
| **Delete** | Move a record to `Archived` (canon §4 soft delete). True erasure occurs only through the retention job (BR-312). | No role has a hard-delete permission in the product. "Delete" in every matrix means Archive. |

#### 31.2.2 Special flags

| Flag | Precise definition | Grant conditions |
|---|---|---|
| **Financial access** | The ability to see monetary values, ledger entries, invoices, payouts, payroll amounts, wallet balances and settlement data, and to perform money-affecting actions within the verbs granted. Absent this flag, monetary columns render as `—` rather than as zero. | Requires MFA (BR-293); subject to SoD-1/2/4/5/8; step-up for release actions. |
| **PII access** | The ability to see personal data above the Internal classification — full mobile numbers, addresses, dates of birth, identity-document references, bank details, verification evidence — in the form each role is entitled to. Sub-flagged by class: `PII-contact`, `PII-financial`, `PII-identity`, `PII-restricted`. | `PII-restricted` (the §17.4 Legally-restricted set) requires a named role, a purpose code per access, rate limiting, subject visibility (BR-318) and dual authorisation for bulk (BR-320). |
| **AI access** | The ability to use the AI assistant on a surface, and — separately — the ability to *approve* AI-prepared Approval-required proposals. Never widens the user's data or action reach (BR-340, BR-352). | Entitlement-gated per plan (§25.9). Approval of AI proposals requires the same authority as the human-equivalent action (BR-343). |
| **Administrative access** | The ability to change how the system behaves rather than what it records: roles and permissions, entitlement overrides, integrations and API keys, workflow automation, notification templates and routing, security settings, retention and classification configuration, jurisdiction configuration. | Four-eyes on grant (BR-286); MFA mandatory; step-up per action; every use audited at For depth. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRM-014 | The four flags shall be independent of the verbs: a role may hold View on a module without Financial access (seeing operational content with monetary values suppressed), and this shall be the default for all operational roles. |
| SUR-PRM-015 | Every API scope, UI capability check, report column and export column shall map to exactly one (module, verb) pair plus zero or more flags. Any capability that cannot be expressed in this taxonomy is a design defect and shall be redesigned, not special-cased. |
| SUR-PRM-016 | `PII-restricted` access shall be held by named individuals, not by roles alone: the role makes it grantable; a separate per-user grant with an expiry makes it active. |

#### 31.2.3 Matrix legend (applies to Matrices A–D)

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **✔** | Permitted within the role's normal scope |
| **✖** | Not permitted |
| **A** | Permitted but requires approval by another authority before taking effect |
| **O** | Own records only (created by, assigned to, or owned by the user) |
| **B** | Own branch only (the user's `branch_scope`) |
| **S** | Own site only (the user's `site_scope`) |
| **M** | Permitted, but data is masked per BR-317 (monetary values suppressed and/or PII masked) |
| **✔ᴬ** | Permitted, and this action additionally requires step-up authentication (§31.11) |

Symbols combine, most-restrictive-first: `✔ B M` = permitted, own branch only, with masked fields. A cell showing `A B` = permitted for own branch, subject to approval. Where a role's scope is inherently narrower than the platform (e.g. City Operations is city-scoped by definition, §22.3), the geographic scope is implicit and not repeated in every cell.

### 31.3 Matrix A — Suraksha internal roles (OPS)

Modules per §22. Column roles: **Super Admin** · **Ops** (National Operations / State Operations / City Operations — one column; the difference between them is `geo_scope`, not capability) · **Command Center Operator** · **Finance** · **Compliance**.

Roles not shown in Matrix A but defined in canon §3 — Founder/Management, Verification, Support, Sales, HR, Recruitment, Marketing, Auditor — are covered by §22.26's module × role visibility table, which is the canonical detail for those roles; Matrix A does not restate it. Two standing rules apply to them: **Auditor** = View ✔ on every module and every record, Export ✔ with logging, Create/Edit/Approve/Delete ✖ everywhere except investigation notes (SUR-OPS-034); **Founder/Management** = View ✔ platform-wide with Financial access, Approve only where explicitly named in §30 (backdated price change, tax back-dating, SoD exception, appeals against Compliance, tier-3 refunds), Administrative access ✖.

### 31.4 Matrix B — Agency roles (Agency Portal)

Modules per §20.1. Column roles: **Agency Owner** · **Agency Admin** · **Branch Manager** · **Operations Manager** · **Supervisor** (field). Scope: Agency Owner and Agency Admin are tenant-wide; Branch Manager is `B`; Operations Manager is `B` unless assigned `ALL`; Supervisor is `S` + `assignment_scope`.

The remaining canon agency roles — Field Officer, Agency HR, Recruiter, Payroll, Agency Finance, Agency Compliance, Agency Sales, Agency Viewer — follow these standing definitions and are not given separate columns: **Field Officer** = Supervisor's set plus multi-site `site_scope` and replacement dispatch; **Agency HR** = Guards/Employees/Leave/Training Create+Edit tenant-wide, no Financial access, no roster Approve; **Recruiter** = Recruitment and Applicants Create+Edit, View on Guards, no PII-identity, no Financial; **Payroll** = Payroll Create/Edit and payroll-relevant attendance View with Financial access, never Approve of its own runs (SoD-2), never attendance Create; **Agency Finance** = all money modules Create/Edit/Approve per §30.6 with Financial access, no operational write, no Administrative; **Agency Compliance** = Documents/KYC/Licences/Compliance Approve plus the tenant compliance veto, no Financial, no roster write; **Agency Sales** = Clients/Leads/CRM/Quotations/Tenders Create+Edit, quotation Approve only within floor (BR-217), no operational or financial write; **Agency Viewer** = View only, masked, within assigned scope, Export ✖.

### 31.5 Matrix C — Client-side roles (Customer Portal & Customer App)

Modules per §15. Canon client roles: Individual Customer · Company Owner · Security Head · Facility Manager · Site Manager · Procurement · Client Finance · Client Viewer. The master brief's "Client Admin" is the canon **Company Owner**; that is the name used everywhere in the product.

Split into two tables to stay within the seven-column limit; the row order is identical in both, so C1 and C2 read as one matrix.

**Individual Customer** is not given a column: it is a single-user account holding the Company Owner permission set restricted to its own bookings, with no team management, no approval chains and no site scoping. ### 31.7 Data-visibility rules beyond module permissions

Module permission answers "may this role touch this kind of thing". Two further layers answer "which rows" and "which fields". Both are enforced server-side; neither is ever implemented in a client.

#### 31.7.1 Row-level scoping chain

| Level | Predicate | Applies to | Failure mode it prevents |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Tenant | `tenant_id = caller.tenant_id` (or caller is a Suraksha platform role within its defined scope) | Every row of every tenant-owned table | Cross-tenant disclosure (BR-322) — the unrecoverable defect |
| 2. Geography (Suraksha only) | `state`/`city` ∈ `caller.geo_scope` | OPS modules for National/State/City Operations | A City Operations user reading another city's operations |
| 3. Branch | `branch_id ∈ caller.branch_scope` unless `ALL` | Agency-side operational and financial rows | A Surat branch manager seeing Ahmedabad payroll |
| 4. Site | `site_id ∈ caller.site_scope` | Client-side roles, Field Officer, Supervisor | A facility manager for one tower seeing the whole campus |
| 5. Assignment | `guard_id ∈ caller.assignment_scope` for the time window | Supervisor (field) | A supervisor retaining visibility of guards no longer under them |
| 6. Ownership | `created_by = caller` or `subject = caller` | `O`-scoped rows: own leave, own attendance, own payslip, own tickets | A guard reading another guard's records |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRM-033 | The six predicates shall compose as a conjunction applied by the data-access layer. A caller's effective row set is the intersection of every predicate that applies to their role, never the union. |
| SUR-PRM-034 | Scope changes (branch reassignment, site removal, assignment end, offboarding) shall take effect within 60 seconds across web, mobile, search indexes, cached dashboards, scheduled reports and AI retrieval. Stale caches are an access-control failure, not a performance issue. |
| SUR-PRM-035 | Aggregate figures shall be computed only over the caller's permitted row set. A dashboard number that includes rows the caller cannot open is a disclosure, and shall be treated as a defect of the same severity as showing the rows themselves. |

#### 31.7.2 Field-level masking — who sees what

Guard personal data follows §17.4 (canonical). This table states the platform-wide default for the fields that recur across entities. `Full` = complete value; `Masked` = partial (last 4, city-only, age band, initials); `Hidden` = field absent from the response entirely; `Restricted` = full value available only with a purpose code, per-access logging and subject visibility (BR-318).

| Field class | Suraksha ops roles | Suraksha Finance | Suraksha Compliance/Verification | Agency ops roles | Agency Finance/Payroll | Client roles | Guard (self) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guard mobile | Masked | Hidden | Full | Full (while linked) | Masked | Hidden | Full |
| Guard alternate contact / email | Masked | Hidden | Full | Full | Masked | Hidden | Full |
| Guard home address | Hidden | Hidden | Restricted | Hidden | Hidden | Hidden | Full |
| Guard DOB | Age | Hidden | Restricted | Age | Age | Age band | Full |
| Guard identity-document numbers | Hidden | Hidden | Restricted | Hidden | Hidden | Hidden | Own, masked |
| Guard bank / UPI | Hidden | Masked | Hidden | Hidden | Masked (Full at payout with step-up) | Hidden | Full (own) |
| Police-verification detail | Hidden | Hidden | Restricted | Hidden | Hidden | Hidden | Status only |
| Guard medical / blood group | Hidden | Hidden | Restricted | Emergency-access only | Hidden | Hidden | Full |
| Guard disciplinary records | Masked | Hidden | Full | Own tenure only | Hidden | Hidden | Own |
| Guard grievance content | Hidden | Hidden | Full (HR/Compliance) | **Never** | Hidden | Hidden | Own |
| Guard earnings / payslip | Hidden | Full | Hidden | Hidden | Full | Hidden | Full (own) |
| Client contact person mobile | Full | Full | Masked | Full | Masked | Full (own org) | Hidden |
| Client commercial rates | Hidden | Full | Masked | Owner/Admin/Finance only | Full | Full (own org) | Hidden |
| Site address / access instructions | Full | Masked | Masked | Full | Masked | Full (own sites) | Full (assigned, on duty) |
| Ledger / settlement detail | Hidden | Full | Masked | Owner/Finance only | Full | Own org only | Hidden |
| Tenant business data (other tenants) | Aggregate only | Aggregate only | Full (compliance purpose) | **Never** | **Never** | **Never** | **Never** |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRM-036 | Masking shall be applied at serialisation. There shall be no endpoint that returns an unmasked payload with a masking instruction for the client to apply (SUR-GRD-006). |
| SUR-PRM-037 | The same masking shall apply to: detail views, list views, search results and search *indexes*, reports, exports, notification bodies, webhook payloads, AI answers, support tooling and impersonated sessions. A field that is masked on screen and full in a webhook is a defect. |
| SUR-PRM-038 | Search shall never be usable as an oracle: a query that matches on a masked or hidden field shall not reveal the field's value through match highlighting, result ordering, result counts or autocomplete. Restricted fields are excluded from the search index entirely. |
| SUR-PRM-039 | Export column sets shall be derived from the caller's masking profile, not chosen by the caller. A user cannot request a column they cannot see, and an export template containing a column the caller lacks shall run with that column omitted and an explicit note in the file, never silently. |
| SUR-PRM-040 | Every unmasking action shall require a purpose code, shall be rate-limited per user per day, and shall be visible to the data subject (BR-318). Exceeding the rate limit raises a P2 security finding rather than merely failing. |

### 31.8 Client-side RBAC for enterprise customers

Enterprise clients run their own user administration inside their account. The platform gives them a bounded, self-serve capability that cannot escape their own tenant boundary (a client organisation is a scoping boundary of its own, orthogonal to agency tenancy).

#### 31.8.1 What a client organisation may manage itself

| Capability | Who | Constraints |
|---|---|---|
| Invite a member | Company Owner; Security Head below own level | Email or verified mobile; invite valid 7 days; invitee sets own credentials and verifies phone (BR-281) |
| Assign a role | Company Owner; Security Head below own level | Cannot grant a role above one's own (BR-284); cannot grant Company Owner except by ownership transfer |
| Set site scope | Company Owner, Security Head | Cannot grant a site outside the granter's own scope |
| Grant "can approve attendance" | Company Owner | An additive authority on top of the role, always visible in the members list |
| Set a spend approval limit | Company Owner | A value cap applied to quotation acceptance and payment authorisation |
| Suspend / remove a member | Company Owner; Security Head below own level | Immediate session revocation (BR-296); historic approvals preserved (BR-298) |
| Transfer ownership | Company Owner only | Step-up authentication, confirmation to both parties, reversible for 24 hours |
| Configure approval chains | Company Owner | See §31.8.2 |
| View account activity | Company Owner, Client Finance | 90-day window, exportable |

#### 31.8.2 Approval chains

Two configurable chains in V1 (§15.11), both versioned, with the version in force stamped on every approval so that a past approval can always be explained.

| Chain | Steps available | Escalation | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Attendance approval** | Single approver, or two-step: Facility Manager → Security Head | Configurable timer ("if not actioned in N days, escalate to…") | The approval is a commercial acceptance (BR-075), never a write to the operational record (SUR-PRM-026). Completion of the final step moves the month to `Verified` and triggers invoicing. |
| **Commercial approval** | Single approver, or two-step: Procurement → Company Owner above a configured value threshold | Same timer model | Acceptance of a quotation above the configured threshold cannot complete on one signature. The threshold is client-configured; the platform enforces it. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRM-041 | No approver shall be able to approve a step they raised, and no single user shall be able to satisfy two steps of the same chain even if they hold both roles. Where a client organisation has only one qualifying user, the chain shall be configured as single-step explicitly rather than collapsing silently. |
| SUR-PRM-042 | Every approval shall record: the chain ID and version, the step, the approver, the timestamp, the authority source (direct/delegated), and the exact record set approved (with a content hash so that later changes are detectable). |
| SUR-PRM-043 | A pending approval assigned to a suspended or removed member shall be reassigned as part of the suspension transaction (BR-297), never left orphaned. |
| SUR-PRM-044 | Client organisations shall be able to see, export and audit their own permission state: who has what role, what scope, what approval authority, what spend limit, and when each was granted and by whom. |

#### 31.8.3 The client-tenant boundary

| Rule | Statement |
|---|---|
| Client org is a scope | A client organisation's users see only their own organisation's bookings, contracts, invoices, sites, attendance and incidents — never another client's, even when both are served by the same agency. |
| No agency data | Client roles never see the agency's internal data: rosters beyond their own sites, guard payroll, agency finances, other clients, agency staff records, or agency compliance evidence. |
| Multi-agency clients | A client served by several agencies sees a unified view of their own sites, with each row attributed to the serving agency. Agencies do not see each other's rows for that client. |
| Cross-membership | One identity may be a member of several client organisations and of an agency (canon: one identity, many memberships, BR-281). Switching context is explicit; permissions never merge across memberships. |
| SSO | `[FUTURE]` per §15.11: SSO/SAML and SCIM for enterprise client accounts. Until then, invitation-based membership with mandatory phone verification is the only path. |

### 31.9 Permission change management

#### 31.9.1 Who can grant what

| Granter | May grant | May never grant |
|---|---|---|
| Super Admin | Any Suraksha internal role, with four-eyes for privileged roles | Anything to themselves; money-releasing authority (SUR-PRM-017) |
| Founder/Management | Approval of SoD exceptions and appeals | Direct role grants (they authorise, Super Admin executes) |
| Compliance | `PII-restricted` per-user grants with expiry; verification authorities | Any operational or financial authority |
| Agency Owner | Any agency role within their tenant, with four-eyes for privileged roles | Anything above Agency Owner; anything outside their tenant |
| Agency Admin | Non-privileged agency roles within the tenant | Payroll, Agency Finance, Agency Compliance, Agency Owner, Administrative access |
| Branch Manager | Non-privileged roles within their branch scope | Any tenant-wide scope; any money authority |
| Company Owner (client) | Client roles below their own, within their organisation | Company Owner (except by ownership transfer); anything outside their organisation |
| Security Head (client) | Client roles below their own, within their site scope | Financial roles; team ownership |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRM-045 | Four-eyes shall be mandatory for granting: Super Admin, Finance, Payroll, Compliance, Verification, break-glass custodian, Agency Owner, Agency Finance, Agency Compliance, Administrative access, `PII-restricted`, and any authority that can release money (BR-286). |
| SUR-PRM-046 | The approver of a privileged grant shall be distinct from both the requester and the subject, and shall not be in an SoD conflict with the granted authority. |
| SUR-PRM-047 | Every permission change shall be audited at **For** depth and notified to the affected user, the granter, the approver and (for privileged grants) Compliance (BR-306). |
| SUR-PRM-048 | Permission changes shall never be performable by API key, workflow automation, import, or AI (BR-337). The grant path is interactive and authenticated only. |

#### 31.9.2 Periodic access review

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Cadence | Privileged roles and `PII-restricted` grants: quarterly. All other roles: half-yearly. Client organisations: prompted annually, self-serve. |
| Reviewer | The role's owning authority (Super Admin for platform, Agency Owner for tenant, Company Owner for client), never the holder. |
| Content | Every holder, their scope, their additive sets, their delegations and elevations, last login, last use of each privileged capability, and SoD conflicts. |
| Default outcome | **Revoke on non-response.** A privileged grant not affirmatively re-approved within the review window is automatically downgraded to the base role, with notification. `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-305]` on whether revoke-on-non-response applies to tenant reviews or only to Suraksha internal reviews. |
| Dormancy | Any privileged capability unused for the configured period (default 90 days) is flagged in the review and is auto-revoked at 180 days unused. |
| Evidence | Each review produces a signed-off record retained per §39, and is the artefact produced for any external assurance process. |

#### 31.9.3 Offboarding

| Step | Requirement | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Reassign open approvals, tasks and owned records (BR-297) | Before deactivation completes |
| 2 | Revoke sessions, tokens, API keys, device bindings platform-wide (BR-296) | ≤ 60 seconds |
| 3 | Revoke delegations both granted and received | Same transaction |
| 4 | Transfer or revoke owned integrations and scheduled exports (BR-304) | Same transaction |
| 5 | Record retained as `Archived` for attribution; historic actions never anonymised (BR-298) | Permanent |
| 6 | Notify the user's manager, the tenant owner and (for privileged roles) Compliance | Immediate |
| 7 | For privileged roles: rotate any shared secrets the user could have accessed | ≤ 24 hours |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRM-049 | Offboarding shall be a single atomic workflow. A partially offboarded user — sessions revoked but API key live, or role removed but delegation active — shall not be a reachable state. |
| SUR-PRM-050 | The platform shall run a daily orphan sweep detecting: active API keys owned by deactivated users, delegations whose delegator is deactivated, approval queues assigned to deactivated users, and site/branch scopes referencing archived objects. Each finding is a P2 with an owner. |

## 32. Data Architecture

This section is the canonical home for entities and their fields (per the anti-repetition map). Every other section references entity names and field names defined here and does not redefine them. Where a field's *business meaning* is owned elsewhere — status transition rules (§29, §30), who may read it (§31), how it is protected (§38), how long it may be kept as a matter of privacy policy (§39), what classification band it falls in (§56) — this section states the storage shape and cross-references the owner.

### 32.0 What this section decides, and what it deliberately does not

| Decided here | Decided elsewhere |
|---|---|
| Multi-tenancy storage strategy, key strategy, audit columns, soft delete mechanics | Security controls, encryption, key management (§38) |
| The entity catalogue: tables, fields, types, constraints, relationships | The permission matrix over those entities (§31) |
| Status lifecycles expressed in the canon's status vocabulary | Workflow step sequences that move those statuses (§29) and the business rules that gate them (§30) |
| Indexing, partitioning, query patterns, volumetrics | Infrastructure sizing and autoscaling (§50), backup/restore mechanics (§49) |
| Retention *mechanism* (tiering, archival, purge jobs) and default retention windows | Retention *policy* and lawful basis (§39), classification bands (§56) |
| Integrity mechanics: constraints, transaction boundaries, outbox, idempotency records, reconciliation | Financial rules the reconciliation enforces (§35) |

**Database platform.** PostgreSQL 16 as the single OLTP store, with PostGIS for geospatial and TimescaleDB (or native declarative partitioning — see §32.4.7) for the high-volume time-series tables. Justification is in §32.0.1; it is stated once and referenced thereafter.

#### 32.0.1 Why PostgreSQL [RECOMMENDED]

| Dimension | Assessment |
|---|---|
| **Why** | The domain is relational and integrity-critical: rosters, assignments, attendance, contracts, invoices and ledger entries all require multi-row transactional consistency and foreign keys. Postgres gives strong constraints, real transactions, row-level security (used for tenant isolation), PostGIS for geofences, JSONB for the genuinely variable parts (AI payloads, integration blobs, form snapshots) and partitioning for GPS/attendance volume — in one engine, operated by one team. The architecture stance in the canon is a modular monolith; one strong database matches it. |
| **Alternatives considered** | (a) **MySQL/MariaDB** — weaker geospatial, no RLS, weaker JSON, weaker partition-wise features; no compensating advantage here. (b) **MongoDB** — attractive for the flexible parts, but the money, roster and attendance core needs cross-document transactions and constraints; we would end up re-implementing referential integrity in application code, which is precisely where multi-tenant data bugs live. (c) **Postgres + a separate document store from day one** — added operational surface for a benefit JSONB already delivers. (d) **Managed proprietary (Aurora/Spanner/Cosmos)** — Aurora Postgres remains a valid *deployment* of this decision (see §47); Spanner/Cosmos add lock-in and cost without solving a problem we have at India-pilot scale. |
| **Trade-offs** | Single-writer primary is a scaling ceiling; we mitigate with read replicas, moving GPS ingest off the primary (§34.3), and a documented shard/split path (§32.1.1.4, §50). Postgres connection handling requires PgBouncer from day one. |
| **Cost** | Managed Postgres for the pilot topology (1 primary + 1 replica, 8 vCPU / 32 GB, 500 GB SSD) is in the ₹35,000–60,000/month band on Indian-region managed services; self-managed on VMs is roughly half that with materially more operational load. GPS volume is the cost driver, which is why it is partitioned and tiered (§32.5). |
| **Scaling** | Vertical to ~64 vCPU comfortably; horizontal via read replicas, then table-level extraction (GPS, audit, notifications) to their own instance, then tenant sharding for the largest Enterprise tenants (§32.1.1.4). |
| **Lock-in** | Low. Postgres is portable across every major cloud and on-prem; PostGIS is open source. TimescaleDB is the one component with a licensing consideration — mitigated by the fallback in §32.4.7 (native partitioning gives us the same shape with more manual work). |
| **Security impact** | Positive: RLS gives a database-enforced tenant boundary in addition to the application-layer check, which is the single most valuable defence against the highest-likelihood catastrophic bug class in a multi-tenant SaaS (cross-tenant data leak). Column-level encryption and key handling are §38's. |

### 32.1 Modelling principles

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-DAT-001 | Every table that holds tenant-owned data shall carry a non-null `tenant_id` and shall be protected by a row-level security policy that filters on the session tenant context; no table shall rely on application-layer filtering alone. |
| SUR-DAT-002 | Every entity shall use a time-ordered UUID (UUIDv7) primary key generated by the application, plus, where users must speak the identifier aloud or type it, a separate human-readable `code` unique within its tenant. |
| SUR-DAT-003 | Operational and financial records shall never be hard-deleted; deletion shall be expressed as `status = 'Archived'` plus `archived_at`/`archived_by`, and physical removal shall occur only through a governed purge job (§32.5.5). |
| SUR-DAT-004 | Every table shall carry the standard audit columns (§32.1.5); every mutation to a governed entity shall additionally produce an append-only Audit Log row (§32.2.44). |
| SUR-DAT-005 | All monetary values shall be stored as `BIGINT` paise with a companion `currency` column defaulting to `INR`; floating-point money is prohibited at schema, ORM and API layers. |
| SUR-DAT-006 | Every field-originated event shall store `device_time`, `server_received_time` and `time_skew_ms`; all business logic, SLA computation and ordering shall use server time unless a rule explicitly names device time. |
| SUR-DAT-007 | Timestamps shall be `TIMESTAMPTZ` stored in UTC; presentation timezone is `Asia/Kolkata` unless the tenant sets otherwise, and date-bucketed reports shall use the tenant's configured operating day boundary, not UTC midnight. |
| SUR-DAT-008 | Geometry shall be stored in PostGIS `geography(Point, 4326)` for positions and `geography(Polygon/MultiPolygon, 4326)` for geofences; `latitude`/`longitude` numeric columns may exist only as a denormalised convenience for export and shall never be the join key. |
| SUR-DAT-009 | No schema change shall be applied outside a versioned, reviewed, forward-only migration with an explicit rollback plan; destructive migrations require the expand/contract pattern (§47). |
| SUR-DAT-010 | Every status column shall be constrained to the canon's status vocabulary; entity-specific sub-states shall be modelled as separate columns or as a `sub_status`, never by inventing new top-level status words. |

#### 32.1.1 Multi-tenancy strategy

The tenant is the **Agency** (canon §3: `tenant_id = agency_id`), with Suraksha's own guarding operation as tenant `SURAKSHA-HQ`. Clients and guards are *not* tenants: a Client is a record inside one or more agency tenants and additionally a first-class identity on the Suraksha side; a Guard belongs to one employing tenant at a time but has a portable person-identity across the platform (§32.2.4 explains the split between `user`, `person` and `guard`).

##### 32.1.1.1 The options

| Model | Isolation | Ops cost at 500 tenants | Cross-tenant queries (Suraksha OPS, marketplace, analytics) | Migration/upgrade cost | Noisy-neighbour risk | Per-tenant restore | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Shared schema, `tenant_id` + RLS** | Logical, enforced by the database engine | Low — one schema, one migration run, one connection pool | Native and cheap | One migration for all tenants | High if unmanaged; mitigated by quotas, statement timeouts, per-tenant rate limits | Hard — requires filtered logical restore into a staging DB | **[RECOMMENDED] for V1 and for the long tail** |
| **B. Schema-per-tenant** | Stronger logical; separate namespaces | Medium-high — N schemas × every migration; catalogue bloat past ~1,000 schemas degrades planning | Requires UNION across schemas or a federated view; marketplace and OPS queries become painful | N migration runs, partial-failure states | Same as A (shared instance) | Medium | Rejected for V1 |
| **C. Database-per-tenant** | Strong; separate credentials, separate backups | High — N instances or N databases, N connection pools, N backup chains | Very painful; needs a separate analytics consolidation path from day one | N migration runs; version drift becomes real | Eliminated | Easy and clean | Reserved for large Enterprise tenants (§32.1.1.4) |
| **D. Cell/pod-based (groups of tenants per cell)** | Strong blast-radius control | Medium (M cells, not N tenants) | Cross-cell requires a consolidation layer | M migration runs | Contained per cell | Per-cell | The **scale** destination (§32.1.1.5), not V1 |

##### 32.1.1.2 The decision

**[RECOMMENDED] Model A — shared schema with `tenant_id` and PostgreSQL row-level security — for V1 and for all Starter/Professional tenants indefinitely, with a defined promotion path to Model C for individual Enterprise tenants and a Model D endpoint at scale.**

Justification, against the criteria the canon requires:

- **Why.** Three of the platform's defining features are inherently cross-tenant: the Trinetra marketplace (§19) matches demand across agencies, Suraksha OPS (§22) supervises the whole network, and Suraksha itself operates as a tenant that subcontracts to other tenants. Models B and C make every one of those a distributed query. At the expected V1 scale (tens of agencies, hundreds by year 2), the isolation benefit of B/C does not pay for the loss of query locality and the multiplication of migration risk. Model A with RLS also gives us defence in depth: an application bug that forgets a `WHERE tenant_id = ?` is *still* blocked by the database.
- **Alternatives and trade-offs** are in the table above. The honest cost of Model A is the noisy-neighbour problem and the difficulty of restoring one tenant's data to a point in time.
- **Cost.** One database instance, one migration pipeline, one backup chain. Model C at 500 tenants would multiply managed-database cost by roughly the number of instances even at minimum sizing; that is the dominant infrastructure line item and it buys isolation we can otherwise achieve for the few tenants that need it.
- **Scaling.** Documented in §32.1.1.4 and §50.
- **Lock-in.** None beyond Postgres itself.
- **Security impact.** RLS is the strongest available control against cross-tenant leakage short of physical separation, and is checkable by automated test (§32.1.1.3). It does not replace §38's controls; it complements them.

##### 32.1.1.3 How Model A is implemented

| Mechanism | Specification |
|---|---|
| Session context | Every database session sets `app.tenant_id`, `app.user_id`, `app.role_keys` and `app.request_id` via `SET LOCAL` inside the request transaction. Connections are pooled by PgBouncer in **transaction** pooling mode; `SET LOCAL` is transaction-scoped, which is what makes this safe with pooling. |
| RLS policy shape | `CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON <table> USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id')::uuid)` with a matching `WITH CHECK` clause so a row cannot be *written* into another tenant. Applied with `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` so the table owner is not exempt. |
| Cross-tenant access | Two, and only two, legitimate paths. (1) **Platform role**: a distinct database role `suraksha_platform` used only by OPS/marketplace/analytics code paths, whose policies permit `tenant_id = ANY(current_setting('app.tenant_scope')::uuid[])` where the array is derived from the caller's §31 permissions. (2) **Migration/maintenance role**, used only by jobs, never by request-serving code. Every cross-tenant read through path (1) writes an Audit Log entry naming the tenants read. |
| Enforced default | A CI test enumerates every table in `information_schema` and fails the build if a table has a `tenant_id` column without an enabled, forced RLS policy, or is on the explicit "global table" allow-list without review. |
| Global (non-tenant) tables | `role`, `permission`, `plan`, `feature_flag`, `country/state/district`, `pincode`, `psara_authority`, `holiday_calendar_template`, `skill_taxonomy`, `industry_vertical`, `system_setting_definition`, `notification_template` (platform defaults), `job_definition`. These are read-mostly reference data with no tenant column. Tenant overrides of any of them live in a paired `*_override` table that does carry `tenant_id`. |
| Shared-but-partitioned identities | `user`, `person`, `device` are platform-global (one human, one login, many tenant memberships) with a `tenant_membership` join table carrying `tenant_id`. RLS applies to `tenant_membership`, not to `user`. Reading a `user` row requires an existing membership overlap, enforced in a security-definer function, not by raw table grants. |
| Noisy-neighbour controls | Per-tenant statement timeout (default 15 s OLTP, 120 s for report jobs), per-tenant API rate limits (§33.1.9), per-tenant concurrent-export cap of 2, and a `pg_stat_statements`-driven weekly report of the top 10 tenants by total exec time. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-DAT-011 | The request-serving database role shall be non-superuser, non-owner and subject to RLS; no request-serving code path shall connect as the schema owner. |
| SUR-DAT-012 | The build shall fail if any tenant-scoped table lacks a forced RLS policy, or if any query in the request path is executed with the platform role outside the audited cross-tenant service layer. |
| SUR-DAT-013 | Every cross-tenant read performed by Suraksha staff or by marketplace matching shall be recorded in the Audit Log with the tenant set, the purpose code and the requesting user. |

##### 32.1.1.4 Promotion path: isolating a large Enterprise tenant

Enterprise is the plan tier where "advanced security controls" and "large deployment support" are contractual (canon §1.4). Some Enterprise buyers will require a dedicated database; some will simply be big enough to hurt everyone else. The path must exist before it is needed.

| Step | Action | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 0. Trigger | Any of: tenant exceeds 5,000 active guards; tenant exceeds 15% of total database CPU-seconds over a 7-day window; tenant's GPS ping rate exceeds 2,000/min sustained; contractual requirement for a dedicated instance or in-region-of-choice residency. | Triggers are monitored, not guessed (§48). |
| 1. Freeze | Tenant is put into a 15-minute maintenance window; writes return `503` with `Retry-After`; the Guard App continues buffering offline (§18) so field operations are unaffected. | Window chosen at the tenant's lowest-activity hour from its own attendance histogram. |
| 2. Extract | `pg_dump --table=... --where="tenant_id = '<id>'"` is not sufficient (dependency ordering); instead a **tenant extraction tool** walks the entity graph in topological order and writes per-table filtered COPY streams. This tool is built in V1 and exercised monthly against a synthetic tenant. | The same tool serves per-tenant restore (§49) and the tenant data-export right (§39). |
| 3. Load | Restore into a dedicated database with identical schema and migration version. | Schema version equality is asserted before and after. |
| 4. Cut over | Tenant routing table (`tenant_id → connection_key`) is updated; application resolves the connection per request from a cached routing map with a 30-second TTL. | The routing indirection is built in V1 even though V1 has one entry, because retrofitting it later is a rewrite. |
| 5. Verify & reconcile | Row counts per table, ledger balance check (§32.7.6), spot checks on the last 24 h of attendance and payments. Old rows are marked `migrated_out_at` and retained read-only for 30 days, then purged. | |
| 6. Cross-tenant features | Marketplace and OPS reads for a promoted tenant go through the platform aggregation API rather than direct SQL; this API exists from V1 (used by analytics) so promotion does not require new code. | This is the main design tax paid up front. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-DAT-014 | The application shall resolve its database connection from a `tenant_id → connection_key` routing map on every request, even while only one connection target exists. |
| SUR-DAT-015 | A tenant extraction and load tool shall exist from V1, shall be exercised at least monthly against a synthetic tenant in a non-production environment, and shall be the single implementation used for tenant promotion, per-tenant restore and data-portability exports. |

##### 32.1.1.5 The scale destination (context only, not V1)

At pan-India scale the endpoint is Model D: cells of ~200–500 tenants each, one Postgres cluster per cell, a global control plane holding `tenant`, `user`, `plan`, routing and billing, and an analytical store consolidating all cells (§32.6). This is described in §50 and in §34.7; it is **not** to be built in V1. The only V1 obligations toward it are the routing indirection (SUR-DAT-014), keeping `tenant_id` on every row (SUR-DAT-001), and not writing queries that assume all tenants share one connection.

#### 32.1.2 Primary key strategy

| Option | Sortability | Index locality | Leak risk | Size | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BIGSERIAL` | Perfect | Perfect | High — sequential IDs leak volume and enable enumeration; also collide when merging data from another instance | 8 B | Rejected for public identifiers |
| UUIDv4 | None | Poor — random inserts fragment B-trees, inflate WAL, hurt cache hit ratio at high insert rates | None | 16 B | Rejected |
| **UUIDv7** (time-ordered, RFC 9562) | By creation time | Good — near-monotonic inserts | Reveals creation time to the millisecond, nothing else | 16 B | **[RECOMMENDED]** |
| ULID | By creation time | Good | Same as UUIDv7 | 16 B binary / 26 char text | Equivalent; rejected only because it needs a custom type or text storage in Postgres |

**[RECOMMENDED] UUIDv7 stored in the native `uuid` column type, generated in the application.** Why: it gives ULID's insert locality with Postgres's native 16-byte type, native index support, and no custom extension. Alternatives and trade-offs are above. Cost: none. Scaling: application-side generation means IDs can be minted offline (critical for the Guard App, which must create attendance and incident records with no network — §18) and before a transaction commits, which the outbox pattern needs (§32.7.5). Lock-in: none. Security impact: creation-time disclosure is acceptable for every entity here; where it is not (nothing currently), a UUIDv4 may be used for that entity specifically.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-DAT-016 | Primary keys shall be UUIDv7 generated client-side (application or mobile device), never database sequences, for all business entities. |
| SUR-DAT-017 | Entities that humans reference verbally or in documents — Booking, Quotation, Contract, Invoice, Payslip, Ticket, Incident, Tender/Bid, Site, Post — shall additionally carry a `code` (e.g. `INV-2026-000481`, `SITE-BLR-0042`) unique per tenant, generated from a per-tenant, per-type sequence with a configurable prefix and reset policy, and never reused. |
| SUR-DAT-018 | Mobile-generated primary keys shall be accepted as-is when the client is trusted-authenticated; the server shall reject a submitted key that already exists with a different payload hash (`409 conflict_duplicate_id`) and shall treat an identical payload hash as a successful replay (§33.1.8). |

Sequence-backed `code` generation uses a `document_sequence(tenant_id, doc_type, fiscal_year, next_value)` row locked with `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` inside the issuing transaction. Gaps are permitted and are not an error, except for Invoice, where GST practice makes gaps undesirable — for Invoice the number is allocated **at issue, not at draft creation**, so a cancelled draft never consumes a number (see §35 for the credit-note treatment of a cancelled *issued* invoice).

#### 32.1.3 Natural keys and uniqueness

| Entity | Uniqueness constraint | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| User | `UNIQUE(phone_e164)` where `deleted_at IS NULL`; `UNIQUE(lower(email))` partial | Phone-first per canon §4 |
| Agency | `UNIQUE(gstin)` partial; `UNIQUE(pan)` partial; `UNIQUE(slug)` | GSTIN/PAN nullable during onboarding |
| Guard | `UNIQUE(tenant_id, employee_code)`; global soft-uniqueness on `person_id` active employment | BR-001 depends on this |
| Site | `UNIQUE(tenant_id, code)` | |
| Assignment | Exclusion constraint on overlapping active assignments per guard (§32.7.2) | Implements BR-001 in the database |
| Attendance | `UNIQUE(assignment_id)` for the primary record; multiple events hang off it | |
| Invoice | `UNIQUE(tenant_id, invoice_number)` where issued | |
| Payment | `UNIQUE(gateway, gateway_payment_id)` | Prevents double-recording a gateway callback |
| Ledger Entry | `UNIQUE(transaction_id, leg_index)` | |
| Idempotency Key | `UNIQUE(tenant_id, endpoint, key)` | §33.1.8 |
| Checkpoint | `UNIQUE(site_id, code)`; NFC/QR tag id `UNIQUE(tenant_id, tag_uid)` | A physical tag may not be registered twice |
| Device | `UNIQUE(device_fingerprint)` per user | §38 owns binding rules |

#### 32.1.4 Soft deletion

Three distinct concepts are often conflated; the platform keeps them separate.

| Concept | Column(s) | Meaning | Visible in normal queries? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Lifecycle end** | `status = 'Completed'` / `'Cancelled'` / `'Expired'` / `'Rejected'` | The record finished its life normally | Yes |
| **Archival (soft delete)** | `status = 'Archived'`, `archived_at`, `archived_by`, `archive_reason_code` | Removed from operational view; retained for audit, legal and analytics | No — excluded by the default repository filter and by a partial index strategy |
| **Erasure** | Row physically removed or irreversibly pseudonymised by a governed purge job; a `purge_record` tombstone remains | Retention window elapsed, or a validated erasure request under §39 | No |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-DAT-019 | The data-access layer shall apply `status <> 'Archived'` by default to every list query, and a query that includes archived rows shall do so through an explicit, permission-checked call (`include_archived=true`, §33.1.4). |
| SUR-DAT-020 | Archiving a parent shall never cascade a physical delete to children; children are either archived by an explicit job or left intact with the parent's archived state visible through the relationship. |
| SUR-DAT-021 | Erasure of personal data shall pseudonymise the person record and its direct identifiers while preserving the operational and financial records that reference it by surrogate key, so ledgers, attendance history and audit trails remain internally consistent (see §39 for scope and lawful basis). |
| SUR-DAT-022 | Audit Log, Ledger Entry, SOS, Incident, Payment and Consent Record rows shall never be updated or deleted by application code; corrections are new rows (reversals, amendments, superseding versions). |

Erasure detail: the `person` row's `full_name`, `phone_e164`, `email`, `address`, `aadhaar_ref`, `pan`, `photo_url`, and biometric template references are replaced with deterministic tombstones (`REDACTED-<person_id_short>`), `erased_at`/`erasure_request_id` are set, and every document blob linked to that person is deleted from object storage with its metadata row retained. Attendance, ledger and audit rows keep `person_id` and therefore remain joinable and countable, but resolve to a redacted identity.

#### 32.1.5 Standard columns

Every table carries these unless explicitly exempted:

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` PK | UUIDv7 |
| `tenant_id` | `uuid` NOT NULL | Except global tables (§32.1.1.3) |
| `created_at` | `timestamptz` NOT NULL DEFAULT `now()` | Server clock |
| `created_by` | `uuid` NULL | User; NULL for system-generated (paired with `created_by_system`) |
| `created_by_system` | `text` NULL | Job/service name when `created_by` is NULL |
| `updated_at` | `timestamptz` NOT NULL | Maintained by trigger, not by application |
| `updated_by` | `uuid` NULL | |
| `version` | `integer` NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 | Optimistic concurrency; incremented by trigger; used by `If-Match` (§33.1.10) |
| `status` | `text` NOT NULL | Constrained to the canon vocabulary via CHECK or enum |
| `archived_at`, `archived_by`, `archive_reason_code` | `timestamptz`, `uuid`, `text` | Soft delete |
| `source` | `text` | `web` / `guard_app` / `agency_app` / `customer_app` / `admin_app` / `api` / `import` / `system` / `ai_assisted` |
| `request_id` | `uuid` NULL | The API request that created the row; ties rows to logs and audit (§48) |

Field-originated tables add `device_time`, `server_received_time`, `time_skew_ms`, `device_id`, `app_version`, `network_type`, `battery_pct`, `is_offline_sync`.

#### 32.1.6 Temporal and history tables

Not everything needs history; history everywhere is expensive and slows writes. The rule is by data class.

| Class | Entities | Mechanism | Retention of history |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Full row history** (every version retrievable) | Contract, Rate Card, Quotation, Invoice (pre-issue drafts), Payroll Run, Roster, Permission/Role assignment, Site geofence, Wake-check schedule, System Setting, Plan, Entitlement | Companion `*_history` table written by an `AFTER UPDATE` trigger storing the full old row, `valid_from`, `valid_to`, `changed_by`, `change_reason` | Life of parent + retention window |
| **Field-level change log** | User, Guard, Guard Profile, Client, Site (non-geometry fields), Agency | Audit Log rows with `before`/`after` JSONB restricted to the changed fields; no separate history table | 7 years (audit class) |
| **Append-only, no history needed** | Attendance events, Location, Checkpoint Scan, Wake Check, SOS, Ledger Entry, Notification, AI Interaction, Audit Log | The row *is* the history | Per §32.5.2 |
| **No history** | Session, cache-like rows, derived read models, Idempotency Key | — | Short |

Effective-dated entities (Rate Card, Contract terms, statutory rate tables, Plan pricing, Salary structure) additionally carry `effective_from` / `effective_to` with a `daterange` exclusion constraint preventing overlaps for the same key. Queries that price or compute anything historical **must** resolve the version effective on the event date, never the current version — this is the single most common source of retroactive billing and payroll errors, and it is enforced by making the pricing functions take an `as_of` date parameter with no default.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-DAT-023 | Any computation that produces money (invoice line, payroll component, settlement, penalty) shall resolve rate, tax and plan versions by the `as_of` business date of the event, and the resolved version identifiers shall be stored on the produced record. |
| SUR-DAT-024 | Effective-dated tables shall enforce non-overlap with an exclusion constraint; gaps are permitted and shall be surfaced as a configuration warning, not silently defaulted. |

#### 32.1.7 Money

Per canon §4 and SUR-DAT-005: `BIGINT` paise. Additional rules:

- Every money column is named `*_paise` (`amount_paise`, `tax_paise`, `net_payable_paise`) so a float assignment is visible in review.
- Rates that are not amounts (percentages, multipliers) are `NUMERIC(9,4)`; per-hour or per-day rates are money and therefore paise.
- Rounding is applied once, at the line level, using half-up to the nearest paisa, and the rounding delta is stored (`rounding_delta_paise`) so an invoice always reconciles exactly to the sum of its lines plus a named rounding line.
- Every financial movement is a double-sided Ledger Entry pair (canon §4); §35 owns the chart of accounts, this section owns the table shape (§32.2.30).
- `currency` is stored (`char(3)`, default `INR`) on every money-bearing record even though V1 is INR-only; adding it later is a schema-wide migration.

#### 32.1.8 Timestamp discipline

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Storage | `timestamptz`, UTC. `timestamp without time zone` is prohibited. |
| Field events | `device_time` (as reported), `server_received_time` (authoritative), `time_skew_ms = server_received_time - device_time`. Skew beyond ±120 s sets `time_integrity_flag = 'skewed'`; beyond ±15 min sets `'suspect'` and is surfaced to the Command Center as a P2 signal and to Compliance as an attendance-integrity indicator. |
| Ordering | All ordering, SLA measurement and escalation timing use server time. The one exception is reconstructing an offline sequence from the Guard App, where `device_time` orders events *within a single device's* offline batch and the batch as a whole is stamped with its server receipt time. |
| Operating day | Attendance, payroll and roster reporting bucket by the tenant's `operating_day_start` (default 06:00 IST) so a night shift crossing midnight belongs to one day. Stored as a generated column `operating_date` on Attendance and Shift to make date-bucketed indexes usable. |
| Duration | Stored as `integer` seconds, never as strings or intervals in money-adjacent tables. |
| Clock source | Server time comes from the application host synced by NTP with drift alerting (§48); the database `now()` is used inside transactions for row timestamps. |

#### 32.1.9 Geospatial storage

| Item | Decision |
|---|---|
| Position | `geography(Point, 4326)` — geography rather than geometry so distance is in metres without projection juggling, which matters because every geofence rule in the product is expressed in metres. |
| Geofence | `geography(Polygon, 4326)` for drawn fences; circular fences store `centre geography(Point)` + `radius_m integer` and are evaluated with `ST_DWithin` (cheaper than polygonising). A site may have multiple fences: `site_geofence(site_id, kind, geom, radius_m, effective_from)` with `kind ∈ {attendance, patrol, alert, restricted}`. |
| Accuracy | Every position stores `accuracy_m`, `altitude_m` (nullable), `speed_mps`, `heading_deg`, `provider` (`gps`/`fused`/`network`/`manual`), `satellite_count` (nullable). Positions with `accuracy_m > 100` are stored but excluded from geofence *decisions*; see §34.3.7. |
| Mock detection | `is_mock_location boolean`, `mock_detection_method text`, `device_integrity_verdict text` (from the attestation check, §38). Flagged pings are stored and marked, never dropped — dropping destroys the evidence trail. |
| Route/trail | Stored as the ordered ping series; a materialised `patrol_route_geom geography(LineString)` is written when a patrol completes, for cheap display and length computation. |
| Indexes | GiST on every geography column; see §32.4.5. |
| Reverse geocoding | Cached in `geocode_cache(geohash7, address_json, provider, fetched_at)` with a 180-day TTL — reverse geocoding every ping would dominate the map-provider bill (§34.6). |

#### 32.2.1 Identity & tenancy

Every table below carries the standard columns from §32.1.5; they are not repeated in the field tables.

##### 32.2.1.1 `person` — the human being

One row per real human, independent of what they do on the platform. A guard who leaves Agency A and joins Agency B is one `person`, two `employment` rows. This split is what makes cross-agency guard portability, duplicate detection and blacklist checks possible without merging tenant data.

| Field | Type | Req | Notes / constraints |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | uuid | Y | UUIDv7 |
| `full_name` | text | Y | 2–120 chars; stored as given, plus `name_normalised` for matching |
| `name_normalised` | text | Y | Generated: lowercase, diacritics stripped, spaces collapsed |
| `dob` | date | N | Required before Verified state on a Guard |
| `gender` | text | N | `male`/`female`/`other`/`undisclosed` |
| `phone_e164` | text | Y | `+91XXXXXXXXXX`; unique among non-erased rows |
| `alt_phone_e164` | text | N | |
| `email` | citext | N | |
| `photo_file_id` | uuid | N | FK `file_object` |
| `blood_group` | text | N | Enum of 8 |
| `emergency_contact_name` | text | N | Required before a Guard reaches Active |
| `emergency_contact_phone` | text | N | Same |
| `permanent_address` | jsonb | N | `{line1,line2,city,district,state,pincode}` |
| `current_address` | jsonb | N | Same shape |
| `home_location` | geography(Point) | N | Derived from current address; used for deployment-distance matching |
| `aadhaar_ref` | text | N | **Reference token only** — never the number; §38 owns tokenisation and §39 the lawful basis |
| `aadhaar_last4` | char(4) | N | For display/matching only |
| `pan` | text | N | Encrypted at rest; format-validated |
| `identity_hash` | text | N | Deterministic hash over (normalised name, dob, aadhaar_last4) for duplicate detection across tenants; not reversible |
| `erased_at` | timestamptz | N | Set by erasure job; see §32.1.4 |
| `status` | text | Y | Active · Archived |

Shift lifecycle: `Draft` (generated by the roster engine, not published) → `Pending` (published, awaiting full assignment) → `Active` (fully assigned, not yet started) → `In Progress` (start time passed) → `Completed` (end time passed and attendance closed) → `Cancelled`. A shift that reaches its start time under-assigned stays `Pending` and raises a deployment-gap alert (§24).

**Overlap prevention (BR-001)** is enforced in the database:

```
ALTER TABLE assignment ADD CONSTRAINT no_overlapping_active_assignment
  EXCLUDE USING gist (
    guard_id WITH =,
    tstzrange(starts_at, ends_at, '[)') WITH &&
  ) WHERE (status IN ('Pending','Active','In Progress'));
```

An authorised exception (canon BR-001 permits one) is recorded by setting `overlap_exception_id` referencing an Approval row; the constraint is bypassed only through a `SECURITY DEFINER` function that requires that approval to exist and be `Completed`, and writes an Audit Log entry. There is no other path.

Attendance lifecycle: `Pending` (assignment exists, shift not started) → `In Progress` (checked in) → `Completed` (checked out, or auto-closed at shift end + grace) → `Verified` (supervisor confirmed) → `Rejected` (verification refused, with reason) → `Failed` (no check-in by the configured cut-off, producing a no-show alert). `Active` is used for the narrow case of an open attendance awaiting first event on a shift already started.

```
CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER ledger_balanced AFTER INSERT ON ledger_entry

```

##### 32.2.7.3 `licence`

Licence geography is a first-class object (canon §1).

| Field | Type | Req | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id`, `tenant_id` | uuid | Y | |
| `licence_type` | text | Y | `psara_state`/`psara_district`/`arms`/`shops_establishment`/`gst`/`pf`/`esi`/`other` |

| `jurisdiction_level` | text | Y | `state`/`district` |

| `issue_date`, `valid_from`, `expiry_date` | date | Y | |

| `restriction_effect` | jsonb | N | What the tenant's configuration does on expiry (BR-002): which operations are restricted |
| `covered_branch_ids` | uuid[] | N | |
| `status` | text | Y | Draft · Pending · Active · Expiring · Expired · Suspended · Cancelled · Archived |

Licence lifecycle: `Draft` → `Pending` (submitted for verification) → `Active` → `Expiring` (inside the reminder window) → `Expired` (past expiry; BR-002 restrictions engage) → `Suspended` (authority action recorded) → `Cancelled`/`Archived`.

#### 32.2.8 AI, audit & platform

##### 32.2.8.1 `audit_log`

| Field | Type | Req | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|

| `impersonated_by_user_id` | uuid | N | Support access is always attributable to a human (§38) |

| `entity_type`, `entity_id` | text, uuid | Y | |

No `updated_at`, no `status`, no update or delete grant. Reads of highly sensitive entities (SOS media, Aadhaar references, payroll) themselves generate `action='read'` audit rows; ordinary list reads do not, because that volume would exceed the operational data itself.

### 32.3 Relationship diagrams

Notation: `1—N` one-to-many (crow's foot at the N end), `1—1` one-to-one, `N—M` many-to-many via a join table named in brackets, `0..1` optional. Every relationship crosses only within a tenant unless marked **[X-TENANT]**.

#### 32.3.1 Identity & tenancy

```
                          ┌──────────────┐
                          │ organization │
                          └──────┬───────┘
                                 │ 1
                                 │
                                 │ N
┌────────┐  1     1  ┌──────┐    ▼           ┌────────┐
│ person ├───────────┤ user │  ┌────────┐  1 │ branch │
└───┬────┘           └──┬───┘  │ agency ├────┤        │
    │ 1                 │ 1    │(TENANT)│  N └───┬────┘
    │                   │      └───┬────┘        │ 1
    │ N                 │ N        │ 1           │
┌───▼────┐        ┌─────▼──────────▼──┐          │ N
│ guard  │        │ tenant_membership │      ┌───▼──────┐
└────────┘        └─────────┬─────────┘      │   site   │
                            │ 1              └──────────┘
                            │ N
                  ┌─────────▼──────────┐   N       M  ┌────────────┐
                  │ membership_role    ├──────────────┤    role    │
                  └────────────────────┘              └─────┬──────┘
                  ┌────────────────────┐                    │ N
                  │ membership_        │              ┌─────▼──────┐
                  │ permission_override│    N       M │ permission │
                  └────────────────────┘  [role_permission]────────┘

┌──────┐ 1    N ┌────────┐ 1    N ┌─────────┐
│ user ├────────┤ device ├────────┤ session │
└──────┘        └────────┘        └─────────┘
```

Cardinality notes: `person 1—1 user` (a human has at most one login); `user 1—N tenant_membership` (one login, many agencies — this is what lets a guard move between agencies and a client hold accounts with several agencies); `agency 1—N branch`; `branch 1—N site`; `role N—M permission`.
