### 32.4 Indexing and query patterns

#### 32.4.1 Index conventions

Every tenant-scoped index leads with `tenant_id` — not for correctness (RLS handles that) but because the planner needs the tenant predicate to be selective. Partial indexes are used aggressively for status-filtered queries because the hot subset (Active shifts, Pending alerts, unpaid invoices) is a small fraction of the table. Covering indexes (`INCLUDE`) are used where a list view reads three or four columns and an index-only scan avoids the heap.

#### 32.4.2 The top 25 read paths

| # | Read path | Where it appears | Query shape | Index that serves it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Live deployment board: all guards on duty now for a tenant | §20, §22, §24 | `assignment` where tenant, `status='In Progress'`, `starts_at <= now() < ends_at` | `idx_assignment_live (tenant_id, status, starts_at DESC) INCLUDE (guard_id, site_id, post_id) WHERE status IN ('Active','In Progress')` |
| 2 | Last known position of every on-duty guard | §24 map, §20 | `location` latest row per `guard_id` | Materialised `guard_last_position(guard_id PK, ...)` updated by the ingest path; **never** a `DISTINCT ON` over `location` |
| 3 | Guard trail for one guard over a time window | §24 drill-down, incident review | `location` where guard, `recorded_at` between | `idx_location_guard_time (tenant_id, guard_id, recorded_at DESC)` on each partition |
| 4 | Today's attendance for a site | §20, §15 client portal | `attendance` where tenant, site, `operating_date = today` | `idx_attendance_site_date (tenant_id, site_id, operating_date) INCLUDE (guard_id, attendance_status, check_in_at)` |
| 5 | Guard's own roster for the next 7 days | §18 Guard App home | `assignment` join `shift` where guard, `starts_at` range | `idx_assignment_guard_time (tenant_id, guard_id, starts_at)` |
| 6 | Open alerts queue, severity-ordered | §24 console | `alert` where tenant scope, `status IN ('Pending','Active','In Progress')` | `idx_alert_open (severity, created_at_server) WHERE status <> 'Completed'` — cross-tenant for OPS, so this index deliberately does **not** lead with tenant_id; a second tenant-leading index serves the agency view |
| 7 | Escalations due to fire | §34.5 scheduler | `escalation` where `next_fire_at <= now()`, `status='Active'` | `idx_escalation_due (next_fire_at) WHERE status IN ('Active','In Progress')` |
| 8 | Wake checks due in the next minute | §34.4 scheduler | `wake_check` where `due_at` window, `status='Pending'` | `idx_wake_due (due_at) WHERE status='Pending'` |
| 9 | Under-staffed shifts in the next N hours | §20 gap board, §24 | `shift` where `assigned_headcount < required_headcount`, `starts_at` window | `idx_shift_gap (tenant_id, starts_at) WHERE status IN ('Pending','Active') AND assigned_headcount < required_headcount` |
| 10 | Guard search for assignment (available, skilled, near) | §20 roster builder | `guard` filtered by availability/skills + `person.home_location` distance | `idx_guard_available (tenant_id, availability_status, guard_type) WHERE status='Active'` + GiST on `person.home_location` |
| 11 | Documents expiring in the next 60 days | §20 compliance, §34.4.6 | `document` where `expiry_date` window, status in Verified/Expiring | `idx_document_expiry (expiry_date) WHERE status IN ('Verified','Expiring')` |
| 12 | Licences expiring / expired | §22, BR-002 | `licence` where `expiry_date <= now()+interval` | `idx_licence_expiry (expiry_date) WHERE status IN ('Active','Expiring')` |
| 13 | Client portal: my sites and today's presence | §15 | `site` where client + attendance aggregate | `idx_site_client (tenant_id, client_id) WHERE status='Active'` + read model `site_daily_presence` |
| 14 | Outstanding invoices / ageing | §20 finance, §22 | `invoice` where `amount_due_paise > 0`, `due_date` | `idx_invoice_outstanding (tenant_id, due_date) WHERE status='Active' AND amount_due_paise > 0` |
| 15 | Payment reconciliation lookup by gateway id | §32.7.6 | `payment` where `gateway`, `gateway_payment_id` | `uq_payment_gateway (gateway, gateway_payment_id)` |
| 16 | Payroll input: attendance for a period + branch | §35 | `attendance` where tenant, branch (via site), `operating_date` range, `status IN ('Completed','Verified')` | `idx_attendance_payroll (tenant_id, operating_date, status) INCLUDE (guard_id, worked_minutes, overtime_minutes)`; branch resolved via a denormalised `branch_id` on attendance |
| 17 | Guard's payslip history | §18 | `payslip` where guard, period desc | `idx_payslip_guard (tenant_id, guard_id, created_at DESC)` |
| 18 | Patrol compliance for a site over a month | §20, client report | `patrol` where site, `scheduled_start` range | `idx_patrol_site_time (tenant_id, site_id, scheduled_start DESC)` |
| 19 | Incident list with filters (type, severity, site, date) | §20, §22, §15 | `incident` multi-filter | `idx_incident_filter (tenant_id, occurred_at DESC) INCLUDE (site_id, severity, incident_type)` + partial on open incidents |
| 20 | Marketplace search: agencies by city + service + rating | §19 | `marketplace_listing` array containment + sort | GIN on `cities`, `service_lanes`; btree on `(rating_avg DESC)` |
| 21 | Tender feed matched to an agency's eligibility | §20 Professional feature | `tender` where state/district in agency licence set, `closes_at > now()` | `idx_tender_open (closes_at) WHERE status='Active' AND verification_status='Verified'` + GIN on eligibility |
| 22 | Notification inbox for a user | §36, all apps | `notification` where recipient, `created_at desc`, unread first | `idx_notification_user (tenant_id, recipient_user_id, created_at DESC) WHERE status IN ('Completed','Pending')` |
| 23 | Audit trail for one entity | §22, §38 investigations | `audit_log` where `entity_type`, `entity_id`, time desc | `idx_audit_entity (tenant_id, entity_type, entity_id, occurred_at DESC)` per partition |
| 24 | Global text search (guards, sites, clients, invoices) | Every product's search bar | Trigram/FTS across a few columns | Per-entity GIN `gin_trgm_ops` on the searchable text, unioned in the application with a per-entity cap; a single cross-entity search index is `[FUTURE]` |
| 25 | Geofence evaluation: which fence contains this point | §34.3 ingest | `site_geofence` where `ST_DWithin(geom, point, 0)` scoped to candidate sites | GiST on `site_geofence.geom`; candidates pre-narrowed by `assignment` (see §34.6.2 — we almost never search all fences) |

Two rules keep this list honest: **(a)** any query in a list view that is not served by one of these indexes must be added here before merge; **(b)** the CI performance suite runs `EXPLAIN` against seeded volumetric data for all 25 and fails on a sequential scan of a table over 100,000 rows.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-DAT-025 | Every list endpoint shall be backed by a named index in §32.4.2, and the build shall fail on a plan regression that introduces a sequential scan on a table exceeding 100,000 seeded rows. |
| SUR-DAT-026 | The current position of an on-duty guard shall be read from a maintained `guard_last_position` read model, never by scanning the ping table. |

#### 32.4.3 Volumetrics

Assumptions used for sizing (labelled because they drive real cost): **[ASSUMPTION: A-240]** V1 pilot = 30 agency tenants, 8,000 active guards, 900 sites; Year-2 = 400 tenants, 120,000 guards, 12,000 sites.

| Table | Rows/guard/day | V1 rows/day | V1 rows/year | Y2 rows/day | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `location` | 90–240 (adaptive, §34.3.1) | ~1.2 M | ~440 M | ~18 M | Dominant table; ~120 bytes/row + index ⇒ ~55 GB/year at V1 |
| `attendance_event` | 3–6 | ~40 K | ~15 M | ~600 K | |
| `attendance` | 1 | ~8 K | ~3 M | ~120 K | |
| `checkpoint_scan` | 8–30 (patrol sites only) | ~60 K | ~22 M | ~900 K | |
| `wake_check` | 0–4 (night only) | ~10 K | ~3.6 M | ~150 K | |
| `notification` | 3–8 | ~45 K | ~16 M | ~700 K | |
| `audit_log` | 5–15 | ~80 K | ~29 M | ~1.2 M | |
| `alert` | — | ~600 | ~220 K | ~9 K | |
| `outbox_event` | — | ~150 K | (7-day retention) | ~2 M | Never accumulates |
| `invoice` + lines | — | ~200/mo | ~30 K | ~400 K | |
| `ledger_entry` | — | ~2 K | ~700 K | ~30 K | |

#### 32.4.4 Partitioning

| Table | Strategy | Partition size | Retention action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `location` | `RANGE (recorded_at)` **daily**, with `LIST (tenant_id)` sub-partitioning deferred until a tenant exceeds 20% of daily volume | ~1.2 M rows/day at V1 | Detach at 90 days → downsample → archive to object storage → drop |
| `attendance_event` | `RANGE (server_received_time)` monthly | ~1.2 M rows/month | Detach at 24 months → cold |
| `checkpoint_scan` | `RANGE (server_received_time)` monthly | | Detach at 24 months |
| `audit_log` | `RANGE (occurred_at)` monthly | ~2.4 M/month | Detach at 12 months → cold storage, retained 7 years |
| `notification` | `RANGE (created_at)` monthly | | Drop at 13 months |
| `webhook_event` | `RANGE (created_at)` weekly | | Drop at 30 days |
| `ai_interaction` | `RANGE (created_at)` monthly | | Drop at 13 months |
| `outbox_event` | Not partitioned; aggressively vacuumed | Small steady state | Delete completed rows after 7 days |
| Everything else | Not partitioned in V1 | | Revisit at 50 M rows |

Partitions are created 30 days ahead by a scheduled job with an alert if the runway falls below 7 days — a missing future partition is an outage, and it is the single most common self-inflicted failure in partitioned Postgres deployments.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-DAT-027 | Future partitions shall be pre-created at least 30 days ahead by a monitored job, and partition runway below 7 days shall raise a P1 operational alert. |

#### 32.4.5 Geospatial index strategy

| Query | Index | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Point-in-fence at ingest | GiST on `site_geofence.geom` | Evaluated only against the fences of the guard's assigned site(s) — an O(1..3) check, not a spatial search (§34.6.2) |
| "Guards near this point" (dispatch, replacement) | GiST on `guard_last_position.location` | `ST_DWithin(location, p, 5000)` with a `status='on_duty'` partial index |
| "Sites within a city/polygon" | GiST on `site.location` | Used by roster planning and the marketplace |
| Trail rendering | Partition-local btree `(guard_id, recorded_at)` | Spatial index is not used for trail queries; the time index is |
| Distance-based matching (guard home → site) | GiST on `person.home_location` + `site.location` | Precomputed into `guard_site_distance_cache` for the top 50 sites per guard, refreshed weekly |

Geography-typed GiST indexes are noticeably larger than btree; `location.location` is deliberately **not** GiST-indexed on the raw ping table because we never spatially search raw pings — that alone saves roughly 30–40% of the table's index footprint.

#### 32.4.6 Time-series strategy for GPS and attendance events

| Concern | Decision |
|---|---|
| Write path | Pings never go directly to the OLTP primary from the request thread. They arrive at the ingest endpoint, are validated, pushed to a queue and written in batched `COPY` inserts (500–2,000 rows) by a consumer (§34.3). |
| Table shape | Narrow columns, no TOAST-able text, `smallint`/`real` where precision permits, `FILLFACTOR=100` (no updates ever). |
| Compression | Partitions older than 2 days are compressed — with TimescaleDB, native columnar compression at ~10–20× on this shape; without it, `pg_dump`-to-Parquet archival plus a downsampled retained table. |
| Downsampling | At 30 days, each guard-day is reduced to: every ping that changed geofence state, every ping with `is_mock` or an exception flag, plus one ping per 5 minutes (nearest to the boundary). Typical reduction 85–92%. |
| Attendance events | Never downsampled — they are evidence for payroll and client billing and are retained in full for 7 years, moving to cold storage at 24 months. |

##### 32.4.7 TimescaleDB vs native partitioning [RECOMMENDED]

| Dimension | Assessment |
|---|---|
| **Why (TimescaleDB)** | Automatic chunk management, native compression on exactly our access pattern, continuous aggregates for the per-guard/per-day rollups we would otherwise hand-build, and time_bucket queries for the trail viewer. It removes about 800 lines of partition-management and rollup code. |
| **Alternatives** | (a) **Native declarative partitioning** — no extension, fully portable, but we write the chunk lifecycle job, the compression story is "archive to Parquet", and rollups are our own materialised views with our own refresh logic. (b) **A separate time-series store (ClickHouse/InfluxDB)** — best raw performance and compression, but a second database to operate, a second backup chain, and joins to operational data become application-side. (c) **Object storage + DuckDB for history, Postgres for the last 7 days** — cheapest at scale, most engineering for the pilot. |
| **Trade-offs** | Timescale's compression makes rows immutable-in-practice (updates to compressed chunks are painful) — acceptable, pings are immutable. Licensing: the community edition covers compression and continuous aggregates but is not permissively licensed for offering Timescale-as-a-service, which we do not do; managed offerings differ by cloud, so availability must be checked against the chosen provider (§47). |
| **Cost** | Compression is the decisive number: ~55 GB/year of raw pings at V1 falls to roughly 4–6 GB compressed. On managed storage that is a small line item; the real saving is in backup size, restore time and replica bandwidth. |
| **Scaling** | Timescale handles our Year-2 volume (~18 M rows/day) on a single node comfortably. Beyond that, ClickHouse becomes the right answer and the migration is a bulk export of already-cold data. |
| **Lock-in** | Moderate but bounded: a Timescale hypertable is still a Postgres table; falling back to native partitioning is a mechanical migration, and we keep the ingest and query code behind a repository interface so the fallback is a swap, not a rewrite. |
| **Security** | Neutral. |

**[RECOMMENDED] TimescaleDB for `location` only, if it is available on the chosen managed platform; otherwise native daily partitioning with a hand-written chunk lifecycle job.** Everything else uses native partitioning. `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-241]` confirms availability on the selected provider before the ingest consumer is written; the decision does not change any table's logical shape.

### 32.5 Data lifecycle

#### 32.5.1 Tiers

| Tier | Where | Latency | Contents | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Hot** | OLTP Postgres, uncompressed | <50 ms | Last 90 days of pings; last 24 months of attendance/patrol/scan; all open operational records; all financial records for the current + previous fiscal year | Normal API |
| **Warm** | OLTP Postgres, compressed partitions + the analytical store | <2 s | 90 days–13 months of pings (downsampled); 24 months–7 years of attendance; closed financial records | Reports and exports; API reads flagged `historical=true` |
| **Cold** | Object storage, Parquet, partitioned by tenant/date, encrypted with a separate key | Minutes to hours | Everything past the warm window, up to the retention limit | Restore-on-request via a Data Export Request or an ops runbook; never served synchronously |
| **Purged** | Gone | — | Past retention, or erased on request | A Purge Record tombstone remains |

#### 32.5.2 Retention by data class

Policy ownership is §39 (privacy) and §56 (classification); this table states the mechanism's defaults, which those sections may override.

| Data class | Examples | Hot | Warm | Total retention | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Location telemetry | `location` | 90 d | 13 m (downsampled) | 13 months **[ASSUMPTION: A-241]** | Operational dispute window + one annual cycle; genuinely sensitive, so the shortest defensible window |
| Attendance & duty evidence | `attendance`, `attendance_event`, `checkpoint_scan`, `wake_check`, `patrol` | 24 m | to 7 y | 7 years | Wage and contract dispute exposure |
| Financial records | invoices, payments, ledger, payroll, payslips, settlements | current + prior FY | to 8 y | 8 years | Statutory-adjacent; configurable per jurisdiction rule |
| Identity & HR | `person`, `guard`, `employment`, documents | Life of relationship | +7 y | 7 y after exit | Employment record keeping |
| Verification & compliance | `verification`, `licence`, police verification | Life | +7 y | 7 y (licences 10 y) | Regulatory defence |
| Safety-critical evidence | `sos`, `incident`, SOS audio/photos | 24 m | to 7 y | 7 years minimum; longer if litigation hold | Never auto-purged while an incident is open or held |
| Candidate data | `application`, unhired candidates | 6 m | 6 m | 1 year unless consent renewed | §39 |
| Audit | `audit_log` | 12 m | to 7 y | 7 years | Tamper-evident chain preserved through archival |
| AI interactions | `ai_interaction` | 90 d | 13 m | 13 months | §41 |
| Notifications | `notification` | 90 d | 13 m | 13 months | Delivery-dispute window |
| Support/CRM | tickets, leads, opportunities | 12 m | 3 y | 3 years | |
| Ephemeral | sessions, idempotency keys, outbox, webhook events, report jobs | ≤30 d | — | ≤30 days | |

#### 32.5.3 Litigation and dispute holds

A `retention_hold(id, tenant_id, scope jsonb, reason, requested_by, approved_by, starts_at, expires_at, status)` row suspends purge for everything its scope matches. The purge job evaluates holds *first* and skips held rows, recording the skip. A hold may be created by Compliance, by a client dispute, or automatically when an Incident of severity P0/P1 is opened (the hold covers that site's data for the surrounding 72 hours and lifts when the incident reaches Completed plus 90 days).

#### 32.5.4 Archival mechanics

| Step | Detail |
|---|---|
| Selection | The archival job selects a whole partition (never a row-by-row scan) |
| Export | `COPY (SELECT * FROM partition) TO PROGRAM 'parquet writer'`, one file per tenant per day where tenant volume justifies it, otherwise one file per day |
| Verify | Row count and a SHA-256 of the sorted file are recorded in `archive_manifest(partition_name, object_key, row_count, checksum, exported_at, verified_at)`; a sample of 1,000 rows is read back and compared |
| Detach & drop | Only after `verified_at` is set |
| Restore | An ops runbook and a tested script; restore target is a staging schema, never the live table |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-DAT-028 | No partition shall be dropped before its archive manifest records a verified checksum and a successful sample read-back. |
| SUR-DAT-029 | Archive restore shall be exercised at least quarterly on a random archived partition, and the exercise result shall be recorded (§49). |

#### 32.5.5 Purge jobs

| Job | Cadence | Scope | Safeguards |
|---|---|---|---|
| `purge.ephemeral` | Hourly | Idempotency keys >24 h, completed outbox >7 d, expired sessions | None needed |
| `purge.webhook_events` | Daily 02:00 IST | >30 d | |
| `purge.notifications` | Daily 02:20 | >13 m | |
| `purge.location_downsample` | Daily 03:00 | Pings 30–90 d old | Writes the downsampled rows before deleting the originals, in one transaction per guard-day |
| `purge.location_expire` | Daily 03:40 | Downsampled pings >13 m | Hold check |
| `purge.candidate_data` | Weekly | Applications >1 y, not hired, consent not renewed | Hold check; notification to Recruitment 14 days before |
| `purge.erasure_queue` | Daily 04:00 | Approved erasure requests | Two-person approval required; produces a Purge Record; never removes financial or audit rows, only pseudonymises identity (§32.1.4) |
| `purge.archived_beyond_retention` | Monthly | Everything past its class retention | Dry-run first, count reported, executed only after the count is within 20% of the prior month's projection — a large unexpected delete is stopped, not executed |

Every purge job writes a `purge_record` (table, tenant, criteria, count, job run id, approver where applicable). Purge records are permanent.

### 32.6 Reporting and analytics data path

#### 32.6.1 The problem

Three consumers want data the OLTP store should not serve: agency dashboards and "advanced analytics" (a paid Professional feature), Suraksha OPS network-wide reporting, and client-facing SLA reports. Running these on the primary is how a live deployment board becomes slow at month-end.

#### 32.6.2 Options

| Option | Fit | Cost | Complexity | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Read replica + materialised views | Serves 90% of V1 needs; same SQL, same schema, no new system | One replica (already wanted for HA) | Low | **[RECOMMENDED] V1** |
| Dedicated columnar warehouse (ClickHouse / BigQuery / Redshift) | Right answer for multi-year, cross-tenant, ad-hoc analytics | New system, new pipeline, ₹25–80 K/month plus engineering | Medium-high | Year 2 trigger (§32.6.5) |
| Postgres logical replication into a second Postgres shaped for analytics | Middle path; no new engine | Modest | Medium | Fallback if ClickHouse is rejected |
| Query the primary with a lower-priority pool | Zero infrastructure | Zero | Zero | Rejected — noisy neighbour on the most critical path |

#### 32.6.3 The V1 design [RECOMMENDED]

- **Read replica** (streaming, async) carries every report, export, dashboard aggregate and analytical query. The application routes by intent: a repository method is declared `@analytical` and gets the replica connection. Replication lag is exposed in the API response header `X-Data-Lag-Seconds` for any endpoint served from the replica, and dashboards state "as of HH:MM" rather than pretending to be live.
- **Materialised read models**, refreshed on a schedule, for the aggregates every dashboard wants: `mv_site_daily_attendance`, `mv_guard_monthly_summary`, `mv_tenant_daily_kpi`, `mv_client_sla_monthly`, `mv_invoice_ageing`, `mv_patrol_compliance_daily`. Refresh is `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY` at 00:30, 06:30, 12:30, 18:30 IST, plus on-demand for a single tenant when a user asks for "recalculate".
- **Incrementally maintained read models** for the handful that must be near-live: `guard_last_position`, `site_current_presence`, `shift_gap_now`, `tenant_open_alert_counts`. These are updated by the event consumers (§34.4), not by a periodic refresh, because a 6-hour-old deployment board is useless.
- **Event stream to a raw event lake**: every outbox event is also written, as JSON lines, to object storage partitioned by date and event type. This costs almost nothing, is the raw material for the warehouse when it arrives, and means we are not reconstructing history from OLTP snapshots in Year 2.

**Why ELT rather than ETL:** land raw events and raw table snapshots first, transform in the destination. Transform-on-load bakes today's business definitions into the pipeline; when the definition of "attendance compliance" changes (and it will, per client contract), we want to recompute history, not lose it. The V1 "destination" is Postgres materialised views; the Year-2 destination is the warehouse; the raw layer is unchanged by that move — which is the entire point.

#### 32.6.4 What analytics may and may not read

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Tenant isolation | The analytical replica enforces the same RLS; agency dashboards run as the tenant role. Cross-tenant aggregates for Suraksha OPS run as the platform role and are audited (SUR-DAT-013). |
| Benchmarks | Cross-tenant benchmark metrics shown to agencies ("your fill rate vs the median in your city") are computed from a k-anonymised aggregate requiring at least 5 contributing tenants and are never resolvable to a competitor. |
| PII | The analytical layer stores `person_id`, not personal identifiers; name/phone resolution happens at render time against OLTP with permission checks. Exports containing PII are Data Export Requests, audited and watermarked. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-DAT-030 | All reporting, export and dashboard-aggregate queries shall execute against the analytical replica; the request path to the primary shall be reserved for transactional reads and writes. |
| SUR-DAT-031 | Any figure served from the replica or a materialised view shall be rendered with its as-of timestamp; no stale aggregate shall be presented as live. |
| SUR-DAT-032 | Cross-tenant benchmark statistics shall require a minimum cohort of 5 tenants and shall never expose a single tenant's value. |

#### 32.6.5 Trigger to build the warehouse

Any two of: (a) materialised view refresh exceeding 10 minutes; (b) more than 25 distinct scheduled reports; (c) a paying customer asking for ad-hoc query access; (d) analytical replica CPU sustained above 60%; (e) more than 500 tenants. Until then, building it is premature.

### 32.7 Data integrity

#### 32.7.1 Constraint policy

Constraints live in the database, not only in the application, because there are five write paths (web, four mobile apps, API, jobs, imports) and application-only validation eventually loses.

| Constraint kind | Where used |
|---|---|
| `NOT NULL` | Every field marked Req above |
| `CHECK` | Status vocabulary, non-negative money, `total = taxable + tax + round_off`, `end > start`, rating 1..5, `accuracy_m >= 0`, E.164 shape, GSTIN shape |
| `FOREIGN KEY` | Every relationship, `ON DELETE RESTRICT` by default; `ON DELETE CASCADE` only for true child rows (invoice lines, tax lines, ledger legs, escalation rung events) |
| `UNIQUE` / partial `UNIQUE` | §32.1.3 |
| `EXCLUDE` | Assignment overlap (BR-001), effective-date overlap on rate cards / salary structures / geofences |
| Deferred constraint trigger | Ledger balance per transaction |
| Composite FK with `tenant_id` | Every FK includes `tenant_id` in the referencing pair (`FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, site_id) REFERENCES site (tenant_id, id)`) so a row can never point at another tenant's row even if application code passes a foreign id |

The composite-FK rule is unusual and worth defending: it costs a little index width and buys structural impossibility of the cross-tenant reference bug. The only tables exempt are the deliberately cross-tenant ones (`marketplace_request`, `marketplace_response`, `assignment.supplying_tenant_id`, `settlement.counterparty_tenant_id`), each of which is individually reviewed.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-DAT-033 | Every foreign key between tenant-scoped tables shall be composite on `(tenant_id, id)`; exemptions shall be enumerated in code with a comment naming the reviewer and the reason. |

#### 32.7.2 Transaction boundaries

| Operation | Boundary | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Guard check-in | One transaction: insert `attendance_event`, update `attendance`, update `guard.availability_status`, insert `outbox_event` | Geofence evaluation happens before the transaction, using data already loaded |
| Roster publish | One transaction per site (not per roster) | A 3,000-assignment monthly roster in one transaction holds locks too long; per-site chunks with a saga-style progress record and a resumable job |
| Invoice issue | One transaction: allocate number, freeze lines, set status, create transaction + ledger entries, insert outbox event | PDF generation is **outside** the transaction, triggered by the event |
| Payment capture (gateway webhook) | One transaction: upsert payment by `gateway_payment_id`, allocate to invoices, create ledger entries, update invoice `amount_due_paise`, outbox event | Idempotent on the gateway id |
| Payroll run | Many transactions: one per payslip, wrapped by a run-level state machine | A single transaction over 8,000 payslips is unmanageable; the run is `In Progress` until every payslip completes, and is resumable |
| GPS ingest | One transaction per batch (`COPY` + read-model update) | No per-ping transaction |
| Assignment create | One transaction; the exclusion constraint decides the outcome | Conflict returns `409` with the conflicting assignment's id |
| SOS | One transaction, minimal: insert `sos`, insert `incident`, insert `alert`, insert outbox | Everything else (notification fan-out, media upload) is asynchronous — the transaction must never wait on a notification provider |

Rules: no external HTTP call inside a transaction, ever. No user-interaction wait inside a transaction. Long-running work is a job with a resumable state machine, not a long transaction. Isolation level is `READ COMMITTED` (Postgres default) with explicit `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` where a read-modify-write races (sequence allocation, wallet balance recompute, `assigned_headcount`); `SERIALIZABLE` is used for exactly one operation — payroll finalisation — where a retry is cheap and a double-run is catastrophic.

#### 32.7.3 Optimistic concurrency

Every mutable entity carries `version`. Update endpoints accept `If-Match: "<version>"`; a mismatch returns `409 version_conflict` with the current representation, and the client shows a merge/refresh prompt rather than silently overwriting. This matters most on rosters and contracts, where two schedulers editing the same week is routine.

#### 32.7.4 Idempotency records

Covered as a table in §32.2.8.6 and as an API contract in §33.1.8. The data rule: an idempotency key's stored response is authoritative for 24 hours; the endpoint's business write and the idempotency row are committed in the **same transaction**, so a crash between them is impossible.

#### 32.7.5 The outbox pattern

The problem: a check-in must both persist and notify. Doing both without a shared transaction means either lost notifications (write succeeded, publish failed) or phantom notifications (publish succeeded, write rolled back).

```
BEGIN;
  INSERT INTO attendance_event ...;
  UPDATE attendance ...;
  INSERT INTO outbox_event (id, tenant_id, aggregate_type, aggregate_id,
                            event_type, event_version, payload, occurred_at,
                            available_at, partition_key, status)
       VALUES (..., 'attendance', :id, 'attendance.checked_in', 1, :payload,
               now(), now(), 'guard:' || :guard_id, 'Pending');
COMMIT;
```

A relay process (`outbox.relay`) claims rows with `SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 200 WHERE status='Pending' AND available_at <= now() ORDER BY occurred_at`, publishes to the broker, marks `Completed`, and on failure increments `attempt_count` with exponential backoff and moves to `Failed` after 10 attempts (dead-letter, alerted). Ordering is preserved per `partition_key` by publishing to a partitioned topic keyed on it; global ordering is explicitly not guaranteed and no consumer may assume it.

Guarantees: **at-least-once** delivery. Every consumer must be idempotent on `event_id`. This is stated once here and referenced by §33.4, §34.4 and §36.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-DAT-034 | Every state change that external consumers depend on shall write an outbox event in the same transaction as the state change; no publish shall occur from application code outside the outbox relay. |
| SUR-DAT-035 | Every event consumer shall be idempotent on `event_id` and shall record processed event ids for at least 7 days. |
| SUR-DAT-036 | Outbox rows failing all retry attempts shall move to a dead-letter state, raise a P2 alert, and be visible in an operations screen with a replay action. |

#### 32.7.6 Reconciliation jobs

Anything derived is eventually wrong; reconciliation is how we find out before a customer does.

| Job | Cadence | Checks | On mismatch |
|---|---|---|---|
| `recon.ledger_balance` | Hourly | Every transaction's debit sum = credit sum; no unbalanced transaction exists | P0 alert, finance notified, transaction quarantined for review — never auto-corrected |
| `recon.wallet_balance` | Hourly | `wallet.balance_paise` = sum of its ledger legs | Recompute cache, log delta; a delta beyond ₹1 raises P1 |
| `recon.invoice_due` | Hourly | `invoice.amount_due_paise` = total − allocated payments − credit notes | Recompute; persistent mismatch raises P1 |
| `recon.gateway_settlement` | Daily 07:00 | Every gateway-reported payment exists locally with the same amount and status; every local Completed payment appears in a gateway settlement within 5 days | Missing local record is created as `Pending` for review; amount mismatch is P0 |
| `recon.attendance_vs_assignment` | Every 15 min | Every `In Progress` shift has an attendance row per assignment; no orphan attendance | Create missing rows in `Pending`; orphans flagged |
| `recon.shift_headcount` | Every 10 min | `shift.assigned_headcount` = count of active assignments | Recompute; a systematic drift means a trigger is broken (P1) |
| `recon.location_gap` | Every 5 min | Every on-duty guard has a ping within the expected interval × 3 | Raises a guard-offline signal (§34.5), not a data error |
| `recon.payroll_vs_attendance` | Per payroll run, pre-lock | Payslip day counts reconcile to attendance rows for the period | Blocks the run from leaving `In Progress` |
| `recon.document_deployability` | Nightly | `guard.deployability` matches the live document/training/verification state | Recompute and, if a guard becomes non-deployable while assigned, raise a P1 to Operations |
| `recon.outbox_lag` | Every minute | Oldest `Pending` outbox row age | >60 s raises P2, >300 s raises P1 |
| `recon.audit_chain` | Daily | Audit hash chain intact per tenant per day | Any break is P0 and a security incident (§38) |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-DAT-037 | Reconciliation jobs shall never silently auto-correct financial records; they may recompute caches and shall always record the delta and alert on it. |
| SUR-DAT-038 | Every reconciliation job shall publish a result record (`reconciliation_run`) with counts checked, mismatches found and duration, retained 2 years and visible in the operations dashboard. |

---

## 33. API Architecture

This section is the canonical home for endpoints. Other sections reference endpoint names; they do not restate request/response shapes. Entity and field definitions come from §32. Permission checks reference §31. Security controls reference §38.

### 33.1 API principles

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-API-001 | The platform shall expose one REST/JSON API over HTTPS, consumed by all five web properties, all four mobile apps, the desktop app and external integrators; there shall be no product-specific backend with its own data access. |
| SUR-API-002 | Every request shall be authenticated, tenant-scoped and permission-checked; the tenant scope shall be derived from the token and never from a client-supplied parameter. |
| SUR-API-003 | Every response shall use the standard envelope (§33.1.6) with a stable machine-readable error code. |
| SUR-API-004 | Every state-changing endpoint that a client may retry shall accept `Idempotency-Key`, and the endpoints listed in §33.1.8 shall require it. |
| SUR-API-005 | Breaking changes shall only be introduced in a new major version; a deprecated version shall be supported for at least 12 months after its successor is generally available. |

#### 33.1.1 Style: REST [RECOMMENDED]

| Dimension | Assessment |
|---|---|
| **Why REST** | Nine first-party clients (including offline-first mobile and a desktop app), an Enterprise integration surface sold to agencies' own IT teams, and a team that will hire generalist Indian backend engineers. REST over JSON is universally understood, trivially cacheable, debuggable with curl, and maps cleanly onto HTTP semantics we already need (conditional requests, status codes, retries, rate limiting). Offline sync (§18) is far easier over idempotent resource endpoints than over an RPC graph. |
| **Alternatives** | (a) **GraphQL** — genuinely attractive for the dashboard-heavy portals (one round trip for a composite screen), but it complicates caching, rate limiting, per-field authorisation (with a §31 matrix this deep, field-level auth in GraphQL is a large and permanent tax), query-cost control and offline sync. (b) **gRPC** — best for internal service-to-service, poor for browser clients and third-party integrators; we have a modular monolith, so there is little service-to-service traffic to optimise. (c) **tRPC/RPC-over-HTTP** — fine for a single TypeScript codebase, wrong when the Enterprise API is a sold product. |
| **Trade-offs** | Over-fetching on composite screens. Mitigated by sparse fieldsets (§33.1.5), a small number of deliberate composite read endpoints (`/dashboard/*`, `/deployment/live`) that are documented as read models, not as general-purpose queries, and by `?include=` expansion. |
| **Cost** | Lowest of the options: no gateway schema layer, no query-cost analysis service. |
| **Scaling** | Stateless, horizontally scalable behind a load balancer; CDN-cacheable for public reads (marketplace listings, website content). |
| **Lock-in** | None. |
| **Security** | Simplest to audit: one URL, one permission, one rate limit. This is the decisive argument given §31's depth. |

GraphQL is `[FUTURE]` and, if ever adopted, only as a read-only layer over the same service objects for the analytics surface.

#### 33.1.2 Versioning

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Location | URL path: `https://api.surakshaguards.in/v1/...`. Chosen over a header because it is visible in logs, curl and CDN rules, and because partner integrators cope with it better. |
| Granularity | One version for the whole API, not per resource. Per-resource versioning produces a matrix nobody can reason about. |
| What is breaking | Removing or renaming a field; changing a type; adding a required request field; changing a default; removing an enum value; tightening validation; changing an error code's meaning; changing pagination semantics. |
| What is not breaking | Adding an optional request field; adding a response field; adding a new enum value **where the field is documented as extensible** (clients must tolerate unknown values — this is stated in the SDK contract and tested); adding an endpoint; relaxing validation. |
| Minor evolution | `X-API-Revision: 2026-08-15` (date-based) opts into non-breaking behaviour changes that some clients may want deterministically pinned (e.g. a new default sort). Absent header = current behaviour. |
| Mobile | The app sends `X-App-Version`; the server may return `426 Upgrade Required` with a store link when a version is below the hard-minimum floor, and a soft-prompt flag otherwise. The hard floor is only raised for security or data-integrity reasons. |

#### 33.1.3 Naming conventions

| Rule | Example |
|---|---|
| Plural, kebab-free, lowercase nouns | `/v1/guards`, `/v1/wake-checks` uses a hyphen only where the entity name is two words |
| Nesting max two levels | `/v1/sites/{site_id}/posts` — deeper relationships use query filters: `/v1/assignments?site_id=…` |
| Actions that are not CRUD are sub-resources with a verb noun | `POST /v1/invoices/{id}/issue`, `POST /v1/sos/{id}/acknowledge`, `POST /v1/assignments/{id}/cancel` |
| Field names | `snake_case`, unabbreviated, money always `*_paise`, times always `*_at`, booleans always `is_*`/`has_*`/`*_required` |
| IDs | Always `*_id`, always the UUID string form |
| Enums | Lowercase snake for machine values; the status enum uses the canon's exact words in their canonical casing (`In Progress`) — the wire value is `in_progress` and the display value is resolved by the client from `/v1/reference/statuses` |
| Collections | Always an object with `data`, never a bare array (so pagination can be added without breaking) |

#### 33.1.4 Pagination, filtering, sorting

| Concern | Design |
|---|---|
| Pagination | **Cursor-based by default**: `?limit=50&cursor=<opaque>`. The cursor encodes the sort key(s) plus the last id, base64url, signed to prevent tampering. Offset pagination (`?page=`) is supported only on endpoints explicitly marked `offset_supported` (reports needing page numbers) and is capped at offset 10,000. Rationale: guard/attendance/ping lists change under the reader's feet, and offset pagination both duplicates and skips rows in that situation. |
| Limits | Default 25, max 100 for entity lists; max 1,000 for `/v1/tracking/pings` batch reads; max 5,000 for export-oriented endpoints, which return `202` + a Report Job instead when the estimated row count exceeds that. |
| Response meta | `{"data":[…],"meta":{"next_cursor":"…","has_more":true,"limit":50}}`. Total counts are **not** returned by default (an exact count on a 400-million-row partitioned table is a scan); `?include_count=true` returns an estimated count with `count_is_estimate: true`, and an exact count only where the filtered set is provably small. |
| Filtering | Explicit query parameters, not a query language: `?status=active&site_id=…&from=2026-08-01&to=2026-08-15&guard_type=pso`. Multi-value uses repetition or comma: `?status=active,in_progress`. Ranges use `_from`/`_to` suffixes. Every filterable field is documented per endpoint; an unknown filter parameter is a `400 unknown_parameter`, never silently ignored — silent ignoring produces "the filter doesn't work" bugs that survive for months. |
| Sorting | `?sort=-created_at,name` (leading `-` = descending). Only whitelisted fields per endpoint, all of which are index-backed (§32.4.2). |
| Sparse fieldsets | `?fields=id,name,status,check_in_at` returns only those fields plus `id`. Applied after authorisation, so a field the caller may not see is omitted regardless of the request. `?include=site,guard,post` expands relationships, each expansion permission-checked independently and capped at 3 includes per request. |
| Date handling | ISO 8601 with offset (`2026-08-15T20:14:03+05:30`) accepted; responses are always UTC with `Z`. Date-only filters are interpreted in the tenant's operating-day frame (§32.1.8), and the response echoes `meta.timezone` so a client can never mis-render a night shift. |

#### 33.1.5 Request/response limits

| Limit | Value | Behaviour when exceeded |
|---|---|---|
| Request body | 1 MB default; 10 MB for `/v1/documents` metadata + inline; 25 MB for a single direct upload | `413 payload_too_large` |
| File upload | Direct-to-object-storage via presigned URL for anything over 5 MB; the API never proxies large files | |
| GPS batch | 500 pings or 512 KB per batch (§34.3.2) | `413`, client splits |
| URL length | 2,048 bytes | `414` |
| Array parameters | 100 values | `400 too_many_values` |
| Response | Soft cap 5 MB; endpoints that could exceed it must paginate | |
| Timeout | 30 s gateway; 15 s application statement timeout; long work returns `202` + job | `504 gateway_timeout` with `retry_safe: true/false` |

#### 33.1.6 Error envelope

Every non-2xx response:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "validation_failed",
    "message": "One or more fields are invalid.",
    "message_locale": "hi-IN",
    "message_localised": "एक या अधिक फ़ील्ड अमान्य हैं।",
    "request_id": "018f2a1c-7b3e-7c2a-9f11-3d6a1c2b4e55",
    "occurred_at": "2026-08-15T14:44:03Z",
    "doc_url": "https://developers.surakshaguards.in/errors/validation_failed",
    "retry_safe": false,
    "details": [
      {"field": "check_in.location.latitude", "code": "out_of_range",
       "message": "Latitude must be between -90 and 90."},
      {"field": "assignment_id", "code": "not_found",
       "message": "No assignment with this id in the current tenant."}
    ]
  }
}
```

Rules: `code` is stable forever and is what clients branch on; `message` is English developer-facing; `message_localised` is present only when the error is surfaceable to an end user in one of the supported languages; `request_id` matches the log and audit correlation id (§48); `retry_safe` tells a mobile client whether its offline queue may retry automatically — this single field prevents duplicate attendance and duplicate payments more effectively than any client-side heuristic.

##### 33.1.6.1 Error code table

| HTTP | Code | Meaning | Retry safe |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `malformed_request` | Body is not valid JSON or is structurally wrong | No |
| 400 | `unknown_parameter` | A query parameter is not recognised | No |
| 400 | `invalid_cursor` | Cursor is malformed, tampered with or expired | No |
| 401 | `unauthenticated` | No token, malformed token | No |
| 401 | `token_expired` | Access token past expiry | Yes, after refresh |
| 401 | `token_revoked` | Session revoked, device unbound, password changed | No |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | Authenticated but the §31 matrix denies this action | No |
| 403 | `tenant_mismatch` | The resource belongs to another tenant | No |
| 403 | `plan_upgrade_required` | Feature gated by plan entitlement (§32.2.5.5) | No |
| 403 | `mfa_required` | The permission's `requires_mfa` is true and the session is not MFA-elevated | Yes, after step-up |
| 403 | `approval_required` | The action created an Approval and awaits a human | No |
| 403 | `device_not_bound` | Guard App request from an unbound device | No |
| 404 | `not_found` | No such resource in the caller's scope (used instead of 403 where existence itself is sensitive) | No |
| 405 | `method_not_allowed` | | No |
| 409 | `version_conflict` | `If-Match` version mismatch | No — client must refresh |
| 409 | `conflict_duplicate_id` | Client-generated id already exists with a different payload | No |
| 409 | `assignment_overlap` | BR-001 violation | No |
| 409 | `state_transition_invalid` | e.g. issuing an already-issued invoice | No |
| 409 | `request_in_progress` | Same idempotency key currently executing | Yes, after backoff |
| 409 | `already_processed` | Idempotent replay of a completed request (returns the original response, informational) | — |
| 413 | `payload_too_large` | | No |
| 415 | `unsupported_media_type` | | No |
| 422 | `validation_failed` | Field-level validation; see `details` | No |
| 422 | `business_rule_violated` | A §30 rule blocked it; `details[].code` names the rule (`BR-002`) | No |
| 422 | `idempotency_key_reuse` | Same key, different body | No |
| 422 | `outside_geofence` | Check-in/scan outside tolerance and override not permitted | No |
| 422 | `insufficient_balance` | Wallet/credit limit | No |
| 423 | `record_locked` | Payroll/billing locked period | No |
| 426 | `upgrade_required` | App version below the hard floor | No |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | Includes `Retry-After` and quota headers | Yes |
| 451 | `restricted_by_compliance` | Configured jurisdiction rule blocks the operation (e.g. BR-002 licence restriction) | No |
| 500 | `internal_error` | Unexpected; `request_id` is the support handle | Yes |
| 502/504 | `upstream_unavailable`, `gateway_timeout` | A dependency failed; `details.dependency` names it | Yes |
| 503 | `service_unavailable` | Maintenance or shed load; `Retry-After` present | Yes |

Note on `404` vs `403`: cross-tenant access attempts return `404 not_found` for entity reads (existence is itself information) and `403 tenant_mismatch` only where the caller legitimately has multi-tenant context and picked the wrong one.

#### 33.1.7 Rate limiting

Limits are per tenant **and** per principal, whichever binds first. Enforcement is a sliding window in Redis with a token-bucket burst allowance; headers `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`, and `Retry-After` on `429`.

| Client class | Sustained | Burst | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Guard App (per device) | 60 req/min | 120 | GPS batches counted as 1 request regardless of ping count |
| Guard App GPS ingest | 12 batches/min | 30 | Separate bucket so telemetry cannot starve check-in |
| Customer App / client portal (per user) | 120 req/min | 240 | |
| Agency Portal (per user) | 300 req/min | 600 | Density-first desktop screens fire many parallel reads |
| Agency Portal (per tenant) | 3,000 req/min Starter · 6,000 Professional · 20,000 Enterprise | 2× | Plan-differentiated |
| OPS / Admin App (per user) | 600 req/min | 1,200 | |
| Command Center console | 1,200 req/min | 2,400 | Plus a WebSocket, which is not rate-limited per message but is per subscription |
| Enterprise API key | 600 req/min default, negotiable to 3,000 | 2× | Entitlement-controlled; per-key, per-scope |
| Partner API key | 120 req/min | 240 | |
| Public/unauthenticated (website forms, marketplace browse) | 20 req/min per IP | 40 | Plus CAPTCHA on repeated failures (§38) |
| Auth endpoints (OTP request, login) | 5 per phone per 15 min; 20 per IP per hour | — | Abuse controls in §38 |
| Export/report creation | 10/hour per user, 2 concurrent per tenant | — | |
| Webhook delivery (outbound) | Per-endpoint `max_rps`, default 10 | — | §33.4 |

**SOS is never rate limited.** `POST /v1/sos` and its retry endpoint are exempt at every layer, including the WAF and the load balancer, per SUR-CMD-016. This exemption is a named test in CI.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-API-006 | SOS submission endpoints shall be exempt from all rate limiting, load shedding, request batching and circuit breaking, and this exemption shall be verified by an automated test in every release pipeline. |
| SUR-API-007 | Rate limit responses shall always include `Retry-After` and the quota headers, and the Guard App shall respect them with jittered backoff rather than tight retry. |

#### 33.1.8 Idempotency

`Idempotency-Key` is a client-generated UUIDv7, scoped per tenant per endpoint, valid 24 hours (§32.2.8.6). Semantics: first request executes and stores the response; an identical replay returns the stored response with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`; a concurrent replay returns `409 request_in_progress`; the same key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reuse`.

| Endpoint | Required? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /v1/attendance/check-in`, `check-out` | **Required** | Offline replay is the normal case; a duplicate check-in corrupts payroll and billing |
| `POST /v1/incidents`, `POST /v1/incidents/{id}/evidence` | **Required** | Guard App retries on flaky networks |
| `POST /v1/sos` | **Required**, but a missing key is never a rejection — the server falls back to (guard_id, device_time) de-duplication and always accepts | Safety outranks protocol purity |
| `POST /v1/patrols/{id}/scans` | **Required** | Offline batch replay |
| `POST /v1/payments`, `/v1/payments/{id}/capture`, `/v1/refunds` | **Required** | Money |
| `POST /v1/invoices/{id}/issue` | **Required** | Number allocation must not double-fire |
| `POST /v1/payroll-runs`, `/{id}/approve`, `/{id}/disburse` | **Required** | Money at scale |
| `POST /v1/wallets/{id}/transactions` | **Required** | Money |
| `POST /v1/bookings`, `POST /v1/quotations/{id}/accept` | **Required** | Double booking / double contract |
| `POST /v1/assignments` (bulk roster publish) | **Required** | A retried publish must not double-assign |
| `POST /v1/notifications/send` (internal/API) | **Required** | Duplicate SMS costs money and trust |
| `POST /v1/tracking/pings` | Optional (batch has its own `batch_id` de-duplication) | Pings are naturally de-duplicable on (device_id, recorded_at) |
| All other POSTs | Optional but honoured | |
| `PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` | Not required — made idempotent by `If-Match` version checking | |

#### 33.1.9 API tiers

| Tier | Audience | Auth | Base | Entitlement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Internal** | The five web properties and four apps | User session tokens (§33.2) | `api.surakshaguards.in/v1` | None; the full surface, permission-gated |
| **Partner** | Vetted integrators (verification vendors, payment/BSP partners, hardware/biometric vendors) | API key + mTLS optional + IP allow-list | Same base, scoped keys | Contractual, per-partner scopes |
| **Public** | Unauthenticated website and marketplace browse, tender listing, careers | None or CAPTCHA-gated | `api.surakshaguards.in/v1/public` | Aggressively cached, no PII |
| **Enterprise API** | Enterprise-plan agencies integrating their own systems | API key with scopes, or OAuth2 client credentials | Same base | **Enterprise plan only** (canon §1.4); `plan_upgrade_required` for lower plans |

The Enterprise API surface is a documented subset — guards, sites, posts, shifts, assignments, attendance (read + limited write), invoices (read), payroll (read), documents (read + upload), incidents (read + create), webhooks. It deliberately excludes: permission and role mutation, subscription mutation, payroll disbursement, direct ledger writes, and anything cross-tenant. Those exclusions are the security boundary of a sold API, and they are stated in the contract as well as enforced by scope.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-API-008 | The Enterprise API shall be entitlement-gated on the Enterprise plan and shall expose only the documented subset; scopes shall be deny-by-default and shall never include permission, subscription, payout or cross-tenant capability. |

#### 33.1.10 Conditional requests and caching

`GET` responses on entity resources carry `ETag` (the `version` for single entities, a hash for collections) and `Last-Modified`. Clients send `If-None-Match` and receive `304`. Mutations require `If-Match` on `PUT`/`PATCH` for entities where concurrent editing is realistic (roster, contract, site, guard, rate card, system settings); elsewhere it is accepted and honoured but optional. Public reads (marketplace listing, tender list, CMS content) are cacheable at the CDN with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300`; every authenticated response is `Cache-Control: private, no-store` by default.

### 33.2 Authentication and authorization for APIs

§38 owns credential storage, MFA enrolment, session revocation policy, brute-force controls and key management. This section owns the API contract.

#### 33.2.1 Tokens

| Item | Decision |
|---|---|
| Access token | JWT, RS256, 15-minute lifetime for staff/agency/privileged roles; 60 minutes for client and guard roles. Claims: `sub` (user_id), `tid` (tenant_id), `mid` (membership_id), `roles[]`, `scope[]` (only for API keys), `bid[]`/`sid[]` (branch/site scope where applicable), `dev` (device_id), `amr[]` (auth methods), `mfa_at`, `jti`, `iat`, `exp`, `iss`, `aud`. |
| Why JWT | Verification without a database round trip on every request at the edge. The cost is revocation latency, mitigated below. |
| Refresh token | Opaque, 30 days for client/guard sessions and 8 hours for privileged staff sessions (canon §4), stored hashed, **rotating** — each use issues a new refresh token and invalidates the old one. Reuse of a rotated token is treated as theft: the entire session family is revoked and a P1 security alert is raised (§38). |
| Revocation | A `jti` deny-list in Redis with a TTL equal to the access-token lifetime, checked on every request. This bounds the revocation gap to zero for the deny-list path while keeping the fast path in-memory. Session-family revocation kills refresh immediately. |
| Step-up | Permissions with `requires_mfa` demand `mfa_at` within the last 15 minutes; otherwise `403 mfa_required` with `details.step_up_url`. |
| Guard App | Device-bound: the token's `dev` claim must match a registered, Active device with the same fingerprint; a mismatch is `403 device_not_bound`. Device change requires re-verification (§18, §38). |
| Tenant switching | A user with several memberships calls `POST /v1/auth/switch-tenant` and receives a new access token; the old one keeps its old `tid`. Tokens are never multi-tenant. |

#### 33.2.2 The mandatory tenant-scoping check

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-API-009 | Every request shall pass through a middleware that (a) extracts `tid` from the token, (b) sets the database session tenant context, and (c) fails closed with `500 internal_error` if the context was not set; no handler shall be reachable without it. |
| SUR-API-010 | No endpoint shall accept `tenant_id` as a request parameter except the explicitly enumerated platform endpoints used by Suraksha staff, which shall additionally require a platform-scope permission and shall write an audit entry naming the tenant accessed. |
| SUR-API-011 | Any resource fetched by id shall be fetched with the tenant predicate applied at the query, in addition to RLS; a handler that loads by primary key alone shall fail code review and shall be caught by a static-analysis rule in CI. |

Belt, braces and a third belt: application query predicate, database RLS policy, and composite foreign keys (§32.7.1). Cross-tenant data leakage is the failure this platform can least afford, and each layer catches a different class of mistake.

#### 33.2.3 Service-to-service and background jobs

Internal workers authenticate with short-lived (10-minute) service tokens issued by the identity service to workload identities, carrying `sub=service:<name>` and an explicit capability list. Jobs that operate across tenants (expiry scans, invoice generation) run per tenant with the tenant context set, iterating tenants explicitly — never with an unscoped connection. A job's audit entries carry `actor_type='system'` and `created_by_system=<job name>`.

#### 33.2.4 API keys and scopes (Enterprise/Partner)

| Item | Decision |
|---|---|
| Format | `sk_live_<26 chars>` / `sk_test_<26 chars>`; only a SHA-256 hash is stored; the plaintext is shown once at creation |
| Binding | Key → tenant + scope list + optional IP allow-list + optional environment |
| Scopes | `guards:read`, `guards:write`, `sites:read`, `sites:write`, `attendance:read`, `attendance:write`, `assignments:read`, `assignments:write`, `invoices:read`, `payroll:read`, `documents:read`, `documents:write`, `incidents:read`, `incidents:write`, `webhooks:manage`, `analytics:read`. Deny-by-default; a key with `guards:read` cannot read attendance. |
| Ceiling | A key can never exceed the permissions of the role it is issued under, and never includes permissions not in the Enterprise subset (§33.1.9) |
| Rotation | Keys have `expires_at` (default 365 days), support overlapping rotation (two active keys), and warn at 30/7/1 days |
| Usage | Per-key usage counters, last-used timestamp, per-key rate limit, and a per-key kill switch in the Agency Portal |
| OAuth2 | Client-credentials flow is offered as an alternative for integrators who prefer it; same scopes, 60-minute tokens |

#### 33.2.5 Webhook signing (outbound)

`X-Suraksha-Signature: t=<unix_ts>,v1=<hex hmac_sha256(secret, t + "." + raw_body)>`, plus `X-Suraksha-Event-Id`, `X-Suraksha-Event-Type`, `X-Suraksha-Delivery-Id`, `X-Suraksha-Attempt`. Receivers must reject a timestamp older than 5 minutes (replay protection) and must compare in constant time. Dual secrets are supported during rotation: both `v1` and `v0` signatures are sent for the rotation window.

#### 33.2.6 Inbound webhooks (from providers)

Razorpay, WhatsApp BSP, SMS and email providers post to `/v1/webhooks/inbound/{provider}`. Each is verified with that provider's documented scheme, is idempotent on the provider's event id, is processed asynchronously (the endpoint persists the raw event and returns `200` fast), and never trusts the payload's amounts without a server-side fetch of the authoritative resource — a signed webhook proves origin, not truth.

### 33.3 API domain specifications

Legend for the endpoint tables: **Auth** = `S` session token, `K` API key permitted, `P` public; **Idem** = idempotency key Required / Optional / n/a. Role names are the canon's exact names; the authoritative matrix is §31 and is not restated here.

#### 33.3.1 Auth domain

| Method | Endpoint | Purpose | Auth | Roles | Idem |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

##### Spec A1 — `POST /v1/auth/otp/verify`

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Auth | Public; protected by rate limit (5/phone/15 min) and device fingerprint |
| Authorization | None pre-auth; the resulting token carries whatever memberships exist |
| Rate limit | 5 verify attempts per OTP; OTP expires in 5 minutes; 3 consecutive failures invalidate the OTP |
| Idempotency | Optional; a repeated verify with the same OTP after success returns `409 already_processed` |
| Side effects | Creates Session and Device rows; sets `phone_verified_at` on first success; writes an Audit Log `login` entry |
| Notifications | New-device login sends a push/SMS notice to existing devices (§36) |
| Audit | `action=login`, actor=user, with ip, user agent, device fingerprint |

Request:

```json
{
  "phone_e164": "+919812345678",
  "otp": "483920",
  "device": {
    "fingerprint": "b1f4c0e2-…",
    "platform": "android",
    "os_version": "14",
    "app_version": "2.3.1",
    "model": "Redmi Note 13",
    "push_token": "fcm:dJx…"
  },
  "requested_tenant_id": null
}
```

Validation: `phone_e164` matches `^\+91[6-9]\d{9}$` for Indian numbers (other country codes accepted where the tenant is configured for them); `otp` is exactly 6 digits; `device.fingerprint` is a UUID; `app_version` is semver.

Success `200`:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6IjIwMjYtMDgifQ…",
    "token_type": "Bearer",
    "expires_in": 3600,
    "refresh_token": "rt_9f2c…",
    "refresh_expires_in": 2592000,
    "user": {
      "id": "018f2a1c-7b3e-7c2a-9f11-3d6a1c2b4e55",
      "display_name": "Ramesh Kumar",
      "phone_e164": "+919812345678",
      "locale": "hi-IN",
      "is_platform_staff": false
    },
    "memberships": [
      {"tenant_id": "018f0a…", "tenant_name": "Sentinel Security Services",
       "membership_id": "018f0b…", "primary_role": "Guard",
       "is_default": true, "status": "Active"}
    ],
    "active_tenant_id": "018f0a…",
    "mfa_required": false,
    "device_id": "018f2b…"
  }
}
```

Errors: `422 validation_failed`; `401 unauthenticated` (`details.code=otp_invalid` or `otp_expired`); `429 rate_limited`; `403 permission_denied` with `details.code=account_suspended`; `409 already_processed`.

##### Spec A2 — `GET /v1/auth/me`

Returns the identity, all memberships, the effective permission key list for the active tenant (resolved per §31), the tenant's entitlements (§32.2.5.5) and feature flags. This is the single call every client makes at startup; it is cached client-side for 5 minutes and invalidated by a `user.permissions_changed` real-time event.

```json
{
  "data": {
    "user": {"id":"018f2a…","display_name":"Priya Nair","locale":"en-IN",
             "mfa_enabled":true,"is_platform_staff":false},
    "active_tenant": {"id":"018f0a…","name":"Sentinel Security Services",
                      "plan_key":"professional","status":"Active"},
    "membership": {"id":"018f0b…","primary_role":"Operations Manager",
                   "roles":["Operations Manager","Agency Compliance"],
                   "branch_ids":["018f0c…"],"site_ids":[]},
    "permissions": ["ops.roster.read","ops.roster.write","ops.assignment.create",
                    "ops.attendance.verify","cmp.document.read","fin.invoice.read"],
    "entitlements": {"advanced_analytics": true, "tender_discovery": true,
                     "enterprise_api": false, "guard_limit": 500},
    "feature_flags": {"ai_roster_suggestions": true, "offline_patrol_v2": false},
    "server_time": "2026-08-15T14:44:03Z"
  }
}
```

##### Spec A3 — `POST /v1/auth/refresh`

Body `{"refresh_token":"rt_9f2c…","device_fingerprint":"b1f4c0e2-…"}`. Returns a new access token **and a new refresh token** (rotation). Errors: `401 token_revoked` when the presented token was already rotated — this response also revokes the whole session family and raises a P1 security alert, so a client must treat it as "log the user out", never as "retry". Rate limit 30/hour per session.

##### Spec U1 — `POST /v1/users/{id}/roles`

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Authorization | Caller needs `iam.role.grant`; may never grant a role whose `max_scope` exceeds the caller's own; granting `Agency Owner` requires the current owner or Suraksha Super Admin |
| Validation | `role_id` exists and is assignable in this tenant's scope; `branch_ids`/`site_ids` must be a subset of the caller's scope; `expires_at` if present is future and ≤ 365 days |
| Side effects | Writes `membership_role`; invalidates the user's permission cache; forces a token refresh via a real-time `user.permissions_changed` event |
| Notifications | In-app + email to the affected user; digest entry to the Agency Owner |
| Audit | `action=approve`/`config_change`, `risk_tier=high`, before/after role sets, reason mandatory |
| Errors | `403 permission_denied`, `422 business_rule_violated` (privilege escalation attempt), `409 state_transition_invalid` |

##### Spec G1 — `GET /v1/guards/search-available`

The roster builder's workhorse; it is the read path that decides whether a scheduler can staff a gap in seconds or minutes.

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Auth / roles | Session; `ops.assignment.create` |
| Query params | `shift_id` (preferred) **or** (`starts_at`,`ends_at`,`site_id`); `guard_type`; `armed_required`; `skills` (comma); `languages`; `max_distance_km` (default 25); `include_conflicts` (default false); `limit` (default 25, max 100); `sort` ∈ `distance`,`-reliability_score`,`-rating_avg` |
| Logic | Filters to `guard.status='Active'`, `deployability='deployable'`, no overlapping assignment in the window (BR-001), not on approved leave, required skills present, documents not Expired, distance from `person.home_location` to `site.location` within limit. Returns a `fit_score` (0–100) combining distance, reliability, site familiarity (prior assignments at this site), and skill overlap — the weighting is tenant-configurable and the components are returned so the scheduler can see *why*. |
| Rate limit | Standard portal bucket |
| Side effects | None (read-only) |
| Audit | None (ordinary read) |
| Errors | `422 validation_failed` (no shift and no window), `403 permission_denied` |

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "guard_id": "018f31…", "employee_code": "SEN-0421",
      "name": "Mahesh Yadav", "guard_type": "guard", "is_armed": false,
      "distance_km": 4.2, "reliability_score": 92.4, "rating_avg": 4.6,
      "prior_shifts_at_site": 37, "languages": ["hi","en","kn"],
      "fit_score": 88,
      "fit_breakdown": {"distance": 24, "reliability": 28,
                        "familiarity": 25, "skills": 11},
      "conflicts": [],
      "document_warnings": [
        {"document_type":"medical_certificate","status":"Expiring",
         "expiry_date":"2026-09-02","days_remaining":18}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "meta": {"next_cursor": null, "has_more": false, "limit": 25,
           "evaluated_count": 214, "excluded": {"overlap": 31, "leave": 8,
           "documents_expired": 5, "distance": 138, "not_deployable": 7}}
}
```

The `excluded` counts matter operationally: when a scheduler sees "no guards available", the honest answer is which filter removed them.

##### Spec G2 — `POST /v1/guards`

Request (abridged to the required set): `person` (`full_name`, `phone_e164`, `dob`, `gender`), `employee_code`, `branch_id`, `guard_type`, `is_armed`, `date_of_joining`, `employment_type`, optional `salary_structure_id`, `reporting_supervisor_id`.

Validation: phone unique among non-erased persons; `employee_code` unique per tenant; `dob` implies age ≥ 18 and ≤ 65 **[ASSUMPTION: A-242]** (configurable per tenant policy, never hard-coded); `is_armed=true` requires `guard_type` ∈ `{guard, pso}` and creates a mandatory arms-document checklist; `date_of_joining` not more than 90 days future.

Side effects: creates `person` (or links an existing person by `identity_hash` with an explicit confirm flag), `guard` in `Draft`, a document checklist derived from `guard_type` + `is_armed` + the tenant's configured requirement set, and an outbox event `guard.created`. Notifications: welcome SMS/WhatsApp with the app link if `phone_verified` is false. Audit: full create record. Errors: `409 conflict_duplicate_id`, `422 validation_failed`, `422 business_rule_violated` (`details.code=plan_guard_limit_reached` when the subscription's `guard_limit` is hit — D-003).

Success `201` returns the guard with `deployability: "blocked"` and `deployability_reasons: ["documents_pending","verification_pending","training_pending"]` — a guard is never deployable on creation, and the API says so explicitly rather than leaving the client to infer it.

##### Spec G3 — `POST /v1/guards/{id}/suspend`

Body `{"reason_code":"document_expired","note":"Police verification lapsed on 12 Aug","effective_from":"2026-08-15T18:30:00Z","auto_unassign":true}`. Authorization: `wf.guard.suspend`, high risk tier, `requires_mfa=true`. Side effects: sets `status='Suspended'`, recomputes `deployability`, and — when `auto_unassign` is true — cancels future assignments and creates Replacement records for any within the next 72 hours, each producing its own alert. Notifications: guard (push + SMS), reporting supervisor, affected site's operations owner, and the client if a contractual notification rule applies (§24). Audit: high risk, reason mandatory. Errors: `422 business_rule_violated` if suspension would leave a site below contracted strength and the caller lacks the override permission — in that case the response `details` names the affected shifts so the caller can arrange cover first.

##### Spec AG1 — `POST /v1/licences`

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Authorization | `cmp.licence.create` (Agency Compliance, Agency Owner) |

| Audit | Full; `risk_tier=high` |
| Errors | `422 validation_failed`, `409 conflict_duplicate_id`, `422 business_rule_violated` (`BR-002` context) |

##### Spec C1 — `PUT /v1/sites/{id}/geofence`

Safety-relevant configuration; changes take effect at the next shift boundary (§22.20), never mid-shift.

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Authorization | `ops.site.geofence.write`; `requires_mfa=false` but `risk_tier=high` |
| Validation | `kind` ∈ `attendance`/`patrol`/`alert`/`restricted`; for `circle`: `radius_m` between the tenant's configured min (default 50) and max (default 500); for `polygon`: 4–200 points, closed ring, area between 100 m² and 5 km², self-intersection rejected; the site's `location` must fall inside the fence |
| Business logic | Creates a new `site_geofence` row with `effective_from` = next shift boundary; the previous row is closed at the same instant. Historical attendance is evaluated against the fence effective at its time, never the current one. |
| Side effects | Outbox `site.geofence_changed`; the tracking pipeline reloads its fence cache for that site; a preview of how many of the last 7 days' check-ins would have fallen outside the new fence is returned — a scheduler tightening a fence from 200 m to 60 m deserves to know it would have failed 40% of last week's check-ins **before** committing |
| Notifications | Operations Manager, site's supervisor, Command Center (site config change) |
| Audit | Full, with geometry before/after |
| Errors | `422 validation_failed` (`geometry_invalid`, `radius_out_of_range`, `site_outside_fence`), `403 permission_denied` |

```json
// request
{"kind":"attendance","shape":"circle",
 "centre":{"latitude":12.9716,"longitude":77.5946},"radius_m":120,
 "effective_from":"next_shift_boundary","reason":"Gate relocated 40m north"}
// 200
{"data":{"geofence_id":"018f52…","kind":"attendance","shape":"circle",
  "radius_m":120,"effective_from":"2026-08-16T02:30:00Z",
  "previous_geofence_id":"018f4e…",
  "impact_preview":{"window_days":7,"check_ins_evaluated":168,
                    "would_be_outside":11,"would_be_outside_pct":6.5}}}
```

##### Spec B1 — `POST /v1/bookings`

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Auth / roles | Session; `b2c.booking.create` (client roles) or `sales.booking.create` (agency Sales creating on behalf) |
| Idempotency | **Required** |
| Rate limit | 10/hour per user |
| Validation | `service_location` inside a serviceable area (D-005) else `422 business_rule_violated` with `details.code=not_serviceable` and the nearest serviceable city; `headcount` 1–200; `start_date` ≥ today + the configured lead time (default 48 h, 4 h for `emergency`); `shift_pattern` totals must not exceed 12 h per guard per day without an explicit `acknowledge_extended_shift` flag; `armed_required=true` requires a client type other than `individual` unless the tenant permits it |
| Business logic | Prices from the effective Rate Card (`as_of` = start date); computes tax lines from the configured jurisdiction rule; for `individual` clients with `booking_type='subscription_monthly'`, creates a Quotation automatically and marks the booking `Pending`; for Government clients, self-serve checkout is blocked (§22) and the booking is routed to the quote/tender path |
| Side effects | Booking + Quotation (+ Lead if the requester is new); outbox `booking.created`; assignment to a Sales owner by the routing rules |
| Notifications | Client: confirmation (in-app + WhatsApp/SMS + email). Agency: new booking alert to Sales and Operations. |
| Audit | Full create |

##### Spec B2 — `POST /v1/quotations/{id}/accept`

Auth: client roles with `b2c.quotation.accept`, or Sales with an on-behalf reason. Idempotency required. Validation: quotation is `Active` and `valid_until >= today`; the accepting user is a contact on the client. Business logic: creates a Contract in `Draft` with the quotation's lines pinned (rate card id + version), creates Sites/Posts if the booking described new ones, marks the Booking `Active`, and — where the tenant requires advance payment — creates a payment intent and holds contract activation until `payment.status='Completed'`. Side effects: outbox `quotation.accepted`, `contract.created`. Notifications: agency Sales, Operations (to begin deployment planning), client confirmation with the contract PDF. Audit: full, `risk_tier=high` (commercial commitment). Errors: `409 state_transition_invalid` (expired or already accepted), `422 business_rule_violated` (`credit_limit_exceeded`).

##### Spec B3 — `GET /v1/serviceability`

Public, CDN-cached 5 minutes. `?pincode=560055` or `?lat=…&lng=…`. Returns `{"serviceable":true,"city":"Bengaluru","state":"KA","lead_time_hours":48,"service_lanes":["residential_rwa","corporate","industrial","event"],"armed_available":true,"nearest_branch_km":6.4}` or, when false, `{"serviceable":false,"nearest_serviceable":{"city":"Bengaluru","distance_km":142},"waitlist_endpoint":"/v1/public/waitlist"}`. The serviceable city list is D-005 configuration data, not code.

##### Spec D1 — `POST /v1/assignments`

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Authorization | `ops.assignment.create`; scope must include the shift's site |
| Idempotency | Required (bulk publish is retried) |
| Validation | Shift exists, is `Draft`/`Pending`/`Active`; guard is `Active` and `deployable`; guard's skills satisfy the post's `required_skills`; `armed_required` matched; the window does not overlap another active assignment (BR-001 — enforced by the exclusion constraint, so the API surfaces the database's answer rather than pre-checking and racing) |
| Business logic | Snapshots `billing_rate_paise` from the contract line effective on the shift date and `pay_rate_paise` from the guard's salary structure; increments `shift.assigned_headcount`; if the shift becomes fully staffed, resolves any open deployment-gap alert |
| Side effects | Outbox `assignment.created`; if within 24 h of start, a push to the guard requiring acknowledgement |
| Notifications | Guard (push + SMS if unacknowledged after 30 min), supervisor, client if the contract requires roster visibility |
| Audit | Full |
| Errors | `409 assignment_overlap` (with the conflicting assignment id, site and window), `422 business_rule_violated` (`guard_not_deployable` with reasons, `licence_restriction` per BR-002, `weekly_hours_exceeded`), `423 record_locked` (roster locked without override permission) |

```json
// 409 example — the conflict is actionable, not just a refusal
{"error":{"code":"assignment_overlap","message":"Guard already assigned in this window.",
 "request_id":"018f2a…","retry_safe":false,
 "details":[{"field":"guard_id","code":"overlap",
   "conflicting_assignment_id":"018f70…","site_name":"Prestige Tech Park — Gate 2",
   "starts_at":"2026-08-16T14:30:00Z","ends_at":"2026-08-17T02:30:00Z",
   "override_available":true,
   "override_endpoint":"/v1/approvals?type=overlap_exception"}]}}
```

##### Spec D2 — `GET /v1/deployment/live`

The single most-read authenticated endpoint in the platform (the Agency Portal board, the Command Center map and the Admin App all poll or subscribe to it).

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Auth / roles | Session; `ops.deployment.read`; results filtered to the caller's branch/site scope |
| Params | `site_id`, `branch_id`, `city`, `status` (`on_duty`,`late`,`absent`,`unreachable`), `include=last_position,guard,site`, `limit` (default 100, max 500) |
| Data source | The maintained read models `site_current_presence` and `guard_last_position` (§32.6.3), not a join over `location` |
| Freshness | Response includes `meta.as_of` and `meta.max_position_age_seconds`; positions older than 5 minutes are marked `stale: true` rather than presented as current |
| Rate limit | 60/min per user (the console uses WebSocket deltas instead of polling — §34.2) |
| Errors | standard |

```json
{
  "data": [
    {"assignment_id":"018f7a…","guard":{"id":"018f31…","name":"Mahesh Yadav",
      "employee_code":"SEN-0421","phone_e164":"+9198******78"},
     "site":{"id":"018f20…","name":"Brigade Gateway","city":"Bengaluru"},
     "post":{"id":"018f21…","name":"Main Gate"},
     "shift":{"starts_at":"2026-08-15T02:30:00Z","ends_at":"2026-08-15T14:30:00Z"},
     "duty_status":"on_duty","checked_in_at":"2026-08-15T02:27:11Z",
     "last_position":{"latitude":12.9899,"longitude":77.5547,"accuracy_m":8,
                      "recorded_at":"2026-08-15T14:41:52Z","age_seconds":131,
                      "stale":false,"inside_geofence":true},
     "battery_pct":47,"open_alerts":0,
     "next_wake_check_at":null}
  ],
  "meta": {"as_of":"2026-08-15T14:44:03Z","max_position_age_seconds":131,
           "counts":{"on_duty":184,"late":6,"absent":3,"unreachable":2},
           "next_cursor":"eyJ…","has_more":true}
}
```

Phone numbers are masked unless the caller holds `pii.phone.read` — the mask is applied server-side, never by the client.

##### Spec D3 — `POST /v1/rosters/{id}/publish`

Authorization `ops.roster.publish`. Idempotency required. Validation: roster is `Draft`; zero unresolved BR-001 conflicts; every shift meets or acknowledges its headcount gap. Business logic: transitions shifts `Draft → Pending/Active`, notifies every assigned guard, and freezes the roster's structure (changes after publish are amendments with an audit trail). Because a monthly roster can be thousands of assignments, publish returns `202 Accepted` with a job handle when the assignment count exceeds 500:

```json
{"data":{"job_id":"018f81…","status":"In Progress","total":2840,"processed":0,
 "poll_endpoint":"/v1/jobs/018f81…","estimated_seconds":45}}
```

Side effects: per-site transactions (§32.7.2), outbox `roster.published` and one `assignment.created` per assignment (batched into the notification digest so 2,840 assignments do not become 2,840 separate pushes — §36 owns the batching rule). Errors: `422 business_rule_violated` with a `details[]` array of conflicts, each naming guard, shift and the conflicting assignment.
