##### Spec AT1 — `POST /v1/attendance/check-in`

The most operationally consequential write in the platform. It must succeed on a weak network, must never double-record, and must be honest about geofence failures rather than silently accepting them.

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Auth | Session token with a `dev` claim matching an Active, bound device (`403 device_not_bound` otherwise) |
| Authorization | `ops.attendance.check_in`; the guard may only check in against their own Active assignment |
| Idempotency | **Required**. Server also de-duplicates on `(assignment_id, event_type, device_time)` |
| Rate limit | 20/min per device (retries), never shed |
| Validation | `assignment_id` belongs to the caller and is `Active`/`In Progress`; `device_time` within ±24 h of server time (beyond that the payload is accepted but flagged `time_skew` and requires supervisor verification); `location.accuracy_m ≤ 100` else `outside_geofence` evaluation is deferred and the record is flagged `low_accuracy`; selfie required when the post's configuration demands it |
| Business logic | Resolves the fence effective at `server_received_time`; computes `distance_m`; if outside tolerance and the post does not permit override, returns `422 outside_geofence` with the distance and the allowed radius; if outside and override is permitted, accepts with `exception_flags:["outside_geofence"]` and routes for supervisor verification. Computes `late_minutes` against `scheduled_start + grace_in_minutes`. Sets attendance `In Progress`. |
| Side effects | `attendance_event` + `attendance` update + `guard.availability_status='assigned'` + outbox `attendance.checked_in`, all in one transaction (§32.7.2). Starts the shift's wake-check schedule if the shift is a night shift. Resolves any open "shift starting, nobody checked in" alert. |
| Notifications | Supervisor gets a batched roll-call update, not one push per guard. Client gets a check-in event only where the contract enables live visibility. Late check-in beyond the configured threshold raises an alert (§24). |
| Audit | An `attendance_event` row **is** the audit for the act; a separate Audit Log entry is written only for manual/override paths |
| Errors | `403 device_not_bound`, `403 permission_denied`, `404 not_found` (assignment not the caller's), `409 state_transition_invalid` (already checked in — returns the existing attendance, `retry_safe:false`), `422 outside_geofence`, `422 validation_failed`, `423 record_locked` (period locked for payroll) |

```json
// request
{
  "assignment_id": "018f7a…",
  "device_time": "2026-08-15T02:27:09+05:30",
  "location": {"latitude":12.98991,"longitude":77.55468,"accuracy_m":8,
               "provider":"fused","speed_mps":0.2,"heading_deg":null},
  "battery_pct": 82, "is_charging": false, "network_type": "4g",
  "is_mock": false,
  "selfie_file_id": "018f7b…",
  "method": "gps",
  "is_offline_sync": false,
  "client_event_id": "018f7c-…"
}
// 201
{
  "data": {
    "attendance_id":"018f7d…","assignment_id":"018f7a…",
    "status":"In Progress","attendance_status":"present",
    "check_in_at":"2026-08-14T20:57:11Z",
    "server_received_time":"2026-08-14T20:57:11Z",
    "device_time":"2026-08-14T20:57:09Z","time_skew_ms":2000,
    "distance_m":14,"geofence":{"id":"018f52…","radius_m":120,"inside":true},
    "late_minutes":0,"exception_flags":[],
    "shift":{"starts_at":"2026-08-14T21:00:00Z","ends_at":"2026-08-15T09:00:00Z"},
    "wake_checks_scheduled":3,
    "next_action":{"type":"none"}
  }
}
// 422 outside geofence — the guard is told the distance, not just "failed"
{"error":{"code":"outside_geofence","message":"You are 340 m from Main Gate. Move closer and try again.",
 "message_localised":"आप मुख्य गेट से 340 मीटर दूर हैं। पास जाकर पुनः प्रयास करें।",
 "request_id":"018f2a…","retry_safe":true,
 "details":[{"field":"location","code":"outside_geofence","distance_m":340,
   "allowed_radius_m":120,"accuracy_m":8,
   "override_available":false,
   "alternative":{"action":"request_supervisor_override",
                  "endpoint":"/v1/attendance/override-requests"}}]}}
```

##### Spec AT2 — `POST /v1/attendance/sync`

The offline path (canon §4: offline-first is mandatory for the Guard App only). Accepts an ordered batch of up to 200 buffered events of any type (check-in, check-out, checkpoint scan, wake-check acknowledgement, incident draft), each with its own client-generated UUIDv7 and `device_time`.

Semantics: **partial success is normal and expected.** The response reports per-event outcomes; the client removes accepted and permanently-rejected events from its queue and retries only those marked `retry_safe`. Events are applied in `device_time` order within the batch. Events older than the tenant's configured offline horizon (default 72 h) are accepted but flagged `late_sync` and routed to supervisor verification rather than silently trusted.

```json
// 207-style body, returned with HTTP 200
{
  "data": {
    "batch_id":"018f90…","received":37,"accepted":34,"rejected":2,"deferred":1,
    "results":[
      {"client_event_id":"018f8a…","type":"check_in","outcome":"accepted",
       "server_id":"018f8b…","exception_flags":["late_sync"]},
      {"client_event_id":"018f8c…","type":"checkpoint_scan","outcome":"duplicate",
       "server_id":"018f8d…","note":"Already recorded; treated as success."},
      {"client_event_id":"018f8e…","type":"check_out","outcome":"rejected",
       "error":{"code":"state_transition_invalid",
                "message":"No open attendance for this assignment."},
       "retry_safe":false},
      {"client_event_id":"018f8f…","type":"wake_check_ack","outcome":"deferred",
       "error":{"code":"upstream_unavailable"},"retry_safe":true,
       "retry_after_seconds":30}
    ],
    "server_time":"2026-08-15T14:44:03Z",
    "clock_skew_ms":1840
  }
}
```

`clock_skew_ms` is returned so the app can correct its own future `device_time` stamps — a cheap, effective defence against a drifting device clock corrupting a month of attendance.

##### Spec AT3 — `POST /v1/attendance/{id}/manual-correction`

Authorization `ops.attendance.correct`, `risk_tier=high`, `requires_approval=true` when the correction changes payable minutes by more than the tenant's threshold (default 60 minutes) or touches a payroll-locked period. Request carries `field`, `new_value`, `reason_code` (from a fixed library: `device_failure`, `network_failure`, `geofence_error`, `supervisor_witnessed`, `data_entry_error`, `client_confirmed`), `note` (mandatory, ≥20 chars), and optional `evidence_file_ids`. Side effects: writes an `attendance_event` of type `manual_correction` with before/after, never overwrites the original event, and (if payroll-locked) creates an arrears item for the next run rather than mutating a closed period. Notifications: guard is told their attendance was corrected and by whom — silent corrections to a person's pay record are not acceptable. Audit: full, high risk, retained 7 years. Errors: `403 approval_required` (returns the created Approval id), `423 record_locked`.

| Method | Endpoint | Purpose | Auth | Roles | Idem |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/v1/tracking/pings` | Batch GPS ingest | S (device-bound) | Guard | O |
| GET | `/v1/tracking/live` | Current positions in scope | S | Ops, Command Center, client (own sites, if enabled) | n/a |
| GET | `/v1/tracking/guards/{id}/trail` | Historical trail for a window | S | Ops, Command Center | n/a |
| GET | `/v1/tracking/guards/{id}/last-position` | Single last position | S,K | Ops, Supervisor | n/a |
| POST | `/v1/tracking/ping-now` | Request an immediate position (push-triggered) | S | Command Center, Supervisor | R |

##### Spec T1 — `POST /v1/tracking/pings`

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Auth | Device-bound session token |
| Authorization | `ops.tracking.write`; a guard may only submit pings for themselves |
| Idempotency | Optional header; server always de-duplicates on `(device_id, recorded_at)` |
| Rate limit | 12 batches/min per device, separate bucket from all other endpoints |
| Limits | ≤500 pings, ≤512 KB per batch; gzip encouraged (`Content-Encoding: gzip`) |
| Validation | Each ping: latitude −90..90, longitude −180..180, `accuracy_m` 0..10000, `recorded_at` not more than 7 days old and not more than 5 minutes in the future; batch must be ordered by `recorded_at` |
| Business logic | Writes are queued, not synchronous (§34.3.3). The endpoint validates, assigns a `batch_id`, enqueues and returns `202` in single-digit milliseconds. Geofence evaluation, derived signals and read-model updates happen in the consumer. |
| Side effects | Derived events (`geofence.entered`, `geofence.exited`, `guard.idle`, `guard.route_deviation`, `guard.mock_location_detected`) are emitted by the consumer, not by this endpoint |
| Notifications | None directly; derived events may raise alerts (§24) |
| Audit | None per ping (volume); mock-location detections are audited |
| Errors | `413 payload_too_large`, `422 validation_failed` (with the index of the first bad ping), `403 device_not_bound`, `429 rate_limited` |

```json
// request
{"device_id":"018f2b…","assignment_id":"018f7a…",
 "pings":[
   {"id":"018fa1-…","recorded_at":"2026-08-15T14:40:02Z","latitude":12.98991,
    "longitude":77.55468,"accuracy_m":8,"speed_mps":0.0,"heading_deg":null,
    "provider":"fused","battery_pct":47,"is_charging":false,"is_mock":false,
    "is_moving":false},
   {"id":"018fa2-…","recorded_at":"2026-08-15T14:41:02Z","latitude":12.98994,
    "longitude":77.55471,"accuracy_m":11,"speed_mps":0.4,"provider":"fused",
    "battery_pct":47,"is_mock":false,"is_moving":true}
 ]}
// 202
{"data":{"batch_id":"018fa0…","accepted":2,"duplicates":0,"rejected":0,
  "server_time":"2026-08-15T14:41:09Z","clock_skew_ms":420,
  "next_config":{"interval_seconds":120,"reason":"stationary_battery_normal"}}}
```

`next_config` is the server steering the device's sampling rate (§34.3.1) — the client obeys it, so sampling policy is changed centrally without an app release.

##### Spec T2 — `GET /v1/tracking/guards/{id}/trail`

Params: `from`, `to` (max 24 h per request), `resolution` ∈ `full`/`5min`/`auto` (default `auto`, which returns full for windows under 2 h and downsampled beyond), `include_events=true` to interleave geofence and checkpoint events. Returns GeoJSON-compatible output plus a summary:

```json
{"data":{"guard_id":"018f31…","from":"2026-08-15T02:30:00Z","to":"2026-08-15T14:30:00Z",
 "resolution":"5min","point_count":144,
 "summary":{"distance_m":4820,"inside_geofence_pct":97.2,
            "idle_minutes":412,"deviation_events":0,"mock_flags":0,
            "gaps":[{"from":"2026-08-15T08:12:00Z","to":"2026-08-15T08:41:00Z",
                     "duration_seconds":1740,"likely_cause":"device_offline"}]},
 "points":[{"t":"2026-08-15T02:30:04Z","lat":12.98991,"lng":77.55468,"a":8,"g":"inside"}],
 "events":[{"t":"2026-08-15T06:02:11Z","type":"geofence.exited","site_id":"018f20…"},
           {"t":"2026-08-15T06:19:44Z","type":"geofence.entered","site_id":"018f20…"}]}}
```

The `gaps` array is deliberate: a trail with a missing half-hour must show the hole, with an honest guess at the cause (device offline, app killed, permission revoked, battery dead), because presenting an interpolated line across a gap is a lie that ends up in a client dispute.

Authorization note: trail access is a privacy-sensitive read (§39). It requires `ops.tracking.history.read`, it is limited to periods when the guard was on duty, and **it writes an Audit Log `read` entry** naming the guard, the window and the requester.

##### Spec P1 — `POST /v1/patrols/{id}/scans`

Idempotency required; accepts 1–50 scans. Validation per scan: checkpoint belongs to the patrol's route; `tag_uid` (for NFC/QR) matches the registered tag — a mismatch is recorded with `is_valid=false` and `invalid_reason='wrong_tag'` rather than rejected, because the evidence that a wrong tag was scanned is worth keeping; `distance_m` within `tolerance_m` else `is_valid=false`, `invalid_reason='out_of_tolerance'`; sequence enforced if the route requires it. Business logic: increments patrol counters; when the last checkpoint is scanned, the patrol may auto-complete if configured. Side effects: outbox `patrol.scan_recorded`, and `patrol.checkpoint_missed` emitted by the scheduler when a checkpoint's window closes unscanned. Notifications: missed checkpoints raise a P2 alert after the configured grace. Errors: `422 validation_failed`, `409 state_transition_invalid` (patrol not In Progress).

##### Spec P2 — `POST /v1/wake-checks/{id}/acknowledge`

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Auth | Device-bound guard session. **AI may never perform this** (canon §1.7, SUR-AI-005) — the endpoint rejects any request whose token carries an AI actor claim |
| Idempotency | Required; a second acknowledgement returns the first result |
| Validation | Wake check is `Pending` and within `window_seconds` of `due_at`; for challenge types, `response` must match; location required if the schedule demands it |
| Business logic | Sets `acknowledged_at` (server time), computes `response_seconds`, marks `Completed`. If the window has already elapsed, the check stays `Failed` and the late acknowledgement is recorded as evidence on the existing escalation — it does **not** cancel an escalation already in flight (§24 owns whether an operator stands it down) |
| Side effects | Outbox `wake_check.acknowledged`; the escalation timer for this check is cancelled if it has not yet fired |
| Notifications | Command Center console updates in real time (§34.5) |
| Audit | Event row is the record |
| Errors | `409 state_transition_invalid` (already Failed — response includes `escalation_id` and `late_acknowledgement_recorded: true`), `403 permission_denied` |

```json
// request
{"response":"7","location":{"latitude":12.98991,"longitude":77.55468,"accuracy_m":12},
 "device_time":"2026-08-15T20:12:41+05:30"}
// 200
{"data":{"wake_check_id":"018fb1…","status":"Completed",
 "acknowledged_at":"2026-08-15T14:42:44Z","response_seconds":23,
 "response_correct":true,"within_window":true,
 "next_wake_check_at":"2026-08-15T17:35:00Z"}}
```

##### Spec I1 — `POST /v1/sos`

The most important endpoint in the system. Everything about it optimises for "always accepted".

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Auth | Guard session. If the token is expired but structurally valid and the device is bound, the request is **still accepted** and flagged `auth_degraded` — a guard in danger must not fail on a token refresh |
| Authorization | Any authenticated guard; no permission check beyond identity |
| Rate limit | **None.** Exempt at WAF, load balancer and application (SUR-API-006) |
| Idempotency | Key requested but never required; server de-duplicates on `(guard_id, device_time ± 10 s)` |
| Validation | Minimal by design: only `trigger_type` and `device_time` are required. Missing location, missing battery, missing everything else is accepted |
| Timeouts | The handler has a hard 2-second budget; it writes `sos`, `incident`, `alert` and an outbox event and returns. Media upload, notification fan-out, call initiation and escalation all happen asynchronously |
| Side effects | SOS + Incident (SUR-CMD-018) + P0 Alert + escalation started; the guard's site, supervisor and Command Center scope are resolved from the assignment |
| Notifications | Immediate multi-channel fan-out per §24/§36; the guard's app receives a delivery confirmation naming which transport succeeded (SUR-CMD-017) |
| Audit | Full; the SOS row itself is undeletable |
| Errors | Only `401` on a completely invalid token and `500`. Everything else is accepted. A `500` triggers the client's fallback to `/v1/sos/retry` and then to the SMS gateway path |

```json
// request (minimum viable)
{"trigger_type":"long_press","device_time":"2026-08-15T20:14:03+05:30"}
// request (full)
{"trigger_type":"long_press","device_time":"2026-08-15T20:14:03+05:30",
 "assignment_id":"018f7a…",
 "location":{"latitude":12.98991,"longitude":77.55468,"accuracy_m":14,
             "age_seconds":22},
 "battery_pct":31,"network_type":"3g","audio_recording_started":true}
// 201 — returns fast, tells the guard what is happening
{"data":{"sos_id":"018fc1…","status":"Active",
 "received_at":"2026-08-15T14:44:04Z","transport_path":"api",
 "incident_id":"018fc2…","alert_id":"018fc3…",
 "command_center":{"notified":true,"expected_ack_seconds":30},
 "media_upload":{"audio_url":"https://uploads…/presigned","expires_in":900},
 "message":"Help is being arranged. Stay on this screen.",
 "message_localised":"मदद भेजी जा रही है। इस स्क्रीन पर बने रहें।"}}
```

##### Spec I2 — `POST /v1/incidents`

Authorization: `ops.incident.create` (guards, supervisors, ops) or `client.incident.create` (client roles, restricted to their own sites). Idempotency required. Validation: `site_id` in the caller's scope; `incident_type` from the taxonomy; `occurred_at` not in the future and not more than 30 days past (older requires `ops.incident.backdate`); `severity` may be proposed by the reporter but is **recomputed** by the severity rules in §24 — a client cannot set P0 by asserting it, and a guard cannot downgrade one. Business logic: creates the incident in `Pending`, generates a code, creates an Alert at the computed severity, and starts the contractual client-notification clock where applicable. Side effects: outbox `incident.created`; evidence upload URLs returned. Notifications: site's supervisor, operations owner, Command Center for P0/P1, client per the contract's rule. Audit: full. Errors: `422 validation_failed`, `403 permission_denied`, `422 business_rule_violated` (`site_not_in_scope`).

##### Spec I3 — `POST /v1/alerts/{id}/acknowledge`

Authorization: `cmd.alert.acknowledge`, restricted to the operator's seat scope. Idempotency required. Business logic: sets `acknowledged_at` (server time — this is the number the SLA is measured on, SUR-CMD-011), assigns the operator, pauses the current escalation rung's timer but never cancels the escalation. Response returns the elapsed ack time against target so the operator sees their own performance immediately. Errors: `409 state_transition_invalid` (already acknowledged, returns who and when), `403 permission_denied` (outside seat scope).

##### Spec PY1 — `POST /v1/payments/intents`

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Authorization | `fin.payment.initiate` (client roles for their own invoices/bookings; Sales on behalf with a reason) |
| Idempotency | **Required** — a retried intent must not create a second gateway order |
| Validation | Exactly one of `invoice_id`, `booking_id`, `subscription_id`; `amount_paise` must equal the outstanding amount unless `allow_partial` is true and the tenant permits partial payment; currency `INR` |
| Business logic | Creates a local `payment` row in `Pending` with our id, then creates the gateway order with our id in the gateway's notes field — so reconciliation can go both ways even if our callback is lost. Never trusts the client-supplied amount: it is recomputed server-side from the invoice. |
| Side effects | `payment` row, outbox `payment.intent_created` |
| Notifications | None until capture |
| Audit | Full, `risk_tier=high` |
| Errors | `422 validation_failed`, `422 business_rule_violated` (`invoice_already_paid`, `amount_mismatch` with the server's figure), `502 upstream_unavailable` (gateway down — `retry_safe: true`) |

```json
// request
{"invoice_id":"018fd1…","amount_paise":6667000,"method_preference":"upi",
 "return_url":"https://surakshaguards.in/portal/invoices/018fd1…"}
// 201
{"data":{"payment_id":"018fd2…","status":"Pending","amount_paise":6667000,
 "currency":"INR","gateway":"razorpay","gateway_order_id":"order_Nx8…",
 "checkout":{"key_id":"rzp_live_…","order_id":"order_Nx8…","amount":6667000,
   "currency":"INR","name":"Suraksha Guards","description":"Invoice INV-2026-000481",
   "prefill":{"contact":"+919845012345","email":"anita@example.com"},
   "notes":{"suraksha_payment_id":"018fd2…","invoice_id":"018fd1…"}},
 "expires_at":"2026-08-15T15:14:03Z"}}
```

##### Spec PY2 — `POST /v1/webhooks/inbound/razorpay`

Signature-verified (provider scheme), idempotent on the provider event id, returns `200` within 1 second by persisting the raw event and enqueuing processing. The processor: fetches the authoritative payment from the gateway API (never trusting the payload's amount), upserts the local payment on `gateway_payment_id`, allocates to invoices, creates the balanced transaction and ledger entries, updates `amount_due_paise`, and emits `payment.completed`. If the local payment row does not exist (callback arrived before our intent commit, or the intent was lost), the processor creates it from the gateway data and flags it for reconciliation rather than dropping it. Duplicate callbacks are the norm and are handled by the event-id check plus the `UNIQUE(gateway, gateway_payment_id)` constraint.

##### Spec PY3 — `POST /v1/refunds`

Authorization `fin.refund.initiate`; `requires_approval=true` above the tenant's threshold (default ₹10,000) with `required_approver_count=2`. Validation: refund amount ≤ captured amount minus prior refunds; reason code mandatory. Business logic: creates a `refund` in `Pending`, calls the gateway, and creates the reversing transaction only when the gateway confirms — a refund is never ledgered on optimism. Side effects: credit note where the refund relates to an issued invoice (BR-003: the invoice is never edited). Notifications: client (email + SMS), Finance. Audit: full, critical risk tier. Errors: `403 approval_required` with the Approval id, `422 business_rule_violated` (`exceeds_captured_amount`), `502 upstream_unavailable`.

##### Spec IN1 — `POST /v1/invoices/{id}/issue`

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Authorization | `fin.invoice.issue`; `requires_mfa=true` |
| Idempotency | **Required** — a retried issue must not consume two invoice numbers |
| Validation | Invoice is `Draft` or `Pending`; has ≥1 line; totals reconcile (`total = taxable + tax + round_off`); client has GSTIN where the client type requires it; `place_of_supply` set; PO reference present when `client.po_required` |
| Business logic | Allocates the next number from `document_sequence` under `FOR UPDATE` inside the transaction, sets `issue_date` and `due_date` (= issue + payment terms), freezes lines, creates the balanced transaction (`invoice_issued`) and ledger entries, and marks `Active`. PDF generation and e-invoice registration (where applicable) happen asynchronously from the emitted event. |
| Side effects | Outbox `invoice.issued`; dunning schedule created (reminders at due−7, due, due+7, due+15, due+30) |
| Notifications | Client billing contact (email with PDF + WhatsApp/SMS summary), account owner |
| Audit | Full, `risk_tier=high` |
| Errors | `409 state_transition_invalid` (already issued — returns the existing number), `422 validation_failed` (`totals_mismatch`, `gstin_required`, `po_required`), `423 record_locked` |

```json
// 200
{"data":{"invoice_id":"018fd1…","invoice_number":"INV-2026-000481",
 "status":"Active","issue_date":"2026-08-15","due_date":"2026-09-14",
 "subtotal_paise":5650000,"tax_paise":1017000,"round_off_paise":0,
 "total_paise":6667000,"amount_due_paise":6667000,
 "place_of_supply":"29","tax_lines":[
   {"tax_type":"cgst","rate":9.0,"taxable_paise":5650000,"tax_paise":508500},
   {"tax_type":"sgst","rate":9.0,"taxable_paise":5650000,"tax_paise":508500}],
 "pdf":{"status":"generating","poll_endpoint":"/v1/invoices/018fd1…/pdf"},
 "transaction_id":"018fd3…"}}
```

##### Spec IN2 — `POST /v1/invoices/generate`

Runs contract-driven generation for a billing period: for each Active contract with `billing_day` in range, aggregates verified attendance against contract lines, applies SLA penalties/credits computed by §24's evidence, and produces Draft invoices. Returns `202` with a job handle. Guarantees: idempotent per (tenant, contract, period) — re-running never creates a second draft for the same period; instead it reports `skipped_existing`. Never issues automatically; issuing is always a human act (or an explicitly configured tenant automation with its own approval record).

##### Spec PR1 — `POST /v1/payroll-runs/{id}/calculate`

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Authorization | `fin.payroll.calculate` |
| Idempotency | Required; recalculation replaces the previous draft payslips atomically per guard and records a recalculation reason |
| Validation | Run is `Draft`; the attendance cutoff has passed; every guard in scope has a salary structure effective for the period; no unverified attendance rows remain (or `allow_unverified` is set with a reason and the count is reported) |
| Business logic | For each guard: pulls attendance for the period, resolves the salary structure and statutory rule versions effective on the period end (`as_of` — SUR-DAT-023), computes earnings and deductions, recovers advances, adds arrears from prior corrections, and produces a Payslip in `Draft`. Runs `recon.payroll_vs_attendance` before completing. |
| Response | `202` + job handle; the run moves to `In Progress` then `Pending` (awaiting approval) |
| Side effects | Locks the attendance rows consumed (`payroll_locked_at`); later corrections become arrears, not edits |
| Notifications | Payroll operator on completion, with the exception list |
| Audit | Full, critical risk |
| Errors | `422 business_rule_violated` (`missing_salary_structure` with the guard list, `unverified_attendance` with counts), `423 record_locked` |

```json
// 202
{"data":{"job_id":"018fe1…","payroll_run_id":"018fe0…","status":"In Progress",
 "guards_in_scope":842,"poll_endpoint":"/v1/jobs/018fe1…"}}
// job result
{"data":{"status":"Completed","payslips_created":838,"skipped":4,
 "gross_paise":1284500000,"deductions_paise":161200000,"net_paise":1123300000,
 "employer_cost_paise":1398700000,
 "exceptions":[
  {"guard_id":"018f31…","code":"missing_bank_details","blocking":true},
  {"guard_id":"018f38…","code":"attendance_unverified","days":3,"blocking":false},
  {"guard_id":"018f44…","code":"negative_net_after_advance_recovery","blocking":true}],
 "statutory_snapshot":{"pf_rule_version":"2026-04-01","esi_rule_version":"2025-07-01",
   "pt_state":"KA","pt_rule_version":"2025-04-01","tds_rule_version":"2026-04-01"}}}
```

##### Spec PR2 — `POST /v1/payroll-runs/{id}/disburse`

Authorization `fin.payroll.disburse`; `requires_mfa=true`; `requires_approval=true` with two approvers already recorded on the run (approval and disbursement may not be the same person). Idempotency required. Validation: run is `Completed` (calculated) and `approved_at` set; no blocking exceptions remain; the funding source has sufficient balance. Business logic: creates a Settlement of type `guard_payout_batch`, creates per-guard payment records, and submits to the payout rail (rail choice is `[DECISION REQUIRED]` per canon §4 — the schema and the API are rail-agnostic and the response names whichever rail executed). Side effects: ledger entries per payslip; run locked. Notifications: each guard receives a payslip-available notification with the net amount; Finance receives the batch summary. Audit: critical, permanent. Errors: `403 approval_required`, `422 business_rule_violated` (`blocking_exceptions_present`, `insufficient_funds`), `502 upstream_unavailable`.

##### Spec W1 — `POST /v1/wallets/{id}/transactions`

Idempotency required. Validation: `amount_paise > 0`; `direction` ∈ `credit`/`debit`; a debit may not exceed `available_paise` unless `allow_negative` is set for that wallet type (only `guard_advance` permits it). Business logic: creates a balanced Transaction with two ledger legs, updates the cached balance in the same transaction, and returns the resulting balance with the ledger entry ids so the caller can prove the movement. Never exposes a "set balance" operation — there is no such thing; a balance is the sum of a ledger.

```json
// request
{"direction":"debit","amount_paise":250000,"reason_code":"advance_disbursed",
 "reference_type":"guard_advance","reference_id":"018ff1…",
 "note":"Festival advance, recoverable over 4 months"}
// 201
{"data":{"transaction_id":"018ff2…","status":"Completed",
 "ledger_entries":[
   {"id":"018ff3…","account_code":"2100-GUARD-ADVANCE","direction":"D","amount_paise":250000},
   {"id":"018ff4…","account_code":"1010-BANK-OPERATING","direction":"C","amount_paise":250000}],
 "wallet":{"id":"018ff0…","balance_paise":1750000,"available_paise":1750000,
           "held_paise":0,"as_of":"2026-08-15T14:44:03Z"}}}
```

##### Spec TN1 — `GET /v1/tenders/matched`

Entitlement-gated: `403 plan_upgrade_required` for Starter (tender discovery is a Professional feature, canon §1.4). Matching logic: the tender's `eligibility` (turnover, experience years, required licence states, manpower strength) is evaluated against the agency's verified profile — and the response returns, per tender, *which criteria matched and which did not*, because "you are not eligible" without a reason is useless.

```json
{"data":[
 {"tender_id":"018ffa…","title":"Provision of security services — 42 posts, 3 campuses",
  "issuing_authority":"Karnataka State Warehousing Corporation",
  "state":"KA","district":"Bengaluru Urban",
  "tender_value_paise":248000000,"emd_paise":4960000,
  "closes_at":"2026-09-04T12:00:00Z","days_remaining":20,
  "verification_status":"Verified","source":"manual_entry",
  "match":{"score":78,"eligible":false,
    "criteria":[
     {"key":"licence_state","required":"KA","actual":"KA","met":true},
     {"key":"min_turnover_paise","required":500000000,"actual":312000000,"met":false},
     {"key":"experience_years","required":3,"actual":6,"met":true},
     {"key":"manpower_strength","required":200,"actual":842,"met":true}]},
  "source_note":"Entered manually by the Suraksha tender desk and verified against the published notice. Suraksha does not claim an official portal API integration."}],
 "meta":{"next_cursor":null,"has_more":false,
   "disclaimer":"Tender data is compiled from public notices. Always verify against the issuing authority's official document before bidding."}}
```

The `source_note` and `disclaimer` are deliberate: the canon forbids inventing third-party APIs, and P3 of the live-site problem list is fake tenders. Every tender the platform shows must carry its provenance.

##### Spec MK1 — `POST /v1/marketplace/requests/{id}/responses`

The cross-tenant write. Authorization: the responding tenant must be Verified, `marketplace_enabled`, hold a valid licence for the request's state (BR-002), and either be invited or the request must be `open`. Validation: `offered_headcount` ≤ requested; `rate_paise` within any band the requester set; the responding agency must have that many deployable guards free in the window — this is checked, not asserted, and the response includes the check result so a requester can trust the number. Data visibility: the responder sees only their own response; the requester sees all (§32.2.6.2). Side effects: outbox `marketplace.response_created`; notification to the requester. Audit: cross-tenant, always audited (SUR-DAT-013). Errors: `403 permission_denied` (not invited), `422 business_rule_violated` (`licence_not_valid_for_state`, `insufficient_available_guards` with the actual count), `409 state_transition_invalid` (request expired or awarded).

Full specification for `POST /v1/notifications/send`: authorization `ntf.send` with an audience scope limit (a Branch Manager may not broadcast tenant-wide); idempotency required (duplicate SMS costs money); validation requires `template_key` and complete template variables — free-text bodies are not accepted on this endpoint, because templates are what make localisation, throttling and provider approval work (§36); the `category` determines whether preferences can suppress it (Critical cannot be suppressed); the response returns a `notification_batch_id` and a per-recipient status poll endpoint. Rate limit: 20 sends/min per user, 1,000 recipients per send, larger audiences via `/v1/announcements` which returns a job.

##### Spec DC1 — `POST /v1/documents/upload-url` then `POST /v1/documents`

Two-step by design: the API never proxies file bytes. Step 1 returns a presigned PUT URL scoped to one object key, one content type and one max size, expiring in 15 minutes. Step 2 registers the document, at which point the file is virus-scanned asynchronously and the document stays `Draft` until the scan passes (`Pending` on pass, `Rejected` with `virus_detected` on fail).

```json
// step 1 request
{"owner_type":"guard","owner_id":"018f31…","document_type":"police_verification",
 "filename":"pv_ramesh_2026.pdf","content_type":"application/pdf","size_bytes":842301}
// step 1 response
{"data":{"upload_url":"https://storage…/…?X-Amz-Signature=…","method":"PUT",
 "headers":{"Content-Type":"application/pdf"},"file_id":"018ffb…",
 "expires_at":"2026-08-15T14:59:03Z","max_size_bytes":10485760}}
// step 2 request
{"file_id":"018ffb…","owner_type":"guard","owner_id":"018f31…",
 "document_type":"police_verification","document_number":"PV/BLR/2026/8821",
 "issued_by":"Commissioner of Police, Bengaluru City",
 "issue_date":"2026-02-11","expiry_date":"2028-02-10",
 "is_mandatory_for_deployment":true}
// step 2 response 201
{"data":{"id":"018ffc…","status":"Draft","virus_scan_status":"Pending",
 "verification":{"id":"018ffd…","status":"Pending","method":"manual_review"},
 "expiry_reminders_at":["2027-12-12","2028-01-11","2028-01-26","2028-02-03","2028-02-09"],
 "guard_deployability_effect":{"before":"blocked","after_verified":"deployable",
   "remaining_blockers":["training_pending"]}}}
```

The `guard_deployability_effect` block tells an HR user exactly what this upload will and will not unlock — one of the highest-value pieces of feedback in the whole product, and it costs one derived computation.

#### 33.3.20 Verification domain

| Method | Endpoint | Purpose | Auth | Roles | Idem |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/v1/verifications` | Request a verification | S,K | HR, Compliance, Verification | R |
| GET | `/v1/verifications` · `/{id}` | Queue / detail | S | Verification, Compliance | n/a |
| POST | `/v1/verifications/{id}/assign` | Assign to an officer | S | Verification lead | R |
| POST | `/v1/verifications/{id}/complete` | Record the decision | S | Verification | R |
| POST | `/v1/verifications/{id}/reject` | Reject with reasons | S | Verification | R |
| GET | `/v1/verifications/providers` | Which methods are available for a type | S | Verification | n/a |

`GET /v1/verifications/providers` exists precisely because provider availability is uncertain: it returns, per verification type, the currently configured method (`api_provider` with the provider name, or `manual_review`), so the UI never promises an instant check that the platform cannot perform. Where no API exists — PSARA licence status is the standing example — the response says so explicitly and the workflow routes to a human with a documented procedure.

`POST /v1/verifications/{id}/complete`: authorization `cmp.verification.decide`; `requires_mfa=true`; validation requires `result`, `result_detail`, and at least one evidence file for `police` and `employment_history` types; side effects recompute the subject's verification status and (for guards) `deployability`, potentially unblocking assignment; notifications to the requester, the guard and — where the client contract requires verified-staff attestation — the client; audit is critical-tier and permanent.

#### 33.3.21 AI domain

| Method | Endpoint | Purpose | Auth | Roles | Idem |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/v1/ai/conversations` | Start a conversation | S | any (role-scoped) | R |
| POST | `/v1/ai/conversations/{id}/messages` | Send a message (text or voice) | S | any | R |
| GET | `/v1/ai/conversations/{id}` | History | S | owner | n/a |
| POST | `/v1/ai/actions/{id}/approve` · `/reject` | Human decision on an approval-required action | S | permission-holder for that action | R |
| POST | `/v1/ai/feedback` | Rate a response | S | owner | O |
| GET | `/v1/ai/capabilities` | What the assistant may do for this role | S | any | n/a |

##### Spec AI1 — `POST /v1/ai/conversations/{id}/messages`

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Authorization | The assistant executes **strictly within the caller's permissions** (canon §1.7); the request carries no elevation path. Every tool the model may call is filtered by the caller's §31 permission set before the model sees the tool list. |
| Validation | `content` ≤ 4,000 characters, or `audio_file_id` for voice; `language` must be one of the supported set |
| Action classes | The response names the action class of anything it did or proposes: `read_only` (executed), `recommendation` (presented, not executed), `approval_required` (an Approval row was created and is returned), `automated` (executed, low-risk only). The prohibited list — payments, payroll changes, permission changes, account deletion, guard termination, compliance status changes, financial settlement, sensitive data export — is refused with `refusal_reason` naming the prohibition. |
| Rate limit | 30 messages/min per user; token budget per tenant per day with a `403 plan_upgrade_required` when a Starter tenant exhausts its basic-AI allowance |
| Side effects | An `ai_interaction` row always; an `approval` row when the class demands it; any executed read is subject to the same audit rules as a direct API call |
| Errors | `403 permission_denied` (the underlying action is not permitted for this role — the assistant says so plainly rather than failing vaguely), `422 validation_failed`, `503 service_unavailable` (model provider down; the response tells the user the assistant is unavailable and offers the manual path) |

```json
// request
{"content":"कल रात ब्रिगेड गेटवे साइट पर कौन-कौन ड्यूटी पर था?","language":"hi-IN"}
// 200
{"data":{"interaction_id":"01900a…","action_class":"read_only",
 "response":"14–15 अगस्त की रात ब्रिगेड गेटवे पर 1 गार्ड ड्यूटी पर था: महेश यादव (SEN-0421), 02:30–14:30 UTC। तीनों वेक-चेक समय पर पूरे हुए। कोई घटना दर्ज नहीं हुई।",
 "entities_referenced":[{"type":"site","id":"018f20…"},
                        {"type":"assignment","id":"018f7a…"}],
 "permission_context":{"role":"Operations Manager","scope":"branch:018f0c…"},
 "citations":[{"label":"Attendance record","endpoint":"/v1/attendance/018f7d…"},
              {"label":"Wake checks","endpoint":"/v1/wake-checks?assignment_id=018f7a…"}],
 "suggested_actions":[
   {"label":"Open the site's night report","endpoint":"/v1/sites/018f20…/reports/night"}],
 "model":{"id":"…","latency_ms":1840,"tokens_in":1420,"tokens_out":210}}}
```

Citations are mandatory on any factual claim: an assistant that states an attendance fact must link the record it read. This is what makes the assistant auditable and is required by §41.

#### 33.3.22 Analytics domain

| Method | Endpoint | Purpose | Auth | Roles | Idem |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/v1/analytics/dashboard/{key}` | A named dashboard's cards | S,K | role-scoped | n/a |
| GET | `/v1/analytics/metrics` | Named metrics with dimensions | S,K | role-scoped | n/a |
| POST | `/v1/reports` | Request a report (async) | S,K | role-scoped | R |
| GET | `/v1/reports/{id}` · `/download` | Poll / download | S,K | requester | n/a |
| GET | `/v1/analytics/benchmarks` | Anonymised peer comparison | S | Agency Owner (Professional+) | n/a |
| GET | `/v1/analytics/sla/{contract_id}` | SLA position with evidence links | S,K | Ops, client | n/a |

All analytics reads are served from the analytical replica and carry `meta.as_of` plus `X-Data-Lag-Seconds` (§32.6.3). Report creation returns `202` with a Report Job; downloads are presigned URLs valid 15 minutes, and every export of a report containing personal data writes an audit `export` entry and embeds a per-user watermark in the file (§38, §39).

`GET /v1/analytics/benchmarks` enforces the k-anonymity floor (SUR-DAT-032): if fewer than 5 tenants contribute to a cell, the cell returns `null` with `suppressed: "insufficient_cohort"` rather than a misleading number.

### 33.4 Webhooks (outbound)

#### 33.4.1 Event catalogue

Events are versioned (`event_version`), named `<domain>.<entity>.<past-tense verb>`, and carry a stable `event_id`. The payload includes the changed entity's public representation plus `changed_fields` on update events. Payloads never include full PII sets — they include ids and the minimum context, and the consumer fetches detail with its own credentials, which keeps the webhook from becoming an unaudited PII export channel.

| Event | Trigger | Typical consumer |
|---|---|---|
| `guard.created`, `guard.updated`, `guard.status_changed`, `guard.exited` | Guard lifecycle | Agency HRMS |
| `guard.deployability_changed` | Documents/training/verification changed the answer | Agency scheduling systems |
| `site.created`, `site.updated`, `site.geofence_changed` | Site config | Client facility systems |
| `assignment.created`, `assignment.cancelled`, `assignment.acknowledged` | Roster | Client visibility feeds |
| `roster.published` | Roster publish | Client, workforce systems |
| `attendance.checked_in`, `attendance.checked_out`, `attendance.exception_raised`, `attendance.verified`, `attendance.corrected` | Duty events | Client dashboards, payroll integrations |
| `shift.understaffed` | Gap detected | Client escalation, ops tooling |
| `patrol.started`, `patrol.completed`, `patrol.checkpoint_missed` | Patrol | Client compliance reporting |
| `wake_check.missed` | Wake check failed | Client night-shift assurance |
| `incident.created`, `incident.updated`, `incident.resolved` | Incident lifecycle | Client incident systems |
| `sos.raised`, `sos.acknowledged`, `sos.resolved` | SOS | **Client emergency integrations only**, never third parties |
| `alert.created`, `alert.escalated`, `alert.resolved` | Alerting | Enterprise ops centres |
| `invoice.issued`, `invoice.paid`, `invoice.overdue`, `credit_note.issued` | Billing | Client and agency accounting |
| `payment.completed`, `payment.failed`, `refund.completed` | Money | Accounting |
| `payroll_run.completed`, `payroll_run.disbursed` | Payroll | Accounting |
| `contract.activated`, `contract.expiring`, `contract.expired`, `contract.amended` | Contract | CRM, client procurement |
| `document.expiring`, `document.expired`, `document.verified` | Compliance | Compliance dashboards |
| `licence.expiring`, `licence.expired` | Licence | Compliance |
| `verification.completed` | Verification | HRMS |
| `booking.created`, `booking.confirmed`, `booking.cancelled` | Demand | CRM |
| `marketplace.request_created`, `marketplace.response_received`, `marketplace.awarded` | Marketplace | Partner agency systems |
| `subscription.activated`, `subscription.expiring`, `subscription.suspended` | SaaS billing | Internal + partner billing |
| `ticket.created`, `ticket.resolved` | Support | Client ITSM |

#### 33.4.2 Delivery guarantees and retry

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Guarantee | **At-least-once.** Consumers must de-duplicate on `event_id` (SUR-DAT-035). Exactly-once is not offered and is not achievable across an HTTP boundary. |
| Ordering | Best-effort per `partition_key` (usually the aggregate id). Cross-aggregate ordering is not guaranteed. Every payload carries `occurred_at` and a per-aggregate `sequence` so a consumer can detect and discard an out-of-order arrival. |
| Timeout | 10 seconds per attempt; a `2xx` is success, anything else is failure |
| Retry schedule | 8 attempts: 10 s, 30 s, 2 min, 10 min, 30 min, 2 h, 6 h, 12 h — full jitter applied |
| Failure handling | After 8 failures the delivery is `Failed` and visible in the Agency Portal's webhook log with a manual replay action. 20 consecutive failures across an endpoint disable it, notify the tenant, and require a manual re-enable (with a test delivery). |
| Payload immutability | The payload is frozen at creation; a retry sends the original bytes, so the signature stays valid and the consumer sees a consistent view even if the entity has since changed. |
| Ordering vs retry | A retrying event does not block later events for the same partition indefinitely; after the second failure the partition continues and the failed event is marked out-of-order on eventual delivery, with `delivered_late: true` in the headers. |

#### 33.4.3 Signature verification and replay protection

Described in §33.2.5. Consumers must: verify the HMAC over the raw body before parsing; reject timestamps older than 5 minutes; store `event_id` for at least 7 days and ignore repeats; and never treat the payload as authoritative for money — fetch the resource.

#### 33.4.4 The duplicate-webhook edge case

The scenario, spelled out because it causes real damage: an agency's accounting integration consumes `invoice.paid`. Our delivery succeeds, but the consumer's response is lost to a network partition, so we retry. The consumer receives the same event twice and posts the receipt twice, and the agency's books show double the revenue.

The platform's obligations: (a) a stable `event_id` that never changes across retries; (b) `X-Suraksha-Attempt` so a consumer can log it; (c) documentation that states at-least-once in the first paragraph, not a footnote; (d) an SDK/sample that shows the de-duplication table; (e) a webhook log in the Agency Portal showing every attempt with its response, so the agency can prove what happened; (f) a `GET /v1/webhook-events/{event_id}` endpoint so a consumer can confirm whether an event it half-processed is genuine. The obligation the platform does **not** take on is exactly-once delivery — promising it would be a lie, and building a consumer that relies on the promise is how this failure becomes silent instead of visible.

The symmetric case — a consumer that returns `500` after successfully processing — is why the replay action exists and why replays are marked `is_replay: true` in the header.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-API-012 | Webhook payloads shall be frozen at creation, retried byte-identical, and carry a stable `event_id`, `sequence` and attempt number; delivery shall be documented as at-least-once. |
| SUR-API-013 | Every tenant shall have a webhook delivery log showing each attempt, its response code and body excerpt, retained 30 days, with manual replay and a test-delivery action. |
| SUR-API-014 | Webhook endpoints shall be validated on registration (HTTPS, public address, successful test delivery) and shall reject private, loopback and link-local addresses. |

### 33.5 API governance

#### 33.5.1 Deprecation policy

| Stage | Duration | Signals |
|---|---|---|
| Announce | ≥90 days before deprecation begins | Changelog entry, email to every tenant with an API key, portal banner |
| Deprecated | ≥12 months | `Deprecation: true` and `Sunset: <RFC 1123 date>` response headers; `Link: <doc>; rel="deprecation"`; usage dashboards show affected callers by tenant and key |
| Brownout | 3 scheduled windows in the final 60 days | The endpoint returns `410 gone` for 1 hour, then 4 hours, then 24 hours, each announced 7 days ahead — brownouts find the integrators who ignore emails |
| Removed | — | `410 gone` permanently with a `details.replacement` pointer |

Security-driven removals may compress this timeline, with the compression reason stated publicly.

#### 33.5.2 Changelog and documentation

A single public changelog at `developers.surakshaguards.in/changelog`, entries dated and categorised (Added / Changed / Deprecated / Removed / Fixed / Security), with the affected endpoints listed and a migration note for anything non-trivial. Documentation is generated from the OpenAPI 3.1 specification, which is itself generated from the code's route and schema definitions — hand-written docs drift, and drifted docs are worse than none. The spec is published at `/v1/openapi.json` and is versioned in the repository, so a diff of the spec is a reviewable part of every pull request.

Documentation includes, per endpoint: purpose, auth, required permission key, plan entitlement, request schema with validation rules, response schema, every error code that endpoint can emit, rate limit bucket, idempotency requirement, side effects, emitted events, and a runnable example. Guides cover: getting started with an API key, pagination, idempotency, webhooks with a de-duplication example, offline sync semantics, error handling, and a sandbox walkthrough.

#### 33.5.3 SDK stance

**[RECOMMENDED]** Ship no hand-written SDKs in V1. Publish the OpenAPI spec, a Postman/Bruno collection, and generator instructions for the four languages Indian integrators actually use (Java, .NET, Python, Node). Rationale: hand-maintained SDKs in four languages is a permanent tax on a small team, they lag the API, and a stale SDK is a support burden that consumes more time than it saves. Reassess when more than 10 Enterprise tenants are integrating, at which point generate — do not hand-write — a TypeScript and a Python client from the spec in CI.

A **sandbox environment** is not optional: `sandbox.api.surakshaguards.in` with seeded demo data, test API keys (`sk_test_`), a webhook simulator that can fire any catalogue event on demand (including duplicates, out-of-order and late deliveries), and a payment gateway in test mode. An integrator who cannot test a duplicate webhook will write a consumer that breaks on one.

#### 33.5.4 Contract testing

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-API-015 | The OpenAPI specification shall be generated from code, published at `/v1/openapi.json`, versioned in the repository, and CI shall fail on any undocumented route or schema divergence. |
| SUR-API-016 | CI shall run a schema-diff check on every pull request and fail on a breaking change unless the change is accompanied by a version bump and a changelog entry. |
| SUR-API-017 | Each first-party client (four mobile apps, five web properties) shall publish consumer contract tests describing the fields and behaviours it depends on; the API build shall run them and fail on a broken consumer expectation. |
| SUR-API-018 | Every endpoint shall have an authorization test asserting that a caller from another tenant receives `404`/`403`, and a permission test per role in §31; these shall be generated from the permission matrix so a matrix change cannot silently outrun its tests. |
| SUR-API-019 | Error responses shall be validated against the error-code table in CI; an endpoint emitting an undocumented code shall fail the build. |

#### 33.5.5 API observability

Per-endpoint p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate by code, rate-limit hit rate, and per-tenant and per-key usage are exported to the metrics pipeline (§48). Every response carries `X-Request-Id`, echoed into logs and audit rows. Slow-query attribution ties a slow endpoint to the SQL statement and the tenant. The API health endpoint `/v1/health` reports dependency health without leaking topology, and `/v1/status` (public) reflects the incident status page.
