### 35.3 B2C money flows

B2C covers individual and small-business customers buying through surakshaguards.in, the Customer Portal (§15) and the Customer App (§16). The lifecycle of a booking itself is defined in §11; here only the money behaviour is specified.

#### 35.3.1 Booking payment models

| Model | When used | Money behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Instant book (pay in full) | Short-duration services with a published rate — event security, bouncer blocks, single-day PSO | Full amount authorised and captured before the booking becomes `Active` |
| Advance + balance | Monthly guarding starting on a future date | Configurable advance (default 25% of first month's taxable value + full tax on that portion) captured at booking; balance invoiced per the billing cycle |
| Quote-accept-and-pay | Anything custom-priced (§11 quotation flow) | No money until the quotation is accepted; acceptance generates a proforma, payment converts it to a tax invoice |
| Monthly recurring | Ongoing residential/small-business guarding | Invoice issued on the billing day; auto-debit attempted if a mandate exists, otherwise a payment link |
| Post-paid on contract | B2B only (§35.4) | Invoice on credit terms |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-041 | Booking states and payment states shall be distinct. A booking may be `Pending` with payment `Completed` (money in, ops not yet confirmed) or `Active` with payment `Pending` (approved credit). The UI shall show both, never one merged badge. |
| SUR-FIN-042 | The advance percentage, its minimum absolute floor, and whether tax is charged on the advance or on the full value shall be configurable per service lane and per city, versioned, and shown to the customer before payment. |
| SUR-FIN-043 | Money shall never be captured before the customer has seen a breakdown screen showing taxable value, each tax line with its rate, any discount, any wallet application, and the exact amount that will leave their account. |

#### 35.3.2 Instant-book checkout — money sequence

| Step | Action | Ledger effect |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Customer confirms cart; platform creates a `PaymentIntent` with an idempotency key derived from `booking_draft_id` | None |
| 2 | Gateway order created; customer redirected/SDK opened | None |
| 3 | Gateway reports authorisation | None (authorisation is not money movement) |
| 4 | Capture confirmed by webhook **or** by server-side verification poll | Dr `PG_CLEARING` / Cr `CUSTOMER_ADVANCE` |
| 5 | Booking transitions to `Active`; tax invoice issued for the service | Dr `AR_TRADE` / Cr `REV_*` + Cr `TAX_OUTPUT`, then Dr `CUSTOMER_ADVANCE` / Cr `AR_TRADE` |
| 6 | Gateway settlement file received (T+1/T+2) | Dr `BANK_OPERATING` + Dr `EXP_PG_FEE` + Dr `TAX_INPUT` / Cr `PG_CLEARING` |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-044 | The platform shall never trust a client-side success callback as proof of payment. Booking confirmation shall be gated on a server-verified capture — webhook signature verified, or an explicit server-to-server fetch of the payment object. |
| SUR-FIN-045 | Authorisation-only flows shall carry an explicit expiry; an authorisation that is not captured within the configured window shall be voided and the booking draft expired, with the customer notified (see §36 event `PAY-07`). |

#### 35.3.3 Advance vs balance

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-046 | For advance+balance bookings the platform shall create a **payment schedule** with dated instalments at booking time, each with its own amount, due date, invoice linkage and reminder plan. The schedule shall be visible to the customer. |
| SUR-FIN-047 | A change to the deployment (guards added, start date moved, site changed) shall regenerate the *unbilled* portion of the schedule and leave billed instalments untouched; the delta shall be presented to the customer for acceptance before any additional charge. |
| SUR-FIN-048 | If the balance instalment fails and the service has started, the account shall enter the B2C dunning ladder (§35.3.7); service suspension for non-payment shall follow the contract's configured notice period and shall require a human decision, never an automatic guard withdrawal. |

#### 35.3.4 Quote-accept-and-pay

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-049 | An accepted Quotation shall generate a **Proforma Invoice** (no ledger posting, no tax liability, its own numbering series) which converts to a Tax Invoice on the configured trigger — payment receipt or service commencement, per tenant configuration. |
| SUR-FIN-050 | Quotation acceptance shall capture the accepting person, timestamp, IP/device and the exact quotation version hash, and shall lock that version; any later change requires a new quotation version and a fresh acceptance. |
| SUR-FIN-051 | A quotation shall carry an expiry date and a price-validity statement; expiry shall block payment against it and shall require re-quotation (see §11 for the lifecycle). |

#### 35.3.5 Monthly recurring billing (B2C)

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-052 | Recurring billing shall run as a scheduled job per tenant per billing day, generating invoices with a deterministic idempotency key `billing:{subscription_or_contract_id}:{period_start}`. A re-run shall be a no-op. |
| SUR-FIN-053 | Invoices shall be generated in `Draft`, held for a configurable review window (default 0 hours for B2C, 24 hours for B2B), then `Issued`. Only `Issued` posts to the ledger. |
| SUR-FIN-054 | Where a mandate (UPI Autopay / e-mandate / card-on-file) exists, an auto-debit shall be attempted on the configured day with pre-debit notification per the mandate's configured lead time. Where no mandate exists, a payment link shall be issued with the reminder ladder in §36. |
| SUR-FIN-055 | Mandate lifecycle events (created, paused, revoked, expired, amount-limit exceeded) shall be first-class records with notifications, and a revoked mandate shall immediately switch the account to link-based collection rather than failing silently each month. |

#### 35.3.6 Payment failure and retry

| Attempt | Timing | Channel | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Due date, 10:00 local | Auto-debit | Pre-debit notice 24h earlier where mandate rules require |
| 2 | +2 days | Auto-debit | Skipped if failure reason is `mandate_revoked` or `account_closed` |
| 3 | +5 days | Auto-debit + payment link | Link sent by push, SMS, email |
| 4 | +9 days | Payment link only | Human follow-up task created for Support |
| Stop | +15 days | — | Account flagged `collection_review`; Finance decides |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-056 | Retry schedules shall be configurable per tenant and per product, with a hard cap on attempts, and shall respect failure-reason classification: `soft` (insufficient funds, temporary decline) retries; `hard` (invalid instrument, mandate revoked, blocked) does not retry and immediately requests a new instrument. |
| SUR-FIN-057 | Every failed attempt shall record the gateway's error code and message verbatim alongside the platform's normalised reason, so that support can answer "why did it fail" without opening the gateway dashboard. |
| SUR-FIN-058 | A failed payment shall never post to the ledger. Only captured money posts. Failed attempts are operational records. |

#### 35.3.7 B2C dunning ladder

| Stage | Trigger | Action | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| D0 | Invoice issued | Invoice + payment link (push/email/in-app) | System |
| D1 | Due − 3 days | Reminder (push + in-app) | System |
| D2 | Due date | Reminder (push + SMS) | System |
| D3 | Due + 3 days | Overdue notice (push + SMS + email) | System |
| D4 | Due + 7 days | Support call task; service-continuity warning per contract | Support |
| D5 | Due + 15 days | Suspension review — Finance decision, client notified with the configured notice period | Finance |
| D6 | Due + 30 days | Escalation to collections queue; interest/late fee applied only if the contract configures one | Finance |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-059 | Late fees and interest shall be applied only where the contract carries an explicit configured clause, shall be computed by a versioned rule, shall post as a separate document (Debit Note), and shall be waivable by Finance with a recorded reason. |
| SUR-FIN-060 | Guard withdrawal for non-payment shall never be an automated action. The platform may create the task and the notice; a named human must approve, and the safety implications of withdrawing from a live post shall be surfaced on the approval screen. |

#### 35.3.8 Wallet

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-061 | The client Wallet shall be a liability sub-ledger keyed by client, never a balance column on the client row. Its balance shall equal the sum of its ledger entries at all times. |
| SUR-FIN-062 | Wallet money shall be classified into `topup_cash` (customer's own money) and `promotional_credit` (issued by Suraksha). Only `topup_cash` is refundable to a bank account; `promotional_credit` is non-refundable, may carry an expiry, and shall be consumed first in any application. |
| SUR-FIN-063 | Wallet application to an invoice shall be an explicit allocation, reversible only by reversing the allocation; the wallet shall never go negative. |
| SUR-FIN-064 | Wallet withdrawal (refund of `topup_cash` to source) shall require identity re-verification, shall be capped per day per client by a configurable limit, and shall be maker-checker approved above a configurable threshold (§35.9.6). |
| SUR-FIN-065 | Wallet statements shall be downloadable by the client with every credit and debit, its source document, and the running balance. |

#### 35.3.9 Refunds, cancellations and dispute freeze

| Cancellation window | Default charge | Configurable per |
|---|---|---|
| > 72h before start | 0% | Service lane, city, contract |
| 24–72h before start | 25% of the cancelled taxable value | as above |
| < 24h before start | 50% | as above |
| After deployment starts | Pro-rata for consumed days + notice-period charge per contract | as above |
| No-show by customer (event/PSO block) | 100% | as above |
| Cancellation by Suraksha / fulfilment failure | 0% and an SLA credit per contract | as above |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-066 | Refunds shall be issued to the original instrument by default. Refund to a different instrument or to a bank account shall require Finance approval, documented reason and beneficiary verification. |
| SUR-FIN-067 | A refund shall never exceed the net captured amount for its source payment, enforced by a database-level check on cumulative refunds per payment. |
| SUR-FIN-068 | Partial refunds shall be allowed with explicit line-level attribution, so the tax reversal on a credit note matches the tax originally charged on those lines. |
| SUR-FIN-069 | When a chargeback or dispute is raised at the gateway, the platform shall place a **dispute freeze**: the disputed amount is moved from the normal balance to a `Disputed` bucket, refunds and further allocations against that payment are blocked, and the case gets an owner, evidence checklist and deadline. |
| SUR-FIN-070 | Dispute outcomes shall post explicitly — `dispute_lost` reverses the revenue and records the fee; `dispute_won` releases the freeze with no revenue change. Neither shall be inferred from a balance movement in the settlement file alone. |

#### 35.3.10 The hard edge cases — exact behaviour

**Case A — payment succeeded at the gateway but the callback never reached the platform.**

This is the single most common real-world money incident. The customer's money left their account; the platform believes the booking failed.

| Step | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| 1 | The client SDK's completion callback is treated as advisory only. On any terminal client outcome (success, failure, abandonment) the app calls `POST /payments/{intent_id}/verify`. |
| 2 | `verify` performs a server-to-server fetch of the payment object from the gateway. If the gateway says captured, the platform posts the capture (idempotent on the gateway payment id) and confirms the booking — regardless of what the client reported. |
| 3 | Independently, a **reconciliation sweeper** runs every 5 minutes over all payment intents in `Pending`/`Authorized` older than 3 minutes and performs the same server-side fetch. Nothing depends on the customer reopening the app. |
| 4 | Independently again, the daily gateway settlement file is matched against posted payments; any gateway payment with no platform posting creates a P1 `orphan_gateway_payment` exception with the customer identified from the gateway payload. |
| 5 | If the booking window has passed by the time the payment is discovered, the platform does **not** silently keep the money: it creates a `payment_without_service` exception, notifies the customer within the SLA, and offers wallet credit or refund. |
| 6 | The customer-facing state during ambiguity is "Payment being confirmed", never "Payment failed". A false "failed" causes duplicate payment attempts, which is a worse outcome. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-071 | Payment truth shall be established by three independent paths — webhook, client-triggered verify, and the sweeper — all converging on the same idempotent posting keyed by the gateway payment id. No single path may be a required dependency. |
| SUR-FIN-072 | The gateway settlement file shall be the final arbiter. Any gateway-side payment absent from the platform ledger, or any platform posting absent from the settlement file, shall raise an exception that cannot be closed without a documented resolution. |
| SUR-FIN-073 | While a payment is in an unresolved state, the platform shall block a second payment attempt for the same booking draft unless the customer explicitly confirms after being shown the pending attempt. |

**Case B — duplicate webhook delivery.**

Gateways deliver at-least-once. The platform must be exactly-once at the ledger.

| Step | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| 1 | The webhook endpoint verifies the signature. Invalid signature → 401, logged as a security event, never processed. |
| 2 | The raw event is inserted into `inbound_webhook_event` with a unique constraint on `(provider, provider_event_id)`. A constraint violation → the handler returns 200 immediately and does nothing else. |
| 3 | If the insert succeeds, the handler enqueues processing. Processing itself is idempotent on the business key (`gateway_payment_id` + `posting_purpose`), so even a duplicate event id from a provider retry with a *new* id cannot double-post. |
| 4 | Out-of-order delivery is handled by state-machine guards: a `payment.captured` arriving after `refund.processed` does not resurrect the payment; each transition validates the source state and records an `out_of_order_event` note if it must be ignored. |
| 5 | Every ignored duplicate is counted in metrics; a sudden rise indicates a provider issue and raises a P2 alert. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-074 | Webhook handlers shall always return 2xx for events they have decided to ignore, so the provider stops retrying, and shall return 5xx only for genuine processing failures that should be retried. |
| SUR-FIN-075 | The raw webhook body shall be retained for 180 days, encrypted, with card/UPI identifiers masked at rest, for dispute defence and replay during incident recovery. |
| SUR-FIN-076 | The platform shall support **manual replay** of a stored webhook event by Finance/Engineering with a recorded reason; replay runs the same idempotent path and therefore cannot double-post. |

**Case C — customer pays twice for the same booking.** Both captures post. The platform detects `duplicate_intent_for_same_draft`, auto-creates a refund proposal for the later capture, notifies the customer, and requires Finance approval only if the amounts differ.

**Case D — refund succeeded at the gateway but the platform lost the response.** The refund request carries an idempotency key derived from `(payment_id, refund_sequence)`; the retry returns the same gateway refund object; the sweeper and settlement file both catch any refund posted at the gateway but not in the ledger.

### 35.4 B2B money flows

B2B covers contracted enterprise clients (§12). The commercial construct is a Contract with one or more Sites, each with Posts and agreed rates.

#### 35.4.1 Contract-based monthly billing

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-077 | A Contract shall carry a versioned **rate card**: per Post or per guard-category rate, rate basis (per guard per month / per guard-day / per guard-hour / per shift), overtime treatment, reliever treatment, escalation clause, billing cycle, cut-off day, credit terms and tax profile. |
| SUR-FIN-078 | Billing basis shall be explicit per contract line: `fixed_deployment` (bill the contracted strength regardless of attendance), `attendance_based` (bill actual approved man-days), or `hybrid` (fixed with deductions for unfilled posts beyond a tolerance). The platform shall not guess. |
| SUR-FIN-079 | The billing period shall be defined by `cycle_start_day` and `cut_off_day`; attendance after cut-off falls into the next cycle as an arrears line, clearly labelled with its original period. |
| SUR-FIN-080 | Contract escalation (annual rate increase, minimum-wage-linked revision) shall be a scheduled, effective-dated rate card version requiring client acknowledgement per the contract's configured mechanism; the platform shall notify 45/30/15 days before an escalation takes effect. |

#### 35.4.2 The attendance → approval → invoice chain

This chain is the spine of B2B revenue. It must be tamper-evident because it simultaneously determines what the client pays, what the guard earns and what the agency is settled.

| Stage | Owner | Output | Lock |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Capture | Guard App | Attendance records with device+server time, geofence result, photo/biometric evidence (§18) | none |
| 2. Supervisor verification | Supervisor / Field Officer | Verified attendance, exceptions flagged | attendance row locked from guard edit |
| 3. Branch review | Operations Manager | Exception resolution, manual overrides with reason | overrides require reason + approver |
| 4. Period close | Agency Payroll / Ops | Attendance sheet for the period, per site | period marked `In Progress` |
| 5. Client approval | Client Site Manager / Facility Manager | Digitally acknowledged attendance sheet | attendance frozen for that site+period |
| 6. Invoice generation | Billing engine | Draft invoice with line-level traceback to man-days | draft |
| 7. Invoice issue | Agency Finance | Issued invoice, ledger posted | immutable |
| 8. Payroll consumption | Payroll run | Wage computation from the same frozen attendance | period locked for payroll |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-081 | An invoice line derived from attendance shall carry a machine-traceable reference to the exact set of attendance records that produced it; clicking the line in the portal shall list them (date, guard, post, shift, hours, exception flags). |
| SUR-FIN-082 | Client approval of attendance shall be an explicit, authenticated act with a recorded identity and timestamp, and shall support partial approval — approving 27 of 30 days with three disputed days routed to an exception flow, which are billed after resolution or dropped by a credit note. |
| SUR-FIN-083 | Where a contract does not require client approval, the platform shall record `client_approval_waived_by_contract` on the invoice, so the difference in evidentiary strength is visible during a dispute. |
| SUR-FIN-084 | Attendance frozen by client approval shall not be editable. A correction after freeze shall create an `attendance_restatement` record, require dual approval (Operations Manager + Agency Finance), and produce either a debit note or a credit note in the next cycle. It shall never modify the original record. |
| SUR-FIN-085 | The platform shall compute and display a **billing vs payroll reconciliation** per site per period: man-days billed, man-days paid, difference, and the reason for each difference (reliever cost absorbed, unfilled post deducted, overtime unbilled). An unexplained difference above a configurable threshold blocks invoice issue. |

#### 35.4.3 Site-wise vs centralised billing

| Model | Description | Invoice structure |
|---|---|---|
| Site-wise | Each Site is invoiced separately, often to different cost centres | One invoice per site per period; separate numbering optional per branch series |
| Centralised | One invoice for all sites under a contract | One invoice with site-grouped line blocks and a per-site subtotal annexure |
| Hybrid | Some sites invoiced to the site, others rolled up to head office | Per-site `billing_target` field decides routing |
| Cost-centre split | One legal invoice, internal split for client's own accounting | Invoice carries `cost_centre_code` per line; the client's export includes it |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-086 | Each Site shall carry a `billing_target` (the invoicing entity), a `billing_address`, a `tax_registration` reference and an optional `cost_centre_code`; the invoice's place-of-supply determination shall be driven from these configured fields. |
| SUR-FIN-087 | Every invoice, whatever the model, shall be accompanied by a machine-readable annexure (CSV + PDF) showing per-site, per-post, per-day detail, because enterprise clients reconcile at that granularity and disputes otherwise become email threads. |

#### 35.4.4 Purchase orders and credit control

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-088 | A Contract may require a Purchase Order. Where `po_required = true`, invoice issue shall be blocked unless a valid PO is attached with a non-exhausted balance; the invoice shall print the PO number and the remaining PO value. |
| SUR-FIN-089 | PO consumption shall be tracked as a running balance; an invoice that would exceed the PO value shall be blocked with an actionable message ("PO SUR/2026/114 has ₹42,000 remaining; this invoice is ₹87,320"), and shall offer to split or request a PO amendment. |
| SUR-FIN-090 | Credit terms (`net_15`, `net_30`, `net_45`, `net_60`, custom days, "from invoice date" vs "from receipt date" vs "from approval date") shall be contract configuration and shall drive due-date computation and ageing. |
| SUR-FIN-091 | A credit limit per client shall be configurable, with utilisation = open receivables + unbilled accrued value. Breach shall raise a P2 alert to Sales and Finance and shall gate new site additions pending Finance override, which is recorded. |
| SUR-FIN-092 | Security deposits and retention money held by the client shall be tracked as receivable sub-balances with expected release dates and a follow-up queue; they shall not be netted invisibly against invoices. |

#### 35.4.5 Receivables ageing and the B2B dunning ladder

Ageing buckets (configurable): Current · 1–30 · 31–60 · 61–90 · 91–180 · 180+ days past due.

| Stage | Trigger | Action | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| B0 | Invoice issued | Invoice + annexure emailed to billing contacts; portal notification | System |
| B1 | Due − 7 days | Statement reminder to Client Finance | System |
| B2 | Due date | Reminder + open-items statement | System |
| B3 | Due + 7 | Escalation to Facility Manager + Client Finance; task for the account owner | Sales/Finance |
| B4 | Due + 15 | Formal overdue letter from the configured template; Security Head copied | Finance |
| B5 | Due + 30 | Credit hold: no new sites, no scope expansion; Founder/Management visibility | Finance |
| B6 | Due + 45 | Service-continuity notice per contract clause; legal/collections review flagged | Management |
| B7 | Due + 90 | Provisioning/write-off review; recovery route decided | Finance |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-093 | The dunning ladder shall be configurable per client tier and per contract, with the ability to pause the ladder (e.g. genuine dispute under investigation) — a pause requires a reason, an owner and an expiry date, and pauses are reported weekly. |
| SUR-FIN-094 | Every dunning communication shall be recorded against the invoice with its channel, template version, recipient and delivery status (§36), so that "we never received the invoice" can be answered with evidence. |
| SUR-FIN-095 | Write-off shall be a maker-checker operation above a configurable threshold, shall post to `EXP_WRITEOFF`, shall never delete the invoice, and shall retain the receivable in reporting under a `written_off` classification for recovery tracking. |

#### 35.4.6 SLA credits

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-096 | SLA definitions (fill rate, punctuality, response time, patrol compliance, report delivery) shall be contract configuration with measurement windows, thresholds and a credit formula expressed as a percentage of the period's contract value or a fixed amount per breach. |
| SUR-FIN-097 | SLA measurement shall be computed from the same operational data used for billing and shall be visible to the client continuously, not only at credit time. A credit that surprises the client is a failure of the design. |
| SUR-FIN-098 | SLA credits shall post as credit notes against `SLA_CREDIT` (contra-income), shall be capped per period per the contract, and shall require Finance approval above a configurable value. |
| SUR-FIN-099 | Where the contract provides for a penalty rather than a credit, the platform shall support a Debit Note issued by the client and recorded as a claim with an approval workflow, never auto-accepted. |

#### 35.4.7 Expansion, renewal and termination billing

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-100 | Mid-cycle expansion (new post, extra guard) shall be prorated from the effective date using the shared proration library, shall be quotable before commitment, and shall appear as a distinct invoice line with its date range. |
| SUR-FIN-101 | Renewal shall generate a renewal quotation at the configured lead time (default 60 days), carrying the escalation, with reminders at 60/30/15/7 days and an explicit `auto_renew` flag per contract. |
| SUR-FIN-102 | Termination shall trigger a final settlement statement: unbilled consumed services, notice-period charges per the contract, deposit refunds, outstanding credit notes, and any asset/uniform recovery — presented as one document with a single net figure. |
| SUR-FIN-103 | No contract shall be closable in the system while an open receivable, an unreleased deposit or an unresolved dispute exists; closure requires either resolution or an explicit written-off/settled disposition. |

### 35.5 Agency settlement

Settlement is how Suraksha pays partner agencies for work fulfilled through the marketplace (§19) and through Suraksha's own client contracts sub-served by agencies. It is money leaving Suraksha to a business counterparty, so segregation of duties is mandatory.

#### 35.5.1 Settlement cycle

| Parameter | Default | Configurable per |
|---|---|---|
| Cycle | Monthly, aligned to the client billing period | Agency agreement |
| Cut-off | Last calendar day of the period | Agency agreement |
| Statement generation | Cut-off + 2 working days | Agency agreement |
| Agency review window | 3 working days | Agency agreement |
| Approval | Within 2 working days of review close | Fixed |
| Disbursement | Approval + 1 working day, or on the configured payout day | Agency agreement |
| Weekly cycle option | Available for high-volume agencies with a good compliance score | Commercial decision |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-104 | A settlement statement shall be an immutable numbered document per agency per cycle, with states `Draft` → `Pending` (agency review) → `Verified` (agency accepted or window lapsed) → `Active` (approved for payment) → `Completed` (disbursed and reconciled), plus `Rejected` and `Cancelled`. |
| SUR-FIN-105 | Where a client has not yet paid, the settlement basis (pay-on-fulfilment vs pay-on-collection) shall be an explicit term of the agency agreement, shown on every statement, and shall drive whether an unpaid client invoice creates a settlement hold. |

#### 35.5.2 Calculation basis

Settlement value per work line = `billable_units × agreed_rate`, where the units come from the frozen attendance chain in §35.4.2 — the same data that billed the client. There is exactly one attendance truth.

| Component | Sign | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Fulfilment value | + | Approved man-days × agency rate (or fixed monthly per post) |
| Overtime/holiday premium | + | Per the agency agreement's configured multipliers |
| Reimbursables | + | Pre-approved only, with document evidence |
| Platform commission | − | Where the model is gross-to-agency; else implicit in the rate |
| Penalties | − | Per the configured penalty schedule (no-show, late relief, uniform/grooming failure, missed patrol) |
| Advance recovery | − | Against `ADV_AGENCY`, per the agreed instalment plan |
| Damage/asset recovery | − | Requires an incident reference and agency acknowledgement or dispute |
| Configured withholding | − | Statutory withholding as configured records (§35.6.7 disclaimer applies) |
| Retention/hold | − | Released per the configured release rule |
| Prior-period adjustments | ± | Each with a reference to the prior statement |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-106 | Every settlement line shall be traceable to its operational source (assignment, attendance period, incident, advance schedule). A line without a traceable source shall not be postable. |
| SUR-FIN-107 | Penalty application shall require the penalty to have been notified to the agency at the time of the event, not first revealed on the statement. An un-notified penalty shall be blocked. |
| SUR-FIN-108 | The platform shall compute an agency's **effective realisation rate** (net settled ÷ gross fulfilment value) per cycle and alert when it falls below a configurable floor, because a collapsing realisation rate is how partners quietly become adversaries. |

#### 35.5.3 Holds

| Hold type | Trigger | Release condition |
|---|---|---|
| Compliance hold | Agency licence `Expiring`/`Expired` (BR-002), missing statutory records per configuration | Document verified |
| Quality hold | Open P0/P1 incident attributable to the agency | Investigation closed |
| Dispute hold | Client dispute on the underlying invoice | Dispute resolved |
| Collection hold | Pay-on-collection model, client invoice unpaid | Client payment received |
| Bank hold | Beneficiary verification failed or bank details changed within the cooling period | Re-verification complete |
| Retention | Contractual retention percentage | Configured release schedule |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-109 | A hold shall move the amount to `SETTLEMENT_HOLD` with an owner, a reason, an expected release date and an escalation if unreleased beyond a configurable ageing (default 30 days). Held money shall be visible to the agency with its reason. |
| SUR-FIN-110 | Bank-detail changes shall trigger a mandatory cooling period (default 48 hours), out-of-band re-verification, notification to all agency admins, and re-verification of the beneficiary before the next disbursement. This is the primary defence against payout fraud. |

#### 35.5.4 Disputes and statements

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-111 | The agency shall be able to raise a line-level dispute during the review window with a reason code and evidence. A disputed line is excluded from the current disbursement and moves to a dispute queue with an SLA (default 5 working days). |
| SUR-FIN-112 | The undisputed remainder shall always be paid on time. Withholding an entire settlement because of one disputed line is prohibited by design. |
| SUR-FIN-113 | Dispute resolution shall be recorded with the decision, the decider, the evidence considered and the resulting adjustment (accepted → next statement credit; rejected → explanation), and shall be visible in the agency's portal history. |
| SUR-FIN-114 | Statements shall be downloadable as PDF and CSV, shall show opening balance, additions, deductions, holds, disbursements and closing balance, and shall reconcile to the agency's ledger sub-balance exactly. |

#### 35.5.5 Approval chain and segregation of duties

| Role | May do | May not do |
|---|---|---|
| Operations (City/State) | Confirm fulfilment, raise penalties | Approve settlements, edit rates, release payments |
| Finance (maker) | Prepare and validate the statement, resolve exceptions | Approve their own prepared statement, change beneficiary details |
| Finance (checker) | Approve statements within their limit | Prepare the statement they approve |
| Founder/Management | Approve above the checker limit | Bypass preparation and validation |
| Payments operator | Execute the approved disbursement file/API | Alter amounts or beneficiaries |
| Auditor | Read everything, export | Change anything |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-115 | The same user shall never be able to prepare and approve the same settlement, enforced in code, not by policy. Attempted self-approval shall be blocked and logged as a P1 control event. |
| SUR-FIN-116 | Approval limits shall be configurable by amount band; exceeding a band escalates to the next approver. Every approval shall capture user, timestamp, IP, device and the exact statement version hash. |
| SUR-FIN-117 | A change to any settlement input after approval shall invalidate the approval and require re-approval from the top of the chain. |
| SUR-FIN-118 | Beneficiary master data (agency bank accounts) shall be maintained by a role distinct from both the maker and the checker of settlements, with dual approval on create and change, and with a penny-drop or equivalent verification where available (A-141 applies). |
| SUR-FIN-119 | Disbursement execution shall reconcile file/API responses back to each settlement line within one working day; unreconciled disbursements shall raise a P1 exception. |

### 35.6 Guard payouts and payroll

Payroll is where a software defect becomes a human harm: a guard who is underpaid this month cannot wait for the next release. The design bias is therefore toward transparency, previewability and irreversibility of approved runs.

#### 35.6.1 Payroll run lifecycle

| State | Entered when | What is true | Who acts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Draft` | Run created for a period + scope (branch, site, guard set) | Inputs snapshot begun; nothing computed | Payroll |
| `In Progress` (Calculated) | Calculation job completed | Every guard has a computed payslip preview; exceptions listed | Payroll |
| `Pending` (Reviewed) | Reviewer signs off exceptions | Variance report accepted; attendance locked | Agency HR / Ops Manager |
| `Verified` (Approved) | Approver approves within limit | Run immutable; ledger accrual posted | Agency Finance / Owner |
| `Active` (Disbursing) | Disbursement initiated | Payment file/API submitted; per-guard status tracked | Payments operator |
| `Completed` (Reconciled) | All lines confirmed or handled | Bank confirmations matched; failures resolved | Finance |
| `Cancelled` | Cancelled before approval only | No ledger effect | Payroll |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-120 | A payroll run shall snapshot all inputs at calculation time — attendance records, rate cards, statutory configuration version, allowance/deduction rules, advance schedules — and store the snapshot with the run, so the run can be recomputed identically at any future date. |
| SUR-FIN-121 | Two payroll runs shall never cover the same guard for the same period. Overlap shall be prevented by a unique constraint on `(tenant_id, guard_id, period)` across non-cancelled runs. |
| SUR-FIN-122 | Calculation shall produce a **variance report** against the previous period per guard: gross change, net change, and the reason bucket (attendance change, rate change, new allowance, new deduction, advance recovery). Any guard with a variance beyond a configurable band (default ±20%) must be explicitly acknowledged before review can complete. |
| SUR-FIN-123 | Zero-pay and negative-net cases shall be blocking exceptions, never silently disbursed as zero. A negative net (deductions exceed earnings) shall cap deductions at the configured floor and carry the remainder forward, with the carry-forward visible on the payslip. |

#### 35.6.2 Attendance-driven wage calculation

| Input | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Present days / shifts | Frozen attendance (§35.4.2) | Only `Verified` attendance counts |
| Shift hours | Shift definition + actual check-in/out | Short shifts handled per the configured policy |
| Overtime hours | Actual hours beyond the configured threshold, approved | Unapproved OT is reported, not auto-paid |
| Weekly off / holiday work | Roster + holiday calendar | Configured multiplier |
| Night shift count | Shift attribute | Configured allowance |
| Leave (paid/unpaid) | Leave module | Paid leave counts as present at base rate |
| Absence | Attendance | Unpaid unless a configured policy says otherwise |
| Allowances | Guard's compensation profile | Fixed or per-occurrence |
| Deductions | Advances, recoveries, statutory configuration | Each with a source document |

#### 35.6.3 Compensation profile

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `wage_basis` | `monthly` \| `daily` \| `hourly` \| `per_shift` |
| `base_rate_minor` | The rate for the basis |
| `attendance_divisor` | For monthly basis: `calendar_days` \| `fixed_26` \| `fixed_30` \| `working_days` — the single most disputed parameter in Indian guarding payroll, therefore explicit and per-contract |
| `ot_multiplier_bp` | Basis points applied to the derived hourly rate |
| `holiday_multiplier_bp` | As above for holiday/weekly-off work |
| `allowance_set_id` | Versioned set of allowance rules |
| `statutory_profile_id` | Versioned configured statutory parameter set |
| `payout_method` | `bank_transfer` \| `upi` \| `cash_acknowledged` |

#### 35.6.4 Worked payroll example

Guard: Ramesh K., unarmed, Site "Vardhman Industrial Park", period 1–30 June.

| Item | Basis | Computation | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base wage | Daily ₹700, 26 days present | 26 × 700 | ₹18,200.00 (1,820,000) |
| Overtime | 12 hours at 150% of hourly | hourly = 700 ÷ 8 = ₹87.50 → OT rate ₹131.25 → 12 × 131.25 | ₹1,575.00 (157,500) |
| Night allowance | 10 nights × ₹50 | 10 × 50 | ₹500.00 (50,000) |
| Uniform/kit allowance | Fixed monthly | — | ₹200.00 (20,000) |
| **Gross earnings** | | 18,200 + 1,575 + 500 + 200 | **₹20,475.00 (2,047,500)** |
| Retirement contribution (employee) | Configured 1200 bp on the configured wage ceiling ₹15,000 | 15,000 × 0.12 | ₹1,800.00 (180,000) |
| Insurance contribution (employee) | Configured 75 bp on gross | 20,475 × 0.0075 = 153.5625 → half-up | ₹154.00 (15,400) |
| Professional tax | Configured slab for the state | flat | ₹200.00 (20,000) |
| Advance recovery | Instalment 2 of 5 | per schedule | ₹1,000.00 (100,000) |
| **Total deductions** | | 1,800 + 154 + 200 + 1,000 | **₹3,154.00 (315,400)** |
| **Net pay** | | 20,475 − 3,154 | **₹17,321.00 (1,732,100)** |

Employer-side configured contributions (cost, not deduction): retirement 1200 bp on ₹15,000 = ₹1,800.00 (180,000); insurance 325 bp on gross = 20,475 × 0.0325 = 665.4375 → ₹665.00 (66,500). **Total employer cost = ₹22,940.00 (2,294,000)**, which is exactly the debit total of the accrual in §35.2.4 example 7. ✓

Every number above is produced by a versioned rule; none is hard-coded. Rates, ceilings, percentages, slabs and rounding are all fields in the configured statutory profile.

#### 35.6.5 Overtime, allowances and deductions

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-124 | Overtime shall be payable only from approved OT records; the platform shall show unapproved OT hours as a separate figure so that unpaid worked hours are visible rather than invisible. |
| SUR-FIN-125 | Allowance rules shall support fixed monthly, per-occurrence (per night shift, per outstation day), per-kilometre, and conditional (only if attendance ≥ N days) forms, each versioned and each traceable on the payslip to its rule. |
| SUR-FIN-126 | Deductions shall be limited by a configurable maximum percentage of net pay per period; a deduction that would breach the cap shall be partially applied and the remainder carried forward automatically. |
| SUR-FIN-127 | Every deduction shall have a source document visible to the guard: advance agreement, damage acknowledgement, statutory rule reference, or leave record. A deduction with no source shall be impossible to create. |

#### 35.6.6 Advances

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-128 | A salary advance shall be a workflow: request (guard or supervisor) → eligibility check (tenure, existing advances, cap as a percentage of monthly earnings) → approval → disbursement → repayment schedule → recovery through payroll. |
| SUR-FIN-129 | Advance disbursement shall post Dr `ADV_GUARD` / Cr `BANK_*`; recovery posts Cr `ADV_GUARD` inside the payroll accrual (as in example 7). The guard's outstanding advance balance shall always equal the sub-ledger balance. |
| SUR-FIN-130 | On separation, outstanding advances shall appear on the full-and-final statement; any unrecovered balance shall be an explicit write-off decision with approval, never a silent adjustment. |

#### 35.6.7 Statutory components — configurable records, not advice

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-131 | All statutory components (retirement fund, insurance contribution, professional tax, employee tax withholding, labour welfare fund, bonus, gratuity accrual) shall be implemented as **configurable parameter sets**: applicability flag, wage base definition, ceiling, employee rate, employer rate, rounding rule, deposit due day, return period, identifier fields, and effective date range. |
| SUR-FIN-132 | No statutory rate, threshold, slab or due date shall be hard-coded in application logic. Changing a rate shall be a configuration change with an effective date, an approver and an audit record — never a code release. |
| SUR-FIN-133 | Every statutory screen, payslip, register and export shall carry the standing notice: **"Suraksha maintains records and performs computations according to the parameters configured by your organisation. It does not provide legal, tax or statutory advice, and does not determine applicability. Your organisation is responsible for the correctness of configured parameters and for statutory filings."** |
| SUR-FIN-134 | The platform shall support jurisdiction-scoped profiles (per state, per establishment), because the same agency may operate under different configured parameters in different states, and shall resolve the profile from the guard's deployment state per a configurable resolution rule. |
| SUR-FIN-135 | Statutory outputs shall be generated as **data exports in configurable layouts** (fixed-width or delimited, layout defined as a template), not as hard-coded government file formats, so that a format change is a template edit. Suraksha shall not claim that any export is certified as compliant with any authority's specification. |
| SUR-FIN-136 | Identifier fields (member/registration/enrolment numbers, tax identifiers) shall be stored encrypted, masked in the UI by default, unmasked only with a permission and an audit entry (see §38, §39). |

#### 35.6.8 Payslips

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-137 | A payslip shall be generated for every guard in an approved run, in the guard's preferred language where a translation exists, showing period, days worked, each earning line with its computation, each deduction with its source, net pay, payout method and payment status. |
| SUR-FIN-138 | Payslips shall be viewable and downloadable in the Guard App (§18) offline after first download, and shall be delivered per §36 event `PAY-15`. |
| SUR-FIN-139 | A payslip shall carry a verification code allowing a third party (e.g. a bank assessing a loan) to verify authenticity via a public endpoint that returns only "valid / issued on / by which agency / net amount", with no other personal data. |
| SUR-FIN-140 | A reissued payslip (after an authorised restatement) shall be clearly marked `Revised` with the revision number and the reason, and the superseded version shall remain accessible. |

#### 35.6.9 Disbursement, failures, and the post-approval rule

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-141 | Disbursement shall support both a **bank bulk file** (configurable layout per bank, generated, checksum-verified, downloaded by an authorised operator over an audited channel) and a **payout API** where procured. The rail choice is D-142 (raised in §25) and is per-tenant configuration. |
| SUR-FIN-142 | Every disbursement line shall carry a unique transaction reference; the response file/API callback shall be ingested and matched line by line, with statuses `Pending`, `Completed`, `Failed`, `Returned`. |
| SUR-FIN-143 | Failed lines shall be grouped by normalised reason (invalid account, name mismatch, account closed, limit exceeded, bank unavailable) with a bulk remediation flow: correct beneficiary (dual-approved) → re-verify → re-issue as a **new** disbursement instruction, never by editing the original. |
| SUR-FIN-144 | A returned payment (money came back) shall post Dr `BANK_*` / Cr `SALARY_PAYABLE`, restoring the liability, and shall notify the guard and the payroll owner within one working day. |
| SUR-FIN-145 | Cash payouts, where used, shall require a photographed acknowledgement with the guard's confirmation in the Guard App, geotagged, and shall be reported separately with a monthly cash-payout ratio metric per branch as a fraud indicator. |
| SUR-FIN-146 | **An approved payroll run shall never be editable.** There shall be no code path, no admin screen and no support procedure that changes an approved run's figures. The only permitted correction is: (a) an off-cycle supplementary run for underpayment, or (b) a recovery entry in a subsequent run for overpayment, or (c) a full reversal run that reverses every ledger line of the original with reason and dual approval, followed by a fresh run. All three are visible to the affected guard. |
| SUR-FIN-147 | Any attempt to modify an approved run's inputs (attendance for the locked period, compensation profile effective in the locked period) shall be blocked with a message naming the run that locked it, and shall be logged as a control event. |

### 35.7 Invoicing and tax

#### 35.7.1 Numbering and sequence integrity

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-148 | Invoice numbers shall be issued from a **sequence** defined per `(tenant_id, branch_id?, document_type, financial_year, series_code)` with a configurable format template (e.g. `SUR/{branch}/{fy}/{seq:05}`), and shall be strictly monotonic with no gaps. |
| SUR-FIN-149 | Numbers shall be allocated only at the moment of issue, inside the same database transaction as the ledger posting, using a row-locked counter — never pre-allocated to drafts, never generated optimistically in application memory. |
| SUR-FIN-150 | If issue fails after number allocation, the transaction rolls back and the number is not consumed. Where an external system forces a consumed-but-unused number, the platform shall record a `void` document for that number with a reason, so the sequence is explainable rather than gapped. |
| SUR-FIN-151 | Separate sequences shall exist for Tax Invoice, Proforma Invoice, Credit Note, Debit Note, Receipt, Settlement Statement, Payslip and Delivery/Service Annexure. Mixing document types in one sequence shall be impossible. |
| SUR-FIN-152 | A daily sequence-integrity job shall verify continuity per series and raise a P1 exception on any gap or duplicate. |

#### 35.7.2 Tax fields and line structure

Tax is modelled as configurable data. The platform implements a tax engine, not a tax opinion.

| Object | Fields |
|---|---|
| Tax profile | `profile_id`, `jurisdiction`, `registration_number` (encrypted), `registration_type`, `place_of_supply_rule`, `default_rate_set`, `effective_from/to` |
| Tax rate set | `rate_set_id`, list of components (`component_code`, `rate_bp`, `applies_when` expression), `effective_from/to` |
| HSN/SAC classification | `code`, `description`, `default_rate_set_id` — data, editable per tenant |
| Invoice line | `description`, `quantity`, `unit`, `unit_rate_minor`, `taxable_value_minor`, `classification_code`, `rate_set_id`, `tax_components[]` |
| Tax component on a line | `component_code` (e.g. `CGST`, `SGST`, `IGST`, `CESS`), `rate_bp`, `amount_minor` |
| Invoice header tax summary | Per component: taxable value, rate, amount — grouped, for the tax register |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-153 | The split of a tax rate into components (intra-jurisdiction split vs single inter-jurisdiction component) shall be determined by a configured `place_of_supply_rule` comparing the supplier's registered jurisdiction with the recipient's/site's, and the resolved rule and its inputs shall be stored on the invoice for audit. |
| SUR-FIN-154 | Reverse-charge, exempt, zero-rated, composition and non-taxable treatments shall be supported as configured flags on the line with a mandatory reason field, printed on the invoice. |
| SUR-FIN-155 | Tax shall be computed per line and rounded per line (SUR-FIN-026); the header summary shall be the sum of line amounts. The platform shall never derive header tax from the header taxable value. |
| SUR-FIN-156 | Where a tax registration number is captured for a client or agency, the platform shall validate format and checksum locally and, where an external validation service is configured, verify and store the result with a timestamp (A-140 applies). Validation failure shall warn, not block, with an override reason. |
| SUR-FIN-157 | Rounding-off adjustment (to the nearest rupee on the invoice total) shall be an optional configured behaviour, and where used shall appear as an explicit `Rounding Adjustment` line with its own ledger treatment, never absorbed into revenue or tax. |

#### 35.7.3 E-invoice / IRN stance

`[DECISION REQUIRED: D-270]` — whether Suraksha and its tenants must produce e-invoices with an Invoice Reference Number, and via which route (direct portal integration, a GSP/ASP provider, or manual upload) depends on turnover thresholds and the client mix, and the applicability determination is not the platform's to make (A-144 applies).

The architecture is built so the answer is a configuration, not a rebuild:

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-158 | The invoice object shall carry optional fields `irn`, `ack_no`, `ack_date`, `signed_qr_payload`, `einvoice_status` (`not_applicable` \| `pending` \| `generated` \| `cancelled` \| `failed`), and `einvoice_provider_ref`, populated only when the tenant enables e-invoicing. |
| SUR-FIN-159 | The e-invoice adapter shall be a pluggable integration (§37) with at least: generate, cancel-within-window, and fetch-status operations, and a manual-entry fallback where an operator records an IRN obtained outside the platform. |
| SUR-FIN-160 | Where e-invoicing is enabled and generation fails, the invoice shall remain `Issued` in the ledger but shall be flagged `einvoice_failed` with a retry queue and an alert; the platform shall never block revenue recognition on a third-party portal's availability, and shall never silently issue a document the tenant believes is IRN-backed when it is not. |
| SUR-FIN-161 | Cancellation of an e-invoiced document after the provider's cancellation window shall be handled by credit note only, and the UI shall state this rather than offering an action that will fail. |

#### 35.7.4 Invoice states and documents

| State | Meaning | Ledger | Mutable |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Draft` | Generated, under review | No posting | Yes |
| `Pending` | Awaiting internal approval (where configured) | No posting | Limited (approver may reject to Draft) |
| `Issued` (Active) | Number allocated, posted, delivered | Posted | No |
| `In Progress` | Partially settled | — | No |
| `Completed` | Fully settled | — | No |
| `Cancelled` | Cancelled before any settlement, by reversal | Reversal posted | No |
| `Archived` | Retained past its active life | — | No |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-162 | Credit and debit notes shall reference the original invoice, shall not exceed the original's value in aggregate without an override, and shall carry their own reason code from a controlled list. |
| SUR-FIN-163 | Invoice PDFs shall be generated once at issue, stored immutably with a content hash, and served from storage — never re-rendered on demand, because a template change would otherwise silently alter a historical document. |
| SUR-FIN-164 | The PDF template shall be versioned; each invoice records its template version. Regeneration for a historical invoice shall be blocked; where a re-render is unavoidable (lost file), it shall use the recorded template version and be flagged as a regeneration in the audit log. |
| SUR-FIN-165 | Invoice delivery shall be tracked (email delivered/opened where measurable, portal viewed, WhatsApp/SMS link sent) and shown on the invoice record for dispute defence. |

### 35.8 SaaS subscription billing

This governs Trinetra/Agency Portal subscriptions (§19, §20). Plan definitions are canon (Starter ₹5,000 / Professional ₹10,000 / Enterprise "Contact Sales") and shall not be altered by this section.

#### 35.8.1 Plan catalogue and entitlements

| Object | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Plan | Commercial package: code, display name, list price, currency, billing period options, visibility (public/private), status |
| Plan version | Effective-dated pricing and entitlement set; existing subscriptions stay on their version until migrated |
| Entitlement | A named capability with a type: `boolean` (module on/off), `quota` (numeric limit), `tier` (basic/advanced) |
| Subscription | Tenant + plan version + period + status + price overrides (Enterprise) |
| Add-on | Priced extra attached to a subscription (extra guard slab, extra branch, custom integration support) |
| Discount | Percentage or absolute, with duration (once, N periods, forever), approval-gated above a threshold |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-166 | Entitlements shall be data, resolved at runtime through a single entitlement service; no product surface shall check `plan == "Professional"` in code. Feature gating checks an entitlement key. |
| SUR-FIN-167 | Enterprise pricing shall never be rendered publicly (canon §1.4). Enterprise subscriptions shall support negotiated price, custom entitlements, custom billing period and a contract reference, all visible only to the tenant and to authorised Suraksha roles. |
| SUR-FIN-168 | Entitlement changes shall take effect within 60 seconds of a subscription change and shall be push-invalidated to running sessions, so a downgrade does not leave a paid feature accessible. |
| SUR-FIN-169 | Downgrade shall never destroy data. Features beyond the new plan become read-only/export-only with a clear message naming the plan that restores them. |

#### 35.8.2 Proration

Worked example: tenant on Starter (₹5,000/month), upgrading to Professional (₹10,000/month) on day 11 of a 30-day cycle, 20 days remaining.

| Step | Computation | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| Unused Starter credit | 500,000 × 20 ÷ 30 = 333,333.33 → half-up | ₹3,333.33 (333,333) |
| Professional charge for remaining period | 1,000,000 × 20 ÷ 30 = 666,666.67 → half-up | ₹6,666.67 (666,667) |
| Net taxable charge | 666,667 − 333,333 | ₹3,333.34 (333,334) |
| Tax at 1800 bp | 333,334 × 0.18 = 60,000.12 → half-up | ₹600.00 (60,000) |
| **Invoice total** | | **₹3,933.34 (393,334)** |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-170 | Upgrades shall be charged immediately with proration and take effect immediately. Downgrades shall take effect at the next period boundary by default, with no refund of the current period unless a configured policy says otherwise. |
| SUR-FIN-171 | Proration shall be day-based on the actual cycle length, shall show the customer the full arithmetic before confirmation, and shall never produce a charge the customer has not seen. |
| SUR-FIN-172 | Mid-period plan changes shall be limited to a configurable count per period (default 2) to prevent proration churn abuse. |

#### 35.8.3 Open decisions carried by this section

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| Billing period (monthly / annual / both, annual discount) and tax treatment | `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-001]` — reserved in canon; architecture supports monthly and annual with deferred revenue (§35.2.4 example 8) |
| Trial length and model (free trial, card-required, feature-limited) | `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-002]` — architecture supports trial states, trial end reminders, and conversion without data loss |
| Plan usage limits (guards, users, sites, branches per plan) | `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-003]` — architecture implements quota entitlements with soft and hard caps |
| Whether the displayed plan prices are tax-inclusive or exclusive on Trinetra | `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-272]` |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-173 | Quota entitlements shall support a soft cap (warn at 80%, 100%, allow overshoot with a notice) and a hard cap (block creation) per quota, configured per plan, so that a growing agency is never abruptly unable to add the guard who is standing at the gate. Guard-safety-critical actions shall never be blocked by a billing quota. |
| SUR-FIN-174 | Trial subscriptions shall have a defined end date, reminders at T−7/T−3/T−1 days, and a conversion path that preserves all data. Trial expiry shall move the tenant to a read-only state for a configurable grace window before any restriction, never to immediate lockout. |

#### 35.8.4 Failed payment, grace, suspension, reactivation, cancellation

| Stage | Timing (default, configurable) | Tenant experience |
|---|---|---|
| Payment failed | Day 0 | Banner + email + push to Agency Owner/Admin; retry scheduled |
| Retry ladder | Day 2, 5, 9 | Same as B2C ladder (§35.3.6) |
| Grace | Day 0–10 | Full access; increasingly prominent warnings |
| Restricted | Day 11–20 | Write access to non-critical modules removed; attendance, SOS, payroll viewing and export remain available |
| Suspended | Day 21+ | Login allowed; data read-only and exportable; operational writes blocked; guard-safety surfaces (SOS routing, attendance capture on the Guard App) continue for a configurable safety window |
| Cancelled | On request or Day 60 | Subscription ends; export window opens |
| Reactivation | Any time before deletion | Payment of dues restores the previous plan and entitlements within 60 seconds |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-175 | Suspension for non-payment shall never disable safety-critical function for guards in the field. SOS receipt, emergency contact routing and attendance capture shall continue for a configurable safety window (default 30 days) irrespective of billing state. This is a deliberate revenue trade-off. |
| SUR-FIN-176 | On cancellation, the tenant shall have a data-export right: a self-service export of all their data (guards, clients, sites, attendance, invoices, payroll history, documents) in open formats (CSV + JSON + original document files) available for a configurable window (default 90 days), downloadable without contacting support. |
| SUR-FIN-177 | Deletion after the export window shall follow the retention policy in §39, shall be preceded by notifications at 30/7/1 days, and shall be logged. Financial records required for statutory retention shall be retained per the configured retention rule even after tenant deletion, in a segregated archive. |
| SUR-FIN-178 | Reactivation shall restore the prior entitlement set, not the current default plan, and shall not require re-onboarding. |

#### 35.8.5 Revenue recognition basics

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-179 | Subscription revenue shall be recognised rateably over the service period. Amounts billed in advance shall sit in `DEFERRED_SUBS` and be released monthly by a scheduled recognition job. |
| SUR-FIN-180 | Setup fees, migration fees and onboarding fees shall be configurable as either recognised on delivery or deferred over the initial term; the choice shall be recorded per contract. |
| SUR-FIN-181 | Guarding revenue shall be recognised as service is delivered (per period), with unbilled delivered service accrued to `UNBILLED_AR` at period end and reversed on invoice issue. |
| SUR-FIN-182 | The platform shall produce a deferred revenue roll-forward (opening, additions, recognised, refunded, closing) per period, reconciling to the `DEFERRED_SUBS` balance exactly. |

### 35.9 Reconciliation and controls

#### 35.9.1 Gateway reconciliation

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-183 | The gateway settlement report shall be ingested daily and matched three ways: gateway payment ↔ platform payment ↔ ledger posting. Matching keys: gateway payment id (primary), then amount+date+order id (secondary). |
| SUR-FIN-184 | Break categories shall be explicit: `in_gateway_not_in_platform`, `in_platform_not_in_gateway`, `amount_mismatch`, `fee_mismatch`, `refund_mismatch`, `settlement_not_received`. Each has an owner, an SLA and a resolution path. |
| SUR-FIN-185 | Gateway fees shall be posted from the settlement file, not estimated at capture time, and the difference between expected and actual fees shall be reported monthly as `fee_variance`. |
| SUR-FIN-186 | A settlement that does not arrive within the gateway's stated T+n window shall raise a P2 alert automatically. |

#### 35.9.2 Bank reconciliation

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-187 | Bank statements shall be ingested (statement upload, or API where a banking integration is procured) and matched to ledger entries on `BANK_*` accounts by reference, amount and date, with fuzzy matching proposals that a human confirms. |
| SUR-FIN-188 | Unmatched inbound credits shall post to `SUSPENSE_IN` with an identification workflow (match to client by UTR narration, amount, or client claim), and shall be reported daily with ageing. |
| SUR-FIN-189 | Unmatched outbound debits shall post to `SUSPENSE_OUT` and shall be treated as a P1 control exception — money left the bank without a platform instruction. |
| SUR-FIN-190 | A bank reconciliation statement per account per period shall be producible showing book balance, unpresented items, unrecorded items and bank balance, and shall be a prerequisite for period close. |

#### 35.9.3 Ledger integrity checks

| Check | Frequency | Failure severity |
|---|---|---|
| Every transaction balances (Σ Dr = Σ Cr) | On write + hourly sweep | P0 |
| Trial balance nets to zero per tenant | Daily | P0 |
| Sub-ledger totals equal control account balances (AR, AP, wallet, advances) | Daily | P1 |
| Hash chain intact per tenant | Daily | P0 |
| No posting into a `Completed` period | Continuous constraint | P1 |
| Document totals equal their ledger postings | Daily | P1 |
| Invoice sequence continuity | Daily | P1 |
| Wallet balances non-negative | Continuous constraint | P1 |
| Refunds ≤ captured per payment | Continuous constraint | P1 |
| Suspense ageing > 5 working days | Daily | P2 |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-191 | Integrity checks shall run as scheduled jobs with results persisted as `financial_integrity_check` records, visible on a Finance dashboard with green/amber/red state and a history, not merely as log lines. |
| SUR-FIN-192 | A P0 integrity failure shall page the on-call engineer and notify the Finance lead, and shall automatically block new postings for the affected tenant only if the failure indicates corruption (hash chain break, unbalanced transaction), with a documented manual override. |

#### 35.9.4 Daily close

| Step | Owner | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Ingest gateway settlement, resolve breaks | Finance ops | Reconciliation status |
| Ingest bank statement, clear suspense | Finance ops | Bank rec status |
| Run integrity checks | System | Check results |
| Review exception queues | Finance | Zero unowned exceptions |
| Post accruals for the day (unbilled service) | System | Accrual transactions |
| Snapshot balances, sign off | Finance | `daily_close` record with signer and timestamp |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-193 | A daily close record shall be created per tenant per day capturing the trial balance snapshot, exception counts, unresolved breaks and the signing user. Failing to close shall not block operations but shall raise visibility after two consecutive misses. |
| SUR-FIN-194 | Month-end soft close shall lock posting to the period for all roles except Finance; hard close shall lock it for everyone, with reopening requiring Founder/Management approval and creating a P1 audit event. |

#### 35.9.5 Exception queues

| Queue | Source | Default SLA |
|---|---|---|
| Orphan gateway payments | Gateway rec | 4 working hours |
| Unapplied receipts | Allocation | 3 working days |
| Suspense items | Bank rec | 2 working days |
| Failed disbursements | Payroll/settlement | 1 working day |
| Payroll variance beyond band | Payroll calc | Before approval (blocking) |
| Billing vs payroll man-day mismatch | Billing | Before invoice issue (blocking) |
| Duplicate payment detected | Payment | 1 working day |
| Disputes and chargebacks | Gateway | Provider deadline − 2 days |
| Sequence gaps | Integrity check | Same day |
| Credit-limit breaches | Credit control | 2 working days |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-195 | Every exception shall have an owner role, an age, an SLA and an escalation; an exception shall never be closable without a resolution code and, where money changed, a link to the correcting ledger transaction. |

#### 35.9.6 Maker-checker and financial audit trail

| Operation | Maker | Checker | Threshold |
|---|---|---|---|
| Settlement approval | Finance | Finance (different user) / Management | Amount bands (configurable) |
| Payroll run approval | Payroll | Agency Finance / Owner | All runs |
| Refund above threshold | Support/Finance | Finance | Configurable (default ₹25,000) |
| Wallet withdrawal | Finance | Finance (different user) | Configurable (default ₹10,000) |
| Beneficiary create/change | Finance ops | Finance lead | All |
| Credit note / SLA credit | Finance | Finance lead | Configurable (default ₹10,000) |
| Write-off | Finance | Management | All |
| Rate card change | Sales/Ops | Finance | All |
| Statutory config change | Payroll | Agency Finance | All |
| Period reopen | Finance | Management | All |
| Ledger reversal | Finance | Finance lead | Configurable |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-196 | The financial audit trail shall capture, for every money-relevant action: actor, role, timestamp (server), IP, device, tenant, before/after values for configuration, the resulting ledger transaction, and the approval chain. It shall be append-only and exportable to an Auditor. |
| SUR-FIN-197 | Auditor role shall have read access to all financial data and exports within its scope, and shall have no write capability anywhere in the financial subsystem. |
| SUR-FIN-198 | Impersonation (support acting as a user) shall be blocked from performing any money-moving operation. A support session may view and prepare, never approve or disburse. |

#### 35.9.7 Fraud controls

| Risk | Control |
|---|---|
| Ghost guards on payroll | Biometric/photo attendance evidence, duplicate-identity detection across guards (phone, bank account, identity document hash), new-guard-first-payroll review queue |
| Shared bank accounts | Detect the same account number across multiple guards or agencies; flag for review, allow with a documented reason (families legitimately share accounts) |
| Beneficiary swap before payout | Cooling period, out-of-band verification, notification to all admins, re-verification (SUR-FIN-110) |
| Attendance inflation | Override-rate monitoring per supervisor and branch, geofence anomaly rate, billing vs payroll reconciliation (SUR-FIN-085) |
| Duplicate/edited invoices | Immutable PDFs with content hash, sequence integrity, public verification code |
| Refund abuse | Refund-rate monitoring per client and per agent, maker-checker above threshold, refund-to-alternate-instrument approval |
| Wallet money laundering | Top-up limits, withdrawal identity re-verification, top-up-to-usage ratio monitoring, source-of-funds flag above a configurable threshold |
| Insider price manipulation | Rate card versioning with approval, alerts on rate changes outside a tolerance band, quarterly rate review report |
| Collusive settlement inflation | Segregation of duties, realisation-rate monitoring, random audit sampling of settlement lines against attendance evidence |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-199 | Fraud signals shall be computed as scheduled analytics with configurable thresholds, surfaced in a Finance risk dashboard, and shall never auto-block a payout without human review — a false positive that leaves a guard unpaid is itself a serious harm. |
| SUR-FIN-200 | A random-sample audit function shall select a configurable percentage of settlement lines, payroll lines and invoice lines per month for evidence verification, with results tracked as a control-effectiveness metric. |

### 35.10 Financial reporting

All reports are tenant-scoped, branch-filterable, date-ranged, exportable to CSV/XLSX/PDF, and reproducible — running the same report with the same `as_of` date must give the same numbers, which requires reporting from ledger entries and effective dates, never from mutable current-state fields.

#### 35.10.1 Receivables and collections

| Report | Key columns | Formula / definition |
|---|---|---|
| Receivables ageing | Client, contract, invoice, due date, Current/1–30/31–60/61–90/91–180/180+ | Bucket by `today − due_date`; amount = invoice total − allocations |
| Ageing summary by owner | Account owner, total open, % > 60 days, oldest item | Aggregation of the above |
| Collections | Period, opening AR, invoiced, collected, credit notes, written off, closing AR | Closing = Opening + Invoiced − Collected − Credits − Write-offs |
| Collection efficiency | Period, DSO, CEI | DSO = (Closing AR ÷ Credit sales in period) × days in period; CEI = (Opening AR + Invoiced − Closing AR) ÷ (Opening AR + Invoiced − Closing current AR) × 100 |
| Unapplied receipts | Client, amount, received date, age | Payments with allocation < payment amount |
| Dispute register | Client, invoice, disputed amount, reason, age, owner | Open disputes with SLA status |

#### 35.10.2 Revenue and profitability

| Report | Key columns | Formula / definition |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue by product | Period, guarding, event, SaaS, commission, other | Sum of income accounts by role key |
| Revenue by branch/city | Branch, revenue, cost of service, gross margin, GM% | GM = Revenue − (COS_WAGES + COS_AGENCY + COS_KIT); GM% = GM ÷ Revenue |
| Revenue by client | Client, revenue, cost, margin, share of total | As above, party-scoped |
| Site profitability | Site, billed value, guard cost, agency cost, margin, margin per man-day | Margin ÷ approved man-days |
| Unbilled revenue | Site, delivered man-days, unbilled value, age | `UNBILLED_AR` balance with detail |
| Contract value | Contract, monthly recurring value, annualised, escalation date | Sum of active contract line values |

#### 35.10.3 Payouts and settlements

| Report | Key columns | Formula / definition |
|---|---|---|
| Payout register | Run, guard, gross, deductions, net, method, status, reference | Per payroll run, exportable for bank/audit |
| Payroll cost summary | Branch, gross wages, employer contributions, total cost, headcount, cost per man-day | Total cost ÷ approved man-days |
| Statutory register (configured) | Component, wage base, employee amount, employer amount, count, due date | Per configured component; export layouts per SUR-FIN-135 |
| Settlement statement | Agency, cycle, gross, deductions, holds, net, status | Per §35.5.4 |
| Settlement ageing | Agency, held amount, hold reason, age | Held balances beyond SLA |
| Advance register | Guard/agency, sanctioned, recovered, outstanding, next instalment | Sub-ledger balances |

#### 35.10.4 Tax registers (configured)

| Report | Content |
|---|---|
| Output tax register | Every issued invoice/debit note: number, date, party, registration number, place of supply, taxable value, per-component tax, total |
| Credit note register | Every credit note with its original document reference and reason |
| Input tax register | Purchase/expense documents with input tax captured (gateway fees, vendor bills) |
| Withholding register | Party, gross, configured rate, withheld amount, deposit due date, certificate reference |
| Reconciliation summary | Output tax per register vs `TAX_OUTPUT` ledger balance vs amounts deposited |

Each carries the SUR-FIN-133 notice.

#### 35.10.5 SaaS metrics

| Metric | Formula |
|---|---|
| MRR | Σ (normalised monthly recurring value of Active subscriptions), where annual plans contribute `annual_value ÷ 12` |
| New MRR | MRR from subscriptions that became Active in the period |
| Expansion MRR | Increase in MRR from upgrades and add-ons on existing subscriptions |
| Contraction MRR | Decrease from downgrades and removed add-ons |
| Churned MRR | MRR lost from subscriptions cancelled or suspended past the recovery window |
| Net MRR movement | New + Expansion − Contraction − Churned |
| ARR | MRR × 12 |
| Logo churn % | Cancelled tenants in period ÷ Active tenants at period start × 100 |
| Revenue churn % | Churned MRR ÷ MRR at period start × 100 |
| Net revenue retention % | (Start MRR + Expansion − Contraction − Churn) ÷ Start MRR × 100 |
| ARPA | MRR ÷ Active tenants |
| Collection rate | Collected ÷ Invoiced in the period |
| Deferred revenue balance | `DEFERRED_SUBS` closing balance |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-FIN-201 | Every metric shall have exactly one implementation in the reporting layer with its formula documented in the UI on hover, so that Sales, Finance and Management never argue about which MRR is correct. |
| SUR-FIN-202 | Metrics shall be snapshotted monthly into an immutable `financial_metric_snapshot` table; historical values shall never be recomputed silently when a definition changes — a definition change creates a new metric version. |
| SUR-FIN-203 | All financial reports shall be schedulable (daily/weekly/monthly) with delivery to configured recipients via §36, with the report parameters and the generating user recorded. |
