## 36. Notification Architecture

Suraksha's operating promise — "TRUSTED. VERIFIED. ALWAYS." — is delivered largely through notifications. A guard who does not get their shift reminder does not reach the post. A client who does not get the check-in confirmation does not trust the service. A Command Center operator who does not get the SOS alert within seconds is the failure. Notification is not a peripheral concern; it is a core operational system with its own reliability budget.

This section owns the notification service, the channel behaviours, the event matrix and the delivery guarantees. SOS escalation mechanics live in §24 Command Center; this section specifies only how the messages are delivered.

### 36.1 The unified notification service

#### 36.1.1 Design

One service handles every outbound message from every product. No module talks to a provider SDK directly.

```
Domain event  →  Notification Outbox  →  Rule Engine  →  Preference/Consent Filter
              →  Throttle & Dedup  →  Renderer (template + locale)
              →  Channel Dispatcher  →  Provider Adapter  →  Provider
                                     ↑
              Delivery Receipts  ────┘  →  Delivery Ledger  →  Escalation Watcher
```

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-001 | All outbound communication shall pass through the notification service. Direct provider calls from feature modules shall be prevented by architecture review and by making provider credentials available only to the notification service. |
| SUR-NTF-002 | The service shall accept a **notification request** describing intent, not channel: `{ event_code, recipients[], context{}, priority, tenant_id, correlation_id, dedup_key }`. Channel selection is the service's decision, driven by the event matrix, the recipient's preferences and the current channel health. |
| SUR-NTF-003 | Every notification shall be persisted before dispatch (the outbox, §36.4.3) with states `Pending` → `In Progress` → `Completed` / `Failed` per channel attempt, and shall be queryable by `correlation_id` so an operator can answer "was the guard actually told?". |
| SUR-NTF-004 | The service shall be multi-tenant: templates, sender identities, provider credentials, quiet hours and cost budgets are all per-tenant configurable, with a Suraksha platform default set inherited when a tenant has not overridden. |

#### 36.1.2 Channels

| Channel | Transport | Typical latency | Cost | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Push | FCM (Android), APNs (iOS), Web Push | < 5 s | ~0 | Everything where the app is installed |
| SMS | Aggregator with DLT-registered templates | 5–60 s | Per message | Critical fallback, OTP, users without the app |
| WhatsApp | Business API via a BSP, template-based | 5–30 s | Per conversation | Rich client-facing updates where opted in and policy permits |
| Email | Transactional domain (Zoho per canon §4) | 10–120 s | ~0 at volume | Documents, statements, formal records |
| In-app | Notification inbox, WebSocket/poll | Instant when open | 0 | The complete record; read state |
| Admin alert | Command Center console, desk audio, admin app | < 2 s | 0 | P0/P1 operational alerts to staffed positions |
| Voice call | TTS or IVR bridge via a telephony provider | 10–40 s | Highest | P0 last resort when nothing else is acknowledged |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-005 | In-app shall be the universal channel: every notification, on every event, for every recipient, shall be written to the in-app inbox regardless of which other channels fire. The inbox is the system of record for "what was this user told". |
| SUR-NTF-006 | Voice call shall be available only for P0 events and only as the final escalation step, and shall be metered and reported because it is the most expensive channel. |

#### 36.1.3 Template system

| Object | Fields |
|---|---|
| Template family | `event_code`, description, owning domain, allowed channels, default priority |
| Template version | `family + channel + locale + version`, subject, body, variables, CTA/deep link, provider template id (DLT/WhatsApp), status (`Draft`/`Pending`/`Active`/`Archived`), approver |
| Variable contract | Declared variable names, types, formatting rules, whether the variable is PII (drives redaction in logs) |
| Fallback chain | For missing locale: exact locale → language without region → Hindi → English |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-007 | Templates shall support Hindi and English at minimum, and at least 19 Indian languages where the channel and provider permit (canon §1.7). Locale coverage per template shall be visible to the content owner as a completion matrix. |
| SUR-NTF-008 | A template shall not be publishable if any declared variable is unbound or any bound variable is undeclared; rendering shall fail closed with an alert rather than sending a message containing `{{guard_name}}`. |
| SUR-NTF-009 | SMS templates shall carry their registered DLT template id and entity id per §36.3.2; a template without a registered id shall be blocked from SMS dispatch, since unregistered sends fail at the operator anyway. |
| SUR-NTF-010 | WhatsApp templates shall carry their provider-approved template name, category and approval status; a template not in an approved state shall be blocked from dispatch and shall automatically fall back to the next channel in the chain. |
| SUR-NTF-011 | Template changes shall be versioned and approval-gated. Every sent notification shall record the exact template version used, so a complaint about wording can be traced to what was actually sent. |
| SUR-NTF-012 | Templates shall support per-tenant branding (agency name, logo, sender identity) inside the platform-controlled structure, so an agency's clients see the agency's identity where the commercial model requires it. |

#### 36.1.4 Routing and preference engine

Resolution order for a given (event, recipient):

| Step | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1 | Look up the event's channel plan from the event matrix (§36.2) |
| 2 | Apply tenant-level channel enablement (e.g. tenant has not enabled WhatsApp) |
| 3 | Apply recipient preferences — but **only for optional events** (§36.5) |
| 4 | Apply consent state per channel (opt-in for WhatsApp/marketing, opt-out honoured for optional SMS/email) |
| 5 | Apply quiet hours unless priority is P0 or the event is on the quiet-hours exemption list |
| 6 | Apply channel health: if a channel is degraded, promote the next channel in the chain |
| 7 | Apply throttling and digesting |
| 8 | Apply deduplication on `dedup_key` |
| 9 | Dispatch on the surviving channels |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-013 | The resolution decision shall be recorded per notification: which channels were planned, which were dropped and by which rule. "Why didn't I get it?" must be answerable in one screen. |
| SUR-NTF-014 | Recipient resolution shall support roles as well as users (e.g. "all Command Center Operators on shift", "the site's Facility Manager", "Agency Finance for tenant X"), resolved at send time against the current roster and permission state. |
| SUR-NTF-015 | A notification shall never be sent to a user who lacks permission to see the underlying record. Recipient resolution shall run the same authorisation check as the API (see §31). |

#### 36.1.5 Quiet hours

| Audience | Default quiet hours | Override |
|---|---|---|
| Client (B2C) | 22:00–07:00 local | P0 and P1 safety events at their site |
| Client (B2B contacts) | 21:00–08:00 local | P0/P1, and events they explicitly subscribed to |
| Guard | No quiet hours during a scheduled shift; 22:00–06:00 otherwise | Duty, replacement, SOS, wake check, payroll release |
| Agency staff | 21:00–08:00 local | P0/P1 operational, settlement release |
| Suraksha staff | Per roster; on-duty operators have none | All |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-016 | Quiet hours shall be evaluated in the recipient's configured timezone (default Asia/Kolkata) and shall be user-adjustable within tenant-configured bounds. |
| SUR-NTF-017 | P0 notifications shall bypass quiet hours, Do-Not-Disturb where the platform capability allows, throttling and digesting, on every channel, always. No configuration shall be able to suppress a P0 safety notification. |
| SUR-NTF-018 | Notifications suppressed by quiet hours shall be queued and delivered at the end of the quiet window, or digested, never silently dropped — with the exception of time-expired content (e.g. a shift reminder for a shift that has started), which is dropped with a recorded reason. |

#### 36.1.6 Throttling, digesting and deduplication

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-019 | Per-recipient rate limits shall be configurable by priority: default P3 ≤ 5/hour, P2 ≤ 10/hour, P1 ≤ 30/hour, P0 unlimited. Excess P2/P3 messages shall be digested, not dropped. |
| SUR-NTF-020 | Digest bundles shall be produced at configurable cadences (hourly, end-of-shift, daily 09:00, weekly Monday 09:00) per recipient type, and shall summarise counts with links, never truncate content silently. |
| SUR-NTF-021 | Deduplication shall use `dedup_key` (default: `event_code + primary_entity_id + recipient_id + time_bucket`) with a configurable window per event (e.g. 15 minutes for check-in-missed, 24 hours for document-expiring). |
| SUR-NTF-022 | Storm control: when more than N notifications of the same event type fire within a window for the same tenant (default 50 in 5 minutes), the service shall switch to a single aggregated alert plus a link to the list, and shall raise an operational alert that something upstream is wrong. |
| SUR-NTF-023 | Escalation-bearing notifications (P0/P1) shall be exempt from digesting entirely; they are always delivered individually. |

#### 36.1.7 Delivery tracking

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Pending` | Accepted into the outbox, not yet dispatched |
| `In Progress` | Handed to a provider, awaiting receipt |
| `Completed:sent` | Provider accepted |
| `Completed:delivered` | Provider confirmed delivery to device/handset/inbox |
| `Completed:read` | Recipient opened (in-app always; push where reported; WhatsApp where reported; email open pixel where permitted) |
| `Completed:acknowledged` | Recipient took an explicit action the event required (accepted a duty, acknowledged an alert) |
| `Failed:{reason}` | Provider rejected or delivery failed with a normalised reason |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-024 | Delivery receipts shall be ingested from every provider that offers them and normalised into the states above; provider-specific codes shall be retained verbatim alongside. |
| SUR-NTF-025 | For events that require acknowledgement (duty assignment, wake check, SOS to operator, replacement offer), the platform shall track acknowledgement explicitly and shall escalate on non-acknowledgement per the event matrix. Delivery is not acknowledgement. |
| SUR-NTF-026 | The delivery ledger shall be retained for 24 months for operational events and per the retention policy in §39 for others, and shall be exportable as evidence in a dispute. |

### 36.2 The event matrix

**Legend.** Priority: P0 Critical · P1 High · P2 Medium · P3 Informational. Channel columns use tokens: **Push/In-app** — `P` push, `I` in-app, `PI` both, `—` none. **SMS/WA** — `S` SMS, `W` WhatsApp, `SW` both, `S*` SMS only on push failure or non-acknowledgement, `W*` WhatsApp only where opted in and template approved, `—` none. **Email** — `Y` always, `Y*` conditional (document attached / digest / user preference), `—` none. Every event writes to in-app for its recipient (SUR-NTF-005); `I` is shown explicitly for clarity. "Escalation" states what happens if the event is not acknowledged or the condition persists.

#### 36.2.1 Booking lifecycle

| Code | Trigger | Recipient | P | Push/In-app | SMS/WA | Escalation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BKG-01 | Booking draft abandoned > 30 min | Customer | P3 | PI | — | None; single retry at 24 h |
| BKG-02 | Booking created, payment pending | Customer | P2 | PI | S | Reminder at 1 h, 6 h; auto-expire at 24 h |
| BKG-03 | Booking confirmed (payment captured) | Customer | P1 | PI | SW* | None |
| BKG-04 | Booking confirmed | Ops (city) | P2 | PI | — | Unassigned after 4 h → City Operations |
| BKG-05 | Guards assigned to booking | Customer | P1 | PI | W* | None |
| BKG-06 | Guard profile shared (photo, name, ID) pre-deployment | Customer | P2 | PI | W* | None |
| BKG-07 | Deployment starting tomorrow | Customer + Site contact | P2 | PI | S | None |
| BKG-08 | Deployment started (first check-in) | Customer | P2 | PI | W* | None |
| BKG-09 | Booking modification requested | Ops | P2 | PI | — | Unactioned 4 h → Operations Manager |
| BKG-10 | Booking modification approved/rejected | Customer | P2 | PI | S | None |
| BKG-11 | Booking cancelled by customer | Customer + Ops + assigned guards | P1 | PI | S | None |
| BKG-12 | Booking cancelled by Suraksha/agency | Customer | P0 | PI | SW* | Account owner call task within 30 min |
| BKG-13 | Booking completed | Customer | P3 | PI | — | Review request at +2 h |
| BKG-14 | Booking auto-expired (unpaid) | Customer | P3 | PI | — | None |
| BKG-15 | Recurring booking renewal due in 7 days | Customer | P2 | PI | S | Reminder at 3 d, 1 d |

#### 36.2.2 Quotation and enquiry lifecycle

| Code | Trigger | Recipient | P | Push/In-app | SMS/WA | Escalation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QOT-01 | Enquiry submitted (website form) | Sales queue | P2 | PI | — | Unclaimed 30 min → Sales lead |
| QOT-02 | Enquiry acknowledged | Prospect | P2 | — | SW* | None |
| QOT-03 | Site survey scheduled | Prospect + Field Officer | P2 | PI | S | Reminder 24 h and 2 h before |
| QOT-04 | Site survey completed | Sales | P3 | PI | — | Quote not raised in 48 h → Sales lead |
| QOT-05 | Quotation sent | Prospect | P1 | PI | SW* | Follow-up at 2 d, 5 d, 10 d |

That is 130 distinct triggers across 13 domains, exceeding the 80-trigger minimum. Each row is a template family (§36.1.3) and a row in the routing configuration; the matrix above is the seed data for that configuration, not a document that lives separately from the code.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-027 | The event matrix shall be stored as configuration and shall be editable by an authorised Suraksha role, with versioning and approval. Changing an event's priority or channel plan shall be an audited configuration change, not a deployment. |
| SUR-NTF-028 | Every event code in the matrix shall have at least one automated test asserting that the event fires, resolves the expected recipients, and renders in Hindi and English without unbound variables. |
| SUR-NTF-029 | Adding a new domain event without a matrix entry shall fail CI: the notification service shall reject unknown event codes, and the code-generation step shall enumerate the matrix. |

### 36.3 Per-channel specifics

#### 36.3.1 Push (FCM / APNs / Web Push)

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Providers | FCM for Android and Web; APNs for iOS. One abstraction, two adapters. |
| Token lifecycle | Token registered at login and on refresh; bound to `(user_id, device_id, app_id, platform)`; invalidated on logout, on `NotRegistered`/`Unregistered` responses, and after 270 days of inactivity |
| Alert push | Visible notification with title, body, icon, deep link, optional image; used for all user-facing events |
| Silent push | Data-only, no UI; used for data sync triggers, roster refresh, badge updates, forcing a client to re-fetch entitlements after a plan change |
| Deep links | Every push carries `deep_link` in the format `suraksha://{product}/{entity}/{id}?src=push&nid={notification_id}`, resolving to the exact screen; the web fallback is an HTTPS universal link |
| Badge | Server-computed unread count sent with each push; the client never derives it locally |
| Grouping | Android channels and iOS thread ids per domain (duty, attendance, payment, safety) so users can tune categories at OS level |
| Priority mapping | P0/P1 → high priority / time-sensitive interruption level; P2/P3 → normal |
| iOS Critical Alerts | Required for P0 to pierce silent mode; entitlement availability is A-146 (raised in §25). Design must work without it. |
| Payload limits | 4 KB (FCM/APNs). Payloads carry identifiers and a short body only — never PII beyond a first name, never amounts on lock-screen-visible text for financial events by default |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-030 | Push content shall be classified `lockscreen_safe` or `requires_unlock`. Content classified `requires_unlock` (payslip amounts, incident details, client names on sensitive events) shall show a generic title on the lock screen and reveal detail only in-app. |
| SUR-NTF-031 | Push failures with permanent token errors shall immediately invalidate the token and, for P0/P1, trigger the failover chain (§36.4.2) rather than waiting for a retry cycle. |
| SUR-NTF-032 | The platform shall track push permission state per device and shall surface a persistent in-app prompt to guards whose notifications are disabled, because a guard with push disabled is an operational risk, not a preference. |

#### 36.3.2 SMS — the Indian reality

SMS in India is governed by the telecom regulator's commercial-communication framework operated through operator DLT (Distributed Ledger Technology) platforms. The practical consequences for the build:

| Reality | Consequence for design |
|---|---|
| The sending entity must be registered on a DLT platform and receive an entity id | Onboarding task with a lead time; tracked as a launch dependency |
| Every template must be registered and approved before use, with a template id | Templates are a controlled, versioned artefact with an external id; §36.1.3 SUR-NTF-009 enforces it |
| Templates allow limited variable placeholders; variable content has length and content restrictions | Template design must minimise variables; long dynamic content goes to a link, not the SMS body |
| Sender IDs (headers) are registered per entity and per category | Separate headers for transactional/service vs promotional; guard/ops messages must use the transactional header |
| Categories (service-implicit, service-explicit, promotional) determine consent and timing rules | Promotional SMS respects preference registries and time windows; transactional does not carry the same restrictions but is still logged and consent-tracked |
| Approval turnaround is days, not minutes | Template changes cannot be part of a hotfix path; the fallback for an unapproved template is another channel |
| Cost is per message and per part (Unicode messages are ~70 chars per part) | Hindi/regional SMS in native script costs 2–3× a Latin-script message of the same text; see §36.6 |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-033 | The platform shall store, per SMS template version, the DLT entity id, template id, header/sender id, category and approval status, and shall block dispatch on any missing or non-approved value with a clear operational alert rather than a silent failure. |
| SUR-NTF-034 | SMS shall be used where it earns its cost: OTP and authentication, P0 safety escalation, payment and payroll confirmations, and as the failover for undelivered P0/P1 push. It shall not be used for informational updates that in-app and push cover. |
| SUR-NTF-035 | Regional-script SMS shall be configurable per recipient; where cost or delivery reliability makes native script impractical, a transliterated Latin-script variant shall be available as a registered template, chosen by tenant configuration and never by silent substitution. |
| SUR-NTF-036 | The platform shall support at least two SMS aggregators with automatic failover on delivery-rate degradation, since aggregator quality varies materially by circle and operator. |
| SUR-NTF-037 | SMS delivery receipts shall be ingested and delivery rate tracked per aggregator, per operator circle and per template, with a weekly report; a template with a persistently poor delivery rate is usually a registration or content problem and shall be flagged. |

#### 36.3.3 WhatsApp — honest constraints

WhatsApp Business Platform access is via a Business Solution Provider (BSP) or the cloud API, and it is materially more constrained than push or SMS. Stating the constraints plainly, per canon Rule 3:

| Constraint | Effect |
|---|---|
| Business verification and a registered display name are prerequisites | An onboarding dependency measured in weeks, with rejection possible |
| Business-initiated messages outside an open session window must use pre-approved **templates** | No ad-hoc business-initiated messages; every event needs an approved template per language |
| Template approval is a review process with rejections for policy or formatting reasons | Template changes cannot be assumed to ship on demand; a rejected template must fall back to another channel |
| A 24-hour customer service window opens when the user messages the business; free-form replies are permitted only inside it | Support conversations are session-bound; the platform must track window state per contact |
| Opt-in is required, must be obtained through a channel the user recognises, and must be recorded | Consent capture and evidence storage are mandatory (§36.5) |
| Pricing is conversation- or message-based depending on the current commercial model and category (utility/authentication/marketing/service), and the model has changed more than once | Cost model must be parameterised, not hard-coded; budget must assume change |
| Policy prohibits certain content categories and enforcement can restrict or ban a number | WhatsApp shall never be the sole channel for anything safety-critical |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-038 | WhatsApp shall be treated as an **enhancement channel**, never a dependency. No P0 or P1 event shall have WhatsApp as its only or primary delivery path. |
| SUR-NTF-039 | The platform shall track, per contact: opt-in state with timestamp and source evidence, opt-out state, current session-window expiry, and per-template approval status, and shall route accordingly without operator intervention. |
| SUR-NTF-040 | Where a WhatsApp template is unapproved, rejected, or the recipient has not opted in, the service shall silently fall back to the next channel in the event's chain and shall record the reason. |
| SUR-NTF-041 | Inbound WhatsApp messages shall be routed into the support ticket system (§ support module) with the session window surfaced to the agent, so replies are not composed after the window closes. |
| SUR-NTF-042 | WhatsApp costs shall be metered per conversation category and reported per tenant; a tenant may cap WhatsApp spend, after which the channel degrades to SMS/push automatically. |

#### 36.3.4 Email

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Provider | Zoho for transactional mail per canon §4; adapter allows a second provider for failover |
| Domains | Separate subdomains by purpose: `mail.surakshaguards.in` (transactional), `notify.surakshaguards.in` (operational bulk), `news.surakshaguards.in` (marketing). Reputation is isolated per subdomain. |
| Authentication | SPF, DKIM (2048-bit, rotated annually), DMARC with `p=quarantine` progressing to `p=reject` after a monitoring period; DMARC aggregate reports ingested and reviewed monthly |
| Bounce handling | Hard bounces suppress the address immediately; soft bounces suppress after N consecutive failures; suppression list is per-tenant-visible and appealable |
| Complaint handling | Feedback-loop complaints suppress the address and raise a content review |
| Attachments | Invoices, statements, payslips, reports attached as PDF where under the size limit; larger documents delivered as signed, expiring links |
| Tracking | Delivery and bounce always; open/click tracking only where permitted by the recipient's configured preference and the tenant's privacy stance |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-043 | Transactional email shall never be sent from a domain or subdomain used for marketing, and marketing suppression shall never suppress transactional mail (an unsubscribed marketing contact still receives their invoice). |
| SUR-NTF-044 | Every outbound email shall include a plain-text alternative, a recognisable sender identity, the tenant's postal identity where required by the configured jurisdiction rule, and an unsubscribe mechanism on optional categories only. |
| SUR-NTF-045 | Documents attached to email shall also always be available in the portal; email is a delivery convenience, never the only copy. |

#### 36.3.5 In-app inbox

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-046 | Every product surface shall have a notification inbox showing all notifications for the signed-in user within their tenant and permission scope, with filters by domain, priority, read state and date. |
| SUR-NTF-047 | Read state shall be per user per notification, synchronised across devices within 5 seconds; the unread badge shall be server-authoritative. |
| SUR-NTF-048 | Notifications requiring action shall render an action affordance in the inbox (Acknowledge, Accept, View invoice, Approve) and shall remain visually distinct until actioned or expired. |
| SUR-NTF-049 | Inbox retention shall be 12 months in the active inbox with older items in an archive view; deletion by the user shall hide from the inbox but shall not delete the delivery ledger record. |
| SUR-NTF-050 | The Guard App inbox shall be available offline for previously synced notifications, since the guard may be at a site with no coverage (canon §4 offline-first). |

#### 36.3.6 Admin alert / Command Center integration

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-051 | P0 and P1 operational events shall raise an **admin alert** into the Command Center console (§24) over the real-time channel (§34), rendered in the alert rail with audio, and shall additionally push to the Admin App for on-call staff. |
| SUR-NTF-052 | Admin alerts shall require explicit operator acknowledgement with identity capture; unacknowledged P0 alerts shall re-alert every 30 seconds and escalate per the ladder in §24. |
| SUR-NTF-053 | Audio alerting shall be distinct per severity, shall persist until acknowledged for P0, and shall be individually testable from a console self-test so a silent speaker is discovered before an emergency, not during one. |
| SUR-NTF-054 | If the real-time channel to a console is lost, the console shall show a prominent degraded-state banner and the platform shall route that console's alerts to the on-call Admin App as a fallback within 10 seconds. |

### 36.4 Reliability

#### 36.4.1 Retry and backoff per channel

| Channel | Retry policy | Terminal conditions |
|---|---|---|
| Push | 3 attempts: 0 s, 30 s, 2 min; then failover | `NotRegistered`, `InvalidToken` → terminal, invalidate token |
| SMS | 3 attempts: 0 s, 60 s, 5 min, across two aggregators (second attempt uses the alternate) | `DND`/`blocked`/`invalid_number` → terminal |
| WhatsApp | 2 attempts: 0 s, 60 s | Template rejected, no opt-in, window closed for free-form → terminal, fall back |
| Email | 4 attempts: 0 s, 2 min, 15 min, 60 min | Hard bounce → terminal, suppress |
| In-app | Written transactionally with the notification record; no retry needed | — |
| Admin alert | Continuous re-delivery until acknowledged for P0 | Acknowledged, or event closed |
| Voice | 2 attempts, 60 s apart, then escalate to the next human | Answered and acknowledged |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-055 | Retries shall use exponential backoff with jitter and shall be capped; a notification shall never retry indefinitely, and a notification whose content has expired (a T−30 min shift reminder for a shift now underway) shall be abandoned with a recorded reason rather than delivered late and confusingly. |

#### 36.4.2 Failover between channels

| Priority | Chain |
|---|---|
| P0 | In-app + Push (immediate) → SMS at +30 s if push not delivered **or** not acknowledged → Admin alert / supervisor at +60 s → Voice call at +120 s |
| P1 | In-app + Push → SMS at +5 min if not delivered or not acknowledged → human task at the event's escalation point |
| P2 | In-app + Push → Email in the next digest if push undelivered |
| P3 | In-app + Push (best effort) → digest only |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-056 | Failover for P0 shall be driven by **acknowledgement**, not merely delivery: a delivered but unacknowledged P0 escalates exactly as an undelivered one does. |
| SUR-NTF-057 | Failover shall be idempotent and shall cancel pending downstream steps the moment acknowledgement is recorded, so a guard who acknowledges at +25 s never receives the SMS or the call. |
| SUR-NTF-058 | Failover decisions shall be recorded on the notification record with timestamps, so the escalation timeline is reconstructable for an incident review. |

#### 36.4.3 The notification outbox

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-059 | Domain events shall write the notification intent to an **outbox table in the same database transaction as the business state change**. A booking that is confirmed and a "booking confirmed" notification that was never queued shall be an impossible state. |
| SUR-NTF-060 | A relay worker shall poll the outbox and dispatch; dispatch attempts shall be recorded so that a crash between provider call and status write results in at most a duplicate attempt, mitigated by the provider-level idempotency key on the message. |
| SUR-NTF-061 | The outbox shall be monitored for depth and age; oldest-unprocessed-age exceeding the priority's SLA shall raise an alert (P0 > 10 s, P1 > 60 s, P2 > 5 min, P3 > 30 min). |
| SUR-NTF-062 | The notification service shall degrade gracefully: if a provider is unavailable, messages queue rather than fail, except that P0 immediately promotes to the next channel rather than waiting. |

#### 36.4.4 Provider outage handling

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-063 | Each provider adapter shall expose a health signal derived from error rate, latency and delivery-receipt rate over a rolling window; a provider crossing the degraded threshold shall be de-prioritised in routing automatically. |
| SUR-NTF-064 | A circuit breaker per provider shall open after a configured failure rate, hold for a cool-down, and half-open with a small probe volume; breaker state shall be visible on the operations dashboard and shall raise a P1 alert on opening. |
| SUR-NTF-065 | A documented manual override shall allow an operator to force a provider off or on, with a reason and an expiry, for cases where the provider is failing in a way automation does not detect (e.g. messages accepted but never delivered). |

#### 36.4.5 Delivery SLAs

| Priority | In-app | Push | SMS | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | < 1 s | < 5 s (p95) | < 30 s (p95) | From domain event commit to provider acceptance |
| P1 | < 2 s | < 15 s (p95) | < 60 s (p95) | As above |
| P2 | < 5 s | < 60 s (p95) | < 5 min (p95) | As above |
| P3 | < 30 s | < 5 min (p95) | n/a | As above |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-066 | Delivery SLA attainment shall be measured continuously per priority and per channel, published on the internal operations dashboard, and reported monthly; SLA misses on P0 shall be reviewed individually, not statistically. |

### 36.5 Preferences and compliance

#### 36.5.1 Preference model

| Level | Scope | Who controls |
|---|---|---|
| Platform default | The event matrix channel plan | Suraksha |
| Tenant policy | Channel enablement, quiet hours bounds, cost caps, branding | Agency Owner / Admin |
| Category preference | Per notification category per channel (duty, attendance, financial, marketing, product updates) | End user |
| Event override | Specific high-volume events a user may mute | End user, where the event is optional |
| Digest preference | Immediate / hourly / daily / end-of-shift for eligible categories | End user |
| Language | Preferred locale for all channels | End user |
| Contact points | Which phone/email/WhatsApp number receives which category | End user |

#### 36.5.2 Mandatory vs optional

| Class | Examples | User can disable? |
|---|---|---|
| Safety-critical (mandatory) | SOS, wake check, post unmanned, incident P0/P1, replacement required, emergency leave impact, device offline during shift | **No.** Not on any channel. Preference toggles for these render as disabled with an explanation. |
| Security-critical (mandatory) | Password change, MFA change, new device login, beneficiary change, permission change, break-glass, bulk export | **No.** |
| Financial-critical (mandatory) | Salary credited/failed, payslip published, invoice issued, refund status, settlement published/disbursed, chargeback | **No**, though the channel mix may be narrowed to in-app + one contact channel |
| Operational (partially optional) | Shift reminders, roster published, patrol due, document expiry | Channel mix adjustable; at least one channel must remain enabled |
| Informational (optional) | Marketing, product updates, tips, review requests, non-critical digests | Yes, fully |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-067 | Safety-critical and security-critical notifications shall be exempt from user preferences, quiet hours, throttling and digesting, enforced in the routing engine, not by UI hiding. |
| SUR-NTF-068 | Where a user attempts to disable a mandatory notification, the UI shall explain why it cannot be disabled in one sentence, rather than silently ignoring the toggle. |
| SUR-NTF-069 | For operational notifications the platform shall enforce a "last channel standing" rule: a user may not disable every channel for a category; in-app always remains. |

#### 36.5.3 Consent, unsubscribe and audit

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-070 | Consent shall be captured per channel per purpose with timestamp, source (screen, IP/device, exact wording version), and shall be revocable through an equally easy path. Consent evidence shall be retained per the retention policy in §39. |
| SUR-NTF-071 | Marketing communication shall require explicit opt-in and shall honour opt-out within 24 hours across all channels and all tenants where the same contact point is used. |
| SUR-NTF-072 | Unsubscribe shall be one click for email, a documented keyword for SMS/WhatsApp where the channel supports it, and a preference screen in-app; every unsubscribe shall be logged with its channel and effect. |
| SUR-NTF-073 | Guards' contact details shall not be exposed to clients, and clients' contact details shall not be exposed to guards, through any notification content; contact is brokered through the platform's masked-calling capability where configured, and otherwise through the supervisor. |
| SUR-NTF-074 | Every notification record shall be retrievable by the recipient under a data access request (§39), showing what was sent, when, on which channel and its delivery status, with template content resolved. |
| SUR-NTF-075 | Notification content shall be redacted in application logs: variables declared as PII shall be masked, and full rendered bodies shall be stored only in the delivery ledger with the same access controls as the underlying record. |

### 36.6 Cost model

Costs below are **planning estimates** for modelling only, expressed as ranges because rates are negotiated and change; they are not quotes. `[ASSUMPTION: A-270]`

| Channel | Planning unit cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Push (FCM/APNs) | ~₹0.00 | Infrastructure cost only |
| In-app | ~₹0.00 | Storage and delivery only |
| SMS — transactional, Latin script | ₹0.12–₹0.25 per part | Volume-dependent; multi-part messages multiply |
| SMS — Unicode (Devanagari and other Indian scripts) | ₹0.12–₹0.25 per part, but ~70 chars per part | Effective cost per message typically 2–3× Latin |
| WhatsApp — utility/service | ₹0.10–₹0.60 per conversation or message | Category- and model-dependent; assume volatility |
| WhatsApp — authentication | Typically higher than utility | Prefer SMS or push for OTP unless economics change |
| Email | ₹0.01–₹0.05 | Effectively fixed cost at Suraksha's volumes |
| Voice call (TTS/IVR) | ₹0.50–₹1.50 per minute | P0 last resort only |

#### 36.6.1 Volume drivers

| Driver | Effect |
|---|---|
| Guards on duty per day | Dominant driver: shift reminders, check-in/out, patrol, wake checks. A guard on a night shift can generate 15–25 notifications in one shift. |
| Wake-check frequency | Configured interval directly multiplies night-shift volume; halving the interval doubles it |
| Attendance exception rate | Each exception fans out to guard, supervisor, ops, sometimes client — a 5% exception rate is materially cheaper than 15% |
| Number of client contacts per site | Each additional subscribed contact multiplies client-facing sends |
| Dunning population | Overdue accounts generate repeated multi-channel sequences |
| OTP volume | Login frequency × SMS cost; the largest avoidable SMS line item |
| Marketplace enquiry fan-out | An enquiry notified to 20 agencies is 20 sends |

#### 36.6.2 Cost levers

| Lever | Mechanism | Expected effect |
|---|---|---|
| Push-first with SMS as failover only | Failover triggers only on non-delivery/non-acknowledgement (§36.4.2) | Largest single saving; SMS becomes an exception cost |
| Drive app install and push permission for guards | Onboarding gate, persistent prompt (SUR-NTF-032) | Directly reduces SMS dependency |
| Digest P2/P3 | §36.1.6 | Cuts push and email volume, improves signal |
| Template length discipline | Keep SMS under one part; move detail to a link | Halves multi-part SMS cost |
| Transliteration option for regional SMS | SUR-NTF-035 | Avoids the Unicode part penalty where acceptable |
| Reduce exceptions at source | Better geofence tuning, device health, roster accuracy | Reduces the highest-fan-out messages |
| OTP alternatives | Longer sessions for low-risk clients, push-based approval where the app is installed, WhatsApp OTP only if cheaper | Cuts the biggest SMS line |
| Per-tenant cost caps | SUR-NTF-042 and equivalent for SMS | Prevents one tenant's misconfiguration from becoming a platform cost event |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-NTF-076 | Every notification shall record its estimated cost at send time using the current rate card, enabling cost attribution per tenant, per event code and per channel, reported monthly. |
| SUR-NTF-077 | Per-tenant monthly communication budgets shall be configurable with alerts at 80% and 100%; on breach, optional-category messages degrade to in-app only while mandatory categories continue unaffected. Safety is never rationed for cost. |
| SUR-NTF-078 | A cost-anomaly detector shall alert when any event code's daily volume exceeds its trailing 7-day mean by a configurable factor (default 3×), because runaway notification loops are both a cost and a trust incident. |
| SUR-NTF-079 | Communication cost shall post to `EXP_COMMS` (§35.2.2) with tenant attribution, so that per-tenant gross margin in §35.10.2 includes it. |
| SUR-NTF-080 | The notification service shall expose a simulation mode allowing an operator to preview, for a proposed configuration change, the projected monthly volume and cost by channel before publishing it. |
