### 38.3 Identity and session security

Identity decisions are settled in canon §4: one central identity service; phone-first OTP; email+password, Google and Apple also supported; phone verification mandatory; MFA optional for clients and enforceable for staff and agency roles; 30-day client sessions and shorter privileged sessions. This subsection specifies how those are secured, not whether they exist.

#### 38.3.1 Credentials and password policy

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-010 | Passwords shall be a minimum of 10 characters for client and guard accounts and 12 for any staff or agency privileged role. No composition rules (no forced symbol/number classes) shall be imposed; length plus screening is the policy. |
| SUR-SEC-011 | Every new or changed password shall be screened against a breached-password corpus and against a context list (brand names, the user's own phone/email/name fragments, the tenant name, sequential and keyboard patterns). Failures are rejected with a specific reason. |
| SUR-SEC-012 | Passwords shall be stored using Argon2id with parameters tuned to at least 64 MiB memory, 3 iterations, parallelism 4, and a 16-byte random per-user salt, with a server-side pepper held in the secrets manager and never in the database. Parameters shall be reviewed annually and stored alongside each hash so that re-hashing on login is possible without a mass reset. |
| SUR-SEC-013 | Where Argon2id is not available in a runtime, bcrypt with cost ≥ 12 is the only permitted fallback, and its use shall be recorded as a security exception with a remediation date. |
| SUR-SEC-014 | Password rotation shall NOT be forced on a schedule. Rotation shall be forced only on: credential-compromise signal, confirmed account takeover, or an administrator-initiated reset following the recovery process (SUR-SEC-026). |

#### 38.3.2 OTP security

Phone-first OTP is the primary path for guards and most clients, so OTP is a first-class attack surface, not a convenience feature.

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-015 | OTP shall be 6 digits, generated from a cryptographically secure RNG, valid for 5 minutes, single-use, and invalidated on first successful verification, on issuance of a newer OTP for the same purpose, and on expiry. OTP values shall be stored only as hashes. |
| SUR-SEC-016 | OTP verification shall permit at most 5 attempts per issued code; on exhaustion the code is destroyed and a new request is required. Request limits: 3 per number per 10 minutes, 10 per number per day, 20 per IP per hour, 100 per IP per day, each configurable per environment. Limits are enforced server-side and independently of the client. |
| SUR-SEC-017 | Login, OTP-request and password-reset responses shall be constant in shape and timing regardless of whether the identifier exists. No response, timing difference or error code shall permit account enumeration. |
| SUR-SEC-018 | OTP alone shall not be sufficient to authenticate any Suraksha staff role or any agency privileged role (Agency Owner, Agency Admin, Payroll, Agency Finance, Agency Compliance). Those roles require password plus a second factor per SUR-SEC-022. |
| SUR-SEC-019 | **SIM-swap consideration.** SMS OTP is a known-weak factor. The platform shall (a) treat a successful login from a new device on a number whose SIM/carrier binding changed recently, where the operator lookup is available, as a high-risk event requiring step-up; (b) impose a configurable cooling-off window (default 24 hours) after a phone-number change during which payout-detail changes, bank-detail changes and bulk exports are blocked; (c) notify the previous email and the previous device of every phone-number change. Where a carrier SIM-swap signal is not available through an Indian aggregator, the platform shall fall back to the cooling-off and notification controls, and this limitation shall be documented rather than assumed away. [ASSUMPTION: A-331] |
| SUR-SEC-020 | Where a device supports it, OTP delivery shall prefer an app-based push challenge over SMS; SMS remains the fallback for feature phones and low-connectivity guards. |
| SUR-SEC-021 | OTP messages shall not contain any personal data beyond the code and purpose, shall state the purpose ("login", "payout change"), and shall carry an explicit "never share this code" line in the user's language. |

#### 38.3.3 Multi-factor authentication

| Role group | MFA stance | Permitted factors | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Suraksha Super Admin, Founder/Management, Finance, Compliance, Auditor | Mandatory, hardware-preferred | Passkey/WebAuthn (preferred), TOTP; SMS not accepted as the second factor | Cannot be disabled by the user; disabling requires two Super Admins |
| Other Suraksha staff (Operations, Command Center, Verification, Support, Sales, HR, Recruitment, Marketing) | Mandatory | Passkey/WebAuthn, TOTP | Enforced at tenant policy level |
| Agency Owner, Agency Admin, Payroll, Agency Finance, Agency Compliance | Mandatory | Passkey/WebAuthn, TOTP; SMS permitted only as a temporary bootstrap with a 14-day expiry | Enforced by platform policy, not agency-configurable downward |
| Other agency roles (Branch Manager, Operations Manager, Field Officer, Supervisor, HR, Recruiter, Sales, Viewer) | Default on, agency may relax to optional per role except where the role can export data | Passkey/WebAuthn, TOTP, SMS | Agency policy within platform floor |
| Client roles (Company Owner, Security Head, Facility Manager, Site Manager, Procurement, Client Finance, Client Viewer) | Optional, strongly prompted; mandatory for Client Finance and for any role that can view full site security arrangements | Passkey/WebAuthn, TOTP, SMS | Client org admin may enforce for their org |
| Individual Customer | Optional | TOTP, SMS | User choice |
| Guard, PSO, Bouncer, Supervisor (field), Specialised Personnel | Not required for daily field use (device binding plus app lock is the practical control); required for changing bank details or personal identifiers | OTP to bound device, app lock biometric | Step-up on sensitive action only |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-022 | MFA enforcement shall be evaluated per role at every session establishment and at every step-up trigger, not only at first enrolment. A user who gains a privileged role while holding an active non-MFA session shall be forced to re-authenticate with MFA before the new role takes effect. |
| SUR-SEC-023 | Step-up authentication shall be required, regardless of session age, for: changing bank or payout details, approving a payout or payroll run, changing another user's role or permissions, bulk export above the configured threshold, viewing an unmasked government identifier, disabling a security control, break-glass elevation, and deleting or archiving records in bulk. |
| SUR-SEC-024 | MFA recovery codes shall be single-use, 10 in a set, shown once, stored hashed, and their use shall raise a security event and notify the account's other channels. |

#### 38.3.4 Sessions and tokens

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Token type | Short-lived signed access token (JWT or equivalent, asymmetric signature) plus opaque, server-stored refresh token. Access tokens are never long-lived; refresh tokens are revocable records, not self-contained claims. |
| Access token lifetime | 15 minutes (staff, agency privileged), 30 minutes (agency standard, client), 60 minutes (guard app, to reduce refresh chatter on poor networks) |
| Refresh token lifetime | 30 days rolling for client and guard; 12 hours for Suraksha staff privileged roles; 7 days for agency standard roles; 1 hour for break-glass |
| Idle timeout | 15 minutes for Finance/Payroll/Audit surfaces; 30 minutes for other staff surfaces; 12 hours for guard app foreground; none for the guard app's offline queue, which is data-at-rest, not a session |
| Absolute lifetime | Session cannot be extended past 30 days (client/guard) or 24 hours (staff privileged) without full re-authentication |
| Rotation | Refresh tokens rotate on every use; the previous token is invalidated. Reuse of a rotated refresh token is treated as theft: the entire token family is revoked and a P1 security event is raised |
| Binding | Every session record stores device ID, app version, platform, IP at issue, and a device fingerprint hash. A refresh presented from a different device ID is rejected |
| Revocation | Immediate, server-side, per session, per device, per user, per role-change, per tenant. Revocation propagates to all edges within 60 seconds |
| Storage on client | Web: refresh token in an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie scoped to the exact host; access token in memory only, never in localStorage. Mobile: OS secure storage (Keychain / Keystore-backed) |
| Claims | Subject, session ID, tenant ID, role set, scope set (state/city/branch/site as applicable), MFA level, issued-at, expiry, token version. Claims are re-derived from the server on refresh, never trusted as long-lived truth |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-025 | Authorisation shall never be decided solely from token claims for sensitive actions; the server shall re-resolve role, scope and tenant from the datastore for any action that moves money, changes permissions, reads unmasked identifiers, or exports data. |
| SUR-SEC-026 | Any change to role, scope, tenant membership, or employment status shall invalidate all of that user's active sessions within 60 seconds and require re-authentication. |
| SUR-SEC-027 | Logout shall revoke the server-side session record, not merely clear client state. "Log out of all devices" shall be available to every user and shall be a single action visible in account settings. |

#### 38.3.5 Device management and binding

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-028 | Every mobile session shall be bound to a registered Device record (canon §3 entity `Device`) holding device ID, model, OS version, app version, first-seen, last-seen, push token, integrity verdict, and status (Active, Pending, Suspended, Archived). |
| SUR-SEC-029 | A Guard account shall be bound to a configurable maximum of active devices (default 1; agencies may raise to 2 for guards who carry a personal and an issued handset). Registering beyond the limit requires OTP plus, where the agency policy demands it, Supervisor approval, and de-registers the oldest device. |
| SUR-SEC-030 | Attendance, patrol, wake-check and SOS events shall be accepted only from an Active bound device for that guard. Events from an unbound device are stored as Pending with an integrity flag and require Supervisor verification before they count (see §26 for the exception workflow). |
| SUR-SEC-031 | Every user shall have a self-service **Login History and Devices** screen showing, for the last 90 days: timestamp, city (from IP geolocation, coarse), device model, app or browser, result (success / failed / blocked), and a per-session "revoke" action. Guard-side this screen is available in the guard's own language. |
| SUR-SEC-032 | Suraksha staff and agency user accounts shall carry an employment status linked to HR; setting status to exited shall immediately disable login, revoke sessions and tokens, and place the account in Suspended, retaining audit history. |
| SUR-SEC-033 | Accounts with no successful login for a configurable period (default 90 days for staff and agency privileged roles, 180 days for others) shall be automatically Suspended and shall require an administrator action plus MFA re-enrolment to reactivate. |

#### 38.3.6 Suspicious-login detection, lockout and recovery

**Signals evaluated at authentication.** Each returns a score contribution; the composite decides allow / step-up / block.

| Signal | Description | Default action |
|---|---|---|
| S-1 New device for this user | No matching device fingerprint in history | Step-up (OTP or MFA), notify user |
| S-2 New coarse geography | Country or state not seen for this user in 180 days | Step-up, notify |
| S-3 Impossible travel | Two successful logins whose separation implies > 900 km/h | Block newer session, notify, raise P1 event |
| S-4 Datacentre / VPN / Tor egress on a field or client account | ASN classified as hosting/anonymiser | Step-up; block for guard accounts, which have no legitimate reason |
| S-5 Credential-stuffing pattern | Many distinct usernames from one IP or ASN, low success rate | Block source, raise P1 |
| S-6 Password sprayed across tenants | Same password attempted against many accounts | Block, notify security |
| S-7 Off-pattern hour for a privileged role | Staff admin login outside the role's normal window | Allow with step-up, log, alert on sensitive actions |
| S-8 Rapid role-privilege usage after a dormant period | Dormant admin account suddenly performing bulk reads | Alert, force step-up |
| S-9 Recently changed phone number or email | Change within the cooling-off window | Sensitive actions blocked (SUR-SEC-019) |
| S-10 Device integrity failure | Rooted/jailbroken or tampered app signature | Restricted mode (§38.7) |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-034 | Account lockout shall be progressive rather than a hard permanent lock: 5 consecutive failures triggers a 60-second delay, 10 triggers 15 minutes, 15 triggers 1 hour plus a notification to the user, and 20 within 24 hours suspends the account pending an identity-verified recovery. Lockout counters are per account and per source, so that one attacker cannot deliberately lock out an entire agency's guards. |
| SUR-SEC-035 | Account recovery shall never rely on knowledge-based questions. Recovery paths are: (a) verified alternate channel (email plus phone, both previously verified), (b) for guards, Supervisor-attested recovery recorded with the Supervisor's identity and reason, (c) for agency privileged roles, Agency Owner approval plus platform Support verification, (d) for Suraksha staff, HR-verified identity plus two-person approval. Every recovery is audited (§38.12) and triggers a 24-hour restriction on payout-detail changes and bulk export. |

### 38.4 Application security

Controls here are OWASP-informed but written as system-specific requirements. "Framework does it by default" is not an accepted answer unless the default is asserted by a test.

#### 38.4.1 Input validation and output encoding

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-036 | All input shall be validated server-side against an explicit schema per endpoint (type, length, range, format, enum membership, and allowed-character class). Client-side validation is a UX aid only and is never trusted. Validation is allowlist-based; blocklists are not accepted as the primary defence. |
| SUR-SEC-037 | Requests containing fields not present in the endpoint's schema shall be rejected, not silently ignored, on every write endpoint. This is the primary mass-assignment defence (SUR-SEC-044). |
| SUR-SEC-038 | Output encoding shall be contextual and applied at render: HTML body, HTML attribute, JavaScript, URL, CSS and SQL contexts each use their own encoder. Templates shall auto-escape by default and any explicitly unescaped render shall require a code-review annotation naming the reviewer. |
| SUR-SEC-039 | Free-text fields that can contain a person's or company's name shall accept Unicode including Devanagari and other Indian scripts, and shall be validated by normalisation and length rather than by ASCII-only rules. Security shall not be achieved by rejecting legitimate Indian names. |

#### 38.4.2 Injection, XSS, CSRF, SSRF

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-040 | All database access shall use parameterised queries or the ORM's parameter binding. Raw or dynamically concatenated SQL is prohibited except in an explicitly reviewed data-migration or analytics module, where it shall be constructed from a fixed allowlist of column and table identifiers and shall be covered by a SAST rule exception recorded with an owner. |
| SUR-SEC-041 | Report builders, saved filters and search endpoints shall never accept SQL fragments, column names or sort expressions directly from the client; they shall accept opaque field keys mapped server-side to permitted columns, filtered further by the caller's permissions (§31). |
| SUR-SEC-042 | Every HTML-rendering surface shall serve a Content Security Policy with `default-src 'self'`, no `unsafe-inline` for scripts, nonce- or hash-based script allowance, `frame-ancestors 'none'` except where an explicitly allowlisted embed exists, and `object-src 'none'`. CSP violations shall be reported to a collection endpoint and reviewed weekly. |
| SUR-SEC-043 | Uploaded file names, document titles, guard and client names, notes, incident narratives, address lines and marketplace listing text shall be treated as untrusted and encoded on every render surface including PDF generation, CSV export (formula-injection prefixing for values beginning `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR), email templates and WhatsApp/SMS templates. |
| SUR-SEC-044 | State-changing requests from browser clients shall be protected by the double-submit or synchroniser CSRF token pattern in addition to `SameSite=Strict` cookies; API clients using bearer tokens in headers are exempt but shall reject requests carrying only cookie credentials. |
| SUR-SEC-045 | Every server-side outbound fetch triggered by user-supplied input (webhook registration and test-fire, logo or document import by URL, marketplace website preview, integration callback validation) shall route through a single SSRF-safe fetcher: scheme allowlist (https only), DNS resolution pinned and re-checked after redirect, denial of private, loopback, link-local, multicast and cloud-metadata address ranges, redirect limit of 2, response size cap, and timeout. Cloud instance metadata shall additionally require session-token access (IMDSv2 or equivalent) at the infrastructure level. |
| SUR-SEC-046 | Outbound HTTP from application workloads shall pass through an egress proxy with a destination allowlist; direct arbitrary internet egress from application subnets is denied. |

#### 38.4.3 Broken access control and IDOR

This is the single most probable serious vulnerability class in this product, because the product is a multi-tenant system whose objects are interesting to outsiders.

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-047 | Authorisation shall be enforced server-side on every request. Hiding a control in the UI is never an access control. Every endpoint shall declare the permission it requires, and a request without a declared permission mapping shall fail closed at the framework level. |
| SUR-SEC-048 | **The mandatory tenant-scoping test on every object fetch.** Every read, update, delete or list operation on a tenant-owned entity shall pass through a data-access layer that requires an explicit tenant predicate. Concretely, for every object-fetch the server shall assert, before returning data: (1) the object exists; (2) `object.tenant_id == session.tenant_id`, or the caller holds an explicitly granted cross-tenant permission (Suraksha Super Admin, Auditor, or a scoped Suraksha operations role) recorded in §31; (3) the object falls inside the caller's branch/state/city/site scope; (4) the object type is one the caller's role may read; and (5) the field set returned is filtered by the caller's field-level permissions (§31, §39.7). A failure of (1) and a failure of (2) shall be indistinguishable to the caller: both return the same "not found" response, so that object existence cannot be probed across tenants. |
| SUR-SEC-049 | A repository or query helper that can express a tenant-owned entity query without a tenant predicate shall not exist. The default query path binds the tenant from the request context; the unscoped variant is a separately named function, is usable only from an allowlisted set of modules (platform admin, migration, audit), and every call site is flagged in code review and covered by a SAST rule. |
| SUR-SEC-050 | Object identifiers exposed to clients shall be non-sequential (UUIDv7 or equivalent). This is a defence-in-depth measure only; unguessability is never relied upon as an access control (canon principle P8). |
| SUR-SEC-051 | Every endpoint shall be covered by an automated authorisation test matrix asserting, for each of: correct tenant + correct role, correct tenant + wrong role, wrong tenant + any role, and unauthenticated — the expected status and the expected absence of data. This matrix is generated from the endpoint registry (§33) so that a new endpoint without tests fails the build. |
| SUR-SEC-052 | Function-level access control shall be verified for non-obvious paths: bulk endpoints, export endpoints, webhook receivers, admin-only mutations, GraphQL-style field resolvers if used, file-download URLs, print/PDF routes, and any endpoint reachable from a mobile app but not from the web UI. |
| SUR-SEC-053 | Signed URLs for media and documents shall be short-lived (default 5 minutes), single-purpose, bound to the requesting user's session where technically possible, and shall be issued only after the same tenant-scoping test in SUR-SEC-048 has passed. Signed URLs shall never be embedded in emails, notifications, or exported reports; those carry a link to an authenticated viewer instead. |

#### 38.4.4 Mass assignment, deserialization, and business-logic abuse

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-054 | Write endpoints shall bind input to an explicit DTO listing permitted fields per role. Fields including `tenant_id`, `organization_id`, `role`, `permissions`, `status`, `verification_status`, `salary`, `rate`, `balance`, `is_verified`, `created_by` and any audit column shall never be settable through a general update endpoint; they change only through their own purpose-built, permission-checked, audited operations. |
| SUR-SEC-055 | Deserialization of untrusted data shall use data-only formats (JSON) with schema validation. Native object deserialization (pickle, Java serialization, PHP unserialize, YAML with object tags) of untrusted input is prohibited. Queue messages shall be schema-validated and shall carry an integrity signature; a message failing either is dead-lettered and alerted. |
| SUR-SEC-056 | Business-logic abuse cases shall be explicitly tested as security cases, not only functional ones: negative or fractional quantities, negative amounts, zero-rate contracts, backdated attendance, future-dated attendance, duplicate submission of the same payment, replay of the same SOS acknowledgement, assignment of a guard to two overlapping shifts (BR-001), and status transitions that skip required states. |
| SUR-SEC-057 | Financial mutations shall be idempotent by client-supplied idempotency key, and every completed financial transaction shall be immutable (BR-003); corrections are new compensating entries, never edits (see §35). |
| SUR-SEC-058 | Changing a bank account, UPI ID or payout destination shall require: step-up authentication, verification of the new destination through the payment provider's account-validation facility where available, a configurable hold period (default 24 hours) before the destination is usable for a payout, notification to all of the account's channels, and a second-person approval when the payee is an agency or a batch payee. |
| SUR-SEC-059 | Payment provider webhooks shall be verified by the provider's signature scheme, checked for timestamp freshness (default 5 minutes), de-duplicated by event ID, and reconciled against a server-initiated status query before any ledger effect is applied. A webhook alone shall never be sufficient evidence of payment. |
| SUR-SEC-060 | Webhook receiver endpoints shall be individually rate-limited, shall not echo request content in errors, and shall respond identically for valid-but-unknown and invalid events. |
| SUR-SEC-061 | Outbound webhooks sent by Suraksha to agency or client systems shall be signed with a per-subscription secret, include a timestamp and a replay nonce, be retried with exponential backoff, and be disabled automatically after a configurable number of consecutive failures with a notification to the subscriber. |

#### 38.4.5 File upload and content safety

The platform ingests a high volume of files from low-trust sources: guard KYC documents, police-verification scans, agency licence documents, client site photographs, incident photos and videos, attendance selfies, and body-camera media where implemented.

| Control point | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Transport | Direct-to-storage upload via a short-lived, single-use pre-signed URL issued only after permission and quota checks; the application never proxies large media through the API tier |
| Type validation | Content-type determined by magic-byte inspection server-side, not by extension or client-declared MIME; allowlist per upload purpose (e.g. KYC accepts JPEG, PNG, PDF only) |
| Size and dimension limits | Per purpose, enforced at issue of the pre-signed URL and re-verified after upload |
| Name handling | Original file name stored as metadata only; storage key is a generated identifier; the original name is never used to build a path and is HTML-encoded on display |
| Storage isolation | Uploaded media is stored in a bucket/prefix that is private by default, has no public access policy, is served only through signed URLs (SUR-SEC-053), and is on a domain that cannot execute scripts in the app's origin |
| Malware scanning | Every uploaded file is scanned before it becomes visible to any user; state is Pending until the scan passes |
| Image handling | Images re-encoded (stripped and re-written) server-side to remove embedded payloads; EXIF stripped except where geotag is deliberately retained for evidentiary purposes and then stored as structured data, not left in the file |
| PDF handling | PDFs scanned, and rendered to the viewer through a viewer that does not execute embedded JavaScript |
| Archive handling | Archives (zip) accepted only for bulk-import purposes, with decompression limits (entry count, total size, path traversal rejection, no symlinks) |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-062 | Every uploaded file shall be malware-scanned before becoming retrievable. A file whose scan fails shall be quarantined, the uploader notified, and a security event raised; a file whose scan is unavailable shall remain Pending, never default-allow. |
| SUR-SEC-063 | Images accepted for identity, attendance and incident purposes shall be re-encoded server-side and shall have metadata handled per the table above. Attendance selfies shall additionally be checked for replay indicators (identical perceptual hash to a previous submission, screen-capture/moiré signature, absent or implausible capture metadata) and flagged for Supervisor review rather than silently rejected. |
| SUR-SEC-064 | Document downloads of identity documents, police-verification records and payroll documents shall be watermarked at render with the viewing user's name, employee ID, tenant and timestamp, and the view shall be audited as a sensitive-read event (§38.12). |

#### 38.4.6 OWASP API Security risks mapped to this system

| API risk | Where it bites in Suraksha | Concrete control |
|---|---|---|
| Broken object-level authorisation | Guard, Site, Post, Shift, Incident, Invoice, Document fetch by ID | SUR-SEC-048, -049, -050, -051 |
| Broken authentication | OTP-heavy login, long guard sessions, refresh handling | SUR-SEC-015 to -027 |
| Broken object-property-level authorisation | Client can read a Guard object but must not see identifiers, salary or home address; Marketing must not see client contact in full | SUR-SEC-048(5), §31, §39.7 |
| Unrestricted resource consumption | OTP sends (real money per SMS), report generation, media transcode, AI calls | SUR-SEC-065, -068, -069, -071 |
| Broken function-level authorisation | Admin mutations reachable from the mobile API surface | SUR-SEC-052 |
| Unrestricted access to sensitive business flows | Bulk guard export, marketplace enumeration, bulk booking creation, mass invite | SUR-SEC-066, -084, -093 |
| SSRF | Webhook config, logo import, integration test-fire | SUR-SEC-045, -046 |
| Security misconfiguration | Verbose errors, permissive CORS, stale debug flags, default credentials | SUR-SEC-069, -136, -143 |
| Improper inventory management | Old API versions and staging hosts left reachable | SUR-SEC-070, -137 |
| Unsafe consumption of third-party APIs | Trusting a verification vendor's or payment provider's response without validation | SUR-SEC-059, -072 |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-065 | Per-endpoint quotas shall exist for anything with real-world cost or bulk-exposure risk: OTP sends, notification sends, report generation, export, media upload, AI interactions, and search. Quotas are per user, per tenant and per IP, and exceeding them returns a structured throttle response, not a failure. |
| SUR-SEC-066 | Bulk and enumeration-prone endpoints (list guards, list sites, search marketplace, list clients) shall enforce a maximum page size, a maximum total pagination depth per session per day, and shall count returned records against the tenant's export/enumeration budget. |
| SUR-SEC-067 | Operations with an external monetary cost (SMS, WhatsApp, voice, model inference, third-party verification calls) shall be protected by a per-tenant spend circuit breaker: a rolling budget, an alert at 80%, and an automatic throttle at 100% that degrades the feature rather than the platform. Emergency paths (SOS, safety notifications) shall be exempt from the throttle and shall have their own monitored budget. |
| SUR-SEC-068 | Expensive asynchronous operations (report generation, export, media transcode, bulk import) shall run on a queue with per-tenant concurrency limits and priority classes, so that one tenant cannot exhaust shared capacity. Queue depth and age shall alert. |
| SUR-SEC-071 | AI interactions shall be quota-limited per user, per tenant and per action class, with token and cost ceilings enforced server-side before the provider call, and with the limits visible to the tenant administrator (§41). |
| SUR-SEC-069 | Error responses shall never contain stack traces, SQL fragments, internal hostnames, library versions or full request echoes in any environment reachable from the internet. Errors carry a correlation ID; detail lives in the log, not in the response. |
| SUR-SEC-070 | An API inventory shall be maintained automatically from the endpoint registry (§33), including version, auth requirement, exposure (public/authenticated/internal), owner and deprecation state. An endpoint not in the inventory shall fail the build; a deprecated endpoint shall be disabled on its sunset date automatically. |
| SUR-SEC-072 | Responses from third-party providers (payment, KYC/verification, SMS, maps, model providers) shall be schema-validated, size-limited, timeout-bounded, and never rendered as HTML or used to construct queries without the same encoding and validation applied to user input. |

### 38.5 API and transport security

#### 38.5.1 Transport

| Aspect | Requirement |
|---|---|
| TLS versions | TLS 1.3 preferred; TLS 1.2 permitted for compatibility with older Android handsets common in the field. TLS 1.0/1.1 and SSLv3 disabled everywhere |
| Cipher suites | TLS 1.3: AES-128-GCM, AES-256-GCM, CHACHA20-POLY1305. TLS 1.2: ECDHE key exchange only, AEAD ciphers only, no CBC, no RSA key exchange, no 3DES, no RC4, no NULL/EXPORT/anon |
| Forward secrecy | Mandatory on all suites |
| Certificates | Automated issuance and renewal, minimum 30-day renewal margin, key size RSA 2048 minimum or ECDSA P-256, expiry monitored with alerts at 30/14/7 days |
| HSTS | `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload` on all surakshaguards.in properties, after a staged rollout that confirms every subdomain is HTTPS-capable |
| Redirects | All HTTP requests 301 to HTTPS; no mixed content permitted; CSP `upgrade-insecure-requests` |
| Internal traffic | TLS between all tiers including within the VPC; database, cache and queue connections use TLS with certificate verification |
| Additional headers | `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `Permissions-Policy` denying camera/microphone/geolocation except where a surface needs them, `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`, `Cache-Control: no-store` on authenticated responses |
| CORS | Explicit origin allowlist per property; no wildcard with credentials; preflight cached briefly; `Vary: Origin` always set |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-073 | TLS configuration shall be continuously verified by an external scan on every public host at least weekly, and any regression below the profile above shall raise a P1 security event. |
| SUR-SEC-074 | Certificate private keys shall be generated and stored in the platform's key management service or the CDN/load-balancer's managed store; keys shall never exist in the repository, in container images, or on developer machines. |
| SUR-SEC-075 | Certificate Transparency logs shall be monitored for unexpected certificates issued for surakshaguards.in and its subdomains; a CAA record shall restrict issuance to the approved CAs. |

#### 38.5.2 API authentication and abuse protection

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-076 | First-party clients (web, mobile, desktop) authenticate with the user's session tokens (§38.3.4). There is no shared static API key for first-party clients, and no secret is shipped inside a mobile or desktop binary that would grant access if extracted. |
| SUR-SEC-077 | The Enterprise API (canon §1.4) shall authenticate with per-tenant, per-integration credentials using OAuth 2.0 client credentials with short-lived tokens, or signed requests where the client cannot hold a token. Credentials are scoped to specific permission sets, are individually revocable, carry an expiry, and are displayed once at creation. |
| SUR-SEC-078 | Every API credential shall have an owner, a purpose, a last-used timestamp and an expiry (default 365 days, configurable down). Credentials unused for 90 days are automatically disabled with notification. |
| SUR-SEC-079 | Rate limiting shall be layered: edge (per IP, per ASN), identity (per user, per tenant), and endpoint (per operation cost class). Limits are configurable per plan tier for the Enterprise API and are published in the API documentation (§33). Throttle responses include `Retry-After`. |
| SUR-SEC-080 | A WAF shall front every public property with, at minimum: managed rule sets for injection, XSS, path traversal and known-CVE exploitation; custom rules for the platform's known-sensitive endpoints; per-endpoint anomaly thresholds; and logging of every block with the correlation ID. WAF rules shall be deployable in count-then-block mode and changes shall be reviewed like code. |
| SUR-SEC-081 | Bot management shall be applied to public pages and forms: quote/contact forms, marketplace search and listing pages, agency and guard signup, login and OTP endpoints. Controls include invisible challenge, progressive challenge on suspicion, ASN and reputation scoring, and honeypot fields. CAPTCHA shall be used only as an escalation, not as the default, because it degrades access for low-literacy and low-bandwidth users. |
| SUR-SEC-082 | DDoS protection shall be provided at the network and application layers by the CDN/edge provider, with an always-on volumetric baseline, autoscaling headroom for the application tier, and a documented runbook for shedding non-essential load (marketing pages, analytics ingestion, non-critical reports) to preserve SOS, attendance and command-centre functions. Availability priorities are specified in §46 and §49; this control names SOS and live tracking as the last services to be degraded. |
| SUR-SEC-083 | The platform shall maintain a **public-endpoint inventory** (below) reviewed at each release; adding a new unauthenticated endpoint requires security review and an entry with exposure rationale. |

#### 38.5.3 Public-endpoint inventory

Unauthenticated or partially unauthenticated surfaces. Anything not on this list must be authenticated.

| Endpoint class | Property | Why it must be public | Abuse risk | Controls |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Marketing pages, service pages, blog, legal pages | surakshaguards.in | Discovery, SEO | Scraping (low value) | WAF, caching, bot scoring |
| Quote/contact/callback form | surakshaguards.in | Primary B2C/B2B lead capture | Spam, lead poisoning, SMS cost | SUR-SEC-081, per-IP and per-number quota, honeypot, no data echo |
| Booking initiation (pre-account) | surakshaguards.in | P10 fix: booking must be startable without an account | Fake bookings, resource use | Phone verification before persistence, rate limit, fraud scoring |
| Login, OTP request, OTP verify, password reset | all properties | Necessary | Stuffing, enumeration, OTP flood | SUR-SEC-015 to -017, -034, -081 |
| Guard job listings and public agency directory | trinetra, guards | Marketplace value proposition requires visibility | Competitor scraping (T-08) | Partial fields public, full detail authenticated, aggressive rate limit, no bulk export, per-IP result caps, watermark/canary listings |
| Agency public profile page | trinetra | Agencies want to be found | Scraping | Same as above; contact details revealed only to authenticated, verified accounts |
| Payment provider webhook receiver | api | Provider must reach it | Forgery, replay (T-15) | SUR-SEC-059, -060 |
| SMS/WhatsApp delivery-status callbacks | api | Provider must reach it | Forgery, spoofed status | Signature verification, allowlisted source ranges where the provider publishes them |
| App download / update manifest | trinetra, guards | Distribution | Tampered binary served | Signed artefacts, TLS, integrity hash published |
| Health check | infra | Load balancer | Information leak | Returns status only, no version, no dependency detail |
| Public status page | status subdomain | Incident transparency | None material | Hosted separately from production |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-084 | The public agency directory and job listings shall expose a deliberately reduced field set to unauthenticated visitors: agency display name, city/state coverage, service lanes, verification badge state, and aggregate rating. Licence numbers, contact details, guard counts, client names, rate cards and site information shall never appear on an unauthenticated surface. |
| SUR-SEC-085 | Marketplace listings shall carry canary records (synthetic listings visible only through specific access paths) so that bulk republication of scraped data can be detected and attributed. |

### 38.6 Data security

#### 38.6.1 Encryption

| Layer | Requirement |
|---|---|
| In transit, external | TLS per §38.5.1 |
| In transit, internal | TLS between all services and to all data stores, with certificate verification enabled |
| At rest, databases | Storage-level encryption with AES-256, provider-managed KMS keys with customer-managed key material where the provider supports it |
| At rest, object storage | AES-256 server-side encryption, bucket policy denies unencrypted writes |
| At rest, backups and snapshots | Encrypted with a distinct key from the primary store; restore requires explicit key access |
| At rest, queues, caches, search indexes | Encrypted; sensitive fields never placed in a search index in plaintext (see SUR-SEC-089) |
| At rest, logs | Encrypted; sensitive values redacted before write (SUR-SEC-119) |
| Field-level | Application-layer envelope encryption for the fields in §38.6.3 |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-086 | All data stores holding personal data shall have encryption at rest enabled at creation; a store created without it shall be blocked by infrastructure policy, not corrected after the fact. |
| SUR-SEC-087 | Encryption keys shall be managed in a KMS/HSM-backed service. Key material shall never be present in application configuration, code, environment variables or container images. Applications receive data keys through the KMS API and hold them only in memory. |

#### 38.6.2 Key management and rotation

| Key class | Purpose | Rotation | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| K-1 Storage master keys | Database, object store, backup encryption | Annual, or immediately on suspected compromise | Provider-managed rotation with key versioning; old versions retained for decryption of existing data |
| K-2 Field-encryption data keys | Envelope encryption of sensitive fields (§38.6.3) | Data-encryption keys rotate per record class annually; the key-encrypting key rotates annually | Re-encryption is a background job with progress tracking, never a big-bang migration |
| K-3 Token signing keys | Access-token signature | 90 days, with overlap window for verification | Asymmetric; public verification key published on a JWKS endpoint |
| K-4 Webhook and integration secrets | Signing inbound/outbound webhooks | 180 days, with dual-secret overlap so rotation is zero-downtime | Per subscription |
| K-5 Service credentials | DB users, queue credentials, third-party API keys | 90 days, automated where the provider supports it | Never shared between environments |
| K-6 Password pepper | Server-side pepper for Argon2id | Rotated only with a versioned scheme and re-hash on next login | Version stored with each hash |
| K-7 TLS private keys | Transport | Per certificate lifetime (≤ 90 days with automated issuance) | Never leaves managed store |
| K-8 Backup restore keys | Restoring encrypted backups | Annual | Split control: restore requires two authorised holders (§49) |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-088 | Every key class shall have a documented owner, rotation period, rotation procedure, and an emergency rotation procedure executable within 4 hours. Emergency key rotation shall be exercised at least annually as part of the incident-response drill (§38.14.5). |
| SUR-SEC-089 | Key usage shall be logged (which principal used which key for what operation) and anomalous key usage — volume spikes, use from an unexpected workload, decryption of a record class the workload does not normally touch — shall alert. |

#### 38.6.3 Field-level encryption and tokenisation

Storage-level encryption protects against stolen disks and misplaced snapshots. It does not protect against an application-layer compromise, a leaked read-replica credential, or an over-broad internal query. The fields below therefore carry application-layer envelope encryption in addition, with decryption gated by permission and audited on every access.

| Field class | Examples | Storage form | Who can trigger decryption | Search behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FE-1 Government identifiers where legally used and consented (§39) | Identity-document numbers, PAN | Encrypted value + blind index (HMAC with a separate key) for exact-match lookup + last-4 in clear for display | Verification role, Compliance, Payroll where the configured purpose requires it | Exact match only via blind index; no partial or wildcard search; no sorting |
| FE-2 Bank and payout details | Account number, IFSC pairing, UPI ID | Encrypted; last-4 in clear | Payroll, Agency Finance, Finance, on step-up | Exact match via blind index for duplicate detection (same account across guards — a fraud signal) |
| FE-3 Biometric references | Face-match template or vendor reference ID | Reference/token only; raw biometric never stored on the platform (see §39.2) | Attendance verification service only, machine-to-machine | Not searchable |
| FE-4 Police-verification and background-verification content | Report body, findings, remarks | Encrypted document; structured status stored separately in clear | Verification, Compliance, and the guard themselves | Not full-text indexed |
| FE-5 Health and emergency data | Blood group, medical notes, emergency contact | Encrypted | Command Center during an active incident, HR, the guard | Not searchable |
| FE-6 Client site security arrangements | Post positions, patrol routes, checkpoint coordinates, shift-gap-revealing schedules | Encrypted at rest at the document level; access strictly scoped | Client's own scoped roles, the serving agency's operational roles, Suraksha operations in scope | Not exposed to global search; per-site search only |
| FE-7 Payment card data | — | **Never stored.** Card data is handled entirely by the payment provider; the platform stores only provider tokens and last-4/brand for display | n/a | n/a |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-090 | Payment card numbers, CVV and full magnetic-stripe-equivalent data shall never touch Suraksha systems, logs, or support tooling. All card interaction happens in the provider's hosted or SDK-collected fields, and the platform stores only provider tokens (SUR-SEC-091). |
| SUR-SEC-091 | Where a value must be usable for matching but not readable, tokenisation or blind indexing shall be used in preference to storing the value. Blind-index keys shall be separate from data-encryption keys and rotatable independently. |
| SUR-SEC-092 | Every decryption of an FE-1 to FE-6 field for human display shall emit a sensitive-read audit event containing actor, purpose code, record, and correlation ID (§38.12), and shall be rate-limited per user per day with an alert on exceedance. |
| SUR-SEC-093 | Bulk decryption (more than a configured number of records in a window) shall require an approved job with a stated purpose, a second-person approval, and shall be time-boxed and fully audited. |

#### 38.6.4 Secrets management

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-094 | All secrets (database credentials, third-party API keys, signing keys, peppers, webhook secrets) shall live in a managed secrets store with versioning, access policy, and audit. Applications fetch secrets at start-up or on demand using workload identity; no secret is baked into an image or a config file in the repository. |
| SUR-SEC-095 | Secrets shall be environment-specific. A production secret shall never be readable from a non-production workload or by a developer role, and a non-production secret shall never grant production access. |
| SUR-SEC-096 | Human access to production secrets shall be exceptional, approved, time-bounded, and audited; the default is that no human can read a production secret value, only rotate it. |
| SUR-SEC-097 | Secret scanning shall run pre-commit, in CI on every push, and continuously across the repository history and the issue tracker. A detected secret triggers automatic revocation-and-rotation workflow, not merely a ticket. |

#### 38.6.5 Database access control and data in use

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-098 | Application database users shall hold only the privileges their module needs; there shall be separate credentials for read-write application access, read-only analytics access, and migration access. No application uses a superuser role. Analytics and reporting read from a replica or a warehouse, never from the primary with an elevated role. |
| SUR-SEC-099 | Direct human access to production databases shall be denied by default. Where an emergency requires it, access is through a session-recorded, approved, time-boxed break-glass path (see §22 and SUR-SEC-125) with all statements logged and the session reviewed within 24 hours. |
| SUR-SEC-100 | Production data shall never be copied into a non-production environment. Lower environments use synthetic data or an irreversibly masked extract in which identifiers, names, phone numbers, addresses, bank details, GPS traces and document files are replaced, not obfuscated. Masking is verified by an automated check that fails if any real-format identifier or real phone number is present. |
| SUR-SEC-101 | **Data in use stance.** Suraksha does not rely on confidential-computing or homomorphic techniques at any planned phase; data in use is protected by process isolation, least-privilege workload identity, memory-safety practices in dependency selection, no core dumps in production, and minimising the time sensitive plaintext exists in memory. This is stated explicitly so that no reader assumes protection the platform does not provide. [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-SEC-102 | Backups shall be encrypted with keys distinct from the production data keys, stored in a separate account/project from production, immutable for their retention window where the provider supports object-lock, and their restore path tested per §49. Restoration into a lower environment is prohibited without the masking pipeline in SUR-SEC-100. |
| SUR-SEC-103 | Data retention and deletion shall be driven by the retention schedule in §39.2 and executed by an automated job whose runs are audited, including counts of records purged, anonymised and retained-under-legal-hold. |

### 38.7 Mobile application security

Four apps (canon §1.2), each with a different risk profile. The Guard App is the highest-risk client because it runs on a low-cost, often rooted, sometimes shared handset carried into a physically insecure environment, and it holds the roster and location data an attacker most wants.

| App | Primary risk | Dominant control |
|---|---|---|
| Guard App | Device theft, root, mock GPS, offline cache extraction, shared device | Device binding, encrypted cache, integrity signals, app lock, minimal cached scope |
| Customer App | Account takeover leading to site-arrangement disclosure | MFA prompting, app lock for site-detail screens, no cached rosters |
| Agency App | Insider bulk access on a mobile surface | Full role enforcement identical to web, screenshot blocking, no bulk export from mobile |
| Admin App | Highest privilege on the least controllable form factor | MFA mandatory, short sessions, no break-glass from mobile, screenshot blocking, watermarking (see §23) |

#### 38.7.1 On-device storage and logging

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-104 | Tokens, keys and any cached personal data shall be stored in OS-provided secure storage (iOS Keychain with `kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly`; Android Keystore-backed keys with `setUserAuthenticationRequired` where the device supports it). Nothing sensitive is stored in shared preferences, plain files, or unencrypted SQLite. |
| SUR-SEC-105 | The Guard App's offline store shall be an encrypted database whose key is held in the Keystore/Keychain and is not extractable; the key shall be additionally wrapped by a value derived from the app-lock credential where the guard has one enabled. |
| SUR-SEC-106 | No app shall write personal data, tokens, coordinates, document contents, or full request/response bodies to system logs, crash reports, analytics events or third-party SDK telemetry. Crash reporting shall be configured to strip user identifiers and payloads; a build-time check shall fail the build if a logging call in a sensitive module is not routed through the redacting logger. |
| SUR-SEC-107 | Keyboard caching, autofill and clipboard shall be disabled on fields holding identifiers, bank details and OTP codes; sensitive values shall be cleared from the clipboard after a short timeout if copying is permitted at all. |

#### 38.7.2 The Guard App offline-cache question

Offline-first is mandatory for the Guard App only (canon §4). That mandate creates a data-at-rest problem on the least trusted device in the estate. The answer is to cache the minimum needed to work a shift, encrypted, and to wipe aggressively.

| Data class | Cached offline? | Scope of cache | Encryption | Wipe trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guard's own profile basics (name, photo, employee ID, current assignment) | Yes | Self only | Encrypted store | Logout, unbind, 7 days idle |
| Today's and tomorrow's own shift, site name, reporting point, post name | Yes | Own assignments only | Encrypted store | Shift end + 24h, logout |
| Site geofence coordinates for own posts | Yes | Own posts only | Encrypted store | Shift end + 24h |
| Checkpoint list and patrol route for own duty | Yes, only for the current duty window | Own duty only | Encrypted store | Duty end |
| Supervisor and emergency contact numbers | Yes | Own chain only | Encrypted store | Logout |
| Other guards at the same site | Minimal: display name and post only, and only where the operational flow requires it (relief handover) | Same site, same shift | Encrypted store | Shift end |
| Full site roster, other shifts, shift-gap-revealing schedule | **Never cached** | — | — | — |
| Client contact details, contract or rate information | **Never cached** | — | — | — |
| Any other guard's identifiers, phone, address, salary | **Never cached** | — | — | — |
| Queued outbound events (attendance, patrol scan, wake-check, incident, SOS) with media | Yes, until acknowledged by the server | Own events | Encrypted store; media encrypted at rest on device | On server acknowledgement; media deleted from app storage after successful upload |
| Historical location track | **Never retained on device** beyond the unsynced queue | — | — | On sync |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-108 | The Guard App's offline cache shall contain only the data classes marked cacheable above. A new cached field requires a documented decision recorded against this table. |
| SUR-SEC-109 | The offline cache shall be wiped on: logout, device unbind, remote wipe command, failed integrity check with policy set to strict, app-lock failure beyond the configured attempt limit, and after a configurable maximum offline age (default 7 days) at which point the app requires connectivity to continue, retaining only the unsynced event queue. |
| SUR-SEC-110 | A remote-wipe command shall be issuable by Agency Admin or Suraksha operations for a lost or stolen device, shall take effect on next app launch or next network contact, and shall wipe the cache and revoke sessions. The unsynced event queue shall be uploaded first where connectivity allows, so that evidence of an incident is not destroyed by the wipe. |

#### 38.7.3 Integrity, tampering and pinning

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-111 | The apps shall check device integrity using platform attestation (Play Integrity on Android, DeviceCheck/App Attest on iOS) plus local root/jailbreak heuristics. **Honest limitation:** these checks are advisory. A determined attacker with a rooted device and a hooking framework can defeat local checks, and platform attestation can be unavailable on legitimate devices (custom ROMs common on cheap handsets, GMS-less devices, older OS versions). Integrity signals are therefore treated as risk inputs, never as an authorisation decision, and never as a reason to accuse a guard of fraud on their own. |
| SUR-SEC-112 | Integrity policy shall be configurable per tenant with three modes: (a) **Monitor** — record the verdict, allow all functions (default); (b) **Restrict** — allow attendance, SOS and patrol, but block bank-detail change, document upload of identity documents, and profile edits; (c) **Block** — deny app use, permitted only where the agency issues its own devices. SOS shall function in every mode, including Block, because refusing an emergency call on the basis of a root check is unacceptable. |
| SUR-SEC-113 | Mock-location detection shall combine the OS mock-location flag, provider consistency checks, movement plausibility (teleport, impossible speed, perfect stillness at exact coordinates), and cross-checks against network-derived location and nearby-device signals where available. A detection shall flag the event for Supervisor review with the evidence shown, not auto-reject it, because false positives on cheap handsets are common and a wrongly rejected attendance costs a guard a day's pay (see §26, §45). |
| SUR-SEC-114 | Certificate pinning shall be applied in the mobile apps to the API domains. **Operational trade-off stated:** pinning breaks the app if a certificate or CA changes unexpectedly, and field devices update slowly, so a bad pin is an outage the platform cannot hotfix. The mitigations are: pin to the intermediate CA's public key rather than the leaf; ship at least two backup pins; ship a pin set with an expiry after which pinning degrades to standard validation rather than hard-failing; and never pin the SOS/emergency path so that an emergency can never be blocked by a pin failure. Pin rotation follows a documented procedure with a minimum two-release overlap. |
| SUR-SEC-115 | Application binaries shall be code-signed, shall verify their own signature and package name at runtime, shall detect common hooking/instrumentation frameworks, and shall be obfuscated to raise the cost of reverse engineering — with the explicit understanding that obfuscation is a cost multiplier, not a control. No security decision shall depend on client-side code being un-analysable. |
| SUR-SEC-116 | Screenshot and screen-recording shall be blocked (Android `FLAG_SECURE`, iOS screen-capture detection and content obscuring) on screens showing identity documents, police-verification records, salary and payslip data, bank details, client site security arrangements, audit logs and full guard rosters. On iOS, where blocking is not fully possible, the screen shall be obscured on capture/recording detection and the attempt logged. Attempted captures on these screens are recorded as security events. |
| SUR-SEC-117 | Apps shall obscure their content in the OS task switcher, shall lock on backgrounding beyond a configurable timeout, and shall offer an app lock (biometric or PIN). App lock shall be mandatory for the Admin App and Agency App, default-on for the Customer App's site screens, and default-on for the Guard App with the option for the guard to disable it only where agency policy allows. |
| SUR-SEC-118 | Deep links and custom URL schemes shall be validated, shall never carry tokens or personal data in the URL, and shall require an authenticated session to resolve to content. |

---

### 38.8 Location and operational-data security

Location is treated as its own data class, above ordinary personal data, because it is the field most capable of causing physical harm. The privacy treatment of location — consent, worker-facing transparency, purpose limitation — is in §39.5; this subsection is the security enforcement.

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-119 | GPS position, geofence events, patrol traces and any derived movement data shall be classified **High Sensitivity**, encrypted at rest, excluded from general search indexes, excluded from general analytics exports, and excluded from any data sent to a model provider (§41). |
| SUR-SEC-120 | Location collection shall be bounded by duty state: collection begins at shift check-in and ends at check-out, with a configurable grace window around each. Outside a guard's duty window, the app shall not collect location, and the server shall reject any location event carrying a timestamp outside the guard's assigned duty window plus grace. |
| SUR-SEC-121 | Location shall be collected at a resolution and frequency no greater than the operational purpose requires: a configurable interval (default 60 seconds on duty, higher-frequency only during an active SOS or an active patrol), with movement-triggered sampling to avoid pointless collection while a guard is static at a post. |
| SUR-SEC-122 | Access to live location shall be restricted to: the guard themselves, their Supervisor and Field Officer in scope, the agency's operational roles in scope, the Command Center during an active incident, and the client's scoped roles **only for guards currently on duty at that client's own site**. No role shall have platform-wide live-location access except Suraksha Command Center and Super Admin, whose access is audited per view. |
| SUR-SEC-123 | Historical track replay shall require a stated reason recorded in the audit log for any window beyond the last 24 hours, and shall be unavailable entirely beyond the configured retention period (§39.2). Bulk export of location history shall require second-person approval. |
| SUR-SEC-124 | A client shall see only guards deployed to that client's own sites, only during those guards' duty windows at those sites, and only the fields §31 grants. A client shall never see a guard's location before check-in or after check-out, never see the guard's home area, and never see guards deployed elsewhere. |
| SUR-SEC-125 | **Site security arrangements are confidential.** Post positions, guards-per-shift, shift-change times, patrol routes, checkpoint locations, response procedures and any data from which a coverage gap can be inferred shall be treated as a restricted class: not present in unauthenticated surfaces, not in marketplace listings, not in general search, not in AI responses to roles without the entitlement, not in exports below the export-approval threshold, and not shared with an agency that is not currently serving that site. |
| SUR-SEC-126 | Any report, export or API response that could reveal a coverage gap (a post with unfilled shifts, an unassigned window, a patrol with no scheduled pass) shall be permission-gated to the client's own scoped roles, the serving agency's operational roles, and Suraksha operations. Aggregate or benchmarking analytics shall be computed so that no individual site's gaps are derivable (minimum aggregation thresholds per §42). |
| SUR-SEC-127 | Where a client relationship ends, the serving agency's access to that site's arrangements shall terminate on the configured off-boarding date, with an audited grace window for settlement and dispute handling only. |

### 38.9 Multi-tenant security

Tenancy is settled in canon §3: every agency-owned row carries `tenant_id`, Suraksha's own guarding operation is tenant `SURAKSHA-HQ`, and `branch_id` is a second axis that never substitutes for tenant isolation. The enforcement layers are those defined in §26(b); this subsection specifies the security requirements on each and the tests that prove them.

#### 38.9.1 Enforcement layers

| Layer | What it enforces | Failure mode it catches | Requirement |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 Session/context binding | Tenant is resolved from the authenticated session at request entry and is immutable for the request lifetime | Client-supplied tenant parameter | SUR-SEC-128 |
| L2 Data-access layer predicate | Every tenant-owned query carries a tenant predicate injected by the framework | Developer forgets a `WHERE tenant_id = ...` | SUR-SEC-129 |
| L3 Database-level isolation | Row-level security policy (or equivalent) as a backstop for L2 | ORM bypass, raw query, reporting query | SUR-SEC-130 |
| L4 Response filtering and field-level permission | Fields the caller may not see are removed before serialisation | Over-fetching, new field leaking into a shared DTO | SUR-SEC-131 |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-128 | Tenant identity shall be derived only from the authenticated session and never from a request parameter, header, path segment, or body field. Cross-tenant access (Suraksha roles) shall be an explicit, permissioned, audited mode with the target tenant recorded on every request, not an ambient capability. |
| SUR-SEC-129 | The data-access layer shall make a tenant-unscoped query on a tenant-owned entity impossible to express through the normal API. See SUR-SEC-049. |
| SUR-SEC-130 | Where the datastore supports row-level security, it shall be enabled on every tenant-owned table with a policy bound to a session variable set from the request context, as a backstop that catches raw-SQL and reporting paths. Where it is not supported, an equivalent enforced view layer shall be used and the gap documented. |
| SUR-SEC-131 | API responses shall be built from explicit per-role serialisers. A new field added to an entity shall not appear in any response until it is added to a serialiser with a role mapping; a test shall assert that every serialised field has an explicit permission mapping in §31. |

#### 38.9.2 Cross-tenant leak vectors and their controls

| Vector | How the leak happens | Control |
|---|---|---|
| Search | A shared search index returns another tenant's documents | Tenant is a mandatory filter on every index query, enforced at the query-builder level; documents carry `tenant_id` and the index is partitioned by tenant where volume allows; a test asserts a query without a tenant filter is rejected |
| Export / report | A report definition joins a table without a tenant predicate | Report definitions execute through the same L2/L3 path as the application; report SQL cannot be authored freehand by tenants; every export is tenant-stamped and its row count is compared against a tenant-scoped control count |
| AI | The assistant retrieves context outside the caller's tenant, or a prompt-injection payload in a free-text field instructs it to | Retrieval executes with the caller's identity through the same authorisation path (§25, §41); no shared vector index across tenants without a hard tenant filter at query time; retrieved content is treated as data, never as instructions; outputs are scanned for identifiers not belonging to the caller's tenant before display |
| Notifications | Recipient resolution picks up a wrong-tenant user; a template renders another tenant's data | Recipient lists are resolved inside the tenant scope; every notification carries a tenant stamp validated against the recipient's tenant at send time; a mismatch is dropped and alerted (§36) |
| File/media URLs | A signed URL issued for one tenant's object is reused | URLs are short-lived, single-purpose, and issued only after the SUR-SEC-048 check; object keys are namespaced by tenant; access logs are correlated to the issuing session |
| Caching | A cache key omits tenant, so one tenant's response is served to another | Every cache key includes tenant and, where relevant, role and scope; a lint rule rejects a cache key built without the tenant component |
| Background jobs | A job runs with an ambient admin context and processes all tenants, emitting per-tenant output to the wrong place | Jobs carry an explicit tenant context per unit of work; cross-tenant jobs are a named, reviewed category and write output only to tenant-stamped destinations |
| Aggregate analytics | Benchmark figures let a tenant infer a competitor's data | Minimum cohort size before any benchmark is shown, suppression of small cells, and no drill-down from an aggregate to a record outside the tenant (§42) |
| Support tooling | An agent viewing tenant A pastes data into tenant B's ticket | Support tooling is tenant-scoped per session, impersonation is explicit and audited (SUR-SEC-176), and copy of sensitive fields from support views is restricted |
| Marketplace | An agency's private data surfaces in a public listing | Marketplace projection is an allowlisted field set (SUR-SEC-084), built by a dedicated publisher, never by exposing the operational entity |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-132 | Each vector above shall have at least one automated test in the isolation suite (§38.9.3) that fails the build when the control regresses. |

#### 38.9.3 The mandatory tenant-isolation test suite

| Test | Method | Pass condition |
|---|---|---|
| TI-1 Object fetch across tenants | For every tenant-owned entity type, seed a record in tenant A and request it as an authorised user of tenant B, at every role | 404-equivalent, no data, no timing difference that distinguishes existence |
| TI-2 List/search across tenants | Query every list and search endpoint as tenant B with data present in tenant A | Zero records from tenant A, including total counts and facet counts |
| TI-3 Parameter injection | Supply `tenant_id`, `organization_id`, `agency_id` in query, body, header and path on every endpoint | Parameter ignored; session tenant governs |
| TI-4 Raw-query backstop | Execute the reporting and migration paths without a session tenant | Row-level security or the view layer denies |
| TI-5 Serialiser leak | Add a field to an entity without a permission mapping | Build fails |
| TI-6 Cache poisoning | Warm a cache as tenant A, request the same resource as tenant B | Distinct responses; a static check confirms tenant is in the key |
| TI-7 Export scope | Run every export as tenant B with tenant A data present | Row counts match the tenant-scoped control query exactly |
| TI-8 Notification routing | Trigger every notification type with adjacent tenants in the data | No delivery to a wrong-tenant recipient; mismatch counter stays zero |
| TI-9 AI retrieval | Ask the assistant for another tenant's data directly, and via an injected instruction planted in a free-text field | Refusal; retrieval trace shows no cross-tenant records |
| TI-10 File access | Attempt to fetch tenant A's object key as tenant B, and reuse a signed URL from a different session | Denied |
| TI-11 Branch scope | As a Branch Manager of branch 1, access branch 2 data within the same tenant | Denied where §31 says denied; tenant isolation not used as a substitute |
| TI-12 Suraksha cross-tenant roles | Exercise every Suraksha role's legitimate cross-tenant access | Access granted only where §31 grants it, target tenant recorded in the audit log on every request |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-133 | The tenant-isolation test suite (TI-1 to TI-12) shall run on every pull request and on a nightly schedule against a seeded multi-tenant dataset. A failure shall block merge and deploy, without exception and without an override path available to individual engineers. |
| SUR-SEC-134 | The isolation suite shall be data-driven from the entity registry (§32) and the endpoint registry (§33), so that a newly added entity or endpoint is covered automatically rather than depending on an engineer remembering to add a test. An entity or endpoint that the suite cannot cover automatically shall be listed as an explicit exclusion with an owner and a review date. |
| SUR-SEC-135 | A confirmed cross-tenant data exposure shall be a P0 security incident by definition, regardless of the number of records involved (§38.14). |

### 38.10 Infrastructure and CI/CD security

#### 38.10.1 Network segmentation and access

| Zone | Contents | Ingress | Egress |
|---|---|---|---|
| Z-0 Edge | CDN, WAF, load balancers, DDoS scrubbing | Internet | Z-1 only, on HTTPS |
| Z-1 Application | API tier, web servers, real-time gateway, worker pool | Z-0 only | Z-2, Z-3, egress proxy only |
| Z-2 Data | Primary database, replicas, cache, queue, search index | Z-1 only, on the specific ports | None to internet |
| Z-3 Media | Object storage for documents, photos, video | Z-1 and signed-URL access from Z-0 | None |
| Z-4 Management | CI/CD runners, observability, secrets store, admin tooling | Identity-aware proxy only, MFA-gated | Z-1, Z-2 for controlled operations |
| Z-5 Non-production | Dev, test, staging | Identity-aware proxy | No path to Z-1, Z-2, Z-3 of production |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-136 | Data stores shall have no public network endpoint. Object storage buckets shall have public access blocked at the account level, and a policy shall prevent an individual bucket from being made public. Infrastructure-as-code policy checks shall fail a plan that creates a publicly readable store or an unrestricted ingress rule. |
| SUR-SEC-137 | An asset inventory shall be maintained automatically for every compute, data, network and DNS resource, including owner, environment, data classification and exposure. An unowned or unclassified resource shall be reported weekly and removed or claimed within 30 days. DNS records pointing to decommissioned resources shall be detected and removed to prevent subdomain takeover. |
| SUR-SEC-138 | **No-SSH stance.** Interactive shell access to production compute shall be disabled by default; there is no SSH key distributed to engineers and no bastion host holding standing access. Operational tasks are performed through automation, deploy pipelines and purpose-built admin operations. Where an emergency requires a session, it is obtained through a cloud-provider session manager with identity-based authorisation, MFA, an approval, a time box (default 60 minutes), full session recording, and an automatic post-session review ticket. |
| SUR-SEC-139 | Human IAM access to production shall be role-based, granted through group membership tied to HR-managed identity, MFA-enforced, and reviewed quarterly with evidence retained. Standing administrative privileges shall be limited to a named, minimal set; all other elevated access is just-in-time with expiry. |
| SUR-SEC-140 | Workload identity shall be used for all service-to-cloud authentication. Long-lived static cloud access keys shall not exist in any environment; any discovered key is revoked immediately as an incident, not a task. |
| SUR-SEC-141 | Production and non-production shall be separate cloud accounts/projects with separate identity boundaries, separate keys, separate secrets, and no network path between them. A credential valid in one shall be invalid in the other. |
| SUR-SEC-142 | Infrastructure shall be defined as code, peer-reviewed, and applied only through the pipeline. Manual console changes to production shall be detected by drift detection within 24 hours, alerted, and either codified or reverted. |
| SUR-SEC-143 | Cloud security posture management shall run continuously against a documented baseline (encryption, public exposure, logging enabled, MFA on privileged identities, key rotation, unused-permission detection). Critical findings shall be remediated within the SLA in §38.13.2. |

#### 38.10.2 Container and image security

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-144 | Container images shall be built from a small, maintained base image; shall run as a non-root user with a read-only root filesystem and no privileged capabilities; and shall not include shells, package managers or build tooling in the final layer where avoidable. |
| SUR-SEC-145 | Images shall be scanned for known vulnerabilities at build and continuously in the registry. A build producing an image with a Critical or High vulnerability with a fix available shall fail; exceptions follow §38.13.4. |
| SUR-SEC-146 | Base images shall be rebuilt and redeployed on a schedule (at least monthly) even absent code changes, so that OS-level patches reach production without requiring a feature release. |
| SUR-SEC-147 | Images shall be signed at build and verified at admission; an unsigned or unverifiable image shall not run in production. A software bill of materials shall be generated per build and retained with the artefact. |
| SUR-SEC-148 | Dependencies shall be pinned by version and integrity hash, resolved from a controlled registry mirror, and screened for typosquatting and newly published packages before first use. Automated dependency-update pull requests shall run the full test suite including the isolation suite. |

#### 38.10.3 Pipeline security and change control

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-149 | The CI/CD pipeline shall enforce, as blocking gates on every change to a protected branch: SAST, secret scanning, dependency/SCA scan, licence check, unit and integration tests, the authorisation test matrix (SUR-SEC-051), and the tenant-isolation suite (SUR-SEC-133). |
| SUR-SEC-150 | DAST shall run against a deployed staging environment at least nightly and before every production release, covering authenticated flows for at least one role per role group. |
| SUR-SEC-151 | Code review shall require at least one approval from someone other than the author; changes touching authentication, authorisation, tenancy, payment, encryption, audit or the AI tool surface shall require an additional approval from a designated security reviewer. Self-approval and self-merge shall be impossible on protected branches. |
| SUR-SEC-152 | The pipeline shall have no ambient production credentials. Deployment uses short-lived, workload-scoped identity issued per run, and pipeline definitions themselves are protected branch content requiring review. |
| SUR-SEC-153 | Production deployment shall require a recorded approval from an authorised approver, shall be traceable from artefact to commit to reviewer, and shall be blocked during a declared production freeze except for an approved emergency change. Emergency changes shall be retro-reviewed within one business day. |
| SUR-SEC-154 | Build artefacts shall be immutable and content-addressed; the artefact deployed to production shall be the exact artefact that passed the gates, verified by digest at deploy time. |
| SUR-SEC-155 | Access to the source repository, artefact registry, secrets store and cloud consoles shall require MFA (phishing-resistant for administrative roles), shall be provisioned and de-provisioned through the HR joiner/leaver process, and shall be reviewed quarterly. |
