### 38.11 Logging, monitoring and detection

#### 38.11.1 Security event catalogue

Every event below is emitted as a structured record with a stable event code, and is available to detection rules. This is the security telemetry stream; it is related to, but distinct from, the audit log specified in §38.12 (audit answers "who did what to which record"; security events answer "what is happening to the platform"). Where an event is both, it is written once to the audit store and mirrored to the detection pipeline.

| Code | Event | Severity default |
|---|---|---|
| SE-01 | Successful login (with device, IP, method, MFA level) | P3 |
| SE-02 | Failed login | P3, aggregated |
| SE-03 | Lockout triggered | P2 |
| SE-04 | OTP requested / verified / failed / exhausted | P3, aggregated |
| SE-05 | MFA enrolled / removed / recovery code used | P2 |
| SE-06 | New device registered / device unbound / remote wipe issued | P2 |
| SE-07 | Password changed / reset / recovery performed | P2 |
| SE-08 | Phone number or email changed | P2 |
| SE-09 | Session revoked (self, admin, system) | P3 |
| SE-10 | Role, permission or scope changed | P1 |
| SE-11 | Tenant membership changed | P1 |
| SE-12 | Break-glass elevation requested / granted / used / expired | P1 |
| SE-13 | Impersonation ("view as") started / ended | P1 |
| SE-14 | Sensitive-field decryption for display (FE-1 to FE-6) | P2 |
| SE-15 | Document view / download of identity, verification or payroll documents | P2 |
| SE-16 | Export generated (type, row count, filters, destination) | P2 |
| SE-17 | Bulk read exceeding threshold (records returned per user per window) | P1 |
| SE-18 | Location history replay beyond 24h / bulk location export | P1 |
| SE-19 | Payout destination changed / payout approved / payroll run released | P1 |
| SE-20 | Refund, adjustment or ledger correction posted | P2 |
| SE-21 | Webhook signature verification failure | P2 |
| SE-22 | Authorisation denial (403) with actor, endpoint, object | P2, aggregated |
| SE-23 | Cross-tenant access attempt detected | P0 |
| SE-24 | WAF block / bot challenge failure / rate-limit exceedance | P3, aggregated |
| SE-25 | Malware scan positive / quarantine | P1 |
| SE-26 | Device integrity failure / mock-location detection | P2 |
| SE-27 | Screenshot attempt on a restricted screen | P3 |
| SE-28 | Configuration change to a security control (WAF rule, MFA policy, retention, integrity mode, IP allowlist) | P1 |
| SE-29 | Secret accessed by a human principal / secret rotated | P1 |
| SE-30 | Key used outside its normal workload or volume envelope | P1 |
| SE-31 | Admin/console action in a cloud account | P2 |
| SE-32 | Audit-store write failure or integrity-verification failure | P0 |
| SE-33 | AI interaction refused for scope, or AI output flagged for cross-tenant identifiers | P1 |
| SE-34 | Backup completed / restore test executed / restore performed | P2 |
| SE-35 | Deploy to production, including actor, artefact digest, approver | P3 |

#### 38.11.2 Detections that matter in this product

| Detection | Rule sketch | Response |
|---|---|---|
| D-1 Impossible travel | Two successful sessions for one identity whose geodesic separation implies > 900 km/h, excluding known VPN egress for staff | Revoke newer session, force MFA re-auth, P1 alert |
| D-2 Bulk export | Export rows or export count exceeds the role's rolling baseline by a configured factor, or exceeds an absolute per-day cap | Throttle, require approval for further exports, P1 alert with the export contents summary |
| D-3 Mass guard-record access | One actor opens more than N distinct guard records, or decrypts more than N identifiers, in a window | Soft-block with a purpose prompt, P1 alert to the tenant's Agency Owner and to Suraksha security |
| D-4 Roster harvesting by a client account | A client account enumerates guard detail beyond its site's active deployment, or pages deeply through guard lists | Throttle, P1 alert, review the account for legitimacy |
| D-5 Privilege change | Any role, permission, scope or tenant-membership change, especially self-affecting or outside business hours | P1 alert to security and to the tenant owner; change is already blocked from self-service where §31 forbids it |
| D-6 After-hours privileged admin access | Suraksha admin or agency privileged action outside the actor's normal window, weighted by sensitivity of the action | P2 alert; P1 if combined with export, payout or permission change |
| D-7 Repeated failed OTP | Failures per number, per IP, per ASN over thresholds; or a spray pattern across many numbers | Progressive challenge, block source, P1 if spray |
| D-8 Cross-tenant probing | Any 403/404 pattern consistent with tenant enumeration, or any hit on the cross-tenant assertion | P0 by SUR-SEC-135 if any data returned; P1 for repeated attempts |
| D-9 Location surveillance pattern | An actor repeatedly viewing the live location of one guard with no incident, ticket or duty relationship | P1 alert, purpose prompt, review — this is the stalking detection |
| D-10 Payout anomaly | New payee added and used within the hold window; multiple guards sharing one bank account; payee changed shortly after a phone-number change | Block, P0/P1 alert to Finance and security |
| D-11 Attendance-integrity cluster | A site or supervisor with an abnormal rate of mock-location flags, replayed selfies or out-of-geofence approvals | P2 alert to agency and Suraksha operations; investigation, not automatic penalty |
| D-12 Dormant admin awakening | An admin account unused for 30+ days performing a sensitive action | Force step-up, P1 alert |
| D-13 Audit anomaly | Gap in the audit hash chain, write failure, or a period with implausibly low audit volume | P0, incident declared |
| D-14 Data-store exposure | Posture management detects a store made public, or an unusual egress volume from Z-2/Z-3 | P0, contain immediately |
| D-15 Support impersonation misuse | Impersonation sessions above a per-agent threshold, impersonation without a linked ticket, or impersonation of a privileged user | P1, review |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-156 | Security events (SE-01 to SE-35) shall be shipped to a central, access-controlled analysis store within 60 seconds of occurrence, in a normalised schema carrying at minimum: event code, timestamp (UTC), actor, tenant, role, source IP, device, correlation/request ID, resource, outcome. |
| SUR-SEC-157 | The analysis store shall be a managed SIEM or an equivalent log-analytics platform with alerting, retention and role-based access. [RECOMMENDED] At MVP a managed cloud-native log platform with scheduled queries is acceptable; a dedicated SIEM is required by the phase in §38.15. |
| SUR-SEC-158 | Detection rules D-1 to D-15 shall exist with documented thresholds, an owner, a runbook link and a tested alert route. Each rule shall be exercised at least quarterly with a synthetic trigger to prove it still fires. |
| SUR-SEC-159 | Logs shall be scrubbed of sensitive values before write: no passwords, tokens, OTPs, keys, full identifiers, bank details, biometric data, exact coordinates in application logs, or document contents. Redaction shall be implemented in a shared logging library and enforced by a static rule; a log line containing an identifier-shaped value shall trigger an alert on the log pipeline itself. |
| SUR-SEC-160 | Security telemetry retention: hot and searchable for 90 days minimum, archived for the period set by the retention configuration (default 12 months, longer where the configured jurisdiction policy in §40 requires), with archives encrypted and access-controlled. Audit-log retention is separate and specified in §38.12.6. |
| SUR-SEC-161 | Alerting shall route by severity: P0 pages the on-call security responder immediately through a channel that does not depend on the platform itself; P1 pages during business hours and notifies out-of-hours; P2 creates a tracked ticket with an SLA; P3 is dashboard-only. Every P0 and P1 alert shall have a runbook. |
| SUR-SEC-162 | The security dashboard shall show, at minimum: authentication failure rate, lockouts, MFA coverage by role, open Critical/High vulnerabilities and their age, WAF block volume, cross-tenant assertion hits (target: zero), export volume by tenant and by actor, sensitive-decryption volume, break-glass sessions in the last 30 days, impersonation sessions in the last 30 days, and audit-chain verification status. |
| SUR-SEC-163 | Monitoring shall itself be monitored: absence of expected telemetry from any component for more than 10 minutes shall raise an alert, so that an attacker silencing a log source is detected by the silence. |

### 38.12 The audit system

This subsection is the canonical specification of the Audit Log (canon §3 entity `Audit Log`). Every other section that states "this action is audited" resolves to this specification and does not redefine the record.

#### 38.12.1 What the audit system is for

Four purposes, in priority order: (1) reconstructing what happened after a security or safety incident; (2) accountability for actions that affect a person's pay, employment, verification status or liberty of movement; (3) dispute resolution between agency, client and guard; (4) evidence for the compliance obligations configured in §40. It is not an application log and not an analytics stream.

#### 38.12.2 The mandatory audit record

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audit_id` | UUIDv7 | Yes | Immutable primary key, time-ordered |
| `occurred_at` | timestamp UTC | Yes | Server clock; for field-originated actions also `device_time` per canon §4 |
| `recorded_at` | timestamp UTC | Yes | When the audit store accepted it; a gap indicates queueing or tampering |
| `actor_type` | enum | Yes | User, System, Integration, AI, Scheduled Job |
| `actor_id` | ID | Yes | User ID, service identity, or job identity |
| `actor_display` | string | Yes | Name and employee/agency ID snapshot at the time, so the record stays readable after renames |
| `actor_role` | string | Yes | Role held at the moment of the action, snapshotted |
| `actor_scope` | JSON | Yes | Branch, state, city, site scope in effect |
| `organization_id` / `tenant_id` | ID | Yes | Owning tenant of the affected resource; `SURAKSHA-HQ` where applicable |
| `on_behalf_of_user_id` | ID | Conditional | Set when the action was performed under impersonation or delegated authority |
| `action` | string | Yes | Stable verb code, e.g. `guard.document.view`, `payroll.run.release` |
| `action_class` | enum | Yes | Read, Create, Update, Delete/Archive, Approve, Export, Auth, Config, Money |
| `resource_type` | string | Yes | Entity name from canon §3 |
| `resource_id` | ID | Yes | Affected record |
| `resource_label` | string | Yes | Human-readable snapshot (guard name masked per policy, site name, invoice number) |
| `previous_value` | JSON | Conditional | Field-level before state for the changed fields only |
| `new_value` | JSON | Conditional | Field-level after state for the changed fields only |
| `diff_summary` | string | Conditional | Human-readable one line for list rendering |
| `reason_code` | enum | Conditional | Required for sensitive reads, break-glass, overrides, exceptions |
| `reason_text` | string | Conditional | Free text where the reason code requires elaboration |
| `approval_id` | ID | Conditional | Links to the `Approval` record where the action required approval |
| `approver_id` / `approver_role` | ID / string | Conditional | Snapshot of who approved |
| `ai_interaction_id` | ID | Conditional | Where the action was AI-proposed (see §25) |
| `request_id` / `correlation_id` | string | Yes | Ties the audit record to logs, traces and downstream effects |
| `session_id` | ID | Yes | The session under which the action occurred |
| `source_ip` | string | Yes | Truncated where privacy policy requires; retained in full for security-class events |
| `device_id` / `user_agent` | string / string | Yes where applicable | Bound device for mobile; browser/app string for web |
| `geo_coarse` | string | Conditional | City/state derived from IP for authentication and sensitive-read events |
| `outcome` | enum | Yes | Success, Denied, Failed, Partial |
| `severity` | enum | Yes | P0–P3, aligned with canon alert severities |
| `record_hash` | string | Yes | Hash of the canonicalised record |
| `chain_hash` | string | Yes | Hash chaining this record to its predecessor in the tenant's audit stream |
| `schema_version` | int | Yes | Audit schema evolution |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-171 | Every audit record shall contain every field marked Required above. A write missing a required field shall be rejected at the audit-store boundary and shall raise SE-32; the originating action shall fail rather than proceed unaudited, for the action classes listed in §38.12.3 as mandatory-blocking. |
| SUR-SEC-172 | Audit writes shall be transactional with the business change for mandatory-blocking classes: either both commit or neither does. For non-blocking classes an asynchronous, at-least-once path with a durable queue and a reconciliation job is acceptable, and any loss shall be detectable and alerted. |
| SUR-SEC-173 | `previous_value` and `new_value` shall record only the fields that changed, shall never contain plaintext of FE-1 to FE-3 field classes (they record a masked form plus the fact of change), and shall be size-bounded with overflow stored as an attached document reference rather than truncated silently. |

#### 38.12.3 Which action classes must be audited

| Class | Examples | Audit | Blocking |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC-1 Authentication and session | Login, logout, MFA change, device bind, password/recovery, impersonation, break-glass | Always | Yes |
| AC-2 Authorisation change | Role, permission, scope, tenant membership, delegation, API credential create/revoke | Always, with before/after | Yes |
| AC-3 Money | Invoice issue, payment capture, refund, adjustment, payout, payroll run release, wallet movement, ledger correction, rate or contract value change | Always, with before/after and approval | Yes |
| AC-4 Person-affecting decisions | Verification status change, blacklist add/remove, termination, disciplinary record, attendance override, leave decision, salary or deduction change, training/qualification status | Always, with before/after and reason | Yes |
| AC-5 Sensitive read | Viewing or decrypting an identifier, bank detail, verification report, payslip, health record; viewing another person's location history; opening a document | Always | Yes |
| AC-6 Export and bulk operation | Any export, bulk update, bulk import, bulk message, mass assignment change | Always, with filters and row count | Yes |
| AC-7 Configuration | Security control change, retention change, notification policy, geofence definition, approval thresholds, integration credentials, compliance rule configuration | Always, with before/after | Yes |
| AC-8 Operational state change | Assignment create/change, shift change, roster publish, incident status change, SOS acknowledge/close, patrol exception approval, replacement | Always | No (async acceptable) |
| AC-9 Content and record edits | Client, site, post, guard profile edits; notes; documents attached or removed | Always, with before/after | No |
| AC-10 Deletion and archival | Any archive, any retention-driven purge, any legal-hold placement or release | Always, with counts and policy reference | Yes |
| AC-11 AI-proposed and AI-executed actions | Any action originating from an AI proposal | Always, linked by `ai_interaction_id` | Yes for Approval-required and Automated classes |
| AC-12 Audit access | Reading the audit log; exporting the audit log | Always, and itself audited | Yes |
| AC-13 Ordinary reads | Opening a list, viewing a dashboard | Not individually audited; captured as aggregate access telemetry (SE-17 covers bulk) | No |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-174 | Classes AC-1 to AC-7 and AC-10 to AC-12 are mandatory-blocking: the business action shall not complete if the audit record cannot be written. |
| SUR-SEC-175 | Ordinary reads (AC-13) shall not be individually audited, to keep the audit store legible and affordable; volume-based access telemetry and the bulk-read detection (D-3) cover the risk. This is a deliberate trade-off, stated so that no reader assumes per-read auditing exists where it does not. |
| SUR-SEC-176 | **Impersonation.** A support or administrative user acting as another user shall do so only through an explicit impersonation mode that: requires a reason code and a linked ticket; is time-boxed (default 60 minutes); is visibly banner-marked in the UI for the operator; is notified to the impersonated user for client and agency accounts unless the configured policy for fraud investigation suppresses it with a recorded approval; is restricted from money movement, permission change and identifier decryption; and stamps every resulting audit record with `on_behalf_of_user_id` and the operator's identity. |
| SUR-SEC-177 | Break-glass sessions (see §22) shall be audited at both the session level and the action level, shall be incapable of modifying or disabling audit logging, and shall generate a mandatory post-session review recorded against the session. |

#### 38.12.4 Tamper resistance

Absolute tamper-proofing is not achievable inside a system whose operators control the infrastructure. The goal is tamper-**evidence** strong enough that undetected alteration requires compromising several independent controls, plus an external copy that an internal actor cannot reach.

| Mechanism | Description |
|---|---|
| M-1 Append-only at the application layer | No update or delete path exists in the audit module. There is no "edit audit record" operation in any codebase, and the API surface offers only append and read |
| M-2 Database-level restriction | The audit table's application role holds INSERT and SELECT only; UPDATE and DELETE are not granted to any application principal. Deletion for retention runs under a separate, approved, audited job identity |
| M-3 Hash chaining | Each record carries `record_hash` and `chain_hash` linking it to its predecessor per tenant stream, so removal or alteration of any record breaks the chain from that point onward |
| M-4 Periodic anchoring | The chain head is anchored at a fixed interval (default hourly) by writing the head hash to a separate, write-once store in a different account with a different credential domain, and by including it in the daily security digest |
| M-5 Immutable secondary copy | Audit records are streamed continuously to write-once, retention-locked object storage in a separate cloud account whose delete permission is held by no production identity |
| M-6 Continuous verification | A verifier job recomputes the chain over a rolling window and over a random historical sample daily; any mismatch raises SE-32 / D-13 as a P0 incident |
| M-7 Separation of duties | The people who can administer production databases shall not be the people who hold the retention/delete role on the audit store or the delete permission on the immutable copy |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-178 | The audit store shall be append-only through mechanisms M-1 to M-3 at MVP, with M-5 immutable secondary copy also at MVP. M-4 anchoring and M-6 continuous verification shall be in place before the platform holds production payroll data for more than one agency. |
| SUR-SEC-179 | No role, including Super Admin and break-glass, shall be able to modify or delete an audit record through any product surface. Retention-driven purge is the only deletion path and it executes as a policy-driven job whose own execution is audited with counts and policy reference. |
| SUR-SEC-180 | Chain verification failure, audit-write failure, or an unexplained gap in audit volume shall be a P0 incident (§38.14) with mandatory management notification. |

#### 38.12.5 Who may read audit logs

| Role | Scope of audit visibility |

| Suraksha Super Admin | All tenants, all classes; reads are themselves audited and reviewed by the Auditor |
| Auditor (Suraksha) | All tenants, all classes, read-only and export-capable with approval; cannot be granted any write permission anywhere in the platform; cannot be removed by a single administrator |
| Compliance (Suraksha) | Compliance-relevant classes (AC-2, AC-3, AC-4, AC-7, AC-10) across tenants in scope |
| Finance (Suraksha) | AC-3 money class, all tenants in scope |
| Suraksha operations roles (National/State/City) | AC-8, AC-9 within their geographic scope; AC-4 where their role owns the decision |
| Support | Only records tied to the ticket's subject, within a bounded time window, and only for the tenant in question |
| Agency Owner, Agency Admin | Their own tenant only, all classes except platform-internal Suraksha actions, which appear as "Suraksha action" with actor role but not individual staff identity unless the configured transparency policy says otherwise |
| Agency Compliance, Payroll, Agency Finance | Their own tenant, their own class (AC-4/AC-3 respectively) |
| Branch Manager | Their branch only, AC-4, AC-8, AC-9 |
| Client Company Owner, Security Head | Their own organisation's records only: actions taken on their sites, their bookings, their invoices, and access to their site data (including which agency or Suraksha user viewed their site arrangements) |
| Guard | Their own record history: who viewed their documents, who changed their attendance, who changed their salary data, who viewed their location history (see §39.5) |
| Everyone else | Own-record history only, as rendered in-record |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-181 | Reading the audit log shall itself be audited (AC-12), including the filter used and the number of records returned. |
| SUR-SEC-182 | The Auditor role shall have read-only access with no write capability anywhere in the platform, shall not be assignable by a single administrator (two-person grant), and its own actions shall be visible to Super Admin and Founder/Management. This mutual visibility is deliberate: nobody watches nobody. |
| SUR-SEC-183 | A guard shall be able to see, in the Guard App, a plain-language history of who accessed their identity documents, their location history and their pay records, expressed as role and organisation (e.g. "Your supervisor at <agency> viewed your location history on 12 March"). Individual staff names are shown where the configured transparency policy allows and the tenant is the guard's own employer. |
| SUR-SEC-184 | Audit export shall be permission-gated, approved, watermarked, row-count-audited, and delivered through an authenticated download rather than email attachment. |

#### 38.12.7 Audit usability

An audit system nobody can read is a compliance artefact, not a control.

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-188 | Every entity detail screen shall carry a **History** panel rendering that record's audit trail in plain language: who, what changed, from what to what, when, and under which approval, with sensitive values masked per §39.7. |

| SUR-SEC-190 | Given a correlation ID from any incident, an investigator shall be able to retrieve the full causal chain — request, authorisation decision, audit records, notifications sent, money moved, AI interactions — in a single query. This end-to-end retrieval shall be exercised in the annual incident-response drill. |

### 38.13 Vulnerability management, testing and exceptions

#### 38.13.1 Sources of findings

| Source | Cadence | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| SCA / dependency scanning | Every build, plus daily re-scan of deployed versions | All application and infrastructure dependencies |
| Container/image scanning | Every build, plus continuous registry scan | All images |
| SAST | Every pull request | All first-party code |
| DAST | Nightly on staging, pre-release | Authenticated and unauthenticated flows |
| Cloud posture management | Continuous | All accounts |
| Secret scanning | Pre-commit, CI, continuous history scan | Repos, issue tracker, wiki |
| External attack-surface scan | Weekly | All public hosts, DNS, TLS, exposed ports |
| Penetration test | See §38.13.3 | Per scope statement |
| Bug bounty / responsible disclosure | Continuous | Public surfaces |
| Manual security review | Per epic touching sensitive areas | Design and code |

#### 38.13.2 Severity and remediation SLA

| Severity | Definition | Remediation SLA | Escalation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | Remote unauthenticated compromise, cross-tenant data access, authentication bypass, mass personal-data exposure, money movement without authorisation | Mitigate within 24 hours, fix within 7 days | CTO notified immediately; incident process if exploitation is plausible |
| High | Authenticated privilege escalation, IDOR on a sensitive object, stored XSS in an admin surface, exposure of a sensitive field to a role that should not see it, exploitable dependency with a public exploit | 14 days | Weekly review with the CTO |
| Medium | Issues requiring unusual conditions, information disclosure of low sensitivity, missing hardening | 60 days | Monthly review |
| Low | Best-practice deviations, defence-in-depth gaps | 180 days or accepted with rationale | Quarterly review |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-191 | Every finding shall be tracked in the standard issue tracker with severity, affected component, discovery source, owner and due date; findings shall not live only in a scanner. Ageing beyond SLA shall appear on the security dashboard and in the monthly management report. |
| SUR-SEC-192 | Severity shall be assigned using the finding's exploitability **in this system**, not the raw CVSS score. A Critical CVSS in a dependency that the platform does not call is not automatically Critical here; a Medium CVSS in the tenancy layer may be Critical here. The rationale shall be recorded. |
| SUR-SEC-193 | Any finding that exposes guard identity data, guard location, or client site security arrangements shall be treated as at least High, regardless of the number of records, because the harm is physical rather than statistical. |

#### 38.13.3 Penetration testing cadence

| Test | Frequency | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Full external application penetration test by an independent firm | Annually, and before the first Enterprise-tier customer goes live | All five web properties, the public API, and the authentication system |
| Mobile application penetration test | Annually, and on any major release of the Guard App or Admin App | All four apps, including offline storage, pinning, integrity handling |
| Multi-tenant isolation-focused test | Annually, and after any change to the tenancy layer | Tenancy, permissions, exports, search, AI retrieval, notifications |
| Cloud configuration review | Annually | All accounts, IAM, network, storage |
| Payment-flow and payout review | Annually, and on any change of payment or payout provider | End-to-end money path including webhooks and reconciliation |
| Internal red-team / assumed-breach exercise | From the phase in §38.15 | Insider scenarios: a compromised agency admin, a compromised support account |
| Retest of findings | Within 30 days of remediation | Previously identified issues only |

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-194 | Penetration-test scope shall explicitly include the critical-path threats in SUR-SEC-007, and the report shall state the tester's conclusion on each. A test that does not attempt cross-tenant access is not an acceptable test for this platform. |
| SUR-SEC-195 | Test findings shall enter the same tracker with the same SLAs; a Critical finding shall trigger the incident process if there is any indication of prior exploitation. |

### 38.14 Incident response

#### 38.14.1 Severity classes

| Class | Definition | Examples specific to Suraksha | Initial response |
|---|---|---|---|
| SEV-0 | Confirmed compromise of personal data, credentials or money at scale; cross-tenant data exposure; audit integrity failure; platform-wide compromise; any incident with an immediate physical-safety implication | Guard roster and site arrangements exfiltrated; live-location feed exposed; payroll diverted; audit chain broken | Immediate page, war room within 15 minutes, executive notification, containment before diagnosis |
| SEV-1 | Confirmed unauthorised access limited in scope; targeted account takeover; a working exploit against a Critical vulnerability; loss of a device holding cached operational data with signs of access | One agency's admin account taken over; a client account harvesting rosters; stolen supervisor phone with app lock defeated | Page during and outside business hours, contain within 1 hour |
| SEV-2 | Attempted but unsuccessful attack with evidence of targeting; credential exposure without confirmed use; misconfiguration exposing data with no evidence of access | Public bucket found and closed with no access logs; credential-stuffing campaign blocked | Response within 4 business hours |
| SEV-3 | Policy violations, isolated suspicious activity, single-user issues | One user sharing credentials; a single mock-location detection | Handled in normal workflow |

#### 38.14.2 Runbook

| Phase | Actions | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Detect and declare | Alert or report received; on-call assesses against §38.14.1 and declares a severity; a correlation ID and incident channel are opened; the clock starts and is recorded | Security on-call |
| 2. Mobilise | Incident commander named (never the same person as the primary investigator for SEV-0/1); scribe assigned; roles assigned for containment, forensics, communications, and — where guards or sites are at risk — field/operations liaison | Incident commander |
| 3. Contain | Revoke sessions and credentials; disable affected accounts or integrations; block source ranges; rotate keys; isolate a compromised workload; enable stricter WAF and rate limits; if site arrangements or guard locations may be exposed, notify Command Center so that at-risk deployments can be reinforced or altered | Containment lead |
| 4. Preserve evidence | Snapshot affected instances and volumes before remediation; export relevant audit and telemetry ranges to the evidence store; record every action taken with timestamps; do not "clean up" before capture | Forensics lead |
| 5. Investigate | Establish entry point, scope of access, data touched, persistence, and whether data left the platform; use the correlation-ID retrieval in SUR-SEC-190; quantify affected data subjects by category | Forensics lead |
| 6. Eradicate and recover | Remove access, patch, redeploy from known-good artefacts, restore from clean backups where needed, verify with targeted testing, monitor for recurrence at elevated sensitivity for 30 days | Engineering lead |
| 7. Notify | Execute the notification decision per §38.14.4 and §39.9; notify affected tenants, clients, guards and authorities as the configured policy requires; maintain a single factual public statement if the incident is public | Incident commander with management and counsel |
| 8. Review | Blameless post-incident review within 5 business days; timeline, root cause, contributing factors, detection gap, containment gap, and dated actions with owners | Incident commander |

#### 38.14.3 Physical-safety escalation

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-201 | Where an incident may have exposed live guard locations, guard home addresses, or client site security arrangements, the incident response shall include an operational limb: Command Center is informed, affected clients are contacted so that arrangements can be changed, affected guards are informed and, where the risk is specific, redeployed. This limb runs in parallel with technical containment and is not deferred to the notification phase. |
| SUR-SEC-202 | The incident severity matrix shall treat potential physical harm as a severity multiplier: an incident that would otherwise be SEV-2 becomes SEV-1, and SEV-1 becomes SEV-0, where a specific person or site is identifiable and at risk. |

#### 38.14.4 Notification obligations as configurable policy

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-203 | Breach-notification obligations differ by jurisdiction, by contract and by the category of data involved. The platform shall hold notification rules as configuration in the compliance engine (§40): trigger conditions, recipient classes (regulator, data subject, client, agency, insurer), deadlines, content templates and record-keeping requirements. Notification timing and thresholds shall never be hard-coded, and this document states product requirements, not legal advice; the configured values are set and reviewed by counsel for each jurisdiction of operation. |
| SUR-SEC-204 | The incident record shall capture the notification decision itself — decided by whom, on what date, on what basis, including a decision not to notify and its reasoning — and shall retain it for the audit retention period. |
| SUR-SEC-205 | Contractual notification commitments made to enterprise clients and agencies (typically expressed in hours) shall be recorded against the tenant so that the incident process can surface the tightest applicable commitment automatically rather than relying on someone remembering a contract term. |

#### 38.14.5 Preparedness

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SUR-SEC-206 | The incident-response plan shall be exercised at least annually with a tabletop covering at minimum one insider scenario and one cross-tenant exposure scenario, and at least annually with a technical drill covering credential revocation at scale, emergency key rotation (SUR-SEC-088), and restore from an immutable backup. |
| SUR-SEC-207 | On-call rotation, contact tree, out-of-band communication channel (independent of platform infrastructure and of the primary email provider), and counsel/insurer contacts shall be documented and tested quarterly. |
| SUR-SEC-208 | Every SEV-0 and SEV-1 incident shall produce dated remediation actions tracked to completion; an incident is not closed when service is restored, it is closed when the actions are done or formally accepted as risk. |
| SUR-SEC-209 | An evidence store shall exist with restricted access, write-once retention and its own audit, so that forensic artefacts cannot be altered by the same identities that administer production. |
| SUR-SEC-210 | Third-party and sub-processor incidents shall be handled under the same process; contracts shall require prompt notification to Suraksha, and the vendor register (§39.8) shall record each vendor's notification commitment and security contact. |

### 38.15 Security requirements by phase

The honest position: most of a security programme can be phased, but a platform holding guard identity data, live locations and site security arrangements cannot phase the controls that prevent a mass leak or an untraceable insider action. The MVP-mandatory column below is not aspirational — a release that fails it does not ship.

| Area | MVP — mandatory, release-blocking | Phase 2 (first 6–12 months post-launch) | Phase 3 / Enterprise readiness |
|---|---|---|---|
| Identity | Argon2id + pepper (SUR-SEC-012), breached-password screening, OTP rate limits and expiry (SUR-SEC-015/016), enumeration resistance (017), MFA mandatory for Suraksha staff and agency privileged roles (018/022), progressive lockout (034), token model with rotation and revocation (§38.3.4), device binding for guards (028–030), login history (031) | Passkeys/WebAuthn as the default second factor, risk-based step-up scoring (S-1 to S-10 fully weighted), SIM-swap signal integration if an aggregator is available | SSO/SAML/SCIM for enterprise clients and large agencies, hardware-key enforcement for the highest-privilege roles |
| Application security | Server-side validation and schema enforcement (036/037), parameterised queries (040), contextual encoding (038), CSP (042), CSRF (044), SSRF-safe fetcher (045), mass-assignment DTOs (054), file-upload controls and malware scanning (§38.4.5), signed short-lived media URLs (053) | Automated authorisation test matrix at full endpoint coverage (051), formula-injection and export hardening at full coverage, deserialization hardening across all queue paths | Continuous DAST across all roles, fuzzing of the field-event ingest path |
| Tenancy | All four enforcement layers (128–131), the isolation test suite TI-1 to TI-12 running in CI (133), fail-closed authorisation (047) | Registry-driven auto-coverage of new entities/endpoints (134), isolation-focused external test | Formal tenancy verification, per-tenant key separation for the largest tenants |
| Data | Encryption at rest everywhere (086), TLS 1.2+/1.3 with the specified profile (§38.5.1), KMS-managed keys (087), secrets manager with no secrets in code (094–097), field-level encryption for FE-1, FE-2, FE-3 (§38.6.3), no card data (090), no production data in lower environments (100) | Field-level encryption extended to FE-4 to FE-6, blind-index rotation tooling, bulk-decryption approval workflow (093), automated key-rotation exercises | Customer-managed keys for Enterprise tenants, data-residency options beyond the default (§39.8) |
| Mobile | Secure storage for tokens (104), encrypted offline store with the cache scope in §38.7.2 (105/108), no sensitive data in logs (106), screenshot blocking on restricted screens (116), app lock for Admin and Agency apps (117), remote wipe (110) | Certificate pinning with the backup-pin and expiry design (114), platform attestation in Monitor mode (111/112), mock-location signal fusion (113) | Restrict/Block integrity modes for agencies issuing devices, tamper-response telemetry, per-tenant mobile policy |
| Location and site data | Duty-bounded collection (120), client-sees-own-site-only (124), site-arrangements confidentiality class (125/126), retention limits (§39.2) | Purpose prompts and reason codes on historical replay (123), stalking detection D-9, gap-inference suppression in analytics | Client-configurable stricter retention, per-site access review reports |
| Infrastructure | No public data stores (136), separate prod/non-prod accounts (141), IaC with policy checks (142), no standing SSH (138), MFA on all cloud access (155), workload identity with no static keys (140) | Posture management with SLA-tracked findings (143), monthly base-image rebuilds (146), signed images with admission verification (147), SBOM retention | Network micro-segmentation, service mesh mTLS, just-in-time access for all human operations |
| CI/CD | SAST, SCA, secret scanning and the isolation suite as blocking gates (149), two-person review with a security reviewer on sensitive paths (151), no ambient production credentials in the pipeline (152), deployment approval and traceability (153) | Nightly DAST (150), dependency auto-update with full-suite verification, provenance attestation | Full supply-chain attestation, reproducible builds, hardware-backed signing |
| Logging and detection | Security event catalogue emitted (156), log redaction (159), P0/P1 alert routing with runbooks (161), detections D-1, D-2, D-3, D-5, D-7, D-8, D-13 | Full detection set D-1 to D-15, dedicated SIEM (157), quarterly detection testing (158), telemetry-absence alerting (163) | 24/7 monitoring coverage, threat-intel enrichment, user-behaviour analytics |

## 39. Privacy

### 39.1 Scope and stance

This section states **product requirements** for how Suraksha handles personal data. It is not legal advice and it does not assert what any law requires. Jurisdiction-specific obligations — lawful bases, notice content, retention floors and ceilings, breach-notification triggers and deadlines, cross-border conditions, and the treatment of government identifiers — are held as **configuration** in the compliance engine (§40), populated and reviewed by counsel for each jurisdiction of operation, and are never hard-coded into application logic (canon §0). Where this section names a default, it is a build-safe default, not a legal conclusion.

The privacy design problem here is unusual in three ways, and the section is written around them:

1. **The most sensitive data belongs to the least powerful people.** Guards are low-wage workers whose employer decides whether they eat next month. Consent obtained from them is not freely given in the ordinary sense, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest engineering. §39.5 addresses this directly.
2. **Some personal data is also physical-safety data.** A guard's live location and a client's site arrangements are not merely private; disclosure can get someone hurt. Privacy controls here overlap with the security controls in §38.8 and are enforced by the same mechanisms.
3. **The platform sits between three parties with conflicting interests** — the client wants maximum visibility, the agency wants maximum control, the guard is the data subject. The product resolves these conflicts with explicit rules, not with whatever the paying party asks for.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRV-001 | Every personal-data field in the platform shall be registered in the data inventory (§39.2) with purpose, subjects, retention, storage location, access roles, masking rule and deletion behaviour. A field not in the inventory shall not be added to any schema; the schema review gate (§39.10) enforces this. |
| SUR-PRV-002 | Lawful basis, notice text, retention values, consent requirements and cross-border conditions shall be configuration per jurisdiction and per tenant, sourced from §40. The application shall read them; it shall not embed them. |
| SUR-PRV-003 | Where the platform cannot satisfy a configured privacy rule (for example, a retention period shorter than an operational dependency allows), it shall fail visibly to Compliance with a named conflict, rather than silently applying the looser rule. |
| SUR-PRV-004 | Privacy settings shall default to the most protective usable state (canon principle P7); loosening any of them is an audited configuration action (AC-7, §38.12.3). |

---

### 39.2 The data inventory

Every category of personal data the platform touches. Categories marked with a purpose of "not collected" appear because a reader would otherwise assume they exist.

#### 39.2.1 Categories, purpose, basis and subjects

| ID | Category and typical fields | Purpose | Legal-basis approach (configured) | Data subjects |
|---|---|---|---|---|

|---|---|
| SUR-PRV-005 | The inventory above shall be maintained as living configuration, not a document: each category is a record in the platform's data-catalogue with its retention, classification and masking rule referenced by the runtime, so that a change to a retention default takes effect in the purge job without a code change. |

### 39.3 Privacy principles applied

#### 39.3.1 Data minimisation — what Suraksha deliberately will not collect

Minimisation is only meaningful if it is specific. The following are explicit non-collection decisions, and each is a requirement, not a preference.

| ID | Not collected | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-PRV-010 | **Off-duty location of any guard.** No background location collection outside the duty window plus its configured grace period, ever, under any tenant configuration. | Continuous tracking of a worker's private life is not necessary for the service and is not offered as a paid feature. |
| SUR-PRV-011 | **Raw biometric images or templates stored by Suraksha.** Face verification uses a vendor reference or an on-device template; the platform stores a reference, not a biometric. | A stolen biometric cannot be reissued. |
| SUR-PRV-012 | **Payment card numbers, CVV or full card data.** | Provider-hosted collection only (SUR-SEC-090). |
| SUR-PRV-013 | **Guard family members' personal data**, beyond a single emergency contact name, relationship and phone. | No operational need. |
| SUR-PRV-014 | **Caste, religion, political affiliation, trade-union membership or sexual orientation**, in any field, free-text-derived tag, or inferred attribute. Free-text fields shall not be mined to derive such attributes, and no filter, sort or search facet shall exist on them. | Discrimination risk in a hiring-heavy workflow. |
| SUR-PRV-015 | **Health data beyond blood group, emergency contact, and duty-relevant restrictions.** No general medical history, no diagnosis codes, no prescriptions. | Not needed to deploy a guard. |
| SUR-PRV-016 | **Continuous audio recording from guard devices.** Audio is captured only on an explicit, user-initiated action (e.g. an SOS voice note) and never ambiently. | Ambient recording is surveillance of the guard and of everyone near them. |
| SUR-PRV-017 | **Access to the guard's phone contacts, photo gallery, SMS or call logs.** The app requests camera, location and notification permissions only, plus storage scoped to its own files. | Nothing in the product needs them. |
| SUR-PRV-018 | **Client-visible guard home address, personal phone number, salary, or identity-document content.** Clients receive a verification status, a name, a photo, and a masked contact channel. | A client does not need to be able to find a guard's home. |
| SUR-PRV-019 | **Behavioural profiling of guards for purposes outside duty performance** — no "productivity score" built from location dwell time, no inference of health, fatigue or personal habits from movement data. Operational metrics are limited to the defined attendance, patrol and incident measures in §42. | The data would support inference far beyond its purpose. |
| SUR-PRV-020 | **Third-party ad-tech trackers on authenticated surfaces.** Marketing analytics exist on public marketing pages under the configured consent rule; no third-party tracker runs inside the customer portal, agency portal, OPS, or any mobile app. | Authenticated surfaces contain operational data. |
| SUR-PRV-021 | **Cross-tenant behavioural data sale or brokerage.** Aggregate market insight may be published only above the minimum-cohort thresholds in §42, and personal data is never sold, licensed or brokered. | Non-negotiable. |

#### 39.3.2 The other principles

| ID | Principle | Applied requirement |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-PRV-022 | Purpose limitation | Every data category has a declared purpose (§39.2.1). Using a category for a new purpose requires a recorded purpose change, a privacy review (§39.10), and — where the configured basis is consent — fresh consent. Location data has an explicit prohibition on secondary use (SUR-PRV-034). |
| SUR-PRV-023 | Storage limitation | Retention is enforced by an automated purge, not by policy text (SUR-PRV-007). Every category has a default and a ceiling. |
| SUR-PRV-024 | Accuracy | Data subjects can correct their own contact details, address and emergency contacts directly; corrections to verification, employment and payroll records go through a request workflow with an owner and an SLA (§39.6). Every correction is audited with before/after. |
| SUR-PRV-025 | Integrity and confidentiality | Enforced by §38; privacy controls do not restate them. |
| SUR-PRV-026 | Accountability | The data inventory, consent records, DSR log, DPIA register, vendor register, breach register and audit log together constitute the evidence base, and each is queryable by Compliance and Auditor. |
| SUR-PRV-027 | **Government identifiers** | The platform shall treat any government identifier as usable **only** for the specific, configured, consented purpose recorded against it, and shall not assume any general right to store or use it. Concretely: (a) the identifier is stored encrypted with a blind index and last-4 display (FE-1); (b) it is never a login identifier, never a primary key, never a search facet, and never exported in bulk; (c) an alternative accepted document shall exist wherever the configured policy permits one, and the alternative shall not degrade the person's access to work; (d) where the configured policy for a jurisdiction prohibits storage, the platform shall store only the verification outcome and a vendor reference; (e) the purpose, basis and consent for each identifier are recorded per person and are withdrawable where the configured basis is consent. |

### 39.4 Consent

#### 39.4.1 What requires consent

| ID | Processing | Consent stance |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-PRV-030 | Core service delivery — deployment, attendance, payroll, invoicing, incident handling | Contract necessity as configured; consent is not the basis and shall not be simulated with a checkbox that cannot be declined |
| SUR-PRV-031 | Government identifier storage and use (DP-02) | Explicit, granular, withdrawable, purpose-named consent, plus the configured jurisdiction rule |
| SUR-PRV-032 | Biometric face verification (DP-09) | Explicit consent, with a non-biometric attendance alternative always offered and equally functional |
| SUR-PRV-033 | Background verification beyond the statutory police verification (DP-12) | Explicit consent, with the scope of checks named |
| SUR-PRV-034 | Health data (DP-15) | Explicit consent; emergency use during an active incident proceeds on a vital-interest basis with after-the-fact notice to the guard |
| SUR-PRV-035 | Body-camera or continuous video capture (DP-19) | Explicit consent from the wearer, plus the configured signage and notice obligations for those recorded; [FUTURE], DPIA-gated |
| SUR-PRV-036 | Marketing communications and non-essential analytics (DP-27) | Opt-in consent, granular by channel, withdrawable in one action |
| SUR-PRV-037 | Marketplace listing of a guard's profile to prospective employers (Trinetra / guard platform) | Explicit opt-in, with a preview of exactly what a viewer sees, and the ability to hide from specific agencies |
| SUR-PRV-038 | Sharing a guard's profile with a client beyond the minimum operational set | Explicit consent per field class, defaulting to the minimum set |
| SUR-PRV-039 | Call recording in support or masked-call flows (DP-20, DP-25) | Notice to both parties and the configured consent rule; recording off by default |

#### 39.4.2 How consent is captured

| Audience | Mechanism | Evidence recorded |
|---|---|---|
| Guard (app, in the guard's language) | Layered notice: a one-screen plain-language summary with icons, expandable detail, and separate toggles per consent item. Read-aloud available for low-literacy users. No pre-ticked boxes. No bundling of core-service acceptance with optional consents | Consent record: subject, item, version of the notice text, language shown, timestamp, method, device, IP, and the exact rendered text hash |
| Guard (assisted onboarding at an agency office) | The same screens, on the guard's own device where possible; where an agency staff member operates the device, the record captures the assisting user's identity and the guard confirms by OTP to their own number | As above plus `assisted_by_user_id` and OTP confirmation reference |
| Client (individual customer) | Standard web/app consent at signup and at the point of each optional processing | As above |
| Client (organisation) | Contractual for core processing; individual consents for the named contacts' marketing preferences | Contract reference plus per-contact records |
| Agency | Contractual at subscription; separate consents for marketplace visibility and for marketing | As above |
| Website visitor | Cookie/consent banner per the configured policy, with reject-all as prominent as accept-all | Consent string, timestamp, policy version |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRV-040 | Every consent shall be stored as an immutable record including the exact notice version and language presented, and shall be reproducible on demand: given a person and a date, the platform shall render what they actually saw. |
| SUR-PRV-041 | Consent shall be granular per purpose. A single "I agree" covering identity storage, biometrics, background checks and marketing shall not exist. Declining an optional consent shall not block onboarding or reduce shift allocation, and the platform shall not expose consent status as a filter or sort in any roster, allocation or recruitment screen. |
| SUR-PRV-042 | Withdrawal shall be available in the same place as granting, in one action, in the user's language, and shall take effect within 24 hours across all processing that depends on it. |
| SUR-PRV-043 | Consent notices shall be versioned; a material change shall require re-consent rather than a silent update, and the platform shall track who has consented to which version. |

#### 39.4.3 Withdrawal and its operational consequences

Withdrawal must be honest about what stops working, without being used as a threat.

| Withdrawn consent | Operational consequence | What must NOT happen |
|---|---|---|
| Biometric verification | Attendance reverts to the non-biometric method (geofence + selfie + supervisor verification). No change to pay, allocation or standing | The guard being deprioritised for shifts, or the withdrawal being visible to allocation logic |
| Government identifier storage | The stored identifier value is purged where no configured obligation retains it; the verification outcome and vendor reference survive; if the configured policy for the jurisdiction makes deployment impossible without it, the platform shall state that specific consequence at the point of withdrawal, referencing the configured rule | A generic "you cannot work" message unsupported by a configured rule |
| Marketplace visibility | The profile is delisted within 24 hours; existing conversations are retained per DP-20 | Retaining the listing "because a recruiter is mid-conversation" |
| Marketing | All marketing channels stop within 24 hours; transactional and safety messages continue and are clearly distinguished | Safety/duty notifications being suppressed as "marketing" |
| Health data | The record is deleted; emergency contact is retained as a separate item with its own consent | Deleting the emergency contact silently, leaving no one to call |
| Background verification (future checks) | No further checks are initiated; existing results are retained per DP-12 retention | Re-running a check on the basis of an old consent |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRV-044 | The consequence of withdrawing each consent shall be shown to the user **before** they confirm withdrawal, in plain language, generated from the configured rule rather than written as static marketing-safe text. |
| SUR-PRV-045 | Consent status shall not be an input to shift allocation, rating, or any ranking visible to an agency, and the AI platform shall not use it as a feature (§41). |

### 39.5 The guard privacy question

Continuous location tracking of low-wage workers is the most ethically serious thing this platform does. The product's position is that tracking is justified only as narrowly as the operational purpose requires, that the worker must be able to see exactly what is held about them, and that the data must not become a general-purpose management surveillance tool. These are product requirements, enforced in code, not statements of intent.

#### 39.5.1 Tracking boundaries

| ID | Boundary | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-PRV-050 | **On-duty only.** Location collection starts at check-in and stops at check-out, with a configurable grace window (default 15 minutes each side, ceiling 30). The app shall not hold a background location permission that operates outside this window, and the server shall reject out-of-window location events (SUR-SEC-120) | App-side duty-state gating plus server-side rejection; both are required so that neither alone can be defeated |
| SUR-PRV-051 | **Geofence-scoped by default.** For static guarding posts, the platform stores geofence compliance (inside/outside, entry/exit, dwell) rather than a continuous coordinate trail. A full coordinate trail is retained only for mobile duties — patrols, escorts, PSO details, and active incidents | Duty-type configuration determines the collection profile |
| SUR-PRV-052 | **No off-duty tracking, at any price.** There is no tenant setting, plan tier, enterprise contract or API that enables location collection outside the duty window. Requests for it are refused at product level | Absence of the capability, verified by a test that asserts out-of-window events are rejected regardless of tenant configuration |
| SUR-PRV-053 | **Frequency proportionate.** Default 60-second interval on duty; higher frequency only during an active patrol or an active SOS; movement-triggered sampling when static | Configurable within a platform ceiling |
| SUR-PRV-054 | **Visible when active.** The Guard App shall show an unambiguous, always-visible indicator when location is being collected, and a one-tap explanation of who can see it right now | Persistent UI element plus the OS-level indicator |
| SUR-PRV-055 | **Emergency exception, bounded.** During an active SOS the collection frequency increases and the audience widens to the Command Center; this is explained in the notice, is time-bounded to the incident plus a configured window, and every widened-access view is audited | Incident-state-driven, auto-reverting |
| SUR-PRV-056 | **Retention limited.** Raw tracks 90 days by default (DP-10), derived duty summaries 12 months. A tenant may shorten these; nothing may lengthen the raw-track ceiling | Purge job with audited counts |

#### 39.5.2 Transparency to the guard

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRV-057 | The Guard App shall include a **"My Data"** area, in the guard's language, showing: what is collected and when, the current retention periods, their own location history on a map for the retained window, who has viewed it and when (SUR-SEC-183), their documents and their status, their attendance and pay records, their consent choices with withdrawal, and a request path for correction, export and deletion. |
| SUR-PRV-058 | The guard shall receive a plain-language, worker-facing disclosure at onboarding — not a legal document — covering: that they are tracked while on duty and only then; what their supervisor, their agency and the client can each see; how long it is kept; what it may and may not be used for; how to see it themselves; and how to complain. It shall be presented in the guard's language, read aloud on request, and acknowledged with a record (§39.4.2). |
| SUR-PRV-059 | Any change to the tracking configuration affecting a guard (frequency, retention, duty-type profile, who can view) shall be notified to the affected guards before it takes effect, with the change described in plain language. |
| SUR-PRV-060 | The guard shall be able to see, per view event, the role and organisation of the viewer and the stated reason where a reason code was required, and shall be able to raise a query on any view they consider unjustified, routed to their agency's compliance contact with a copy to Suraksha Compliance. |

#### 39.5.3 Prohibited uses

| ID | Prohibition |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRV-061 | Location and duty data shall not be used to infer or record anything about a guard's private life, religion, health, associations or movements outside duty; no such field, derived attribute or report shall exist. |
| SUR-PRV-062 | Location data shall not be used as the sole basis for a disciplinary or pay decision. A geofence anomaly generates a review item with the evidence shown to the guard and a right to respond; the decision is made by a person and is recorded as an AC-4 audited action. |
| SUR-PRV-063 | Location data shall not be shared with any third party other than the serving agency, the client for their own site during duty, and emergency services during an active incident. It shall not be provided in response to an informal request, and any lawful-authority request shall follow the documented process in §40 with a recorded decision. |
| SUR-PRV-064 | Location data shall not be used to build cross-tenant products (heatmaps, movement datasets, "market intelligence") in any form from which an individual or an individual site is derivable, and shall not be sold, licensed or brokered in any form (SUR-PRV-021). |
| SUR-PRV-065 | Location data shall not be sent to a model provider or used to train any model (§41). AI features that reason about duty compliance shall operate on derived, minimised signals (on-time, in-geofence, patrol completion) rather than raw coordinates. |
| SUR-PRV-066 | Suspected misuse of location access — including the stalking-pattern detection D-9 — shall be treated as a security incident and a privacy incident, investigated, and reported to the affected guard where the investigation confirms it. |

#### 39.5.4 The consent honesty problem

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRV-067 | The platform shall not present tracking consent as if it were freely given where refusing it would end the guard's employment. Where the configured basis for on-duty tracking is contract necessity, the notice shall say so plainly ("this is part of the job, here is exactly what it covers and what it does not"), rather than presenting a consent checkbox the guard cannot meaningfully decline. Where a processing activity is genuinely optional (biometrics, marketplace listing, marketing, background checks beyond the statutory), the toggle shall be real and refusal shall be consequence-free (SUR-PRV-041). |
| SUR-PRV-068 | Because consent from a guard is structurally weaker than consent from a client, the platform shall compensate with structural controls rather than paperwork: hard limits that no tenant can raise (SUR-PRV-052, -056), transparency by default (SUR-PRV-057), prohibitions enforced by the absence of the capability (SUR-PRV-061 to -065), and access logging visible to the guard (SUR-SEC-183). |
| SUR-PRV-069 | A guard shall have a route to raise a privacy complaint that does not go through their employer: an in-app path to Suraksha Compliance, with the complaint visible to the agency only in anonymised aggregate unless the guard consents to disclosure, and with a documented anti-retaliation position recorded against the agency's platform terms. [DECISION REQUIRED: D-333] |

### 39.6 Data subject rights

Rights are configured per jurisdiction (§40); the platform implements the capability so that a configured right can be exercised without engineering work.

| ID | Right | Implementation | SLA (default, configurable) |
|---|---|---|---|
| SUR-PRV-070 | Access — what do you hold about me | Self-service first: the "My Data" area (guards), account data page (clients, agency users). Anything not self-service is a request producing a structured report of categories, purposes, recipients, retention and sources | Self-service immediate; request acknowledged in 3 business days, fulfilled in 30 calendar days |
| SUR-PRV-071 | Correction | Self-service for contact details, address, emergency contact, language, notification preferences. Request workflow for verification, employment, attendance and payroll records, routed to the owning role with evidence attached | Acknowledged 3 days; resolved 15 days; disputed corrections recorded as a dispute note attached to the record |
| SUR-PRV-072 | Export / portability | Machine-readable export (JSON + CSV) of the subject's own records, delivered through an authenticated download, generated asynchronously, notified on completion, link expiring in 7 days | 7 calendar days |
| SUR-PRV-073 | Deletion / erasure | Executed as: delete what has no retention obligation; anonymise what must survive as an operational or financial record (SUR-PRV-008); retain under legal hold what is held; and report back to the subject, per category, exactly what was deleted, what was anonymised, what was retained and under which configured rule | Acknowledged 3 days; executed 30 days |
| SUR-PRV-074 | Objection / restriction | The subject may object to a specific processing purpose; the platform marks the affected processing as restricted, which suppresses non-essential uses (marketing, marketplace visibility, optional analytics) while core service processing continues where the configured basis permits | 7 calendar days |
| SUR-PRV-075 | Rights relating to automated decisions | Where an automated or AI-assisted process contributes to a decision affecting a person (allocation ranking, verification flag, attendance rejection, blacklist proposal), the person may request the basis, and a human review path exists. AI never makes these decisions autonomously (canon §1.7, §41) | Explanation 7 days; human review 15 days |
| SUR-PRV-076 | Complaint | In-app and email routes; for guards, a route independent of their employer (SUR-PRV-069) | Acknowledged 3 days |

#### 39.6.1 The deletion-versus-retention conflict, stated honestly

Deletion requests will frequently conflict with retention obligations: a guard who leaves and asks for erasure is attached to payroll records, statutory employment records, incident records that may be evidence, and financial ledger entries that cannot be rewritten (BR-003). The platform's answer is a per-category resolution, computed and shown, never a blanket refusal and never a blanket deletion.

| Category | On an erasure request |
|---|---|
| DP-01, DP-02, DP-03, DP-09 | Identifier values and biometric references purged unless a configured obligation retains them; document images purged at the configured floor; the verification **outcome** retained as a status without content where an obligation applies |
| DP-04 | Purged; historical payouts retain a non-reversible reference |
| DP-05, DP-06, DP-07, DP-08 | Purged or replaced with a surrogate, except where needed to identify the subject of a retained statutory record |
| DP-10 | Purged immediately, subject to any active investigation hold |
| DP-11, DP-12 | Retained where a configured obligation applies, restricted to Compliance-only access; otherwise purged |
| DP-13, DP-14 | Retained under the configured employment and payroll record obligation; access narrowed to Payroll and Compliance; the person's contact details detached |
| DP-15 | Purged |
| DP-18, DP-19 | Retained where the incident is subject to a claim, dispute, hold or configured obligation; the subject's identifying details minimised in copies shared with clients |
| DP-24 | Ledger entries never deleted; counterparty identity replaced with a surrogate where the configured rule permits |
| DP-20, DP-22, DP-25, DP-26, DP-27 | Purged |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRV-077 | Every data-subject request shall be recorded in a DSR register with subject, request type, receipt date, identity-verification method, categories affected, actions taken per category, the configured rule relied on for any retention, decision maker, and completion date. The register is auditable and reportable. |
| SUR-PRV-078 | Requester identity shall be verified proportionately — for an account holder, authenticated session plus step-up; for a former guard without account access, an OTP to the registered number plus a documented alternative where the number is lost, never a demand for a fresh copy of an identity document as the only option. |
| SUR-PRV-079 | A request shall not be refused because it is inconvenient, and shall not be silently partially fulfilled. Every refusal or partial fulfilment shall name the configured rule relied on and shall be reviewable by Compliance. |
| SUR-PRV-080 | Requests arriving through an agency about their own guard shall be routed to the guard for confirmation where the request would reduce the guard's own access to their data, so that an employer cannot exercise a worker's rights against them. |
| SUR-PRV-081 | DSR SLA breaches shall alert Compliance at 75% of the elapsed SLA, and the DSR queue shall appear on the Compliance dashboard with ageing. |

### 39.7 Masking and access rules

The authoritative role-by-permission matrix is §31; this table specifies **field-level visibility** for sensitive fields only, expressed by role group, and §31 consumes it. Where the two ever disagree, §31 governs the permission and this table governs the rendering.

Legend: **F** = full value · **M** = masked · **S** = status/derived only · **–** = not visible · **F\*** = full value only after step-up plus purpose code, and audited as a sensitive read (SE-14)

| Sensitive field | Guard (self) | Agency ops roles | Agency HR/Payroll/Compliance | Suraksha ops | Suraksha Verification/Compliance/Finance | Client roles |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Government identifier (DP-02) | M (last 4) | – | F\* (Compliance/Payroll where purpose configured) | – | F\* | – |
| Identity document image (DP-01) | F (own) | – | F\* watermarked | – | F\* watermarked | – |
| PAN (DP-03) | M | – | F\* (Payroll) | – | F\* (Finance) | – |
| Bank / UPI (DP-04) | F (own) | – | F\* (Payroll) | – | F\* (Finance) | – |
| Guard personal phone (DP-05) | F (own) | M + masked-call channel | F | M + masked-call channel | F\* | – (masked channel only) |
| Guard home address (DP-07) | F (own) | S (city/state) | F | S (city/state) | F\* | – |
| Guard photo (DP-08) | F (own) | F | F | F | F | F (on-duty guards at own site only) |
| Attendance selfie (DP-08) | F (own) | F (own guards) | F | F | F | S (attendance status only) |
| Biometric reference (DP-09) | S (enrolled yes/no) | – | S | – | S | – |
| Live location (DP-10) | F (own) | F (own guards, on duty) | – | F (in scope) | – | F (own site, on duty, current only) |
| Location history (DP-10) | F (own, retained window) | F\* (reason code beyond 24h) | – | F\* | – | S (duty compliance summary for own site) |
| Police verification (DP-11) | S + own copy | S | F\* | S | F\* | S |
| Background verification (DP-12) | S + own copy | S | F\* | S | F\* | S |
| Salary / payslip (DP-14) | F (own) | – | F (Payroll) | – | F\* (Finance) | – |
| Health / emergency contact (DP-15) | F (own) | – (except during active SOS) | F (HR) | S; F during active SOS (Command Center) | – | – |
| Client contact details (DP-16) | – | F (serving roles) | – | F | F | F (own org) |
| Site security arrangements (DP-17) | S (own post only) | F (serving sites) | – | F (in scope) | – | F (own sites) |
| Incident narrative (DP-18) | F (own involvement) | F (own sites) | S | F | F | F (own sites, third-party details masked) |
| Ledger / invoice detail (DP-24) | – | S | – | S | F | F (own org) |
| Audit log (§38.12.5) | S (own-record access history) | S | S (own tenant class) | S (scope) | F (Compliance/Auditor) | S (own org) |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRV-085 | Masking shall be applied server-side at serialisation (SUR-SEC-131). A masked value shall never be transmitted in full to a client that must not display it, and unmasking shall be a separate, permissioned, audited request — never a client-side toggle over data already delivered. |
| SUR-PRV-086 | Masking shall apply consistently across every surface: UI, API, export, report, PDF, notification, search result, AI response and support tooling. A field's mask is defined once with the field, not per screen. |
| SUR-PRV-087 | Every F\* reveal shall require a purpose code from a configured list, shall emit SE-14, shall be rate-limited per user per day, and shall be visible to the subject where §39.5.2 applies. |
| SUR-PRV-088 | Guard-to-client and client-to-guard contact shall go through a masked-number or in-app channel by default; direct personal numbers shall not be exchanged by the platform. Where a configured tenant policy permits direct exchange for a specific operational reason, it shall be per-assignment, time-bounded and audited. |
| SUR-PRV-089 | Bulk exports shall apply the requester's masking rules to every row, shall be watermarked with requester identity, and shall be counted against the export budget (SUR-SEC-066) with the contents summarised in the audit record. |

### 39.8 Cross-border transfer, hosting and vendors

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRV-090 | **Data residency.** Primary storage and processing of all personal data shall be in India. [RECOMMENDED] This is the build default because the platform serves an India-first market, holds data about Indian workers and Indian sites, and may be subject to configured residency conditions; hosting elsewhere would create an avoidable dependency and an avoidable review burden. |
| SUR-PRV-091 | Backups, replicas, disaster-recovery copies, log stores, analytics stores and support tooling shall follow the same residency rule as the primary store. A vendor that cannot keep data in India shall not be used for a category that carries a residency requirement in the configured policy. |
| SUR-PRV-092 | Where a capability is genuinely unavailable in-region (certain model providers, certain fraud or verification services), the transfer shall be: category-limited (never DP-01, DP-02, DP-09, DP-10, DP-11, DP-12, DP-14, DP-15, DP-17), documented in the vendor register with the transfer mechanism relied on per the configured policy, approved by Compliance, disclosed in the privacy notice, and re-reviewed annually. |
| SUR-PRV-093 | Model providers shall receive no data from the categories listed in SUR-PRV-092, shall be contractually prohibited from training on Suraksha data, shall have zero-retention or short-retention configured where the provider offers it, and shall be preferred in-region where an in-region option of adequate quality exists (§41). |
| SUR-PRV-094 | A **vendor and sub-processor register** shall be maintained containing: vendor, service, data categories accessed, purpose, processing location, sub-processors, contract and data-processing-agreement reference, security assessment date and outcome, breach-notification commitment, security contact, deletion-on-termination commitment, and review date. |
| SUR-PRV-095 | No vendor shall receive personal data before the register entry exists, the agreement is signed, and a security assessment proportionate to the data category is complete. Vendors touching DP-01, DP-02, DP-09, DP-10, DP-11, DP-12 or DP-14 require the full assessment including evidence of independent certification or an equivalent review. |
| SUR-PRV-096 | Data-processing agreements shall require, at minimum: processing only on documented instructions; confidentiality; the security measures assessed; sub-processor notice with an objection window; assistance with data-subject requests; breach notification within a stated period recorded in the register (SUR-SEC-205); deletion or return on termination with certification; and audit or evidence rights. |
| SUR-PRV-097 | Clients and agencies shall be able to see the current sub-processor list for their tenant, and shall be notified of material changes with a configured notice period. |
| SUR-PRV-098 | Vendor access shall be technically enforced: scoped credentials, least privilege, no standing access to production data stores, all access audited, and immediate revocation on contract end (which shall be a tracked task, not an assumption). |

### 39.9 Breach response — the privacy limb

Technical incident response is §38.14. This subsection covers the personal-data assessment that runs in parallel.

| Step | Requirement |
|---|---|
| B-1 Assess | Determine, per data category (DP-nn): whether personal data was accessed, exfiltrated, altered or destroyed; the number of affected data subjects by category; whether the data was encrypted and whether the keys were also exposed; and whether the exposure creates a risk of physical harm (location, home address, site arrangements) as distinct from financial or reputational harm |
| B-2 Risk-rate | Rate the likely harm using categories that fit this product: physical safety, financial loss, employment consequences, identity misuse, distress, confidentiality of a client's security posture. Physical-safety risk automatically escalates the incident severity (SUR-SEC-202) |
| B-3 Decide notification | Apply the configured notification rules (§40) for each recipient class — regulator, data subjects, client organisations, agencies, insurer — recording the trigger evaluated, the deadline computed, and the decision |
| B-4 Notify | Use the prepared templates: what happened, when, what data, what the recipient should do, what Suraksha has done, and a contact route. For guards, notice must be in their language, by push and SMS, in plain words, and must not require reading a legal document to understand the risk |
| B-5 Record | Maintain a breach register entry regardless of whether notification was required, retained for the configured period |
| B-6 Remediate | Track corrective actions to completion; where the breach revealed a design weakness in a privacy control, raise it as a change with an owner and a date |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRV-100 | A breach register shall exist recording every confirmed or suspected personal-data breach: date discovered, date occurred, categories, subject counts, cause, containment, notification decision with its basis, notifications sent, remediation actions and closure date. Entries shall be retained for the configured period and shall be reviewable by Compliance and Auditor. |
| SUR-PRV-101 | Notification content, recipients and deadlines shall be configuration, reviewed by counsel per jurisdiction (SUR-SEC-203). This document does not state when notification is legally required. |
| SUR-PRV-102 | Where a breach may expose guard location, guard home address or client site arrangements, the affected individuals and clients shall be informed as an operational safety measure regardless of whether a notification threshold is met, because the mitigation (changing arrangements, redeploying a guard) can only be performed by them. |
| SUR-PRV-103 | Data subjects notified of a breach shall be told what specific data of theirs was involved, not a generic category list, where the investigation can establish it. |
