### 39.10 Privacy by design in the SDLC

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-PRV-110 | Every feature shall pass a **privacy screening** at design: does it introduce a new data category, a new purpose for an existing category, a new recipient, a new retention need, a new automated decision, or a new cross-border flow? A "yes" to any triggers the review gate; a "no" is recorded and takes two minutes. |
| SUR-PRV-111 | **DPIA trigger criteria.** A full privacy impact assessment shall be required for: (a) any new processing of location, biometric, health, or verification data; (b) any expansion of who can see guard personal data; (c) any new automated or AI-assisted decision affecting a person's work, pay or standing; (d) body-camera, video analytics, face recognition beyond one-to-one attendance matching, or any always-on capture; (e) any new cross-border transfer of a restricted category; (f) any large-scale migration of legacy agency data (the Enterprise OCR migration in canon §1.4); (g) any new data-sharing with a client beyond the minimum operational set; (h) any change that lengthens a retention period. |
| SUR-PRV-112 | A DPIA shall record: the processing and its necessity, the data categories and subjects, the risks to individuals ranked including physical-safety risk, the mitigations, the residual risk, the decision, the approver, and a review date. It shall be signed off by the privacy owner and, for physical-safety-relevant processing, by the COO or CTO. |
| SUR-PRV-113 | Schema changes shall pass a gate: every new column or document field holding personal data must declare its category, classification, retention, masking rule and access roles, or the migration is rejected (SUR-PRV-001). |
| SUR-PRV-114 | Default-private stance: new fields default to not-visible outside the owning tenant and the data subject; new sharing capabilities default to off; new notification types default to transactional-only; new analytics events default to excluding personal identifiers. Widening any default is a reviewed change. |
| SUR-PRV-115 | Privacy tests shall exist alongside security tests: masking assertions per role for every sensitive field, retention-purge assertions per category, consent-gating assertions for every consent-dependent processing path, and an assertion that out-of-duty-window location events are rejected under every tenant configuration (SUR-PRV-052). |
| SUR-PRV-116 | A named privacy owner shall exist with the authority to block a release on a privacy ground, escalating to the CTO and COO. The role may be held alongside compliance responsibilities at current scale, and shall be separated as the organisation grows. [DECISION REQUIRED: D-334] |
| SUR-PRV-117 | Privacy notices, the worker-facing disclosure (SUR-PRV-058), the cookie policy and the sub-processor list shall be versioned, published, and reviewed at least annually and on any material processing change. The known problem P7 (template legal pages, canon §1.8) shall be resolved before launch: the published notices must describe what this platform actually does. |
| SUR-PRV-118 | Training on privacy handling shall be mandatory for every role that can see unmasked personal data, repeated annually, with completion tracked; support and verification staff shall additionally be trained on identity verification for data-subject requests and on refusing informal data requests. |

## 40. Compliance

### 40.0 What this section is

This section specifies a **configurable compliance engine** — software that stores obligations as data, tracks evidence against them, computes status, reminds people, and gates operations according to rules that a Suraksha Compliance officer configures and a qualified adviser reviews.

Three framing statements govern everything below, and they are absolute:

1. **No legal conclusion is hard-coded.** The platform never asserts what a law requires. It asserts what a *configured rule* requires. Every threshold, lead time, evidence list, validity period and consequence in this section is a **default value shipped in a seed catalogue**, editable per jurisdiction and per tenant, not a statement of law.
2. **Jurisdiction rules are data, not code.** Adding a state, changing a renewal lead time, or adding a required document must never require a code deployment (§40.1.5).
3. **This document states product requirements, not legal advice.** Every seeded rule carries a `counsel_review` block (§40.1.2) that is empty until a qualified adviser has reviewed it, and the UI shows that emptiness plainly (§40.12).

Where this section names a number — "90/60/30/7 day reminders", "12-month retention", "expiry blocks new allocation" — read it as *the default configuration value we recommend shipping*, not as a claim about any statute.

**Canonical homes referenced, not repeated:** BR-002 and all business rules live in §30 · the compliance veto in guard allocation lives in §25.15.5 · the OPS Licences and Compliance modules' screen detail lives in §22.17 · the Agency Portal compliance dashboard's screen detail lives in §20 · entity fields live in §32 · notification channels and delivery live in §36 · permission matrix in §31 · retention and data-subject mechanics in §39 · security controls in §38.

---

### 40.1 The compliance engine architecture

#### 40.1.1 Design principle

The engine has exactly four moving parts, and nothing else in the platform is allowed to compute compliance:

```
  ┌────────────────────┐    ┌───────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────┐
  │ RULE CATALOGUE     │    │ COMPLIANCE OBJECTS│    │ EVIDENCE STORE   │
  │ (versioned data)   │    │ (licence, verif., │    │ (documents,      │
  │ jurisdiction-scoped│    │  training, …)     │    │  attestations)   │
  └─────────┬──────────┘    └────────┬──────────┘    └────────┬─────────┘
            │                        │                        │
            └────────────┬───────────┴────────────────────────┘
                         ▼
              ┌──────────────────────────┐
              │  EVALUATOR               │  pure function; no side effects
              │  (rule × object × clock) │  → status + reasons + due dates
              └───────────┬──────────────┘
                          ▼
        ┌─────────────────┴──────────────────┐
        ▼                 ▼                  ▼
   STATUS STORE      CONSEQUENCE       REMINDER
   (materialised)    DISPATCHER        SCHEDULER
                     (gates, flags)    (§40.5)
```

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMP-001 | Compliance status shall be produced only by the evaluator. No module shall compute its own view of whether a licence, verification, training record or statutory record is valid; all modules shall read the materialised status store. |
| SUR-CMP-002 | The evaluator shall be a deterministic pure function of (rule version, compliance object state, evidence state, evaluation timestamp). Given the same inputs it shall always produce the same output, and every evaluation shall record the rule version used. |
| SUR-CMP-003 | The evaluator shall never write to the compliance object. Status is materialised in a separate store keyed by (object_id, rule_id, rule_version) so that a rule change can be re-evaluated without mutating history. |
| SUR-CMP-004 | Every computed status shall carry a machine-readable **reason set** (which rule clause produced it, which evidence was missing or expired, which date drove it) and shall be renderable to a human in one sentence per reason. |
| SUR-CMP-005 | AI shall never set, alter or override a compliance status (canon §1.7; §25.7.1 rows 22, 24, 60). AI may explain, prioritise and draft; the status is the evaluator's output or a dual-controlled human decision. |

#### 40.1.2 The rule definition schema

A rule is a row in the rule catalogue. These are its fields.

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `rule_id` | string, stable | Namespaced identity, e.g. `IN.GJ.AGENCY_LICENCE.STATE` (§40.1.3) |
| `rule_version` | integer | Increments on every published change; never reused |
| `title` | localised string | Human label shown in dashboards and reminders |
| `description` | localised markdown | What the obligation is, in operational terms |
| `jurisdiction` | jurisdiction ref | Country / state / district / "global" (§40.8) |
| `object_type` | enum | Which compliance object this rule attaches to (§40.2.1) |
| `scope` | enum | `tenant` · `branch` · `site` · `person` · `contract` · `transaction` |
| `applicability` | expression | Boolean predicate over object + context; if false the rule does not apply |
| `evidence_required` | array | Ordered list of evidence item specs (§40.1.2.1) |
| `verification_method` | enum | `document_upload` · `internal_verification` · `external_lookup` · `attestation` · `system_generated` (§40.2) |
| `validity_basis` | enum | `fixed_period` · `document_stated_expiry` · `event_anchored` · `perpetual` · `periodic_filing` |
| `validity_period` | duration | Used when `validity_basis = fixed_period` (e.g. P1Y, P5Y) |
| `renewal_lead_time` | duration array | Ordered reminder offsets, e.g. `[P90D, P60D, P30D, P7D, P1D]` |
| `grace_period` | duration | Post-expiry window before hard consequence, default P0D |
| `consequence_on_breach` | consequence block | §40.1.2.2 — what happens, and it is data |
| `severity` | enum | P0 · P1 · P2 · P3 (canon alert severities) |
| `owner_role` | role ref | Default accountable role (canon role names only) |
| `escalation_ladder_id` | ref | Which ladder in §40.5 applies |
| `effective_from` / `effective_to` | date | Effective-dating (§40.1.4) |
| `supersedes` | rule ref | Prior rule this replaces |
| `counsel_review` | block | `{reviewed_by, reviewer_type, reviewed_on, reference_note, status}`; empty = unreviewed |
| `source_note` | free text | Where the configuring officer says this came from — a reference, not a legal citation the platform asserts |
| `tenant_overridable` | boolean | Whether an agency tenant may tighten (never loosen) this rule |
| `status` | enum | Draft · Pending · Active · Suspended · Archived |

##### 40.1.2.1 Evidence item spec

| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `evidence_code` | Stable code, e.g. `POLICE_VERIFICATION_REPORT` |
| `label` | Localised |
| `mandatory` | Boolean, or an expression (e.g. mandatory only for armed category) |
| `accepted_formats` | PDF / JPG / PNG; max size; page count |
| `extractable_fields` | Fields OCR may propose (number, issue date, expiry date, issuing office) — proposal only, per §25.7.1 row 23 |
| `expiry_source` | `document_stated` · `derived_from_issue_date` · `none` |
| `verification_required` | Whether a human Verification role must confirm before the evidence counts |
| `redaction_profile` | Which fields are masked in exports and non-privileged views (§39) |
| `alternatives` | Other evidence codes that satisfy the same requirement (any-of groups) |

##### 40.1.2.2 Consequence block

The consequence block is the reason this engine is configurable rather than hard-coded. It is a list of typed consequences, each with a trigger state.

| Consequence type | Parameters | Example configured use |
|---|---|---|
| `notify` | audience roles, channels, template_id | Reminder at T-90 |
| `flag` | flag_code, surface list | Amber dot on the guard row |
| `task` | task template, assignee role, due offset | "Start Gujarat licence renewal" task at T-60 |
| `block_action` | action codes (e.g. `ALLOCATION_CREATE`, `SITE_ONBOARD`, `MARKETPLACE_LISTING`), scope | New allocations blocked in that jurisdiction |
| `restrict_action` | action codes + override authority + override reason requirement | Existing deployments continue but need a management decision |
| `withdraw_badge` | badge code | Marketplace "Verified" badge withdrawn (§22.17.3) |
| `downgrade_score` | score name, delta | −15 on the allocation skill factor (§25.15.5) |
| `suspend_object` | object type | Suspend the licence object pending renewal evidence |
| `escalate` | ladder id, severity | Raise to Founder/Management at T+7 |
| `report_only` | report id | Counted in the monthly compliance report, no operational effect |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMP-006 | Consequences shall be declared as data in the rule and executed by the consequence dispatcher. No consequence shall exist as an `if (licence.expired)` branch inside a feature module. |
| SUR-CMP-007 | `block_action` consequences shall be enforced server-side at the action's authorisation point, not in the UI alone, and shall return a structured refusal naming the rule, the object and the remediation path. |
| SUR-CMP-008 | Every consequence execution shall write an audit entry linking the rule version, the object, the consequence type and the affected action or entity. |

#### 40.1.3 Rule catalogue structure

The catalogue is namespaced so that jurisdiction scoping is readable at a glance and inheritance is unambiguous.

```
IN                                  ← country level
├── IN.GLOBAL.*                     ← applies everywhere in India
│   ├── IN.GLOBAL.GUARD_KYC
│   ├── IN.GLOBAL.POLICE_VERIFICATION
│   └── IN.GLOBAL.EMPLOYMENT_RECORD
├── IN.GJ.*                         ← state: Gujarat
│   ├── IN.GJ.AGENCY_LICENCE.STATE
│   ├── IN.GJ.GUARD_TRAINING
│   └── IN.GJ.AHMEDABAD.AGENCY_LICENCE.DISTRICT   ← district under state
├── IN.MH.*                         ← state: Maharashtra
└── IN.RJ.*
```

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Resolution order | Most specific wins: district → state → country → global. A district rule with the same `object_type` and `scope` **replaces** the state rule for entities in that district; it does not merge. |
| Additive rules | A rule may be marked `additive = true`, in which case it stacks with the inherited rule instead of replacing it (used for district-specific extra evidence). |
| Conflict detection | Publishing a rule that would silently replace another with different `evidence_required` raises a publish-time warning listing the affected entity count; the publisher must acknowledge it. |
| Catalogue packs | Rules ship in **packs** — a versioned bundle per jurisdiction (`IN.GJ v4`). A pack is the unit of review, approval and publication. Tenants may pin a pack version briefly during a transition (max configured 90 days) but drift is reported. |
| Seed catalogue | Suraksha ships a seed pack per serviceable state with `counsel_review.status = Unreviewed`. The compliance dashboard shows an explicit "N rules in this jurisdiction have not been reviewed by counsel" banner until cleared (§40.12). |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMP-009 | Rule resolution shall be deterministic and explainable: for any entity, the UI shall show which rules apply, from which level of the namespace they were inherited, and which rules were overridden. |
| SUR-CMP-010 | A rule pack shall be publishable only by the Compliance role with a second approval by Super Admin or Founder/Management; publication shall be an audited event carrying the diff. |

#### 40.1.4 Versioning and effective-dating

Compliance history must remain truthful. If a lead time changes from 60 to 90 days in March, a status computed in February must still be explainable under the February rule.

| Concept | Specification |
|---|---|
| Immutable versions | A published `rule_version` is immutable. Editing produces a Draft of version n+1. |
| Effective-dating | Each version carries `effective_from` and optional `effective_to`. Versions may be scheduled forward — publish today, effective 1 April. |
| Evaluation clock | The evaluator selects the rule version whose effective window contains the **evaluation date**, not the object's creation date, unless the rule sets `anchor = object_created` (used for grandfathering). |
| Grandfathering | A rule version may carry `grandfather_until` and a predicate; objects created before the effective date continue under the prior version until that date. Grandfathered objects are visibly badged. |
| Retro-evaluation | When a version becomes effective, the engine re-evaluates all in-scope objects within a configured window (default 15 minutes) and produces a **change report**: how many objects changed status, in which direction, and which operations became blocked. |
| Dry run | Any Draft version can be evaluated in dry-run mode against live data without writing status, producing the same change report. Dry run is mandatory before publication of any rule with a `block_action` consequence. |
| Audit view | For any object, "Status history" shows every status, the timestamp, the rule version in force, and the evidence state at that moment. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMP-011 | Published rule versions shall be immutable; corrections shall be made by publishing a new version, never by editing a published one. |
| SUR-CMP-012 | Publication of a rule version containing a `block_action` or `suspend_object` consequence shall require a completed dry run within the preceding 24 hours, and the dry-run change report shall be attached to the approval record. |
| SUR-CMP-013 | Historical status shall always be explainable under the rule version in force at the time, and the UI shall never retroactively restate a past status under a current rule. |

#### 40.1.5 How a rule change propagates without code deployment

| Step | Actor | System behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Author | Compliance (Suraksha) or Agency Compliance (tenant-scoped tightening only) | Rule editor form (§40.8.4); creates Draft version n+1 with a change note |
| 2. Validate | System | Schema validation, expression compilation, reference integrity (roles, templates, action codes all exist), conflict detection against the namespace |
| 3. Dry run | Compliance | Evaluates against live data; produces change report (objects affected, status transitions, actions that would become blocked, notification volume that would be generated) |
| 4. Counsel review | External adviser, recorded by Compliance | `counsel_review` block populated: reviewer name, type (internal counsel / external counsel / consultant / none), date, reference note, status ∈ Reviewed / Reviewed-with-caveats / Unreviewed |
| 5. Approve | Super Admin or Founder/Management (second pair of eyes) | Approval record with the diff, the change report and the counsel block attached |
| 6. Publish | System | Version marked Active, effective per its `effective_from`; cache invalidation broadcast |
| 7. Re-evaluate | System | Background re-evaluation of in-scope objects; status store updated; consequence dispatcher runs |
| 8. Notify | System | Affected tenants notified of any change that alters their obligations or blocks an action, with the change note, before the effective date where the publication was forward-dated |
| 9. Observe | Compliance | 7-day watch window: reminder volume, block events, override requests, support tickets tagged to the rule |
| 10. Roll back | Compliance + Super Admin | Publishing a corrective version that restores prior parameters; rollback is a new version, never a deletion |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMP-014 | No jurisdiction rule change shall require an application deployment. The full path from authoring to enforcement shall be data-only. |
| SUR-CMP-015 | Notification volume shall be estimated in the dry run and a publication projected to generate more than a configured threshold (default 5,000 notifications in 24 hours) shall require explicit acknowledgement and shall be rate-shaped on release (§36). |
| SUR-CMP-016 | Tenants shall be notified before a rule change that introduces a new blocking consequence takes effect, with a minimum configured notice period (default 14 days) unless the change is marked urgent with a recorded reason. |

#### 40.1.6 Evaluation triggers

| Trigger | Scope evaluated | Latency target |
|---|---|---|
| Evidence uploaded, verified, rejected or replaced | That object | Synchronous, < 2 s |
| Compliance object created or field edited | That object | Synchronous |
| Nightly clock tick (configured hour per timezone) | All active objects | Complete within the maintenance window |
| Rule version becomes effective | All in-scope objects | Within 15 min |
| Action authorisation check (allocation, onboarding, invoice issue) | The specific objects the action depends on | Synchronous, < 200 ms from the materialised store, with a freshness assertion |
| Manual re-evaluate | Selected objects | On demand, audited |
| Tenant onboarding / migration import | All imported objects | Batch, with a completion report |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMP-017 | Action authorisation shall read the materialised status store and shall additionally assert that the status is fresher than a configured staleness bound (default 24 h); a stale status shall force a synchronous re-evaluation rather than being trusted. |
| SUR-CMP-018 | Clock-driven transitions (Valid → Expiring → Expired) shall be computed in the jurisdiction's configured timezone, not in UTC, and shall be idempotent under retry. |

#### 40.1.7 A worked rule (illustrative default, not a legal statement)

```yaml
rule_id: IN.GJ.AGENCY_LICENCE.STATE
rule_version: 4
title: { en: "Gujarat state agency licence", hi: "गुजरात राज्य एजेंसी लाइसेंस" }
jurisdiction: { country: IN, state: GJ, district: null }
object_type: AGENCY_LICENCE
scope: tenant
applicability: "tenant.operates_in_state('GJ') == true"
evidence_required:
  - evidence_code: LICENCE_CERTIFICATE
    mandatory: true
    accepted_formats: [pdf, jpg]
    extractable_fields: [licence_number, issue_date, valid_upto, issuing_authority, districts_covered]
    expiry_source: document_stated
    verification_required: true
  - evidence_code: RENEWAL_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT
    mandatory: false          # becomes relevant in Renewal Pending
    expiry_source: none
verification_method: internal_verification   # external_lookup unavailable — see SUR-CMP-062
validity_basis: document_stated_expiry
renewal_lead_time: [P90D, P60D, P30D, P15D, P7D, P1D]
grace_period: P0D
severity: P0
owner_role: Compliance
escalation_ladder_id: LADDER_LICENCE
consequence_on_breach:
  - state: Expiring
    do: [ notify(Compliance, Founder/Management), task(RENEW_LICENCE, Compliance, due=T-45), flag(LICENCE_EXPIRING, [ops_dashboard, agency_360, marketplace_internal]) ]
  - state: Expired
    do: [ block_action([ALLOCATION_CREATE, SITE_ONBOARD, CONTRACT_ACTIVATE], scope=jurisdiction:GJ),
          restrict_action([ALLOCATION_CONTINUE], override_authority=Founder/Management, reason_required=true),
          withdraw_badge(MARKETPLACE_VERIFIED),
          escalate(LADDER_LICENCE, P0) ]
effective_from: 2026-04-01
counsel_review: { status: Unreviewed }
tenant_overridable: false
```

The `block_action`/`restrict_action` split is the concrete expression of BR-002 (§30): **new** deployments in that jurisdiction stop; **existing** deployments are surfaced for a named human decision rather than silently continued or silently terminated. Which of the two applies to which action code is configuration, not an assumption baked into code.

---

### 40.2 The compliance object model

#### 40.2.1 Object inventory

| Object | Scope | Owner (Suraksha) | Owner (tenant) | Typical verification method | Gates |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Agency Licence — state | Tenant × state | Compliance | Agency Compliance | Internal verification of uploaded certificate | Allocation, onboarding, marketplace badge |
| Agency Licence — district | Tenant × district | Compliance | Agency Compliance | Internal verification | Allocation in that district |
| Guard Verification (KYC set) | Person | Verification | Agency Compliance | Internal verification per document | Guard activation, allocation |
| Police Verification | Person | Verification | Agency Compliance | Internal verification of report + status field | Allocation (hard veto) |
| Training Certification | Person × course | HR/Training | Agency HR | Trainer attestation + certificate | Allocation for the category |
| Employment Record | Person × employer | HR | Agency HR | System-generated + signed artefacts | Payroll, statutory registers |
| Contract Record | Client × agency | Sales/Finance | Agency Sales | System-generated + signed artefacts | Invoicing, deployment |
| Statutory Registration Record | Tenant | Compliance | Agency Compliance | Document upload | Configured filings, tender eligibility |
| Statutory Contribution Record | Person × period | Finance/Payroll | Payroll | System-generated from payroll run | Filing calendar items |
| Wage Record | Person × period | Payroll | Payroll | System-generated from payroll run | Statutory registers, disputes |
| Tax Registration Record | Tenant | Finance | Agency Finance | Document upload | Invoice issuance format |
| Invoice/Tax Document Record | Transaction | Finance | Agency Finance | System-generated | Financial reporting, retention |
| Insurance Record | Tenant / site / person | Compliance | Agency Compliance | Document upload | Contract clauses, tender eligibility |
| Weapon Authorisation Record | Person × weapon | Compliance | Agency Compliance | Internal verification | Armed post allocation (hard veto) |
| Site Compliance Record | Site | City Operations | Operations Manager | Attestation + client documents | Site activation |
| Filing Calendar Item | Tenant × obligation × period | Compliance | Agency Compliance | Evidence upload after filing | Compliance score, inspection pack |

Every object shares a common envelope so that dashboards, reminders, exports and audit behave identically across all of them.

| Common field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `object_id`, `object_type`, `tenant_id`, `branch_id?` | Identity and tenancy (canon §3) |
| `subject_ref` | The entity it is about (agency / guard / contract / site / period) |
| `jurisdiction_ref` | Country/state/district it is scoped to, nullable for global objects |
| `identifier` | Licence number, registration number, certificate number |
| `issued_on`, `valid_from`, `valid_upto` | Dates driving the lifecycle |
| `issuing_authority` | Free text plus optional coded authority reference |
| `evidence[]` | Links into the evidence store with per-item verification state |
| `verification_state` | Pending · In Progress · Verified · Rejected |
| `compliance_status` | The evaluator's output (§40.3) |
| `status_reasons[]` | Machine-readable reason set |
| `next_action`, `next_action_due`, `owner_user_id` | Accountability |
| `renewal_ref` | Link to the successor object when renewed |
| `source` | manual · migrated · api · ocr_assisted |
| `confidence` | Where OCR proposed values, retained with the human confirmation record |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMP-019 | All compliance objects shall share the common envelope so that any new object type is automatically supported by the dashboard, reminder, export, audit and retention machinery without bespoke work. |
| SUR-CMP-020 | Evidence documents shall be stored write-once; a correction shall add a new version and retain the superseded one with its verification history (§38 for storage controls, §39 for retention). |
| SUR-CMP-021 | Where OCR proposed a field value, the stored record shall retain both the proposed value with its confidence and the human-confirmed value, and shall never present the proposed value as verified (§25.7.1 row 23). |

#### 40.2.2 Agency Licence (state and district scoped)

Per the canon: PSARA licences are issued at **state** and **district** level; operating in four states requires four state licences; city/district-only operation takes a district-scoped licence. Licence geography is therefore modelled as a first-class object, never as a text field on the agency profile.

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Cardinality | One licence object per (tenant, jurisdiction). A tenant operating in 4 states with 2 district-only licences holds 6 objects. |
| Geography payload | `states_covered[]`, `districts_covered[]` — captured explicitly, because a state licence may in configuration be recorded as covering all districts or an enumerated subset. Which is true for a given licence is entered from the certificate, not inferred. |
| Evidence required (default) | Licence certificate (mandatory) · renewal application acknowledgement (when Renewal Pending) · any endorsement/amendment documents · previous licence for continuity |
| Verification method | Internal verification by the Verification role against the uploaded certificate. **External automated verification is not assumed** — no public verification API is presumed to exist (SUR-CMP-062). |
| Validity | `document_stated_expiry` — the date read from the certificate and confirmed by a human, never derived. |
| Renewal lead time (default) | 90 / 60 / 30 / 15 / 7 / 1 days, plus daily after expiry |
| Consequence configuration (default) | Expiring → notify + task + flag. Expired → BR-002 configured restrictions: block new allocations, site onboarding and contract activation *in that jurisdiction*; restrict continuation of existing deployments pending a named Founder/Management decision; withdraw the marketplace Verified badge; P0 escalation. |
| Suspended | Set manually by dual control (Compliance + Super Admin) with mandatory evidence, or by a configured rule. Consequences are the Expired set plus blocking of the tenant's marketplace listing. |
| Cross-object effect | A guard's allocation to a site inherits the site's jurisdiction; the licence covering that jurisdiction is what the veto checks (§40.6, §40.8.3). |
| Who may edit | Suraksha Compliance for `SURAKSHA-HQ` and for verifying tenant submissions; Agency Compliance may upload and submit but never set `Verified` or `compliance_status`. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMP-022 | Licence geography shall be stored as structured state and district references, never as free text, and shall be the basis of every jurisdiction check in the platform. |
| SUR-CMP-023 | A manual change to a licence's `compliance_status` or `verification_state` shall require dual control (Compliance plus Super Admin or Founder/Management), mandatory evidence, and a reason from a coded list; the change shall be a P0 audit event. |
| SUR-CMP-024 | Where a state licence's certificate enumerates specific districts, the platform shall treat districts outside that enumeration as uncovered and shall not infer statewide coverage. |

#### 40.2.3 Guard Verification (the KYC document set)

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Structure | A parent verification object per guard, with child evidence items. The parent's status is the roll-up: worst child status wins. |
| Evidence required (configurable default set) | Identity document · address document · photograph · date-of-birth evidence · educational/qualification evidence where the rule requires it · previous employer reference where configured · medical fitness where configured · bank account proof (for payroll, not for compliance gating) |
| Any-of groups | Identity may be satisfied by any one of a configured list; the rule's `alternatives` field expresses this so no specific document is hard-required by code. |
| Verification method | Internal verification. Only the **Verification** role may set `Verified` (§22.17.2). No other role, and never AI. |
| Validity | Per item: some perpetual, some `document_stated_expiry`, some `fixed_period` from issue. |
| Expiry behaviour | Item expiry demotes the parent to Expiring/Expired per §40.3; the guard's document-compliance dot changes; allocation consequences follow §40.6. |
| Name variance | Where names differ across documents, a name-variance workflow records a canonical name decision with the deciding user (§22.6). Unresolved variance holds the parent at Pending. |
| Rejection | A rejected item carries a coded reason and a re-upload path; the guard sees the reason in the Guard App in their language. |
| Privacy | Document content is retrievable only by roles holding the permission, every reveal is logged, and content is never pasted into an AI response (§25.2.7, §39). |

#### 40.2.4 Police Verification

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Object | One per guard per employer engagement, with a configured re-verification cycle (default `fixed_period` P2Y — a default, not a legal assertion). |
| States | Not Started · In Progress (submitted, awaiting outcome) · Verified · Rejected · Expired · Renewal Pending |
| Evidence required (default) | Submission acknowledgement (for In Progress) · verification report/outcome document (for Verified) · any adverse-finding note |
| Verification method | Internal verification of the outcome document. External lookup is **not** assumed available (SUR-CMP-062); where an authority provides a checkable reference, the platform stores the reference and supports manual confirmation. |
| Consequence configuration | This is the strictest object in the platform. Default: missing, expired or Rejected → **hard allocation veto with no override by any role** (§25.15.5). "In Progress" deployment, where the configured rule permits it at all, requires a recorded override by Compliance with a reason and an expiry on the override itself. |
| Adverse finding | An adverse outcome sets Rejected and triggers a mandatory human review workflow with an outcome decision by Compliance; the guard is informed of the decision and the contest path (§41.6). No automated termination (§41.6, canon §1.7). |
| Renewal | At T-90 a renewal task is created; at expiry the veto applies regardless of renewal progress unless the configured rule grants a grace period, which defaults to zero. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMP-025 | The police-verification veto shall be configured as non-overridable by default, and any deployment permitted with verification "In Progress" shall require an explicit, time-bounded, reason-coded override by the Compliance role, counted and reported monthly. |
| SUR-CMP-026 | An adverse verification finding shall never itself terminate, blacklist or deactivate a person. It shall create a human review task with a decision, a recorded reason, notification to the person and a contest path (§41.6). |

#### 40.2.5 Training Certification

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Object | One per (guard, course, cycle). Courses are configured: induction, refresher, category-specific (armed handling, PSO, fire, first aid, event crowd), client-specific site training. |
| Statutory vs non-statutory | Each course carries a configured `statutory` boolean per jurisdiction. Statutory expiry is a hard veto for the relevant post category; non-statutory expiry applies a soft penalty (default −15 on the allocation skill factor) plus a flag (§25.15.5). |
| Evidence required | Certificate · trainer attestation · assessment score where configured · attendance record for the session |
| Verification method | Trainer attestation. AI may never mark training complete (§25.7.1 row 42). |
| Validity | `fixed_period` from completion (defaults: induction perpetual with refresher cycle P1Y; armed handling P1Y; first aid P2Y — all configurable). |
| Expiry behaviour | Expiring at the configured ladder; Expired applies the configured consequence for that course's statutory flag. |
| Category linkage | The post's required course set is derived from the post's `guard_category` and the site's jurisdiction; a guard missing a required course for that category is ineligible for that post but may remain eligible for others. |

#### 40.2.6 Employment Record

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | The record that a person is engaged by a tenant on stated terms — the anchor for wage, contribution and register generation. |
| Evidence required (configurable) | Appointment/engagement letter · signed terms acceptance · identity linkage to the verified KYC set · nominee/emergency contact declaration · statutory declaration forms where the jurisdiction rule configures them |
| Verification method | System-generated artefacts plus signed-document upload; e-sign where available (§37). |
| Validity | Perpetual while the engagement is Active; closes on exit with an exit record. |
| Statuses | Draft · Active · Suspended (disciplinary hold) · Completed (exited) · Archived |
| Expiry behaviour | Not expiry-driven; instead **completeness**-driven. A missing mandatory artefact holds the record at Pending and can be configured to block payroll inclusion or allocation. |
| Consequence configuration | Default: incomplete employment record → flag + task; configurable to block payroll release for that person (a tenant-tightenable rule). |
| Exit | Exit record captures date, reason category, notice handling, dues settlement reference, and asset/kit return. Exit does not delete anything; retention per §40.7.3. |

#### 40.2.7 Contract Record

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Purpose | The commercial and service agreement between an agency (or Suraksha) and a client; the basis for deployment authority, SLA measurement, invoicing and dispute handling. |
| Evidence required | Executed contract document · annexures (scope, posts, rates, SLA) · purchase order where applicable · client authorised-signatory evidence where configured · insurance certificates where the contract requires them |
| Verification method | Internal verification of execution (both signatures present, dates consistent, annexures attached). |
| Validity | `document_stated_expiry` from the contract term; auto-renewal clauses recorded as a structured flag with a notice-period field. |
| Statuses | Draft · Pending (awaiting execution) · Active · Expiring · Expired · Suspended (service hold) · Completed · Cancelled · Archived |
| Expiry behaviour | Expiring ladder 90/60/30/7 with renewal task to the owning Sales role; Expired → configured consequence, default: block new invoice issue against that contract, flag active deployments for a management decision, notify client and account owner. Deployments are **not** automatically stopped — that is an operational decision with client and workforce consequences. |
| Cross-object effect | Contract clauses feed compliance checks: required guard categories, required training, required insurance, required background-verification standard, penalty/shortfall terms. These are captured as structured clause records so the compliance engine can check them, not as an opaque PDF. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMP-027 | Contract obligations that the platform is expected to monitor (required categories, training, insurance, verification standard, reporting cadence, penalty terms) shall be captured as structured clause records at contract onboarding; a clause not captured structurally shall not be claimed as monitored anywhere in the product. |
| SUR-CMP-028 | Contract expiry shall never silently terminate deployments; it shall raise a decision task with the affected guard count, site list and revenue exposure. |

#### 40.2.8 Statutory record-keeping (contribution, wage and register records) — as configurable records

The platform models these as **configurable record types with configurable filing obligations**. It does not assert what any scheme requires; it stores what the configured rule says must be kept and produced.

| Record type | Grain | Generated from | Evidence | Default consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Contribution record (e.g. provident-fund-type scheme, configured as `EPF`) | Person × period | Payroll run outputs (§35) | Filing challan/receipt upload | Missing filing evidence → task + flag; overdue beyond configured days → escalate |
| Contribution record (e.g. insurance-type scheme, configured as `ESIC`) | Person × period | Payroll run outputs | Filing challan/receipt upload | Same ladder, separate obligation |
| Wage record | Person × period | Payroll run outputs; wage rate configuration per (jurisdiction, category, skill band) | Payslip artefact, disbursement reference | Rate below configured floor → block payroll release with an override by Agency Finance + Founder/Management, reason recorded |
| Attendance/muster register | Person × period × site | Attendance system (§26/§32) | System-generated, exportable | Data-quality flag if manual-entry proportion exceeds configured threshold (§42.6) |
| Overtime record | Person × period | Attendance + payroll | System-generated | Breach of configured hour ceiling → flag; allocation-time enforcement per §25.15.5 |
| Leave record | Person × year | Leave module | System-generated | Balance anomalies flagged |
| Register set (configurable list) | Tenant × register × period | Register generator (§22.17.4) | Generated document with a generation record | Missing period → task |
| Filing calendar item | Tenant × obligation × period | Configuration | Evidence of filing | Ladder per §40.5 |

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Wage rate configuration | A table of (jurisdiction, effective_from, guard_category, skill_band, rate_basis, rate_amount, components). Rates are **entered by the tenant or by Suraksha Compliance**, versioned and effective-dated exactly like rules. The platform never fetches or asserts a rate. |
| Rate-change propagation | A new rate version triggers a dry run showing affected guards, cost delta per site and contract-margin impact, so the commercial consequence is visible before it lands. |
| Register generator | Registers are defined as **templates** (columns, grouping, period, format) attached to a jurisdiction rule. Adding a register for a new state is adding a template, not writing code. |
| Filing calendar | Obligation, jurisdiction, periodicity, due-date expression (e.g. "15th of the following month" as a configured expression), owner role, evidence spec, escalation ladder. Entirely data. |
| Evidence of filing | The platform records that a filing was made by holding the uploaded acknowledgement; it does not and cannot confirm acceptance by any authority. This limitation is stated in the UI. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMP-029 | Wage floors, contribution schemes, register templates and filing calendars shall all be configurable data with effective-dating; none shall be hard-coded, and none shall be described in the product as a legal requirement. |
| SUR-CMP-030 | Where a payroll run would produce a wage record below the configured floor for the applicable jurisdiction and category, the run shall be blocked at review with the affected list, and release shall require a dual-control override with a coded reason retained for the record's full retention period. |
| SUR-CMP-031 | The platform shall label filing evidence as "acknowledgement recorded by the tenant", never as "filing accepted", because acceptance is not observable to the platform. |

#### 40.2.9 Tax registration and invoice records

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Tax registration record | Tenant-level, per registration type and jurisdiction: identifier, registered name, address, effective dates, evidence document. Drives invoice document format and the fields printed on it (§35 owns the financial mechanics). |
| Validity | Perpetual unless the configured rule sets a period; amendments create new versions with effective dates. |
| Expiry/invalidity behaviour | If a registration record is marked invalid or expired, the configured consequence defaults to: warn on invoice creation, block issuance of documents that assert that registration, escalate to Finance. |
| Invoice/tax document record | Transaction-grain, system-generated, immutable once issued (BR-003 — completed financial transactions are never silently modified). Corrections are credit/debit notes, never edits. |
| Compliance relevance | Retention (§40.7.3), reconciliation completeness (a period with gaps in the document sequence is a compliance finding), and evidence-pack inclusion. |
| What the platform does not do | It does not compute a tax position, determine applicability, or file anything. It applies configured tax treatment to documents and retains them. GST treatment itself is D-001 (canon). |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMP-032 | Issued financial documents shall be immutable and sequentially accounted for; any gap or out-of-sequence issue in a period shall raise a compliance finding automatically. |
| SUR-CMP-033 | The platform shall apply configured tax treatment to documents and shall not present any tax determination as advice; the configuration screen shall carry the counsel-review banner (§40.12). |

#### 40.2.10 Site, insurance and weapon records (condensed)

| Object | Key fields | Verification | Default consequence on breach |
|---|---|---|---|
| Site Compliance Record | Site jurisdiction, client-provided permissions, safety induction date, emergency contacts, night-work suitability attestation, client-required documents | Attestation by City Operations / Operations Manager plus client documents | Incomplete → block site activation (configurable); expired induction → flag + task |
| Insurance Record | Policy type (as configured), insurer, policy number, cover amount, period, insured scope (tenant/site/person) | Document upload + internal verification | Expiring ladder; Expired → flag on contracts that reference it, block tender submission that requires it, notify Finance |
| Weapon Authorisation Record | Person, weapon reference, authorisation identifier, issuing authority, validity, linked training | Internal verification | Invalid/expired → hard veto for armed posts, no override (§25.15.5) |

### 40.3 The universal compliance status lifecycle

Every compliance object in §40.2 uses the same lifecycle. This is what makes one dashboard, one reminder engine and one export work across all of them.

```
                     ┌────────┐
                     │ Draft  │ (created, evidence incomplete)
                     └───┬────┘
                         │ submit
                         ▼
                   ┌───────────┐   reject   ┌──────────┐
                   │  Pending  ├───────────►│ Rejected │
                   └─────┬─────┘            └────┬─────┘
                         │ verify                │ re-submit
                         ▼                       │
   ┌────────────────► ┌───────┐ ◄────────────────┘
   │  renewal         │ Valid │
   │  verified        └───┬───┘
   │                      │ clock reaches (valid_upto − lead_time)
   │                      ▼
   │                 ┌──────────┐
   │                 │ Expiring │ ── renewal submitted ─┐
   │                 └────┬─────┘                       │
   │                      │ clock passes valid_upto     ▼
   │                      │                    ┌──────────────────┐
   │                      ▼                    │ Renewal Pending  │
   │                 ┌─────────┐ ◄─────────────┤ (overlay state)  │
   │                 │ Expired │  no outcome   └────────┬─────────┘
   │                 └────┬────┘  by valid_upto         │ renewal verified
   └───────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┘
                          │ manual action (dual control) / rule
                          ▼
                     ┌───────────┐
                     │ Suspended │
                     └───────────┘
                          │ restore (dual control) → Valid / Expiring
                          ▼
                     ┌──────────┐
                     │ Archived │ (superseded or retention-closed)
```

#### 40.3.1 State definitions and operational effect

| State | Meaning | Default operational effect | Configurable? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Draft** | Object created, evidence not yet submitted | No effect; not counted in compliance %, shown as "not started" | Counting behaviour configurable |
| **Pending** | Evidence submitted, awaiting human verification | Treated as **not valid** for gating unless the rule explicitly permits provisional operation with an override | Yes, per rule |
| **Rejected** | Verification failed with a coded reason | Same as missing; blocks whatever a missing object blocks; re-submission path always open | Reason list configurable |
| **Valid** | Verified and within validity window | No restriction | — |
| **Expiring** | Verified, within `renewal_lead_time` of `valid_upto` | **Operationally identical to Valid** by default — warnings only. Reminders fire, tasks are created, flags appear, soft allocation penalty may apply near the end of the window | Yes; a tenant may tighten to restrict |
| **Expired** | Past `valid_upto` (+ grace) without a verified successor | The rule's `block_action` / `restrict_action` set applies | Yes — this is the core of BR-002 configurability |
| **Renewal Pending** | Renewal evidence submitted, outcome not yet received; overlays Expiring or Expired | Softens the Expired consequence *only if the rule configures a `renewal_grace`*; otherwise informational | Yes, per rule; default is **no softening** |
| **Suspended** | Manually or rule-suspended pending investigation or authority action | The Expired consequence set plus any suspension-specific consequences (e.g. marketplace listing hidden) | Yes |
| **Archived** | Superseded by a successor object, or retention-closed | No operational effect; remains in audit and evidence packs per retention | — |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMP-034 | These nine states shall be the only compliance states in the platform; no module shall introduce a local state such as "almost expired" or "under review". |
| SUR-CMP-035 | Expiring shall be non-restrictive by default. Any configuration that makes Expiring restrictive shall require a dry run and shall notify affected tenants before taking effect. |
| SUR-CMP-036 | Renewal Pending shall never by itself restore operational rights unless the rule explicitly configures a renewal grace, and the grace shall have a maximum duration and a hard stop. |

#### 40.3.2 Transition triggers

| From → To | Trigger | Actor | Side effects |
|---|---|---|---|
| — → Draft | Object created (manually, by onboarding wizard, by migration, or auto-created by a rule becoming applicable) | Any authorised role / system | Owner assigned from rule default |
| Draft → Pending | All mandatory evidence uploaded and submitted | Object owner | Verification queue item created (§22.17.2) |
| Pending → Valid | Human verifier sets Verified with all mandatory items accepted | Verification role only | Status materialised; consequences of prior state cleared; renewal reminders scheduled |
| Pending → Rejected | Verifier rejects with a coded reason | Verification role only | Notification to submitter with reason; re-upload task |
| Rejected → Pending | Corrected evidence re-submitted | Object owner | New verification queue item; prior rejection retained |
| Valid → Expiring | Clock reaches `valid_upto − max(renewal_lead_time)` | System (nightly + on-demand) | First reminder in the ladder; renewal task created at the configured offset |
| Expiring → Renewal Pending | Renewal evidence (acknowledgement) uploaded | Object owner | Ladder switches to the renewal-follow-up ladder |
| Expiring → Valid | Successor object verified before expiry | Verification role | Old object → Archived with `renewal_ref` set; reminders cancelled |
| Expiring → Expired | Clock passes `valid_upto + grace_period` | System | `block_action` / `restrict_action` consequences dispatched; P0/P1 escalation per rule |
| Renewal Pending → Valid | Successor verified | Verification role | Consequences cleared; change notified to everyone who received the block notice |
| Renewal Pending → Expired | Clock passes `valid_upto + grace` with no successor | System | Full Expired consequence set; the fact that a renewal is pending is shown but does not soften unless configured |
| Any → Suspended | Manual dual-control action, or a rule consequence | Compliance + Super Admin / Founder/Management | Mandatory evidence and coded reason; P0 audit event; affected-entity report generated |
| Suspended → Valid/Expiring | Restoration with evidence | Same dual control | Restoration reason recorded; consequences cleared; tenants notified |
| Valid/Expired/Suspended → Archived | Superseded by successor, or entity archived, or retention window closed | System | Retained per §40.7.3; still exportable in evidence packs for its retention period |

#### 40.3.3 Configurable lead times — shipped defaults

| Object | Reminder ladder (before expiry) | Renewal task created at | Post-expiry cadence | Grace default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Agency Licence (state) | 90 · 60 · 30 · 15 · 7 · 1 | T−90 | Daily | 0 days |
| Agency Licence (district) | 90 · 60 · 30 · 15 · 7 · 1 | T−90 | Daily | 0 days |
| Police Verification | 90 · 60 · 30 · 15 · 7 | T−90 | Daily | 0 days |
| Guard KYC item | 60 · 30 · 15 · 7 · 1 | T−45 | Every 2 days | 0 days |
| Statutory training | 60 · 30 · 15 · 7 · 1 | T−60 | Daily | 0 days |
| Non-statutory training | 30 · 7 | T−30 | Weekly | 30 days |
| Contract | 90 · 60 · 30 · 15 · 7 | T−90 (to Sales owner) | Daily | 0 days |
| Insurance | 60 · 30 · 15 · 7 | T−60 | Daily | 0 days |
| Weapon authorisation | 90 · 60 · 30 · 15 · 7 · 1 | T−90 | Daily | 0 days |
| Tax registration | Event-driven (no fixed expiry by default) | On amendment | — | — |
| Filing calendar item | 15 · 7 · 3 · 1 before due | T−15 | Daily after due | Per obligation |
| Site induction | 30 · 7 | T−30 | Weekly | 14 days |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMP-037 | Every lead time, grace period and cadence in the shipped defaults shall be editable per jurisdiction and per tenant (tightening only for tenants), with the effective-dating machinery of §40.1.4. |
| SUR-CMP-038 | Reminder ladders shall be idempotent: re-running a day's evaluation shall not re-send a reminder already sent for that offset. |

### 40.4 Compliance dashboards

§22.17 and §20 own the screen furniture of the Compliance modules. This subsection specifies the **dashboard content** — the exact cards, horizons, queues, drill-downs and exports — so that both surfaces render the same semantics from the same evaluator output.

#### 40.4.1 Suraksha OPS compliance dashboard

Audience: Compliance (owner), Auditor (read-only), Founder/Management (score + top risks), National/State/City Operations (their scope), Verification (queue focus).

| # | Card | Content | Primary number | Click-through |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | **Compliance Score** | Configured weighted composite with the formula visible on hover (§22.17.4 weights: licence currency 30, guard document compliance 25, verification coverage 20, filings on time 15, open findings 10) | 0–100 with 30-day sparkline | Score breakdown by component, each drilling to its own list |
| C2 | **Licences at Risk** | Own + tenant licences in Expiring / Renewal Pending / Expired / Suspended, grouped by state | Count, with Expired shown separately in red | Licence list filtered; each row → Licence 360 |
| C3 | **Deployment Exposure** | For every Expired or Suspended licence: active deployments, guards and sites in that jurisdiction that the configured consequence affects | Guards affected | Affected deployment list with the management-decision action |
| C4 | **Guard Document Compliance** | % of active guards with all mandatory objects Valid; split by branch and by state | % | Non-compliant guard list, grouped by missing object |
| C5 | **Police Verification Coverage** | Active guards by verification state (Valid / In Progress / Expiring / Expired / Rejected / Not started) | % Valid | Guard list per state bucket |
| C6 | **Training Currency** | Statutory vs non-statutory currency by category (Unarmed / Armed / PSO / Bouncer / Supervisor / Specialised) | % current | Guard list per course |
| C7 | **Verification Queue Health** | Items pending, oldest age, median turnaround, rejection rate, per verifier | Oldest age in hours | Verification workspace (§22.17.2) |
| C8 | **Filing Calendar** | Obligations due in the next 30 days by jurisdiction, with owner and evidence state; overdue items pinned | Count due ≤7 days | Filing item detail with evidence upload |
| C9 | **Open Findings** | Findings by severity and age, with the owner and due date; findings aged past due highlighted | Count P0+P1 | Findings tracker |
| C10 | **Statutory Record Completeness** | Periods with missing generated registers, missing contribution records, or gaps in financial-document sequences | Count of gaps | Gap list per tenant/period |
| C11 | **Override & Exception Register** | Compliance-related overrides used in the period (working-hour overrides, provisional deployments, wage-floor overrides), by role and branch | Count, with 3+/branch/month flagged | Override list with reasons and approvers |
| C12 | **Tenant Compliance Ranking** | Agencies ranked by their compliance score, with the worst 10 pinned; marketplace badge state shown | Count below threshold | Agency 360 → compliance tab |
| C13 | **Unreviewed Rules** | Rules in Active packs with `counsel_review.status = Unreviewed`, by jurisdiction | Count | Rule catalogue filtered |
| C14 | **Evidence Pack Requests** | Open requests for audit packs, their scope and due date | Count open | Pack builder (§40.7) |

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Default time range | "Now" for state cards (C2–C7, C10, C13); rolling 30 days for activity cards (C7 turnaround, C11, C14); rolling 90 days for the C1 sparkline |
| Filters | Jurisdiction (country/state/district) · tenant · branch · object type · status · owner role · severity · guard category · risk band |
| Refresh | Status cards hourly from the materialised store, plus immediate refresh on any evaluator write affecting the current filter; queue cards every 5 minutes |
| Scope enforcement | Every card is scope-injected: State Operations sees their state only, City Operations their city; the card shows "(your scope: Gujarat)" so a number is never mistaken for a national one |
| Empty states | Named and actionable ("No licences expiring in 90 days. Next expiry: Rajasthan, 142 days.") — never a blank card |

#### 40.4.2 Expiry horizon views

One reusable component, used identically in OPS and the Agency Portal.

| Horizon | Contents | Default sort | Bulk actions |
|---|---|---|---|
| **7 days** | Everything with `valid_upto` within 7 days, plus everything already Expired | Severity, then days remaining ascending | Send reminder, assign owner, create renewal task, export |
| **30 days** | Adds the 8–30 day band | Days remaining | Same, plus bulk owner assignment |
| **60 days** | Adds 31–60 | Object type, then days | Same |
| **90 days** | Adds 61–90 | State/branch, then days | Same, plus "plan renewals" view grouping by owner workload |

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Columns | Object type · subject (guard/agency/contract/site) · jurisdiction · identifier · valid_upto · days remaining · status · owner · last reminder sent · renewal state · blocking? (yes/no with the action codes) |
| The "blocking?" column | Computed from the rule's consequence block — it tells the user *what will actually stop* when this expires. This is the single most useful column and is mandatory. |
| Grouping | Toggle: by object type · by owner · by state/branch · by tenant (OPS only) · by blocking impact |
| Density | Table default; a calendar view is available showing expiries by date so renewal workload can be levelled |
| Export | CSV and XLSX with the same columns plus rule_id and rule_version; PDF for a formal list |

#### 40.4.3 The exception queue

The exception queue is where compliance work actually happens. It is a single prioritised worklist, not a set of scattered filters.

| Exception class | Entry condition | Default priority | Required outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Expired blocking object | Any object in Expired whose rule carries `block_action` | P0 | Renewal verified, or a recorded management decision |
| Suspended object | Any Suspended object | P0 | Restoration or a documented closure |
| Adverse verification finding | Police verification Rejected, or adverse note | P0 | Human review decision with reason and notification |
| Verification queue breach | Item pending beyond the configured SLA (default 48 h) | P1 | Verified or Rejected |
| Rejected evidence not re-submitted | Rejected for more than configured days (default 7) | P1 | Re-submission or escalation |
| Overdue filing | Filing calendar item past due | P1 | Evidence uploaded or exception documented |
| Wage-floor breach at payroll review | Payroll run blocked by the configured floor | P1 | Correction or dual-control override |
| Expiring within 7 days with no renewal activity | No renewal task progress and no evidence | P1 | Task assigned and progressed |
| Data inconsistency | Name variance unresolved; licence jurisdiction not covering an active deployment; guard category without required training; document sequence gap | P2 | Resolution with a recorded decision |
| Unreviewed rule in force | Active rule with `counsel_review.status = Unreviewed` | P2 | Review recorded or rule suspended |
| Override cluster | ≥3 overrides of the same type at one branch in a month | P2 | Investigation finding |
| Stale ownership | Object whose owner is inactive or unassigned | P3 | Reassignment |

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Queue behaviour | Assignable, claimable, snoozable with a mandatory reason and a maximum snooze (default 7 days), and never silently closable — every exit writes an outcome record |
| SLA per class | Configured per class; breach escalates per §40.5 |
| Bulk handling | Permitted only for homogeneous P2/P3 classes (e.g. reassign 40 stale-owner items). Never for P0. |
| Ageing display | Days in queue, colour-banded; the oldest item's age is a headline metric on C7 |

#### 40.4.4 Agency Portal compliance dashboard (Professional and Enterprise)

Per the canon plan matrix, the compliance dashboard is a **Professional+** feature. Starter tenants get expiry reminders and document status inside the guard and agency profile screens, but not the dashboard, the exception queue or the audit-pack export.

| # | Card | Content | Starter | Professional | Enterprise |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | My Compliance Score | Same composite, tenant-scoped, formula visible | — | Yes | Yes |
| A2 | My Licences | Own state/district licences with status and days remaining | Read-only list in profile | Card + drill-down | + multi-entity view |
| A3 | Guard Documents | % compliant, non-compliant list, missing-item breakdown | Basic list | Full card + bulk reminder | + bulk import/renewal workflows |
| A4 | Police Verification | Coverage by state bucket | Basic list | Full | Full |
| A5 | Training Currency | By category and course | — | Yes | + custom courses |
| A6 | Expiry Horizon (7/30/60/90) | The §40.4.2 component | 30-day only, read-only | All horizons + bulk actions | + scheduled export |
| A7 | Exception Queue | Tenant-scoped worklist | — | Yes | + custom classes and SLAs |
| A8 | Filing Calendar | Configured obligations with owners and evidence | — | Yes | + multi-entity, custom obligations |
| A9 | Deployment Blockers | What is currently blocked and why, with the remediation path | Inline warnings only | Card | Card + API |
| A10 | Client Compliance Requests | Evidence packs requested by clients, with due dates | — | Yes | + templated packs per client |
| A11 | Audit Pack Builder | §40.7 | — | Standard packs | Custom packs, scheduled, API |
| A12 | Statutory Records | Register generation status, contribution record completeness | — | Yes | + custom registers |

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Scope | Strictly `tenant_id`; Branch Manager sees their branch only; Agency Viewer read-only |
| Refresh | Hourly, plus immediate on evidence upload or verification outcome |
| Export | CSV/XLSX/PDF; Professional gets manual export, Enterprise gets scheduled and API |
| Tone | The dashboard states status and consequence; it never states obligation as law. Every card footer links to "How these rules are configured" (§40.12) |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMP-039 | OPS and Agency Portal compliance dashboards shall render from the same evaluator output and the same status store; the two surfaces shall never be able to disagree about an object's status. |
| SUR-CMP-040 | Every compliance card shall be able to answer "what does this stop me doing?" — the consequence set shall be visible from the card, not only in the rule catalogue. |
| SUR-CMP-041 | Compliance exports shall carry the rule version, the evaluation timestamp and the generating user, and the export event shall itself be audited. |

### 40.5 Reminder and escalation ladders

Delivery mechanics, channel selection, quiet hours, throttling and template management belong to §36. This subsection defines **who is told, when, and what happens if nobody acts**.

#### 40.5.1 Ladder structure

A ladder is data: an ordered list of steps, each with an offset, an audience, a severity and an action.

| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ladder_id` | e.g. `LADDER_LICENCE` |
| `steps[]` | `{offset, audience_roles[], channels[], template_id, severity, action}` where offset may be pre-expiry (T−n), post-expiry (T+n) or queue-age based |
| `stop_condition` | What ends the ladder (status becomes Valid; successor verified; exception closed) |
| `repeat` | Cadence after the last step (e.g. daily until stopped) |
| `quiet_hours` | Whether the ladder may break quiet hours; only P0 ladders may |
| `dedupe_window` | Prevents multiple objects generating repeated identical messages to one person; digest instead |

#### 40.5.2 The ladders

**LADDER_LICENCE** (agency licence, state or district; also used for weapon authorisation)

| Step | When | Audience | Channel | Severity | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | T−90 | Object owner (Compliance / Agency Compliance) | In-app + Email | P3 | Renewal task created with a due date at T−45 |
| 2 | T−60 | Owner + Agency Owner / National Operations | In-app + Email | P2 | Task overdue check |
| 3 | T−30 | + Founder/Management (Suraksha) or Agency Owner (tenant) | In-app + Email + WhatsApp | P1 | Deployment-exposure report attached |
| 4 | T−15 | + State Operations for the jurisdiction | All incl. SMS | P1 | Blocking preview: "on <date>, N allocations will be blocked" |
| 5 | T−7 | + Super Admin | All | P0 | Daily thereafter |
| 6 | T−1 | Everyone above | All incl. call task | P0 | Command Center informational note |
| 7 | T+0 (expiry) | Everyone above + affected Branch Managers | All | P0 | Consequences dispatched; management-decision task created for existing deployments |
| 8 | T+1 daily | Everyone above | In-app + Email daily, WhatsApp every 3 days | P0 | Escalation to Founder/Management weekly summary |

**LADDER_PERSON_DOC** (guard KYC, police verification, statutory training)

| Step | When | Audience | Channel | Severity | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | T−60 | The guard (their language) + their Supervisor | Push + SMS | P3 | Guard App task "renew document" with what is needed |
| 2 | T−30 | + Agency HR / HR | Push + In-app + Email | P2 | Renewal task assigned |
| 3 | T−15 | + Branch Manager / City Operations | + WhatsApp | P2 | Allocation soft-flag begins |
| 4 | T−7 | + Agency Compliance / Compliance | All | P1 | "This guard becomes ineligible on <date>" with their upcoming shifts listed |
| 5 | T−1 | Same | All | P1 | Roster impact preview: shifts needing replacement |
| 6 | T+0 | + Operations Manager, Command Center (if the guard has a shift within 24 h) | All | P0 for on-duty guards, P1 otherwise | Veto applies; replacement task auto-created for affected shifts |
| 7 | T+2 daily | Same | Digest | P1 | Counted in branch compliance metrics |

**LADDER_CONTRACT**

| Step | When | Audience | Channel | Severity | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | T−90 | Account owner (Sales / Agency Sales) | In-app + Email | P3 | Renewal opportunity created in CRM |
| 2 | T−60 | + Operations Manager / City Operations | In-app + Email | P2 | Deployment and revenue exposure attached |
| 3 | T−30 | + Agency Owner / Founder/Management | + WhatsApp | P2 | Client-facing renewal communication drafted (AI draft, human sends — §25.7.1 row 18) |
| 4 | T−15 | + Finance | All | P1 | Billing continuity check |
| 5 | T−7 | Same | All | P1 | Escalation: named decision owner required |
| 6 | T+0 | All above | All | P1 | Invoice issuance blocked per configured consequence; deployment decision task raised |

**LADDER_FILING**

| Step | When | Audience | Channel | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Due−15 | Obligation owner | In-app + Email | P3 |
| 2 | Due−7 | + Compliance / Agency Compliance | + WhatsApp | P2 |
| 3 | Due−3 | + Finance | All | P2 |
| 4 | Due−1 | + Agency Owner / Founder/Management | All | P1 |
| 5 | Due+1 daily | All above | All | P1, escalating to P0 at Due+7 |

**LADDER_QUEUE** (verification and exception SLA breaches)

| Step | When | Audience | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | SLA×0.75 | Assigned verifier | P3 |
| 2 | SLA breach | + Verification lead | P2 |
| 3 | SLA×2 | + Compliance | P1 |
| 4 | SLA×4 | + Founder/Management, appears on C7 as a named breach | P0 |

**LADDER_EXCEPTION_P0** (expired blocking objects, suspensions, adverse findings)

| Step | When | Audience | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | On creation | Compliance + object owner + affected branch | P0 |
| 2 | +4 h no acknowledgement | + Founder/Management (Suraksha) / Agency Owner (tenant) | P0 |
| 3 | +24 h unresolved | + Super Admin; item pinned to the OPS command band | P0 |
| 4 | +72 h unresolved | Weekly management report entry, permanent finding record | P0 |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMP-042 | Every compliance object type shall be attached to exactly one ladder; an object type with no ladder shall fail rule publication validation. |
| SUR-CMP-043 | Reminders to guards shall be sent in the guard's configured language, shall state exactly which document, which date and what to do, and shall be readable at low literacy — short sentences, one action, plus a voice option in the Guard App (§25.4). |
| SUR-CMP-044 | Reminders shall be deduplicated per recipient per day into a digest where more than a configured number (default 5) of items would otherwise be sent, except P0 items which are always sent individually. |
| SUR-CMP-045 | Every reminder and escalation sent shall be recorded against the compliance object so that the evidence pack can show a documented reminder trail. |
| SUR-CMP-046 | An escalation shall never be closable by the person or branch that is its subject; closure requires the escalation owner or above. |

### 40.6 Deployment gating

This subsection states **which compliance outcomes stop work**. The mechanism lives in §25.15.5 (the allocation-engine compliance veto) and the rules live in §30. This is the compliance-side view: the complete gate list, the warn list, and the override authority table.

#### 40.6.1 Hard blocks (allocation refused)

| Condition | Scope of block | Override | Cross-reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| Police verification missing, Expired or Rejected | All allocations for that person | **None** | §25.15.5 |
| Guard status not Active (Suspended, Archived, exited) | All | **None** | BR-001 context |
| Blacklisted or under disciplinary hold | All | **None** | §22.6 |
| Mandatory KYC evidence missing, Expired or Rejected | All | **None** | §40.2.3 |
| Statutory training Expired for the post's category | Allocations to posts of that category | **None** | §40.2.5 |
| Weapon authorisation invalid or Expired | Armed posts | **None** | §40.2.10 |
| Agency licence Expired or Suspended for the deployment's jurisdiction | **New** allocations in that jurisdiction | **None** for new | BR-002, §40.2.2 |
| No licence object at all covering the deployment's jurisdiction | New allocations in that jurisdiction | **None** | §40.8.3 |
| Overlapping active assignment | The specific overlapping assignment | Authorised exception per BR-001 | §30 |
| Working-hour ceiling breach | The specific assignment | State Operations only, reason recorded, notified to Compliance, counted; ≥3/branch/month is itself a finding | §25.15.5 |

#### 40.6.2 Warnings (allocation permitted, flagged)

| Condition | Effect | Who sees it |
|---|---|---|
| Any mandatory object in Expiring within the configured window (default 7 days) | −5 allocation score, risk flag on the approval card, auto-created renewal task | Allocator, approver, owner |
| Non-statutory training Expired | −15 skill factor, risk flag | Allocator, approver |
| Police verification "In Progress" where the rule permits provisional deployment | Requires the time-bounded Compliance override; flagged on every shift until resolved | Allocator, Compliance, Branch Manager |
| Site induction expired | Risk flag; supervisor accompaniment suggested | Allocator, Supervisor |
| Insurance record Expiring | Flag on contracts referencing it | Sales, Finance, Compliance |
| Guard's employment record incomplete | Flag; configurable to block payroll inclusion but not allocation by default | HR, Payroll |
| Contract Expiring within 30 days | Flag on new allocations to that client's sites | Sales, Operations |

#### 40.6.3 Non-allocation gates

| Action | Blocking condition (configured default) | Override authority |
|---|---|---|
| Site activation | Site compliance record incomplete | City Operations with reason |
| Contract activation | Licence not Valid for the site's jurisdiction; mandatory contract evidence missing | Founder/Management, dual control |
| Invoice issuance | Contract Expired; tax registration record invalid | Finance + Founder/Management, dual control |
| Payroll release | Wage record below configured floor; mandatory employment artefacts missing (where configured) | Agency Finance + Founder/Management (tenant) / Finance + Super Admin (Suraksha) |
| Marketplace listing visible + Verified badge | Licence not Valid | **None** — the badge is a public claim and is never overridable |
| Tender/bid submission | Any mandatory eligibility evidence missing | Founder/Management, with the missing items listed in the override record |
| Guard activation | Mandatory KYC not Verified; police verification not at least In Progress | Compliance, with reason and an override expiry |
| Migration import commit | Imported objects failing schema or mandatory-evidence checks | Enterprise onboarding lead + Compliance, per-batch, with an exception report |

#### 40.6.4 Override governance

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| What an override is | A time-bounded, reason-coded, named-approver permission to proceed despite a configured non-hard gate. It never changes the object's compliance status. |
| Never overridable | The §40.6.1 "None" rows, and the marketplace Verified badge. These are structural: no UI path, no API path, no role. |
| Required fields | Approver identity and role · reason from a coded list · free-text justification (mandatory, minimum length enforced) · expiry date/time (mandatory, maximum per override type) · affected entities |
| Notification | Every override notifies Compliance immediately and appears in card C11 |
| Expiry | On override expiry the gate re-applies automatically; a renewal of the override requires a fresh approval at one level higher |
| Reporting | Monthly override report by type, branch, approver and reason; clustering (≥3 same-type at one branch) opens an automatic P2 finding |
| Audit | Override records are retained for the full retention period of the underlying object, and are always included in evidence packs |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-CMP-047 | Hard blocks shall be enforced at both recommendation time and commit time, and a person who becomes non-compliant between the two shall be refused at commit with the reason (mirrors SUR-AI-027). |
| SUR-CMP-048 | No override shall be permanent; every override shall carry a mandatory expiry with a configured maximum per type (default 30 days, 7 days for provisional deployment). |
| SUR-CMP-049 | Overrides shall be surfaced to the affected person where the override concerns them (e.g. a guard deployed on a provisional basis is told, in their language, what is outstanding and by when). |
| SUR-CMP-050 | The platform shall never present an override as making an obligation satisfied; the object remains in its true state and the dashboard continues to show it. |
