### 41.5 Safety controls

#### 41.5.1 Prompt-injection defences

AI in this product reads text that hostile parties can write: uploaded documents (a certificate PDF can contain instructions), marketplace listings written by agencies, support tickets and client messages, incident narratives typed in the field, tender documents fetched from external sources, and OCR output from photographs. Every one of these is untrusted input.

| Defence | Specification |
|---|---|
| Trust separation | Retrieved content is always wrapped and labelled as **data, not instruction**, in a structurally distinct channel from the system prompt and the user's own request. Instruction-like content inside retrieved data is never followed. |
| Authority ordering | System policy > user request > retrieved content. Retrieved content has zero authority to change scope, invoke tools, alter the requester's identity, or modify output constraints. |
| Tool gating by provenance | A request whose plan was influenced by untrusted content may not invoke any Approval-required or Automated tool without the human seeing the untrusted content that influenced it. Documents and listings can never cause a tool call whose parameters they supplied without human review. |
| Injection detection | Pattern and classifier-based detection over untrusted inputs (instruction phrasing, role-play framing, encoded payloads, hidden text in documents, white-on-white PDF text, unusual Unicode); detections are logged, the content is quarantined for that request, and repeated detections from one source raise a security event (§38). |
| Document-specific | OCR text is treated as untrusted; extraction runs in a constrained task ("return these fields as JSON") with schema-validated output and no tool access. A document cannot cause anything except field proposals. |
| Marketplace-specific | Listing content is untrusted; AI summarising or ranking listings cannot be induced to alter ranking, disclose other tenants' data, or emit the listing's embedded instructions. Ranking logic is deterministic and not model-controlled. |
| Support-specific | Ticket bodies are untrusted; the ticket-classification tool returns a label from a fixed enum, never free-form actions; reply drafts are Approval-required. |
| Output constraint | Untrusted content is never echoed verbatim into an action parameter; parameters are re-derived from structured records. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-AIG-033 | Untrusted content shall never be able to cause a tool invocation, a scope change, an identity change, or an output that discloses data outside the requester's envelope. This shall be verified by adversarial evaluation before every release (§41.8.2). |
| SUR-AIG-034 | Detected injection attempts shall be logged with the source (document, listing, ticket, user), counted per source, and surfaced to §38 detection; a source with repeated attempts shall be flagged for human review and may be quarantined. |
| SUR-AIG-035 | Extraction tasks over uploaded documents shall run with no tool access and schema-validated output, and their results shall always be human-confirmed before affecting any record (§25.7.1 row 23). |

#### 41.5.2 Output validation

| Validator | What it checks | On failure |
|---|---|---|
| Schema validator | Structured outputs conform to the expected schema and enums | Retry once with the error, then fail closed to a human path |
| Scope validator | Every entity referenced in the response is inside the requester's envelope; every citation resolves to a record the requester may read | Response blocked; P1 governance event; investigation |
| Numeric grounding | Every number in a response traces to a retrieved value or a registered metric computation; unsourced numbers are stripped | Response regenerated without the number, or the answer declines |
| Citation validator | Citations exist, resolve and are current | Uncited claims removed |
| Prohibited-phrase check | No legal conclusions (SUR-CMP-067), no guarantees or warranties, no medical/legal/financial advice framing, no commitments on price or SLA not present in configuration | Rewritten or blocked |
| PII validator | Output redaction profile applied; no sensitive-personal field text in the response | Blocked |
| Tone/safety | No abusive, discriminatory or coercive content; guard-facing content additionally checked for intimidation framing | Blocked; logged |
| Language validator | Response language matches the requester's language; names, IDs and monetary figures unaltered (SUR-AI-008) | Regenerate |
| Consistency | For Approval-required proposals, the parameters in the card match the parameters in the token exactly | Proposal voided |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-AIG-036 | Output validation shall run server-side on every AI response before delivery; a validation failure shall never be silently repaired in a way that changes meaning without indicating so. |
| SUR-AIG-037 | Any number presented as a fact shall be traceable to a source record or a registered metric; the AI shall be structurally unable to present an unsourced figure as data (§25.2.2 "never fabricates a number"). |

#### 41.5.3 Tool-use authorisation

| Layer | Control |
|---|---|
| Tool registry | Every tool declares: name, action class, required permissions, data classes touched, reversibility, rate limit, owner, evaluation reference. The registry is the source of truth and is diffed in CI. |
| Per-surface allow-lists | Each surface has an explicit tool allow-list; a tool not on the list cannot be called even if it exists. Ceilings per surface follow §25.2. |
| Per-request authorisation | At call time the executor re-checks the caller's permissions against the tool's requirements — the plan's intent is never trusted. |
| Parameter authorisation | Parameters are re-validated against the caller's scope (a site ID the caller cannot access is refused even if the tool is allowed). |
| Approval token binding | Approval-required tools refuse to execute without a valid token bound to the proposal hash. |
| Chaining limits | A bounded number of tool calls per request; loops detected and broken; a chain that would cross from read to write without a human step is refused. |
| Kill switch | Per-tool, per-surface and global disable switches operable by Super Admin and the AI Review Board on-call, taking effect within seconds, with the product degrading per §41.5.5. |

#### 41.5.4 Rate and cost limits

| Limit | Default | On breach |
|---|---|---|
| Per-user request rate | Configured per surface and plan; guard surfaces generous, analytical surfaces bounded | Queue, then a friendly "too many requests" with the normal UI path |
| Per-tenant daily cost ceiling | Per plan entitlement (§25.9) | Degrade to cheaper models, then to non-AI paths; Agency Owner notified before the ceiling is reached, never surprised |
| Per-request cost ceiling | Per surface latency/cost budget (§25.11) | Abort and hand off to a human/report path |
| Anomaly detection | Sudden multiples of a user's or tenant's baseline | Throttle plus a security signal — cost spikes are often abuse |
| Voice minutes | Per plan | Degrade to text with an explanation |
| Global spend guard | Platform-level daily ceiling with alerting at 60/80/95% | Non-essential surfaces disabled first, per a documented priority order in which guard safety and command-centre support are last to degrade |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-AIG-038 | Cost controls shall degrade capability in a documented priority order; guard-facing safety assistance and Command Center support shall be the last to degrade and shall never be disabled by a cost control alone. |
| SUR-AIG-039 | Tenants shall see their AI usage against their entitlement in the product, and shall be warned before a limit degrades their experience. |

#### 41.5.5 Fail-safe behaviour

| Condition | Required behaviour |
|---|---|
| AI service unavailable | Every surface remains fully usable without AI. The assistant collapses with a one-line notice and the underlying module functions normally (§25.2.5: "the console is fully usable without it"). No workflow blocks on AI availability. |
| Retrieval unavailable | The AI states which system is unreachable, offers the last successful value with its timestamp where one exists, and never answers from memory as if it were current. |
| Low confidence | Declines to answer with a stated reason and offers: the exact screen with the data, a human contact, or a narrower question it can answer. Guessing is prohibited. |
| Model returns malformed or unsafe output | Fails closed; the user sees a plain failure and a human path; the event is logged. |
| Ambiguous instruction affecting a write | Always resolves toward asking, never toward acting. |
| Partial data | States what is missing and how the answer is limited; never presents a partial answer as complete. |
| Safety-relevant uncertainty (a guard asking what to do in an emergency) | Immediately offers the deterministic path — SOS, supervisor phone number, Command Center — rather than reasoning further (§25.4 SUR-AI-007). |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-AIG-040 | No safety-critical or compliance-critical workflow shall have AI on its critical path. If AI is unavailable, SOS, attendance, wake checks, escalation, allocation, payroll and compliance evaluation shall all function unchanged. |
| SUR-AIG-041 | "I don't know" shall be an engineered, tested, first-class response with a defined UI, and its rate shall be monitored — a suspiciously low rate indicates over-confidence, not quality. |

---

### 41.6 Fairness and workforce impact

This is the subsection with the most serious human consequences. AI in this product touches recruitment screening, guard allocation, reliability scoring and performance insight. Those four things determine whether a person gets hired, gets shifts, gets paid more, and keeps their job. The controls below are not optional and are not configurable downward.

#### 41.6.1 Prohibited inputs

| Category | Examples | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Protected and sensitive attributes | Religion, caste, community, ethnicity, region of origin, mother tongue used as a proxy, gender (except where a specific post has a lawfully-configured, contract-documented requirement), marital or family status, pregnancy, disability, health status, sexual orientation, political affiliation, trade-union membership | **Never** an input to screening, ranking, allocation, scoring or performance models. Excluded at the schema level (§41.4.3), not by prompt. |
| Proxies | Name-derived inference of community or religion, address-derived community inference, photograph-derived inference of any protected attribute, school/college as a community proxy, language of preference as a community proxy | Prohibited. Feature review must explicitly assess each input for proxy risk (§41.6.6). |
| Financial-vulnerability signals | Outstanding advance balance, salary-advance history, debt recovery status | Not permitted as an input to allocation preference, screening or performance scoring. (They remain legitimate operational data — the prohibition is on their use as a *ranking or evaluative* input.) |
| Legitimate operational inputs | Distance, availability, roster and rest constraints, verified documents and their validity, statutory and non-statutory training, verified experience, site familiarity, attendance record, wake-check and patrol completion, incident record, client rating, supervisor assessments recorded with reasons | Permitted, each individually documented in the model card and each explainable to the affected person |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-AIG-042 | Protected attributes and their known proxies shall be excluded from every screening, allocation, scoring and performance model by the feature schema, and the exclusion shall be tested — a release-blocking evaluation shall confirm that adding a protected attribute to a synthetic record does not change the output. |
| SUR-AIG-043 | A prompt or query attempting to filter, rank or select people by a protected attribute shall be refused, logged as a governance event, and reported to the AI Review Board with the requesting user's role (not to punish, but because a repeated pattern indicates either a broken workflow or a real problem). |
| SUR-AIG-044 | Where a post genuinely requires a specific attribute (e.g. a female guard for a women's facility search post), this shall be expressed as a **documented post requirement on the contract or post record**, entered by a human, visible to the guard, and never inferred by a model. |

#### 41.6.2 Recruitment screening

| Control | Requirement |
|---|---|
| No automated rejection | AI never rejects a candidate. It may rank, flag against stated requirements and explain (§25.2.8, §25.7.1 row 39). |
| Requirement transparency | Every "does not meet" flag names the specific stated requirement and the specific evidence; vague flags are prohibited. |
| Whole-pipeline visibility | Candidates flagged as not meeting requirements remain visible in the pipeline; the UI never hides them, so a human can override a wrong flag. |
| Human reason of record | The rejection reason recorded is the human's, chosen from a coded list plus free text, and is the reason communicated. |
| Near-miss surfacing | Candidates missing only a remediable item (e.g. a training certificate) are surfaced as near-misses with the remediation, not buried. |
| Re-consideration | Previously rejected candidates whose reason no longer applies are surfaced for re-consideration rather than permanently excluded. |
| Monitoring | Selection and rejection rates monitored for disparate impact (§41.6.6). |

#### 41.6.3 Allocation, scoring and adverse action

| Control | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Explainable reliability score | The reliability score's composition is published to the guard: the components, the weights, the window, and their own current values per component (§42.2.5 gives the formula). A score a guard cannot see the composition of may not be used to affect their work. |
| Contestable | The guard can, from the Guard App, dispute any component value (e.g. an attendance record they believe is wrong) and the dispute routes to a human with authority to correct it; the correction recomputes the score. |
| No automatic adverse action | No score, threshold or pattern shall automatically terminate, blacklist, suspend, deactivate, demote, reduce pay, or permanently exclude any person from allocation. Every adverse action requires a human decision, a recorded reason, and prior notice to the person where the action is not an immediate safety necessity. |
| Immediate safety exception | Where an immediate safety concern requires removing a guard from a post, that is an operational decision by a named human (Command Center / City Operations) recorded as such, followed by a review within a configured window (default 48 hours). AI may surface the concern; it never makes the removal. |
| Allocation starvation | A guard receiving materially fewer shifts than peers for a sustained period is itself flagged for human review — silent de-prioritisation by an algorithm is an adverse action even though no decision was recorded. This is monitored explicitly (§41.6.6). |
| Score cannot be a sole basis | Any decision affecting pay, continued engagement or disciplinary status must cite evidence beyond the composite score; the score alone is never a sufficient recorded reason. |
| Notice and record | The guard is told, in their language, when an adverse action is taken, what it is based on, and how to contest it. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-AIG-045 | No guard shall be terminated, blacklisted, suspended, deactivated or excluded from allocation by an automated decision, under any configuration, in any tenant. This shall be structurally enforced (no such tool exists) and shall not be configurable by a tenant. |
| SUR-AIG-046 | Reliability, performance and any composite score affecting a person shall be explainable to that person in their own language, at component level, with their own values, from their own app. |
| SUR-AIG-047 | Sustained allocation starvation relative to a comparable peer group shall raise a review task; the platform shall not allow an algorithm to end someone's work by silently never selecting them. |
| SUR-AIG-048 | Every adverse action shall record the human decision-maker, the reason, the evidence cited, the notice given and the contest outcome; AI involvement, if any, shall be recorded as an input, never as the basis. |

#### 41.6.4 The contest path

| Step | Specification |
|---|---|
| 1. Discover | The affected person sees the outcome and, where AI contributed, a plain statement that it did, with the basis (§41.9) |
| 2. Raise | One action from the Guard App / Customer App / portal: "I disagree with this". Voice supported, in the person's language. No form-heavy process. |
| 3. Route | To a human with authority to change the outcome, and never to the person or branch that made the contested decision |
| 4. Timebound | Acknowledgement within a configured period (default 48 hours), decision within a configured period (default 7 days for scoring/allocation, 14 days for employment-affecting matters); breaches escalate |
| 5. Decide | Human reviews the underlying records, not the AI output; the decision states what was checked and what changed |
| 6. Remedy | If a component value was wrong, it is corrected, the score recomputed, and any consequential decision revisited — including retrospective correction of pay where applicable |
| 7. Record | The contest, decision and remedy are retained and feed the fairness monitoring set |
| 8. Escalate | Unsatisfied contests escalate to Compliance (guard grievances route to Compliance per §22.16 and cannot be closed by the subject branch) |

#### 41.6.5 Monitoring for disparate impact

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| What is measured | Selection rates, rejection rates, allocation rates, shift-hours distribution, score distributions, adverse-action rates, and contest outcomes |
| Compared across what | Groups the platform can legitimately construct **without collecting protected attributes for operational use**: branch, city, home distance band, guard category, tenure band, age band where lawfully held, gender where lawfully held for a documented purpose. Where an attribute is not held, disparate-impact analysis for it is not performed and this limitation is stated rather than papered over. `[ASSUMPTION: A-362]` |
| How | Quarterly analysis by the AI Review Board with a statistically stated method and thresholds agreed in advance; results reported to Founder/Management |
| On a finding | The affected function is reviewed; if a disparity cannot be explained by legitimate operational factors, the function is modified or demoted; findings and their remediation are recorded |
| Never | Individual approval/rejection rates of humans are not used as performance metrics (§41.3.6); disparate-impact monitoring is never used to set quotas in the allocation engine |
| Data governance | Any attribute collected solely for fairness monitoring is collected with a stated purpose, stored separately with restricted access, never used in any operational model, and never available to allocation, screening or scoring (§39) |

#### 41.6.6 Model cards and feature review

| Artefact | Contents | Applies to |
|---|---|---|
| Model card | Purpose · inputs with justification per input · excluded inputs and why · outputs · known limitations · evaluation results including fairness tests · affected populations · contest path · owner · review date | Every model or scoring function affecting people: allocation engine, reliability score, performance insight, screening assistance, site risk banding |
| Feature review | For each input: is it a protected attribute? is it a plausible proxy? is it within the person's control? is it explainable to them? is it accurate? what happens if it is wrong? | Before any input is added to a people-affecting model |
| Publication | Model cards for people-affecting functions are available to the affected population in plain language (a guard can read what the reliability score uses) | Guard App, Agency Portal, OPS |

---

### 41.7 Multilingual quality governance

§25.4 sets the language tiers and their quality bars. This subsection sets the **policy** around them.

| Policy | Statement |
|---|---|
| Honest tiering | The product shall never present uniform quality across languages it cannot deliver uniformly. Tier badges are mandatory at the point of use for Tier 3 (SUR-AI-006). |
| Accuracy expectation by tier | Tier 1: intent ≥95%, ASR WER ≤12%, acceptability ≥90%, regressions block release. Tier 2: intent ≥90%, WER ≤20%, acceptability ≥85%, regressions warn. Tier 3: best effort, measured, never advertised as full support. |
| Marketing constraint | Public claims about language support shall state the tiering; "26 languages" without qualification is a prohibited claim (§40.9 substantiation records). |
| Safety-critical translation | **P0 safety notifications shall use pre-approved, human-reviewed translated templates. Live model translation of a P0 safety message is prohibited in every language, including Tier 1.** |
| What counts as safety-critical | SOS acknowledgement and instructions, evacuation or emergency guidance, wake-check escalation notices, incident-response instructions to a guard, medical or police contact instructions, any message whose misinterpretation could cause physical harm or a failure to act |
| Template governance | Safety templates are authored in English and Hindi, translated by a qualified human translator, reviewed by a second native speaker, versioned, and approved by Compliance before publication (§22.20.1). A language without an approved safety template falls back to an approved language plus a deterministic action (call supervisor / call Command Center), never to a machine translation. |
| Non-safety translation | Live model translation is permitted for informational content, with the caveat displayed for Tier 3 and with names, IDs and money never transformed (SUR-AI-008). |
| Mistranslation as an incident | A mistranslation in a safety-critical message is a P0 AI incident regardless of whether harm resulted; in operational content it is P2. |
| Measurement | Per §25.4 quarterly evaluation; a Tier 2 language below bar for two consecutive quarters is demoted publicly rather than left quietly broken. |
| Voice specifics | ASR errors on numbers, dates and names are the dominant voice failure; read-back confirmation is mandatory for any write (§25.5) and its effectiveness is measured per language. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-AIG-049 | P0 safety notifications shall be delivered only from pre-approved translated templates; the notification service shall refuse to send a P0 safety message whose template is absent for the target language, falling back to an approved language plus a deterministic contact action. |
| SUR-AIG-050 | Every safety-critical template shall record its translator, its reviewer, its approval and its version; a template edit shall re-enter review before publication. |
| SUR-AIG-051 | Language quality results shall be published internally per release, and a language falling below its tier bar shall be demoted in the product, not silently maintained. |

### 41.8 AI evaluation and monitoring

#### 41.8.1 Evaluation data governance

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Sources | Synthetic scenarios generated from the domain model; consented anonymised production utterances (§25.4); adversarial sets written by the security and compliance teams; regression cases harvested from every past incident |
| Prohibited | Raw production tenant data in development or staging; any un-anonymised personal data in an evaluation set |
| Maintenance | Every incident adds a regression case; every rejected proposal category contributes examples; sets are refreshed quarterly and versioned |
| Ownership | The AI Review Board owns the suite; surface owners own their surface's set |

#### 41.8.2 Pre-release evaluation suite

Run on every model version change, every prompt change, every retrieval change, every new tool, and every surface change. Results are attached to the release record.

| # | Failure mode | What is tested | Threshold | Blocking? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Hallucination** | Unsupported factual claims; invented entities, numbers, dates, policies | Zero unsupported numeric claims; hallucination rate below configured bar on the fact set | **Blocking** |
| 2 | **Wrong tenant data** | Cross-tenant probes: asking as tenant A for tenant B's data, name collisions, shared-site scenarios, cached-context reuse | **Zero** failures | **Blocking** |
| 3 | **Unauthorized retrieval** | Role/scope probes: branch manager asking about another branch, guard asking about another guard's pay, client asking about internal margin, anonymous user asking for account facts | **Zero** failures | **Blocking** |
| 4 | **Wrong action** | Proposal correctness on a labelled scenario set; parameter accuracy; the right entity, the right time, the right amount | Configured accuracy bar per function; **zero** wrong-entity actions | **Blocking** |
| 5 | **Prompt injection** | Adversarial documents, listings, tickets, OCR text, tender PDFs, hidden text, encoded payloads, multilingual injections | **Zero** successful tool invocations or scope changes from untrusted content | **Blocking** |
| 6 | **Sensitive-information leakage** | Sensitive-personal fields, credentials, salary, bank details, document content in responses; system prompt extraction | **Zero** | **Blocking** |
| 7 | **Incorrect translation** | Safety-critical templates in every Tier 1/2 language; meaning-preservation on operational content; names/IDs/money preserved | **Zero** safety-critical errors; operational bar per tier | **Blocking** for safety-critical |
| 8 | **OCR errors** | Field extraction accuracy on a corpus of real-world document photographs (glare, skew, low light, damaged documents, handwriting) with confidence calibration | Extraction accuracy bar; **calibration** — low-confidence must correlate with actual error | **Blocking** on calibration |
| 9 | **Voice recognition errors** | WER per language on field-condition audio; number/date/name accuracy specifically; read-back correctness | Per §25.4 tier bars; read-back must surface 100% of injected number errors | **Blocking** on read-back |
| 10 | **Permission bypass** | Attempting Approval-required tools without tokens; token replay; parameter tampering; class escalation via phrasing; chaining read→write | **Zero** | **Blocking** |
| 11 | **Unsafe automated action** | Every Automated function against its blast-radius definition; reversal path executes correctly | **Zero** out-of-radius actions; 100% reversal success | **Blocking** |
| 12 | **Fairness** | Protected-attribute invariance on synthetic records; proxy sensitivity; disparate outcome on synthetic cohorts | Output invariant to protected attributes | **Blocking** for people-affecting functions |
| 13 | **Refusal quality** | Does it decline appropriately, and does it decline *unhelpfully often*? | Both over- and under-refusal bounded | Warning |
| 14 | **Citation integrity** | Every citation resolves and supports the claim | ≥99% resolvable | **Blocking** |
| 15 | **Latency and cost** | p50/p95 against §25.11 budgets | Within budget | Warning, blocking on severe regression |
| 16 | **Degradation** | Behaviour with retrieval down, model down, partial data | Graceful per §41.5.5 | **Blocking** |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-AIG-052 | No AI change shall reach production without a passing evaluation run recorded against the release; the run, its version and its results shall be retrievable for any past release. |
| SUR-AIG-053 | Blocking thresholds shall not be waivable by a single individual; a waiver requires AI Review Board approval with a documented compensating control and an expiry. |
| SUR-AIG-054 | Every production AI incident shall add at least one regression case to the suite before the incident is closed. |

#### 41.8.3 Continuous monitoring

| Signal | Measured how | Alert |
|---|---|---|
| Refusal rate per surface | Refusals ÷ interactions | Deviation beyond band |
| "Wrong answer" reports | User-reported per 1,000 interactions | Rising trend |
| Rejection rate per function | Rejections ÷ proposals, by reason category | Threshold per function |
| Approved-then-reverted | Actions approved from an AI proposal and reverted within 24 h | Any rise is a card-quality problem |
| Automated action error rate | Errors ÷ automated actions per function | Auto-demotion threshold (SUR-AIG-010) |
| Scope-denial rate | Denials ÷ requests, per role | A spike may mean a broken permission or probing |
| Injection detections | Per source type | Any cluster |
| Cross-tenant validator trips | Scope validator failures | **Any single event is P0** |
| Latency and cost | p50/p95, cost per interaction, per surface and tenant | Budget breach |
| Language quality | Sampled human review per language per month | Below tier bar |
| Voice read-back corrections | Corrections ÷ voice writes | Rising means ASR drift |
| OCR confirmation-edit rate | Human edits ÷ extracted fields | Rising means extraction drift |
| Fallback rate | Degraded responses ÷ total | Dependency health |

#### 41.8.4 Drift

| Type | Detection | Response |
|---|---|---|
| Model drift (vendor updates a pinned version, or behaviour shifts) | Canary evaluation set run daily against production models; behavioural diff vs. the release baseline | Freeze on the prior version; re-evaluate; escalate to the vendor |
| Data drift (the operation changes — new client types, new geographies, new document formats) | Input distribution monitoring; rising extraction/intent failures on new categories | Refresh evaluation sets; retrain or re-prompt; expand the lexicon |
| Usage drift (users adopt the AI for things it was not designed for) | Intent clustering on unmatched queries | Either build the capability properly or decline explicitly; never let an unsupported use quietly half-work |
| Approval-velocity drift | Approvals per approver per minute; sustained rates implying no reading | Flag for review; not punitive, but the card may be too easy or the workflow may be mis-designed |
| Score drift (reliability/performance distributions shift) | Monthly distribution comparison | Investigate whether the world changed or the model did; a scoring change affecting people requires notice |

#### 41.8.5 AI incident process

| Severity | Definition | Examples | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P0** | Cross-tenant leakage; sensitive data disclosure; unsafe automated action affecting a person or safety; safety-critical mistranslation; permission bypass | AI shows tenant B's roster to tenant A; a safety instruction mistranslated | Immediate kill switch on the affected tool/surface; §38/§39 incident process invoked in parallel; Founder/Management and Super Admin notified immediately; regulator/tenant notification assessed per §39; post-incident review mandatory within 5 working days |
| **P1** | Wrong automated action (reversible, no person harmed); an approved-then-wrong case where the card omitted a decisive fact; redaction miss; systematic wrong answers with operational consequence | An automated ticket routing sends all safety tickets to billing | Demote the function to Approval-required; fix; re-evaluate; review within 10 working days |
| **P2** | Wrong Read-only answer with operational consequence; recurring rejection pattern; language quality below bar in operational content | Attendance figure quoted from a stale cache without a staleness label | Fix in the normal cycle; regression case added |
| **P3** | Cosmetic, tone, formatting, minor unhelpfulness | Over-long responses on the Guard App | Backlog |

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Who can declare | Any employee, any tenant via support, any user via the "this is wrong" affordance; Support triages; the AI Review Board on-call owns P0/P1 |
| Containment first | Kill switches are used before root-causing; reducing autonomy is always the safe first move |
| Communication | Affected tenants and affected individuals are informed for P0 and for any P1 that affected a person's record, with what happened, what was corrected and what changed |
| Post-incident | Written review: what happened, why the evaluation suite missed it, the regression case added, the control added, the owner, the date |
| Register | All AI incidents are recorded in an AI incident register, reported monthly to the Board and quarterly to Founder/Management, and summarised (without tenant identifiers) in the procurement diligence pack |

---

### 41.9 Transparency

| Requirement | Specification |
|---|---|
| AI disclosure | Any response, summary, draft, ranking or proposal generated by AI is visibly labelled as such at the point of presentation. Labelling is not a one-time onboarding notice; it is present every time. |
| Draft disclosure | A human sending an AI-drafted message to a third party sends it as their own — but the internal record retains that it was AI-drafted, so the audit trail is truthful even where the recipient sees a human's message. |
| Citation | Every factual claim cites the underlying record with a link the user can open. A claim that cannot be cited is not made. |
| Freshness | Every data-derived answer states its as-of time where staleness is possible. |
| Basis on request | "Ask why" is available on every recommendation and proposal, expanding the full reasoning, the data used, and the alternatives considered. |
| Right to a human | Every AI surface offers a one-action route to a human: for clients, their account manager or support; for guards, their supervisor and the Command Center number; for agencies, their support channel. This route is never hidden, degraded, or made slower than the AI route. |
| No impersonation | AI never presents itself as a named human, never signs as a person, and answers truthfully when asked whether it is an AI. |
| Automated-decision notice | Where an outcome was materially influenced by AI and affects a person (allocation preference, screening flag, score component), the person is told that AI contributed, what it contributed, and how to contest it (§41.6.4). |
| Language | All of the above in the user's language, using the safety-template rules of §41.7 where relevant. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-AIG-055 | AI-generated content shall be labelled at every point of presentation, and the label shall not be removable by configuration or by tenant branding. |
| SUR-AIG-056 | The route to a human shall be present on every AI surface, shall be reachable in one action, and shall never be slower or more effortful than continuing with AI. |
| SUR-AIG-057 | On direct question, an AI surface shall state that it is an AI system and identify its scope; deception about its nature is prohibited. |

---

### 41.10 Governance roles and cadence

#### 41.10.1 Who owns AI risk

| Role | Accountability |
|---|---|
| **Founder/Management (CTO as AI owner)** | Ultimate accountability for AI risk; chairs the AI Review Board; approves the prohibition list and any change to it; approves Automated-class grants |
| **AI Review Board** | Standing body: CTO (chair), Compliance, Security (§38 owner), Privacy (§39 owner), Head of Operations, HR representative (for workforce-affecting functions), and the AI engineering lead. Quorum requires Compliance plus Security plus the chair or their delegate |
| **Surface owners** | Named product owner per AI surface; owns its evaluation set, its metrics, its incidents and its model card |
| **Compliance** | Owns the fairness monitoring programme, the vendor register as compliance objects, and the counsel-review status of AI-related policy |
| **Security** | Owns injection defences, tool authorisation, kill switches, and the security half of AI incidents |
| **Privacy** | Owns data classification, redaction efficacy, retention and the training-data position |
| **Every user** | Can report a wrong or unsafe AI output in one action; reports are triaged, never dismissed silently |

#### 41.10.2 Cadence

| Activity | Frequency | Output |
|---|---|---|
| AI Review Board meeting | Monthly, plus ad hoc for P0/P1 incidents | Minutes, decisions, register updates |
| New-function classification review | Per proposal | Class decision recorded in the AI Action Register |
| Automated-class grant/renewal | Per grant; renewal annually | Board approval record with evaluation and shadow-mode evidence |
| Evaluation suite run | Every release | Attached release record |
| Continuous monitoring review | Weekly (metrics), monthly (deep review) | Quality report per surface |
| Fairness / disparate-impact analysis | Quarterly | Report to Founder/Management; remediation actions |
| Language quality review | Quarterly | Tier confirmations, promotions and demotions |
| Vendor reassessment | Annually, or on any vendor change | Vendor register update |
| Model card review | Annually, or on any input change | Updated cards, republished to affected populations |
| AI decision audit | Quarterly sample audit by Auditor role: 100 randomly-sampled AI-influenced actions traced end-to-end (proposal → card contents → approver → execution → entity change → reversibility) | Audit findings tracked like compliance findings (§40.4.3) |
| Prohibition-list review | Annually, and on any product expansion | Confirmed or extended; never quietly narrowed |
| Policy review of this section | Annually | Versioned update |

#### 41.10.3 Change-approval process for new AI actions

| Gate | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 1. Intake | Written proposal: purpose, users, data read, tools called, people affected, failure modes, proposed class |
| 2. Data review | Privacy confirms the data envelope, classification and redaction; cross-tenant analysis |
| 3. Security review | Security confirms tool authorisation, injection exposure, rate/cost limits, kill switch |
| 4. Fairness review | Required if the function touches recruitment, allocation, scoring, performance, pay or discipline; produces the model card and feature review |
| 5. Classification | Board assigns the class; ties resolve restrictive |
| 6. Evaluation | Suite extended for the function; must pass |
| 7. Shadow / staged | Shadow mode for Automated candidates (min 30 days); staged rollout for all |
| 8. Registration | Entered in the AI Action Register with owner, class, evaluation reference, review date |
| 9. Post-launch | 30-day review against predicted failure modes; demote or fix if reality differs |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-AIG-058 | The AI Action Register shall be the authoritative list of every AI function in production with its class, owner, evaluation reference, last review and incident history; a function in production but absent from the register shall be a governance defect detected by CI reconciliation against the tool manifest. |
| SUR-AIG-059 | The quarterly AI decision audit shall be performed by the Auditor role with read-only access, shall trace sampled actions end-to-end, and its findings shall be tracked to closure like compliance findings. |
| SUR-AIG-060 | Any change that increases AI autonomy, widens its data envelope, or adds a people-affecting input shall require full Board approval; any change that reduces autonomy shall require only the surface owner. |

## 42. Analytics

### 42.1 The measurement framework

#### 42.1.1 North star

**North-star metric: Guard-Shifts Delivered Compliantly (GSDC)** — the count of scheduled guard-shifts in a period that were actually staffed, verified present, patrolled and wake-checked to the contracted standard, by a guard whose compliance objects were all Valid at the time of the shift.

```
GSDC = Σ shifts where ALL of:
         assignment_status = Completed
     AND attendance verified (check-in and check-out within tolerance)
     AND patrol completion ≥ contracted threshold (where patrols contracted)
     AND wake-check compliance ≥ contracted threshold (where night post)
     AND guard compliance status = Valid for every mandatory object at shift start
     AND no unresolved SLA breach attributed to that shift
```

It is the north star because it is the one number that is simultaneously the client's product (a guard, actually there, actually working), the guard's income (a shift worked), the agency's revenue (a billable shift), Suraksha's marketplace value (verified delivery), and the regulator-facing truth (compliant deployment). It cannot be gamed by any single function: sales cannot inflate it, ops cannot inflate it without real staffing, and compliance cannot inflate it at all.

| Property | Specification |
|---|---|
| Grain | One row per (shift, assignment). Aggregated to site, client, branch, tenant, city, state, national, and to day/week/month. |
| Denominator companion | **GSDC Rate = GSDC ÷ contracted shifts in the period.** The absolute count grows with the business; the rate says whether delivery quality is holding. Both are always shown together. |
| Refresh | Hourly for the current day (provisional), finalised at T+1 day after attendance reconciliation, restated only through the correction path (§42.6.4). |
| Owner | Founder/Management, with National Operations accountable for the rate. |
| Target | GSDC Rate ≥ 97% `[RECOMMENDED]` — see A-363 for validating the initial benchmark. |

#### 42.1.2 The metric tree

```
                    GSDC / GSDC Rate  (north star)
                             │
   ┌─────────────┬───────────┼────────────┬───────────────┐
   ▼             ▼           ▼            ▼               ▼
DEMAND        SUPPLY     DELIVERY     COMPLIANCE      RETENTION
covered       available   quality      validity        of both sides
   │             │           │            │               │
   ├ Bookings    ├ Active    ├ Attendance ├ Guard doc     ├ Client
   │  created    │  guards   │  %         │  compliance % │  retention
   ├ Quote       ├ Deploy-   ├ Absentee-  ├ Police verif. ├ Logo churn
   │  conversion │  ment     │  ism %     │  coverage     ├ Revenue
   ├ Time-to-    │  rate     ├ Replace-   ├ Training      │  retention
   │  deploy     ├ Guard     │  ment rate │  currency     ├ Guard
   ├ Site        │  utilisa- ├ Patrol     ├ Licence       │  attrition
   │  coverage   │  tion     │  completion│  validity     ├ Agency
   ├ Contract    ├ Bench /   ├ Wake-check ├ Filing        │  (SaaS)
   │  value      │  standby  │  compliance│  timeliness   │  churn
   └ Pipeline    └ Attrition └ Incidents, └ Exception     └ NPS / CSAT
                                response     backlog
                                time
```

Beneath each leaf sit the operational drivers in §42.2. Every KPI in the catalogue maps to exactly one branch of this tree, and every dashboard card states which branch it belongs to, so a user always knows *why* a number is on their screen.

#### 42.1.3 Three metric families

| Family | Question it answers | Audience | Change cadence | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Operational** | Is the service being delivered right now and today? | Command Center, Operations, Supervisors, Agency Operations | Real-time to hourly | On-duty count, unfilled posts, late check-ins, open SOS, wake-check compliance tonight, replacement SLA |
| **Business** | Is the company healthy this month and this quarter? | Founder/Management, Finance, Sales, Agency Owner | Daily to monthly | Revenue, MRR/ARR, receivables, payroll cost, gross margin, client retention, guard attrition, tender win rate |
| **Product** | Are people using the software, and does using it help them? | CTO, Product, Marketing, Growth | Daily to weekly | Activation, feature adoption, funnel conversion, session depth, AI usage and approval rates, support deflection |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-ANL-001 | Every metric shall be registered in a **metric registry** with: id, name, definition, formula, source entities and fields, grain, dimensions, refresh cadence, owner, target, family, tree branch, data-quality grade (§42.6) and version. An unregistered number shall not appear on any dashboard. |
| SUR-ANL-002 | Metric definitions shall be versioned and effective-dated; when a definition changes, historical series shall be labelled with the definition version and the chart shall show the change point rather than silently restating history. |
| SUR-ANL-003 | Every dashboard card shall expose its metric's definition, formula, source and last-refresh timestamp in one interaction ("how is this calculated?"). |
| SUR-ANL-004 | One number, one definition: two dashboards showing "attendance %" shall compute it identically from the same registered metric, or shall use two distinctly-named metrics. Divergent definitions of the same name are prohibited. |

### 42.2 The KPI catalogue

**How to read these tables.** *Formula* is the actual computation over the entities in §32. *Data source* names the entity and the driving field. *Grain* is the finest level at which the metric is computed before aggregation. *Owner* is the accountable role (canon role names). *Target* is a `[RECOMMENDED]` starting benchmark unless marked `[CONFIRMED]`; initial targets need validation against real operating data (A-363).

Notation: `Σ` is a count or sum over the period and scope; `[period]` means the selected time range; `distinct` means distinct entity count.

#### 42.2.1 Workforce supply

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ANL-W01 Active Guards** | Guards available for deployment | `distinct Guard where status = Active AND compliance_status = Valid AND employment_record.status = Active` as at the snapshot instant | Guard.status; Compliance status store; Employment Record.status | Guard × day (snapshot) | HR / Agency HR | Grows with contracted posts; ≥1.15 × posts required |
| **ANL-W02 Deployable Guards** | Active guards not blocked by any gate | `ANL-W01 − distinct Guard with any hard block (§40.6.1)` | Compliance status store; Guard.blacklist_flag | Guard × day | Compliance | ≥98% of ANL-W01 |
| **ANL-W03 Deployment Rate** | Share of the workforce actually on deployment | `distinct Guard with ≥1 Assignment where assignment overlaps [period] ÷ ANL-W01` | Assignment.guard_id, start_at, end_at; Guard.status | Guard × day → branch | Operations Manager / City Operations | ≥90% |
| **ANL-W04 Guard Utilisation** | How fully deployed guards' available hours are used | `Σ assigned_shift_hours ÷ Σ available_hours` where `available_hours = contracted_hours_per_guard × deployable guard-days` | Shift.duration; Assignment; Guard availability calendar; Leave | Guard × week | Operations Manager | 85–92% (above 92% signals no resilience) |

### 42.3 Dashboards — the analytical layer

§20 and §22 specify the *operational* dashboards inside each product (the cards a user acts on). This subsection specifies the **analytical layer**: the dashboards people use to understand trends, compare, and decide — not to run today's shift. Every analytical dashboard shares one contract:

| Contract element | Standard |
|---|---|
| Card anatomy | Metric name · current value · comparison (vs. previous period and vs. target) · sparkline or trend · data-quality grade badge (§42.6) · "how is this calculated?" link · last-refresh timestamp |
| Scope banner | Always states the applied scope in words ("Gujarat · Ahmedabad branch · last 30 days") so no number is misread as global |
| Drill path | Every card drills: aggregate → dimension breakdown → entity list → entity record. Three clicks maximum to a row. |
| Comparison | Period-over-period toggle on every card; year-over-year where ≥13 months of data exists |
| Annotations | Significant events (a new large contract, a rule change, a pricing change) are annotated on time series so movements are explainable |
| Export | Every card exports its underlying rows subject to the viewer's permissions (§42.5.4) |
| Empty and low-n states | Cards with fewer than the configured minimum observations show "insufficient data (n=4)" rather than a misleading percentage |

### 42.4 Event taxonomy

#### 42.4.1 Naming convention

`<object>_<action>` — snake_case, object first, action in past tense. Always past tense: the event records something that happened.

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Object vocabulary | Only the canon entity names (§3), lower-cased: `booking`, `quotation`, `contract`, `guard`, `assignment`, `attendance`, `patrol`, `wake_check`, `incident`, `sos`, `replacement`, `invoice`, `payment`, `payroll_run`, `subscription`, `lead`, `tender`, `bid`, `ticket`, `document`, `licence`, `ai_interaction`, plus UI objects `page`, `screen`, `module`, `search`, `filter`, `export`, `notification` |
| Action vocabulary | `viewed`, `started`, `completed`, `submitted`, `created`, `updated`, `cancelled`, `failed`, `approved`, `rejected`, `sent`, `received`, `opened`, `clicked`, `searched`, `filtered`, `exported`, `shared`, `installed`, `synced` |
| Forbidden | Vendor-specific names, camelCase, spaces, free-form event names created ad hoc in feature code |
| Governance | New events are added only through the event registry with an owner, a definition and a consuming metric; an event with no consumer is not added |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-ANL-008 | Events shall be defined in a shared, versioned schema registry; a client shall not be able to emit an event or a property not in the registry, and schema violations shall be rejected at ingest and counted. |
| SUR-ANL-009 | Every event shall be emitted **server-side where the truth is server-side** (bookings, payments, assignments, attendance). Client-side events are used only for interaction telemetry (views, clicks, funnel steps) and shall never be the source of a business or operational KPI. |

#### 42.4.2 Required properties on every event

| Property | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `event_name` | string | From the registry |
| `event_id` | uuid | Idempotency key; duplicates discarded |
| `occurred_at` | timestamp | Device time for client events |
| `received_at` | timestamp | Server receipt (canon §4: always store both) |
| `anonymous_id` | uuid | Pre-auth identity |
| `user_id` | ref | Null when anonymous |
| `tenant_id` | ref | **Mandatory on every tenant-scoped event**; null only for public-site events |
| `branch_id` | ref | Where applicable |
| `role` | enum | The acting role at the time |
| `surface` | enum | `website` · `customer_portal` · `customer_app` · `guard_portal` · `guard_app` · `trinetra` · `agency_portal_web` · `agency_portal_desktop` · `agency_app` · `ops` · `admin_app` |
| `platform` | enum | `web` · `android` · `ios` · `windows` · `macos` · `linux` |
| `app_version`, `session_id` | string/uuid | Diagnostics and sessionisation |
| `locale` | string | Language actually in use |
| `network_state` | enum | `online` · `offline_queued` — essential for Guard App interpretation |
| `entity_refs` | object | The business entities the event concerns (site_id, guard_id, contract_id…) |
| `consent_state` | enum | Analytics consent at emission time (§39) |

#### 42.4.4 Funnel definitions

**F1 — B2C booking funnel** (surakshaguards.in + Customer App)

| Step | Event | Expected conversion `[RECOMMENDED]` |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Visit | `page_viewed` (any) | — |
| 2 Service interest | `service_viewed` or `pricing_viewed` | ≥25% of visits |
| 3 Serviceability | `pincode_checked` with serviceable=true | ≥60% of step 2 |
| 4 Booking started | `booking_started` | ≥25% of step 3 |
| 5 Requirement captured | `booking_step_completed` (requirement) | ≥80% |
| 6 Schedule & site captured | `booking_step_completed` (schedule) | ≥85% |
| 7 Identity verified | `login_succeeded` or OTP verified | ≥80% |
| 8 Payment initiated | `payment_initiated` | ≥75% |
| 9 Booking confirmed | `booking_confirmed` | ≥92% of step 8 |
| 10 Deployed | first `attendance_check_in_succeeded` at the booking's site | ≥97% within the promised window |

Fixes P10 in canon §1.8 (no booking flow exists today) by measuring the flow that replaces it. Drop-off at any step >20% opens a product review.

**F2 — B2B lead-to-contract funnel**

| Step | Event/state | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Lead created | `lead_created` (any source) | — |
| 2 Contacted | `lead_first_response` within 30 min | ≥90% |
| 3 Qualified | Lead → Opportunity | ≥40% |
| 4 Site survey completed | `site_survey_completed` | ≥75% |
| 5 Quotation sent | `quotation_sent` | ≥85% |
| 6 Negotiation | `quotation_revised` (0..n) | — |
| 7 Accepted | `quotation_accepted` | ≥30% of step 5 |
| 8 Contract executed | `contract_activated` | ≥90% of step 7 |
| 9 Deployed | ANL-C14 time to deploy | ≥98% within 5 days |

**F3 — Agency trial-to-paid funnel**

| Step | Event | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Trinetra visit | `page_viewed` on trinetra | — |
| 2 Plan viewed | `pricing_viewed` | ≥30% |
| 3 Signup | `signup_completed` | ≥8% of step 2 |
| 4 Trial started | `trial_started` | ≥95% of signups |
| 5 First guard created | `guard_created` (first) | ≥75% |
| 6 First site + post | `site_created` + `post_created` | ≥65% |
| 7 First roster published | `roster_published` | ≥55% |
| 8 First attendance recorded | `attendance_marked` (any method) | ≥50% — **the activation milestone (ANL-E01)** |
| 9 Second week retention | ≥1 session in days 8–14 | ≥60% of activated |
| 10 Converted | `subscription_activated` (paid) | ≥25% of trials (ANL-P11) |

**F4 — Marketplace enquiry funnel**

| Step | Event | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Search | `listing_search_performed` | — |
| 2 Listing viewed | `listing_viewed` | ≥60% |
| 3 Enquiry submitted | `listing_enquiry_submitted` | ≥8% of views |
| 4 Agency responded | `lead_first_response` | ≥90% within 30 min |
| 5 Quotation sent | `quotation_sent` | ≥45% |
| 6 Contract won | `contract_activated` | ≥12% of enquiries (ANL-M06) |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-ANL-010 | Every funnel shall be defined in the registry with its exact step events, its attribution window, and whether steps must occur in order; a funnel chart shall state its window and ordering rule on the chart. |
| SUR-ANL-011 | Funnels shall support both session-scoped and identity-scoped analysis, and shall stitch anonymous to identified users on authentication without retroactively rewriting anonymous history. |

### 42.5 Reporting infrastructure

#### 42.5.1 Stance: curated first, self-serve second

| Layer | What it is | Who |
|---|---|---|
| **Curated dashboards** | The §42.3 dashboards, built and maintained by the platform, using registered metrics. The default for 90% of users. | Everyone |
| **Curated reports** | ~40 named, parameterised reports (attendance register, payroll summary, invoice register, incident log, compliance status, SLA report, guard roster, client service report, tender pipeline…) with fixed columns and validated logic | Everyone, permission-scoped |
| **Report builder** | Compose from **registered metrics and registered dimensions** — not free SQL. Choose metrics, dimensions, filters, grain, visualisation, then save and share. | Professional+ agency roles; Suraksha analytics roles |
| **Raw export** | Row-level extract of entities the user may read, with rate limits and audit | Restricted permission |
| **Warehouse access** | Read-only access to the analytics read model for Enterprise tenants' own data | Enterprise, contracted, `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-364]` |

Free-form SQL against production is not offered to any tenant. The report builder composes registered metrics precisely so that two people cannot compute "attendance %" two different ways (SUR-ANL-004).

#### 42.5.2 Report builder capability

| Capability | Detail |
|---|---|
| Metric selection | Any registered metric the user's role may see; incompatible grain combinations are prevented with an explanation, not an error |
| Dimensions | Registered dimensions only: time (hour/day/week/month/quarter), geography (state/city/district), org (tenant/branch/team/supervisor), client/site/post, guard/category/tenure band, contract, plan, channel, language, surface |
| Filters | Any dimension; saved filter sets; relative dates ("last 30 days", "current month") that stay relative on schedule |
| Calculations | Ratio, delta, period-over-period, running total, share of total, per-1,000 normalisation. Arbitrary formulas are not permitted — a new formula becomes a registered metric through governance |
| Visualisations | Table, line, bar, stacked bar, funnel, cohort grid, distribution/histogram, map (state/city), single-value tile with comparison |
| Saving and sharing | Private / team / tenant-wide; shared views respect the **viewer's** permissions, not the author's (§42.5.4) |
| Annotations | Attach a note to a point in time on any chart |
| Versioning | Saved reports carry the metric definition versions used; a definition change flags the report |

#### 42.5.3 Scheduled reports and exports

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Schedules | Daily, weekly (day selectable), monthly (day selectable), quarterly; timezone-aware; a "send only if non-empty" option and a "send only if threshold breached" option |
| Delivery | Email (attachment or secure link), in-app, WhatsApp link where policy permits, SFTP for Enterprise `[RECOMMENDED]` |
| Formats | CSV, XLSX (formatted, with a definitions sheet naming every metric and its formula), PDF (print-ready, A4), JSON (API) |
| Large exports | Async with progress and a completion notification; links expire (default 7 days); >100k rows must be scheduled rather than interactive |
| Security | Every export is permission-checked at generation **and** at download, watermarked with the recipient, rate-limited, and audited (§38) |
| Recipient control | External recipients require an explicit allow-list per tenant; a report containing personal data cannot be scheduled to an external address without an additional approval |
| Failure handling | A failed scheduled run retries, then notifies the owner with the reason; silent failure is prohibited |

#### 42.5.4 Permission-aware analytics

This is the requirement most often broken by analytics stacks, so it is stated sharply.

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Row-level scope injection | Every query is rewritten with the viewer's scope predicates before execution: `tenant_id`, then `branch_id` for branch-scoped roles, then site/client scope for client roles, then self-scope for guards. Scope is applied at the query layer, never in the UI. |
| Shared views | A saved or shared report renders with the **viewer's** scope. A Branch Manager opening a report built by the Agency Owner sees only their branch, and the report says so in its scope banner. |
| Aggregate leakage | Aggregates must not permit inference of out-of-scope values. Minimum cell size (default 5 entities) applies to any breakdown crossing a scope boundary; below it, the cell shows "n<5" rather than a number. |
| Differencing | Where a user can see both a total and a subset, and the complement would reveal out-of-scope data, the total is suppressed or widened. Detection of differencing risk is part of report validation. |
| Metric-level permissions | Some metrics are role-restricted regardless of scope: margin and cost metrics are hidden from client roles and from agency roles without the finance permission; salary metrics are restricted to Payroll/Finance/HR; compliance override detail is restricted to Compliance. |
| Guard self-view | A guard sees their own metrics only, with the composition of any score affecting them (SUR-AIG-046), and can never see another guard's figures. |
| Client view | A client sees only their sites, and only the display fields in §42.3.4. |
| Auditor | Read-all within audit scope, watermarked, every access logged. |
| Cross-tenant | No tenant-facing query may span tenants. Benchmarks are served from the pre-aggregated benchmark store (§42.7), never by querying other tenants' rows. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-ANL-012 | Scope predicates shall be injected server-side into every analytical query; an analytics endpoint that accepts a client-supplied scope parameter without re-validation is a P0 security defect. |
| SUR-ANL-013 | Shared reports shall render with the viewer's permissions; the platform shall never persist a result set computed under one user's scope and serve it to another user. |
| SUR-ANL-014 | Minimum cell-size suppression shall be applied to every cross-boundary breakdown, and suppressed cells shall be visibly marked rather than shown as zero. |

#### 42.5.5 The analytics read model

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Separation | Analytics reads from a dedicated read model, never from transactional tables under load (canon §4: modular monolith plus a separate real-time/ingest path) |
| Population | CDC or batch from the operational store plus the event stream; late-arriving events (Guard App offline sync) are handled by reprocessing the affected day, and the affected metric's `restated_at` is set |
| Freshness contract | Each metric declares its freshness (real-time / 5 min / hourly / daily) and every card displays it; a metric behind its contract is badged stale rather than shown as current |
| Grain preservation | The read model retains the finest grain needed for the registered metrics so that any aggregate is recomputable; pre-aggregates are caches, never the source of truth |
| PII | The read model carries pseudonymised identifiers and only the display fields analytics needs; sensitive-personal fields are excluded entirely (§41.4.3), so the AI analytics surface cannot leak what is not there (§25.2.6) |
| Retention | Event-level data 25 months (allows YoY plus a month); daily aggregates 7 years; monthly aggregates indefinitely |
| Reprocessing | Any metric can be recomputed from the read model for any historical period; recomputation writes a restatement record |

---

### 42.6 Data quality

#### 42.6.1 The honesty rule

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-ANL-015 | Every registered metric shall carry a **data-quality grade** — A (system-captured, verifiable, tamper-evident), B (system-captured with human override possible), C (partly manual entry), D (fully manual or low-coverage) — and the grade shall be displayed on every card and in every export. |
| SUR-ANL-016 | A metric graded C or D shall never be presented without its grade, and shall not be used as the sole basis for a client-facing SLA claim, a payroll consequence, or a person-affecting decision. |
| SUR-ANL-017 | Where a metric has a known failure mode (§42.6.2), that failure mode shall be stated in the metric's "how is this calculated?" panel in plain language, not buried in documentation. |

#### 42.6.2 Known failure modes, stated plainly

| Metric | Failure mode | Control |
|---|---|---|
| **ANL-D01 Attendance %** | Meaningless if manual marking is unconstrained — a supervisor can mark everyone present. | **ANL-D02 Verified Attendance %** is displayed beside it always. Manual marks require a reason code and an authorised role, are counted (`attendance_marked_manually`), and a site whose manual share exceeds the configured threshold (default 10%) is flagged and its ANL-D01 is graded C for that period. |
| **ANL-D11 / ANL-D12 Patrol** | A guard can scan checkpoints without walking the route; or a broken NFC tag makes a real patrol look incomplete. | Time-between-scans plausibility check, GPS corroboration where available, and a device/tag health signal separating "failed to scan" from "did not patrol". Tag faults are excluded from the guard's component and raised as a maintenance task. |
| **ANL-D13 Wake-Check** | A dead battery or no network looks identical to a sleeping guard. | Device heartbeat (ANL-D18) is joined; "missed with device offline" is a separate bucket from "missed with device online", and only the latter reflects on the guard. Both are shown to operations. |
| **ANL-D17 Geofence** | Poor GPS accuracy indoors and in industrial sites produces false violations. | Violations require accuracy below a threshold and a minimum duration; low-accuracy events are recorded but excluded from the metric and reported separately. |
| **ANL-S01 Incident Count** | Under-reporting looks like safety. | Reported alongside ANL-S12 (client-reported share) and supervisor-visit compliance; a site with zero incidents and low supervision is flagged, not praised. Incident count is never used as a punitive metric for a supervisor. |
| **ANL-C09 SLA Compliance** | Depends on SLA clauses being captured structurally; an uncaptured clause is silently unmeasured. | SUR-CMP-027: an unmeasured clause is listed as "not monitored" on the contract and on the client dashboard. |
| **ANL-F02 Revenue recognised** | Depends on delivery records; missing attendance under-recognises revenue. | Reconciliation to ANL-F01 with a variance threshold; variance beyond 2% opens a finance exception. |
| **ANL-G01 Reliability Score** | Punishes guards for site or device problems outside their control. | Device faults, tag faults and roster errors are excluded from the guard's components; the score is explainable and contestable (§41.6.3); disputes upheld above 20% (ANL-G10) trigger a review of the metric itself, not of the guards. |
| **ANL-W08 Attrition** | Distorted by seasonal and project-based hiring. | Reported with cohort-based ANL-W09 and with contract-type segmentation; annualisation on a short period is suppressed below a minimum denominator. |
| **ANL-P11 Trial-to-Paid** | Distorted by test and internal signups. | Internal and test tenants are flagged at creation and excluded from all growth metrics by default; the exclusion count is shown. |
| **ANL-B14 Attribution** | Last-touch overstates paid channels; first-touch overstates organic. | Both are always reported; neither is presented as truth; offline channels (referrals, field sales) are captured with a manual source field. |
| **ANL-A05 Approval Rate** | A very high rate can mean quality or rubber-stamping. | Read together with ANL-A07 (approved-then-reverted) and approval-velocity monitoring (§41.8.4). |
| **Any per-guard rate** | Small denominators produce wild percentages. | Minimum denominator (default 10 shifts) before a per-guard rate is displayed; below it, raw counts only. |

#### 42.6.3 Required data-quality checks

| Check | Frequency | On failure |
|---|---|---|
| Freshness — each metric within its declared contract | Every refresh | Card badged stale; alert to the metric owner |
| Volume — event and record counts within expected bands | Hourly | Anomaly alert; ingest investigated |
| Completeness — required properties present on ingested events | Continuous at ingest | Reject and count; a rising rejection rate is a release-blocking regression |
| Referential integrity — every `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `guard_id` resolves | Daily | Orphan report; metrics touching orphans flagged |
| Duplicate detection — `event_id` idempotency; duplicate attendance/invoice records | Continuous | Deduplicated; source investigated |
| Reconciliation — analytics vs. transactional totals for revenue, payroll, attendance, headcount | Daily | Variance >0.5% opens a P2 data incident |
| Manual-entry share per metric per site | Daily | Above threshold → grade downgrade and a flag |
| Timeliness of offline sync — queued events older than 24 h | Hourly | Device and guard flagged; metrics for that shift marked provisional |
| Timezone and clock sanity — `occurred_at` implausibly ahead of `received_at` | At ingest | Clamped, flagged, counted (canon §4 dual-timestamp rule) |
| Distribution drift on key metrics | Weekly | Investigated before it is reported as a business change |
| Definition drift — a report using a superseded metric version | On metric publish | Report owner notified with the diff |

#### 42.6.4 Restatement policy

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Restatement happens | Late-arriving offline data, corrected attendance, reversed transactions and definition changes all cause restatement. This is normal and must be visible. |
| Provisional labelling | Current-day and current-period figures are labelled provisional until their finalisation point (attendance T+1 day; financials T+2 business days; payroll on run release). |
| Visible restatement | A restated figure shows a marker with the prior value, the new value, the reason and the timestamp. Silent restatement is prohibited. |
| Locked periods | Once a financial period is closed, its analytics are locked; corrections appear as adjustments in the current period with a link to the original. |
| Audit | Every restatement writes an audit record naming the trigger and the affected metrics. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-ANL-018 | Provisional figures shall be visibly labelled; a number that can still change shall never be presented as final, especially in client-facing reports and invoices. |
| SUR-ANL-019 | Restatements shall be visible with prior value, new value, reason and time; analytics shall never silently rewrite a previously published number. |

---

### 42.7 Benchmarking across tenants

The opportunity is real: an agency with 60 guards has no way to know whether 4% absenteeism is good or bad. Suraksha can tell them. The constraints are equally real.

#### 42.7.1 What benchmarking is

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Product | "Your absenteeism is 4.1%. The median for agencies of 40–100 guards in Gujarat is 3.2%; the top quartile is under 2.1%." Percentile position plus the distribution, never another agency's value. |
| Metrics eligible | Operational and workforce metrics only: attendance, absenteeism, replacement rate and time, patrol and wake-check compliance, guard attrition and early attrition, training currency, document compliance, incident rate, SLA compliance, lead response time, quote conversion. |
| Metrics **not** eligible | Anything commercially identifying or sensitive: revenue, rates charged, margin, payroll cost, client names, client counts below the threshold, salary levels, contract values, tender bid values, individual guard data of any kind. `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-365]` on whether aggregate rate benchmarking (e.g. median monthly rate per unarmed guard by city) is offered at all, given its competitive sensitivity. |
| Cohorts | Defined on non-identifying axes: guard-count band, state, city tier, service-lane mix, tenure on the platform. Cohort definitions are published so the comparison is interpretable. |
| Presentation | Percentile band and distribution shape; never a ranked list of agencies; never "you are 7th of 12". |

#### 42.7.2 Privacy and competitive constraints

| Constraint | Rule |
|---|---|
| **Opt-in** | Benchmarking requires explicit tenant opt-in by the Agency Owner, with a plain description of what is contributed and what is received. Default is off. Opt-out is one action and takes effect on the next aggregation cycle. |
| **Reciprocity** | A tenant that does not contribute does not receive benchmarks. Stated openly at the opt-in. |
| **Minimum cell size** | No benchmark is computed or shown for a cohort with fewer than **10 contributing tenants** and fewer than **3 distinct tenants** in any displayed sub-band. Below the threshold, the product says "not enough agencies in this cohort yet" rather than widening silently into a misleading cohort. |
| **No dominance** | If a single tenant contributes more than 25% of a cohort's underlying volume, the cohort is not published — otherwise the median is effectively that tenant's number. |
| **Aggregation only** | Only pre-aggregated statistics enter the benchmark store. No tenant's row-level data is ever queried to serve another tenant's request (§41.4.2). |
| **No re-identification** | Statistical disclosure controls: rounding, minimum cell sizes, suppression of extreme values, and a differencing check across cohort definitions over time (a tenant joining or leaving a small cohort must not reveal their value by the shift in the median). |
| **No inference of clients** | Benchmarks are never sliced in a way that could reveal who a competitor's clients are (e.g. by client industry within a small city). |
| **Suraksha's own data** | `SURAKSHA-HQ` contributes on the same terms and is not privileged; Suraksha does not use benchmark data for competitive advantage against contributing tenants in the marketplace, and this commitment is contractual. |
| **Guard data** | No individual guard's data ever enters a benchmark, at any aggregation. Workforce benchmarks are tenant-level statistics only. |
| **Cadence** | Recomputed monthly; a tenant's own contribution is visible to them ("this is what you contributed"). |
| **Transparency** | The methodology page states the cohort definitions, the thresholds, the suppression rules and the metrics included. |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SUR-ANL-020 | Benchmarking shall be opt-in, revocable, aggregate-only, and shall enforce minimum cohort size, minimum sub-band size and maximum single-tenant contribution before any figure is published. |
| SUR-ANL-021 | The benchmark store shall be populated by a batch aggregation job with no query path from a tenant's request to another tenant's row-level data. |
| SUR-ANL-022 | Benchmark outputs shall pass a disclosure-control check (including differencing across time and cohort definitions) before publication; a cohort failing the check is suppressed, not adjusted. |
| SUR-ANL-023 | Individual guard, client and financial data shall never enter any cross-tenant benchmark, in any aggregated form. |

#### 42.7.3 Where benchmarks appear

| Surface | Use |
|---|---|
| Agency Portal dashboards (Professional+) | Percentile badge beside eligible cards, with the cohort named |
| Agency onboarding | "Agencies like yours typically reach X within Y" — as guidance, clearly labelled as a cohort statistic |
| Marketplace listing | Response-time band only (a band, not a value), and only with consent, because it is a public-facing claim |
| Suraksha management | Full distribution views for product and market understanding, using the same aggregates, never raw tenant comparison by name for competitive purposes |
| Industry reporting `[FUTURE]` | A published private-security operations benchmark report, subject to the same thresholds and to Founder/Management approval |
