| TC-GAP-014 | Poor accuracy fix overlapping the fence | Reported accuracy 120 m, centre 80 m outside a 50 m fence | 1 Check in | Result is `Pending` verification rather than a hard inside/outside decision; the accuracy radius is stored; supervisor sees "accuracy too low to decide" with the numbers | P0 |
| TC-GAP-015 | Wrong-site check-in | Guard at Site B, assigned to Site A; both belong to the same tenant | 1 Check in | Recorded against the **assigned** shift with flag `wrong_site` naming Site B; not converted into attendance at Site B; supervisor alerted; Site A remains an open post until covered (SUR-EDG-004) | P0 |
| TC-GAP-016 | Geofence exit during a shift | Guard checked in, then walks 300 m away for 12 minutes | 1 Replay the trace | Exactly one `geofence_exit` event after the configured consecutive-fix and dwell thresholds; one `geofence_entry` on return; supervisor alerted per the site's configured rule | P0 |
| TC-GAP-017 | Boundary flapping suppressed | Trace crossing the fence 20 times in 5 minutes | 1 Replay | At most one exit and one entry within the debounce window; no alert storm; the raw fixes are retained for audit | P1 |
| TC-GAP-018 | Attendance period locking (BR-422) | Period end reached | 1 Lock the period; 2 attempt to add or edit attendance in it | Post-lock changes are rejected; the only route is a correction record that is separately auditable and re-opens nothing silently | P0 |
| TC-GAP-019 | Shift crossing midnight | Shift 22:00–06:00 | 1 Check in at 22:00; 2 check out at 06:00 | Counted as one attendance of 8 hours attributed to the shift's roster date per the configured rule; never split into two partial days or double-counted (SUR-EDG-041) | P0 |
| TC-GAP-020 | Attendance visible to the correct parties only | Guard, supervisor, agency, client, and a second tenant | 1 Fetch the attendance record as each | Guard sees their own; supervisor and agency roles see it per §31; client sees the permitted summary without biometric artefacts; the second tenant gets `404` | P0 |
| TC-GAP-021 | Late check-in classification | Guard checks in 25 minutes after shift start; late threshold 15 minutes | 1 Check in | Attendance recorded with `late` and the exact minutes; the late rule feeds payroll and SLA reporting; the guard sees the recorded lateness | P1 |
| TC-GAP-022 | Attendance photo storage and access | Check-in with a selfie | 1 Fetch the photo URL as an authorised supervisor; 2 as a client user; 3 as another tenant; 4 after the retention period | Authorised access succeeds; client access follows the §39 rule for biometric artefacts; other tenant `404`; after retention the object is unavailable and the attendance record remains with a retention marker | P0 |

| Test Case ID | Negative case | Edge case |
|---|---|---|
| TC-GAP-001 | Check-in against a shift the guard is not assigned to → rejected `404` | Two guards check in for the same post within one second → both recorded; strength counted correctly |
| TC-GAP-002 | Distance value tampered client-side → server recomputes from raw coordinates | Site fence smaller than typical GPS error → site configuration warns at creation and the fence has a configurable tolerance |
| TC-GAP-003 | Reason field left empty on the early-check-in path → blocked | Guard arrives early for a genuine shift-swap → approved via the recorded reason path, not by disabling the rule |
| TC-GAP-004 | Two devices logged in as the same guard checking in simultaneously → one succeeds, the second is a no-op; multi-device use is flagged | Duplicate arriving 6 hours later from an offline queue → deduplicated by client event ID |
| TC-GAP-005 | Check-out without a matching check-in → rejected with a clear message | Check-out outside the geofence → recorded and flagged, shift still closes |
| TC-GAP-006 | Auto-close suppressed to inflate hours → not configurable below the audit floor | Guard checks out 4 hours after auto-close → correction path used; both timestamps retained |
| TC-GAP-007 | Face match threshold lowered per-tenant to bypass review → threshold is platform-governed, changes audited | Guard's appearance changed (beard, spectacles) → repeated reviews trigger a re-enrolment prompt |
| TC-GAP-008 | Approver is the same person as the guard under a second account → blocked by identity, not by account | Manual attendance for a period already locked → requires the correction path (TC-GAP-018) |
| TC-GAP-009 | Supervisor vouching from 30 km away → recorded and flagged; vouching outside the site is not silently accepted | Supervisor vouching for 20 guards in 60 seconds → permitted but flagged for review as a bulk pattern |
| TC-GAP-010 | Device time back-dated to before shift start → same server-time evaluation | Genuine timezone change while travelling → all evaluation is UTC-based, no false skew |
| TC-GAP-011 | Mock-detection flag stripped from the payload → server-side integrity signal is independent of the client claim | Legitimate developer-options user with no mock app → not flagged; the specific mock setting is checked, not developer mode |
| TC-GAP-012 | Coordinates injected while location services are off → mismatch detected and flagged | GPS off due to battery-saver → the app names the specific setting |
| TC-GAP-013 | Precise permission revoked mid-shift → tracking gap recorded and the guard prompted | Device with no GPS hardware → the site must be configured for an alternative method before assignment |
| TC-GAP-014 | Accuracy value forged as 5 m → cross-checked against fix-to-fix plausibility | Accuracy improves 30 seconds later → the improved fix resolves the pending decision automatically |
| TC-GAP-015 | Attendance forcibly attributed to Site B via API → rejected | Site A and Site B fences overlap → the assigned site wins; the overlap is flagged at site configuration |
| TC-GAP-016 | Exit event suppressed by a client-side setting → server evaluates | Guard legitimately patrols outside the fence → the site's patrol route defines permitted excursions, no alert |
| TC-GAP-017 | Debounce configured to infinity to hide exits → bounded by a platform maximum | Fence crossing at the exact debounce boundary → deterministic, documented tie-break |
| TC-GAP-018 | Lock removed to allow an edit → unlock requires a named approver and is audited | Correction submitted after payroll has run → SUR-EDG-036 applies |
| TC-GAP-019 | Midnight-crossing shift counted on both dates in a report → single attribution asserted in the report test | Shift crossing month-end → attributed per the configured rule, and payroll/invoice tests assert the same rule |
| TC-GAP-020 | Client requesting the raw selfie object URL → `404`/denied | Client and agency belong to the same corporate group → still separate tenants, still isolated |
| TC-GAP-021 | Lateness recomputed to zero by editing shift start after the fact → shift edits after attendance require an approver and are audited | Guard late due to a site-access delay recorded by the client → reason code applied, lateness retained with the reason |
| TC-GAP-022 | Signed photo URL shared externally → bound to identity and expires | Retention period elapses mid-dispute → legal-hold flag preserves the object and is audited |

### 44.6 Patrol and checkpoints — TC-GAP-023 to 032

*Scope: patrol rounds, checkpoint scanning, round completion and exception handling (WKF-14; BR-415, BR-446).*

| Test Case ID | Scenario | Preconditions | Steps | Expected Result | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TC-GAP-023 | Complete a patrol round | Route with 6 mandatory checkpoints; round window 22:00–22:45 | 1 Start the round; 2 scan all 6 in sequence within the window; 3 end | Round `Completed`; each scan stores method, coordinates, `device_time` and `server_received_time`; round appears in the client's patrol report | P0 |
| TC-GAP-024 | Missed mandatory checkpoint (BR-415) | Same route | 1 Scan 5 of 6; 2 end the round | Round is **not** `Completed`; it is closed as incomplete listing the missed checkpoint; supervisor alerted; the shortfall appears in the SLA report | P0 |
| TC-GAP-025 | Checkpoint scanned outside the round window | Round window closed | 1 Scan a checkpoint 10 minutes late | Scan recorded with flag `out_of_window`; it does not count toward completion; the round remains incomplete | P0 |
| TC-GAP-026 | NFC/QR scan at the wrong physical location | Checkpoint tag photographed and scanned from 200 m away | 1 Scan | Scan recorded and flagged `location_mismatch` with the distance; does not count toward completion; supervisor alerted | P0 |
| TC-GAP-027 | Patrol performed offline | Airplane mode for the whole round | 1 Complete the full round offline; 2 restore connectivity | All scans queue locally with their device timestamps; on sync, the round evaluates identically to an online round; no duplicates; sequence preserved | P0 |
| TC-GAP-028 | Randomised patrol schedule | Site configured for randomised rounds | 1 Generate schedules for 30 nights | Start times vary within their windows with no repeating pattern across nights (BR-450); no round starts outside its window | P1 |
| TC-GAP-029 | Photo/note evidence at a checkpoint | Checkpoint configured to require a photo | 1 Scan without a photo; 2 scan with a photo | First blocked with the requirement stated; second accepted; photo stored and linked to the scan | P1 |
| TC-GAP-030 | Patrol during an active incident | Incident `In Progress` at the site | 1 Start the round | Round proceeds; scans are linked to the incident timeline so the incident report shows patrol activity during the event window | P2 |
| TC-GAP-031 | Guard not assigned attempts a patrol | Guard assigned to a different site | 1 Attempt to start the round | Rejected `404`; no round created; the attempt is audited | P0 |
| TC-GAP-032 | Patrol compliance reporting | 30 days of rounds with known outcomes | 1 Run the patrol compliance report for the site | Completed/incomplete/missed counts match the underlying records exactly; the report is scoped to the requesting tenant and role | P1 |

| Test Case ID | Negative case | Edge case |
|---|---|---|
| TC-GAP-023 | Round started by a guard on break with no active attendance → blocked | Two guards patrolling the same route simultaneously → both rounds tracked separately, checkpoints not shared |
| TC-GAP-024 | Incomplete round marked complete via API → rejected | Checkpoint tag physically destroyed → supervisor marks it out-of-service; it is excluded from mandatory counts from that timestamp, audited |
| TC-GAP-025 | Device time back-dated to fake an in-window scan → server-received time governs | Scan at the exact window boundary second → inclusive boundary, documented and consistent |
| TC-GAP-026 | Distance recomputed client-side to zero → server recomputes | Checkpoint indoors with no GPS → configured indoor tolerance applies; the tolerance is per-checkpoint and audited |
| TC-GAP-027 | Offline scans replayed twice after sync → deduplicated by client event ID | Round spans the offline→online transition mid-way → single coherent round, not two |
| TC-GAP-028 | Schedule generated with a fixed seed producing identical times → detected by the pattern assertion | Round window shorter than the route's minimum walking time → flagged at configuration |
| TC-GAP-029 | Photo replaced with a previously-taken image → capture is camera-only, gallery selection disabled for evidence |Photo capture fails on a low-storage device → guard is told storage is full; the scan is not lost |
| TC-GAP-030 | Patrol data used to close an incident automatically → incidents require explicit closure (BR-418) | Incident raised mid-round → round continues and both records cross-link |
| TC-GAP-031 | Route ID from another tenant → `404` | Guard reassigned to the site mid-round → the started round completes under the original assignment |
| TC-GAP-032 | Report requested for another tenant's site → `404` | Report over a period containing a site fence change → both fence versions referenced, results not retroactively rewritten |

### 44.7 Wake check — TC-GAP-033 to 042

*Scope: night anti-sleep wake checks, randomisation, acknowledgement and escalation (WKF-15; BR-416, BR-450).*

| Test Case ID | Scenario | Preconditions | Steps | Expected Result | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TC-GAP-033 | Wake check fires and is acknowledged | Night shift `In Progress`; wake checks enabled | 1 Wait for the scheduled check; 2 acknowledge within the window | High-priority notification delivered even in doze; acknowledgement recorded with device and server times and location; wake check `Completed` | P0 |
| TC-GAP-034 | Missed wake check escalates (BR-416) | Wake check fired | 1 Ignore the first prompt; 2 ignore the single re-prompt; 3 let the window close | Wake check `Missed` after the re-prompt and window; escalation ladder starts at the configured rung (supervisor → field officer → command center); every rung notified and audited | P0 |
| TC-GAP-035 | Randomised firing times (BR-450) | 30 nights of schedules for one post | 1 Generate and inspect | Firing times are unpredictable within their windows; no arithmetic progression, no repeating minute across nights; all inside the permitted window | P0 |
| TC-GAP-036 | Wake check while the device is offline | Airplane mode when the check is due | 1 Fire the check; 2 restore connectivity after the window | The device shows the check on reconnect with its original due time; the server treats the unacknowledged window as `Missed` and escalates at the time it was missed, not at reconnect (SUR-EDG-007 pattern) | P0 |
| TC-GAP-037 | Acknowledgement requires proof of wakefulness | Configured challenge (e.g. tap-the-code or scan) | 1 Acknowledge with the wrong response; 2 with the correct response | Wrong response does not acknowledge and consumes an attempt; correct response acknowledges; attempts recorded | P1 |
| TC-GAP-038 | Wake check suppressed on a non-night shift | Day shift | 1 Inspect the schedule | No wake checks generated for shifts outside the configured night window unless explicitly enabled for that post | P1 |
| TC-GAP-039 | Wake check during an active SOS | SOS `In Progress` from the same guard | 1 Fire a scheduled wake check | The check does not escalate as a missed check while an SOS is open; it is recorded as `suppressed_emergency` and the operator sees it in the SOS timeline (SUR-EDG-057) | P0 |
| TC-GAP-040 | Guard on an approved break | Break recorded | 1 Fire a check during the break | Behaviour follows the site's configured break rule; whichever rule applies, the outcome is recorded explicitly — never an unexplained missing check | P2 |
| TC-GAP-041 | Wake check reporting | 30 nights of data | 1 Run the wake-check compliance report | Acknowledged/missed/late counts match the records exactly; median acknowledgement latency reported; scoped to tenant and role | P1 |
| TC-GAP-042 | Client visibility of wake checks | Client user at the site | 1 View the night report | Client sees acknowledgement outcomes and counts per the §31 permission; no guard location trace beyond what the client role permits | P1 |

| Test Case ID | Negative case | Edge case |
|---|---|---|
| TC-GAP-033 | Acknowledgement sent from a device not registered to the guard → rejected | Acknowledgement lands 1 second before window close → `Completed`, server clock authoritative |
| TC-GAP-034 | Escalation suppressed by acknowledging after the window → still `Missed`, late acknowledgement recorded separately | Supervisor unavailable at the first rung → ladder auto-advances to the next rung (SUR-EDG-006) |
| TC-GAP-035 | Schedule regenerated repeatedly to find a predictable slot → generation is server-side and audited | Two posts at the same site → schedules independent, not correlated |
| TC-GAP-036 | Offline acknowledgement backdated into the window → server-received time governs; recorded as late | Device offline for the entire night → all checks `Missed`, one consolidated escalation, not N alert storms |
| TC-GAP-037 | Challenge answer harvested from a screenshot → challenge is single-use per check | Guard cannot read the challenge in darkness → high-contrast/large-target mode verified in the field trial |
| TC-GAP-038 | Wake checks forced onto a day shift via API without configuration → rejected | Night shift starting at 19:00 in winter vs summer → window is configured by clock time, not by daylight |
| TC-GAP-039 | Emergency flag set falsely to avoid checks → flag derives from an actual open SOS/incident, not a user toggle | SOS closes mid-window → the next scheduled check resumes normally |
| TC-GAP-040 | Break created retroactively to excuse a missed check → retroactive breaks require an approver and are audited | Break overlapping a check boundary → rule applied at the check's fire time |
| TC-GAP-041 | Report requested across tenants → `404` | Report over a period where the wake-check policy changed → each night evaluated under the policy in force that night |
| TC-GAP-042 | Client fetching the guard's raw location from the wake-check record → denied | Client at a multi-agency site → sees only their own contracted posts |

| TC-OPS-008 | Incident linked to a replacement | Guard-related incident causing removal | 1 Trigger a replacement from the incident | Replacement created per WKF-18 and linked; the coverage gap is recorded (BR-420) | P1 |
| TC-OPS-009 | Incident report export | Closed P1 incident | 1 Export the report as PDF | The PDF contains the full timeline with server timestamps, evidence references, investigator, corrective action and approver; it is watermarked with the requester and time | P1 |
| TC-OPS-010 | Incident analytics | 90 days of incidents | 1 Run the incident report by category, site and severity | Counts, median time-to-acknowledge and time-to-close match the records exactly; scoped to tenant and role | P1 |

| Test Case ID | Negative case | Edge case |
|---|---|---|
| TC-OPS-001 | Incident created against another tenant's site → `404` | Evidence upload fails mid-way → incident is still created; missing media is flagged for retry, never silently dropped |
| TC-OPS-002 | Severity downgraded to avoid notifications → downgrades require a reason, an approver and are audited | Category default overridden at raise → the override and reason are recorded |
| TC-OPS-003 | Closure forced via API without the three prerequisites → rejected | Investigator leaves the organisation mid-investigation → reassignment required before closure; the original investigator remains in history |
| TC-OPS-004 | Auto-created incident closed automatically with the SOS → prohibited; explicit closure required | SOS classified genuine then re-classified → the incident remains, annotated with the reclassification |
| TC-OPS-005 | Offline incident submitted twice on flaky sync → deduplicated by client event ID | Device factory-reset before sync → SUR-EDG-046 applies |
| TC-OPS-006 | Client user searching the incident ID directly → `404` | Client offboarded while holding the incident → visibility passes to the remaining client users per §31 |
| TC-OPS-007 | Reassignment to a user in another tenant → rejected | Reassignment during an open SLA breach → breach record retained against the original owner |
| TC-OPS-008 | Replacement created without recording the gap → asserted recorded | Guard removed but returns before the shift starts → replacement cancelled, gap duration recomputed to actual |
| TC-OPS-009 | Export by a role without export permission → denied and audited | Export of an incident containing another client's data at a shared site → foreign data excluded from the PDF |
| TC-OPS-010 | Report aggregating across tenants → asserted scoped | Period spanning a severity-policy change → each incident evaluated under the policy in force at raise |

| TC-AGN-005 | Licence geography bounds allocation (BR-406) | Site in a district not covered by any verified licence | 1 Attempt to allocate | Blocked naming the district and the licence gap; the post remains an open post (BR-412) | P0 |
| TC-AGN-006 | Rest-period constraint | Guard finished a shift 3 hours ago; minimum rest is 8 hours | 1 Attempt to allocate | Blocked with the earliest permissible start shown; override follows TC-AGN-003 | P0 |
| TC-AGN-007 | Guard acceptance step | Post configured to require guard acceptance | 1 Allocate; 2 guard accepts in the app | Assignment `Pending` until acceptance, then `Active`; non-response by the configured deadline returns the post to open and notifies the allocator | P1 |
| TC-AGN-008 | Bulk allocation for a new contract | 20 posts across 3 sites | 1 Run bulk allocation | Every successful allocation is created atomically per post; failures are listed individually with reasons; a partial run never leaves an assignment without its post record | P1 |
| TC-AGN-009 | Unmet strength must be an explicit open post (BR-412) | Post needs 3, only 2 allocated | 1 Save the roster | An `open post` record exists for the shortfall with its count and duration; the roster never renders as complete; the gap appears in the coverage report | P0 |
| TC-AGN-010 | Allocation visibility and scope | Branch Manager of Branch 1 | 1 Open allocation for a Branch 2 post | `404`; Branch 1 candidates only appear for Branch 1 posts unless cross-branch sharing is explicitly enabled and audited | P0 |

| Test Case ID | Negative case | Edge case |
|---|---|---|
| TC-AGN-001 | Candidate list requested for another tenant's post → `404` | Two candidates with identical scores → deterministic tie-break, documented |
| TC-AGN-002 | Constraint disabled per-tenant to force allocation → hard constraints are platform-governed; changes audited | Certification verified during the allocation session → constraint re-evaluated, allocation proceeds |
| TC-AGN-003 | Approver is the same person as the requester → blocked | Override approved then the approver's role revoked → the assignment stands; the approval remains attributed with its timestamp |
| TC-AGN-004 | Overlap created through two concurrent allocation sessions → serialised server-side, second rejected | Shifts that touch exactly (06:00 end, 06:00 start) → permitted only if the rest rule allows; otherwise blocked with the rule named |
| TC-AGN-005 | District spoofed on the site record → licence check uses the geocoded district | Licence verified for the district mid-session → re-validated at allocation, then permitted |
| TC-AGN-006 | Rest period computed from scheduled rather than actual end → asserted computed from actual check-out where available | Guard's previous shift auto-closed → rest computed from the auto-close time, flagged |
| TC-AGN-007 | Acceptance submitted by a different guard → `404` | Guard accepts after the deadline → acceptance rejected; post already reopened |
| TC-AGN-008 | Bulk run partially committed on failure → asserted per-post atomic | Bulk run exceeding the entitlement limit → stops at the limit with a clear message, no partial silent truncation |
| TC-AGN-009 | Open post suppressed from the report → prohibited (BR-420) | Shortfall covered 10 minutes later → the open-post record retains its true 10-minute duration |
| TC-AGN-010 | Branch filter removed client-side → server enforces branch scope | Guard shared across branches by policy → sharing is explicit, recorded and visible on the assignment |

### 44.12 Replacement — TC-AGN-011 to 018

*Scope: replacing a guard mid-roster or mid-shift and recording coverage gaps (WKF-18; BR-419, BR-420).*

| TC-AGN-011 | Planned replacement before shift start | Assignment `Active`, shift starts in 6 hours | 1 Initiate replacement with a reason; 2 select a compliant candidate; 3 confirm | Outgoing assignment `Cancelled` with the reason; incoming assignment created; both guards, the supervisor and the client contact notified; no coverage gap recorded because the shift had not started | P0 |

| TC-AGN-013 | Replacement must not create an overlap (BR-419) | Candidate already on another active shift | 1 Attempt to allocate them as replacement | Blocked with the conflict shown; the post stays open until a compliant candidate is chosen | P0 |
| TC-AGN-014 | No replacement available | No compliant candidate exists | 1 Attempt replacement | The post is recorded as an open post for the full remaining duration; escalation fires to the operations chain and the client contact per the configured rule; the system never shows the post as covered | P0 |
| TC-AGN-015 | Replacement payroll split | 8-hour shift split 3 h / 5 h | 1 Run payroll for the period | Each guard is paid for their actual attended duration; the sum never exceeds the shift's payable hours; the split is visible in both payslips | P0 |
| TC-AGN-016 | Replacement billing impact | Same shift, usage-based contract | 1 Generate the client invoice | The client is billed per the contract rule for the covered period; the 90-minute gap is treated per the contract's SLA/credit terms and shown explicitly on the invoice or credit note | P0 |
| TC-AGN-017 | Replacement chain | Guard A replaced by B, B replaced by C in one shift | 1 Execute both replacements | All three assignments and both gaps are recorded in one coherent shift timeline; no assignment is overwritten; the post's total covered and uncovered minutes sum to the shift duration | P1 |
| TC-AGN-018 | Client-requested replacement | Client raises a request to remove a specific guard | 1 Client submits with a reason; 2 agency executes | The request is recorded with the client's identity and reason; the guard is not told the client's verbatim reason unless the configured policy permits; the replacement follows the normal compliance checks | P1 |

| Test Case ID | Negative case | Edge case |
|---|---|---|
| TC-AGN-011 | Replacement initiated for another tenant's assignment → `404` | Outgoing guard checks in anyway after replacement → check-in flagged `not_assigned`, recorded, not counted |
| TC-AGN-012 | Gap duration edited to zero → not editable; derived from timestamps | Replacement arrives before the outgoing guard leaves → overlap recorded as double-cover, not as a gap |
| TC-AGN-013 | Overlap allowed via an exception without an approver → rejected | Candidate's conflicting shift is cancelled during the attempt → re-evaluated, then permitted |
| TC-AGN-014 | Open post auto-closed at shift end to hide it → the record retains the full duration | Client waives coverage for the remainder → waiver recorded with the client user's identity; the gap record still exists |
| TC-AGN-015 | Both guards paid for the full 8 hours → asserted impossible | Replacement never checks in → only the first guard is paid; the rest is a gap |
| TC-AGN-016 | Client billed for the uncovered 90 minutes with no credit → asserted per the contract rule, and the rule is shown | Contract has no SLA clause → the default configured treatment applies and is stated on the invoice |
| TC-AGN-017 | Chain flattened into a single assignment → asserted three distinct records | Two replacements at the same minute → deterministic ordering by server timestamp |
| TC-AGN-018 | Client requesting a replacement at a site they do not contract → `404` | Request made 30 minutes before shift start → treated as an emergency replacement with its gap consequences |

| TC-GAP-048 | Media upload resumption | 6 photos and 1 voice note queued on a 2G link | 1 Start sync; 2 interrupt at 60%; 3 resume | Uploads resume from the last committed chunk; no re-upload from zero; all media arrive intact with checksums matching | P0 |

| TC-GAP-050 | Queue size limit and eviction policy | Queue filled beyond the configured maximum | 1 Continue generating events | Safety events (SOS, incident) are never evicted; the app warns the guard and the supervisor that the queue is near capacity; if eviction of low-priority telemetry occurs it is recorded as a named gap, never silent | P0 |
| TC-GAP-051 | Local data at rest | Queued events containing personal data on a lost device | 1 Inspect device storage with the app locked | Queue contents are encrypted at rest; media are not readable from the device gallery or a file browser; the app is not backed up to cloud backup services in plaintext | P0 |

| TC-GAP-056 | Reconnection storm | 500 devices reconnect simultaneously after a 90-minute outage | 1 Restore connectivity | All queues drain within the §46 window; no duplicates; backoff prevents thundering-herd failure; no event is lost or reordered within a device | P0 |

|---|---|---|

| TC-FIN-005 | Same person approving twice from two devices → counted as one approver | Run value crossing the threshold after recalculation → the second approver requirement is re-evaluated |
| TC-FIN-006 | Approval API called with a spoofed desktop user-agent → surface is determined server-side by client registration, not by header | Owner using the desktop app → treated as a desktop surface and permitted |
| TC-FIN-007 | Prompt-injected payroll instruction inside a guard's name field → refused (AIQ-6) | AI asked to *explain* the run → permitted as read-only with citations |
| TC-FIN-008 | Single-sided entry created by a code path → asserted impossible; the invariant test fails the build | Rounding across 8,000 payslips → the residual is posted to the configured rounding account, total variance zero |
| TC-FIN-009 | Provider reporting success for a payslip never sent → reconciliation against the provider statement catches it | Partial batch success → per-payslip status, never a whole-batch assumption |
| TC-FIN-010 | Held payslip released without correcting the bank detail → requires the corrected verified document | Hold cleared mid-disbursement → included in the same run only if it clears before the payout cut-off, else the next run |
| TC-FIN-011 | Payslip PDF URL shared → bound to identity and expires | Guard employed by two tenants → sees only their own tenant's payslip in each context |
| TC-FIN-012 | Component edited by direct API before the status check → rejected by the state machine | Run completed with a known error → corrected by adjustment, and the error is recorded on the original run |
| TC-FIN-013 | Correction applied retroactively into the completed run → prohibited | Correction reducing pay below already-disbursed → recovery follows the configured recovery rule with the guard notified |
| TC-FIN-014 | Overtime hours entered manually without an attendance basis → requires a reason and an approver | Hour that is both overtime and night → applied per the explicit stacking configuration, asserted deterministic |
| TC-FIN-015 | Full-month pay for a 10-day joiner → asserted pro-rata | Joiner and leaver on the same post in one period → both payslips correct, sum does not exceed the post's payable hours |
| TC-FIN-016 | Run executed concurrently twice → serialised; the second is rejected | Run spanning a tenant's plan downgrade → data beyond the new limits is read-only but payroll for the period completes |

| TC-PRM-017 | Guard retaining a cached roster PDF → server denies new fetches; the cached copy is out of platform scope and is covered by the device policy | Guard reassigned to the same site later → access resumes from the new assignment |
| TC-PRM-018 | Refresh token minting a new session with the old permissions → asserted re-evaluated | Revocation during a long-running export → the export is cancelled and the partial file is not delivered |
| TC-PRM-019 | Escalation attempted through a workflow automation → automations run under the triggering user's permissions, never wider | Legitimate delegation → performed by an authorised role, time-boxed and audited |
| TC-PRM-020 | Scope widened by a query parameter → server ignores it | State added to the user's scope mid-session → applies within the configured window |
| TC-PRM-021 | Timing difference revealing existence → asserted within noise | Legitimate duplicate within the same tenant → a specific, helpful message with a link is permitted |
| TC-PRM-022 | Suite subsetted to fit the build window → the `other-tenant` plane is never subsetted | New entity added without permission declarations → build fails at the generator, not at runtime |

| TC-TRN-011 | Unsigned build served during a release → download blocked with an error rather than serving | Checksum page cached from a previous release → versioned per build |
| TC-TRN-012 | Load test passing by returning stale cached facets → freshness asserted | All listings in one district → clustering and pagination still correct |

|---|---|---|
| TC-CMP-001 | Verification performed by the document's owner → blocked by separation of duty | Document with no expiry date → treated as non-expiring only if the type permits; otherwise the date is mandatory |

| TC-CMP-007 | Dashboard counting archived documents → asserted excluded, with an explicit archived view | Document in two mandatory sets → counted once, drill-through shows both contexts |

| TC-DAT-001 | Batch upload and extraction | Enterprise plan; 500 scanned muster-roll pages | 1 Upload the batch; 2 run extraction | A batch record is created with page count and checksum; extraction produces per-field values with per-field confidence; nothing is written to live entities yet | P0 |

| TC-DAT-004 | Reconciliation sign-off required to commit (BR-440) | Batch reviewed; control totals mismatched by ₹1,200 | 1 Attempt commit; 2 explain each variance; 3 commit | Commit blocked while any variance is unexplained; each variance requires an individual explanation and a named signer; commit then succeeds and records the sign-off | P0 |
| TC-DAT-005 | Duplicate detection against existing data | Batch containing 30 guards already in the tenant | 1 Run the batch | Duplicates are flagged with a side-by-side comparison; the reviewer chooses merge, keep-both or skip per record; no silent merge or silent skip occurs | P0 |
| TC-DAT-006 | Rollback of an uncommitted batch | Batch reviewed, not committed | 1 Discard | All staged records are removed; the source files and the audit record of the discard are retained; no live entity is affected | P0 |

| TC-DAT-009 | Handwritten and poor-quality scans | 200 pages of handwriting, faded and skewed scans | 1 Extract | Field-level accuracy is measured and reported per batch; below-threshold fields all route to review; the batch reports its own extraction quality to the reviewer before commit | P1 |
| TC-DAT-010 | Large migration performance | 50,000 pages | 1 Run extraction and review | Extraction completes within the §46 batch window; the review queue paginates and remains responsive; progress and ETA are shown; a failure mid-way resumes rather than restarts | P1 |

| Test Case ID | Negative case | Edge case |
|---|---|---|
| TC-DAT-001 | Batch uploaded on a non-Enterprise plan → denied by entitlement | Batch with mixed document types → each type routed to its own extraction profile, mismatches flagged |
| TC-DAT-002 | Status set to `Active` via API on staged records → rejected | Migrated guard already `Active` from a normal registration → treated as a duplicate (TC-DAT-005) |
| TC-DAT-003 | Confidence threshold lowered to clear the queue → threshold is platform-governed and changes are audited | Field the OCR did not detect at all → presented as missing, mandatory, and blocking |
| TC-DAT-004 | Variance explained with an empty string → rejected | Variance caused by a rounding convention → explained once and applied consistently, recorded |
| TC-DAT-005 | Silent merge on matching name only → matching requires the documented key set | Two genuinely different guards with the same name and DOB → keep-both with a recorded decision |
| TC-DAT-006 | Discard performed after commit → not available; post-commit changes use TC-DAT-007 | Discard during extraction → extraction cancelled cleanly, no partial staging |
| TC-DAT-007 | Batch record edited to hide an error → immutable | Correction affecting an already-run payroll → adjustment path (TC-FIN-013) |
| TC-DAT-008 | Batch ID enumerated across tenants → `404` | Same source document uploaded by both tenants → independent batches, no shared extraction cache keyed by content across tenants |
| TC-DAT-009 | Quality report omitted so a bad batch commits unnoticed → report is mandatory pre-commit | Page rotated 180° → auto-orientation attempted, failures flagged rather than mis-extracted |
| TC-DAT-010 | Resume restarting from page 1 → asserted resumes | Migration running during month-end payroll → scheduled or throttled per the §46 contention allowance |

|---|---|---|
| TC-NTF-001 | Template with an unresolved `{{variable}}` reaching a user → build-blocking lint failure | SMS exceeding one segment → split correctly, key fact in the first segment |

| Test Case ID | Negative case | Edge case |
|---|---|---|
| TC-AI-001 | Answer citing a record the user cannot open → fails | Question spanning a period where the data model changed → answer states the boundary rather than blending |

| TC-AI-008 | OCR text auto-executed during migration review → prohibited | Injected text in a language the OCR mis-reads → still content, never instruction |
| TC-AI-009 | Refusal only at the model layer with the action layer permissive → fails; the enforcement must be an unreachable code path | Prohibited action requested by Super Admin → still refused for AI; the human path remains available |

| TC-AI-011 | Automation widening its own scope on retry → fails | Automation firing during restricted mode → suppressed with a recorded reason |
| TC-AI-012 | Write occurring then rolled back → asserted never attempted | Chain where every step is individually permitted → permitted, and each step traced |
| TC-AI-013 | Assistant choosing the more destructive interpretation → fails | User confirms the ambiguous choice explicitly → executes with the confirmation traced |
| TC-AI-014 | Emergency phrase discarded as low confidence with no escalation → fails | Guard speaks a mixed-language sentence → handled or escalated, never silently dropped |
| TC-AI-015 | Machine-translated safety string shipped without human review → blocked at the gate | Language with no reviewer available → the string ships in the fallback language, recorded as a known gap |
| TC-AI-016 | Trace missing the retrieval ID list → Sev-2, blocks the feature | Very long conversation → trace is complete and paginated, not truncated |
| TC-AI-017 | Fallback path silently doing nothing → asserted explicit message | AI down during an SOS → SOS path is entirely independent of AI, asserted |
| TC-AI-018 | Leakage appearing only under concurrency → the probe mix makes this detectable, and any instance blocks release | Load causing retrieval timeouts → the assistant refuses rather than answering from partial context |

### 44.28 Reporting and analytics — TC-ANL

*Scope: report correctness, scoping, performance and event instrumentation (§42).*

| Test Case ID | Scenario | Preconditions | Steps | Expected Result | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TC-ANL-001 | Report figures match source records | Known dataset | 1 Run the attendance, coverage, incident, payroll-summary and invoice-summary reports | Every figure equals an independent recomputation from raw records to the exact unit; a single discrepancy fails the case | P0 |
| TC-ANL-002 | Report scoping by role and tenant | Each role, with foreign and other-branch data present | 1 Run every report as each role | Aggregates change only with the visible row set (cross-reference TC-PRM-008) | P0 |
| TC-ANL-003 | Date range and timezone handling | Reports across month and financial-year boundaries | 1 Run for each boundary | All ranges are inclusive/exclusive per the documented convention and evaluated in IST consistently; a record never appears in two adjacent periods or in neither | P0 |
| TC-ANL-004 | Scheduled report reflects scope at send time | A user whose scope narrows after scheduling | 1 Schedule; 2 narrow the scope; 3 let it send | The delivered report reflects the narrowed scope; the change is recorded on the delivery | P0 |
| TC-ANL-005 | Export equals on-screen data | Any report with an export | 1 Compare the export against the on-screen result | Row counts and values match exactly; the file records the requester, scope and generation time | P0 |
| TC-ANL-006 | Analytics event instrumentation | Instrumented journeys | 1 Complete booking, check-in, SOS and payroll journeys | Every declared event fires exactly once with its declared properties; no PII beyond the declared schema; no event fires on a failed action | P1 |
| TC-ANL-007 | Report performance at range | Largest tenant, 36-month range, 200 concurrent runs | 1 Run the load profile | Completion within §46; no lock contention degrading operational writes beyond the §46 allowance | P1 |
| TC-ANL-008 | Empty and partial states | Tenant with no data; report with a failed data source | 1 Run each | Explicit empty state with an explanation; a partial result is labelled partial with the missing source named — never silently rendered as complete | P1 |

| Test Case ID | Negative case | Edge case |
|---|---|---|
| TC-ANL-001 | Figure sourced from a stale materialised view presented as live → freshness stated on every report | Report over a period containing a business-rule change → each record evaluated under the rule in force then |
| TC-ANL-002 | Aggregate computed pre-filter then filtered for display → fails | Role with access to exactly zero rows → explicit zero, not an error |
| TC-ANL-003 | UTC used for one report and IST for another → asserted consistent | Financial year boundary at 31 March 23:59 → correct attribution |
| TC-ANL-004 | Scope pinned at schedule time → fails | Recipient offboarded before send → delivery suppressed and recorded |
| TC-ANL-005 | Export truncated at a row cap without notice → cap stated and the file marked truncated | Export of 500,000 rows → streamed or queued, never silently capped |
| TC-ANL-006 | Event containing a raw mobile number → fails the schema check | Event fired offline → queued and sent once on reconnect |
| TC-ANL-007 | Load passing by serving cached results → freshness asserted | Report run during month-end batch → contention within the §46 allowance |
| TC-ANL-008 | Partial result shown as complete → fails | Data source recovering mid-render → the report states its as-of time, not a blended state |

### 44.29 Security — TC-SEC

*Scope: authentication, authorisation, injection, transport, storage, rate limiting and audit integrity (§38).*

| Test Case ID | Scenario | Preconditions | Steps | Expected Result | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TC-SEC-001 | Broken object-level authorisation sweep | Full route inventory | 1 For every route, access another user's and another tenant's object | 100% denied with `404`; zero routes rely on client-supplied scope (cross-reference TC-PRM-002) | P0 |
| TC-SEC-002 | Broken function-level authorisation | Low-privilege session | 1 Call every admin-only and Suraksha-only endpoint | All denied server-side; no endpoint relies on UI hiding; every attempt audited | P0 |
| TC-SEC-003 | Mass assignment | Any update endpoint | 1 Submit `tenant_id`, `role`, `status`, `balance` and `verified` in the payload | Protected fields are ignored or rejected; no privilege, tenancy, status or financial field is settable from the client | P0 |
| TC-SEC-004 | SQL/NoSQL injection | Every text input and query parameter | 1 Submit injection payloads | Inputs are parameterised; no error reveals schema, driver or query text; the generic error envelope is returned | P0 |
| TC-SEC-005 | Stored and reflected XSS | Agency profile, incident description, guard name, ticket body, report labels | 1 Submit script payloads; 2 view in web, mobile web, PDF export and email | No execution in any render path; content is escaped; the raw payload is retained for audit | P0 |
| TC-SEC-006 | SSRF via user-supplied URLs | Webhook, profile link and document-fetch inputs | 1 Submit internal addresses, metadata endpoints, redirects and DNS-rebinding hosts | All blocked by an allow-list; redirects re-validated; no internal service is reachable; attempts audited | P0 |
| TC-SEC-007 | Insecure direct file access | Document, photo and invoice objects | 1 Request objects by predictable path; 2 reuse a signed URL from another identity; 3 reuse after expiry | All denied; URLs are identity-bound and short-lived; the storage bucket is not publicly listable | P0 |
| TC-SEC-008 | Transport security | All endpoints and all apps | 1 Attempt plaintext HTTP; 2 attempt TLS downgrade; 3 attempt a proxy MITM against the mobile apps | HTTP redirects to HTTPS with HSTS; downgrade refused; the mobile apps refuse the intercepted connection and never fall back | P0 |
| TC-SEC-009 | Secrets handling | Built mobile and desktop artefacts, repository, logs | 1 Scan each | No API keys, tokens, private keys or credentials in binaries, source or logs; the secret scanner runs in CI and fails the build on a finding | P0 |
| TC-SEC-010 | Rate limiting and abuse | Login, OTP, search, export, booking and AI endpoints | 1 Exceed the configured rates from one and from many sources | Limits enforced per identity, per IP and per tenant as configured; SOS is explicitly exempt; limit events are recorded | P0 |
| TC-SEC-011 | Audit log integrity | Any state change | 1 Perform changes; 2 attempt to update or delete an audit entry | Every change has an entry; update and delete are impossible through any interface; tampering attempts are themselves recorded | P0 |
| TC-SEC-012 | Session fixation and hijacking | Any session | 1 Attempt to set a session identifier pre-login; 2 replay a captured token from a different device fingerprint | Identifier is regenerated on authentication; anomalous reuse is detected per §38 and challenged or terminated | P0 |
| TC-SEC-013 | CSRF | All state-changing browser routes | 1 Submit cross-origin state-changing requests | Rejected; anti-CSRF protection and same-site cookie policy verified on every such route | P0 |
| TC-SEC-014 | Password and credential policy | Registration and change flows | 1 Attempt weak, breached and repeated passwords | Rejected per policy; passwords are stored with the approved hashing algorithm and parameters; policy failures give actionable messages without hinting at stored values | P0 |
| TC-SEC-015 | Encryption at rest | Database, object storage, backups, device queue | 1 Inspect each medium | Personal and financial data are encrypted at rest per §38; keys are managed outside the application; a restored backup is unusable without the key | P0 |
| TC-SEC-016 | Dependency and supply chain | Repository and build | 1 Run dependency scanning; 2 verify build provenance | No High/Critical vulnerability ships; an SBOM is produced per release; artefacts are signed and verified before deployment | P0 |
| TC-SEC-017 | Insecure deserialisation and file upload | All upload endpoints | 1 Upload polyglot files, oversized files, disallowed types and files with malicious names | Type verified by content not extension; size limits enforced; names sanitised; files stored outside the web root and never executed | P0 |
| TC-SEC-018 | Business-logic abuse | Booking, refund, wallet and subscription flows | 1 Attempt negative quantities, negative amounts, replayed refunds and price manipulation | All rejected server-side with recomputation; no path allows value to be created from a client-supplied number | P0 |
| TC-SEC-019 | Enumeration resistance | Identifiers across the platform | 1 Attempt sequential enumeration of bookings, invoices, guards and documents | Identifiers are non-sequential and unguessable; responses and timings do not distinguish "exists elsewhere" from "does not exist" | P0 |
| TC-SEC-020 | Privileged access and break-glass | Production access paths | 1 Attempt production data access outside the documented path; 2 exercise break-glass | Direct access is blocked; break-glass requires the documented approval, is time-boxed, is fully audited and triggers a notification to Security and Founder/Management | P0 |
| TC-SEC-021 | Mobile-specific hardening | All four apps | 1 Attempt root/jailbreak use, screen capture of sensitive screens, clipboard capture of credentials, and backup extraction of app data | Integrity signals detected and reported; sensitive screens block capture where the platform allows; credentials are excluded from clipboard and from device backups | P0 |
| TC-SEC-022 | Penetration test remediation | Findings from the previous cycle | 1 Re-test each finding | Every High/Critical is closed and verified; accepted risks carry a named owner, a stated compensating control and a review date | P0 |

| Test Case ID | Negative case | Edge case |
|---|---|---|
| TC-SEC-001 | A route passing because the test used its own object → fixtures assert a genuinely foreign object | Route added by a feature flag → flagged routes are included in the sweep |
| TC-SEC-002 | Endpoint permitted because the UI hides it → server enforcement asserted | Endpoint permitted for a role in one product but not another → asserted per product context |
| TC-SEC-003 | Field accepted then overwritten later in the request lifecycle → asserted never accepted | Legitimate admin field update → performed through its dedicated, audited endpoint |
| TC-SEC-004 | Injection succeeding in a search or report filter → all filter paths included | Payload in a name field that is also rendered in a PDF → covered by TC-SEC-005 |
| TC-SEC-005 | Payload executing in the email client only → email render path included | Payload using bidi or zero-width characters → normalised and escaped |
| TC-SEC-006 | Allow-list bypassed by a redirect → redirects re-validated at each hop | Legitimate customer webhook to a public host → permitted and recorded |
| TC-SEC-007 | Object accessible because the bucket policy was loosened for a migration → asserted denied at all times | Document deliberately shared with a client → explicit, recorded, revocable grant |
| TC-SEC-008 | App falling back to HTTP on a captive portal → asserted refuses | Corporate proxy with a custom root CA → documented enterprise handling, never a blanket trust-all |
| TC-SEC-009 | Secret present in a source map or a crash report → included in the scan | Secret rotated but the old value still valid → rotation asserted to revoke |
| TC-SEC-010 | SOS rate-limited under abuse-protection defaults → prohibited (BR-417) | Legitimate burst from a shared agency IP → limits keyed by identity as well as IP |
| TC-SEC-011 | Entry deleted through a database maintenance path → append-only enforced at storage level | Log volume spike → entries buffered durably, never dropped |
| TC-SEC-012 | Token accepted from a wholly different device with no challenge → fails | User genuinely switching networks → not challenged unnecessarily; the signal set is documented |
| TC-SEC-013 | Route exempted for convenience → exemptions require a recorded justification and are reviewed | State-changing GET endpoint → asserted not to exist |
| TC-SEC-014 | Password policy enforced client-side only → server enforces | Password containing Devanagari → accepted, normalised consistently |
| TC-SEC-015 | Backup readable in a lower environment → backups are never restored to lower environments (§43.5) | Key rotation → old data remains readable through the documented key hierarchy |
| TC-SEC-016 | Build deployed without provenance verification → deployment blocked | Vulnerability with no available patch → compensating control recorded with an owner and a date |
| TC-SEC-017 | File type inferred from extension → asserted content-based | Legitimate large scan for OCR migration → within the documented limit, streamed |
| TC-SEC-018 | Amount recomputed from a client-supplied subtotal → asserted recomputed from source records | Legitimate zero-value transaction → permitted only where explicitly configured, with a reason |
| TC-SEC-019 | Invoice numbers sequential and therefore enumerable → invoice numbers are sequential by law-adjacent convention, so access control and timing parity are asserted instead | Public marketplace listing IDs → deliberately public, and asserted to expose nothing private |
| TC-SEC-020 | Break-glass used without the notification firing → fails | Break-glass during a production incident → still time-boxed and audited, no exception |
| TC-SEC-021 | Screenshot blocking absent on the payslip screen → fails | OEM that ignores capture flags → documented as a known platform limitation with a compensating control |
| TC-SEC-022 | Finding closed without re-test evidence → not closable | Finding in a third-party component → tracked with the vendor, compensating control recorded |

### 44.30 API contract — TC-API

*Scope: contract conformance, versioning, idempotency, pagination and error semantics (§33).*

| Test Case ID | Scenario | Preconditions | Steps | Expected Result | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TC-API-001 | Schema conformance | OpenAPI spec merged | 1 Call every endpoint with valid inputs | Every response validates against its declared schema; an undeclared field in a response fails the build | P0 |
| TC-API-002 | Status code semantics | All endpoints | 1 Exercise success, validation failure, unauthenticated, unauthorised, not-found, conflict and rate-limited paths | Codes match the spec exactly; cross-tenant not-found is `404`, never `403` (§43.8.2) | P0 |
| TC-API-003 | Error envelope consistency | All error paths | 1 Trigger each error class | Every error uses the standard envelope with a stable machine-readable code, a human message and a correlation ID; no stack trace, SQL, internal hostname or library name appears | P0 |
| TC-API-004 | Idempotency | All create and money-moving endpoints | 1 Submit the same idempotency key twice; 2 submit the same key with a different body | The first returns the original result with no duplicate side effect; the second is rejected with a key-conflict error | P0 |
| TC-API-005 | Pagination correctness | Endpoints returning collections | 1 Page through a 10,000-row collection while inserting and deleting rows concurrently | No row is skipped or duplicated under the documented cursor semantics; the page size cap is enforced | P0 |
| TC-API-006 | Filtering and sorting | Collection endpoints | 1 Apply every documented filter and sort | Results match the filter exactly; sorts are deterministic including ties; undocumented parameters are ignored, never applied | P1 |
| TC-API-007 | Versioning and backward compatibility | Previous and current contract versions | 1 Run the previous version's contract suite against the current build | All previously-published behaviour holds; a breaking change without a version bump fails the schema-diff gate | P0 |
| TC-API-008 | Authentication on every route | Full route inventory | 1 Call every route unauthenticated; 2 with an expired token; 3 with a token from another tenant | All denied except the explicitly-declared public routes; the public list is asserted against the spec | P0 |
| TC-API-009 | Rate limit headers and behaviour | Rate-limited endpoints | 1 Exceed the limit | `429` with the documented retry-after; limit headers present and accurate; the SOS path is exempt | P0 |
| TC-API-010 | Payload limits and malformed input | All endpoints | 1 Send oversized bodies, deeply nested JSON, wrong content types and truncated payloads | Rejected with the documented code before any processing; no partial write; no crash and no memory exhaustion | P0 |
| TC-API-011 | Webhook contract | Outbound webhooks | 1 Register, receive, fail, and let the system retry | Payloads validate against the published schema; signatures verify; retries use the documented backoff and stop at the documented limit; a delivery log is queryable | P0 |
| TC-API-012 | Enterprise API key scope | Enterprise tenant with an API key | 1 Call in-scope endpoints; 2 out-of-scope endpoints; 3 another tenant's data; 4 after key revocation | In-scope succeeds; out-of-scope denied; cross-tenant `404`; post-revocation denied within the configured window; all calls attributed to the key in the audit log | P0 |

| Test Case ID | Negative case | Edge case |
|---|---|---|
| TC-API-001 | Response containing an extra debug field → build fails | Nullable field returned as absent vs null → the spec fixes one convention and it is asserted |
| TC-API-002 | `403` used where `404` is required → fails | Conflict and validation both applicable → the documented precedence applies |
| TC-API-003 | Error text differing between environments → asserted identical | Error during a partial batch → per-item results, never a bare 500 |
| TC-API-004 | Key reused across tenants → rejected | Key reused after the retention window → treated as a new request, documented explicitly |
| TC-API-005 | Offset pagination drifting under concurrent writes → cursor semantics asserted | Page size above the cap requested → capped with the applied value returned |
| TC-API-006 | Sort by an unindexed field causing a timeout → sortable fields are an explicit allow-list | Filter on a field the caller cannot see → treated as no-match, never as an existence oracle |
| TC-API-007 | Field removed without a version bump → schema-diff gate fails | Additive field in a minor version → permitted; old clients unaffected, asserted |
| TC-API-008 | Public route added without a spec declaration → build fails | Health endpoint → public by design, asserted to expose no version-sensitive detail |
| TC-API-009 | Limit evaded by rotating tokens → keyed by identity and tenant as well | Limit hit during month-end batch → documented higher tier for server-to-server callers |
| TC-API-010 | Oversized body accepted then truncated → asserted rejected | Legitimate large OCR upload → uses the dedicated chunked upload path |
| TC-API-011 | Webhook retried forever → asserted bounded | Consumer down for 24 hours → deliveries queued to the documented limit, then reported as failed with a replay path |
| TC-API-012 | Key scope widened by a query parameter → server ignores | Key used during restricted mode → field-safety endpoints remain available per BR-438 |

## 45. Edge Cases

**How to read this section.** Every edge case has an ID `SUR-EDG-nnn` and is specified across nine attributes. Because the canon caps tables at seven columns, each group is presented as two tables covering the same IDs: **Table A** gives Scenario · Why it happens · Exact system behaviour; **Table B** gives User-visible outcome · Data/financial consequence · Notifications · Audit · Test case reference. The two tables are one record per ID.

"Exact system behaviour" is the specification a developer builds to. Where a rule is configurable, the behaviour states *that it is configured and where*, never "it depends". Nothing in this section is allowed to resolve to silence: every case ends in a recorded state that someone can see.

### 45.1 The named cases — SUR-EDG-001 to 021

#### Table A — scenario, cause, behaviour

| ID | Scenario | Why it happens | Exact system behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| SUR-EDG-001 | Guard has no internet during a shift | Rural sites, basement gate posts, exhausted data packs, operator outages | The Guard App operates fully offline: check-in, patrol, wake-check acknowledgement, incident capture and SOS queue locally with `device_time` and an integrity-protected client event ID. The UI states "saved on device — pending sync" with a live pending count and never shows a synced state. On reconnect the queue drains in chronological order, idempotently, and the server stamps `server_received_time`. Server-side evaluation uses the pair (BR-446). The portal shows the guard as "device offline, last seen HH:MM", never as absent |
| SUR-EDG-002 | GPS disabled | Guard turns off location to save battery, battery-saver disables it, permission set to "approximate", OEM restriction | The app blocks nothing but records honestly: at check-in it names the exact setting to enable and offers a one-tap route to it. If the guard proceeds, the event is recorded `no_location` and routed to supervisor verification; it is never accepted as on-site and never silently rejected (BR-414). Approximate-location permission is treated identically to disabled for geofence purposes. If location stops mid-shift, the guard is warned within the configured window and a telemetry gap with its true duration is recorded |
| SUR-EDG-003 | Phone battery dies mid-shift | 12-hour night shifts on low-end devices, no charging point at the post | Below 15% and again below 5% the app warns the guard and notifies the supervisor, reduces location frequency, and keeps SOS fully enabled. On power-off, queued events survive in encrypted storage. The server sees telemetry stop and, after the configured silence threshold, raises a `device_silent` alert to the supervisor — it never converts silence into absence. On reboot the app resumes automatically, drains the queue, and the offline window is recorded as a telemetry gap with its exact duration |
| SUR-EDG-004 | Guard reaches the wrong site | Similar site names, first day at a new post, roster change not read, two sites of the same client nearby | Check-in is recorded against the **assigned** shift with flag `wrong_site` naming the detected site and the distance; it is never converted into attendance at the detected site. The guard sees the correct site name, address and a map route. The supervisor is alerted immediately. The assigned post remains an open post (BR-412) until covered, and the `UNSTAFFED_POST` clock runs from shift start (BR-420) |
| SUR-EDG-005 | Duplicate attendance | Double tap, retry on a slow network, offline queue replay, two devices, supervisor also marking manually | Device-originated duplicates are collapsed by client event ID; API duplicates by idempotency key. A manual entry colliding with a device entry does not overwrite it: both are retained, the record is flagged `conflicting_attendance`, and a supervisor must resolve it with a reason before the period can lock. Payable hours are computed from the resolved record only |
| SUR-EDG-006 | Supervisor unavailable when an escalation reaches them | Off duty, phone off, on another emergency, left the organisation | Every escalation ladder is contiguous and time-bounded: if a rung does not acknowledge within its configured window, the ladder advances automatically to the next rung (field officer → operations manager → command center → on-call management) without skipping. The final rung repeats at its configured interval and never goes silent. Non-acknowledgement is recorded against the individual and feeds the responsiveness report |
| SUR-EDG-007 | Missed check-in | Guard overslept, transport failure, forgot, device problem, genuinely absent | At shift start + configured grace with no check-in, the shift is flagged `no_show_pending` and the guard is prompted directly. At the second threshold the supervisor is alerted with a one-tap "vouch present" or "confirm absent" action. If neither happens by the third threshold, the post is recorded as an `UNSTAFFED_POST` from shift start (BR-420) and replacement is triggered (WKF-18). The absence is never assumed from silence alone — it is always the outcome of a recorded decision or an expired ladder |
| SUR-EDG-008 | SOS raised while offline | The exact condition an SOS is most likely to occur in | The app creates the SOS locally and immediately attempts every available transport in parallel, including the configured SMS fallback where telephony is present. The device shows unambiguously that the SOS is queued and how long it has been queued. On any connectivity it transmits with the original trigger timestamp. The operator console shows trigger time, receipt time and the delay prominently. The SOS is never dropped, never expired and never deduplicated on arrival (BR-417) |
| SUR-EDG-009 | Agency licence expires | Renewal not filed, verification pending at the regulator, state vs district scope lapse | At the configured pre-expiry thresholds the agency is warned repeatedly. On expiry the licence becomes `Expired` and its configured restrictions apply automatically (BR-002, BR-436): no new allocations in the covered geography, marketplace listing withdrawn for that geography, settlement payout held (BR-431). Existing shifts complete — guards on post are never abandoned. Field-safety capability (attendance, patrol, wake check, incident, SOS) remains fully functional |
| SUR-EDG-010 | Fake GPS / mock location | Guard attempts to check in from home; rooted device with a location hook; emulator | The event is **recorded and flagged**, never silently rejected (BR-414). Detection uses OS mock-location signals plus device-integrity signals plus plausibility checks (teleport, impossible speed, zero jitter). The guard sees a neutral "this check-in needs verification" message, never an accusation. The supervisor and Compliance see the specific flag. The device is marked for review; repeat detections escalate per §38 |
| SUR-EDG-011 | Client payment fails | Card declined, UPI timeout, insufficient funds, bank outage | The payment is `Failed` with the specific retryable reason shown; no ledger entry is created. The booking or invoice remains in its pre-payment state with a retry action. For bookings, allocation does not begin (BR-403). For subscriptions and contracts, the configured dunning sequence runs and grace applies before any restriction (BR-438). Nothing is silently cancelled |
| SUR-EDG-012 | Guard document expires mid-contract | Police verification, training certificate or ID validity lapses during a live deployment | Warnings fire on the configured ladder. On expiry the document is `Expired` and its configured restriction applies automatically, recorded with the source document (BR-435). The **current shift completes**; no further assignment is made. A replacement task is raised for subsequent shifts, and the client is notified per the configured rule. Renewal verification lifts the restriction within the configured window, and the restricted period stays in the compliance record |
| SUR-EDG-013 | Payment succeeds but the callback fails | Gateway webhook lost, our endpoint briefly down, client closed the app mid-redirect | Reconciliation runs on the configured interval, queries the gateway for all payments in a non-terminal state past their timeout, and completes them. The completion is idempotent: exactly one ledger entry, one invoice, one confirmation, one activation — no matter how many times reconciliation or a late callback runs |
| SUR-EDG-014 | Duplicate webhook | Gateway retry policy, at-least-once delivery, replay | Webhooks are processed idempotently keyed on the gateway payment/event ID. Duplicates are acknowledged with `200`, logged, and produce no second effect. A duplicate carrying a *different* amount for the same ID is never auto-applied: it is quarantined and escalated to Finance |
| SUR-EDG-015 | Two admins edit the same roster | Shared ops desks, a supervisor and a branch manager working the same shortage | Optimistic concurrency on the roster version. The second save is rejected with a conflict showing exactly what the first user changed and offering reload-and-reapply. Silent last-write-wins is prohibited. Edits to disjoint shifts do not conflict. Both the successful edit and the rejected attempt are audited |
| SUR-EDG-016 | Guard assigned to overlapping shifts | Manual allocation error, replacement chain, two branches both claiming the guard | Blocked at allocation by BR-001 with the conflicting assignment displayed. An authorised exception may be recorded; if used, both assignments carry the exception flag, the approver and the reason, and payroll and invoicing treat the overlap per the configured rule rather than paying or billing the same hour twice implicitly |
| SUR-EDG-017 | Site deleted while an active deployment exists | Cleanup by an admin, client offboarding, duplicate-site tidy-up | Sites are never hard-deleted (canon §4). Archiving is blocked while any `Active` assignment, open shift, unlocked attendance period or unsettled invoice references the site. The blocker is named precisely. Once cleared, the site becomes `Archived`, remains fully readable for audit, payroll and invoicing, and disappears only from operational pickers |
| SUR-EDG-018 | User changes their mobile number | Lost SIM, number ported, new operator, guard switching phones | The change requires OTP verification on the new number and notification to both numbers. The `user_id` is unchanged, so all history, assignments and queued offline events remain attributed correctly. The old number no longer authenticates. For a guard mid-shift, queued events sync normally because they carry the `user_id`, not the number |
| SUR-EDG-019 | Agency subscription expires | Card failure, deliberate non-renewal, dispute | After the configured grace, restricted mode applies (BR-438). **Attendance capture, patrol, wake checks, incident reporting and SOS remain fully functional** — field safety is never a paid feature. Administrative, analytical, marketplace and bulk-export modules are restricted. No data is deleted. Reactivation restores full entitlements within the configured window |
| SUR-EDG-020 | AI service unavailable | Model provider outage, index rebuild, our own degradation | Every AI entry point degrades to its documented non-AI path with an explicit message naming AI as unavailable. No operational workflow depends on AI to complete. Requests are not retried indefinitely; queued approval-required AI actions do not execute on recovery without re-validating preconditions (BR-441). The SOS and attendance paths have no AI dependency at all |
| SUR-EDG-021 | Notification provider fails | Push provider outage, SMS gateway throttling, WhatsApp policy block, email deliverability | The engine fails over to the next configured channel within the configured window; success requires a delivery receipt, not a send attempt. If every channel fails for a P0, an independent operations alert reaches on-call and the command center console shows the degradation. Undeliverable notifications are queued and retried, never discarded |

#### Table B — outcome, consequence, notification, audit, tests

| ID | User-visible outcome | Data / financial consequence | Notifications | Audit | Test case |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SUR-EDG-001 | Guard sees a pending-sync counter; supervisor sees "device offline, last seen"; client sees an offline indicator, not an absence | No loss; attendance and pay computed after sync from the reconciled record | Guard: local confirmation. Supervisor: device-offline alert past the silence threshold | Every queued event logged on sync with both timestamps and the offline duration | TC-GAP-043 to 056, TC-GAP-053 |
| SUR-EDG-002 | Explicit instruction naming the setting; check-in marked "needs verification" | Attendance payable only after supervisor verification; unverified events excluded from payroll input until resolved | Guard: enable-location prompt. Supervisor: verification task | Flag, permission state and verification decision recorded | TC-GAP-012, TC-GAP-013 |
| SUR-EDG-003 | Low-battery warnings; supervisor sees the device go silent; no false absence | Telemetry gap recorded with true duration; attendance unaffected if check-in already captured | Guard at 15% and 5%. Supervisor on device-silent | Gap start/end, battery level at last report, resume time | TC-GAP-043, mobile battery suite §43.9.3 |
| SUR-EDG-004 | Guard sees the correct site with a route; supervisor sees a wrong-site alert | Assigned post accrues `UNSTAFFED_POST` minutes; client SLA/credit applies per contract | Guard: correction prompt. Supervisor + operations: wrong-site alert | Detected site, distance, assigned site, resolution | TC-GAP-015 |
| SUR-EDG-005 | Guard sees one active session; supervisor sees a conflict task if manual and device entries disagree | Payable hours from the resolved record only; period cannot lock while a conflict is open | Supervisor: conflict-resolution task | Both raw records, the resolution, the resolver and the reason | TC-GAP-004, TC-GAP-008 |
| SUR-EDG-006 | Escalation visibly moves to the next name; the alert never sits unowned | No financial effect; responsiveness metrics affected | Each rung notified on all enabled channels; final rung repeats | Every rung, its window, the non-acknowledgement and the advance | TC-GAP-034, TC-CMD-007 |
