### 51.7 Phase 5 — Scale

#### 51.7.1 Objective and the business question it answers

**Objective:** enterprise integrations, government readiness, advanced intelligence, and the operational and technical capacity for pan-India scale.

**Business question answered:** *"Can we serve a client with 10 sites and 150 guards, and an agency with 2,000 guards across four states, without bespoke engineering per account?"* This is GOAL-10, GOAL-11 and GOAL-08 at full size.

#### 51.7.2 Scope

| Area | Content | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Enterprise integrations | Enterprise API, webhooks at scale, SSO (SAML/OIDC) and SCIM provisioning, custom integration framework, biometric device integrations | canon §1.4 Enterprise list; §33, §37 |
| Enterprise controls | Advanced security controls, custom roles, custom workflows, custom reporting, SLA instrumentation, dedicated onboarding tooling | canon §1.4 |
| Government readiness | Tender pack generation, eligibility checklists at scale, B2G document packs, audit evidence packs (§40), state-by-state jurisdiction packs | §13, §40 |
| Advanced intelligence | Forecasting (demand, attrition, absenteeism), roster optimisation, anomaly detection on attendance and patrol, incident pattern analysis — each gated on data sufficiency | §25, §41 |
| Marketplace depth | Subcontracting and lead handoff (`SUR-SCR-234`), settlement runs (`SUR-SCR-460`, `461`, `331`), premium/sponsored placement operations | §19, `WKF-23` |
| Scale engineering | Read replicas, partitioning of the high-volume event stores, regional edge for the real-time path, load shedding, per-tenant rate limiting, cost-per-tenant observability | §50, §34, §48 |
| Surface completion | The `Ph3` remainder (~42 screens): visitor management, training, shift swap, advances, statutory registers, report builder, ROI calculator, trust/status page, privacy request self-service (`SUR-SCR-105`) | §28 |
| Geographic scale | Additional state licences as data objects; multi-state operations, state-scoped ops roles, jurisdiction-specific compliance packs | canon §1, §40 |

#### 51.7.3 Explicitly out of scope

International/multi-currency operation. Hardware manufacture (wearables, panic buttons, cameras). Becoming a lender against receivables. Anything on the §51.11 deferred list whose trigger has not fired. Non-security verticals.

#### 51.7.4 Dependencies

| Type | Dependency | Consequence if missing |
|---|---|---|
| Prior phase | Phase 4 data foundation for any predictive model | Forecasts with no backtest |
| Prior phase | Phase 3 tenancy at volume; Phase 2 real-time path proven | Scale work is applied to an architecture that has not met load |
| External | State PSARA licences in each new state, with licence geography as data (canon §1) | Expansion is illegal, not just unsupported |
| External | Enterprise procurement requirements — security questionnaires, DPA terms, penetration test reports, ISO evidence | Deals stall in procurement regardless of product fit |
| External | Government tender portal behaviour; no public API assumed | Discovery remains assisted; the roadmap must not promise a feed |
| Decision | **D-592** which additional revenue lines (§52.6) are funded here | Scope is otherwise unbounded |

#### 51.7.5 Team shape

Approximately **42** across product (4), design (4), backend (11), frontend (7), mobile (3), AI/ML (4), data (3), QA (4), DevOps/SRE (3), plus a solutions-engineering function (2–3, not counted above) that exists specifically so that "custom integration" is a repeatable service rather than an engineering interrupt.

#### 51.7.6 Duration

**24 weeks for the first tranche**, then continuous `[ASSUMPTION: A-587]`. Phase 5 is the first phase that does not end; it converts into a steady-state delivery organisation with quarterly planning. The gate below is therefore an *entry* gate into steady state, not an exit gate.

#### 51.7.7 Key risks

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Every enterprise deal demands one bespoke integration | Engineering becomes a services shop; margin collapses (§52.3.7) | Integration framework + a priced integration SKU (§52.6); refuse bespoke work below a price floor |
| Predictive models are built before the data supports them | Confident wrong forecasts damage trust more than no forecasts | Data-sufficiency gate per model: minimum history, minimum volume, backtest published |
| Multi-state expansion outruns licence coverage | BR-002 restrictions fire constantly, or worse, are overridden | Licence geography as a hard gate on deployment creation, not a warning |
| Scale work is deferred until an outage forces it | A P0 at the worst possible moment — a client's night shift | §50 capacity model reviewed quarterly with a headroom threshold that triggers work |

#### 51.7.8 Acceptance criteria

| # | Criterion | Measure |
|---|---|---|
| A5-1 | ≥1 live client with ≥10 sites and ≥150 guards fully managed on-platform including client-side RBAC and consolidated billing | GOAL-10 |
| A5-2 | ≥1 agency tenant with ≥1,000 guards across ≥2 states operating on the portal | Tenant metrics |
| A5-3 | ≥25 tenders tracked end to end to outcome | GOAL-11 |
| A5-4 | ≥5,000 marketplace listings with ≥2,000 licence-verified | GOAL-08 |
| A5-5 | ≥12% of verified listed agencies on a paid plan | GOAL-09 |
| A5-6 | Enterprise API and SSO delivered against a real customer's environment with no code fork | Integration record |
| A5-7 | Platform meets §46 NFR targets at 5× the Phase 4 exit load in a load test | §50 capacity test |
| A5-8 | Every predictive model in production has a published backtest and a documented failure mode | §41 model register |

#### 51.7.9 Go/no-go decision

Phase 5 has a **continue/reshape** decision rather than a stop: at the 24-week mark, if A5-1 and A5-2 are met, the organisation moves to quarterly planning against §42 metrics. If neither is met, the honest conclusion is that the platform has product-market fit at small scale only, and the correct reshape is to double down on the SMB agency segment and the direct guarding business rather than continue funding enterprise capability. Decision owner: Founder/Management as a group.

#### 51.7.10 What is demonstrable

A multi-state agency's national operations view; an enterprise client's consolidated invoice across ten sites; a completed government tender pack; a load-test report; and — the most commercially useful artefact — a reference customer in each of the three segments willing to take a call.

#### 51.8.2 Serial chain vs parallel work

| Strictly serial (cannot be compressed by adding people) | Genuinely parallel |
|---|---|
| Tenancy → everything | Marketing site ∥ OPS internals |
| Site/Post/Shift/Assignment → Attendance → Payroll → Invoice | Guard App ∥ Command Center console (against a contract) |
| Guard App adoption → live tracking, wake-check compliance, attendance-driven billing | Trinetra marketing ∥ Agency Portal build |
| Real operational data → analytics → AI recommendation quality | Design system ∥ backend domain work |
| Verified guard supply → deployment → everything downstream | Compliance rule packs ∥ product features |

#### 51.8.3 The single longest pole

**The Guard App and the field-capture chain that depends on it.** Not because it is the largest codebase — the Agency Portal is far larger — but because it is the only item on the critical path whose completion depends on things engineering cannot schedule:

1. **Device reality.** The target device is a ₹6,000–15,000 Android phone (§17.1, `D-103`). Background location, alarm delivery and battery optimisation behave differently on every major Indian OEM skin, and each behaviour is discovered empirically, not from documentation.
2. **Human adoption.** A guard must install the app, keep it installed, keep location on, and respond to a 02:00 full-screen prompt. No amount of engineering makes that happen; incentive design (payslip visibility, GOAL-06), supervisor enforcement and app weight do.
3. **Field trial calendar.** Wake checks, night patrol and SOS can only be validated on real night shifts at real sites. A two-week trial is two weeks; it cannot be parallelised into four days with four teams.
4. **Downstream breadth.** GOAL-01 (provable duty), GOAL-04 (wake checks), GOAL-05 (replacement speed), GOAL-03 (attendance-approved invoicing), the client portal live surfaces, the Command Center's entire alert supply, the Agency Portal's core value proposition, and every AI feature about field operations are all downstream of it. It is the one component whose slippage moves every subsequent gate.

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-RDM-006 | Guard App field trials shall begin during Phase 1 — with a deliberately minimal build covering check-in and check-out only — so that device, battery and adoption learning is acquired before the Phase 2 build commits to an architecture. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-RDM-007 | Guard App adoption rate shall be a reported weekly metric from the first install, owned by the COO, not a Phase 2 exit measurement. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-RDM-008 | No client-facing surface shall advertise live tracking, wake checks or GPS attendance for a deployment whose guards are not on the Guard App; the surface shall state the actual data source instead. | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### 51.9.2 The reasoning for this sequencing

| Sequencing choice | Reason |
|---|---|
| Client-facing web (surface 1) first, in full | It is the only surface that produces revenue on day one, it is the cheapest to build, and it is the one that repairs the credibility damage catalogued in canon §1.8. It also generates the demand that every later phase needs to have something to operate on. |
| OPS (surface 2) alongside it, not after | A booking with no fulfilment console is a lead form. OPS and the client surface are two halves of one transaction and cannot be sequenced apart. |
| Guard platform web (surface 3) minimally in Phase 1, properly in Phase 2 | A guard must be registered and verified before he can be deployed, so a thin registration and document path is Phase 1. His self-service records are only interesting once there are records — Phase 2. |
| All four mobile apps deferred past Phase 1 | Mobile is the most expensive place to iterate on an unvalidated flow. Phase 1 validates booking on the web where a change takes a day, not a store review cycle. The one exception is the minimal Guard App trial build (SUR-RDM-006), which exists to learn about devices, not to ship features. |
| Guard App (surface 7) in Phase 2, ahead of everything agency-facing | It is the longest pole (§51.8.3) and the source of all field data. Everything downstream is blocked on it, so it must start as early as the domain model allows. |
| Customer App and Admin App (surfaces 6, 9) in Phase 2 with the Guard App | They share the mobile toolchain, the push infrastructure and the real-time client. Building them in the same phase amortises that setup across three apps instead of paying it three times. |
| Trinetra (surface 4) thin in Phase 1, real in Phase 3 | The marketing shell and plan pages must exist early so agency demand can be captured and the directory seeded; the marketplace and self-serve signup only make sense once there is a portal to sign up to. |
| Agency Portal (surface 5) in Phase 3 | It is a *surfacing* of Phases 0–2 services to a second tenant class. Building it earlier means building it against a domain model that has never been operated. |
| Agency App and Desktop (surfaces 8, 10) with or after the portal | Both are companions to a product that must exist first. The desktop shell ships in Phase 3 because §1.3 makes it a headline promise on Trinetra; its native extras follow in Phase 4. |

#### 51.9.3 The strategic question: lead with B2C guarding, or with B2B SaaS?

This is the most consequential sequencing decision in the document, and the two options have genuinely different economics.

| Dimension | Lead with guarding (B2C/B2B service) | Lead with Agency SaaS (B2B software) |
|---|---|---|
| Time to first revenue | ~1 month after MVL — a booking is paid on day one | 6–9 months — supply must be found, listed, verified, trialled, converted |
| Gross margin | ~13% unarmed, ~13% armed by percentage (§52.2) | ~63–72% contribution (§52.3) |
| Working capital | Heavy: guards are paid monthly, clients pay on 30–45 day terms; ~45 days of direct cost is permanently tied up (§52.7.6) | Light to negative: subscriptions are collected in advance |
| Proof required to sell | A licence, a guard, a uniform and a reference | A working operations system, a reference agency, and credibility with a sceptical, software-averse buyer |
| What it teaches you | Exactly how guarding actually works — rosters, reliefs, absconding, wage disputes, client escalations. This is the specification for the SaaS product | How agencies buy software. Useful, but you cannot design the product without the operational knowledge above |
| Failure mode | Scaling a low-margin, working-capital-hungry services business without a technology moat | Building 110 screens for a customer you have never observed, then discovering the workflows are wrong |
| Competitive position | Competes with 35,000 agencies (`A-001`) | Competes with legacy Indian guard-management software and with Excel |

**[RECOMMENDED] Lead with the guarding business, run Suraksha's own operation as tenant `SURAKSHA-HQ` on the multi-tenant platform from Phase 0, and ship the Agency SaaS in Phase 3.**

The reasoning, in priority order:

1. **The SaaS product's specification is the guarding operation.** Rosters, weekly-off relief, absconding, replacement at 03:00, wage advances, attendance disputes — these are not discoverable from interviews. Running the operation is the cheapest, fastest and most accurate product research available, and it is research that competitors cannot buy.
2. **Credibility is the SaaS product's entry ticket.** The buyer is an agency owner who has been sold software before. "We run our own 500-guard operation on this, here is the Command Center, here is last night's wake-check log" is a qualitatively different sales conversation from a feature list. Phase 2's demo (§51.4.10) is simultaneously the best B2C marketing asset and the best B2B SaaS sales asset — one build, two funnels.
3. **Cash timing.** Guarding revenue starts in month ~9 of the roadmap and scales linearly with deployments. SaaS MRR does not become material until month ~18 even in a good case. Leading with SaaS means financing the entire build with no revenue at all.
4. **Waste risk.** The single largest waste exposure in this plan is 110 Agency Portal screens built for imagined workflows. Phase 3 as a *surfacing* exercise over proven services is a fraction of the risk of Phase 3 as a *discovery* exercise.
5. **The marketplace bridges the two.** Trinetra's directory can be seeded and verified during Phases 1–2 at low engineering cost, so the SaaS funnel is filling while guarding pays the bills. GOAL-08 (directory) is a prerequisite for GOAL-09 (conversion), and it has a long lead time — it should start early even though the product it feeds ships late.

**The honest counter-argument, stated rather than hidden.** A capital-efficiency-driven investor would sequence the reverse: SaaS has five times the margin and negative working capital, and the guarding business could be argued to be a distraction that consumes management attention and cash for a 13% margin. That argument is correct on the numbers and wrong on the sequencing risk. The mitigations that make the recommendation safe are:

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-RDM-009 | Suraksha's own guarding operation shall run as tenant `SURAKSHA-HQ` on the same multi-tenant platform sold to agencies, with no private code path, no bypassed entitlement and no schema exclusive to it. If a capability is built for HQ it is built for tenants. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-RDM-010 | Guarding operations shall not consume engineering capacity outside the roadmap: operational requests are triaged into the phase backlog like any other requirement, and "the ops team needs it today" is not a scheduling authority. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-RDM-011 | The guarding business shall carry an explicit deployment cap per phase (a number of guards beyond which no new contract is signed without a funded operations expansion), so that a low-margin, working-capital-hungry business cannot silently absorb the company's cash before the SaaS engine starts. `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-581]` | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-RDM-012 | The Trinetra plan comparison page shall show, per feature, whether it is available now or scheduled, with a date band; selling a Professional feature that ships two phases later is prohibited. | [RECOMMENDED] |

### 51.10 The minimum viable launch

#### 51.10.1 Definition

**The smallest coherent thing that can go live and serve a real client with real guards** is:

> One client, one site, one to three posts, four to eight verified guards, two shifts a day, in one serviceable city, for one calendar month — booked online, paid online, deployed from OPS, attended on the Guard App with GPS and face capture, watched by a Command Center that is actually staffed, and invoiced from the attendance the client can see.

This lands at the **end of Phase 2**, not the end of Phase 1. Phase 1 alone produces a booking and a manual deployment, which is a business but not the business described in canon §1 — the brand's claims (24/7 command center, live GPS tracking, GPS attendance, wake checks) are all Phase 2. Launching at the end of Phase 1 requires removing those claims from the website, which is possible but wastes the differentiator.

`[RECOMMENDED]` Run a **Phase 1 soft launch** — real bookings, real deployment, honest website that does not claim live tracking — and treat the **Phase 2 exit as the marketing launch**, when every claim on the site is true.

### 51.12 Parallelisation plan

#### 51.12.1 The tracks

| Track | Owns | Unblocked by |
|---|---|---|
| **Platform/backend** | Identity, tenancy, entitlements, domain services, money, jobs | Nothing after Phase 0 week 3 |
| **Client web** | Main website, booking, client portal | Design tokens + API contracts |
| **Ops web** | OPS console, Command Center UI | Design tokens + API contracts |
| **Agency web** | Agency Portal, Trinetra | Design tokens + API contracts + entitlement service |
| **Mobile** | Guard App, Customer App, Agency App, Admin App | Design tokens + API contracts + push infra |
| **Real-time** | Ingest, presence, location stream, alert pipeline | Phase 0 identity; then independent |
| **AI/Data** | Event pipeline, read model, dashboards, AI platform | Instrumented events (which ship with every feature) |
| **Design** | Design system, then per-surface design ahead of build | Runs one phase ahead of engineering, permanently |
| **QA/automation** | Test framework, regression suite, device lab, tenancy and entitlement suites | Runs with every track, never after |
| **Content/legal/compliance** | Truthful content, legal pages, rule packs, DPA, policies | Independent of engineering entirely |

#### 51.12.2 What makes parallelism actually work here

| Enabler | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Contract-first APIs** | §33's OpenAPI-first discipline means every web and mobile track builds against a published contract and a mock server from day one. This is what allows Command Center UI and real-time ingest to be built simultaneously. |
| **Design one phase ahead** | Design finishing Phase N+1 while engineering builds Phase N is the single highest-leverage scheduling rule in this plan. Design working in the same sprint as engineering serialises the whole organisation. |
| **Entitlements as data** | SUR-FIN-166 means the Agency Portal team never waits for a "plan gating" feature; they read an entitlement key that already exists. |
| **Instrumentation with the feature** | Analytics events (§42.4) are part of a feature's definition of done, so the data track is never blocked waiting for backfill. |
| **Content is not an engineering dependency** | Legal pages, rule packs and truthful marketing copy are produced by a non-engineering track that starts in Phase 0 — the failure mode being avoided is the whole site waiting on a privacy policy. |

#### 51.12.3 Per-phase parallel map

| Phase | Runs simultaneously | Genuine cross-track blocker |
|---|---|---|
| Ph0 | Platform ∥ Design system ∥ DevOps ∥ Security ∥ QA framework | Nothing — this is the most parallel phase |
| Ph1 | Client web ∥ Ops web ∥ Platform ∥ Content/legal ∥ Data instrumentation ∥ (minimal Guard App device trial) | Booking API contract must be frozen by week 3 or client web and platform diverge |
| Ph2 | Mobile (Guard/Customer/Admin) ∥ Real-time ∥ Ops web (Command Center) ∥ Client web (live surfaces) ∥ Device lab | Offline sync semantics must be agreed in week 1 — mobile and platform both depend on it |
| Ph3 | Agency web ∥ Trinetra ∥ Payroll backend ∥ Agency App ∥ Desktop packaging ∥ Onboarding playbook | Payroll data model blocks payroll UI, billing and settlement; freeze it first |
| Ph4 | AI/Data ∥ every surface's depth work ∥ compliance depth | AI needs the read model; the read model needs the event pipeline — sequence those two, parallelise the rest |
| Ph5 | Enterprise integrations ∥ scale engineering ∥ government readiness ∥ marketplace depth | Load testing must precede, not follow, the scale changes it validates |

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-RDM-015 | API contracts for a phase shall be published and frozen (additive changes only) by the end of that phase's week 3; a breaking contract change after the freeze requires an explicit cross-track agreement recorded in the phase log. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-RDM-016 | Design shall deliver the next phase's screen designs before the current phase's build ends; a phase that begins without designs shall be reported as a schedule risk at the phase gate. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-RDM-017 | Content, legal and compliance deliverables shall be tracked in the same plan as engineering deliverables, with the same gating force: an unpublishable legal page blocks a launch exactly as a failing test does. | [RECOMMENDED] |

### 51.13 Resourcing reality-check

#### 51.13.1 What this roadmap assumes

| Phase | Engineering + product + design FTE | Cumulative elapsed | Non-engineering operational headcount added |
|---|---|---|---|
| Phase 0 | 12 | 8 weeks | — |
| Phase 1 | 22 | 22 weeks | City ops, verification, sales (≈6) |
| Phase 2 | 31 | 38 weeks | Command Center 7, field supervision (≈4) |
| Phase 3 | 39 | 58 weeks | Onboarding/CS 2, agency sales (≈4) |
| Phase 4 | 36 | ~80 weeks | Support (≈3) |
| Phase 5 | 42 | 104 weeks → | Solutions engineering 3, ops expansion |

**Peak build team: ~42.** **Elapsed to a running guarding business (Phase 2 exit / MVL): ~38 weeks (~9 months).** **Elapsed to two revenue engines (Phase 3 exit): ~58 weeks (~13.5 months).** All figures `[ASSUMPTION: A-588]`.

The assumption underneath every duration is that these are *effective* FTEs: people who are already hired, already onboarded, and not simultaneously running production support for the live guarding operation. Hiring time is not included and is typically 6–10 weeks per senior role in this market.

#### 51.13.2 What happens at half the team

At **~18–20 FTE peak** — a plausible funded reality — the timeline does not double, because the roadmap is not perfectly parallel. What actually happens:

| Effect | Consequence |
|---|---|
| Serial chains are unaffected by team size | The Phase 0 tenancy work, the payroll data model, the offline sync design and the field-trial calendar take the same elapsed time |
| Parallel tracks collapse into sequences | Client web and Ops web cannot run simultaneously; mobile apps are built one at a time instead of three at once |
| Coordination overhead falls | A 20-person org communicates more cheaply than a 42-person one, recovering perhaps 10–15% |
| Quality debt accrues faster | With one QA per five engineers instead of one per eight, the regression suite lags and Phase 4 slows disproportionately |

**Estimated elapsed at half size** `[ASSUMPTION: A-589]`:

| Milestone | At full team | At half team | Multiplier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Phase 0 exit | 8 weeks | 11 weeks | 1.4× |
| Phase 1 exit | 22 weeks | 34 weeks | 1.5× |
| Phase 2 exit (MVL) | 38 weeks | 62 weeks | 1.6× |
| Phase 3 exit (two engines) | 58 weeks | 100 weeks | 1.7× |
| Phase 4 exit | ~80 weeks | ~145 weeks | 1.8× |

The multiplier grows with each phase because the later phases are the more parallel ones — Phase 4's ten simultaneous surface-depth streams are exactly what a small team cannot run.

#### 51.13.3 What to do instead of accepting a 1.8× timeline

`[RECOMMENDED]` At half team size, **do not run this roadmap slowly. Run a different roadmap.**

| Change | Rationale |
|---|---|
| Keep Phase 0 intact at full relative investment | Tenancy, permissions and money cannot be done cheaply; they can only be done once |
| Cut Phase 1 to the MVL screen list (§51.10.2) plus nothing | 80 screens instead of 110; the deferred 30 are marketing depth, not revenue |
| Ship the Guard App with 12 screens, not 29 | Check-in, check-out, wake check, SOS, sync status. Patrol, tasks, leave, payslip and supervisor screens wait |
| Build **one** mobile app in Phase 2 — the Guard App | The Customer App and Admin App are conveniences; the client web portal and OPS web already serve those users |
| Defer the Agency Portal to a genuinely later date and say so publicly | Half-building an ERP is worse than not starting it. Trinetra sells the marketplace listing and a waitlist, not a product that does not exist |
| Keep the Command Center staffed regardless | It is an operational cost, not an engineering one, and the brand claim depends on it |
| Take the phase gates more seriously, not less | A small team cannot afford to build the wrong thing even once |

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-RDM-018 | Phase durations shall be restated whenever the effective team size changes by more than 20%, and the restated plan shall be circulated to Founder/Management with the changed assumptions named. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-RDM-019 | Production support for the live guarding operation shall be resourced explicitly (an on-call rotation with allocated capacity), not absorbed silently from feature capacity. `[ASSUMPTION: A-590]` a steady-state allocation of 15% of engineering capacity from Phase 2 onward. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-RDM-020 | Hiring lead time shall be planned as a dependency with the same visibility as a technical dependency; a phase whose team is not hired by its start date is a phase that has not started. | [RECOMMENDED] |

| SUR-RDM-024 | A phase demo shall be given to at least one real external user (client, guard, or agency owner as appropriate) before its gate decision, and their reaction recorded. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-RDM-025 | The Guard App adoption rate, proof-completeness rate, booking completion rate, and paid-tenant count shall be published internally weekly from the moment each becomes measurable, so that phase gates are confirmations of known facts rather than discoveries. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-RDM-026 | Any change to canon §1.4's three plans, or to the phase in which a canon-listed plan feature becomes available, requires Founder/Management approval recorded against `D-580`–`D-599` or the plan-governance process in §52.8. | [CONFIRMED] |

## 52. Monetization

Every number in this section shows its arithmetic and labels its inputs. Nothing here is a forecast. Where an input is not confirmed by the founders or visible in the live product, it carries an `[ASSUMPTION: A-nnn]` tag and appears in the register at the end. Plan definitions are canon §1.4 and are reproduced, never altered. Financial mechanics — ledger, proration, dunning, revenue recognition — are owned by §35 and referenced, not repeated. Metric definitions are owned by §42 and referenced by their `ANL-` identifiers, never redefined.

### 52.1 The two revenue engines

Suraksha operates two businesses that share one platform and have almost nothing else in common.

| | **Engine A — Guarding service** | **Engine B — Agency SaaS** |
|---|---|---|
| What is sold | Deployed guard-months (B2C and B2B) | A subscription to the Agency Portal (canon §1.4) |
| Buyer | Homeowner, RWA, business, enterprise, government | PSARA-licensed agency owner (~35,000 addressable, `A-001`) |
| Price anchor | ₹18,500 unarmed · ₹38,000 armed PSO · plan cards ₹18,000 / ₹22,000 / custom, all excl. 18% GST (canon §1.5) | ₹5,000 Starter · ₹10,000 Professional · Enterprise "Contact Sales", never displayed (canon §1.4) |
| Revenue shape | Recurring monthly service revenue, tied to headcount deployed | Recurring subscription revenue, tied to tenant count and plan mix |
| Gross margin | Thin — see §52.2 | High — see §52.3 |
| Working capital | Heavily negative: wages paid monthly, receivables at 30–45 days | Positive: collected in advance |
| Scaling constraint | People — recruitment, verification, supervision | Onboarding capacity and support |
| Marginal cost of one more unit | ~87% of price | ~15–30% of price |
| Surfaces | Main website, client portal, Customer App, Guard App, OPS, Command Center | Trinetra, Agency Portal, Agency App, Desktop, OPS tenant management |

A third, smaller engine — marketplace monetisation — is specified in §52.5, and candidate fourth lines in §52.6.

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-MON-001 | The two engines shall be reported separately in every management view: separate revenue, separate contribution, separate cost base, separate headcount. A blended "revenue" figure that mixes a 13%-margin service business with a 70%-margin software business is prohibited in internal reporting. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-MON-002 | Shared platform cost shall be allocated between the engines on a stated, stable basis (recommended: active guard-months for Engine A, active tenants for Engine B), and the basis shall not be changed without Finance approval and a restatement of prior periods (§42.6.4). | [RECOMMENDED] |

---

### 52.2 Engine A — guarding service economics

#### 52.2.1 What the price covers

The canon's anchors are monthly prices for a deployed position. `[ASSUMPTION: A-591]` The ₹18,500 unarmed anchor represents **one guard, one 12-hour post, 26 duty days in a calendar month, in a tier-2 city, excluding 18% GST**, with relief cover for the four weekly offs either not provided or billed separately. This assumption is the single most important input in this section and must be confirmed against actual signed contracts before any of the figures below are used commercially.

#### 52.2.2 The cost stack — unarmed guard, ₹18,500 bill rate

All statutory rates are treated as **configurable data** per canon §0; the percentages below are the planning inputs, not legal statements, and the platform stores them as rules per jurisdiction (§40).

| Line | Basis | Input | Amount (₹/month) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | Bill rate, excl. GST | canon §1.5 | **18,500** |
| B1 | Guard wage (Basic + DA), 26 duty days | `[ASSUMPTION: A-592]` | 10,500 |
| B2 | Provident fund, employer share @13.00% of B1 | 10,500 × 0.1300 | 1,365 |
| B3 | State insurance, employer share @3.25% of B1 | 10,500 × 0.0325 = 341.25 | 341 |
| B4 | Bonus provision @8.33% of B1 | 10,500 × 0.0833 = 874.65 | 875 |
| B5 | Gratuity provision @4.81% of B1 | 10,500 × 0.0481 = 505.05 | 505 |
| | *Statutory sub-total* | 1,365 + 341 + 875 + 505 | *3,086* |
| B6 | Uniform amortised | ₹4,200 kit ÷ 12 months `[A-593]` | 350 |
| B7 | Equipment & consumables (torch, batteries, register, raincoat) | `[A-593]` | 100 |
| B8 | Supervision | 1 Field Officer : 25 guards; loaded FO cost ₹32,000 → 32,000 ÷ 25 | 1,280 |
| B9 | Recruitment & replacement amortised | ₹3,600 per hire ÷ 9-month average tenure `[A-593]` | 400 |
| B10 | Induction training amortised | ₹1,800 ÷ 9 months | 200 |
| B11 | Police verification & KYC amortised | ₹800 ÷ 9 months = 88.89 | 89 |
| B12 | Group personal accident insurance | ₹600/year ÷ 12 | 50 |
| **B** | **Total direct cost** | 10,500 + 3,086 + 350 + 100 + 1,280 + 400 + 200 + 89 + 50 | **16,055** |
| **C** | **Gross contribution** | 18,500 − 16,055 | **2,445** |
| **D** | **Gross margin %** | 2,445 ÷ 18,500 × 100 | **13.2%** |

#### 52.2.3 Wage sensitivity — why this margin is fragile

Wage is the dominant variable and it is set by state minimum-wage notifications that vary widely. Holding every other line constant (statutory percentages recompute on the wage):

| Guard wage (B1) | Statutory (B2–B5) | Other direct (B6–B12) | Total cost | Contribution | Margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ₹9,500 | 9,500 × 0.2939 = 2,792 | 2,469 | 14,761 | **3,739** | **20.2%** |
| ₹10,500 | 10,500 × 0.2939 = 3,086 | 2,469 | 16,055 | **2,445** | **13.2%** |
| ₹11,500 | 11,500 × 0.2939 = 3,380 | 2,469 | 17,349 | **1,151** | **6.2%** |
| ₹12,500 | 12,500 × 0.2939 = 3,673 | 2,469 | 18,642 | **−142** | **−0.8%** |

*(0.2939 = 0.1300 + 0.0325 + 0.0833 + 0.0481, the combined employer statutory load on wage.)*

**The finding, stated plainly:** at a ₹12,500 wage — entirely plausible in a metro — the ₹18,500 anchor is loss-making before a single rupee of overhead. The ₹18,500 price is therefore an **entry anchor for a low-wage market, not a national price**. The commercial implications are:

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-MON-003 | The pricing engine shall compute a minimum viable bill rate per city from the configured wage, statutory rates, supervision ratio and target margin floor, and shall block quotation below that floor without an approval recorded against the approver (§52.8). | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-MON-004 | "From ₹18,500" shall only be displayed for cities where the computed floor is at or below ₹18,500; other cities shall display their own computed from-price. Displaying a national from-price that no city can profitably serve is prohibited. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-MON-005 | Every quotation and contract shall record the wage assumption, statutory rate set and supervision ratio used to price it, so that margin erosion from a wage revision is detectable per contract (`ANL-F09`, `ANL-F10`). | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### 52.2.4 The cost stack — armed officer / PSO, ₹38,000 bill rate

| Line | Basis | Input | Amount (₹/month) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | Bill rate, excl. GST | canon §1.5 | **38,000** |
| B1 | PSO wage (ex-services or licensed armed personnel) | `[ASSUMPTION: A-592]` | 24,000 |
| B2 | Provident fund, employer @13.00%, restricted to the ₹15,000 wage ceiling `[A-594]` | 15,000 × 0.1300 | 1,950 |
| B3 | State insurance — not applicable above the wage threshold; substituted by workmen's compensation cover | `[A-594]` | 250 |
| B4 | Bonus provision @8.33% on the ₹7,000 statutory ceiling `[A-594]` | 7,000 × 0.0833 = 583.10 | 583 |
| B5 | Gratuity provision @4.81% of B1 | 24,000 × 0.0481 = 1,154.40 | 1,154 |
| | *Statutory sub-total* | 1,950 + 250 + 583 + 1,154 | *3,937* |
| B6 | Weapon, licence, ammunition and secure storage, amortised | `[A-593]` | 1,200 |
| B7 | Uniform & kit (higher specification) | | 500 |
| B8 | Supervision at a closer 1:15 ratio | 32,000 ÷ 15 = 2,133.33 | 2,133 |
| B9 | Recruitment & replacement amortised | ₹9,000 per hire ÷ 14-month tenure = 642.86 | 643 |
| B10 | Training incl. weapons refresher and range practice | ₹6,000/year ÷ 12 | 500 |
| B11 | Enhanced verification amortised | ₹1,500 ÷ 14 = 107.14 | 107 |
| B12 | Insurance (higher cover) | | 150 |
| **B** | **Total direct cost** | 24,000 + 3,937 + 1,200 + 500 + 2,133 + 643 + 500 + 107 + 150 | **33,170** |
| **C** | **Gross contribution** | 38,000 − 33,170 | **4,830** |
| **D** | **Gross margin %** | 4,830 ÷ 38,000 × 100 | **12.7%** |

**The finding:** armed deployment has a *similar percentage* margin but **1.98× the absolute rupee contribution** per position (₹4,830 vs ₹2,445). Since supervision, command-centre and overhead costs are largely per-guard rather than per-rupee, absolute contribution is what pays the fixed base. Mix therefore matters more than rate:

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-MON-006 | Sales targets and incentives shall be set on gross contribution (₹), not on revenue (₹) or headcount, so that the armed, PSO and specialised lanes are not under-sold relative to their contribution. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-MON-007 | Contribution per deployed position shall be visible per contract and per site in the OPS finance surfaces, using `ANL-F09` and `ANL-F10`. | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### 52.2.5 From contribution to profit — the fixed-cost bridge

Contribution above is *before* overhead. The fixed base for the guarding engine:

| Fixed cost block | Monthly `[ASSUMPTION: A-595]` | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Command Center: 6 operators × ₹35,000 loaded + 1 supervisor × ₹60,000 | 270,000 | SUR-CMD-001 requires no unmanned minute; this is the minimum viable 24×7 rota |
| Branch/city operations, admin, office, compliance | 450,000 | Per operating city |
| Platform, infrastructure and product cost allocated to Engine A | 150,000 | Allocation basis per SUR-MON-002 |
| **Total fixed** | **870,000** | |

**Command-centre cost per deployed guard, which is the clearest illustration of why scale is not optional:**

| Guards deployed | 270,000 ÷ guards | Cost per guard |
|---|---|---|
| 250 | 270,000 ÷ 250 | ₹1,080 |
| 500 | 270,000 ÷ 500 | ₹540 |
| 1,000 | 270,000 ÷ 1,000 | ₹270 |
| 2,500 | 270,000 ÷ 2,500 | ₹108 |
| 5,000 | 270,000 ÷ 5,000 | ₹54 |

At 250 guards the command centre alone consumes 44% of the ₹2,445 unarmed contribution. At 2,500 it consumes 4%.

**Break-even headcount for Engine A**, at a blended contribution of ₹2,680 per guard-month (90% unarmed at ₹2,445 + 10% armed at ₹4,830 → 0.90 × 2,445 + 0.10 × 4,830 = 2,200.50 + 483.00 = ₹2,683.50, rounded to ₹2,680):

> 870,000 ÷ 2,680 = **325 deployed guards** to cover the fixed base of one operating city with a staffed command centre.

`[ASSUMPTION: A-595]` This is an illustrative structural model on the inputs above, not a target or a forecast.

### 52.3 Engine B — SaaS plan economics

#### 52.3.1 The three plans (canon §1.4, reproduced exactly, never altered)

| | **Starter — ₹5,000** | **Professional — ₹10,000** | **Enterprise — Contact Sales** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Positioning | Small & medium agencies | Growing agencies | Large agencies and groups |
| Included | Dashboard · Guard management · Client management · Sites · Attendance · **Basic** live tracking · Leave · **Basic** payroll · Invoicing · Notifications · Mobile app · **Basic** AI · Marketplace integration · **Basic** analytics | **All Starter** + Government tender discovery · Advanced analytics · Recruitment pipeline · CRM · Multi-branch management · Workflow automation · Compliance dashboard · Asset management · Visitor management · Advanced reporting · Marketing tools · Website/profile management | **Everything** + OCR-based legacy data migration · Large-scale migration · Custom integrations · Biometric integrations · Advanced security controls · Dedicated onboarding · Custom workflows · Enterprise API · Custom reporting · Large deployment support · SLA · Dedicated account/support |
| Public price | Displayed | Displayed | **Never displayed** |

#### 52.3.2 Target customer profile per plan

| | Starter | Professional | Enterprise |
|---|---|---|---|
| Guard count `[A-596]` | 20–100 | 100–500 | 500+ |
| Branches | 1 | 2–10 | 10+, multi-state |
| Office staff | 2–5 | 6–25 | 25+ |
| Current system | Excel, WhatsApp, a paper register | Excel plus a legacy desktop product | A legacy product plus bespoke spreadsheets, plus a paper archive |
| Buyer | Agency Owner, personally | Agency Owner with an Operations Manager | Owner/board, with a procurement and IT review |
| Decision time | Days | 2–6 weeks | 2–6 months |
| Biggest pain | "I do not know who is on post right now" | "I cannot bill accurately or find guards fast enough" | "I cannot see the group, and I fail compliance audits" |
| Persona reference | §9 agency personas | §9 agency personas | §9 + §12 enterprise personas |

#### 52.3.3 The value metric

`[RECOMMENDED]` The value metric is the **active deployed guard count**, expressed as an included quota per plan with priced add-on slabs — not per-seat pricing.

| Option | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Per-seat (office users) | Rejected. Agencies minimise office logins to save money, which suppresses exactly the adoption the product needs (GOAL-07) and destroys the data the platform runs on |
| Per-guard, fully linear | Rejected as the headline. The canon fixes ₹5,000 and ₹10,000 as plan prices, and a per-guard headline contradicts them |
| **Flat plan price + included guard quota + add-on slabs** | **Recommended.** Preserves the canon's prices exactly, ties price to value received, and creates a natural, honest upgrade path as the agency grows |
| Per-site | Rejected. Sites vary enormously in guard count; the correlation with value is weak |

#### 52.3.4 Entitlement design

Entitlements are data resolved at runtime (SUR-FIN-166). Three types exist (§35.8.1): `boolean` (module on/off), `quota` (numeric), `tier` (basic/advanced). The canon's plan text maps to them directly:

| Canon plan phrase | Entitlement type | Key |
|---|---|---|
| "guard management", "invoicing", "notifications" | boolean | `module.guards`, `module.invoicing`, `module.notifications` |
| "**basic** live tracking" vs full | tier | `tracking.tier = basic \| advanced` |
| "**basic** payroll" vs full | tier | `payroll.tier = basic \| full` |
| "**basic** AI" vs advanced | tier + quota | `ai.tier`, `ai.interactions_per_month` |
| "**basic** analytics" vs "advanced analytics" | tier | `analytics.tier` |
| "multi-branch management" | boolean + quota | `module.multibranch`, `quota.branches` |
| "government tender discovery", "CRM", "recruitment pipeline", "workflow automation", "compliance dashboard", "asset management", "visitor management", "advanced reporting", "marketing tools", "website/profile management" | boolean | one key each; all `false` on Starter |
| "OCR migration", "custom integrations", "biometric integrations", "enterprise API", "custom workflows", "custom reporting", "SLA", "dedicated account/support" | boolean | all `false` below Enterprise |

#### 52.3.5 Upgrade triggers designed into the product

An upgrade should be the obvious next action at a moment of felt need, never a sales interruption.

| # | Trigger moment | Where it surfaces | Upgrade offered |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Guard quota reaches 80%, then 100% | Persistent banner in Guards list (`SUR-SCR-257`), per SUR-FIN-173 soft-cap behaviour | Add-on slab, or Professional |
| 2 | Agency opens a second branch | Settings → Branches (`SUR-SCR-356`) | Professional (multi-branch is a canon Professional feature) |
| 3 | A marketplace lead arrives and there is nowhere to track it | Lead notification → Leads list is locked (`SUR-SCR-333`) | Professional (CRM) |
| 4 | Agency starts hiring — repeated manual guard creation in a week | Guards list heuristic | Professional (recruitment pipeline) |
| 5 | A licence or document expiry is missed | Document expiry board (`SUR-SCR-349`) after the event | Professional (compliance dashboard) |
| 6 | Payroll exceptions exceed a threshold on basic payroll | Payroll exception review (`SUR-SCR-315`) | Professional (full payroll) |
| 7 | A report is requested that basic analytics cannot produce | Analytics home (`SUR-SCR-351`) | Professional (advanced analytics/reporting) |
| 8 | A government tender relevant to the agency's licence geography is published | Notification + locked tender feed (`SUR-SCR-342`) | Professional (tender discovery) |
| 9 | AI interaction quota exhausted | AI copilot workspace (`SUR-SCR-353`) | Professional (advanced AI + higher quota) |
| 10 | Tenant crosses 500 guards, or requests an integration, biometric device, or SSO | Any of the above surfaces | Enterprise (Contact Sales) |

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-MON-008 | Every upgrade trigger shall fire at a moment of demonstrated need, shall name the specific capability the tenant is missing, and shall lead to a one-click upgrade preview showing the exact prorated charge (SUR-FIN-171) before any commitment. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-MON-009 | Upgrade prompts shall be rate-limited to a maximum of one persistent prompt per surface and three per session; a product that nags is uninstalled. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-MON-010 | No upgrade prompt shall appear on a safety-critical surface (SOS, alert handling, attendance capture) under any circumstance. | [CONFIRMED] |

#### 52.3.6 Expected ARPU — with the arithmetic

`[ASSUMPTION: A-596]` for every input below.

| Plan | List price | Avg. realised discount | Net subscription | Avg. add-ons | **Expected ARPU** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Starter | ₹5,000 | 8% → 5,000 × 0.92 = 4,600 | ₹4,600 | ₹800 (one guard slab) | **₹5,400** |
| Professional | ₹10,000 | 10% → 10,000 × 0.90 = 9,000 | ₹9,000 | ₹1,400 | **₹10,400** |
| Enterprise | Negotiated | — | ₹45,000 equivalent monthly | included | **₹45,000** |

**Blended ARPA** at a plan mix of 60% Starter / 32% Professional / 8% Enterprise `[A-596]`:

> (0.60 × 5,400) + (0.32 × 10,400) + (0.08 × 45,000)
> = 3,240 + 3,328 + 3,600 = **₹10,168 per account per month** (`ANL-P12`)

#### 52.3.7 Cost to serve, and contribution margin

| Cost line | Starter | Professional | Enterprise | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Infrastructure (compute, storage, real-time, backups) | 380 | 760 | 3,200 | Scales with guards, events and documents `[A-597]` |
| Support (tickets × cost per contact) | 520 | 900 | 9,000 | Enterprise includes dedicated support per canon §1.4 |
| AI inference | 240 | 620 | 2,400 | Per the Phase 4 cost ceiling (A4-5), `[A-586]` |
| Payment processing @2% of ARPU | 5,400 × 0.02 = 108 | 10,400 × 0.02 = 208 | 400 (bank transfer, not card) | Gateway fee |
| Onboarding, amortised | ₹6,000 ÷ 24 months = 250 | ₹15,000 ÷ 30 months = 500 | ₹300,000 ÷ 36 months = 8,333 | Expected tenant life `[A-597]` |
| **Total cost to serve** | **1,498** | **2,988** | **23,333** | |
| **ARPU** | 5,400 | 10,400 | 45,000 | |
| **Contribution (₹)** | **3,902** | **7,412** | **21,667** | ARPU − cost to serve |
| **Contribution margin (%)** | **72.3%** | **71.3%** | **48.1%** | |

**Blended contribution** at the 60/32/8 mix:

> (0.60 × 3,902) + (0.32 × 7,412) + (0.08 × 21,667)
> = 2,341.20 + 2,371.84 + 1,733.36 = **₹6,446 per account per month**
> = 6,446 ÷ 10,168 × 100 = **63.4% blended contribution margin**

**Two findings worth management attention:**

1. **Enterprise has the lowest percentage margin** (48.1%) because onboarding, migration and dedicated support are real costs the canon's Enterprise feature list commits to. It has by far the highest absolute contribution (₹21,667), so it is worth selling — but only if onboarding and migration are **charged separately** rather than absorbed. See §52.6.
2. **AI inference is the cost line most likely to break the model.** At Starter, ₹240 of AI cost against ₹3,902 of contribution is 6%. If unconstrained AI usage tripled that to ₹720, Starter contribution falls to 68.9% — survivable. If it reached ₹2,000, contribution falls to 40.8% — not survivable at ₹5,000. This is why `ai.interactions_per_month` is a quota entitlement and not an unlimited promise.

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-MON-011 | AI inference cost shall be metered and attributed per tenant, reported monthly against that tenant's contribution, and shall trigger an alert when it exceeds a configured percentage of the tenant's ARPU (recommended threshold: 15%). | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-MON-012 | Enterprise deals shall not be approved where the modelled contribution margin after onboarding, migration and dedicated-support cost is below a configured floor (recommended: 40%), without Founder/Management approval. | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### 52.3.8 D-001 — billing period and GST treatment `[DECISION REQUIRED]`

**[RECOMMENDED] proposal, for management to approve or reject:**

| Aspect | Recommendation | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| Billing periods offered | **Monthly (default) and Annual (optional)** | Monthly removes the commitment objection for a first-time SaaS buyer; annual improves cash and retention for those ready |
| Annual incentive | **Two months free** — Starter ₹50,000/year (5,000 × 10), Professional ₹100,000/year (10,000 × 10); effective discount 16.67% | A round, explainable offer. "Two months free" is understood immediately; "16.67% off" is not |
| Monthly price | Unchanged at the canon's ₹5,000 / ₹10,000 | The canon is a foundation rule |
| Enterprise | Annual or multi-year, invoiced per contract; never publicly priced | canon §1.4 |
| GST display | **Prices displayed exclusive of 18% GST, with the inclusive amount shown alongside at checkout** — "₹5,000 + GST (₹5,900 total)" | The buyer is a GST-registered business claiming input credit, so ex-GST is the meaningful number; the inclusive figure prevents checkout surprise. This also resolves `D-272` consistently |
| Invoicing | GST invoice PDF issued automatically on every charge, with the tenant's GSTIN from their billing profile | §35; parity with the B2C invoicing already built |
| Revenue recognition | Annual amounts to `DEFERRED_SUBS`, released monthly (SUR-FIN-179) | Already specified |
| Mid-term change | Upgrades prorated immediately; downgrades at period boundary (SUR-FIN-170) | Already specified |

#### 52.3.9 D-002 — trial model `[DECISION REQUIRED]`

**[RECOMMENDED] proposal:**

| Aspect | Recommendation | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| Length | **14 days**, extendable twice by 15 days with a recorded reason and approver (aligns with `D-141` in §22) | Long enough to roster a real month's start; short enough to create urgency |
| Card required | **No** | An Indian SMB agency owner will abandon at a card form before seeing value. Card-required trials optimise a conversion rate by shrinking the top of the funnel |
| Entitlements during trial | **Professional-level**, so the tenant experiences the upgrade target, not the floor | Trialling Starter then selling Professional requires the buyer to imagine a product; trialling Professional then landing on Starter creates a real, felt upgrade trigger |
| Trial caps | 25 guards, 3 sites, 5 users, 200 AI interactions | Prevents trial-as-free-tier abuse without obstructing an honest evaluation |
| Data on conversion | **Zero data loss**, always (SUR-FIN-174) | The single most common reason a trial does not convert is fear of re-entering data |
| Expiry behaviour | Read-only grace for 14 days, then restricted, per §35.8.4 — never immediate lockout | A tenant with guards on post cannot be locked out of their roster |
| Guided-pilot variant | For agencies >100 guards: a **30-day guided pilot** with an onboarding specialist, gated on the tenant completing three onboarding milestones | Larger agencies need help, not more days |
| Measurement | `ANL-P11` trial-to-paid, target ≥25% | Already defined in §42 |

#### 52.3.10 D-003 — plan usage limits `[DECISION REQUIRED]`

**[RECOMMENDED] proposal.** All limits are quota entitlements with the soft/hard cap behaviour of SUR-FIN-173; **no quota may ever block a safety-critical action** (SOS, attendance capture, alert handling).

| Quota | Starter | Professional | Enterprise | Cap type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Active guards | 100 | 500 | Negotiated (default unmetered, fair use) | Soft at 100%, hard at 120% of quota |
| Office users (seats) | 5 | 25 | Negotiated | Soft |
| Sites | 15 | 100 | Negotiated | Soft |
| Branches | 1 | 10 | Negotiated | Hard (multi-branch is a plan feature, not a quota) |
| Document storage | 2 GB | 25 GB | 100 GB+ | Soft, then read-only for new uploads |
| AI interactions / month | 300 | 3,000 | Negotiated | Soft, then degrade to the cheaper model tier, never a hard block |
| API calls / day | 1,000 (read-only keys) | 20,000 | Negotiated | Rate-limited, not blocked |
| Data retention in-product | 24 months | 36 months | Contractual | Older data exportable, never deleted without notice (§39) |

**Add-on slabs** `[RECOMMENDED]`, priced so that upgrading a plan is usually the better deal — the add-on exists to avoid a cliff, not to replace the ladder:

| Add-on | Price | Note |
|---|---|---|
| +50 active guards | ₹1,000/month | At +200 guards (₹4,000) a Starter tenant is paying ₹9,000 and should be moved to Professional at ₹10,000 with a 500-guard quota — the product should say so |
| +5 office users | ₹500/month | |
| +25 GB storage | ₹400/month | |
| +1,000 AI interactions | ₹600/month | Priced above the ₹240–620 inference cost line |

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-MON-013 | Quota consumption shall be visible to the tenant in Settings at all times, with warnings at 80% and 100% (SUR-FIN-173), and shall never fail silently. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-MON-014 | When cumulative add-on spend on a plan exceeds the price of the next plan tier, the product shall proactively tell the tenant that upgrading is cheaper, and offer it. Extracting revenue from a customer who is on the wrong plan is prohibited. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-MON-015 | Plan quotas shall be stored as plan-version data (§35.8.1); raising a quota for new customers shall not silently raise or lower it for existing ones, and any change to an existing tenant's quota shall be notified in advance. | [RECOMMENDED] |

### 52.4 Plan comparison and feature-gating specification

#### 52.4.1 The definitive comparison table

#### 52.4.2 How a locked feature appears — visible-but-locked vs hidden

`[RECOMMENDED]` **A hybrid, with a stated rule rather than a designer's judgement call:**

| Feature class | Presentation | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| **Professional features, viewed from Starter** | **Visible but locked.** The nav item is present, greyed with a small lock; clicking opens a purpose-built page describing the capability with a real screenshot, the plan that unlocks it, and an upgrade preview with the exact prorated charge | Discoverability drives expansion (`ANL-P14`). A Starter tenant who never learns the CRM exists cannot upgrade to it. The upgrade trigger design in §52.3.5 depends on the locked item being visible at the moment of need |
| **Enterprise-only features, viewed from Starter or Professional** | **Hidden from navigation**, consolidated on a single "Enterprise capabilities" page reachable from Settings and from the pricing page | Enterprise items (biometric integrations, OCR migration, SSO, custom workflows) are irrelevant to a 40-guard agency. Showing eleven permanent locks makes the product feel like a demo of a better product |
| **Quota-limited capability at its cap** | **Fully visible and usable**, with a soft-cap warning and an in-context upgrade offer (SUR-FIN-173) | The tenant already owns the capability; the limit is about volume, not access |
| **Tier-limited capability** ("basic" vs advanced) | **Fully visible at the basic tier**, with the advanced controls present but locked and labelled with what they do | The canon's own wording is "basic X", not "no X". Hiding the difference makes the plan comparison unverifiable in-product |
| **Anything the tenant already has data in** | **Never locked to invisible.** Always at minimum read-only and exportable | SUR-FIN-169. A downgrade that hides a tenant's own data is indistinguishable from data loss |

**Guardrails on the locked-state pattern:**

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-MON-019 | No more than three locked items shall appear in any single navigation group; beyond three, the group shall collapse to one "More in Professional" entry. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-MON-020 | A locked feature page shall show what the feature actually does with a real screenshot or a short interactive preview against sample data, never a marketing paragraph alone. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-MON-021 | Locked states shall never appear inside an operational workflow the tenant is mid-way through (rostering, attendance approval, incident handling); the lock is presented at entry, not at the point of completion. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-MON-022 | Search results, notifications and AI responses shall not surface content the tenant's plan cannot access without clearly marking it as a locked capability. | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### 52.4.3 The upgrade flow

| Step | Behaviour | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Entry | From a locked feature page, a soft-cap warning, an upgrade trigger (§52.3.5), or Settings → Subscription (`SUR-SCR-357`) | |
| 2. Comparison | The §52.4.1 table with the tenant's current plan marked and the delta highlighted | |
| 3. Preview | Exact prorated arithmetic shown before commitment — unused credit, new-plan charge for the remaining period, net taxable, GST, total (§35.8.2 worked example) | SUR-FIN-171 |
| 4. Authorisation | Only Agency Owner or a role with the subscription-management permission may confirm (§31) | |
| 5. Payment | Immediate charge; on success the subscription changes plan version | SUR-FIN-170 |
| 6. Entitlement propagation | New entitlements live within 60 seconds, push-invalidated to open sessions | SUR-FIN-168 |
| 7. Confirmation | In-product confirmation, GST invoice by email, and a "what you just unlocked" checklist linking to the three highest-value new capabilities | |
| 8. Rate limit | Maximum 2 mid-period plan changes per period | SUR-FIN-172 |

#### 52.4.4 The downgrade flow and the fate of higher-plan data

| Step | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| 1. Entry | Settings → Subscription only. A downgrade is never a one-tap action from a banner |
| 2. Impact statement | Before confirming, the tenant sees a precise, itemised list: which modules become read-only, which quotas will be exceeded and by how much, how many records are affected, and what the export options are. Generic warnings are prohibited |
| 3. Quota conflict | If the tenant currently exceeds the target plan's quota (e.g. 260 guards moving to a 100-guard Starter), the downgrade is permitted but existing records are **retained and remain operational**; only *new* creation is capped. Deactivating 160 guards to fit a plan is not a behaviour the product will cause |
| 4. Timing | Takes effect at the next period boundary; no refund for the current period unless a configured policy says otherwise |
| 5. Data created under the higher plan | **Never deleted, never hidden.** Becomes read-only and exportable, with an inline message naming the plan that restores write access |
| 6. Reversal window | Downgrade can be cancelled at any time before the period boundary, restoring the current plan with no charge |

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-MON-023 | Downgrade shall never destroy, hide or make un-exportable any data created under a higher plan (SUR-FIN-169). Records created by a Professional-only module remain visible, readable and exportable on Starter indefinitely. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-MON-024 | The downgrade impact statement shall be generated from live tenant data (actual record counts, actual quota positions), not from a static template. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-MON-025 | A tenant exceeding a quota after downgrade shall never have existing entities deactivated, suspended or deleted by the platform as a consequence of the plan change. | [CONFIRMED] |

#### 52.4.5 Proration, failed payment, dunning, suspension, reactivation, cancellation

These mechanics are specified in §35.8.2 and §35.8.4 and are not restated. The commercial positions taken on top of them:

| Question | Position | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Proration on upgrade | Day-based on actual cycle length, charged immediately, arithmetic shown | §35.8.2 |
| Proration on downgrade | None; effective at period boundary | SUR-FIN-170 |
| Failed payment | Retry at day 2, 5, 9; grace with full access to day 10 | §35.8.4 |
| Restricted state | Day 11–20: non-critical writes removed; attendance, SOS, payroll viewing and export remain | §35.8.4 |
| Suspension | Day 21+: read-only and exportable; login retained | §35.8.4 |
| **Safety carve-out** | SOS receipt, emergency routing and Guard App attendance capture continue for a configurable 30-day safety window regardless of billing state. **This is a deliberate revenue trade-off and the correct one**: a guard's safety is not a billing lever | SUR-FIN-175 |
| Involuntary churn control | Card-expiry pre-warning at 30/15/7 days; UPI mandate and bank-transfer alternatives offered before the ladder starts; `ANL-P16` target ≤20% of churn | §42 |
| Cancellation | Self-service, with a required reason code, an offer of a downgrade or a pause as an alternative, and no retention gate that requires speaking to a person | |
| Data-export right | Self-service export of all tenant data — guards, clients, sites, attendance, invoices, payroll history, documents — in CSV + JSON + original files, for 90 days, without contacting support | SUR-FIN-176 |
| Deletion | After the export window, per §39 retention, with notice at 30/7/1 days; statutory financial records segregated and retained | SUR-FIN-177 |
| Reactivation | Restores the **prior** entitlement set, not the current default plan; no re-onboarding | SUR-FIN-178 |

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-MON-026 | Cancellation shall never require a phone call, an email, or a support ticket. A cancellation flow that is harder than the signup flow is prohibited. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-MON-027 | The cancellation flow shall offer a **pause** (subscription suspended, data retained, no charge, reactivation on demand) as an explicit alternative, for the seasonal agencies common in this industry. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-MON-028 | Cancellation reason codes shall be a fixed, analysable set feeding `ANL-P06` and `ANL-P16`, with a free-text field that is read, not stored and ignored. | [RECOMMENDED] |

### 52.5 Marketplace monetization

Trinetra plays three roles (§19.1): marketplace, SaaS marketing site, desktop distribution. Its monetisation must not compromise the first, because the marketplace's product **is trust**, and trust that can be purchased is worth nothing.

#### 52.5.1 The foundational rule

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-MON-029 | The verification badge shall never be purchasable, in whole or in part, at any tier. Verification status is earned through the licence and document verification workflow (§19.4.3) and nothing else. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-MON-030 | Paid placement shall never alter the organic ranking score (§19.5). Sponsorship buys a labelled slot, never a position in the organic list. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-MON-031 | Subscription status shall never be a ranking signal (§19.5 "explicitly not signals"). An unsubscribed but excellent agency shall outrank a subscribed but poor one. | [CONFIRMED] |

#### 52.5.2 Listing tiers

| Tier | Price `[RECOMMENDED]` | Contents | Eligibility |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Basic listing** | Free | Name, licence geography, services, contact via OTP-verified enquiry, response-time band | Any agency that completes registration |
| **Verified** | Free — **earned, not bought** | Verification badge tiers per §19.5 (Licence Verified · Verified + Compliant · Suraksha Trusted) | Passing the §19.4.3 verification workflow |
| **Premium profile** | ₹2,500/month | Video, expanded gallery, downloadable brochure, "Featured" ribbon, richer profile layout — **presentation only, never a truth claim** (§19.4.6) | Licence Verified or above |
| **Sponsored placement** | ₹6,000/month per (state × service) slot `[A-598]` | Max 2 labelled slots per results page, label in the same size as the agency name; 1 rotated slot per state landing page | Licence Verified or above; suspended or unverified agencies can never buy placement |

Placement pricing is `D-165` in §19; the figures above are this section's concrete proposal for that decision.

#### 52.5.3 Lead fees versus subscription

`[RECOMMENDED]` **Leads remain free to verified agencies; the marketplace is monetised through placement and, primarily, through subscription conversion.** This confirms the working default already recorded at `D-164` (§19.4.5).

| Model | Assessment |
|---|---|
| **Per-lead fee** | Rejected as the primary model. It creates a direct incentive for Suraksha to generate lead volume rather than lead quality, and quality is the entire product. It also taxes the agencies least able to pay, suppressing exactly the supply that makes the directory useful |
| **Lead credits (prepaid bundles)** | Parked. Mechanically the same incentive problem, with added billing complexity |
| **Free leads to verified agencies + paid placement + SaaS conversion** | **Recommended.** Free leads maximise supply and response rates, which is what makes the marketplace worth visiting; placement monetises visibility without touching trust; the real monetisation is the funnel into the Agency Portal (GOAL-09) |
| **Free leads to subscribers only** | Rejected. It converts the directory into a paywalled lead-gen tool, kills the non-subscriber supply the directory needs, and contradicts §19.4.5's magic-link lead inbox for non-subscribers |

**Why this is commercially rational, not charitable:** a marketplace lead delivered free to a non-subscriber arrives in a lightweight inbox that demonstrates, on every single response, what the full CRM would give them (§19.4.5 step 5). The lead *is* the sales demo. Charging ₹200 for it would earn ₹200 and lose the conversion.

#### 52.5.4 The take-rate question: if Suraksha brokers work to agencies

When Suraksha wins demand it cannot fulfil directly — a city where it has no licence, a spike it cannot staff — it can route the work to a marketplace agency. This is genuine brokerage and needs a genuine commercial model.

| Option | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Introduction fee (one-off, fixed) | Simple and low-conflict, but undervalues a multi-year contract |
| **Take rate on contract value** | `[RECOMMENDED]` **6–8% of the ex-GST contract value for the first 12 months, then 3% thereafter while the platform continues to carry the contract's operations** `[A-598]` |
| Per-guard-month fee | Equivalent arithmetic, harder to explain |
| Suraksha as prime contractor, agency as subcontractor | Highest margin and highest control, but Suraksha carries the client SLA and the compliance exposure for work it does not supervise |

At 7% on a ₹18,500 unarmed position, that is **₹1,295 per guard-month** — compared with ₹2,445 contribution on a direct deployment, but with **zero wage, statutory, supervision or working-capital exposure**. On a contribution-per-rupee-of-capital basis, brokered work is markedly better business than direct deployment; on absolute contribution it is worse. The right posture is that brokerage fills the gaps direct operations cannot, not that it replaces them.

`[DECISION REQUIRED: D-582]` on the exact take rate and whether it applies to the whole contract or only the first term.

**Non-negotiable conditions on any brokered work:**

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-MON-032 | Brokered work shall be disclosed to the end client: the client shall be told which agency is fulfilling, that agency's verification status, and who carries the SLA. Undisclosed subcontracting is prohibited. | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-MON-033 | Settlement to the fulfilling agency shall run through the standard settlement flow (`WKF-23`, §35.5) with defined cycles, holds and dispute handling; ad-hoc payment outside the ledger is prohibited (BR-003). | [CONFIRMED] |
| SUR-MON-034 | Take rate shall be contractual, disclosed to the fulfilling agency before acceptance, and identical for all agencies in the same tier — never negotiated per agency in a way that correlates with subscription status. | [RECOMMENDED] |

#### 52.5.5 The conflict of interest, addressed honestly

**The problem, stated without softening.** Suraksha operates a guarding business that competes with the agencies it sells software to, and it operates a marketplace where those same agencies are listed. An agency owner is being asked to put their client list, their guard roster, their rates and their margin into a system operated by a competitor, and to be ranked in a directory that competitor controls. A sceptical agency owner is not being paranoid; they are being reasonable. If this is not addressed before it is asked, it will be asked in the middle of a sales call and answered badly.

**What makes it worse if ignored:**

| Failure mode | Consequence |
|---|---|
| Suraksha's own listing outranks paying agencies | The directory is discredited in a week |
| A Suraksha salesperson has visibility of a tenant's client list | One incident ends the SaaS business permanently |
| Benchmarks reveal a competitor's rates or margins | Breach of §42.7.2 and of trust |
| Suraksha wins a tender an agency was bidding for, using platform-visible bid data | Litigation-grade breach |

**The mitigations, in decreasing order of strength:**

| # | Mitigation | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **`SURAKSHA-HQ` is not listed in the Trinetra directory at all.** Suraksha does not appear in, rank in, or receive leads from the marketplace it operates. `[RECOMMENDED]`, `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-588]` | Strongest. It removes the conflict at the marketplace layer entirely, at the cost of forgoing marketplace demand for HQ |
| 2 | **Contractual data commitment.** The Agency Terms & DPA (`SUR-SCR-245`) state that tenant operational data — clients, rates, guards, margins, bids — is never accessed for Suraksha's own commercial purposes; breach is a defined contractual remedy, not a policy statement | Strong, and enforceable |
| 3 | **Technical access firewall.** Suraksha's guarding sales and operations roles have no permission path to agency-tenant operational data. Support access to a tenant requires an approved, time-boxed, tenant-visible impersonation session with an audit record (§31, §38) | Strong, and verifiable |
| 4 | **Ranking algorithm published**, with subscription status and sponsorship explicitly excluded as signals, and a "why am I ranked here" panel showing each agency its own component scores (§19.5) | Strong, because it is checkable by the agency itself |
| 5 | **Benchmarking constraints** already specified: opt-in, aggregate-only, minimum cohort sizes, no dominance, and a contractual commitment that Suraksha does not use benchmark data competitively against contributing tenants (§42.7.2) | Strong |
| 6 | **Tender segregation.** Where a tenant is bidding on a tender, Suraksha shall not bid on the same tender using platform-derived knowledge; the rule and its enforcement are auditable | Necessary, and the hardest to prove |
| 7 | **Geographic separation** — Suraksha operates guarding only in a declared list of cities, published, and positions itself as software-only elsewhere `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-580]` | Moderate. Clean while the list is short; erodes as the guarding business expands |
| 8 | **Independent audit** of the data firewall and ranking neutrality, published annually | Moderate but high-signal |

**Pricing and positioning implications — the part that is usually left out:**

1. **A trust discount is real and should be priced in, not argued away.** An agency choosing between Suraksha and a neutral vendor is taking a risk Suraksha's competitors do not ask them to take. `[RECOMMENDED]` treat the canon's ₹5,000 and ₹10,000 as *already* reflecting that discount — they are low for the functional depth described in canon §1.4 — and resist the temptation to raise them on feature-parity arguments.
2. **Position Trinetra as the brand, not Suraksha.** The canon already separates them (`trinetra.surakshaguards.in`, "TRINETRA by Suraksha"). Lead with Trinetra in all agency-facing material; the Suraksha relationship is disclosed, never hidden, but it is not the headline.
3. **Never sell "join the network that competes with you".** The marketplace pitch to an agency is visibility and enquiries; the SaaS pitch is operational control. Neither pitch should imply that Suraksha's own guarding operation is a partner, a customer or a benefit to them.
4. **Make the commitments falsifiable.** "We do not look at your data" is worth nothing; "here is the audit log of every Suraksha access to your tenant, visible to you in-product, and here is the annual audit report" is worth a sale.

| ID | Requirement | Label |
|---|---|---|
| SUR-MON-035 | Every Suraksha-side access to an agency tenant's data shall be visible to that tenant in an access log within their own portal, including the actor, the reason and the duration. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-MON-036 | The conflict-of-interest position, the data commitments and the ranking-neutrality rules shall be published on Trinetra as a standing page, not buried in terms, and shall be presented during agency onboarding as a step the tenant must read. | [RECOMMENDED] |
| SUR-MON-037 | Suraksha shall not bid on a government tender that a subscribed tenant is bidding on where the tenant's bid is visible on the platform; the rule shall be enforced by a check in the tender workspace and audited. | [RECOMMENDED] |
