### 55.6 Decisions blocking Phase 0 / Phase 1

Fourteen decisions must be answered before meaningful code is written. Nine are marked **Pre-P0** — literally before the first sprint, because they determine what is built, where it runs, or what it costs. Five more are marked P0/P1 but block a workstream that starts in week one. Each is summarised below in the form management needs to approve or reject it in one meeting.

| ID | Owner | Blocks | Latest responsible moment |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-001 | CEO | Subscription, invoicing, pricing page, revenue reporting | Pre-P0 |
| D-002 | CEO | Signup, entitlement service, activation sequence | Pre-P0 |
| D-003 | CEO | Entitlement service, plan margins, add-on revenue | Pre-P0 |
| D-005 | CEO | Serviceability check, licences, jurisdiction packs, recruitment, marketing | Pre-P0 |
| D-167 | Compliance | Guard and client data model; the highest-blast-radius storage choice in the platform | Pre-P0 |
| D-550 | CTO | Hiring, repository structure, CI toolchain, the shared-code story | Pre-P0 |
| D-555 / D-601 | CTO | Every line of infrastructure-as-code | Pre-P0 |
| D-626 | CTO | Traceability tooling; the §56 index becomes unmaintainable without it | P0 |
| D-600 | CTO | Mobile team shape and the safety-path reliability model | P0 |
| D-125 | CTO | Mobile hiring for the other three apps | P0 |
| D-604 / D-605 | COO / CTO | On-call rota and support staffing from day one of live operation | P1 |
| D-620 | CEO | Whether guarding contracts may be signed at all in Phase 1 | P1 |
| D-621 | Compliance | Whether the first deployment may proceed | P1 |
| D-622 | COO | Whether the first contract may start | P1 |

**One-page summaries of the nine Pre-P0 decisions.**

**D-001 — SaaS billing period and GST treatment.** *The question:* how the ₹5,000 and ₹10,000 plans are billed and taxed. *Why now:* every subscription object — plan version, billing period, proration rule, invoice line, tax line — is shaped by the answer, and the pricing page and Trinetra checkout both render from it. *Recommendation:* offer monthly and annual; display prices exclusive of GST with the tax line shown at checkout, matching the B2C convention in canon §1.5; bill annual upfront at ten months' price; charge GST on the plan value with place of supply from the tenant's registered address; issue the invoice at period start. *What approving this costs:* nothing to build later; annual prepay improves cash at the cost of a discount. *What rejecting it means:* name the billing period and the display convention, and D-272 must match.

**D-002 — Trial length and model.** *The question:* what an agency gets before paying. *Why now:* it defines the signup flow, the entitlement service's trial state, the activation email sequence and the M5 measurement in A-606. *Recommendation:* 14 days at Professional tier, no card, full functionality capped at 25 guards, converting to Starter on expiry unless upgraded; one trial per verified agency identity; extensions per D-141. *Why this shape:* a card-required trial suppresses the very supply the marketplace needs; a Starter-tier trial cannot demonstrate the features that justify Professional. *What rejecting it means:* choose the length, the tier and whether a card is required — those three answers are enough to build.

**D-003 — Plan usage limits.** *The question:* the guard, user, site, storage and AI-interaction caps per plan. *Why now:* the entitlement service is a Phase 0 component and cannot be written without numbers; and without caps the unit economics in §52 are undefined at exactly the tenant sizes that matter (D-561, R-585). *Recommendation:* Starter 100 guards / 5 users / 10 sites / 10 GB / 1,000 AI interactions; Professional 500 / 20 / 50 / 50 GB / 10,000; Enterprise negotiated. Overage handled by the D-584 add-on slabs. **Field-safety paths — attendance, patrol, wake check, SOS — are never capped**, regardless of plan state. *What rejecting it means:* supply different numbers; the shape (caps plus paid slabs plus uncapped safety) should not change.

**D-005 — Serviceable cities for V1.** *The question:* where Suraksha operates in V1. *Why now:* the booking flow's serviceability check, licence coverage (A-626), jurisdiction packs (D-360), recruitment pilots (A-622) and every city fixed-base commitment (A-595) all resolve from this list. *Recommendation:* one anchor city for the guarding operation where a current state PSARA licence is already held, plus up to two adjacent districts for marketplace and SaaS only. Everything outside becomes a waitlist lead (BR-402). Add a second city only after the anchor reaches break-even at roughly 325 guards. *Why so narrow:* R-604 and R-623 both argue that concentration is cheaper to survive than dispersion. *What rejecting it means:* name the cities and confirm a current licence for each; the platform treats the list as configuration either way.

**D-167 — How government identity numbers are stored.** *The question:* full, masked, or verification-outcome only. *Why now:* it determines the guard and client data model, the encryption design, the masking rules in §56.5, and the blast radius of any breach — all Phase 0 decisions. *Recommendation:* store a masked reference plus the verification outcome only, unless a specific lawful basis is configured for a given document type. *Why:* the platform's largest identity corpus belongs to the least powerful participants; the cheapest way to protect it is not to hold it. *What rejecting it means:* name the lawful basis and the retention rule (D-278) at the same time, because the two cannot be decided separately.

**D-550 — Backend and mobile framework.** *The question:* one backend language for API and workers, and one cross-platform mobile framework. *Why now:* hiring, repository structure and CI all follow from it, and changing it later is a rewrite. *Recommendation:* pick one of each and record it as an ADR before the first sprint; pair with D-600, which carves out native Kotlin for the Guard App's safety path. *What rejecting it means:* state the languages; the register only requires that the choice be made once and written down.

**D-555 / D-601 — Cloud provider and Indian region pair.** *The question:* which cloud, which primary region, which DR region. *Why now:* no infrastructure-as-code can be written before it, and a late reversal costs six to ten weeks dominated by data transfer. *Recommendation:* AWS Mumbai primary, Hyderabad for DR, managed containers and managed Postgres/Redis/storage, plus an out-of-account immutable backup copy. *Dependency:* A-330 and A-570 must be verified in the same week — customer-managed KMS keys, object-lock storage and SSH-less session access must exist in-region, or the compensating control is designed before launch rather than after.

**D-626 — Owner of the requirement ID index.** *The question:* who keeps §56.2 true. *Why now:* the index is accurate on the day it is written and wrong two sprints later unless it is generated. *Recommendation:* a CI job parses every `SUR-`, `BR-`, `WKF-` and `TC-` ID from the specification repository and regenerates §56.2 on each merge; duplicates and gaps fail the build; Product owns the job. *What rejecting it means:* name a human owner and a review cadence, and accept that §56.6 cannot be re-run cheaply.

**D-600 — Guard App native versus React Native.** *The question:* whether the Guard App is native Kotlin while the other three apps share a cross-platform framework. *Why now:* battery, OEM process kills, exact alarms and SOS cold-start all sit under the safety-critical path, and the answer determines the mobile team's shape and the first hires. *Recommendation:* native Kotlin for the Guard App, React Native for Customer, Agency and Admin apps; confirm with an eight-week measured prototype against A-583's battery target and D-527's SOS latency target. *What rejecting it means:* if React Native is chosen for all four, A-583 and D-527 become the acceptance criteria for that choice, and R-160 rises to a gating risk.

### 55.7 Decision-making protocol

| Decision class | Who decides | Who must be consulted | Escalation | Recorded as |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Commercial: pricing, plans, discounts, contract terms, take rates | CEO | CTO on cost-to-serve; Finance on margin; Compliance on contract terms | Founder/Management (all three founders) where the decision changes a published price or a plan boundary | Pricing/plan version with an effective date; register row updated with the answer and the decider |
| Technical: architecture, frameworks, vendors, infrastructure, release policy | CTO | COO on field impact; Compliance on residency and retention | Founder/Management where cost exceeds the approved infrastructure budget or residency is affected | ADR in the engineering repository, referenced from the register row |
| Operational: rosters, SLAs, escalation ladders, staffing, field policy | COO | Command Center lead; Compliance on anything touching verification or deployment eligibility | Founder/Management where a safety commitment or a client SLA changes | SOP version with an effective date and a training record |
| Compliance and privacy: retention, identity data, jurisdiction rules, ethical boundaries | Compliance | CTO on feasibility; CEO on commercial impact; external adviser where named | Founder/Management, and for D-613, D-614, D-615 a **written board-level decision** that cannot be delegated | Policy document plus configuration change, both versioned; jurisdiction rules always as data (canon §0) |
| Product: rules, defaults, boundaries, plan gating presentation, UX policy | Product | The owner of any affected surface; QA where a gate threshold changes | CTO for technical conflicts; CEO for commercial conflicts | Requirement ID updated in the specification, with the register row closed against it |
| Anything with a safety consequence | The owning role **plus** a second named approver from a different function | Command Center lead always | Founder/Management always notified, never bypassed | Register row plus an entry in the safety-decision log reviewed quarterly |

**Five standing rules.**

1. **One decider per decision.** Consultation is not co-decision. If two roles both believe they own a decision, that itself escalates to Founder/Management the same week.
2. **A decision is not made until it is written down.** The register row must carry the answer, the decider, the date, and the artefact (ADR, SOP, policy, plan version). A decision communicated only verbally is still open.
3. **Deferral is a decision.** If a decision passes its "decide by" phase, the recommended default is deemed adopted, recorded with the date it lapsed, and the owner is notified. This is deliberate: an unowned default is better than an unbounded pause, and the record makes the drift visible.
4. **Reopening requires new information.** A settled decision (§55.8, or a closed row here) is reopened only by naming what changed — a measurement, a regulation, a vendor, a cost. Preference is not new information.
5. **Communication follows the artefact.** When a decision closes, the owner notifies: the affected engineering leads, whoever writes customer-facing copy about it, and the register maintainer. Decisions that change a published promise additionally require a note to Sales before the change ships.

### 55.8 Decisions already made — do not reopen

These are settled in canon §4 and elsewhere in the canon. They are recorded here so that they are not accidentally re-litigated as if they were open items. Reopening any of them requires rule 4 above.

| Area | Settled position | Source | Why it is settled |
|---|---|---|---|
| Identity model | One central identity service across all products; phone-number-first with OTP; email+password, Google and Apple also supported; phone verification mandatory | Canon §4 | India-first; a second identity system would fragment every surface |
| MFA policy | Optional for clients; enforceable for staff and agency roles | Canon §4 | Insider risk sits with privileged roles (R-301) |
| Session lengths | 30-day client sessions; shorter privileged sessions | Canon §4 | Field and client convenience against privileged-session exposure |
| Client payments | Razorpay for UPI / card / netbanking, with auto GST invoice PDFs | Canon §4 | Chosen; the *payout* rail remains open (D-142/D-211/D-243), and R-625/D-624 govern the concentration risk |
| Notification channels | Push + SMS + WhatsApp (where policy permits) + Email (Zoho) + In-app | Canon §4 | WhatsApp is an enhancement channel only (R-275) |
| Time integrity | Always store both `device_time` and `server_received_time` for field events; never trust device time alone | Canon §4, BR-446 | Attendance and safety evidence must survive a dispute |
| Deletion policy | Operational and financial records are never hard-deleted; `status=Archived` plus a retention policy. Audit logs are append-only | Canon §4 | Evidence preservation and BR-003 |
| Money representation | Integer paise, never floats; every financial movement is a double-sided ledger entry | Canon §4 | R-243 and R-270 are unmanageable otherwise |
| Offline-first scope | Mandatory for the Guard App only; every other client assumes connectivity | Canon §4 | Offline everywhere would multiply cost with no field benefit |
| Architecture stance | Modular monolith plus a separate real-time/ingest path; extract services only where load or team boundaries justify it | Canon §4 | A-566: the team cannot operate microservices |
| Design system | One system across all products; light theme base #F6F7F9; Suraksha navy/steel; operational clarity over decoration; mobile-first for field, density-first for desktop | Canon §4 | R-196 is the risk of not holding this line |
| Plan structure and prices | Starter ₹5,000, Professional ₹10,000, Enterprise "Contact Sales" with the price never displayed, and the stated feature split | Canon §1.4 | Foundation rule. D-001/D-002/D-003 decide *how* they are sold, never *what* they cost |
| B2C price anchors | Unarmed from ₹18,500/month; armed PSO from ₹38,000/month; plan cards at ₹18,000 / ₹22,000 / custom; all excl. 18% GST | Canon §1.5 | Published on the live site. A-623 tests whether they hold, but they are not open to silent change |
| AI action classes | Read-only, Recommendation, Approval-required, Automated (low-risk only); the eight prohibited actions may never be executed by AI, including indirectly | Canon §1.7, BR-442 | Non-negotiable governance boundary |
| AI language scope | Voice and text; Hindi and English plus at least 19 Indian languages where technically feasible; strictly role- and permission-aware | Canon §1.7 | Foundation rule; D-525 scopes only the safety-critical translation set, not the language commitment |
| Tenancy model | Every agency-owned row carries `tenant_id`; Suraksha's own operation is tenant `SURAKSHA-HQ`; `branch_id` is a second axis, never a substitute | Canon §3 | R-192, R-240 and R-576 all depend on this being singular and absolute |
| Product and property names | The five web properties and four mobile apps as named in canon §1.1–§1.2 | Canon §1.1–§1.2 | Renaming would invalidate every cross-reference in this document |
| Role vocabulary | The exact role names in canon §3 for Suraksha, Agency, Client and Guard sides | Canon §3 | The permission matrix (§31) and every test generated from it depend on the names |
| Status and severity vocabulary | Draft · Pending · Active · In Progress · Completed · Verified · Rejected · Expiring · Expired · Suspended · Cancelled · Failed · Archived; severities P0–P3 | Canon §3 | Cross-surface consistency; new statuses require a canon change, not a local one |
| Licence geography | PSARA licences are state- and district-scoped and are a first-class data object; operating in four states requires four state licences | Canon §1 | BR-002, BR-405 and BR-406 all derive from it |
| Legal framing | The platform never states a legal conclusion; jurisdiction rules are configurable data, never hard-coded logic | Canon §0 | R-361 is the risk of breaking this |

## 56. Requirement Traceability & Master Matrices

This section closes the loop. Everything specified in sections 1–52 and 57–60 is connected here to everything else that must exist for it to be real, and the document is then reviewed against itself.

### 56.1 The traceability model

Every capability in this platform is traceable along a single chain. A capability that breaks the chain at any link is not buildable, not testable, or not defensible.

```
Business Requirement  →  Product (surface)  →  User / Role  →  Screen  →  Workflow
        →  Business Logic (rule)  →  API  →  Database (entity)  →  Permission
        →  Security control  →  Notification  →  Analytics event  →  QA test  →  Acceptance criteria
```

**How to read the chain.** A *Business Requirement* (`SUR-<AREA>-nnn`) states what the business needs. It is delivered on one or more *Products* — the five web properties and four mobile apps of canon §1.1–§1.2 — to specific *Roles* from canon §3. Roles reach it through *Screens* (`SUR-SCR-nnn`, catalogued in §28) arranged into *Workflows* (`WKF-nn`, §29). The workflow's decisions are governed by *Business Rules* (`BR-nnn`, §30), executed through *APIs* (§33) against *Entities* (§32), gated by *Permissions* (§31, `SUR-PRM-nnn`) and *Security controls* (§38, `SUR-SEC-nnn`). State changes emit *Notifications* (§36, `SUR-NTF-nnn`) and *Analytics events* (§42, `SUR-ANL-nnn`). Each link is verified by *Test cases* (`TC-<AREA>-nnn`, §44) and closed by *Acceptance criteria* written Given/When/Then per canon §7 point 18.

**How the ID schemes connect.**

| Relationship | Rule | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|
| Requirement → Screen | Every requirement that a user performs names at least one `SUR-SCR-nnn`. Requirements that are purely backend (e.g. most `SUR-DAT`, `SUR-SCL`) name none, and must say so explicitly | §28 review; a user-facing requirement with no screen is a §56.6 finding |
| Screen → Workflow | Every screen belongs to at least one `WKF-nn` or is explicitly catalogued as a standalone utility screen | §29 cross-check |
| Workflow → Business rule | Every workflow step that can be refused, approved or escalated cites the `BR-nnn` that governs it | R-300's CI conformance gate |
| Business rule → API + Test | Every `BR-nnn` has ≥1 API enforcement point and ≥1 `TC-` referencing its ID | Build-blocking CI check (§30.13.1) |
| API → Entity → Permission | Every endpoint names the entities it touches and the `SUR-PRM-nnn` scope required; every tenant-scoped entity carries `tenant_id` | Generated from the machine-readable permission matrix (A-522) |
| Permission → Test | The permission suite is generated, not hand-written; it is release-blocking and technically unwaivable (R-520) | §43.8 generation from §31 |
| Anything sensitive → Data class | Every entity field maps to exactly one class in §56.5, which fixes its encryption, masking, retention, export and logging behaviour | Schema review; class is a required column in the data dictionary |
| Requirement → Phase | Every requirement carries a phase from §51 and appears in the feature matrix (§56.4) with the same phase | Regenerated by the D-626 CI job |

**Direction of travel.** Forward traceability answers "is this requirement actually built and tested?" Backward traceability answers "why does this endpoint exist, and who asked for it?" Both are needed: the first prevents gaps, the second prevents scope that nobody owns. The D-626 job generates both directions from the specification repository, which is the only way this stays true after two sprints.

**Three observations the index itself surfaces**, carried into §56.6 as findings:

1. **The screen-to-requirement ratio is inverted for four surfaces.** `SUR-CPT` (5), `SUR-CAP` (4), `SUR-GRD` (13) and `SUR-ADP` (15) carry very few requirements against a 503-screen inventory. Their depth lives in the module write-ups of §15–§23 rather than in numbered requirements. This is legitimate — the canon's 20-point template does not require every UI detail to become a numbered requirement — but it means those four surfaces are weakly traceable and their acceptance criteria are harder to generate. See finding F-04.
2. **`SUR-SCR` at 503 is larger than every functional area combined for several products**, which confirms the §51 concern behind D-589: screen count, not requirement count, is the real scope measure.
3. **The BR range has a deliberate gap (361–400).** BR-401–450 were raised by §29 as workflow-derived rules. The gap is reserved, not lost; it must not be silently filled by a future author without an entry here.

| Wallet | Segregated liability, daily zero-drift reconciliation | Top-up received, low balance | Float balance, top-up frequency | TC-FIN-046…055 | Wallet float reconciles daily to zero drift and is never used as working capital |
| Settlement | Beneficiary cooling period, dual authorisation | Settlement due, hold applied, paid | Settlement cycle time, hold rate | TC-FIN-056…070 | A settlement line exists only for a Completed, client-invoiced deployment period |
| Subscription | Entitlement evaluated server-side only | Trial ending, payment failed, grace, restricted | Trial→paid, churn, MRR movement | TC-TRN-001…015 | Restricted mode never removes attendance, patrol, wake check, incident or SOS |
| Entitlement | No client-side enforcement; quota checked per call | Quota 80%, quota reached, add-on purchased | Quota utilisation, add-on attach | TC-TRN-016…022 | A downgrade never deletes data; excess entities become read-only and exportable |
| Marketplace listing | Verification gate before indexing | Listing published, verification expiring | Listing views, lead conversion | TC-TRN-023…032 | An agency cannot be listed without a Verified licence covering the listed geography |
| Verification | PII-restricted access, per-record decryption audit | Document rejected, verification complete | Queue age P90, pass rate | TC-GRD-001…012 | A guard cannot reach Active until every mandatory document is Verified |
| Tender | Eligibility check, override reason recorded | Tender matched, deadline approaching, bid submitted | Match relevance, bid win rate | TC-TRN-033…040 | A bid cannot be submitted without a passed eligibility check or a recorded override |
| Recruitment | Candidate data minimisation | Interview scheduled, offer issued | Time-to-hire, offer acceptance | TC-GRD-013…020 | A candidate becomes a Guard only through the verification path |
| Documents | Class-based encryption and masking (§56.5) | Expiring 30/7/1, expired, restriction applied | Expiry backlog, restriction incidents | TC-CMP-001…015 | An Expired document applies its configured restriction automatically |
| OCR migration | Critical-field confidence floor, no bulk accept for identity/financial | Batch ready for review, commit complete, variance report | Field accuracy, manual-review rate | TC-AGN-039…050 | A batch cannot commit without reconciliation sign-off on control totals |
| Notifications | Mandatory classes bypass preferences; anti-storm quarantine | (this is the notification system) | Delivery rate by channel, acknowledgement rate | TC-NTF-001…020 | A P0 safety notification is delivered on an acknowledgement-driven failover ladder |
| AI query | Tenant-partitioned retrieval, output scanning, injection filters | (none by default) | Query volume, cost per tenant, refusal rate | TC-AI-001…015 | An AI response never contains an identifier from another tenant |
| AI approval | Human identity executes; preconditions re-validated at execution | Approval requested, approved, executed | Approval latency, rubber-stamp pattern flags | TC-AI-016…025 | An Approval-required action executes only under the approver's identity |
| Command centre alerting | Acknowledged delivery for P0/P1, independent reconciliation poll | Alert raised, escalated, handover | Alerts per operator-hour, acknowledgement latency | TC-CMD-026…035 | A silent gateway failure is detected within one reconciliation cycle |
| Compliance expiry | Dual control on rule changes, dry run before blocking consequences | Rule published, restriction pending, restriction applied | Rules unreviewed, restriction volume | TC-CMP-016…030 | A blocking rule change requires a dry run and a second approval |
| Audit | Append-only, hash-chained, immutable secondary copy | (digest to tenant monthly) | Audit volume, search latency | TC-SEC-001…015 | An audit entry can never be modified or deleted, including by a Super Admin |
| Identity | MFA enforcement by role, session limits, device binding | New device, password changed, MFA enrolled | Login success rate, MFA coverage | TC-SEC-016…035 | A privileged session cannot exceed its configured shorter lifetime |
| Permissions | Generated enforcement config; release-blocking test suite | Grant issued, grant expiring, access review due | Grants per role, dormant grants | TC-SEC-036…055 | No role can read data outside its tenant and scope, in any surface |
| Tenancy | Query predicate + RLS + composite FK; cache keys include tenant | Tenant suspended, restored | Cross-tenant test results, per-tenant resource share | TC-SEC-056…070 | The tenant-isolation suite passes with zero failures; the gate is unwaivable |
| Search | Scope injected server-side; no cross-tenant index | (none) | Search latency, zero-result rate | TC-SEC-071…078 | A search never returns a record the caller could not open directly |
| Reporting | Viewer-scoped rendering, minimum cell size, differencing checks | Scheduled report ready | Report usage, export volume | TC-ANL-001…015 | A shared report renders in the viewer's scope, never the author's |
| Support | Read-only impersonation by default, tenant-visible log | Impersonation started, ticket updated | First-response time, deflection rate | TC-OPS-001…012 | Every impersonation session is logged and visible to the tenant |
| Offboarding | Revocation within the configured window; owned approvals reassigned | Exit recorded, access revoked, settlement issued | Revocation latency, orphaned approvals | TC-AGN-051…058 | Offboarding cannot complete while any owned approval is unassigned |
| DR | Immutable out-of-account copy; key generations retained | (internal only) | RPO/RTO observed in drills | TC-DR-001…012 | A restore succeeds using only the offline package, demonstrated annually |

**Reading the boundaries.** Three patterns are deliberate and should not be "fixed" in implementation. First, **the Guard column is narrow by design** — a guard's app does one job well; every additional feature is a battery and comprehension cost (R-160, A-621). Second, **payroll approval, contract creation, rule packs and audit are desktop/web only** — BR-425 forbids payroll approval on a mobile surface, and the same reasoning extends to the other three. Third, **iOS trails Android on every field capability**, which is a consequence of D-162 and A-146, not an oversight; night-shift roles are Android-first until the entitlement is granted.

### 56.5 The data classification matrix

Eight classes. Every field in every entity maps to exactly one, and the class fixes its behaviour everywhere in the platform. A field with no class fails schema review.

**Table 1 — Class behaviour: encryption, access, masking, retention**

| Class | Encryption requirement | Access requirement | Masking rule | Retention default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Public** | TLS in transit; no at-rest requirement | Unauthenticated read permitted | None | Indefinite while published |
| **Internal** | TLS + volume encryption at rest | Authenticated, any role within the tenant | None | Life of the parent record, then archive per §39 |
| **Confidential** | TLS + at-rest encryption with a customer-managed key | Authenticated + role scope + tenant predicate | Partial in list views; full value only on the detail screen with a logged read | Life of the contract + 7 years for contract-linked records |
| **Highly Sensitive** | Field-level encryption with per-record key derivation | Named per-user grant with expiry (SUR-PRM-016); PII-restricted marker | Always masked except to a grant holder acting on a named purpose | Minimum viable; raw payloads 24 months (D-278) |
| **Financial** | Field-level encryption for instrument data; ledger rows integrity-hashed | Finance roles + four-eyes on movement; append-only ledger | Bank accounts show last 4 only; amounts never masked | 8 years, litigation hold overrides (BR-003) |
| **Identity** | Masked reference stored, not the full number (D-167); hash for matching | Verification and Compliance roles only, per-record decryption audited | Always masked to every other role, including Super Admin, without a purpose code | Outcome for the employment record's life; images 24 months |
| **Location** | Encrypted at rest; tenant-partitioned storage | Duty-scoped: only within the assigned site and duty window | Client-facing views show site-level presence, never individual position (D-248) | 90 days raw, 12–24 months downsampled (D-242, D-335) |
| **Security Operational** | Encrypted at rest; restricted key access | Command Center and named operational roles; never client-facing | Site vulnerability detail and post plans masked in exports | Life of the contract + 12 months |

**Table 2 — Class behaviour: export, logging, permitted roles**

| Class | Export permission | Logging requirement | Roles permitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Public** | Unrestricted | Access not logged | Everyone, including anonymous |
| **Internal** | Any tenant role with an export entitlement; volume counted against the export budget | Export logged with row count | All roles within the tenant and branch scope |
| **Confidential** | Export entitlement + reason; bulk export alerts at D-2/D-3 thresholds | Every read of the detail view logged; exports logged with row count and reason | Agency Owner, Agency Admin, Operations Manager, Branch Manager (scoped), Suraksha Ops roles (scoped) |
| **Highly Sensitive** | **No bulk export.** Single-record export only, with a purpose code and dual authorisation | Per-record read logged with purpose; monthly holder count published (R-303) | Verification, Compliance, and named grant holders only |
| **Financial** | Finance export entitlement; control totals attached to every batch | Every read of instrument data logged; every movement double-entry logged | Finance, Agency Finance, Payroll, Auditor (read-only) |
| **Identity** | **Never exported in raw form.** Verification outcome only | Every decryption logged with actor, purpose and record | Verification only, with expiry-bound grants |
| **Location** | Aggregated exports only; raw tracks exportable solely for a named dispute or investigation | Every raw-track access logged and visible to the guard concerned | Operations Manager, Field Officer (own scope), Command Center Operator (live only) |
| **Security Operational** | Export prohibited outside the tenant; client copies redacted | Access logged; changes require a second approver | Command Center Operator, Operations Manager, Site-scoped Supervisor |

**Table 3 — Data elements mapped to classes**

| Data element | Class | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Marketing site content, service catalogue, published pricing | Public | Must be free of fabricated claims (R-103) |
| Agency marketplace listing (public profile) | Public | Verification badge derives from Confidential source data |
| Client review text and rating | Public | Pre-publication screening per D-218 |
| Guard name and employee code | Internal | Not public; visible within the employing tenant |
| Roster and shift schedule | Internal | Aggregated views only to clients (BR-100, D-309) |
| Site name and city | Internal | Full address is Confidential |
| Guard Aadhaar / government ID reference | Identity | Masked reference + verification outcome only (D-167) |
| Guard PAN | Identity | Masked; retained for payroll linkage only |
| Guard photograph (profile) | Highly Sensitive | Used for face match; never exported in bulk |
| Guard selfie captured at check-in | Highly Sensitive | Duty-linked; retention follows attendance evidence |
| Face-match template or vendor reference | Highly Sensitive | Never stored centrally (D-337) |
| Police verification result | Identity | Outcome retained; underlying report 24 months (D-278) |
| Background verification vendor payload | Identity | Raw payload deleted at 24 months; hash retained |
| Guard bank account and IFSC | Financial | Last 4 shown; beneficiary changes have a cooling period (R-272) |
| Guard salary structure and payslip | Financial | Guard sees own; Branch Manager scoped; never client-visible |
| Payroll run and variance report | Financial | Immutable once approved; desktop-only approval |
| Guard live GPS position | Location | Duty window only; never individual position to clients |
| Guard location history / track | Location | 90 days raw, downsampled thereafter (D-335) |
| Guard device identifier and binding | Confidential | Rebind events logged; 12 months after last use (D-192) |
| Guard disciplinary record | Highly Sensitive | Never cross-tenant (D-166, D-240) |
| Guard leave and absence record | Confidential | Aggregate only to clients |
| Guard attrition-risk factors | Highly Sensitive | No composite score displayed (D-370) |
| Client site full address | Confidential | Masked in list views and in marketplace contexts |
| Site post plan and shift gaps | Security Operational | Discloses when a site is unguarded — treat as the most operationally dangerous data we hold |
| Site geofence coordinates | Security Operational | Never exported outside the tenant |
| Site access instructions / gate codes | Security Operational | Command Center continuity pack only; nightly refresh (R-575) |
| Client contact name, phone, email | Confidential | Escalation contacts additionally marked for out-of-hours use |
| Client contract and commercial terms | Confidential | Pricing visible to Finance and Sales scopes only |
| Client GSTIN and billing profile | Financial | Validated per D-121/A-140 |
| Invoice and credit note | Financial | Immutable; gapless numbering (BR-427) |
| Payment instrument token | Financial | Tokenised at the gateway; never stored raw |
| Wallet balance and ledger entries | Financial | Segregated liability; reconciled daily (D-586) |
| Settlement statement and deductions | Financial | Source reference required on every deduction line |
| Agency PSARA licence document | Confidential | Geography drives BR-406; expiry drives BR-002 |
| Agency GSTIN, PAN, incorporation documents | Financial | Verified before any money movement (R-635) |
| Agency compliance score | Confidential | Never published; affects settlement basis (D-276) |
| Incident report and evidence | Security Operational | Client receives a redacted version |
| SOS record, audio and photo evidence | Security Operational | 36 months (D-144); never rate-limited, never auto-closed |
| Wake check acknowledgement history | Confidential | Never client-visible at event level (D-309) |
| Attendance event with device metadata | Confidential | Both `device_time` and `server_received_time` retained (BR-446) |
| Audit log entries | Confidential | Append-only, hash-chained, immutable secondary copy |
| AI interaction transcript | Confidential | Tenant-partitioned; voice audio not retained in V1 (D-366) |
| Session token and refresh token | Highly Sensitive | Never logged, never exported, revoked on offboarding |
| Login history and device records | Confidential | 24 / 12 months (D-192) |
| Support ticket content and attachments | Confidential | May contain any class; attachments inherit the strictest class present |
| Impersonation session record | Confidential | Tenant-visible by right (R-142) |
| Tender document and bid content | Confidential | Bid pricing is commercially sensitive within the tenant |
| OCR staged records pending review | Inherits source | A staged record carries the class of the field it will become |
| Backup archives and restore points | Inherits source | Encrypted with retained key generations (R-577) |

### 56.6 Completeness verification report

No new screen ID required |

It is referenced as a control but has no surface | Resolved: it must be a screen, because a control an agency cannot see is not a mitigation. Add one screen to the Agency Portal settings area in §28, Phase 3 |

| D-628 | Product | Which section owns the workflow → notification mapping? Each is specified separately and no artefact holds the join, so a workflow can ship with no notification and nothing fails | §36 owns it as a matrix keyed on WKF-nn; a workflow with no notification row is a review finding |

#### 56.6.4 Honest summary of this review

The document is structurally complete: all 60 sections exist, 2,872 requirements are issued without duplication, the register IDs are disjoint and preserved, and every one of the 40 critical capabilities traces end to end from requirement to acceptance criterion.

Three weaknesses are real and should not be papered over. **First, traceability depth is uneven.** Four surfaces are specified in prose rather than in numbered requirements, which makes their acceptance criteria harder to generate and their coverage harder to assert (F-04, D-627). **Second, the register is larger than the team.** 137 risks, 119 assumptions and 189 decisions is an honest inventory of a ten-surface platform, but a five-to-eight person team at MVP (A-566) cannot service all of it; the value of §53.12, §54.8 and §55.6 is precisely that they name the small subsets that must be worked, and everything else is scheduled, not urgent. **Third, several decisions were asked more than once by different section authors** (F-27 to F-33), which is the predictable consequence of parallel authoring. None of the duplicates conflict in substance, but four of them carry different recommended defaults, and those must be reconciled in a single sitting per owner rather than answered independently.

The most consequential single gap this review found is **F-05**: there is no workflow between contract signature and first shift covered. That is the exact handover where a client's expectation is set, a site is surveyed, escalation contacts are captured and the first night is either boring or a founding disaster (R-604). It is the cheapest workflow in this document to write and the most expensive one to leave missing.


## 57. Final Technical Architecture

### 57.0 What this section is, and what it is not

This is the consolidation. Sections 32 (data), 33 (API), 34 (real-time), 35 (financial), 36 (notifications), 37 (integrations), 38 (security), 39 (privacy), 41 (AI governance), 42 (analytics) and 46–50 (NFR, DevOps, observability, DR, scalability) each decided their own domain in detail. This section does three things those sections cannot do individually:

1. It draws the **whole** system in one picture and names every deployable unit in it.
2. It makes and defends the **technology selections** that were deliberately left open earlier, using the seven lenses the brief demands — Why · Alternatives · Trade-offs · Cost · Scaling · Vendor lock-in · Security impact.
3. It states the **cross-cutting mechanisms** that must be built exactly once and reused everywhere, and traces one request end to end to prove they compose.

It does **not** re-specify entities (§32), endpoints (§33), transports (§34), controls (§38) or metrics (§42). Where a decision was already settled there, it is referenced, not repeated. Where this section reaches a different or more specific conclusion than an earlier section, that is called out explicitly and raised as a decision item.

**Standing architectural constraint (canon §4):** modular monolith plus a separate real-time/ingest path. Every recommendation below is chosen to be *good inside a monolith and not a barrier to later extraction*. Any technology whose main benefit only appears in a microservice topology is rejected on those grounds alone.

---

```
                │
┌───────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  L10 EXTERNAL INTEGRATIONS (§37)                                             │
│  Payments (Razorpay) · Payout rail [D-243] · SMS/DLT aggregators ×2 ·        │
│  WhatsApp BSP · Email (Zoho) · Push (FCM/APNs) · Maps & geocoding ·          │
│  OCR/document AI · LLM/ASR providers · Accounting export · Biometric         │
│  devices (Enterprise) · Government portals — manual/assisted only, no        │
│  invented APIs (canon §0)                                                    │
└───────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                │
┌───────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  L11 OBSERVABILITY & SECURITY  (wrap every layer above, not below them)      │
│  Logs (structured, request-ID, tenant-ID, PII-scrubbed) · Metrics (RED +     │
│  business) · Traces · Alerts & synthetic probes incl. the SOS probe ·        │
│  Error tracking · Audit trail · Secrets manager · KMS/envelope encryption ·  │
│  Vulnerability & dependency scanning · Access review · Backup/restore/DR     │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

#### 57.1.2 What actually lives in each layer

| Layer | Concretely contains | Owns which decisions | Fails how |
|---|---|---|---|
| L0 Actors | 4 audience families with wildly different devices: a ₹6,000 Android phone in a guard's pocket, a 24-inch operator console, a facility manager's laptop, an agency owner's desktop app | None — but it sets every constraint that matters (bandwidth, literacy, battery, screen density) | Not applicable |
| L1 Presentation | 5 web properties, 4 mobile apps, 1 desktop app, one design system, one i18n catalogue, one analytics SDK | Rendering, offline behaviour (Guard App only), local state, accessibility | Degrades: cached shell + last-known data + queued writes |
| L2 Edge | CDN, WAF, DDoS protection, TLS termination, bot rules, static asset and map-tile caching | Coarse rate limiting, geo rules, request ID | Fails open for static, closed for `/api` |
| L3 Gateway/BFF | Route table, token validation, tenant resolution, idempotency, per-tenant + per-principal limits, OpenAPI contract enforcement | The public shape of the system (§33) | 429/503 with `Retry-After`; never a silent partial write |
| L4 Identity & Access | One identity service, one permission evaluator, one scope resolver, one audit hook | Who you are, which tenant, which branch/site, what you may do (§31) | Hard fail — no fallback path bypasses it, ever |
| L5 Core business | The commercial and contractual system of record: agencies, clients, sites, posts, contracts, money | Business rules (§30), lifecycle statuses (canon §3) | Fails to a read-only or queued state; financial writes never partially apply |
| L6 Operational | The field-time system: what happened at a post tonight, and who was told | Alerting, escalation, SLA measurement, geofence truth | SOS path is the last thing to degrade; everything else sheds load first |
| L7 AI | Orchestrator, prompt/context assembly, model adapters, action-class gate, interaction log | Nothing authoritative — AI proposes, the core modules decide (§41) | Fails invisible: the product must remain fully usable with AI off |
| L8 Data | One Postgres cluster as truth, PostGIS, partitioned time-series, one replica | Consistency, integrity, retention | Primary loss = declared incident; replica loss = reports degrade only |
| L9 Cache/Queue/Search/Storage | Redis, Postgres FTS, object storage | Throughput and latency, not truth | Cache loss = slow, not wrong. Stream loss = pings lost (acceptable), never check-ins |
| L10 Integrations | Every third party, each behind an adapter with a documented degraded mode (§37) | Nothing authoritative; all are replaceable | Each has a named fallback; none may block a life-safety path |
| L11 Observability & Security | Telemetry, secrets, keys, scanning, audit, backup | Detection and evidence | If observability is down, the system is *assumed* impaired until proven otherwise |

**The one rule that makes this diagram real:** a layer may call the layer directly below it and the cross-cutting layer (L11). It may not reach two layers down. The single deliberate exception is the signal ingest path, which goes L1 → L3 → L9 (stream) → L6 consumer → L8, bypassing L5 entirely — because a GPS ping must never contend for the same resources as an invoice run (§34.3).

### 57.2 Component inventory

**Criticality tiers** (used throughout §58 and §59):

| Tier | Meaning | Availability intent | On-call response |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T0** | Life-safety. Failure can leave a person in danger without help. SOS raise → operator screen → escalation → outbound contact. | Highest; degraded modes are designed, not improvised | Immediate page, 24×7 |
| **T1** | Operations- and revenue-critical. Failure stops guards working, clients seeing service, or money moving. | High | Page within business-critical hours, escalate out of hours |
| **T2** | Important. Failure degrades work but has a manual workaround for a day. | Standard | Ticket, next business day |
| **T3** | Deferrable. Failure is visible only to internal users or delays non-urgent output. | Best effort | Backlog |

#### 57.2.1 Runtime components

| # | Component | Responsibility | Depends on | Data stores | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C-01 | `edge` (CDN + WAF) | TLS, static/tile cache, coarse rate limits, DDoS, request-ID | DNS, cert automation | None | T1 |
| C-02 | `api` (modular monolith) | All L3–L5 concerns: product API, business modules, admin, enterprise API | Postgres, Redis, object storage, identity module (in-process), providers | Postgres primary + replica, Redis, object storage | T1 |
| C-03 | `rt-gateway` | WebSocket termination, subscription authorisation, fan-out to consoles (§34.2) | Redis Pub/Sub, identity token validation | Redis only (stateless otherwise) | T0 (SOS console path) |
| C-04 | `ingest` | `/ingest` endpoint + validation + dedupe + stream publish (§34.3) | Redis Streams | Redis; no direct OLTP writes | T1 |
| C-05 | `signals-consumer` | Consume pings, geofence + hysteresis evaluation, emit domain events, write location partitions | Redis Streams, Postgres, in-memory fence cache | Postgres (location), Redis | T1 |
| C-06 | `worker-critical` | Escalation timers, SOS follow-ups, wake-check misses, replacement clocks. Never shares a queue with reports. | Redis, Postgres, notification providers | Postgres, Redis | **T0** |
| C-07 | `worker-default` | Outbox drain, notifications dispatch, webhooks, document processing, sync jobs | Redis, Postgres, providers, object storage | Postgres, Redis, object storage | T1 |
| C-08 | `worker-heavy` | Payroll runs, invoice batches, report/PDF rendering, OCR migration, exports, analytics rollups | Redis, Postgres replica, object storage, OCR provider | Postgres replica (read), primary (write results), object storage | T2 |
| C-09 | `scheduler` | Leader-elected cron: expiry sweeps, nightly rollups, retention jobs, reconciliation, freshness checks | Redis lock, Postgres | Postgres (`job_run`) | T1 |
| C-10 | `ai-orchestrator` | Intent → permission pre-check → scoped context → model → action-class gate → log (§25/§41) | Identity/permissions, Postgres, LLM/ASR providers | Postgres (`ai_interaction`), Redis | T2 |
| C-11 | `media-processor` | Image compression, EXIF strip, virus scan, thumbnailing, face-template extraction, OCR submission | Object storage, OCR provider | Object storage, Postgres metadata | T2 |
| C-12 | `web-suraksha` | Marketing site + customer portal (surakshaguards.in) | `api`, CDN | None (SSR cache) | T1 (portal), T2 (marketing) |
| C-13 | `web-ops` | OPS console incl. Command Center surfaces (ops.) | `api`, `rt-gateway` | None | **T0** |
| C-14 | `web-ap` | Agency Portal SaaS (ap.) | `api`, `rt-gateway` | None | T1 |
| C-15 | `web-trinetra` | Marketplace, SaaS site, desktop downloads (trinetra.) | `api`, object storage | None | T2 |
| C-16 | `web-guards` | Guard self-service web (guards.) | `api` | None | T2 |
| C-17 | `app-guard` (Android) | The field tool: duty, attendance, patrol, wake check, SOS, offline queue | `api`, `/ingest`, FCM, device GPS/camera | On-device encrypted SQLite | **T0** |
| C-18 | `app-customer` | Booking + client portal in hand | `api`, FCM/APNs | Local cache | T2 |
| C-19 | `app-agency` | Agency Portal companion | `api`, FCM/APNs | Local cache | T2 |
| C-20 | `app-admin` | OPS in app format for authorised staff | `api`, FCM/APNs, `rt-gateway` | Local cache | T1 |

| C-22 | `postgres-primary` | Single source of truth, PostGIS, partitions, RLS, outbox | Storage, backup target | — | T1 |
| C-23 | `postgres-replica` | Reporting/analytics reads, restore-target rehearsal | `postgres-primary` | — | T2 |
| C-24 | `redis` | Cache, rate limits, deny-list, locks, Streams, Pub/Sub | — | — | T1 |
| C-25 | `object-storage` | Documents, media, invoices, exports, installers | KMS | — | T1 |
| C-26 | `observability` | Logs, metrics, traces, alerts, synthetic probes, error tracking | All components | Its own retention store | T1 |
