### 58.19 The rollback plan

A launch is not a one-way door, and pretending otherwise is how teams push through a failing launch. Rollback here means three different things at three different layers, and each needs its own pre-agreed trigger.

#### 58.19.1 The three rollback layers

| Layer | What "rollback" means | Reversible? | Time to execute | Pre-agreed trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Software release** | Revert to the previous release per §47.12; feature-flag off the offending capability | Yes, minutes | ≤15 min for flags; ≤45 min for a full revert | Any P0 defect; SLO burn beyond the launch-week budget; a data-integrity suspicion |
| **Operational mode** | Platform stays up; the field reverts to the documented manual fallback (paper attendance register, phone-based wake checks, direct-dial SOS) while software is fixed | Yes, hours | ≤30 min to declare and communicate | Two consecutive failures of any safety-critical path (SOS, wake check, attendance) |
| **Launch itself** | Stop deploying under the platform: return the launch client to a manually-operated service, or, in the extreme, withdraw the deployment | Partially — reputationally costly | 24–72 hours | A safety incident attributable to the platform; a compliance finding; a confirmed data breach; discovery that a §58.8 item was not actually remediated |

#### 58.19.2 What cannot be rolled back, and how it is protected

| Irreversible thing | Protection before launch |
|---|---|
| Money already moved (payments, payouts) | BR-003: never silently modified. Reversal is a new compensating entry, never an edit. Verified at LR-073. |
| Notifications already sent to guards and clients | Send-throttles on launch day; critical templates reviewed by two people; a "stop all non-critical sends" kill switch tested at LR-088. |
| Data already disclosed to a wrong party | Prevented, not remediated — hence the isolation suite (§58.3) is `HARD` with no waiver. |
| App builds already installed on guards' phones | Staged rollout at 10% for 48 hours; forced-update mechanism verified at LR-092 so a bad build can be superseded quickly. |
| A guard deployed under an invalid compliance state | Deployment gating (LR-057) blocks it at source. |
| Public claims already published | The claim register (§58.8.3) and the CI content check. |

#### 58.19.3 Rollback authority

`[DECISION REQUIRED: D-619]` — who may call a rollback at each layer, and whether that authority can be exercised without consensus. **Recommended default:** software rollback may be called unilaterally by the on-call engineer or the CTO, with no approval required and no blame attached; operational-mode rollback by the Command Center lead or COO; launch rollback only by Founder/Management, but **any** of the three founders may call it alone. The principle is that reverting must always be cheaper and less career-risky than pressing on.

---

### 58.20 The GO / NO-GO protocol

#### 58.20.1 The meeting

| Property | Specification |
|---|---|
| When | T-3 days from the intended go-live, with a short T-1 confirmation call for anything that was open at T-3. Never on the go-live day itself — a decision made under time pressure is not a decision. |
| Who decides | The three founders — CEO, CTO, COO — jointly. **Unanimity required for GO.** Any one of them may declare NO-GO alone. |
| Who attends | Founders (deciding), plus the domain owners for Compliance, Finance, Command Center, Support and Verification (presenting), plus the Auditor role (challenging). |
| Inputs | The completed §58 checklist with evidence links, the open-waiver log, the pentest retest letter, counsel's review letters, the last 7 days of synthetic-probe history, the rollback plan, and the launch-day comms plan. |
| Output | A signed decision record: GO / GO-WITH-WAIVERS / NO-GO, listing every waiver with owner and close-by date, and the named person who will run the launch day. |
| If NO-GO | The blocking items are re-scoped with dates, and a new go/no-go date is set. A NO-GO is never re-decided informally over a call; it goes back through the same meeting. |

#### 58.20.2 The evidence standard

GO requires, without exception:

1. **Every `HARD` row verified**, by the named verifier, with dated evidence attached.
2. **Every `SOFT` waiver** has a named owner and a close-by date within 30 days of launch.
3. **No open Critical or High** security finding, and no open Critical defect from §44.
4. **Seven consecutive days of green** on the synthetic SOS probe (LR-128).
5. **A rehearsed rollback** — not a documented one; someone has actually executed the software rollback in staging within the last 14 days.

#### 58.20.3 The hard blockers — the veto list

These veto launch regardless of commercial pressure, contractual deadlines, investor timelines or a client's own launch date. They are listed separately so that nobody has to argue the case in the room; the case was made here, in advance, in writing.

| # | Hard blocker | Why it vetoes |
|---|---|---|
| HB-1 | **Any unremediated item in §58.8 (P1–P7 fabricated content)** | We would be selling trust while publishing untruths. There is no version of this business that survives that being discovered by a client, a regulator, an acquirer or a journalist. |
| HB-2 | **SOS path not proven end to end on the real device matrix under adverse conditions** (LR-015, LR-016, LR-128) | A guard who presses SOS and gets nothing is the failure mode that ends the company and, more importantly, harms a person. |
| HB-3 | **Tenant-isolation or permission suite not fully green** (LR-024–LR-028) | A cross-tenant leak in a business holding guard identity documents and client site security details is unrecoverable. |
| HB-4 | **Any guard deployable without a complete verification chain**, or deployment gating not enforced (LR-056, LR-057) | This is the licensed-operator obligation and the single failure mode that ends the licence. |
| HB-5 | **Backups not restore-tested** (LR-037) | Untested backups are not backups. |
| HB-6 | **Legal pages or privacy policy not counsel-reviewed and published** (LR-048, LR-060) | Collecting biometric and location data from a low-wage workforce without a lawful, published basis is not a paperwork gap. |
| HB-7 | **No 24/7 answered escalation number, or Command Center rota with an unmanned minute** (LR-105, LR-107, LR-069) | The product is a promise of response. Without a human on the other end, the software is decoration. |
| HB-8 | **Critical open security findings, or secrets not rotated** (LR-033, LR-034) | Launching with a known exploitable path is a decision to be breached at a time of the attacker's choosing. |
| HB-9 | **GST invoicing or payout rail unverified** (LR-072, LR-075) | Taking money without a compliant invoice, or promising wages we cannot actually disburse, creates obligations we cannot honour. |
| HB-10 | **Payroll/attendance evidence chain unverifiable** (LR-076, LR-013) | If we cannot prove who worked when, we can neither bill honestly nor pay honestly. |

#### 58.20.4 What is explicitly *not* a reason to launch

Stated plainly, because these are the arguments that will actually be made in the room: a client has already signed; the guards have already been recruited; the investor update is next week; the competitor is launching; the team has worked very hard; "we'll fix it in week two"; "nobody will look at that page"; "it's only for the demo". None of these move a `HARD` row. The purpose of writing the veto list before the pressure exists is so that the room is arguing against a document rather than against a colleague.

---

## 59. Post-Launch Operations

### 59.0 What changes the day a real client depends on this

Before launch, the system's failure mode is embarrassment. After launch, its failure modes are a guard alone at a gate with no way to call for help, a client site left unguarded, a wage paid late to someone who cannot absorb a late wage, and a compliance record that cannot be produced when asked. Every practice in this section exists to convert those risks into routine.

Three principles govern everything below.

| Principle | Consequence |
|---|---|
| **The operating rhythm is the product's immune system.** | If a meeting has no decision output and no owner, delete it. Every cadence below states what it decides. |
| **Every recurring judgement becomes a runbook.** | The second time a human makes the same call, it is written down. The third time, it is measured. The fourth time, it is a candidate for automation with an approval gate (§25 action classes). |
| **The workforce is an operational system, not an HR afterthought.** | Guard attrition, grievance response and payment timeliness are operated with the same rigour as uptime, because they are the supply side of the product. |

Process identifiers below are `OPR-nn`. These are process labels, not canon §2 requirement IDs.

---

### 59.1 The operating rhythm

| Cadence | Forum | Time-box | Attendees | Inputs | Decides |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Daily 09:15** | Ops standup | 15 min | National Operations (chair), City Operations, Command Center lead, Support lead, on-call engineer | Overnight alert digest, unfilled posts today, open P0/P1 incidents, SOS log, guards with expiring documents in 7 days, payment failures | Who owns each open item today; what escalates to founders |
| **Daily 09:30** | Alert review (engineering) | 15 min | CTO or delegate, on-call engineer, previous on-call | Alerts fired in 24h, noise ratio, SLO burn, synthetic probe history, error-tracking new-issue list | Which alerts are retuned or deleted; which defects are hot-fixed today |
| **Weekly Mon 11:00** | Quality & incident review | 60 min | CTO, National Operations, Command Center lead, Support lead, Compliance, QA owner | All incidents (production and field) from the week, post-mortem actions overdue, defect trend, client complaints, guard grievances, waiver log from §58 | Post-mortem action owners and dates; whether any waiver has aged out; what gets escalated to the roadmap |
| **Weekly Wed 16:00** | Leadership metrics | 45 min | Founders, National Operations, Finance, Sales | The weekly leadership metric set — see §59.15 | Interventions for any metric outside its band |
| **Weekly Fri 15:00** | Verification & compliance queue | 30 min | Compliance (chair), Verification, HR, Recruitment | Verification queue depth and age, expiry sweep results, exception backlog, licence status | Staffing shifts, exception approvals, escalations |
| **Monthly, working day 3** | Financial close | Half day | Finance (chair), Founders, Auditor role | Ledger close, reconciliation breaks, receivables ageing, payroll variance, unit economics vs §52 model | Sign-off of the close; write-offs; pricing escalations |
| **Monthly, working day 5** | Compliance review | 90 min | Compliance (chair), Founders, National Operations, external counsel as needed | Licence register, jurisdiction rule changes, guard compliance coverage %, filings due, DSR log, audit-readiness gaps | Rule-configuration changes; remediation owners |
| **Monthly, week 3** | Customer & workforce health | 60 min | COO (chair), CSM owner, HR, Support | Tenant health scores, activation milestones, churn risk list, guard attrition, grievance ageing, payment-timeliness SLA | Intervention list for named accounts and named sites |
| **Quarterly** | Security review | Half day | CTO (chair), Founders, Compliance, external tester as scheduled | Access review, pentest/retest status, vulnerability ageing, incident themes, key rotation, vendor register, DR test results | Security backlog priorities; whether a new pentest is triggered |
| **Quarterly** | Architecture & capacity review | Half day | CTO, engineering | Growth against §50.2 volumetrics, the §57.8 trigger table, cost per unit, top bottlenecks | Which §57.8 evolution triggers have been hit |
| **Quarterly** | Roadmap re-plan | Half day | Founders, CTO, Sales, National Operations | Feedback-to-roadmap intake (§59.11), §51 phase status, competitive input | Next quarter's committed scope |

**The rule that keeps this honest:** every cadence above produces a written output in the same place, and the weekly leadership meeting opens by reading the overdue-actions list from every other forum. An operating rhythm without an overdue-action feedback loop degrades into status theatre within two months.

---

### 59.2 Support model

#### 59.2.1 Tiering

| Tier | Who | Handles | Target first response | Escalates when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **L0 — self-serve** | Help centre, in-app guidance, AI assistant in read-only class (§25) | "How do I…", status lookups, document re-upload, invoice download | Instant | User asks twice, or the AI's confidence gate refuses |
| **L1 — Support** | Support role, business hours + launch-period extended cover | Account, booking, billing queries, guard app setup, attendance disputes, complaint intake | Per §59.2.2 | Requires data change beyond L1 permissions, or is a suspected defect |
| **L2 — Operations** | City/State/National Operations, Command Center Operator for live events | Anything touching a live deployment: replacements, coverage, escalations, site issues, incident follow-up | 15 min for live-shift issues | Requires a code change, or a platform behaviour cannot be explained |
| **L3 — Engineering** | On-call engineer, then the owning engineer | Defects, data corrections, integration failures, performance problems | Per severity (§59.4) | Requires a decision on scope, cost or customer commitment |
| **L4 — Founders** | Founder/Management | Commercial concessions, contractual disputes, reputational events, anything with legal exposure | Same business day | — |

#### 59.2.2 Response and resolution targets

`[DECISION REQUIRED: D-604]` — the exact committed targets per plan, and whether Starter-plan agency tenants receive any contractual response commitment at all. Recommended defaults, to be confirmed before any SLA is signed:

| Severity | Definition | First response | Update cadence | Resolution target | Applies to |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **S1** | Safety path affected (SOS, wake check), or a site is unguarded, or the platform is down for a tenant | 15 min, 24×7 | Every 30 min | 4 h workaround | All plans, all clients, all guards |
| **S2** | A core workflow blocked for a tenant (attendance, payroll run, invoicing) with no workaround | 1 h business hours, 2 h out of hours | Every 2 h | 1 business day | All paid plans |
| **S3** | Degraded or inconvenient; workaround exists | 1 business day | Daily | 5 business days | All plans |
| **S4** | Question, cosmetic, enhancement request | 2 business days | On change | Best effort / roadmap intake | All plans |

**Non-negotiable:** S1 targets do not vary by plan or by whether the requester pays. A guard on the Starter tenant of a small agency gets the same S1 response as an Enterprise client, because the thing at risk is the same.

#### 59.2.3 Guard-side support

Guards will not raise tickets in English through a web form. The channel must be: in-app, in their language, one tap from the home screen, with voice input (§25), and with a callback option. Guard tickets are routed to a queue staffed by people who speak the guard's language and are measured on *resolution*, not on handle time. Grievances are a separate, protected path — see §59.7.3.

---

### 59.3 On-call

Reference §47.16 for the runbook model; this is the human layer.

| Aspect | Specification |
|---|---|
| Rota shape | Primary + secondary, weekly rotation, published a month ahead. At launch scale the pool is small — `[ASSUMPTION: A-605]` the founding engineering team can sustain a 1-in-2 rota for no more than the first 90 days before a third engineer must join the rota. |
| Coverage | 24×7 for P0/P1 alerts. Anything below P1 waits for business hours by policy (§48.14), and paging for a P2 is treated as an alert-tuning defect. |
| Acknowledgement | 5 minutes for a P0 page; auto-escalate to secondary at 5 min, to CTO at 10 min, to Founder/Management at 20 min. |
| Handover | Written handover at rotation change: open incidents, deferred items, anything fragile, any manual state in the system. A verbal-only handover is not accepted. |
| Compensation and load | `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-605]` — on-call allowance, time-off-in-lieu after a disturbed night, and the point at which founders stop being the escalation path of last resort. The pattern to avoid is the one where the CTO is permanently on-call and quietly becomes the single point of failure for the whole company. |
| Sustainability metric | Pages per on-call week, and nights disturbed per rotation. If pages/week exceeds 3 for two consecutive rotations, alert tuning becomes the top engineering priority — ahead of features. This is a rule, not a preference. |
| Access | On-call has a documented, audited break-glass path to production data (§38), time-boxed and reviewed at the quarterly security review. |

---

### 59.4 Production incident management

#### 59.4.1 Severity, using the canon alert vocabulary

| Severity | Field meaning | Examples | Comms | Post-mortem |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P0 Critical** | Life-safety or total loss of service | SOS not delivering; Command Center blind; platform down; suspected data breach; guard location pipeline dead | Immediate internal page; client notification within 30 min; founder informed immediately | Mandatory, published internally within 5 business days |
| **P1 High** | Core function broken for many, or one tenant fully blocked | Attendance not recording at multiple sites; payments failing; notification provider outage; payroll run failure | Internal within 15 min; affected clients within 2 h | Mandatory within 10 business days |
| **P2 Medium** | Degraded, workaround exists | Slow dashboards; delayed reports; one integration failing; elevated error rate | Internal only unless a client noticed | At the weekly review; written only if it recurs |
| **P3 Informational** | Noise, single-user issue, cosmetic | One user's export failed | Ticket only | None |

#### 59.4.2 Roles during an incident

| Role | Held by | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Incident Commander | On-call engineer initially; CTO or a trained IC for P0 | Owns the incident; makes calls; is *not* the person debugging |
| Ops Lead | Command Center lead or National Operations | Owns the field: manual fallbacks, guard and client safety, physical response |
| Comms Lead | Support lead; Founder/Management for P0 external comms | Owns what clients, guards and staff are told and when |
| Scribe | Anyone available | Timestamped log of what was observed, decided and done — this is the post-mortem's raw material and cannot be reconstructed later |

**The field-first rule.** For any incident that touches a guard's safety or a site's coverage, the Ops Lead's manual fallback (§49.12) is invoked *in parallel* with the technical fix, never after it. Nobody waits for a deploy to protect a site.

#### 59.4.3 Post-mortems

Blameless, written, and specific. Required sections: timeline with timestamps; customer and field impact quantified; root cause; why it was not caught earlier (test gap, monitoring gap, or design gap); what would have made detection faster; action items with owners and dates. Two standing rules: **no action item without a named individual and a date**, and **actions from post-mortems outrank feature work** in the next sprint unless a founder explicitly overrides in writing. Post-mortem action ageing is reported at the weekly quality review.

---

### 59.5 Change management with live clients

Before launch, changes are cheap. After launch, every change lands on a guard's phone at 22:00 and on a client's dashboard during their audit.

| Change class | Examples | Approval | Notice to customers | Window |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Standard** | Bug fix, copy change, non-visual refactor, flag-off feature merge | Peer review + CI green | None | Any business hour |
| **Normal** | New feature behind a flag, schema addition, new notification template, UI change | CTO or delegate; product sign-off | Release notes in-app | Business hours, Tue–Thu |
| **Customer-visible** | Workflow change, screen redesign, permission change, pricing/plan change, changed notification content | Founder/Management + Support briefed | ≥7 days' notice; ≥30 days for anything contractual or price-affecting | Scheduled |
| **High-risk** | Destructive migration, ledger-touching change, identity/permission-model change, payout logic, geofence evaluation logic | CTO + Founder/Management; rollback plan reviewed; restore point verified | Maintenance notice where downtime is possible | Low-traffic window; never Friday; never month-end for finance paths |
| **Emergency** | Fix for an active P0/P1 | Incident Commander alone | Post-hoc | Immediate |

**Freeze windows.** No non-emergency deploys during: month-end financial close (working days 1–3), payroll disbursement day, any client's declared high-risk event (a festival deployment, a VIP visit, an audit), and the 24 hours before a scheduled DR test. Freezes are published in the engineering calendar and enforced by the release pipeline, not by memory.

**Deprecation policy.** Nothing a customer depends on is removed without: 90 days' notice for API and integration behaviour, 30 days for UI workflows, a documented migration path, and usage telemetry proving who is actually affected. Silent removal is treated as a P2 incident.

---

### 59.6 Customer success for agency tenants

The SaaS side (canon §1.4) lives or dies on whether an agency actually *switches its operations* to the Agency Portal. An agency that logs in twice a month is already churned; it just has not told us yet.

#### 59.6.1 Onboarding and activation milestones

| # | Milestone | Target from signup | Why it is the milestone | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | Account created, owner MFA enabled, branding set | Day 0 | Baseline | Sales → CSM |
| M2 | ≥10 guards imported with documents attached | Day 3 | Data is the switching cost; without it nothing else works | CSM |
| M3 | ≥1 client and ≥1 site with a real geofence and ≥1 post configured | Day 5 | The operational skeleton | CSM |
| M4 | First roster published for a real week | Day 7 | The moment the portal starts describing reality | CSM |
| M5 | **≥80% of that week's shifts have platform attendance** | Day 14 | *The activation event.* Everything before this is setup; this is adoption | CSM + Ops |
| M6 | First payroll run computed in-platform and reconciled | Day 30 | The financial switching cost — after this, leaving is expensive | CSM + Finance |
| M7 | First invoice raised to their client from the platform | Day 45 | Their revenue now flows through us | CSM |
| M8 | A second user role in daily use (supervisor or branch manager) | Day 60 | Single-user tenants churn; multi-user tenants stick | CSM |

An agency that has not reached M5 by day 21 is flagged red regardless of what it says in a call. `[ASSUMPTION: A-606]` — that M5 by day 14 is achievable for a typical 30–80 guard agency; validate on the first ten tenants and re-baseline.

#### 59.6.2 Health scoring

| Signal | Weight | Direction | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Attendance events per active guard per week | 30% | Higher better | The truest usage signal; it cannot be faked by logging in |
| Weekly active users ÷ licensed users | 20% | Higher better | Adoption breadth beyond the owner |
| Roster published ahead of the week | 15% | Higher better | Shows the portal is the planning system, not a record-keeper |
| Payroll/invoice run in-platform last cycle | 15% | Binary | The financial switching cost |
| Support tickets per 100 guards, and their sentiment | 10% | Lower better | Friction and frustration |
| Payment/subscription health (on-time, no failed charges) | 10% | Higher better | Commercial intent |

`[DECISION REQUIRED: D-608]` — final weights and the red/amber/green thresholds. Recommended: Green ≥70, Amber 40–69, Red <40, with any tenant that misses M5 or has a failed payment forced to Red regardless of score.

#### 59.6.3 Churn intervention playbook

| Trigger | Intervention | Owner | Escalation if unresolved in 14 days |
|---|---|---|---|
| Health drops two bands in a month | Diagnostic call within 3 days; identify the blocking workflow | CSM | COO |
| M5 missed by day 21 | On-site or screen-share working session; import their data *for* them | CSM + Ops | COO |
| Champion leaves the agency | Re-onboard the successor within 7 days; treat as a new activation | CSM | Sales |
| Failed payment or downgrade request | Commercial conversation before dunning escalates; understand the reason before defending the price | Finance + CSM | Founder/Management |
| Repeated S2 tickets on one workflow | Engineering review of that workflow; the tenant becomes a design partner for the fix | CTO | Founder/Management |
| Explicit cancellation | Exit interview, recorded and coded into the churn-reason taxonomy; full data export offered without friction | Founder/Management | — |

**Exit data policy.** A churning tenant's data export is provided quickly and completely. Holding data hostage is both wrong and, in a market of ~35,000 agencies that talk to each other (A-001), commercially suicidal.

---

### 59.7 Guard workforce operations

This is the part of operations that a software-centred team most reliably under-resources, and it is the part that determines whether the product exists at all.

#### 59.7.1 Recruitment pipeline health

| Metric | Definition | Review cadence | Intervention threshold |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pipeline coverage | Verified bench guards ÷ open positions next 30 days | Weekly | <1.5× |
| Time-to-verified | Application → deployable status, median and P90 | Weekly | P90 > 10 days |
| Verification pass rate | Approved ÷ decided, by source channel | Monthly | A channel below 50% is paused and reviewed |
| Source mix | Share by channel (referral, walk-in, agency partner, digital) | Monthly | Any single channel >60% is a concentration risk |
| Cost per verified guard | Fully loaded acquisition cost | Monthly | Above the §52 model assumption |
| Offer-to-join drop-off | Joined ÷ offered | Monthly | <70% triggers a wage/expectation review |

#### 59.7.2 Attrition monitoring

Attrition is measured at 7, 30 and 90 days separately, because the causes differ: 7-day attrition is an onboarding and expectation-setting failure; 30-day is a site-fit or supervisor failure; 90-day is a wage, workload or career failure. Every exit is coded to a reason from a fixed taxonomy, and reasons are reported by **site and by supervisor**, not only in aggregate — attrition concentrates around specific posts and specific people, and an aggregate number hides exactly the thing you need to act on. `[ASSUMPTION: A-607]` — a baseline attrition assumption is required for the §52 model; it must be set from the first two quarters of real data, not borrowed from industry commentary.

#### 59.7.3 Grievance handling

| Property | Specification |
|---|---|
| Channel | In-app, in-language, one tap, with voice input and a callback option; plus a phone number that reaches a person, not an IVR tree |
| Protected categories | Wage disputes, safety at post, harassment, supervisor conduct, document retention, forced overtime |
| Confidentiality | A grievance about a supervisor is never routed to that supervisor. Routing rules enforce this in the tool, not by convention |
| Acknowledgement | Within 24 hours, in the guard's language |
| Resolution target | 7 days for wage and safety; 14 days for others; every breach reported at the monthly workforce review |
| Escalation | Unresolved grievances escalate to HR then COO automatically on the clock, without the guard needing to chase |
| Reporting | Volume, category, ageing and outcome reported monthly to Founder/Management; a rising trend in one category is treated as an operational defect |

#### 59.7.4 Payment timeliness as a retention lever

For a workforce at this wage level, a wage that arrives three days late is not an inconvenience; it is a missed rent payment. Payment timeliness is therefore operated as a hard SLA with the same seriousness as uptime.

| Metric | Target | Escalation |
|---|---|---|
| % of guards paid on or before the committed date | ≥99.5% | Any miss is a P1 operational incident with a named owner |
| Median delay for the misses | 0 days | >1 day triggers a founder-level review |
| Payout failure rate (bank rejections) | <1% | Weekly review of the failure reasons; bank-detail capture is fixed upstream |
| Payslip availability | Same day as payment, in-app, in-language | Weekly check |
| Wage-query resolution | <48 hours | Grievance path if breached |

`[DECISION REQUIRED: D-607]` — the committed payment date (T+n from cycle close) and whether a late payment carries an internal penalty or a goodwill payment to the guard. Recommended: commit to a date that is comfortably achievable, publish it to guards, and treat missing it as an incident. A conservatively-set, always-met date beats an aggressive, sometimes-met one.

---

### 59.8 Agency-partner management

Distinct from §59.6: this is about agencies as **supply** in the marketplace (§19 Trinetra), not as SaaS tenants — though many are both.

| Process | Specification |
|---|---|
| Onboarding | Licence verification (geography and expiry as first-class data), document set, capability declaration (services, cities, headcount), commercial terms, and a small first assignment before any large one |
| Performance scorecard | Fill rate against requests; time-to-fill; guard compliance coverage %; attendance quality at their deployed posts; incident rate; client complaint rate; settlement disputes |
| Tiering | Partners are tiered on the scorecard; tier drives routing priority in the marketplace and commercial terms. The tier and its inputs are visible to the partner — an opaque ranking creates disputes and gaming |
| Quality intervention | Two consecutive amber periods → improvement plan with named metrics; a third → routing suspension; a compliance failure → immediate suspension pending review (BR-002) |
| Settlement | Reconciled monthly against the ledger (§35); disputes have a named owner, a 10-day resolution target, and a documented arbitration step before escalation |
| Compliance | Partner licence expiry is monitored on the same ladder as our own; an expired licence triggers the configured restrictions automatically, not by someone remembering |
| Relationship | Quarterly business review with the top partners by volume; annual with the rest |

---

### 59.9 Continuous compliance operations

Reference §40 for the engine; this is the staffing and cadence around it.

| Operation | Cadence | Owner | What "good" looks like |
|---|---|---|---|
| Expiry sweep | Nightly, with the reminder ladder at T-60/30/15/7/1 (configured) | Compliance | Zero documents that expire without at least three prior reminders having been delivered and read-receipted |
| Verification queue | Continuous, staffed to the queue-depth model below | Verification | P90 age < 3 working days; zero items older than 10 days without an escalation |
| Exception register | Weekly review | Compliance | Every exception has an owner, an expiry date, and a reason; no exception is renewed twice without founder approval |
| Licence register | Monthly | Compliance | Every licence (ours and partners') has geography, expiry, renewal owner and evidence attached |
| Jurisdiction rule review | Monthly, plus on notification of change | Compliance + counsel | Rule changes land as configuration with an effective date; never as a code change |
| Audit-readiness pack | Quarterly refresh | Compliance | Producible within 24 hours of a request, without an engineering ask |
| Filing calendar | Monthly | Finance + Compliance | Zero late filings; each filing has an owner and a T-7 reminder |

**Verification queue staffing model.** The queue is the deployment bottleneck: a guard cannot be deployed until verified (§58.6 LR-057), so a backlog here is a revenue and coverage problem, not an admin problem. Staff it from the arithmetic — `reviewers = (expected applications/day × minutes per review) ÷ (productive minutes per reviewer-day)` — recomputed monthly against actual throughput, with a documented surge plan for recruitment drives. `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-609]` — whether verification review is staffed in-house or partly outsourced to a BPO with our checklist, and how quality is sampled either way. Recommended: in-house at launch scale for judgement quality; outsource only the mechanical document-completeness pass, never the decision.

---

### 59.10 Data-quality operations

Reference §42.6. Operationally, four things run continuously:

| Check | Frequency | Failure handling |
|---|---|---|
| Orphan and referential checks (assignments without shifts, attendance without assignments, ledger entries without a counterpart) | Nightly | Ticket to the owning module with a 48-hour fix target; ledger breaks are P1 |
| Duplicate detection (guards by phone/ID, clients by GSTIN, sites by geofence overlap) | Nightly | Merge queue reviewed weekly by Verification; merges are audited and reversible |
| Completeness scores per entity (guard profile, site, client) | Weekly | Below-threshold records are surfaced in the owning role's task inbox, not in a report nobody opens |
| Metric reconciliation (platform figure vs manual recomputation for the north star and the top five KPIs) | Monthly | Variance >0.5% blocks the monthly reporting pack until explained |

**The correction path.** Data is never fixed by a direct database write. Every correction is made through an application path that produces an audit entry and, for financial data, a compensating ledger entry (BR-003). Where no application path exists, building one is the fix; a one-off script is permitted only under incident conditions, with two-person approval and a post-mortem.

---

### 59.11 Feedback to roadmap

| Stage | Mechanism | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Capture | Every channel writes into one intake: support tickets tagged `enhancement`, CSM call notes, guard grievances coded as product friction, Command Center operator observations, sales lost-reason codes, NPS/CSAT verbatims, AI refusal logs (what users tried to do that the system would not) | Support |
| Deduplicate and quantify | Weekly triage: cluster into themes, attach the number of distinct tenants and guards affected and the revenue at risk | Product (CTO) |
| Decide | Quarterly roadmap re-plan (§59.1), against §51's phase plan; anything jumping the queue must displace something explicitly | Founders |
| Close the loop | Every requester is told the outcome — shipped, planned, or declined with a reason. Declining honestly is fine; silence is not | Support |

**The one signal to weight above all others:** something a Command Center operator or a field supervisor does manually every single shift because the software cannot do it. That is a defect wearing a feature request's clothing.

---

### 59.12 Cost and unit-economics monitoring

| Metric | Cadence | Owner | Alert |
|---|---|---|---|
| Infrastructure cost per active guard per month | Monthly | CTO | >15% above the §52 model, or any month-on-month step change |
| Cost per 1,000 GPS pings, per notification, per AI interaction, per OCR page | Monthly | CTO | Any line growing faster than its driver volume |
| AI spend per tenant, with the top 10 tenants named | Monthly | CTO | A single tenant exceeding its plan's implied allowance (§52.4) |
| Notification spend by channel, with the SMS/WhatsApp mix | Monthly | Finance | WhatsApp category or rate changes; SMS volume growth outpacing guard growth |
| Gross margin per service line and per plan | Monthly at close | Finance | Any line below the §52 model floor |
| Payment gateway MDR and settlement timing | Monthly | Finance | MDR drift or settlement delay affecting working capital |
| Cost of a deployed guard-month, fully loaded | Monthly | Finance + COO | Variance against §52.2 |

**Standing rule:** every new cloud or vendor line item gets an owner and a monthly figure at the moment it is created. Untracked spend compounds silently and is discovered at exactly the wrong time.

---

### 59.13 Capacity reviews

Quarterly, against §50.2 volumetrics and the §57.8 trigger table. The review answers four questions with numbers, not opinions: *(1)* which resource will hit 70% utilisation first at the current growth rate; *(2)* how many weeks of headroom that implies; *(3)* which §57.8 evolution trigger is closest; *(4)* what the lead time is for the response, including any vendor procurement. Anything with less than one quarter of headroom becomes committed engineering work in the next roadmap re-plan. The specific things to watch first, from §57.2.2: Postgres write IOPS from the location and audit tables, Redis memory, WebSocket sockets per gateway instance, and month-end worker contention.

---

### 59.14 Release cadence after launch

| Property | Specification |
|---|---|
| Backend/web | Continuous delivery to production, trunk-based, behind flags. Target: multiple deploys per week; a week with zero deploys is a smell, not an achievement |
| Mobile | Fortnightly train, with staged rollout (10% → 50% → 100% over 72 hours) and an out-of-band lane for safety-path fixes. `[DECISION REQUIRED: D-610]` — confirm fortnightly versus monthly once store review turnaround is measured |
| Desktop | Monthly, auto-update with signature verification and rollback (§47.14) |
| Hotfix | Any time, minimum viable diff, same review standard, post-hoc note at the next daily standup |
| Release notes | Written for the audience: operational language for clients and agencies, plain-language in-app notes for guards, technical changelog internally |
| Quality gate | Every release carries the §44 regression suite green, the isolation suite green, and a passing synthetic SOS probe post-deploy — automated, blocking, with no override that does not page a founder |

---

### 59.15 The weekly leadership metric set

Defined once in §42 — this is the *operating* view: the fixed agenda of the Wednesday leadership meeting, in order, with each item's canonical definition owned by §42.

1. **GSDC and GSDC Rate** (§42.1.1) — the north star; absolute and rate, always together.
2. Delivery quality — attendance %, absenteeism, replacement rate, patrol and wake-check compliance.
3. Safety — SOS count, response times against target, incidents by severity, open incidents past SLA.
4. Coverage — unfilled posts, time-to-deploy, bench depth.
5. Compliance — guard compliance coverage %, verification queue age, expiring-in-30-days count, exception backlog.
6. Workforce — new joiners, attrition at 7/30/90 days, grievances open and aged, payment-timeliness SLA.
7. Commercial — new bookings, MRR/ARR, receivables ageing, collection rate, churn and logo movement.
8. SaaS health — active tenants by health band, activation milestone M5 conversion, at-risk list by name.
9. Platform — availability against SLO, P0/P1 incident count, error budget consumed, pages per on-call week.
10. Cost — infrastructure cost per active guard, AI and notification spend, gross margin trend.

**Rule:** each metric is presented with its target band and its trend, and only metrics outside their band get discussion time. A meeting that reads all ten numbers aloud has no time left to decide anything.

---
